title: Layers: Add Layer Mask uses the active selection
author: Multipad-cyber
body:
## What

Like Photoshop, adding a layer mask while something is selected now uses the selection as the mask:

| Add a mask | No selection | With a selection |
|---|---|---|
| Click | Reveal All (unchanged) | **Reveal Selection** |
| ⌥-click | **Hide All** | **Hide Selection** |

This applies to the **Add a mask** button at the bottom of the Layers panel and to **Add Layer Mask** in the layer context menu.

## How

`layer_menu_ui::add_mask_command(has_selection, alt)` picks one of the existing `layer.layerMask.*` commands, so the button and the context menu behave the same. No new engine commands, and no change to the commands themselves.

## Tests

- `add_mask_uses_the_selection`: the mapping, plus an engine round trip checking that the new mask matches a rectangular selection (inside revealed, outside hidden).
- `entries_follow_layer_state`: the context menu offers Reveal Selection only when there is a selection.
- `every_entry_is_a_known_command`: now covers the menu with and without a selection.

Checks run locally: `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib layer_menu_ui` (3 passed), `cargo xtask layers` (OK), `cargo check -p photocraft-ui-egui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (OK).

I also tried it by hand in the macOS release build: marquee and polygonal lasso selections, then the mask button with and without ⌥.

Note: with Rust 1.99, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --no-deps -- -D warnings` reports some existing `chunks_exact` / `filter` lints in files this PR doesn't touch (`gpu_canvas.rs`, `palette.rs`, `tone.rs`, `liquify_ui.rs`, `brush_panel.rs`), probably new lints in that clippy version. The two changed files are clean. I left those alone to keep this PR focused.

title: MCP: a panicking command no longer wedges the headless session
author: storybored379
body:
headless_op ran every tool under one Mutex<Headless> and mapped a
poisoned lock to "session lock poisoned". So after any command panicked
(e.g. a bug in a filter), every later tool call (doc_inspect, doc_new,
doc_save...) failed for the rest of the MCP session, losing unsaved
work. Edits run on a copy of the document (Session::edit), so the
session is still consistent after a panic: recover the guard with
PoisonError::into_inner and keep serving. The panicking call itself
still returns an error. 1 test (automation server).


### How it was found and tested
- Reproduced end-to-end through the headless MCP server (`photocraft-cli mcp`), then fixed.
- Regression test added; verified it **fails without the change and passes with it**. `cargo test -p photocraft-automation` passes on current `main`; `cargo fmt --check` clean on the touched crate.
- Files: `crates/automation/src/server.rs`
- Clean-room: no third-party source consulted; only public specs and black-box tools (poppler/ffprobe etc.) as oracles.

Found and fixed with Claude Code (AI-assisted).

title: GPU: Rgba16Float fallback when Rgba32Float isn't renderable (fixes #7)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #7. Also addresses the GPU-startup crash class in #4.

**Crash:** on adapters that can't use `Rgba32Float` as a render target (Intel Vulkan on Linux/Windows), opening a document/image panicked immediately:
```
In Device::create_render_pipeline, label = 'fs_content'
  Color state [0] is invalid: Format Rgba32Float is not renderable
```

**Fix:** the accumulation/render-target format is now chosen per adapter. `Compositor::preferred_acc_format(adapter)` returns `Rgba32Float` where it's renderable and `Rgba16Float` otherwise. The compositor carries the format through pipeline creation, the accumulation texture, byte-size, and the readback (half-float decode). The app selects it from the eframe adapter.

- **Capable GPUs: unchanged** — default stays `Rgba32Float`; GPU↔CPU parity is still exact (18/18 within 1/255).
- **Limited GPUs:** `Rgba16Float` (half) — renderable on all backends, ~0.12/255 precision, plenty for display (the CPU compositor remains the exact oracle).
- **Test:** `rgba16f_fallback_path_renders` forces the fallback on any GPU and confirms blend + adjustment render within display tolerance — so the fallback is exercised in CI even without the affected hardware.

I couldn't test on the exact Intel/Vulkan driver, but the fallback path itself is now covered by a test. @hambydustin-eng — this should also help #4; the Windows DX12 workaround you found was the same root cause (default backend's 32f render target).

title: cms tests: system_profiles skips malformed named-colour profiles
author: storybored379
body:
On Debian/Ubuntu with colord installed, `cargo test -p photocraft-cms` fails in `system_profiles`:

```
/usr/share/color/icc/colord/x11-colors.icc: unsupported ICC feature: curve type "\0\u{1}\0\0"
```

That file is a named-colour (`nmcl`) profile whose B2A0 `lutBToAType` is invalid per the ICC spec:
it declares 3 input channels, but the M-curve offset (32) leaves room for one curve before the
matrix offset (48), and the 48-byte matrix overlaps the B curves at 64. The parser reads the second
M curve at offset 48 and rightly rejects it, so this is a host-file problem, not a parser bug.

### What changed
Test only (`crates/cms/tests/cms.rs`): named-colour profiles are never used for conversions (the
test already skips them right after parsing), so `system_profiles` now also skips them when they
fail to parse. Any other profile that fails to parse still fails the test.

### How it was found and tested
- Found running the workspace tests on a Debian host with colord's profiles installed.
- `system_profiles` **fails on `main`** on that host with the error above and passes with the change.
  On machines without colord's `x11-colors.icc` (macOS, a bare container) the test passes either way.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-cms` passes; `cargo clippy -p photocraft-cms --all-targets` adds no
  warnings; the new lines are rustfmt-clean (the file itself has pre-existing rustfmt drift, left
  untouched).
- Files: `crates/cms/tests/cms.rs`
- Clean-room: ICC.1 specification only; no other CMM's source consulted.

Found and fixed with Claude Code (AI-assisted).

title: Codecs: camera raw files fail with a clear "not supported" error
author: storybored379
body:
Camera raw files are TIFF-structured, so `detect` sends them to the TIFF decoder, which can't make
sense of them:

- a raw image with the TIFF/EP CFA (32803) or DNG LinearRaw (34892) photometric interpretation fails
  with `Tiff: unknown photometric interpretation` (what opening a CR2/NEF/ARW shows today);
- a CR2 can fail with `Tiff: colour type YCbCr(8)`;
- a DNG, or a raw whose sensor data sits in a SubIFD behind an RGB IFD0, quietly opens that small
  preview as if it were the photo.

PhotoCraft has no raw developer, so the honest answer is a clear "not supported".

### What changed
- `codecs/src/codecs/tiff.rs`: before decoding, a small structural check recognizes camera raw
  layouts: the CR2 signature after the TIFF header, a DNGVersion tag, or a CFA / LinearRaw image in
  IFD0, its SubIFDs (tag 330) or the following IFDs (at most 16 IFDs visited). It only does
  bounds-checked reads of header bytes; anything malformed counts as "not raw" and falls through to
  the normal decoder. Such files now return `CodecError::Unsupported` with
  `camera raw files (such as CR2, NEF, ARW or DNG) are not supported`.
- Ordinary TIFFs decode as before (the existing round-trip, metadata and malformed-input suites pass unchanged).

### How it was found and tested
- Found when a camera raw file opened through the headless MCP server (`photocraft-cli mcp`) failed with the TIFF
  photometric error; reproduced with tiny synthetic TIFF-based raw files built in the test (no real
  photos or committed media).
- New `crates/codecs/tests/camera_raw.rs`: CFA, LinearRaw, raw-in-SubIFD behind an RGB preview, DNG
  and CR2 cases expect the camera-raw error; plain RGB/gray TIFFs still decode; every truncation of a
  raw header returns without panicking. 5 of its 7 tests **fail on `main` without the fix** (the
  messages above, or the preview decoded) and pass with it.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-codecs -p photocraft-io`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-codecs --all-targets`
  (no new warnings),…

title: Layer Style › Blending Options › Blend If (render, PSD round trip, command)
author: storybored379
body:
Blend If (Layer Style › Blending Options › Blend If: *This Layer* / *Underlying Layer*, Alt-drag to split a point) is how Photoshop users knock out a layer's whites or blacks, drop a sky in only over the bright parts of the photo, or keep texture out of the shadows. PhotoCraft didn't model it at all: the PSD reader parsed the layer blending ranges but nothing used them and the writer always emitted full ranges, so **opening and saving a PSD that uses Blend If silently removed it**, and the layer rendered unblended.

### What changed
- **doc:** `Layer::blend_if: BlendIf`, a list of `[This Layer, Underlying Layer]` slider pairs (entry 0 = Gray, then the mode's channels), each `BlendRange { black: [lo, hi], white: [lo, hi] }` on 0..255 as in the PSD record. `BlendRange::weight` is the dialog's behaviour: hidden below the black point or above the white point, a linear ramp across a split point.
- **io:** import/export map the layer record's blending ranges (Adobe Photoshop File Format Specification, *Layer records* › "Layer blending ranges data": composite gray source/destination, then a source/destination range per channel, each black low/high, white low/high). Layers without Blend If still write full ranges for gray + every channel, byte-for-byte as before.
- **format:** `.pcraft` saves it (`#[serde(default)]`, omitted when default, so existing files load unchanged).
- **compose (CPU):** after a layer (or a clipped layer) is composited, the result is mixed back towards the backdrop by `k = Π weights` over This Layer's own colour and the colour beneath it (Gray = Rec. 601 luma of R, G, B; then each channel). The mix is done on premultiplied colour, which is exactly compositing the layer at `k × alpha` because every blend mode's source-over result is linear in the source alpha (a test checks Blend If at half strength equals 50 % opacity, Multiply over a semi-transparent backdrop). Adjustment layers are judged by their result; pixels where the layer has no content don't …

title: Filter › Other › Minimum / Maximum: Preserve Roundness
author: storybored379
body:
Photoshop's Minimum and Maximum dialogs have a **Preserve: Squareness | Roundness** option. PhotoCraft only had the square element, so growing or choking a mask with Maximum/Minimum always gives boxy corners: a round dot grows into a square, and a soft rounded selection edge turns into a staircase. Roundness is the option people pick when spreading or choking masks and cutouts.

### What changed
- **algo:** `Preserve { Squareness, Roundness }` on `FilterParams::Minimum` / `Maximum` (`#[serde(default)]`, so older actions, smart filters and `.pcraft` files keep Squareness). Roundness takes the extreme over a disc, every offset with `dx² + dy² ≤ radius²` (fractional radii honoured: radius 1 is the four neighbours, 1.5 the 3×3 block). Each row of the disc is a horizontal window evaluated with the van Herk / Gil-Werman running min/max, so the cost is O(radius) per pixel regardless of window width. The square path is untouched.
- **engine:** `filter.other.minimum` / `filter.other.maximum` accept `"preserve": "squareness|roundness"` (default Squareness, as in Photoshop). The param shows up in `commands` / MCP, and the schema-driven filter dialog picks it up as a dropdown with live preview (same mechanism as every other filter choice; not checked visually here).

### How it was tested
- `algo`: a single lit pixel grown by Maximum matches the disc (and the square for Squareness) exactly at radii 1, 2, 3.5, 6 at 8/16/32-bit; Minimum and Maximum with Roundness match an exhaustive brute-force disc search on a textured image (radii 1, 1.5, 2.9, 4); the running-extreme helper matches `windows()` for every window size; old JSON params without `preserve` still parse. The two Roundness variants are added to `all_filters()`, so the existing tile-independence, selection and serde round-trip tests cover them too.
- `engine`: `filter.other.maximum {radius: 4, preserve: "roundness"}` grows a dot into the radius-4 disc at 8/16/32-bit, undoes in one step, the default stays Squareness, and …

title: feat(ui): confirm before discarding unsaved changes
author: torstfugl
body:
Closes #9.

## Summary

Adds confirmation before commands discard unsaved document changes.

Covered actions:

- Close / Close All / Close Others
- Revert
- Exit
- Native window close

Dirty documents get `Save / Don't Save / Cancel`; Revert gets `Revert / Cancel`.

## Implementation

Discard checks are centralized in `menus::invoke`. Commands that may discard work are listed in `DISCARDING` in `discard_ui.rs`.

If confirmation is needed, the command is suspended in `PhotocraftApp::discard` and resumed through `invoke_unguarded` after the affected documents are resolved.

Pending targets use `DocId` rather than tab indices, so tab changes cannot retarget a suspended command.

Native window close is handled separately in `discard_ui::guard_window_close` using `ViewportCommand::CancelClose` until confirmation succeeds.

A cancelled save dialog keeps the prompt open. Other save failures are reported in the status bar.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui`: 153 passed
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo xtask layers`
- Manually tested Close, Close All, Close Others, Revert, Exit, `Ctrl+Q`, window close, and Esc on Windows

## Limitations

The discard prompt is currently UI-only, so control-channel callers cannot inspect or answer it. `engine.execute` is unaffected.

Not tested on macOS, Linux, or web.

title: Never crash: steering rules, clippy.toml, forbid unsafe
author: echelon
body:
First PR of the never-crash rollout (`craftrules/standards/never-crash.md`).

title: Never crash: psd, codecs, format, io are panic-free
author: echelon
body:
Part of the never-crash rollout (`craftrules/standards/never-crash.md`, AGENTS.md *Never crash*). These are the file readers and writers, so they come first.

### Changes
- **Real crash fixed: crafted TIFF.** `tiff` 0.10 indexed an empty `SampleFormat` list (`index out of bounds: the len is 0`), so a 140-byte TIFF crashed File › Open. I found it by mutation-fuzzing the readers (psd, codecs, cms, lut and pcraft, about 240k cases); it was the only crash found. The fix bumps codecs' `tiff` to 0.11, which `image` already pulls in, so the duplicate 0.10 leaves `Cargo.lock`. I dropped one match arm for the deprecated `Value::RationalBig`, which 0.11 never produces. Regression test: `codecs/tests/malformed.rs::tiff_empty_sample_format_is_an_error`, which panics on tiff 0.10 and passes now.
- `codecs::Image::new` returns `Result` instead of panicking when the byte size overflows `usize` (only callers were tests).
- `format`: `par_compress` joins every worker and turns a worker panic into `FormatError::Io` instead of `expect`.
- `io`: `par_map` joins every worker before handing on a worker's panic (`resume_unwind`, the same as the sequential path), so `thread::scope` no longer panics over an unjoined thread. Threading a `Result` through the PSD exporter's emit chain would have been a much larger change.
- `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]` in all four crates. `psd::testgen` (test and fuzz data generator) and io's effects test module carry narrow allows.

### Checks
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-{psd,codecs,format,io} --all-targets`: no new warnings. The only warnings left are the pre-existing `chunks_exact` / `question_mark` ones in other crates.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-{psd,codecs,format,io}`: all pass.
- `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` for the four crates: OK. `cargo xtask layers`: OK.

title: Never crash: cms is panic-free
author: echelon
body:
Part of the never-crash rollout (`craftrules/standards/never-crash.md`, AGENTS.md *Never crash*). Independent of the other never-crash PRs.

### Real crash fixed
A gray ICC profile (for example, embedded in a PSD) whose `A2B0` tag is stored with the `mBA ` type parses fine. Re-encoding its RGB view (`Profile::gray_as_rgb`, which `composite_profile` uses for gray documents) then hit `panic!("unsupported lutAtoB stage layout")` in the ICC writer.
- `write::encode` leaves out a LUT whose stage layout its tag type can't store; `encode_mft`/`encode_ab` return `Option` instead of `expect`/`assert!`/`panic!`.
- `gray_as_rgb` drops the gray profile's LUTs. They take one input channel and would have stopped the RGB view from being the matrix/TRC model it builds; `is_matrix_shaper()` was false.
- Regression test: `cms/tests/cms.rs::gray_profile_with_reversed_lut_type_reencodes` builds that profile by hand. It panics in `write.rs` before the fix.

### Other sites
- `math::rgb_to_xyz_matrix` returns `None` for dependent primaries; its only caller uses constant built-in primaries.
- `Builtin::profile` indexes its cache by discriminant (new test `builtin_all_in_declaration_order`) instead of `position().expect`.
- If the shipped coated CMYK bytes ever fail to parse, the profile is rebuilt with `synth::coated_cmyk()` (the generator of those bytes) instead of panicking.
- Two constant-only `expect`s (inverse of the Bradford matrix, built-in primaries) use the documented narrow `#[allow(clippy::expect_used)]` with a reason.
- `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]` in `photocraft-cms`.

### Checks
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-cms --all-targets`: clean, with no new warnings.

title: CI: green on all platforms (rustfmt config, clippy 1.99, FXC-safe adjust shader)
author: echelon
body:
CI has been red on `main` on every run, for three separate reasons. This fixes all three.

**1. Format (Ubuntu).** The repo had no rustfmt config and had never been formatted, so `cargo fmt --check` always failed. This adds the same `rustfmt.toml` as EffectCraft/FilmCraft (`max_width = 160`, `use_small_heuristics = "Max"`), which also keeps the churn small. The formatting is a single commit with no code changes, and it's listed in `.git-blame-ignore-revs`.

**2. Clippy (macOS).** CI uses the latest stable Rust (1.99), whose clippy adds `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` and `some_filter`. The 21 sites are mechanical: `as_chunks` drops the remainder exactly like `chunks_exact`. Clippy still passes on 1.96.

**3. GPU tests (Windows).** On D3D12 without DXC, wgpu compiles shaders with FXC, which aborted on `fs_adjust` ("internal error: compilation aborted unexpectedly"). wgpu turns that into a panic, so all 19 GPU parity tests failed. A bisect on the Windows runner pinned it to two `adjust()` cases, Exposure and Selective Color, which loop over dynamically indexed vector components. They are now unrolled with the same math. GPU-vs-CPU parity passes on Metal and on the Windows runner.
   - The app could crash the same way, so `Compositor::try_new_with_format` now catches pipeline build errors, and the canvas falls back to the CPU compositor instead of panicking. A new test covers this.

Local results: fmt, `cargo test --workspace` (87 suites), clippy 1.99 `-D warnings`, layers, wasm and `panic_hunt` all pass.

Open PRs (#31) will need `cargo fmt` after this lands.

title: PSD round trip: read/write Vibrance, Color Balance, B&W, Photo Filter, Channel Mixer; corpus floors
author: echelon
body:
## What changed

**`crates/io/src/adjust_map.rs`**: parses and writes the five adjustment blocks that used to be missing. The layouts come from the public Adobe spec. Where the spec leaves something out, I followed the ag-psd docs (MIT) and the code comments say so.
- `vibA`: versioned descriptor (version 16) with `vibrance` and `Strt`. A missing key counts as 0.
- `blnc`: shadows, midtones and highlights as 3×i16 each, then a preserve-luminosity byte.
- `blwh`: versioned descriptor with the six weights, `useTint` and `tintColor` (`RGBC`). Missing weights fall back to Photoshop's defaults.
- `phfl`: version 2 (colour structure in RGB, CMYK, Lab or Gray) or version 3 (Lab ×100 as i32), then density % and preserve luminosity. Written as version 2 RGB, which keeps the colour at 16 bits.
- `mixr`: version 1, monochrome flag, then 10-byte records (4 sources + constant, in %). Written as R, G, B plus a gray record. In CMYK documents, a mixer that uses the black source stays raw.

**Nothing is dropped silently any more.** Every evaluated `Adjustment` kind now has an encoding:
- A Color Lookup with no table, or a bad one, is written as an identity 2³ cube with dither off. It renders the same.
- A Gradient Map with 0 or 1 stops is written as the two-stop gradient it renders as.
- The "not yet written" warning can now fire only for an `Unsupported` block whose key is malformed.

**No doc model changes were needed.** `photocraft-doc` already has every field PSD needs: the B&W tint, the Photo Filter colour, and the Channel Mixer constant and monochrome flag. `crates/format` is untouched.

**Fill export fix, found by the new corpus step.** Gradient fills that had no Photoshop pixels were exported in the canvas frame, not the frame their masks give them. The re-imported file was shifted (`gradient-fill.psd`/`.psb`, max error 0.26). There is a new `photocraft_compose::render_fill_content`, a small additive public fn, and export now uses it.

title: security: authenticate control channels and bound transport resources
author: Gh0stlyKn1ght
body:
## Summary

- require a first-frame bearer-token authentication handshake on the desktop and headless TCP control servers
- generate 256-bit per-launch credentials with the operating-system CSPRNG, with explicit token and token-file configuration for automation
- authenticate the MCP-to-GUI bridge before forwarding requests
- bound control requests to 1 MiB, batches to 256 steps, active connections to 16, and socket I/O to 30 seconds
- document the implemented controls and remaining capability/filesystem-policy limitations

## Security impact

Before this change, any local process able to connect to the loopback control port could enumerate and invoke the exposed automation surface. The servers also accepted unbounded JSON lines, unbounded batch lengths, and one worker thread per accepted connection.

After this change, control methods are unavailable until the client proves possession of the control token. Oversized requests and batches are rejected before dispatch, and each listener enforces a fixed connection ceiling and I/O timeout.

This PR does not claim to implement capability-scoped commands or workspace-scoped filesystem access; those remain documented follow-up work.

title: macOS: open files from Finder/Open With/Dock; file path, recent, warnings and .pcraft fixes
author: echelon
body:
On macOS, double-clicking a PSD in Finder, using Open With, or dropping a file on the Dock icon now opens it. This works when the click launches the app and when it is already running. Opening and saving files also gets several related fixes.

## macOS open-documents
Finder, Open With, Dock drops and `open -a PhotoCraft x.psd` don't pass the file on the command line. They send a `kAEOpenDocuments` Apple event, and winit 0.30.13 ignores it. winit also owns the `NSApplicationDelegate`, and its macOS docs say to handle this with your own Objective-C class via `declare_class!`. That needs `unsafe`, which our workspace forbids.

- **New dependency: `fmv-macos-events = "=0.1.0"`** (MIT OR Apache-2.0, macOS-only, 168 lines). It registers an `NSAppleEventManager` handler for `odoc` and `quit` behind a safe main-thread API. It registers before the event loop starts and again at `NSApplicationWillFinishLaunching`, so the event that launches the app is caught too. It leaves winit's delegate alone. Its only dependencies are `objc2 0.6.4`, `objc2-app-kit 0.3.2` and `objc2-foundation 0.3.2`, which are already in the lockfile, so it adds no other new crates. I read the whole source; the lockfile checksum matches the archive I audited, and the version is pinned exactly.
  - **Please review:** this crate is new (26 downloads, one version, written for another viewer app). The other options were writing the Objective-C glue ourselves, which needs `unsafe` in our crates, or single-instance socket forwarding, which can't help because Finder never passes files as arguments.
- `apps/photocraft/src/apple_events.rs` turns these events into `OsEvent::Open(paths)` / `OsEvent::Quit`. The UI drains them every frame through the new `Services::os_events` and wakes the UI when they arrive.
  - Open events open each file and focus the window.
  - A quit event (Dock › Quit, logout) goes through the normal close path, which asks about unsaved changes. Before, AppKit would have ended the process witho…

title: fix(ui): brush and eraser show the real stroke while drawing
author: sommerper
body:
While dragging, the Brush and Eraser drew a hard, flat egui polyline at the brush width; the soft brush only appeared on release.

The engine's new `brush_cmds::LiveStroke` shares `paint.stroke`'s setup and renders incrementally with `StrokeRenderer` onto a copy of the document. The canvas shows that copy and recomposites only each step's damage (preview key = stroke key + step). The commit passes the live stroke's seed, so its pixels match the preview, and reuses the canvas so only the stroke rect refreshes.

Downsampled CPU textures (documents over 4096 px, the Navigator) now update partially too, aligned to the downsample factor, instead of re-flattening the whole document.

title: Colour-managed canvas: document profile -> monitor (P3/Adobe RGB/ProPhoto/Gray/CMYK), linear EXR, embedded CMYK
author: echelon
body:
Colour-managed canvas for #46: non-sRGB documents now show their real colours.

## What changed
- **The canvas is always colour-managed** (`engine/src/display_color.rs`). It converts document profile → monitor profile, relative colorimetric + BPC. The result is cached per (document profile, mode, monitor) as a `CanvasDisplay`.
  - **Identity fast path:** when the source and monitor profiles match (or the transform is within half an 8-bit step of identity), nothing runs. Untagged sRGB, sGray, CMYK and Lab documents on an sRGB monitor take this path.
  - **GPU:** `canvas_lut` folds the transform into the existing 33³ display LUT, with Proof Colors, Gamut Warning and the 32-bit preview still applied on top. Filter and proxy previews use the same LUT.
  - **CPU canvas and Navigator:** an 8-bit `photocraft-cms` transform of the composite.

- **Monitor profile:** a new Edit › Color Settings › **Monitor Profile** setting (`auto` | built-in RGB id | `.icc` path).

title: Sandboxed WebAssembly plug-ins: photocraft-plugins (wasmi), plugin.* commands, Filter › Plug-ins
author: echelon
body:
## What

A sandboxed **WebAssembly plug-in API** (maintainer decision: no native `.8BF` hosting).

- **New crate `photocraft-plugins` (L4)**, registered in `xtask/src/layers.rs`. It is a host built on [`wasmi`](https://github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi) 2.0, a pure-Rust interpreter licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0. We write no unsafe code. The crate carries the never-crash `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, …)]` header.
  - **No host imports:** no WASI, file system, network, clock or randomness. A module that imports anything is rejected.
  - **Fuel budget per call:** 50 M instructions plus 4,000 per sample. It is metered in 20 M slices through wasmi's resumable out-of-fuel calls, so a **wall-clock deadline** (60 s, native) is checked between slices.
  - **Other limits:** memory cap 512 MiB, recursion cap 1,024, wasmi `EnforcedLimits::strict()`, module size ≤ 32 MiB.
  - **Fresh instance per band.** If one band fails, the other bands are aborted. Traps, exhausted budgets, malformed modules, bad manifests, out-of-range pointers and non-zero return codes all come back as `Err`. NaN or infinite output keeps the original value.
  - wasmi is built with the **portable dispatcher**. The default tail-call dispatcher overflowed the *host* stack on a `(loop (br 0))` module in our test profile, which aborts the process. Portable dispatch can't do that.
  - **Builds for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`**, so plug-ins work in the web build too. The web build has no wall clock, so fuel alone bounds a run there.
- **ABI v1** is documented in `docs/plugins.md`:
  - `pc_abi_version`, `pc_manifest` (JSON: id, name, version, kind `filter`, typed params schema, `overlap`, `area`) and `pc_alloc`.
  - `pc_filter(buf, len, w, h, channels, format, params, params_len)` filters in place on interleaved normalised `f32`.
  - `format` packs depth, alpha and the PSD colour-mode number. Nothing is converted, so it works at 8, 16 and 32 bits and in any colour mode.
  - Params are validated, defaulted and clamped by the ho…

title: Image › Adjustments overhaul: full params, one editor per kind, live-preview dialogs, Curves point deletion
author: echelon

title: Large images: adapter texture limits, banded compositing/export, proxy thumbnails, history byte budget
author: echelon
body:
Large documents (14k+) for #49: they now stay on the GPU up to the adapter's texture limit, and no path holds a full-size float composite any more.

## What changed

**GPU limits.** egui-wgpu asks for `max_texture_dimension_2d = 8192`, so every document over 8192 px fell back to the CPU compositor on every refresh. The desktop and web apps now request the adapter's own texture and buffer limits (`gpu_canvas::use_adapter_limits`; 16384 on the M4 Pro). Everything else stays egui's default: no extra features, and WebGL2 base limits on GL. The Rgba16Float and float-target fallbacks are untouched, and no WGSL changed. `interactive_bench` and `fx_bench` now request the same limits as the app.

**Compositor (`photocraft-compose`).**
- `render_tiled` writes tiles straight into the output. Before, it kept a second full-size copy (6.3 GB peak at 14k).
- New streaming APIs:
  - `render_bands`: hands the composite to a sink in ~8 MP bands.
  - `render_reduced`: banded area average, bit-identical to the old flatten-then-average.
  - `flatten_to_surface`: used by Flatten Image, Merge Visible, Copy Merged and the other flattened-surface users.
- `thumbnail()` works from a downsampled proxy for documents over 16 MP, when the proxy is faithful (no layer effects or vector masks). The proxy code moved from ui-egui to `compose::proxy`. This covers the navigator, channel thumbnails, histogram, `.pcraft` previews, the file browser and the automation thumbnails.

**Canvas.**
- The CPU fallback (`GpuCanvas::refresh`, factored out of `ensure_gpu`) renders and uploads in bands, with no full float composite and no full RGBA8 copy.
- The CPU-canvas texture is reduced in bands.
- On the GPU canvas the Navigator uses a cached 512 px thumbnail. Before, it ran a full-resolution CPU flatten on every revision.

**IO.**
- Flat export (PNG/JPEG/TIFF…, including indexed PNG) streams bands. The single-layer native path copies rows (the per-pixel `to_vec` is gone). Buffers come from `try_reserve`, so a f…

title: Persist brush presets (user + imported .abr) in a size-aware preset store
author: echelon
body:
## What changed

New `photocraft_engine::preset_store`: user and imported (`.abr`) brush presets survive a restart.

- **Layout** (`<config dir>/Presets`, desktop): one `<group>-<hash>.pcbrushes` JSON file per preset group (settings with every bitmap — sampled tip, Dual Brush tip, texture tile — replaced by a reference), content-addressed tips in `tips/<blake3>.pctip` (zlib, stored at 8 bits when the tip came from 8-bit data, else 16), and `index.json` (group order and deleted built-ins). Renaming/regrouping rewrites a small JSON file only. Tips nothing references are deleted.
- **Built-ins are never written.** A deleted built-in stays deleted; saving over a built-in or renaming one makes it a user preset that persists and replaces the built-in on load.
- **Sync on change:** brush preset mutations (`brush.presets.save/delete/importAbr`, `brush.defineFromSelection`, Preset Manager rename/delete/move, preset-file import) call `Session::brush_presets_changed()` (bumps `ToolState::presets_rev`). `Session::execute` syncs the attached store after the command, rewriting only groups whose content changed (snapshot compare). No debounce needed: a rename in a 500-preset store takes ~7 ms.
- **Safety (Rule 9):** atomic writes (temp + rename), size caps (16 MB group file, 64 MB tip, 2 GB store, 16384 px / 64 Mi-sample tips, 4096 groups), file names sanitised and validated so a backend can't leave its directory. Corrupt/oversized/unknown files, and groups with missing tips, are skipped with a warning and **left on disk** (a sync never deletes a file it didn't load, and tip GC is off when something failed). Write failures surface in the status bar.
- **Platform:** storage goes through a `PresetBackend` trait; `DirBackend` is `cfg(not(wasm32))`, `MemBackend` is used in tests. title: raw: Sony cRAW, Panasonic RW2 (RawFormat 5), uncompressed ORF + ORF previews; NEF blocked (clean-room)
author: echelon
body:
Extends the clean-room `photocraft-raw` decoder with three more vendor formats, and records why Nikon compressed NEF is still missing. Refs #50; the issue stays open for NEF, CR3, RAF and colour calibration.

## What decodes now

| Format / variant | Status |
|---|---|
| **Sony compressed ARW ("cRAW", SonyRawFileType 2)**, 14-bit output | ✅ decoded (ILCE-7M3, ILCE-7M4 samples) |
| **Panasonic RW2, RawFormat 5, 12-bit** (10 px per 16-byte block) | ✅ decoded (DC-G9) |
| **Panasonic RW2, RawFormat 5, 14-bit** (9 px per 16-byte block) | ✅ decoded (DC-GH5S) |
| **Olympus ORF, uncompressed 16-bit** | ✅ decoded (E-1, E-400) |
| Olympus compressed ORF (E-M1, E-M10 III, XZ-2) | ⏪ preview fallback. The maker-note preview (CameraSettings 0x0101/0x0102) is now found, so these open as 3200×2400 previews. Before this they failed with no preview |
| Panasonic RW2 RawFormat 4 and older (GH5, GX80, G9 high-res) | ⏪ preview fallback (JpgFromRaw) |
| **Nikon compressed NEF, lossless (NEFCompression 3) and lossy type 1/2 (1/4)** | ⏪ preview fallback. **Blocked on clean-room grounds, see below** |
| Sony "Compressed RAW 2" (type 6), Pentax compressed PEF | ⏪ preview fallback |

### Why NEF is blocked
Nikon's compressed NEF uses fixed Huffman tables that the file does not carry, plus a split-row variant for lossy type 2. I searched for an independent public description: Bill Claff's NEF Compression page, Laurent Clévy's NEF write-up, libopenraw's format notes, Jeffrey Friedl's analysis, the ExifTool Nikon tables, the img2nef docs and others. The only places that give the Huffman tables or the decoding procedure are dcraw/LibRaw source, or write-ups taken from it: Clévy's page says it is "commented dcraw" and quotes the code, and img2nef is GPL-3.0. ExifTool documents the metadata (NEFCompression 0x93, NEFLinearizationTable 0x96) but not the bitstream. The brief says not to guess from GPL sources, so I stopped on NEF. It still opens the embedded full-size JPEG. Unblocking it needs either …

title: GPU canvas: Rgba16Float display texture for 16/32-bit documents (#46)
author: echelon
body:
## What changed

The remaining part of #46: 16- and 32-bit documents are no longer shown through an 8-bit canvas texture.

- **Float canvas texture.** `GpuCanvas::format_for` picks `Rgba16Float` for 16/32-bit documents when the adapter can sample, filter, render to and copy it (`supports_f16_canvas`, which checks the format features). `Rgba8Unorm` stays for 8-bit documents and is the fallback. Tiles, mips (16F mip/encode pipelines are built only when supported), damage-rect uploads and the CPU band upload all follow the texture's format. A change of depth recreates the texture.
- **Memory budget.** 16F doubles the texture cost (36 MP: 183 → 367 MB with mips). High-bit documents above `F16_BUDGET_PX` = 100 MP (about 1.07 GB with mips) fall back to `Rgba8Unorm`. That way a 14k² 16-bit document stays on the GPU at 1.05 GB instead of needing 2.1 GB, in line with #71. Tile size and adapter limits are unchanged. `PHOTOCRAFT_CANVAS_F16=0` turns the float canvas off and `=1` ignores the budget.
- **Both refresh paths write it.**
  - wgpu compositor: the encode pass gets a 16F pipeline and drops the upper clamp, so values above 1.0 survive.
  - CPU fallback: a new f32 → half conversion (round to nearest even, saturating, NaN → 0) and a band buffer reused across bands.
  - The compositor's WGSL `adjust()` switch is untouched.
- **32-bit preview without clipping.** View › 32-bit Preview Options (exposure/gamma) moved from the display LUT into the canvas shader, where it runs before the colour-management/proof LUT. Values above 1.0 that the float texture keeps are now exposed into range instead of clipped.
  - New engine API: `ColorState::gpu_canvas_lut` (the LUT without the HDR step) and `ColorState::hdr_preview`. `canvas_lut`/`display_lut` are unchanged for other callers.
  - `CanvasDisplay::texture_buffer` no longer clamps linear values before sRGB-encoding them. The result is identical for 8-bit, because the 8-bit conversion clamps afterwards.
- Colour management (doc profi…

title: Adjustment dialogs: GPU live preview through a clipped adjustment layer (#77)
author: echelon
body:
## What changed

While an Image › Adjustments dialog (Levels, Curves, Hue/Saturation and the rest) is open on a pixel layer, the canvas no longer re-runs the command on a CPU proxy for every change. It shows the committed document plus a **temporary adjustment layer clipped to the target**: the dialog's settings, with the selection as its mask. The canvas compositor (wgpu) draws that layer, so a change only swaps the layer's adjustment in a shallow copy. The base document and the damage region are built once per dialog session. OK still runs the real destructive command (one history step). Cancel drops the preview and leaves the document untouched.

New module `crates/ui-egui/src/adjust_preview.rs`, with these GPU-path details:
- **Damage region.** A change recomposites only the target's content within the selection, grown by effect reach. Of that region, only the part the view currently shows is redone. The rest catches up when the view moves there (`switch_damage` / `uncovered`). Switching back to the document (Cancel or Preview off) recomposites the whole region.
- **Zoomed out on a large document** (more than 4 MP, view under 50 % in physical pixels): the preview is composited on a copy reduced to about screen resolution (`proxy_factor`), with its own document and layer ids and its own GPU texture. The copy is built once per session and zoom factor.
- **Navigator** waits until the settings have been still for 200 ms before updating, instead of building a thumbnail on every change.
- **Histogram** in Levels/Curves is not recomputed on each change. It was already cached per document revision (`tone::histograms`), and the preview doesn't change the revision.
- `GpuCanvas::supports(doc)` says whether the wgpu compositor would draw a document. The layer path is only used where it would; documents it doesn't cover keep the proxy preview.

**Cases that keep the CPU proxy preview**, because the layer composite can't match the command (see the module docs):
- targets tha…

title: fix(ui): shape tools show the shape while dragging
author: sommerper
body:
While dragging, the Shape tools drew a 1 px white box, which is invisible on a white canvas (the Line tool drew a 1 px segment). The shape only appeared on release.

The drag now previews the shape the commit will create: filled with the foreground colour, stroked with the stroke width, with the accent path outline on top. `vector_ui::shape_geometry` builds the `shape.create` params from the drag and is shared by the preview and `finish_shape`. The new `engine::vector_cmds::shape_path` turns those params into the same path `shape.create` builds (`live_from_params` + `live_path`). ⇧/⌥, corner radius, polygon sides, line weight and stroke width all show in the preview. The test `shape_preview_is_the_committed_path` checks that the previewed path equals the committed layer's path for every built-in shape tool.

Known limits: Custom Shape previews only its bounding box outline, because filling a non-convex shape needs triangulation. Preview colours skip the canvas colour management; the shape is exact once committed.

Unrelated cleanup, easy to drop: the preview needed a `[f32; 4]` → `Color32` helper (`rgb32`), so `hex()` and the options-bar fill swatch now call it instead of each repeating the same float-to-byte closure. The output is identical. I can revert those two hunks if you'd rather keep the PR to the feature alone.

title: security: bound automation previews and reply resources
author: Gh0stlyKn1ght
body:
Headless automation previews and control replies previously had no output-specific ceilings.
This change rejects oversized previews before compositing and bounds encoded replies and
retained batch results across headless JSON lines, desktop TCP, and MCP.

## Changes

- Cap headless preview requests at a 2048-pixel edge and 67,108,864 source pixels. Full-size
  previews (`maxSide: 0`) must fit the same edge ceiling; a smaller preview remains available.
- Reject PNG results above 5 MiB before base64 encoding or rendered-file writes.
- Bound JSON-lines replies and encoded MCP tool-result envelopes at 8 MiB, replacing an
  oversized reply with a complete error rather than emitting partial JSON.
- Charge retained batch replies incrementally and stop later steps when their quota is
  exhausted, including with `stopOnError: false`.
- Apply the existing 1 MiB request ceiling to headless JSON-lines stdio as well as TCP.
- Bound incoming bridge replies in raw bytes. Drop oversized frames without retrying an
  operation that may have completed; truncation inside UTF-8 follows the same rule.
- Decode bridged PNG screenshots with explicit edge, pixel, and allocation ceilings.
- Add sanitized regression tests and update the protocol/security documentation.

## Behavior and compatibility

An oversized full-size preview returns an error; requesting a smaller preview still works.
Explicit trusted-local CLI rendering retains its existing behavior. Reply-budget errors can
occur after an edit has run: the error reports that the operation may have completed, earlier

author: Ni-zav
body:
## PR #96 ,,, Liquify undo

**Title:** `fix(ui): make Liquify undo work with focused controls`

Fixes #96.

Liquify already has local Undo handling, but its full-window dialog contains focusable controls. When a slider owns keyboard focus, egui reports that it wants keyboard input and the global shortcut dispatcher returns before Liquify sees Ctrl/Cmd+Z.

This change gives Liquify's local shortcuts first refusal while the dialog is open, before the egui focus gate, while still leaving text-edit fields alone.

### What changed

- Route Liquify shortcuts before the general egui keyboard-focus guard.
- Preserve normal text-edit behavior.
- Add regression coverage for undo while a Liquify control owns keyboard focus.

### Regression test

The test:

1. Opens Liquify.
2. Creates a Liquify stroke.
3. Gives keyboard focus to an egui control.
4. Sends Cmd/Ctrl+Z through the actual shortcut handler.
5. Verifies the Liquify stroke is removed.

title: Menu overlap and overflow #92
author: Ni-zav
body:
Title: fix(ui): keep menu popups interactive and within the viewport

Fixes #92.

There were two related problems with larger menus.

When a submenu was tall enough to be moved upward over the menu bar, hovering inside that popup could also hit one of the menu titles underneath it. That caused the active top-level menu to switch unexpectedly.

Some menus could also grow past the bottom of the window, which made the lower entries impossible to reach.

This change:

makes the hover-switch logic check which UI layer is actually under the pointer, so a popup properly takes priority over the menu bar behind it;

limits tall menu levels to the available window height and makes them scroll instead of overflowing.

I added tests for both the overlapping-popup case and the menu-going-past-the-bottom case.

title: fix(ui): make Move transform controls interactive
author: Ni-zav
body:
Fixes #89.

This also fixes the transform/rotation part of #94. I left #94 open because #87 is already working on the shape preview/outline side of that report.

Show Transform Controls currently draws the box and handles around the selected layer, but they're only visual — you can't actually grab them.

This wires those controls into the existing Free Transform implementation.

Now:

dragging one of the handles starts Free Transform;

the area just outside the box can be used for rotation;

dragging inside the box still behaves like the normal Move tool.

I also changed the bounds calculation to use the engine's transform bounds instead of only raster surface bounds. That means shape layers can use the same controls too, which is what makes the rotation case in #94 work.

Tests cover shape layers, handle hit testing, the rotation area, and making sure the middle of the box still belongs to the Move tool.

title: Japanese support: IME input in the Type tool and CJK glyphs in the UI
author: kntrttm
body:
## Problem
Japanese could not be typed or displayed in the UI.
- Menus, panels and dialogs showed tofu (□) for Japanese text, because only Inter and JetBrains Mono were registered.
- In the Type tool, IME composition (kana → kanji) did not work. Only pasting worked.

## Cause
- `theme::install_fonts` registers no font with Japanese glyphs, and eframe's default fonts have none either.
- The Type tool handled `Event::Text` and `Event::Paste` but not `Event::Ime`. It also never set `output.ime`. egui-winit calls `set_ime_allowed` only when `output.ime` is `Some`, so the OS IME was never enabled.

## Changes
- **Type tool IME** (`type_tool.rs`, `state.rs`)
  - Handle `ImeEvent::Preedit` and `ImeEvent::Commit`.
  - The preedit text is written into the layer and replaced on every update, so it lays out like typed text. It is underlined until committed.
  - The caret rect is reported through `output.ime` every frame while editing, which enables the IME and positions the candidate window.
  - A stale preedit range (for example after undo) is ignored instead of panicking.
- **UI fonts** (`theme.rs`)
  - Append the first installed OS Japanese font to the end of every egui font family: Hiragino, Yu Gothic, Meiryo, Noto Sans CJK JP or IPA fonts, depending on the OS.
  - Latin text still uses Inter / JetBrains Mono. Only missing glyphs fall through.
  - No font is bundled, so there is no license or `ATTRIBUTION.md` change. A missing font is not an error. Native only (`cfg(not(wasm32))`).
- **Text engine** (`fonts.rs`): try Japanese fallback families before the SC ones.

## Not covered
- The web build still has no CJK font. This needs a bundled Noto Sans JP subset plus an `ATTRIBUTION.md` row.
- UI strings are not translated (no i18n yet).
- Text layers do not set a `ja` locale, so shared Han characters may use Chinese forms in some fallback cases.

title: fix(ui): pasting an image copied in another app never ran
author: tiredIsa
body:
## What changed

Ctrl+V / Edit › Paste did nothing when the image was copied in another app (screenshot, browser): the key press was eaten silently and the menu item stayed grey.

- `edit.paste`'s `enabled` predicate only checks `session.clipboard`, but the OS clipboard import ran inside `run()`/`invoke` — *after* the enablement gate. The shortcut handler consumed the key, `is_enabled` returned false, and nothing ran; the menu showed Paste disabled for the same reason.
- `logic()` now mirrors the OS clipboard into the session clipboard at 4 Hz (a full clipboard read every frame is too costly), so `has_clip` is accurate for the menu, the command palette and shortcuts.
- The shortcut handler force-imports before the enabled check on a consumed paste press, covering the <250 ms staleness window.
- A new `clip_external` flag (set on OS import, cleared by our own copy/cut) keeps `menus`' `edit.paste` handler centring external images — without it, an image pulled in by the poll looked "internal" and pasted at (0,0) instead of being centred, like Photoshop does for foreign clipboard content.

## Testing

- `cargo +1.97.1 test -p photocraft-ui-egui`: 209 passed, including the new `clipboard_tests::external_clipboard_enables_and_centres_paste` (Paste greys before the import, enables after, and centres the external image).
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`, `cargo fmt --check`: all clean.
- Verified live on Windows: image copied in another app → Ctrl+V creates a centred layer.

## Still open / notes

- Paste stays enabled after copying *text* in another app (the OS clipboard then has no image, and the session clipboard keeps its last image). arboard exposes no cheap "has image" probe, so Paste greys only when the clipboard is truly empty. Arguably friendlier than Photoshop's greying anyway.
- No commands were added or changed, so parity and `panic_hunt` are unaffected.

title: perf(compose): reuse bounded pattern preparation across render tiles
author: MikeeI
body:
## Summary

Pattern fills and effects repeatedly convert the entire source pattern into premultiplied float pixels for each CPU render tile.
This shares demand-prepared immutable patterns within a rendering invocation, including streaming bands.

The preparation owner reserves capacity before initialization and releases its mutex before conversion.
It retains at most 64 MiB of prepared pixel buffers and 64 entries.
Patterns that exceed that capacity use the existing direct-conversion path.
This bounds retained cache payload, not total render memory or concurrent fallback allocations.

Pattern lookup precedence, bilinear sampling, wrapping, phase, rotation, scale, and premultiplication stay with their existing owners.
Preparation executes in the requesting worker's document CMYK scope; no converted data persists across rendering invocations.

## Validation

- `cargo test --locked -p photocraft-compose`: 97 unit tests and 3 integration tests passed.

- `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm`: passed.
- Independent source review covered concurrency, lookup identity, CMYK scope, fallback, and lifetime.

With eight Rayon workers and three warm samples, median composition time was 3543.639 ms before and 1216.037 ms after.

title: Mix pass-through group coverage in premultiplied space
author: MikeeI
body:
### Problem

Pass-through group opacity and masks currently interpolate straight RGB and alpha independently.
Over a transparent backdrop this attenuates RGB twice when the result is subsequently composited.
For an opaque F32 child `[2,0,0,1]` in a half-opacity group, the CPU renderer returns `[1,0,0,0.5]` instead of `[2,0,0,0.5]`.

### Changes

- Weight the before/after composites by their alpha and group coverage.
- Interpolate premultiplied colour, then convert back to the buffer's straight-alpha representation.
- Return transparent black for zero combined alpha without dividing by zero.
- Apply the same equation to the GPU coverage shader.
- Extend the existing group-opacity test with the transparent-backdrop HDR case.

The shader's quantization, channel-mixing, and clipping-difference modes retain their existing equations.
The unchanged clipping-difference approximation and its RGB clamps are outside this fix.

### Verification

- The CPU regression failed before the fix and passed afterward.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu`: passed.

title: Disambiguate colliding document identities at session admission
author: MikeeI

title: Crop tool: move and resize the crop frame, Space repositions while drawing
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #100

## What changed
The Crop tool's gestures now live in a new module, `crates/ui-egui/src/crop_ui.rs`. Before this, every drag drew a new frame.

- **Drag inside the frame moves it.** This is Photoshop's *Classic Mode* behaviour: the frame moves over a fixed image. The tool has no Classic/modern option, so frame-move is the default. Moving the frame snaps its edges, like the Move tool's layer bounds (View › Snap and smart guides).
- **Drag an edge or a corner to resize.** You can grab an edge anywhere along it, not just at the drawn handle.
  - **Shift** keeps the frame's aspect ratio. On a corner the larger extent wins; on an edge drag the other side resizes about its centre.
  - **Alt** resizes about the centre.
  - A **ratio preset** in the options bar (1:1, 16:9, Original, custom w:h) always holds.
  - Dragging past the opposite side flips the frame. If a gesture collapses the frame below 1 px, the frame goes back to how it was.
- **Drawing a new frame:**
  - Drag outside the frame (or with no frame) to draw one. **Shift** makes it square and **Alt** draws from the centre.
  - **Holding Space while drawing moves the frame being drawn** (like Photoshop's marquee tools). Space used to switch to the Hand tool mid-drag and pan the view. It still pans when no crop gesture is in progress.
  - A click outside the frame keeps the current frame.
- **Cursors:** diagonal or straight resize arrows over corners and edges, a move cursor inside the frame, and a crosshair outside it.
- **Overlay:** short handle bars at the middle of each edge, alongside the existing corner handles.
- **Enter** commits and **Esc** cancels, as before. Esc now also drops a gesture that is still in progress.
- **Automation:** `ui.pointer` accepts `space: true` (documented in `docs/control-protocol.md`).

title: Community batch follow-ups: on-demand OS clipboard paste; fmt + egui 0.36 test port
author: echelon
body:
Follow-ups from landing the community batch (#87, #93, #97–#99, #101–#106, #108–#112):

- **#102 clipboard, reviewed change:** removes the 4 Hz background mirroring of the OS clipboard. Reading the whole system clipboard (possibly a large image) four times a second in the background is a privacy concern (macOS warns about apps reading the pasteboard without user action) and wastes CPU. Paste is now enabled whenever the session clipboard has content or a clipboard service exists with a document open; the OS clipboard is read only on an explicit paste. An empty or non-image clipboard is a quiet no-op with a status message. #102's centring of external images is kept. Tests: Paste enabled with zero reads; exactly one read per paste; 20 idle frames make zero reads.
- **Formatting and tests:** rustfmt at width 160 for #97/#98/#99/#101 code. #97's and #98's tests called `Context::run`, which isn't in egui 0.36, so they were ported to `run_ui`; #98's overlap test now waits three frames for popup hit-testing.

title: Fix flaky canvas_geom undo test (process-wide text gamma raced by another test)
author: echelon
body:
## Root cause

`canvas_geom::tests::turns_at_every_depth_and_mode` failed once on Windows CI (run 37263145060, commit ad86321, no code change) at the bit-exact `flatten(before) == flatten(after undo)` check.

Undo is fine. The cause is **test interference through process-wide state**: `color_cmds::settings_tests::blend_text_gamma_setting` switched the compositor's application-wide text gamma (`psblend::set_text_gamma`, Color Settings > Blend Text Colors Using Gamma) from 1.45 to 1.0 and back, while the other engine unit tests ran on parallel threads. The turns test document has a type layer. If the toggle landed between the "before" flatten and the "after undo" flatten, the anti-aliased glyph edges blended under different gammas. In the failing log, `blend_text_gamma_setting ... ok` is stamped 0.5 s before the turns test reports FAILED, so the two ran at the same time. The race window is only a few microseconds, which is why it showed up once, on the slowest runner.

Reproduced locally by toggling the gamma in a concurrent test. The same assertion fails with the new diagnostic: `Cw90 16 rgb: undo left 70 pixels different (max 0.0215); first (x, y, undone, before): (5, 5, ...)`. Those are glyph-edge pixels of the "Fj" type layer.

## Fix

- Moved `blend_text_gamma_setting` to `crates/engine/tests/text_gamma.rs`, its own test binary and process, so it can't race unit tests that composite type. It now also checks the 1.0 and 1.8 values and the restore.
- Documented the hazard on `psblend::set_text_gamma`.
- The undo assertion in `check_turn` now reports the turn, depth, mode, number of differing pixels, max difference and the first differing pixel, instead of dumping two 2560-element vectors.

The bit-exact expectation stays: undo restores the same document, and the CPU compositor is deterministic for a fixed gamma.

Not changed: `crates/gpu/tests/parity.rs::type_layers_blend_with_text_gamma` also toggles the gamma in its binary. No other test there composites type, so…

title: Dock: fixed-height panel groups, splitters, collapse, reorder; panels never vanish
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #88, Fixes #129

## What changed
**#88: group heights no longer follow their content.** Before, Properties grew when an adjustment layer was selected and squeezed Layers, and a layer with few properties let Layers grow again, so Layers moved whenever the selection changed. Now:
- New `ui-egui/src/dock.rs`: `DockLayout { order, heights, collapsed }` lives in `UiState::dock` (`#[serde(default)]`, so old state loads; you can set it with `ui.set {dock: …}`, which is documented in `docs/control-protocol.md`). Each group gets a fixed height. The last expanded group (Layers by default) fills the rest of the column. Content taller than its group scrolls inside the group, and Layers/History keep their own row scrolling and footer.
- **Resize:** drag the gap between two groups. Min heights are 80 pt (Layers 140). Heights are clamped to the window, and when the window is short the groups give way, starting with the one nearest the bottom.
- **Collapse:** double-click a tab, or use the panel menu. The hamburger/ellipsis button used to do nothing. It now offers Collapse/Expand, Move Group Up/Down and Close Tab Group.
- **Reorder:** drag a group by its tab strip and a drop line shows where it lands. Window › Workspace › Lock Workspace blocks this.
- **Persistence:** New Workspace saves the dock layout. Reset Workspace (and picking a preset) restores the default heights, order and tabs. The live layout (panels, tabs, dock) is kept in the preferences as `panelLayout`, written when the mouse is released, and restored at launch while Preferences › Workspace › Remember Workspace Changes is on. This adds one field to `photocraft-engine` `Preferences`.

**#129: panels switched or disappeared after a click.** The right icon rail *toggled visibility*, so one stray click on the Layers/Properties/Color icon hid that panel. Now:

title: Layers groups expand/collapse (#126); every displayed shortcut fires (#127)
author: echelon
body:
## #126: Layers panel groups expand and collapse

- Group rows now have a disclosure triangle. Clicking it opens or closes the group. Alt/Option-click sets every group in the document to the new state. The triangle takes the click, so the click doesn't also select the row or start a drag.
- Row order is fixed. The panel used to reverse a pre-order walk, so each group's header row appeared *below* its children. Now each group sits directly above its contents, as in Photoshop. Children of closed groups are hidden, but a Kind filter still shows matches inside closed groups.
- The state is `Group::expanded`. It was already round-tripped as the PSD section divider's open/closed folder type and in `.pcraft`. It is toggled by the new `layer.setExpanded` command (`{"layer"?, "expanded"?, "all"?}`, in the new `engine/src/group_view_cmds.rs`), which is a view change: no history step, and a clean document stays clean. `document.inspect` reports `expanded`, and the command is documented in `docs/control-protocol.md`.
- Layers rows now carry their layer name for accessibility, which the UI tests use.

Tests:
- Engine: toggling, `all`, no history, not dirty, and graceful failure for bad params.
- kittest: clicking a triangle toggles the group at 1x, 1.5x and 2x UI scale, without changing the selection or adding history. Closing a nested parent hides the child group's row. Alt-click toggles all groups. The collapsed state survives PSD export and import, and PSD-imported groups toggle.

## #127: shortcuts shown in menus and tooltips now fire

title: Type tool: caret/selection land on the glyph under the pointer; font size is live, one undo step, ~60x faster (#123, #124)
author: echelon
body:
## What was wrong

**#123: selection offset from the cursor.** There were two causes:
1. **Drag anchor.** egui only reports a drag once the pointer has moved past its click distance (about 6 pt). The canvas sent the tool's `Down` at the pointer position *at that moment*. So a Type-tool drag selection started a glyph or more from where the button went down. The same offset hit every tool, which is why the crop test from #132 had the offset written into it.
2. **PSD type.** An imported type layer keeps Photoshop's pixels until it is edited, but caret placement and hit-testing use our layout. When fonts are substituted, or line metrics differ, the glyphs you see and the caret positions don't line up. A click on the visible text could also miss the layer.

**#124: size slow and "no effect".** Each step of a size drag:
- recomposited the **whole document** (type edits had no damage rect; 24 MP CPU path: 300 to 490 ms per step, and seconds on real layout PSDs where the GPU compositor falls back);
- recorded **one history step** (a drag left dozens of undo steps).

Also, the size field showed and set the layer's *unscaled* size. Photoshop shows size × transform scale, so in PSDs with scaled type (common in layouts) the numbers didn't match the visible text. Wrong selection ranges from #123 meant edits could also land on the wrong characters. One thing to know: growing paragraph text past its box hides the lines that overflow, as Photoshop does.

## What changed
- `canvas.rs` (3 lines): a gesture's `Down` uses `pointer.press_origin()`.
- `type_tool.rs`:
  - Clicking into a type layer whose pixels aren't our layout re-renders it first, inside the edit session's single history step. Esc/Cancel restores Photoshop's pixels; native layers record nothing.
  - Hit-testing also accepts the layer's shown pixels.
  - Scrubbing any type field coalesces per drag: live every frame, one undo step. The key is the dragged widget plus the press time.
  - The options bar and Properties show …

title: fix(geom): saturate Rect::translate and inflate on i32 overflow
author: kevin9327
body:
## Summary

`Rect::from_xywh` already uses `saturating_add` so a huge width cannot wrap the far edge. `translate` and `inflate` used plain `+`/`-`, so nudging a layer whose coordinates sit near `i32::MAX`/`MIN` panicked in debug builds (and wrapped to the opposite side in release).

Use saturating arithmetic there too, matching `from_xywh`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p photocraft-geom --lib`
- [x] New `translate_and_inflate_saturate_on_overflow` (fails with the old `+`/`-`, passes after)

title: fix(ui): make tall menus scrollable on short displays
author: Ni-zav
body:
Fixes #138.

The previous menu overflow fix keeps tall menus inside the viewport, but on shorter displays they can still be difficult to actually scroll.

This tightens the available height for menu popups so the scroll area becomes active before the menu reaches the bottom of the window.

It also explicitly allows the supported scroll inputs for the menu content, including the mouse wheel and direct dragging.

I added a regression test using a short viewport that opens the Filter menu, sends a mouse-wheel event, and verifies that the menu content actually moves.

title: fix(ui): keep Layers row badges clear of names
author: Ni-zav
body:
Fixes #144.

The Layers panel currently lays out the layer name at its full natural width and then paints the right-side indicators (`fx`, blend mode, lock, and link) over the same space. With longer layer names, the text can therefore run underneath those indicators.

This changes the row layout so the indicator area is reserved first and the layer name uses the space that's actually left.

Long names now truncate with an ellipsis instead of overlapping the badges. The secondary layer description follows the same width limit, and inline rename also stays inside that safe area.

I also added a regression test covering long-name truncation.

title: PSD type layers: bounds regression tests; #148 is the layer's vector mask, not text bounds
author: echelon
body:
## Findings

I couldn't reproduce #148 as a text-bounds bug. Imported type layers already keep their full bounds.

- **The canvas clip is a vector mask.** In the designer QA PSD (generator from #144, `designer_psd`), "Headline 105" is the leaf with `i = 105`. The generator adds a 300×200 vector mask (`layer.vectorMask.add`, `[x, y]..[x+300, y+200]`) to every leaf with `i % 10 == 5`, so the text is cut at x = 685, the mask's right edge. Snapshot of the app with that PSD open:
  - As imported, the line reads "Headline 105: Aut". Properties shows W 541, H 29, X 388, Y 577.
  - After `layer.vectorMask.delete` on that layer, the full "Headline 105: Autumn collection" renders. Properties is unchanged, because the pixels were never clipped.
- **The other cut-off headlines are expected too.** "Headline 71" starts at x = 1287 and runs off the 1600 px canvas. "Headline 88" sits under opaque layers above it.
- **H 29 px is correct.** It is the ink height of a 36 px (36 pt at 72 ppi) line with no descenders, which is what Photoshop reports for a type layer's pixel bounds. A line with descenders measures about 35 px.
- **Round trip keeps the bounds.** Export → import of point and paragraph text created with `type.create` gives byte-identical pixel bounds and the same transform, shape and size.
- **Real Photoshop files land in the right place.** In the real-file corpus, all 21 Photoshop-authored type layers are within the geometry tolerance when we re-render them (`text_corpus`). That includes point and box text, Arial, Arial Black and Myriad, and 12–30 pt.

## Change

This PR only adds a regression test, `crates/io/tests/psd_type_bounds.rs`. It builds type layers the way the Adobe spec describes Photoshop writing them:
- A `TySh` with the text→document transform.
- EngineData with `EngineDict` / `StyleRun` / `ParagraphRun`, with `FontSize` and `Leading` in text-space units.
- `BoxBounds` for paragraph text.
- `bounds` / `boundingBox` and the trailing integer bounds.

title: Brushes: Tilt Scale, Brush Projection, Spacing checkbox, section locks, Mixer Wetness/Mix; Brushes grid + drag and drop; options bar through tools.setBrush
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #95. This closes the gaps #136 listed. Pen pressure on macOS and Linux is still tracked in #79.

## What changed

**Brush model** (`crates/paint`):
- **Tilt Scale** (Shape Dynamics, 0–200 %). It applies when Size's Control is Pen Tilt, and Photoshop greys the slider otherwise. A tilted pen squashes the tip's height before the tip angle is applied. At full tilt the height is multiplied by `1 − tiltScale/2`, so 0 % (the default) leaves the tip unchanged.
- **Brush Projection** (Shape Dynamics). The pen's barrel rotation turns the tip. Its tilt foreshortens the tip along the tilt direction by cos(tilt). This is done as a projection in the rasteriser, so sampled tips work too. Dual Brush dabs are never projected.
- **Spacing checkbox** (`spacingEnabled`). Photoshop's docs say: "When this option is deselected, the speed of the cursor determines the spacing." With it off, a dab goes down every 8 ms of stroke time (`SPEED_SPACING_MS`), so faster strokes spread their dabs further apart. Dabs are never closer than 0.5 px. Points without timestamps get one dab each. Chunked input gives the same dabs.
- **Section locks** (`locks`). Every section except Brush Tip Shape has one. When you pick a preset, each locked section keeps its current settings, and the locks carry over.
- **Mixer Brush**: Transfer gains **Wetness Jitter** and **Mix Jitter** (each with a Control and a Minimum), applied per dab in `mixer.rs`. The brush also carries `mixer` (Wet, Load, Mix, Flow, **Sample All Layers**). `paint.mixerBrush` uses these unless its params override them.

**Engine**
- New `brush_preset_cmds.rs` with `brush.presets.rename`, `brush.presets.move` (within or between groups, `before`/`index`), `moveGroup`, `renameGroup` and `deleteGroup`. Each has a graceful-failure test.
- The preset store index (#82) now also saves the full panel order, including built-ins. It is only written once the order differs from the default. Reordering, regrouping, renaming and deleting all persist across…

title: fix(ui): refresh Liquify preview after undo
author: Ni-zav
body:
Fixes #158.

Liquify undo rebuilds the deformation field, but the existing preview texture is updated from pixels that have not been rerendered. That can leave the visible image unchanged even though the stroke was removed.

This rerenders the dirty proxy pixels after rebuilding the field and after whole-field operations, before the texture upload consumes them.

The regression test applies two strokes, undoes one, and checks that the preview pixels change and match the rebuilt field.

The Eyedropper sampled only on the initial pointer press. Moving across the canvas while holding the button did not update the colour.

This shares the sampling path between pointer-down and pointer-move events, keeping Alt sampling for the background colour and ignoring transparent samples as before.

The regression test presses on a red area, drags to a green area, and checks that the foreground colour updates.

title: CJK UI font fallback: Simplified/Traditional Chinese and Korean, lazily loaded in locale order (#149)
author: echelon
body:
## Problem
#101 always registered one Japanese system font (Hiragino / Yu Gothic / Noto CJK JP) as the UI fallback. Hiragino has no Hangul and no simplified-only Han such as 图, so Simplified Chinese (图层) and Korean (카드 배경) layer names were drawn as empty boxes.

## Changes
- **`photocraft-text::cjk`** (new): CJK script knowledge shared by the UI and the Type tool.
  - `classify(c)`: Han, Kana, Hangul or Bopomofo.
  - `script_order(locale)`: the order fonts are tried in. `ja` puts Japanese first, `zh-Hans`/`zh-CN` puts SC first, `zh-Hant`/`TW`/`HK`/`MO` puts TC first, and `ko` puts Korean first. Any other locale puts SC first, so Japanese forms are used for shared Han only under a Japanese locale. Kana always prefers a JP font, Hangul a KR font and Bopomofo a TC font.
  - `ui_locale()` (cached, no unsafe): checks `PHOTOCRAFT_LOCALE`, then the OS, then `LC_ALL`/`LC_MESSAGES`/`LANG`/`LANGUAGE`. On macOS it reads the first `AppleLanguages` entry from `~/Library/Preferences/.GlobalPreferences.plist` with a small bounds-checked `bplist00` reader. On Windows it reads `HKCU\Control Panel\International\LocaleName` via `reg query`, and only the first time a CJK font is needed.
  - Per-platform font files. A face inside a `.ttc` is chosen by family name through skrifa, not a hard-coded index:

title: GPU compositor: paged residents and effect maps, so 20k+ documents refresh on the GPU (#49)
author: echelon
body:
Documents larger than the GPU texture limit (16384 px on most adapters) now composite on the GPU instead of falling back to the CPU.

## What changed

**Paged residents** (`crates/gpu/src/lib.rs`)
- Layer and mask surfaces are stored in square **pages**: up to `PAGE` = 2048², never larger than the device limit, aligned to the document grid. Previously each layer was one texture.
- The canvas is processed **page cell by page cell**. Each cell's chunks (1024², aligned to the grid) bind only that cell's pages: per cell, a uniform record per pass plus per-pass bind groups.
- Pages upload **on demand**, only for cells inside the requested region. A viewport refresh touches only its cells.
- Pages are evicted **least recently used first** once they pass a byte budget (`RESIDENT_BUDGET` = 4 GiB, set with `set_resident_budget`). Cells run in reverse order on every other frame, so a repeated full refresh of a document over budget starts on pages that are still resident.
- A new page is assembled straight into one mapped staging buffer and copied with `copy_buffer_to_texture`. Incremental tile uploads work as before, by copy-on-write `Arc` identity.

**Paged effect maps** (`fx.rs`, `sync_fx`)
- An effect region larger than the limit is built **per page cell**, over a window: the cell grown by the effects' reach (`MapProgram::reach`, the same reach that `windows()` uses, + 2 px). The maps are therefore exact inside the cell.
- Damage tracking, field reuse and the move fast path work per window. Paged effect entries are evicted LRU under `FX_BUDGET`.
- `Compositor::supports` no longer rejects documents or effect regions above the limit. It still rejects Multichannel documents, patterns larger than the real device limit, and effects whose reach would make a page window exceed the device limit.

**Bounded huge refreshes**
- `render` now submits partway through a frame once any of these passes its threshold since the last submit: staged uploads (512 MB), evicted bytes (512 MB), or…

title: Photoshop oracles via storytold/photocraft-corpus: pinned corpora, corpus feature, test-corpus, CI job
author: echelon

## What

This PR measures PSD fidelity on the features `corpus/psd` barely touches: **smart filters, effect shapes, the text engine, and adjustments in every mode and depth**. It does that against Photoshop-authored oracles. It also adds a pinned, verified, opt-in corpus workflow, which CI enforces.

The oracle PSDs themselves are not in this repository. They live in **https://github.com/storytold/photocraft-corpus**:

- 256 PSDs under `photoshop/`, authored from scratch with Photoshop 2026 by an ExtendScript generator. The generator is committed there too.
- A README in the craft frame, `AGENTS.md`, `SHA256SUMS`, and the MIT/Apache-2.0 licence files.

|---|---|
| `cargo xtask corpus` | Lists every corpus, its pin, and whether it is present |

title: PSD fidelity: 16/32-bit colour modes, Lab, Levels, Exposure, Dissolve oracle (corpus 133 → 140, psd-tools 212 → 222)
author: echelon
body:
PSD fidelity: 16/32-bit colour modes, Lab, Levels, Exposure and a Dissolve oracle. Rebased on #195. **`corpus/psd`: 133 → 140 of 170** (128 vs the merged image + 12 vs the thumbnail; floor 140). **psd-tools set: 212 → 222 of 309** (212 merged + 10 thumbnail; floor 222). Round trips stay at 169 and 307. The one psd-tools round-trip diff, `colormodes/4x4_16bit_cmyk`, is the slack in #195's floor of 307.

## Root causes and fixes

**colormodes 4x4_{16bit_grayscale,16bit_lab,16bit_rgb,32bit_grayscale,32bit_rgb}: 100 % of pixels differed.** These were not depth or decoding bugs. Photoshop stores no fill-layer pixels in 16/32-bit files, so our procedural gradient fill was compared directly for the first time. Three things were wrong:
- **Gradient geometry.** Photoshop lays Linear and Reflected gradient fills out between end points truncated to the pixel grid. On a 4 × 4 canvas, a 30° Reflected fill ends at the corner `(4, 0)` rather than `(4, 0.845)`, so it renders as `t = |x − y| / 4` (effectively 45°). New `compose::fill_layout` expresses the snapped end points as the angle, scale and centre offset that `effects::gradient_t` and the GPU's `gradient_t` already take, so the CPU and GPU share one layout. On large frames and exact angles the result is unchanged (tested).
- **Lab colours in descriptors** (`LbCl`: Lmnc / A / B) were not parsed, so the 16-bit Lab fill fell back to black → white. They are now parsed and written.
- **Lab interpolation.** Classic gradients with Lab stops now interpolate in L\*a\*b\*, as Photoshop does in Lab documents.
- **16-bit Lab a\*/b\* scale.** Photoshop stores a\*/b\* as `32768 + 256·a` (0..65280), not on the full 0..65535 range. This was measured from the file: a stop with `LbCl` a\* = 52.29 is stored as 46154 in the merged image. The scale is now applied to layer pixels, the merged image and patterns on import and export, and it round-trips exactly. The doc model keeps a\*/b\* on the 8-bit scale at every depth.

title: fix(clipboard): use the wayland clipboard for images
author: nuIIpointerexception
body:
## fix

on wayland, ctrl+v pasted nothing when the image came from another app,
and ctrl+c wrote it where no wayland app could read it.

arboard reaches the clipboard through x11 unless its
`wayland-data-control` feature is on. the two clipboards are separate on
wayland, so an image copied in chrome was never found. with the feature,
arboard uses wayland when `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set and falls back to x11
otherwise, so x11, macos and windows are unchanged.

wayland hands the clipboard to whoever owns it, so both services share
one long-lived handle instead of building and dropping one per call.

## verified

over the control channel on hyprland: a png from another process pastes
as a new layer at the source size, an external reader sees the copy, and
an empty clipboard stays a quiet no-op. clipboard tests pass (5), and
`cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` are clean.

## dragging

dead on wayland, from a file manager or a browser alike. winit 0.30 has
no wayland drag and drop. winit 0.31-beta adds it and egui-winit pins
`^0.30.13` on master, so this waits on egui.

|---|---|---|

| psd-tools/effects/shape-fx2.psd | 0.0110 / 1.46 % DIFF | 0.0043 / 0 % **PASS** |

2. **Spread/choke dilation uses the 5×5 chamfer metric**, like strokes already did. A group drop shadow around an ellipse is round at 0° and 45° and falls short in between, peaking near 15°, which is where the chamfer metric overestimates. Was 5/255 off with the exact Euclidean dilation, now within 2/255. GPU: spread uses the `StrokeOutside` field, and the new `ChokeInside` field replaces `OutsideInverse`.
3. **Text blending gamma**: type layers now mix coverage in *linear light raised to 1/γ* (γ = 1.45), not in encoded values raised to γ. Every coverage level of layer_effects' blue overlay edges now lands within 0.6/255; the old power mix was 6/255 too light near full coverage. This also makes ag-psd float-color pass. CPU and WGSL (`text_enc`/`text_dec`) are updated together.
