title: Layout documents: fix GPU device loss, live Move tool, local damage, no per-frame work (#125, #128)
author: echelon
body:
Layout documents (many text layers, groups, smart objects and effects) were slow to work with, and moving a layer could take the app down. To reproduce it, this PR adds a generator for a designer's layout and a benchmark that drives the real app on it. It then fixes what the benchmark turned up.

## The main finding (#128 "froze for a while, then disappeared")

On a 4000×3000 layout with 174 layers, the **first GPU composite lost the wgpu device**. The GPU planner shaded every layer's Content and Blend passes over every 1024-px chunk. That came to billions of fragment invocations in one submission, and macOS killed the command buffer. The app then panicked at its next GPU call (`Buffer 'pc_compose_uniforms' is invalid`). It happens on current `main`, with all the community perf PRs merged.

Fix: a plain layer that is transparent outside its composite bounds, and covers at most half the canvas, now composites only over its bounds and is copied back into the backdrop. "Composite bounds" means the layer's pixels plus effect reach; for a group, its visible children with theirs. Effect layers already worked this way. Empty layers draw nothing. The first full composite of the layout now takes about 50 ms warm. GPU vs CPU results on all 157 corpus PSDs are unchanged (`fx_bench --compare`), and there is a new parity test.

## Other fixes

- **The Move tool moves the layers live.** While dragging, the canvas shows the layers at the pointer and recomposites only where they were and are (`move_ui`). Before, it drew an arrow and committed everything on release. The preview shifts the rendered type, shape and smart-object pixels; the commit re-renders them.
- **Release is one `layer.translate`, one undo step.** Its damage rect refreshes the same area instead of the whole document.
- **A Move-tool click no longer nudges the layer.** With snapping on (the default), the release point snapped to a nearby edge, so a plain click moved the layer, added a history step, and recomposited …

title: Atomic saves: one crash-safe atomic_write for every document write
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #203

A crash, full disk or killed process mid-save used to truncate the destination and destroy the user's previous file. Every document write now goes through one shared `photocraft_format::atomic_write(path, bytes)`.

## How it writes
1. Temp file in the **same directory** (unique hidden name, `create_new`), `write_all`, `sync_all`.
2. Copy the existing file's permissions onto it (a 0600 file stays 0600); write through symlinks rather than replacing them.
3. Rename over the target. **Windows:** retried with exponential backoff on `PermissionDenied` (antivirus / indexer locks); `std::fs::rename` is `MoveFileExW(MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)`.
4. fsync the directory on Unix (best effort: the new bytes are already in place).

On any failure the original is untouched and the temp file is removed. `EXDEV` and unwritable folders return a clear error ("…the original file was not changed") and **never** fall back to writing in place.

## Routed through it
- App services `write` (Save, Save As, Export, Save for Web, preset export) and the preferences file. The old prefs `write_atomic` is now a thin wrapper.
- Engine `file_cmds::write_file`, plus every command that still called `fs::write` directly: layer export, smart object contents, pattern export, data-set export, video frames/GIF, droplet shims, preset store.
- Automation `files::save` (`doc.save`, CLI `convert` and `batch`), `write_render`, and capability-scoped `AuthorizedWorkspace::write` (same steps through the `cap-std` directory handle, so paths stay confined).
- The `.pcraft` store (zip and directory bundles, autosave sidecars).
- Web is unchanged: writes there go through platform services (downloads).

## Tests
`crates/format/src/atomic/tests.rs` injects failures through the `AtomicFs` seam: write fails halfway (disk full), rename fails, cross-device rename, a transient lock that's retried, and a lock that outlasts the retries. A real read-only folder test (where an in-place write would have succeeded) cove…

title: PSD stroke effects: outlines of filled shapes, vector stroke above interior effects, joined subpaths
author: echelon
body:
PSD fidelity for the Stroke layer effect on shape layers, and multi-subpath shape components.

Multiple instances (several Strokes / Drop Shadows / Inner Shadows / Colour and Gradient Overlays) were already in the doc model (`LayerEffects::items` is a list), PSD import/export (`frameFXMulti` & co. in `lfx2`/`lmfx`), `.pcraft`, CPU and GPU. This PR adds a PSD round-trip test for them and fixes what the corpus showed was wrong in stroke rendering.

## What changed

- **Strokes follow a filled shape's outline** (`compose::effect_outline` / `effect_shape`). Photoshop builds a filled shape layer's effects from its vector outline, not its pixels: where a gradient fill fades to transparent the stroke still runs along the whole path. The effect shape is the content's alpha completed by the path's coverage where the fill is see-through (`l + (1 − f) × coverage`, `f` = local fill opacity), so Photoshop's own rasterization still wins where the fill is opaque (shape-fx2's pentagon is ~0.4 px fuller than its path). Shapes whose vector stroke reaches past the path keep using their pixels.
- **Outside strokes share AA edge pixels with the shape as disjoint areas** (`effects::outline_share`): an edge pixel of an opaque fill ends opaque; a faded fill's edge pixel keeps only the part outside the path.
- **A shape's vector stroke is drawn above its clipped layers and the fill's interior effects** (colour/gradient/pattern overlays, satin, inner glow/shadow) **and below the stroke effect**; the layer mask applies to fill ∪ stroke together (was applied to each part separately: 0.75 instead of 0.5 alpha under a 50 % mask). The split-off stroke is fitted to Photoshop's pixels (`shape_split`).
- **Gradient strokes span the stroke's extent**: the shape's pixel bounds grown by the outside width less 1 px (a 4 px stroke on a 22 px square spans 28 px, as Photoshop).
- **`PathOp::Join`** for PSD subpath operation −1: the subpath belongs to the previous shape component and is filled together with…

title: Retouch tools paint the mask/channel target; Sample All Layers for Blur/Sharpen/Smudge; premultiplied Smudge (#207)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #207

## What changed
- **Paint target.** `run_stroke` (`crates/engine/src/retouch_cmds.rs`) now goes through `channel_cmds::target_surface`, the same paint-target logic the Brush uses. Clone Stamp, Healing Brush, Spot Healing, Dodge, Burn, Sponge, Blur, Sharpen, Smudge and History Brush now paint whatever is targeted:
  - the layer mask (`"target":"mask"`)
  - an alpha channel (`{"channel":i}`)
  - the Quick Mask
  
  The retouch ids are added to the routed set, so when `target` is absent it's filled in from the Channels panel. History Brush samples the same target from the chosen history state. The commands are enabled for a layer with a mask or a targeted channel, as the Brush is.
- **Sample All Layers** (`"sampleAllLayers"`) for Blur, Sharpen and Smudge, on layer pixels:
  - each dab's effect runs on a copy of the visible composite, which carries over between dabs
  - the result is laid onto the layer under the dab, so an empty layer above the image picks up the blurred or smudged picture
  
  `retouch_ui::finish_stroke` passes the checkbox and `paint_target()` to the command.
- **Premultiplied Smudge** (`crates/paint/src/retouch.rs`). The carried colour is premultiplied. The sequential-dab mix-back (`apply_dab_stroke`) also mixes premultiplied when alpha changes. Smudging across a transparent edge no longer drags black into the colour.

`edit.transform` with an alpha-channel target is handled in the #205 PR.

## Tests
- Engine, for every retouch tool: with the mask targeted only the mask changes; with an alpha channel targeted only the channel changes. Also covered: the Channels panel target is used when `target` is absent, the Quick Mask, and graceful errors for a missing mask, channel or Quick Mask.
- Sample All Layers: Blur and Sharpen on an empty layer over a checkerboard; Smudge dragging colour from the layer below. Each is also checked with the option off.
- No dark fringe when smudging into transparency, at 8/16/32-bit (engine), plus unit tests in …

title: PSD export: write tagged blocks other readers can parse (#200)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #200

## Root causes

Re-saving third-party PSDs produced blocks that psd-tools rejected or misread. Reproduced with `photocraft-cli convert in.psd out.psd` over the ag-psd test set (173 files) plus the pinned psd-tools set (309), checking input and output with psd-tools 1.23: **203 of 482 outputs gained a psd-tools error** that the input did not have (35 of them the `PlLd` "Invalid data section size" from the issue). There were five separate bugs:

1. **`PlLd` held `soLD` data (the reported bug).** A smart object's `psd_raw` comes from `SoLd`, the importer's first choice. On export it was written over the first of `SoLd`/`PlLd`/`SoLE` in *file* order. Photoshop writes `PlLd` first, so the `PlLd` key ended up holding a `soLD` structure. It was not a length or padding bug: the block was internally consistent, but under the wrong key. Export now picks the key in the importer's priority order and checks it against the data kind (`plcL` → `PlLd`, `soLD` → `SoLd`/`SoLE`).
2. **Global blocks were padded to even.** Photoshop pads document-level blocks to 4, and psd-tools steps through them that way. One odd block (for example a 77-byte `CAI `) shifted every block after it (`Invalid signature (b'IMOC')`, `Invalid data section size: 2/3`). They are now padded to 4.
3. **The layer info body (including the `Lr16`/`Lr32` global block) was padded to even.** It is now padded to 4 (`LayerInfo::pad_to`), as Photoshop writes it.
4. **Odd-length layer blocks** (a regenerated `lfx2`) had their pad byte outside the length. Photoshop and psd-tools keep it inside. It is now inside. An odd unknown block therefore comes back one zero byte longer on the first save, and is stable after that.
5. **PSB long-length keys.** `cinf` and `lnkE` carry 8-byte lengths in real PSB files (ag-psd `psb2`, `cyllinder-warp`). The spec lists only 13 such keys, so we misread these and wrote them back wrong. The list now also has `lnk3 lnkE pths extd extn FELS cinf artd`: `lnkE` and `cinf` were seen in t…

title: Packaging: Linux runtime deps + start-up library check (#201); wasm 26.3 -> 18.8 MiB (#198)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #201
Fixes #198

## #201: Linux .deb panics without libxkbcommon-x11

winit 0.30 and wgpu `dlopen` the windowing and GPU libraries. They aren't ELF `NEEDED` entries, so the package tools can't infer them, and `xkbcommon-dl` panics when `libxkbcommon-x11.so.0` is missing.

I checked the winit/x11-dl/x11rb/xkbcommon-dl/wayland-sys sources to see what actually gets loaded:

| Session | Libraries loaded |
|---|---|
| X11 | libX11.so.6, libX11-xcb.so.1, libxcb.so.1, libXcursor.so.1, libXi.so.6, libxkbcommon.so.0, libxkbcommon-x11.so.0 |
| Wayland | libwayland-client.so.0, libxkbcommon.so.0 |
| GPU (wgpu) | libvulkan.so.1 or libEGL.so.1 |

libXrandr isn't loaded (RandR goes through x11rb's protocol code), and neither is fontconfig (fonts are found by scanning directories).

- **.deb** `Depends` now has `libxkbcommon-x11-0`, `libwayland-client0`, `libx11-6`, `libx11-xcb1`, `libxcb1`, `libxcursor1` and `libxi6`. These were previously absent or only in Recommends. It keeps `libxkbcommon0` and `libvulkan1 | libegl1`. `Recommends` now has `mesa-vulkan-drivers`, `libegl-mesa0` and `xdg-desktop-portal`.
- **.rpm** declares the same libraries by soname (`libxkbcommon-x11.so.0()(64bit)`, …, `(libvulkan.so.1()(64bit) or libEGL.so.1()(64bit))`), so they resolve on both Fedora and openSUSE.
- **Flatpak**: no change. The freedesktop runtime already provides all of these.
- **AppImage and tarball**: these can't declare dependencies, so the start-up check below covers them.
- **Start-up check** (`apps/photocraft/src/linux_libs.rs`, Linux only, never wasm):
  - Runs before eframe starts. It picks the session type the way winit does (`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_SOCKET`, then `DISPLAY`).
  - Looks the libraries up in `ldconfig -p` (matching the architecture tag, so an i386-only copy doesn't count), then in `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and the usual library directories. It uses no `dlopen` and no `unsafe`.
  - If a library is missing, it prints the soname and the install command for the distro (a…

title: Scorecard: cargo xtask perf + scorecard, budgets, checklists, nightly perf (#221)
author: echelon
body:
Part of #221.

One place that says, with numbers CI keeps current, how PhotoCraft does on performance, file compatibility, tools, UI, type, automation, reliability and distribution: [`docs/scorecard.md`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/feat/scorecard/docs/scorecard.md).

## What's here

### `cargo xtask perf` (`xtask/src/perf.rs`)
- Builds and runs the release benches with `--json`, then merges them into `target/perf/results.json` keyed by scenario id (P1…P48). Each scenario records p50, p95 and max (nearest rank over the samples), peak RSS measured in-process, and GPU bytes held by the canvas.

  - `enforce = false` marks targets the code doesn't meet yet. They are reported as over budget, and only regressions fail them.

- Exits non-zero on a broken enforced budget, a p50 regression over 15 % (`--threshold`), or a failed bench row.
- `--quick` uses small synthetic documents: about 60 s here once built.

title: Fix live brush preview drawing a polygon (#189)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #189

## Root cause
Up to v0.1.1 the Brush drag was drawn as a stand-in: an egui polyline in the foreground colour, as wide as the brush, plus a filled circle on press. The soft stroke only appeared on release. egui tessellates a thick polyline by offsetting every point along its normal. When the line is much wider than the spacing between pointer samples (any zoomed-in drag), those quads fold over each other. The result is the hard pie wedges and pac-man shapes in the recording, fanning out from the start point. I extracted the GIF frames and they match: a hard disc on press, then wedges, then the soft stroke on release.

#64 (shipped in v0.2.0, a few hours before this report) replaced the Brush/Eraser stand-in with the engine's `LiveStroke`. On current main the Brush preview is the committed stroke. I reproduced in the real app (offscreen wgpu harness, `ui.pointer` mid-drag) and the canvas at the last pointer move differs from the canvas after release by **0/255** in every case I tried:
- zoom 50 %, 100 %, 400 % and 1200 %
- smoothing 0, 10 and 50 %
- soft and hard brushes
- 8-, 16- and 32-bit documents
- pressure on and off
- GPU canvas and CPU canvas (flipped view)
- UI scale 1x and 2x

The same brush-wide polyline still drew the **retouching tools' trail** (Dodge, Burn, Sponge, Blur, Sharpen, Smudge, Clone Stamp, Healing, History Brush, Background Eraser, Quick Selection). At 400 % a Dodge drag showed exactly the reported polygon artifact, in translucent white.

## Fix
- `crates/ui-egui/src/stroke_trail.rs`: the retouch trail is now a footprint mask in document space. Each segment is stamped as one capsule and overlaps take the maximum coverage, so they don't double up. The mask side is capped at 1024 px. It is drawn as one texture with partial uploads. No brush drag draws an egui polyline any more.

## Tests

title: Free Transform: selection moves only its part of a linked mask; masked preview; target masks and channels (#205)
author: echelon

Fixes #205

- **Linked mask with a selection.** `transform_layer` used to warp the whole linked mask while only the selected pixels moved. title: CR2: measure the colour filter row phase instead of assuming RGGB (#193)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #193

## Root cause

`cr2.rs` anchored RGGB at the image-area origin, from the SensorInfo left/top borders. I measured CC0 samples of 26 Canon models from raw.pixls.us and developed each with all four phases. Comparing the results by eye (ColorChecker, test charts, foliage, sky, skin tones) showed:

- **Red is in the even data columns on every model.**
- **Which data rows hold red varies by model, and the SensorInfo borders don't predict it.**
  - EOS 7D, 550D, 600D, 1200D and 5D Mark II start with a **green/blue** row (GBRG at data (0,0)). All five have top border 56.
  - The 40D, 400D, 450D, 500D, 1000D, 1100D, 5D, 30D, 1D Mark III and 1Ds Mark III have an **odd** top border. The 5D Mark III, 6D, 5DS R, 100D, 650D, 700D, 760D and 1D X have an **even** one. All of these start with a **red/green** row (RGGB at data (0,0)).

So the issue's own observation holds: neither the image-area origin nor the sensor origin is right for all models. The suggested "odd border offset shifts the phase" rule doesn't hold either. The 7D and 5D Mark III both have even borders but opposite phases. The 40D and 1100D have odd top borders, and the old code was also wrong for them (and for the rest of the odd-border group), not just for the four reported models. I found no structural cue that predicts the phase: LJPEG component count, slice layout and frame height all fail on at least one model.

## Fix

- Column phase: fixed, red in the even data columns (observed on all 26 models).
- Row phase: **measured from the data** (`measured_red_row`). The two greens of a 2×2 cell lie on one diagonal and share a filter. Compared with the red/blue diagonal, the green diagonal has (a) the smaller difference between diagonal neighbours and (b) nearly equal means. **Both cues must agree.** The measurement samples every other row pair of the image area and skips clipped and black samples. It adds only a few ms on a 22 MP file.
- If the cues disagree (flat, black or heavily clipped frames), a **fa…

title: Vertical type (tategaki): lay out, render, edit and round-trip (#199)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #199

Vertical text layers were stored and saved, but they were laid out horizontally. They now get a real tategaki layout.

## What changed
- **Layout (`photocraft-text`)**
  - **Flow:** vertical type is the horizontal line-space layout turned 90° clockwise. Columns run top to bottom and advance right to left. Leading is the distance between columns.
  - **Point text:** the column's centre line passes through the anchor, and the column starts at the anchor's y. This is the same convention as Photoshop: a Photoshop-made vertical PSD imports with its anchor exactly there.
  - **Box text:** columns wrap within the box height, start at the box's right edge, and drop columns that overflow.
  - **CJK:** characters stay upright and centred on the column. Vertical placement comes from `VORG`, then `vhea`/`vmtx` (top side bearing + outline top), then the ideographic em box.
  - **Punctuation:** characters get the font's `vert` alternates (、。 and small kana). Brackets, ー, dashes and full-width parentheses use their alternate, or rotate when the font has none.
  - **Latin:** non-CJK text runs rotated 90° clockwise, Photoshop's default.
  - **Styles:** baseline shift moves glyphs to the right, underline sits right of the column, strikethrough runs through the centre. Faux styles and warp keep working.
  - **API:** `TextLayout` gains `vertical`, `to_text`/`to_line`, `line_bounds`, `hit_test_line` and `caret_segment`. `bounds()` is in text space for both orientations, so warp, PSD bounds and hit-layer checks are correct.
- **Engine:** Convert to Paragraph Text / Convert to Point Text keep vertical columns in place. `type.orientation.vertical` no longer reports `"rendered": "horizontal"`.
- **Type tool:** caret, selection, IME rectangle and click/drag hit testing follow the columns. ↑/↓ move along a column; ←/→ move to the next/previous column. The options-bar "Toggle text orientation" button now works.
- **PSD:** export writes `WritingDirection 2` / `Procession 1` for vert…

title: GPU: crash-safe startup and device-loss fallback (#243, #4)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #243
Refs #4 (needs confirmation from the reporter on the Intel hardware)

## Device loss (#243)
- New `photocraft_gpu::health::DeviceHealth`: registers wgpu's device-lost callback and an uncaptured-error handler. It records a fault instead of using wgpu's default handler, which panics (`Buffer 'pc_compose_uniforms' is invalid`). `wait`/`poll` skip a lost device and catch the panic `Device::poll` raises on one.
- `Compositor::set_health` adds a check before each render, after intermediate submits and before readback. The change in `gpu/src/lib.rs` is additive.
- `GpuCanvas`: every entry point (`upload_*`, `composite`, `refresh`, `set_display_lut`, `read_texels`, the paint callback's prepare and paint) checks the flag first. `composite` is wrapped in `catch_unwind` as a last resort. `init_buffer` replaces `create_buffer_init`, which calls `expect` on the mapped range and panics on a lost device.
- New app module `gpu_status`: on a fault it drops the GPU canvas and frees its resources. Every view then draws through the CPU compositor for the rest of the session, documents are untouched, and a non-modal notice says **"GPU device was lost; using the CPU renderer."**
- No device recreation: eframe owns the device. After a real driver reset the window may stop presenting, but nothing panics and the documents stay.

## Crash-safe startup (#4)
- Before the device is created, `apps/photocraft/src/gpu_startup.rs` writes `gpu-starting.json` (backend, then adapter and driver) to the config dir and holds an OS file lock on it (`File::try_lock`). It clears the marker once the first frames (and any document opened at launch) have drawn.
- An unlocked marker at the next launch means the previous start died in the driver. That launch moves to the next safer backend:
  - Windows: Vulkan → DX12 → CPU
  - Linux: Vulkan → GL → CPU
  - macOS: Metal → CPU
- A locked marker means another instance is starting, not a crash.
- The working choice is remembered in `performance.gpuBackend`…

title: Stylus pressure, tilt, rotation and eraser on macOS and X11
author: echelon
body:
Part of #79: macOS and Linux X11 are done; Linux Wayland is a documented follow-up (below).

## What
winit 0.30 drops tablet data on macOS and Linux, so strokes painted at pressure 1. A new isolated helper crate, **`photocraft-tablet`** (`crates/tablet`, L0 standalone), reads the tablet data beside winit. The desktop app writes each sample into the existing `StylusFeed`, the same per-point path the web runner and automation already use. That path feeds pressure, tilt and rotation into `LiveStroke` and `paint.stroke`.

- **macOS**: an AppKit *local event monitor* (`NSEvent addLocalMonitorForEventsMatchingMask:handler:`) reads `pressure`, `tilt`, `rotation` and `subtype` from mouse and tablet-point events, and `pointingDeviceType`/`isEnteringProximity` from proximity events. It runs inside `-[NSApplication sendEvent:]` before winit's view gets the event, so the sample is current when egui handles the matching pointer event. The monitor only reads fields that are valid for each event type, to avoid AppKit exceptions.
- **Linux X11**: a second, pure-Rust X connection (x11rb `RustConnection`, safe) selects XInput2 `RawMotion`/`RawButtonPress`/`RawButtonRelease` on the root window. It also listens for hierarchy and device changes. Raw events reach every client even while winit holds the drag's implicit grab. Valuators are found by their label atoms ("Abs Pressure", "Abs Tilt X/Y", "Abs Rotary Z") and normalised from the device's min/max. It only starts when eframe's display handle is Xlib/Xcb.
- **Eraser end**: when the pen's eraser end comes in, the app selects the Eraser tool; when the tip comes back, it restores the previous tool, like Photoshop. It never switches during a drag. This works on macOS (proximity device type), X11 (an eraser device name) and the web (Pointer Events `buttons & 32`).

title: PSD manual and optical kerning: import, export, render, edit (#206)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #206

## What changed
- **Model**: `CharStyle.kern`, the manual kerning after a character in 1/1000 em, sits next to the auto mode (Metrics, Optical or Off). `.pcraft` stores it, and older manifests load it as 0.
- **PSD (observed in Photoshop 2026, clean-room)**:
  - A manual kern k after character c is written on character c+1 as `AutoKerning false` + `Kerning k`. Photoshop's writer does the same.
  - When Photoshop reads a file without `Txt2`, it takes `Kerning` on j as the kern after j−1. It also treats `AutoKerning false` on j as "character j−2 is manual". We write and read with the same rules.
  - Metrics, Optical and "0" exist only in the document's `Txt2` (style key `/11`). Import now reads them when the `TextIndex` object still holds the layer's text, so Optical is no longer downgraded to Metrics.
- **Layout**:
  - Manual kerning is applied as post-shaping offsets, so glyphs, carets, line extent and alignment all follow it.
  - Mode changes split shaping runs, as in Photoshop: pairs into or out of a manual character are not auto-kerned.
  - **Optical kerning** comes from glyph outline profiles sampled at 48 heights. It uses the closest approach plus the capped white space beyond it, compared with the font's "oo" pair. A linear model is fitted to Photoshop's output, plus a point-size term.
- **Engine**:
  - `type.edit {"kerning": number|"metrics"|"optical"|"off", "range"?}`.
  - `type.edit {"kernPair": {"at", "by"}}`: Photoshop's Alt+←/→, starting from the kerning the pair currently has.
  - Parameters are validated, and bad values return `BadParams`.
- **UI**:
  - In the Type tool, Alt/Option+←/→ at a collapsed caret kerns the pair before it by ±20; with ⌘/Ctrl held it's ±100. Each press is one history step.
  - Word movement is now on ⌘/Ctrl+←/→, Photoshop's mapping. Alt+Shift+←/→ still extends the selection by word, and Home/End go to the line edges.

title: Align the CJK fallback font's baseline with Latin text
author: kntrttm
body:
## Problem

CJK fallback fonts ( #185) sit too high next to Latin text.
egui centres a fallback face's row inside the primary font's row, so a face
with a large line gap rides above the Latin baseline. Hiragino Sans (ascent
0.88, descent 0.12, line gap 0.5 em) ends up about 0.23 em high next to Inter,
which is visible in layer names, tab titles and the Properties header
("Hello 日本語" has the kanji floating above "Hello").

## Change

`crates/ui-egui/src/cjk_fonts.rs`:
- `vertical_metrics(font, index)` reads ascent, descent and line gap (in em)
  from the face's `hhea` table (and `unitsPerEm` from `head`), including faces
  inside a `.ttc`. Every offset is bounds-checked; malformed data returns
  `None`.
- `baseline_offset(face, primary)` computes the `y_offset_factor` that puts the
  face's baseline where the primary font's would be. The result is clamped to
  ±0.5 em, and a non-finite value becomes 0.
- `add_to_all_families` sets that offset on each registered CJK face, using
  Inter as the reference. JetBrains Mono differs from Inter by under 0.005 em,
  so one offset serves both families.

Only the fallback face is adjusted: the primary font defines the row, and
moving it would shift every Latin label in the UI. If a face's metrics cannot
be read, no offset is applied (previous behaviour).

## Offsets for the system fonts on macOS

| Font | Offset (em) |
|---|---|
| Hiragino Sans | 0.234 |
| Apple SD Gothic Neo | 0.064 |
| Heiti SC / TC | 0.019 |
| PingFang SC / TC | 0.004 |

PingFang already matches Inter, so its rendering does not change.

## Testing
- New unit tests: `hhea` parsing (Inter's known values; empty, truncated and
  corrupt data, including a huge face index, all return `None`) and
  `baseline_offset` (Hiragino against Inter, identical metrics give 0, NaN
  gives 0, JetBrains Mono agrees with Inter within 0.005 em).
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib`, `cargo clippy --all-targets
  -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` pass.
- Visual check on macOS…

title: Colours: handle non-hex Unicode values without an internal error
author: storybored379
body:
A colour value such as `#€€` has the expected byte length, but slicing it into two-byte hex pairs splits a character. Pointillize, Filter Gallery, Render Tree and preference colour parsing can therefore fail before handling the invalid value.

Use checked slices so invalid components follow the existing fallback and invalid preference colours return `None`. Valid hex colours keep their existing behaviour.

title: Marquee: stop the selection at the canvas edge
author: Multipad-cyber
body:
## Problem

A rectangular or elliptical marquee dragged past the canvas kept its full dragged size, so the selection extended outside the document. On a 64 × 48 canvas, `select.rect {"x": -20, "y": 10, "width": 200, "height": 100}` gave `selectionBounds` `[-20, 10, 200, 100]`. Only the plain (no feather, replace) path was affected: feathered marquees and add/subtract/intersect already go through `combine`, which works inside `doc.bounds()`.

## Fix

In `select.rect`, as in Photoshop:

- The new shape is cut at the canvas edge (`r.intersect(&doc.bounds())`). The ellipse keeps the dragged geometry (centre and radii from the full rectangle) and is only cut, not squeezed.
- A marquee that selects nothing on the canvas (for example, dragged entirely outside it) deselects, instead of leaving an empty `Some(selection)` that other commands (Add Layer Mask, fills, strokes) would treat as a real one.

## Tests

- New `marquee_dragged_past_the_canvas_stops_at_its_edge`: a rectangle and an ellipse past the edges, and a marquee entirely off-canvas. It failed before the fix and passes now.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine`: 559 passed. `panic_hunt -- --ignored`: passed. UI marquee/snap tests (`snap_ui`, `marquee`): 10 passed.
- Release build for macOS (arm64) compiles with no warnings. Tested by hand in the app: rectangle and ellipse marquees dragged past the canvas edges stop at the edge, and a marquee dragged entirely outside the canvas leaves no selection.

Not changed: the rubber-band outline while dragging is still drawn where the pointer is; only the resulting selection is cut.

author: Multipad-cyber
body:
Three places where the Background layer (e.g. after opening a JPG) didn't behave like Photoshop:

## 1. Double-click the Background
**Before:** a double-click started the in-place rename. Renaming can't unlock the Background (it's recognised by name *and* locks), so nothing useful happened.
**Now:** a double-click turns it into a normal layer, "Layer 0", via `layer.new.layerFromBackground`, the same as the simple themes' lock button. Other layers still rename on double-click.

## 2. Add a layer mask to the Background
**Before:** the mask was added but the layer stayed a locked Background (lock icon still shown).

## 3. Cut / Clear / Layer via Cut on the Background
**Before:** they punched transparent holes into the Background, ignoring its transparency lock.
**Now:** the area is filled with the **background colour** and the Background stays locked, as in Photoshop and as PhotoCraft's Eraser already does on the Background. `edit.cut`, `edit.clear` and `layer.new.layerViaCut` share one helper, `edit_cmds::clear_area`, instead of two copies. Layer via Cut still lifts the original pixels onto the new layer. Normal layers still get transparency.

title: Portable mode: keep settings beside the exe in the Windows portable zip (#228)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #228

## Problem
The Windows portable zip wrote its preferences, brush presets, crash-recovery autosaves and GPU startup marker to `%APPDATA%\Photocraft`, so it wasn't portable.

## Change
Everything the desktop app persists already went through `services::config_dir()`. I audited every config, data and cache path in `apps/` and `crates/`: there are no `dirs`/`directories` calls, eframe persistence is off and the app writes no log files. `config_dir()` now delegates to one resolver in the new `apps/photocraft/src/app_dirs.rs`, which checks in this order:

1. `PHOTOCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR`, when set and non-empty (unchanged).
2. **Portable mode:** if a `portable.txt` or `PhotoCraft.portable` file sits beside the executable, everything goes in `<exe dir>\PhotoCraftData\`: `preferences.json`, `Presets\`, `Recovery\` and `gpu-starting.json`. This works the same on macOS and Linux.
3. The platform convention, as before (`%APPDATA%\Photocraft`, `~/Library/Application Support/Photocraft`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/photocraft`).

The resolver runs once per process. It creates `PhotoCraftData` and checks that it can write a file there. If it can't (read-only drive, or the zip extracted into Program Files), it falls back to the platform folder. It never crashes: it logs a warning, prints it to stderr and shows a notice in the app ("Portable mode is off").

Packaging: `package.ps1` copies the new `packaging/windows/portable.txt` into the portable zip. The file explains itself to users. The MSI doesn't install a marker, so installed builds keep using `%APPDATA%`. Docs are updated in `docs/releasing.md` and `docs/control-protocol.md`.

## Tests
Six unit tests in `app_dirs`, which run on every platform and fake `HOME`/`APPDATA` through an injected env:
- No marker: the platform dir is used (per-OS expectation) and no `PhotoCraftData` folder is created.
- Either marker: the data dir is `<exe>/PhotoCraftData`, every derived path is under the exe dir, nothing is written to the fake user fold…

title: Windows taskbar icon: .exe icon id for the MSI shortcut + icon regression tests (#248)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #248

## Diagnosis
The screenshot in #248 shows four things:
- Explorer shows `photocraft.exe` with its icon, so the embedded `.ico` resource works.
- The title bar shows the icon, so the runtime window icon works.
- The taskbar button is a **blank page**.
- So is a shortcut on the desktop.

The taskbar matches a running window to the Start Menu shortcut that launches its executable, and it shows that shortcut's icon. Our Start Menu shortcut is *advertised*. Windows Installer caches an advertised shortcut's icon under its `<Icon Id>` as a file name, and `PhotocraftIcon` had no extension. The shell can't read that file, so it shows a generic page (ICE50).

## Change
- **`photocraft.wxs`:** the icon id becomes `PhotocraftIcon.exe`. These are **the same lines as community PR #238**, kept byte-identical so that whichever PR merges second rebases cleanly. Please merge #238 first; this PR then only adds the tests and docs below. I left out #238's `check-icons.ps1` and ICE50 `wix msi validate` step so they don't conflict; they stay #238's.

  - The runtime window icon decodes, is square, at least 256 px, and isn't blank.
  - `assets/app-icon/photocraft.ico` (what `build.rs` embeds as icon resource 1) has 16/24/32/48/64/256 px entries. Each is a valid PNG or BMP whose real size matches its directory entry.

title: New Document: a typed Width/Height reaches Create (#254)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #254

## Root cause
Typing a size in File › New stored it in the dialog fields as a JSON **float** (`json!(from_unit(..))` gives `512.0`). `file.new` reads `width`/`height` with `Value::as_u64`, which returns `None` for any float, so the command quietly fell back to its default **1920 × 1080**. Presets store integers, so picking a preset worked and typing never did. Focus handling wasn't involved: egui's `DragValue` updates while you type, so Enter and clicking Create both already saw the new value. It was the type that was wrong.

## Fix
- `new_doc_ui`: typed sizes (in any unit) and the Orientation swap store whole pixels, clamped to 1–300000 (`px_value`).
- `file.new`: also accepts a finite float size (rounded and clamped), so an agent sending `512.0` gets 512 instead of a silent 1920.
- Painted dialog buttons (`widgets::primary_button`/`secondary_button`: Create, OK, Close…) now report an accessibility label, so agents and tests can find them.

## Tests
Kittests drive the real dialog (`crates/ui-egui/src/new_doc_ui.rs`, `tests::dialog`). Six of them fail before the fix:
- type 512 × 512, then Enter
- type, then click Create without leaving the Height field
- type over a selected preset
- click a preset card after typing
- inches at 300 ppi (2 × 1.5 in → 600 × 450)
- switching units leaves the pixel size alone
- orientation swap keeps whole pixels

There's also an engine test that `file.new` takes `512.0` / `511.6` and survives `-5.0` / `"x"`.

Gate: fmt and clippy `-D warnings` (1.99.0), ui-egui and engine tests, `panic_hunt --ignored`, `xtask layers`, `xtask wasm`, `xtask scorecard --check`.

Visual check: in an offscreen snapshot (1× and 2×) I clicked into Width, typed 512, did the same for Height, then clicked Create. The new document is 512 px × 512 px (72 ppi).

author: echelon
body:
## Photoshop's equivalent of the request

#231 asks for Krita's Shift+drag to resize the brush. In Photoshop, Shift with a painting tool already means *straight line* (Shift-click from the last stroke, Shift-drag at 0/45/90°; implemented in #188). So this PR implements **Photoshop's own on-canvas resize gesture** instead:

- **Windows / Linux:** Ctrl+Alt+drag
- **macOS:** Control+Option+drag

Behaviour:
- Horizontal drag changes the diameter: the circle's edge follows the pointer.
- Vertical drag changes the hardness: down is harder, and 200 screen points cover 0–100 %.
- The brush circle stays where the drag began. It is tinted red with a solid core that shows the hardness, and a **Diameter / Hardness** readout sits beside the pointer, which is hidden.
- Nothing is painted and **no undo step** is created. The drag is a series of `tools.setBrush` calls sharing one `coalesce` key, so it is a single journal entry. Because it is routed in `tool_event`, the control channel's `ui.pointer` (with `ctrl` + `alt`) drives it too.
- It works with every painting tool (Brush, Eraser, Background Eraser, Clone Stamp, Healing, Spot Healing, History Brush, Blur, Sharpen, Smudge, Dodge, Burn, Sponge) and with Quick Selection.
- Keyboard shortcuts stay customizable through Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts where applicable. This gesture is a pointer modifier, like Photoshop's, not a menu shortcut.

The marquee's W × H readout is generalised into `canvas::draw_readout`, which both overlays share.

## Tests (`brush_resize.rs`)
- `ctrl_alt_drag_resizes_every_brush_tool_without_painting_or_history`: for every applicable tool, dragging right grows the size, dragging down raises the hardness, and releasing the keys mid-drag keeps resizing until the button comes up. After release there is no history entry, no `paint.stroke`, and exactly one journaled `tools.setBrush`.

title: Menus are as tall as their items; scroll only when the window is too short (#235)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #235

## Root cause
The small-display work (#145 / #160 / #168) draws each menu level in an `egui::ScrollArea` with `max_height` set to the room between the menu bar and the bottom of the window (`menu_nav::level`). A `ScrollArea`, though, is also capped by its `Ui`'s available height, and a popup's `Ui` is only as tall as the popup was on the previous frame. On the first frame that's egui's `default_area_size` (400 pt). So the menu came out ~400 pt tall, the next frame measured it at ~400 pt again, and every menu and submenu stayed at that fixed height and scrolled, even at 1440 × 900.

## Fix
`menu_nav::level` now also sets `min_scrolled_height` to the available room, so the scroll area can grow past the popup's previous size. Auto-shrink then fits it to the rows. A menu scrolls (with the ▲/▼ arrows) only when its rows don't fit in the window. Submenus share this code path, so they're fixed too. `Nav` now records the shrunk view rect and each level's content height.

## Tests (`menu_nav_tests.rs`)
- At 1440 × 900, every top-level menu that fits the window (File included) has a popup exactly as tall as its rows plus the frame, shows no scroll arrows, and has every row on screen.
- At 1440 × 900, nine submenus of Filter, Image and Layer are also exactly as tall as their rows.
- At 1000 × 500, File overflows, stays inside the window, shows the scroll arrows, and the mouse wheel reaches its last row.
- The tall-window tests fail without the fix ("File: the menu is 386 pt tall for 792 pt of rows").
- The existing small-display, keyboard and scroll-arrow tests still pass.

Visual check: offscreen snapshots of File and Filter at 1440 × 900 and 1000 × 500, at 1× and 2×. On the tall window both menus show every item with no scrollbar (before the fix, File stopped at "Export" and scrolled). On the short window both scroll, with arrows, and stay inside …

Shift-click straight lines already work on main (#188, `stroke_constraint.rs`). Clicking, then Shift-clicking a second point, paints a straight line in one undo step. title: Selection drag previews: regression tests for #253 (visible mid-drag, 1x and 2x)
author: echelon
body:
Refs #253

## Root cause
In **v0.2.0** (`ad86321`), `draw_drag_preview` drew the Rectangular and Elliptical Marquee previews as a plain **1 px white** outline:

```rust
// v0.2.0 crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs
painter.add(egui::Shape::ellipse_stroke(r.center(), r.size() / 2.0, Stroke::new(1.0, Color32::WHITE)));
// or
painter.rect_stroke(r, 0.0, Stroke::new(1.0, Color32::WHITE), egui::StrokeKind::Middle);
```

`file.new` defaults to a **white** background, so the preview was drawn white on white and couldn't be seen. Release committed the selection, which is drawn as black-and-white marching ants, so the ants appeared only then. That is exactly the reported symptom. It also explains why only the two marquee tools were affected: in 0.2.0 the Lasso preview already had black dashes over white, so it stayed visible.

#188 (`4b53f62`, merged **after** v0.2.0, not an ancestor of the tag) replaced this with contrasting animated ants (`tool_feedback::draw_ants`, #172). So **main already has the fix**. It ships in the next release.

Repaints are not the cause. egui-winit already redraws on every pointer motion event. During a drag the ants also call `request_repaint_after(100 ms)`, so frames keep coming while the pointer is held still.

## This PR
Adds `crates/ui-egui/tests/drag_preview_canvas.rs`. These are wgpu kittests that send **real egui pointer events** (press, then moves past the click distance) and check the rendered pixels mid-drag:
- **Rectangular and Elliptical Marquee:** contrasting ants along every edge, on white and on black documents, at **1x and 2x**. The outline also follows each pointer move, so no frame shows a stale preview.
- **Lasso:** contrasting ants along the path. **Crop:** the area outside the frame dims while dragging.
- **Held drag:** a repaint is requested within 100 ms while the pointer is still.

title: Fast Select › Modify › Smooth and Feather (part of #211)
author: echelon
body:
Part of #211

## What
Select › Modify › Smooth and Feather (and every `feather` param that goes through `sel::feather`: `select.rect`, lasso, vector selections) used a naive O(N·r) box blur and a direct O(N·6σ) Gaussian. Both were single-threaded over the full canvas.

- **`crates/algo/src/selection_blur.rs`** (new)
  - **Smooth**: a running-sum box with edges replicated, O(1) per pixel. The contrast curve is unchanged.
  - **Feather**: σ = radius/2, kernel truncated at ⌈3σ⌉ and normalized, zero beyond the canvas (same semantics as before). Kernels up to r 12 are convolved directly. Wider kernels become a 5-term cosine series fitted per call by least squares, and each term is a sliding windowed sum (`Σ m[x+j]·e^{iωj}`). The cost no longer grows with the radius. The fit error is checked (≤ 0.3/255 per pass); if a fit misses, it falls back to direct convolution.
  - Work covers only the mask's non-zero bounds grown by the radius. Rows run through `par_rows`/`par_map` (serial on wasm). The vertical pass walks 64-column strips row by row, with no transpose. Windows inside a constant run (inside or outside the selection) skip the arithmetic.
- **`selection.rs`**: `mask_from_surface`, `mask_to_surface` and `combine` now use tiled GRAY8 fast paths: a byte table, parallel quantize, and only non-empty tiles are allocated. Replace no longer reads the old selection. These conversions were 40 ms + ~250 ms of each command.
- **engine**: `select.modify.*` refuse non-finite or out-of-range radii (the dialogs' 200/500/1000 limits) with `BadParams`.

## Numbers (24 MP, Apple M4 Pro, heavily shared machine)
| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Smooth r 50 (P26) | p50 19 296 ms (baseline), 5 338 ms (my run, load ~180) | p50 99.9 / p95 216 ms over 20 samples at load 104–114; fastest samples 32 ms |
| Feather r 50 (P27) | p50 42 668 ms (baseline), 4 335 ms (my run) | p50 122 / p95 357 ms at the same load; fastest samples 30 ms; one run p50 33 ms |

title: Compositor: effect maps never block inside parallel tiles (fixes #276 deadlock)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #276

## The deadlock

`effect_maps` built a layer's effect maps inside `OnceLock::get_or_init` from the parallel per-tile render. The build runs Rayon work of its own (gradient fill rows, `path_coverage` strips). While the worker waits on that work, it can steal another tile of the **same layer**. That tile then blocks in `get_or_init` on the lock held further up the same thread's stack, and the process sits at 0 % CPU forever.

**Reproduced on `main`:** the new regression test hung on the old code with an 8-thread or 16-thread pool and hit its 120 s watchdog. It passed with 2 or 4 threads, where stealing across that wait is rare. A `sample` of the hung process (0.0 % CPU) showed 8 of 11 threads parked in `std::sync::once::queue::Once::call`. They were under `OnceLock<FxEntry>::initialize`, called from `effect_maps` at `lib.rs:1277`, inside `rayon_core::WorkerThread::wait_until_cold`. That is the stack the issue describes.

## Fix (`crates/compose/src/lib.rs`)

- **Prepare once per render.** `render_tiled_with` (the path behind `render`, `render_tiled`, `render_bands`, `flatten*`, `render_reduced*`, thumbnails and the GPU fallback's region renders) now builds the effect maps for every visible layer that can reach the render rect **before** the parallel tiles start. Groups and clipping groups are walked with a depth cap. The builds run in parallel across layers, inside the tiles' CMYK and Lab thread-local setting. The finished `Arc<FxMaps>` are pinned in the render `Ctx`, so tiles only read them, and cache eviction can't force a rebuild partway through a render. This works the same way patterns and vector masks are already prepared (#104/#112).
- **Non-blocking cache (fallback).** The global cache keeps the same key, byte budget and eviction. Slots are now filled with `get()`, and on a miss the thread builds the maps and calls `set()`. The first build wins and the others are dropped. Nothing waits on another thread's build, so a tile that misses the prepare st…

title: Smart Objects and Smart Filters survive PSD save and open
author: echelon
body:
Part of #215

## What changes

**Export (smart objects stay smart objects)**
- Every smart object is written as one. Before, PhotoCraft-made or edited ones were flattened to pixels.
- We write `PlLd` + `SoLd`: `Idnt`, `placed`, the transform quad, `Sz`, `Rslt`, the warp (presets and 1×1 custom meshes), and `filterFX`.
- The source goes into `lnk2` (item version 7, NUL-terminated name). A `.pcraft` source becomes a **PSB of the nested document**, written by our own PSD writer and recursive up to 8 levels deep. Image files are embedded as they are. A linked file on disk is read and embedded, with a warning.
- Each filtered smart object also gets an `FEid` filter cache: the unfiltered placed pixels plus the filter mask. Photoshop **crashes** when it re-renders an `FEid` item that has no pixel planes. It also clips filters to the planes' bounds and reads white under transparent pixels. All three behaviours are handled and checked against Photoshop.
- Imported smart objects that nothing changed are written byte for byte. Edited ones are regenerated from the imported descriptor, so unknown keys are kept.
- Unreferenced `lnk2` items are dropped, and identical sources share one item.
- `PlLd` is always written next to `SoLd`, as Photoshop does in every corpus file.

**Import (filters come in live)**
- The `filterFX` list maps to `SmartFilter`, with each filter's enabled flag, blend mode and opacity. 14 filters map both ways:
  - Gaussian, Box and Motion Blur
  - Unsharp Mask
  - Add Noise (with its seed)
  - Median, High Pass, Maximum, Minimum
  - Mosaic, Emboss
  - Levels, Curves, Shadows/Highlights
- Any other filter is kept **verbatim** as `psd.unsupportedFilter` (its descriptor stored as hex). It is listed in the Layers panel as "(kept, not editable)". It can be hidden, moved or deleted but not edited, and it is written back unchanged.
- The filter mask and its switches come from `FEid`.

title: Background jobs: engine job API, progress and cancel (part of #210)
author: echelon
body:
Part of #210 (1/2: engine API + cancellation points; the app UI is the stacked PR).

## What
- `engine/jobs.rs`: a command runs as a job via `Session::start`: its heavy part runs on a worker thread (`std::thread`, results over a channel) against a copy-on-write document snapshot and gets a `JobCtx` (`progress(f32, &str)` backed by `AtomicU32::fetch_max`, so monotonic; `cancelled()` backed by `AtomicBool`). `poll_jobs` (each frame) applies the result on the calling thread as **one undo step** through the normal command path (journal, history, damage, post-command hooks). `Session::execute` is unchanged (runs inline), and wasm always runs inline: commands are written once (`jobs::run` / `jobs::edit_job`).
- Cancel discards the result; the document is never touched by a worker. A panic in the worker becomes an error. Applying refuses if the document changed meanwhile.
- A running job locks its document: edits, undo/redo are disabled with "“Gaussian Blur” is still running on this document; wait for it to finish or cancel it (Esc)"; queries and document-independent commands still run. Closing the document cancels its jobs.
- `Session::start_open` (background file open, reads + decodes on the worker), `start_job` (non-command jobs), `wait_job`, `cancel_job`, `jobs()`; commands `jobs.list`, `jobs.cancel`.
- Cancellation points (`photocraft_raster::Interrupt`, a Sync cancel check + progress sink): filters per tile (`algo::apply_in_with`), Content-Aware Fill per EM iteration / PatchMatch pass / row band + cancellable membrane solve, Content-Aware Scale per seam, Photomerge per stage and image, ABR import per brush, PSD/PSB open per layer record (`io::import_with`).

title: Stamp Visible (Cmd+Alt+Shift+E) and Alt+Merge: merge into a new layer, keeping the originals
author: christosdaggas
body:
Refs #217

Adds Photoshop's **stamp** commands: merging into a **new** layer while **keeping the original layers**. This PR is independent; it's based on the current `main`.

## What you can do now

| Action | Shortcut | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **Stamp Visible** | ⌘⌥⇧E / Ctrl+Alt+Shift+E | A new "Layer N" above the active layer, holding everything visible merged together. Hidden layers stay out of it, and nothing else changes. |
| **Stamp Layers** (several layers selected) | ⌘⌥E / Ctrl+Alt+E | A new "*top layer* (merged)" layer above the topmost selected one. The selected layers stay as they are. |
| **Stamp Down** (one layer selected) | ⌘⌥E / Ctrl+Alt+E | A copy of the layer is merged into the layer below it. The layer itself stays, and stays active. |
| **⌥/Alt + Layer › Merge Visible** | — | Runs Stamp Visible, as in Photoshop. |
| **⌥/Alt + Layer › Merge Layers / Merge Down** | — | Runs Stamp Layers / Stamp Down. |

Each one is a single undo step.

## How it's built
- Two new engine commands in `layer_multi_cmds.rs`: `layer.stampVisible` and `layer.stampLayers` (one layer: Stamp Down). Photoshop has no menu items for them, so like the fill keys they live under Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts and can be rebound, recorded and driven by agents.
- `composite_layer` is the shared "composite these layers into a new raster layer" helper. Merge Layers now uses it too, so all of them composite identically.
- `menus::alt_variant` maps a menu item to its ⌥ command; the menu bar runs it when Alt is held while an item is chosen.
- Errors, never panics: nothing visible to stamp, no layer below, stamping into a group.

## Testing
Run locally on Linux:
- `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo xtask layers`: all pass.
- `panic_hunt`, which fuzzes every command including the new ones: passes. `parity`: unchanged. `scorecard`: UI-217-22 → done.

Fixes #297

Two Photoshop mouse gestures that were missing. This PR is independent and based on the current `main`.

| Gesture | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| **Alt + mouse wheel** | panned the canvas | **zooms in/out around the pointer, about 5 % per wheel notch** (smooth on trackpads) |

title: Fix EXIF orientation on import and prevent double rotation on export (#285)
author: christosdaggas
body:
## Summary

Fixes #285 — **JPEG EXIF orientation ignored on open but kept on export (rotated images export sideways)**, reported by @bekhruzbekswe.

- Apply all eight EXIF orientations, including mirrored variants, at the shared codec decode boundary used by desktop and CLI imports.
- Reset the main-image Orientation tag to `1` after transforming the pixels, preventing a second rotation on export. Preserve pixel sample bits, ICC profiles and unrelated EXIF bytes; swap horizontal/vertical resolution when axes swap.
- Use bounded, checked EXIF parsing and fallible pixel-buffer allocation. Ignore malformed, unsupported or ambiguous orientation entries without following thumbnail/sub-IFD chains.

For the issue's `4032×3024`, Orientation-6 input, opening now produces an upright `3024×4032` document. Export retains Orientation `1`. An explicit `90cw` command then applies an additional user-requested rotation, rather than serving as an import workaround.

- Five orientation unit/property tests passed: all supported layouts and sample depths, no-copy identity handling, prefixed EXIF, duplicate entries, and arbitrary malformed bytes.
- Process-level CLI regression passed: oriented JPEG → PNG, explicit rotation → JPEG, and `.pcraft` save/reopen. Tests verify physical PNG dimensions and raw exported EXIF, and independently inspect JPEG/PNG/WebP metadata through decoder backends.

title: fix(ui): feed every pointer move per frame so fast strokes stay smooth
author: leonaci
body:
Fixes #316.

## Problem
Fast strokes render as a coarse polyline (jagged curve), reproduced with a **pen tablet**. The canvas drag loop read only `response.interact_pointer_pos()` once per frame; egui-winit pushes one `egui::Event::PointerMoved` per winit `CursorMoved`, and those accumulate while a frame is slow, so the intermediate samples never reached the tool. A tablet reports at a high rate, so many samples are dropped per frame. The paint engine (`PathWalker`) stamps dabs along straight segments between input points, so sparse samples give a polyline.

The fix is input-path agnostic: pen and mouse moves both arrive as `PointerMoved`, so both are recovered.

## Fix
- Collect the frame's pointer moves while the gesture's button is held, in order, bounded to the gesture's own press..release interval (`pointer_moves`). A move before a press or after a release in the same frame is dropped, and the start/stop frames keep their valid samples.
- Only path-driven tools take the whole batch (`freehand_tool`: brush, pencil, eraser, background eraser, history brush, the retouch tools, lasso, quick selection). Other tools keep the pointer's latest position, as before.
- A frame with no raw move but a held gesture falls back to the latest position (the old behaviour).
- The samples still go through `tool_event`, so the snap / transform / brush-resize pre-handlers run; the live stroke is updated once per frame (`defer_live_stroke`) instead of once per sample.

## Tests
- `pointer_moves_are_bounded_by_the_press_and_release` (pure, `canvas.rs`)
- `freehand_tools_are_the_ones_that_follow_a_path` (pure, `canvas.rs`)
- `one_frame_feeds_every_pointer_move_not_just_the_latest` (harness regression: six `PointerMoved` queued into one frame all reach the committed stroke). Checked red on the old code and green after.

`cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the UI lib tests (454 passed) are green. No command changed, so parity is unchanged.

title: Apply EXIF orientation on open, write Orientation = 1 on export (#285)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #285

**Before:** an iPhone JPEG (stored 4032×3024, EXIF Orientation = 6) opened sideways, and its exports kept Orientation = 6. Viewers then rotated the file a second time.

**Now it works like Photoshop:**
- **Open.** JPEG, PNG (`eXIf`), WebP and TIFF (IFD0 tag 274) images open upright. The pixels are rotated or flipped for orientations 2–8, the DPI swaps on quarter turns, and the EXIF/XMP orientation is rewritten to 1. `DecodeOptions::keep_orientation` opts out.
- **Export.** Every encoder writes Orientation = 1: JPEG/PNG/WebP EXIF and XMP, TIFF XMP, and the PSD EXIF (1058) and XMP (1060) resources. This holds even when a document's metadata still claims another orientation, as with a PSD from elsewhere or the hand-rotated case in the issue.
- **RAW.** Developed raws are still oriented only by `photocraft-raw` and carry no EXIF, so nothing is rotated twice. The embedded-preview fallback uses the preview's own EXIF orientation if it has one, otherwise the raw's IFD0 tag. It applies exactly one.
- **Place/Embed, thumbnails, CLI/batch.** Smart-object source decode, contact-sheet thumbnails and `photocraft-cli run`/convert all go through `photocraft_io::import` → codecs, so they are upright too.
- **Never crash.** The parser is bounded: IFD0 only, at most 1024 entries, checked offsets, SHORT/LONG only. Malformed, truncated or out-of-range values read as 1. Proptests feed it random EXIF and XMP.
- **Performance.** `Image::oriented` handles any layout and depth with parallel row bands (rayon on native, serial on wasm) and 64-px column blocks. In release, 24 MP RGB8 takes 9.5 ms for a 90° CW turn, 9.3 ms for 180° and 13.3 ms for 90° CCW (budget ≤ 50 ms; `rotating_24_mp_is_fast`, ignored by default).

## Tests
- `crates/codecs/tests/orientation.rs`
  - Orientations 1–8 for JPEG and PNG, plus TIFF from its own IFD0 tag; WebP covers 3, 6 and 8. Each one opens with the upright pixel layout.

title: macOS CLI: verify the shipped CLI is Developer ID signed and notarized in the release workflow (#308)
author: echelon
body:
## What I found

`packaging/macos/package.sh` already signs `photocraft-cli` with the Developer ID and the hardened runtime and notarizes its zip. I downloaded the published v0.1.1 and v0.2.0 CLI zips and checked the binary inside each:

```
$ spctl --assess --type install -vv photocraft-cli-0.2.0-macos-universal/photocraft-cli
photocraft-cli: accepted
source=Notarized Developer ID
origin=Developer ID Application: Learning Machines LLC (DJ6XS33FX8)
```

Two things make it look unsigned:

- **No stapled ticket.** A bare Mach-O can't hold one (only `.app`, `.dmg` and `.pkg` can), so Gatekeeper checks the notarization online the first time a quarantined copy runs. Offline, that first run can be refused.
- **The wrong check.** `spctl --assess --type execute` (the default type) says "rejected (the code is valid but does not seem to be an app)" for any command-line tool, even a notarized one. `--type install` is the right check.

Nothing in the workflow proved the CLI was notarized, so a broken run could ship an un-notarized CLI without anyone noticing. This PR adds that check.

## Changes

- **`packaging/macos/verify.sh`** (new) checks the artifacts as users download them. It unpacks the CLI zip and requires, for the binary inside:
  - `codesign --verify --strict`
  - both architectures
  - the hardened runtime flag
  - a `Developer ID Application` authority whose team is `APPLE_TEAM_ID`
  - a secure timestamp
  - `spctl --assess --type install` reporting `source=Notarized Developer ID`, retried because the online lookup can lag behind notarytool's "Accepted"

  For the DMG it checks `codesign --verify`, `stapler validate` and `spctl --type open`. With signing secrets present it fails the job on any miss. Without them it only checks signature integrity and prints warnings, the same way `package.sh` handles missing secrets.
- **`release.yml`:** a *Verify signatures and notarization* step after packaging, in the existing `release` environment with the existing secrets. No …

title: Keyboard Shortcuts: Ctrl+F records as Ctrl+F, not Ctrl+ControlLeft (#292)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #292

**Root cause.** egui 0.36 reports modifier keys as key presses of their own (`Key::ControlLeft`, `ShiftLeft`, `AltLeft`, `SuperLeft`…). Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts used the first key press it saw as the shortcut's key. Pressing Ctrl+F sends Ctrl first, so the dialog recorded **Ctrl+ControlLeft**, which is what the screenshot shows. Ctrl+F itself was never reserved or remapped.

**Fix.**
- Key capture skips modifier keys and waits for the key pressed with them.
- `shortcut_text` never returns a modifier key as the key.
- Any non-system combination can now be bound.
- The existing conflict handling (#275) still applies: a shortcut that's already in use is named in the dialog and moved when you click OK.

**Tests** (`crates/ui-egui/src/shortcut_capture_tests.rs`, kittest):
- Ctrl+F, pressed as a real keyboard sends it (ControlLeft, then F with Ctrl held), records `Cmd+F` (shown as Ctrl+F off the Mac), at 1× and 2×.
- Ctrl, Shift, Alt or ⌘ pressed on its own keeps the capture open and assigns nothing. The next key is then recorded with the right modifiers.
- Giving ⌘J (Layer via Copy) to Search shows the "already in use" warning, and after OK one command owns ⌘J.

**Visual check.** Rendered offscreen with the snapshot example at 1366×768, 1× and 2×: the row shows the new shortcut and "assigned." with no stray key names.

title: Layers panel: rename commits on click elsewhere, Enter or Tab; one at a time (#314)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #314

**Root cause.**
- **Clicking elsewhere didn't commit.** The rename field called `request_focus()` every frame. A click elsewhere makes egui drop the field's focus, but the next `request_focus()` took it straight back in the same frame. So `lost_focus()` never fired: the field never committed and stayed open until Enter.
- **A second rename broke the panel.** Rename state was stored per layer (`("rename", layer_id)`), so starting a second rename opened a second field. Both asked for focus every frame and took it from each other, so every field stayed open and the panel stopped working.

**Fix** (`layer_row_ui.rs`: one `Rename` state, plus `start_rename`, `rename_field` and `end_rename`):
- Only one rename is open at a time. Starting another (double-click, the row's context menu, or Layer › Rename Layer) commits the open one first.
- The field takes focus only when it opens, with the whole name selected so typing replaces it, as in Photoshop.
- A click anywhere else, **Enter** or **Tab** commits. **Esc** cancels. An empty or unchanged name renames nothing.
- If the layer being renamed goes away (deleted, filtered out, or inside a group that was closed), the rename ends.
- While the field is open it keeps its keys: Esc and Tab don't reach the tools or panel shortcuts in the frame where egui drops focus.

**Tests** (`layer_row_ui/rename_tests.rs`, kittest at 1× and 2×):
- A click on the canvas commits and closes the field.
- Enter commits, Tab commits, Esc cancels (the layer selection is untouched), and an empty name is ignored.
- Starting a second rename commits the first. Only the second field is drawn, and typing goes to it.
- Layer › Rename Layer from the menu commits an open rename.
- Deleting the layer ends the rename, and tool keys work again afterwards.

**Visual check.** Rendered offscreen at 1366×768, 1× and 2×: one field over the name, typed text replaces the selected name, and nothing is clipped.

title: PSD export: 32-bit files open in Photoshop (HDR toning Color Mode Data, #291)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #291

## Root cause
Every 32-bit PSD Photoshop saves carries an HDR toning record in the **Color Mode Data** section: `hdrt` (v3) followed by `hdra` (v6), 110 bytes. All 20 Photoshop-authored 32-bit oracles in the corpus have the same bytes. Adobe's spec only documents this section for indexed and duotone images, so we wrote it empty. Photoshop 2026 refuses a 32-bit file without the record ("the open options are incorrect").

How I narrowed it down, editing our plain one-layer 32-bit export by hand and opening each variant in Photoshop through JSX:
- Our export with the layer section removed still failed, which rules out `Lr32`, channel compression and layer records.
- Our export with all of Photoshop's image resources still failed. Photoshop's file with *our* resources opened.
- The header and the merged image (raw, big-endian IEEE floats) matched Photoshop's.
- Our export with Photoshop's Color Mode Data **opened**. With only the `hdrt` record, only its 8-byte header, or 16 zero bytes, it still failed.

The rest of the 32-bit layout was already correct: `Lr32` global block with a classic layer info length of 0, ZIP-with-prediction channels, raw merged data and finite big-endian floats.

## Changes
- `crates/psd/src/hdr.rs` (new): `default_toning_data()` / `color_mode_data_for_depth()`, written field by field. The layout comes from observing Photoshop-saved files.
- `crates/io`: the PSD and Multichannel exporters write it for 32-bit files only. 8/16-bit output is unchanged byte for byte.

## Tests
`crates/io/tests/psd32_export.rs`:
- Strict 32-bit layout check on flat and layered RGB/Gray exports:
  - depth is 32 and the toning data is present
  - resources 1005 and 1057 are present, and 1057 has real merged data set
  - layer info sits in `Lr32` with a classic layer info length of 0
  - channel compression is raw or ZIP (no RLE) and every channel decodes
  - the merged image is raw with finite floats
  - strict tagged-block re-parse passes
- 8/16-bit exports…

title: Cmd+Enter (Ctrl+Enter) loads the path as a selection (#306)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #306

**Root cause.** Make Selection from Path (`path.toSelection`) had no shortcut, so Cmd+Enter (Ctrl+Enter off the Mac) wasn't bound to anything, on any platform. The other Enter handlers weren't involved:
- The Pen tool's "finish path" handler only consumes a plain ↩, so it doesn't take Cmd+Enter first.
- The type tool takes Cmd+Enter only while editing text, to commit it.

**Fix.**
- `path.toSelection` now has the default shortcut **Cmd+Enter**. Like every command shortcut, it's listed and rebindable in Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts.
- Run from a shortcut or a menu (no `name` given), the shell picks the path the way Photoshop does:
  - A path being drawn with the Pen is finished first, then loaded.
  - Otherwise the path selected in the Paths panel, with any tool.
  - Otherwise the work path, then the selected layer's shape path or vector mask.
- With no path, the status bar says why instead of nothing happening. The new string is in `tl!`, with a `ja.tsv` entry.
- Text fields keep ↩, and plain ↩ with the Pen still only finishes the path.

**Tests** (`crates/ui-egui/src/path_selection_tests.rs`, kittest through the whole app):
- Pen tool with a work path: ⌘↩ makes a selection with the path's exact bounds.
- A path being drawn: ⌘↩ finishes it into the work path and loads it. Plain ↩ only finishes it.
- Brush tool with a saved path selected in the Paths panel: ⌘↩ loads that path. If the selected path is deleted, it falls back to the work path.
- No path: an error on the status bar and no selection. ⌘↩ is in the binding table, and after rebinding to ⌘⇧Y, ⌘↩ no longer fires and ⌘⇧Y does.

**Visual check.** Rendered offscreen at 1366×768 (1× and 2×) with the Pen tool and a work path. After ⌘↩ the marching ants follow the path.

title: Move tool: Auto-Select on by default; a click picks and drags the layer under the pointer (#296)
author: echelon
body:
## What changed

The Move tool's **Auto-Select** is now on by default. Clicking on the canvas selects the layer under the pointer, and dragging moves that layer, as in current Photoshop. `layer.pickAt` and the options-bar checkbox already existed (#183, #226), but the option defaulted to off, so canvas clicks never switched layers.

How a press with the Move tool behaves now:

- It picks the topmost visible layer with pixels under the pointer. Hidden layers and layers inside hidden groups are skipped. A layer mask hides pixels from the pick.
- **Group** mode picks the outermost group that holds that layer.
- **⌘-click (Ctrl-click on Windows and Linux)** inverts the option for that one click. With Auto-Select on, it moves the selected layer without picking. With it off, it picks.
- **Shift-click** adds the layer to the selection.
- **New:** clicking one of several selected layers keeps the whole selection, so the drag moves all of them, as Photoshop does. Before, the click collapsed the selection to one layer.

Saved tool presets that don't have the field also get the new default (`serde(default = "yes")`). Tool options are not saved across launches, so existing users get the new default straight away.

## Crash-safety fix found by the new tests

`layer.pickAt` with a huge `x` or `y` (for example `1e12`, which saturates to `i32::MAX`) built an empty 1×1 read rect. That tripped the raster debug assertion, which the command guard caught as an internal error. The pick now returns no layer for those coordinates. The regression test is `hostile_params_are_errors_or_misses_not_panics`.

## Tests

- `pick_cmds` (engine):
  - Group mode picks the outermost group.
  - A hidden group hides its layers from the pick.
  - A multi-layer selection is kept, and Shift adds a layer.
  - Hostile params return an error or no layer, never a panic.
- `move_auto_select_tests` (UI, through `canvas::tool_event`):
  - The default is on.
  - A press picks a layer and the drag moves it.

author: echelon
body:
Part of #220 (its Windows on ARM64 part), requested across all the Craft apps.

**Release:**
- `release.yml` builds, signs and packages a **Windows ARM64** MSI and portable zip alongside x64 and x86: `photocraft-<version>-windows-arm64.msi` and `…-arm64-portable.zip`. The release job already collects every `release-*` artifact, so they're attached to the draft release.

2. **install and run on ARM64**: on GitHub's Windows 11 ARM64 runner, installs the MSI silently and checks that both installed binaries are ARM64. title: Menus: no menu or submenu covers the menu bar (#319)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #319

**What the video shows.** It was recorded on v0.2.0, on a 1280×720 display at 2× (the window's content is about 1280×703 pt). The Edit, Layer and Image menus are taller than the room under the menu bar, so egui slides each popup up over the bar. That causes two problems:
- The menu titles disappear under the open menu, so the bar "doesn't show properly" for those menus.
- The pointer resting on the title lands on the menu's first row, so Layer › New opens by itself.

The popups also fade in, so they look translucent for a frame.

**Root cause on main.** #168 and #272 already bound top-level menus to the room under the bar. A submenu, though, was still allowed the whole window height. At the reporter's size, Image › Adjustments still slid up over the bar and hid Select, Filter and View. Layer's low submenus overlapped it too.

**Fix** (`menu_nav::level_room`): every level stays below the menu bar.
- A top-level menu hangs from the bar, as before.
- A submenu gets whichever room is larger: from its row down to the window's bottom, or from the bar down to its row (egui opens it upward when that fits). It scrolls inside that room with the existing ▲/▼ arrows, wheel and drag, instead of being slid over the bar.
- The row each open submenu hangs from is remembered in `Nav` (`set_anchor`).

**Tests:**
- `no_menu_or_submenu_covers_the_menu_bar` (kittest): at 1280×703 (1× and 2×) and 1366×768, each long menu and every submenu in view stays below the bar, keeps every menu title uncovered and stays inside the window. With the old submenu sizing it fails at 1280×703 (Layer's submenus).
- `level_room_keeps_every_level_below_the_bar`: unit test, including NaN and too-small inputs.

**Visual check.** Snapshots at 1280×703, 1× and 2×:
- Image › Adjustments now hangs from its row below the bar and scrolls.
- Image › Analysis, low in the menu, opens upward.
- All titles stay visible, and nothing is clipped.

title: prefs_usage: find the test module in CRLF checkouts (fixes Windows CI on main)
author: bommerts
body:
## Problem

`every_preference_is_read_or_hidden` (`crates/engine/tests/prefs_usage.rs`) fails on the Windows CI job on main. The last three finished `ci.yml` runs on main failed this way:

```
these preferences are read now: remove them from prefs::HIDDEN_UNTIL_IMPLEMENTED so the dialog shows them: [
    "rawDefaults.applyAutoTone",
    "type.smartQuotes",
]
```

Neither preference is actually read. The only mentions are in the `prefs_ui.rs` unit test `unimplemented_preferences_are_hidden_from_the_dialog`.

## Cause

`production()` strips each file's unit-test module by searching for `"#[cfg(test)]\nmod "`. A Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf` has `\r\n` there, so the search misses and the whole file, tests included, counts as production code. It passes on macOS and Linux, which check files out with `\n`.

## Fix

Find `#[cfg(test)]` followed by either `\r\n` or `\n`, then `mod ` / `pub mod ` (the earliest match). No change to `HIDDEN_UNTIL_IMPLEMENTED`: both preferences stay hidden, as `unimplemented_preferences_are_hidden_from_the_dialog` expects.

## Tests

On Windows 11 (Rust 1.99, autocrlf checkout):
- Before: `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test prefs_usage` fails as above, on unmodified `main`.
- After: both tests in `prefs_usage` pass (`every_preference_is_read_or_hidden`, `the_scanner_finds_reads`).
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --tests -- -D warnings` are clean.

Test-only change. No production code is touched.

title: Menus stay above the taskbar; oversized windows open maximized (#315)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #315

**Stacked on #337 (#319).** This branch contains that commit. Merge #337 first, or merge this PR on its own to land both.

**Root cause.**
- PhotoCraft opens a 1440×900 window. On a 1366×768 display that window runs past the bottom of the screen and under the Windows taskbar.
- egui sizes and places menus by the window's content rect, so a long menu's last items ended up under the taskbar or off-screen. Since #168, that includes the menu's ▼ scroll arrow.
- v0.2.0, which the reporter was running, had no menu scrolling at all, which is why the menus couldn't be scrolled or dragged.

**Fix.**
- `work_area::visible_rect` computes the part of the window the user can actually see:
  - It takes the window's content rect and cuts it to its monitor, using `ViewportInfo` `monitor_size` and `inner_rect`.
  - It keeps a 48 pt margin clear at the monitor's bottom for the taskbar or Dock. egui doesn't expose the OS work area, so this is a fixed margin.
  - A maximized or full-screen window is already inside the work area, so it keeps the whole window. So does a window on a monitor we can't place.
- Menus and submenus are now bounded by that visible part (`menu_nav::level_room_in`). They scroll with the ▲/▼ arrows, the wheel and drag.
  - egui still places popups within the whole window. So a submenu is given its upward room only when egui would actually open it upward. Otherwise it scrolls downward from its row, above the taskbar.
- `work_area::fit_window` fixes the cause at startup:
  - Once the monitor is known, a window bigger than it is maximized, which puts it in the work area.
  - Photoshop also opens maximized on small displays.
  - This is skipped on macOS, which keeps windows on screen itself.
- The snapshot example gains `--monitor WxH --window-top Y`, to render a window running under a taskbar.

**Tests** (`menu_nav_tests.rs`, kittest, 1366×768 display with a simulated taskbar). Two windows are tested: the default 1440×900, and a full-height 1366×737 one u…

title: Dock: visible splitter grips, exact drags, double-click reset (#295)
author: echelon
body:
## What I found

The right dock already had splitters (#88): the 6 pt gap between two groups resized them. Two problems made them hard to use:

- **Nothing showed where they were.** The gap looked like plain dock background until you hovered exactly on it.
- **Drags came up short.** Each frame applied egui's `drag_delta`, so the movement before the drag threshold was lost. A short drag moved the splitter less than the pointer, and the error added up over repeated drags.

## Changes (`crates/ui-egui/src/dock.rs`)

- **A visible grip:** three faint dots sit in every gap between groups. Hovering shows the resize cursor and a full-width accent line, which turns solid while dragging.
- **A bigger grab area:** the gap plus 3 pt above and below, 12 pt in all. The splitters are now registered after every group, so they win the pointer over the tab strip and body edges they overlap.
- **Drags track the pointer exactly.** The resize is measured from the press point against the heights at the press. The pointer and the edge stay together, and stopping at a group's minimum height doesn't drift.
- **Minimum heights** are unchanged: 80 pt, and 140 pt for Layers.
- **Double-clicking a splitter** gives the groups on both sides their default heights again. Other groups keep the sizes you gave them.
- **Collapsed groups:** a collapsed group has no splitter. The splitter above it resizes against the next expanded group, and expanding a group brings back its dragged height.
- **Persistence** is unchanged. Sizes live in `DockLayout::heights`, which `ui.set {dock}`, workspaces and `prefs.panelLayout` already carry (#181, #147).

## Control protocol

`ui.press {x, y}` and `ui.release {x, y}` are the two halves of a click. With `ui.move` between them, an agent can hold a drag across calls, for example to drag a dock splitter and take a screenshot mid-drag. `ui.move` and `ui.click`, which weren't documented before, are now in `docs/control-protocol.md`.
