title: FreeBSD CI: run the GPU integration tests one at a time
author: bflatastic
body:
The FreeBSD workflow has failed on about half of recent runs (main and PRs alike), always with a `SIGSEGV` in a `photocraft-ui-egui` GPU integration test: `drag_preview_canvas`, `color_managed_canvas`, `adjust_preview_gpu`. The crash comes within ~0.05 s of the binary printing `running 2 tests` / `running 3 tests`, before any test finishes, while binaries that start one test at a time pass. That points at the VM's software Vulkan driver crashing when several threads create a GPU device at once. These tests pass on Linux, macOS and Windows.

This runs `photocraft-ui-egui`'s integration tests with `--test-threads=1` on FreeBSD only. Its lib and doc tests and the rest of the workspace run as before. (`--lib` and `--doc` can't be combined, so they are two commands.)

Checked locally that the `--test '*'` selection runs all seven GPU integration binaries serially. The FreeBSD job is being run three times in parallel on this commit to confirm the crash is gone.

title: Monitor profile auto follows each window's display; what is applied is visible (#569)
author: ha1des
body:
Fixes #569.

With Monitor Profile = auto, macOS showed every window in the menu-bar display's profile: the reader asked AppKit for the "main screen" from a windowless `osascript` helper, which is the menu-bar display. On the reporter's Mac (built-in display as menu-bar display, external ROG PG32UQX) images were oversaturated on the external display.

- **Each window uses the profile of the display it is on.** The reader lists every display (id, name, frame, ICC profile, its System Settings name); each window picks the display it overlaps most (AppKit's `NSWindow.screen` rule). Moving a window switches the profile without a restart. Two windows of one document on different displays each keep their own: the GPU canvas shares the document texture and keeps a display LUT per (document, display); CPU textures are per (document, display).
- **Displays are read again** when PhotoCraft comes back to the front (calibration, System Settings), when any window is on an unknown or resized display (connect, remove, rearrange), and when Edit › Color Settings opens. Automatic triggers run at most every 30 s (deferred, not dropped). **No periodic re-read**, per the decision on #569 (a read costs about 0.2 s of CPU for an event that practically doesn't happen while PhotoCraft stays in front). The helper is stopped after 10 s; a failed re-read keeps the previous reading and says so.
- **What is applied is visible.** `ColorState::monitor_status_for` reports per display: `auto`, `manual`, or `fallback` to sRGB with the reason (missing, unreadable, non-RGB, unusable as a destination). Shown in Help › System Info (one line per display), the Color Settings dialog (refreshed while open) and `edit.colorSettings` (`monitorStatus`, `displays`); a fallback in auto posts a notice once.

No `unsafe`: AppKit is still read through `osascript`. The alternative of letting macOS colour-match the output is #581 (needs an owner decision); the installed-profile chooser is #575.

title: fix(type): preserve IME composition boundaries and event order
author: kijoong-kim
body:
An empty IME preedit notification could replace selected text even when no composition was active. Editing events arriving in the same frame as preedit/commit could also be handled against the wrong composition boundary. This patch preserves an idle selection and evaluates composition ownership separately for each event.

### Change and reproduction

- Select existing text, then deliver an empty preedit with no marked range: text and selection stay intact.
- Compose ㅎ → 하 → 한 and commit: exactly one 한 remains.
- Navigation before preedit and after commit in the same frame retains its order. Normal deletion resumes after composition clears.
- Add regression tests and `docs/ime-editing.md`, including the full-shell IME-enable characterization.

### Validation

Standalone branch based on `bf545e0e8119e405b0c28c1bb4a72366184fe37f` (0.3.0):
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --locked`: 638 passed, 3 existing ignored, zero failures.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: passed.

The tests inject already-correct IME events; they do not prove the host's native first-key delivery. The first Korean key falling back to a raw jamo on macOS was independently reproduced in a plain egui TextEdit and is addressed by a separate dependency patch. This PR does not claim to resolve all of #456 or to implement Korean composition. UI translations, font lookup and native dependency changes are intentionally separate contributions.

title: fix(macos): recover first Korean IME fallback at the native boundary
author: kijoong-kim
body:
On a fresh macOS app launch with Apple Korean 2-set, the first key may arrive as raw `insertText("ㅎ")` instead of `setMarkedText("ㅎ")`. winit 0.30.13 then forwards ordinary text; typing g/k/s produces ㅎㅏㄴ. The same retained event, interpreted one more time, starts normal preedit and produces 한.

### Native boundary repair

Detect only the initial Apple Korean batch containing exactly one insertText callback with the same single compatibility jamo as the original event. Reinterpret that retained event synchronously once, before any ordinary keyboard event is emitted. Existing marked text, other callbacks, modifiers/repeats, nested keys, or changed source/focus/IME state exclude replay. The batch is removed and the attempt is consumed before re-entering AppKit; no borrow crosses native calls. A failed retry falls through to the existing keyboard dispatch once.

No timer, delayed key queue, user-text recomposition or input logging is added. `docs/macos-korean-ime.md` documents reproduction, the decision boundary and limitations.

### Dependency integration decision — draft for review

This draft temporarily vendors the crates.io winit 0.30.13 source under Apache-2.0 and changes only three macOS source files. The dependency is excluded from PhotoCraft's workspace. The large source diff mostly consists of the unchanged dependency; the actual repair is in `ime_startup.rs`, `view.rs` and the module declaration. The manifest override affects all targets, but behavioral changes are macOS-only.

Related upstream work: rust-windowing/winit#3095 and open PR rust-windowing/winit#4693 at `4a2da8232e0d6211a1322ad9c33d45729bc02bfb`. That proposal uses a delayed retry. This independently tested alternative retries immediately and does not reuse its timer/queue implementation. Please review whether PhotoCraft should carry a temporary vendor override or wait for a released upstream fix. Remove the override only after verifying an upstream replacement.

## Problem

Image › Apply Image onto an empty (transparent) layer fills it with opaque black when the blending is Multiply (the dialog's default) or another darkening mode.

Repro: fill a document with `#c08040`, add a new layer, Apply Image with the merged composite and Multiply → the new layer is `(0, 0, 0, 255)`. With Normal it is `(192, 128, 64, 255)`, as expected.

## Cause

`apply_image` (`crates/engine/src/channel_cmds.rs`) blended the source against the colour stored in transparent pixels, which is 0, so `multiply(0, src) = 0`. It then set the alpha to `max(alpha, w)`, which made those black pixels opaque.

## Fix

The source is applied like a brush stroke onto the layer:

- The blend acts in proportion to the layer's own alpha: `blended = src + (blend(base, src) − src) · α_base`. Where the layer is empty, the source shows as is.
- With Preserve Transparency off, the alpha grows by source-over (`α' = w + α_base·(1 − w)`) and the colour is the matching non-premultiplied mix.
- With Preserve Transparency on, the alpha is unchanged (as before).

On fully opaque pixels this gives exactly the old formula `base + (blend − base)·w`, so the existing `apply_image_hand_computed` test still passes unchanged.

## Tests

- New `apply_image_onto_transparent_layer` at 8, 16 and 32-bit: Multiply onto an empty layer gives the source colour, fully opaque; 50% opacity gives the source colour at 50% alpha; Preserve Transparency leaves an empty layer empty. It fails before the fix with `[0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0]`.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine`: 633 passed.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`: everything passes except `cms::system_profiles` (a colord ICC profile on my machine) and `gpu parity::adjustment_layers`. Both fail the same way on unmodified `main` in my environment (Arch Linux, Rust 1.95), so they are unrelated to this change.
- The rebuilt CLI gives the source colour on an empty layer for Multiply, Normal, Screen and Darken.

title: algo: fix flaky cancel/progress test - tile workers report out of order
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What

`tests_ext::cancelled_filters_return_none_and_progress_is_monotonic` in `crates/algo` was flaky:
it failed roughly once per few hundred runs under load (observed once in a full
`cargo test --workspace`).

## Why

`apply_tiled_with` filters tiles with `chunk.par_iter()` and each worker reports progress
(`0.98 * n / total`) from its own thread (`crates/algo/src/lib.rs:932-944`). The values are
monotonic in the finish counter, but the delivery order is not: when a worker holding a smaller
value is preempted between its `fetch_add` and its callback's load, while another worker stores a
larger value first, the test's non-atomic load→assert→store sees progress "go backwards" and
panics — from a worker thread.

`Interrupt` never promised ordered delivery (its callbacks are `Sync` precisely so rayon workers
can call them), and its engine consumer already handles this: `JobCtx::progress` keeps
`fetch_max` of the f32 bits ("keeps progress monotonic even with several reporting threads",
`crates/engine/src/jobs.rs:65`).

## The fix (test-only)

The progress callback now mirrors `JobCtx::progress`:

- `fetch_max` on the `f32` bits as the high-water mark (non-negative floats order like their bits),
- an in-range assert (`0.0..=1.0`),
- the high-water mark must reach exactly `1.0`.

Renamed to `cancelled_filters_return_none_and_progress_never_regresses` to describe what it
actually guarantees. No production code changed.

The identical-looking asserts in `content_aware.rs` and `io/tests/cancel.rs` stay strict: those
paths report progress from a single thread (sequential pyramid levels / per-layer decode, no
`par_iter`), so strict monotonicity is guaranteed there.

## Proof

Stress repro on Windows x64 (test binary, `--test-threads=1`, 4 busy-loop processes for load):

| Build | Runs | Failures |
|---|---:|---:|
| before the fix | 300 | 1 (panicked at the old `tests_ext.rs:682`, in a worker thread) |
| after the fix | 300 | 0 |
| after, rebased on current `main` | 150 | 0 …

author: makemake-kbo

## Summary

Adds a Nix flake that builds PhotoCraft the way a release is built, plus a `nix develop` shell with debugging, profiling and GPU tools. It also includes a one-line portability fix to a test that failed on NixOS and in the Nix build sandbox.

title: Actions: actions.record/stop/play/list commands for agents and the CLI (part of #219)
author: mvanhorn
body:
## What changed

The `actions.record/stop/play/list` item from the Actions list in #219 (scorecard AUTO-219-3). Recording and playback used to live only in `UiState`, so agents, `photocraft-cli` and MCP could not record or replay an action. The list now lives on the engine `Session` and every surface calls the same commands.

- **New commands** in `crates/engine/src/actions_cmds.rs`. They have descriptive ids and no menu entry, and none of them records itself into a journal or an action:
  - `actions.list`, `actions.get {action}`: the list, and one action's steps as `[[id, params]…]`, the shape `file.automate.batch` and droplets already read.
  - `actions.record {name?}` (new action) or `{action}` (append), and `actions.stop`.
  - `actions.play {action, from?}`: replays the steps. It stops at the first failing step and returns `{ran, failed: {step, id, error}}` instead of an error, so a partial run is reported. A play inside a play is refused. Each step stays its own history step, as in Photoshop.
  - `actions.delete {action}`.
- **Security:** `authorize_engine_command` only saw the top-level id, so a recorded `file.open` could run inside `actions.play` over MCP. `Session::authorize` is a per-step hook. Untrusted sessions install the same check they apply to top-level calls: headless MCP with or without a workspace, control-channel requests, and commands run from synthetic automation input (`automation_input`). The last two go through `Services::automation_authorize`. `Headless::trusted_local` and the local UI don't install it, so a recorded `file.*` step still replays there.
- **Panel:** `ui-egui/src/actions.rs` dispatches these commands. Batch and Create Droplet read `session.actions`. Only `selected` and `expanded` stay as UI state.
- **Persistence:** the list is saved as `actions.json` next to the brush presets, through `PresetStore`. Before this change it was never written to disk. A missing file is an empty list. A corrupt, wrong-version or oversized (>16 MB) …

title: Type: hitTest, caret and navigate commands so agents can edit text by position (part of #219)
author: mvanhorn
body:
## What changed

The caret part of the "Agent coverage" item in #219 (scorecard AUTO-219-9, whose note said "no caret API"). The Type tool already sends every edit to the engine by character index (`type.edit replace`, `type.setStyle range`, `kernPair at`). The missing piece was geometry: no command mapped a document point to a character index, a character index to a caret, or a caret to the next word or line. `type_tool.rs` did all three privately.

- **New queries** in `crates/engine/src/type_caret_cmds.rs`. They are `journal: false` with no menu entry, and coordinates are in document pixels, so rotated, scaled and vertical type all work:
  - `type.hitTest {layer?, x, y}` → `{layer, index, line, inside}`. Without `layer` it picks the topmost visible type layer under the point, in the same order as the Type tool. A miss is an error. With `layer` it returns the nearest caret even when `inside` is false.
  - `type.caret {layer?, index}` → `{index, line, segment: [[x,y],[x,y]]}`.
  - `type.navigate {layer?, index, move, x?}` takes `move` as `wordPrev|wordNext|linePrev|lineNext|lineStart|lineEnd|start|end` and returns `{index}`. `x` keeps the column across repeated line moves, like ↑/↓ in the editor.
- **Shared code:** `word_boundary`, `line_step`, `line_edge` and the char↔byte hit-test helpers moved from `ui-egui/src/type_tool.rs` into `photocraft-text`. - Edits still go through `type.edit` / `type.setStyle` with a caller-chosen `coalesce`. There is no new engine state and no new undo rule.

title: Box Blur: up to 26x faster at large radii (same running-sum boxes as Gaussian Blur)
author: Ar-maan05
body:
Box Blur convolved every pixel with a 2r+1 tap kernel along each axis, so a radius 400 blur did ~200x the work of radius 2. Gaussian Blur in the same file already avoids this with running-sum box passes (`gaussian_boxes`, cost independent of radius). This PR pulls that body out into `box_passes(src, out, alpha, widths)`, keeps `gaussian_boxes` as a one-line call into it, and routes Box Blur through it with a single box of width 2r+1.

## Timing

`apply_in` on a 2000 x 1500 RGBA8 layer, release build, 2 rayon threads:

| Radius | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 132 ms | 50 ms | 2.7x |
| 50 | 617 ms | 72 ms | 8.6x |
| 150 | 2.54 s | 192 ms | 13x |
| 400 | 6.97 s | 269 ms | 26x |

Radius 1..4 keeps the direct kernel: at those sizes it is slightly quicker than the running sum, and their output is unchanged.

## Output

Mathematically the same box; only the float summation order changes. Against the old direct kernel on noisy RGBA with varying alpha (300 x 200, radii 5..400) the max difference is 4e-6. No 16-bit sample moves by more than one level, and an 8-bit sample changes only when it sits on an exact half-level tie (at most 0.06% of samples, by one level). The new test `box_passes_match_the_direct_box_kernel` pins the result to the direct kernel within 1e-5 for radii 5, 17 and 60.

## Checks

- `cargo test -p photocraft-algo`: 238 passed
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-algo --no-deps --all-targets`: clean
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean

title: document.pixel: no panic at x or y = i32::MAX, and no wrap-around past it
author: Ar-maan05
body:
`document.pixel` (also reachable through the control protocol) panics when x or y is `i32::MAX`:

```
thread '...' panicked at crates/engine/src/commands.rs:830:92:
index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0
```

`Rect::from_xywh(x, y, 1, 1)` saturates `x + 1` to `i32::MAX`, giving an empty rect, so `render` returns no pixels and `.px[0]` indexes an empty Vec. A second, quieter problem on the same lines: the coordinates are cast with `as i32`, so `{"x": 4294967296}` wraps to 0 and returns the pixel at column 0 instead of an error.

## Fix

- Read x and y with `i32::try_from`; anything outside i32 is `BadParams` ("x must fit in 32 bits").
- Take `.px.first()` and fall back to transparent, which is what every other off-canvas pixel already returns.

## Test

`document_pixel_at_the_coordinate_limits` reads `(i32::MAX, 0)` and `(i32::MIN, i32::MAX)` (both transparent) and checks that x = 2^32 is rejected. On main it fails with the panic above; with the fix it passes.

## Checks

- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib`: 653 passed
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --no-deps --all-targets`: no new warnings (the 3 reported are in color_cmds.rs and fill_cmds.rs, untouched)

title: Minimum / Maximum (Squareness): up to 37x faster at large radii, bit-identical output
author: Ar-maan05
body:
Filter > Other > Minimum and Maximum with Preserve: Squareness (the default) scanned all 2r+1 samples for every pixel, once along rows and once along columns, so the run time grew linearly with the radius (0.2..500). Preserve: Roundness, in the same file, already takes each window with `running_extreme` (van Herk / Gil-Werman, constant work per pixel whatever the window). This PR uses `running_extreme` for both passes of the square as well.

## Timing

`apply_in`, Maximum (Squareness), 2000 x 1500 RGBA8, release build, 2 rayon threads:

| Radius | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 141 ms | 139 ms | same |
| 10 | 443 ms | 153 ms | 2.9x |
| 50 | 2.80 s | 234 ms | 12x |
| 200 | 14.27 s | 384 ms | 37x |

## Output

Bit-identical. A min or max returns one of the samples in the window, so changing how the window is scanned cannot change the value. The new test `square_min_max_matches_the_direct_window_exactly` compares `min_max` with a direct (2r+1)^2 scan using `assert_eq!` on the f32 output: noisy RGBA, radii 1, 2, 3, 7 and 20, both Minimum and Maximum, including an output rect that reaches past the source and windows wider than the output. The benchmark output hashes also match before and after at every radius.

- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-algo --no-deps --all-targets`: clean
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean

title: Surface Blur: 13x to 40x+ faster on 8-bit layers (sliding histogram)
author: Ar-maan05
body:
Filter > Blur > Surface Blur summed the full (2r+1)^2 window for every pixel and channel. At the maximum radius of 100 that is 40,401 samples per pixel, so the filter took over a minute on a 0.75 MP image.

## Fix

The weight of a sample depends only on its value and the centre value (`1 - |v - v0| / t`), so the window sum can be taken from a histogram of the window. For 8-bit layers (checked per tile: every colour sample in the window is exactly `k / 255`), `surface_8bit` keeps a 256-bin histogram per channel, slides it along the row (one column removed and one added per step, O(radius)), and sums only the levels within the threshold of the centre (the others have zero weight), each weighted with the same expression as before. Transparent pixels are left out of the histogram, as the direct sum skips them, and samples outside the source read as 0, as `Image::get` returns.

The direct sum stays (as `surface_direct`) for 16-bit and 32-bit layers and for small windows where it is cheaper (radius up to about 5 at the default threshold).

## Timing

`apply_in`, Surface Blur, 1000 x 750 RGBA8, release build, 2 rayon threads:

| Radius | Threshold | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 15 | 214 ms | 229 ms | same (direct sum) |
| 15 | 15 | 1.48 s | 112 ms | 13x |
| 30 | 15 | 6.10 s | 143 ms | 43x |
| 30 | 255 | 6.10 s | 254 ms | 24x |
| 100 | 15 | ~66 s (extrapolated) | 421 ms | ~150x |

## Output

Not bit-identical: the sums are now taken per level (in f64) instead of per sample (in f32). On the benchmark image above, after rounding to 8 bits, at most 0.023% of samples differ and none by more than one level. The new test `surface_blur_8bit_histogram_matches_the_direct_sum` pins the histogram to the direct sum within 1e-5 for radii 1, 4 and 12 and thresholds 2, 15, 60 and 255, on noisy RGBA with transparent pixels and an output that reaches the source edge, and checks that non-8-bit input falls back to the direct sum.

title: fix(ui): search palette: the Enter that opens a dialog no longer closes it
author: Mawfyy
body:
Fixes #536

## Cause

`Edit › Search` (the palette) and the dialog OK footer consume the **same key event in the same frame**:

- `lib.rs:959-960` runs `palette::show` and then `dialogs::show` in one update.
- The palette processes `Enter` → runs `edit.keyboardShortcuts` → the *Keyboard Shortcuts and Menus* dialog opens.
- `dialogs::show` then draws that dialog in the same frame, and its footer (`dialogs.rs:183`) reads `ui.input(|i| i.key_pressed(Key::Enter))` → still true → treats it as **OK** → `dialogs::confirm` runs → the dialog is closed before it is ever visible.

So selecting the entry with `Enter` appears to do nothing — the dialog opens and closes inside one frame. It affects **every** palette-launched dialog opened with Enter (Preferences, Color Settings, New Document, Export…); clicking a palette row with the mouse is unaffected. title: codecs: decode deep OpenEXR (deepscanline/deeptile), composited flat or structured
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What

Deep OpenEXR files (`deepscanline` / `deeptile`) failed with

```
codec: OpenExr: malformed data: not supported: deep data not supported yet
```

because the `exr` crate rejects deep headers outright (its `MetaData::validate` refuses `deep`, and its deep chunk framing is an unfinished guess — the code says "TODO just guessed"). This PR decodes them:

- **Opening a deep file works**: the samples are composited into the flat image and a new `DecodeWarning::DeepFlattened` says what was lost (per-pixel depth), surfacing through the existing warnings path to the status bar and notices.
- **The structured samples are available** as `photocraft_codecs::decode_deep_exr() -> DeepImage` (per-channel sample vectors plus cumulative per-pixel counts), so deep layers in the document model — open-with-depth, stacking deep files by sample merge — can build on this without codec rework later.

## How

`crates/codecs/src/codecs/deep_exr.rs` walks the chunk stream directly, per the OpenEXR file-layout specification (clean-room; the byte layout was verified against real files):

- offset tables after the headers (earlier parts' tables skipped),
- deep chunks of `[y | tile coords][u64 packed table size][u64 packed data size][u64 unpacked data size][compressed cumulative sample-count table][compressed sample data]`,
- NONE, RLE and ZIPS — ZIPS means zlib, then the +128 difference predictor and the half-split byte interleave, applied to the count table and the sample data alike (this is exactly what the reference files contain; the `exr` crate applies the same transforms to flat data). A payload already at the uncompressed length is stored raw. ZIP-16 and mip/rip-map deep tiles decline with a clear `unsupported`,
- the cumulative u32 counts are validated (monotone, implying exactly the declared data size), per-pixel counts go through `Limits` before allocation, and every length/offset from the file is bounds-checked — truncated, duplicated-offset, oversized and misframed files re…

title: Type: a forced line break (U+0003) breaks the line instead of drawing a box
author: EthanSuquet
body:
PSD type stores a line break inside a paragraph (Shift+Return) as U+0003,
and the layer text keeps it as is. The layout passed it to the line
breaker as an ordinary character: it isn't a break opportunity there, so
the line ran on, and the font has no glyph for it, so a missing-glyph box
was drawn in its place. Nothing showed until the text was re-laid out,
because an opened layer draws its saved pixels; any edit of the text, an
Image Size or an export at another scale then turned a two-line headline
into one long line with a box in the middle.

The layout now hands U+0003 to the line breaker as a newline (same byte
length, so every text offset stays put): the line ends, the next one
starts with the paragraph's leading and no paragraph spacing, and no
glyph is drawn. The text itself is unchanged, so PSD save writes it back.

Test: forced_line_break_starts_a_line_in_the_same_paragraph (fails
before: one line), covering point, centred and box text and rendering at
8, 16 and 32 bits.

Found while exporting a batch of real-world designer PSDs (not attachable); the test reproduces it synthetically.

title: JPEG export no longer fails when the document's XMP is over 64 KB
author: EthanSuquet
body:
A JPEG holds XMP in one APP1 segment, at most 65,533 bytes. Documents
from the source application often carry far more: their XMP lists every
document ever placed in them (DocumentAncestors, thousands of ids) and
the text of every type layer (TextLayers). The encoder passed the packet
through whole, the segment was refused, and the export failed with "App
segment exceeds maximum allowed data length of 65533". That stopped
every JPEG path: Export As, Save a Copy, convert, Layers and Artboards to
Files, Batch and Image Processor. 3 of 16 real designer documents in a
sweep hit it.

When the packet doesn't fit, the encoder now leaves out those two
layered-document properties (any namespace prefix), which a flat image
doesn't need; everything else in the packet is kept. If it still
doesn't fit, the XMP is left out, and so is an EXIF block over 64 KB.
Both cases are reported ahead of time by a new fidelity warning,
MetadataTooLarge, so the export shows what was dropped. Formats without
a segment limit (PNG, TIFF, WebP) still keep the packet whole.

Test: jpeg_with_oversized_metadata_still_encodes (fails before: encode
error), at 8, 16 and 32 bits.

Found while exporting a batch of real-world designer PSDs (not attachable); the test reproduces it synthetically.

title: Image Size keeps the canvas border opaque instead of fading it
author: EthanSuquet
body:
Resampling read the pixels beyond a layer's content as the default pixel
(transparent for layers, white for masks). For content that reaches the
canvas edge, such as a Background or any full-canvas layer, the filter
taps past the border mixed that in, so after Image Size the outermost
rows and columns were translucent: a white Background enlarged 200 %
came out with alpha 162/255 in the corners and 203/255 along the edges.
Export As at any scale other than 100 %, and Generate Image Assets at
200 %, run Image Size first, so every such export had a translucent
frame. Channels, the quick mask and the selection faded the same way.

Image Size now resamples layers, masks, channels and the selection with
resize_surface_in_canvas: taps past the canvas edge (or past a layer's
own pixels where they extend beyond the canvas) read the nearest edge
sample. Inside the canvas nothing changes, so a layer away from the edge
keeps its soft border. resize_surface itself, used by transforms and
placing, is unchanged.

Tests: canvas_edges_repeat_instead_of_fading (algo: every filter, up and
down, 8, 16 and 32 bits; inner layers unchanged) and
image_size_keeps_canvas_edges_opaque (engine; fails before: corner alpha
0.635), which also checks a full selection stays full to the edge.

Found while exporting a batch of real-world designer PSDs (not attachable); the test reproduces it synthetically.

title: fix(i18n): follow native UI languages on first launch
author: neko233-com
body:
PhotoCraft defaults `interface.language` to `auto`, but Windows currently reads the dates/numbers region rather than the user's UI-language preferences, and macOS starts `defaults` to inspect a language list. First launches can therefore select a different language from the desktop UI.

This uses the native UI-language preference list on Windows and macOS and falls back to English when detection fails or no supported language is found. Existing saved manual choices keep their precedence. The first launch and older preference files without a language field continue to use Auto; startup does not persist a detected choice over the user's settings.

## Change

- Use the native-only, pinned safe `sys-locale = 0.3.2` API: `GetUserPreferredUILanguages` on Windows and `CFLocaleCopyPreferredLanguages` on macOS. Locale tags are matched in preferred order against the existing registry, including regional and Chinese script variants.
- Cache bounded OS tags once per process. Detection errors, empty results and unavailable languages resolve to `en`. No custom unsafe code, registry parser, `.plist` parser or subprocess is added to UI language detection.
- Keep `PHOTOCRAFT_LOCALE` as a single-tag launch override; Unix locale variables do not preempt Windows/macOS UI preferences. Web Auto retains its English fallback and has no new dependency.
- Add startup/rendering tests and document the preference precedence, fallback and platform scope.

This is a **single native startup behavior change**, independent of the language-pack/hot-reload architecture proposal in #625. It retains the bundled catalogs and their registry, and uses the existing `prefs.set` command. No document/export behavior changes are included.

## Validation

Source: [`47acd64`](https://github.com/neko233-com/photocraft/commit/47acd64c9a6f2bb7373a5bf79f72a920c6693d5e), based on `7055f0c`.

title: layer.showOnly: ⌥-click a layer's eye to show only that layer
author: jason4short
body:

- **New engine command `layer.showOnly {"layer": id?}` → `{shownAlone}`**, so scripts, the control channel and agents can use it:
  - It hides every other layer and keeps the layer's enclosing groups visible, so the layer still renders.

  - Run on another layer while one is shown alone, it moves the solo and keeps the original snapshot.
  - The snapshot is per-document view state (`DocState::show_only`), not history. Each run is one undoable visibility step.

title: macOS: menus open on press; only the title bar's free gap drags the window
author: jason4short
body:
Split out of #405.

## Menus open on press
Menu titles open their menu as soon as the mouse button goes down, and never toggle on release, so the menu doesn't blink. One gesture can press a title, drag to an item and release on it to run it. A plain click still opens the menu and leaves it open, and pressing an open title closes it.

egui's `menu_button` toggles on release, so each title now drives its own `Popup::menu`, using the bar's `MenuConfig` style and close behaviour. The release that ends the opening press would count as a click outside the popup, so that one release is ignored.

## Only the title bar's free gap drags the window (macOS)
The window draws under a transparent title bar, so AppKit dragged it from anywhere in that strip, menus included: press a title, drag towards an item, and the window moved.
- `mac_window.rs` turns AppKit's own title-bar dragging off (`NSWindow.setMovable(false)`) with safe `objc2` calls and no `unsafe`. The crates are pinned exactly to the versions already in `Cargo.lock`.
- The app's drag region (`ViewportCommand::StartDrag`, which works on an unmovable window) is now only the free gap between the menus and the right-hand controls.

**Testing:** a new harness test (`press_drag_release_runs_a_menu_item`) presses View, drags to Rulers and releases, which toggles rulers and closes the menu, then checks that a click leaves the menu open. Clippy is clean, `cargo fmt --check` passes, and `cargo test --workspace` passes. I also tried it by hand on macOS.

title: Layered TIFF: open and save Photoshop layer data in TIFF files, in either byte order (part of #215)
author: ljkx
body:
Closes the "Layered TIFF" item of #215 (scorecard FILE-215-7).

Photoshop keeps a layered TIFF's layers in two private tags: 37724 (`ImageSourceData`, the same layer section a PSD has, after the string `Adobe Photoshop Document Data Block`) and 34377 (the image resources). PhotoCraft now reads and writes both, so a TIFF opens with its groups, masks, layer styles, type, shapes, smart objects, adjustment and fill layers, paths and guides exactly as the PSD path would, and saves them back. Any other TIFF reader still sees a normal flat TIFF (the composite).

## What's in it

**`photocraft-psd`: `tiff` module.** `ImageSourceData` parses and writes the tag (PSD- and PSB-sized data); `resources_from_bytes` / `resources_to_bytes` handle 34377; `into_psd` / `from_psd` bridge to `PsdFile`.

The hard part is byte order. Adobe's TIFF Technical Note is silent, but Photoshop files (and the two implementations that read them, Krita and psdtags) show that in an Intel-order (`II`) TIFF the whole block structure is byte-swapped: every signature and key reversed (`MIB8`, `ryaL`), every integer and double little-endian, UTF-16 little-endian, while the pixel samples inside channel data stay big-endian and RLE row counts follow the container. The `tiff::transcode` walker converts between the two orders field by field, with every length re-patched. It knows the layer-info structure, masks (including the parameters/real-mask ordering quirk), blending ranges, descriptors, and every block `photocraft-io` maps: `luni lsct lyid lclr iOpa fxrp brst shmd` (per item), `lfx2 lmfx lfxs lrFX`, `TySh`, `SoLd SoLE PlLd`, `lnk2 lnk3 lnkD lnkE`, `vmsk vsms vogk vscg vstk`, `SoCo GdFl PtFl`, the binary adjustments (`levl curv hue2 brit thrs post expA blnc mixr selc phfl grdm`), `Patt`, `FEid FXid`, `FMsk LMsk`, `Anno`, `CAI GenI OCIO extn pths cinf artb artd`, `Txt2`. Unknown blocks that parse as a (versioned) descriptor are converted too; anything else is dropped **with a warning** rather than passed t…

title: Selections: drag to move the outline; ⌘-drag floats the selected pixels (engine commands)
author: jason4short
body:
Split out of #405, reworked as requested so the floating selection is **driven by engine commands**, which agents, scripts and the control channel can use as well as the canvas.

## Engine: `float_cmds`
- **`select.float {"dx": px, "dy": px}` → `{layer, offset}`:** the first call cuts the selected pixels of the active layer into a floating piece, and every call moves it by whole pixels. Later calls move the same piece without cutting anything new. The document is unchanged while the piece floats (`DocState::floating`). The selection stays where it was until the drop.
- **`select.drop {}` → `{dropped, offset}`:** drops the piece into its layer and moves the selection with it, as one history step ("Move Selected Pixels"). The result is exactly what the canvas showed, because both use `CutParts::moved`.
- **Any other command drops it first.** A hook at the top of `dispatch` does this, so the piece lands where it was shown before the command runs. **Undo** puts it back instead, since nothing has been changed yet. A floating piece is also invalidated if the document's revision moves under it.
- **Fast:** the layer is split once, only inside the selection, and the piece is cropped to it, so placing it costs the piece's size rather than the layer's. On a 6000×4000 layer with a 500×400 piece that's 18 ms to cut and under 5 ms per move. Bench: `cargo test --release -p photocraft-engine float_drag_bench -- --ignored --nocapture`.
- **Enabled when** there's a selection and the active layer is an unlocked pixel layer.

## Canvas: Marquee and Lasso
- **A drag inside the marching ants moves the outline** (`select.transformSelection` with `dx`/`dy`). A click inside without moving deselects. ⇧ and ⌥ drags still draw, so combining selections is unchanged.
- **⌘-drag runs `select.float`:** the piece follows the pointer live, through the existing move preview. Plain drags on the floating piece move it again, and a press anywhere else (or with ⇧/⌥) runs `select.drop`.
- A move cursor a…

This PR flips them to **done** with evidence and regenerates `docs/scorecard.md` (no code changes).

## Re-verification against the current tree

- **One shared `photocraft_format::atomic_write`** (`crates/format/src/atomic.rs`): same-directory temp file, `create_new` + `write_all` + `sync_all`, rename, Unix directory fsync, Windows `PermissionDenied` rename retry with backoff — and **every document write site routes through it**: engine `file_cmds::write_file` and `preset_store`, automation `files.rs`/`headless.rs`/`workspace.rs` (cap-std variant shares `temp_name`/`retry_rename`), the app's `services.rs::write_atomic`, and `format`'s store/autosave writers.

title: Text fields stop resetting the input method every frame, so keys no longer repeat endlessly on Wayland (#585)
author: ianswope
body:
Fixes #585.

### Cause

The command palette calls `resp.request_focus()` on every frame, and the channel rename field does the same while it is open. In egui 0.36 each `request_focus` also calls `interrupt_ime()`, which egui-winit turns into `set_ime_allowed(false)` + `set_ime_allowed(true)`. On Wayland that is a `zwp_text_input_v3` disable/enable pair every frame.

With an input method running (fcitx5 here), each pair makes the compositor drop and retake the input-method keyboard grab, and the client sees the keymap flip back and forth every few milliseconds. A key release that lands in one of those gaps never reaches winit, and winit's client-side repeat keeps going until the window closes. That is why it is intermittent, why it only happens in text fields, and why a synthetic key from `wtype` (which bypasses the IME grab) does not reproduce it.

### Evidence (Arch, Hyprland, fcitx5, `WAYLAND_DEBUG=client`)

- Before, with the palette open: 269 `zwp_text_input_v3.enable` and 942 `wl_keyboard.keymap` events in one short session. A single physical press of "k" repeated without end on the first try.
- After: 0 enable/disable and 0 keymap events over 34 frames with the palette open and focused; 1 `enable` for the whole run.

### Change

Both fields request focus only when they do not already have it, the same guard the brush, preset and font-search fields already use. Every other `request_focus` call site in `ui-egui` is already guarded or runs once on an event.

### Tests

`palette::tests::open_palette_interrupts_the_ime_only_when_it_takes_focus` and `channels_panel::tests::rename_field_interrupts_the_ime_only_when_it_takes_focus` run four frames and assert `should_interrupt_composition` is not set after the field holds focus. Both fail on `main` (`[None, Some(true), Some(true), Some(true)]`). `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings` are clean.

title: Numeric fields evaluate typed arithmetic
author: rosematcha
body:
Fixes #601

Typing `1280*2` or `658*1.5` into a numeric field now applies the result when you press Enter or Tab or click away. The fields take `+ - * /`, with `*` and `/` first, so `20*2+5-2` gives 43, as in Photoshop. This covers every field built on `widgets::value_field` (Canvas Size, Image Size, New Document, adjustments, options bars, the Layers panel) plus the number fields in Preferences and the generic command form.

Plain numbers still apply as you type. Arithmetic waits until you commit it; otherwise `5/2` in a pixel field would be applied and rounded to 3 halfway through `5/2*2`. `value_field` now reports `changed()` only when the value changes, not on every keystroke, so typing doesn't add empty `layer.setProps` steps to the history. The floating Properties card scopes its fields to each layer, so arithmetic you're still typing for one layer can't be committed to the next one you select. Division by zero and other invalid input leave the field unchanged.

Not included: units inside expressions (`3cm*50%`) and parentheses. Arithmetic typed into the canvas brush picker is lost on Enter, because the picker closes before the field commits; plain numbers work there as before. Scorecard row UI-217-13 stays partial, with its note updated.

Tests: `widgets.rs` checks the parser, then types into a real field and commits with Tab, and with Enter while an OK button reads the value in the same frame, as dialogs do. It covers a caller that rounds, and plain digits applying while arithmetic waits. `panels.rs` checks that a sum left half-typed in one layer's Properties card doesn't land on the next layer.

title: Optional generative AI: Generate, Generative Fill, Expand Canvas and Variations through a user-supplied OpenAI key (#41)
author: josusotz-code
body:
## What

A first take on #41, behind the provider interface the issue asks for, with OpenAI's Images API as the first backend and a key the user supplies.

- New crate `photocraft-gen` (L4): an `ImageProvider` trait (generate, edit with mask, variations), an OpenAI implementation, and an HTTP transport behind its own trait so tests never touch the network. `ureq` is a native-only dependency; the web build doesn't send these requests and `cargo xtask wasm` stays green.
- Four engine commands, with menu entries and translations in every catalog:
  - `image.ai.generate` (Image): prompt → new layer.
  - `edit.ai.generativeFill` (Edit): selection + prompt → new layer, composited back into the selection's bounds.
  - `image.ai.expandCanvas` (Image): grows the canvas and fills the new border. The generated border fades into the original over a band of up to 64 px, and its colour is matched to the original along that band, so there's no hard seam.
  - `layer.ai.variations` (Layer): a variation of the visible image (`source: "composite"`, default) or of the active layer only (`source: "layer"`).
- Each command runs as a cancellable background job, creates exactly one new layer, records one undo step and never touches existing pixels. Like everything else, they work from the UI, the CLI, the control channel and MCP.

## Opt-in and privacy

Nothing changes unless `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set in the app's environment. Without it, the commands are disabled and return "Generative AI is off: set OPENAI_API_KEY". The key is only used in the HTTPS `Authorization` header: it is never written to `.pcraft`, journals, logs or error messages (there is a test for that). `docs/roadmap.md` spells out exactly what each command sends to OpenAI.

This doesn't try to settle which backend PhotoCraft should use. `ImageProvider` is small enough to put the Storyteller/ArtCraft API, or the generic HTTP provider suggested in #41, behind it later.

title: Free Transform: picking another tool applies the transform
author: rosematcha
body:
Fixes #670

With Free Transform open, picking another tool left the box on screen and clicks kept going to it until you pressed ↩ or Esc. Now picking another tool applies the transform, as Photoshop has done without a prompt since CC 2019, and a click with the new tool goes to that tool. title: Flat exports embed no document XMP by default; Export As gains a Metadata choice (#647)
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What

Fixes #647. The document's XMP packet lists the **text of every type layer** (`photoshop:TextLayers`) and **one id per placed document** (`photoshop:DocumentAncestors`) — data a flat web image should not carry: 14–116 KB per export on real designer PSDs, and layer text leaking into images that show only part of the design. Until now `EncodeOptions::embed_metadata` defaulted to true, so Export As, `photocraft-cli convert`, Save a Copy and Layers/Artboards to Files copied the whole packet into every PNG/JPEG/WebP.

## The change

- **io**: `ExportOptions.xmp` (`XmpEmbed::All | None`, **default `None`**) drops the packet from flat exports before the codecs see it. Layered saves (PSD, PSB, `.pcraft`) always keep everything; DPI, ICC and EXIF are unaffected. Every flat-export path (Export As, Save a Copy, the CLI, Layers/Artboards to Files, Batch, Image Processor) shares `photocraft_io::export` and gets the safe default — this also makes #645's >64 KB JPEG overflow much rarer.
- **Export As dialog**: a Metadata dropdown (**None / All**, default None — the source application's Export As defaults to none too; Save for Web keeps its richer Copyright choice). The file-size estimate follows the choice.
- **Follow-up idea** (not here): a Copyright mode for Export As by moving Save for Web's `web_xmp` filter down from the engine into io.

## Tests

- New `crates/io/tests/xmp_export.rs`: a document whose XMP contains both leak markers exports **without any of it** by default (png/jpg/webp/tif), `XmpEmbed::All` embeds it, and PSD/`.pcraft` keep it whatever the option.
- `metadata_roundtrip_png` and the stale-orientation test updated to the new contract — and they now also verify that with `All`, an embedded stale orientation is still rewritten upright (`tiff:Orientation="1"`).

title: Filter › Render › Relight: redirect a photo's lighting
author: mvanhorn
body:
## What

Adds **Filter › Render › Relight** (`filter.render.relight`), which changes where the light comes from in an existing photo. Lighting Effects bump-maps a surface. Relight works differently: it estimates the image's albedo and shading, then reapplies a directional lamp, so the bright side moves around the subject instead of producing an embossed look.

## The change

- **algo**: new tiled `relight` kernel, a Retinex albedo estimate plus Lambertian shading. Its parameters are angle, elevation, intensity, ambient, warmth, and softness. Intensity `0` leaves the image unchanged. Shading gradients are sampled at ±σ, so the light still shows on large documents instead of turning into a flat multiply.
- **engine**: `filter.render.relight` in `filters_ext`. It respects selections, records as a smart filter, and is one history step.
- **ui**: a live-preview dialog with six sliders, a menu entry, and strings for all shipped locales.

title: Drag-and-drop: place onto the canvas in Free Transform, open at a tab slot
author: carterwsmith
body:
Dropping files on the window now depends on where they land, like Photoshop:

- **Canvas:** each file is placed as an embedded smart object and goes straight into Free Transform. Esc removes it; Enter makes the place and transform one "Place Embedded" undo step. Several files are placed one after another.
- **Tab strip:** files open with their tabs at the slot under the pointer. An insertion line shows the slot while dragging.
- **Anywhere else** (panels, dialogs, no document), or when the position is unknown: files open at the end, as before. Brush and gradient preset files always go to their libraries.

## Design decisions

- **Pointer from the OS.** winit 0.30's drops carry no position, and the window gets no pointer events during an OS drag. eframe 0.36.2 is the latest and is tied to winit 0.30; winit 0.31, which has drag positions, is still in beta. So `Services::cursor_pos` is filled by the desktop shell (`apps/photocraft/src/cursor.rs`) using safe bindings only, no `unsafe`:
  - macOS: AppKit through objc2-app-kit, already in the lockfile.
  - X11: x11rb `QueryPointer`.
  - Windows: `GetCursorPos` from `winsafe` (new, no dependencies of its own).
  - Wayland: winit 0.30 delivers no drops there, so nothing is needed.
  - I rejected `mouse_position` (panics without X11) and `device_query` (macOS Accessibility prompt, links libX11).
- **Drop target.** `DropTarget::{Canvas, Tabs(slot), Elsewhere}` is worked out from last frame's canvas rect and tab rects. A point under an egui window or dialog counts as elsewhere.
- **Place reuses ⌥⌘T's mechanism.** `TransformSession.copy: bool` became `made: Option<MadeLayer { Copy, Place }>`, so cancelling takes the new layer back and committing folds it into one step, the same as the existing Free Transform copy.
- **Tab order is a command.** `document.move` (`{"document": index?, "to": index}`) reorders tabs, so agents, MCP and scripts can do it too. Tab-slot drops use it, and so do background opens, which carry `OpenTab.slot…

title: type.edit: a reversed runs range is a bad-params error, not a panic (#714)
author: mnmlyw
body:
Fixes #714.

## What changed

A `type.edit` run with `end < start` reached `style_range` with `a > b`, and the styled run's length (`cb - ca`) underflowed:
- **Debug builds:** a panic, which the dispatch guard reported as a generic internal error.
- **Release builds:** a wrapped, huge run length stored in the layer.

The fix:
- **`type.edit` validates every run up front**, next to the existing kerning check. It rejects `end < start` with a `BadParams` error that names the run, e.g. ``runs[0]: `end` (2) is before `start` (5)``. The check runs before the edit, so the layer is unchanged and no history step is recorded, even when an earlier run in the list was valid. As the issue asks, the exact-inverse input errors rather than being silently reordered.
- **`style_range` treats a reversed range as empty** (`b = b.max(a)`), so no other caller can underflow it. Every current caller already passes ordered ranges.

## Tests

- `type_cmds::tests::edit_rejects_a_reversed_runs_range`:
  - The issue's repro, a reversed run after a valid one, and a run whose `end` is listed before its `start`. Each returns `BadParams`, the run layout is unchanged, and no history step is added.
  - Control: `{"start":2,"end":5}` still applies faux bold (runs 2/3/6).
- `type_cmds::tests::style_range_reversed_is_a_no_op`.
- On `main`, both fail with `attempt to subtract with overflow` at `type_cmds.rs:303`.
- Gates (all pass or clean):
  - `cargo test -p photocraft-engine` (655 passed)
  - `clippy --all-targets -D warnings`
  - `fmt --check`
  - `xtask layers`
  - `xtask wasm`
  - `panic_hunt -- --ignored`

No UI change, so no screenshots.

title: Find and Replace Text: no panic searching a non-type active layer (#703)
author: mnmlyw
body:
Fixes #703.

## What changed

With `allLayers: false`, `edit.findAndReplaceText` keeps only the active layer in its search list. When that layer isn't a type layer the list is empty, and the `find`/`change`/`changeFind` loop indexed `layers[(start + k) % layers.len().max(1)]`, which is `layers[0]` on an empty vector, and panicked.

The loop now reads the layer with `get()` and stops when there is none. The command then finds nothing and returns `{"found": null}`, as it already does when nothing matches. This is the outcome the issue proposes. `changeAll` already returned `{"count": 0}` on this input and is unchanged.

## Tests

- `edit_menu_cmds::tests::find_in_the_active_layer_finds_nothing_when_it_is_not_type`:
  - The issue's repro for `find`, `change` and `changeFind`, forward and backward.
  - Each returns `found: null` / `changed: null` and records no history step. `changeAll` returns `count: 0`.
  - Control: with the type layer active, the same `allLayers: false` search finds `abc`.
  - On `main` it fails with `index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0` at `edit_menu_cmds.rs:733`.
- Gates (all pass or clean):

  - `clippy --all-targets -D warnings`

title: Select Linked Layers excludes an unrelated active layer
author: CQMHV
body:
Fixes #720.

Select Linked Layers could keep an unrelated active layer selected: the command passed the old active layer to `set_selection`, which adds that layer back when it is outside the linked groups. A following multi-layer delete, merge or alignment could therefore affect an unrelated layer, and the reported selection count was wrong.

Keep the active layer when it belongs to the linked groups; otherwise select the last linked layer in document order and use it as the selection anchor. This follows the existing Select All Layers behavior without changing the shared selection helper.

Three regression tests cover the reported command sequence and a subsequent delete/undo, preserving either linked active layer, repeated selection, unchanged history/dirty state, and graceful failure without a linked selection. The behavior tests cover 8-, 16- and 32-bit documents. The exclusion regression was also run with the original logic and failed with three selected layers instead of two; the committed fix was then restored and validated.

author: rosematcha
body:

title: fix(photocraft): reject an unparseable --control port instead of silently dropping it (#701)
author: bfenty
body:
# PR #701 — fix(photocraft): reject an unparseable --control port

**Branch:** `fix/701-control-port-validation`
**Title:** fix(photocraft): reject an unparseable --control port instead of silently dropping it (#701)

## Body

Fixes #701.

`--control` and `PHOTOCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT` were read with `.parse().ok()`, so a typo (`--control 78787`), a missing value, or a following flag consumed as the value (`--control --safe-gpu`) left the app running with **no control server and no diagnostic** — an agent could not tell a granted control channel from a typo.

Changes in `apps/photocraft/src/main.rs`:
- New `parse_control_port(value, source)` returns an error naming the value and the expected range, matching the style of `photocraft-cli serve` (`bad --port`).
- Both sources (env var and flag) are validated; collected errors print as `photocraft: --control: `78787` is not a valid port (expected a number from 0 to 65535)` and the launch exits non-zero instead of silently omitting the server.
- `--control` with no following value is now an error instead of silently disabling the control server, and it no longer swallows the next argument (`--safe-gpu` survives).

The restoration check from the issue is covered:
- invalid port → named error + non-zero exit (no silent no-server launch)
- `--control --safe-gpu` → missing-value error, `--safe-gpu` no longer consumed
- valid port path untouched (discriminating control)

Tests: two new unit tests in `control_port_tests` (valid values incl. `0` and whitespace; out-of-range / flag-as-value / empty all rejected with the value named).

Verified locally (`cargo test -p photocraft --bin photocraft`):

```
test result: ok. 54 passed; 0 failed
```

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy -p photocraft --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

title: Large PSBs open with their pixels: decode planes past 2 GiB, plus 4-5 GB PSB fixtures (#375)
author: alexanderalber
body:
Refs #375. Follows #401, which made the read itself work; this makes what comes after it work. I still couldn't get the reporter's file, so this doesn't close the issue either, but it fixes the next wall a 4–5 GB Photoshop PSB runs into.

## Cause

- **One decode was capped at 2 GiB** (`photocraft_psd::compression::MAX_DECODED_BYTES`, unchanged since the first commit). Real PSBs pass that in one plane set: the merged image of a 30000² RGB file is 2.7 GB, a 33000² 16-bit layer channel 2.2 GB.
- **What users saw:**
  - flattened PSB: the document opens with **no layers**;
  - layered PSB: every channel is "treated as empty", and the layer comes out **opaque black**, because a missing transparency channel is filled with full alpha. Saving that destroys the image.
- **Saving hit the same cap:** the exporter silently fell back to uncompressed data (a 0.10 GB file became 2.76 GB), and PhotoCraft then couldn't decode the merged image of its own file.

## Change

- **`MAX_DECODED_BYTES`: 8 GiB on 64-bit, 2 GiB elsewhere**, the budget `photocraft-codecs` already uses for `Limits::max_alloc`. It stays a backstop against decompression bombs: the decoders bound their output by their input on their own (RLE at most 64x, Raw needs every byte present).
- **Raw and RLE output buffers use `try_reserve_exact`**, so a machine without that much memory gets an error instead of an abort.
- **PSD import:** a channel that is present but can't be decoded leaves its layer empty (transparent), as the warning already said, instead of opaque black.

## Large-file fixtures (#216)

- **`cargo run --release -p photocraft-psd --example big_psb -- <dir>`** writes five PSBs straight from the spec, independent of our writer and its limits:

  | File | Size on disk | What it exercises |
  |---|---|---|
  | `flat8-40k-raw` | 4.80 GB | offsets past 4 GiB, 4.8 GB merged image |
  | `layer8-25k-raw` | 4.38 GB | layer data past 4 GiB |
  | `flat8-29k-rle` | 0.04 GB | 2.52 GB merged image, flattened |
  | `l…

title: fix(algo): blur small sigmas instead of silently no-oping (#706)
author: bfenty
body:
# PR #706 — fix(algo): blur small sigmas instead of silently no-oping

**Branch:** `fix/706-gauss-small-sigma`
**Title:** fix(algo): blur small sigmas instead of silently no-oping (#706)

## Body

Fixes #706.

`gauss_box_radii` followed Kovesi 2010 exactly, and the rounded box triple degenerates below sigma ≈ 0.577: `wl` floors to 1, `m` clamps to 3, and all three radii come out `(1-1)/2 = 0`. `box_rows_n`/`box_cols_n` early-return on radius 0, so `gauss_blur_n` handed the buffer back byte-identical for every sigma in `[0.3, 0.577)` — right inside the documented ranges of Camera Raw `sharpenRadius` (0.5..3) and `noiseColor`, HDR Toning `radius` (1..500), Shadows/Highlights mask blur, and Oil Paint cleanliness.

**Fix:** when the triple degenerates to all zeros, clamp to a single radius-1 pass — the smallest blur that actually blurs. The clamp only engages where the ideal box widths are already at their floor (`w_ideal < 2`), so every sigma the paper handles well is bit-for-bit unchanged; only the silent no-op band changes behaviour.

**Tests:** adds the command-level regression test from the issue (`crates/engine/tests/gauss_small_sigma.rs`): the `sharpenRadius: 0.5` case with its `3.0` control, asserting the small-radius case changes pixels.

Verified locally on `main` before/after:

title: fix(algo): radial blur samples at arc length instead of a 64 cap (#515)
author: bfenty
body:
# PR #515 — fix(algo): radial blur samples at arc length instead of a 64 cap

**Branch:** `fix/515-radial-blur-sample-density`
**Title:** fix(algo): radial blur samples at arc length instead of a 64 cap (#515)

## Body

Fixes #515.

Both radial methods computed the sample count as `((swept_length).ceil()).clamp(1, 64)`. The 64 cap means that on a 1000px canvas a 100° spin at the edge samples every ~27px of a ~785px arc — the "blur" then aliases (banding, spokes/rings survive) instead of averaging what it sweeps.

**Fix:** extract the density rule into `spin_samples` / `ray_samples` helpers and drop the cap — ~1 sample per pixel of swept length, minimum 1. The formula already yields <64 samples for small radii and small amounts, so every previously-unclamped case is bit-identical; only the clamped (aliasing) regime changes.

**Test:** `radial_sample_counts_follow_arc_length` pins the rule at the issue's exact scenario — r=450 at 100° → 786 spin / 225 zoom samples (old code: 64) — plus the centre identity case (1 sample).

Honest note: I also tried pixel-level aliasing probes (spoke/ring patterns at r≈445 tuned to beat with the 64-sample step). They were not reliably discriminating between clamped and unclamped sampling — bilinear prefiltering softens the aliasing at exactly one Nyquist ratio — so I dropped them rather than ship flaky tests. The density test fails on `main` and passes here; the visual fix follows directly from the sampling math.

title: Bound layer-group nesting at import and Group Layers (stack-overflow guard)
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What

A PSD whose layer records nest groups deeper than the document model allows (each level costs only a `lsct` divider + folder record pair, so a ~10 MB file can carry thousands) overflowed the stack in the PSD importer's tree recursion — and again in `Document::walk` (behind nearly every engine command), the layers panel, PSD export and Drop. No lint, panic hook or `panic_hunt` run catches a stack overflow. The only nesting cap that existed lived in the `.pcraft` **save** path (`MAX_GROUP_DEPTH = 100` in `photocraft-format`), so such a file imported "fine" and then bricked saving.

## Change

- `photocraft-doc` now owns the limit — `MAX_GROUP_DEPTH = 100`, the value the format crate already enforced — plus `Document::max_group_depth()`, an iterative depth measure that cannot itself overflow. `photocraft-format` re-exports it from doc instead of defining its own copy.
- PSD/PSB **import** rejects files nested deeper than the cap with an actionable `Unsupported` error, mirroring what the `.pcraft` loader already does (`group_depth()` reads the section-divider sequence iteratively, exactly like `layer_tree`'s stack, so the check itself cannot be made to recurse).
- The never-fail `psd_to_document` (public API, used by tests and the flattened-export fallback) keeps working on such files instead of overflowing: its `build` recursion stops at the cap and warns about the unimported remainder.
- `apply_link_groups` (resource 1026) recurses over the same unbounded tree and is bounded the same way.
- `layer.groupLayers` refuses to nest past the cap. The check runs inside the `edit` closure, so a rejected call records no history step and leaves the document untouched.

## Tests

- `group_nesting_past_the_cap_is_rejected` (io): a builder-made 101-deep PSD → `import` errors with the limit; `psd_to_document` still returns a depth-100 document plus a warning (this used to recurse to the file's depth).
- `group_nesting_at_the_cap_imports` (io): exactly 100 deep imports clean…

title: CI: never cancel main's runs; trim per-PR runner time
author: tanish2k09
body:
## What and why

**Main's CI hasn't really been running.** `ci.yml` cancels in-progress runs on every ref, so each merge to main cancelled the previous main run. Between 09:56 and 20:34 UTC on 2026-10-07, **80 of 83 push runs on main were cancelled** (1 success, 2 failures). The cost showed up quickly: #663 and #700 were each green on their own, but together they made `cargo fmt --check` fail on main (`xtask/src/i18n_coverage.rs:559`, fixed in #798). Every PR updated to main then failed Format until that was fixed.

PR runs are also slow: 50 min median and 66 min p90 for a successful CI run, before queueing, with ~37 runs queued at peak. Part of that is jobs that rarely catch anything on PRs.

## Changes

- **`ci.yml` concurrency:** `cancel-in-progress` only for `pull_request`. On main, a run in progress finishes; a merge landing meanwhile waits and runs next, so main states get checked to the end.
- **`ci.yml` test matrix:** a small `platforms` job selects the OSes:
  - main, `workflow_dispatch`, and PRs labelled **`full-ci`**: Linux, macOS, Windows (as today);
  - other PRs: Linux, plus macOS and Windows when they touch platform-sensitive code: `apps/`, `crates/{ui-egui,text,gpu,tablet,heif}/`, any `build.rs`, `Cargo.lock`, `ci.yml`.
  - The macOS-only and Windows-only failures in the last day were all in UI/app/text code, which still gets all three OSes.
- **`ci.yml` craft-fonts run:** the second Linux test run with `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` covers only the crates that read craft-fonts (`photocraft-text`, plus the UI's CJK fallback in `photocraft-ui-egui`), not the whole workspace a second time.
- **FreeBSD and Windows ARM64:** nightly on main instead of on every main push and every `Cargo.toml` change; PRs that change their own packaging still run them. The FreeBSD VM job takes 1–5 h and was being cancelled on main anyway.

Unchanged: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `xtask layers`, `scorecard --check`, corpus tests and the wasm check still run on every PR.

title: Reject geometry params that would silently wrap through i64->i32 narrowing
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What

`commands::int` returns an unbounded `i64`, and the geometry call sites narrowed it with `as i32` — which **wraps by multiples of 2³²**. From every front door (UI, CLI, control channel, MCP):

- `layer.translate {"dx": 4294967346}` (= 2³²+50) moved the layer **50 px**; `dx: 3000000000` moved it to a large **negative** offset
- `select.rect` / `document.pixel` read coordinates unrelated to the numbers passed
- `image.crop` cropped a rectangle somewhere else entirely
- artboard `x`/`y` keys landed elsewhere

No panic, no `Err` — the document was silently mutated and then autosaved, and the behaviour is identical in debug and release, so `panic_hunt` cannot catch it. Two related neighbours fixed in the same spirit:

- `edit.contentAwareFill {"area": [1e30, 0, 1e30, 10]}` **panicked in debug builds** (`i32::MAX + i32::MAX` in the rect additions) and produced a garbage sampling window in release. (Float→int casts already saturate in Rust; the integer additions did not.)
- `filters::i` wrapped the same way: `filter.other.offset {"horizontal": 3000000000}` came back as a negative offset.

## Change

- New `commands::int_i32(cmd, p, key)`: `None` when absent, a `BadParams` error ("outside the 32-bit coordinate range") when the value would wrap. `select.rect`, `document.pixel`, `layer.translate`, `image.crop` and the artboard rect keys go through it; in-range values (negative, past-canvas) behave exactly as before.
- `image.crop` builds its rectangle with `saturating_add` (`x + w` overflow).
- The content-aware-fill `area` parser returns `BadParams` for malformed arrays (wrong length, non-numbers, non-finite — it used to silently fall back to a misleading "needs `area` or `channel`" error) and saturating arithmetic for huge ones — a huge area is now simply a whole-canvas window, which is what the downstream `intersect(&doc.bounds())` already assumed.
- `filters::i` clamps out-of-range values to the `i32` range, matching how the neighbouring filter params clamp.

A Photoshop template (.psdt) is an ordinary PSD that opens as a new, untitled document, so a save can't land on the template ([Adobe Community](https://community.adobe.com/t5/photoshop/what-is-a-psdt-file-type/m-p/8362261)). PhotoCraft read these files but didn't list them in File › Open, and it opened them under the template's name and path.

Now `.psdt` is in the Open filter (desktop and web), and a template opens as the first free "Untitled-N" with no path. File › Save then goes to Save As with `Untitled-N.psd` suggested, and the template still goes to Open Recent. One correction to the issue: Ctrl+S already refused to write over a .psdt (#416); the problem was that Save As suggested the template's own path.

`file_cmds::is_template` and `untitled_name` are used by every open path: File › Open, Open Recent, drops, launch arguments, background opens, the control channel's `app.open`, `file.openAs` and headless `doc_open`. The UI translates "Untitled" and also skips names used by files still opening, so two templates opened at once get Untitled-1 and Untitled-2.

Tests: synchronous and background opens (names, no path, Open Recent, the suggested Save As name), `app.open`, `file.openAs` with and without `as`, and MCP `doc_open` with a pathless save refused and the template unchanged.

Validation: `cargo fmt`, `clippy -D warnings` on engine, automation, ui-egui and both apps, the engine/automation/ui-egui suites, `xtask layers`, `xtask wasm` and panic_hunt pass. Checked in the desktop app as well: a .psdt opened from the command line comes up as Untitled-1 with its layers and no path.

title: Geom: Rect::width and height no longer overflow on i32-extreme rects (#675)
author: Luna161
body:
Fixes #675

## What was wrong

`Rect::width()` and `Rect::height()` computed `x1 - x0` with plain `i32` subtraction. With extreme edges the subtraction overflows: debug builds panic with `attempt to subtract with overflow` and release builds wrap. The `warp.*` commands build a `Rect` straight from the JSON `rect` param, so user input could reach this.

## Fix

Both methods now return `x1.abs_diff(x0)` when `x1 > x0`, and 0 otherwise (same for y). The distance between any two `i32` values fits in a `u32`, so the result is exact. No casts, no clamping.

I didn't go with `saturating_sub`. It avoids the panic, but a valid rect like `[i32::MIN, …, i32::MAX, …]` would then report a width of `i32::MAX` instead of its real extent. `is_empty`, `intersect`, `union` and the rest are unchanged.

## Tests

New `width_and_height_do_not_overflow_on_extreme_edges` in `crates/geom/src/lib.rs`:
- inverted `MAX..MIN` rect → `(0, 0)` and `is_empty()`
- widest rect `MIN..MAX` → `width() == u32::MAX`, height exact, `size()` agrees

With the old `width()`/`height()` restored:
```
test tests::width_and_height_do_not_overflow_on_extreme_edges ... FAILED
thread 'tests::width_and_height_do_not_overflow_on_extreme_edges' panicked at crates/geom/src/lib.rs:56:9:
attempt to subtract with overflow
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 13 filtered out
```
With the fix:
```
test tests::width_and_height_do_not_overflow_on_extreme_edges ... ok
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 13 filtered out
```

Gates: `cargo fmt --check` clean, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-geom --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo test -p photocraft-geom --lib` 14 passed, `cargo xtask layers` OK.

## Follow-up

`warp_cmds` still accepts absurd `rect` params. It should reject them up front with a proper parameter error. I left that out to keep this change to the geom leaf fix.

title: fix(engine): clone source_rect clamps huge mapped coordinates (#716)
author: bfenty
body:
# PR #716 — fix(engine): clone source_rect clamps huge mapped coordinates

**Branch:** `fix/716-clone-source-overflow`
**Title:** fix(engine): clone source_rect clamps huge mapped coordinates (#716)

## Body

Fixes #716.

`Mapping::source_rect` cast input-derived floats with `as i32` and then added the bilinear apron (`x1.ceil() as i32 + 2`). A large `source` (the issue's repro: 3e9 with `rotation: 45`, which forces the resample branch) saturates the cast to `i32::MAX` and the `+ 2` overflows — debug panics at `clone_source.rs:127`, and with overflow checks off the add wraps to an inverted rect that silently samples the wrong region. Same path is reachable from `paint.healingBrush`.

**Fix:** clamp to the i32 range before casting and apply the apron with saturating arithmetic — the same convention the sibling `Rect::inflate` uses for apron arithmetic, per AGENTS.md's rule for input-derived offsets. Normal-sized sources produce bit-identical rects; out-of-canvas sampling already tolerates transparent reads downstream in `sample`.

**Tests:** adds unit tests in `clone_source.rs`:
- the issue's 3e9 + 45° repro stays ordered (fails on main with `attempt to add with overflow` at line 127)
- a negative huge source clamps the same way
- a normal mapping's rect is unchanged (control)

Verified locally:
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine`: all suites ok, 0 failed
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean

title: undo/redo report the step's damage instead of recompositing the whole canvas
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What

`Session::edit`, `undo` and `redo` all cleared `last_damage`, so **every undo of a local edit recomposited the entire document** instead of the edited area. Measured on the committed perf baseline (20 MP): P6 *undo a move* 256 ms p50 against a ≤25 ms budget, P7 *redo* 144 ms. Only `layer.setProps` and the move paths computed damage; undo/redo of the exact same edits threw it away.

## Change

Undo and redo now diff the two documents on either side of the history step (`layer_multi_cmds::step_damage`):

- Every layer whose **pixel identity** changed contributes the union of its change bounds on both sides — a move reports where the layer was *and* where it landed (same shape `layers_damage` already produces for moves), a stroke reports the stroked layer's extent.
- The identity (`layer_fp`) covers everything the compositor reads: blending, placement, masks, effects, content specs, and pixels via their **copy-on-write tile pointers** — a rewrite always produces new tiles, an untouched layer hashes equal. Both documents stay alive for the comparison, so tile addresses cannot be reused under it (the same pinning argument the CPU effect-map cache makes).
- Steps the fingerprint cannot bound still composite everything, **by construction**: canvas size/pixel-format/profile changes, layer-structure changes (order, additions, removals, kind flips), and video layers return `None`. Mode conversions, flatten/merge, crop and structural undos therefore keep the full-recomposite path without relying on the edit having recorded its target layers correctly (an edit addressed via an explicit `layer` param can touch a layer outside the session's target — the diff approach doesn't care).

`Session::edit`'s default stays `None` (opt-in damage per command) — this PR only claims the undo/redo path.

## Tests

- `undo_and_redo_report_only_the_edited_area`: stroke and move undos/redos report the exact bounded rect; a paint edit reports the layer extent on both sides.
- `undo_of_doc…

title: fix(engine): stack mode refuses a source with no visible layers (#717)
author: bfenty
body:
# PR #717 — fix(engine): stack mode refuses a source with no visible layers

**Branch:** `fix/717-stack-empty-source`
**Title:** fix(engine): stack mode refuses a source with no visible layers (#717)

## Body

Fixes #717.

`stack_image` filtered the source document's layers to the visible ones and fed the result to `stack::combine` unconditionally. With every layer hidden the frame list is empty while the composited buffer keeps the canvas rect, so `buffer_to_surface` wrote a 0-length pixel array into `Surface::write_region` and tripped its length assertion (`raster/src/lib.rs:384`). The dispatch guard turned the panic into the generic internal error the issue reports.

**Fix:** return a specific error — "the smart object's contents have no visible layers" — when the visible set is empty, per AGENTS.md rule 9 (return `Err`, never panic, for any document state). The document is left unchanged, as before, but callers now see why.

**Tests:** adds `crates/engine/tests/stack_empty_source.rs` following the issue's repro (convert → editContents → hide the sole layer → saveContents → close → stackMode.mean):
- the all-hidden source must produce the *specific* error, not the catch-all (on main it gets the catch-all, with the `write_region` assertion firing in the log)
- control: stack mode over a source with visible layers still succeeds

title: Add the Content-Aware Move tool (#213)
author: alexanderalber
body:
Adds Photoshop's Content-Aware Move tool (scorecard TOOL-213-4, follow-up to the Patch tool in #381).

**What it does**
- New command `paint.contentAwareMove {offset, mode: move|extend, structure: 1..7, color: 0..10, sampleAllLayers}`. The selected content is pasted where it was dragged. `color` fits its colour to the new place (0 keeps it, 10 is a full seamless clone, as in Patch). A band along its edge, whose width `structure` sets (7 = none), is re-synthesised with `content_aware::fill` so that the content merges in. In Move mode the old place is then filled content-aware, without sampling the moved content, so the object doesn't come back as a ghost. Extend keeps the original. The selection moves with the content.
- One undo step. Runs as a background job (#210): progress dialog, Esc cancels, and the document stays unchanged until the job applies. Works on layer pixels, masks and channels, at 8/16/32-bit and in any colour model. Sample All Layers paints the visible result onto the target layer, e.g. an empty layer above the image.
- New `Tool::ContentAwareMove` in the J group, using the Patch tool's gestures: outside the selection a drag draws a lasso, inside it drags the selection. Options bar: Mode, Structure, Color, Sample All Layers. New strings are added to all eleven catalogs.

**Numbers** (`retouch_bench`, release, 6016×6016, elliptical selection dragged 300 px)

| Selection | Move | Extend (Color 5) |
|---|---|---|
| 100×100 | 70 ms | 35 ms |
| 250×250 | 240 ms | 129 ms |
| 500×500 | 0.93 s | 0.53 s |
| 1000×1000 | 2.6 s | 1.5 s |

**Tests**
- Engine tests at 8/16/32-bit, covering:
  - move and extend, undo/redo including the selection
  - Structure 7 copies exactly; lower Structure blends the edge; Color 10 adapts the colour
  - a canvas-edge and overlapping move, a transparent layer, a mask target, grayscale
  - Sample All Layers onto an empty layer
  - graceful failure on bad params
- A job test: same result as inline, and cancelling leaves the docume…

# PR #718 — fix(engine): migratePresets marks the preferences dirty

**Branch:** `fix/718-migrate-presets-rev`
**Title:** fix(engine): migratePresets marks the preferences dirty (#718)

## Body

Fixes #718.

The preset library persists with the preferences document, and every other preset-mutating path signals that through `Session::presets_changed` (bumps the preset revision *and* the preferences revision). The shell's persist loop is gated solely on `prefs.rev()`. `migrate` only incremented the preset revision, so a migration that appended groups was never written to the preferences file until some unrelated preference change happened — quitting before that loses the migration.

**Fix:** call `presets_changed()` when the migration actually adds something, exactly like the sibling preset commands. A migration that adds nothing still leaves both revisions untouched.

- importing a new gradient group must bump `prefs.rev()` (on main it stays at 0 while `presets.gradients` grows)
