title: image.crop rejects an origin or far edge that can't be moved within i32 instead of panicking (#959)
author: mnmlyw
body:
Fixes #959.

## What changed

`crop_doc` in `crates/engine/src/image_cmds.rs` moved the document by `-r.x0, -r.y0` with no check. With `x` or `y = i32::MIN` (-2147483648) the negation overflows and panics. With an origin just above i32::MIN, the move pushes layer pixels past i32::MAX, and `translate_surface` panics on a length mismatch.

- **Origin check:** `crop_doc` negates the origin with `checked_neg`. If that fails it returns a BadParams error naming the origin, before any pixels are deleted. The issue asks for an actionable error with the document unchanged, and this does that.
- **Translation check:** `translate_doc` first checks that every surface (layers, masks, caches, channels, quick mask, selection) still fits in the 32-bit range after the move. Only then does it move anything; otherwise it returns BadParams. Crop, Trim and Canvas Size all use this path.
- **Far edge (beyond the issue):** in an explicit crop rectangle, `x + width` and `y + height` are now checked instead of saturated. Before, a rectangle ending past i32::MAX silently cropped less than requested; now it is rejected with the sum named. This follows #803's rule of rejecting out-of-range values over capping them. It's easy to drop if you'd rather keep this PR to the panic.
- **Nothing changes on error:** the errors come before or inside the transactional edit. The document, revision and history stay as they were.

Not changed here: the same saturating move can still panic through `translate_surface` and `shift_surface` from other callers with extreme coordinates (paste, floating selections, smart objects, place, variables, artboards). That's better fixed once in those helpers, in a separate PR.

## Tests

- `image_cmds::tests::crop_rejects_origins_that_cannot_move_to_zero`:

title: Deep EXR: write the flattened pixel by layout, not a fixed RGBA quadruple
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What

Grayscale deep EXR files (channels `Y` + `A` + `Z`) flattened wrong: the tail of the composite loop wrote a fixed `[R, G, B, A]` quadruple into the output row, so a **GrayA** image's alpha slot received an un-premultiplied **luminance copy** (α=1.0 for a 0.5-alpha file) while the real accumulated alpha fell past the row's end. The image opened as opaque with a wrong channel.

(A user of our fork noticed "something with grayscale" on deep EXR — this was it.)

## Change

The flattened pixel is now written by layout: `RGB(A)`, `gray + A`, `gray` — alpha in the slot it belongs to, and the redundant post-loop luminance rewrite is gone. RGB(A) paths are byte-identical.

## Tests

`grayscale_deep_keeps_its_alpha`: a `Y + A + Z` file with premultiplied Y=0.5 at α=0.5 must flatten to GrayA `(1.0, 0.5)` (this test fails on main with `alpha 1, want 0.5`), and a `Y + Z` file flattens to opaque Gray `0.4`.

Gates: `cargo test -p photocraft-codecs` all suites green · clippy `--no-deps` clean · `cargo fmt` · `xtask wasm`.

title: Link Layers allocates a group id that can't overflow (#961)
author: mnmlyw
body:
Fixes #961.

## What changed

`link_layers` in `crates/engine/src/layer_multi_cmds.rs` picked the new link group as `max(link_group) + 1`, and computed it even when unlinking. A loaded `.pcraft` or PSD can store `u64::MAX`, so the addition panicked in overflow-checked builds.

- **Shared overflow-safe allocator:** the new `Document::unused_link_group()` in `crates/doc/src/lib.rs` returns the highest id + 1 when that fits. Otherwise it returns the smallest free id from 1, and it never wraps, so a new link can't join an unrelated group (such as an existing group 0).
- **Link Layers uses it only when linking:** unlinking no longer computes an id. If no id is left, the command returns an error and changes nothing.
- **Beyond the issue:** the same function now reads the first selected group with `first()` and the member counts with `get()` instead of indexing. Neither could panic today; this just removes the indexing.
- **Not changed:** stored ids aren't rewritten on load, so round trips keep their numbering.

## Tests

- `layer_multi_cmds::tests::link_layers_beside_a_maximal_stored_group`:
  - A layer stored at `u64::MAX` linked with an unlinked layer: both share one new group (not `u64::MAX`) that no other layer uses, and one history step is recorded.
  - Unlinking then relinking the pair gives group 1.
  - Two unlinked layers linked beside an untouched `u64::MAX` pair get their own group, and the pair is unchanged.
- `layer_multi_cmds::tests::unlink_a_maximal_stored_group`: unlinking a pair stored at `u64::MAX` clears both, undo restores them, and relinking three layers gives a fresh shared group.

title: Timeline: out-of-range duration and fps are rejected, and stepping never panics (#1009)
author: mnmlyw
body:
Fixes #1009.

## What changed

`timeline.create` in `crates/engine/src/timeline_cmds.rs` kept any `duration` up to `u64::MAX`, and `step` moved the playhead with `(t.current as i64 + delta).clamp(0, t.duration as i64 - 1)`. That panics when the upper bound goes negative (duration above `i64::MAX` as `i64`, or a stored duration of 0) or when the subtraction overflows.

- **Validated params:** `timeline.create` rejects a `duration` outside `1..=1000000` or not a whole number, and an `fps` that isn't finite in `(0, 1000]`, with `BadParams` naming the value. This happens before anything changes. `null` still means the default. On `main` these were accepted or silently replaced: `duration` 0 became 1, `fps` 0 and -24 became 30, `fps` 1e300 was stored as infinity (`"fps": null` in `timeline.info`), and `duration` -1 fell back to 30.
- **Saturating step:** new `Timeline::step` in `crates/doc/src/video.rs` replaces the `i64` clamp. It never panics and always lands on a valid frame for any stored timeline, including one loaded with duration 0.
- **`timeline.setProps` validated too (beyond the issue):** it could store the same panicking `duration` (`u64::MAX`) and invalid `fps`.
- **Non-finite fps falls back to 30 (beyond the issue):** `Timeline::new` and `Timeline::clamp` now treat NaN and inf like fps ≤ 0.

The 1 000 000-frame and 1000 fps caps are a choice; I found no existing limit to match. Happy to change them.

## Tests

- `timeline_cmds::tests::create_rejects_out_of_range_params`:
  - Rejected with `BadParams`, leaving timeline, revision and history depth unchanged:
    - `duration`: 0, `u64::MAX`, `i64::MAX + 1`, `MAX_DURATION + 1`, -1, 2.5, `"24"`.
    - `fps`: 0, -24, `MAX_FPS + 1`, 1e300, `"fast"`.
  - The issue's repro: next/previous frame still step the existing timeline (5 → 6 → 5).
  - Control: `MAX_DURATION` at `MAX_FPS` is accepted and steps at both ends. `null` params give the 30/30 defaults.

title: Content-Aware fill: a huge selection extent returns the size error instead of overflowing (#963)
author: mnmlyw
body:
Fixes #963.

## What changed

`content_aware` in `crates/engine/src/fill_cmds.rs` computed the sampling margin as `ext * 3 / 4` in u32 before its 400 M-pixel window cap. A loaded document with a selection extent above 1 431 655 765 px overflowed and panicked instead of returning the size error. `content_aware_fill` in `crates/engine/src/edit_menu_cmds.rs` (`edit.contentAwareFill`) had the same overflow in i32 and no window cap at all.

- **Shared margin:** a new `fill_cmds::sampling_margin` computes three quarters of the hole's larger side in u64, saturated to i32, with a minimum of 32.
- **Shared cap:** a new `fill_cmds::window_size` checks the window against the existing 400 M-pixel cap with a u64 product and returns "the selection is too large for Content-Aware fill" before anything is read or allocated.
- **`edit.contentAwareFill` (beyond the issue):** uses the shared margin, saturates its extent instead of casting with `as i32`, and checks the window cap for every sampling mode (auto, rectangular, custom). Before, it had no cap.
- **Content-Aware Move (beyond the issue, no behaviour change):** its sampling window uses the shared margin, still clamped to `MAX_MARGIN`.

Not changed: `edit.fill` with `pattern` or `history` contents still sizes its buffers from the raw selection bounds with no cap.

## Tests

- `fill_cmds::tests::content_aware_huge_extent_is_an_error`:
  - Cases: the issue's repro (second selection tile at tx 5 600 000 on a 2e9 × 2e9 canvas), wide and tall extents just above and just below the u32 overflow point, a corner-to-corner selection on an i32::MAX canvas with a piece at i32::MIN, and a u32::MAX canvas. Each asserts an error that isn't the internal-error fallback (the size error for all but the u32::MAX canvas), the same document `Arc`, no new history step and unchanged layer pixels.

title: Applying a text data set re-renders the type layer instead of blanking it (#990)
author: ianswope
body:
Fixes #990.

### Cause

`apply_to_doc` (`crates/engine/src/variables_cmds.rs`) replaced a text-replacement variable's text and set `t.cache = None` with the comment "force re-render", but nothing re-rendered it. The compositor draws a type layer from that cache (`layer.surface()`), so after `image.applyDataSet` the text layer contributed no pixels. `file.export.dataSetsAsFiles` applies the same helper to a clone and exports it directly, so every exported row with a text value was missing its text as well.

The issue's trace was static. I confirmed it at runtime on `main` (`e694208`): a 32 px "HELLO" layer drew 617 dark pixels before applying a "BYE" data set and 0 after.

### Change

After setting the text, the layer is re-rendered with `type_cmds::refresh`, the same call `type.edit` makes through `with_text_layer`, against a snapshot of the document (tiles are `Arc`-shared, so the clone is cheap). Clearing `runs` and `paragraphs` is unchanged.

### Tests

`variables_cmds::tests::applied_text_is_rendered_in_the_document_and_in_exports` creates a real type layer, binds it to a text variable, then checks that the exported PNG for the row and the document after `image.applyDataSet` both still draw text. It fails on `main` ("the exported row keeps its text") and passes with the fix.

`cargo test -p photocraft-engine`, `panic_hunt -- --ignored`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

title: Clone Stamp: live stroke, strokes start on the press, source preview under the brush
author: jason4short
body:
Part of #213, live previews for brush-based tools. This one covers the **Clone Stamp**.

Until now the Clone Stamp drew a translucent grey trail while dragging and showed the cloned pixels only on release. Now:

- **It renders live, like the Brush.** `retouch_cmds::LiveClone` feeds the same `StrokeRenderer` the commit's coverage uses (`stroke_coverage`). For the tiles each step changes, it redraws from the pre-stroke pixels with the clone source sampled through the coverage so far, using the same `clone_sample` and `apply_coverage` as `paint.cloneStamp`, so the preview is what the commit paints. Like the Brush's live stroke, it also draws what finishing would add (`tail_preview`), so a lone first dab and the smoothing catch-up show while drawing.

Other tools keep the click distance.
- **Source preview under the brush.** After ⌥-click sets a source, the brush shows the pixels a stroke there would clone, shaped and faded like one dab of the current brush (size, hardness, tip and opacity, from the same renderer). The first stroke ends the preview, a new source brings it back, and holding ⌥ hides it while you pick a new source. The texture is rendered once per source, brush or revision.

title: Holding a number key sets one digit's opacity, not a two-digit value (#953)
author: ianswope
body:
Fixes #953.

### Cause

`opacity_keys::handle` matched `Event::Key { pressed: true, .. }` and the `..` dropped `repeat`. The first auto-repeat of a held digit, if it came within `TWO_DIGITS_MS` (800 ms) of the press, was taken as the second digit of a two-digit value. Holding 4 set 44% instead of 40%, and holding 0 flipped between 100% and 0% as repeats paired up.

### Change

A repeat of a held digit is still consumed (so it doesn't fall through to another shortcut) but is no longer pushed as a press. Two separate presses of the same key (4, release, 4 → 44%) still make a two-digit value.

### Tests

`opacity_keys::tests::a_held_digit_is_one_digit` sends the press and one repeat of `4` in a single frame, as egui reports a held key, and checks that the brush opacity is 0.40 and the repeat isn't left in the event queue. It then checks that a real second press still gives 0.44. Without the fix it fails with `0.44`.

`cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

title: Artboards: coordinates past the 32-bit range are rejected instead of overflowing (#931)
author: mnmlyw
body:
Fixes #931.

## What changed

Artboard commands in `crates/engine/src/artboard_cmds.rs` did i32 arithmetic on board coordinates:
- Default placement added the 100 px gap to the rightmost board's right edge.
- Editing subtracted the old origin from the new one.
- Exporting negated the board origin.

For a board at an i32 extreme, each of these overflowed. Checked builds panicked, and the dispatch guard turned that into a generic internal error. Rects were also built with `Rect::from_xywh`, which clamps the far edge to `i32::MAX`, so boards were silently stored narrower than requested, down to width 0.

- **Checked board rects:** a new `board_rect` builds x, y, width and height in i64. Any edge outside the i32 range is a BadParams error naming the values; it's no longer clamped. The `"rect"` array is parsed as i64 instead of `as i32`.
- **Default placement:** the gap is computed in i64. If there's no room right of the rightmost board, the command errors and asks for an explicit `"x"`, rather than picking a spot that could overlap a board. An explicit `x` or `rect` still works.
- **Edit:** the move offset is computed in i64 before the document changes. A move that needs more than 32 bits is rejected when the contents move too. With `"moveContents": false` it succeeds, because only the board rect changes.
- **Export (beyond the issue):** `artboard_document` uses `checked_neg`, so a board at `i32::MIN` returns an error instead of panicking. Every board's document is built before any file is written, so a failed export writes nothing. `artboard_document` now returns a `Result`; its only callers are in this file.

title: Brush Scatter: out-of-range amounts are rejected and dab rects can't overflow (#977)
author: mnmlyw
body:
Fixes #977.

## What changed

`tools.setBrush` and a stroke's own `brush` patch accepted any Scatter amount. `DabBuilder::build` multiplies it by the radius in `f32`, so an amount like `1e38` overflowed the dab centre to infinity. `dab_rect` then cast that centre to `i32` (saturating at `i32::MAX`) and built the rectangle with unchecked arithmetic, which panicked with overflow checks on. The Dual Brush scatter had the same path.

- **Validation:** brush validation rejects a primary Scatter amount outside 0 to 10 (the 1000 % slider maximum) with a bad-params error naming the value, before the session brush changes. In `tools.setBrush` the check also runs between its two merges, so an amount that only fits as infinity is reported as `inf` instead of a `null` type error. Scatter above 100 % keeps working.
- **Capped in the renderer:** `bounded_for_render` caps the primary and Dual Brush Scatter at the new `MAX_SCATTER` for direct users of the paint API (NaN scatters nothing, infinity is treated as the maximum). Every brush engine builds its dabs through `DabGenerator`, so this one cap covers them all, and ordinary amounts give bit-identical dabs.
- **Dual Brush scatter validated the same way** (beyond the issue).
- **Negative Scatter amounts rejected** (beyond the issue): they are outside the documented range and previously did nothing.
- **Saturating dab rectangle** (beyond the issue): `BrushContext::dab_rect` and `retouch::dab_rect` now share one helper with saturating arithmetic, so a far or non-finite centre or reach gives a well-formed rectangle instead of an overflow.

A stored preset or session brush with Scatter above 10 and scattering enabled now makes strokes fail with that error, as an oversized brush size already does.

title: Layer comps: offsets that don't fit i32 are dropped with a warning instead of overflowing (#1017)
author: mnmlyw
body:
Fixes #1017.

## What changed

Layer comp positions were computed with unchecked `i32` arithmetic on values from files:
- Import (`crates/io/src/comps_map.rs`) added the layer origin to the `cmls` `Ofst` offset, and truncated 64-bit descriptor integers with `as i32`.
- Export subtracted the layer origin from the stored position.
- Applying a comp (`crates/engine/src/comps_cmds.rs`) subtracted the layer's current position.

Extreme offsets panicked with overflow checks on, and wrapped silently with them off.

- **Import:** offsets are kept as `i64`. Origin + offset is checked, and a sum that doesn't fit `i32` drops that position, with an import warning naming the layer and offset. Visibility from the same entry is kept. `comps_from_psd` keeps its signature; a new `decode_comps` also returns the warnings, which `psd_import` adds to the import warnings.

- **64-bit offsets (beyond the issue):** `LargeInteger` offsets are no longer truncated with `as i32`. They go through the same check, so they're dropped with a warning instead of wrapping (2^32+1 used to become 1).

title: CPU effect maps: key fill layers by their cached pixels, drop opacity/visible
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What

The CPU layer-effect map cache keyed a **Fill layer by its Fill spec alone**. But what shapes the maps is the layer's *cached pixels* whenever they still match the fill — the render a PSD import stores, and what Image › Transform, crop and canvas ops rewrite **in place** without touching the spec. After such a rewrite the CPU compositor kept serving the pre-rewrite maps: flattens, exports and the CPU canvas showed the **drop shadow of the pre-rewrite shape** while the live GPU canvas was correct — until budget eviction or a purge. (Found in a full-codebase audit; the GPU side already keys by the cache surface, which is why the two paths disagreed.)

Second half: `layer.opacity` and `layer.visible` were hashed into the same key although the maps don't depend on them — `fill_opacity` shades the maps, layer opacity is applied when the maps are composited, and visibility only skips the lookup entirely. An opacity slider drag or a show/hide toggle on a styled layer rebuilt every shadow and glow map over the whole layer region for nothing. The GPU's `fx::shape_key` keeps both out for exactly this reason; the CPU key now matches.

## Change

`layer_identity` (compose): the `Fill` arm hashes the cache surface's tile fingerprint while `cache.fill == fill`, and `visible`/`opacity` leave the key. Checked against `composite_with_effects_prepared` and `build_maps_prepared`: only `fill_opacity` is read while building maps.

## Tests

`fill_layer_pixel_rewrites_refresh_the_effect_maps` (engine): a fill layer with the cached-pixels state a PSD import produces, with a drop shadow; after an in-place rewrite of the cache (what Image › Transform does), the warm-cache composite must equal a purged-cache composite. Fails on main (`the effect maps track the cache surface, not the Fill spec alone`), green with the key fix.

title: Install PhotoCraft with Homebrew: brew install --cask storytold/tap/photocraft (#342, #592, #1033)
author: bflatastic

Fixes #342. Fixes #592. Fixes #1033.

macOS users can install and update PhotoCraft with Homebrew:

```sh
brew install --cask storytold/tap/photocraft
```

## What

- **`packaging/homebrew/photocraft.rb`**: a cask for the release's notarized, stapled **universal** DMG (`photocraft-<v>-macos-universal.dmg`). Apple silicon and Intel use the same file, so the cask has one `url`/`sha256` and no `on_arm`/`on_intel`. It also has:
  - `verified:` on the GitHub URL, because the homepage is getartcraft.com.
  - `depends_on macos: ">= :big_sur"`, matching `LSMinimumSystemVersion` 11.0 and `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET`.

  - `uninstall quit: "ai.storyteller.photocraft"`.
  - A `zap` that removes `~/Library/Application Support/Photocraft`. That is the single directory `apps/photocraft/src/app_dirs.rs` uses for preferences, presets, recovery autosaves, `ui.ron` and the GPU marker. The `zap` also removes the preferences plist and saved window state macOS keeps for the bundle id.
  - It's committed at 0.3.0 with that release's real sha256.
- **`packaging/homebrew/update.sh <version>`**: sets `version` and `sha256` from the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and refuses pre-releases. It edits through a temp file rather than `sed -i`, so the same script works on macOS (BSD) and Linux (GNU). This follows `packaging/arch/update.sh` from #374.
- **`.github/workflows/homebrew.yml`**: a separate workflow, like `aur.yml` in #374. - `csv_import_errors_leave_existing_data_sets_unchanged`: empty and invalid-UTF-8 input returns an error without changing existing data sets.

title: Preferences: reset a single shortcut or menu colour override (#988)
author: tiredIsa
body:
Fixes #988

## Problem

`prefs.set` and `prefs.get` accept `shortcuts.<command id>` and `menus.colors.<id>`, but resetting one of those keys failed with "unknown preference": `Preferences::reset` looked for its value in the empty default map. The command also read the same path for its response, which would fail once the override was removed.

## What changed

- Resetting an individual shortcut or menu colour removes just that override, using the existing handling for command ids containing dots.
- `prefs.reset` returns `null` for the removed override. Resetting an already absent map key also succeeds, matching the existing shortcut-removal behavior.
- The control-protocol documentation describes the result.

- Four new tests cover the preference API and registered commands: dotted ids, preservation of unrelated overrides and settings, default shortcut fallback (including a disabled shortcut), revision bumps, save/load, repeated and absent-key resets, and the existing `section` alias.

title: Layers panel: Alt-click the line between two layers creates or releases a clipping mask (#967)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #967.

**Cause.** The Layers panel had no hit target for the line between two rows, so Alt-click there just selected a layer.

**Fix.** New `crates/ui-egui/src/clip_line_ui.rs`. After the panel draws its rows, it checks for Alt held over the top edge of a row (a ±3 pt band). If the row drawn above is the sibling directly above in the stack, it does three things:
- shows a clip cursor (the Lucide `corner-right-down` icon through `icons::cursor`)
- registers a click target on top of the two rows, so the click doesn't select a row
- on click, runs the existing `layer.createClippingMask` on the upper layer, or `layer.releaseClippingMask` if it is clipped already. That is one history step, and the layer selection doesn't change.

There is no clip line in these cases:
- inside an open group (a group and its first child)
- under a group's last child
- across rows hidden by a Kind filter or isolation

The band also leaves the eye column (Alt-click there is Show Only) and the effects triangle alone. A collapsed group can be clipped to the layer below it.

**Photoshop parity.** This matches Photoshop: Alt/Option-click the border between two layers clips the upper one to the layer below, and Alt-click again releases it. One difference: Photoshop's Release also releases the clipped layers above the one you click. This PR reuses the existing release command, which releases only that layer (left as is).

**Tests** (`clip_line_ui/tests.rs`):
- Alt-click on the line clips, then releases. It is one history step and the selection doesn't change.
- A plain click on the line doesn't clip.
- The clip cursor shows only while Alt is held over a line.
- `at()` rules: siblings in the stack, open and closed groups, a filtered-out row in between, the eye column, the middle of a row.

I checked an offscreen render at 2× (clip cursor on the line between `b` and `a`; after the click, `b` shows the clipped ↳ marker).

title: Move tool moves the selected pixels when there is a selection (#578)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #578.

**Cause:** the Move tool always ran `layer.translate`, so it ignored the selection. The floating-selection machinery (`select.float` / `select.drop`) was only reachable through the marquee/lasso ⌘-drag.

**Fix:** with a selection, the Move tool reuses that machinery (`move_ui::moves_selected_pixels` / `float_selected`):
- **Drag**, from anywhere on the canvas: cuts the active layer's selected pixels and drags them as a floating piece. The canvas shows the piece live, as the marquee ⌘-drag already does. The hole is transparent. On the **Background** it takes the background colour: `select.float` now allows the Background despite its position lock and fills the hole, the same way Edit › Cut does.
- **⌥-drag** copies the selected pixels and leaves the originals (new `select.float` param `"copy": bool`). It no longer duplicates the layer. ⌥ on a piece that is already floating drops it where it is and drags a copy.
- **⇧** constrains the drag to multiples of 45°. Layer drags stay horizontal/vertical, as before.
- **Arrow keys** nudge the selected pixels 1 px (⇧ 10 px, ⌥ copies).
- **↩**, Deselect or any other command drops the piece as **one "Move" history step**. One undo restores everything. The drop label changed from "Move Selected Pixels" to "Move", as in Photoshop.
- A click that moves nothing leaves no floating piece behind, so the next ⌘Z isn't spent putting it back. This also applies to the marquee ⌘-click.

**Unchanged:** Auto-Select (and ⌘-click) when there is no selection. With a selection the press moves pixels and does not pick a layer. title: ⌘/Ctrl-scroll pans the canvas sideways; scroll bars always shown (#635, #620)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #635.
Fixes #620.

**Cause.** egui's default `InputOptions` turn ⌘/Ctrl + wheel into a zoom, which is also how Windows delivers a precision touchpad pinch (Ctrl + wheel, the legacy fallback). That's why the earlier attempt (#362) broke pinch-zoom on Windows. The canvas scroll bars only appeared on an axis where the image didn't fit.

**Fix.**
- `wheel_nav::configure` (called from `setup_context`) sets egui's `zoom_modifier` to none and `horizontal_scroll_modifier` to ⇧ | ⌘/Ctrl. Now ⌘/Ctrl + wheel scrolls sideways exactly as ⇧ + wheel does, with the same smoothing, and only a real pinch (`Event::Zoom` from winit's `PinchGesture` on macOS, or from the browser on the web) or a touch screen reaches `zoom_delta`.
- Windows: `wheel_nav::fold_legacy_pinch` runs in `raw_input_hook` (`cfg!(target_os = "windows")`). It turns Ctrl + wheel events in fractions of a notch (a touchpad pinch) back into `Event::Zoom`, at egui's previous Ctrl-scroll zoom speed, before egui sees them. Ctrl + a notched mouse wheel (whole notches) scrolls sideways. A whole-notch step within 0.25 s of a pinch step still counts as pinch. This needs no `unsafe` and no DirectManipulation crate (issue question 3). Linux follows Windows (Ctrl, issue question 2); winit delivers no pinch there.
- Preferences › General › Zoom with Scroll Wheel now swaps the two: the wheel zooms and ⌥/Alt + wheel scrolls. ⇧ and ⌘/Ctrl + wheel still scroll sideways.
- Scroll bars (`scrollbars.rs`) are always shown in Standard Screen Mode. `Span::extent(overscroll)`: with Overscroll on, an image that fits the window can be scrolled edge to edge with the bars. With it off, the thumb fills the track (the image stays centred, as before). When zoomed in, the extent is unchanged.

title: Pen tablets: the pen works on Wayland (through Xwayland), macOS pressure fixes (#639, #759)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #639. Addresses #759 (macOS part; the Windows "Windows Ink off" comment is left to #943).

## Cause
- **Wayland (#639):** compositors (Mutter, KWin) give a pen only to clients that bind `zwp_tablet_v2`. winit 0.30 doesn't bind it, so the pen got no input at all in our window: no cursor movement, no clicks, no strokes. Reporters confirmed that the same AppImage works with pressure on X11.
- **macOS (#759):** the AppKit local event monitor was installed in `main` before `eframe::run_native`, so before winit had created the shared `NSApplication`. That ordering is the one path the monitor's tests never cover, because `monitor_macos` creates `NSApp` first. Separately, the pen's button-up carries pressure 0. Because the UI reads the latest sample when the frame runs, that 0 thinned or erased the stroke's last moves in the same frame.

## Fix
- **Wayland:** when a pen is attached, the window opens through Xwayland. Xwayland binds tablet-v2 and serves the pen as an XInput2 device, which our existing X11 reader handles (pressure, tilt, eraser end). That reader's pressure path is the one users confirmed works.
  - A pen is detected by `BTN_TOOL_PEN` in `/proc/bus/input/devices`, which covers tablet styli, pen displays and pen-enabled touchscreens.
  - The switch also needs `$DISPLAY` to be set and the X11 libraries to be found (the existing `linux_libs` probe). The preflight check then runs for the X11 libraries.
  - It uses `winit::platform::x11::EventLoopBuilderExtX11::with_x11()` through eframe's `event_loop_builder`. `winit` was already in Cargo.lock and is now a direct dependency, pinned `=0.30.13`, because eframe doesn't re-export the trait.
  - `PHOTOCRAFT_NATIVE_WAYLAND=1` keeps native Wayland. The app prints one stderr line when it switches.
- **macOS:**
  - The monitor is now installed from eframe's app creation, once `NSApp` exists, and is kept in a `OnceCell` until the event loop returns.

title: File dialogs no longer freeze or crash the app (#673, #574)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #673.
Fixes #574.

**Cause.** Every file dialog (Open, Save As, Export As, Place, scripts, notes, presets, Measurement Log export, Save for Web…) ran rfd's *synchronous* dialog from inside winit's event handler. On macOS that runs `-[NSSavePanel runModal]` there; if AppKit delivered another event while it was open (a trackpad gesture, say), winit panicked inside an `extern "C"` callback and the process aborted (`panic_cannot_unwind`, #673). On Linux the event loop was frozen for as long as the dialog stayed open, so compositors (Hyprland) flagged the app as not responding (#574).

**Fix.** `Services::pick_open` / `pick_open_paths` / `pick_save` (synchronous) are replaced by one asynchronous `Services::file_dialog`:
- `crates/ui-egui/src/file_dialog.rs`: a command asks with `ask_file` (or `pick_save` / `pick_file_bytes` / `open_dialog_file`) and hands over a continuation. `poll_file_dialog`, at the end of `logic` and `ui`, shows the queued dialog with the window (`eframe::Frame`) as its parent and runs the continuation when the answer arrives through a `FileDialogReply` (`Send`, wakes egui). The window keeps drawing and responding meanwhile.
- Desktop (`apps/photocraft/src/services.rs`): rfd's `AsyncFileDialog` is built on the main thread with `set_parent` (a sheet on macOS, an owned modal dialog on Windows/Linux) and awaited on a helper thread with a small std-only `block_on`. No new dependency.
- Web: the same service (Open hands over the file's contents, Save gives the download name). Place and Run Script on the web now receive the picked file; before, it went through the inbox and opened as a document.

title: Wayland: drop notice offers paste and the XWayland command for this install (#338, #386)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #386. Part of #338.

## Cause
eframe 0.36.2 runs on winit 0.30.13, and winit 0.30 has no Wayland drag and drop. The Wayland notice from #430 told every user to run `WAYLAND_DISPLAY= photocraft`. That command is wrong for two of our Linux packages:
- **AppImage** (the #338 reporter's build): there is no `photocraft` on the PATH.
- **Flatpak**: the manifest uses `fallback-x11`, so the sandbox gets no X socket while Wayland is available. Unsetting `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` can't help.

The notice also left out pasting. #430 dropped that advice because #384 wasn't merged yet. #384 has since landed, so Ctrl+V on a file copied in Files, Dolphin or Thunar now pastes it.

## Fix
- **Shell** (`apps/photocraft`): `services::xwayland_command` picks the relaunch command for how PhotoCraft was installed:
  - Flatpak (`FLATPAK_ID`): `flatpak run --nosocket=wayland --socket=x11 <id>`
  - AppImage (`APPIMAGE`): `WAYLAND_DISPLAY= '<path>'`, POSIX-quoted
  - anything else: `WAYLAND_DISPLAY= photocraft`

  Outside Flatpak there is no command when `DISPLAY` is unset (no XWayland). `main` sets it only on Wayland.
- **ui-egui**: `Services::xwayland_command` is a new field.
  - The notice now reads: File › Open, or copy the image in your file manager and paste it with {paste}. When there is a command, a second line reads: To drop files, start PhotoCraft under XWayland: `{command}`.
  - The Wayland start-screen hint now reads "Use File › Open, or paste a copied image with {paste}." It no longer mentions File › Open alone.
  - `{paste}` is Edit › Paste's effective shortcut, so it follows Keyboard Shortcuts overrides. If that binding was removed, it falls back to "Edit › Paste".

title: Paste into a targeted layer mask (or channel) instead of making a new layer (#1035)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #1035.

**Cause.** `edit.paste` and the Paste Special commands always made a new raster layer. Unlike fills, filters and adjustments, they ignored the layer-mask / channel target.

**Fix.**
- **Shared paste path:** `edit_cmds::paste_to_target` takes the paste when the target isn't the layer's pixels (`"target"`: `mask`, `{"channel": i}` or `quickMask`). It places the clipboard as a normal paste would: the same offset logic, now shared as `paste_offset`, so in place, centred on the view, or on the selection for Paste Into. It then composites the pixels over the mask or channel in Normal mode at 100 %.
- **Compositing reuses Fill:** the composite goes through Fill's tiled `blend_into` (new `fill_cmds::composite_over`). The grey target keeps the luminosity of the pasted pixels, and their transparency lets the existing mask show through. It is one history step and makes no new layer. Like a layer paste, it deselects.
- **Paste Into / Outside:** with a mask or channel target, these limit the paste to the selection or to its inverse, rather than adding a new layer with a mask. The inverse-selection mask is now built once and shared by both paths. The pixel path passes `"target":"pixels"` explicitly to its inner `edit.paste`.
- **Targeting:** the four paste ids join `channel_cmds::routed`, so they follow the target like fills and filters do. The engine fills in `"mask"` while the mask is viewed (⌥-click). The shell's `with_mask_target` fills it in when the mask thumbnail is the target. The params docs list `"target"`.

**Photoshop parity.** Pasting with the layer mask shown (⌥-click its thumbnail) puts the clipboard's grey values into the mask, gradients included, as in Photoshop. A targeted alpha channel or Quick Mask also takes the paste, which is what Photoshop does when a single channel is the target.

title: Layers panel: hovering a blend mode previews it live on the canvas (#970)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #970.

**Cause.** The Layers panel's blend-mode dropdown only reported a click, so nothing on the canvas changed until a mode was chosen.

**Fix.**
- **Dropdown:** new `widgets::dropdown_hovered` also returns the option under the pointer in the open list. `widgets::dropdown` now wraps it, so the other dropdowns are unchanged.
- **Panel state:** each frame the Layers panel draws the dropdown, it passes the hovered mode to the new `crate::blend_preview::hover`. A chosen mode is still committed with `layer.setProps`, one history step as before.
- **Preview:** `blend_preview::display_doc` is one more step in the existing live-preview chain, `canvas::display_doc`, next to the Move and Patch previews. - **Duotone:** previews still display through the inks.

**Photoshop parity.** This matches Photoshop's live blend-mode preview: hovering a mode in the Layers panel list previews it on the selected layer, moving off the list reverts, and only a click applies it.

title: Red Eye tool in the J-group flyout
author: mvanhorn
body:
## What

Adds the **Red Eye** tool to the J-group flyout. Click a red pupil and it's neutralized in one undoable step. White catchlights and the iris are left alone.

## The change

- **algo**: new `redeye` kernel. It builds a red mask inside the click window, cleans it with an erode and blur, and moves the masked pixels toward a darker, desaturated pupil. The tile halo is 5 px, which covers the full erode and blur reach.
- **engine**: new `paint.redEye` command. **Pupil Size** sets the search window, and **Darken Amount** sets how dark the pupil goes. Several clicks passed in `points` make one history step.
  - A click with no red near it returns `no red-eye pixels near the click` instead of doing nothing. A grayscale document gives the same error.
  - Empty or invalid params, more than 64 points, or a window over 512² return an error before anything is allocated.
  - The command is disabled when there's no document, the layer is pixel-locked, or the layer is a type layer.
- **ui**: Red Eye sits last in the J-group slot with its own icon. It has an options bar for Pupil Size and Darken Amount (both default to 50) and a circle cursor at the search radius. A miss shows the error in the status bar. The new strings are translated for every locale.

title: Delete with nothing selected deletes the selected layers, of any kind (#1077)
author: metzmehard
body:
Fixes #1077.

## Problem

Delete / Backspace is bound to **Edit › Clear** (`edit.clear`), which only works on pixel layers. When an adjustment, fill, type, shape or smart object layer was selected, pressing the key only showed "Clear is not available: active layer is a … layer" on the status bar. On a pixel layer with no selection, the key cleared the whole layer and kept it.

## Fix

Photoshop deletes the selected layers when you press Delete with no active selection. The shortcut dispatcher (`shortcut_dispatch::delete_key_command`) now sends Clear's key to `layer.delete` when:

- nothing is selected, and
- the composite is targeted: no single channel, no Quick Mask and no targeted layer mask.

`layer.delete` already deletes every selected layer in one undo step. Everything else still goes to Edit › Clear: a selection, a targeted mask or a targeted channel. The menu item and the `edit.clear` command, as agents and MCP see them, don't change. Only the key press is rerouted, so a rebound Clear shortcut behaves the same way.

- `delete_without_a_selection_deletes_the_selected_layer`: an adjustment layer, Delete and Backspace, from the canvas and after clicking a Layers panel row. The layer is deleted, and one ⌘Z brings it back.
- `delete_without_a_selection_deletes_every_selected_layer`: a pixel layer and an adjustment layer are selected, and both are deleted.

title: Deep layers: LayerContent::Deep renders, saves and moves; io::import_deep_exr
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What

Phase 2 of deep EXR support: the **document model keeps the depth data**. #642 added the decode (deepscanline/deeptile → structured `DeepImage`); flattened opens were the only option. This is the foundation the stacking workflow builds on — the layer kind, rendering, persistence and the import entry point.

## Change

- **`LayerContent::Deep(DeepData)`** in `photocraft-doc`: the sample channels, the per-pixel cumulative counts, and the data's canvas origin (`x`/`y`, so moving the layer is a field update).
- **`compose::deep`**: renders the layer by depth-compositing — samples stably sorted by Z (NaN last), front-to-back `over` with premultiplied colour and per-channel alpha (`AR`/`AG`/`AB` or `A`), the same math the codecs-side flatten established, but straight into the compositor's premultiplied buffers per region. - **Canvas semantics kept honest**: whole-canvas translation moves the deep origin like every other content (crop's re-origin rides along); `Image Size` **refuses** on deep documents (resampling samples silently would desync them); the GPU plan **declines** deep documents (the canvas automatically falls back to the CPU compositor, the existing path); proxies flatten once and downsample that; PSD export writes the composited pixels with a warning (PSD has no deep representation).
- **`io::import_deep_exr`**: opens a deep EXR as a document with one deep layer (`import` keeps opening them flattened).
- Layers panel: a deep kind filter and icon; new `tl!` string translated in all 12 catalogs.

title: ORF: a file cut short inside IFD0 is malformed, not the compressed variant (#1008)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #1008

## Root cause

`orf::decode` tells the undecoded compressed/packed variant apart from an uncompressed ORF by summing IFD0's `StripByteCounts` and comparing the sum with `width × height × 2`. `Tiff::tag_uints` returns an empty list when the entry is missing or unreadable, so a file whose IFD0 entry table is cut short (a partial download, a damaged card) sums to **zero** and takes the "compressed" branch:

```
unsupported camera raw: Olympus compressed (or packed) ORF is not decoded
```

The same file truncated a few bytes earlier (`ORF has no IFD0`) or later (`raw data lies outside the file`) is correctly reported as malformed, so the error class depended on where the damage landed rather than on the file's condition — and named a variant the user's camera does not produce.

## Fix

Every ORF, compressed or not, declares its strip byte counts, so missing or unreadable counts are damage: `decode` now returns `RawError::Malformed("ORF IFD0 has no readable strip byte counts")` before the compression check. Nothing else changes; a genuinely compressed ORF (counts present, below 16 bits/sample) still returns `Unsupported`, and `photocraft-io` still falls back to the embedded preview for it.

## Tests

`orf_truncated_in_ifd0_is_malformed_not_the_compressed_variant` in `crates/raw/tests/vendor_codecs.rs`: builds the crate's synthetic uncompressed ORF, cuts it right before the `StripByteCounts` entry (width, height and compression survive) and asserts `Malformed`; then checks that **no** prefix of the file reads as the compressed variant. Before the fix it fails at the first assertion with the `Unsupported` error above.

`cargo test -p photocraft-raw` (all 66 tests), `cargo clippy -p photocraft-raw --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass locally.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Surface Blur: 4x to 20x faster on 16-bit and 32-bit layers (ranked window sums)
author: tanish2k09
body:
Follow-up to #631, which made 8-bit Surface Blur fast with a sliding 256-bin histogram. 16-bit and 32-bit layers still summed the whole (2r + 1)² window for every pixel and channel: about 40,000 samples per pixel at radius 100.

## How

A histogram doesn't carry over to these depths. At the default threshold of 15, a 16-bit window spans about 9,600 levels, and floats have no levels at all. What does carry over is that the weight `w = 1 - |v - v0| / t` is **linear in v on each side of the centre value**. Over the samples within the threshold below `v0`:

- `Σw = ((t - v0)·n + Σv) / t`
- `Σv·w = ((t - v0)·Σv + Σv²) / t`

The same holds symmetrically above `v0`. So the weighted mean only needs the count, Σv and Σv² of two value ranges.

`surface_ranked` (`crates/algo/src/blur.rs`) works like this:
- It ranks each tile window's distinct values. Any depth works, including negatives and values above 1.
- A Fenwick tree over the ranks holds (count, Σv, Σv²) in f64 and slides along each row, one column out and one in per step.
- Each pixel queries the two ranges, so a pixel costs **O(r · log n) instead of O(r²)**.
- The range bounds use the direct sum's own f32 weight test, so the same samples count. Transparent pixels are skipped as before.
- Non-finite samples make it decline, and the direct sum handles them.

It's used from radius 10, where it overtakes the direct sum (measured, below). The 8-bit histogram path is unchanged and still tried first.

## Numbers (release, Windows, 32 threads)

`photocraft_algo::apply`, Surface Blur at threshold 15 on **24 MP 16-bit RGBA**. The "before" run used the same build with the new path forced off.

| radius | before | after | speed-up |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 3.14 s | 0.69 s | 4.5× |
| 25 | 18.6 s | 1.59 s | 11.7× |
| 50 | 71.6 s | 3.59 s | 20× |

That image is made of flat blocks, which keeps few distinct values. On noisy content the gain is smaller. Per 256 px tile of a smooth gradient plus noise (`surface_timing`, ignored test):…

title: Deep stacking: sample-level merge (Nuke DeepMerge) and File › Open as Deep
author: Elvis33LE
body:
> Builds on #1088 (`LayerContent::Deep`) — rebased on top of it.

## What

Deep stacking, Nuke-`DeepMerge`-style: **`DeepData::merge`** unions two deep layers into one — the union grid over both extents, every pixel holding the **concatenated sample lists** of both inputs, channels united by name (a side without a channel contributes zeros, so every channel stays aligned with the merged counts). The renderer's existing per-pixel **Z sort** then composites the whole stack, so what you see is the true depth composite of both inputs — a far sample peeks through a near translucent one *across inputs*, which per-layer flattening can never do.

Wired in:

- **Merge Down / Merge Layers** with deep inputs merge samples and **stay deep** (an all-deep selection folds into one deep layer; mixed stacks take the existing flatten path, which renders deep layers correctly).
- **File › Open as Deep…** (`file.openDeep`, paths or the picker): EXRs open through `io::import_deep_exr` as a background job (worker on native, inline on wasm) and arrive as deep layers ready to stack. Translated in every catalog.

So the workflow is: Open as Deep… ×2 → select both → Merge Layers (or Merge Down) → the canvas shows the depth-stacked result; save keeps the merged samples (.pcraft, from #1088).

## Tests

- doc: `deep_merge_unions_grids_channels_and_samples` — union grid/origin, channel union with zero-fill, counts, sample-less pixels.
- engine: `merging_deep_layers_merges_samples_and_renders_the_stack` — two offset 1×1 deep layers merge; the shared pixel holds both inputs' samples; the render shows the front sample; and with the depths swapped the same merge renders the other colour — the composite follows **Z, not layer order** (the point of deep merging).

Gates: doc 49 + engine 750 green · panic_hunt green (mergeDown behaviour changed) · ui-egui lib green except the machine-local wgpu `ctrl_f` · i18n gates green (incl. the ellipsis rule the catalogs enforce) · clippy `--no-deps` clean · fmt …

title: Autosave: a thread that fails to start is reported, not a silent no-op
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What

`Autosaver::new` discarded the thread-spawn result with `.ok()`: under thread or resource exhaustion the recovery channel pointed at a dead receiver, every queued snapshot's `send` failed silently, and `last_result` stayed `None` — **crash recovery was off while looking fully on**. A data-loss path that never touches the save pipeline the atomic-write tests cover.

## Change

The spawn failure is recorded in `last` (through a small `note` helper with the same poisoned-lock tolerance the worker path has), so `last_result()`/`flush()` report it and recovery health checks see a dead autosaver instead of assuming one.

## Tests

`a_spawn_failure_is_reported_not_silent` pins what the spawn-failure arm records.

Gates: `cargo test -p photocraft-format` all suites green · clippy `--no-deps` clean · fmt.

title: Absolute colorimetric refuses a zero or non-finite media white (#972)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #972

**Root cause.** `connection()` scales the PCS by `src.media_white() / dst.media_white()` for the absolute colorimetric intent without checking the divisor. A v4 profile whose `wtpt` tag holds zeros is parsed and stored verbatim, so the scale becomes NaN and every colour through a direct absolute transform — or a paper-simulating proof — comes out NaN.

**Fix.** The transform is refused with `CmsError::Invalid` when either media white has a zero, negative or non-finite component. The other intents never divide by the media white and are unchanged.

**Tests.** `absolute_colorimetric_refuses_a_degenerate_media_white` in `crates/cms/tests/cms.rs` builds sRGB variants with a zero, negative and non-finite `wtpt` (and confirms a parsed v4 profile keeps the zero verbatim), checks the direct absolute transform and the paper-simulating proof — including the relative-first-leg proof — are refused with a message naming the media white, and that the other intents through the same profiles still produce finite output.

**How tested.** `cargo test -p photocraft-cms` (all green), `cargo clippy -p photocraft-cms --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p photocraft-cms -- --check`.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: PSD: a spec-order mask record is not misread as Photoshop's order when that reading is implausible (#949)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #949

**Root cause.** `real_before_parameters` chose Photoshop's layout for a layer-mask record (real/user mask first, parameters after) whenever the record length happened to fit a parameter-flags byte at offset 36 — even when that byte was just part of the real mask's rectangle. A density-only record written in the spec's order then had its density byte read as the real mask's background and the parameter silently lost.

**Fix.** The decision is now a *tie-break*: when both orders fit the record length, Photoshop's reading has to be plausible (background 0 or 255, only known parameter-flag bits set) or the spec-order reading with a real mask wins. Records that only fit one order are read exactly as before, so the heuristic strictly narrows the set of records read in Photoshop's order rather than widening or shifting it.

**Tests.** `crates/psd/tests/roundtrip.rs` gains a round-trip of a density-only, spec-order mask record that previously came back with its density misread as the real mask's background, plus cases that still take the Photoshop reading when it is plausible.

**How tested.** `cargo test -p photocraft-psd`, `cargo xtask test-corpus -p photocraft-psd` (corpus test green, no regressions), `cargo clippy -p photocraft-psd --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p photocraft-psd -- --check`.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Color Lookup: keep the .cube input domain and reject the ones we cannot apply
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What

`.cube` `DOMAIN_MIN`/`DOMAIN_MAX` (and `LUT_3D_INPUT_RANGE`) were parsed and then thrown away — a log-domain or extended-range look was applied to plain 0..1 inputs, silently shifting its colours; the in-code comment admitted the assumption.

## Change

- The domain travels with the parsed `LutFile` (`domain_min`/`domain_max`), validated: every component finite and `min < max` per channel (a degenerate domain is a parse error, not a division by zero later).
- `colorLookup` **refuses a non-default domain with the reason** instead of applying it wrongly — the same unsupported-over-wrong-output call the codecs make (deep EXR before it was supported, for one). Photoshop's default 0..1 domain files are unaffected.
- Honoring a custom domain end to end means carrying it through `ColorLookup` (doc, compose, gpu, PSD round trip) — that's the open follow-up this stores the data for.

## Tests

`cube_domain_is_kept_and_validated` (cms: default parses as default, custom domain kept, degenerate rejected) and the engine-side rejection assertion in the colorLookup suite.

title: Nearest Neighbor: sample single source pixels on reductions without averaging (#1114)
author: MokuLakshithReddy
body:
Fixes #1114

### Problem
In `crates/algo/src/resample.rs:88`, the nearest-neighbor branch was guarded by:
```rust
if filter == Resample::Nearest && scale >= 1.0
```
When reducing (`scale < 1.0`), Nearest Neighbor fell through to the multi-tap filter path. With `stretch = 1.0 / scale` and `support = 0.5 * stretch`, this computed a box filter over neighboring source pixels and averaged them (e.g. turning a 1 px checkerboard into 0.5 grey).

### Solution
- Removed `&& scale >= 1.0` so `Resample::Nearest` takes the single nearest-sample branch uniformly at any scale (enlargements, 1:1, and reductions).
- Added a unit test in `crates/algo/src/resample.rs` (`nearest_neighbor_reduction_does_not_average`).
- Added an integration test in `crates/engine/src/image_cmds.rs` (`nearest_neighbor_reduction_keeps_source_values`).

title: Desktop: write log records to standard error and a rotating log file
author: switch87
body:
## Why

The desktop app never installs a logger, so the ~40 `log::warn!` / `log::error!` calls across the workspace go nowhere. That includes exactly the messages you need when something goes wrong on a user's machine:

- `gpu_startup`: *"the previous start didn't finish (GPU backend …); …"*, the decision to fall back to a safer backend

And a launch from a desktop menu, the Dock or the Start menu has no terminal at all, so even `RUST_LOG` can't help an ordinary user produce something to attach to an issue.

Installing 0.3.0 on Gentoo (KDE Plasma 6.7 Wayland, Radeon 780M, Mesa 26.1) I got a window that stayed empty. But along the way the crash guard had silently switched the app to the GL backend and persisted `performance.gpuBackend = "gl"`, and its `log::warn!` explaining why went nowhere. With this PR the first two minutes would have looked like this:

title: GPU startup: a failed CPU start no longer pins later starts to CPU
author: shovel-kun
body:
## Problem

Running on Linux under XWayland (`env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY cargo run --release -p photocraft`), every launch failed with:

```
Error: Wgpu(CustomNativeAdapterSelectionError("no graphics adapter found"))
```

`gpu-starting.json` contained `{"backend":"cpu", ...}`. A start that returns an error keeps its marker so the next start tries a safer backend (#4). But the CPU path is the end of every chain (`next_safer(Cpu, _) == Cpu`), so a failed CPU start (here: the GL adapter can't present under XWayland) left a marker that planned every later start on CPU again. It failed the same way each time. The app never recovered on its own; deleting the marker by hand fixed it, and the next start ran on Vulkan.

## Fix

`gpu_startup::keep_marker_after_error(plan, os)`: after an error, the marker is kept only when a safer backend exists. It is cleared after failed starts on CPU, under `--safe-gpu` and under `WGPU_BACKEND` (no plan reads that marker). GPU backends still move down the chain exactly as before.

## Tests

- `a_failed_start_keeps_its_marker_only_when_a_safer_backend_exists`: the predicate on every OS chain.
- `a_failed_cpu_start_does_not_pin_later_starts`: regression test; a failed CPU start's marker no longer makes the next start `cpu`.
- Manual check: I put the stuck marker back. One failing start cleared it, and the next start came up on Vulkan.
- `cargo test -p photocraft --bins gpu_startup`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

Still open (not in this PR): the CPU/GL path itself finds no surface-capable adapter under XWayland.

title: CI: Support Linux i686 builds.
author: Smu1zel
body:
## Why?
Currently, 32-bit Windows is supported, but not 32-bit Linux. Since rustc supports it (i686-unknown-linux-gnu), we might as well support it. A caveat of this target is that this will require SSE2, but it is *very* unlikely someone would have a good time running this on a Pentium III.

## How?
This is a bit tricky to implement, given that Actions gives us no 32-bit distros to use. As a workaround, use ubuntu-22.04, create a Debian 12 i386 container, and perform most of the build operations inside it. Also, refactor package.sh a bit to make this design work.

## Alternatives
We *could* just cross-compile, but once GitHub removes ubuntu-22.04 (it's already deprecated), the binary is going to get linked against whatever glibc version is in the next oldest distro, which would probably make it impossible to run for 99% of users. The glibc version in Ubuntu 26.04 is already too new for Void Linux (2.43 vs 2.41), so this sounds like the best approach to make everyone happy.

Alternatively, we could use zigbuild and manually specify a glibc version easily (but potentially risk GTK ABI drift), but let me know what you think of this first. Most tests pass (except WASM; that shouldn't be my fault), and it will likely port easily to the rest of the *Craft suite.

title: Keep the active document when closing another tab
author: CQMHV
body:
Closing a background document could activate a different tab: with A, B and C open and C active, closing A switched to B. Keep the same active document as tab indices shift; closing the active tab still selects its next neighbor, or the previous one at the end.

Adds regression coverage for all background-tab positions, active-tab fallback, the last document, invalid indices, Close Others and Close All.

- `cargo clippy --locked -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed without lint exemptions.

author: switch87

title: Place Scale Marker: fix crash on images under 8 px tall
author: alonfaraj
body:
### Bug
`Image › Analysis › Place Scale Marker` panicked on any image under 8 px tall, with default settings.
`place_scale_marker` clamps the bar height to `2.0..=h / 4.0`; below 8 px the upper bound is under 2, and `f64::clamp` panics when min > max.
On desktop the engine's last-resort guard reported "failed with an internal error" and the web build aborts.

### Fix
The upper bound no longer drops below 2 px. Images 8 px or taller get the same marker as before, shorter ones get a 2 px bar, placed partly above the canvas as short images already were.

### Test
Test `place_scale_marker_on_a_short_image_does_not_panic` (1–7 px tall) panicked before the fix.

title: Command lookup: index registered and shell command IDs
author: Elvis33LE
body:
Opening a menu or palette repeatedly resolves command IDs against the entire command list. Store the ordered specs and an ID-to-index map in one `OnceLock`, and cache the shell command IDs in `is_live` as a set. Public ordering, first-match duplicate semantics and dynamic shell routes stay the same.

Tests compare every registered ID and catalog route with the previous linear lookup, including missing IDs and duplicate registration. On an AMD Ryzen AI 7 350 (Windows, 32 GB RAM, Rust 1.99.0, normal release profile, no concurrent build), 31 samples of 100 batches of 817 registered and 100 missing IDs give p50 **0.156661 → 0.013456 ms per batch** (11.6×), p95 **0.171514 → 0.020049 ms**. The linear reference in the new binary gives p50 0.159080 ms. These numbers isolate lookup, not a complete menu frame.

Validation on the combined three-change candidate: affected engine/UI/ops/PSD suites (2004 passed), all-target clippy with warnings denied, adversarial `panic_hunt`, layering, wasm, formatting, quick performance scenarios and scorecard consistency passed. The offscreen UI snapshot was rendered and visually checked. Each PR has an independent branch based on main at `5896f0b`; GitHub CI validates this isolated change. No full-mode budget or published baseline is changed.

Related: #209, #221. This is audit item P5, not scorecard scenario P5 (visibility).

title: History: count retained tiles incrementally below the byte budget
author: Elvis33LE
body:
Each edit calls `History::trim`, which previously rebuilt a set from every retained state and every tile even when history was comfortably below its byte budget. Track retained tile references incrementally across record, eviction, undo/redo, branching, purge and clear. Check current document tiles on each trim so coalesced edits remain accounted for; walk old states only when the budget requires eviction. `pixel_bytes` uses the same retained count.

The accounting scope and eviction policy are preserved. Regression tests compare against the original full-walk oracle at 8/16/32-bit depths, including aliases, masks/channels, current-document changes, budget changes and transferred tiles of mixed lengths.

Release measurements on AMD Ryzen AI 7 350 (Windows, 32 GB RAM, Rust 1.99.0, no concurrent build): dense 6000×4000 document, 50 COW states, 150 layers sharing the initial image, 31 samples. `record + trim` p50:

| Depth | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| 8-bit | 62.0653 ms | 1.6908 ms |
| 16-bit | 62.0477 ms | 1.1895 ms |
| 32-bit | 61.9662 ms | 1.2477 ms |

`trim` alone is 62.2–62.8 → 0.375–0.377 ms p50. The one-layer fixture gives `record + trim` 0.125–0.127 → 0.0075–0.0080 ms. Document mutation/compositing are excluded; these are component timings, not full P13/P14 timings. Sampled whole-process peak working set for the layered run is effectively unchanged (554.0 → 554.2 MB).

Validation on the combined three-change candidate: affected engine/UI/ops/PSD suites (2004 passed), all-target clippy with warnings denied, adversarial `panic_hunt`, layering, wasm, formatting, quick performance scenarios and scorecard consistency passed. Each PR has an independent branch based on main at `5896f0b`; GitHub CI validates this isolated change. No full-mode budget or published baseline is changed.

Related: #209, #221, especially interactive P13/P14. This is audit item P4, not scorecard scenario P4 (blend mode). It is separate from #810's undo/redo damage tracking.

title: PSD save: stream Lr16/Lr32 layer blocks into the output
author: Elvis33LE
body:
Saving 16/32-bit PSDs materialized the Lr16/Lr32 layer payload in a temporary buffer and cloned the surrounding global tagged blocks before copying them into the final output. Write the layer payload directly into the output, patch its encoded length and borrow the neighboring blocks. This removes the temporary payload copy and the opaque-block clones while preserving insertion order and padding.

Tests compare the streamed bytes with the materialized writer for PSD/PSB, Lr16/Lr32/Layr, insertion positions and unusual padding; valid 16/32-bit files also round-trip through the parser.

Release measurements on AMD Ryzen AI 7 350 (Windows, 32 GB RAM, Rust 1.99.0, no concurrent build): `to_bytes` for prepared raw 24-MP RGB data, 11 samples after warmup, excluding compression and disk I/O:

| Depth | p50 before → after | p95 before → after |
|---|---:|---:|
| 16-bit | 75.289 → 65.623 ms | 81.218 → 67.355 ms |
| 32-bit | 164.182 → 132.118 ms | 209.660 → 139.756 ms |

The temporary payload is approximately 144/288 MB respectively. Sampled whole-process peak working set across both depths is 1444.1 → 1348.1 MB; this is not an allocation counter or a per-depth measurement. Existing P43 uses an 8-bit fixture and does not measure this path.

Validation on the combined three-change candidate: affected engine/UI/ops/PSD suites (2004 passed), all-target clippy with warnings denied, adversarial `panic_hunt`, layering, wasm, formatting, quick performance scenarios and scorecard consistency passed. Pinned real-file PSD corpora passed. Each PR has an independent branch based on main at `5896f0b`; GitHub CI validates this isolated change. No full-mode budget or published baseline is changed.

Related: #221.

title: Windows: use native bitmap cursors for brush tips
author: mrjeye
body:
On Windows, brush-tip circles and precise crosshairs currently move only when the canvas presents another frame. A user reported lag over the canvas while menus remained responsive; switching Painting Cursors to Standard restored normal responsiveness.

This change sends brush circles and crosshairs to the OS through egui's existing `CustomCursorImage` API, so their movement no longer waits for canvas rendering. A per-pass lifecycle clears stale images when leaving the canvas or changing tools and respects later widget cursor overrides. Black/white outlines retain visibility over grey, as required by #737.

Native bitmaps are used in the Windows root viewport. Other platforms and immediate viewports keep a painter fallback. Tips beyond winit's 2048 px bitmap limit retain their full software outline with a native crosshair at the hotspot. title: Design: bounded GPU stack prefix reuse for property edits
author: Elvis33LE
body: Property edits currently execute every GPU composite pass over the damage region. This design proposes root-stack checkpoints with conservative snapshot invalidation, bounded memory and unchanged fallback semantics. It covers clipping, groups, adjustments, global inputs, partial damage and encoder ownership before the implementation follow-up. Related: #209, #221. No runtime code changes.

title: Clone Stamp / Healing Brush: a far source is a bad-params error, not an out-of-bounds slice (#1111)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #1111

## Root cause

`paint.cloneStamp` / `paint.healingBrush` with a far `source` or `offset` (`[3e9, 0]`, `[2147483647, 0]`) panicked at `crates/paint/src/retouch.rs:54` (`range start index 120 out of range for slice of length 92`), surfaced by the dispatch guard as an internal error.

`Mapping::offset()` saturates its `as i32` cast and `Rect::translate` saturates each edge independently, so the sample window for a translation came back *narrower* than the stroke bounds. `clone_sample` then did `r.rect = rect`, relabelling the short buffer as full-size, and `Region::px` indexed past it. #716 fixed the rotated/scaled branch (`source_rect`); this is the pure-translation branch.

## Fix

`clone_sample` is now fallible and takes the command id. In the translation branch it checks that the translated window kept the stroke rect's size; if not, the command returns `BadParams` naming the offset, and the document and history are untouched (the error propagates out of `run_stroke`'s `edit` closure before anything is written). A source far outside the canvas but inside the i32 range still clones transparency exactly as before.

## Tests

`clone_and_heal_with_a_far_source_are_plain_errors` in `crates/engine/src/retouch_cmds/tests.rs`: both tools, the issue's inputs plus a negative far source, asserts `BadParams` (not `Other`), the layer pixel is unchanged, no history step was recorded, and that an in-range far source (`[1e6, 1e6]`, and the issue's `2147483000` case, which never saturates) keeps working. Fails on `main` with the internal error shown in the issue.

Gates: `cargo test -p photocraft-engine` (retouch + clone_source), `clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, `fmt --check`, and `panic_hunt --ignored` all green.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: A non-Unicode command-line argument is a usage error, not a startup panic (#1108)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #1108

## Root cause

`apps/photocraft-cli/src/main.rs` and `apps/photocraft/src/main.rs` both read `std::env::args()`, which panics on an argument that is not valid Unicode. `photocraft-cli info $'caf\xe9.png'` died in `library/std/src/env.rs` with exit 101 before printing anything, and a file manager handing the desktop app a Latin-1 file name would do the same before any window opened.

## Fix

- **CLI:** new `photocraft_cli::run_os(&[OsString], ..)` converts each argument and turns a failure into a usage error naming the argument's position and a lossy rendering (exit 2, with the usage text), the same shape as an unknown flag. `main` calls it; `run(&[String])` is unchanged for in-process callers.
- **Desktop:** the argument loop matches on `OsStr::to_str`. Flag values that are paths (`--control-token-file`, `--automation-read-root`, `--automation-write-root`) become `PathBuf`s straight from the `OsString`, so they now work with any file name; a non-Unicode `--control-token` is reported as a control-argument error like a bad `--control` port (#701); non-Unicode *file* arguments are collected and shown in an error notice ("Could not open … the path is not valid Unicode") once the app is up, so the launch itself still succeeds.

## Tests

`a_non_unicode_argument_is_a_usage_error_not_a_panic` (`apps/photocraft-cli/tests/cli.rs`, unix): runs the binary with a `caf\xe9.png` argument for `info` and `convert`, asserts exit 2, the message, and no panic output. Panicked with exit 101 on `main`.

Gates: `cargo test -p photocraft-cli`, `clippy -p photocraft-cli -p photocraft --all-targets -D warnings`, `fmt --check` green.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: GPU composite: reuse unchanged lower-stack chunks for property edits
author: Elvis33LE
body:
Property edits currently execute the entire GPU stack over every damaged chunk, even when lower layers are unchanged. Reuse one bounded lower-stack composite: the planner records boundaries after complete root-level units, including clipped layers, and the renderer restores cached chunks before executing the suffix. This follows the separate design in #1164.

Invalidation compares complete COW layer snapshots and every non-layer document field, covering masks, nested groups, adjustments, patterns, profiles and global light. Slot/pass offsets and occlusion pruning must still match. Edits below the checkpoint discard all its chunks and adapt to an earlier boundary. Planning and support checks still run; existing unsupported features such as Blend-If continue to use the CPU path. Caller-owned encode cannot establish or consume checkpoints because its submission is not guaranteed.

The checkpoint is capped at 512 MiB, reserved from the existing combined cache allowance rather than added to the total budget. Admission stops when full. Budget shrink/zero, document closure, texture-limit changes and failed renders release it. GPU memory reporting includes its chunks. GpuCanvas preserves the diagnostic cache-budget override when updating the overall memory budget.

Measured on Windows / AMD Radeon 860M / Ryzen AI 7 350 / Rust 1.99, release, no concurrent builds. bench_stack_reuse synchronizes each GPU render of twelve dense raster layers at 6000x4000; these component timings exclude the display/mipmap sink. Eleven warm opacity edits, same binary with cache budget 0 or 512 MiB:

| Depth | Top-layer p50, off → on | Middle-layer p50, off → on |
|---|---:|---:|
| 8-bit | 229.3 → 31.2 ms | 177.9 → 109.5 ms |
| 16-bit | 228.4 → 25.5 ms | 179.2 → 113.7 ms |
| 32f | 186.2 → 26.4 ms | 187.4 → 121.1 ms |

Each cached run held 384 MB and reused 24 chunks. Top-layer renders skipped 552 planned prefix passes per frame; middle-layer renders skipped 264. The first middle-layer edit still …

title: Fix transform cancellation undoing the wrong document
author: CQMHV
body:
Switching documents during Free Transform on a copy or a dropped file could undo the newly selected document's last edit and erase its redo history, while leaving the created layer in the original document.

Cancel using the preview's stable document ID, then restore the selected tab. Check document identity before cleanup or commit, including documents that share layer IDs. Roll back only the layer's creation step, preserving history when the source is closed, the copy was already undone, or a later edit exists.

Fixes #1099.

Validation (Windows, Rust 1.99.0):
- `cargo +1.99.0 test -p photocraft-ui-egui --locked`: 892 passed, 3 existing ignored (831 unit tests and 61 integration tests).
- `cargo +1.99.0 clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo +1.99.0 xtask layers` and `cargo +1.99.0 xtask wasm`: passed.
- `cargo +1.99.0 fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Before/after offscreen snapshots inspected.

The complete test run used `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 RUST_TEST_THREADS=2` after the initial parallel build exhausted local memory. The PR was created as a draft before any tests ran. Final duplicate checks covered all 133 open PRs (including drafts), related PRs in all states, and the #1099 timeline; no equivalent fix was found.

The five new regressions fail against the unchanged production code on main at `5896f0b`: copying across documents, closing the source, an already undone copy, a subsequent edit, and an actual canvas drop. The switching-copy test also covers reordered tabs and cancel/frame-cleanup/commit entry points.

Offscreen snapshots use identical synthetic rectangles. Before, switching from A's copy transform to B removes B's blue fill and leaves A's copy; after, B's fill remains and A's copy is removed.

title: Color Lookup: install LUT packs once, browse them in one list
author: Jeremy8776
body:
## What

Color Lookup could only load one LUT at a time by typing its path. This adds a **LUT library**: install a folder (or `.zip`) of LUTs once as a *pack*, then pick from them in the existing **3D LUT File** control. A pack is just a folder of `.cube` / `.3dl` / `.look` files.

![Color Lookup in the Properties panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jeremy8776/photocraft/f55ace98c8132c237b17b937b41989928e2e44af/lut-properties.png)

*Synthetic demo looks; nothing third-party. Rendered offscreen with the `snapshot` example.*

## The control

The dropdown is replaced by one list, not a section added beside it:

- None, Favorites, Recent, Built-in and every pack are collapsible sections; folders inside a pack are nested sections. Rows show the file name only; a long name ends in an ellipsis and the tooltip has the path, type, size and title.
- The list fills the Properties group: it measures what the editor draws below it, so it follows the group's height without leaving dead space.
- **Up / Down** move through the LUTs and scroll to follow, **Enter** applies. Moving (or resting the pointer on a row) **previews on the canvas with no history entry**; a click or Enter applies it once through Color Lookup's existing `file` param, so the table is embedded in the document and documents never depend on the library.
- **Install Pack...** picks a folder; a folder or `.zip` dropped on the window installs too. Files added to the library by hand show up within a couple of seconds.
- Star a LUT to keep it under Favorites; the last 12 used are under Recent. **Remove Pack** (hover the header, click twice).
- A pack whose LUTs are all already in another pack is marked *Duplicate of ...*. Installing skips LUTs whose content (blake3) is already installed and reports them, so installing a folder and then its parent no longer stores everything twice. `allowDuplicates` overrides.
