title: Refuse to save a .pcraft holding a NaN or infinite float, instead of writing one that never opens again (#1101)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #1101

## Root cause

`PcraftWriter::prepare` serialises the manifest with `serde_json::to_vec_pretty`, which writes a non-finite `f32`/`f64` as `null`. The manifest's float fields are not `Option`, so `null` fails to deserialise. A document that picked up a NaN or infinity (a PSD `expA` block, a descriptor double) therefore saved and autosaved with a success report, and every later open failed with `manifest JSON: invalid type: null, expected f32`.

## Fix

JSON has no spelling for these values, so the save is refused rather than writing a file that can never be read back:

- `crates/format/src/finite.rs`: `finite::check` walks the manifest with a `serde::Serializer` that produces no output and fails on the first non-finite float. It tracks struct fields, sequence indices, enum variants and map keys, so the error names the value (e.g. `document.layers[2].content.adjustment.exposure`).
- `PcraftWriter::prepare` runs it before serialising, so the one-shot, incremental, directory-bundle and autosave paths all share the gate.
- New `FormatError::NonFinite { path }`: "`…` is NaN or infinite, which a .pcraft manifest cannot hold; reset that value and save again".

The manifest is small next to the tiles, so the extra walk is negligible. Sanitising the known PSD import sources is a separate follow-up; this closes the "saved fine, cannot reopen" hole for every source.

## Tests

- Unit: `finite_values_pass_and_each_position_is_named` — finite data passes; a NaN/∞ in a field, a nested `Vec`, a struct variant, a tuple variant and a map each report the expected path.
- Integration (`crates/format/tests/roundtrip.rs`): `a_non_finite_float_is_refused_at_save_rather_than_breaking_every_later_load` — NaN and −∞ in an Exposure adjustment and +∞ in `resolution_dpi` are refused with `FormatError::NonFinite` naming the field, through both `save_to_bytes` and `PcraftWriter::save_zip`; the same document with finite values round-trips unchanged. The Exposure case is the issue's re…

title: PSD notes: an icon position near i32::MAX saturates on save instead of overflowing (#939)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #939

## Root cause

`write_note` (`crates/io/src/annotations_map.rs`) built the note's icon rectangle as `[y, x, y + 20, x + 16]` with plain `i32` arithmetic on a position that comes straight from the file's `Anno` block (or from `notes.set`). For a stored icon top at or above `i32::MAX - 19` that overflowed on *every* PSD save — `export_blocks` regenerates the comparison block before it decides whether the stored one can be kept verbatim — as a panic in debug (surfaced by `file.saveACopy` as an internal error, no file written) and a wrapped bottom edge in release.

## Fix

The far edge uses `saturating_add`, matching the `as i32` cast that already saturates the origin, so the written rectangle is always representable and the note survives a round trip at its stored position. The popup path already went through `f64` and a saturating cast and needed nothing. No signature change: `write_note` stays infallible, and unchanged notes still compare byte-exact (the existing verbatim-preservation tests are untouched).

## Tests

`a_note_icon_near_i32_max_saves_with_representable_geometry` (`crates/io/tests/annotations.rs`): builds the issue's `Anno` fixture at `i32::MAX - 5` (plus a far-left and an `i32::MIN` variant), imports, exports, asserts the written icon rectangle is `[top, left, top ⊕ 20, left ⊕ 16]`, and re-imports the note at its position with its text; also covers a model position beyond `i32` and NaN, and the ordinary `[42, 28]` control. Panicked at `annotations_map.rs:183` with `attempt to add with overflow` on `main`.

Gates: `cargo test -p photocraft-io --test annotations`, `clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, `fmt --check`, and `cargo xtask test-corpus -p photocraft-io` (full corpus suite, 0 failures) green.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Fix: Resolve issue where various file formats save incorectly as a `.psd`
author: Cyanoxide
body:
### What
Several save dialogs added an extra extension to the file name when the file type wasn't in the save panel's list of types. For example, `Export As` saved `.webp` files as `.webp.psd` ([Resolved here](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/724)), and `Save for Web (Legacy)` saved `.gif` files as `.gif.psd`. Flagged by @tanish2k09.

This PR refactors [my previous webp fix](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/724) to apply to all save dialogs, so files save with the extension you chose, where possible.

### Problem
`SAVE_FILTERS` only lists a few file types (PSD, PCraft, PNG, JPEG, WebP, TIFF, Targa, OpenEXR). When the suggested name's extension isn't in that list, `Photoshop` stays selected as the first type, and the save panel adds `.psd` to the name. The same happens with extensions the list spells differently, so `.jpeg` became `.jpeg.jpg` and `.tiff` became `.tiff.tif`.

`Save As` also always suggested the opened file's name, even for formats PhotoCraft can't write, like `.dng`.

### Resolution
`save_filters` now puts the suggested name's file type first. If that type isn't in `SAVE_FILTERS`, it adds a new one for it at the top (for example `.gif`, `.csv` or `.pcpresets`).

`Save As` keeps the opened file's name only if it can write that format. Otherwise it suggests `.psd` (`cat.dng` > `cat.psd`, not `cat.dng.psd`), and you can still choose something else.

I tested every save dialog, both before and after the change. Here are the outliers and the corrections this PR applies:

- `Save As` on an opened `.gif`: `*.gif.psd` > `*.gif`
- `Save As` on an opened `.bmp`: `*.bmp.psd` > `*.bmp`
- `Save As` on an opened `.jpeg`: `*.jpeg.jpg` > `*.jpeg`
- `Save As` on an opened `.tiff`: `*.tiff.tif` > `*.tiff`
- `Quick Export` as `.gif`: `*.gif.psd` > `*.gif`
- `Save for Web (Legacy)` as `.gif`: `*.gif.psd` > `*.gif`
- `Save for Web (Legacy)` as `.wbmp`: `*.wbmp.psd` > `*.wbmp`
- `Export Presets`: `*.pcpresets.psd` > `*.pcpresets`
- `Measurement Log`…

title: channel.merge: reject a repeated source index instead of closing an unrelated document
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #934

## Root cause
`channel.merge` parses `documents` with a range check only. It closes the sources afterwards by sorting the list and calling `Session::close` on each index in reverse, and `close` removes by *current* index. With `documents: [0, 0, 1]` every validation passed (the repeat counts as a plane), then the close loop ran `close(1)`, `close(0)`, `close(0)` — and the last call removed the document that had shifted into index 0, one that was never named as a source, taking its unsaved edits and undo history with it while the command reported success.

## Fix
Repeated indices are rejected as bad params (`document N is listed more than once`) before any plane is built or anything is closed. The first-source lookup also goes through `get()` instead of indexing the document list.

## Tests
`merge_rejects_a_repeated_source_and_keeps_unrelated_documents` in `crates/engine/src/channel_cmds/tests.rs`: splits a document, adds an unrelated edited RGB document, runs the repro and asserts the error, that the document set is unchanged, that the unrelated document still undoes, and that a well-formed `[0, 1, 2]` merge still closes exactly the named sources. Fails on `main` (the merge succeeds and the unrelated document is gone), passes with the fix. `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib channel_cmds` (29 tests) and `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` are green.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Fit Artboard on Screen: no i32 overflow for a board with large coordinates
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #981

## Root cause
`fit_artboard` (`crates/ui-egui/src/artboard_ui.rs`) computed the view centre as `(b.x0 + b.x1) as f32 / 2.0` with unchecked i32 addition. A board near ±2^30 on either axis, or one whose far edge `Rect::from_xywh` saturated at `i32::MAX` (`x = 2147483600`, width 1000), overflows the sum: `attempt to add with overflow` in test/debug builds, escaping the control handler because shell view commands sit outside the engine's dispatch guard; a wrapped, wrongly placed centre in release.

The same repro exposed a second overflow in the engine: `layer.new.artboard`'s default placement computes `right + GAP` from the rightmost board's `x1`, which may already be `i32::MAX`, so any further `layer.new.artboard` on that document panicked inside `run` (Rule 9).

## Fix
- The midpoint is computed in `f64` and rounded to the `f32` the view stores, so every board's true centre is used and nothing wraps.
- The default placement uses `saturating_add(GAP)`. When that base saturates to a zero-width rectangle, `rect_param` now returns its existing "size must be positive" error instead of the command panicking.

## Tests
- `fit_artboard_centres_a_board_with_large_coordinates` (`crates/ui-egui/src/artboard_ui.rs`): all three boards from the issue, through `ui.menu.invoke` → `view.fitArtboardOnScreen`, asserting the centre equals the true midpoint rounded to f32. Panics with `attempt to add with overflow` on `main`, passes with the fix.
- `new_artboard_next_to_a_board_at_the_i32_edge` (`crates/engine/src/artboard_cmds/tests.rs`): a board at the saturated edge followed by `layer.new.artboard {}` (clean `Err`) and a keyed board (`Ok`). Panics on `main`, passes with the fix.
- The existing `fit_artboard_and_menu_items` control (`[200,0,50,20]` → centre `[225,10]`) still passes. `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are green.

title: filter.cameraRaw: refuse an area too large to develop instead of overflowing
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #962

## Root cause
`rgba_region` (`crates/engine/src/lens_cmds.rs`) sized its working buffer with `area.width() * area.height()` in `u32`. A legal 65536×65536 canvas (`file.new` / `image.canvasSize` allow sides up to 300000 with no aggregate cap) is exactly 2^32 pixels, so the product overflowed: `attempt to multiply with overflow` inside the command's `run` in overflow-checked builds (dispatch reported an internal error), and in release the product wraps to 0 and the first tile read indexes past the empty buffer.

## Fix
- `filter.cameraRaw` checks the area it is about to develop (canvas ∪ the target layer's content bounds) against a new `MAX_RAW_PIXELS` (400 MP; the pipeline holds ≥ 48 bytes per pixel) before anything runs, and returns a bad-params error naming the size and the limit. Identity settings still take their shortcut.
- `camera_raw_surface` carries the same guard (an oversized area is returned unchanged), so the Camera Raw preview and the Smart Filter re-apply path, which call it directly, cannot overflow either. The buffer length is computed in `u64`.

## Tests
`camera_raw_rejects_an_area_too_large_to_develop` in `crates/engine/src/lens_cmds.rs`: the issue's exact repro (8×8 transparent → canvas 65536×65536 → `exposure: 1`) must return `EngineError::BadParams` mentioning "too large"; a direct `camera_raw_surface` call over a 65536×65536 area returns the surface untouched; a normal document still develops. Panics with `attempt to multiply with overflow` on `main`, passes with the fix. `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib lens_cmds` (6 tests) and `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` are green.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: image.analysis.recordMeasurements: refuse an area too large to measure instead of overflowing
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #933

## Root cause
With no selection, `selection_rows` measures the whole document, and `selection_mask` sized its coverage mask with `r.width() * r.height()` in `u32` (`crates/engine/src/analysis_cmds.rs`). A legal 65536×65536 document (`file.new` caps each side at 300000, not the product) is exactly 2^32 pixels, so the multiply overflowed inside the command's `run`; dispatch's guard turned the panic into an internal error. In release the product wraps to 0: the mask is empty, `gray_image` still renders the full region (~64 GiB of f32 RGBA), and `measure_features` then indexes past the empty mask. The label counter was also incremented before the rows were computed, so the failed call consumed "Measurement 1".

## Fix
- `selection_rows` computes the pixel count in `u64` before anything is allocated and refuses more than `MAX_MEASURE_PIXELS` (400 MP; the gray render alone is 16 bytes per pixel) with an `Err` that names the size and the limit and says to select a smaller region. The mask is sized from that checked count.
- `next_measurement` is bumped only after the rows exist, so a failed measurement does not skip a label.

## Tests
`record_measurements_refuses_an_area_too_large_to_measure` in `crates/engine/src/analysis_cmds/tests.rs`: the issue's repro (65536×65536 transparent document, `source: "selection"`) returns the "too large to measure" error with an empty log, and the next measurement on a normal document is still labelled "Measurement 1" with the right area. Panics with `attempt to multiply with overflow` on `main`, passes with the fix. `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib analysis_cmds` (12 tests) and `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` are green.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: PSD plane shuffles in bands; the document histogram computes off the UI thread
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What

Two audit perf points (the third, a backdrop-snapshot pool, was implemented, **measured, and withdrawn** — see the end).

### 1. PSD plane shuffles in bands (io)

`interleave`/`deinterleave` walked every pixel of a 20 MP image on one thread during PSD open and save, while the file's own U8 fast path already went through `par_map`. Both now split the rows into one band per core (`pixels::bands`) and merge the band results in order:

| 20 MP, release (i7-class Windows laptop) | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| interleave RGB u16 | 152.0 ms | **101 ms (1.5×)** |
| deinterleave RGB u16 | 461.2 ms | **160 ms (2.9×)** |
| interleave RGBA f32 | 328.7 ms | 220 ms (1.5×) |
| deinterleave RGBA f32 | 730.2 ms | 396 ms (1.8×) |

`--serial`/default modes of the included `bench_shuffles` example measure both paths in one binary. First cut used `concat()`-style merging and measured *slower* than serial (thread-per-band + full-buffer copies); writing bands into a preallocated output / pre-grown planes is what actually wins.

**Test:** `banded_shuffles_match_a_sequential_reference` — odd pixel counts crossing band boundaries, all depths, a missing plane (fill path), inverted channels, against an inline sequential reference.

### 2. Histogram off the UI thread (ui-egui)

The Histogram panel computed its payload **inline in the frame** every 250 ms while stale — measured **41.5 ms UI-thread stall on a 24 MP document** (`histogram_payload_cost_is_the_frame_stall_we_removed` prints the number), on top of brush work. `compute_histograms` now runs on a named worker thread; the panel keeps showing the previous histogram with the existing "cached data" warning until the result lands, repaints on delivery, and a stale result cannot overwrite a newer revision.

**Test:** `panel_histogram_is_computed_off_the_ui_thread` drives one egui frame and asserts the job is scheduled for the right document/revision, delivers off thread, and respects revisions.

title: Paint Bucket and Gradient keep alpha on a transparency-locked layer (#1104)
author: prekabreki
body:
Fixes #1104

### Problem
`paint.bucket` and `paint.gradient` did `let (surf, _) = target_surface(...)`, discarding the transparency-lock flag, and the algo functions they call (`bucket_fill`, `bucket_fill_src`, `paint_gradient`) hard-coded `false` into `composite_area`, which already supports locking alpha. On a transparency-locked layer, transparent pixels became opaque.

### Solution
- `photocraft-algo`: `paint_gradient`, `bucket_fill` and `bucket_fill_src` take a `lock_transparency: bool` and pass it to `composite_area` instead of `false`. No other callers in the workspace.
- `paint_cmds.rs`: pass the lock flag from `target_surface` (true only for a layer's pixels, so masks and channels are unaffected).
- `crates/engine/tests/fill_lock_transparency.rs`: both tools leave transparent pixels transparent and still paint the opaque ones. Both failed before the fix.

### Checks
`cargo test -p photocraft-algo -p photocraft-engine`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo xtask wasm`.

title: Clear, Cut and Image › Adjustments refuse a pixel-locked layer (#1103)
author: prekabreki
body:
Fixes #1103

### Problem
`edit_cmds::clear_area` (Clear, Cut, Layer via Cut), `commands::destructive_adjust` (Image › Adjustments) and `edit_cmds::auto_adjust` (Auto Tone / Contrast / Color) called `surface_mut()` directly, with no lock check, so they rewrote pixel-locked layers.

### Solution
The three call sites now get the surface from `commands::paint_surface(doc, id, &Value::Null)`, the helper the paint tools already use. It refuses a pixel- or fully-locked layer with "Could not complete your request because the layer "…" is locked". `Session::edit` discards the change on error. Mask and channel targets in `destructive_adjust` are untouched (Photoshop lets you edit a locked layer's mask).

`crates/engine/tests/pixel_lock_edits.rs`: each command is refused and the pixels are unchanged, and unlocking makes them work again. It failed before the fix.

### Checks
`cargo test -p photocraft-engine`, `panic_hunt -- --ignored`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Filters respect layer locks; render filters and Fill Path refuse a pixel-locked layer (#1102)
author: prekabreki
body:
Fixes #1102

### Problem
Filters never consulted layer locks. Pixel- and fully locked layers were rewritten, and on a transparency-locked layer a blur changed alpha. Flame / Tree / Picture Frame (`render_cmds.rs`) and `path.fill` (`vector_cmds.rs`) also drew on pixel-locked layers.

### Solution
- `filters::run_filter` checks `effective_locks` (so a locked parent group counts) before it touches the layer. It refuses a pixel- or fully locked layer with the paint tools' message "Could not complete your request because the layer "…" is locked". Channel, Quick Mask and mask targets still filter as before.
- With transparency locked, `run_filter` puts the layer's alpha back afterwards, only in the tiles the filter changed. This is the same tile walk as `channel_cmds::restrict_to_color`.
- Flame / Tree / Picture Frame get the surface through `commands::paint_surface`, which already refuses locked layers. `path.fill` adds the same pixel-lock check and keeps its own "needs a pixel layer" message.

`crates/engine/tests/filter_locked.rs` covers:
- pixel and all locks refuse Gaussian Blur, and the pixels stay unchanged
- Tree, Picture Frame and Fill Path refuse a pixel-locked layer
- a transparency-locked blur keeps alpha at the stroke edge and doesn't spread into transparent pixels
- an unlocked layer still filters

Everything except the unlocked case failed before the fix.

### Not in this PR
- The Filter menu isn't greyed out on a locked layer (`has_filterable_layer`). The command refuses with a message instead. Relight already greys out via `relight_enabled`.

### Checks
`cargo test -p photocraft-engine`, `panic_hunt -- --ignored`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p photocraft-engine`.

title: Add optional local models for subject matting and object selection
author: mighty-programmer
body:
PhotoCraft uses Classical segmentation for Select Subject, Object Selection and Remove Background. This adds optional on-device CPU methods: **BiRefNet HR Matting** for subject alpha/background removal and **SAM 2.1 Large** for box object selection. `local-ml` is off by default; users explicitly download and select each model. No account, generative feature or learned weight is included.

Related to the local-models portion of #219. The smart-features scorecard remains **partial**; web inference and representative alpha-matting evaluation remain open.

## Behavior and boundaries

- Native L4 `photocraft-ml` backend, pinned ONNX Runtime, engine background jobs and the existing selection/removal commands. Default and wasm builds retain Classical and omit the native runtime.

- CMS converts inference input to sRGB. Source pixels, bit depth, colour model, selection modes, locks, cancellation and one-step Undo/Redo remain intact. Recorded actions pin their method. Trusted CLI/batch use requires an explicit model-cache capability; untrusted MCP gains no filesystem access.
- `.github/workflows/local-models.yml` is **manual-only** (`workflow_dispatch`). Its optional three-platform matrix is never triggered by pushes or PRs.
- All 20 complete language catalogs contain the 18 model labels, including the newly added Hungarian, Serbian, Turkish and Vietnamese catalogs. The runtime coverage regression passes. Current upstream appearance, preferences, selection behavior and every other contributor's credit are preserved.

title: Toolbar: the header chevron switches between one and two columns (#1197)
author: prekabreki
body:
Fixes #1197

### Problem
In the Pro theme the toolbar header draws Photoshop's `»` chevron, but it was allocated with `Sense::hover()` and only painted (`panels.rs:66-69`), so clicking it did nothing. The column count came only from `toolbar_needs_double` (window height).

### Solution
- `state::Panels` gets `toolbar_double: bool` (`#[serde(default)]`, so older state and workspace files load as before).
- The chevron takes clicks and toggles that flag. The toolbar is two columns when the flag is on **or** when one column doesn't fit, so the automatic behaviour is unchanged. The chevron shows `«` while two columns are shown. It reuses the already-translated "Toolbar" string as its accessible label, so there are no new translation strings.
- `panels::toolbar_tests::header_chevron_toggles_two_columns` (kittest) clicks it twice and checks the flag and the toolbar width. It fails with the old hover-only sense.
- In the Pro theme the two columns now flow across tool groups. Rows were cut per group, so groups with an odd number of tools left half-empty rows next to Move and the Eyedropper. Pro draws no dividers between groups. The other themes keep per-group rows between their dividers.

Checked in the release app over the control channel: Pro theme, `ui.click` on the chevron → two columns, click again → one column (screenshots of each).

### Not in this PR
- The non-Pro themes still don't draw the chevron.
- When one column doesn't fit, two columns are forced and the click has no visible effect.

author: XusBadia
body:
## What

The macOS DMG opened as a plain white Finder window. It now opens like this:

![PhotoCraft DMG window in Finder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XusBadia/photocraft/dmg-preview/finder.png)

The icon's figure as a cover on the PhotoCraft colour field, PhotoCraft.app and the `Applications` link side by side on Paper, and a small PhotoCraft-specific touch: the arrow and the mono line under the title come from the app's craft. Ink, Paper and the app colour only; Inter and JetBrains Mono.

## How

Same approach as VectorCraft's, which has landed (storytold/vectorcraft#493):

- `packaging/macos/dmg/background.svg`: the source. Its text is outlined, so rendering it needs no fonts, and the figure is an `<image>` of the existing icon in `assets/app-icon/`.
- `background.tiff`: 1x 660×400 + 2x 1320×800 in one HiDPI TIFF (Deflate, sRGB; ~1 MB).
- `dmg-layout.DS_Store`: Finder's view settings (window 660×400 content, icon size 128, PhotoCraft.app at (326, 205), Applications at (574, 205), the background). It's named so it isn't mistaken for, or ignored like, a Finder-generated `.DS_Store`.

title: Find host CJK fonts inside Flatpak

title: fix(ui): make Auto scaling follow desktop DPI
author: ghreprimand
body:
On a 4K monitor configured for 125% or 166.7% desktop scaling, **UI Scale → Auto** currently raises PhotoCraft to at least 200%. This makes controls larger than the user’s chosen desktop scale, even though egui already provides the native scale.

Auto now uses that native desktop/browser scale directly, independent of resolution. Moving between monitors follows the new monitor’s scale. Explicit percentage choices remain absolute overrides, and missing/invalid native scales still fall back to 100%. The UI design documentation now describes this behavior.

- `cargo test --locked -p photocraft-ui-egui`: **888 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored**.

- Native Linux/Wayland release build verified on actual 3840×2160/125% and 3840×2560/166.7% monitors: the control channel reported **1.25** and **1.6666666** pixels per point after moving the window between them. The installed v0.3.0 AppImage reported **2.0** with Auto.

author: bani4kaskashka
body:
**What.** In Photoshop, holding Alt (Option) while dragging a layer in the Layers panel drops a copy at the new spot and leaves the original where it was. - `panels.rs::layer_drag_and_drop` reads Alt on release and passes it as `copy`. While a row is dragged with Alt held, the cursor is egui's `Copy` icon.

**Not in this PR.** A row drag (move or copy) still carries only the dragged layer, not the whole layer selection. Photoshop moves or copies every selected layer; the footer drop here already does. Left for a follow-up so this stays small.

title: Startup: preserve the GPU backend after windowing errors
author: liowald
body:
A Linux launch with `DISPLAY`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, and `WAYLAND_SOCKET` absent exits with a windowing error before graphics initialization, but leaves `gpu-starting.json`. The next launch treats that as a GPU crash and can unnecessarily switch from Vulkan to GL and remember the fallback.

Classify the returned error before retaining the marker. Windowing and app setup failures clear the current attempt's marker, restoring genuine crash evidence from any earlier launch. Renderer errors and unhandled driver crashes retain their recovery behavior.

Two Linux subprocess regressions exercise the actual desktop executable with isolated configuration: a clean failed launch leaves no marker or preference changes; a failed launch after an existing Vulkan crash preserves that original marker. Both failed before their fixes. A marker lifecycle test covers successful starts, app errors, and renderer errors.

Related to #1145, which addresses repeated failure at the end of the CPU fallback chain. This handles a separate case: windowing failures that supply no GPU crash evidence, including preservation of a prior crash marker.

Validation on Linux (dependency optimization overridden to zero for the first two commands):

- `cargo test -p photocraft --config 'profile.dev.package."*".opt-level=0'`: 61 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft --all-targets --config 'profile.dev.package."*".opt-level=0' -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask layers`, formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent final review: no actionable findings.

Native macOS and Windows launches were not exercised locally.

title: PSD export parallel layer channels; shared proxy cache; banded CMYK export
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What

Three audit perf points: two landed with before/after numbers, one implemented, **measured and withdrawn**.

### 1. PSD export: channel encodings precomputed in parallel over layers

`emit` previously processed layers strictly in turn — the parallelism only covered the ≤5 channels *inside* one layer, so a 150-layer file waited for each layer's compression before starting the next. Now every pixel-bearing layer's heavy path (surface → interleaved → planes → encoded channels) is precomputed in parallel **over the layers** before `record` runs; ids are assigned in emit order first so `record` finds its entry by the same id, and output stays **byte-identical** (the round-trip suite pins it).

**document_to_psd, 120 layers × 2000×1500, release:** **3961 → 2035 ms (1.95×)**; output 18 623 174 bytes identical on both sides (`bench_layer_export` example).

### 2. Shared proxy cache for thumbnails (compose + ui-egui)

Navigator, channel thumbnails and the histogram worker each built their own reduced proxy document (full clone + per-layer downsamples, calling thread) when the same snapshot burst through the panels. `compose::proxy` now has a bounded two-slot cache (`proxy_document_arc`), keyed by the snapshot `Arc`'s address with the entry pinning that Arc (address reuse under a live entry is impossible → exact key). `thumbnail_buffer_arc`/`compute_histograms` take the `Arc`; the histogram's layer isolation happens on the cached proxy copy, keeping all previous results byte-identical (histogram tests pin them). Memory note: an entry pins its snapshot while cached (two slots, replaced on the next revision burst).

### 3. CMYK → sRGB flat export in row bands

`cmyk_image_to_srgb` materialized three full-size f32 buffers (~1.4 GB churn at 36 MP). The transform walks plain strided slices, so the image now passes through in row bands (~32 MB budget): the peak transient drops by two document sizes, converted pixels unchanged (colour-managed test).

### Withdrawn: parallel…

title: Add full Type Color Picker and screen eyedropper with magnification
author: abc2cb
body:
The Type options bar and Character panel currently open a compact color popup, and color-selection panels cannot sample another application. This change opens the existing full Color Picker for text and adds a shared **Pick screen color** action to full dialogs and compact popups.

Related to #1128.

### Behavior

- Text color targets the selected characters, or the active text layer when no characters are selected. OK uses the existing `type.setStyle` command; Cancel leaves the text and history unchanged. Foreground color remains independent.
- Native screen sampling on X11, Windows and macOS uses a snapshot with an 11 × 11 pixel loupe, 4×–24× wheel magnification, a center-pixel outline and a hex readout. Click selects; Escape cancels.
- Full dialogs preview the sampled color before OK. Compact popups keep their immediate-edit behavior, preserving alpha/additive blending and float RGB precision.
- Cancellation, changed editing targets, invalid capture data and stale worker results are handled without applying a color to another target. Snapshots stay in memory and are released after sampling.

### Platforms and limits

The UI is shared Rust. X11 uses a native X11 client, Windows uses safe native capture bindings, and macOS uses safe CoreGraphics bindings while preserving the macOS 11 deployment target. Wayland delegates to the XDG color portal; supported browsers use the standard EyeDropper API. Portal/browser magnification is controlled by those implementations.

Screen capture is bounded to 64 × 1024 × 1024 pixels (about 67 MP) across 16 displays and the GPU texture-size limit; this does not limit documents. Published X11 primary-display and macOS snapshot ICC profiles are converted through PhotoCraft CMS; unavailable profiles and Windows captures use an sRGB fallback. HDR/mixed-monitor color accuracy and current macOS permissions need manual platform validation.

title: Select › Color Range: Photoshop's Sampled Colors model, Subtract from Sample and the eyedropper on the image
author: Unemars
body:
**Cause.** Select › Color Range compared colours in a way that doesn't match Photoshop, so the same sample and Fuzziness selected visibly different areas (on a test photo at Fuzziness 80, sampling skin also took a yellow background and foliage). The dialog's eyedroppers only worked on its small preview, not on the image.

**How Photoshop's model was found.** Black-box, clean-room: Photoshop 25.4 was driven by ExtendScript and by real clicks in its dialog, and its masks were read back as numbers (RAW export) for synthetic stripes, Lab grids and photos. No Photoshop code or assets were looked at. What the masks show:
- Samples make a Lab box (per-axis min/max). A pixel's distance to the box is the largest of ΔL·2.55, 3·Δa and 3·Δb (outside the box; 0 inside).
- The mask is a quadratic B-spline falloff: `P(t) = 1 − 2t²` for `t ≤ ½`, `2(1 − t)²` for `t < 1`, else 0, with `t = d / (Fuzziness·256/255)`; coverage = `min(255, floor(256·P))`.
- 8-bit documents compare on the 8-bit Lab grid. One a/b step above the box counts +0.5, one below −0.5, an exact match 0.
- Subtract from Sample reshapes the box per axis in steps of a fifth of the falloff width (L: F/2.55, a/b: F·256/255/3), and the order of + and − clicks matters.
- The eyedropper takes a single pixel (Point Sample).

**Fix.**
- `photocraft_algo::selection`: `LabRange` (`spanning`, `grow`, `subtract`), `lab_range_coverage[_8bit]`, `color_range_lab` (rows in parallel, Localized Color Clusters falloff kept).
- `select.colorRange` (Sampled Colors): samples converted to Lab through the document's profile (`photocraft-cms`), with an optional `order` param (`["+","-",…]`) for the click order. Without `order`, all additions come first, then the subtractions.
- Color Range dialog: while it's open, the image itself is its eyedropper (Photoshop). The pipette cursor is the Color Picker's (`icons::cursor`, Precise cursors honoured), with + / − while Shift / Alt add or subtract. Pan and zoom under the dialog still work. `ui.point…

title: PSD: preflight pattern allocations and reuse decoded buffers
author: Streetblock
body:
The existing `huge_pattern_rect_with_tiny_channel_payload_is_rejected` regression can abort while allocating a 3.6 GB channel before the reader notices that all channels together exceed its existing budget. This change validates the complete pattern before decoding any channel, and removes an unnecessary full-plane allocation/copy for channels that already fill the tile.

Follow-up to #743 and #683.

### Changes

- Preflight channel metadata and aggregate padded output before decoding. The RGB32 reproducer requests 10.8 GB in total and is rejected before its first 3.6 GB allocation.
- Reuse the decoded `Vec` for full-size channels. Preserve the previous normalization of unused 1-bit row-tail bits in place.
- Use fallible reservation for genuinely padded channels and return an error when reservation fails.
- Keep the existing 8 GiB / 2 GiB target-dependent budget and public APIs unchanged; introduce no additional padding-size or expansion-ratio limit.
- Extend regressions across PSD global pattern blocks, PAT and embedded ABR, including CMYK16 with alpha; correct PAT mutation offsets to use its actual 10-byte header. Cover buffer reuse at 1/8/16/32 bits, allocation errors, and valid padding larger than 64 MiB.

title: Preferences › Performance › Low Resolution Previews: live previews at full resolution when it's off
author: Unemars
body:
**Cause.** Live previews of a large document render on a reduced copy (`proxy::factor`, about 2.5 MP). A 16 MP camera photo previews at every 3rd pixel, and the GPU canvas draws that copy 3× magnified, in 3×3 blocks, at 100 %. This happens in filter dialogs, in Image › Adjustments dialogs zoomed out (or where they fall back to the filter preview), and on an adjustment layer whose Properties slider is dragging. You can't judge fine detail (sharpening, noise, edges) until OK. Measured on a 4992×3292 NEF with Unsharp Mask at 100 %: in the reduced preview, 71 % of neighbouring screen pixels are identical, against 27 % in the image itself.

**Fix.** Preferences › Performance › **Low Resolution Previews** (`performance.lowResolutionPreviews`), on by default. On, nothing changes. Off, every live preview renders at full resolution:
- filter previews run with factor 1;
- an adjustment layer's drag previews through the regular full-size path (`display_doc`) instead of `ensure_proxy_preview`;
- `adjust_preview::gpu_proxy` (zoomed-out adjustment dialogs) is skipped;
- the CPU canvas counts the full-size composite as cheap.

Older preference files load with it on (`serde(default)`). The label is translated in every catalog.

**Cost.** Turning it off is the user's trade. On the same 16 MP photo, an Unsharp Mask slider change refreshes in about 0.75–0.8 s instead of about 40 ms. Adjustments that preview on the GPU stay cheap.

**Tests:**

author: seltzdesign
body:
Fixes #1187.

## Problem
With Interface › UI Scale set to **Auto**, any 4K monitor got at least 200%. That overrode the scale picked in the OS. On Windows with two 3840×2160 monitors at 125%, PhotoCraft drew the UI at 200%, so text and controls were too big.

## Fix

| Monitor | System scale | Auto before | Auto now |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4K | 100% | 200% | 200% |
| 4K | 125% | 200% | **125%** |
| 4K | 150% | 200% | **150%** |
| 4K | 300% | 300% | 300% |
| 1080p / 1440p | any | system | system |

The fixed choices (75%–300%) are unchanged. `docs/ui-design.md` › High DPI is updated.

title: Color Balance: Photoshop's slider double-click reset, wheel and arrow steps, Alt+Cancel Reset, Properties Reset and history
author: Unemars
body:
**Cause.** In Color Balance, a double-click on a slider doesn't put it back to 0 as it does in Photoshop. Up/Down in a field moved the value by 0.5, which rounds away on negative values, so Up did nothing below zero.

**How Photoshop behaves.** Measured on Photoshop 25.4 (clean-room: scripted clicks with xdotool in the real dialog and Properties panel, then the settings read back through ExtendScript), from Midtones +40 −30 +20:

| Gesture | Photoshop |
|---|---|
| Double-click a slider's knob or track | that slider of the shown tone → 0 (not the value the dialog opened with) |
| Double-click the label or the field | nothing |
| Click on the track | the knob jumps to the pointer |
| Shift / Ctrl / Alt with clicks, double-clicks, drags | no effect |
| Wheel over a slider | dialog: ±1 per notch, Shift ±10 (Ctrl/Alt ±1); Properties: nothing |
| Up/Down in a field | ±1, Shift ±10 |
| Hold Alt (dialog) | Cancel becomes Reset: every tone 0, Tone back to Midtones, Preserve Luminosity kept, dialog stays open |
| Properties edits in a row | one history step ("Modify Color Balance Layer"), until another step comes between |
| Properties Reset | after edits: back to the settings the layer had when the panel started showing it (Tone kept); again (or with no edits): the defaults (every tone 0, Midtones, Preserve Luminosity kept); part of the same step |

**Fix:**
- `widgets::RowGestures` and `slider_row_with` add three optional gestures:
  - `reset`: a double-click on the slider sets this value. Double-clicks are counted the Windows way, within 0.5 s, and the click after a double-click starts a new count; egui would call a third quick click a triple-click even when the first two weren't a double.
  - `wheel_step`: whole notches add up, so high-resolution wheels count fractions correctly; Shift multiplies the step by 10.
  - `key_step`: Up/Down, with Shift ×10, while the field is being edited.

  `slider_row` and `value_field` behave as before.
- Color Balance uses all three. The…

title: Adobe assets: new crate; read and write Photoshop action files (.atn) (#219)
author: chikien276
body:
First step toward `.atn` import (#219, scorecard `AUTO-219-2`; also asked for in #1163). This PR is format-only: it adds the `photocraft-adobe-assets` crate planned in `docs/architecture.md` and starts it with a reader and writer for Photoshop action files. Nothing in the engine or UI changes yet.

## What it does

- `atn::parse(&[u8]) -> Result<AtnSet>` and `atn::write(&AtnSet) -> Vec<u8>` for version-16 action files: the set, its actions (name, function key, Shift/Command, colour, expanded) and their steps (enabled and dialog toggles, event id, display name, parameters).
- Unmodified files write back byte for byte: names keep their stored UTF-16 code units and bytes.
- Each step's parameters are kept as the raw bytes of one ActionDescriptor; decode them with `photocraft_psd::Descriptor::from_bytes`.

## Why raw descriptor bytes

`adobe-assets` is `Class::Standalone` in `xtask/src/layers.rs`, so it can't depend on `photocraft-psd`, not even as a dev-dependency. Rather than copy the descriptor model or add a layering exception, the crate finds where each descriptor ends with a structural walk. The walk accepts the same value types and reference forms as `photocraft_psd::descriptor`, with the same nesting bound (64). The import command (next PR) sits in a layer that may use both crates, so it decodes the bytes there.

If you'd rather have this module in `photocraft-psd` next to `abr` and `grd`, that's a small move: tell me and I'll change it.

## Where the layout comes from

Clean-room: from Photoshop-saved action files and nothing else. The module docs separate what was observed from what is only accepted:

- **Observed:** the set/action/step layout, `TEXT` event ids, the `0` / `0xFFFFFFFF` descriptor marker, and descriptors without the version prefix that layers use.
- **Accepted but not yet seen in a saved file:** event ids stored as `long` + a four-character code, the descriptor format's other id form.

The reader is ported from our production action reader (a C#…

title: Quick Selection: a far stroke point no longer overflows the bounding box (#964)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #964.

## Problem
`quick_select` built the stroke's bounding box with `x1.ceil() as i32 + 1`. For a stroke point at or past 2^31, the `as i32` cast saturates to `i32::MAX` and the `+ 1` overflows. With overflow checks on, that panics inside `select.quick`, and dispatch returns an internal error. In release it wraps. The points come unchecked from the CLI, MCP, the control channel and engine callers.

## Fix
The upper bounds use `saturating_add(1)`. A far point now just misses the canvas (`None`). A stroke that also has a point on the canvas still selects from that point. `stroke_mask` already clamps its loops to the working image, so a far point doesn't make it do any extra work.

## Tests
- New `segment::tests::quick_select_far_point_misses_without_overflow` covers points at 3e9 on either axis, `f32::MAX` and -3e9, plus a near point paired with a far one. It panics without the fix in the default test profile.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-algo --lib quick_select`: 4 passed.

title: Select › Modify refuses a negative radius instead of clamping it (#993)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #993.

## Problem
`modify()` in `crates/engine/src/selection_cmds.rs` rejected only non-finite radii and radii above the dialog's maximum, then clamped with `r.max(0.0)`. A negative radius therefore reported success. Expand and Contract left the selection unchanged, and Border cleared it. The function's own comment says out-of-range values are "refused, never clamped silently".

## Fix
A negative radius now gets the same `BadParams` error as an over-maximum one ("radius must be a number in 0..max"), and the selection is untouched. Zero is still accepted as before, so no existing caller changes behaviour.

## Tests
- `selection_cmds::tests::modify_commands` now also tries -5, -0.5 and `f64::MIN` for all five Modify commands and expects an error.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib modify_commands` passes.

`cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` on Rust 1.97 reports one pre-existing `manual_range_contains` in `fill_cmds.rs:409`, which this PR doesn't touch.

title: New adjustment and fill layers take the active selection as their mask (#1250)
author: Pathos0925
body:
Fixes #1250.

## Problem

Photoshop masks a new adjustment or fill layer with the active selection, so the adjustment acts on the selected area only. `layer.newAdjustmentLayer.*`, `layer.newFillLayer.solidColor`, `.gradient` and `.pattern` inserted the layer without reading `doc.selection`, so select → New Adjustment Layer gave an unmasked adjustment over the whole image (the issue's CLI repro: `"hasMask": false`).

## Fix

The Gradient tool's fill-layer command (`gradient.fillLayer.create`) already did the right thing. Its inline code becomes the shared `commands::selection_mask`, and every adjustment and fill layer creator uses it: all `layer.newAdjustmentLayer.*`, `layer.newFillLayer.solidColor` / `.gradient` / `.pattern`, and the Gradient tool's command.

The selection stays active afterwards, matching the issue's stated expectation (same result as `layer.layerMask.revealSelection`) and that command's current behaviour. Photoshop itself drops the marquee once it becomes the mask; if you want that, it should change for Reveal Selection and these commands together, and I'm happy to do it here or as a follow-up.

## Tests

- `new_adjustment_and_fill_layers_are_masked_by_the_selection`: five commands at 8, 16 and 32-bit each get a linked, enabled mask that reveals the selection and hides the rest; the composite outside the selection is untouched; undo removes the layer. Fails on `main` with "no layer mask", passes here.
- `new_adjustment_and_fill_layers_have_no_mask_without_a_selection`.
- The issue's CLI repro now reports `"hasMask": true` for the Hue/Saturation layer.

Checks run: `cargo test -p photocraft-engine` (all green), `panic_hunt --ignored`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui` (green apart from two `canvas_16f` GPU tests that hit the egui-wgpu staging-buffer panic of #1215 on this machine), clippy on the engine. Not run locally: `cargo xtask wasm` (no wasm32 target installed); the change is pure document-model code.

title: PSD export: write empty layer and mask channels as raw
author: DWAA1660
body:
PhotoCraft v0.5.0 writes an empty ZIP prediction stream for zero-sized layer and mask channels in 32-bit PSD exports. Photoshop's fixture files use the raw compression code with no payload. This difference makes psd-tools 1.24.0 attempt to decompress a zero-sized channel and reject the export with `width 0 out of range [1, 300000]`.

The exporter now uses raw compression when either channel dimension is zero. Nonempty channels keep their existing compression. The shared path covers empty pixel/adjustment/group channels and uniform masks in PSD and PSB.

Refs #1281. This is a candidate for the reported Photoshop 26.6.0.14 compatibility error, not a confirmed fix for that specific file. The screenshot confirms PhotoCraft v0.5.0 and Photoshop's exact error, but we do not have the failing PSD or a local Photoshop installation to verify reopening. Direct validation in Photoshop 26.6.0.14 is still needed before treating this as the fix for #1281.

Validation:
- A new synthetic regression fails on main and passes with the change; RGB/Gray, 8/16/32-bit, PSD/PSB, empty layers and uniform masks.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-io`: 289 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask layers`: passed.
- Independent experiment: all 258 Photoshop-authored originals decode with psd-tools. Before the change, 18 PhotoCraft exports fail; after the change, all 258 exports decode, including merged and layer pixel data. These are PhotoCraft corpus fixtures, not the reporter's file.

title: Document tabs: elide and overflow into a » menu when they are too many (#1276)
author: LordFarquaadtheCreator
body:
## What the issue reports

20 documents open, and the tabs past the right edge of the strip are unreachable: only a sliver of the next tab stays visible, clicking it shows the document but never brings its tab into focus, and there is no way to scroll the strip (#1276).

## Root cause

The *document* tab strip lays every tab out at its natural width from the strip's left edge and never clamps to the strip width, so once the tabs are wider than the window the last ones run off it — `pro_tabs` in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` (Pro themes) advanced `x = r.right()` with no bound at all, and the Studio strip used a plain horizontal layout that egui simply clips. Neither had a scroll area, an overflow menu, or any notion of "keep the active tab visible".

The dock **panel** strips already solved this in #151: `tab_strip::fit` shrinks tabs, elides their labels, and moves what still doesn't fit into a `»` menu, with the selected tab always kept on the strip. The document strips were never wired to it.

## Fix

Both document strips now lay out through `tab_strip::fit`:

- tabs that don't fit shrink (long titles elide with `…` and show the full title on hover), and the ones that still don't fit move into a `»` menu at the end of the strip;
- the active document's tab always stays on the strip, and picking a document from the menu brings its tab onto the strip;
- files still opening in the background (#210) are tabs too: they share the fit's index space and the same menu;
- tabs that **do** fit keep their exact natural widths, and no `»` button appears — the strip is pixel-identical to before in the common case.

title: Free Transform: W/H fields reach 1000000% and X/Y the 300000 px document limit (#1267)
author: marcardenas
body:
Fixes #1267.

The Free Transform options bar clamped **W/H to ±10000%** and **X/Y to ±30000 px**, although `edit.transform` accepts any matrix and documents go up to 300000 px a side (`image.canvasSize`). Scaling overlays onto large stitched mosaics needs more.

## Change

  - `SCALE_LIMIT_PCT = 1_000_000` (a 300 px layer can span the largest document)
  - `POSITION_LIMIT_PX = 300_000` (the document size limit)

title: Select › Modify: Apply effect at canvas bounds, so Contract/Feather/Border work after Select All (#1277)
author: marcardenas
body:
Fixes #1277.

After **Select › All**, Contract and Smooth changed nothing and Border emptied the selection: the canvas edge was never treated as a selection edge.

## Change (`crates/engine/src/selection_cmds.rs`)
- **Contract, Smooth, Expand, Feather** gain Photoshop's *Apply effect at canvas bounds* option: `applyAtCanvasBounds: bool = false`. The schema-driven dialog shows it as a checkbox.
  - **On:** the canvas edge counts as a selection edge. Select All → Contract 4 shrinks 4 px from every edge, and Feather softens the edges.
  - **Off (Photoshop's default):** the selection continues past the canvas, so edges on the canvas border stay put.
- **Border** has no such option in Photoshop. It now always follows the canvas edge, so Select All → Border gives a band inside the edge instead of an empty selection.
- How it works: when the selection touches the canvas edge, the mask is padded by `2r + 2` px (empty when on, edge-replicated when off), the existing `photocraft-algo` op runs on it, and the result is cropped back. Selections clear of the edge are not padded and behave exactly as before.

Behaviour note: Feather previously always faded at the canvas edge (zero beyond the canvas). It now does so only with the option on, matching Photoshop's default.

## Tests
- `modify_select_all_honours_canvas_bounds`: Select All with the option off/on for each op, plus Border.
- `modify_away_from_the_canvas_edge_ignores_canvas_bounds`: an interior selection gives the same result either way.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine` ✅, `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui` ✅, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` ✅, `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored` ✅

title: fix(cli): report missing font fallbacks in run, info and convert

title: type.create: an unknown or out-of-range kerning is a bad-params error, as in type.edit (#994)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #994.

`type.create` passed `kerning` to `apply_char_props` without checking it first. An unknown string such as `"tight"` was saved as Metrics kerning, and an out-of-range number such as `1e9` was clamped to `KERN_MAX`. The command still reported success in both cases. `type.edit` and `type.setStyle` already reject these values with `check_kerning`.

`type.create` now calls `check_kerning(p)` before `check_size_tracking`, the same way `type.edit` does. An invalid kerning is a bad-params error, and no layer is created.

Test: `kerning_params_fail_gracefully` now also covers `type.create`. It checks that `"tight"`, `1e9`, `-5000`, `true` and `[1]` each return an error and leave the layer count unchanged. It also checks that `"optical"` and `-50` still create a layer with Optical kerning and Off/-50 kerning.

title: Control server: a bad JSON reply carries "id": null like every other unknown-id error (#1006)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1006.

After authentication, the desktop control server (`apps/photocraft/src/control_server.rs`) answered a line that is not valid JSON with `{"ok": false, "error": "bad JSON: ..."}`. That reply had no `id` key. Every other reply where the request id is unknown uses `"id": null`. This includes the server's own connection-limit and oversized-line replies, and the headless `rpc::respond` reply to the same malformed-JSON input. The reply now carries `"id": null`, so all these replies use the same envelope.

Test: `bad_json_reply_carries_a_null_id_and_the_connection_keeps_serving` drives `serve` over a real loopback connection:
1. It authenticates and sends `{not json}`.
2. It checks through the object map that the reply has an `id` key with value null. Indexing a `Value` gives null for a missing key too, so it could not catch the bug. The test also checks `ok: false` and the `bad JSON: ` text.
3. It then sends a valid request with id 7 and checks that the reply carries id 7 and the handler's result.

title: SVG opens as shape layers and places as a vector smart object (FILE-215-9, part of #215)
author: ljkx
body:
Part of #215 (FILE-215-9: "SVG opens and places as shape layers or a vector Smart Object", scorecard row was `missing`).

## What

**Open an SVG** and you get a document of editable shape layers. **Place** one (Embedded or Linked) and you get a vector smart object that is rasterised at its placement scale, so it stays sharp at 1 000 % where a resampled raster would blur, and whose Edit Contents opens the shape-layer document.

New module `crates/io/src/svg.rs`, wired into `photocraft_io::import` by extension (`.svg`, `.svgz`) or by content sniffing.

- **Parsing** is `usvg`'s (already in the tree through `egui_extras`'s icon loader): CSS, `use`, units, nested transforms, `viewBox`, and text shaped into outlines with the bundled craft fonts plus the system's fonts on the desktop (wasm: craft fonts only).
- **Paths → `ShapeLayer`**: the transform chain is baked into the knots, quadratics are raised to cubics, a closing segment that returns to the start merges into it, and every subpath after the first *joins* the component so the fill rule counts winding across the whole path as SVG does (a hole drawn as a second subpath stays a hole under even-odd). Fill colour/opacity and rule; stroke width (geometric mean under a non-uniform scale), colour, opacity, caps, joins, miter limit, dashes.
- **Groups → layer groups** with opacity and blend mode. Groups that only carry a transform are not layers; usvg's id-only wrapper groups collapse onto their single child.
- **Text → a group of outline shapes** named after the text; without a usable font it is dropped with a warning instead of silently.
- **Gradients** become the layer's own gradient fill (stops with opacity, direction as Photoshop's angle; radial as the radial style) with a warning that the exact geometry is not kept.
- **What the shape model can't hold is rasterised, not dropped**: `clip-path`, `mask`, `filter`, pattern paints and `<image>` subtrees render through `resvg` into a pixel layer over their bounding box (th…

title: Gradient tool: a handle dragged past the 10% scale floor stops; the other handle stays put (#1243)
author: marcardenas
body:
Fixes the "other gradient point moves around" part of #1243.

## Cause
Live gradients are Gradient Fill layers whose scale is clamped to Photoshop's 10–150% (`SCALE_RANGE` in `gradient_fill_cmds.rs`). The clamp is meant to stop the dragged handle there. But `gradient.fill.set` took the centre from the requested points: for Linear that's the midpoint of the start and the dragged end. With the scale clamped, the gradient was re-centred on that midpoint, so the handle that wasn't being dragged slid along the line. The floor is 10% of the frame's chord, which depends on the angle, and that's why the limit looked different on X and Y.

## Change
- In `apply_set`, when only `from` or only `to` is given and the scale clamps, the offset is shifted so the handle that wasn't given keeps its place. The dragged handle stops on the line at the floor.
- `apply_set` also drives the drag preview, so the canvas preview matches the commit.

## Not changed
The 10% floor itself is kept, because it matches Photoshop's Gradient Fill Scale range and the PSD round-trip. If you'd rather let live gradients go shorter, lowering `SCALE_RANGE.0` is a one-line follow-up.

## Tests
- New `a_clamped_handle_drag_leaves_the_other_handle_alone`: every style, horizontal and vertical, dragging the end and the start past the floor. Without the fix it fails with `linear: start moved to [12.1, 16.0]` (it should stay at `[14, 16]`).
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine` ✅, `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib gradient` ✅, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` ✅, `panic_hunt` ✅

title: Filter › Last Filter applies to the active layer, not the layer the filter first ran on (#1270)
author: marcardenas
body:
Fixes #1270.

## Cause
`filter.lastFilter` replays the most recent `filter.*` entry in the session journal unchanged. The Filter Gallery (`gallery_ui::commit`), Camera Raw and Adaptive Wide Angle dialogs put `"layer": <id>` in their params, so Last Filter ran the filter again on **that** layer instead of the active one. In the issue's screenshot the last filter was Reticulation, a Filter Gallery effect. When the original layer is hidden, covered, or a different layer from the one selected, the menu item looks like it does nothing. If that layer has since been deleted, the command fails.

## Change
`last_filter()` in `crates/engine/src/filters.rs` drops the recorded `layer`. Last Filter then applies to the current layer with the same settings, as Photoshop's does. Filters run from the menus or over automation without `layer` behave as before.

## Tests
- New `last_filter_applies_to_the_active_layer`: runs a filter with an explicit `layer`, makes a new layer active, then runs Last Filter. The new layer is filtered and the first one is left alone. Without the fix it fails.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine` ✅, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` ✅, `panic_hunt` ✅

title: Open camera raws in Camera Raw first (Open / Cancel)
author: switch87
body:
Photoshop opens a raw file in Adobe Camera Raw before it becomes a document. PhotoCraft developed it with the default settings straight away and said so in a warning ("… developed with default settings (ahd demosaic, as-shot white balance) …"), so you could only adjust afterwards, through Filter › Camera Raw Filter on already developed pixels.

## Behaviour

An interactive open (File › Open, Open Recent, drag and drop, the command line) of a raw developed from its sensor data now shows the Camera Raw dialog first. It is titled "Camera Raw (name)" and has **Open** and **Cancel**.

- **Open**: when Temperature, Tint or Exposure changed, the raw is re-developed with them applied to the sensor data (`photocraft_io::raw::import_raw_tuned`):

  - Temperature / Tint become the filter's own gains `[1 + .35t, 1 − .25tn, 1 − .35t]` on the as-shot white-balance multipliers.

  The other settings are applied as one `filter.cameraRaw` step. The document then starts unmodified (`saved_revision = revision`).
- **Without an as-shot white balance, or without the file's bytes** (a background open from bytes): Temperature / Tint stay RGB adjustments, as in the filter.
- **Cancel** closes the document again.
- **The "developed with default settings" note** is not shown when the dialog is, because the dialog shows how the raw is developed.
- **Preference** `rawDefaults.openInCameraRaw` (default on): the first Camera Raw Defaults setting that does something, so it is visible in Edit › Preferences. The other `rawDefaults.*` stay hidden.
- **Automation opens** (`app.open`, MCP, CLI) never show the dialog. `ui.inspect.cameraRaw.openingRaw` reports `{name, path}`, and commit returns `{document, redeveloped, filter?}`. Documented in `docs/control-protocol.md`.

title: raw: decode Nikon compressed NEF (lossless + lossy)
author: switch87
body:
Refs #50. Nikon's default NEF (TIFF compression 34713) still opened as the embedded 8-bit JPEG preview. This decodes the sensor data.

## What decodes now

| NEF variant | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Lossless compressed (`0x0096` v`0x46`), 12 / 14 bit | preview fallback | decoded |
| Lossy type 1 (`0x44 0x10`, full curve) | preview fallback | decoded |
| Lossy type 2 (`0x44 0x20` / `0x40`, 257-point curve) | preview fallback | decoded |
| "Lossy after split" (non-zero split row) | preview fallback | preview fallback, unchanged |

Real file: a Nikon D3200 lossy-type-2 12-bit NEF now opens as 6080×4012 RGB/16 (before: 6016×4000 8-bit preview). Decode 169 ms, develop 397 ms (AHD), release build.

## Clean-room

Why #83 stopped: Nikon's Huffman tables are not in the files, and the only listing found was GPL decoder source. LightCraft has since recovered them by black-box analysis of CC0 raw.pixls.us samples (the same scenes shot compressed and uncompressed, then a beam search over code assignments). They were verified there on ~45 files from ~35 bodies (storytold/lightcraft#86). This PR takes over only the format facts and the four tables, with the sources listed in the module docs: Clévy and Claff prose write-ups, ExifTool tag names and T.81. No decoder code is shared. `crates/raw/src/nefc.rs` is written against this crate's own TIFF reader, bit reader and error type, per AGENTS.md ("repos don't share code"). No dcraw/LibRaw/rawspeed/rawler code was read.

Also: Nikon `BlackLevel` (`0x003d`) is in 14-bit units whatever the sample depth, so it is divided by 4 for 12-bit data. LightCraft measured this on D750 / D850 / Z 50 files. Before, a 12-bit file with the tag got 4× its black level.

A Nikon maker note without a `BlackLevel` tag now means "black-subtracted in camera" (black 0, no warning): a D3200 NEF's darkest samples are 0–4, median 81 of 4095. Files without a Nikon maker note keep the warning.

title: Linux: display server preference (X11 / XWayland) so file drops work
author: switch87
body:
Refs #386 (direction 2).

On a Wayland session, dropping a file on the window does nothing. winit 0.30.13 (eframe 0.36) has no Wayland drag and drop: it only arrives with winit 0.31, which egui doesn't use yet. Until now the only workaround was launching with `WAYLAND_DISPLAY= photocraft`.

## Change

- **New preference:** Preferences › Performance › **Linux display server**: `auto` (default) | `x11`, applies at next launch. It is `performance.linuxDisplayServer`, a `LinuxDisplayServer` choice.
- **How `x11` is applied:** at startup `main.rs` reads the preference (`gpu_startup::read_display_server`, next to the GPU-backend reader). It then sets eframe's `event_loop_builder` to `EventLoopBuilderExtX11::with_x11()`, so winit uses its X11 backend and the window runs through XWayland, where drops work.
  - No environment variable is touched, so no `unsafe` (edition 2024 `remove_var`).

  - Other platforms ignore the preference.
- **New dependency:** `winit = "=0.30.13"` (Linux only, `x11` feature) for the trait import. It is already in Cargo.lock through eframe and pinned exactly, like `x11rb`.
- **Wayland drop notice:** it now points at the preference instead of the environment variable. Every catalog is updated, and the new label is translated.

## Tests

- `display_server_preference_is_read_before_the_window_opens`: x11, auto, unknown value, wrong type, broken JSON, missing file, no path.

title: Shape gradients: honour midpoints, opacity stops, offset, dither and align
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What

Shape layers now honour **every** gradient fill field. `vector::Paint::from_fill` used to
discard `opacity_stops`, `midpoints`, `offset`, `dither` and `align` (and to sample stops
unsorted, with its own simplified geometry), so a Photoshop file whose shape fill uses any of
those rendered with the wrong ramp, alpha, position or banding behaviour — even though the PSD
import (`vscg` → `fill_from_desc`) reads all of them into the model.

`Paint::Gradient` now carries the full ramp (sorted colour stops, per-segment midpoints,
opacity stops, dither) and the compositor's geometry: the centre `offset` (PSD `Ofst`),
Photoshop's whole-pixel end-point snapping for Linear/Reflected fills, pixel-corner sampling
for those two styles, and the "Align with layer" frame choice (the shape's bounds, else the
canvas). Shape strokes paint through the same path, so stroked gradients get the fix too.

## How

`photocraft-vector` (L2) cannot depend on `photocraft-compose` (L3), so the ramp and geometry
are ported next to `Paint` with mirrors of `effects::gradient_units`/`effects::gradient_t`,
`fill_layout::gradient_layout`, `gradient_fill::{Ramp, midpoint_remap, dither}` — the same
arrangement the compositor already has with the Gradient tool's destructive painting
(`algo::paint`). Two couplings keep the copies honest:

* a parity test in `photocraft-compose` (which *can* see both) renders each non-default field
  × all five styles × both frames as a shape layer and as a fill layer and requires the same
  pixels;
* `from_fill` binds every `Fill::Gradient` field — no `..` — so a new gradient field fails to
  compile here until the shape renderer honours it.

`CompiledShape::new` takes the canvas now (it anchors unaligned gradients); `render_shape`'s
signature is unchanged — every caller already passes the canvas.

Known gap, unchanged by this PR: pattern fills in shapes still render transparent
(`Paint::None`); they need the document's pattern table, which lives above the vector cr…

title: Fix keyboard navigation in blend mode dropdown
author: rozaqabdul656

title: Feature: Add incrementation with up/down arrow keys on numeric fields
author: Cyanoxide
body:
### What
Numeric fields can now be incremented with the `up`/`down` arrow keys while they're focused. Modifiers can also be used for larger and smaller steps:

- `up` / `down`: 1
- `shift` + `up` / `down`: 10
- `cmd` / `ctrl` + `up` / `down`: 0.1

_Fields with a small range (10 or less, like the gamma value in `Levels`) step 10 times finer: `up` / `down` by 0.01 and `shift` by 0.1. Note that there's no finer `cmd` / `ctrl` step, as these fields only allow two decimal places._

### Problem
Currently the arrow keys do nothing in most numeric fields. The exception is fields with a small range, like the gamma value in the `Levels` dialog, where they step by 0.01 only, with no modifier for larger steps.

### Resolution
`value_field` now handles the arrow keys before the field is drawn, so it can apply its own step sizes. Before adding a step, the value is rounded to the nearest whole number (or to 0.1 with `cmd` / `ctrl`), so whole number fields drop stray decimals.

- `55.4` + `up` > `56`
- `55.6` + `up` > `57`
- `55.4` + `down` > `54`
- `55.4` + `shift` + `up` > `65`
- `55.47` + `cmd` + `up` > `55.6`

_I personally believe the rounding isn't necessary but I wanted to match parity with Photoshop. I have isolated this rounding to a single commit so it can easily be removed if desired._

If a sum has been typed but not yet confirmed (for example `5+5`), pressing `up` / `down` works it out first, as `enter` would, then steps the result: `5+5` + `up` > `11`, again to match parity with Photoshop.

I also checked that the shortcuts `cmd` / `ctrl` + arrow and `shift` + arrow aren't already used by anything else while a field is focused.

Four tests have been added to cover the change: stepping by 1, 10 and 0.1, rounding and fine fields, stepping a typed sum, and leaving unfocused fields alone.

### Verification
To verify, open a new document and, with the paintbrush selected (which it is by default), click into the `Opacity` field in the options bar. `up` / `down` should incre…

title: Fix #1272: a reassigned shortcut runs its new command
author: bflatastic
body:
## What

Giving F5 to Select › Modify › Feather… in Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts warned that Brush Settings would lose it. After OK, though, F5 kept toggling Brush Settings (#1272).

## Why

- The dialog lists Photoshop's Window › Brush Settings item (`window.panel.brushSettings`), so OK cleared that id. The key was bound to the shell command behind it (`window.toggle.brushSettings`), which kept its F5 default.
- Shell commands came first in the binding table, so they won any key they shared.
- The same held for F6 (Color), F7 (Layers), and shortcuts set through `edit.keyboardShortcuts` by agents or MCP. The engine's `removeConflicts` only knows engine commands.

## Fix (`shortcut_dispatch::bindings`)

- A key the user assigned to a command wins over any default that still names it.
- An edit to a Window › panel row applies to the shell command it runs, via `menus::panel_alias`.

## Tests

- `a_function_key_moved_off_a_panel_toggle_runs_its_new_command`: drives the dialog, presses F5 and checks it dispatches Feather, not Brush Settings.
- `a_user_shortcut_wins_over_a_default_it_was_not_moved_from`: F7 set through `edit.keyboardShortcuts` goes to Feather, not Layers.

Closes #1272

title: Fix #1323: a Distort corner stops before the box folds over
author: bflatastic
body:
## What

Dragging a Distort corner past the opposite diagonal turned the transform box into a bow tie, and the image into an extreme smear (#1323).

## Fix

- Distort, and Perspective (which moves two corners), now move along the drag only as far as the box stays convex. They stop just short of flat, as Photoshop and Photopea do.
- A drag that keeps the box convex is unchanged.
- `keep_convex` binary-searches the furthest convex point along the drag.
- A box that isn't convex to begin with, or has NaN or zero-area corners, is left free. The helper never panics.

## Tests

- `a_distort_corner_stops_before_the_box_folds_over`: the TL corner, dragged far past BR, stops just before the TR–BL diagonal. The other corners don't move, and a later convex drag isn't held back.
- `keep_convex_leaves_a_degenerate_start_alone`.

Closes #1323

title: Docker web deployment
author: fplachecinski
body:
Adds Docker support for self-hosting PhotoCraft’s browser app, with a documented build-and-run workflow and HTTPS reverse-proxy guidance.

- Builds the existing Rust/WebAssembly app with Trunk and serves it through non-root NGINX.
- Includes gzip compression, correct Wasm MIME types, cache policies, and a health endpoint.
- Uses thin LTO and one compilation job to reduce build memory requirements.


**Validation**: ARM64 image build, HTTP smoke test, dependency-layer checks, and Chrome startup with WebGL2 all passed. The Dockerfile supports amd64, but that architecture has not yet been tested.

Editing runs in the browser; files are opened locally and saves are downloaded. Deployment does not add server-side document storage or web autosave.

title: Select › Modify: Apply effect at canvas bounds, carrying #1296 by @marcardenas
author: bflatastic
body:
## What this is

This is @marcardenas's #1296, with one follow-up commit from me. Their commit keeps its authorship, and I'll rebase-merge.

**#1296 (by @marcardenas):** Photoshop's **Apply effect at canvas bounds** option for Contract, Expand, Smooth and Feather.
- Off (Photoshop's default): a selection is taken to continue past the canvas.
- On: the canvas edge is a selection edge, so Select All → Contract shrinks from the edges.

**My follow-up:**
- The canvas-edge margin was 2r for every operation, so Feather 1000 added 2002 px a side, about 320 MB extra on a 24 MP selection. It now pads by each operation's reach (Feather 1.5 r, the others r).

- The new dialog option ("Apply At Canvas Bounds") is translated in all 12 shipped languages.

## Review

- **Security:** engine-only; no dependencies, I/O or `unsafe`.
- **Note for #1277:** the option is off by default, as in Photoshop. To shrink from the canvas edges after Select All, tick **Apply effect at canvas bounds** in the Contract/Feather dialog.

title: GPU startup: windowing errors keep the backend; a failed CPU start doesn't pin CPU, carrying #1228 by @liowald and #1145 by @shovel-kun
author: bflatastic
body:
## What this is

This carries two GPU-startup PRs that conflict with each other. Both authors' commits keep their authorship, and I'll rebase-merge.

**#1228 (by @liowald):** only a renderer (`eframe::Error::Wgpu`) error counts as a driver crash. A windowing error, such as a missing display, or an app-setup error no longer pushes the next launch onto a "safer" backend. A previous crash marker is kept rather than overwritten.

**#1145 (by @shovel-kun):** a failed start on the CPU backend has no safer backend to fall back to. Keeping its marker used to pin every later start to CPU, so it is now cleared.

**Rebase:** #1145 is rebased onto #1228, and their conditions are combined:
- The marker is kept only for a renderer error *with* a safer backend left.
- Previous crash evidence is restored only for a non-renderer error.

## Review

- **Security:** app startup only; no dependencies or `unsafe`. The file I/O is the existing crash-marker file in the config dir.

title: Camera Raw opens in a window of its own
author: switch87
body:
Builds on #1309 (open raws in Camera Raw first): this branch contains that commit, so merge #1309 first or review only the last commit.

The Camera Raw dialog (Filter › Camera Raw Filter, and the open-time dialog) was a full-window overlay inside the PhotoCraft window. It also covered PhotoCraft's own title bar, so it looked like a fullscreen app without window controls. Adobe Camera Raw is a separate window.

## Change

- **Own window:** the dialog is shown in an egui immediate viewport, an OS window with a title bar. Its title is "Camera Raw (name)" or "Camera Raw Filter (layer)". The default size is 1360 × 900, it is resizable, and the minimum is 900 × 600.
- **Still modal:** the main window is dimmed and takes no input while the dialog is open, as in Photoshop. Shortcuts were already blocked.
- **Closing the window is Cancel.** For the open-time dialog that also closes the raw being opened.
- **Fallback:** where the platform has no extra windows (`ctx.embed_viewports()`, the web build), the dialog is drawn over the main window as before, with its painted title strip.
- **Drawing code unchanged** apart from the title strip, which is not painted when the OS window shows the title.
- `docs/control-protocol.md` (Camera Raw dialog) describes the window.

## Tests

`cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui` green (the dialog tests drive it through `menu` and are unaffected). `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

By hand on KDE Plasma 6: the window opens with KDE decorations, can be moved, resized and maximized, the main window behind it is dimmed and inert, and close = Cancel.

title: PNM: the file, not the header, bounds what a decode reserves (#1110)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #1110.

The Netpbm decoder sized its reservations from the header, before checking that the file holds that much data.

## Fixes

| Site | Trigger | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| ASCII PGM/PPM, `pnm.rs:158` | `P3\n32768 32768\n255\n` (19 bytes) | `Vec::<u32>::with_capacity(n)`: 12 GiB, 4× the `Limits` budget. With `Limits::none()` a 2³¹ × 2³¹ header panics with "capacity overflow" | capacity `n.min(rest / 2 + 1)`: each sample is at least a digit and a separator |
| ASCII / binary PBM, `pnm.rs:121` | `P1` or `P4` header with no raster | reserves `w × h` bytes first. With `Limits::none()` that is 2⁶² bytes and the process aborts | P1 caps by the remaining bytes; P4 checks the raster length before reserving |
| Sample counts (P1-P7, PFM) | `Limits::none()` with `u32::MAX` sides | `w × h × channels`, `n × 2` and the PFM `row × h × 4` are unchecked: "attempt to multiply with overflow" | new `sample_count` uses `checked_mul`; the length checks use `checked_mul` with `is_none_or` |

`Limits::none()` documents that it is "still bounded by `usize` overflow checks", so the last row brings the decoder in line with that.

On wasm32 the default `max_alloc` is 2 GiB, and a 4-bytes-per-sample reservation of more than 2³¹ bytes exceeds `isize::MAX` there. So I expect a header like `P2 23000 23000 255` to have panicked in the web build under default limits. I have not run this on wasm.

- `pnm_header_alone_reserves_nothing_without_limits`: P1-P4 headers of 2³¹ × 2³¹ with no raster are errors. Before the fix, the test binary aborted (`memory allocation of 4611686018427387904 bytes failed`). Run on their own, the P2 and P3 cases panicked with `capacity overflow`.

title: Edit › Toolbar: hidden tools leave the toolbar (#1116)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1116.

What the user saw: unticking a tool in Edit › Toolbar… and confirming left the tool in the toolbar. The dialog saved `prefs.toolbar.hidden`, but the toolbar was drawn from the constant `TOOL_SECTIONS` and never read that setting.

What changed: the toolbar now draws from `visible_sections`, which is `TOOL_SECTIONS` without the hidden tools. A flyout group keeps only its visible tools. - `hidden_tools_leave_the_toolbar` draws the toolbar and counts the tool buttons. Hiding every tool removes every slot. Hiding Brush, Pencil and Mixer Brush removes one slot. Hiding only Sponge keeps its slot.
- `a_slot_keeps_only_its_visible_tools_and_its_index` checks the filtered groups, that each group keeps its index, that an empty section is dropped, and that lowercase command names give the same result.

title: New Document: a size typed in millimetres or another physical unit keeps its digits (#1147)
author: MarekSpodBiedry

Fixes #1147.

In the New Document dialog, Width and Height in millimetres (or another physical unit) were turned into whole pixels on every keystroke and then converted back. The field rewrote the text while you typed: 8 mm became 23 px, which showed as 8.1. Height showed a ".9" that could not be deleted.
