title: fix(Text): served fonts become script fallbacks on the web
author: hamada147
body:
Follow-up to #1875, the part it left open (#1615): script fallback from served fonts, plus SRI and startup preloading. Which is was recommended in the comments of #1837

## Problem

With #1875 a host can serve Noto Sans Arabic, but Arabic typed in the default font (Inter) still shows as boxes on the web, unless the user picks an Arabic family by hand. Nothing connects a character's script to the served font for it, although the manifest's scripts `field` says which scripts each font is for.

## Change

- Script fallback: `served` reads the manifest's `scripts`. For each script the bundled fonts don't cover (Arab, Hebr, Deva, Thai, Jpan, Hans, Hant, Kore), the first family listed for it is that script's fallback, so a craft-fonts checkout makes Noto Sans Arabic the Arabic fallback.
  - Layout asks for the fallback a paragraph's text needs (`request_for_text`).
  - Once it arrives, `FontDb` adds it to the fallback stack, and type layers whose text uses that script re-render. Previously only layers named in that family re-rendered.
  - Han follows the UI locale's CJK order, as installed CJK fonts already do.
- SRI: the manifest's SHA-256 becomes the fetch's `integrity` (`sha256-<base64>`), so the browser rejects a file whose bytes differ. Lines without a valid hash fetch as before.
- Startup preloading: after reading the manifest, the web shell asks for the fallbacks of the scripts in `navigator.languages`, so an Arabic-speaking user's font is ready before they type.
- Nothing changes for hosts without a manifest or without `scripts` fields. No new dependencies; Rust only.

## Tests

- `served::tests`: manifest `scripts/sha256` → scripts and integrity; first family per script is its fallback (Latin and Cyrillic excluded); characters → scripts (including Han by locale); browser languages → scripts; Hebrew text, a Hebrew layout and a `he-IL` browser each request the served fallback, and Latin text requests nothing.

title: Brush strokes carry their timing: the first moves count, smoothing feels the same on any device, a held airbrush builds up
author: tanish2k09
body:
Part 3a of the owner-approved brush overhaul. The audit found these defects in the canvas → engine path. Each is a root cause behind user reports:
- #2057 ("the brush glides")
- airbrush Build-up doing nothing in the app
- strokes starting with a straight segment and no pressure ramp-in (#1420, #2036, #1776)

## What changes

1. **Every stroke point carries a time.**
   - **Before:** `StrokePoint.time` was always 0 from the canvas (`feed_live_stroke` used `StrokePoint::new`, and `stylus.stroke_points` never sent `timeMs`). So speed spacing (Spacing off), airbrush Build-up and Stroke Catch-Up worked from scripts but **never from the UI**.
   - egui's pointer events carry no timestamps, so a frame's samples are spread evenly between the previous point and the frame time (`spread_ms`). That's monotonic, and a press frame's moves share its time.
   - `Stylus` keeps a per-point time track next to the pose track.
   - `stroke_points` (the commit) and `feed_live_stroke` (the live preview) send identical times, relative to the first point, as `timeMs`. Strokes with no time variation (automation) are unchanged.
2. **The first moves count.**
   - **Before:** a stroke starts on the press, but moves were fed only once egui recognised a drag (past its 6 pt click distance), so the first points of every stroke were dropped.
   - Moves are now fed from the press on while a press-started stroke is active.
3. **Smoothing pulls by time, not by event count.** Exponential smoothing now moves `1 − (1 − a)^(dt / 16 ms)` of the way. A 1000 Hz mouse and a 60 Hz pen end in the same place after the same time, where before it was 99 % vs 36 %. Without Stroke Catch-Up, a paused pointer stops the brush (Photoshop). Input without timestamps keeps one step per point.
4. **A held pointer keeps time running, only when it matters.**
   - While the stroke changes with time, the held point repeats every 16 ms and the canvas keeps repainting. "Changes with time" means airbrush Build-up is on, or smoothi…

title: feat(canvas): Caps Lock forces the precise crosshair for painting tools (#1758)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #1758.

Caps Lock now forces the precise crosshair for painting tools, exactly like Photoshop, whatever the Cursors › Painting preference. Painting is unaffected — only the cursor changes.

egui and winit have no Caps Lock (there is no `egui::Key` variant, no modifier field, and egui-winit drops the `NamedKey::CapsLock` key event), so instead of adding keyboard plumbing to winit/egui the state is polled from the OS once per frame:

- **X11 / XWayland**: XKB's Lock-modifier state through the existing pure-Rust `x11rb` client (`xkb_use_extension` → `xkb_get_indicator_map` to find the Lock-modifier mask, then `xkb_get_state` each frame).
- **Windows**: `GetKeyState(VK_CAPITAL)` through the existing safe `winsafe` binding.
- **macOS**: `CGEventSourceFlagsState` (`kCGEventFlagAlphaShift`) through `core-graphics2`'s event feature.
- **Native Wayland**: there is no global keyboard-state query, so there the service is `None` and the cursor follows the preference (the feature degrades, no false behaviour).

The override lives in the one canvas cursor block that paints the painting cursor; every other cursor path is untouched.

**Tests** (real canvas via `egui_kittest`): with Caps Lock on, Brush, Pencil, Clone Stamp, Healing, Eraser and Quick Selection draw exactly the crosshair the Precise preference draws — and differ from the Standard cursor; Move, Rect/Ellipse Marquee, Crop, Zoom and Hand are byte-for-byte unchanged. Releasing Caps Lock restores the preference cursor. 1,254 ui-egui tests pass.

title: Pen pressure follows every sample: moves in one frame no longer share the frame's last pressure
author: tanish2k09
body:
**Stacked on #2110** (brush phase 3a). I'll retarget this to `main` when #2110 merges. Brush phase 3b of the owner-approved brush overhaul.

## Why

Pen pressure arrived as **one value per frame**. `StylusFeed` was a single latest-value slot (`Arc<Mutex<Option<PenSample>>>`), and every pointer move in a frame took `stylus.pressure()`, the last value. On Windows, the touch-force path kept only the frame's last force. A fast pen stroke (several moves per frame) therefore painted stair-stepped line weights. That's the top artist complaint in the brush audit:
- #2046 ("the pressure lags and then suddenly jumps")
- #2036 ("distinct steps in pen pressure")
- #1776 ("jaggedy stair like line weights")
- #610 ("the pressure curve is choppy")

## What

- **`StylusFeed` queues every sample.** `set()` keeps the latest sample (proximity, eraser end, tilt) and also appends to a bounded queue (1024). `drain()` hands the canvas the samples in order. The public API is otherwise unchanged, so the macOS, X11 and web sources need no changes. The WinTab source in #1911 (approved after fixes) can push into it as is. Lock poisoning is handled with `into_inner`.
- **Each move gets its own sample.**
  - Each frame takes the drained queue plus egui `Touch` forces, in order.
  - Pointer move *k* of *n* takes the pressure, tilt and rotation interpolated at its share of the frame, starting from the previous frame's last sample. Rotation takes the shorter way round.
  - A mouse, Use Tablet Pressure off, or a frame without pen samples behave as before.
- **A new stroke starts fresh.** Its first moves interpolate from this frame's samples, never from a sample a previous stroke left behind.
- **The stylus updates once per egui frame** (`update_for_frame`). `canvas_view` runs once per view, and egui can run a frame in several passes. A second `update` drained an empty queue and dropped the frame's samples, a latent bug with split views.

|---|---|
| `stroke_timing_tests::mo…

title: Masks: mask button adds a vector mask instead of replacing the layer mask (#2075)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #2075.

**Why:** The Layers panel "Add a mask" button always ran Layer Mask › Reveal All / Hide All / Reveal or Hide Selection, and those commands replace the layer's mask. A second click, with or without Alt, silently discarded the existing (possibly painted) mask; Alt-click only looked like an "invert". In Photoshop this button never replaces a mask: it adds a layer mask when there is none, adds a vector mask once a layer mask exists (tooltip "Add vector mask"; Alt/Option-click adds a hide-all vector mask), and adds nothing once the layer has both.

title: Keep startup responsive while recovering autosaved documents
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
A large crash-recovery snapshot was decoded synchronously inside `PhotocraftApp::new`, blocking startup before the window became usable. List only recovery metadata after construction, then decode one entry at a time through the existing background-job system.

title: EXR: multi-part files open the colour part; exr_info lists them all
author: Elvis33LE
body:
A Maya/Arnold render writes one part per AOV (`Z`, `beauty`, `diffuse`, …). The decoder took part 0 silently, so a depth-only part failed the whole file with `no R/G/B or Y channels`, and there was no way to see or choose a part.

**What this does**

- `decode()` opens the part that looks most like a colour image — RGBA beats RGB beats YA beats a single channel, earliest wins — so a `Z`-first AOV stack opens its beauty, and a pure depth file still opens as grayscale. Multi-part files carry a `DecodeWarning::MoreParts` naming how many parts exist (same pattern as multi-page TIFF).
- `exr_info(bytes, limits)` lists every part from the headers alone (name, view, size, channel names + sample types, deep/tiled) — the data a part chooser needs, without decoding pixels.
- `decode_exr_part(bytes, part, opts)` decodes one chosen part; F16 parts stay F16.
- Deep parts stay with the deep decoder by design: a file that has any is refused here with a pointer to `decode_deep_exr` (mixing flat and deep parts in one decode is explicitly out of scope for now).

Header facts are read through the unvalidated meta parse, the same route the deep decoder uses, because the `exr` crate's validation rejects deep headers outright; every part's declared size is limit-checked before any pixel allocation, as before.

**Tests** (`crates/codecs/tests/exr_multipart.rs`, synthetic multi-part files via the `exr` crate with per-part compressions): part listing, colour-ranked auto-pick against exact pixels, part-by-index decode (a `Z` part becomes Gray instead of an error), out-of-range index, stereo views listed with the left view winning the auto-pick, single-part files not warning, F16 round trip, and a truncation sweep that must error, never panic. Full gate locally: 582 codec tests green, clippy `-D warnings` clean, fmt, `xtask layers`, `xtask wasm`, `xtask test-corpus --changed`.

title: perf: bevel_bench, the cost of changing a chisel bevel's size (#2006 follow-up)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
Follow-up to #2006, which asked for a bevel benchmark under `perf/`.

## What
`bevel_bench` (example of `photocraft-ui-egui`, next to `fx_bench`) times the case #2006 made dearer: dragging a Chisel Hard inner bevel's size on a 12 MP document, on an anti-aliased ellipse (smooth outline) and on a text paragraph (many thin edges), at sizes 8, 50 and 250, GPU canvas and CPU compositor.

Each case warms the caches one pixel below the size, then times refreshes with the size growing by one pixel each. That makes the GPU canvas rebuild its distance fields every time (it keeps them while the size shrinks) and the CPU compositor miss its map cache.

Registered in `perf/budgets.toml` as P52–P59 with no budgets (track only, like P45 and P46); `docs/scorecard.md` regenerated (the rows read "not run" until the next baseline). `docs/development.md` lists the bench.

```sh
cargo run --release -p photocraft-ui-egui --example bevel_bench -- [--size 4000x3000] [--reps 9] [--scene ellipse|text] [--no-cpu] [--json out.json]
cargo xtask perf --bench bevel_bench          # or --quick (1200×800, 3 reps)
```

## Does it see #2006?
RTX 4080 SUPER, release, 9 reps, p50 ms, before #2006 (3bc49f5e) → after (f4c1048e), same bench file on both:

| row | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| ellipse, size 8 (GPU / CPU) | 88 / 406 | 105 / 472 |
| ellipse, size 50 (GPU / CPU) | 169 / 428 | 199 / 546 |
| ellipse, size 250 (GPU / CPU) | 305 / 554 | 460 / 1019 |
| text, size 8 (GPU / CPU) | 119 / 402 | 140 / 797 |
| text, size 50 (GPU / CPU) | 141 / 473 | 252 / 1108 |
| text, size 250 (GPU / CPU) | 238 / 636 | 557 / 1247 |

Runs on this machine vary by about 20%, hence 9 repetitions; the regression rule (15%) may need a looser threshold for the GPU rows on shared runners.

## Checks
`cargo test -p xtask` (48), `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `fmt`, `xtask layers`, `xtask scorecard` (regenerated), `xtask perf --quick --bench bevel_bench` (all eight rows tracked).

title: Releasing a brush stroke no longer freezes: the commit takes the pixels the live stroke already drew (P32: 136 ms → 0.8 ms)
author: tanish2k09
body:
**Stacked on #2112 → #2110.** I'll retarget it as those merge. This is brush phase 4 of the owner-approved overhaul and fixes #2068 ("Brush rendering UI Lock").

## Why

On release, `finish_gesture` dropped the live stroke and ran `paint.stroke` over every point. That rasterized the whole stroke a second time, synchronously on the UI thread. Then `shown_as_document` marked the live preview as the document's *previous* revision, so the commit's damage (the stroke's bounding box, about 18 MP for a diagonal stroke) was re-composited and re-uploaded too, even though the canvas already showed exactly those pixels. The cost grows with stroke length.

## What

- **Engine (`brush_cmds.rs`, `lib.rs`):** `Session::offer_live_stroke(LiveStroke)` hands a finished live stroke to the next command.
  - `stroke_with` (`paint.stroke` and `paint.pencil`) takes the offered pixels only when the command, the document's id and revision, the params (minus points and seed), the seed and **every point** match. In that case it sets the target surface to the live one, with damage equal to the live bounds, and returns `"fromLive": true`.
  - Otherwise the offer is ignored and the stroke renders as before.
  - The command still goes through `Session::dispatch` (authorization, journal, one history step, `after_command`), so the journal and actions replay the same stroke from scratch.
  - `LiveStroke` now records its points and the document revision it started on.
- **UI (`canvas.rs`):**
  - `commit_brush_stroke` pushes the release frame's unfed points into the live stroke, offers it, runs the same `app.run("paint.stroke", …)` as before (with the same mask target, automation gate and jobs handling), and withdraws the offer.
  - On `fromLive`, it keeps the stroke's per-step damage for one revision (`CommittedStroke`). `damage_since` then gives each canvas cache only the steps it hadn't shown: usually nothing, the release frame's last dabs when it had any, and the whole stroke for a cache that neve…

title: raw: fit non-DNG colour to the camera's embedded JPEG
author: switch87
body:
Non-DNG raws (NEF, ARW, CR2, RW2, ORF…) have no colour calibration: they were developed with the neutral fallback (camera channels as sRGB primaries, no tone curve), which renders flat, grey and slightly green next to the camera's own rendering. Every such file carries a JPEG the camera rendered from the same sensor data — this fits that rendering per file and uses it.

**Method** (`crates/raw/src/look.rs`, independent implementation following the prose description in LightCraft's `docs/camera-preview-colour.md`, storytold/lightcraft#165): the white-balanced sensor data and the decoded, uprighted JPEG are reduced to a common grid of at most 256 cells on the long edge. Each cell pairs balanced camera RGB with the JPEG's linear ProPhoto colour. The model is the develop pipeline itself, `y ≈ f(M·c)`, fitted by alternating isotonic regression for a monotone tone curve `f` and weighted, ridge-regularized least squares for the 3×3 matrix `M` (weights scaled to approximate L\*, Tukey biweights against misaligned edges and local tone mapping, clipped and near-black cells excluded).

**Acceptance**: only a look that clearly helps is used — the reference must show the same picture in colour (lightness correlation ≥ 0.7, ≥ 2 % of cells with chroma > 4), the matrix must be plausible, and the held-out mean CIE76 ΔE must drop to at most 85 % of the fallback's. Otherwise the neutral sRGB-primaries fallback stays, with its usual note.

**Wiring**: `DevelopOptions.camera_look` takes the fitted `CameraLook` (matrix + tone curve) for one develop; `develop` reports "colour fitted to the camera's embedded JPEG (mean ΔE …)". `photocraft-raw` cannot decode JPEG, so `crates/io` decodes the smallest embedded preview at least 512 px long, converts it to sRGB when it carries another ICC profile, and develops files without calibration through the fit automatically.

**Tests**:
- `crates/raw`: recovers a known matrix and tone curve from synthetic camera-space patches to within 0.06; follows raw…

title: Select and Mask: 4x faster CPU refinement with exact octagonal morphology
author: excited-raccoon
body:
Shift Edge was scanning a full 3x3 neighborhood once per radius step. A 64 px shift meant 64 passes. This replaces those passes with an exact square/Manhattan-ball decomposition and **O(N log(r+1))** work, where N is the number of mask pixels.

## Results

**The actual tiled CPU refinement path is about 4x faster**, including guide sampling, guided filtering, boundary distances, quantization and mask assembly:

| Document | Before p50 | After p50 | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 6000 x 4000 | 3019.176 ms | 761.687 ms | 3.96x |
| 7200 x 5000 | 3705.934 ms | 920.891 ms | 4.02x |

- Circular soft-mask kernels: **20.76-172.16x faster** at 24-36 MP, radii 4-64.
- Dense fractional 24 MP matte, radius-64 dilation, with no constant tile shortcuts: **14.208 s -> 394.622 ms (36.00x)**.
- Serial 384x384 radius-64 kernels: **12.77-12.98x faster**.
- Large-mask workspace allocation bound drops about **40% at 24 MP / 43% at 36 MP**, from 192/288 MB to about 115/163 MB, including output and scratch for 16 workers.
- Every measured pixel and full refinement mask matches the previous implementation exactly.

AWS c7i.4xlarge, Xeon Platinum 8488C, 16 vCPUs, Rust 1.99.0, normal release profile. Warmup followed by three alternating paired runs; tables show medians. The soft-mask fixture is circular with a 7 px fractional edge. Full refinement uses the normal cropped selection on a synthetic RGB guide, radius 64 and Shift Edge +100%. UI rendering and history are outside that CPU timing. Memory figures are derived allocation bounds, excluding source/caller copies.

## How it works

The old alternating unit squares/crosses equal a square of radius `ceil(r/2)` followed by a Manhattan ball of radius `floor(r/2)`. The square uses van Herk / Gil-Werman window extrema. Five radius-d balls, centered here and d pixels along each axis, make a radius-2d ball. Binary doubling builds the remaining radius in logarithmic passes. Canvas clipping preserves the footprint.

Large masks use bounded halo t…

title: TGA: save the document's alpha channel as 32-bit alpha (#2124)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #2124.

Saving as Targa dropped the document's alpha channel: flat exports never read `doc.channels`, so a TGA got alpha only from layer transparency.

Photoshop 25.1, checked by scripting it (new documents saved as copies with `TargaSaveOptions`, bytes decoded): a 32-bit Targa's alpha is the document's alpha channel when there is **exactly one** (spot channels don't count); layer transparency is composited over white; with two or more alpha channels the alpha is opaque (all 255), even with `alphaChannels = true`; grayscale Targas never get alpha. 16-bit documents can't be saved as Targa in Photoshop at all.

## Change
- `io::flat`: a TGA export of an RGB document with exactly one alpha channel writes RGBA with that channel as alpha (32 bpp, 8 alpha bits). A transparent composite is composited over white first (with a warning). Rows are processed in bands.
- Several alpha channels: image unchanged, plus a warning that none was written (as in Photoshop). Grayscale or no channel: unchanged.
- 16-bit documents are written as 8-bit TGA (no panic).

## Tests
- `tga_writes_the_alpha_channel_as_32_bit_alpha` (8- and 16-bit; header, alpha bytes 255/128/0, colours, re-import)
- `tga_alpha_channel_wins_over_transparency_and_skips_spot_channels`
- `tga_ignores_several_alpha_channels_and_grayscale`
- `cargo test -p photocraft-io` all pass (new tests fail without the `src` change); `cargo clippy -p photocraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not included / not verified
- No Targa options dialog (16/24/32 bpp, RLE). A document *without* an alpha channel but with transparency still writes that transparency as alpha (Photoshop would composite over white at 24 bpp); kept to not change existing exports.

title: Distance fields on threads: bevel size changes 2-3x cheaper (#2119)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
Fixes #2119.

## Problem
Since #2006 a chisel bevel size change cost up to twice as much on the GPU canvas (12 MP, size 250: 286 → 446 ms), and the CPU compositor's edt-heavy fields were single-threaded.

## Cause
- A size change grows the effect region, so every step rebuilds the shape and both distance fields from scratch (growing them in place, idea 5, would not apply).
- The GPU path cut each field into bands of `max(128, halo)` rows, each computed from a window grown by the halo (`reach + 10` for the bevel fields). At size 250 that is 262-row bands from ~786-row windows: every pixel went through the transform and the edge refinement about 3×, a 12 MP region gave ~12 tasks for 32 threads, and the two fields ran one after the other.
- Banded and whole-region fields were not identical either: on a rebuild they differed from the CPU's field by up to 0.07 px (ellipse) and 1.3 px (600 discs) on a few dozen pixels at size 250 (ties between equidistant edge pixels resolve per window, and the refinement is sensitive to the winner).

## Fix
Two commits.
1. **compose: the Euclidean passes run on threads.** `edt_nearest` (column pass, row pass), `sharp_edges` (rows), `refine_edge_normals` and the final per-pixel maps of the bevel and plain Euclidean fields use scoped OS threads (`par_units`/`par_fill`: groups of rows handed out from a queue). Not rayon, for the reason `rows_par` gives (#276). Maps under 65536 px and wasm stay on the calling thread. Same arithmetic per unit, so the fields are bit for bit the old ones. `edt_nearest` returns `u32` indices (20 → 16 B/px).
2. **gpu: one window instead of bands** for the Euclidean kinds (chiselled bevels, precise glows). A rebuild is the whole region, exactly what the CPU computes. Partial updates (brush dabs) still compute the damage grown by the halo. Chamfer fields (shadows, strokes, spread) keep bands: their sweep is sequential. wasm keeps bands too (no threads; bands keep memory small).

## Result
RTX 4080 SUPER, 32 threads…

title: Layers: mask thumbnails update after Invert and other whole-mask edits (#2117)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #2117.

In Photoshop the Layers panel mask thumbnail updates immediately after any change to the mask (Image › Adjustments › Invert, fills, filters), not only after brush strokes. PhotoCraft kept a freshly added Reveal All mask white after Ctrl+I until you Alt-clicked it.

**Why:** the thumbnail cache is keyed on `surface_fingerprint`, which only hashed tile coordinates and tile `Arc` addresses. A new mask has no tiles, and inverting it only changes the surface's default pixel (1.0 → 0.0), so the key didn't change and the stale thumbnail stayed. Brush strokes create tiles, which is why they refreshed it.

## Change
- `surface_fingerprint` also hashes the surface's default pixel. Every cache built on it (layer and mask thumbnails, cached content bounds, the selection outline) now refreshes after edits that only change the default pixel, with no per-command special case.

## Tests
- `mask_thumb_refresh_tests::fingerprint_sees_the_default_pixel`
- `mask_thumb_refresh_tests::inverting_a_tileless_mask_refreshes_its_thumbnail` (drives the app: Reveal All mask, Layers panel drawn, Invert on the mask; the thumbnail key changes and matches the inverted mask)
- Both fail without the fix. `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- mask_thumb thumb channels` (31 passed); `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not verified
- Not checked visually in the running app or with a snapshot; the test checks the thumbnail cache key, not the texture's pixels.
- Tests live in a new module rather than `mask_thumbs_ui/tests.rs` to stay clear of open #1997.

title: Soft brushes paint soft strokes and thin lines stay even: a Gaussian-like tip and area coverage for tiny tips
author: tanish2k09
body:
Brush phase 1 of the owner-approved overhaul ("option A" after reviewing renders).

## Why

The brush audit found two tip-level causes of the "raw" look.

1. **Soft strokes came out hard.** Flow builds up where dabs overlap, as Photoshop documents and as `CoverageMap::accumulate` already does, and that stays. The soft tip, though, was a smoothstep that keeps most of its area near full strength. So the ~10 overlapping dabs of a stroke at the default 10 % spacing saturated it: a 100 px hardness-0 stroke had a soft edge **half** as wide as one dab of the same brush (16 px vs 31 px).
2. **Thin lines beaded.** Small dabs were point-sampled at pixel centres. A 1 px dab's total coverage swung between 1.00 and 1.17 depending on where it landed within a pixel.

## What

- **`tip_falloff` (`paint/src/lib.rs`):** the soft region now falls off as `(1 − t²)⁴`, a Gaussian-like curve.
  - It tracks `exp(−4.6 t²)`, reaches exactly 0 at the edge with a flat tangent, and is exactly reproducible: three multiplies, no `exp`, so goldens match on every platform and wasm.
  - The hard core is unchanged. `dab_coverage` keeps its 1 px edge ramp on top, and the brush preview and retouch footprints pick the curve up automatically.
- **Small tips (`paint/src/render.rs`):** computed, non-aliased tips under 3 px radius are rasterized by covered area. A 4×4 grid per pixel is used, with each sample anti-aliased over its own quarter pixel so coverage changes continuously with position.
- **Default spacing stays at 10 %.**
  - I tried Photoshop's documented 25 %. It restores more of the soft edge (82 % with smoothstep, 92 % with this curve), but renders showed visible **beading along soft strokes** with either curve: a 2–5 % ripple at the dab spacing, which is visible on dark colours.
  - That needs Photoshop-authored reference strokes to settle. The owner agreed to revisit it with an oracle.

title: Smudge: use the Brush Settings spacing for retouch strokes (#2140)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #2140.

**Why:** in Photoshop the Smudge tool, like every brush-based tool, lays its dabs every Spacing % of the tip diameter set in Brush Settings › Brush Tip Shape (1 % is a continuous smear, 1000 % isolated smears). PhotoCraft's retouch commands defaulted `spacing` to a fixed 25 %, and the UI never sends it, so the Brush Settings value was ignored. Size and hardness already came from the session brush; spacing didn't.

## Change
- `parse_brush` (`engine/src/retouch_cmds.rs`) defaults `spacing` to the session brush's spacing (Brush Settings), like size and hardness; an explicit `spacing` param still wins. Used by committed and live strokes.
- Because `parse_brush` is shared, Blur, Sharpen, Dodge, Burn, Sponge, Clone Stamp, Healing Brush, History Brush and Pattern Stamp follow Brush Settings spacing too, as in Photoshop.
- Params doc: `spacing … =Brush Settings spacing`.

- `blur_reduces_local_variance_and_sharpen_increases_it`: its Protect Detail sharpen stroke is pinned to `"spacing": 25`. At the brush's default 10 % it exceeds the test's bound, because Protect Detail clamps each dab to the working copy's current 3×3 range and creeps with denser dabs (pre-existing, just more visible now; worth a separate issue).
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine` (all pass), `panic_hunt -- --ignored`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- retouch smudge dab blur sharpen dodge` (20 passed).

title: EXR: Cryptomatte layers list, decode and hash to the specification
author: Elvis33LE
body:
Cryptomatte (specification 1.2) carries per-pixel object and material IDs with coverage in `<layer>NN.red`/`.green` channel pairs, announced by `cryptomatte/<key>/name|hash|conversion|manifest` header attributes — the ID channels Arnold, V-Ray, Redshift, Mantra/Karma and Cycles write next to the beauty pass. This adds the codec side of reading them, the foundation for a "click an object to select it" picker.

**API**

- `cryptomatte_layers(bytes, limits)` lists every layer from the headers alone: name, 7-hex metadata key, channels, the embedded manifest parsed into (ID value, name) pairs (capped at 16 MiB, entries that are not hex-string pairs are skipped like the reference readers tolerate), and a sidecar `manif_file` pointer (reading files stays with the I/O layer).
- `decode_cryptomatte(bytes, layer_name, limits)` returns the per-pixel (ID, coverage) pairs with coverage above zero, sorted by descending coverage. Channel matching is lenient about `CryptoAsset` vs `crypto_asset` naming and the short `.r`/`.g` suffixes, like the reference regex. Files with deep parts are refused, consistent with the other flat part decoding.
- `cryptomatte_id(name)` hashes a name the reference way — MurmurHash3 x86-32 (seed 0), the exponent fixed away from denormals/infinity/NaN, the bits read as an f32 value — verified bit-exact against the **official test vectors** from the reference test suite (`hello`, `cube`, `sphere`, `plane`, plus two UTF-8 names). `cryptomatte_key` exposes the 7-hex metadata key, `cryptomatte_preview_color` the reference preview colour.

**Tests** (`crates/codecs/tests/exr_cryptomatte.rs`, 11): the official hash vectors, the exponent fix, key/colour derivations, listing and manifest round trip on a synthetic file (stream 00 `cube` @0.6 everywhere, stream 01 `sphere` @0.25 in one column), exact per-pixel pairs, short suffixes, unknown layer name, a plain RGB file listing nothing, a corrupted manifest degrading to empty (samples still decode), a truncation swe…

With no pixel selection, Copy now includes masked pixel layers and multiple selected layers in main's existing whole-layer clipboard path. Paste preserves editable raster/vector masks and hidden colour, using the existing duplication, colour/profile/depth conversion and single undo step.

This replaces the original parallel snapshot implementation. `takes_whole`, `whole_layer` and `paste_layers` remain the shared path introduced by #2653 and #2686; no clipboard fields, dependencies or production UI changes are added.

- Multiple layers copy in document order; a selected group's children are included only once. Adobe documents [copying one or multiple selected layers](https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/desktop/create-manage-layers/create-layer-compositions/copy-and-paste-layers.html).
- A composited bitmap respects masks for external clipboard export and bitmap destinations. Underlying layer bounds preserve placement even when a mask hides all colour.
- Pasted layers receive fresh recursive IDs. Matching-format surfaces retain copy-on-write sharing. Paste translation moves unlinked masks too, without changing ordinary layer movement.
- Pixel selections, Cut and Copy Merged retain bitmap semantics. Paste Into/Outside explicitly use the bitmap and destination selection mask. Existing channel/mask routing and native clipboard ownership handling are reused.

The retained regressions cover mask preservation and independent edits at 8/16/32-bit depth, profile/depth conversion, unlinked masks, fully hidden raster/vector masks, multiple selected layers, parent/child normalization, one-step undo/redo, bitmap selection copy and Paste Into/Outside. Two UI regressions retain coverage of native bitmap export and external clipboard replacement.

Details and scope are in [docs/clipboard.md](https://github.com/optimalbytee/photocraft/blob/codex/mask-clipboard/docs/clipboard.md). Editable layers remain within one application session. Cross-process layered exchange, vector-path copying…

title: Add the Remove tool with non-local patch completion
author: JohnnYoru
body:
Adds Photoshop-style **Remove** to the J group (first in the flyout): paint over something, or circle it, and it is filled from its surroundings.

### What's in it
- **`paint.remove`** (`engine/src/retouch_cmds/remove.rs`): brush params plus `closeLoops` (default on: a stroke around an object also removes what it encloses) and `sampleAllLayers`. Runs as a background job (progress, cancel, one undo step), respects the selection and the transparency lock, and works on masks, alpha channels and the Quick Mask. A stroke whose bounding box is too large is refused before its coverage is rendered.
- **`photocraft_algo::nonlocal`**: non-local patch completion after Newson, Almansa, Gousseau and Pérez (*Non-Local Patch-Based Image Inpainting*, IPOL 2017):
  - texture features (local mean of |∂x|, |∂y|) in the patch distance;
  - onion-peel initialisation;
  - match fields upsampled between levels;
  - a best-patch final copy;
  - two additions: a median-capped Poisson correction of the edge mismatch, and a smooth correction of visible interior seams (after *Image Melding*).
- **`photocraft_algo::remove`**: loop closing, dilation, hole thickness, and tile-by-tile filling of sparse holes (long thin strokes).
- **UI**: `Tool::Remove` (J, first in the flyout), Sample All Layers option, tinted stroke trail, new icon derived from Lucide `bandage` (row in `ATTRIBUTION.md`). The label is translated in all 16 catalogs.
- `inpaint::complete` (Content-Aware Fill, Spot Healing, Content-Aware Move) is unchanged.

### Measurements
- **`remove_quality`** (new example): 20 holes in 5 public-domain photos; sources in `docs/development.md` › Remove Tool quality. The fill keeps **0.89** of the original's texture, against **0.54** with the Wexler/PatchMatch completion, which mostly produced blurred blobs. PSNR goes from 19.8 to 19.0 dB, as expected when a blur is replaced by plausible texture.

title: Pen pressure curve: Preferences › Tools shapes how pen pressure reaches every brush
author: tanish2k09
body:
Brush phase 6a of the owner-approved overhaul. It adds the global half of scorecard **TOOL-213-11** ("Editable pressure curve, global and per control"), as requested in #610 ("the pressure curve is choppy… please add curves").

Photoshop has no curve of its own and relies on the tablet driver's; Krita, Procreate and Clip Studio offer one. The audit found no curve anywhere in the engine, `paint` or `ui-egui`.

## What

- **Preference `tools.pressureCurve`:** `[input, output]` points in 0..1, linear `[[0,0],[1,1]]` by default. It's automatable through `prefs.set` and validated by `check_value`: 2..=16 pairs within 0..1, with errors that say what's allowed.
- **`photocraft_engine::prefs::PressureCurve`:**
  - A monotone cubic (Fritsch–Carlson), so a firmer press never gives less pressure.
  - It doesn't trust its input, because a whole-section update or a hand-edited preferences file can store anything. Non-finite points are dropped, the rest clamped, sorted and limited to one point per input (the later one wins), capped at 16, with outputs made non-decreasing. The curve is flat beyond the end points (a floor and a ceiling).
  - It evaluates in range for NaN and out-of-range input.
- **Stylus (`ui-egui/src/stylus.rs`):** every pen sample's pressure passes through the curve before any brush sees it, so the live stroke, the commit and the journal all agree. The curve is rebuilt only when the points change. A mouse stays at 1.
- **Editor (`ui-egui/src/pressure_curve_ui.rs`):** shown in Preferences › Tools under Use Tablet Pressure. Drag a point to move it, click empty space to add one, right-click a point to remove it (at least two stay). The Linear, Soft and Hard presets reuse translated strings. title: Masks: target a new layer mask and keep separate colour pairs for mask and pixels (#2166)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #2166.

**Why.** Photoshop keeps one foreground/background pair for layer masks and one for layer pixels, and swaps them when the edit target changes. Measured in Photoshop 25.1 via scripting:
- With red/blue, adding a layer mask targets the mask and shows white/black.
- Targeting the pixels brings red/blue back; targeting the mask again shows white/black.
- Green set on the pixels survives a round trip through the mask.
- A grey picked on the mask is remembered: it comes back on the next mask target, and also when a mask is added to another layer.

PhotoCraft left the colours alone when a mask was targeted, and adding a mask didn't target it.

**Change**
- Engine: `ToolState::target_mask` puts the current pair aside and brings back the other target's pair. The pair is app-wide, as in Photoshop; the mask pair starts at white/black, and colours picked while a mask is targeted are remembered for masks. Runtime state only (not persisted), no new command.
- UI: the effective target (mask flag set, active layer has a mask, composite channel, no Quick Mask) goes to the engine after every command, frame and control request. Mask thumbnail clicks, Channels clicks, the mask view and `ui.set maskTarget` all swap. A layer without a mask, or deleting the targeted mask, returns to the pixels' pair.
- Layer › Layer Mask › Reveal All / Hide All / Reveal Selection / Hide Selection / From Transparency now target the new mask, as in Photoshop.
- docs/control-protocol.md: a note on `maskTarget`.

**Tests**
- engine `tests::mask_and_pixels_keep_their_own_colour_pair` and ui-egui `clipboard_tests::targeting_a_mask_swaps_to_its_own_colour_pair` follow the Photoshop sequence above (end to end through `app.run` for the UI test).

title: Canvas: clip the Free Transform preview to the canvas (#2027)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #2027.

**Why.** Photoshop never shows pixels that lie outside the document canvas, also not while Free Transform is live: only the transform box, its handles and the reference point reach over the pasteboard (see the screenshots in the issue). PhotoCraft drew the moving pixels of a Free Transform or Warp preview wherever the box went, so a layer moved or scaled past the canvas edge stayed visible on the pasteboard.

**Root cause.** While transforming, the canvas composite hides the transformed layer and `transform_tool::draw_overlay` / `draw_warp` draw its pixels as a textured mesh through the canvas painter, which is clipped to the viewport, not to the document. The composited canvas itself (CPU and GPU) already clips correctly; the overlay is shared by both paths.

**Change** (`crates/ui-egui/src/transform_tool.rs` only)
- The preview meshes (Free Transform/perspective grid and Warp mesh) are built in document space, and `clip_to_canvas` clips each triangle to `[0, 0, width, height]` (Sutherland–Hodgman, UVs interpolated) before mapping it to the screen.
- Clipping in document space stays exact under a rotated or flipped view, where a screen clip rectangle would not. A preview fully on the canvas is drawn unchanged.
- The box, handles, reference point and path outline still draw over the pasteboard.

**Tests**
- New `transform_tool::tests::preview_pixels_past_the_canvas_are_hidden`: a box scaled past a 64×64 canvas, rendered at view rotations 0°, 30° and −75° flipped. Every preview vertex stays on the canvas, the canvas corners are still covered, and an in-canvas preview keeps its full mesh. It fails on main (`vertex [-16.0, -16.0] off the canvas`).

title: Window edges: easier to grab, theme-safe cursors, and no lost hover after a resize (#1581)
author: MrCloudy2
body:
Fixes #1581.

With the custom title bar (Windows and Linux) the app draws its own resize zones. On Linux they were hard to use. Three causes, all in `crates/ui-egui/src/titlebar.rs`:

1. **Cursor names some themes don't have.** Edges asked for `ew-resize` / `ns-resize`. capitaine-cursors (and other themes) don't ship those, so X11 fell back to the core font's big arrow and KDE Wayland showed the plain arrow: no sign you'd found the edge. Edges now use the one-sided cursors (`w-resize`, `e-resize`, `n-resize`, `s-resize`), as GTK and KDE window borders do. Corners keep `nwse-resize` / `nesw-resize`: in those themes the one-sided corner names (`nw-resize` → `top_left_corner`) are a different style from the edges.
2. **A thin zone.** 5 pt → 8 pt, about a native resize border. It trims the outer 3 pt of the left toolbar buttons; corners stay 12 pt so Close loses no more of its area.
3. **Hover lost after every other resize (KDE Wayland).** The compositor keeps the button release of an OS resize (`BeginResize`), so egui kept the edge pressed: zones stopped hovering until the next click, and egui-winit, which only re-sends a cursor that changed, never restored the resize cursor the compositor had replaced. Now:
   - `release_after_os_resize` (called from `raw_input_hook`) ends the press on the input after the hand-off, **only** while egui still has the button down and that input carries no release of its own. Where the OS delivers the release (Windows, X11), it adds nothing, so a doubled release can't become a click on what's under the edge.
   - On the first pointer motion after that, the default cursor is shown for one frame, so the resize cursor is sent again.
   - The egui-winit cursor dedupe going stale after a compositor-driven resize is arguably an upstream issue; this works around it locally.

**Tests:** `after_an_os_resize_the_edge_hovers_and_shows_its_cursor_again` (fails without the fix), `a_release_the_os_sends_is_not_doubled`, and `edge_zones_resize_unless_ma…

title: GPU startup: CPU mode on Linux falls back to Vulkan to present the window (#1337)
author: MrCloudy2
body:
Fixes the remaining part of #1337.

The marker half of #1337 (a failed CPU start pinning later starts) was fixed on Oct 8 by 43b4742e. What remained is the reporter's suggested fix: CPU rendering mode still could not start on Linux with NVIDIA.

**Cause.** CPU mode limits the window's wgpu instance to GL on Linux (`backends`). With NVIDIA's EGL the GL adapter can't present to the window (wgpu: "EGL says it can present to the window but not natively"), and llvmpipe isn't offered, so the adapter selector found nothing: every start exited with `CustomNativeAdapterSelectionError("no graphics adapter found")`. Preferences › Performance › CPU therefore made the app unstartable, and Preferences was unreachable to undo it.

**Fix** (`apps/photocraft/src/gpu_startup.rs`)
- CPU mode on Linux creates the instance with `GL | VULKAN`.
- `rank` puts every GL adapter before any Vulkan one in CPU mode, so wherever a GL adapter can present, the choice is exactly as before (llvmpipe, then hardware GL). Vulkan is only used to present the window when no GL adapter can; compositing stays on the CPU.
- Windows (DX12) and macOS (Metal) are unchanged: their CPU-mode instances still have one backend.

**Tests:** `cpu_on_linux_falls_back_to_vulkan_only_when_gl_cannot_present` (GL wins when it can present; Vulkan software then hardware when it can't; other modes rank as before); the `backends` expectation is updated. 19/19 `gpu_startup` tests pass.

**Checks run** (head `7b8c145e`, Linux x86_64):
- `cargo test -p photocraft --bin photocraft gpu_startup`: pass
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: pass
- **Live, NVIDIA RTX 3060 (proprietary driver) + Intel UHD 750, KDE Plasma 6:** with `"renderingMode": "cpu"`, `main` exits at startup with the error above on both XWayland and native Wayland; with this change the app starts and renders on both (verified via `ui.screenshot` over the control channel). No lavapipe installed, so the window used a hardware Vulkan ada…

title: Filters: preview at the scale OK applies (#2063)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #2063.

**Why.** In Photoshop a filter preview shows its features (ripples, dots, fibres, cells, flames) at the size the filter applies them. Our filter dialog previews large documents on a 1/k proxy and divides only a few known pixel params by k:
- Ripple, Diffuse, Oil Paint, Flame, Fibers and Mezzotint showed features k times larger than what OK applied.
- Params divided below their minimum were clamped: Pointillize's 5 px cells became 12 px, and nothing below about 8 px changed. This is the "nothing below 8 px" in the issue.

**Root cause per filter** (measured by comparing the k=4 preview with the full-resolution result downsampled by 4)
- Ripple: wavelength fixed at 8/16/32 px by its size choice.
- Diffuse and Mezzotint: work per pixel.
- Fibers: noise at a fixed frequency in pixels.
- Oil Paint: smoothing and bristle widths fixed in pixels.
- Flame: `length`/`width`/`interval` are pixel sizes that weren't scaled.
- Pointillize, Crystallize, Color Halftone: the scaled value got clamped to the minimum.
- Unsharp Mask, Gaussian Blur, Lighting Effects: already correct.

**Change**
- New `filter_dialog::preview_factor(command, params, k)` picks the preview's proxy factor per command:
  - The filters with fixed pixel sizes (Ripple, Diffuse, Oil Paint, Flame, Fibers, Mezzotint) preview at full resolution.
  - Other filters use the largest factor up to k at which no pixel-sized range param, divided by it, drops below the command's minimum.
- `canvas.rs` `ensure_filter_preview` uses that factor.

**Performance** (6000×4000, filter + flatten, release)

| Filter | k=4 (ms) | k=1 (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| Ripple | 273 | 3651 |
| Oil Paint | 313 | 3271 |
| Diffuse | 188 | 2282 |
| Fibers | 148 | 1968 |
| Mezzotint | 196 | 1827 |
| Flame | 56 | 489 |

At default params, Pointillize (5 px) now previews at k=1, Color Halftone (8 px) at k=2 and Crystallize (10 px) at k=3. Previews run on the background worker and are cancelled when superseded, so the window doesn't freeze, …

title: automation: accept absolute paths beneath the automation roots (#2176)
author: SBaksa
body:
Fixes #2176.

Automation file paths (`doc_open`, `doc_save`, render/export targets) only took forward-slash relative paths. With `--automation-read-root C:/`, `doc_open {"path": "C:/Users/me/a.png"}` was refused, while `Users/me/a.png` worked. The sibling apps take absolute paths.

**How it stays safe:** absolute paths are only translated, never resolved.
- `open_root` also keeps each root's absolute path. It's trusted launch configuration, and `std::path::absolute` is textual, with no link resolution.
- `request_path` compares an absolute request path with the root **component by component, as text**. Only the drive letter is compared without case. If the request lies beneath the root, the root's components are stripped and the remainder goes through the existing `relative_path` checks: no `..`, `.` or empty components, no `:` prefixes or streams, no device names.
- The result is opened through the **same `cap-std` directory capability** as before. Nothing is canonicalised or looked up on the filesystem, so link escapes and races are handled exactly as today.
- Each authority uses its own root: reads against the read root, writes and exports against the write root. With no root granted, an absolute path is refused as before.
- Unusual spellings of the same place (`\?\C:\…`, 8.3 short names, a root spelled through a symlink) don't match and are refused, which fails closed.

I deliberately didn't canonicalise the request path, as #2176 suggested and pdfcraft's `--root` does. That would resolve paths outside the capability, open a check-then-open race, and not work for new output files.

**Tests:**
- `workspace.rs` unit tests:
  - An absolute path beneath the root reads and writes the same file as its relative path, with both `\` and `/` spellings, including in a subfolder.
  - Refused, with nothing created: an absolute path outside the root, `<root>/../outside/…`, the root itself, `<root>/CON`, and `<root>/a.bin:hidden`.
  - Separate read and write roots are each enf…

title: Keep duplicated Smart Objects linked to shared contents
author: harrisonoconnorhover

title: Web: leave the JPEG XL DNG decoder out of the wasm (25.1 MB -> 24.3 MB)
author: echelon
body:
Follow-up to the failing **web build and wasm size gate** job (added by #1689), which runs `packaging/web/package.sh`.

## Root cause

The wasm was already near the line before today: `0493d06a` (before today's landings) built to **25,645,282 bytes**, over the 24 MiB (25,165,824-byte) gate the job enforces. Today's landings added another 1.34 MB, taking `782bcb67` to **26,980,503 bytes**. A twiggy per-crate diff of the pre-wasm-opt binaries (0493d06a vs 782bcb67) puts most of the growth in one place:

| --- | ---: |
| `jxl_*` crates (jxl-oxide, #2047) | +593 KB code |

| `serde_json` | +79 KB |
| ui-egui / engine / io / web (features) | +190 KB |

The rest of `.rodata` is embedded data: the i18n catalogs (1.84 MB of TSV) and the bundled Inter and JetBrains Mono fonts (1.52 MB).

`0c72d954` (already on main) deflates the catalogs and fonts and brings the wasm to 25,144,413 bytes. That is 21 KB under the gate, so the next feature would break it again.

- **photocraft-raw: jxl-oxide is native-only.** On wasm32, a JPEG XL-compressed DNG segment (DNG 1.7, compression 52546, e.g. Samsung Expert RAW) returns `RawError::Unsupported`: "JPEG XL-compressed DNG (DNG 1.7) can't be opened in the browser version of PhotoCraft; open it in the desktop app". title: Cmd held is the Move tool with the painting tools (Cmd+Alt duplicates)
author: texjer
body:
TLDR:

Split out of #1285 (part 2): holding Cmd (Ctrl off the Mac) makes the Move tool temporary with the painting, retouching and other non-selection tools, as in Photoshop. Cmd-drag with the Brush moves the layer, Cmd+Alt-drag duplicates it first, Cmd-drag inside a selection floats the selected pixels, Cmd-click picks the layer under the pointer, and the Brush is back when Cmd comes up.

## Change

- `hold_keys` gains `Temporary::Move`, a modifier rather than a rebindable key. `cmd_moves(tool)` lists the tools it applies to: not the Hand, Rotate View, Zoom, Crop, Slice, Path Selection, Pen, shape or Type tools (Cmd means something else to each), and not the selection tools, whose Cmd is already handled per press (#896).
- The canvas sets `PhotocraftApp::tool_override` for the frame; the tool state machine, `move_ui::moves_selected_pixels` and the tool modules that gate on the tool read `active_tool()`. The held-tool latch lasts through the release frame, so the Move's Up commits the move rather than reaching the Brush.

## Off the Mac: Ctrl+Alt-drag

There Cmd+Alt is Ctrl+Alt, which `brush_resize` already uses for the on-canvas brush resize. **Decision: the brush resize wins with the brush tools** (Brush, Pencil, Mixer Brush, Eraser… and Quick Selection, the tools `brush_resize::applies` to); with every other Cmd-as-Move tool (Gradient, Eyedropper, …) Ctrl+Alt-drag duplicates the layer. That keeps the gesture main documents ("Control+Alt+drag works everywhere") and Windows users keep Alt+right-drag for resizing too. For reference, Photoshop on Windows gives Ctrl+Alt-drag to the duplicate and leaves resizing to Alt+right-drag, so flipping it would be a one-line change in `brush_resize::is_gesture` if you prefer that.

Tests pin both layouts on any host: `cmd_alt_drag_duplicates_the_layer_then_moves_the_copy` now sends the Mac's ⌘⌥ explicitly (the old helper mapped Cmd to Ctrl on Windows/Linux, where the test would have hit the resize) and adds the Ctrl+Alt case wit…

title: Move tool on a locked layer: Photoshop's message
author: texjer
body:
TLDR:

Split out of #1285 (part 3): dragging with the Move tool (or Cmd with a marquee) on a layer it can't move now shows Photoshop's "Could not use the move tool because the layer is locked." instead of doing nothing.

## Change

- `move_lock.rs`: `blocked()` decides before the press goes anywhere: the Background or a position-locked layer without a selection, a fully locked layer whose selected pixels can't float, any locked layer among several selected. As in Photoshop the message comes when the pointer starts to drag; a plain click says nothing, and nothing is moved or added to history. The message is the ordinary Error dialog, so `ui.dialog.confirm` closes it.
- The float lock rule moves to `float_cmds::locked_for_float` (engine) so the UI asks the same question the float command does. The Background's selected pixels still move (its lock is partial).
- Auto-Select picks the layer under the pointer before the lock check, so the message is about the layer that would actually move.
- The string is in every catalogue, Dutch and Ukrainian included; each row sits right after `Move Tool`, so main's end-of-file appends don't collide with it.

## Checks

- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- marquee move_lock move_ every_tl_literal`: 65 passed (4 new).
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`.
- With #2248: whichever lands second adds the Cmd-with-the-Brush case to `selected_pixels_move_off_the_background_but_not_off_a_fully_locked_layer`.

title: kys import: first launch asks before importing; edit.keyboardShortcuts importKys (#1987 review)
author: texjer
body:
TLDR:

Follow-up to #1987 with @tanish2k09's review points: the first launch now **asks** before importing a shortcut set found beside Photoshop instead of applying it, `edit.keyboardShortcuts {"importKys": <xml>}` imports a set from agents, the CLI and MCP, the import error is translated, and `.kys` input is capped at 4 MiB.

## First launch asks

`kys_import::auto_import` is replaced by `offer_import` + `show_offer`. At the first launch with no shortcut overrides, if the newest Photoshop install has a live set that would change anything, a small centred window says "PhotoCraft found your keyboard shortcut set {set} from another image editor on this computer: {n} of its shortcuts differ from PhotoCraft's. Import it?" with **Import** / **Don't Import** (and a line that Reset All to Defaults undoes an import). Nothing is applied until Import. Either answer is recorded in `dialogs.photoshopShortcuts` (`{"source", "imported"}`), so it is asked once. A user who already changed a shortcut is not asked, and neither is a set equal to the defaults. `ui.inspect` shows a pending offer as `kysOffer`. The wording names no other product (#1985).

## Engine command

Parsing and label matching moved from `ui-egui` to `photocraft_engine::kys` (roxmltree moves with it), so headless sessions can import:

```json
{"command": "edit.keyboardShortcuts", "params": {"importKys": "<photoshop-keyboard-shortcuts>…"}}
```

The rows become `set` entries (a key equal to the command's default restores the default; keys also given in `set` win), applied through the existing path, so a moved key is taken from its old owner. The result gains `import` (`name`, `imported`, `set`, `unknown`, `unreadable`, `alternates`, `toolKeys`). In the engine the candidates are the command specs; the app's dialog passes its menu items first, so Photoshop's menu-order tie-breaks still apply there. Documented in `docs/control-protocol.md`.

title: Expand arithmetic expressions across numeric inputs
author: TheSeanLavery
body:
Numeric fields already support basic arithmetic, but parentheses, powers, remainder, and constants fail to parse, and a few separately implemented numeric inputs still accept only literal numbers. Expand the shared parser to handle expressions such as `(30+15)*2`, `2^3`, and `pi*2`, and connect manual kerning, crop-ratio components, Layer Style angles, and Indexed Color counts to it. Indexed Color continues to reject fractional and negative counts.

Preserve the existing shared-field behavior: plain numbers update live, arithmetic applies on Enter/Tab/click-away, and field limits and integer conversion remain unchanged. Limit expression length and recursion depth; reject malformed expressions, zero divisors, and non-finite results. No scripting or new dependencies.

title: Web: an embedding API (window.photocraft, postMessage, Photopea-compatible mode)
author: jmverges
body:
Closes #1614.

A page that embeds the web build can hand it a document and take the edited one back. Three layers, all in `apps/photocraft-web`:

**`window.photocraft`** (the app's own page)
```js
photocraft.info()                       // {app: "0.6.0", format: 1}
photocraft.isDirty()                    // + a "photocraft-dirty" event on window when it changes
await photocraft.open(bytes, "a.psd")   // ArrayBuffer / typed array / Blob → {warnings} once open; rejects with File › Open's error
await photocraft.save("psd")            // Uint8Array, exported as File › Export does; PSD/PSB/.pcraft leave the document clean
await photocraft.request("ui.inspect")  // the desktop control-channel methods, through PhotocraftApp::with_control
```

**`postMessage`** (cross-origin iframe, opt-in with `?embed=<origin>`)
- `{photocraft: id, method: "open" | "save" | "isDirty" | "info"}` gets `{photocraft: id, ok, result | error}`. `save` transfers an ArrayBuffer, and the app posts `ready` and `dirty`.
- Calls are taken from that origin only, and replies go to the parent at that origin only. The origin is normalised as `MessageEvent.origin` writes it.
- `request` is not offered here. The embedder names itself in `?embed=`, so that check keeps strangers out of the conversation but can't tell a trusted embedder from any site. The README says so and points to `frame-ancestors`.

**Photopea-compatible mode** (https://www.photopea.com/api/)
- `#{"files":[…],"server":{"url":…,"formats":["psd"]}}` in the URL opens `files` (fetched without cookies). File › Save in one of `formats` POSTs Photopea's body (a 2000-byte JSON header, then the file) instead of downloading.
- The parent gets Photopea's strings (`done`, `saving`, the server's `app.echoToOE("…")` text, `saved` / `error`), plus `loading:<name>` and `open-error:<name>`.
- One upload at a time, latest wins. A failed upload shows a notice in the app and keeps the leave-page prompt on until a save gets through. The status bar still says "…

title: Security: harden document exports and automation inputs

title: Add GitHub update checks
author: anuzdhk
body:
Part of #220 (Update check item only).

## What this does
- Adds **Help > Check for Updates** (manual check).
- Adds an **opt-out periodic background check**, controlled by a toggle in General preferences.
- Fetches the latest release from the public GitHub Releases API, compares it to the running version using semver, and shows an update dialog with the new version, release notes and a download link.

The release parser and rate-limit logic live in the engine; the menu item and dialog are wired into the egui shell.

title: Scroll the viewport while outlining with Polygonal Lasso
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Polygonal Lasso now scrolls the canvas while the pointer rests near or just past an active viewport edge, including between vertex clicks with the button released. This lets a zoomed-in outline continue into an offscreen area without manually switching to navigation.

Fixes #2231.

Scrolling keeps placed vertices in document coordinates, uses the existing rotated/mirrored view mapping and Overscroll bounds, and requests further frames for a stationary pointer. Returning to the interior, opening a dialog or using temporary navigation stops automatic motion. An unfinished polygon is tied to its starting document so switching documents or tools cannot later commit it to a different document.

- Native offscreen replay uses real pointer clicks/movement and 60 stationary frames at 60 fps on the same synthetic marker document. Main leaves the camera unchanged at all four edges. title: Add cargo xtask doctor: a fresh checkout now tells you what's missing
author: dottedt
body:
## What this does

Adds `cargo xtask doctor`, one command that tells you what a PhotoCraft checkout needs and, where it
can, installs it:

- the Rust components and the `wasm32` target the gates use
- Linux system libraries, and the macOS/Windows build tools
- the test corpus, `mdbook`, and the packaging/release tools

## Why

Right now that knowledge is spread across docs prose and CI YAML, so it's easy to miss. A checkout
without the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target only finds out when `cargo xtask wasm` fails with
`can't find crate for core`, with no hint at the fix. (That target is a separate `rustup target add`;
installing Rust doesn't include it.) The README also jumps straight to `cargo run`, assuming a ready
toolchain and system libraries.

## What you get

- `cargo xtask doctor` lists every prerequisite by area, with a present/missing status and the exact
  fix. `--fix` installs the required ones (`--fix --all` adds the optional tooling), `--json` is
  machine-readable, and `--markdown` regenerates the docs page.
- `docs/prerequisites.md`, generated from that list and checked in CI, so it can't go stale.
- `cargo xtask ci` / `cargo xtask wasm` check their own prerequisites first and fail with
  `run cargo xtask doctor --fix` instead of a confusing error.
- README "Get started" and the dev guide now say: install Rust, then run `cargo xtask doctor --fix`.

## On purpose, not included

- No `rust-toolchain.toml`. The project supports a range of toolchains (MSRV 1.95) and CI uses
  floating stable, so a committed toolchain file would override a contributor's toolchain and force
  the nightly fuzz job onto stable. `doctor --fix` installs into whatever toolchain you already use.
- CI-downloaded tools (nfpm, actionlint, zsync) aren't listed; they're CI details, not developer
  prerequisites.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p xtask`
- `cargo xtask doctor --check`
- `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask scorecard --check`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: Free Transform: the Hand tool no longer steals a resize drag (#2302)
author: maxm11
body:
## What

Fixes #2302. With the Hand tool selected, ⌘/Ctrl+T opened the Free Transform box, but then dragging a transform handle panned the view instead: the resize was lost and the preview appeared to vanish.

## Why

In `canvas_view`, the selected (or held) Hand had two effects:

- `if tool == Tool::Hand && response.dragged()` panned the view, skipping the `else if primary` branch entirely;
- `if tool == Tool::Hand { buttons = cleared }` then suppressed the tool event, so `tool_event` → `transform_tool::pointer` never saw the drag.

## Fix

A single `transform_owns_pointer` flag now gates both spots:

```rust
let transform_owns_pointer = primary && app.ui.transform.is_some() && temporary.is_none() && !middle;
let hand_pan = tool == Tool::Hand && !transform_owns_pointer;
```

So while a Free Transform box is open, only the **selected** Hand yields to the box (and only on the **primary** canvas that draws and drives it). The held Hand (Space) and a middle-button drag still pan, and a secondary document window's Hand is unaffected — addressing the two review findings on the first revision.

## Tests

- `transform_undo_tests::the_hand_tool_does_not_steal_a_free_transform_drag` — the original bug; fails on the old code.
- `transform_undo_tests::holding_space_still_pans_while_transforming` — the space-held temporary Hand still pans (fails if the condition drops `temporary.is_none()`).
- `canvas::tests::a_secondary_canvas_hand_pans_while_a_transform_is_open` — a secondary window's Hand still pans while the main window transforms (fails if the condition drops `primary`).

Full ui-egui lib suite green (1315), `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo xtask layers` OK.

`cargo xtask wasm` couldn't run locally (Homebrew rust without the wasm32 std component); the change is input routing only and CI covers wasm.

title: Layer Style: a disabled effect keeps its faint label (#2288)
author: maxm11
body:
## What

Unchecking an effect in the Layer Style dialog no longer leaves its name lit as though it were still on.

## Why

Two things kept the label from returning to its original look:

- the label colour was `on || is_sel`, and toggling a checkbox also selects the row, so the name stayed bright after unchecking;
- a present-but-disabled instance rendered in `text_dim`, while an effect that was never added uses `text_faint`, so a disabled effect never matched the other rows.

## Change

The left list's effect label now uses `if on { t.text } else { t.text_faint }`. Selection is still shown by the row fill. A disabled effect now reads exactly like one never added, as in Photoshop. (`is_sel` is still used for the row background.)

## Tests

- New regression test `layer_style::tests::disabled_effect_label_reads_as_faint` renders the dialog with an off, still-selected instance and checks the painted label colours; it fails on the old code (`#EEEEEE` vs `#A0A0A0`).

- `cargo xtask layers` OK.

Fixes #2288.

title: Canvas: UI Scale must not magnify the image (#2121)
author: maxm11
body:
Closes #2121.

**No product behaviour change.** The report — UI Scale magnifies the image, so 150% UI Scale draws 100% zoom at 150% — is the bug #1943 fixed in #1978. Interface › UI Scale is egui's `zoom_factor`, folded into `pixels_per_point` together with the display scale. `canvas_view` stores the view zoom as device pixels per document pixel, every point-space conversion divides it by the **full** `ctx.pixels_per_point` (`PhotocraftApp::point_zoom`), and the GPU shader multiplies it back to device pixels. So 100% is one document pixel per *physical* display pixel at any UI scale. The report is from v0.5.0, which predates #1978. This PR is test coverage plus comments, not a fix.

## Coverage

`crates/ui-egui/tests/ui_scale_canvas.rs` renders a black 60 px document through the real app on the **GPU and CPU canvas** at UI Scale 100/125/150/200% and zoom 100/200%, and measures the document's on-screen size from the pixels (like `checker_canvas.rs`). It stays 60×60 / 120×120 physical px at every UI scale.

Unlike a point-space assertion, it fails on either regression:
- canvas stops dividing by `pixels_per_point` → **75×75** at 125% UI Scale (both GPU and CPU tests);
- GPU shader stops multiplying back by `pixels_per_point` → **48×48** at 125% (GPU test; the CPU test is unaffected, as expected).

The tests skip when no wgpu adapter is present (repo convention).

## Comments

`View::zoom`, `PhotocraftApp::ppp` and `canvas_view` now name Interface › UI Scale explicitly, since `pixels_per_point` folds in both the display scale and the UI scale.

## Verification

`cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --test ui_scale_canvas` and `--lib` green (the one pre-existing macOS-only `mask_thumbs_ui` label failure also fails on a clean origin/main; it hard-codes `Alt` where macOS paints `⌥`). `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo xtask layers` clean. `cargo xtask wasm` can't run here (no wasm32 std component); the non-test ch…

title: Crop/marquee readout and Properties W/H/X/Y in the ruler unit (cm, mm, in…)
author: llduyll10
body:
## Problem

With Edit › Preferences › Units & Rulers › Rulers set to Centimeters (or mm, inches…), the rulers and the Canvas Size dialog follow the unit, but the lengths shown while working stay in pixels:

- the W × H readout beside the pointer while drawing or resizing a crop frame or a marquee;
- the Properties panel: a layer's Transform W / H / X / Y, and the document's Canvas W / H.

Photoshop shows all of these in the ruler unit, so laying out print work in cm means converting by hand.

## Fix

- `canvas::size_readout` formats the crop and marquee readouts with `UnitsAndRulers::format` at the document's resolution (`readout_in` does the formatting, so it can be tested without an app). Pixels still read `1644 px`.
- `layer_props_ui::LenUnit` converts document px ↔ the ruler unit (`Unit::from_px` / `to_px`, percent of the canvas size). The Transform fields and the Canvas W / H fields show the value in that unit with its suffix, and a typed value is converted back to px before the same `edit.transform` / `layer.translate` / `image.canvasSize` commands run. The 0.5 px change threshold is checked in px, so a small change in cm still applies.

## Tests

- New `marquee_tests::size_readout_follows_the_ruler_unit`: px, cm and mm readouts (1644 px at 72 dpi → `58.00 cm`).
- New `layer_props_ui::tests::transform_fields_show_and_take_the_ruler_unit`: cm ↔ px both ways, px unchanged, percent of the canvas.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui` (crop, marquee, props_layout, doc_props, layer_props filters), `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.

title: fix(adjust): colourize at 0% saturation greys out (#2326)
author: mroxso
body:
## Problem

With Hue/Saturation ▸ Colourise ticked, dropping the Saturation slider to 0% still left colour in the image (issue #2326). Photoshop removes all colour at 0% saturation, whether or not Colourise is on.

## Cause

The colourise path floored the saturation at 25%: `ss = s.abs().max(0.25)` in the CPU compositor and `ss = max(abs(sat), 0.25)` in the GPU shader. So a 0% slider still produced a 25%-saturated result, and low values (e.g. 10%) were silently raised to 25%.

## Fix

Take the slider literally: `ss = s.clamp(0.0, 1.0)` in both `crates/compose/src/adjust.rs` (the CPU oracle) and `crates/gpu/src/compose.wgsl`, keeping CPU/GPU parity. Hue is unchanged; lightness is preserved as before, so 0% saturation now yields the grey of the original lightness.

## Tests

- New regression test `hue_saturation_colorize_zero_saturation_is_grey` (compose): colourise at 0% saturation is colourless with lightness preserved for several hues, and 10% saturation is honoured exactly (no floor).
- `cargo test -p photocraft-compose` (184 passed), `cargo test -p photocraft-gpu --test parity` (34 passed, includes the colourise case), `cargo clippy -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo xtask layers` clean.

Closes #2326

title: UI font fallback: Thai and other non-CJK scripts draw in the Layers panel (#2275)
author: maxm11
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2275. A text Layer name in a script the bundled UI fonts lack (Thai, Arabic, Hebrew) showed missing-glyph boxes, even though the canvas rendered it with a fallback font.

**Root cause.** The canvas falls back through the Type tool's font database (`fonts::fallback_candidates`, which carries `THAI_FAMILIES`), but the egui shell's lazy UI fallback (`cjk_fonts.rs`) only knew the four CJK scripts — `missing_char` filtered to `cjk::classify`, so a Thai character never loaded a fallback and stayed tofu.

**Fix.** The UI loader now handles non-CJK scripts too:

- New `FontDb::fallback_face_for(c) -> Option<(family, bytes, face index)>` returns the first installed fallback face (in the same order the canvas falls back) whose charmap covers `c`; ASCII is skipped, bytes are bounded at 128 MB, malformed data yields nothing, never a panic.
- The loader classifies a glyphless character via `served::script_of` (Thai `Thai`, `Arab`, `Hebr`, `Deva`) and registers the returned face's bytes in the egui font stack, deduped per `(family, index)`.
- `exhausted` now waits for the non-CJK scripts as well, and `CjkFontPlugin` only requests a repaint when it made progress (a load, or a newly tried script), so a character no fallback applies to can't spin the frame loop.

CJK behaviour is unchanged: CJK characters still take the locale-ordered script-font path.

## Verification

- Offscreen render (`snapshot --safe-gpu`) of `file.new` + `layer.new.layer {"name": "สวัสดี ภาษาไทย"}`: the Thai name now draws in the Layers panel, Properties header and title bar. (Before: boxes.)

title: fix(cms): parse DeviceLink profiles (LUT channels vs output space, not a 3-ch PCS)
author: mroxso
body:
## Problem

A well-formed ICC **DeviceLink** profile (class `link`) failed to parse with `CmsError::Invalid("invalid ICC profile")`, telling the user their file is corrupt when it is valid and merely unsupported (#2337). This also made the deliberate `Unsupported` path in `link_stages` unreachable: no non-Lab DeviceLink ever got past parsing.

## Cause

`parse_profile` validated every AToB/BToA tag against a hard-coded 3-channel PCS. For a DeviceLink that is wrong: per ICC.1:2010 §10.4 the header's *PCS field* (bytes 20..24) carries the **output colour space**, not a PCS — a CMYK→CMYK press link legitimately carries 4→4 LUTs.

## Fix

- `Profile` gains `link_output: Option<ColorSpace>` — the output space, parsed from bytes 20..24 for the `link` class only (`None` elsewhere).
- Channel validation compares AToB outputs / BToA inputs against the link's output space (falling back to 3 for every other class, and skipping the check when the output space is unknown). Error messages now name both spaces for a link (`Cmyk→Cmyk`).
- `link_stages`: a Lab-input DeviceLink now parses, so the guard is tightened — only links ending in a PCS space (Lab/XYZ) may be linked; others get a clear `Unsupported`, never a silent mis-decode.
- `write::encode` writes the output-space signature into bytes 20..24 for DeviceLink profiles, so a parsed link re-encodes faithfully.

## Tests

- New `devicelink_profiles_parse`: a crafted CMYK→CMYK link (4→4 `mft2` A2B0/B2A0) parses, reports `link_output == Cmyk`, and yields `Unsupported` (not `Invalid`) as a transform source; a link whose AToB output contradicts its output space is still `Invalid`.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-cms` (incl. `system_profiles`, `malformed_profiles_are_rejected_without_panicking`), `cargo clippy -p photocraft-cms --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo check --workspace`, `cargo xtask layers` green.

title: cms: accept ICC DeviceLinks whose output isn't a 3-channel PCS
author: kavishkashehan726-sudo
body:
A DeviceLink's header PCS field holds its output colour space (ICC.1:2010 §7.2.7), so a CMYK→CMYK link has a 4→4 AToB0. The LUT channel check hard-coded 3 outputs and rejected such files as invalid, so users were told a well-formed profile was corrupt and never reached the "DeviceLink profiles cannot be used" error.

Check DeviceLink LUTs against the header's output space instead, and only let a Lab DeviceLink through link_stages when its tables end in 3 channels, so a Lab→CMYK link gets the unsupported error rather than building a mismatched transform.

Fixes #2337

title: HEIF: decode with heic-decoder instead of heic-rs (correct iPhone colours, 62/63 conformance)
author: Multipad-cyber
body:
Replaces heic-rs 0.1.1 inside `photocraft-heif` with [`heic-decoder`](https://crates.io/crates/heic-decoder) 0.1.0. The crate's API is unchanged, so `photocraft-codecs`, `photocraft-io` and the apps need no changes beyond the dependency.

**Disclosure:** I maintain heic-decoder. Like heic-rs, it is pure Rust, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, MIT OR Apache-2.0, has no C dependencies and builds for wasm. Its HEVC output is bit-exact against HM, the HEVC reference decoder. The numbers below come from running both decoders through `photocraft-heif`'s own pipeline (probe, then RGB/RGBA8 or RGB/RGBA16 output) on the same files.

## Why

### 1. iPhone photos open with the wrong colours today

iPhone HEICs have no `colr/nclx` box. They signal their colour (BT.601 matrix, **full range**, Display P3 primaries) only in the HEVC stream's VUI. heic-rs discards the VUI (`src/hevc/ps/vui.rs`: "every field is discarded") and falls back to BT.709 limited range (`Nclx::default`). As a result, every iPhone photo PhotoCraft opens is off by about 8 levels on average.

Compared with Apple's own decode (`sips` → PNG) of iPhone photos, mean |error| per channel in 8-bit levels:

| | heic-rs 0.1.1 | heic-decoder 0.1.0 |
|---|---|---|
| 5 unrotated 12 MP iPhone photos (personal, not shared) | **7.4 – 8.7** (max 26–28) | **0.08 – 0.11** (max 9–12) |
| `with-exif.heic` (corpus; has an `nclx` box) | 0.24 | 0.30 |

The corpus never caught this because its iPhone-like file carries an `nclx` box. Two new corpus files now cover it (see Testing).

### 2. More files open

| Files | heic-rs 0.1.1 | heic-decoder 0.1.0 |
|---|---|---|
| [Nokia HEIF conformance suite](https://github.com/nokiatech/heif_conformance) | 44 / 63 | **62 / 63** (only `multilayer004`, AVC, fails) |
| Sony a6700 4:2:2 10-bit camera photo ([public sample](https://github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/16018)) | error: "picture is not fully covered by slices" | opens, 4128×6192, HM-exact |

title: Linux/BSD: a second launch opens its files in the running window (#1540)
author: MrCloudy2
body:
Fixes #1540. Covers the single-instance part of #1266.

Opening an image from a file manager (Dolphin's Open With, a double-click) runs `photocraft <path>`, and every launch started its own app and window. Photoshop runs once; a file opened while it's running lands in the existing window as a tab.

**Change** (`apps/photocraft/src/single_instance.rs`, wired in `main.rs`; `cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))`)
- The first instance listens on a Unix socket. A later launch sends its paths (made absolute against its own cwd), waits for `ok`, and exits. The running window opens them through the existing `OsEvent::Open` path, the same one macOS Apple events use (`drain_os_events`: `open_paths` + `ViewportCommand::Focus`). So Workspace › Open Documents as Tabs applies as for any other open.
- **Socket:** `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/photocraft-<hash>.sock` (per user, 0700; shared by a Flatpak app's instances), else the settings directory. Mode 0600. The hash is of the settings directory, so separate `PHOTOCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR`s (tests, agents, portable copies) stay separate apps.
- **Protocol:** a version header (`photocraft-open-1\0`), then NUL-terminated path bytes (non-UTF-8 paths survive the trip). Connections without the header are ignored, input is capped (1 MiB, 4096 paths), and only absolute paths are taken.
- **Never blocks a launch:** a stale socket (crashed instance) is replaced; no answer within 2 s or any error starts the launch normally. The listener is dropped before the CPU-mode relaunch, which would otherwise hand its files to the exiting process.
- **Opt-out:** `--new-instance` or `PHOTOCRAFT_NEW_INSTANCE=1`. `--control` instances neither forward nor listen. Launches with non-UTF-8 paths start their own window, which reports them as before.
- std only: no new dependency, no `unsafe`.

**Tests** (8 in `single_instance::tests`): hand-off end to end over a real socket; a second listener defers to a live one; relative paths dropped; stale socket replaced; a non-answeri…

title: Fix/camera raw dehaze
author: XGenietony
