title: Handle allocation failures in large pixel operations
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What changes

Large copy, paste, erase, fill and transform operations can request full-image buffers or tile copies. This adds fallible raster allocation/read/write/convert helpers and propagates clear errors through the engine's staged edit paths so an allocation failure leaves document pixels and history unchanged. Warp output is reserved fallibly and extents above 400 MP are rejected before large intermediates are built. PSD export warns if optional smart-filter re-rendering cannot allocate.

Test-only allocation failpoints cover paste, erase, fill, transform, import and save transaction boundaries; save tests verify the prior file remains intact. Reliability scorecard rows REL-212-1 and REL-212-3 are marked partial because internal allocation paths across all format encoders/decoders still need a wider audit. This is a scoped implementation toward #212, not a claim that its entire codec-wide audit is complete.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-raster -p photocraft-algo -p photocraft-io --lib` (1,630 passed; ignored benches excluded)

Related to #212.

title: Image Size: Resample off keeps the pixel readouts honest (#2393)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2393

## What

With Resample off, `image.imageSize` keeps the pixel dimensions and only changes the resolution. The dialog still accepted pixel Width/Height edits, though, and showed them in its readouts (`200 px × 50 px`, `39K (was 20K)`). OK then kept 100 × 50.

The dialog now follows Photoshop when Resample is off:
- **Width/Height stay at the document's pixels**, and so do the Dimensions line and the Image Size estimate.
- **Pixels / Percent:** the Width and Height fields are disabled, because the pixel count can't change.
- **Physical units (in, cm, mm, pt, pica):** editing Width or Height changes the **resolution** to fit that size and keeps the pixels. Example: 100 px at 72 ppi set to 2 in wide gives 50 ppi.
- The constrain chain stays linked.

All changes are in `crates/ui-egui/src/sizing.rs` (dialog only, no engine change).

## Tests

These are kittest widget tests that drive real pointer and keyboard input into the Width field:
- `resample_off_keeps_pixel_dimensions_in_the_dialog`: typing 200 in px leaves the fields at 100 × 50 @ 72, and the readouts show `100 px × 50 px` and `20K (was 20K)`. After OK the document is unchanged.
- `resample_off_physical_width_changes_the_resolution`: typing 2 in gives 50 ppi, 100 × 50 px, before and after OK.

Both fail on `main`. They read `(200, 50, 72)` and `(144, 50)`, which reproduces the issue.

title: Modular side panels: move, add and close tabs and panels
author: luniiya
body: The right side panel was getting hard to work with, both as a user and in the code. Every panel was wired by hand in a few big files, you couldn't really add or close tabs, and there was no clean way to add new panels later (plug-ins for example). So I reworked it, taking inspiration from inspector style side panels in other editors. Before this, the side panel was 6 fixed groups and every tab was stuck in its group forever. You couldn't move a tab to another panel, you couldn't add a new panel, and closing a tab just hid it with no way back except digging through Window > Panel. In Studio, Properties was a floating card that didn't act like the other panels. And adding a new panel in the code meant editing an enum and a bunch of match blocks across several files. The goal of this PR is to make the user experience of the side panel better and the code more maintainable, with a way to add modules easily in the future. Each panel content is now a module, one file in crates/ui-egui/src/modules/. build.rs picks them up, so adding a module is just adding a file. The side panel is a list of panels, each holding tabs of modules. Old saved layouts and workspaces migrate on load. For Pro we tried to leave the UI as unchanged as possible since it's the Photoshop look, but we added the UX flows : - hover a tab to get a close button, or middle click it like in a browser - a small round + after the last tab to add a tab to that panel - Add Tab in the panel menu - a + at the bottom of the icon column to add a new panel Here is the before and after of the pro themes and the ux flow added : , Studio, Adwaita and the other themes get an inspector style side panel: card headers with menu, collapse and close buttons, a fold to an icon column where each icon opens its module as a flyout (right click for close tab / close tab group), a searchable pick…

title: Crop tool: Photoshop's default mode turns the image behind an upright box; Use Classic Mode (P), Auto Center Preview (#1919)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #1919.

By default, Photoshop's Crop tool keeps the crop box upright and turns the image behind it. Dragging outside the box rotates the image about the box centre, and dragging inside moves the image under the box. Auto Center Preview keeps a resized box in the middle of the canvas. "Use Classic Mode" (P) is the older behaviour, where the box turns and moves over a fixed image. PhotoCraft only had Classic Mode. title: Blend modes: Fill below 100% works inside the blend for Photoshop's special eight
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## What's wrong

In Photoshop, a layer's **Fill** and **Opacity** look the same for most blend modes, but not for eight of them (the "special eight"): Color Burn, Linear Burn, Color Dodge, Linear Dodge (Add), Vivid Light, Linear Light, Hard Mix and Difference. For those, Photoshop applies Fill *inside* the blend. PhotoCraft treated Fill as plain opacity for every mode, so these layers look wrong whenever Fill is below 100%. That's a common technique (e.g. Linear Dodge at low Fill for glows, Hard Mix at low Fill for contrast).

Example, Background `#c89664`, a `#64b4dc` layer in Difference at Fill 50%:

| | result |
|---|---|
| Photoshop 27.11 | (150, 60, 10) |
| PhotoCraft `main` (= Opacity 50%) | (150, 90, 110) |
| this PR | (150, 60, 10) |

## What Photoshop does (measured)

Scripted on Photoshop 27.11 (Windows): 24 single-pixel cases, eight modes × Fill 25 / 50 / 75%, with two colour pairs. Below 100% Fill, Photoshop pulls the layer's colour toward the mode's **neutral colour** (the one that leaves the backdrop unchanged) and blends that at full strength:

| modes | neutral |
|---|---|
| Color Dodge, Linear Dodge (Add), Difference | black |
| Color Burn, Linear Burn | white |
| Vivid Light, Linear Light | 50% gray |

Hard Mix has its own closed form: `clamp((b − f·(1 − t)) / (1 − f))`. It's the hard threshold at f = 1 and the backdrop at f = 0. Opacity still mixes the result in, as usual.

This reproduces **31 of the 32** measured values within 1 level. The exception is Hard Mix at Fill 75%, off by 3 in one channel: dividing by 1 − f = 0.25 magnifies Photoshop's 8-bit rounding. (Linear Burn gives the same result for Fill and Opacity either way, which is why it never looked broken.)

## Change
- **CPU** (`compose/psblend.rs`): `fill_is_special`, `blend_rgb_fill` and `composite_fill`. `composite_layer_plain`'s final blend of pixel, shape and type layers (`blend_into_fill`) passes Opacity and Fill separately. Other modes, and Fill = 100%, take exactly the previous p…

title: Move tool: Ctrl/Cmd+arrow nudges the layer from any tool (#2474)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #2474.

## Why
In Photoshop, holding Ctrl (Cmd on macOS) is the temporary Move tool for most tools. So Ctrl/Cmd+arrow nudges the selected layer 1 px, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+arrow 10 px, and Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+arrow duplicates first. PhotoCraft only nudged with the Move tool itself. egui's `consume_key` never ignores an extra Ctrl/Cmd, so Ctrl/Cmd+arrow did nothing anywhere, not even with the Move tool.

## Change
- `hold_keys::cmd_nudges`: Ctrl/Cmd+arrow nudges in three cases:
  - wherever Ctrl/Cmd is already the temporary Move tool for drags (`cmd_moves`, #249)
  - with the Move tool
  - with the selection tools, where it moves the selected pixels as Photoshop's temporary Move tool does; plain arrows still move the outline (#1428)

  It doesn't nudge during Free Transform, while editing text, or while a polygon or Magnetic Lasso border is in progress.
- `move_mods::arrow_keys` adds Command to its modifier patterns in those cases, so the existing nudge does the work (1 / 10 px, Alt duplicates first).
- `nudge` decides on floating the selected pixels as the Move tool. The temporary-tool override exists only inside the canvas frame, so from the shortcut handler a Brush or Marquee would otherwise have been seen as the active tool.
- Direct Selection now keeps Ctrl/Cmd for itself, like Path Selection (in Photoshop, Ctrl/Cmd there switches between the two). Pen, shape, Hand, Zoom, Crop and Type keep their current behaviour.
- Focused widgets and text fields keep their own Ctrl/Cmd+arrow handling, because the nudge only runs with `Focus::None`.

New, with real key events and both Windows (Ctrl) and macOS (⌘) modifiers:

title: Select › Modify › Smooth: a hard threshold, as in Photoshop, not soft edges
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## What's wrong

Select › Modify › Smooth is meant to round a selection's corners and drop specks. PhotoCraft box-averaged the selection and then applied a soft contrast curve, `(v − ½)·4 + ½`, which leaves a band of **half-selected pixels along every edge**, including straight ones. Fill or delete after Smooth and you get a grey fringe that Photoshop doesn't produce.

32×32 square at (16,16) in 64×64, Smooth 8 px, filled white:

| point | Photoshop 27.11 | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| (16,32) plain left edge | 255 | 158 | 255 |
| (18,18) | 0 | 45 | 0 |
| (19,19) | 0 | 126 | 0 |
| (20,20) | 255 | 214 | 255 |

## What Photoshop does (measured)

Scripted on Photoshop 27.11: every sampled pixel along the edge row (x = 8…24) and the corner diagonal is exactly 0 or 255. The straight edge stays at x = 16, and the corner is cut exactly where a box average over the (2r+1)² window crosses ½. For example, (19,19) averages 0.498, giving 0, and (20,20) averages 0.585, giving 255.

## Change
- `algo::selection_blur::smooth` (and its test oracle): the same box average, then a hard threshold at ½ instead of the contrast curve.

## Tests
- `selection_blur::tests::smooth_matches_photoshop`: the measured row and diagonal, exactly.
- `smooth_matches_direct_box` now allows the fast and direct versions to differ only where the average is within 1e-4 of ½. A hard threshold turns summation-order rounding there into a 0/1 flip; it found one such pixel.

## Checks run (head `a1d9e70f`, Linux x86_64)
- `cargo test -p photocraft-algo --lib selection`: pass; `cargo test -p photocraft-engine` filtered to `smooth` and `select`: pass
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-algo --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: clean in changed files
- Re-ran a 121-case Photoshop parity batch through `photocraft-cli`: only the Smooth case changed, and it now matches exactly.

**Not measured:** Smooth on an already-soft (feathered) selection. With a hard threshold that becomes hard too; Photoshop wasn't che…

title: Capture marquee selection modifiers at mouse press
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:

title: Marquee: keep one-pixel rows and columns on release (#2391)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2391

## Root cause

`finish_gesture` (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`) deselected any marquee rectangle narrower or shorter than 2 px (`x1 - x0 < 2.0 || y1 - y0 < 2.0`). The live preview (`marquee_preview_px`, which draws the ants and the W/H readout) showed any whole-pixel rectangle, including 1 px wide ones. The 2 px threshold was really a click check, because floor/ceil turns a click between pixel edges into a 1×1 rectangle. As a result, a deliberate one-pixel column or row showed while dragging and then left no selection on release. If the drag started outside an existing selection, it also cleared that selection.

## Fix

- `marquee_preview_px` now decides "still a click" by screen distance (`shape_dialog::is_click` at the view zoom, 3 screen px). It also returns `None` for zero-area rectangles.
- Release commits exactly `marquee_preview_px`, so the preview and the committed selection can't disagree. `None` still deselects, so a plain click clears the selection as in Photoshop.
- When the release would deselect, no ants are drawn.

## Tests

`marquee_tests::a_one_pixel_column_or_row_is_kept_on_release` is a trimmed version of the issue's kittest reproduction. It uses real pointer events at 800% with snapping off.
- It runs the Rectangular and the Elliptical Marquee, each drawing a 1 px column and a 1 px row.
- Each case runs with and without an existing selection that the drag starts outside of.
- It checks the preview and readout during the drag, the committed selection after release, and that a plain click still deselects.

The test fails on `main`: it gets `Rect{0,0,0,0}` where it expects `Rect{10,10,11,51}`.

```
cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- marquee canvas select drag snap hold_keys shape_dialog   # 385 passed, 4 ignored
cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt -p photocraft-ui-egui -- --check
```

title: Select › Modify › Border: Photoshop's soft band, 2r wide, not a hard r-pixel ring
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## What's wrong

Select › Modify › Border built a **hard** band only **r** pixels wide (expand by r/2 minus contract by r/2). Photoshop's Border is a **soft** band **2r** wide, centred on the selection edge, which is what makes it useful for soft halos and edge clean-up. In PhotoCraft the same Border 4 gave a thin, hard-edged ring.

32×32 square at (16,16) in 64×64, Border 4 px, filled white; row y = 32, x = 8…24:

| | values |
|---|---|
| Photoshop 27.11 | 0 0 0 0 **63 127 191 255 255 191 127 63** 0 0 0 0 0 |
| `main` | 0 0 0 0 0 0 255 255 255 255 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 |
| this PR | 0 0 0 0 64 128 191 255 255 191 128 64 0 0 0 0 0 |

## What Photoshop does (measured)

Scripted on Photoshop 27.11: the band fades linearly from fully selected at the edge to nothing r pixels out, on both sides. Along the inside of a corner, the diagonal (16,16) to (19,19) reads 255, 191, 127, 63, so it follows the distance to the edge. Formally: a pixel `D` away (centre to centre) from the nearest pixel on the other side of the edge is selected `1 − (D − 1) / r`.

## Change
- `algo::selection::border`: that formula, using the existing exact distance transform (`selection::edt`) on both sides of the edge. As with Expand and Contract, "inside" means coverage ≥ ½.

## Tests
- `selection::tests::border_matches_photoshop`: the measured row and corner diagonal (±1).
- `expand_contract_border` still holds.
- The EDT refactor guard (`selection_modifiers_keep_fractional_coverage`) pinned Border to the old expand − contract formula. It now covers only Expand and Contract, with a pointer to the new test.

title: Move tool: outline follows the moved layer (#2413)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2413

## Root cause

The blue box in the screenshots is View › Show › Layer Edges (`0x2d8ceb`). `canvas_view` painted it **before** reading the frame's tool events, and painted it from the **session** document. Both bugs come from that:

1. **Wrong layer:** the Move tool's press, including its Auto-Select `layer.pickAt`, runs after the outline was painted. So the frame in which Auto-Select picks a new layer still outlined the previously selected one. If no further frame was painted, it stayed there.
2. **Trailing:** during a live Move drag, the pixels come from the preview document at the drag offset (`move_ui::display_doc`). The outline used the committed, unmoved bounds, so it stayed where the layer started until release.

## Fix

- `canvas.rs`: the outline's z-slot is reserved where it used to be drawn (`painter.add(Shape::Noop)`), so it still sits under the selection outline and tool overlays. The slot is filled after the tool events (`painter.set`) from the new `layer_edges_rect`. That rect is the content bounds of the active layer, cached per tile, shifted by the offset the image was drawn with this frame.
- `move_ui.rs`: `MovePreview` records the `moving` layers (the move targets plus their descendants) once per preview revision, so there is no per-frame scan. The new `shown_offset` returns the drawn offset for a layer.

## Tests

New `move_outline_tests.rs` uses egui_kittest with real pointer events through `canvas_view`, and reads the stroked rect from the frame output:
- `the_outline_belongs_to_the_layer_auto_select_picked`: B is active, then a press and drag on A. The pick frame outlines A, the next frame outlines A at +5 px, and after release the outline is where A landed.
- `the_outline_moves_in_lockstep_with_a_fast_drag`: four large jumps, one per frame. Each frame, the outline is where the layer is drawn. After release, it is where the layer was dropped.

Both fail on `main`. The pick frame drew B's rect, and the drag outline stayed at the orig…

title: Text fields: copy, cut and paste through the Mac menu's key equivalents
author: Trade-Mottoes
body:
With the native menu bar, AppKit takes ⌘C / ⌘X / ⌘V as Edit › Copy, Cut or Paste's key equivalent whenever that item is enabled. The key then reaches egui as a plain key press, and text fields ignore it, because they act on `Event::Copy` / `Cut` / `Paste`. As a result, pasting text into a dialog's input or a panel's search box only worked while PhotoCraft's own clipboard was empty.

While typing, `clipboard_keys` now turns those presses into Copy / Cut, and turns ⌘V into `RequestPaste`. egui-winit never sends these presses itself, so behaviour without the native menu is unchanged.

This overlaps #2466, which does the same for the type tool's editor only (`!text_edit_focused()`). This version also covers egui text fields, where the native menu takes the key in the same way. Happy to rebase onto #2466 if that lands first.

**Test:** `menu_key_equivalents_reach_a_text_field_as_clipboard_events`. It fails without the change. `cargo xtask ci` passes on macOS (fmt, clippy, test, layers, wasm).

title: Colour swatches open PhotoCraft's Color Picker: filter dialogs, Preferences, Note, Count, artboard (part of #2144)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Part of #2144 ("use the same color picker throughout the app"). #2049 did Layer Style and the text styles, and #2019 did Edit › Fill and Edit › Stroke. This PR does five more places; the rest (adjustment editors in Properties, the shape tools' options-bar fill/stroke, and the Filter Gallery) follow in a second PR.

## Problem

These swatches opened egui's compact colour popup instead of PhotoCraft's Color Picker (HSB/RGB/Lab/CMYK and hex fields, gamut warning, the image eyedropper, OK/Cancel):

- filter dialogs with a colour parameter: Color to Alpha's colour, Picture Frame's vine, flower and leaf colours, Tree's colours, and others;
- Preferences colours (guides, grid, slices, …);
- the Count tool's group colour (options bar);
- the Note tool's colour (options bar);
- an artboard's custom background colour (Properties).

The Count and Note swatches also used `color_edit_button_rgb`, which treats its values as **linear** RGB, but the values they edit are sRGB (`count.setGroup` colours and the `notes.add` colour). So the popup showed and stored a different shade from the one in the document.

title: Perf nightly: macOS, Linux and Windows runners, one baseline per machine
author: 1Git2Clone
body:
**TL;DR:** the perf nightly's regression check never ran: its only baseline came from an M4 Pro, not the runner. It now runs on macOS, Linux and Windows, each against a baseline from its own hardware, and fails on regressions over 25 % that a retry confirms. Cost: ~18–24 min per runner per night. Plain `cargo xtask perf` is unchanged.

> [!NOTE]
> GitHub's hosted runners are shared resources, so timings are noisy. CI flags regressions over 25 % instead of the local 15 %, retries the benches once before a failure counts, and only reports regressions when a CPU canary says the machine is over 20 % slower than when its baseline was recorded. This isn't fine-grained, but it catches big regressions (e.g. a cache that stops working); a dedicated runner would allow the 15 % default again.

## Why

Until now every perf number came from a single machine: `perf/baseline.json` was recorded on one M4 Pro, and Linux and Windows performance was never measured. The [perf nightly](https://github.com/1Git2Clone/photocraft/blob/perf-nightly-runner-matrix/.github/workflows/perf-nightly.yml) ran on a macOS runner whose machine class never matched that baseline, so its regression check was skipped every night. `xtask` rightly refused to compare across machines, but the run still passed, so nothing flagged it.

## It already caught a regression

On its first run against the previous baselines (recorded on an older upstream), the Linux job [failed](https://github.com/1Git2Clone/photocraft/actions/runs/38071213180/job/114268917615), as designed: on a quiet runner (CPU canary 140 / 140 ms) the content-aware scenarios regressed in the run and again in the retry.

title: Speed up Iris Blur without changing output
author: optimalbytee
body:
Iris Blur repeatedly recalculates pin geometry and blurs trailing source margins that cannot affect the output. This prepares pin geometry once per tile, skips saturated distance calculations, premultiplies contiguous samples and trims each Gaussian level's right/bottom halo. The original top/left running-sum order is preserved for exact output, including HDR cancellation.

The existing seven Gaussian levels, weights, radii and sample counts remain unchanged. Tilt-Shift and Field retain their full windows. No UI, engine command, preview-worker, dependency or architecture-specific code changes are included.

Frozen-base differential tests check exact finite f32 bits (including signed zero) and matching NaN classifications across channel counts, RGB/Gray/CMYK/Lab, U8/U16/F32, alpha, selections, tile sizes, HDR, extreme/nonfinite pin geometry and cancellation.

### Performance

Source handoff measurements on Windows x86_64, Ryzen 7 9700X, Rust 1.99.0, normal release profile and eight Rayon workers. Full-size baseline medians pool six samples from two rounds around three candidate samples; proxy cases use five samples per implementation.

| Workload | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 24 MP, default blur 15 | 626.8 ms | 426.9 ms | 1.47× |
| 24 MP, rotated blur 80 | 1395.7 ms | 1092.7 ms | 1.28× |
| 24 MP, two pins | 1789.9 ms | 1016.2 ms | 1.76× |
| 36 MP, two pins | 2595.8 ms | 1822.8 ms | 1.42× |
| 36 MP, HDR F32 blur 80 | 2346.8 ms | 1702.1 ms | 1.38× |

title: perf: Reduce allocations and redundant work in image processing
author: reneleonhardt

## Summary

- Use `zlib-rs` with runtime CPU detection for workspace `flate2`.
- Remove redundant PNG filter passes, PSD interleave copies and RLE payload buffers.
- Accelerate ZIP CRC-32 and avoid repeated sparse-mask allocations and copies.
- Reuse bounded compositor scratch, tone tables and pure Rust zstd workspaces; inline pixel compositing and PSD sample encoding.
- Add optional `photocraft-format/native-zstd` compression and bounded tile decoding on native and WASM. Pure Rust remains the default; the bundle format is unchanged.

## Validation

Native timings use Apple M4 Max/macOS ARM64, Rust 1.99 and matched release settings (O3, no LTO, 16 codegen units). Saves run in memory; profiling follows timing.

The full `cargo xtask perf` suite compared `main` at `05e0b1f` with the compression, allocation and PNG-filter changes. Later optimizations have separate focused measurements below.

| Operation | Main p50 | Optimized p50 | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Open layered PSD, 20 MP | 239.5 ms | 221.0 ms | −7.7% |

| Save PSD, 36.2 MP | 689.8 ms | 626.6 ms | −9.2% |

author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
Fixes #2490

`app.open` over the control/MCP channel could not open `.pcraft` files in **directory** form — the native on-disk layout the app's own File › Save and crash recovery write — because the automation read path serves regular files only. Agents had to round-trip through `photocraft-cli convert`.

A unit test feeds a reader that ignores the hint and asserts the bound.

A regular file at the path is `Ok(None)` — a structural fallback marker, not an error-string match — so the zip form falls back to the bytes path without a cross-crate string contract. Tests cover directory loading, the zip fallback, missing paths, non-regular entries, and escaping symlinks.

title: Pixelate: CMYK Facet 13.7x faster, Lab halftone 5.0x faster
author: excited-raccoon
body:
Facet was calculating the same 3x3 quadrants up to four times, including their color conversions. Color Halftone was rereading the same five source taps and recalculating a dot's radius for neighbouring pixels.

This shares Facet's luma and quadrant statistics through a three-row ring, and caches each halftone cell's radius in its rotated screen grid. Both keep the original arithmetic order, tie choices, coverage and color handling. Scratch is bounded per tile, with a direct calculation fallback.

Full tiled filter application on 24 MP images, 16-vCPU m7i.4xlarge, three alternating before/after pairs:

| Filter / model | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Facet / CMYK8 | 7.888 s | 0.574 s | 13.74x |
| Color Halftone / Lab8 | 3.589 s | 0.718 s | 5.00x |
| Facet / RGB8 | 0.684 s | 0.312 s | 2.20x |
| Color Halftone / RGB8 | 1.137 s | 0.604 s | 1.88x |

These timings include tile reads, filtering, assembly, depth conversion, writeback and pruning. All 36 full-image comparisons were byte-identical, across 24/36 MP, 8/16/32-bit samples and halftone radii 2/8/64.

The original scalar kernels are kept as independent test oracles. Tests cover all color models, transparency, soft selections, tile seams, thin regions, HDR/non-finite samples and fallback paths.

Passed: 401 algorithm tests, clippy with warnings denied, formatting, dependency layering, the full wasm check, `cargo xtask perf --quick`, and scorecard generation.

[Reproduction commands, all timings and output hashes](https://github.com/excited-raccoon/photocraft/blob/perf/pixelate-reuse-20261010/docs/pixelate-performance.md).

title: Move tool: Auto-Select picks a type layer inside its text bounds (#2370)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2370

Part 1 (a locked layer shouldn't move) was already fixed by #2249. This PR covers part 2.

## Root cause
`layer.pickAt` (Move tool Auto-Select, and Cmd/Ctrl-click while Auto-Select is off) hit-tested every layer by the alpha of the single pixel under the pointer. A type layer is mostly transparent, so a click in the gap between its letters picked the layer below it, and the drag moved that layer instead of the text.

## Fix
In Photoshop, Auto-Select picks a type layer anywhere inside its text bounds. `layer.pickAt` now does the same: a type layer is hit anywhere inside the bounds of its rendered text (`content_bounds()` of the type cache, which is in document space, so it follows the layer's position and transform). Everything else is unchanged:
- Pixel, shape, smart object and fill layers keep the pixel hit test.
- Hidden layers and hidden groups, artboard clipping, layer masks, fully locked layers (clicked through) and Group mode work as before.
- The right-click canvas layer list (`"list": true`) still names only the layers with pixels under the pointer. `pick_cmds::layers_at`, which the layout bench/perf tests use, keeps its pixel-only behaviour.

The hit area is the text's pixel bounds, not a paragraph text box.

## Tests
In `crates/engine/src/pick_cmds.rs`:
- `auto_select_hits_a_type_layer_between_its_letters`: a synthetic type cache with two glyph blocks. A click in the gap picks the type layer, a click outside the bounds picks the Background, and the right-click list is unchanged.
- `auto_select_hits_typed_text_in_a_gap_between_letters`: the same check through `type.create` (`"I   I"`) and the type engine.

Both tests fail with the fix disabled (they pick the Background instead of the type layer) and pass with it.

title: Preserve HDR range in float adjustments and stack statistics
author: grlessa
body:
Neutral Exposure, Levels and Curves layers currently clamp RGB float documents to 0..1, so an unchanged pixel such as `[4, 2, 0.5]` loses its highlights. Stack statistics also clamp float results: the mean of 2 and 4 becomes 1 instead of 3.

This preserves Exposure highlights, evaluates 32-bit RGB Levels analytically over signed/HDR samples, and bypasses the bounded Curves LUT for untouched float RGB channels. Exposure retains negative results with signed gamma too. CPU and GPU implement the same behaviour. Stack statistics retain their numerical results; the destination surface handles integer clipping. Edited Curves keep their current spline/LUT behaviour; this does not claim full Photoshop HDR extrapolation parity.

Regression tests cover neutral and edited adjustments, negative values, alpha, full document rendering, GPU parity (including paged rendering), and statistical HDR results. The new compose regressions failed on the base revision before the fix. Existing integer adjustment paths remain covered by the original tests and real-file corpus.

The PSD reference comparison also quantized float merged planes through `composite_rgba8`, clipping the signed/HDR values it should test. The new path reads native-depth RGB/Gray float planes and retains the merged-alpha marker while removing layers, so an opaque extra channel is not interpreted as transparency. Independent synthetic planes and Photoshop RGB32/Gray32 Exposure/Levels oracles cover both problems. No tolerances or corpus floors are relaxed.

Validation on main `0b4b1e42`, Rust 1.95, macOS/Metal, with separate artifacts per branch and no application window:

- CPU compositor: **205 unit + 3 artboard tests passed**, 1 pre-existing ignored; algorithms: **443 passed**, 18 pre-existing ignored.
- GPU: **24 unit, 44 parity, 3 device-loss and 1 vector-mask tests passed**. Real Metal execution is logged; no adapter skip occurred.

title: Speed up large Content-Aware Scale operations
author: Elvis33LE

Content-Aware Scale recomputes its full-resolution seam energy map for every removed seam. On tall images, this patch finds seam paths on a vertically averaged proxy (up to 512 rows), maps the paths back to source columns, then removes original full-resolution pixels. Small shrinks keep the existing exact path; output dimensions and pixel depth are unchanged.

On the same Windows machine (AMD Radeon 860M), the 24 MP release scenario measured 12,187 ms before and 2,640 / 2,685 / 2,641 ms after (median 2,641 ms, p95 2,685 ms): about 4.6× faster and below P28's 3,000 ms target. The checked-in 954,192 ms result is from an Apple M4 Pro and is stale; it was not replaced with measurements from a different machine class.

This addresses the Content-Aware Scale row of #211. The broader issue remains open for its other algorithms and workflows.

## Validation

Before, a Filter Gallery choice given an unlisted name was ignored (`set_choice` returns false, nobody checked it) and the filter ran with the default, replying `ok`. Found on main for:

- Artistic: `paintDaubs.brushType`, `roughPastels.texture`/`.light`, `underpainting.texture`/`.light`
- Brush Strokes: `sprayedStrokes.strokeDirection`
- Distort: `glass.texture`
- Sketch: `basRelief.light`, `conteCrayon.texture`/`.light`, `graphicPen.strokeDirection`, `halftonePattern.patternType`, `plaster.light`
- Texture: `grain.grainType`, `texturizer.texture`/`.light`

Now an unknown choice name, or a choice given as a bool/array/object, is a bad-params error naming the parameter, through the existing `validate_params` hook (before any document change):

- `gallery_cmds::validate_params` reads the choices from `GalleryFilter::params()`, so every gallery filter is covered with no second table, and each effect of a `filter.filterGallery` stack is checked too (the error names the effect index).
- `filters/validation.rs` hands non-core ids to it (one line).
- Unchanged: names stay case-insensitive, a numeric choice index still works (and is still clamped as the dialog stores it), stored smart filters keep their tolerant decoding.

Test: `unknown_choice_names_are_bad_params_without_editing` walks every choice param of every gallery filter — bad values are rejected both as a single command and inside a `filterGallery` stack without touching pixels or history; every listed name (upper-cased) and the last index still run.

Note: touches the same lines of `validate_params` as #2548; whichever lands second gets a trivial rebase.

Checks: `cargo fmt`, engine gallery/filters tests locally; full CI (ubuntu + windows tests, wasm32, web build, corpus) green on the fork.

title: Free Transform: refuse a locked layer up front, with Photoshop's message (#2585)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2585

**Root cause.** `transform_tool::begin` (the shared entry for ⌘T, Edit › Transform › Scale/Rotate/…, Warp, ⌥⌘T and the Move tool's Show Transform Controls handles) had no lock check. The only check was in `transform_cmds::transform_layer`, at commit, so the box opened on a position-locked layer (or a layer in a locked group), previewed every drag, and the work was lost when ↩ failed with `layer "…" is locked`.

**Fix.**
- `photocraft_engine::transform_cmds::locked_for_transform(doc, id)` applies the commit's own rule up front: the layer's own position/all lock or an enclosing group's, a locked layer inside a group being transformed, never the Background (the engine turns it into Layer 0, as Photoshop does). Commit and pre-check share one `transform_locks` helper, so they can't drift apart. Groups are walked with an explicit stack, not recursion.
- `transform_tool::begin` asks it before anything else is set up and refuses with Photoshop's alert, "Could not complete the Free Transform command because the layer is locked.", in the Error dialog, the same way the Move tool's lock message is shown (#2249). The string is translated in all 16 catalogues.
- Background behaviour is unchanged.

**Tests**
- `photocraft-engine` `transform_cmds::tests::locked_for_transform_matches_the_commit`: the pre-check agrees with `edit.transform` for a position-locked layer and a layer inside a locked group, and lets the Background through.
- `photocraft-ui-egui` `canvas::transform_controls_tests::free_transform_on_a_locked_layer_is_refused_up_front`: ⌘T (`edit.freeTransform`) and a press on the Move tool's transform-control handle both open no box and show the alert. With the check disabled it fails: `left: Ok({"transform": …})`, `right: Err("Could not complete the Free Transform command because the layer is locked.")`.

title: Quit and Close All: answering No closes that document (#2547)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
When you quit (or Close All / Close Others) with several unsaved documents, answering No didn't close that document. It was only crossed off an internal list, and nothing closed until the very end, so the tab stayed open. With several files all called "Untitled" it looked like the same question was coming back.

Now each question switches to the document it asks about, the first one included. Each document closes as soon as you answer it: right away for No, after the save for Yes. After the last answer the app quits (or Close All finishes). Cancel still stops the quit, and the documents you hadn't answered yet stay open with their changes. Documents already answered stay closed, so four existing tests that expected all-or-nothing were updated. Closing or reverting a single file works as before.

Added tests that open two dirty documents, quit, answer No and check that each prompt shows its own document and that the app can quit after the last answer. They also cover Cancel and Close Others.

Closes #2547.

title: Save As to a flat format keeps the layered original (#2550, #2579)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Save As to JPEG or PNG used to make the flat file the document's file. A layered document (or one already saved as PSD) was renamed to the JPEG and marked saved, so Ctrl+S opened the Save As dialog with JPEG picked instead of saving the PSD, and closing no longer warned about unsaved layers. `app.save` on the desktop did the same for any format, unlike the headless server since #1547.

Now a Save As to a flat format is a copy when the flat file can't hold the document: more than one plain layer, or the document already lives in a PSD, PSB, .pcraft, OpenRaster or TIFF. The document keeps its name, file and unsaved state, so Ctrl+S keeps writing the layered original. A flat image that isn't backed by a layered file still becomes the file you save it as. `app.save` only takes over the document for layered formats, using a helper shared with the headless server.

One judgement call: a single-layer document that came from a PSD is also kept on the PSD after a JPEG Save As (the reporter's case). I couldn't confirm whether Photoshop switches a flat image over to the JPEG there, so this errs on the side of keeping the layered file.

New tests in `save_identity_tests.rs` cover both cases and failed before the change. The `app.save` test in `control.rs` now also checks the document's name and path after a PNG save. One #2234 assertion that expected a layered document to become the JPEG was updated.

This sits next to #2515 (Ctrl+S on a flat PNG or JPEG writes in place). Both add the same `plain_raster` helper, so expect a small merge conflict.

Closes #2550. Closes #2579.

title: Keep the blend-mode preview between list rows (#2553)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Moving the pointer down the Layers panel blend-mode list made the canvas preview flicker. egui leaves a small gap between the list rows, and over that gap no row counts as hovered, so the preview fell back to the layer's current mode until the pointer reached the next row.

The dropdown now reports the nearest row as hovered while the pointer is between rows of the open list. Leaving the list still clears the preview as before. The list looks the same.

Added a kittest that opens the Layers blend dropdown and moves the pointer in half-point steps across several rows and the gaps between them. It checks that a mode is previewed at every step; before this change it failed inside the first gap.

Closes #2553.

title: Keep Duotone ink colours when converting to RGB, CMYK or Lab (#2383)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Converting a Duotone document to RGB, CMYK or Lab threw away the inks and converted the stored gray pixels, so a brown duotone or orange monotone came out neutral gray. Fill, text and effect colours stored in Duotone mode weren't converted at all.

Now the conversion first renders the document through its inks (the same `Duotone::render` model the canvas uses, in sRGB), then converts that through the CMS to the destination profile. Grayscale still keeps the underlying gray, and undo restores the Duotone document. Layers are inked one at a time so the layer structure survives; with blend modes or partial opacity that can differ slightly from the display, which inks the flattened result.

Tests cover 8, 16 and 32-bit, the default duotone, a custom orange monotone and a quadtone, against the displayed colours for each target mode, plus undo and fill-layer colours.

Closes #2383.

title: Legacy Brightness/Contrast: brightness first, then contrast around 128, as in Photoshop
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## What's wrong

Brightness/Contrast with **Use Legacy** on applied contrast first and then added the brightness. Each slider on its own was correct, which is why the corpus didn't catch it, but any setting that moves **both** came out wrong. Brightness +40 with contrast +30 mapped mid-grey 128 to **168**; Photoshop gives **185**. Across the midtones it was up to 17 levels too dark. There was also a ½-level pivot error that shows at high contrast (contrast 80 moved 128 to 130).

## What Photoshop does (measured)

Scripted on Photoshop 27.11: a gray ramp (0, 16, …, 240, 255) through seven legacy settings (brightness ±40, +100; contrast ±30, +80; and +40/+30 together). Photoshop scales contrast around **128/255**, adding the brightness **before** the contrast when contrast is raised and **after** it when contrast is lowered:

`out = (v + b − 128/255) · k + 128/255` for c ≥ 0, and `out = (v − 128/255) · k + 128/255 + b` for c < 0, with `k = 1 / (1 − c/100)` for c ≥ 0 and `1 + c/100` for c < 0, as before.

The sign rule comes from two sources: the measured +40/+30 case needs brightness first, and the corpus's `psd-tools/adjustments/brightnesscontrast_legacy_grayscale.psd` (brightness −23, contrast −26) needs contrast first. The measured cases with lowered contrast had brightness 0, so they can't tell the two orders apart.

| brightness, contrast | at gray 0 / 128 / 176 | Photoshop | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| +40, +30 | | 3 / 185 / 253 | 0 / 168 / 237 | 2 / 185 / 253 |
| 0, +80 | at 112 / 128 / 144 | 48 / 128 / 208 | 50 / 130 / 210 | 48 / 128 / 208 |

Every one of the 119 measured values now matches within 1 level.

## Change
- `compose::adjust`: contrast around `LEGACY_PIVOT` (128/255), brightness before it (c ≥ 0) or after it (c < 0).
- **GPU** adjustment kernel (`compose.wgsl` case 4, `plan.rs`): the same formula: the pivot goes in `p0.z`, and brightness goes in `p0.x` (before contrast) or `p0.w` (after).

## Tests

title: Rulers: keep tick marks and labels out of the origin corner
author: arthurdeka
body:
Fixes #2600.

Ruler ticks, labels and pointer markers use a painter clipped to the whole canvas area. Near the origin, they can paint over the reserved square where the horizontal and vertical rulers meet.

This clips each ruler's drawing to its own strip, including pointer markers. The origin corner remains available for the ruler-unit context menu.

### Visual evidence

Same offscreen ruler fixture, Pro Medium, 560 × 400, pointer over the origin corner:

![Origin corner comparison: before on the left, after on the right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/arthurdeka/photocraft/536d123a/issue-evidence/2026-10-10/2600/origin-comparison.png)

title: Image warp: grab anywhere on the grid, Ctrl-click to cut, Warp in the transform menu
author: Jeremy8776
body:
Refs #214 (the Free Transform right-click menu item).

Warp mode of Free Transform now works from anywhere inside the grid, not only on its points.

## What changes

- **Grab anywhere.** Press and drag on any part of the grid and the surface under the pointer follows it exactly. The surrounding anchors bend with it, fading out with distance, so neighbouring cells and dividers move too.
- **The border stays put.** A pull from inside the picture leaves the outer border where it is. A grab made near the border bows it through its own two handles, and the four corners never move.
- **Ctrl-click cuts the grid** vertically and horizontally at the pointer (Option-click still works). Near an existing line it cuts only the perpendicular direction.
- **Warp in the right-click menu** of a Free Transform box, after Perspective. The menu now marks only the box's real current mode (Warp was being read as Free Transform and lit up as well). The row is off for a lone mask, channel or path, which Warp does not apply to.
- **Smooth lines.** Dragging an anchor or a handle keeps every grid line smooth through its anchors, so a drag no longer creases the line.
- **Quieter grid points.** Anchors are smaller. A handle and its arm show only near the pointer or while being dragged.
- **No comb on hard pulls.** The preview used to draw a pulled-over fold in row order, so its layers showed as thin wedges. It now draws the most displaced cells first and samples finer where the warp pulls hard.
- **Warp options bar.** The bar now reads Split, Grid, Warp style, then the orientation button and Bend / H / V, which are always shown and only act on a preset style. A new **Reset** button puts the grid back to the default untouched one without leaving warp mode.
- **Buttons next to the fields.** Cancel and Commit (and the mode switch) sit right after the fields instead of at the far right of the window. A bar too narrow for both pins them to the right edge and clips the fields, so they stay reachable.…

title: Re-render shapes when an artboard move grows the canvas (#2389)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Moving an artboard past the right or bottom edge of the canvas left its shapes invisible or cut off. Shape pixels are clipped to the canvas, and both move paths (`layer.artboard.set` and `layer.translate`) re-rendered the shapes before `fit_canvas` grew the document, so they were drawn against the old edge until a later shape edit refreshed them.

`fit_canvas` now re-renders shapes whenever it changes the canvas size, so every caller gets this. It re-renders all shapes in the document, not only the moved board's, which also fixes shapes elsewhere that the old canvas had clipped. Nothing extra runs when the size doesn't change.

Added a test covering both move commands, the right-edge, bottom-edge and partial-overlap cases, and undo/redo.

Closes #2389.

title: Dock splitters push the neighbouring groups instead of stopping (#2573)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Dragging a dock splitter only traded height with the next group, so it stopped dead once that group hit its minimum. Now the groups on the side you drag into shrink in turn, nearest first, each down to its minimum, and the group on the other side grows by what they gave up. Collapsed groups are skipped and the filler (Layers) takes its share, so the column height doesn't change. It works in both directions, like Photoshop: dragging up now pushes the groups above instead of stopping at the dragged group's minimum.

Added tests for the layout math (pushing down and up, collapsed groups, the filler, stopping when everything is at minimum) and a kittest that drags the Swatches splitter past Properties' minimum. The existing splitter test now expects that dragging up pushes Color too.

Closes #2573.

title: Tools: a tool key brings back its group's last-used tool (#2608)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2608

## Root cause
`shortcuts::handle` picks a tool from its key group (`Tool::key`). When the current tool was outside the group it always chose `group[0]`, so after using the Polygonal Lasso, switching to the Brush and pressing L gave the plain Lasso. The toolbar slot remembered its last tool only for drawing its button (egui temp data); the shortcut path never asked.

It affected every group with more than one tool (M, B, E, I, J, S, O, G, T, A, U, W, C, L), not only the Lasso.

## Fix
- `UiState::group_tools` (serde default): the last tool used in each shortcut group, at most one per group. `remember_group_tool` records the current tool at the start of `shortcuts::handle`, so a tool picked any way (toolbar, flyout, shortcut, automation) counts.
- From another group, the key now picks the group's last-used tool (falling back to the first one). Inside the group, L / ⇧L still cycles as before, with and without Use Shift Key for Tool Switch.

## Tests
- `shortcuts::tests::tool_key_brings_back_the_groups_last_used_tool`: Polygonal Lasso → B → L gives the Polygonal Lasso; cycling to the Magnetic Lasso, then M, then L gives the Magnetic Lasso; same with Use Shift Key for Tool Switch on. Fails without the fix (`left: Lasso, right: PolygonLasso`).
- The existing `pencil_tests::b_cycles_brush_pencil_and_mixer_brush` still passes.

## Commands
```
cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- tool_key_brings_back b_cycles_brush shortcuts state:: input_tests marquee_tests control::
cargo clippy -j 4 -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt -p photocraft-ui-egui -- --check
```

title: Keep plug-in menu rows under Filter › Plug-ins in every language (#2540)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Fixes #2540.

## The bug

`plugin_ui::insert_menu_items` built the menu path it inserts the plug-in rows at from **translated** strings:

```rust
let path: Vec<String> = vec![tl!("Filter").into(), tl!("Plug-ins").into()];
```

But `MenuItem::path` is the *untranslated* English path that comes from a command's engine spec (`crates/engine/src/plugin_cmds.rs`: `menu: &["Filter", "Plug-ins"]`). The renderer groups rows by that raw path and translates only at display time — `menus.rs` keys a submenu on `it.path[depth]`, collects children with `c.path[depth] == name`, and only then draws `ui.menu_button(i18n::tr(lang, name), …)`.

So under any language whose catalog translates those two menu names, the plug-in rows were filed under a path no menu node matched and were never drawn. Installed WebAssembly plug-ins simply did not exist under Filter ▸ Plug-ins.

Every other path producer already feeds untranslated English — the menu catalogue, `UI_COMMANDS`, engine `c.menu`, and the dynamically built File ▸ Open Recent. `plugin_ui.rs` was the only one using `tl!`.

## The fix

Take the path from the `Install Plug-in…` item the rows are inserted above, rather than rebuilding it:

```rust
let Some(path) = items.get(at).map(|i| i.path.clone()) else { return };
```

That keeps the rows with the item they sit next to even if the submenu is ever renamed, and uses `get()` rather than indexing.

## Test

`plugin_ui::tests::plugin_menu_path_stays_untranslated_in_other_languages` installs the real `invert.wasm` fixture inside a Japanese language scope and asserts the row's path is `["Filter", "Plug-ins"]` and matches Install's.

It first asserts that Japanese genuinely translates both names, so it cannot silently become a no-op if the catalog changes. That guard matters: **German would not have caught this bug**, because `de.tsv` maps `Filter`→`Filter` and `Plug-ins`→`Plug-ins` verbatim. The pre-existing English test also passed with the bug present, since `tl!` reads the thread-local l…

title: fix: Preserve CMYK solid and gradient fills through PSD round trips
author: reneleonhardt
body:
## Summary

- Generate CMYK solid and gradient fills directly in ink channels at 8, 16 and 32-bit depth, sharing samples between rendering and PSD export to prevent colour changes after reopening.
- Preserve valid imported fill caches and use the document ICC profile when separating RGB fill colours.
- Route uncached CMYK solid and gradient fills through the CPU compositor; cached fills retain GPU support. Patterns, blending and effects keep their existing rendering paths.
- Reuse exact 8-bit CMYK conversions within each pixel row, with one cached ink tuple and separate alpha.

## Validation

- The real uncached 16-bit CMYK gradient's maximum rendered round-trip error falls from 0.12541771 to zero. Its separate Photoshop rendering mismatch remains.
- Synthetic round trips cover all depths, five gradient styles, ICC profiles, transparency, gradient options and tiled rendering. Unit tests cover ink interpolation, GPU fallback and bitwise conversion parity across tile boundaries.
- psd-tools export round trips rise from 307 to 308; the floor is raised to 308. Mixed and Photoshop round trips remain 169 and 258, and oracle matches remain 146, 237 and 133. Mutated imports produce no panics.
- All 674 Raster, Compose, IO and GPU tests pass, alongside colour and corpus tests, Clippy, formatting, workspace layering and WASM checks.
- Matched O3/M4 Max conversion reads at 1 MP improve from 66.2 to 15.2 ms for smooth 8-bit CMYK ramps (77%), 65.5 to 43.6 ms with dithering (33%), and 70.0 to 63.2 ms for random colours (10%). All output checksums match. The 16/32-bit conversion loops stay unchanged; solid fills convert one sample per render tile.

title: Add Arabic text support: visual RTL editing, paragraph direction, kashida and digit shapes
author: diax7
body:
Arabic is read by more than 400 million people. In PhotoCraft today, tracking tears Arabic letters apart, the caret moves the wrong way through right-to-left text, and there is no right-to-left control. This PR fixes those and adds the controls Arabic typesetting needs; it addresses the RTL items of #218.

## Screenshots

title: Dropdowns: open lists start at their widest option's width (#2607)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2607

## Root cause
egui's `Button::selectable` (used for every dropdown row) only draws its frame when the row is hovered or selected. For a plain row it lays out with `button_padding - bg_stroke.width` and no stroke; for a hovered row it adds the stroke back. PhotoCraft's theme gives the inactive state a 1 pt stroke, so a row is 2 pt wider while hovered. The ComboBox popup keeps the widest width it has seen (`set_min_width(available_width)`), so when scrolling moves the widest option (e.g. "Linear Dodge (Add)") under the pointer, the list grows by 2 pt and stays that way. Hovering at the top without scrolling never reached the widest row, which is why it looked tied to scrolling.

## Fix
`crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs`: a small `fit_widest_option` helper measures the option labels (same font, no wrapping) and sets the list's minimum width to the widest label plus the button padding on both sides, which is exactly the hovered width. `dropdown_with` (`dropdown`, `dropdown_hovered`, `dropdown_wheel_hovered`) and `dropdown_with_tooltips` call it, so every shared dropdown opens at its final width.

Overlap note: #2612 also edits `dropdown_with`, in a different part of the closure (the row loop). This PR only adds one line at the top of the closure, so the two shouldn't conflict.

## Tests
- `widgets::tests::dropdown_list_keeps_its_width_while_scrolling`: opens the Brush Mode dropdown (all layer blend modes, ProMedium theme), scrolls the list a line at a time with the pointer over the rows, and asserts the popup width never changes. Without the fix it fails (`141.3 -> 143.3`). With the fix it passes.

- `cargo clippy -j 4 -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: Close a document tab with a middle click (#2570)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Fixes #2570.

Middle-clicking a document tab closes it, as in a browser. Both tab strips get it — `tabs()` (Studio) and `pro_tabs()` (Pro).

## The change

One shared rule, called from each strip in place of the bare `xresp.clicked()`:

```rust
fn tab_close_clicked(resp: &egui::Response, xresp: &egui::Response) -> bool {
    xresp.clicked() || xresp.middle_clicked() || resp.middle_clicked()
}
```

The `xresp.middle_clicked()` term is load-bearing: the × rect sits inside the tab rect and is interacted with *after* it, so it wins the hit test. Without that term, a middle click on the last ~16 pt of a tab would silently do nothing.

No new command — this sets the `close` variable both strips already route through `file.close` with `{"document": i}`.

## Unsaved changes are still guarded

`menus::invoke` runs `discard_ui::intercept` before dispatch, and `DISCARDING` lists `("file.close", Reach::Target)`, with `discarded()` reading the `document` param. Because the middle click only sets the existing `close` variable, it inherits that guard verbatim: a dirty document still gets Save / Don't Save / Cancel. There is a test for exactly this.

## Drag-to-reorder is unaffected

On the tab body (`Sense::click_and_drag()`) a middle *press* sets `potential_drag_id`, but `is_dragged` stays false while the pointer is inside and hasn't moved far, so a plain middle click still registers as a click. A middle press-drag-release behaves as a primary one does today — it reorders rather than closes, because `click` is `None` after a real drag. Pre-existing, unchanged.

## Tests

- `canvas::tests::middle_clicking_a_tab_closes_that_document` — three clean documents, middle-click the middle tab, in **both** Studio and Pro strips. Asserts only that document closed, that it was the tab under the pointer rather than the active one, and that no prompt appeared.
- `canvas::tests::middle_clicking_an_edited_tab_prompts_instead_of_discarding` — an edited document middle-clicked brings up the unsave…

title: Curved shapes no longer report bounds 1 px too wide (#2537)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Curved shapes reported bounds one pixel too wide, e.g. a 600×600 ellipse showed W 601 in Properties and `shape.info`.

The rasterizer adds up each row's coverage in f32. The left edge adds coverage and the right edge subtracts it, but for curved or off-grid edges the two don't cancel exactly, so the pixel just past the shape kept about 1e-7. Shape layers wrote the fill colour there and content bounds counted it.

Coverage below 1e-6 is now set to 0 when a row is written (a NaN too). That is under half a 16-bit step, so 8- and 16-bit coverage values don't change; only those stray pixels become empty. Selections, vector masks and strokes use the same rasterizer and get the same fix.

Tests cover exact bounds of an ellipse, rounded rect, star and a custom Bézier path at 8, 16 and 32-bit, as a layer and as a selection, and check that real thin antialiased edges (a 1-px bar, a 1% sliver, a 1e-4 sliver at 32-bit) still count. The `shape.info` repro from the issue is a test too. vector, engine, ui-egui, compose, gpu and io tests pass, and so do the io and engine corpus tests.

Side note: `xtask test-corpus --changed` doesn't pick up `crates/vector`, though PSD shape layers and vector masks render through it.

Closes #2537.

title: Spot Healing: the drag trail shows the dabs the heal covers (#2364)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2364

## Root cause
While dragging, the Spot Healing Brush (like the other non-live retouching tools) draws a translucent trail from `stroke_trail::Trail::feed`. That stamps a hard round capsule at the base brush size (`tools.brush.size`). It ignores hardness, pen pressure and Shape Dynamics. The heal itself (`paint.spotHealing` → `stroke_coverage`) uses the brush engine's dab coverage, so the result was right but the preview looked like a 100 % hard, 100 % pressure stroke.

## Fix
- `stroke_trail::Trail::feed_dabs` renders the trail from a `photocraft_paint::StrokeRenderer`, the same renderer `stroke_coverage` uses. Each frame it pushes the new drag points (with pressure) and restamps only the tiles that changed. It also shows what finishing would add (`tail_preview`: the press's lone first dab, smoothing catch-up), as `LiveRetouch` does.
- `retouch_cmds::stroke_brush(base, params)` is split out of `parse_brush`, so the preview and the command build the stroke's brush the same way (opacity/flow 100 %, spacing, hardness, dynamics) instead of duplicating that logic.
- Only Spot Healing uses the new path. Remove, Pattern Stamp, Quick Selection etc. keep the capsule trail.

## Tests
- New: `canvas::tests::spot_healing_trail_is_the_coverage_the_heal_uses`. A soft brush (hardness 0) with pen-pressure size is dragged at pressure 0.5. The trail must match the heal's `stroke_coverage` for the same stroke pixel for pixel (±1/255), show a soft edge, and be empty 10 px off the path. Without the fix it fails (`(15, 15): trail 81, heal 0`).
- `retouch_drags_show_the_footprint_without_wedges` now drives the Remove tool, which still uses the capsule trail, so it keeps testing what it was written for.

title: Paste: a web Ctrl/Cmd+V key press and its paste event are one paste (#2638)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2638

### Root cause
eframe's web runner (0.36.2, `web/events.rs`) forwards the Ctrl/Cmd+V `keydown` as `Event::Key { key: V, pressed: true, modifiers: command }` and doesn't prevent its default, so the browser then fires `paste`, which eframe turns into `Event::Paste(text)` when the clipboard holds text. Both arrive in the same frame. `shortcuts::clipboard_keys` passed the key press through and also turned the `Paste` event into a second Cmd+V press, so `edit.paste` ran twice. Ctrl/Cmd+X with `cut` and Ctrl/Cmd+C with `copy` had the same issue.

On desktop egui-winit drops the key press whenever it sends `Copy`/`Cut`/`Paste`, so only the web build was affected.

### Fix
`clipboard_keys` keeps track of the last command C/X/V key press in the frame that hasn't been paired with a clipboard event yet. A `Copy`/`Cut`/`Paste` event that follows its own key press now counts as that press and doesn't add a second one. On desktop nothing changes: the image-only paste (a release without a press), the Mac native-menu key equivalent and Shift+Insert work as before.

### Tests
- New: `shortcuts::tests::web_paste_key_and_paste_event_are_one_press`. Cmd+V press + `Paste`, and Cmd+X press + `Cut`, in one frame each give exactly one press, and the V release doesn't paste again. Without the fix it fails with `left: (2, 2), right: (1, 1)`.
- Existing `each_paste_key_is_one_press`, `clipboard_events_become_pixel_shortcuts_outside_text`, `ctrl_and_shift_insert_copy_and_paste_on_linux` and `native_menu::tests::a_paste_key_equivalent_pastes_once` still pass.

### Commands

title: fix(vector): eliminate float residue in rasterizer coverage accumulation
author: buivanvu94
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2537

Shape layers with curved edges (ellipses, rounded rectangles, stars, custom curves, etc.) were reporting content bounds one pixel wider than the actual shape (e.g. an exact 100×100 ellipse reported W 101, 600×600 reported W 601).

### Cause
In `crates/vector/src/raster.rs`, each row's cell accumulator `RowState::acc` prefix-summed deltas into `sum`. Because curved non-axis-aligned edges did not cancel exactly to zero in 32-bit float arithmetic across the row, pixels immediately past the right edge of curved shapes retained a tiny residual positive coverage (e.g. `~8.94e-8`). The subsequent clamp kept this value, leading surface content-bounds scans to consider those pixels as non-empty content and expand the reported width by 1 pixel.

### Solution
1. **Accumulate in f64**: Changed `RowState::acc` from `Vec<f32>` to `Vec<f64>`, and kept cell delta calculations in `draw()` and `add_full()` in `f64` rather than casting down to `f32`.
2. **Snap coverage residue**: In `render_into()`, snap `sum` to `0.0` if `|sum| < 1e-6`, and snap `sum` to `1.0` if `|sum - 1.0| < 1e-6`, preventing tiny cancellation noise from bleeding into pixels outside the geometry.
3. **Tests**:
   - Added `curved_shape_coverage_does_not_bleed_past_bounds` in `crates/vector/src/raster.rs` asserting 0.0 coverage beyond the geometry.
   - Added `curved_shapes_report_exact_content_bounds_without_residue` in `crates/engine/src/vector_cmds/tests.rs` asserting exact bounds for shapes created via `shape.create`.

### Verification
- `cargo test -p photocraft-vector`: 46/46 passed
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine`: 100% passed
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-vector -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed (0 warnings)
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored`: passed

title: Smart Objects: converting several layers keeps them at the contents top level (#2648)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2648

**Root cause**
`convert` in `crates/engine/src/smart_cmds.rs` wrapped the selected top-level layers in a temporary `Layer::group(..)` and passed it to `layer_to_smart`. That group ended up in the nested document, so Edit Contents showed one group named after the top layer. Photoshop puts the selected layers at the top level of the embedded document.

**Fix**
The embedding part of `layer_to_smart` is now `layers_to_smart(doc, name, layers)`. It builds the nested document from the layers directly (bounds, effects margin and nested smart-object check across all of them). `layer_to_smart` calls it with the one prepared layer and then sets the outer properties as before. With several layers, `convert` calls `layers_to_smart` with the selected layers, so they sit at the top level of the contents in stacking order. The wrapper was a pass-through group at full opacity with no mask or effects, so the composite is the same. A single selected group still converts with that group kept as is. The other callers (Load Files into Stack, automate) are unchanged.

**Tests** (adapted in `crates/engine/src/smart_cmds/tests/selection.rs`)
- `selected_pixels_become_one_editable_smart_object_in_every_mode_and_depth`: the top-level layers of the contents are the selected layers in order. The existing composite check against Group Layers + Convert still passes in every mode and depth.
- `selected_group_and_descendant_are_embedded_once`: a selected group plus a layer become the two top-level layers, and the group is kept.
- Both fail without the fix (the top level is a single wrapper group).

title: Smart Objects: Copy/Paste with no selection keeps the smart object (#2428)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2428

## Root cause
`edit.copy` always lifted the active layer's rendered pixels into the clipboard (`Clip { surface, bounds }`), and `edit.paste` always made a new `Layer::raster` from them. So a smart object came back as a pixel layer after Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V. #541 / #841 chose this on purpose ("Paste makes a new pixel layer").

## Photoshop behaviour
Since CC 2018, Photoshop has a *layer-based copy*. With no pixel selection, Ctrl+C on the highlighted layer copies the layer itself, and Ctrl+V pastes it as a layer. That works within a document and across documents. With an active selection, Copy still copies pixels. I worked this out from Adobe community threads about the CC 2018 feature, not from Adobe's release notes. I'm confident about the smart object case. I did not verify exactly which properties Photoshop keeps for every layer kind, so this PR only changes smart objects.

## Fix
- `Clip` gets `layers: Option<Box<Document>>`. With no selection, and when the active layer is a smart object in an RGB, Gray, CMYK or Lab document, Copy also stores the layer in a scratch document in the source's colour. The pixels stay on the clipboard for Paste Into, mask and channel targets, New from Clipboard and the OS clipboard.
- On Paste or Paste in Place into the pixel target, `paste_layers` takes a fresh `duplicate()` and converts it to the destination's profile and bit depth. It moves the copy by the same offset the pixels would get (in place, view centre or canvas centre) and inserts it above the active layer as one "Paste" step.
- Following the issue reporter (and #2576), a pasted smart object gets a **fresh contents id**. It holds the same contents but isn't linked to the copied one. Duplicate Layer and Layer via Copy still share contents (#2222).
- The contents-id, colour and depth handling and the translation code in `layer.copyToDocument` move into the shared helpers `adapt_copies` and `translate_copies` in `layer_copy_cmds.rs`. Its behaviour is unchanged.

title: Control channel: input methods reject bad params instead of using defaults (#2449)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
The control channel's synthetic input methods (`ui.pointer`, `ui.click`/`ui.move`, `ui.key`, `ui.screenshot`) read each value with `as_f64`/`as_bool`/`as_str` and fell back to a default on anything else. So `"button":"ritgh"` became a left click, `"kind":"dwon"` became a move, `"ctrl":"yes"` became false, and all of them replied ok.

They now validate the whole request before doing anything, the same way `ui.set` does. Unknown fields (top-level, under `modifiers`, or inside an event), wrong JSON types, unknown `button`/`kind`/`tool` values and out-of-range `pressure`/`tiltX`/`tiltY`/`rotation` return an error naming the parameter, and nothing is queued or applied. Enum errors list the accepted values, and an unknown `tool` gives the same error as `ui.set`. A `null` field still means omitted, and valid calls behave as before. One stricter case: `ui.move` now only takes `x` and `y`; extra fields such as `button` used to be ignored.

Tests in `control.rs` cover each method with an unknown field, a wrong type, a bad value and an out-of-range number, plus the valid calls. `docs/control-protocol.md` lists the accepted values. `ui.resize` is left for a follow-up, as the issue suggests.

Closes #2449.

author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:

title: Speed up large group merges (#1561)
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What changed

Layer merges no longer composite the full document when the visible layers occupy a smaller area. Merge Down, Merge Layers, and Merge Visible now use visible content bounds and render in bands directly into the output surface, avoiding a full-canvas RGBA buffer and a second converted float buffer. Opaque Background layers still composite over white.

## Validation

- Added pixel-equivalence coverage for group merges at 8, 16, and 32-bit depths.
- Release benchmark on a 5000×7073 canvas with four 1000×1000 layers: 2,629.6 ms on the old full-canvas path and 26.9 ms on the bounded/banded path (97.8× faster), with matching pixels.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine`, Clippy, layers, full WASM matrix, format check, and `cargo xtask perf --quick` pass.

Fixes #1561

title: raster: a shifted surface copies in one pass per row without pre-filled tiles
author: Elvis33LE
body:
While measuring **P14** (move on a 15000×10000 16-bit document) I reworked `Surface::translated`'s misaligned path. This is deliberately a modest, self-contained cleanup — the diagnosis of where P14's budget actually goes is in [#209 (comment)](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/209#issuecomment), and the budget-relevant work (texture-limit paging, #49) is separate.

**What changes**

- The misaligned path no longer allocates every target tile through `Tile::filled` (which, for a nonzero default pixel, wrote the full tile per-pixel before ~95 % of it was overwritten) and no longer computes spans through per-row closures. Each stored row is written directly: content spans copy as single memcpys crossing source tiles as needed, and the vacated edges fill from one prebuilt default row.
- `Tile::filled` builds its default rows in bulk (256 row copies instead of 65 536 per-pixel copies) — this helps every nonzero-default fill (background clears, write-path tiles), not just translates.

**Tests:** the existing read-back oracle (`translated_matches_reading_the_moved_pixels`, every depth, negative offsets, tile crossings, the i32-limit case) is green, plus the whole raster suite; engine/compose suites over the shift paths green; clippy/fmt clean.

Honest numbers: on a transparent-default layer the scenario cost is allocation-bound and stays ~the same (39–40 ms for the copy on a 9.4 MP RGBA16 layer, RTX 3090); the win is the nonzero-default cases and a leaner loop. The P14 budget on texture-limited devices needs the paging work called out in the #209 comment.

title: Layer > Rasterize > Layer Style bakes effects; Rasterize Layer converts vector masks (#2245)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Adds Layer > Rasterize > Layer Style, which bakes a layer's effects into its pixels. The layer is rendered on its own through the compositor, so the result matches what the canvas showed. The layer keeps its own opacity, blend mode, knockout and Blend If. Fill opacity, the effects and any masks go into the pixels, including pixels past the canvas. Type, shape, fill and Smart Object layers are rasterized first, in the same history step. It's also in the Layers panel context menu.

Rasterize > Layer and All Layers now turn a vector mask into a pixel mask too, and leave effects live. That follows Photoshop's split between Rasterize > Layer and Rasterize > Layer Style as far as I could find it described (Adobe's help page itself didn't load). Menu enablement follows both.

On the issue's acceptance question: for a Normal layer with Normal-mode effects the flattened document is the same before and after (tested at 8, 16 and 32 bit, with undo). Effects in other modes, like the default Multiply shadow or Screen glow, are evaluated against the layer's own transparent background, so they can look different afterwards; one layer of pixels can't hold several blend modes. Layers clipped to a baked layer now clip to its shadow and glow too.

Parity floor goes to 628. #2663 raises it to 628 as well, so whichever lands second needs `FLOOR` and `docs/parity.md` bumped once more.

Closes #2245.

title: Move tool: the drag's box and snapping follow the Auto-Selected layer (#2666)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2666

## Root cause

`canvas::tool_event` runs `snap_ui::filter_event` first. On the press, that calls `snap_ui::begin`, which takes the Move gesture's rect from `selected_layers()` and leaves those layers out of the snap targets. After that, the Move tool's press handler runs Auto-Select (`layer.pickAt`). So the drag's box (`snap_ui::draw`), the rect that snapping aligns, and the excluded targets all belonged to the layers selected **before** the pick:
- With another layer selected, that layer's box moved with the pointer instead of the dragged layer's box, and snapping aligned the wrong edges.
- With an empty layer or a group selected, there was no rect, so no box was drawn (only the arrow) and nothing snapped. This is the "no box with Show bounding box when dragging layer on" symptom.

## Fix

In the Move tool's press, `snap_ui::begin` runs again (`snap_ui::retarget_move`) when `layer.pickAt` changed the selection. Presses that don't change it skip the extra target build.

Related: #2565 (#2413) moves the View › Show › Layer Edges outline during a Move. That's a different overlay with separate code, and the two branches merge without conflict.

## Tests

`snap_ui::tests::move_tool_box_and_snapping_follow_the_auto_selected_layer`: with another layer selected, then with an empty layer selected, Auto-Select picks the mover. The test checks that the gesture rect is the mover's bounds and that the drop snaps to the target's edge. Without the fix it fails: the rect is the target's `[300, 200, 350, 260]`, and with the empty layer it is `None`.

```
cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- move snap auto_select   # 114 passed
cargo clippy -j 4 -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt -p photocraft-ui-egui -- --check
```

author: vangel76

title: fix(move): refresh snapping after Auto-Select picks a layer
author: Ni-zav

When Move Tool Auto-Select is enabled, snapping is initialized using the previously selected layers before the layer under the pointer is picked.

The problem is especially noticeable when moving between layers with different bounds or when an empty layer was previously selected.

`canvas::tool_event` initializes snapping through `snap_ui::filter_event` before executing `layer.pickAt`.

title: Move tool: ⌘-drag temporary Move gets the drag box and snapping (#2681)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2681

## Root cause
`snap_ui::begin` picked the snap gesture from `app.ui.tool`, the selected tool, rather than the tool the press acts as. Holding ⌘ (Ctrl) with a painting tool makes it the Move tool (`tool_override`, or ⌘ sent with the event), and ⌘ with a marquee or lasso outside the selection moves the layer (`canvas::command_moves_layer`). Those drags moved the layer but got no moving box and no smart-guide, guide or grid snapping; with a marquee the pointer snapped like a marquee corner instead.

title: Five exact-output speedups: dense Extrude 160s to 0.39s
author: excited-raccoon
body:
Five CPU operations were repeating source and sampling work for every output pixel. This removes that work while keeping the existing output and parameter behavior.

Full-operation release medians on a 16-vCPU m7i.4xlarge, three alternating before/after pairs per case:

| Operation | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Extrude Blocks, 8 px / depth 128, 24 MP RGB8 | 160.30s | 0.39s | 414.69x |
| Wind / Blast, 24 MP CMYK8 | 6.23s | 0.71s | 8.79x |
| Spin Blur, 36 MP RGB8 | 9.44s | 5.87s | 1.61x |
| Lens Correction, 24 MP CMYK16 | 0.81s | 0.56s | 1.43x |
| Trap, 50 px, 36 MP CMYK16 | 4.63s | 1.33s | 3.47x |

Default 30 px / depth 30 Extrude also improves from 2.06s to 0.33s at 24 MP (6.26x).

Extrude rasterizes each swept block once. Wind scatters only actual source streaks. Spin Blur prepares rotation tables and uses fixed-channel sampling. Lens shares interpolation geometry across color and alpha at the same source point. Wide Trap uses prefix/suffix maxima with contiguous column writes. Original tie rules and float arithmetic order are retained, with bounded scratch and direct fallbacks.

All 72 full-image before/after output comparisons match bit for bit across 24 cases at 8/16/32-bit depths. New reference tests also cover all eight color models, alpha, selections, tile boundaries, unusual coordinates and fallback paths where applicable.

407 algorithm tests passed, with 14 existing ignored tests. fmt, clippy with denied warnings, layers, full wasm, quick perf and scorecard checks passed. Synced and rebased onto current main before publishing.

[Full timing matrix, raw results and reproduction](https://github.com/excited-raccoon/photocraft/blob/6ab9aaa8a7397982ba307d7418a450744e3c2479/docs/five-algorithm-performance.md). These are CPU operation times, including surface assembly, excluding UI, undo and Trap document flattening.

title: Edit: Copy/Paste with no selection keeps type, shape and group layers (#2670)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2670

**Depends on #2653 (its commit is included); review/merge that first.** Only the last commit belongs to this PR.

### Root cause

#2653 adds Photoshop's layer-based copy (with no pixel selection, Copy takes the active layer whole and Paste recreates it), but only for smart objects. Type and shape layers still pasted as a flattened pixel layer. Edit › Copy was disabled on a group because a group has no pixels of its own.

### What changed (`crates/engine/src/edit_cmds.rs`)

- `takes_whole` decides when Copy takes the layer whole: no pixel selection, a single selected layer, a layered colour mode, and a smart object, **type layer, shape layer or group**. `whole_layer` stores it in a scratch document, as #2653 does.
- Paste goes through #2653's `paste_layers`, unchanged. The layers get fresh ids (`Layer::duplicate`, the group's children included). They are converted to the destination's profile and bit depth (`adapt_copies`) and moved like pasted pixels (`translate_copies`, which recurses into groups). Text stays editable, shapes keep their vector data, and a group keeps its children, masks, effects and blend modes.
- Groups: Copy is now enabled for a group when there's no selection (`can_copy`). The clipboard pixels are the group's composite, for Paste Into, masks, channels and other apps. With a selection, a group still can't be copied, as before.
- Unchanged: pixel layers, several selected layers, and any copy with a pixel selection all take pixels. These weren't verified in Photoshop, so they keep the current behaviour. Paste into a Bitmap/Indexed document still pastes pixels. One change relative to #2653 alone: the whole-layer copy now needs exactly one selected layer, so a smart object copied while several layers are selected takes pixels too (with #2653 alone it was copied as a layer).

### Photoshop verification (2026-10-10)
