title: File Info shows Camera Data from EXIF/XMP (#2424)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
File Info now shows a read-only Camera Data section: make, model, date taken, exposure, f-stop, ISO, focal length (and the 35 mm equivalent) and lens, formatted the way Photoshop shows them (1/250 s, f/8, ISO 400, 33.1 mm). The values come from the document's EXIF block as loaded (JPEG APP1, PSD resource 1058) through the existing `photocraft_algo::exif` reader, which now also reads DateTimeOriginal. Without an EXIF block, the XMP tiff:/exif:/aux: copies are used. A file with no camera data shows the dialog as before.

`file.fileInfo` returns the same data as a read-only `camera` object, so agents get it too. Editing the description fields doesn't touch it.

I also hardened the EXIF reader: offsets and sizes use checked arithmetic (usize is 32 bits on wasm), and a tag's value has to fit inside the payload. A new test feeds it hostile counts, offsets, cyclic IFDs and noise.

Labels are translated in all 16 catalogs. They use a `cameraData` context because "Make" already exists as the verb.

Not covered yet: RAW and TIFF imports don't keep their EXIF block, so they only show camera data if their XMP has it.

Closes #2424.

title: Pencil/Eraser: round Pencil cursor and Eraser Pencil mode (#2662)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2662

## Root cause
- **Pencil cursor:** `canvas.rs` always outlined `paint::grid_square`, the whole-pixel square an aliased dab can touch. The dab itself (`render.rs`) fills only the pixels whose centres lie within its radius of the grid centre, so it is a square only up to 3 px and a disc from 4 px on. Large Pencil sizes showed a square cursor over a round stroke.
- **Pixel eraser:** the Eraser always committed `paint.stroke` (soft, anti-aliased). It had no Mode option, and its pro options bar showed a blend-mode dropdown that the engine ignores for erasing (`with_blend_mode` forces Normal).

## Changes
- `pencil_tip_is_round(size)`: the cursor draws a circle on the same grid-snapped square when the dab is round, and keeps the square for 1–3 px tips, which really are squares.
- Eraser › Mode: Brush / Pencil (`tool_options.eraser_mode`, serde default `brush`). It replaces the unused blend-mode dropdown in the pro bar and is added to the classic bar. Pencil mode routes the stroke, both live and on release, through `paint.pencil` with `"erase": true`: hard, aliased, at full flow, with locked transparency handled the same way. It also uses the Pencil's pixel-grid cursor. Hardness, Flow and Airbrush are greyed out in Pencil mode.
- Photoshop's Block mode (a fixed-size square tip) is not included: it needs a square dab shape the paint engine doesn't have yet. It can follow up.

## Tests
- `pencil_tests::the_cursor_is_round_exactly_when_the_pencil_dab_is`: for sizes 1–12 it paints one real dab and checks that the cursor is round exactly when the dab's corner pixel is empty.
- `pencil_tests::the_eraser_in_pencil_mode_erases_aliased_pixels`: a soft Eraser in Pencil mode commits `paint.pencil` with erase and leaves no partial alpha.
- Both fail without the fix (cursor always square → `4 px` assertion; Eraser → `paint.stroke`).

title: Copy and paste a single channel from the Channels panel (#2307)
author: fabianghe
body:
Fixes #2307.

With a colour channel (Red, Green, Blue, …) targeted in the Channels panel, **Copy** copied the whole layer and **Paste** made a new layer. So a channel couldn't be copied into another one, which is a common way to pack masks into a texture's channels. This change matches Photoshop:

- **Copy** with a colour or alpha channel targeted copies that channel's values as a grayscale clip, inside the selection or across the whole canvas. With an alpha channel targeted, Copy needs no pixel layer.
- **Paste**, **Paste in Place** and **Paste Into** with a colour channel targeted write the clip's luminosity into that channel of the active layer, in one undo step.
  - The other channels and the layer's transparency are left alone.
  - A pixel lock refuses the paste.
  - Paste Into keeps to the selection.
- Pasting into alpha channels, masks and the Quick Mask goes through the existing `paste_to_target` path (#1035), so it is unchanged. With the composite targeted, a grayscale clip still pastes as a new grey layer.

## How
The logic lives in a new `engine/src/channel_clip.rs`. `edit.copy`, `paste()` and `paste_into` only call it, which keeps the overlap with #2184 (layer masks across Copy/Paste) to a few lines. Colour channel values are written directly into sample *k*, so the result is exact at every depth and in every colour model.

Cut still behaves as before. Cutting from a channel can come in a follow-up.

## Tests
New tests in `engine/src/channel_clip/tests.rs`:
- Copy Red, paste into Blue, at 8, 16 and 32 bit: no new layer, Blue matches the old Red, and the paste undoes in one step.
- An alpha channel copies as grayscale and pastes into Green. The composite target still makes a new layer.
- Copy works with an alpha channel targeted and no pixel layer.
- Paste Into a colour channel keeps to the selection.
- Failures leave everything as it was: an empty selection leaves the clipboard alone, and a pixel-locked layer refuses the paste.

title: Guides: ⌘-drag over a guide moves it with the selection tools too (#2690)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2690

**Root cause.** In Photoshop ⌘ (Ctrl) is the Move tool with any tool, and the Move tool drags a guide under the pointer before anything else. Painting tools already get this through the held-⌘ Move override (`hold_keys::cmd_moves`), so `tool_event` sees `Tool::Move` and its guide check runs. The marquees, lassos and Magic Wand keep their own tool under ⌘ (`canvas::command_moves_layer` handles them), so the guide check never ran: a ⌘-drag over a guide moved the layer (Lasso: drew an outline) and left the guide in place.

**Fix.**
- `canvas::command_guide_at`: a ⌘ press with a selection tool over a guide takes the guide, using the Move tool's hit test (`rulers::guide_at`), so hidden or locked guides are still not hit. Not while a polygon or lasso outline is being drawn, or during Free Transform. `tool_event` checks it before the selection tools see the press. The existing guide-drag Move/Up handling does the rest.
- `snap_ui::begin_guide`: the drag snaps like the Move tool's guide drag (never to guides). Without it a marquee's point snapping would pull the guide back onto its old position.
- `lasso_ui`: during such a guide drag the Lasso passes its events on to the canvas, as it already does for a selection move.
- The cursor over a guide is the guide's double arrow with ⌘ held, too.

**Relation to #2684.** #2684 (⌘-drag temporary Move: drag box and snapping) also touches `tool_event` and `snap_ui::begin`. This change stays out of those hunks: the new helper sits after `command_moves_layer`, and `begin_guide` is a separate function. `git merge-tree` merges both #2684 and #2675 cleanly with this branch.

**Tests.** `rulers::tests::command_drag_over_a_guide_moves_the_guide_with_any_tool`: ⌘ + Brush, Rectangular Marquee, Lasso and Magic Wand over a vertical guide move the guide and leave the layer alone. title: Free Transform frames the whole type layer; Distort/Perspective greyed for type (#2630)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Free Transform on a type layer with a marquee selection showed a box around only the selected part of the text and previewed half the glyphs moving, but the commit then moved the whole layer. Type can't be partly transformed, so the frame and preview now cover the whole layer for type, shapes and smart objects, the same as the engine already did. Pixel layers still move just the selected pixels.

Distort and Perspective were enabled for editable type and then failed with a status message on commit. They're now greyed for type layers in the Edit menu and the canvas context menus, like Photoshop, and come back once the type is rasterized (or when a mask or channel is targeted).

I couldn't reproduce Free Transform missing from a menu: it's enabled for type layers in the Edit menu and the marquee and transform-box context menus. While the Type tool is editing text, Ctrl+T toggles the Character panel, as in Photoshop, which may be what the report ran into.

Tests cover the whole-layer frame (engine and UI), the commit result, and the menu enablement before and after rasterizing.

title: PSD: warn on an unreadable Lr16/Lr32 layer block and save one layer list (#2700)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2700

## Root cause
`PsdFile::from_bytes` (`crates/psd/src/file.rs`) looks for the global `Lr16`/`Lr32`/`Layr` block of a 16/32-bit file and parses it with `&& let Ok(info) = LayerInfo::read_body(..)`. When parsing fails, the error is dropped. The block stays in `global_blocks` and `layer_info` stays `None`, so `psd_import` treats the file as flattened and opens the merged composite as one Normal "Background" layer with no warning. The raw block is then kept in `metadata.psd_global_blocks`. On a PSD save the exporter writes its own `Lr16` and also re-emits the preserved one, so the output holds two layer lists.

## Fix
- **psd:** the new `PsdFile::unreadable_layer_block()` returns the kept layer block and its parse error. It only reports when `layer_info` is `None`. `from_bytes` is unchanged, so the byte-level round trip still keeps the block verbatim.
- **io import:** a warning names the block and the error, for example: `the layers (Lr16 block) could not be read (...); only the merged image was opened. Saving as PSD replaces the unreadable layer data`.
- **io export:** a preserved `Lr16`/`Lr32`/`Layr` block is skipped whenever the export writes the document's own layer records.

### Why drop the raw copy rather than skip writing our own
`Lr16`/`Lr32`/`Layr` isn't an unknown block. It *is* the layer list, and the document model owns the layers. Keeping it next to ours gives a file with two contradictory layer lists. Writing only the raw block and not our own would silently throw away every layer edit made after the open, and would pair stale layers with a new composite. The import keeps the raw block in the document metadata, so `.pcraft` saves still carry it. The PSD writer replaces it only when it writes real layers. If the document has no layer records, nothing contradicts the block and it is still written verbatim. The new import warning says that a PSD save replaces the unreadable data, so the user can decide before overwriting the original.

## Relatio…

title: Channels: Cut with one channel targeted clears only that channel (#2698)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2698

Depends on #2695 (its commits are included); review/merge that first. Only the last commit (e183a5c) belongs to this PR.

## Root cause
`edit.cut` is not one of the commands that follow the Channels panel target (`channel_cmds::routed`). It also never checked the target itself. So with a single colour channel (e.g. Red) targeted, Cut always ran the whole-layer path: it copied the full RGBA layer and cleared every channel in the selection.

## Fix
Cut now checks the target in the same way as #2695's Copy and Paste. With a colour channel targeted (`channel_clip::cut`), it matches Photoshop:
- It copies that channel as a grayscale clip, reusing #2695's `channel_clip::copy`.
- It fills the cut area of that channel only with the background colour's value for that channel. The background colour is first encoded in the layer's colour model, so this works at every depth and in every mode. Partial selection coverage blends towards that value.
- The other channels and the layer's transparency are untouched.
- The whole Cut is one undo step.

Nothing changes when the composite or an alpha channel is targeted. A pixel lock still refuses before anything is copied.

## Tests
- `channel_clip::tests::cut_a_colour_channel_clears_only_that_channel` sets up Red targeted, a rect selection and a non-default background colour, then runs Cut. It checks that:
  - the clip is grayscale and holds the old red values;
  - red in the rect takes the background's red, while green, blue and alpha are unchanged;
  - pixels outside the selection are unchanged;
  - a single undo restores everything.
- With the `edit.cut` change reverted, the test fails (the clip is `Rgb`, not grayscale); with the change restored, it passes.

author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Pixel Aspect Ratio and its Correction toggle were stored but never used by the canvas, so the image always showed square pixels.

The canvas transform now carries the displayed pixel aspect ratio and stretches document x by it before rotation and flip. Drawing, the pointer-to-document mapping (painting lands under the cursor), pan and zoom-about, rulers and grid, Fit/Fill on Screen, scrollbars, the Navigator box and paste-in-place visibility all use it. Correction is now on by default, like Photoshop; with the default Square ratio nothing changes. The document's pixels don't change. The Move tool's drag arrow now goes through the same transform, so it also follows flip and rotation.

A corrected view is drawn on the CPU canvas path for now, like a flipped view, because the GPU shader assumes square pixels. Left for follow-ups: elliptical brush cursors, and keeping the ratio per document (it's view state today; PSD resource 1064 isn't read or written).

Tests cover the stretched screen rect, mapping round trips with flip and rotation, a click painting the right pixel at 2:1, correction off restoring square display, and Fit/Fill with the stretched width.

Closes #2594.

title: Color Replacement tool on the toolbar (#1045)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Adds the Color Replacement tool to the toolbar. The engine already had `paint.colorReplacement`, but there was no way to use it with the mouse.

The tool sits in the Brush (B) flyout after the Mixer Brush, so B and Shift+B cycle to it, and `ui.set` can select it. It works like the other brush tools: brush cursor, `[` and `]`, Alt+right-drag. The options bar has Mode, Sampling (Continuous, Once, Background Swatch), Limits, Tolerance and Anti-alias, each mapped to the command parameter of the same name, and the foreground colour is the replacement colour. Strokes show live while you drag, and each stroke is one history step.

To make the live view match the result at the end of a drag, `LiveDab` can now show the stroke's last dab while dragging, and the recolouring code is shared between the live view and the commit. `paint.colorReplacement` now refuses a mask, channel or Quick Mask target; before, it ignored the target and always recoloured the layer.

Engine gaps I didn't paper over: there's no Sample All Layers option, and Find Edges is Contiguous without the soft tolerance edge rather than Photoshop's edge-preserving version. The new options aren't settable through `ui.set` yet (same as Background Eraser's).

The icon is Lucide's brush with two swap arrows added, listed in ATTRIBUTION.md. The new label is translated in all 16 catalogs. Tests cover each sampling mode on a red/blue image at 8 and 16 bits, Contiguous vs Discontiguous, every options-bar control reaching the command, the live view matching the result, undo/redo, the B cycle and the flyout.

Closes #1045.

title: Brush: Wet Edges acts on the whole stroke, not each dab (#2088)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2088

## Root cause
`BrushContext::rasterize` multiplied every dab by its own wet-edge profile (half the paint inside, full paint at the rim). The stroke buffer then max-accumulated these dabs. Along the stroke, each pixel took the strongest value from any neighbouring dab, and that was usually another dab's darker rim. The result was a chain of rings instead of one stroke with a lighter interior.

## Fix (`crates/paint/src/render.rs`)
- With Wet Edges, a dab no longer applies the profile itself. It accumulates into the stroke buffer like any other dab (flow builds up to the opacity ceiling). It also records how deep it reaches each pixel (`1 − rn`).
- The coverage tile keeps the deepest value any dab reaches at each pixel (`CovTile::depth`). This buffer is allocated only for wet strokes.
- The wet-edge transfer is applied to the stroke's accumulated coverage at composite time, in the same place as the other stroke-level masks. This covers `composite`, `coverage_at`/`coverage_in` (live stroke trail, retouch tools), `dense_coverage`, the tail preview and symmetry unions (depth is max-merged). The live preview and the committed result therefore match.
- As a result, the stroke's interior is evenly light and only the stroke's own outline is darker, for both hard and soft tips. Overlapping or self-crossing parts of one stroke don't darken.
- `rasterize` (a single dab, used by the per-dab retouch footprints) still applies the profile to that one dab. For a single dab the result is the same as before.
- Behaviour change: wet strokes now build up with Flow like normal strokes. They used to max-accumulate. The interior is still capped at half the ceiling.
- No new allocations on the per-dab path, and the per-tile work stays limited to the dirty tiles.

## Tests
- New: `brush_tests::wet_edges_shape_the_stroke_not_each_dab`. It paints a straight stroke of overlapping dabs (40 px, hardness 0.8) and checks that the alpha along the centre line varies by less than 0.02 and…

Added an egui event test covering:

- Wheel-up zoom increases the zoom level.
- Wheel-down zoom decreases the zoom level.
- Wheel zoom does not alter the document center.

title: Channels: Delete with one channel targeted clears only that channel (#2720)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2720

**Root cause:** `edit.clear` never looked at the Channels panel target. It isn't one of the commands `channel_cmds::routed()` restricts to the targeted colour channel, so with Red targeted it filled every channel of the Background with the background colour, and made a normal layer's pixels transparent.

**Fix:** with a single colour channel targeted, Clear now sets only that channel inside the selection (or the whole canvas) to the background colour's value for it (converted to the layer's colour model, so it works for RGB, CMYK, Lab and any depth). Partly selected pixels blend. The other channels and the layer's transparency stay, and it is still one undo step. The new helpers are `channel_cmds::targeted_color` and `channel_cmds::clear_color_channel`, and `edit.clear` in `commands.rs` calls them.

**Relation to #2712 (Cut, #2698):** same behaviour for Cut. This PR is based on `main` and touches different lines (Clear doesn't need the clipboard). The fill loop in #2712's `channel_clip::cut` does the same thing as `clear_color_channel`, so once both are merged, Cut can call `clear_color_channel` instead.

**Tests:** `channel_cmds::tests::clear_with_a_colour_channel_targeted_clears_only_that_channel` covers the Background and a normal layer at 16-bit: target Red, make a rect selection, Delete. Only red changes inside the rect, nothing changes outside, and one undo restores it. Without the fix it fails: the pixel becomes `[0.8, 0.1, 0.9, 1.0]` (every channel set to the background colour).

title: Marquee hinting follows a rotated view like the release does (#2512)
author: switch87
body:
The live ants for the Rectangular/Elliptical Marquee (and Object Selection) were an axis-aligned screen box built from the two projected corners of the drag:

```rust
let r = Rect::from_two_pos(xf.to_screen(a[0], a[1]), xf.to_screen(b[0], b[1]));
```

A rotated view projects the drag's document-space rectangle onto a rotated one, and the box through two of its corners is a different shape in a different place. On a 30° view a corner of the preview landed **21 × 50 px** away from the corner of the selection it previews. The release was always right, only the hinting was drawn elsewhere.

`marquee_drag_ants` now builds the outline in document space and maps every point through the view: four corners for the rectangle, the ellipse inscribed in it for the elliptical marquee (with as many vertices as its size on screen asks for, as `ellipse_points` does). Every point is snapped to the half-pixel grid like every other ants outline (`marching_ants_segments`), so the lines stay crisp at any zoom. Unrotated the mapping is only a scale, and the corners come out where they always did — the existing `the_live_outline_snaps_to_pixels_and_matches_the_committed_selection` keeps passing unchanged.

## Tests

`marquee_tests::the_live_outline_matches_the_committed_selection_in_a_rotated_view` drags a marquee in a 30° view for both tools and checks what is drawn against the selection the release commits:

- each corner of the rectangular marquee is the mapped corner of the dragged rectangle (0.01 px tolerance),
- each point of the elliptical marquee maps back (`to_doc`) onto the dragged ellipse,
- and the release commits what the hinting showed.

With the old axis-aligned box the same test fails on corner 1 at `[486.5, 201.5]` where the rectangle's corner is at `[507.5, 251.5]`.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib` — 1658 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean

title: Type: tabs advance to tab stops; Tab key types a tab (#1881)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Tabs in type layers now advance to the next tab stop instead of rendering as a single space (the box-glyph part was already fixed in #1942).

Stops use a 36 pt interval, measured from the anchor for point text and from the box's left edge for paragraph text. The layout keeps the tab in the text and only widens its advance, so carets, selections and PSD round trips are unchanged. Paragraph text breaks lines with the real tab widths: it starts from a safe upper bound (a space plus one interval) and re-breaks until the widths settle, so expanded tabs never overflow the box and lines don't wrap early. Centred and right-aligned lines stay aligned.

Pressing Tab in the Type tool now types a tab, as in Photoshop.

Limits: custom tab stops from PSDs aren't read yet, so only the default stops apply, and 36 pt is my assumption for Photoshop's default (I couldn't find it documented). Stops are measured from the box edge, not the paragraph indent, and a justified line containing a tab can end slightly short of the right edge.

The io and engine corpus tests pass with no differences.

Closes #1881.

title: Lasso: ⌘-drag outside the selection moves the layer (#2725)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2725

**Depends on #2699.** This branch is based on #2699's branch and extends its `lasso_ui::handed_over()`. Until #2699 merges, the diff here includes its commit; only the last commit (a87c6b1d) belongs to this PR.

## Root cause
With the Lasso, `canvas::tool_event` calls `lasso_ui::pointer` before it reaches the ⌘ temporary-Move check (`canvas::command_moves_layer`, which already lists the Lasso). `pointer` took every press outside the selection, so a ⌘-drag drew an outline. `lasso_ui::canvas_input` also forwarded move and release events only for an outline or a selection move, so the canvas never saw the rest of a layer drag.

## Fix (`crates/ui-egui/src/lasso_ui.rs`)
- `pointer`: a press where `command_moves_layer` holds is handed to the canvas, the same way a press inside the selection already is.
- `handed_over`: also covers a Move drag the canvas started for the Lasso, and `move_blocked` (a locked layer, so Photoshop's lock message still appears when the pointer moves).

A ⌘-drag inside the selection already cut and floated the selected pixels (`selection_drag_kind`), and it still does.

Related: #2684 (`event_tool` and the snapping for the temporary Move). That change doesn't conflict with this one.

## Tests
- `lasso_ui::tests::real_canvas_cmd_drag_outside_the_selection_moves_the_layer`: drives the real canvas (egui_kittest). It does a ⌘-drag on a painted layer with no selection, then checks that the layer moved, that no outline is left in progress and that no selection was made. Without the fix it fails: `left: (1.0, 0.0) right: (0.0, 1.0)`, so the layer did not move.
- A temporary probe, not committed, confirmed two more cases. A ⌘-drag inside a selection still floats the pixels. A ⌘-drag on the locked Background shows the lock message.

title: Smart filter edits: re-render from cached stages, in a background job
author: twentymls
body:
## Problem

Clicking a smart filter's eye in the Layers panel (or editing a smart filter's params, blending, order) froze the window with no feedback, then everything updated at once. Two causes:

- `edit_filters` re-rendered the smart object from the placed source through **every** visible filter, so hiding the top filter of a stack reran all the filters under it.
- It ran through `Session::edit`, not a job, so the work happened on the UI thread: no progress, no cancel, the eye didn't change until the render finished.

## Change

- **Cached render stages** (`smart_cmds/stack_cache.rs`): each render keeps the placed source and the result after every visible filter, keyed by blake3 of the source contents, the placement (transform, warp, perspective, stack mode, format, canvas) and the filters so far (command, params, blend, opacity). A re-render starts from the deepest cached stage, so an edit only reruns the filters from the edited one up. Bounded at 768 MiB (64 entries, least recently used dropped first); Edit › Purge › All drops it. Adding a filter on top benefits too, since `add_smart_filter` goes through the same render.
- **Background job**: `edit_filters` applies the edit at once (so bad params such as an out-of-range `index` still fail immediately) and re-renders through `jobs::edit_job`. Started with `Session::start` (the UI, the control channel), it runs on a worker with progress per filter and stops between filters when cancelled; `Session::execute` behaves as before.

## Measurements

Release build, M-series Mac, a 3000×4498 RGB 8-bit smart object with five smart filters (Lens Blur 45, Wave, Gaussian Blur 35, Motion Blur 220, Add Noise 24), timed through `photocraft-cli serve`:

| Action | Before (v0.6.0) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Hide the top filter (Add Noise) | 1.33 s | 0.02 s |
| Show it again | 1.49 s | 0.02 s |
| Hide the bottom filter (Lens Blur) | 0.85 s | 0.74 s (reruns the four above it) |
| Show it again | 1.52 s | 0.02 s |

title: Selection: moving a selection outline snaps its bounds, not the pointer (#2736)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2736

**Root cause.** `snap_ui::begin` picks the snap gesture from the tool alone. A marquee is a "point tool", so a drag that starts *inside* the selection (which moves the outline, or with ⌘ cuts the pixels into a floating piece) snapped the pointer like a new marquee corner. The outline then moved by however far the pointer jumped, so its edges ended up next to the target, not on it. The Lasso isn't a point tool, so it didn't snap at all.

**Fix** (`crates/ui-egui/src/snap_ui.rs`):
- `begin` now takes the press modifiers. When `canvas::selection_drag_kind` says the press drags the selection, it starts a new `Gesture::SelectionMove { rect }` over the selection's bounds (plus the floating offset). That rect snaps the same way the Move tool's box does.
- The selection's own (starting) edges are removed from the targets, so the outline can't snap back to where it began. A ⌘-cut piece also leaves its own layer out of the targets.
- The Move tool's box isn't drawn for this gesture; the marching ants already show the outline.

**Relations.** #2684 makes the same `begin(app, p, mods)` signature change, with the same doc comment and call site, so whichever PR merges second should rebase cleanly. #2675 (`retarget_move`) and #2699 (`begin_guide`) touch nearby lines in `snap_ui.rs` but not the same ones.

**Tests.** `snap_ui::tests::selection_drag_snaps_the_selection_bounds` covers Rectangular Marquee, Lasso and ⌘-cut. In each case the outline's right edge comes within 2 px of a guide while the pointer is 7 px from the document centre. Without the fix it fails: the selection ends at 175–225 instead of 170–220.

**Commands**
- `cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- snap selection marquee lasso` (144 passed)
- `cargo clippy -j 4 -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt -p photocraft-ui-egui -- --check`

title: Channels: Delete with an alpha channel targeted fills that channel (#2734)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2734

**Depends on #2730** (this branch is based on it; the first commit is #2730's). Only the last commit belongs to this PR.

**Root cause:** `edit.clear` is not in the channel-routed command set (unlike Edit › Fill), so it never saw an alpha channel or Quick Mask target and always cleared the active layer. Its precondition was `has_pixel_layer`, so it was also disabled on a non-pixel layer even with a channel targeted.

**Fix:**
- `channel_cmds::targeted_channel(s)` returns the targeted alpha channel or the Quick Mask (as `"target"` params); `channel_cmds::clear_channel` fills the selection (or the canvas) of it with the background colour, as gray, through Fill's compositing (new `fill_cmds::fill_color`), so partly selected pixels blend. The layer is untouched, and it is one undo step ("Clear").
- `edit.clear` checks that target first, then the colour-channel target from #2730, then clears the layer as before. Its precondition is now `has_pixel_or_channel`, like `edit.fill`.

**Tests:** `channel_cmds::tests::clear_with_an_alpha_channel_or_quick_mask_targeted_fills_it_not_the_layer` (alpha channel: selected area becomes the background colour, outside unchanged, layer unchanged, one undo; Quick Mask: mask filled, layer unchanged). Without the fix it fails (`left: 1.0, right: 0.0`: the channel stays white).

title: Actions: record File › Save and Save As steps and replay them (#2032)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #2032 (the save steps; renaming an action follows in a separate PR)

## Root cause
File › Save and Save As are handled by the desktop shell (`menus.rs` → `PhotocraftApp::save_as`, which opens the save dialog, the TIFF Options prompt or a background save job). They never pass through `Session::execute`, so they were never added to `session.journal`, which is what `actions.record` / `actions.stop` copy steps from. `actions_cmds::replayable` would also have dropped them, since neither id is an engine command.

## Fix
- **Shell (`ui-egui/src/lib.rs`, `menus.rs`, `tiff_options_ui.rs`):** once a save has its target, the shell journals it, as it already does for the view commands:
  - File › Save back to the document's own PSD/PSB/.pcraft → `["file.save", {}]`
  - Save As (direct path, after the save dialog, or after the TIFF Options answer) → `["file.saveAs", {"path": …, "tiffLayers": bool?}]`. The format comes from the path's extension.
- **Engine (`actions_cmds.rs`):** new `shell_save_command()`; `replayable()` accepts these steps.

title: Brush cursor: Normal Brush Tip ring on the tip's real 50% contour (#2744)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2744

**Root cause.** #2167 changed the soft tip falloff (`photocraft_paint::tip_falloff`) to `(1 - t²)⁴`. Its 50 % point is at `t = √(1 - ½^¼) ≈ 0.399` of the way from the hard core to the edge. The Normal Brush Tip cursor in `canvas.rs` still used `r · (0.5 + 0.5 · hardness)`, the midpoint of the old smoothstep. Soft brushes got a ring that was too large: at size 21, hardness 0 it was 5.25 px instead of 4.19 px, and at hardness 50 it was 7.88 px instead of 7.34 px. Hard brushes were unaffected.

**Fix.** A new pure helper, `photocraft_paint::half_coverage_radius(radius, hardness)`, inverts `tip_falloff` (NaN hardness counts as 0, the rest is clamped). The cursor now calls it, so the ring and the engine use the same formula. That one line in `canvas.rs` is separate from the Pencil cursor arm that #2694 changes.

**Tests.** `brush_tests::half_coverage_radius_is_the_tips_50_percent_contour` checks `tip_falloff` at the helper's radius for hardness 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 0.99: each value is 0.5 ± 1e-3. It also checks hardness 1 (the full radius) and NaN (a finite result). With the old formula in the helper, the test fails with `hardness 0: ring at 5.25`.

**Commands**
- `cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-paint --lib -- half_coverage tip_falls`
- `cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- cursor`
- `cargo clippy -j 4 -p photocraft-paint -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt -p photocraft-paint -p photocraft-ui-egui -- --check`

title: Print on Windows, installed ICC profiles, and Mirror
author: Moiztermind
body:
Closes #2697.

File › Print couldn't reach a printer on Windows (it spools with `lp`), and the profile menus
only listed the built-ins. This closes both gaps.

**What changes**
- **Windows printing:** a Printer menu listing the system's printers; Print Settings… opens the
  driver's own dialog; the paper comes from the driver; the image prints through GDI with ICM
  off, so "PhotoCraft Manages Colors" reaches the printer unconverted.
- **Installed profiles:** Print, Proof Setup, Convert to Profile and Assign Profile list every
  ICC profile installed in the OS (Windows, macOS, Linux) after the built-ins.

title: Fix Brush Preset picker dismissal on quick trackpad taps
author: zi-ger
body:
Fixes #2360.

title: Color Sampler tool (#1046)
author: roaldosulejmani
body:
Adds the **Color Sampler** to the Eyedropper (`I`) flyout: click to pin numbered sample points to canvas pixels, drag to move, Alt-click (or drag off-canvas) to remove, **Clear All** in the options bar, at most 10 per document. Each point reads one composite pixel (RGB 0–255 and naive device CMYK, the same as the pointer readout) and the Info panel lists them under their number with the position in the ruler unit; the readouts refresh when the document changes.

Points are per-document engine view state (`DocState.color_samplers`): they belong to their document, are discarded on close, and are not saved to `.pcraft` or PSD. They are driven by commands shared by the UI, CLI, control channel and MCP (`view.colorSamplers.add/.move/.delete/.clear/.list`); the mutations change no pixels and add no History step.

Points follow the canvas geometry (crop, Canvas Size, Image Size, Image rotation/flip, rotated crop) through a pending `Session.sampler_map` that `Session::edit` applies before culling the points that land outside the new canvas; the count removed is reported in the status bar.

Non-goals: averaged sample sizes, ICC/profile-managed CMYK, Camera Raw samplers, persistence, Measurement Log / Ruler.

title: PSD: parallel RLE for the merged image; layer channels decode and gather on all cores
author: Elvis33LE
body:
P43/P44 follow-up from measuring the "Save .psd / Open .psd, 36 MP, 3 layers" rows (baseline 3 047 ms / 3 535 ms on the M4 Pro; 2.86 s / 1.12 s on an RTX 3090 machine). Instrumenting the export/import stages showed:

- the merged image's **PackBits RLE ran on one thread** over ~144 MB (`encode_rle` in the `psd` crate, row by row),
- the layer gather (`to_interleaved` over every full-canvas layer) was sequential,
- and each layer's channels decoded one after another on open.

**What changes**

- `encode_rle` packs rows in parallel chunks (rows are independent; each chunk yields its count bytes and packed rows, concatenated in order; a worker's error surfaces like the sequential path's). This is the merged image's compression and the biggest single win.
- The layer gather runs in row bands on all cores before the per-channel RLE, and `pixel_channels` no longer clones the full surface per layer (it borrows and returns its warnings).
- A layer's channels decode side by side on open (the warnings land in the same order afterwards).

**Measured** (same document, RTX 3090, release): save **2.86 s → 2.55–2.64 s**, open's import stage **1.12 s → 1.07 s** (`psd_to_document` 745 → 564 ms). The remaining save time is dominated by the merged composite render itself (~0.7 s of CPU compositing), and the open time by the first full refresh.

**Tests:** the whole `psd` suite (177 + 27, including the RLE round trips and the per-row count-table cases), the `io` suites, and the PSD corpus round trips are green; clippy/fmt clean.

title: Add Anchor Point and Delete Anchor Point tools (#1044)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Adds Photoshop's Add Anchor Point and Delete Anchor Point tools to the Pen flyout (P cycles Pen, Add, Delete). They work on the same paths Direct Selection edits: a targeted vector mask or the active shape's path, then the work path. Hovering highlights the segment or anchor a click would change, the cursor shows a + or −, Alt swaps the two tools and Cmd/Ctrl gives Direct Selection.

Two new commands, `path.addAnchor` and `path.deleteAnchor`, back them, so the CLI and MCP can do the same edits. Adding splits the segment at the clicked point with de Casteljau, so a curve keeps its exact shape. Deleting joins the neighbours and keeps their handles; Photoshop re-fits the curve there, so a deleted anchor can change the shape more than it would in Photoshop (a follow-up). A closed subpath stays closed, and a path's only anchor can't be deleted. Each click is one history step, and bad indices or `t` return an error without touching the document.

The tool icons are derived from Lucide `pen-tool`, with an ATTRIBUTION.md row. Labels are translated in all 16 catalogs.

Tests cover the geometry (the split stays within 0.01 px of the original curve), undo/redo, saved paths, shape layers at 8/16/32 bits, vector masks, bad params and the canvas clicks. panic_hunt is green.

Closes #1044.

title: Paint a pen tap at its own pressure, not full or zero (#1798)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Pen taps painted a full-size dab no matter how hard you pressed. A tap often starts and ends before the UI frame runs, and by then the platform has already cleared the pen sample (macOS proximity, a non-tablet button-up, the web's pointerleave) or set it back to pressure 0 (X11, macOS hover). So the press read as a mouse at pressure 1.0, or got the lift's 0. The last moves of a stroke that lifted in the same frame had the same problem and left a full-pressure blob at the end.

The stylus now ignores zero-pressure samples in a frame that had real contact, and falls back to that frame's last contact sample when the feed is empty or at 0. A tap (released where it was pressed) paints at the highest pressure seen since the press, so a tap spread over two frames isn't stuck at its first light sample. Mouse taps still paint full size.

Tests drive the real canvas with egui events and pen samples: light vs firm taps give proportionally sized dabs, a 0/0.6/0 tap paints at 0.6, a two-frame tap gets its peak, a mouse tap is full size, and a stroke keeps its last real pressure whether the lift clears the pen or reports 0. I couldn't test on real hardware. On Windows, winit reports pressure 0 as no pressure at all, so a contact whose only sample is 0 still paints at 1.0. This may also explain the release blobs in #1302, but I couldn't check that on a Mac.

Closes #1798. #1933 is a duplicate.

title: Layers panel: load a fallback font for layer names in other scripts (#2275)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Layer names in scripts that Inter doesn't cover (Thai in this issue, also Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari and so on) showed boxes in the Layers panel even when the canvas found a font. The UI's lazy font loader only knew CJK and a short list of Thai font paths (#2280).

This adds `photocraft_text::scripts`. It maps characters to 20 scripts and picks candidate fonts by file name (Noto, Windows, macOS and common Linux fonts) from a one-time listing of the system font folders. The UI loader tries each script once when one of its characters is missing, reads at most six files, and registers the first face whose cmap really has the character, at the lowest priority so Latin text keeps Inter. Plain Latin text loads nothing, and the web build doesn't change.

egui shapes each font run, so Thai marks and Arabic joining look right, but there's no bidi yet: Arabic and Hebrew words show in left-to-right order. Fallback is per script, so a rare character the chosen font lacks stays a box.

Tests build tiny in-memory fonts for Thai, Arabic and Devanagari, so they don't depend on installed fonts. Checked visually with Leelawadee UI and Nirmala UI: Thai, Devanagari, Arabic and Hebrew layer names render. Separate gap noticed while testing: the canvas's own fallback list has no Indic fonts, so Devanagari type still shows "no glyph" on the canvas.

Closes #2275.

title: PSD export: pad regenerated fill blocks to 4 bytes, as Photoshop does
author: Sir-Starch
body:
## Summary

PSD/PSB export now pads regenerated fill blocks (`PtFl`, `SoCo`, `GdFl`) to a multiple of 4 inside the length field, as Photoshop does.

This makes the exported file match what Photoshop itself writes. It has not been tested in Photoshop (none was available), only against Photoshop-authored files.

## Cause

Photoshop writes every layer-level tagged block with its pad inside the length, to a multiple of 4. All 258 Photoshop-authored fixtures in `corpus/photoshop` and all 309 in `corpus/psd-tools` (48 of them PSB) follow this. The exporter padded regenerated blocks to *even* only, so a Pattern Fill's `PtFl` came out 2 bytes short of the boundary for half of all pattern names (e.g. 266 or 330 bytes), which left the layer record's extra data unaligned.

## How it was found

- Re-saved every corpus file with `photocraft-cli convert`, then diffed the tagged-block sets against the originals with psd-tools.
- Wrote a raw-bytes structural linter (section lengths, block/extra-data alignment, channel data sizes, RLE row tables, mask record sizes) and calibrated it on the originals: 0 violations on all 258 files in `corpus/photoshop`.
- Re-saving `stroke.psd` produced two `PtFl` blocks of 330 bytes. After this change that file has 0 such violations.

## Fix

`fill_rule` in `crates/io/src/psd_export.rs` zero-pads the regenerated fill block to a multiple of 4 where it is produced. The generic pad loop is unchanged on purpose: padding every layer block to 4 there also changes preserved blocks, which `psd_structure` (`lfx2` must stay byte-identical), `roundtrip` and `comps_artboards` (`shmd` is length-structured) rely on staying as they were read.

## Validation

- New `crates/io/tests/psd_block_alignment.rs`: Pattern Fill layers with names of 1 to 10 characters, 8/16/32-bit, PSD and PSB; every layer block must be 4-aligned. Fails on `main` (`block PtFl is 266 bytes`), passes with this change.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-io --lib --tests --no-fail-fast`: 51 test binari…

title: TGA: targa options asks for 24 or 32 bits/pixel, same as in Photoshop
author: Matty-PW
body:
Follow up to #2482 

Saving a Targa picked its depth automatically. Photoshop asks (Targa Options > Resolution) and texture workflows need to choose, and need the colours under a zero alpha kept exactly.

### What changes
- **Targa Options dialog:** Save As and Save a Copy to an RGB `.tga` ask for 24 or 32 bits/pixel, starting at 32 when the document has an alpha channel as Photoshop does.
- **Export As:** TGA gets a Resolution dropdown (Auto, 24 or 32). Auto keeps the old behaviour.
- **Scripting:** `tgaBits: 24 | 32` on the save commands, batch tools, control channel and MCP, plus `--tga-bits` on the CLI. Scripted saves never show the dialog.

### How each depth is written
- **32-bit:** a single alpha channel becomes the file's alpha. Colours are written straight, never premultiplied or cleared under alpha 0. Without an alpha channel, layer transparency is used.
- **24-bit:** no alpha. Transparency is composited over white, with a warning naming any alpha channels left out.
- **Behaviour change:** an opaque RGB document with two or more alpha channels is now written as 32-bit with an opaque alpha, matching what #2482 measured in Photoshop.

### Tests and docs
- New tests in io, engine, ui-egui, MCP and the CLI, including a byte-identical RGB + alpha round trip and an all-black alpha that keeps every colour.
- clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers` and `panic_hunt` pass.
- Book, control protocol, CLI and param docs updated; new strings translated in all 16 locales.

### Not covered
- Photoshop's 16 bits/pixel option.
- Layer transparency at 32 bits without an alpha channel (the open question in #2482).

title: Batch: skip recorded view steps in batch and droplets (#2752)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2752

**Depends on #2746.** This branch is stacked on #2746 (record Save / Save As in actions), because it extends the `retain` that #2746 adds to Batch and Create Droplet. Only the last commit (`Batch: skip recorded view steps…`) belongs to this PR; once #2746 merges I'll rebase so the diff shows only that commit. title: Spot Healing: Create Texture keeps the film grain (#2104)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2104

### Where #2104 stands on `main`
I re-ran the reporter's synthetic measurement on `main` @ 9ccea326. The image is 400×300 flat (150, 120, 100) with Gaussian grain of σ 12. Content-Aware and Proximity Match already keep the grain. #2202 (merged after the reporter's retest at 29d5f791) made Content-Aware copy patches instead of blurring them. **Create Texture** was the part still losing grain, and that is what this PR fixes.

### Root cause
`inpaint::synthesize` (Create Texture) averaged each new block 50/50 into the overlap that was already synthesised. Two unrelated grain patterns averaged together keep only about 1/√2 of their standard deviation, so the fill came out smoother than its surroundings. Overlapping strokes each sample the strokes before them, so the loss compounded: 57 % of the grain was left after eight strokes.

### Fix
Blocks are now joined along the **minimum-error boundary cut** from A. Efros, W. Freeman, *Image Quilting for Texture Synthesis and Transfer*, SIGGRAPH 2001. This is the paper the module already cites; the old code used a feather instead of the cut. A dynamic-programming cut runs through the overlap with the block to the left and with the block above. Each pixel is copied from either the earlier fill or the new block and is never averaged, so the grain survives. The change is limited to `synthesize`, which only Spot Healing's Create Texture calls.

### Measurements
Synthetic grain image, red channel, as % of the untouched grain (Photoshop 27.11 numbers are from the issue).

One dab, hardness 100 (std-dev in the healed disc; surroundings 12.06):

| Content-Aware (`main`) | 85 % | 91 % |

title: Arrow-key nudges: a run of nudges is one History state, with Tools preferences (#2259)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
Closes #2259

Tapping or holding an arrow key nudged the selected layers one pixel per History state, so one Undo took back one pixel. A run of nudges of the same thing is now one state, and one Undo takes the whole run back. A preference turns it off.

## What changes

Nudges that follow each other share one `coalesce` key, which the engine already folds into one history step. A run goes on while:

- the previous nudge was of the same thing (the selected layers, or the selection outline),
- it came at most **Nudge Bundle Pause** ago (default 1 s, longer than a key's auto-repeat delay, so a held key is one state),
- and nothing else touched the document in between: another edit, Undo/Redo, a different layer selected or a save each end the run.

Covered: arrow keys with the Move tool, ⌘/Ctrl+arrows from other tools (#2474), arrow keys with a selection tool (the outline), and the Free Transform box (it keeps its own session history, its nudges fold into one session step).
Not changed: selected pixels float until dropped, which was already one state. ⌥+arrow copies the layer each time, so it never joins a run.

Preferences › Tools:

- **Bundle Arrow-Key Nudges** (`tools.bundleNudges`, default on). Off gives a state per press, as before.
- **Nudge Bundle Pause (ms)** (`tools.nudgeBundlePauseMs`, 100–10000, default 1000). Hidden while bundling is off.

Both work through `prefs.set`, so agents can use them; an agent calling `layer.translate` / `select.transformSelection` itself gets the same with a shared `coalesce` key. Labels are translated in all catalogues; `docs/control-protocol.md` and the scorecard (TOOL-2259-1) are updated.

## Evidence

title: Esc deselects when no active operation needs cancelling
author: mroxso
body:
## What

Closes #2674

`Esc` now runs Select ▸ Deselect when a selection exists and no active operation needs the key. `⌘/Ctrl+D` keeps working as before.

## How

`shortcuts::handle` already gives `Esc` to the operations that own it (transform, pen, lasso, polygon, crop, magnetic lasso, distort, inline type) and returns early for menus, dialogs, the unsaved-changes prompt and focused text fields. The new fallback sits after all of those and only consumes the key when a selection actually exists, so nothing changes when there is nothing to deselect.

It also stays out of the way of states that handle `Esc` later in the frame (after `logic`): full screen mode, the ⌘K palette, the canvas tool menu, the canvas layer menu, the brush picker, Rotate View, Adaptive Wide Angle, the Filter Gallery, the TIFF prompt, any open egui popup (combo boxes, context menus) and the toolbar tool flyout.

## Tests

- `escape_deselects_when_nothing_else_needs_cancelling` — Esc clears the selection; with no selection Esc is untouched (no history step, no error).
- `escape_with_a_dialog_open_cancels_the_dialog_not_the_selection` — the dialog keeps `Esc`.
- `escape_with_the_palette_open_does_not_deselect` — the palette keeps `Esc`.

Full `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui` (1719 lib tests + integration), `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are green; `cargo xtask layers` passes. Verified against the running app over the control channel: `select.all` → `ui.key Escape` → `select.deselect` reports disabled (selection gone), a second `Esc` is a no-op. `cargo xtask wasm` could not run here (the wasm32-unknown-unknown target is not installed in this environment; untouched crates fail identically).

Closes #2674

title: Lasso: Free Transform drags work with the Lasso tool selected (#2153)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #2153 (part 2: Lasso selections not responding to transform operations). Part 1 (brush lag with the Navigator open, Windows, v0.5.0) is not addressed here; on `main` the Navigator already keeps its image during a live brush stroke (`navigator_waits_for_drag`).

## Root cause
The freehand Lasso reads its own pointer events (`lasso_ui::canvas_input`), and `canvas_view` clears the generic drag buttons whenever the Lasso is the selected tool. That reader forwards a press, but forwards moves and the release only while a lasso outline (or selection move) is in progress. With a Free Transform / Transform box open, the press reached the box (`transform_tool::pointer` runs first in `tool_event`), but the moves and release were dropped, so the box never changed. The Polygonal Lasso, the marquees and the path tools use the generic drag path, so transforms worked with them. The report reads as "lasso selections don't transform" because people transform right after drawing the selection, with the Lasso still selected.

## Fix
When a Free Transform box owns the pointer (`transform_owns_pointer`, already used for the Hand in #2302), the Lasso doesn't take the canvas input, and the box gets the usual drag events. One-line change in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`.

## Tests
- `transform_undo_tests::the_lasso_tool_does_not_swallow_a_free_transform_drag`: a lasso selection with the Lasso tool selected, then Free Transform, a corner drag through the real canvas, and Enter. The box scales and the resize is committed. It fails on `main` (the box stays at its original quad) and passes with the fix.

title: Actions: double-click an action to rename it (#2032)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2032 (together with #2746: #2746 records File › Save / Save As in actions, this PR adds renaming; with #2746 this completes #2032).

## Root cause
There was no way to rename an action: the engine had no rename command and double-clicking an action row in the Actions panel played it, so every action kept its default `Action N` name. In Photoshop, double-clicking an action's name edits it in place.

## What changed
- **Engine:** new command `actions.rename {"action": name|index, "name": str} → {action, index}`.
  - Empty, whitespace-only and duplicate names are rejected and the old name is kept (names stay unique because actions are addressed by name).
  - Nested `actions.play` steps that call the action by name (including pending steps while recording) and its function-key binding (`actions.play:<name>` shortcut override) follow the new name, so nothing silently stops working.
  - Refused during playback, like the other action edits. Persisted through the existing `actions.rev` bump.
  - The `actions.play:` prefix now lives in the engine (`PLAY_SHORTCUT_PREFIX`); the panel reuses it.
- **Actions panel:** double-clicking the action's name opens an in-place field with the name selected. Enter, Tab or clicking elsewhere commits through `actions.rename`, Esc cancels; a rejected name shows the reason in the status bar. Double-clicking elsewhere on the row still plays the action as before.
- `docs/control-protocol.md`: documents `actions.rename`.

PhotoCraft has no action sets yet, so only actions can be renamed. There is no Action Options… dialog either; this PR does not add one.

The edits are textually separate from #2746 (which touches the playback branch and `replayable` in the same files), #2441 and #1991.

## Tests
- `actions_cmds::tests::rename_keeps_calls_and_function_key_and_rejects_bad_names` (engine): rename by index → `actions.list` shows the new name, the nested call and F-key follow; empty, whitespace, duplicate, wrong-type, out-of-range and missing n…

title: Dock: drag a tab to reorder it within its group (#2272)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Dock tabs couldn't be dragged to reorder them. They only reacted to clicks, so dragging a tab moved the whole group instead.

Now you can drag a tab left or right along its strip to reorder it. A blue line shows where it will land, and a plain click still selects the tab. Dragging the empty part of the strip still moves the group, and so does dragging a tab off the strip, since moving a single panel to another group or floating it isn't supported yet. Lock Workspace stops reordering too.

The order is stored by tab name in `DockLayout.tabOrder`, so it survives the Color/Swatches swap between themes. It's saved in the remembered layout and in workspaces, and can be set with `ui.set {dock: {tabOrder: …}}`. Unknown names or malformed values fall back to the default order. `dockTabs` keeps using the default indices.

Tests cover dragging Paths before Layers in Pro and Studio, clicking after a reorder, the prefs and workspace round trips, bad saved orders, dragging a tab off the strip, and Lock Workspace.

Closes #2272.

title: Move tool: ⌘-drag with a painting tool floats the selected pixels from the control channel too (#2768)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2768

**Depends on #2684** (uses its `canvas::event_tool`). This branch is stacked on it, so the diff shows #2684's commit too until that one merges; the change here is the last commit.

### Root cause
`move_ui::moves_selected_pixels` asked `app.active_tool()`, which only sees `tool_override`, set by the canvas while ⌘ is physically held. The control channel (`ui.pointer`), MCP and tests send ⌘ on the event instead. `canvas::tool_event` turned that into the Move tool, but the selected-pixel checks inside the press still saw the Brush, so with a selection the drag moved the whole layer instead of floating the selected pixels.

### Fix
The press asks with the event's tool (`moves_selected_pixels_with(app, tool)`, where `tool` comes from `event_tool`) in:
- the floating-piece drop check at the top of `tool_event` (a second ⌘-drag keeps moving the same piece rather than dropping and re-cutting it)
- the Auto-Select pick and the float in the Move branch
- `move_lock::blocked`
- `snap_ui::moving_rect` (the snap box is the selection, not the layer)

Keyboard nudges still use `moves_selected_pixels(app)` as before.

### Tests
- `move_ui::tests::command_drag_with_a_painting_tool_moves_only_the_selected_pixels`: Brush, selection, two ⌘-drags with ⌘ sent on the event. The piece floats and moves, and the unselected pixels stay put. Without the fix it fails (`offset == None`, so nothing floats).

title: Eraser: Block mode (#2770)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2770

Depends on #2694 (its commit is included; this PR's own change is the last commit).

## What changed
Photoshop's Eraser has Mode: Brush / Pencil / **Block**. #2694 added Pencil; Block was missing because the paint engine had no square dab. Block erases a hard, aliased square of 16 **screen** pixels, so its size in document pixels is `16 / zoom` (taken at stroke start); Size, Hardness, Opacity and Flow don't apply.

- **paint**: `BrushSettings.square` (together with `aliased`) rasterises every pixel of the dab's whole-pixel grid square, ignoring angle and roundness. Serialised only when true, so existing brushes and presets are unchanged.
- **engine**: `paint.pencil` takes `"block": true`. The brush becomes a fresh square, aliased, full-opacity, full-flow brush of `brush_cmds::block_size(zoom)` = `round(16 / zoom)` px (clamped 1..5000), from the stroke's existing `"zoom"` param; colour, erase, smoothing and seed still come from the resolved brush. A `zoom` that is not a positive number returns an `Err`. The params doc lists `block` and `zoom`.
- **ui**: the Eraser's Mode dropdown gains Block. In Block mode the Eraser commits `paint.pencil` with `"block": true` (live and on release), shows the block's square cursor on the pixel grid, and greys out the brush preset/Size, Hardness, Opacity and Flow.

## Tests
- `pencil_tests::the_eraser_in_block_mode_erases_a_16_screen_px_square`: a soft, 5 px, 50 % opacity, 30 % flow Eraser in Block mode clicked on an opaque layer clears exactly a 16×16 square at zoom 1 and an 8×8 square at zoom 2, with no partial alpha, through `paint.pencil` with `"block": true`.
- Without the square dab in `paint/src/render.rs`, the test fails with `left: (208, 16, 16) right: (256, 16, 16)` (a round aliased disc instead of the square).

cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-paint --lib -- render brush
cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ig…

title: fix(compose, gpu): round dithered gradient fills to the document dept…
author: kavishkashehan726-sudo
body:
…h (#2755)

A live gradient's dither adds a fraction of a level of noise, but gradient fill layers kept it in float. Color Dodge divides by 1 - cs, so under a bright dodge layer that sub-level noise came out as speckle several levels high, and channels at 0 were lifted off black (coloured fringes).

title: Batch: a failed step inside a called action fails the file and the script (#2779)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2779

## Root cause
`actions.play` returns `Ok` with a `failed` entry when a step inside the called action fails. Action playback (headless and desktop) promotes that to a failure with `actions_cmds::nested_failure`, but two other step runners didn't:

- `automate_cmds::run_steps` (File › Scripts › Browse and Script Events) only treated `Err` as a failure, so the script reported `"ok": true` and ran the later steps.
- `file_cmds::batch` (File › Automate › Batch, and Run Droplet, which goes through it) ran each file in a fresh scratch session with no actions, so any batched action that calls another action failed on every file with `no action named …`.

## Fix
- `run_steps` checks `nested_failure`, records the error on that step and stops.
- `batch` gives each scratch session a copy of the caller's actions list and playback stack, and turns a nested failure into a per-file error (the file goes to `errors` and isn't saved, like any other failing step). Copying the playback stack means an action that batches itself is caught as a recursive call instead of recursing without end.

## Relation to #2746 / #2761
Both PRs change the `steps.retain(...)` filtering at the top of `batch` and `create_droplet`. This PR only changes the per-step result handling inside the batch closure and `run_steps`, so the diffs don't overlap.

## Tests
- `automate_cmds::tests::a_failed_step_inside_a_called_action_fails_scripts_and_batch`: a script stops on a failing nested action call; Batch plays a called action and reports a failure inside one as a file error; an action that batches itself returns instead of overflowing. Without the fix it fails (`ok` is `true`).

## Commands
- `cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-engine --lib -- batch script droplet actions`
- `cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored`
- `cargo clippy -j 4 -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt -p photocraft-engine -- --check`
- `cargo check -j 4 -p photocraft-ui-egui --ta…

title: Variables: applied text keeps the type layer's style (#2742)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Applying a data set that sets a type layer's text cleared the layer's style runs, so the text was redrawn from just the family, size and colour. Weight, italic, tracking, underline, caps and the paragraph settings were lost, both on the canvas and in Export Data Sets as Files.

Now the new text takes the style of the first character it replaces, and the first paragraph's settings, which is what Photoshop does. The value itself is still applied exactly as given, including CRLF line breaks from CSV imports. For a multi-paragraph layer, every paragraph now gets the first paragraph's settings (before, they all fell back to the defaults).

Tests cover the repro from the issue, a two-run layer (the result uses the first run's style), an empty value, undo, and a PSD export.

author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2786

Independent of #2783 (that PR fixes the same problem for the in-app File › Automate › Batch); this one only touches the CLI.

**Root cause**

`photocraft-cli batch` runs each input in a fresh `Headless::trusted_local()` session whose Actions list is empty, so an `actions.play` step fails with `no action named …` on every file. And `--actions` only accepted one action's steps, so there was no way to give the CLI the called actions: the Actions panel's own `actions.json` (`{"version": 1, "actions": [{"name", "steps"}…]}`) failed with `step needs "command"`. - Each per-file session gets the whole set, so nested Play Action steps resolve. The session's playback stack still stops self-recursion (`recursive action call`) and caps nesting at 16.

title: Layers: Layer via Copy duplicates every selected layer (#2777)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2777

## Root cause
`layer.new.layerViaCopy` (`layer_via` in `crates/engine/src/edit_cmds.rs`) always worked on the active layer only. Without a pixel selection it duplicated just that layer, and it never checked the layer selection. `layer.duplicate` already had a multi-layer path (`layer_multi_cmds::duplicate_selected`), but Layer via Copy didn't use it.

## Fix
With no pixel selection and more than one layer selected, Layer via Copy now calls `duplicate_selected`: every selected layer is copied in a single undo step, each copy goes directly above its original, and the copies become the new selection. Copies are made with `layer_copy`, the same function Duplicate Layer uses, so smart objects still share their content (#2222). The copies stay in place, as with single-layer Layer via Copy. The history step is named "Layer Via Copy". `duplicate_selected` now takes the history label as a parameter and also returns `"layer"` (the new active layer) next to `"layers"`.

When there is a pixel selection, nothing changes: Layer via Copy still copies only the selected pixels of the active layer.

## Tests

It checks that both layers are copied, each copy sits above its original, the copies are selected and it is one undo step. It then undoes, sets a pixel selection and checks that only one new layer is created. Without the fix it fails (`left: 4, right: 5`: only the active layer was copied).

title: Droplets: carry the actions their Play Action steps call (#2794)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2794

Depends on #2783: this branch is based on it (the per-file batch sessions get the caller's actions and playback stack there). Until #2783 merges, the diff here also shows its commit; the change for this issue is the last commit.

## Root cause
`file.automate.createDroplet` wrote only the chosen action's own steps. A Play Action step (`actions.play`) inside it names another action that the droplet file didn't contain. `photocraft-cli droplet` and the droplet's `.command` shim run `file.automate.runDroplet` in a fresh `Session` with no actions, so every file failed with `no action named …`.

## Fix
- `actions_cmds::called_actions` collects the actions the steps call, followed transitively through nested Play Action steps, with a seen-set and the 16-level playback cap. They come out in list order. Index references (`{"action": 1}`, which the panel's play button records) are rewritten to names so they resolve without the rest of the list.
- `createDroplet` saves them under `"calledActions"`. It doesn't use `"actions"`, because the CLI's `batch --actions` (#2792) reads that key as an action set.
- `runDroplet` passes them to `file.automate.batch` as `calledActions`. The per-file sessions then play from that list instead of the caller's. The list is parsed as data and capped at 4096 actions; a bad value is a `BadParams` error.
- Droplets without the key behave as before. Self-calls are still caught at playback by the existing recursion check.

## Tests
- `automate_cmds::tests::droplets_carry_the_actions_their_play_steps_call`:
  - A droplet whose action plays `Outer`, which in turn plays `Rotate` by index, embeds only `Rotate` and `Outer` and no `actions` key.
  - In a fresh `Session` it processes every file.
  - A droplet built from a self-calling action fails each file instead of looping.
  - An old-format droplet still runs.
- Fails without the fix: there is no `calledActions` in the file, and the fresh-session run reports `no action named \`Outer\`` for e…

title: View: Pattern Preview tiles the document around the canvas (#1067)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #1067.

View › Pattern Preview could be checked but did nothing: `view.patternPreview` only toggled a flag that nothing read. In Photoshop, Pattern Preview shows the document repeated as a seamless tile around the canvas, so what leaves one edge shows up at the opposite one. That's how tileable textures are made.

## Change
- New `pattern_preview.rs` works out which copies cover the visible canvas. It caps them at 31 per axis, centred on the view, so a tiny document zoomed far out stays cheap.
- GPU canvas: each copy is another paint callback over the same document texture, offset by whole document sizes in the tile shader (`ViewParams::offset`, in the spare view-uniform slots `d.xy`).
  - Nothing is composited again, and seams are exact.
  - The checkerboard is anchored per copy, so every copy looks the same.

title: Spot Healing: Content-Aware dab no longer scans every patch in full (#2771)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2771

## Root cause

A Content-Aware Spot Healing dab spent about 70 % of its time (`perf`) in `photocraft_algo::inpaint::onion_peel`, the initial fill at the coarsest pyramid level of `inpaint::complete`. For every hole pixel it computed the full 7×7 sum of squared differences against **every** valid source patch, with no early exit. The pyramid shrinks the hole to about four patches across, and the sampling window is about 4× the dab. So the coarsest level is always about 100² with ~10 000 sources and ~600 hole pixels, which made a dab cost ~200–450 ms whatever its size. The sampling window was already bounded; the problem was this exhaustive initialisation.

## Fix (results are bit-identical)

- **`onion_peel`**: still an exhaustive scan that picks the same source, the first minimum in source order, but most candidates are rejected early:
  - The target's known offsets and samples are gathered once per front pixel.
  - An upper bound on the best error comes from the filled neighbours' sources (shifted, as in PatchMatch propagation), or from every 16th source at the hole's edge.
  - A candidate's sum is abandoned once its mean exceeds that bound or reaches the best so far.
  - Sums keep the original order and only grow, so the winner, ties included, is unchanged.
- **PatchMatch `vote`**: the weight `exp(-cost / 2σ²)` is computed once per target, not once per covered pixel (49×).
- **PatchMatch `dist`**: a fast path for target patches fully inside a level with no void pixels: row slices, same summation order.

Content-Aware Fill, Remove, Patch and Content-Aware Move go through the same code, so they get faster too.

## Before / after

`retouch_bench` (a single-size focused variant), release, 6016×6016 8-bit, one single-dab stroke through `Session::execute`. The machine was heavily loaded (load average 27–52), so these are best of 3 alternating rounds × 5 dabs:

| Content-Aware dab | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 50 px | 178 ms | 63 ms |
| 100 px | 190 ms …

title: Pencil: 1 px lines step pixel by pixel, no doubled corners (#2139)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2139

## Root cause
The path walker spaced every brush's dabs by distance (Spacing × diameter, 0.25 px for a 1 px Pencil). The aliased Pencil snaps each dab to the pixel grid (`render::grid_center`), so along a sloped line the x and y pixel boundaries were crossed by different dabs: the dab sequence went `(x, y) → (x+1, y) → (x+1, y+1)` instead of stepping diagonally. That left an L-shaped doubled pixel at every step of the staircase, the uneven, thick look in the reporter's comparison.

## Fix
`crates/paint/src/dynamics.rs`: when the tip is aliased and its dabs are at most one pixel apart (`size × spacing ≤ 1`, e.g. 1–4 px Pencils at 25 %), `PathWalker` steps each segment pixel by pixel instead: one dab per pixel along the major axis, on the line between the pixels holding the segment's ends, placed at the pixel's dab centre (0.5 offset for odd diameters, 0 for even, matching `grid_center`). That is a Bresenham line. Larger or spaced-out Pencils, anti-aliased brushes, speed spacing (Spacing unchecked, with timestamps) and the airbrush keep the old distance walk. A non-finite or absurdly long span (> 10⁷ px) falls back to distance spacing, so there is no new panic or hang path.

Before / after, 1 px Pencil from (2.5, 2.5) to (22.5, 9.5):

```
before                        after
..##......................    ..##......................
....###...................    ....###...................
.......###................    .......###................
..........###.............    ..........##..............
............####..........    ............###...........
...............####.......    ...............###........
..................###.....    ..................###.....
.....................##...    .....................##...
```
Before: 24 pixels, with the runs overlapping by a column at 3 steps. After: 21 pixels, one per column.

2 and 3 px lines also come out regular. Freehand strokes with dense input points look practically unchanged. Each segment is now a…

title: Web: File › Open opens every selected file (#2802)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2802

## Root cause
The web build's file dialog service (`apps/photocraft-web/src/web.rs`) always called `rfd::AsyncFileDialog::pick_file()` and ignored `FileDialogRequest::Open { multiple, .. }`. `FileDialogAnswer::Contents(name, bytes)` could also hold only one file, so the shell had no way to receive more than one. The desktop build uses `pick_files()` and opens each path in its own tab.

## Change
- `crates/ui-egui/src/file_dialog.rs`: new `FileDialogAnswer::ContentsMany(Vec<(String, Vec<u8>)>)`. File › Open opens each file as its own document and reports a file that fails to open without stopping the rest, as the desktop's multi-path open does. Single-file pickers (Place, presets, scripts) take the first file if they are ever given this variant.
- `apps/photocraft-web/src/web.rs`: when the request has `multiple` set, use `pick_files()`, read every file and answer with `ContentsMany`. Single-file requests behave as before.

Dropping several files onto the web page already opened all of them, so it is unchanged.

## Tests
- `file_open::tests::the_web_opens_every_selected_file`: answering File › Open with three files (one broken) opens the two good ones as separate documents and shows an error notice for the broken one. It fails when only the first file is opened (`left: ["one.png"]`, `right: ["one.png", "two.jpg"]`).

## Commands

title: select.cryptomatte: click an object, select its coverage
author: Elvis33LE
body:
The Cryptomatte picker on top of the merged #2180 codec — the Arnold/V-Ray/Redshift workflow: click an object in the render, get its exact selection.

**`select.cryptomatte {x, y, layer?, tolerance?, mode?}`**

- Reads the ID at the clicked pixel of the active document's **source EXR** (the Cryptomatte layer by name, default the first; the document must have been opened from a saved `.exr`, everything else says so).
- Builds the selection from every pixel that ID **covers** — partial coverage becomes a partial mask, so an edge falls between both objects instead of hard-cutting. `tolerance` groups near-identical IDs (default 0: exact).
- Returns the ID, the **manifest's object name**, the pixel count and the layer used — the name is what a status-bar line or MCP caller shows.
- `mode` replace/add/subtract/intersect combines like the marquee tools; clicking a pixel with no samples deselects in replace mode (Magic Wand behaviour).

Everything is a command, so the control channel, CLI and MCP drive the same selection headlessly; the UI picker panel can follow as a thin shell.

**Tests** (synthetic 4×4 file: `cube` at coverage 1 on the left half, `sphere` at 0.5 on the right, manifest naming both): exact pixels and name for a full-coverage click, 0.5 mask at the half-covered pixel, add/subtract arithmetic (0.5 − 0.5 → 0.25), layer-by-name, and a hostile-param sweep (missing, non-numeric and out-of-bounds coordinates, unknown layer and mode — all `Err`, never a panic). `panic_hunt` green; engine suite 1161 green; clippy/fmt clean.

title: wasm: gate native-only constants so wasm32 builds without dead-code warnings (#2808)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2808

## What / why
On `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, three constants were dead code because their only users are native-only:

Fixes #1946.

In Photoshop's layer name and value fields, as in native Windows and macOS text fields, a drag selection in a single-line field follows only the pointer's horizontal position. PhotoCraft followed the vertical one: drifting a few points above the field selected everything to the start, and below it everything to the end. egui's `TextEdit` picks the character under the pointer with `Galley::cursor_from_pos`. title: Tools: remember tool options between launches (#2814)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2814

## Root cause
`ToolOptions` (`crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs`), which holds the options-bar settings, was only serialized for Tool Presets. Nothing saved it at exit or restored it at launch. The preferences file kept the engine preferences, the panel layout (`panelLayout`) and the brush picker view (`brushPicker`), but not the tool options. So unticking Move > Auto-Select (the setup asked for in #2706), setting a marquee Feather, choosing a crop ratio and so on only lasted until the next launch. Photoshop remembers each tool's options between sessions.

## What is persisted and where
- `Preferences::tool_options` (`toolOptions` in the prefs JSON): a new shell-owned `Value`, like `brushPicker`. It holds only the `ToolOptions` fields that differ from their defaults, so if a default changes in a later release, users who never touched that option get the new one.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/tool_memory.rs`:
  - `persist` runs every frame after the panels, next to `brush_picker::persist`. It waits until the pointer is up, so a slider drag doesn't write on every step. When nothing changed it costs one struct compare. Options set through the control channel or by a tool preset are remembered too.
  - `restore` runs in `prefs_ui::load` at launch and applies the saved values field by field.
- Per-document state (crop rect, polygon in progress and the like) lives outside `ToolOptions` and is not saved. Brush tips and sizes belong to the session brush, which #2516 handles separately. There is no Reset Tool / Reset All Tools command yet, so nothing needed to change there.

## Compatibility and robustness
- Old preference files have no `toolOptions` key, so the defaults apply, as before.
- If `toolOptions` is not an object, it is ignored with a log warning.
- An unknown key is ignored.
- A field that doesn't read back keeps its default, logs a warning and leaves the other fields alone. That covers a wrong type and a number outside the `f32` range (it would become infinity).

body:
Selecting Zoom on Windows falls back to the arrow, and Eyedropper sampling overwrites the comparison ring's reference colour. This PR supplies cached Windows zoom cursors and retains the foreground/background colours from before each sampling gesture.

The sampling HUD stays centred on the pointer, with the new colour above and the retained previous colour below. Its 120-point diameter follows display DPI rather than document zoom, with a neutral gray surround and an open centre. `edit.transform` only transformed an alpha channel or the Quick Mask when the caller passed an explicit `"target"`. The Free Transform box in the UI does pass one, but nothing else did:

title: Docs: claim an issue with an "I'm working on this." comment (#2418)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #2418.

Several issues got two competing PRs (9 in the last 300, see #2418) because agents start coding without checking whether someone else already has. Contributors already use a plain `I'm working on this.` comment as a claim; this PR tells agents about it and backs the comment with a draft PR, which is what other agents actually find. No bot, workflow, labels or permissions needed.

## Change
`AGENTS.md` › *4. Picking work*: new **Claiming an issue** subsection.
- Check the issue is free: no `I'm working on this` comment under 72 hours old, and no open PR, searched by number and by feature keywords.
- Claim before writing code: open a draft PR from an empty WIP commit with `Fixes #N`, and comment `I'm working on this.`
- Push progress to the draft often, so others can see the claim is alive.
- Re-check before every push and before marking it ready. If a competing PR is further along, hand over.
- If you stop, delete your claim comment, close the draft and delete the branch.
- A claim expires after 72 hours with no new commit, PR or update.

`docs/contributing.md`: a one-line rule pointing to that section.

## Why a draft PR and not only a comment
- A comment alone gets overlooked: #3368 was claimed 12 minutes before #3412 was opened for the same fix.
- A draft shows up in the issue's *Development* sidebar and in `gh pr list`, which is what agents search.
- Searching only by issue number misses work: #2867 was already covered by the long-open #884.
- When two people collide, the one further along should keep it (#3437 vs #3506).

## Tests
Docs only, so there's nothing to test.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
