title: Numeric fields: typed units, scrubby labels, double-click reset (#3099)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3099 (scorecard row UI-217-13, part of #217)

Arithmetic in value fields already worked (#726, #2252). Three parts were still missing. They now live in the shared widgets, so every field gets them.

## What changed
- **Units in expressions** (`numeric_expression::parse_with_units`, `widgets::value_field`): a number may be followed by a unit: `px`, `in`, `cm`, `mm`, `pt`, `pica`/`pc` or `%`. The unit is converted into the field's own unit, which comes from its suffix. Lengths convert through pixels at the active document's resolution and the Units & Rulers point size. The app sets these each frame with `widgets::set_field_resolution`; without a document they are 72/72. Image Size and New Document show their unit in a separate menu, so they pass it with their own resolution through `widgets::value_field_units`. A field's own non-unit suffix is accepted too (`45°`). `%` after a number means percent only when nothing follows it; `10%3` is still the remainder.
- **Invalid input is rejected and the old value stays:** a unit that can't convert (a length in a % field, `%` in a px field, any unit in a unitless field), plus `1/0`, `1e400`, `((((`, unicode, unknown words and overflowing conversions.
- **Scrubby labels** (`widgets::scrub_label`): dragging a label moves the value field drawn right after it on the same row, one step per point. Shift makes the step ×10 and Alt makes it a tenth as fast. A small-range field steps by 0.01. While the link is active the cursor is the horizontal resize arrow.
  - The link is only made when the field starts within 24 pt to the right of the label (slider rows link across the whole row). A label such as `Mode:` in front of a dropdown therefore never scrubs an unrelated field.
  - It is wired into options-bar labels (`opt_label`: Size, Feather, Opacity, Flow…), every `slider_row` (adjustments, filters, Camera Raw) and the Character panel's icon labels.

title: Web: opt-in embedding bridge for host pages (?host=parent)
author: CyberFox-81
body:
A page that frames PhotoCraft on the same origin can now open files in it and store what it saves, through postMessage, instead of saves and exports becoming browser downloads. Built for a Nextcloud integration, but nothing in it is host-specific.

Only the web shell changes; it plugs into the hooks the app already has:
- photocraft:open from the parent goes through the inbox, like a picked or dropped file
- Services::file_dialog asks the parent where Save, Save As and Export go (photocraft:pick-save / photocraft:picked); File > Open keeps the browser's picker
- Services::write sends the bytes to the parent (photocraft:save)
- photocraft:dirty reports unsaved changes; the parent guards leaving the page, so the shell's own beforeunload guard stays off
- photocraft:ready and photocraft:failed report start-up

Enabled only by ?host=parent inside a frame; only the parent window on the page's own origin is heard or answered. Without it nothing changes.

title: Shortcuts: layout-independent brush keys, Photoshop's German keys plus a fallback for all layouts (#3109)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3109

**Depends on #3106.** This branch is stacked on it. Until #3106 merges, the diff also shows #3106's commits.

## Root cause
Photoshop's `[` `]` (brush size) and ⇧[ ⇧] (hardness) need AltGr on many layouts, so Photoshop itself uses layout-specific keys per language. On German it is `Ö` / `#` (⇧ for hardness). egui has no key for `ö` or `#`, so egui-winit reports the physical key (`;`, `\`), which nothing was bound to.

## Design (layout independent, no hardcoded German path)
New module `crates/ui-egui/src/layout_keys.rs`, called at the top of `shortcuts::handle`. It uses what egui already gives us (`Event::Key { key, physical_key, modifiers }` plus the adjacent `Event::Text`), so no OS layout API and no new dependency. I looked at layout-detection crates: they need OS APIs per platform (and don't work on wasm), while winit's `KeyCode` is exactly the physical key egui already forwards as `physical_key`.
1. **Data table** `LAYOUTS` (`Layout { keys: &[(typed text, shift, key)] }`) for layouts whose Photoshop keys are known. Today: German (`ö`/`Ö` -> `[`, `#`/`'` -> `]`). `COMMON` holds the rows valid everywhere (#3106's `*` -> `+`, `_` -> `-`). To add a layout, append a `Layout` with rows taken from Photoshop itself, plus a test. I could not verify Photoshop's French AZERTY keys from public sources, so there is no AZERTY row.
2. **Fallback for every other layout**: when the keys at the US `[` / `]` positions (egui `physical_key` OpenBracket/CloseBracket) type something that is not a bracket, they act as `[` / `]`. So AZERTY (`^`, `$`), Spanish/Italian (`+`) etc. get working brush size/hardness keys. It never applies with Cmd/Ctrl/Alt, and switches off once a real bracket is typed (e.g. Dvorak) or a table layout's symbol was seen (so German `+` is not a brush key).
3. Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts overrides are unchanged: this only decides which key a press is. Documented in `docs/ui-parity.md` (Keyboard shortcuts).

title: Puppet Warp: the mesh follows the object outline (#3105)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3105 (scorecard TOOL-214-6, part of #214)

## What was wrong
`algo/puppet.rs` `build_mesh` kept every square grid cell that touched the layer's opaque pixels. The mesh edge was a staircase up to a cell outside the shape, and two shapes closer than about one cell shared cells, so a pin on one dragged the other along. In Photoshop the mesh follows the outline (grown or shrunk by Expansion), and an unpinned separate shape stays where it is.

## What changed (algo only; the engine params and UI are unchanged)
- **Outline:** the opaque region (alpha > 0.05) becomes a signed distance field (exact Euclidean distance transform on a block grid, at most 1024 blocks across), offset by **Expansion**, so growing and shrinking are continuous rather than a block stamp. Marching squares traces its zero contour into closed loops (holes too).
- **Boundary points:** each loop is simplified with Douglas–Peucker (half a block, at least 0.5 px), which keeps sharp corners, then its sides are split to the **Density** spacing.
- **Inside:** a triangular lattice at the same spacing, kept at least half a step inside the outline.
- **Triangulation:** incremental Bowyer–Watson Delaunay with neighbour links and a visibility walk. Outline sides missing from the triangulation are split at their midpoints (conforming Delaunay, bounded), and only triangles inside the outline are kept (even-odd test, row-bucketed).
- **Solver ordering:** vertices are numbered in reverse Cuthill–McKee order, which keeps the banded Cholesky narrow. Disconnected pieces no longer widen the band.
- Density now counts steps across the region the mesh covers (the bounds grown by Expansion), so a +200 px Expansion on a 20 px layer no longer builds a 40k-vertex mesh. The old grid builder had the same blow-up.

Visual check (snapshot example, Show Mesh on): the mesh hugs the ellipse, the bar and the separate disc. The disc has its own mesh and stays put while the bar is dragged.

title: Write TIFF spot and alpha channels the way Photoshop does
author: Zer0C00L01
body:
I run a DTF shop, and the RIP reads the spot plate out of a Photoshop TIFF. PhotoCraft was putting that plate in the transparency sample, so the RIP treated the ink as a hole in the shirt.

This writes spot colours and extra alpha channels as TIFF extra samples, up to sixteen, and writes the Photoshop channel resources for the name, ink colour, and solidity. Layered files use a 14-byte user mask, a white-matted composite when transparency is not saved, and spot ink stored as zero, which is what Photoshop writes. author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3116

Depends on #3115 (stacked on it, which is stacked on #3108). Until those merge, the diff here includes their commits; the last commit is this PR's change.

## What changed

Photoshop has Set Black / Neutral Gray / White Point eyedroppers in the Levels dialog and in the Properties panel of a Levels adjustment layer. PhotoCraft had neither.

- **Engine** (`adjust_params.rs`): `levels_eyedropper` resolves a colour sample into Levels.
  - **RGB:** Black and White move each channel's input black or white to the sample's value in that channel, so the sample maps to the output black or white. Gray sets each channel's midtone gamma so the channel maps to the sample's Rec. 709 luma. That removes the cast and keeps the brightness. The gamma is found by bisecting on the compositor's own Levels curve, so the shadow toe is included. Output levels and the composite record are kept.

  - **CMYK and Lab:** these return `Err`, same as Curves.
  - The input range keeps at least 2 levels. Samples are clamped to 0..1, so 32-bit samples above 1 are safe, and non-finite samples return `Err`.

On a layer it samples the image below that layer and counts as one undo step. Curves and Levels share the param parsing and the dispatch (`adjustment_eyedropper`, `eyedropper_from_params`, `layer_eyedropper`).
- **Dialog** (`adjust_dialog.rs`): the Levels dialog shows the same three eyedropper buttons as Curves and samples the same way. Nothing changes in the document until OK.

title: ui(theme): modernize shadows with delicate multi-layer depth
author: TheTeslak
body:
Previously, shadows across elevation surfaces (popups, menus, floating panels, modals) and the canvas felt muddy, harsh, and dated. In particular, heavy single-layer drop shadows with aggressive opacity created dirty dark bands and visually cluttered outlines, especially noticeable in light themes.

Bring shadow rendering up to modern UI design standards with delicate, clean multi-layer elevation and diffuse lighting:

- Theme: introduce `popup_shadow` token alongside `shadow` across all themes (Dark, Light, Pro, Classic, Adwaita, Breeze, Solarized) with softened, refined alphas to eliminate muddy contrast.
- Theme: implement `upgrade_shadow` and `upgrade_popup_shadow` with `ShadowElevation` levels (Low, Medium, High, Modal), replacing dirty single drops with modern multi-layer ambient and directional key lighting.
- Canvas: replace harsh canvas edge shadows in both CPU painter and GPU fragment shader with soft quadratic diffuse falloff, removing dark bands.
- UI: apply delicate elevation across menus, dialogs, dock tabs, toolbars, palette pickers, and overlay cards.
- Tests: add unit tests for multi-layer shadow injection, zero-alpha no-op handling, and modal backdrop isolation.

title: Add backlog triage tooling: script, de-rot and auto-label workflows, …
author: shmuelbiller1
body:
Add backlog triage tooling: script, de-rot and auto-label workflows, guides
The queue, not the code, is the bottleneck. On 2026-10-11 the repo had 942
open items (647 issues, 295 PRs): only 26 PRs (9%) were mergeable with green
CI, 107 (36%) had merge conflicts, and 929 items (98%) had no labels. Fixes
exist and are waiting on review.

scripts/pr-triage.py classifies every open item (area/kind/platform/size),
cross-references mergeability against check runs, and prints three lists in
the order they can be acted on: merge-now (clean+green, zero work),
auto-rebase (green but drifted), then failing. Every mutating flag is
dry-run until --yes. Stdlib only and shells out to gh, so it never holds a
token.

Two workflows stop the rot recurring:
- pr-derot.yml rebases every open non-draft PR every six hours. Updating a
  branch that is merely behind is mechanical; PRs that still conflict are
  reported, and that list is the real work queue. Nothing merges or closes.
- auto-label.yml labels items as they are opened, so the 98%-unlabelled
  problem cannot come back. Bulk-labelling the existing 900 is left as a
  deliberate one-off because it notifies ~900 authors.

Both were checked against the live API: the de-rot filter was rewritten
after measuring that mergeStateStatus almost never reports BEHIND on this
repo (out-of-date PRs return UNSTABLE instead), and the triage fetch was
made to retry after a throttled run silently reported 0 mergeable PRs.

docs/backlog-triage.md is generated; docs/backlog-shortcuts.md is the
hand-written companion (fast dev loop, where the cheap work hides, perf
ranked by ratio). It notes that the largest measured perf win in the
project - https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/2596, P28 Content-Aware Scale 954,192 ms -> 2,641 ms - is
already written, green, and sitting unmerged.

AGENTS.md gains a "check the PR queue first" step and pointers to both docs.

title: Vanishing Point: on-canvas plane editor with Create/Edit Plane, grid and paste (#3122)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3122 (part of #214, scorecard row TOOL-214-14)

## What changed
Filter › Vanishing Point… only opened the generic parameter dialog, so you had to type plane corners as JSON. It now opens a dialog mode on the canvas, built like the Perspective Warp and Puppet Warp modes (`distort_ui`):

- **Create Plane (C):** four clicks make a plane. The clicks can come in any order: corners are normalised clockwise from the top-left (`VpPlane::normalized`), which is the order paste and tear-off expect. Without this, a plane clicked counter-clockwise would paste mirrored.
- **Edit Plane (V):** drag a corner node, or drag an edge node to slide that edge along the plane's own perspective. The homography is frozen at the press, and the edge stops before it crosses the horizon or folds the quad. Click a plane to select it. Delete/Backspace removes it.
- **Grid:** cells are square in the plane's metric (the same camera lift the engine uses), and **Grid Size** sets the cell size in px at the nearest edge. The grid is drawn in the accent colour for a valid plane and warning yellow for a doubtful one (both vanishing points finite but no real focal length fits them, or a corner sharper than 10°). A red outline with no grid marks an invalid quad (self-intersecting or dented). This follows Photoshop's blue/yellow/red (`VpPlane::check` in `photocraft-algo`).
- **Paste on OK:** with an image on the clipboard, the selected plane previews it pasted in perspective (a texture mesh through the plane's homography, clipped to the plane). Drag to move it; **Width** sets its size, and **New Layer** renders it onto a new layer. ✓ / ↩ runs `filter.vanishingPoint` with `{"planes", "paste", "newLayer"}` as one history step, so actions record it and agents can replay it exactly. Esc drops a half-clicked plane first, then cancels. An invalid plane keeps the mode open, and the status bar says why.

title: fix(ui): remember the last-used tool in each single-key group (close #2608)
author: rollroyces
body:
## Summary

Tool keys cycling to the group's first tool on every press. Pressing `L` from Brush always went back to Freehand Lasso, never to the last Lasso the user had picked (e.g. Polygonal Lasso). Photoshop remembers the last-selected tool in each single-key group so a press of the group key returns to it.

### Fix

- `crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs`: new field `UiState::last_in_group: HashMap<char, Tool>` and `UiState::set_tool(t)` that updates both `tool` and `last_in_group[t.key()]`. Default-skipped in serialisation so existing UI state stays byte-identical.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs`: the toolbar slot click and the Hand-tool double-click route through `set_tool` so mouse picks populate the same memory.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs`: the single-key cycling arm in `handle` consults `last_in_group.get(&t.key())` first when the current tool is outside the group, falling back to `group[0]` only on a fresh install. The shift_switch / cycle / keep-current branches are unchanged.

### Tests

`cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib shortcuts` ✓ (25 tests, including 1561 filtered). Verified end-to-end.

title: fix(type): return caret after normalized CRLF insertion (#3074)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
Fixes #3074

## Problem

`type.insertText` normalized CRLF to LF when storing text, but calculated its returned caret from the original input. Inserting `x\r\ny` therefore returned index 4 even though the stored text `x\ny` has three characters, so querying that caret failed.

## Change

Use the existing newline normalizer before counting inserted characters. Add an engine regression that checks the normalized text and passes the returned caret to `type.caret`.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests -j 12 -- --test-threads=8` (1,199 unit tests passed, 12 ignored; all integration test binaries passed)
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -j 12 -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo xtask layers`
- `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=12 cargo xtask wasm` (all 24 checks passed)
- `cargo build -p photocraft-cli -j 12`
- CLI smoke: CRLF insertion returned caret 3, and `type.caret` accepted index 3.

Corpus and performance checks were not run because this change only affects a text caret index; it does not touch file formats or pixel rendering.

title: Dialogs: the live dialog stays in front of older ones (stuck stacked profile prompts)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
## Problem

Opening three PNG screenshots together (File › Open with several selected; each has macOS's "Display" profile) put up three Embedded Profile Mismatch prompts. Sometimes the prompt in front was greyed out: OK, Cancel and the radio buttons ignored clicks, and the app had to be quit. A user hit this on 2 of 3 tries.

Over the control channel the dialog stack looked right: three prompts, the newest last. The cause is two rules that disagree:

- `dialogs::show` lets only the last dialog take input and disables the others.
- egui only lets the modal drawn on top take input, and it raises an area that is pressed or that wasn't drawn the frame before (`Area::show` in egui 0.36).

When egui raised an older prompt above the live one, the prompt in front was one we had disabled, and the live one behind it was blocked by egui. Neither could be answered. The stacked prompts sit in the same place and are the same size, so the live one was also hidden.

I couldn't pin down which egui rule fired in the user's session: in tests all three files open within two frames, and no click timing I tried reproduced it. The fix doesn't depend on the trigger.

## Fix

`dialogs::show` raises the live (last) dialog when another dialog is drawn above it (`older_dialog_above`, checking egui's layer order). It raises only then: raising every frame put the dialog above its own popups, which broke the Fill dialog's colour and pattern pickers and a Preferences dropdown (caught by their existing tests).

This applies to any stacked dialogs (a Color Picker over Fill, for example), not just the profile prompts.

title: fix(type): navigate adjacent line with large leading (#3066)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
Fixes #3066

## Problem

`line_step` chose the destination line by hit-testing a point just beyond the current caret. With 40-point leading, that point remained closer to the current line, so `lineNext` and `linePrev` returned the original indices.

## Change

Resolve the caret's current laid-out line, select the adjacent line directly, then find the closest caret on that line at the requested x position. Add a regression for 40-point leading in both directions.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p photocraft-text --lib -j 12 -- --test-threads=8` (116 passed, 4 ignored)
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests -j 12 -- --test-threads=8` (1,198 passed, 12 ignored; all integration test binaries passed)

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo xtask layers`
- `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=12 cargo xtask wasm` (all 24 checks passed)
- `cargo build -p photocraft-cli -j 12`
- CLI reproduction: with 40-point leading, navigation now returns 4 and 1; the default-leading control remains 4 and 1.

Arial is unavailable on the test host, so the CLI reproduction used its Liberation Sans fallback; the regression uses bundled Inter. I did not manually drive the desktop arrow keys; the UI handler calls the same `line_step` helper. title: Read applied Sony RAW metadata and crop ILCE-6000 images
author: optimalbytee
body:
Older Sony ARWs can carry applied white balance and black levels only in encrypted SR2SubIFD metadata. PhotoCraft previously estimated WB from the scene and used a 512 black fallback, even when the file specified different levels. This change reads the observed common-key metadata with bounded allocation and checked offsets, keeps usable plain tags authoritative, and retains existing fallbacks for malformed metadata or other keys.

The measured ILCE-6000 image area now produces 6000 × 4000 images from its 6048 × 4024 sensor without overriding an explicit crop. Three measured files use their identical camera-applied WB instead of different grey-world estimates; full-resolution 16-bit ProPhoto-compatible development is retained. The pinned public RX0 fixture now asserts black 800 and applied WB. Sensor pixels continue through the RAW development pipeline.

Only the observed `11 22 33 44` key is supported. Metadata allocation is capped at 1 MiB and `Limits.max_alloc`; offsets, directory lengths and level values are checked. Synthetic regressions cover both byte orders, independent keystream observations, metadata precedence, invalid levels/gains, truncation, out-of-block offsets and allocation limits. The cipher data was independently recovered from black-box metadata observations; no sibling decoder implementation, camera colour table or dependency is included. See [the measurement and scope notes](https://github.com/optimalbytee/photocraft/blob/codex/sony-arw-metadata/docs/sony-arw-metadata.md).

Validation repeated after integration onto current upstream main (`79261615`):

- `cargo test -j 12 -p photocraft-raw --features corpus --locked`: 120 tests passed, including the SHA256-verified public RAW corpus.
- `cargo clippy -j 12 -p photocraft-raw --all-targets --features corpus --locked -- -D warnings`: passed.

title: Window menu: list the open documents, the active one checked (#2991)
author: brennanMKE
body:
Fixes #2991.

In Photoshop, the **Window** menu ends with the open documents. The active one has a check, and choosing one brings it to the front. PhotoCraft's Window menu didn't list them, in either menu bar. The only ways to switch documents were the tabs, their » overflow menu and Ctrl+Tab. #1264 asked for this list too, but it was closed by #1367, which added only the overflow button. On #2780 a macOS user also looked for open images in the Window menu.

## Change

- **The list:** Window now ends with a separator and one row per open document, in tab order. Each row is labelled with the document's name, and the active document has a check. Choosing a row activates that document.
- **Native macOS menu bar:** the documents come after Bring All to Front.
- **In-window menu bar** (Windows, Linux and `--in-window-menus`): the documents come after Theme.
- **Names:** document names aren't translated. A rename by Save As updates the row.
- **Control channel:** the rows are `window.document.<index>`, and `ui.menu.invoke` on one replies `{document: index}`. A stale or out-of-range index returns an error. `docs/control-protocol.md` is updated.

### Native menu: rebuild only Window

The native menu bar is rebuilt only when `structure_key` changes, and `mac_menu_appkit` checks that opening a document doesn't rebuild it. Document rows can't be inserted into the Window menu in place:
- AppKit adds its own items to the Window menu (Fill, Center, Move & Resize, the window list…).
- muda's `Submenu::insert` index then means different rows in muda and in NSMenu, so inserting at a position can panic.

So:
- `structure_key` leaves the document rows out, and a new `window_key` covers the whole Window menu.
- When only `window_key` changes, `MacMenu::rebuild_window` replaces the Window submenu on its own and makes it the app's windows menu again. AppKit then adds its items back.
- Switching documents changes neither key, so only the check moves (in place, as before).

title: fix(ui): respect explicit dropdown defaults in schema dialogs (#3056)
author: buivanvu94
body:
Closes #3056.

### Summary

In schema-generated dialogs, choice/dropdown parameters with an explicit default notation (e.g. `="good"` in Radial Blur, or `="relative"` in Convert to Profile and Proof Setup) were previously discarding the declared default because `Kind::Choice` only stored a list of option strings and initialized fields to `options[0]`.

This PR:
1. Updates `Kind::Choice` in `crates/ui-egui/src/filter_dialog.rs` to store explicit defaults: `Kind::Choice { options: Vec<String>, default: Option<String> }`.
2. Updates `parse_spec` to parse explicit default values (both quoted like `="good"` and unquoted identifiers).
3. Updates dialog initialization in `open`, `open_with_spec`, and dropdown UI rendering to initialize fields to `default` if present, falling back to `options.first()`.
4. Updates `gallery_ui.rs` and `menus.rs` pattern matching for `Kind::Choice`.
5. Adds regression unit test `schema_dialogs_respect_explicit_dropdown_defaults` verifying:
   - Radial Blur selects `"good"`, not first option `"draft"`.
   - Convert to Profile and Proof Setup select `"relative"`, not first option `"perceptual"`.
   - Choices without explicit defaults retain their first option.
   - Remembered dialog preferences still override initial defaults.
   - Choices whose explicit default is the first option are preserved.

title: docs(raw): measured notes on Panasonic RW2 RawFormat 3/4
author: Gotya-OFFCIAL
body:
## What

Measured notes on Panasonic RW2 RawFormat 3/4 (vendor-compressed, 12-bit) — container
tags, payload geometry, per-byte content sensitivity, quantisation behaviour, and a
negative result that should stop the next attempt from repeating mine.

No decoder here. Nothing was read from dcraw, LibRaw, RawSpeed, rawler/dnglab or any
other decoder implementation; every number comes from treating the sample files as byte
sequences. This follows the route the Nikon NEF work took (#1310), where the format
facts came from black-box analysis rather than from a description of somebody's code.

## Why bother, when the decoder in #1884 was declined

Because the useful output of that attempt is not the code, it is the measurements — and
they are cheap to check. Three of them are not obvious from the outside:

**1. The payload is not a fixed-layout raster.** Four frames of one static scene, same
camera and settings, seconds apart:

| File | Payload | 16-byte groups |
|---|---|---|
| P1340729 | 19,070,976 | 1,191,936 |
| P1340730 | 19,062,272 | 1,191,392 |
| P1340731 | 19,072,512 | 1,192,032 |
| P1340732 | 19,096,064 | 1,193,504 |

The length varies by 33,792 bytes (0.18 %) between frames that show the same scene.

**2. Group 0 already differs completely between those four files**, even though the
stream starts in the masked border rows where the scene is identical and only sensor
noise differs. The first 16 bytes of each file share nothing.

Together these say the encoder is sequential and error-feedback-like: a small input
difference is amplified along the prediction chain instead of staying local, coded length
drifts with content, and output at one position cannot be related to the image at one
position.

**3. Consequently, positional analysis returns nothing.** In the samples here only three
byte positions correlate with image content at all (byte 7 at 0.850 for lag 1, byte 5 at
0.648, byte 4 peaking at lag 1032 = three rows); the other thirteen sit below 0.07 at
every lag…

title: fix(mode): restore indexed pixels after clearing transparency (#3080)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
## Summary

Color Table applies transparency by setting matching layer pixels to alpha zero. When the transparent entry was cleared, the edit skipped those zero-alpha pixels, leaving the composite transparent even though the table no longer had a transparent entry.

This restores alpha for pixels matching the previous transparent palette entry when that entry is removed. Unrelated transparent pixels retain the existing skip. The regression covers the red baseline, assigning and clearing transparency, RGB conversion, opaque blue recoloring, and Undo restoration.

Fixes #3080

title: fix(image): arbitrary canvas rotation moves position-locked children in groups (#3078)
author: buivanvu94
body:
Closes #3078.

### Summary

In `image.rotation.arbitrary` (`rotate_arbitrary`), canvas-wide rotation is meant to rotate the entire canvas including locked layers. Previously, it cleared `position` and `all` locks only on top-level layers before invoking `transform_layer`. When a layer inside a group had a position lock, the group recursion in `transform_layer` encountered the child's lock and failed with `layer "<name>" is locked`.

This PR:
1. Implements `with_released_movement_locks` in `crates/engine/src/mode_cmds.rs` to recursively release `position` and `all` locks across a layer and all its descendants during canvas rotation, safely restoring each layer's original locks afterwards.
2. Updates `rotate_arbitrary` to use `with_released_movement_locks` when calling `transform_layer`.
3. Adds unit test `rotate_arbitrary_rotates_grouped_locked_children_and_preserves_lock` in `crates/engine/src/mode_cmds/tests.rs` verifying:
   - Arbitrary 30° rotation succeeds on grouped documents with position-locked children and grows 16×16 to 22×22.
   - Position locks on grouped children are preserved after rotation.
   - Individual Free Transform on the position-locked child continues to be refused.
   - Undo restores the original canvas size and document state.
   - 90° canvas rotation matches the dedicated right-angle rotation `image.imageRotation.90cw`.

### Verification

- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib rotate_arbitrary_rotates_grouped_locked_children_and_preserves_lock` (passed)
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib mode_cmds` (13/13 passed)
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` (passed, 0 warnings)
- `cargo xtask layers` (passed, 29 crates clean)
- `cargo xtask wasm` (passed, 24 crates clean)
- `cargo fmt --check` (clean)
- `cargo xtask scorecard --check` (up to date)

title: fix(filters): process untouched Reveal All masks (#3082)
author: Sir-Starch

## Problem

Solarize and Add Noise reported success when targeting an untouched Reveal All mask but left it unchanged. The mask stores white as its default value, so `content_bounds()` was empty and filter area planning skipped the canvas.

## Fix

Include the document canvas when planning output for channel and mask filters, while preserving any off-canvas content bounds. The regression compares Solarize and seeded Add Noise on untouched Reveal All and equivalent Reveal Selection masks, and verifies the layer pixels remain unchanged.

Fixes #3082

## Verification

Corpus and performance checks were not run. This change only fixes output-area selection for targeted channel and mask filters; it does not change codecs, document serialization, or the filter algorithms.

title: fix(crop): unlock Background when extending canvas (#3081)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
## Problem

An explicit Crop that extended an opaque Background beyond the old canvas left transparent pixels on a still-locked Background. Fill succeeded on existing pixels, but its transparency lock kept it from painting the new border.

## Fix

Detect when the crop frame extends beyond the previous canvas and convert a Background to a normal layer as part of the crop edit. In-bounds and shrink-only crops keep the Background unchanged. The regression covers the Fill result, the lock and name transition, and undo restoring the crop and original Background.

Fixes #3081

## Verification

- `crop_extension_converts_background_before_fill` failed before the fix because the border remained transparent after Fill, and passes after it.
- `nice -n 10 cargo test -q -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -j 12 -- --test-threads=8` (1,199 passed, 12 ignored, plus engine integration targets).
- `nice -n 10 cargo clippy -q -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -j 12 -- -D warnings`

Corpus and performance checks were not run. The change only updates layer state when a crop creates transparent canvas area; it does not touch file formats or a hot pixel path.

title: fix(transform): identity transform makes feathered selection edges translucent (#3079)
author: buivanvu94
body:
Closes #3079.

### Summary

When Free Transform (`edit.transform`) is applied to an active feathered selection with an identity transform matrix, the engine previously split the surface into lifted (`alpha * k`) and rest (`alpha * (1 - k)`) surfaces via `split_selected`, warped the lifted surface, and normal-blended it back over the rest surface via `composite_over`. Because Porter-Duff Over compositing assumes independent layer coverage, the resulting opacity $k + (1 - k)(1 - k) = 1 - k(1 - k)$ caused feathered pixels ($0 < k < 1$) to become translucent even though coordinates were unchanged.

This PR:
1. Adds `Homography::is_identity` to `photocraft-algo` to test if a homography is an identity transformation.
2. In `transform_layer` (`crates/engine/src/transform_cmds.rs`), early-returns when `h.is_identity()` (after validating layer locks and converting position-locked Background), completely bypassing splitting, warping, and recompositing for identity transforms.
3. In `transform`, avoids unnecessary resampling of lone target channels/masks and selection outlines when `h.is_identity()`.
4. Adds regression unit test `feathered_selection_identity_transform_preserves_pixels` in `crates/engine/src/transform_cmds.rs` verifying:
   - Full RGBA preservation across the canvas when transforming a feathered selection with an identity matrix.
   - Exact `[1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0]` at feathered edge `(4,8)`.
   - Undo restoration.
   - Continued refusal of locked layers.

### Verification

- `cargo test -p photocraft-algo --lib homography_is_identity` (passed)

title: Render Video: animated GIFs keep their transparency (#3061)
author: fabianghe
body:
Fixes #3061.

**File › Export › Render Video** as an animated GIF turned fully transparent pixels opaque black, while a PNG sequence and a static GIF kept their transparency. There were two problems.

1. **No transparent index.** `render_video_with` quantised every frame with `transparent: None`. Each frame now does what Save for Web's GIF already does (`web_cmds.rs`), in a small `gif_frame` helper:
   - Pixels under 50% opacity get a transparent index. The rest are drawn opaque.
   - The palette is built from the visible pixels, with one entry kept for transparency. A fully transparent frame still gets a valid palette.
2. **Frames were never cleared.** `encode_gif_animated` wrote disposal 1 ("leave in place") for every frame. Every frame covers the whole image, so once transparency works, earlier frames would show through the transparent areas of later ones as ghosting. A frame with a transparent index now uses disposal 2 ("restore to background"). Opaque frames are unchanged and keep disposal 1.

## Verified with the issue's own steps
I ran the CLI commands from #3061 and decoded the results with Pillow 11.3:

```
animated/Untitled.gif frames 2
  frame 0 corner (0, 0, 0, 0) disposal 2
  frame 1 corner (0, 0, 0, 0) disposal 2
square/Untitled.gif (transparent doc with a red 4×4 square) frames 2
  frame 0 corner (255, 0, 0, 0)  centre (255, 0, 0, 255) disposal 2
  frame 1 corner (255, 0, 0, 0)  centre (255, 0, 0, 255) disposal 2
```

## Tests
- `engine/src/video_cmds/tests.rs`:
  - `animated_gif_keeps_transparency`: a transparent doc with a red square renders to a GIF. Both frames carry the transparent flag and disposal 2. On re-import the corner is transparent and the square is red.
  - `a_fully_transparent_animated_gif_frame_encodes`.
- `codecs/src/web.rs`: `transparent_frames_are_cleared_before_the_next` checks the Graphic Control Extension byte (0x04 opaque, 0x09 transparent) and the decoded alpha.
- The existing `render_video_to_animated_gif` (opaque frames) sti…

title: fix(ui): respect native desktop scale under Auto UI scaling (#1278)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
Resolves #1278

### Problem
Previously, when `interface.ui_scale` was set to `Auto` (the default), PhotoCraft forced a 200% scale factor whenever a 4K display was detected if the reported system scale was 1.0 (unscaled). On large 4K monitors (such as 32", 43", or multi-monitor setups) run intentionally at 100% desktop scale, this made PhotoCraft's window and UI elements unexpectedly huge and oversized compared to all other apps in the Craft suite.

### Solution
- Let `UiScale::Auto` respect the desktop environment's native scale without arbitrarily doubling it on 4K displays.
- Users who desire 200% scaling can select 200% from the Interface preferences dropdown.
- Updated unit tests in `crates/ui-egui/src/prefs_ui.rs` to verify that native desktop scale is preserved under `Auto`.

title: [Not merging] CI: Depot runner trial (measurements kept for reference)
author: echelon
body:
> **Closed as unwanted.** We won't move CI to Depot. The trial measured real gains, but they don't pay for themselves on this repo (see *Decision* below). Kept here for reference.

Trial of Depot-managed runners for the Linux jobs in `ci.yml` (2026-10-11), comparing wall-clock time and cost against GitHub-hosted runners.

## What was changed (branch since deleted)

| Job | Runner |
|---|---|
| test (Linux), corpus tests, web build | `depot-ubuntu-24.04-8` |
| wasm32 check | `depot-ubuntu-24.04-4` |
| select platforms, fuzz | `depot-ubuntu-24.04` |

Also needed: the Depot labels in `.github/actionlint.yaml`, or `actionlint` fails on unknown runner labels. Windows and `release.yml` were left unchanged.

## Timings

The GitHub baseline is the median of the last 5 green `main` runs on `ubuntu-latest`, which has 4 vCPUs for public repos, with a warm cache. The warm Depot run restored a 1.2 GB rust-cache with an exact key match.

| Job | GitHub (4 vCPU, warm) | Depot cold | **Depot warm** |
|---|---|---|---|
| test (Linux), 8 vCPU | ~28 min (23–33) | 13m30s–16m01s | **9m59s** (2.8×) |
| corpus tests, 8 vCPU | ~9.3 min | 4m00s–4m23s | **3m00s** (3.1×) |
| web build, 8 vCPU | ~5.2 min | 3m30s–3m48s | **3m01s** (1.7×) |
| wasm32 check, 4 vCPU | ~1.4 min | 2m37s–2m54s | **1m04s** (1.3×) |
| select platforms, 2 vCPU | ~6s | 9s–29s | 8s |

## Caching notes

- On Depot runners, the GitHub Actions cache API (`actions/cache`, `Swatinem/rust-cache`) is sent to Depot Cache automatically. It's separate from GitHub's cache, so the first runs after switching are cold.
- Depot Cache isn't scoped by branch. Our `save-if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` still means only `main` saves.
- Depot runners also come preconfigured to use sccache with Depot Cache (set `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache`). This trial didn't test it.

## Cost

- **GitHub today.** This repo is public, so standard Linux/Windows/macOS minutes are free. October 1–11 shows $2,325.89 gross for photocraft, but **$5.81 net**, all of i…

title: SVG: warn when text has no font to use (fixes the FreeBSD svg test)
author: diegochagas
body:
Fixes the FreeBSD job, red on main since the SVG reader landed in #1305 (first red run f82a55f on 2026-10-09; last green ec7302f, before #1305): `crates/io/tests/svg.rs::text_becomes_outline_shapes_or_warns_without_a_font` fails with `["SVG: nothing to draw (an empty drawing)"]`.

## What changed

The FreeBSD image has `fontconfig` and `freetype2` but no font package, and no bundled craft fonts, so the reader's font database is empty. With an empty `fontdb`, usvg 0.45 drops the `<text>` element **while parsing** (verified with a probe: `usvg::Tree::from_str` on the test's SVG yields a root with no children and a zero bounding box), so the reader's existing note at `svg.rs` ("text needs a font the drawing can use; none matched") never runs: it needs a `usvg::Node::Text` to reach the conversion. The file opened as an empty drawing with no word about the text.

- `parse` now returns the tree together with `fontless_text`: the drawing may contain text and the loaded database has no faces. `import_svg` turns that into the warning *"SVG: the text needs a font and none is installed, so it was dropped"* before converting, so a user on a font-less system learns why the text vanished; the per-text note for drawings that do have fonts but none matching stays.
- `options()` takes the database instead of deciding it; `parse_with(bytes, fonts)` is the seam the test uses to hand in an empty database. `rasterize` is unchanged in behaviour.

## How it was tested

- New unit test `text_without_any_font_is_reported_not_silently_dropped`: an SVG with `<text>` parsed against an empty database opens with no layers and a warning containing "font"; a drawing without text parsed the same way gets no font warning.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-io --test svg` (16, including the FreeBSD one in both of its branches: with fonts here, and without through the unit test) and `--lib svg`: ok. `cargo clippy -p photocraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean. `car…

title: Preserve solid vector shapes alongside bitmaps in SVG/PDF exports
author: TheSeanLavery
body:
Depends on #2872. The signed-in account cannot merge upstream, so this PR currently includes that export-catalog foundation. The mixed-export implementation is commit `27b6bad6`; once #2872 lands, the foundation overlap disappears.

SVG and PDF delivery previously flattened the document to one image, losing scalable shapes. This follow-up mixes actual solid Bézier fills and centered solid/dashed strokes with PNG bitmap layers. SVG/SVGZ reopen our unchanged output as editable shape and raster layers; PDF writes real path/form objects, bitmap images, soft masks and document DPI. Bitmap layer opacity remains separate from PNG samples, preserving faint overlays.

Export As scaling and disabling transparency retain vectors, with a white solid background added to the temporary export document. SVG/PDF labels no longer describe every output as raster-only, and the SVG capability notice is translated in all shipped catalogs.

Supported vector delivery uses RGB with the default or built-in sRGB profile. Text/fonts, gradients/patterns, boolean operations, masks/effects, clipping and backdrop-dependent blending use a warned raster fallback of the affected stack prefix; later supported shapes can remain vector. Other working spaces retain existing composite raster delivery. PDF is single-page and export-only. This is a delivery format, not a complete native document round trip.

Geometry, XML, encoded payload, recursion and decoded SVG layer budgets are bounded. SVG reopening rejects stale private geometry after external visual edits, unsafe namespaces/styles and pathological dash density; it contains no hidden whole-document payload.

Validation on the current upstream branch: 13 focused IO tests, 1,830 UI tests, strict IO/UI Clippy, formatting, dependency layers and full WASM check passed locally. GitHub corpus, WASM and web-size gates passed at `7bb746aa`. Linux CI tests also passed; Windows CI remains pending. Independent resvg/Poppler render checks cover mixed geometry, wi…

title: fix: macOS Monterey crash on Intel Iris Pro (disable wgpu indirect validation)
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3107 (macOS Monterey startup crash on Intel Iris Pro GPU)

The app crashed with "Compiler encountered an internal error" → "WGPU error: Parent device is lost" on Intel Iris Pro (device ID 0x0d26, Metal GPUFamily 1) running macOS Monterey 12.7.6.

## Root Cause

wgpu 30 compiles two internal compute shaders for indirect draw/dispatch validation by default. Metal's shader compiler crashes on these shaders on Intel Iris Pro, resulting in `RequestDeviceError(Device(Lost))`.

Both `--safe-gpu` and `PHOTOCRAFT_CPU_CANVAS=1` failed because macOS has no software graphics adapter—the CPU fallback still opens the window through Metal, hitting the same compiler crash.

## Fix

One line in `apps/photocraft/src/gpu_startup.rs`: disable wgpu's `VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL` flag. PhotoCraft never uses indirect draw or dispatch calls, so this validation is unnecessary.

Applied on all platforms (not macOS-only) to remove the same driver-crash risk on other GPUs.

## Testing

- Added regression test `device_creation_skips_indirect_validation_shaders`
- All 20 `gpu_startup` tests pass
- Sabotage test confirmed (removing fix causes test to fail)
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` clean
- Environment override `WGPU_VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL=1` re-enables validation

## Risks

- **Not tested on Intel Iris Pro hardware** — waiting for reporter confirmation
- Future trap if indirect calls added later (code comment guards against this)

## Workaround

Reporter can test before merge: `WGPU_VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL=0 photocraft`

---
— sent on behalf of @mjohnson7cd by Claude Code

title: fix(type): exclude text inside hidden groups from automatic hit testing
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Automatic `type.hitTest` can return text layers inside hidden groups.

Although the text layer itself is marked visible, it should not be
automatically selectable when one of its parent groups is hidden.

Fixes #3075.

## Root cause

The automatic hit-testing path checked each text layer's own
visibility flag without considering the visibility of its ancestors.

## Changes

- Check visibility along the complete layer path.
- Exclude text when any containing group is hidden.
- Preserve explicit hit-testing of a named hidden text layer.
- Add a regression test covering nested groups, visibility changes,
  and explicit targeting.

## Validation

- Verified the committed changes against the upstream baseline.
- Added a focused regression test.
- Rust tests and CI have not been executed.

title: fix(type): use the correct line at soft-wrap caret boundaries
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

At the beginning of a wrapped line, `type.caret` can report the
preceding line even though the caret geometry belongs to the next
visual line.

The same boundary error affects `type.navigate` with `lineStart`
and `lineEnd`.

Fixes #3068.

## Root cause

Adjacent visual lines can share a character offset.

The previous line-index lookup selected the first matching range,
while caret geometry could correctly resolve the following line.

## Changes

- Prefer the following visual line when resolving a shared caret
  boundary.
- Make line-edge navigation use the same line selection.
- Preserve pointer-based hit-testing by determining the visual line
  from the pointer's position.
- Add text-layout regression coverage for wrapped lines, forced
  breaks, and ordinary paragraph breaks.
- Add engine-level regression coverage for caret and line navigation.

## Compatibility

The change preserves existing character indices and text content.

It corrects line identity without changing the document format or
introducing additional history steps.

## Validation

- Verified the committed changes against the upstream baseline.
- Added focused text-layout and engine regression tests.
- Rust tests and CI have not been executed.

title: fix(crop): retain partial aspect-ratio input while typing
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Entering a custom crop aspect ratio can be frustrating because the
first numeric field resets to zero before the second field is filled.

This prevents users from reliably entering ratios such as 4:5 or 16:9.

Addresses the numeric-input problem reported in #3145.

## Root cause

The options bar reconstructs the numeric fields from the committed
crop-ratio value on every UI frame.

However, it only commits changes when both values are greater than
zero.

When a user enters the first number while the second is still zero,
the first number is discarded on the next frame.

## Changes

- Retain incomplete numeric input in transient UI state.
- Restore the first number while the second is being entered.
- Apply the crop aspect-ratio constraint only when both values are
  positive.
- Discard stale input when selecting another preset.
- Reset the transient input state when Clear is selected.
- Add regression coverage for incomplete input and preset changes.

## Scope

This change addresses custom aspect-ratio entry.

The separate crop-handle snapping, undo behavior, and requested
ratio information display mentioned in #3145 are not changed.

## Validation

- Verified the committed changes against the upstream baseline.
- Added a focused regression test for draft-value restoration.
- Rust tests, interactive UI testing, and CI have not been executed.

title: fix(masks): preserve off-canvas alpha in From Transparency
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Layer > Layer Mask > From Transparency loses mask coverage for pixels
temporarily positioned outside the document canvas.

Moving a raster layer partially off-canvas, converting its transparency
to a mask, and moving it back can leave previously visible pixels hidden.

## Root cause

The conversion intersects the raster surface's content bounds with the
document bounds before transferring alpha into the mask.

This excludes valid off-canvas pixels that still belong to the layer.

## Changes

- Transfer alpha across the raster layer's complete content bounds.
- Preserve mask coverage outside the canvas.
- Leave the existing alpha-to-mask conversion behavior unchanged for
  pixels inside the canvas.
- Add a regression test covering off-canvas coverage and restoration at
  8-, 16-, and 32-bit document depths.

## Validation

- Source and affected diff reviewed.
- Regression test added but not executed locally.
- Cargo tests, platform checks, and CI remain pending.

## Issue

Fixes #3043

title: fix(layers): remap linked-layer groups when copying between documents
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Copying linked layers into another document can accidentally associate
them with unrelated layers already linked in the destination.

Both documents may independently use the same linked-group identifier.
Subsequent linked-layer operations can then affect layers that were
never intended to be linked together.

## Root cause

Cross-document copying duplicates layers while preserving their
document-local link-group identifiers.

The destination may already use those identifiers for different groups.

## Changes

- Remap copied link-group identifiers to unused destination identifiers.
- Preserve relationships between copied layers belonging to the same
  source group.
- Keep separate copied groups distinct.
- Preserve existing destination link relationships.
- Add regression tests for identifier collisions, independent groups,
  and undo/redo of the copy operation.

## Validation

- Source and affected diff reviewed.
- Two regression tests added but not executed locally.
- Cargo tests and CI remain pending.

## Issue

Fixes #3045

title: fix(history): preserve an empty layer selection across undo and redo
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

When all layers are intentionally deselected, creating a new layer and
then undoing the creation unexpectedly selects the Background layer.

The restored layer target no longer matches the state immediately
before the edit.

## Root cause

History restoration only recognizes targets with an existing active
layer.

A valid empty target falls through to the normal active-layer repair
logic, which selects the top available layer.

## Changes

- Recognize an intentionally empty layer target during history
  restoration.
- Restore no active layer and no selected layers when that state was
  recorded.
- Clear the corresponding layer anchor.
- Preserve existing fallback behavior for invalid or deleted targets.
- Add a regression test covering deselection, layer creation, undo,
  redo, repeated undo, and ordinary selected-target restoration.

## Validation

- Source and affected diff reviewed.
- Regression test added but not executed locally.
- Cargo tests and CI remain pending.

## Issue

Fixes #3042

title: fix(layers): select Shift ranges in visible panel row order (#3041)
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Shift-click range selection produces incorrect layer membership around
expanded groups.

For example, selecting the range between a layer and an adjacent group
can unexpectedly include the group's children. Selecting from the group
to a child can omit intermediate displayed rows.

## Root cause

Range selection uses Document::walk(), whose traversal order differs
from the Layers panel's visual order around nested groups.

## Changes

- Calculate selection ranges using the Layers panel's top-to-bottom
  ordering.
- Place group rows directly above their children.
- Respect collapsed groups when calculating visible ranges.
- Preserve programmatic access to hidden group children by falling
  back to expanded ordering when an endpoint is not visible.
- Add a regression test covering forward and reverse selection ranges
  across groups and child layers.

## Validation

- Source and affected diff reviewed.
- Integration regression test added but not executed locally.
- Cargo tests and CI remain pending.

## Issue

Fixes #3041

title: fix(io): preserve group fill opacity in OpenRaster exports
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

OpenRaster export can lose the visible effect of group fill opacity.

A group with 50% fill opacity may reopen at full opacity even though
its exported merged preview reflects the intended transparency.

## Root cause

The exporter writes group opacity independently from fill opacity.

For raster layers, fill opacity can be applied directly to the exported
pixels. Groups have no equivalent single pixel payload, so that
conversion does not preserve their fill contribution.

## Changes

- Combine group fill opacity with serialized group opacity.
- Keep raster-layer opacity separate because raster fill opacity is
  already applied to the exported pixels.
- Clarify export warnings to distinguish the two conversion paths.
- Add regression tests for group fill opacity, combined opacity values,
  and OpenRaster round-trip behavior.

## Validation

- Source and affected diff reviewed.
- Two regression tests added but not executed locally.
- OpenRaster runtime round trips, cargo tests, and CI remain pending.

## Issue

Fixes #3048

title: fix(video): preserve transparent pixels in animated GIF exports
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Render Video can turn transparent pixels into opaque pixels when
exporting an animated GIF.

Transparent source frames may consequently produce an opaque black
background, despite retaining transparency in other export formats.

## Root cause

Animated GIF export quantizes frames without reserving a transparent
palette entry and passes no transparent index to the GIF encoder.

## Changes

- Detect frames containing transparent pixels.
- Reserve an additional palette index for transparency when needed.
- Pass that index through pixel quantization and animated GIF encoding.
- Retain the existing palette behavior for fully opaque frames.
- Add regression tests covering transparent animated GIF frames and
  the fully opaque control case.

## Validation

- Source and affected diff reviewed.
- Two regression tests added but not executed locally.
- Animated GIF runtime decoding, cargo tests, and CI remain pending.

## Issue

Fixes #3061

title: fix(vector): pivot explicit path transforms on target layer (#3062)
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Numeric path transformations can use the wrong pivot when the command
explicitly targets a layer other than the active layer.

Scaling the target shape may consequently move it far from its
expected position.

## Root cause

path.transform correctly resolves the layer being modified but
independently resolves the pivot through the active layer's path.

The transform target and pivot can therefore refer to different
shapes.

## Changes

- Resolve numeric-transform bounds from the explicitly targeted layer.
- Support both shape paths and vector-mask paths.
- Preserve existing behavior when no explicit layer is provided.
- Leave the explicit transformation-matrix path unchanged.
- Add regression tests for scaling an inactive shape layer and using
  an explicit matrix.

## Validation

title: fix(vector): preserve scaled live-line thickness during endpoint edits
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

After uniformly scaling a live line shape, editing an endpoint without
changing its position can unexpectedly reduce the line's thickness.

A four-pixel line scaled by two becomes eight pixels thick, but a
subsequent endpoint edit regenerates the path using the original
four-pixel weight.

## Root cause

The affine transformation updates the live line's endpoints without
updating its stored weight.

Later edits regenerate the line geometry from inconsistent live-shape
parameters.

## Changes

- Update live-line weight when applying positive axis-aligned scaling.
- Account for the line's direction when calculating the perpendicular
  width scale.
- Preserve the original weight for translation-only transforms.
- Keep the line editable after transformation.
- Add regression tests for uniform scaling, subsequent endpoint edits,
  translation, and horizontal/vertical nonuniform scaling.

## Validation

- Source and affected diff reviewed.
- Three integration regression tests added but not executed locally.
- Cargo tests and CI remain pending.

## Issue

Fixes #3063

title: fix(history): read locked history sources (#3076)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
Fixes #3076

## Problem

History Brush and Fill with History read a selected historical layer through the write-target helper. When that snapshot had pixel locks enabled, the helper rejected the read and both commands reported that the target did not exist.

## Fix

Add an immutable target-surface lookup for history reads. It reads layer pixels, masks, alpha channels, and Quick Mask without applying write-lock checks, and both history consumers use it. Current destination edits continue through the existing lock-checked write path.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -j 12 -- --test-threads=8` (1,202 passed, 12 ignored, integration targets passed)
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib history_ -j 12 -- --test-threads=8` (25 passed)
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -j 12 -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check`
- `cargo xtask layers` (29 crates) and `cargo xtask wasm` (24 checks)
- CLI repro: both commands restore pixels from the locked source state; state-0 controls pass; both commands still reject a currently locked destination.

Corpus tests were not run because this engine-only change does not touch the file-format crates covered by the opt-in corpus suite. No performance benchmark applies to this history lookup.

The fallback validates dimensions and payload bounds, supports uncompressed 24-bit and 32-bit DIBs, and promotes nontrivial 32-bit alpha bytes to an explicit mask.

title: GPU memory budget: read installed RAM on Windows
author: dhiorns15
body:
`gpu_canvas::physical_memory()` had no Windows implementation, so it returned `None` on every Windows machine. The wgpu compositor's memory budget then assumed 16 GB of RAM and capped layer textures at a quarter of that (4 GB):

- **Large machines** got too little. On a 62 GB PC with the default 8 GB Memory Usage, the budget was 4 GB instead of the full 8 GB allowance.
- **An 8 GB laptop with an integrated GPU** got too much: 4 GB of textures in RAM it shares with the system, where a quarter of the real RAM is 2 GB.

This reads installed RAM with `GlobalMemoryStatusEx` through `winsafe`, the safe binding the desktop app already uses (same pinned `=0.0.29`, `kernel` feature only; no `unsafe`). macOS, Linux and FreeBSD are unchanged.

**Tests**
- New: `gpu_canvas::tests::windows_reports_installed_ram` (Windows only). It fails before the fix, which returns `None`.
- Clean: `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm`.

title: fix(actions): avoid replaying Browse script edits twice
author: Ni-zav

## Summary

Fix action recordings that execute Browse script commands twice during playback.

## Problem

Recording a Browse script captures both the commands executed inside

During playback, the recorded commands run individually before the
Browse command runs them again.

For example, a script containing one 90-degree rotation can produce
two rotations during playback.

## Changes

title: fix(masks): bake feathered coverage when applying a layer mask
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Preserve softened mask edges when applying a feathered layer mask.

Fixes #3044.

## Problem

Applying a feathered layer mask removes the mask but sharpens its edge.

The resulting layer no longer matches the appearance displayed before
Apply.

## Root Cause

The Apply command reads mask coverage through `LayerMask::values_into`,
which handles mask density but does not perform feathering.

The compositor applies feathering separately.

## Changes

- Use the compositor's combined-mask coverage for enabled feathered
  pixel masks.
- Bake the softened coverage into the raster layer's alpha.
- Avoid baking an independent vector mask that remains attached.
- Preserve the existing path for masks without feathering.
- Add regression coverage for 8-, 16-, and 32-bit documents.
- Add a disabled-mask regression test.

- Two regression tests added.

title: fix(video): retain original footage for Restore Frame and Show Altered Video
author: Ni-zav

## Summary

Preserve original imported video frames independently from their
edited versions.

Fixes #3059.
Fixes #3060.

  layers.

- Prevent original-footage previews from overwriting edited frames.
- Keep original and altered frame stacks aligned during insertion,
  duplication, and deletion.
- Preserve original-frame snapshots in native PhotoCraft documents.
- Support loading older documents without original-frame snapshots.
- Validate frame counts when loading saved video data.

## Tests

Added regression coverage for:

- Restoring individual imported frames.
- Restoring all imported frames.
- Switching between original and altered footage.
- Scrubbing while original footage is displayed.
- Restoring blank video layers.

Extended the native-format video round-trip test.

title: fix(compose): resolve Dissolve coverage across adjustment, effects, a…
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Correct Dissolve blending in adjustment layers, layer effects, and
clipped layers.

Fixes #3050.
Fixes #3051.
Fixes #3052.

## Problem

Dissolve should resolve partial opacity into spatially distributed
pixel coverage.

Several compositor paths instead interpolate colors continuously,
producing uniform gray where the output should contain separate
opaque source and background pixels.

The affected paths include:

1. Adjustment layers using Dissolve at partial opacity.
2. Layers using Dissolve with enabled layer effects.
3. Clipped layers using Dissolve.

## Root Cause

These specialized composition paths bypass the standard Dissolve
coverage calculation.

They apply ordinary opacity interpolation even when the selected
layer blend mode is Dissolve.

## Changes

### Adjustment Layers

- Resolve adjustment opacity and mask coverage using the existing
  deterministic Dissolve threshold.
- Select either the adjusted or original color at each pixel.
- Preserve the backdrop alpha.

### Clipped Layers

- Apply binary Dissolve coverage to clipped content.
- Preserve the clipping base's alpha.
- Keep Normal blending behavior unchanged.

### Layer Effects

- Resolve layer opacity as coverage when combining the completed
  effect stack with its backdrop.
- Avoid continuously interpolating the effect stack under Dissolve.
- Preserve continuous interpolation for other blend modes.

## Tests

Added regression tests covering:

- Dissolve adjustments producing binary coverage.
- Clipped Dissolve matching an unclipped control over an opaque base.
- A redundant Color Overlay preserving Dissolve coverage.
- Normal blending continuing to produce continuous opacity.

## Validation

- Source and commit diff reviewed.
- Three regression tests added.
- CPU compositor tests, GPU parity checks, and CI remain pending.

title: raw: charge the lossless-JPEG intermediate and segment-sized buffers against max_alloc (#2925)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #2925

## What's wrong

`read_plane` charged the assembled image plane against `Limits` (`limits.check(width, height, samples * 2)`), but every per-segment buffer is sized from the **segment**, not from the image: tile geometry comes from `TILE_WIDTH` / `TILE_LENGTH`, which the file declares itself and `segments()` only bounds at `1 << 16` per axis. So an 8×8 image in a DNG that declares one 512×512 lossless-JPEG tile passes the plane check (128 bytes) and still allocates the whole 512 KiB intermediate — the "checked before allocating" promise in `crates/raw/src/lib.rs` did not hold for that buffer.

## What changed

- One `limits.check(s.w, s.h, samples * 2)` per segment, **before** the compression dispatch: a segment has to be a plausible buffer on its own. That bounds every branch that sizes a buffer from segment geometry (uncompressed, deflate, lossy JPEG, JPEG XL, lossless JPEG), which is remediation 2 in the issue.
- In the lossless-JPEG branch the decoder's sample cap becomes `min(geom, (max_alloc - scatter) / 2)`:
  - `geom` is unchanged (`s.w * s.h * samples * 4`, the existing headroom), so nothing that decoded before is refused because of geometry;
  - a frame the entropy stream declares is now bounded by the budget too, not only by the segment (remediation 1);
  - `scatter` reserves the `Quads` scatter buffer out of the same budget, so output + scatter stay inside one `max_alloc`.

Legitimate strip/tile layouts are unaffected: real strips are clamped to the image, real tiles are smaller than it, and both are far below any default budget.

## Tests

`crates/raw/tests/hostile.rs` — the two `LimitExceeded` assertions failed before the change; the remaining assertions are non-regression checks on fixtures that were already valid:

- `lossless_jpeg_intermediate_is_charged_against_max_alloc`: the same file decodes under default limits, is refused under a 64 KiB budget the image itself fits into, still decodes under a 4 MiB budget that holds the intermedia…

title: fix(compose): preserve Dissolve coverage for adjustments, styles and clipping
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Keep smart-filter mask coverage aligned with smart objects during
document-wide geometry operations.

Fixes #3077.

## Problem

Image Size, Canvas Size, and Crop can leave selection-derived
smart-filter masks at incorrect positions.

The problem becomes particularly visible when a smart filter is
hidden and shown again, triggering a fresh render using the displaced
mask.

Consequently, filtering may affect the wrong portion of the image.

## Root Cause

The shared surface traversal used by canvas geometry operations
processes smart-object appearance caches but omits their
smart-filter mask surfaces.

The mask therefore retains its old coordinates or dimensions while
the associated content moves or resizes.

## Changes

- Include smart-filter mask surfaces in the shared layer-surface
  traversal when mask processing is enabled.
- Treat those surfaces as masks rather than color pixels.
- Resample smart-filter masks during Image Size operations.
- Translate smart-filter masks during Canvas Size and Crop.
- Preserve existing smart-object and filter structures.
- Retain the existing distinction between mask and color-surface
  interpolation.

## Tests

Added three integration regression tests:

1. Image Size preserves selection-derived smart-filter coverage
   after resampling.
2. Canvas Size preserves filter coverage after a right-anchored
   canvas extension.
3. Crop preserves filter coverage after translation.

Each test exercises smart-filter re-rendering by hiding and
showing the filter.

## Validation

- Source and commit diff reviewed.
- Three regression tests added.
- Rust tests, rendering comparisons, and CI remain pending.

title: Help > System Info: the details a bug report needs, in sections
author: dhiorns15
body:
**Builds on #3189**, which it needs for the Windows RAM line. Until that merges, this PR also shows its one commit, "GPU memory budget: read installed RAM on Windows".

Help › System Info used to be ten flat lines:
- "windows x86_64", with no Windows version or build;
- raw names like `dx12 (discreteGpu)`;
- nothing on the CPU, memory, fonts or pen input, or where the log file is.

Most issues here are picked up by agents working from what the reporter pasted, so the report now answers the usual first round of questions itself. It's grouped into sections:

| Section | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Application | version, build profile and target, install kind (Installed, Portable, AppImage, Flatpak, Snap, Built from source), UI language, uptime |
| System | OS name and build, CPU, threads, installed and available RAM. Windows: from the registry, named 11 for builds 22000 and up because `ProductName` still says "Windows 10". macOS: `sw_vers`, plus Rosetta. Linux: os-release, kernel and session |
| Graphics | adapter with its PCI `vendor:device` id; type and API in plain words (Dedicated GPU, DirectX 12); driver; the backend chosen at launch, only when it differs from the preference; startup fallback; compositor; GPU memory budget |
| Displays | the window's display, UI and OS scale, window size, monitor profiles |
| Pen input | where pen data comes from on this platform, and what has arrived this session (pressure, tilt, rotation, eraser end) |
| Fonts | craft-fonts bundle, family count, and the fallback fonts actually found (the Thai, CJK and emoji coverage) |
| Session | each document's size, mode, depth, layers, undo states and pixel memory (never its name); PhotoCraft's memory use; Memory Usage limit; plug-ins |
| Files | settings, log and crash-recovery folders |

**Privacy.** Document names, document paths and pixels are never included. The home folder is written `~`, so the report can be pasted into a public issue as is.

title: fix(shapes): preserve transformed outline on unchanged live geometry edits
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3064.

Reapplying unchanged rectangle dimensions after a nonuniform
transformation should not alter the existing rounded corners.

## Root Cause

A transformed live shape retains its parameter values, but its
vector path can contain geometry that those values cannot fully
represent.

The shape editing command regenerated the path whenever geometry
parameters were supplied, even when those parameters were unchanged.

This discarded the transformed corner geometry.

## Changes

- Compare the requested live-shape parameters with existing values.
- Preserve the current vector path when geometry is unchanged.
- Regenerate the path when geometry parameters actually change.
- Preserve the existing PSD vector data on unchanged edits.

## Regression Coverage

Added tests across 8-, 16-, and 32-bit documents covering:

- Nonuniformly scaled rounded rectangles.
- Reapplying unchanged rectangle dimensions.
- Reapplying unchanged corner radii.
- Applying an actual corner-radius change.
- Restoring geometry through Undo.

## Validation

Regression tests added. Rust tests and CI have not been executed.

author: Ni-zav

## Root Cause

The paragraph-style implementation treated the preceding paragraph

Additionally, paragraph-run normalization discarded zero-length

## Changes

- Correct paragraph selection at the end-of-text caret.
- Support explicitly styled zero-length terminal paragraphs.
- Preserve final paragraph formatting during run normalization.
- Preserve formatting when inserting text into the empty paragraph.
- Handle the synthetic terminal paragraph marker when importing
  PSD text data.

## Regression Coverage

Added tests covering:

- Formatting the empty paragraph after a trailing newline.
- Preserving the previous paragraph's alignment and geometry.
- Inserting text into the previously empty paragraph.
- Retaining paragraph formatting through PSD text serialization.

## Summary

Restore Frame and Restore All Frames currently replace imported
video-frame pixels with transparency instead of restoring footage.

## Root Cause

The restoration commands unconditionally replace frames with
new blank raster surfaces.

This works for blank video layers but destroys the displayed
source pixels of imported image sequences.

## Changes

- Load source frames before beginning the edit transaction.

- Preserve the existing blank-frame restoration behavior.
- Avoid modifying the document when source loading fails.

title: fix(masks): preserve feathered coverage when applying layer masks
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3044.

Applying a feathered layer mask currently removes the soft edge,
producing a visibly harder transition than the original rendering.

## Root Cause

The Apply Layer Mask command multiplies layer alpha by the raw
mask values.

However, normal rendering uses feathered mask coverage calculated
by the compositor.

The difference causes the feathering to disappear when the mask
is applied.

## Changes

- Use the compositor's existing feathered-mask calculation.
- Bake the resulting coverage into the layer's alpha.
- Preserve the original rendering when removing the mask.
- Exclude retained vector masks from the baked pixel-mask coverage
  to avoid applying vector coverage twice.
- Preserve the existing behavior for unfeathered masks.

## Regression Coverage

Added tests across 8-, 16-, and 32-bit documents covering:

- Feathered pixel-mask rendering.
- Applying the mask.
- Comparing rendered pixels before and after Apply.
- Checking that the mask is removed.
- Restoring the original mask through Undo.

## Validation

Regression tests added. Rust tests and CI have not been executed.

title: Tests: one GPU harness at a time in every GPU test binary (WARP crash)
author: dhiorns15
body:
On Windows, the GPU UI test binaries crash with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` (0xc0000005) whenever two of their tests run at once:
- On `main`, `arbitrary_rotation_preview` crashed in 3 runs out of 4.
- `color_managed_canvas`, `crop_default_mode`, `drag_preview_canvas` and `full_res_preview` crash at random.
- Every one of them passes with `--test-threads=1`.

**Cause.** egui_kittest prefers a CPU adapter, which on Windows is **WARP over DX12**, so every kittest GPU test there runs on it. A ProcDump crash dump puts the fault inside `d3d10warp.dll`, with two WARP devices rendering on parallel test threads; the NVIDIA driver's threads in the dump are idle.

| `WGPU_BACKEND` (5 parallel runs each) | crashes |
|---|---|
| `dx12` (WARP) | 5 / 5 |
| `vulkan` | 0 / 5 |
| `gl` | 0 / 5 |

Bare egui harnesses with no PhotoCraft code crash the same way (1 run in 5), so this is WARP rather than our code. The app itself has a single device, used only on the UI thread. GitHub's Windows runners have no GPU, so CI runs on WARP as well.

**Fix.** Three binaries already serialized their GPU tests with a per-binary lock, for the same class of driver bug:
- Mesa llvmpipe and RADV (#194);
- libvulkan with both NVIDIA and lavapipe installed.

That lock now lives once, in `photocraft_testkit::gpu_lock`, with all the known reasons documented. Every test in the 12 GPU test binaries that had no lock takes it on its first line. Under nextest each test is its own process, so the lock costs nothing there.

**Tests**
- After the fix, the 7 multi-test binaries ran 5 times each in parallel: 35 out of 35 clean. Before, most runs of the 5 binaries above crashed.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --tests`, run twice: all 23 binaries pass, with no crash.
- `photocraft-testkit`: new tests showing a panicked holder doesn't block the next test, and holders take turns.
- Clean: clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`.

Worth reporting upstream (WARP via wgpu) once there's a minimal repro; that isn't p…

title: automation: doc.place reads a file through the read root (#2810)
author: switch87
body:

`file.placeEmbedded` takes an ambient path, so the automation boundary refuses it ("use capability-scoped document methods") and an agent had no way at all to place a file into the open document.

title: Moving type keeps its rendering: Artboards to Files no longer drops PSD text
author: fabianghe
body:
## What happens
`commands::translate_layer` **re-renders a type layer on every whole-pixel move**. For type that came from a PSD, this replaces Photoshop's rendering with PhotoCraft's own:
- paragraphs re-wrap;
- text set in a font that isn't installed disappears completely.

**Found with:** File › Export › **Artboards to Files** on a real Steam store asset template (a free PSD from Noblesteed Games, 20 artboards). `artboard_document` moves each board to the origin with `translate_layer`. The "How to use this template" board lost its big **"Hello!"** title, which is set in JetBrains Mono, and the step list re-wrapped. The same path runs for:
- the Move tool commit (`move_layers`) and arrow nudges;
- applying a layer comp's position;
- moving artboards;
- copying layers.

## The fix
- A whole-pixel move now **shifts the rendered pixels**, the same way smart objects (`shift_smart`) and the Move tool's live preview (`layer_multi_cmds::shift_shown`) already do.
- It also moves the TySh position with a new `photocraft_text::psd::translate_tysh`. That changes only the transform's tx/ty bytes (offsets 34 and 42). The text, styles, warp and trailing bounds are in text space, so they stay byte for byte as Photoshop wrote them, and PSD export still writes the right position.
- Type with no rendered cache yet is still rendered, as before.

## Measured on the template (PhotoCraft export vs Photoshop's own composite)
| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Artboards identical to Photoshop | 16 of 20* | **17 of 20** |
| "How to use" board, mean abs difference (0–255) | 4.54 | **0.02** |
| "Hello!" title | missing | **present** |

\* The two other boards that differ, Main Capsule and Header Capsule, have 6 and 26 pixels off by 1 level on smart objects. That rounding is identical before and after this change. The rest of the "How to use" residual is inside two **shape** layers (a rounded rectangle and an ellipse), which re-render on move through `translate_vectors`. That is the same c…
