title: Preserve 16-bit Affinity pixels and recover source-backed raster layers
author: grlessa
body:
Affinity RGB16 pixel layers currently lose precision, and wholly source-backed raster layers can import empty. This change preserves native 16-bit pixels and masks and recovers complete source-backed RGB8/RGB16 layers as editable raster layers.

Recovery requires the exact complete byte-tile grid in all four channels. Mixed source-backed/edited grids retain their stored tiles with warnings; the original is never substituted over edits. Missing/corrupt originals warn, and differing dimensions, colour model or depth are rejected. Embedded ICC profiles on recovered layers explicitly warn that they were not applied. Placed images remain smart objects; the Affinity source is read-only.

Twelve original synthetic regressions cover Stored/Zlib/Zstd containers, exact 16-bit samples, masks, mixed-depth promotion, premultiplied-alpha interpolation, edited grids, malformed/mismatched originals, profile warnings, smart objects and native/PSD round trips. Seven of the initial eight regressions fail against pre-fix `3e000bc`. An original RGB16 TIFF saved in an existing Affinity 3.3.0 installation reproduced the problem and imported all 65,536 RGBA16 samples exactly after the fix. The README records that black-box validation separately from the original reader's provenance. No proprietary executable code, resources or locally application-made documents are committed.

Remaining limitations include mixed source/edited tiles, float pixel formats, document colour-profile mapping, adjustments and live filters. This preserves precision in the supported paths; it does not claim universal Affinity colour fidelity.

Current integration (2026-10-14): merged main `c699e3cd` (0.9.0 source preparation). Resolved `docs/file-format-parity.md` by retaining both the Affinity precision/recovery notes and main’s PSD `Mt16`/`Mt32` transparency notes, along with both progress histories. The recorded black-box validation remains accurate.

title: fix(masks): Apply sharpens a feathered layer-mask edge (#3044)
author: buivanvu94
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3044.

When applying an enabled pixel layer mask ("Layer › Layer Mask › Apply"), `apply_mask` in `crates/engine/src/layer_menu_cmds.rs` called `mask.values_into(r, &mut m)` which only takes mask density into account, completely omitting `mask.feather`. During composition, the compositor applies Gaussian blur for feathered masks via `photocraft_compose::masks::combined_mask`. Applying a feathered mask stripped the feather blur and baked a hard edge into the layer alpha, noticeably sharpening the transition.

This PR:
- Updates `apply_mask` in `photocraft-engine` (`crates/engine/src/layer_menu_cmds.rs`) to evaluate feathered pixel layer masks using `photocraft_compose::masks::combined_mask` across the canvas, matching the compositor's rendering, before multiplying layer alpha pixels.

- Adds regression unit tests across sample depths (8/16/32-bit) and for the exact issue reproduction sequence, verifying that the post-Apply composite preserves soft edge pixels within 8-bit rounding tolerance, restores identically upon undo, and keeps unfeathered masks sharp.

title: 8-bit documents: soft, low-flow brush strokes are dithered instead of banded
author: tanish2k09
body:
Brush phase 6c of the owner-approved overhaul.

## Why

Strokes composite in float (an f32 stroke buffer over the pre-stroke pixels), and then `write_region` rounds each pixel to 8 bits. A soft, low-flow stroke's gradient then collapses into visible bands. The audit measured a soft 120 px brush at flow 5 % / opacity 30 %: 35 distinct levels across the stroke against 119 at 16-bit, with concentric bands showing once contrast is stretched.

## What

`StrokeRenderer::composite` (`paint/src/render.rs`), for 8-bit targets only:
- Every pixel the stroke changes gets the same offset `(hash2(x, y) − 0.5) / 255` on all channels before quantisation. That covers normal, other blend modes, Dissolve and the eraser.
- Fractional values round up or down in proportion, so the bands become grain finer than one level.
- **Exact colours never change.** The offset stays strictly within ±0.5 of a level, and `write_region` clamps then rounds half-up, so a value already on a level rounds back to itself. Pixels the stroke doesn't touch aren't dithered.
- **Deterministic.** The offset depends only on the pixel's position, so the live preview (which re-composites from the pre-stroke pixels each step), the commit and a journal replay produce identical pixels.
- Channels share one offset, so there's no colour noise.

16-bit and float documents are unchanged. Photoshop doesn't dither brush strokes; this goes beyond it, on purpose.

## Tests

- `brush_tests::an_8bit_soft_stroke_is_dithered_instead_of_banded` compares row averages along a straight soft, low-flow stroke against a float render. Along the stroke every pixel of a row has the same true value, so plain rounding puts the whole row on one wrong level. **Main: 0.49 levels off (failed). This PR: < 0.15.**
- `brush_tests::dithering_never_moves_an_exact_colour_or_an_untouched_pixel`: solid paint keeps its exact 8-bit colour; untouched pixels stay identical.
- The existing live-equals-commit pixel tests (engine) pass unchanged.
- Gates: paint…

title: Liquify: the brush fades to nothing at its edge at every Density (#2606)
author: dhiorns15
body: Fixes the tearing in #2606. **Cause.** A Liquify dab's strength was `(1 − Density) + Density · (1 − t²)²`, so at the brush rim it stopped at `1 − Density` instead of 0: - half strength at the default Density 50; - full strength (a hard-edged disc) at Density 0. Forward Warp therefore moved the pixels just inside the brush and left the ones just outside, tearing the image along every dab's circle. A dab lands every fifth of the radius, so along a stroke those tears stack into the sawtooth edges and stripes in the issue's screenshot. Density was also backwards: 0 gave the strongest, flattest brush. **Fix.** A new `liquify::falloff` blends `(1 − t²)³` at Density 0 (effect in the centre, feathered) toward `(1 − t⁴)²` at Density 100 (full effect across most of the brush). Both curves are 1 at the centre and reach 0 at the rim with a flat slope, matching how Photoshop describes Density. Every Liquify brush tool, and Freeze/Thaw, uses it. **Before / after** Left: before · right: after. One Forward Warp stroke (size 200, pressure 100, a 360 px drag) on a grid, at Density 0, 50 and 100. **Notes** - Liquify still moves pixels rather than smudging them, as Photoshop's does. The issue's "smudge" request is about the tool itself, not this bug. - Saved Liquify strokes replay through the same code, so an existing Liquify smart filter re-renders with the smooth falloff. - Where a drag squeezes content hard there is still some moiré: the source isn't prefiltered when it's minified. That's separate from this fix and I've left it for a follow-up. **Tests** - New: `the_brush_fades_to_nothing_at_its_rim_at_every_density` covers the curve (1 at the centre, 0 and flat at the rim, falling all the way, Density widening the core, NaN and out-of-range values). - New: `forward_warp_leaves_the_brush_rim_in_place`: the outer 3 % of the brush …

title: Native brush outline and crosshair cursors on macOS, X11 and Wayland (#1343)
author: tanish2k09
body:
Part of #1343 (cursor lag), done jointly with @jerrykimo's #968.

## What
The brush outline and the crosshairs (Precise, crosshair-while-painting, the big-tip hotspot) were OS cursor bitmaps only on Windows (#1160). On macOS, X11 and Wayland the app painted them into the canvas, so they trailed the hardware pointer by render + present + compositor latency and "jumped to catch up" on slow frames, which is what the #1343 reports describe. The latency-surface experiments didn't perceptibly help, which fits: the outline was the lagging thing, not the strokes.

`tool_cursor` now uploads the bitmap on every desktop root viewport (eframe/egui-winit 0.36 upload `cursor_image` through winit `CustomCursor` on all of them). The web build and immediate viewports keep the painted path.

- **macOS sizing (from #968):** winit takes an `NSCursor` image's size in logical points, so on macOS the bitmap scales only with the UI zoom (`native_scale`); Windows, X11 and Wayland take physical pixels.
- **Size cap off Windows:** 255 px, because X servers and hardware cursor planes commonly cap at 256 and fall back to software cursors (or reject the image) past that. #968 used 128. A larger tip keeps today's fallback: the painted full-size outline plus a small OS crosshair at the hotspot. Windows keeps 2048.

title: Control-channel document events and `app.capabilities`
author: emmertex
body:
> **Stacked on #3244** (which includes the earlier PRs in this series): this branch contains their commits. Please review only the commits after them; it will be rebased once #3244 merges.

### Summary
- `events.subscribe {events?}` on the TCP control channel pushes `document.opened`, `document.saved`, `document.closed` lines (`{"event", "params": {path, format, docId}}`, no `id`) on the same connection, always in opened → saved → closed order. - Documented in `docs/control-protocol.md` › Events. MCP notifications and `photocraft-cli serve` events are follow-up work.

### Motivation
Tools that hand a file to an editor need to know when it was saved (to re-read it) and when the user is done, without polling or relying on window focus.

### Test plan
- `doc_events` unit tests (order, filters, Save As path on close, dead subscribers, limits, bad names) and an app-level test through `control::handle`.
- `control_server` test: reply before events, events have no id, second subscribe refused, connection keeps serving.

title: Menus: a submenu stays open while the pointer heads for it (#1218)
author: brennanMKE
body:
Fixes the submenu part of #1218.

In the in-window menu bar (Windows, Linux, and macOS with `--in-window-menus`), moving from a submenu's row toward one of its lower items crosses the rows below. Unless the pointer moved in a straight line, the submenu closed on the way, and the crossed rows lit up or opened their own submenus. In the report's example, going from Image › Mode to 16 Bits/Channel crosses Adjustments.

## Cause

egui's `SubMenu` keeps an open submenu only while `is_moving_towards_rect` is true: the pointer's current direction, averaged over the last 0.1 s, must point straight into the popup. A bowed path, or any pause of more than about 0.1 s, fails that test. egui then closes the submenu, and the next frame opens the submenu of the row under the pointer. `menu_nav` also moved the highlight to every row crossed.

## Fix

macOS and Photoshop judge this with a triangle. `menu_nav::Nav::row` now does the same for submenu rows:

- **The triangle:** from the point where the pointer left the row to the submenu's near edge, with 24 pt of slack above and below.
- **While the pointer is inside it:** if egui closes the submenu, `MenuState::open_item` is restored straight after the row is drawn. Later rows therefore can't open their own submenus.
- **Highlight:** the row stays lit, and the rows crossed don't light up.
- **When the submenu switches:**
  - when the pointer rests on another row for 0.3 s;
  - when it moves outside the triangle (straight down, or back to the left);
  - on a click or a key, as before.

  When the submenu lets go, the row under the pointer takes the highlight.
- **Keyboard:** ↑ and ↓ move the highlight as before; the pointer's hold no longer overrides them.

The change is about 130 lines in `menu_nav.rs`, with no change to egui. Nested submenus get the same behaviour, since each level runs the same code.

**Not in this PR:** the issue's second request, a reduced-motion mode. Menus fade in over egui's global `animation_time` (1/12 s), a…

title: test(paint): pin the retouch dab footprint to the Full Size ring
author: switch87
body:
Closes #1761.

This is the regression test @theriseandfallofitall asked for: one that pins "changed radius ≈ size/2, inside the Full Size ring".

`crates/paint/src/retouch.rs` gains `footprint_stays_inside_the_full_size_ring`. For a single dab of radius 10.5 px it walks the whole `footprint` rect at hardness 1.0, 0.5 and 0.0, measures each painted pixel's distance from the centre using pixel centres (`x + 0.5`, `y + 0.5` — the same sampling `footprint` and `render.rs` use), and asserts:

- **nothing paints past `radius + 0.5`** at any hardness. The half pixel is the anti-aliased edge of `dab_coverage`, which returns 0 from `d >= radius + 0.5`. This is the invariant that a larger-than-cursor brush would break.
- **something does paint** at every hardness, so the test cannot pass by painting nothing.
- **a hard tip reaches the ring** (`hardness == 1.0` → farthest painted pixel is beyond `radius`). Softer tips are deliberately *not* held to that: `dab_coverage` blends the AA edge with the hardness falloff, so at hardness 0.5 coverage reaches 0 at `radius` itself and the farthest painted pixel sits at ~10.12 px. That matches @vangel76's probe (10.12–10.27 px for Spot Healing at hardness 50) and is the falloff working as intended, not a defect.

That last point is why the test is written this way rather than asserting "changed radius ≈ size/2" flat: at a soft tip the ring is the 50 % contour, so painting past it is correct and only the Full Size tip pins the outer bound.

Verification:

```
cargo test -p photocraft-paint --lib          85 passed
cargo clippy -p photocraft-paint --all-targets -- -D warnings   clean
cargo fmt -p photocraft-paint -- --check      clean
```

The test lives in the existing `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `retouch.rs`, next to `coverage_matches_apply_stroke_bounds`, and follows its style. No production code is touched.

title: Type: fall back to installed Khmer, Lao and Burmese fonts (#218)
author: RaccoonPie-314
body:
## The bug

Khmer (and Lao / Burmese) text renders as `.notdef` boxes even though the OS has a font for the script — #218, scorecard item TYPE-218-3.

## Root cause

Not detection, and not shaping. Each layer tested separately:

| layer | result |
|---|---|
| detection | `FontDb::load_system_fonts()` finds *Khmer Sangam MN* |
| loading + shaping | laying the same text out with that family gives real clusters, coeng subscripts included |
| **selection** | the fallback stack never contains a Khmer-capable family |

`fallback_candidates()` is a list of family names filtered against what is installed (`FontDb::refresh_generics`). It carried Thai, CJK, Arabic and Hebrew entries, but nothing for Khmer, Lao or Burmese. `layout.rs` builds each run's CSS family list from exactly that stack plus a trailing `sans-serif`, which resolves to Inter — so an installed Southeast Asian font could not be reached from a Latin-only face, and every cluster became `.notdef`.

## Changes

**photocraft-text** — `KHMER_FAMILIES`, `LAO_FAMILIES` and `MYANMAR_FAMILIES` join `fallback_candidates` next to `THAI_FAMILIES`. The web build's served-font path gets the matching `Khmr` / `Laoo` / `Mymr` script codes, character ranges and `km` / `lo` / `my` languages, so a host serving `Noto Sans Khmer` works there too.

**photocraft-ui-egui** — the UI's lazy loader had one non-CJK slot (Thai: `Sources::thai`, `thai_tried`, `is_thai`, `thai_font_files`). It becomes a `LazyScript` slot table fed by `script_font_files(mac, win, noto_stem, family)`, so the three scripts are data rather than a third and fourth copy of the same state machine. This half matters on its own: tab titles, layer names and panel labels were tofu for the same reason but through a different stack than the canvas.

Family names follow Microsoft's [script and font support](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/globalization/fonts-layout/font-support) table (`Khmer UI` / `Lao UI` on Windows 8, `Leelawadee UI` from 8.1, `Myanmar Text`) and th…

title: Windows installer: refuse Windows 7 and 8 with a clear message (#2310)
author: dhiorns15
body:
Closes #2310.

**The problem.** PhotoCraft can't run on Windows 7 or 8. Since Rust 1.78 the standard library calls `ProcessPrng` in `bcryptprimitives.dll`, which only exists on Windows 10 and later, so Windows refuses to start the program before any of our code runs:

> The procedure entry point ProcessPrng could not be located in the dynamic link library bcryptprimitives.dll.

`docs/gaps.md` already lists Windows 7 as out of scope, and `docs/releasing.md` says the builds are for Windows 10+. The MSI, though, installed on Windows 7 anyway, leaving people with that cryptic error.

**The change**
- **Installer:** the MSI now stops on Windows 7 and 8 with "PhotoCraft needs Windows 10 or later. This version of Windows can't run it."
  - A registry search sets `WINDOWS10ORLATER` from `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\CurrentMajorVersionNumber`. That value exists only from Windows 10 on, in both the 32-bit and 64-bit registry views, so the x86 MSI gets the same check.
  - The rule is `<Launch Condition="Installed OR WINDOWS10ORLATER">`, so repair and uninstall still work on any Windows.
  - MSI's own `VersionNT` isn't used: it has reported both 603 and 1000 on Windows 10 (it's 1000 on the Windows 11 PC I tested on).
- **README:** the Windows downloads section now says Windows 10 or later is required. The portable zip can't check anything, because Windows rejects the exe before it runs.

**Verified locally (WiX 5.0.2, as in CI)**
- `package.ps1 -Arch x64 -SkipBuild` builds the MSI and passes its ICE50 validation.
- Read back from the built MSI:
  - `LaunchCondition`: `Installed OR WINDOWS10ORLATER` with the message.
  - `AppSearch` and `RegLocator`: the search, which runs at sequence 50, before `LaunchConditions` at 100.
  - The property is listed in `SecureCustomProperties`.
- Running `AppSearch` in a Windows Installer session, with nothing installed: on Windows 11 the property is `#10` and the condition is true. With the property cleared, as on Windows 7…

title: Edit > Copy takes a targeted layer mask, so masks travel between layers and documents (#2928)
author: vbasky
body:
Part of #2928: the copy & paste half. The ⌥-drag half belongs on the mask-drag start that #3118 is landing, and this branch deliberately does not touch that plumbing.

## Root cause
Copy never knew about the targeted mask. With a mask targeted, ⌘C copied the layer's pixels (or refused on a pixel-less layer), so a mask could never be moved to another layer or document. Paste was ready all along: pasting into a targeted mask has worked since #1035, and the session clipboard is shared between documents.

## What changed
- `edit.copy` honours `"target":"mask"`: the mask's values, as a grayscale clip — inside the selection, or the whole canvas when there is none, as Photoshop copies a mask whole. An untouched Reveal All / Hide All mask copies at its default value, so plain masks transfer too. Pasting then **replaces** the target mask (the request in #2928).
- `edit.copy` joined `routed()`/`edits_mask()`: the ⌘C dispatched while the Layers panel targets a mask carries the target, and Copy is enabled on adjustment and fill layers (which have no pixels of their own) exactly while their mask is targeted. ⌥-viewing a mask targets it as for every other routed command.
- Agents can drive it directly: `edit.copy {"target":"mask"}` → `edit.paste {"target":"mask"}`, in the same or another document; different canvas sizes centre the paste like any other paste.

## Tests
- `copy_with_the_mask_targeted_takes_the_mask_as_grayscale` — copy → paste into another layer's reveal-all mask at 8/16/32 bits, values and bounds, one undo step on the paste, none on the copy.
- `an_untouched_mask_copies_the_whole_canvas_at_its_default` — a never-painted Reveal All mask still transfers.

title: PNG export: Indexed Color keeps the document resolution (#3047)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3047

## Root cause
Indexed Color documents are exported to PNG through a dedicated palette encoder (`encode_png_indexed`, used by `export_mode_specific` in `crates/io/src/flat.rs`). Unlike the ordinary PNG encoder, it never set `pixel_dims`, so no `pHYs` chunk was written and the file reopened at 72 ppi.

## Fix
- `photocraft_codecs::encode_png_indexed` takes an optional `dpi` and writes `pHYs` (metres, rounded like the RGB path) when both axes are positive and finite.
- The flat exporter passes the document resolution under the same `embed_metadata` rule as the ordinary PNG encoder.
- Save for Web PNG-8 passes `None` (unchanged behaviour; its PNG-24 path also only writes metadata on request).

## Tests
- `crates/io/tests/modes.rs::indexed_png_keeps_the_document_resolution`: a 300 ppi Indexed document exports as a palette PNG (colour type 3) and reopens at 300 ppi. Fails without the fix (reopens at 72 ppi), passes with it.

## Commands
- `cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-io --test modes --test flat --test png_text_metadata`
- `cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-codecs --lib -- png`

title: ui: keep the Color panel knob in the corner it was dragged to
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #3228

## Cause

The Color panel's SV field rebuilds its `Hsva` from the stored colour every frame, and the colour lives as RGB. At the bottom edge the value is 0 — black — and black reads back as `s = 0`, so the frame after the drag that put the knob in the bottom-right corner the knob was drawn at `x = s = 0`: bottom-left. The colour round-trips correctly, the field position does not survive it.

The field already remembered the *hue* for a degenerate colour ("Keep hue stable for greys"), but not the saturation.

## Fix

Remember what the field was actually showing — hue **and** saturation — in the same temp entry, and restore both only where the colour itself cannot carry them:

* **black** (`v` ≈ 0): neither hue nor saturation survives the RGB round trip, so restore both — the knob stays in the corner it was dragged to;
* **a grey** (`s` ≈ 0): the saturation really is zero, which is where the knob belongs, only the hue was undefined — restore the hue alone;
* **any other colour**: untouched.

## Tests

* `field_hsva_keeps_black_where_it_was_and_leaves_a_real_colour_alone` — the three cases above.
* `dragging_to_the_bottom_right_keeps_the_knob_there` — a real drag through the harness into the corner: the field picks black there, keeps the dragged saturation, and the next frame draws the knob in that corner.

Verified locally: `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib color_tests` (19 passed), `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers`. The full crate suite runs in CI.

## What changed

PhotoCraft had no way to turn UI animation off. Menus, popups and collapsing sections always fade or slide over egui's `animation_time`, and scroll areas glide to their target. #217 asks for a toggle, and #1218 asks for the same thing as a reduced-motion mode. #3251 fixes that issue's submenu part and leaves this out.

- **New preference:** Preferences › Interface › **Enable animations** (`interface.enableAnimations`, on by default). It is saved with the other preferences, and agents can set it with `prefs.set`.

- **On:** it puts egui's defaults back.
- **Theme changes:** the setting is re-checked every frame, like `sync_tooltips`, because a theme change rebuilds the style. It writes only when the value differs.
- **Prefs audit:** the field is read, so the count of settings that do nothing stays at 43 (now of 151).
- **Translations:** the label "Enable animations" is in all 16 catalogs.
- **Scorecard:** UI-217-10 moves from `missing` to `partial`. Animations are done. The Home screen already lists recent files (#2691). Still open: the canvas pattern toggle (#2317 / #2264) and an option to hide the Home screen recents.

## Tests

`enable_animations_off_stops_fades_and_scroll_glides_and_is_remembered` (in `prefs_ui.rs` tests):

title: Vanishing Point: tear off planes and clone in perspective (#3280)
author: vangel76
body:

#3133, which this builds on, is merged; this branch is current with main.

## What changed

title: Rulers: stay level and fully ticked on a rotated view; guides turn with the image (#3233)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3233
Fixes #3277

## Root cause

- **Rulers (#3233):** `draw_rulers` computed the visible range with `xf.to_doc` of the ruler's end points and placed ticks with `xf.to_screen(px, 0).x` (or `.y`), both through the *rotated* view. With a rotation, a document axis no longer runs along the screen axis, so the ticks were squeezed into a short stretch (none at 90°) and the rest of the ruler was empty, as in the issue screenshot.
- **Guides (#3277, found while fixing this):** `draw_guides` drew a vertical guide as a screen-vertical line through the screen position of `(pos, 0)` (likewise for horizontal ones). On a rotated view that line no longer marks the guide's document coordinate, while hit-testing and snapping still use it.

## Fix

- Rulers are screen chrome and stay level: they now measure with the view minus its rotation (`ruler_xform`). Zoom, flip and pixel aspect stay the same, so the ticks never stretch, and 0 is anchored at the screen position of the document origin as the rotated view draws it. Tilted guides therefore meet the rulers near their numbers. Unrotated views are unchanged.
- Guides belong to the document (as in Photoshop) and turn with the image: `guide_segment` draws the document line x = pos (or y = pos) across every document point the clip rect shows. Unrotated, that is still the clip's full height/width.
- Ruler labels left of / above the origin read without a minus sign (`ruler_label` prints the absolute value), as in Photoshop 2026 ("1000 500 0 500 1000"); this applies to every view, and `rotated_view_keeps_full_rulers` now checks it (fails with the old signed labels: tick -800 labelled "-800").

Before (issue) vs after: the rulers are fully ticked at -119°, and a vertical guide at x = 500 and a horizontal one at y = 300 now cross the rotated image at those coordinates (checked with the `snapshot` example).

Verified against Photoshop 2026: rulers stay level at zoom scale, anchored at the document origin's screen position; guides turn w…

title: Smart Filters: distinct editors, shared disclosure and stable alpha
author: abc2cb
body:
Double-clicking a Smart Filter row currently reopens its parameter dialog, with no separate target for that filter's blending. The shared mask is only a placeholder, and the layer disclosure does not hide Smart Filters. This change gives the filter name and right-hand Blending Options icon separate double-click targets, displays the real shared mask, and uses one disclosure for layer effects and Smart Filters without changing document pixels or history.

Blending Options edits the selected filter's Mode and 0–100% Opacity, with temporary Preview, a bounded CMS-aware image viewport, OK, Cancel, and Undo/Redo. The UI sends 1% as 0.01. Parameter editors reopen stored values and update the existing filter instead of appending a duplicate; Invert has no invented parameter editor and Camera Raw keeps its dedicated editor. Captured document/revision/filter identity and a bounded weak document snapshot guard reject stale editors, including reopening the same saved document with the same IDs.

Native QA also reproduced an existing Smart Filter opacity defect: translucent alpha 128 became 129 at 1% and 160 at 50%. Smart Filter strength now interpolates premultiplied input/filtered results, preserving coverage for alpha-preserving filters. Normal mode also interpolates actual coverage changes; non-Normal modes retain source-over semantics when the filtered surface changes alpha, preserving input-only and output-only pixels around blur edges. This does not alter global layer compositing.

The PR builds on merged #2229 and #2739. Their implementations are not duplicated: current Smart Object source APIs, cached stages and background jobs are retained. Six new localization keys are supplied in all 16 catalogs. Behavior and storage limits are documented in `docs/smart-filters.md`.

title: fix(io): smooth PSD gradients no longer overshoot their stops (#3028)
author: Sir-Starch
body: Fixes #3028 ## Problem The Gradient Map in the issue (0% `#cacaca`, 27% `#1c1c1c`, 53% `#1c1c1c`, 72% `#949494`) renders far too dark in the middle: the 27%-53% stretch should be a flat `#1c1c1c`, but PhotoCraft dips well below it. ## Cause The PSD importer bakes Smoothness into dense stops in `gradient_bake::eval` (Catmull-Rom blended with linear). The tangent at each stop comes from its neighbouring stops. For the segment between the two equal-coloured stops, both end colours are the same, yet each end tangent is non-zero (it is taken from the neighbouring stops, `#cacaca` on one side and `#949494` on the other), so the Hermite curve undershoots the plateau. On the issue's file the output at t = 0.396 was 0.034 (9/255) instead of 28/255. The stop positions and colours are parsed correctly; only the interpolation is off. ## Fix Clamp each interpolated channel to the range of the segment's own two end colours (in the method's interpolation space: sRGB, linear light or Oklab). Smoothness still eases the ramps, but it can no longer invent a colour outside the segment, so a plateau stays exactly flat. It is a small change in `eval`. `bake` is shared, so this also applies to gradient fills, gradient overlays and smoothed opacity stops read from PSD files, not only to Gradient Map. Any smooth segment whose Catmull-Rom curve used to leave its endpoints' range is now bounded by it. ## Result Measured on the issue's PSD, per pixel against Photoshop's embedded composite (red channel; the render is grayscale): | | max error | mean error | pixels off by more than 8/255 | |---|---|---|---| | before (`main`) | 19 | 4.48 | 205 263 | | after | 6 | 1.66 | 0 | The pixel the issue's dark band centres on, (445, 506), was `9` against Photoshop's `28`; it is now `28`. title: Decode Panasonic RW2 RawFormat 3/4 (vendor-compressed sensor data)
author: Gotya-OFFCIAL
body:
# Decode Panasonic RW2 RawFormat 3/4 (vendor-compressed sensor data)

`crates/raw/src/rw2.rs` only handled RawFormat 5 (uncompressed); everything else fell back to the embedded 1920×1440 JPEG preview with a `raw-fallback` warning. This adds a full sensor decoder for RawFormat 4 — the compressed variant used by e.g. the DMC-GX7 (4816×3464, 12-bit) — and maps RawFormat 3 to the same row layout.

## What it does

RawFormat 4 stores 14 Bayer pixels per 128-bit block: two unchanged 12-bit seeds, then four groups of three 8-bit differences plus a 2-bit shift code (`{0,1,2,4}` left shift). Each difference predicts against the previous same-colour pixel; a zero difference copies the immediately preceding sample. Rows stride `(w·9 + 2·(w/14))/8` through 16 KiB strips with an XOR-0x3FF0 page interleave and a split rotation; near a page boundary the 16-bit read window wraps inside the strip instead of crossing into the next one.

## Provenance / licensing

Implemented independently for this project — no code was copied from GPL/LGPL decoders. The bitstream layout was derived from sample files (Panasonic DMC-GX7) and verified bit-exact against LibRaw's `raw_image` output via the rawpy bindings:

- 4816×3464 DMC-GX7 samples: **0 mismatches / 16,682,624 pixels** (two separate files)
- the row/stride/page model and predictor recurrence are documented from observation in `rw2.rs` comments

## Verification

- `cargo test -p photocraft-raw` — all green, incl. new `rw2_format4_round_trip_is_exact` (synthetic encoder → exact round-trip) and `rw2_format4_crosses_pages`
- end-to-end on the real GX7 files: full-resolution develop into 4592×3448 16-bit ProPhoto RGB, no fallback warning
- raw sensor layer bit-exact vs LibRaw (see above)

## Notes

- Colour calibration for Panasonic bodies is still absent (pre-existing behaviour, still warned) — the RAW decode itself is the fix here.

title: ui: Dust & Scratches previews at full resolution, as it applies
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #3265

## Cause

`full_resolution_preview` in `crates/ui-egui/src/filter_dialog.rs` decides which live previews run on the reduced proxy and which run at full resolution, and Dust & Scratches was not in `FULL_RESOLUTION_PREVIEW`.

Its `radius` *is* a pixel param, so `preview_factor` clamps the proxy factor to `radius / 1` — but only that. At the default radius the preview happens to land on full resolution; at a practical radius it previews at the document's full factor (k = 4 on a 24 MP document), on an image where downsampling has already averaged away the specks the filter exists to remove, with a radius that then covers k times the area it covers in the result, upscaled back for display. Hence the blocky preview in the report, and a preview that shows nothing removed.

`OK` always applied at full resolution — the result was never wrong, only the interactive feedback was.

## Fix

Add `filter.noise.dustAndScratches` to `FULL_RESOLUTION_PREVIEW` and name it in the category comment next to the other per-pixel noise filters.

## Test

The issue asks for one on the intended preview-quality path, so `("filter.noise.dustAndScratches", {"radius": 4, "threshold": 0})` joins `fixed_size_filters_preview_at_the_scale_they_apply`, which already asserts both that `preview_factor` comes out as 1 and that the shown preview is what OK applies.

Verified: with the list entry removed the test fails with `left: 4, right: 1` at the `preview_factor` assertion — the defect itself; with it, `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib` (1828 passed), `clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, `fmt --check` and `cargo xtask layers` are all clean.

title: Codecs: decode PNM straight into the budgeted output buffer (#2938)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2938

## Root cause
`Limits::max_alloc` budgets the decoded pixel buffer, and `Limits::check` charged exactly that before decoding. But the PNM decoder then collected every sample into a `Vec<u32>` first (4x the output of an 8-bit image; for 16-bit, `Image::from_u16` added a further `u16` → byte copy, so roughly 8 bytes per 2-byte sample at peak). PFM did the same with a `Vec<f32>` next to the output bytes. None of that scratch was covered by the budget.

## Fix
This takes the first option from the issue: keep the intermediate in the budgeted output type. A small `Samples` writer reserves the output bytes with `try_reserve_exact`, so a failed allocation becomes `LimitExceeded`. It checks each value against `maxval`, rescales it the same way as before and appends it in native-endian order. P2/P3/P5/P6/P7 build the `Image` from those bytes with `from_raw`. PFM writes native-endian `f32` bytes straight into the output rows, still bottom-to-top. The ASCII reservation stays bounded by the file length (#1110). The decoded values don't change.

## Tests
- New `crates/codecs/tests/pnm_peak_memory.rs`, Linux only and in its own process. It resets the peak RSS through `/proc/self/clear_refs`, decodes a 4096² 8-bit P5 (16 MiB of output) and asserts that the peak grew by less than 2x the output. Without the fix it fails: `decoding a 16777216 byte image raised peak RSS by 84189184 bytes`. With the fix it passes, and it was stable over repeated runs. Where the kernel doesn't allow `clear_refs`, the test skips.
- The existing value tests in `malformed.rs` (maxval rescaling for 8 and 16 bit, PFM bottom-up and endianness), `limits.rs` (bomb headers, #1110 reservations) and `roundtrip.rs` still pass.

## Commands
```
cargo test -p photocraft-codecs --lib --test pnm_peak_memory --test limits --test malformed --test roundtrip --test detect_caps
cargo clippy -p photocraft-codecs --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt -p photocraft-codecs -- --check
cargo xtask test-corpus -p phot…

title: Format: admit the declared .pcraft canvas before loading it (#2935)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2935

Also the load-time half of #2934 (the GPU destination-texture budget follows in a separate PR).

## Root cause

`store::load` read the manifest and handed `m.document.size` straight to `Loader::document`, which copied it into the `Document`. `LoadOptions` bounded manifest, blob and decompressed bytes, but nothing bounded the declared canvas. A few bytes of JSON could declare a canvas of any size, up to `u32::MAX` × `u32::MAX`, and the CPU reduction, thumbnails and display textures then work in proportion to that area.

## Fix

- `LoadOptions` gains `max_canvas_side` (default `MAX_CANVAS_SIDE` = 300000: Photoshop's PSB limit, the same as the PSD header check and `file.new`) and `max_canvas_pixels` (default `MAX_CANVAS_PIXELS` = 300000², the full PSB canvas).
- The default admits every canvas the app lets a user create: `file.new`, Canvas Size, Image Size with Resample off and PSB import all reach 300000 × 300000. A lower area cap (an earlier revision used 2^32 = 65536²) would let a user create and save a document that then refuses to reopen. Callers that handle untrusted files (previewers, batch jobs) can lower either budget.
- `store::load` calls `admit_canvas` right after reading the manifest, before any tile or blob is decoded. It rejects an empty canvas (`Corrupt`), a side over the limit and an area over the limit (`LimitExceeded`, with the declared size in the message).
- Loading stays proportional to the file, not to the declared canvas: layers, masks and channels are sparse tiles read from the bundle under the byte budgets, so a 300000² manifest with no content allocates nothing for its area (the test checks the tile count).
- A compile-time assert in `engine/src/document_preset_cmds.rs` ties `file.new`'s `MAX_DIMENSION` to the loader's defaults, so the two can't drift apart again.
- The fuzz target and `book/src/security/parser-hardening.md` are updated to match.

## Tests

title: GPU canvas: price the display textures before building them (#2934)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2934

The load-time half (a `.pcraft` canvas above 300000 px per side or 4 gigapixels is refused) is #3295. This PR adds the GPU-side budget the issue asks for, which also covers documents that arrive by other routes (PSB, Canvas Size, `file.new`).

## Root cause

`DocTextures::new` built a full-resolution, mipmapped texture set covering the whole canvas in `DEFAULT_TILE` tiles. The only limit was the side length of each texture, so the size of the canvas alone decided how much GPU memory was committed. A 300000×300000 canvas asks for about 480 GB, and an admitted 65536² canvas asks for about 23 GB. `fits_budget` only covers resident layer pages, not this destination set.

## Fix (`crates/ui-egui/src/gpu_canvas.rs`, `canvas.rs`)

- `canvas_texture_bytes(size, tile, bpp)` prices the set in closed form, over at most four distinct tile shapes and every mip level, with saturating arithmetic. Any declared size costs O(1) to price. The result matches `texture_info`.
- `canvas_budget(ram)` returns a quarter of physical memory, assuming 16 GB when RAM is unknown, and never goes below `MIN_GPU_BUDGET`. This is the same RAM cap `memory_budget` uses. The value is stored in `Resources` and can be changed with `GpuCanvas::set_canvas_budget`.
- `DocTextures::new` returns `None` and creates nothing when the set is over budget. All three callers handle that: `upload_full_as`, `composite` (which returns `Unsupported`) and `upload_composite`.
- `GpuCanvas::refresh` returns kind `REFRESH_OVER_BUDGET` and drops any stale set. `ensure_gpu` checks `fits_canvas` before the per-frame memory-budget walk, and returns `false` on that kind just as it does for `"lost"`. The document is then drawn on the reduced CPU canvas (at most `MAX_TEXTURE` per side), so a large document still displays.

title: Move tool: double-click type on the canvas to edit it (#1132)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Closes #1132.

Since Photoshop CC 2019, double-clicking a type layer on the canvas with the **Move** tool starts editing its text, with no manual tool switch. PhotoCraft only did this from the Layers panel's type thumbnail.

With the Move tool selected, a double-click on type now:
- picks the topmost visible type layer under the pointer, using the Type tool's own hit test, and makes it the active layer;
- opens an edit session with the caret on the glyph under the pointer;
- switches to the Type tool (Vertical Type for vertical text).

A double-click anywhere else does nothing. ⌘ held over another tool (the temporary Move) doesn't trigger it. An open transform box keeps its double-click, which commits the transform.

### Changes
- `type_tool::edit_at`: starts an edit at a document point, reusing `hit_layer`, `begin_edit` and `hit_offset`. A PSD type layer is re-rendered inside the edit session, as when you click into it with the Type tool.
- `canvas.rs`: calls `edit_at` on a Move tool double-click when no transform box is open.
- `docs/ui-parity.md`: adds a row to the Move tool table.

### Testing
- New test `type_tool::canvas_tests::move_tool_double_click_on_type_edits_it`. It double-clicks a glyph while another layer is active and checks:
  - the Type tool takes over;
  - the caret sits on that glyph;
  - the type layer becomes active;
  - no history step is added;
  - typed text lands at the caret;
  - a double-click off the text stays with the Move tool.
- The test fails without the `canvas.rs` change, with the tool staying Move.
- The type tests' harness steps a quarter second per frame, which is past egui's 0.3 s double-click delay, so this test uses a 60 fps harness (`fast_harness`).
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests`: 1834 lib tests plus all integration test files pass.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt` are clean.

author: vangel76
body:

The global pen curve (Preferences › Tools › Pressure Curve) existed; each brush dynamic had no own response to its control. title: Brush: smooth edges on large hard round strokes (#3240)
author: dhiorns15
body: Closes #3240. **Cause.** At Photoshop's default 25 % spacing, neighbouring round dabs sit a quarter of their width apart. Where their circles cross, a hard edge is notched by `r − √(r² − (s/2)²)`, about 3 % of the radius. For a 400 px tip that's **6 px**, which is the scalloped edge in the issue; at 100 px it's 1.3 px. **Fix.** The painting tools take shorter steps when a plain, full-Flow round tip's Spacing would notch the edge by more than half a pixel. That covers Brush, Pencil and Eraser, in both the live stroke and the committed one. - A softer rim hides a notch up to a fifth of its width, so the step can stay longer as hardness drops; by about 85 % hardness nothing changes. - At full Flow the extra dabs only add coverage along the edge. The stroke's pixels inside are identical, and the tests check that. **Left exactly as before** (same dabs, same pixels), because for these extra dabs would change the look: - Flow below 100 %: the overlap rings of a low-Flow stroke are how it builds up. I tried compensating each dab's flow instead; it kept the centre density, but the stroke's ends looked different, so I dropped it. - Sampled tips, roundness below 100 %, scattering, random size/roundness/opacity/flow/colour jitter, Fade, per-tip texture, Dual Brush, Wet Edges, Noise and Build-up. - Tools that pick up or sample per dab (Smudge, Mixer Brush, the retouching tools): `StrokeRenderer::smooth_edges()` is opt-in and they don't call it. **Numbers** (a 1000 px drag, release build) | Tip | Edge ripple | Dabs | Time | |---|---|---|---| | 400 px, hardness 100 % | 6.06 → **0.17 px** | 11 → 36 | 12 → 27 ms | | 100 px, hardness 100 % | 1.26 → **0.17 px** | 41 → 71 | 3 → 4 ms | | 1000 px, hardness 100 % | (bumps) → smooth | 5 → 23 | 35 → 100 ms | | 400 px, hardness 90 % | 4.38 → 2.43 px | 11 → 12 | same | | 400 px, hardness ≤ 75 % or Flow 30 % | unchanged | unchanged | same | **Before / after**

title: Fix/curved stroke splineFix faceted strokes on fast curves: add a midpoint Bézier spline stage before smoothing
author: Marpuriganesh
body: ## Problem Fast circular strokes come out faceted, like a polygon with visible corners instead of a round curve. This happens with smoothing off and with smoothing on (shown here at 10). | Before | After | | :---: | :---: | | || | Faceted curves (Brush, smoothing 10) | Round curves (same brush and settings) | ## Cause The engine only sees the pointer events the platform delivers, roughly one per frame, so a fast circle is only about 10 points per loop. Those points were joined with straight lines and dabs were spaced along that polyline, so every event became a corner. Smoothing doesn't fix this: both modes (exponential and pulled string) move the brush toward each new point in a straight line, which adds corners of its own. ## Change A new `Spline` stage in `crates/paint/src/dynamics.rs` turns the sparse points into a smooth path before smoothing and dab spacing: input -> Spline -> Smoother -> PathWalker -> dabs - Midpoint quadratic Bézier: for consecutive points p0, p1, p2 it draws a curve from mid(p0,p1) to mid(p1,p2) with p1 as the control point. Pieces start where the previous one ended, so there are no gaps or jumps. - The stroke start is passed through unchanged. A straight lead-in runs from the first point to the first midpoint, and a straight run from the last midpoint reaches the last input point exactly. - Every `StrokePoint` field (pressure, tilt, rotation, wheel, time) is interpolated along the curve, so pressure dynamics and time-based behavior (speed spacing, airbrush build-up, smoothing) keep working. - Curve pieces are sampled into chords of about 2 px, capped at 64 per piece. - A stroke of two points stays one straight segment, as before…

title: fix(format): persist the Save As filename in .pcraft manifests (#3312)
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Fixes native .pcraft files retaining the previous document name after Save As.

Fixes #3312.

## Root Cause

The document is serialized before the session updates its name following a successful save.

As a result, the saved manifest contains the original filename even though the session displays the new one.

## Changes

- Create a temporary document snapshot with the destination filename before native serialization.
- Apply the correction to disk-based saves and byte encoding.
- Preserve the original document until the write succeeds.
- Leave unrelated export formats unchanged.

## Tests

Added regression coverage for:
- Native Save As and reopening.
- Consecutive saves under different filenames.
- Saving back to an existing native file.
- Native byte encoding without modifying the source document.

Tests have not yet been executed.

title: fix(format): share identical tiles when loading .pcraft
author: predic8
body:
Fixes #3315.

`.pcraft` saves deduplicate tiles by content hash, but load decoded and charged each reference separately. Large solid documents failed with `LimitExceeded` on reopen, and smaller ones lost tile sharing (huge RAM use).

`Loader` now caches decoded tiles by (hash, pixel format) for the duration of a load. Repeated references reuse one `Arc<Tile>` without refetching, re-decompressing or re-charging `max_total_bytes`.

Test: `identical_tiles_are_loaded_once_and_shared` reloads 1600 references to one tile under an 8 MiB budget and checks they share one `Arc`. `cargo test -p photocraft-format`, clippy and `cargo xtask layers` pass.

title: Group effects follow their children's effects, not just their pixels (#3274)
author: alexanderalber
body:
Fixes #3274.

## Why
A group with an effect (e.g. Drop Shadow) around a layer with its own outside Stroke showed the stroke cut off at the child's pixel bounds on the canvas, and the group's shadow followed the cut shape. The exported PNG looked right.

The group's effect region (`compose::effect_region`, `gpu::bounds::effect_region`) and the empty-tile check (`compose::empty_in`) were computed from `layer_bounds`, which for a group is the union of its children's *pixels*. The children's own effect reach was missing, so everything past it was clipped: on the GPU by the effect passes' clip, on the CPU when rendering tiles away from the pixels (a whole-document render, as in export, happened to cover it).

## Change
- New `photocraft_compose::effect_source_bounds`: `layer_bounds`, except that a (non-artboard, non-shapeless) group's visible children count grown by their own effect margin, recursively.
- Used by `compose::effect_region`, `compose::empty_in` and `gpu::bounds::effect_region`. Other `layer_bounds` callers are unchanged (`composite_bounds` already includes child margins; the gradient/pattern frame `sb` stays on the pixels).

## Tests
- New `group_effects_reach_past_children_effects` (compose): a 6 px outside stroke on a child, a 2 px drop shadow on its group; 1×1 renders check the stroke left of and below the pixels, the shadow below the stroke, and white past it. Fails without the fix.
- New case in `layer_effects_on_groups_clipping_and_fills` (gpu parity): a child with an 8 px stroke in a group with a drop shadow. With only the GPU half of the fix reverted it fails (max diff 41.99/255); with the fix it passes. Run on an RTX 3090, so the GPU path really executed.

title: Color panel: HSB on sRGB values, like Photoshop (#3323)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Closes #3323.

The Color panel converted the foreground to and from hue, saturation and brightness with egui's `ecolor::Hsva`, which works in **linear light**. Photoshop's HSB works on the sRGB-encoded values, and so does PhotoCraft's own Color Picker dialog. As a result, in the panel:
- the colour field's left edge halfway down was drawn as **188** grey, not 128, which is what the issue reports;
- a 50% grey (128) read as about **22%** Brightness on the HSB sliders, where Photoshop shows 50%.

### Changes (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs`)
- `srgb_hsva` and `hsva_srgb` now use the Color Picker's `rgb_to_hsv` and `hsv_to_rgb`, so the panel and the dialog give the same numbers for the same colour.
- A new helper, `hsva_color32`, does the drawing. The colour field, the hue strip, the HSB slider tracks, the swatch and the stored-HSB check all use it instead of `Color32::from(Hsva)` and `Hsva::to_srgb`. `Hsva` is now only a container for the four numbers.

Picking in the field already used the same HSB as the drawing, so what you click and what you see still agree. Both now follow Photoshop's sRGB HSB.

### Testing
- New test `panels::color_tests::color_panel_hsb_is_srgb_like_photoshop`:
  - grey 128 has Brightness 50%;
  - HSB with S 0% and B 50% gives sRGB 0.5, and the field paints it as `Color32::from_gray(128)`;
  - a saturated colour gets the same H, S and B as the Color Picker dialog.
- It fails without the change; the grey's Brightness came out at about 0.22.
- The existing round-trip test `srgb_hsva_roundtrip` still passes.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests`: 1932 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt` are clean.

#3228 (the field's knob jumping at the bottom-right corner) touches the same function. It's a separate fix that someone else has claimed, and this PR doesn't change the knob.

title: Moving a shape keeps its rendering: Artboards to Files matches Photoshop
author: fabianghe
body:
Follow-up to #3218, which fixes the same problem for type. This one is for shape layers.

## What happens
`vector_cmds::translate_vectors` **re-renders a shape layer on every move**. For a shape from a PSD, this replaces Photoshop's anti-aliasing with PhotoCraft's own. The same path runs for:
- File › Export › **Artboards to Files**, which moves each board to the origin;
- the Move tool commit (`move_layers`) and arrow nudges;
- applying a layer comp's position;
- moving artboards;
- copying layers.

**Found with:** a real Steam store asset template (a free PSD from Noblesteed Games). With #3218 applied, every remaining difference between PhotoCraft's "How to use this template" artboard and Photoshop's own composite was inside its two shape layers, a rounded rectangle and an ellipse.

## The fix
- A whole-pixel move now **shifts the rendered pixels**, through one `vector_cmds::shift_shape` helper.
- `layer_multi_cmds::shift_shown` (the Move tool's live preview) already did this. It now calls the same helper, so the preview and the committed move always agree.
- Rules kept from that preview code:
  - The render is cut at the canvas, so a shape reaching past it still renders again. So does a fractional move.
  - The path moves either way, so PSD export writes the new position: `psd_raw` is only reused while it still decodes to the path.
  - `fit_canvas` still re-renders shapes when an artboard move grows the canvas (#2389 / #2623). Its test passes unchanged.

## Measured on the template (with #3218)

title: MCP: command_batch says it is not atomic, and the docs explain recovery
author: KnottyDyes
body:
Agents read the `command_batch` tool description rather than `docs/mcp.md`, and the description only said the batch stops at the first error. An agent can take that for a rollback.

title: Format: reopening a .pcraft shares deduplicated tiles again (#3315)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3315

## Root cause
Saves deduplicate tiles by content hash: a solid fill shares one `Arc<Tile>`, so a white 300000² canvas stores a single tile. The loader did not do the same in reverse. `Loader::surface` (crates/format/src/convert.rs) called `LoadFetch::tile` (crates/format/src/store.rs) once per tile *reference*. Each call decompressed the tile, re-checked its hash, charged `max_total_bytes` again, and copied the bytes into a fresh tile at that coordinate. As a result:
- A solid canvas above about 65536² (8-bit), 46341² (16-bit) or 32768² (32f) saved fine, but reopening it failed with `LimitExceeded("bundle expands beyond 17179869184 bytes")`.
- Smaller canvases reopened but lost the sharing. A solid 30000² 32-bit document grew from about 1 MB to about 14 GB in memory.

## Fix
During a load, `Loader` now keeps the tiles it has already decoded, keyed by sample type and content hash. Each distinct tile is decompressed, hash-checked and charged against the budget once. Every later reference gets the same copy-on-write `Arc<Tile>` through `Surface::put_tiles`, so the reopened document keeps the sharing the save had. An edit splits the tile off as usual (`Arc::make_mut`).

Hostile-input protections are unchanged:
- `max_total_bytes` still bounds the distinct decoded bytes.
- An extra reference costs one map lookup and one `Arc` clone. The number of references is bounded by `max_manifest_bytes`, as before.
- Invalid hashes still fail in `LoadFetch::tile`. The cache only holds tiles that were verified.
- If a cached hash is referenced again with a different tile length, the load fails as corrupt instead of putting a wrong-sized tile into the surface.
- Duplicate-coordinate and coordinate-range checks run before the cache lookup, as before.

## Tests
- `roundtrip::solid_fill_reopens_with_one_shared_tile`: a solid 2048² RGB document at 8, 16 and 32-bit saves and reopens with a budget of one tile. The reopened document equals the original, and all 64 tiles are one …

title: Color panel: HSB over the encoded values, not linear light (#3323)
author: myangaa1
body:
Fixes #3323.

The Color panel's field, hue strip and Hue/Saturation/Brightness sliders used egui's `Hsva`, which is HSV over *linear* RGB. Half-way down the field, and at 50 % brightness, that is linear 0.5 = sRGB 188, a light grey, where Photoshop (and PhotoCraft's own Color Picker dialog) show 128. Grey 128 read back as 21 % brightness in the sliders.

The panel now keeps HSB over the sRGB-encoded components (a small `Hsb` in `panels.rs`, built on the dialog's `rgb_to_hsv` / `hsv_to_rgb`), so the panel and the dialog agree: the midpoint is 128, 50 % is 50 %, and the field and sliders shade evenly. The hex/RGB readout and the remembered hue for greys work as before.

Before / after (Pro theme, foreground red; snapshot example, measured along the field's left edge): the grey ramp was 253 → 144 over the visible field and 208 at its middle; it is now a straight 250 → 0 ramp with 128 at the middle.

Tests: `srgb_hsb_roundtrip` and `color_panel_hsb_is_in_gamma_space` (grey 128 ⇄ B 50 %, (255, 128, 0) ⇄ H 30° S 100 % B 100 %, and the panel equals the dialog). `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests` (1850 passed) pass.

Not changed: `widgets::hue_stops()` (the hue slider tracks shared with Hue/Saturation, Camera Raw and the brush Hue Jitter slider) still mixes in linear light; it only affects the look of those tracks, not any value, so I left it for a separate change if wanted.

## Better Than PS
Photoshop limits live type:
- Edit › Transform › Warp takes only the warp styles (Warp Text).
- Distort, Perspective and the split warps are greyed until the type is rasterized, and then the text can no longer be edited.

title: fix(presets): never overwrite preset or actions files that failed to load
author: tms-h
body:
## Summary

Keep brush preset group files and `actions.json` intact when they fail to load, instead of overwriting them on the next save.

## Problem

When a brush group file can't be loaded, the preset store skips it with a warning. That happens when the file is corrupt, written by a newer version (`version != 1`), or has missing tips. The comment at the skip says the file is "left on disk untouched".

But the next sync writes the group's file name again, with only the presets currently in memory. Saving a single new brush therefore replaces the whole skipped file, and every preset in it is lost. For example, a user who downgrades PhotoCraft loses their ungrouped presets on the next brush save.

`actions.json` has the same behaviour. A file that fails to load (corrupt, too large, or an unsupported version) loads as an empty list, and the next action change rewrites it with only the new actions.

## Root Cause

- `open` drops a group file that fails to parse or has missing tips (`preset_store.rs:617`, `:668`) without remembering it. `sync` then sees no loaded entry for `group_file_name(group)` and calls `write_group` (`:867`).
- `load_actions` (`:695`) returns the same empty list for "unreadable" as for "no file", so `sync_actions` (`:1012`) can't tell them apart.

## Changes

- Record the names of group files skipped at load. `sync` leaves those files unchanged and adds a warning instead of writing them.
- `load_actions` returns `None` when `actions.json` exists but couldn't be loaded. A missing file still means an empty list, as on a first launch. `sync_actions` then leaves the file unchanged and adds a warning.
- Two regression tests on `MemBackend`, one per file type. Each seeds a `version: 2` file, saves a brush or records an action, and checks that the file is byte-for-byte unchanged and a warning was raised.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib preset_store`: all pass. Each new test fails with its fix reverted and passes with it.
- `cargo …

title: Tests: bad-layer-id checks use an id that can't exist (#3343)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3343

## Root cause
Layer ids come from one process-wide counter (`NEXT_ID` in `crates/doc/src/lib.rs`). `LayerId`, `DocId` and `SmartContentsId` all draw from it, and `ensure_ids_above` raises it whenever a test loads a file. A full `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib` runs about 1,200 tests in one process, so the counter passes 9999. Many "no such layer" checks used small sentinels (`"layer": 9999`, `999_999`, `99_999`, `LayerId(9999)`, `"reference": 9999`, `"to": 9999` …). When a layer that the test itself just created gets that id, the command succeeds and the `is_err()` assertion fails. Which test gets the id depends on thread scheduling, so CI fails at random. This is the failure in `type_extra_cmds::tests::vertical_orientation_renders_columns_inside_the_canvas` (tests.rs:112).

I confirmed it locally with a throwaway test (not committed): after `photocraft_doc::ensure_ids_above(9998)`, the next `type.create` gets layer id 9999, and `type.orientation.vertical {"layer": 9999}` then returns `Ok`.

## What changed
This is a test-only change. Every bad-layer-id sentinel in the `photocraft-engine` tests (lib and `tests/`) and the `photocraft-ui-egui` lib tests is now `u64::MAX`, which the counter never reaches. That's 28 files, plus a follow-up commit for the sentinels that landed on main since (extra_cmds, layer_copy_cmds, layer_style, pattern_fill_cmds, smartselect_cmds, type_extra_cmds, vector_cmds, explicit_layer_target). Commands read the id with `as_u64`, so `u64::MAX` still reaches the lookup and fails with `no such layer LayerId(18446744073709551615)`, not with a parameter error. I checked the error text for the affected commands with a throwaway test. The adversarial `panic_hunt` params are unchanged, because they don't assert `Err`. Document indices, job ids and style indices are not drawn from this counter, so they stay as they are.

- `cargo test -j 4 -p…

title: CR2: decode Canon sRAW/mRAW (subsampled lossless JPEG small/medium raw)
author: Elvis33LE
body:
Canon sRAW1/sRAW2/mRAW open now instead of refusing: `09.canon.sraw1.cr2` from raw.pixls.us develops into its 3872×2574 image where it previously fell back to the embedded JPEG preview with "Canon sRAW / mRAW is not supported yet".

**What the files are:** a lossless JPEG whose first component samples at 2×2 (sRAW1/mRAW) or 2×1 (sRAW2) with 1×1 chroma — a subsampled MCU of 4 or 2 luma values plus centred Cb/Cr, decoded through a chain predictor (the luma samples chain through each other, all sharing the luma Huffman table; dcraw's assignment).

**The decode** (`ljpeg::decode_sraw` + the sRAW branch of the CR2 reader, clean-room from the public lossless-JPEG spec and dcraw's published algorithm):
- MCU-interleaved lossless scan with the chaining predictor and per-component restart semantics,
- luma placement per 2×2/2×1 block, Cb/Cr centred at 1<<14 shared per block,
- chroma upsampling the way dcraw does it (odd rows then odd columns average their neighbours, +1 >> 1; the last row/column replicate),
- Canon's fixed YCbCr→RGB matrices per body generation, with the firmware-version hue rule (MakerNote 0x0007 `Firmware Version 2.1.2`, dcraw's `ver > 1.0.0.6` check for the 5D Mark II),
- the per-file `sraw_mul` scale record from the ColourData block (dcraw's walk off the white balance, G == 1170),
- the 16-bit difference category fixed at **−32768** per T.81 H.1.2.2 — our reader had **+32768**, which no CFA file ever hit.

The sensor is 3-sample linear RGB (no CFA), white 16383, and the file's as-shot white balance applies as with the CFA path.

**Verification:** pixel-exact against an instrumented dcraw (public-domain reference) — the first six converted RGB values of the 5D Mark II sRAW1 file match bit for bit: (497,704,190), (496,702,193), (484,683,186), (480,676,187), (488,688,191), (492,694,193). title: CMYK documents keep their exact inks: export, PSD merged image and Flatten (follow-up to #4199)
author: SBaksa
body:
Follow-up to #4199 (#2220).

#4199 made layered CMYK documents export as CMYK TIFF and JPEG with their profile. It gets there by compositing in RGB and converting back through the profile, so, as its notes say, the original inks don't survive. K-only black (C0 M0 Y0 K100) comes back as four-colour black (about C18 M11 Y12 K91), which matters for print (K-only type and line art). The same loss happens in a CMYK PSD's merged image, and in Flatten Image, Merge/Stamp Visible and Copy Merged.

This PR mixes the layers on their ink values instead, wherever the stack allows, so opaque pixels keep their exact inks.

### What changes
- **TIFF/JPEG export** of a CMYK document: #4199's profile handling is unchanged (invalid, non-CMYK or unusable profiles are rejected; untagged documents embed coated CMYK). The pixels then come from the ink composite. TIFF keeps transparency; JPEG is composited over blank paper. RGB-only formats keep #4199's direct sRGB composite.
- **`compose::cmyk`** (new) does the ink mixing:
  - **Content:** pixel, type, shape and smart object layers; solid and gradient fills (through #2628's `render_cmyk_fill`); masks; isolated and pass-through groups; clipping groups; knockouts.
  - **Blend modes:** every separable mode, applied to each ink's brightness as the RGB compositor applies it per channel. That includes #2552's Fill rule for the special eight and Dissolve's noise.
  - **Adjustments:** Invert, Posterize, and Levels/Curves recorded on the CMYK channels.
  - **Layer effects:** shadows, glows, strokes, colour and gradient overlays, satin, and bevel without texture. These run through the existing compositor on two stand-in RGB documents whose channels hold the brightness of C, M and Y, then of K. That is exact because everything allowed there works channel by channel, and a property test checks it: random effect stacks rendered with the inks in different channels must agree.
- **Fallback:** anything else keeps #4199's path, the RGB composite converted…

title: perf: Minimum/Maximum (Preserve: Roundness) up to 4× faster, identical output
author: arhammusheer
body:
Speeds up Minimum and Maximum without changing a bit of their output. With Preserve: Roundness they're 2.8–4.1× faster from radius 5 up; with Preserve: Squareness, 1.1–1.3×. This follows #3224 and is independent of it, branched from `main`.

Method, raw numbers and how to reproduce them: [`docs/min-max-performance.md`](docs/min-max-performance.md).

## Results

Each figure is the median of three alternating before/after pairs against `main` at 01833cfa, on an Apple M2 Pro, with a 6000×4000 RGBA8 layer through `apply_in`. Every output's SHA-256 matches `main`.

| Filter | Preserve | Radius | `main` | This PR | |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Maximum | Roundness | 1 | 199 ms | 161 ms | 1.2× |
| Maximum | Roundness | 5 | 684 ms | **239 ms** | 2.9× |
| Maximum | Roundness | 20 | 3,860 ms | **948 ms** | **4.1×** |
| Maximum | Roundness | 50 | 12,665 ms | **3,834 ms** | 3.3× |
| Maximum | Roundness | 100 | 34,536 ms | **12,168 ms** | 2.8× |
| Minimum | Roundness | 20 | 3,588 ms | **942 ms** | 3.8× |
| Maximum | Squareness | 5 / 50 | 293 / 563 ms | 263 / 420 ms | 1.1× / 1.3× |
| Minimum | Squareness | 50 | 505 ms | 422 ms | 1.2× |

## What changed (`crates/algo/src/other.rs`)

- **Shared rows.** Disc rows with the same half-width need the same horizontal extremes of a source row: both halves of the disc, and the runs near its middle. Each is now computed once per half-width and kept until the last disc row that needs it, instead of once per disc row.
- **Same order.** The rows are combined per pixel in the same order as before (top to bottom, `pick(running, row)`). LLVM leaves unspecified which zero `fmax(+0, −0)` returns, so keeping the order keeps even zero signs identical on every target.
- **Fewer overheads.** The window is read once per channel instead of one `Image::get` per sample per disc row. The running extremes reuse their buffers and walk blocks of `k` instead of testing `i % k`.

title: fix(engine): create new layer masks at the document depth
author: piero-83
body:
New masks created in 16-bit and 32-bit documents currently use 8-bit samples. Saving and reopening the document as PSD changes those masks to the document depth, so an identical later soft brush stroke can produce different mask coverage and composite pixels depending on whether the document was reopened as native or PSD.

Convert newly created pixel masks to the document's sample depth using the existing fallible surface conversion, propagating conversion errors through the command result. This covers adjustment and fill masks, Reveal/Hide All, Reveal Selection, and gradient-fill selections. Selection coverage, sparse defaults, and existing masks are preserved.

Creation tests cover 8/16/32-bit masks in RGB, Grayscale, CMYK, and Lab documents, fractional selection coverage, and Undo/Redo. RGB round-trip tests verify identical later soft mask edits and composite pixels after native and PSD reopening at each depth. Two regressions fail on the unmodified base and pass with this change.

Validation on base `094d0776d14114a3f6989cdc150e30d5c21de1d9`:

title: Clip the checker under rounded colour swatches to their corners (#3208)
author: myangaa1
body: Fixes #3208. The colour swatches (Layer Style's Stroke, Color Overlay and the rest, and every `color_swatch` / `color_swatch_button` in `widgets.rs`) painted a square checkerboard under a rounded fill, so the checker's light cells showed at the four corners: white specks on the dark themes. title: fix(gpu): request CPU fallback for gradient stops closer than a LUT entry (#3053)
author: buivanvu94
body:
Closes #3053.

### Summary

The GPU compositor samples gradient ramps into a 4096-sample lookup table (LUT) and linearly interpolates adjacent entries. When gradient stops are closer than one LUT interval (`1.0 / 4095.0`, ~0.000244), linear interpolation cannot represent the steep transition without introducing significant error (up to 0.5 per RGB channel), exceeding the 1/255 CPU parity tolerance.

Previously, `check_gradient_stops` only caught strictly coincident stops (`w[0] == w[1]`).

This PR:
1. In `crates/gpu/src/plan.rs:check_gradient_stops`, checks whether adjacent stop positions are closer than `1.0 / 4095.0`, requesting fallback to the CPU compositor just like coincident stops.
2. Adds unit regression test `close_distinct_gradient_stops_request_cpu` in `crates/gpu/tests/parity.rs` verifying that close distinct stops (such as 0.4999 and 0.5 from #3053) request the CPU fallback and meet parity contracts.

### Verification
- `cargo test -p photocraft-gpu --test parity close_distinct_gradient_stops_request_cpu` (passed)
- `cargo test -p photocraft-gpu --test parity` (38/38 passed)
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean)
- `cargo xtask layers` (clean)

title: Window: a window saved while minimized reopens at the minimum size, not 160 × 64
author: KattKnight
body:
On Windows, PhotoCraft can reopen as a 160 × 64 strip on every launch.

**Cause.** eframe saves the window's size on exit. If the window is minimized at that moment, Windows
reports a 160-pt-wide window with almost no height, and eframe's own clamp only raises it to 64 pt.
On the next start eframe restores that size, and `with_min_inner_size(760 × 480)` isn't applied to a
restored window, so the window stays 160 × 64. It stays that way, because each exit saves the small
size again. Found while driving the app over the control channel: `ui.screenshot` and `ui.inspect`
both reported a 160 × 64 window, and `ui.ron` held `inner_size_points: (160, 64)`.

**Fix.** A `window_builder` hook (`at_least_min_size` in `apps/photocraft/src/main.rs`) grows a
restored window that is smaller than the minimum size up to it, keeping its centre. A window at or
above the minimum, or a maximized one, is unchanged. The rest of `ui.ron` (panel layout) is kept,
unlike `ui_state::sanitize`, which removes files that would crash startup.

**Tests.**
- New `a_window_saved_while_minimized_reopens_at_the_minimum_size`: the saved 160 × 64 window opens
  at 760 × 480 and stays centred, a too-narrow window only grows wider, and normal sizes are unchanged.
- Live, with the broken `ui.ron`: before, 160 × 64 for the whole run; after, 760 × 480. Without a
  saved layout, 1440 × 900 as before.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test -p photocraft`, rustfmt: clean.

title: Copy takes every selected layer, Paste recreates them (#2478)
author: DomiLuebben
body:
Fixes #2478.

## Problem
With several layers selected and no pixel selection, Edit › Copy only copied the active layer's pixels, so Paste made one layer. Photoshop copies all selected layers and pastes them back as layers.

## Fix
`copy` in `crates/engine/src/edit_cmds.rs` now puts the selected layers on the session clipboard as whole layers: those that no selected group already carries (`layer_multi_cmds::top_level`), bottom-to-top, in a scratch document. `paste_layers` already recreates a list of layers (it loops over `copies.layers`), so Paste needed no change. The OS clipboard still gets the merged pixels, as for a group.

- A pixel selection keeps the old behaviour: the active layer's selected pixels, as one layer.
- A single selected layer behaves as before (`takes_whole` is untouched).
- The Background in the set pastes as an ordinary, unlocked layer, like Duplicate Layer makes it.
- `Copy` is enabled whenever several layers are selected, even if the active one is a group.

## Tests
`edit_cmds::tests::copy_and_paste_several_selected_layers` (both layers' bounds, order, one undo step, pixel selection still copies one layer) and `copying_the_background_with_another_layer_pastes_an_ordinary_layer`. Both fail without the change. `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib` passes (1234 tests) and `cargo fmt --all --check` is clean. `cargo clippy -D warnings` on Rust 1.95 reports one `collapsible_match` in `color_to_alpha_cmds.rs`, which is on `main` already and not touched here.

Not covered: layers selected in different groups paste flat above the active layer, not back into their groups.

title: Content-Aware tools: faster, cancellable at once, same pixels (P21, P22, P49)
author: Unemars
body:
**TL;DR:** the Content-Aware tools from #2202 (Fill, Spot Healing, Patch, Content-Aware Move) get their time back without changing a pixel, and a cancelled 24 MP fill stops within tens of milliseconds. The P49 row, which #2575's nightly found over its 200 ms budget, fits again. It is also faster than main with #2805, which sped up the same onion peel and votes meanwhile.

**Problem.** #2202 made the fill match Photoshop's, and the new perf nightly (#2575) caught what it cost on a Ryzen 5 3600X:

| Scenario | Before → after #2202 (p50) | Budget |
|---|---|---|
| P21 Content-Aware Fill 10 MP | 105 → 537 ms (5.1×) | 1500 ms |
| P22 Spot Healing 10 MP | 54 → 130 ms (2.4×) | 500 ms |
| P49 Cancel Content-Aware Fill 24 MP (max) | 136 → 566 ms (4×) | **200 ms** |

**Why it was slow:**
- **Cancel (P49).** Long stretches of the 24 MP job never looked at the cancel flag: Auto sampling's min cut (~300 ms), the window copy and mosaic, the pyramid, the onion-peel initialisation and the colour-adaptation votes. Freeing full-size buffers (match field, costs, a 560 MB gain/bias buffer, two or three 280 MB window copies) added to the wait too, at about 80 µs per MB.
- **P21 / P22.** Colour adaptation (on by default since #2202) had no early out, the onion peel searched every source exhaustively, and PatchMatch kept only 2–7 threads busy on the small pyramid levels.

**Change.** Same algorithm, same floating-point order, so every result stays bit for bit what it is on main:
- **Solver bounds.** The solver works over the hole's bounds grown by a patch: match field, costs, votes and the per-target tables are kept only there, since nothing outside changes or is matched.
- **Votes.** A vote computes each target's weight and match centre once and writes into one buffer instead of a `Vec` per pixel. It walks only the offsets inside the image, with the channel count and colour adaptation fixed at compile time. The sums and their order are unchanged.
- **Colour adaptation.** It reuses each p…

title: Linux: say so when no file dialog can open (#3354); read ldconfig on non-English systems
author: DomiLuebben
body:
Refs #3354 (does not fix the reporter's environment, but makes the failure visible).

## 1. No file dialog: tell the user instead of doing nothing
`rfd` opens the XDG file chooser portal through `libdbus-1` (loaded at run time) and falls back to `zenity`. When neither works, for example in a minimal labwc/Void session without a portal backend, it only logs the failure and answers "nothing picked". The app took that for Cancel, so File › Open / Save / Export did nothing and said nothing.

- `apps/photocraft/src/file_dialog_probe.rs` looks once, on a background thread at start-up, for the three pieces: `libdbus-1.so.3` in the linker cache, the portal's `FileChooser` interface on the session bus (a `version` property read, 5 s timeout), and `zenity` on `PATH`.
- When a dialog comes back empty and none of them is there, the shell answers with the new `FileDialogAnswer::Unavailable(message)`. `ask_file` turns that into an error, so the status bar says what to install (xdg-desktop-portal with a backend, libdbus, or zenity) and suggests dropping or pasting a file meanwhile.
- The probe only explains an empty answer; it never blocks a dialog. Anything it can't tell counts as present, so a system where dialogs work never sees the message. Linux only; other platforms compile an empty `start()`.

## 2. `ldconfig -p` was unreadable on non-English systems
`linux_libs::read_ldconfig` accepted the listing only if its first line contained "libs found in cache". On a German system the header is "5522 Bibliotheken im Cache … gefunden", so the cache counted as unreadable and the start-up library check silently fell back to a directory search. `ldconfig` now runs with `LC_ALL=C`, and any listing that starts with a count is accepted. The probe above reads the same cache.

## Tests
- `file_dialog_probe`: no message when a portal, zenity or an unknown answer is present; messages for a missing portal and for missing libdbus; `PATH` lookup.
- `file_dialog::tests::an_unavailable_dialog_is_re…

title: feat(ui): Motion Blur and other filter angles get the angle dial (#3152)
author: Kartik8Dwivedi
body:
## Summary
Motion Blur's Angle is now a dial you can click or drag, with a degree field next to it, as in Photoshop. Drop Shadow already had this dial; it is now a shared widget, and the filter dialog uses it for the other direction angles too.

## Root cause
`filter_dialog::body` drew every numeric range param with `widgets::slider_row`, so the angle was a straight slider. The only dial was private to `layer_style.rs` and fixed to -180..180.

## What changed
- New `widgets::angle_dial_row(ui, label, &mut angle, range)` in `widgets/angle_dial.rs`, moved out of `layer_style::angle_row`:
  - The dial points within -180..180, and its result is clamped to the param's range. The field accepts the whole range, so Motion Blur keeps a 270° value.
  - The field is the dialogs' `value_field`, so Angle gets the opening focus with its text selected (#1757), plus Tab order and arrow steps.
  - Arrow keys on the focused dial wrap round only when the range is the dial's own -180..180 (Drop Shadow). On a wider range they step on, so 270° goes to 271°, not -89°.
  - Clamping uses `max`/`min`, not `f32::clamp`, so a malformed (reversed) range cannot panic.
- Layer Style (Drop Shadow and the other effects) uses the shared widget with -180..180.
- The filter dialog uses the dial for direction angles measured counter-clockwise from three o'clock, the dial's convention (checked against each algorithm): Motion Blur, Emboss, Oil Paint, Lighting Effects, Relight and Global Light.
- These keep the slider:
  - Twirl, Rotate Arbitrary, Crop, Lens Correction and the Blur Gallery filters, whose angle is an amount of rotation;
  - Flame, whose 0° points up.

## Tests
- `dialogs::tests::motion_blur_angle_dial_sets_the_angle_by_click_and_drag` (kittest, real dialog) checks:

title: Make magnetic lasso edge direction polarity-independent
