title: Actions: replay tests for crop, filters, selections and styled text on a second document (#3410)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #3410 (scorecard AUTO-219-4, part of #219)

## What was missing
Action replay was only tested for new layer + rect select + fill and for an explicit transform. Nothing checked that a recorded crop, filter, selection sequence or styled type layer replays on a second document with the same result.

## Change
Tests only, in a new file `crates/engine/tests/action_replay.rs` (`actions_cmds.rs` is untouched, since several open PRs change it). Each case builds three identical documents: a gradient background plus a layer with two rectangles. It records on A, plays on B and runs the same commands directly on C. Each test then checks:
- B == C and A == C: canvas size, every layer compared in full (pixels, style, type content and its rendered cache) and the selection mask. Layer ids are left out because they are counted across the whole session.
- `failed` is absent, `ran` equals the number of steps, and history grows by one step per played step.
- The result differs from the untouched document, so a test can't pass without doing anything.

Cases, each at 8/16/32-bit:
- `replayed_crop_matches_direct_crop_at_each_depth`: `image.crop`
- `replayed_gaussian_blur_matches_direct_blur_at_each_depth`: `filter.blur.gaussianBlur` radius 3.5
- `replayed_selection_operations_and_fill_match_direct_at_each_depth`: elliptical `select.rect`, add, subtract, `select.modify.feather`, `select.inverse`, `edit.fill`
- `replayed_styled_type_layer_matches_direct_at_each_depth`: `type.create` with font, size, colour, tracking, underline and name

Scorecard: AUTO-219-4 is now `done` (`scorecard/automation.toml`, regenerated `docs/scorecard.md`). Also removed from docs/gaps.md G11, with a revision-history row.

title: Properties: a new adjustment or fill layer shows its settings, not its mask (#3369)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #3369.

**Why:** In Photoshop, a new adjustment or fill layer targets its layer mask, so painting edits the mask right away. The Properties panel still shows the layer's own settings, such as the Curves graph. It switches to the mask controls only when you click the mask thumbnail. PhotoCraft targeted the mask correctly (#2166), but Properties then showed Density/Feather, so you had to click the layer before you could edit the adjustment you had just made.

**Change**
- New UI state `properties_layer` (serde, readable over the control channel): the adjustment or fill layer whose settings Properties shows even though its mask is targeted.
- It is set when `layer.newAdjustmentLayer.*` / `layer.newFillLayer.*` succeeds. The mask stays targeted, so painting, Invert and Delete still act on the mask.
- It is cleared when you click the mask thumbnail, target the pixels, select another layer or set `ui.set {maskTarget}`. Properties then shows the mask controls again.
- The single check sits in `mask_props_ui::targeted()`, which both Properties views use: docked (Pro) and floating (Studio).

**Tests**
- New kittest test `a_new_adjustment_or_fill_layer_shows_its_settings_until_the_mask_thumbnail_is_clicked` (Curves and Solid Color), with real clicks:
  - after creation, the mask is targeted and Properties shows the settings;
  - a row click keeps the settings view;
  - clicking the mask thumbnail shows Density.
  - It fails without the fix.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib`: 1920 passed. One type-tool test (`options_font_family_preserves_peer_faces_and_batches_layer_flags`) failed once while the machine was under load; it passed on reruns and passes on main.

**Not verified**
- Not checked visually in the running app.
- The Studio floating Properties is covered only through the shared `targeted()` path.

title: ci: refactor workflows to use storytold/craft-common-actions
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Summary
Refactors repetitive CI/CD workflows across PhotoCraft to call centralized reusable workflows and composite actions hosted in the organization repository [`storytold/craft-common-actions`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions).

### Design Decisions
- **Hosted in Organization Repository**: Workflows live under `storytold/craft-common-actions` (no personal fork/repository).
- **Intentionally Tracks `@main` (Not SHA Pinned)**: Callers deliberately track `@main` with an inline explanation comment so that org-wide CI improvements, security fixes, and build optimizations propagate across all 13+ craftapps automatically without requiring individual PR churn in every repository.
- **Explicit Secrets**: Only the exact required signing secrets are passed explicitly (`secrets: inherit` is avoided).
- **Node 24 Runtimes**: All composite and third-party actions inside `storytold/craft-common-actions` are updated to Node 24 (and pinned internally to immutable commit SHAs), eliminating Node 20 deprecation warnings.
- **Strict Verification**: Build utilities like `nfpm`, `actionlint`, and `trunk` are verified against SHA256 checksums.
- Preserves 100% of existing packaging, release matrix, and linting semantics for PhotoCraft.

title: Fix Color Balance tonal ranges and slider axes
author: imSlicedBread
body:
Fixes #3423.

Color Balance sliders represent the Cyan–Red, Magenta–Green, and Yellow–Blue axes. The CPU and GPU paths treated them as independent RGB offsets, and the tonal masks used encoded-value Rec.601 luma. This made an sRGB gray value of 128 fall outside the Shadows range.

Use document-decoded linear Rec.709 luminance for the tonal masks, map each slider to its RGB opponent axis, and keep the CPU and GPU implementations aligned. A regression test covers the reported Shadow adjustment on neutral gray with Preserve Luminosity both enabled and disabled.

I reproduced the reported adjustment in Photopea on neutral 8-bit sRGB gray; PhotoCraft’s previous shadow mask left the pixel unchanged.

Checks:
- cargo test -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu
- cargo clippy -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings
- cargo fmt -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu -- --check
- cargo xtask layers
- cargo xtask wasm

title: File > Save As / Save a Copy / CLI can write PDF (#3401)
author: vbasky
body:
Closes #3401 (the Save As side; PDF read stays tracked by #2541).

## What changed
- **The PDF writer moved below the seam.** The print path's one-page writer (Flate image XObject, ICCBased profile, marks, text) was engine-local and unreachable from the export dispatch, so it now lives in `crates/io/src/pdf.rs` (L4). `print_cmds` re-exports the same names — behaviour is byte-identical, and the whole print suite still passes unchanged.
- **New `pdf::export`**: the document flattened to one page — RGB, Grayscale or CMYK at 8 bits, composited over paper white (zero ink for CMYK), the embedded ICC profile travelling as an ICCBased colour space, page size = pixels × 72 ÷ document resolution (so a 300 ppi 3000×2000 doc prints as 10×6.67 in). Anything the format can't hold is a warning, not a silent loss.
- **One dispatch point**: because Save As, Save a Copy, `file.export`, Export As and the CLI's convert/batch all route through `photocraft_io::export` by extension, a `.pdf` name now just works everywhere: desktop, control channel, MCP, actions and `photocraft-cli`. PDF joined the Save As filter list after PSD (second, as Photoshop's own dialog ranks it).

## Refusal paths (Rule 9)
Lab/Indexed/other modes → `convert … to RGB first (Image > Mode)`; zero-sized documents → an actionable error; bad `ExportOptions` are ignored, not panicked on. `panic_hunt` untouched (no new command ids; the dispatch change is additive).

## Tests
Six new io tests: a structural oracle (startxref → the xref table; every recorded offset really precedes its `n 0 obj`), inflate-and-compare pixel content (white paper, a 50% red-over-white blend, per-mode channel counts), dpi → MediaBox maths, ICC bytes round-tripping through the profile object, and refusal of other modes through both `pdf::export` and the general dispatch.

`cargo test -p photocraft-io` (134) · engine lib (1244) · ui-egui lib (1926) · app crate · clippy `-D warnings` · fmt · `xtask layers` · `xtask wasm` — all green.

title: PSD gradients: read the interpolation method Photoshop writes; add Smooth
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## What's wrong

Gradient fills and gradient effects read their interpolation method from `gs99`, a key Photoshop doesn't write. Photoshop 27.11 stores it as the enum **`gradientsInterpolationMethod`** (`Perc`, `Lnr `, `Smoo`, `Gcls`), so **every Perceptual, Linear or Smooth gradient opened as Classic**. No file in the corpus contains `gs99`, while 14 files contain `gradientsInterpolationMethod`.

It shows once a gradient fill is re-rendered (any edit). Measured on gradient fill layers saved by scripted Photoshop 27.11, against Photoshop's own composite in each file, after changing the fill's angle:

| Method | `main` (max error) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Classic | 1 | 1 |
| Perceptual | 31 | 1 |
| Linear | 74 | 1 |
| Smooth | 30 | 2 (two stops) |

Smooth, Photoshop's default method since 2024 (also Gradient Map's default), had no model at all.

## What Photoshop does (measured)

Scripted on Photoshop 27.11: two-stop gradients on three colour pairs, sampled every 4–8 px, plus three- and four-stop gradients.
- **Perceptual, Linear, Classic:** the existing `gradient_bake` model is right once the method is read.
- **Smooth:** runs straight across each segment in Oklab with its own easing. The curve is the same for every colour pair, and Smoothness doesn't change it. It fits no simple formula, so it's kept as a measured 17-point table (`SMOOTH_EASE`).
- Midpoints: Photoshop applies `Clrs[i].Mdpn` to the segment **ending** at stop `i`. PhotoCraft already reads them that way.

- `io::blocks::gradient_method`: reads `gradientsInterpolationMethod`, with `gs99` kept as a fallback; used by gradient fills and gradient effects.

title: Color Balance: Photoshop's per-channel levels and gamma curves
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## What's wrong

Color Balance added a share of each slider, weighted by the pixel's lightness, and then (with Preserve Luminosity) rescaled to the old luma. That isn't what Photoshop does. On the corpus's Photoshop-made file `photoshop/adjustments/rgb8/color-balance.psd` (all three tones moved, Preserve Luminosity on), `main` is up to **43 levels off on 99% of the pixels**.

## What Photoshop does (measured)

Scripted on Photoshop 27.11: a gray ramp and 16 pure colours through each slider at ±25, ±50 and ±100, with Preserve Luminosity on and off, plus two and three tones and two sliders at once (86 cases). Every slider is a **levels-and-gamma curve on each channel**:

- **Preserve Luminosity off:** a slider moves only its own channel. Midtones is gamma 2^−a. Shadows is gamma 2^(−a/2), after a black point at 0.39·|a| when lowered. Highlights is gamma 2^(−a/2), after a white point at 1 − 0.39·a when raised.
- **Preserve Luminosity on:** midtones is gamma 2^(−a/2) on the slider's channel and 2^(a/2) on the other two. Shadows and highlights go by the *differences* between a tone's sliders: each channel gets a black point at 0.39·(max − own) for shadows and a white point at 1 − 0.39·(own − min) for highlights.
- **Order:** highlights, then shadows, then midtones.

(`a` = slider / 100. Shadows −100 maps 99.6 of 255 to black, and highlights +100 maps 155.5 to white, hence 0.39.)

## Results

| | measured cases within 1 level | worst | corpus file: worst / mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 0 / 86 | 128 | 43 / 20.9 |
| #3434 | 0 / 86 | 150 | 54 / 24.6 |
| **this PR** | **85 / 86** | 9 | **4 / 1.4** |

#3434 (opened today) fixes the same issue a different way: linear-light tonal masks, checked against Photopea. I ran its branch through the same Photoshop measurements so the two can be compared directly. The one case here off by more than 1 is midtones +100 below about 28 of 255, where Photoshop flattens the steepest gamma near black (up to 9 levels).

title: Warp presets: Photoshop's Bezier control grids instead of approximations
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## What's wrong

The 15 warp presets (Edit › Transform › Warp, smart object warps, **Warp Text**) were closed-form approximations of each style's look, and up to **70 px off** Photoshop's. For example:
- **Arc** kept its centre fixed and pulled the ends in. Photoshop keeps the inner edge's corners and raises the middle.
- **Flag** waved the opposite way, at about a third of the height.
- **Squeeze** shrank the height. Photoshop pinches the sides in.

## What Photoshop does (measured)

Scripted renders on Photoshop 27.11 of a grid image whose colours encode each pixel's own position, 102 cases: every preset at bend ±50 and ±100, both distortions, vertical orientation, and square, wide (256×96) and tall (96×256) boxes. **Every preset is a single bicubic Bezier patch** (least-squares fits land within 0.5 px), with this control grid:
- **Arc:** each row is a circular arc of b·π around one centre, and the inner edge keeps its chord. **Arch, Bulge, Arc Lower/Upper and Shell** are built from the same arcs. The arcs stay circular in pixels on any box.
- **Flag, Wave, Fish, Rise, Fisheye, Inflate, Squeeze, Twist:** control points move linearly with the bend, in box units.
- **Distortion:** vertical scales the top and bottom rows about their midpoints and blends the rows between; horizontal scales each column. **Vertical orientation** swaps the axes and the two distortions.

## Results
- All 102 cases land within **1 px (median)** of Photoshop's pixels (95th percentile ≤ 2 px).
- Corpus, Photoshop-made warped text (ink bounds; the fonts differ here, so bounds are the comparison):

title: feat(vector): shape-tool modes, paints and live controls
author: Skyfuller1303
body:
Shape controls previously mostly configured the next shape, coupled paint to foreground/background colors, and left geometry overlays behind while moving a layer. This change edits the active shape, keeps fill and stroke independent, and provides automatic shape transform controls with vector previews.

Refs #2496, #1053, #1520, #1521, #1175, #2400, #2512, #2537, #2567.

## Scope

- Shape / Path / Pixels modes for Rectangle, Ellipse, Triangle, Polygon, Line and Custom Shape; Work Path conversion to selection/mask/shape; raster blend, opacity and anti-alias controls.
- Independent Solid / Gradient / Pattern / No Color fill and stroke pickers, alpha-aware local Color Picker, gradient stops/presets, pattern swatches, stroke settings and active-layer editing. Native/PSD mapping preserves the new paint parameters within the supported mapping.
- Click-to-create sizing, linked W/H, centered/constrained drawing, per-corner Rectangle radii and canvas handles, rounded polygons/triangles, stars, line arrowheads and custom-shape presets.
- Boolean operations, component alignment/distribution/arrangement and pixel-grid alignment. Building on upstream [#2906](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/2906), selected-layer combination preserves compound operands, EvenOdd holes and empty intersections. Non-Shape layers in a mixed selection remain untouched.

title: Crop tool: switching to another tool commits the pending crop (#3368)

body:
Fixes #3368.

**Why.** With an edited Crop frame, picking another tool (from the toolbar or by its key) left the crop pending and never applied it. In Photoshop, switching to another tool commits the crop silently. An untouched default frame is just dropped.

**Change.**
- `crop_ui::frame()` is the per-frame crop sync that every tool switch passes through (toolbar, shortcut keys, tool presets, control channel). It now commits an edited frame through the existing `canvas::commit_crop`, the same path as ↵, once the current tool is no longer Crop.

- `crop_ui`: a turned frame in the default mode crops turned and leaves the view upright.
- `crop_ui`: an untouched default frame (whole canvas or selection) crops nothing.
- `crop_ui`: the stylus eraser flip and a gesture in progress keep the frame pending.

title: Automation: --font-dir and type.registerFonts for headless sessions (#3393)
author: funkvay-star
body:
Fixes #3393

Headless sessions could only use bundled and installed fonts. This adds two ways to load fonts from a file or folder:

- `--font-dir <dir|file>` (repeatable) on `convert`, `info`, `run`, `batch`, `serve` and `mcp`: trusted launch configuration, loaded before anything opens so PSD font matching sees it.
- `type.registerFonts {path}` → `{families, files, skipped}`. Over `serve` and headless MCP the path resolves under `--automation-read-root`.

Fonts go into the process-wide text engine, so `type.fonts`, type layers and PSD import in every session of the process see them.

### What changed
- **text**: `FontDb::register_font_path` (file, or folder 8 levels deep) and `register_font_files` (bytes already read). Limits: 256 MiB per file, 4096 files, 1 GiB total, checked before reading. Bad files are skipped and reported; registering the same file twice adds no faces; WOFF/WOFF2 get a clear error.
- **engine**: `font_cmds.rs` with `type.registerFonts`. No menu, no history step, not recorded in Actions (`journal: false`, like `type.fonts`).
- **automation**: `AuthorizedWorkspace::read_font_files` walks the read root through cap-std (links can't escape) with a running byte total. Errors name the client's path, never the host root. Still refused inside `actions.play` steps and on the desktop control channel.
- **cli**: `--font-dir` on six subcommands. Missing paths or font-less folders exit 1; skipped files are `warning:` lines on stderr, so stdout stays clean; refused with `mcp --bridge`.
- **testkit**: `fonts::renamed_font(family)` renames the bundled Inter at test time, so no font files are committed.
- **docs**: CLI help, book CLI and MCP pages, `docs/mcp.md`, `docs/control-protocol.md`, `docs/development.md` (including `PHOTOCRAFT_NO_SYSTEM_FONTS=1` with `--font-dir` for machine-independent output).

A note up front: @itrycodinganditsbad offered to take #3439 while I was running the last checks on this one (I'd started before their comment). Fixes #3439. Holding `~` (the backtick key) with the Brush or Pencil makes the strokes started while it is held erase, as in Photoshop. Releasing the key paints again, and the tool never changes.

A command whose params document `"layer":id` acts on that layer, but its availability check (`enabled`) looked at the **active** layer. So with any other layer selected, a call that names a valid layer is refused:

```
photocraft-cli run Template.psd --cmd layer.smartObjects.replaceContents \
  --params '{"layer":94,"path":"newbg.png"}'
error: command `layer.smartObjects.replaceContents` is not available right now:
       the active layer is a Group layer, not a smart object
```

Layer 94 is a smart object; the selected layer is an artboard group. Rasterize, Export Contents, Merge Down and the other commands that take `"layer"` behave the same way. title: Profile prompts on open: one file at a time, before it opens, and the answer goes to that file
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
## Problem

With Edit › Color Settings › Profile Mismatches: Ask When Opening on (PhotoCraft's default), opening several files at once whose embedded profile doesn't match the working space (three macOS screenshots, tagged "Display") went wrong:

- every file opened at once, and every Embedded Profile Mismatch prompt went up at once, stacked in the same place;
- each answer went to the **active** document (`color.profileMismatch` acts on `s.active()`), not to the file its prompt was for: "Discard" three times discarded only the last file's profile;
- no prompt said which file it was about.

## Photoshop

Checked in Photoshop 27.11 with Ask When Opening on, opening the same three files together:

- one prompt at a time, before that file opens: 'The document "Screenshot 2026-10-10 at 10…" has an embedded color profile that does not match the current RGB working space.', then Embedded and Working;
- the file's tab appears only after OK, then the next file's prompt comes up;
- Cancel cancels all the opens: that file and the ones still to come.

## Fix

A file that asks is held back until its prompt is answered, and the answer is applied to that file before it opens.

- **Engine.**
  - `ColorState::open_question(&doc)` says, without changing anything, whether opening asks: Ask When Opening is on and the profile is mismatched or missing. It returns what the prompt shows.
  - `ColorState::resolve_open(&mut doc, action)` applies the answer: preserve, convert, discard or assignWorking.
  - The background open job (`Session::start_open`) parks such a document instead of adding it. The job then returns `{held, name, warnings, color}`, and the shell takes the document with `Session::take_held_open`.
- **Shell: new `open_prompt` module.**
  - Files decoded inline or in the background join a queue. Only the first one's prompt is shown, and it names its file.
  - OK applies the answer, opens the file, then moves on to the next.
  - Cancel drops the file and everything still queued…

title: Brush: remember the last selected brush across restarts (split from #2516)
author: siraxe
body:
# Brush: remember the last selected brush across restarts (split from #2516)

**Split from #2516**, like the brush-outline PR: the persistence half is independent of the
outline, so it lands and is maintained on its own. Based directly on `main`.

## What

- The brush the tool was last using — settings, tip/pattern references and the name of the preset
  it was picked from — is saved to `Preferences::lastBrush` and restored at launch: options bar,
  painting cursor and Brushes panel highlight start where the session left off.
- Saved once the pointer is up (`last_brush::persist` in the frame loop, like the Brush Preset
  picker's view), restored by `last_brush::restore` from `prefs_ui::load`. Stored tips load with
  the preset store; a malformed remembered brush keeps the default.
- Bitmaps never enter the preferences document: remembered tips/patterns are references (a loaded
  stored tile drops its full bitmap) and a sampled bitmap too big to embed is skipped, so the
  previous value stands rather than the prefs file growing by megabytes.

## Review fix from #2516 — change-driven, no per-frame work

`remember_brush` no longer clones the brush and serialises it to JSON every frame to compare with
the stored value. `ToolState::brush_rev` is bumped by every setter of the brush or the picked
preset (`tools.setBrush`, preset save/delete/rename/setCurrent/deleteGroup,
`brush.defineFromSelection`, `brush.presets.importAbr`, the store's tip re-linking, and the shell's
tool-switch/reset paths); `remember_brush` serialises only when the revision moved since
`brush_saved_rev`. An unchanged brush costs one counter compare per frame. A restore counts as
saved, so the launch value is never rewritten.

5 new engine tests (revision gating — an unchanged brush never serialises, rejected changes don't
move the revision, picked-preset tracking, restore round trip, no embedded bitmaps).

title: Linux: StartupWMClass is the window's app id
author: atoslins
body:
`packaging/linux/ai.storyteller.photocraft.desktop` says `StartupWMClass=photocraft`, but the window carries the app id `ai.storyteller.photocraft` (`APP_ID`, through `with_app_id`), natively on Wayland and under XWayland alike. The key is meant to name the class the window maps with ([Desktop Entry spec](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/desktop-entry-spec/latest/recognized-keys.html)), so anything that matches a window to its launcher by it never matches PhotoCraft. The entry predates `with_app_id` by a day, which is likely how they drifted apart.

VectorCraft, GridCraft and WordCraft already use the app id. This PR does the same, and adds a test that reads the entry and compares its `StartupWMClass` with `APP_ID`.

`StartupNotify=false` (#2089/#2097) stays as it is: GNOME on Wayland ends startup notification through an xdg-activation token, not the class. With the right class, X11 window managers could end it again (mutter matches the class in `find_startup_sequence_by_wmclass`), but turning it back on is a separate decision.

**Checked**
- Window class with PhotoCraft 0.7.0 on Hyprland 0.56.2: `ai.storyteller.photocraft` both on Wayland and with `WAYLAND_DISPLAY= photocraft` (XWayland).
- The new test fails on `main` and passes with the change.
- `cargo test -p photocraft --bin photocraft`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`.

Also adds my entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

title: perf: Edit > Clear works tile by tile on large selections (#3463)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #3463

Clear went through `try_clear_surface` (or `try_fill_surface` with the background colour on a Background layer). Both read the whole selection bounds into one f32 buffer (768 MB for 8000x6000 RGBA), looked up the selection's tile map once per pixel, and wrote every tile in the bounds back. All of it ran on one thread. Tiles the selection didn't touch were still copied, so they stopped being shared with the undo state.

Both functions now go through a small `edit_tiles` helper that works on the encoded tiles in parallel:

- a tile that is fully selected and fully cleared is dropped, since it would only hold empty pixels and the old code pruned it afterwards anyway
- a fully selected tile under an opaque fill that may set alpha becomes one shared solid tile
- everything else is edited pixel by pixel with the same decode, math and encode as before, and a tile is copied only when one of its pixels actually changes

The per-pixel math hasn't changed, so the results match the old pass exactly, including soft and feathered selections, locked transparency and transparent pixels that still carry a colour. `float_cmds` and `warp_cmds` call the same two functions, so they get the speedup too.

Timings for Edit > Clear on an 8000x6000 8-bit document, release build, 24 threads, using `benchmark_clear_large_selection` (ignored test in `pixels_tests.rs`):

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| layer, rect selection 10 px in from the edges | 1.95-2.08 s | 18-25 ms |
| layer, feathered ellipse (200 px) | 1.81 s | 37-51 ms |
| Background, rect selection | 2.91-2.98 s | 90-113 ms |
| Background, feathered ellipse (200 px) | 2.99 s | 85-101 ms |

Tests:
- `tiled_clear_and_fill_match_one_pass_over_the_area` checks clear and fill against a copy of the old whole-region pass. It covers RGB/CMYK/Lab/Gray at 8/16/32 bits, with and without alpha, no selection and a soft selection, opaque and translucent colours, and locked and unlocked transparency. Pixels have to be bit-iden…

title: Format: check pattern sizes on load (#3478)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3478

## Root cause
The `.pcraft` loader (`crates/format/src/convert.rs`) copied each pattern's `width`/`height` from the manifest without checking them. Pixels come from tiles, so a pattern with no tiles can claim 65535 × 65535 px in a file of about 1 KB. Painting it went through `compose::pattern::pattern_rgba`, which allocates `width × height × 16` bytes. That's an allocation failure, which aborts the process. `PreparedPatterns::get` also built an unbudgeted tile whenever the budget refused one. In `engine/src/pattern_cmds.rs`, `brush_texture` and `average_color` computed `(width * height) as usize` in `u32`, which overflows.

## Fix
- **format**: on load, reject a pattern that's 0 px on a side (`Corrupt`) or larger than 30 000 px on a side (`LimitExceeded`). 30 000 is the PSD reader's `MAX_EDGE`; Define Pattern stops at 4000.
- **doc**: add `Pattern::pixel_count()` (u64), `Pattern::is_paintable()` and `pattern::MAX_PAINT_PIXELS` (2^26 px, which keeps the f32 RGBA working copy at 1 GiB or less).
- **compose / gpu**: a pattern too large to paint now paints nothing, the same way a missing pattern does. This covers `Tile::new_in`, `pattern_rgba`, `PreparedPatterns::get` and the three pattern lookups in the GPU plan. Nothing gets allocated for it.
- **engine**: `brush.texturePattern` refuses such a pattern with an error. `average_color` uses overflow-free math over a bounded corner. The Fill, Paint Bucket and Pattern Stamp errors now say "empty or too large to paint".

## Tests
Each test fails without the fix:
- `format/tests/corruption.rs::pattern_sizes_from_the_file_are_checked`: 65535² gives `LimitExceeded` and 0 × 24 gives `Corrupt`; the sample still loads. Without the fix, the file loads.
- `compose pattern::tests::patterns_too_large_to_paint_are_skipped_without_allocating`: a 9000 × 8000 pattern with no tiles is skipped. Without the fix, it allocates 1.1 GB and returns a tile.
- `engine pattern_cmds::tests::a_pattern_too_large_to_paint_is_refused_not_all…

title: Save: show save progress as Saving NN% in the status bar and tab title (#3389)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #3389.

## Why
Background saves (Ctrl+S, #2072) reported progress 0 the whole time: `photocraft_io::export` encoded the file in one call and the bytes were written in one call, so the status bar showed only an indeterminate bar and never a percentage. Photoshop shows "Saving NN%" in the status bar and appends " - Saving NN%" to the document tab while it saves.

## Change
- `photocraft_io::export_with(doc, name, opts, &Interrupt)` reports encoding progress and can be cancelled (`export` is unchanged and writes identical bytes): PSD/PSB per layer record and per composite band; layered TIFF likewise plus its encoder stages; .pcraft after its previews; flat formats once the composite is rendered.
- `photocraft_format::atomic_write_progress` writes in 8 MiB chunks and reports the fraction written (flush and rename unchanged).
- The desktop save maps encoding to 0–85 % and writing to 85–99 %; 100 % once the file is in place. Cancel during encoding now stops the encoder instead of waiting for it.
- Status bar: a save reads "Saving 45%" next to the bar (file name on hover); other jobs are unchanged. Percentages round down, so 100 % only shows when done.
- Tab title: " - Saving 45%" on the saving document's tab in both tab strips (e.g. `Untitled @ 100% (Layer 1, RGB/8)* - Saving 45%`), gone when the save ends.
- New string `Saving {percent}` in every complete catalog.

Measured on a 24 MP, 5-layer RGB/8 PSD (572 MB, release): progress now advances roughly linearly (13 % at 0.5 s … 90 % at 5.0 s, 100 % at 5.6 s on a loaded machine) instead of sitting at 0.

## Tests
- `crates/io/tests/export_progress.rs`: progress is monotonic and ends at 1.0 for PSD/PSB/layered TIFF/.pcraft/PNG/JPEG at 8 and 16 bit; same bytes as `export`; cancelling returns `Cancelled`.

title: Fix Windows desktop cursor stutter with non-vsynced presentation
author: sarseev
body:
Fixes storytold/photocraft#382

## Problem
With PhotoCraft focused, moving the pointer outside the window caused
the desktop cursor to stutter.

## Change
Request AutoNoVsync for Windows window presentation instead of the
default AutoVsync. Preserve backend selection, frame latency, and
on-demand repainting. Other platforms remain unchanged.

Add a configuration regression test and document the validation procedure.

## Validation
An A/B comparison on the affected machine confirmed that the original
presentation mode reproduces the stutter and the patched mode removes it.

## Tradeoffs
Non-vsynced presentation can introduce tearing and higher rendering
rates during activity. No continuous idle rendering is introduced.

title: Format: index ZIP entries by name and use crc32fast (#3474)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3474

## Root cause
- `ZipReader::find` (`crates/format/src/zip.rs`) scanned `entries` linearly by name. Loading a `.pcraft` ZIP bundle calls it once per tile/blob reference (`ZipSource::get` → `read_by_name`), so a load did O(refs × entries) string compares: with ~50k tile objects that is on the order of 10^9 compares. The OpenRaster reader in `photocraft-io` (`ora.rs`) uses the same lookup per layer.
- `crc32` was a hand-rolled byte-at-a-time table CRC-32, run over every entry on save and again on load.

## Fix
- `ZipReader::new` builds a `HashMap<String, usize>` name → index once (O(entries)); `find` is now an O(1) average lookup, so a load is O(refs + entries). For duplicate names the first entry wins, exactly as the old front-to-back scan did. `entries` stays public (tests and callers read it) and is documented as read-only.
- `crc32` delegates to `crc32fast::hash` (same IEEE polynomial; slicing-by-16 with SIMD where available, pure-Rust fallback on wasm). `crc32fast` 1.5.2 was already in `Cargo.lock` through `flate2`, so this adds no new crate to the build.

The improvement is argued from complexity only; **no timings were measured** (shared, heavily loaded build machine).

## Tests
- `crc_known_value` (kept) and new `crc_matches_bitwise_reference`: `crc32` matches a bit-at-a-time IEEE CRC-32 oracle over lengths 0..1000 that cross the SIMD/slicing block sizes.
- `find_locates_every_entry_in_a_large_archive`: 3000 entries, every name is found and reads back its own payload; missing names return `None`.
- `duplicate_names_resolve_to_the_first_entry`: preserves the old first-match behaviour. Verified it fails when the index uses plain `insert` (last wins) instead of `entry().or_insert`.

These are behaviour-preservation tests; the change itself is a complexity fix, so there is no failing-before case beyond the duplicate-name check above.

title: File › Save writes an edit copy handed over by another app back in place (LightCraft's Edit in PhotoCraft)
author: HarrisXiu
body:
PhotoCraft's half of storytold/lightcraft#918 ("Edit in Photocraft"). The LightCraft half is a separate PR there; each works without the other.

## The problem

A photo manager's "Edit in…" renders a copy of a photo, opens it in an editor and reads the file again after the save. LightCraft's copy is a 16-bit TIFF. File › Save sends a TIFF through Save As like any flat file (#416), so for a file that exists only to be changed the user gets a dialog on every save, and choosing another name or format there leaves LightCraft watching a file that never changes.

## What changes

A launch with the environment variable `PHOTOCRAFT_EDIT_IN_PLACE` set (anything but empty or `0`) marks the files on **that launch's command line** as edit copies (`DocState::edit_in_place`). For such a document File › Save writes back to the TIFF it was opened from: no Save As, no TIFF Options prompt, layers kept in the file.

The #416 rule is otherwise unchanged. The mark is narrow on purpose:

- **Only that launch's command-line files.** File › Open, drops, recent files and Apple events open ordinary files.
- **Only a TIFF, and only while it keeps the document's colour mode and channels** (`tiff_layers::holds`: RGB, Grayscale or CMYK, no alpha channels). Lab, Multichannel, Indexed, Bitmap and Duotone documents, and documents with alpha channels, go through Save As as before.
- **Until the document is saved to another file.** A Save As that writes a copy (a PNG of a layered document) leaves it on the TIFF.
- **The control channel's `app.save` is unchanged**: without a `path` it still writes back to layered files only.

Details and the contract for the calling app: `docs/edit-in-place.md`.

## Decisions a maintainer may want to change

- **An environment variable, not a flag.** An older PhotoCraft ignores an unknown variable; an unknown flag is opened as a file name (`Some(s) => files.push(..)` in `main.rs`). A flag can be added beside it.
- **The mark is kept per path until the document arrives…

title: Format: overflow-safe blob decode and bounds-checked ZIP reads (#3486)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3486

## Root cause
- `LoadFetch::blob` (`crates/format/src/store.rs`) capped the zstd decode with `take(self.opts.max_blob_bytes as u64 + 1)`. With `max_blob_bytes: usize::MAX` ("unlimited"), that addition overflows. Debug builds panic. Release builds wrap to `take(0)`, so every blob decodes empty and fails its hash, and no bundle with blobs loads. `ZipReader::read` already saturates the same bound.
- `ZipReader::read` (`crates/format/src/zip.rs`) sliced `&self.bytes[e.data_offset..e.data_offset + e.compressed]` unchecked, but `Entry` is `pub` and `Clone`, so an entry from another archive panics.

## Fix
- New `decompress_bounded(data, max, exact)`, used by both the blob read and the tile decode (`decompress`). Its bound saturates.
- `ZipReader::read` uses checked `get` and returns a `Corrupt` error for an out-of-range entry.
- Cleanup with no behaviour change: `Collect::tile` reuses `tile_le()` instead of its own big-endian branch, and `Object::content()` produces the stored bytes once. `existing_object_is_valid` no longer builds them twice, and `Object::compressed` uses `content()` too.

`#3339` touches `store.rs` only in `load()`, a few lines below these hunks, so the two shouldn't conflict.

## Tests
Each test fails without the fix:
- `format/tests/corruption.rs::an_unlimited_blob_budget_still_loads_blobs`. Without the fix: `attempt to add with overflow` at `store.rs:233`.
- `zip::tests::an_entry_from_another_archive_is_an_error_not_a_panic`. Without the fix: `range end index 4127 out of range for slice of length 101`.

## Commands
```
cargo test -p photocraft-format
cargo clippy -p photocraft-format --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt -p photocraft-format -- --check
cargo xtask layers
cargo xtask wasm

title: Autosave: best-effort cleanup after commit; sweep orphaned recovery bundles (#3489)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3489

## Root cause
1. `PcraftWriter::save_dir` (`crates/format/src/store.rs`) commits by writing the manifest, then deletes objects the new manifest no longer references with `std::fs::remove_file(..)?`. Any failure there (a file that vanished, a locked file on Windows, a non-file at that path) returned `Err` from a save that had already completed, so autosave reported a failure for a good save.
2. Autosave writes the bundle before the `<key>.json` sidecar (`autosave.rs`). `list_recovery` skips bundles without a sidecar and nothing deletes them, so a crash during a document's first autosave left a partial `<key>.pcraft` folder in the recovery directory forever. Temp files from an interrupted atomic write (`.<name>.<pid>-<n>.pcsave.tmp`, `atomic::temp_name`) were never swept either (`list_objects` only looks at `.zst`).

## Fix
- `save_dir`: post-commit removal of unreferenced objects is best-effort. `objects_removed` counts only real removals; a leftover is retried on the next save (it is listed again).
- `RecoveryStore::new` (called once when the app opens its recovery directory) runs a conservative, best-effort `sweep_orphans`:
  - removes `<key>.pcraft` folders (real directories, sanitized key) that have **no** `<key>.json` (anything at that path, even a broken sidecar, keeps the bundle);
  - removes `*.pcsave.tmp` files in the recovery dir, in bundles and their `tiles/`/`blobs/`, whose embedded pid is **not** this process;
  - both only when untouched for 24 hours (bundle, `tiles/` and `blobs/` mtimes), so another running instance's in-progress first autosave is never touched. Symlinks, unparsable names and other files are left alone, nothing outside the recovery dir is visited, and errors are ignored.

## Tests
- `tests/autosave.rs::failed_cleanup_after_commit_does_not_fail_the_save`: a folder squatting on an unreferenced tile name makes the cleanup fail; the save must still return `Ok` (with `objects_removed == 0`) and load back identical. **Fails with…

title: fix(type): use the correct line at soft-wrap caret boundaries
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

At the beginning of a wrapped line, `type.caret` can report the
preceding line even though the caret geometry belongs to the next
visual line.

The same boundary error affects `type.navigate` with `lineStart`
and `lineEnd`.

Fixes #3068.

## Root cause

Adjacent visual lines can share a character offset.

The previous line-index lookup selected the first matching range,
while caret geometry could correctly resolve the following line.

## Changes

- Prefer the following visual line when resolving a shared caret
  boundary.
- Make line-edge navigation use the same line selection.
- Preserve pointer-based hit-testing by determining the visual line
  from the pointer's position.
- Add text-layout regression coverage for wrapped lines, forced
  breaks, and ordinary paragraph breaks.
- Add engine-level regression coverage for caret and line navigation.

## Compatibility

The change preserves existing character indices and text content.

It corrects line identity without changing the document format or
introducing additional history steps.

## Validation

- Verified the committed changes against the upstream baseline.
- Added focused text-layout and engine regression tests.
- Rust tests and CI have not been executed.

title: Android tablet build with pen pressure (photocraft-android)
author: cristiancolosimo
body:
## What

A native Android build for tablets: new `apps/photocraft-android` crate running the same `PhotocraftApp` in an eframe NativeActivity on wgpu/Vulkan (no wasm, webview or JS). Built with `packaging/android/build.sh` (cargo-apk, arm64, minSdk 29). Details in `apps/photocraft-android/README.md`.

- **Pen pressure:** winit's Android touch force feeds the existing `stylus` module.
- **Pen vs. finger:** winit 0.30 drops the Android tool type, so `patches/winit` (0.30.13 plus one change, `patches/README.md`) encodes it in the high bits of `Touch::id`. `Stylus::finger_down()` makes the canvas use the Hand tool while a finger is down and no pen is, so fingers pan/pinch and only the stylus paints. Other platforms never set the flags, so nothing changes there.
- **File dialogs:** an in-app browser over shared storage (needs "All files access"); SAF needs a Java callback a NativeActivity can't receive.
- **System bars:** `target_sdk 34`, `NoActionBar.Fullscreen` theme, layout inside the activity content rect.
- `ui-egui`: eframe's `accesskit` is enabled only off Android (it requires `android-game-activity`).

## Things to look at

- `unsafe`: `android_main` needs `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]`, so this crate denies `unsafe` and allows it in one file (like `photocraft-tablet`) instead of inheriting the workspace `forbid`. One `// SAFETY:` comment.
- The vendored winit patch (3 MB) is a deliberate stopgap until winit 0.31's pointer kinds.

## Tested

`cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui -p photocraft-android --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib stylus` (new finger/pen test), `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`. On a real tablet: the app starts and pen pressure works. The system-bar fixes, file browser and finger pan were built but are not yet confirmed on a device. Not run: the full test suite, `panic_hunt` (no commands changed), `cargo xtask scorecard`.

title: feat(export): optionally trim transparent margins from layer files
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Layers to Files always exports each layer at the full document dimensions, even when its visible content occupies only a small area.

For workflows involving sprites, isolated assets, and reusable design elements, this leaves unnecessary transparent margins around every exported image.

Addresses #3447.

## Changes

- Add an optional `trim` parameter to `file.export.layersToFiles`.
- Expose a Trim checkbox in the Layers to Files dialog.
- Calculate the visible alpha bounds of each isolated layer before export.
- Crop the temporary export document to those bounds using the existing document-cropping implementation.
- Account for the rendered result, including masks and layer effects.
- Preserve full document dimensions when trimming is disabled.
- Keep entirely transparent layers exportable without creating zero-sized images.
- Leave the original document unchanged.

## Compatibility

Trimming is disabled by default, preserving existing export behavior and automation scripts.

The option applies independently to each exported layer.

## Tests

Added regression tests covering:
- Default full-canvas exports.
- Trimmed exports and pixel preservation.
- 8-, 16-, and 32-bit source documents.
- Non-destructive export behavior.
- Entirely transparent layers.

The tests have not been executed locally. CI validation is pending.

## Issue

Addresses #3447.

title: fix(io): a fresh Metrics type layer writes no empty Txt2 stub (#3514)
author: dottedt
body:
Fixes #3514.

The report isolates the cause precisely: PSD export always writes a document-level `Txt2` block, and for a fresh document its document-resources dictionary (`/0`) is the empty `<< >>` that Photoshop never writes; Photopea's reader fails on it. Removing that block (or not writing it, as 0.3.0 did) makes Photopea open the file with live, editable text.

This writes the block only when it carries something:
- the file already had one - round-trip its resources, pen positions and extras;
- or a layer uses the **Optical** auto-kern mode, the one mode EngineData's `AutoKerning` cannot distinguish (#1348).

A plain Metrics document therefore writes no `Txt2`, matching 0.3.0 and fixing the report.

The `TySh` 4-byte-alignment warning Photopea logs is separate and not addressed here (Photopea tolerates it; psd-tools reads it).

Tests: `photocraft-text` `needs_txt2_only_for_optical`; `photocraft-io` `fresh_metrics_text_writes_no_txt2_block`. Full `photocraft-text` (123) and `photocraft-io` suites pass; fmt and clippy clean.

author: dottedt
body:
Fixes #3497.

A monochrome LinearRaw DNG (one sample per pixel - a Leica M Monochrom file, or a VueScan black-and-white film scan) was refused on open with `unsupported camera raw: LinearRaw data with 1 samples per pixel`, because `dng::decode` only accepted the 3-sample LinearRaw case. The develop path already handles a single-plane RGB image, so this expands a 1-sample LinearRaw plane to three identical channels at decode: the file opens as RGB with the grey in all three channels - the shape the report asked for.

The CFA (1 sample) and 3-sample LinearRaw paths are unchanged.

Tests: `crates/raw/tests/dng.rs` `gray_linear_raw_opens_as_rgb` (the synthetic DNG generator gains a monochrome-LinearRaw mode; the test checks the three channels are equal and that `develop` stays neutral grey). Full `photocraft-raw` suite passes; fmt and clippy clean.

title: History: jump to a state in one step (history.selectState) (#2966)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #2966.

**Why:** clicking a History state ran Edit › Undo / Redo once per state. Each step added 1 to the document revision, so the canvas could no longer tell what the jump changed: it recomposited the whole document and, on the GPU path, re-uploaded every changed layer. This is part of the "very laggy history usage" report.

**Merge order: please merge #3545 and #3567 (Snapshots, @itsF4LCON) first.** This PR touches the same History code; I'll rebase this onto them right after (both change `fn history` in `panels.rs`).

## Change
- New command `history.selectState {"state": index}` (same numbering as `history.deleteState`, redo states included). It returns the document to that state in one step: one revision, one damage rect, the state's targeted layers restored as Undo does. Later states stay redoable until the next edit. UI, CLI, control channel and MCP share it.
- The History panel runs it once per click (errors go to the status bar); an open Free Transform still blocks it, and the transform also refuses it for every caller.
- A floating selection goes back as with Undo instead of being dropped as a new step that would discard the redo states.
- History rows get accessibility labels.

## Measurements
Release build, 30 states back, click → drawn (offscreen harness, GPU sync):

| Document | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 24 MP, GPU canvas | 5.2 ms | 3.7 ms |
| 24 MP, CPU canvas | 363 ms | 230 ms |

title: Actions: a recorded File › Save of a flat file saves the file it is played on (#3531)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3531

Follow-up to #2032 (comment from MikeySnowspikes: a recorded Save says it saved but doesn't overwrite the original).

## Root cause
A layered document (PSD/PSB/.pcraft) already recorded a real `file.save` step. A flat file (PNG, JPEG, ...) has no in-place Save yet: Save opens the save dialog, and confirming it recorded a Save As with the fixed path of the file it was recorded on. Playing the action on another file wrote that first file again and reported "Saved a.png"; the document the action ran on was never written.

## Fix
- File › Save that had to ask for a file name and was confirmed with the document's own file is recorded as `file.save` (not a Save As to a fixed path). Save As keeps its recorded path.
- Replaying `file.save` writes back to the active document's own file for layered files and for flat formats the codecs can write; otherwise it returns an error that says what is needed.
- Interactive Save is unchanged (the dialog behaviour of #2515 is not touched).

## Tests
- `recorded_save_overwrites_the_flat_file_the_action_is_played_on` (real PNG files on disk): fails before the fix (b.png untouched, step recorded as `file.saveAs`), passes after.
- `recorded_save_overwrites_the_layered_file_the_action_is_played_on` (PSD, already worked) guards the layered path.

## Commands
`cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- save actions:: file_dialog file_open`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p photocraft-ui-egui -- --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`. No command added or changed, so no panic_hunt.

title: fix(gpu): require consent to persist CPU recovery
author: Ni-zav
body:
Fixes #3483.

## Problem

An interrupted GPU startup can trigger PhotoCraft's recovery
sequence:

Vulkan → OpenGL → CPU

On Linux/NVIDIA systems where the OpenGL adapter cannot present
to the window, this can end in CPU rendering.

Once the CPU renderer starts successfully, PhotoCraft
automatically saves CPU mode to the user's preferences.

Consequently, closing the recovery dialog without choosing
an option can leave every subsequent launch using software
rendering, even when Vulkan is available.

## Root Cause

The desktop startup callback persists CPU mode when a
fallback succeeds, independently of the user's decision.

The backend persistence logic can also save CPU as the
preferred backend.

## Changes

- Stop automatically persisting CPU rendering after startup
  recovery.
- Keep CPU fallback temporary for the current session.
- Preserve the recovery dialog's explicit preference controls.
- Continue remembering successful hardware backend fallbacks.
- Prevent CPU fallback from silently replacing the saved
  GPU backend.
- Update graphics recovery documentation.

## Regression Tests

Added tests covering:

- CPU fallback following an OpenGL startup failure.
- Temporary CPU mode requested through --safe-gpu.
- Preservation of the original automatic GPU policy.
- Persistence of successful hardware backend recovery.
- Explicit CPU selection remaining supported.

Existing recovery-dialog tests cover saving the user's
"Keep Using CPU" and "Retry GPU" choices.

## Scope

This addresses unintended preference persistence.

It does not change the Linux GPU adapter-selection algorithm
or the Vulkan → OpenGL → CPU fallback sequence.

## Validation

Changes committed and pushed to the fork.
Branch rebased onto current upstream main.

Local tests and CI have not been run.

title: psd: harden the standalone binary parsers (fuzz + property tests, gradient/swatch correctness)
author: agent-346022
body:
## Summary

Photoshop colour palettes (`.aco`/`.ase`), gradients (`.grd`) and patterns are files people download in bulk, so plenty are malformed. A broken or hostile one must raise a clean error — never crash (losing the user's work) and never silently produce a wrong colour. That is the project's first rule (`AGENTS.md`, "Never crash"). This hardens every standalone parser in `photocraft-psd` and puts each under a libFuzzer target plus deterministic property tests.

- `grd.rs` — one float guard (`finite`): only `NaN` falls back to a default; `±inf` and over-`f32::MAX` values saturate (monotonic, no snap-to-default that would invert a value). **Hue wraps** (`370° → 10°`) instead of clamping to a different colour at the boundary. RGB/CMYK/Gray clamped to `0..=1`, L\* to `0..=100`, a\*/b\* to the CIELAB gamut `-128..=127`.
- `aco.rs` / `ase.rs` / `io.rs` — a shared `utf16_units` caps swatch names **without splitting a surrogate pair** (the old `encode_utf16().take()` could write broken UTF-16 for emoji/CJK above U+FFFF).
- `patterns` / `filter_effects` / `metadata` / `resources` / `tagged` — already well defended; review found no latent panic, so these get fuzz targets + property tests only (no production change).

Touches only `crates/psd/` plus the fuzz CI matrix.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p photocraft-psd` — 371 pass
- [x] `cargo clippy -p photocraft-psd --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo check -p photocraft-psd --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`
- [x] `cargo +nightly fuzz build` — 13 targets; smoke runs clean (metadata 11.5M, patterns 2M, filter_effects 5.9M, resources 3.5M, tagged 5.4M execs)
- [x] `cargo xtask test-corpus -p psd -p io` — io oracle / round-trip / mutation corpora pass (no regression on real presets)
- [x] Mutation checks: a\*/b\* clamp-weakening and hue-guard-removal mutants both killed

title: PSD: Backgrounds survive a round trip through PhotoCraft
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## What's wrong

Every PSD with a Background layer came back from PhotoCraft with an **ordinary bottom layer**. Opened in Photoshop it's no longer the Background: it's unlocked, can move and can hold transparency.

Measured with scripted Photoshop 27.11: I opened PhotoCraft's re-exports of all 427 PSD/PSB files in the corpus. **317 lost their Background** this way. Their composites were otherwise identical.

## What Photoshop does (measured)

Photoshop opens a PSD's bottom layer as the Background **when that layer's record has no transparency (`-1`) channel**, whatever its name and lock flags say. It then locks it and shows it as "Background": psd-tools' "Фон" and ag-psd's "bg" or "Layer 1" all open as Backgrounds. PhotoCraft always wrote the `-1` channel.

| | channels | flags |
|---|---|---|
| Photoshop's Background (`photoshop/adjustments/rgb8/invert.psd`) | 0, 1, 2 | `00001001` |
| PhotoCraft's export of it (`main`) | **−1**, 0, 1, 2 | `00000001` |
| this PR | 0, 1, 2 | `00001001` |

## Change
- **Export** (`psd_export::psd_background`): the bottom top-level layer is written without the `-1` channel when it's a locked (transparency and position), unclipped, unmasked raster that's opaque over the whole canvas at full opacity and Normal, as a Background always is. Flags are written as Photoshop writes them: bit 4 marked meaningful, and "pixel data irrelevant" on adjustment layers.
- **Import** (`psd_import::mark_background`): like Photoshop, a bottom raster layer whose record has no `-1` channel becomes the Background (locked, named "Background").

## Results
- Of the 227 corpus files whose bottom layer is a Background, PhotoCraft's export now writes **227** the way the original does (`main`: 0), and no other bottom layer turns into one.
- Corpus oracles and round trips are unchanged: io 148/170, psd-tools 237/309, Photoshop 137/258 on the same commit, and every round trip renders the same.

title: fix(engine): a PSD type layer names the installed font, not an invented one (#3556)
author: dottedt
body:
Fixes #3556.

A type layer created with a font by family name stored no PostScript name, so PSD export invented one - the family with its spaces removed plus `-Regular` (e.g. `Franklin Gothic Demi Cond` → `FranklinGothicDemiCond-Regular`). Photoshop looks type up by PostScript name, so it flagged the font as missing and substituted Myriad Pro as soon as the text was edited, even though the font is installed.

`apply_char_props` now resolves the family's installed face (matching weight and italic) from the font database whenever the family, style, weight or italic is set, and stores that face's real PostScript name. An explicit `postscriptName` still wins, and a family PhotoCraft does not have keeps no name, so the export falls back as before.

Test: `a_family_font_gets_the_installed_postscript_name`; the existing named-face test now expects the resolved name.

Gates: `cargo test -p photocraft-engine` (including `panic_hunt`), `cargo xtask parity --check` and `cargo xtask wasm` pass.

title: Save As: a saved .pcraft manifest reports the file it was saved under
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #3312.

Narrowed as requested by @echelon: this now carries **only** the `photocraft_io::export` half — the desktop `File › Save As` / export path — plus its test. The unrelated JPEG XL / PCX / KRA codec commits and their `jxl-oxide` dependency are dropped from this branch (they belong in their own PR, and dependency additions go through a maintainer). The stray `scal to fit` typo was introduced by the commit that has since been dropped, so it is gone with it.

## Root cause

Every `.pcraft` writer serialises the document *before* `DocState::saved_to` adopts the new name, so the bytes always carry the previous identity:

```rust
let (bytes, warnings) = export(&st.doc, &path, settings)?;   // manifest gets the old name
write(&path, &bytes)?;
st.saved_to(path);                                           // name adopted here
```

## Fix

`photocraft_io::named_for_file(doc, name) -> Cow<Document>`: when `name` is a file (a path, or `name.ext`) the document is serialised under that file's name, so what lands in `manifest.json` is the identity the save is about to adopt — the same rule every other format already follows on import, where `document.name` comes from the file it was read from. A bare extension (`"pcraft"`) names no file and changes nothing.

Applied once, in the `.pcraft` branch of `export_stages`, which both `export` and `export_with` funnel through — so `apps/photocraft/src/services.rs` is covered on both of its paths:

| call site | path |
| --- | --- |
| `services.rs:242` → `photocraft_io::export_with` | `Services::save_file` / `automation_save` (worker-thread Save) |
| `services.rs:384` → `photocraft_io::export` | Export |
| `web.rs:355` → `photocraft_io::export` | web build |
| `file_cmds.rs:295` → `photocraft_io::export` | engine file command |

`export_stages` gained progress reporting and cancellation since this branch was cut, so the `named_for_file` snapshot is taken before the thumbnail and composite previews are rendered from it — the previe…

title: fix(engine): image.canvasSize rejects unlisted anchors instead of landing between two (#2946)
author: agent-346022
body:
## Summary

`image.canvasSize` with a misspelled `anchor` silently anchored the canvas somewhere that is **neither** what the caller asked for **nor** the documented `center` default — a resize offset nobody chose, with no error.

`anchor_factors` resolved the x and y axes independently and with different rules (x looked for a capitalised `"Left"`/`"Right"`, y for a lowercase `"top"`/`"bottom"` prefix), so a typo matched one and missed the other:

| anchor | lands at |
|---|---|
| `"topLeft"` | top-left (correct) |
| `"topleft"` | top-**centre** — not one of the nine |
| `"TopLeft"` | **left**-centre — a different anchor, silently |

- `crates/engine/src/image_cmds.rs` — match `anchor` exactly against the nine documented values via one `ANCHORS` table; anything else is a `BadParams` error naming `anchor` and listing them (the convention #507 set for other command params). The nine valid values keep the exact factors they had, and an omitted `anchor` still means `center`. The Canvas Size dialog picks from a nine-cell grid, so the UI cannot hit this; only command/MCP callers could.

Fixes #2946.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib image_cmds::` — 23 pass (new `canvas_size_anchor_offsets_and_rejects_unlisted` covers the nine offsets, the omitted default, and the misspellings from the issue)
- [x] `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored` — passes (no command panics on adversarial params)
- [x] `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers` — clean

Made with love by Claude

title: PSD: alpha channel resources count the merged transparency; 13-byte DisplayInfo
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## What's wrong

Photoshop 27.11 **refuses to open** some PSDs that PhotoCraft writes. I opened PhotoCraft's re-exports of the 427 corpus files in scripted Photoshop, and two of them failed (`ag-psd/layer-mask/src.psd`, `psd-tools/effects/stroke-without-vector-mask.psd`) with:

title: Glows: Photoshop's precise ramp; centre-source glows inverted after the contour
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## What's wrong

Two glow bugs, measured against Photoshop 27.11:
- **Precise** Outer and Inner Glows stayed solid for about half their size, then dropped off steeply. Up to **122 levels off**.
- **Centre-source** Inner Glows (Softer and Precise) were up to **115 levels off**, even though the edge-source Softer glow already matched.

## What Photoshop does (measured)

Scripted on Photoshop 27.11: a 128 px square with one glow (Normal, black, 100%, Range 50%), sampled pixel by pixel across its edges. Outer and inner, both techniques, sizes 10 and 20, spread 0/40%, choke 0/30%, edge and centre source: 16 cases.
- A **Precise** glow is `1 − D / (size + 1)` beyond the solid spread/choke part, where D is the centre-to-centre distance to the edge. Photoshop's black glow over white reads 47, 93, 140, 186, 232 at 2–10 px out. `main`'s ramp ended at `size`, and the default 50% Range then doubled it.
- A **centre-source** Inner Glow is **exactly `1 −` the edge glow** (0 levels apart, for both techniques), taken *after* the contour and Range. `main` inverted before them.

## Change
- `compose::effects::glow_map`: a Precise glow's raw coverage is 0.5 at the edge, falling to 0 at `size + 1`, and solid within the spread/choke. The shared Range step (`v / range`) then gives Photoshop's ramp at the default 50%. The centre-source inverse is now taken after the contour and Range.
- **GPU:** the same ramp in `fs_mglow`, and an "invert after the contour" mode (`p0.y = 2`) in `fs_mfinish`, used only by glows (Satin keeps its own invert).

Only Range 50% has been measured. For other Range values, this keeps PhotoCraft's existing `v / range` model for both techniques.

## Results

| | `main` (worst) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Precise outer (4 cases) | 110–122 | 1 |
| Precise inner, edge and centre (4) | 58–64 | 1 |
| Softer inner, centre (2) | 110–115 | 1 |
| Softer outer and inner-edge (6) | 1–4 | unchanged |

title: fix(smudge): smear smoothly on fast strokes instead of stamping echoes
author: FredApps
body:
Fixes #3573

## Root cause
The Smudge tool carries a picked-up copy of the pixels from one dab to the next. Its dabs were placed at the brush **Spacing**, which is 10–25 % of the diameter. On a big brush that means a dab every 10 px or more, and each dab stamped the carried copy again, so every edge the stroke crossed left a row of bands or echoes instead of a smooth smear. This matches the "actual" screenshot. The path walker already interpolates between pointer events and carries the leftover distance across segments, so sparse pointer events weren't the problem. The problem was the distance between dabs.

## Fix
- `engine/retouch_cmds.rs`: a new `smudge_spacing` respaces Smudge strokes to about 1 px between dabs, with a floor of 1 % of the diameter, which is the walker's minimum. It applies to both the commit and the live preview (`DabTool::parse`). A Spacing of 100 % or more, where dabs don't touch, is a deliberate choice and is left as it is (#2140, `smudge_uses_the_brush_settings_spacing` still passes).

author: dottedt
body:
Fixes #3546.

`destructive_levels_dont_clip_in_32_bit` asserted that a 32-bit document maps Levels black to 0 and white to 255 - the old 0..1 lookup-table behaviour. #2592 (`Preserve HDR range in float adjustments`) made a 32-bit RGB Levels adjustment evaluate the float curve directly, so it deliberately runs past the output range: black goes below 0 and white above 1. title: Fuzz: ignore the same build leftovers in every fuzz crate
author: s17sh70x2jfl031ag
body:
Running the fuzz targets locally left untracked files in the checkout, because the five fuzz crates' `.gitignore` files don't match:

- `crates/raw/fuzz` has no `.gitignore` at all
- `crates/psd/fuzz` doesn't ignore `Cargo.lock`
- `crates/format/fuzz` doesn't ignore `coverage/`

This gives all five the same list that `codecs` and `affinity` already use: `target/`, `corpus/`, `artifacts/`, `coverage/` and `Cargo.lock`.

**How I checked:** I created the files a fuzzing run leaves behind (`Cargo.lock`, and files in `corpus/`, `artifacts/`, `coverage/` and `target/`) in all five fuzz crates. Before this change, `git status` listed six untracked paths: `format/fuzz/coverage/`, `psd/fuzz/Cargo.lock`, and `raw/fuzz`'s `Cargo.lock`, `artifacts/`, `corpus/` and `coverage/`. After it, it lists none. I found this while running the PSD, codecs, format, raw and Affinity fuzz targets overnight.

title: Edit › Transform › Skew: corners and sides move along one axis, like Photoshop (#3437)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #3437. @davidmann4 closed their draft (#3506) and asked for this PR.

## Problem

In Edit › Transform › Skew, a corner drag scaled the box like Free Transform, and the side handles moved freely in both directions. A drag outside the box rotated it.

## Photoshop

Checked in Photoshop 27.11 by @kayrockscreenprinting.

- **Image layer:** a corner moves alone, horizontally or vertically, whichever way the drag mostly goes.
- **Side handles:** the top and bottom handles slide only horizontally, the left and right ones only vertically.
- **⌥:** moves the opposite corner or edge the other way.
- **Type layer:** a corner slides its whole edge instead: the top or bottom edge for a sideways drag, the left or right one for an up/down drag. The text stays a parallelogram and remains live type.
- **Outside the box:** a drag doesn't rotate the box.
- **⇧:** changes nothing.

## Fix

All in `transform_tool.rs`. Free Transform, Distort and Perspective are unchanged.

- `apply_mode_drag` applies a handle drag for the current mode. The canvas calls it instead of turning the mode into modifier keys (`mode_mods`), which can't express "a corner moves on one axis".
- **Corners.** A corner moves along one of its two edges, whichever the drag mostly follows, in the box's own frame, so a rotated box skews along its sides.
  - On editable type (`moves_type`), the corner's edge partner moves with it. A trapezoid would make the commit fail ("Distort and Perspective need rasterized type").
  - ⌥ moves the opposite corner, or on type the opposite edge, by the same amount the other way.
- **Side handles.** These slide only along their edge, as ⌘⇧ does in Free Transform.
- **Outside the box.** `mode_allows` (was `distort_allows`) now also blocks outside drags in Skew mode, so neither the rotation nor the rotate cursor happens. A click outside still commits.

## Tests

Written first, each failing before its change:

- `skew_mode_moves_a_corner_or_an_edge_along_one_axis`:
  - corners on each …

title: Chisel bevels: Photoshop's facet slope and ramp ends
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## What's wrong

Bevel & Emboss with **Chisel Hard** or **Chisel Soft** drew facets about **twice as steep** as Photoshop's. On a 128 px square with an Inner Chisel Hard bevel (size 10, depth 100%, light from the top), the lit facet reads **217** where Photoshop shows **188**. The ends of each facet also differed. Up to 154 levels off (Outer Chisel Hard).

## What Photoshop does (measured)

Scripted on Photoshop 27.11: one Bevel & Emboss on a 128 px square, Global Light off, light at 90°/30°, sampled pixel by pixel across the edges. Chisel Hard and Soft, inner and outer, size 10 and 20, depth 100 and 300.
- **Slope:** a chisel facet rises to the same `depth × size / 2` as a Smooth bevel, but over `size + 1` px, so its slope is `depth × size / (2 (size + 1))`. Size 10 → 0.455 (measured 0.452–0.457). Size 20 → 0.476 (measured 0.471–0.480).
- **Ramp ends:**
  - **Inner Hard** runs from half a pixel beyond the edge to `size + ½`, so the facet is flat right up to the edge pixel.
  - **Inner Soft** starts a pixel further out (a steeper edge pixel) and is **not blurred**.
  - **Outer Hard** ends a pixel further out.
  - **Outer Soft** is a pixel shorter, with a steeper edge pixel.
  - Outer chisel bevels also shade, at half strength, the pixel where their ramp reaches zero. Emboss styles already did this.

(Smooth bevels already match Photoshop within 1–3 levels and are unchanged.)

## Change
- `compose::effects`: `bevel_geom`'s chisel depth scale is `depth × size / 2`, and `bevel_chisel_h` has the measured ramps. The Chisel Soft blur stays only for Emboss and Pillow, which aren't modelled yet. Outer chisel bevels reach one pixel past their ramp.
- **GPU:** the same ramps in `fs_mbevelh` (Chisel Soft flag in `p0.z`), the Emboss-only blur, and the outer reach-past flag in `p3.x` of `fs_mbevelshade`.

## Results

| case | `main` (worst) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Inner Chisel Hard (size 10, size 20, depth 300) | 27–29 | 0–1 |
| Inner Chisel Soft | 29 | 1 |
| Outer Chisel Ha…

title: Free Transform several selected layers together (#3592)
author: FredApps
body:
Fixes #3592

Selecting several layers and pressing Ctrl+T (Free Transform) now transforms all of them together, like Photoshop: one bounding box around every selected layer's content, the same move/scale/rotate/skew/distort applied to each layer around the shared pivot, committed as **one** undoable step. Cancel (Esc) leaves every layer as it was.

## Design
It reuses the existing single-layer path rather than adding a parallel one.

**Engine (`edit.transform`)**
- New optional `"layers": [id, …]` param. `multi_targets` filters the list. With two or more layers left, `transform_many` builds one homography from the shared `rect` (the union of each layer's `transform_bounds` by default) and the `quad`/`matrix`. It then runs the existing `transform_layer` and `refresh_text` on each layer inside a single `s.edit("Free Transform")`, and warps the selection outline once. With only one layer left, it falls back to the normal single-layer path.
- The quad/matrix parsing and the affine detection moved into small helpers (`homography`, `affine_of`, `rect_param`). The single-layer path uses them too and behaves the same as before.

**UI (`transform_tool`)**
- `begin()` checks `DocState::selected_layers()`. When `multi_targets` returns two or more layers, `begin_many` opens the box around `multi_bounds`. The document under the box has those layers hidden, or has their selected pixels lifted out for pixel layers when there's a selection. The moving content previews as one composite of just those layers, and what covers the topmost moving layer still draws over it (`Above`).
- `TransformSession` gets a `layers: Vec<u64>` field (serde default, empty for single-layer sessions). `commit()` adds `"layers"` to the `edit.transform` call. Box undo/redo, nudges, the options bar fields, the pivot and Esc all work unchanged, because they only act on the quad.

## Edge cases

This one-line change preserves the same sample decoding, sparse-tile defaults, runtime mask depth, coverage clamp and blending arithmetic. title: Brush: symmetric live strokes update only what changed (#3593)
author: xsvm
body:
## Problem

With painting symmetry on, every pointer event in `LiveStroke::push` (`crates/engine/src/brush_cmds.rs`) cloned the primary and every mirrored `StrokeRenderer`, finished the copies, merged all passes again in `composite_union_many`, composited the whole stroke (`all = true`) and restored every pass's full bounding box from the pre-stroke pixels. The cost of one event grew with the area painted so far, so a stroke was quadratic. Without symmetry the live stroke already composites only the dirty coverage tiles.

## Change

- `StrokeRenderer::composite_union_live` (`crates/paint/src/render.rs`) merges the passes incrementally. On each push it touches only these tiles: the ones any pass dirtied (including dual-brush coverage), plus the smoothing-tail tiles from the previous and current push. For those tiles it takes each pass's finished coverage (`CoverageMap::finished_subset`) and `union_max`es them in pass order. It then restores just those tiles from `pre` and composites them. `UnionLive` carries the tail tiles and bounds between pushes.
- When the number of distinct passes changes mid-stroke, for example when a mirror stops coinciding with the primary, the next push re-merges every tile once.
- `LiveStroke` keeps a `UnionLive` instead of the per-pass regions and calls the new function from its symmetric branch. Release still commits the live pixels (c6a525cc), so the output must stay byte-identical to the old full merge.

## Tests

`live_union_of_passes_matches_merging_the_finished_passes_after_every_chunk` (`crates/paint/src/brush_tests.rs`):
- Brushes: plain, smoothing, dual brush, color dynamics, wet edges, Dissolve, erase, and per-stroke texture.
- Surfaces: U8, U16 and F32 RGB with alpha.
- Pass setups: 2 passes; 4 passes where two join partway through; 4 passes under a grayscale selection.
- After every chunk of 1, 2 or 3 points, the live surface must equal clone + `finish` + `composite_union_many` onto a fresh copy of `pre`, byte for byte. The liv…

title: Move: an unlinked layer mask moves alone when targeted (#3604)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3604

## Root cause
Dragging the layer already left an unlinked mask in place (`translate_layer` only shifts `linked` masks), but the other half of Photoshop's behaviour was missing: with the mask thumbnail targeted and its chain off, the Move tool moves the mask alone. `layer.translate` ignored the target, so it always moved the layer.

## Fix

- `channel_cmds::follows_target` includes `layer.translate`, so the shell adds the target when the Layers panel targets the mask (drag commit, arrow-key nudge).
- New `layer_multi_cmds::moved_target` for the live drag preview.

## Tests (fail without the fix)
- engine `translate_with_the_mask_targeted_moves_an_unlinked_mask_alone` (8 and 16 bit, undo) and `translate_leaves_an_unlinked_mask_in_place` (guards the existing drag-the-layer half)
- ui-egui `dragging_with_an_unlinked_mask_targeted_moves_the_mask_alone` (preview + commit; linked mask and pixel target still move the layer)

title: ops: count selection masks in history pixel budget
author: Streetblock
body:
Normal selection masks were omitted from history's pixel-memory accounting. Repeated selection edits could retain large masks while `pixel_bytes()` reported no selection memory, so `trim()` would not evict those older states when the byte budget was exceeded.

Include `Document::selection` in the shared `tiles::surfaces` visitor. This makes direct pixel-byte totals, history-only unique bytes, and the incremental tile-reference tracker account for the same selection surfaces. Shared tile allocations still count once; reference tracking includes aliases so removing one snapshot does not discard a tile still held by another owner.

The existing minimum-undo policy is preserved: the newest undo state is retained even when the current document plus that state exceed `max_bytes`.

### Reproduction and measurements

A document with no raster layers isolates selection memory: five independently allocated 24-MP GRAY8 selection masks, `History::new(50)`, an 8-MiB byte budget, and `trim()` after each recorded selection edit. Baseline: upstream `16bdcbd54e5d87cf0212b5961ac35347f27e0e21`. Release build on Windows, Intel i9-13900H.

| Metric | Upstream | Fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Actual unique selection-tile bytes retained by current + history | 120 MiB | 48 MiB |
| Reported pixel bytes | 0 MiB | 48 MiB |
| History-only unique bytes reported | 0 MiB | 24 MiB |
| Undo states retained | 5 | 1 |

That is **60% less retained selection-tile memory in this fixture**. The remaining 48 MiB are the current selection and the latest undo selection. Each uses 24 MiB of padded tile storage; keeping both follows the existing policy, so this is deliberately not a strict 8-MiB cap.

Separately sampled process peak working set was **147.61 → 99.36 MiB** in the two single fixture runs. This descriptive process metric also includes fixture construction, masks before trimming, allocator behavior and runtime overhead. It does not establish a general application-RAM reduction or a runtime improv…

title: Image Adjustments: Desaturate, Equalize and Replace Color on a smart object (#3606)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3606

## Root cause
#2229 routed most Image › Adjustments on a smart object through `adjust_as_smart_filter`, but Desaturate, Equalize and Replace Color had their own `enabled` checks (pixel layer only) and never called it, so they were refused with "not a pixel layer".

## Change
- All three are enabled on a smart object and record `image.adjustments.<kind>` as a smart filter (selection becomes the filter mask, one history step), re-run via `adjust_as_filter`.
- Replace Color records the foreground colour it was run with, so the filter does not change when the foreground does. Localized Color Clusters on a smart object return an error instead of being silently ignored.
- Equalize's body is now `equalize_pixels`, shared by the command and the filter; Desaturate's adjustment is shared too.
- Not covered: Match Color (needs a source document) and HDR Toning (flattens).

## Tests
- `desaturate_equalize_and_replace_color_record_smart_filters`: each filter's render equals the destructive result on the same pixels, and undo removes it. Fails on main ("runs on a smart object"). Updated the older test that asserted Replace Color stays disabled.
- `replace_color_smart_filter_keeps_the_foreground_it_was_run_with` (requested in review): Replace Color without `color` records the foreground; after changing the foreground and re-rendering the filter (hide and show), the flattened result still equals the destructive result with the original foreground. With the recording disabled, it fails (the filter renders with black instead of the foreground).
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib -- adjust_cmds smart`, clippy `-D warnings` (--lib --tests), fmt on the changed files, `cargo xtask layers` pass after merging current main.

## Credits
Thanks to @vbasky (#4759, the same feature), whose PR showed that a Replace Color smart filter renders black when `color` is omitted; this PR records the foreground colour to avoid that.
