title: fix(ui): one eliding label for fixed-width chrome, so translations can't overrun (#3580)
author: dottedt
body:
Fixes #3580. This is the app-wide mechanism, not a one-off guard.

**Root cause.** A translated label drawn beside a fixed-width control can run over its neighbours. The Layers Lock/Fill row guarded only the redundant "Lock:" caption, so "Fill:" ("Заливка:" in Russian; longer still as pt-br `Preenchimento:` / fr `Remplissage :`, the worst catalogs) overran the lock icons.

**The mechanism.** `widgets::elided_label(ui, text, max_w)` is the one primitive for fixed chrome: it lays the text out no wider than its room, cuts it with `…`, and shows the full string on hover. It builds on the existing `tab_strip::elided` (already used for document tabs, layer names and brush names), so overlap becomes structurally impossible in *every* locale with no per-language code. The Opacity/Fill scrub labels now elide to the room beside their field.

**The rule** is documented in `docs/ui-design.md`: wrap by default; beside a fixed control, elide; a *redundant* caption may drop on a narrow dock (the lock icons carry the meaning). This mirrors Photoshop — a fixed layout with elision + tooltips, not per-locale reflow.

**Other places to adopt this preventatively** (each is a label sharing a row with a fixed-width control, so it can overrun in a longer locale):
- the **Opacity** label — #2309 drops it on a narrow dock; it could elide instead,
- **options-bar** and **toolbar** labels (the densest rows),
- **filter / adjustment dialog** field labels,
- **brush / tool panel** rows,
- any new label added beside a fixed-width field.
Use `elided_label` when in doubt; the guard is structural, so it needs no per-language test.

Test: `widgets::tests::elided_label_never_exceeds_its_room`. Full `photocraft-ui-egui` suite (2077) passes; fmt and clippy clean.

title: fix(windows): strip sizing border and clear WFCPRESENT on custom titlebar (#2850)
author: Korg1ch
body:
Closes #2850, closes #3225, closes #3430, closes #3550

## Summary

On Windows 10 with Intel Haswell OpenGL (`ig75icd64.dll` on Intel Iris Pro 5200 #2850 / HD Graphics 4600 #2246), keeping `WS_THICKFRAME` and `WS_EX_WINDOWEDGE` on an undecorated window leaves a 7 px non-client sizing border (`WINDOWINFO.cxWindowBorders = 7, cyWindowBorders = 7`) that offsets the WGL surface by `(7, 7)` px relative to pointer input and inflates maximized windows beyond `rcWork`. In addition, because winit 0.30 swallows `WM_NCCALCSIZE(wparam = 1)` when `MARKER_DECORATIONS` is false, `DefWindowProcW(WM_NCCALCSIZE)` (`xxxCalcClientRect` in `win32kfull.sys`) never runs after `WS_CAPTION` is stripped — leaving the kernel's internal `WFCPRESENT` flag set on `tagWND` so `WM_NCACTIVATE` and `SetWindowTextW` still paint the classic Windows Basic caption bar (`[icon] PhotoCraft [-] [□] [X]`) over the top bar.

```diff
 window_frame::service(cc, custom_titlebar)
+  send_viewport_cmd(ViewportCommand::Decorations(true))
+    # winit forwards WM_NCCALCSIZE(wparam=1) to DefWindowProcW and clears MARKER_UNDECORATED_SHADOW
   on each frame (raw_input_hook)
-    strip WS_CAPTION | WS_BORDER (kept WS_THICKFRAME | WS_EX_WINDOWEDGE -> 7px border & WFCPRESENT=1)
+    resizing = primary_mouse_button_down() && pointer_pressing_resize_zone(8pt)
+    strip WS_CAPTION | WS_BORDER | WS_THICKFRAME(!resizing) and WS_EX_WINDOWEDGE
+    if maximized && rcWindow != monitor.rcWork
+      SetWindowPos(rcWork, SWP_FRAMECHANGED | SWP_NOZORDER | SWP_NOACTIVATE)
+    else if style_dirty
+      SetWindowPos(SWP_FRAMECHANGED | SWP_NOMOVE | SWP_NOSIZE | SWP_NOZORDER | SWP_NOACTIVATE)
+        -> DefWindowProcW(WM_NCCALCSIZE) clears WFCPRESENT=0 and sets rcClient == rcWindow
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** On Windows 10 (Intel Iris Pro Graphics 5200, OpenGL, 1920×1080 with top taskbar `rcWork = (0, 30, 1920, 1080)`):
  ```text
  Normal:    style=0x160F0000 ex=0x00040110 borders=(7,7) win=(240,90,1680,990) cli=(240,91,1680,991…

title: fix(ui): a launch does not restore the Brush Settings window (#3548)
author: dottedt
body:
Fixes #3548.

My first pass said this wasn't reproducible — I was wrong, and the reporter's repro (open Brush Settings from the options-bar toggle, quit, relaunch) pinned it: Workspace > Remember Workspace Changes persists `prefs.panel_layout`, which is `dock::snapshot`, and its `panels` object held every flag including the floating `brush_settings`. On the next launch `dock::restore` applied it, so the window came back with nothing open.

This drops `brush_settings` from the snapshot and ignores it when restoring a layout (older saved layouts that carry it are handled too), so the workspace still remembers the real dock panels and layout but the transient Brush Settings window is never restored.

Test: `dock::tests::restoring_a_saved_layout_never_reopens_brush_settings`. Full `photocraft-ui-egui` suite (2077) passes; fmt and clippy clean.

title: History Options: Automatically Create First Snapshot, New Snapshot When Saving, Show New Snapshot Dialog by Default (#2966)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #2966. The three snapshot options of History panel ☰ › History Options… that #3535 leaves out, as in Photoshop:

- **Automatically Create First Snapshot** (default on): a new or opened document starts with a snapshot of itself, named after it; off, it starts without one (the camera's first snapshot is still "Snapshot 1").
- **Automatically Create New Snapshot When Saving** (default off): each save of the document to its own file adds a snapshot of it as saved, named with the local time (`HH:MM:SS`). Not a history state, and the document stays clean. A flat export is a copy and adds none. Hooked into both the GUI's save job and the headless `doc.save`; the web build has no local clock and names it "Snapshot N".
- **Show New Snapshot Dialog by Default** (default off): a plain click on the camera button opens New Snapshot, as ⌥-click does.

Each is a preference agents can set and read (`history.options`, `prefs.set historyOptions.*`, `ui.inspect`), next to the two options from #3535. The dialog shows all five in Photoshop's order (a new `__order` key for form dialogs, since the field map is sorted by key).

**Builds on #3567, please merge that first.** Until #3567 and #3535 land, the diff includes them; this PR's own change is c39de363. I'll rebase once they're in.

title: HEIF: move the heic-rs pin from 0.1.1 to 0.1.4
author: s17sh70x2jfl031ag
body:
heic-rs 0.1.2 to 0.1.4 fix six panics on malformed files, which I found by fuzzing and reported privately upstream (credited in the [heic-rs changelog](https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)). Four panic in release builds: a `uuid` box too small for its extended type, a block starting right of the picture, a conformance window larger than the picture, and a reference row below the picture. Two only panic with overflow checks on: a PCM bit depth above the sample bit depth, and a slice QP out of range. heic-rs reports the API, MSRV and output as unchanged.

On native, `guarded()` already turns these panics into errors. The web build enables `heif`, though, and wasm32 aborts on panic (as the root `Cargo.toml` notes), so there a malformed HEIC file could take down the tab. With 0.1.4 the decoder returns an error instead.

**The change:** both exact pins move to `=0.1.4`: `crates/heif` and the codecs fuzz target, which calls heic-rs directly (leaving that one at 0.1.1 would stop the fuzz target building). `Cargo.lock` changes only heic-rs. `guarded()` and its comments stay: they describe 0.1.1 and remain a useful backstop.

**Checked**, as the pin comment asks:
- **HEIF corpus tests** (`cargo xtask corpus --heif`; codecs and io with `corpus,heif`, plus `photocraft-heif`): 20 passed on 0.1.1 and the same 20 on 0.1.4, including the comparisons with Apple's decodes.
- **Fuzz targets:** `decode_heif` and `decode_any` build on 0.1.4. All 397 crashing inputs my earlier fuzzing collected on 0.1.1 run clean through both, and a fresh 5-minute run of each (1.1 million inputs) found nothing.

title: Crop tool: a resized frame snaps its handle, not the pointer (#3638)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #3638 (split out of #1919).

When you resize the crop frame with View › Snap on, the snap line can show on an edge while the frame stops a few pixels away from it. This happens with Auto Center Preview off and in Classic Mode, whenever the handle isn't grabbed exactly. A recrop over hidden pixels (Delete Cropped Pixels off) then commits a transparent strip. In Photoshop the frame edge lands on the edge it snaps to.

### Change
- `snap_ui::live_crop_handle` → `crop_handle` now covers every crop resize, not just Auto Center Preview ones. It snaps the handle of the frame `crop_ui` would build (`crop_mode::resized_frame` with Auto Center, `crop_ui::resized_turned` without), then moves the pointer by the difference: 1:1 without Auto Center, 2:1 with it (1:1 with Alt).
- The corner formula for a held ratio uses the matching growth factor (both sides with Auto Center or Alt, otherwise only the grabbed side).
- Before, resizes without Auto Center fell back to `snap_point(pointer)`, so the frame missed the target by the grab offset (up to the 8 px grab radius).

### Tests
- New `crop_mode::tests::a_recrop_handle_snaps_exactly_to_the_hidden_pixels_edge`: Delete Cropped Pixels off, crop, then recrop outward to the hidden edge. It covers Classic on/off × Auto Center on/off × right/top edge, top-left/bottom-right corner × grab offset −4/0/+4 px, plus the corners with the original ratio held. It checks the frame lands exactly on the edge, the committed size, and that the layer bounds match the new canvas (no transparent strip). On main, 24 of 32 combinations failed; all pass with this change.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests crop`: 102 passed
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib snap`: 28 passed
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean

### Not verified
- Turned frames (angle ≠ 0) in Classic Mode now also go through handle snapping. The maths is the one the Auto Center path already…

title: fix(linux): avoid duplicate AppImage desktop launcher (#3623)
author: Korg1ch
body:
Closes #3623

## Summary

When a user runs the PhotoCraft AppImage on a system with an external AppImage integrator (`AppImageLauncher`, `appimaged`, `Gear Lever`), two launchers appear in the application menu: one created by the external integrator and one created by `packaging/linux/AppRun` (#617).

```diff
 packaging/linux/ai.storyteller.photocraft.desktop
+  X-AppImage-Integrate=false

 packaging/linux/AppRun :: integrate()
-  write $XDG_DATA_HOME/applications/ai.storyteller.photocraft.desktop
+  if $DESKTOPINTEGRATION is set OR another $apps/*.desktop Exec= references $appimage
+    rm -f $apps/ai.storyteller.photocraft.desktop (clean up existing duplicate)
+  else
+    write $apps/ai.storyteller.photocraft.desktop
   install hicolor icons into $XDG_DATA_HOME/icons/hicolor
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** Running `AppRun` alongside an `AppImageLauncher` entry (`appimagekit-photocraft.desktop`) kept both `.desktop` files in `$XDG_DATA_HOME/applications`, and the packaged `.desktop` lacked `X-AppImage-Integrate=false`.
  **After:** `bash packaging/linux/apprun-test.sh` passes all 11 checks (including external `.desktop` deduplication, `DESKTOPINTEGRATION=AppImageLauncher`, and `X-AppImage-Integrate=false`):
  ```text
  $ sh -n packaging/linux/AppRun && bash -n packaging/linux/apprun-test.sh && bash packaging/linux/apprun-test.sh
  AppRun desktop integration ok
  ```

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Self-contained in `packaging/linux/` (`AppRun`, `ai.storyteller.photocraft.desktop`, `apprun-test.sh`).

**Blast Radius:** low

Affects only Linux AppImage desktop-entry integration; hicolor icons are still installed so Wayland compositors and external `.desktop` launchers resolve `Icon=ai.storyteller.photocraft`.

author: buivanvu94
body:

title: Stroke layer effect: the outer edge stays round at wide sizes (#3646)
author: dottedt
body:
The layer stroke's outer edge came from a 5x5 chamfer distance transform whose level sets are polygons (an ~8-fold octagon), so a wide stroke showed flat facets and the boundary wandered by about 10 px at 245 px. The outer edge now uses the exact Euclidean distance transform; the inside edge keeps the chamfer, whose sub-pixel edge seeding is fitted to Photoshop at small offsets.

The first commit was CPU only, but the canvas is drawn on the GPU, which built the outer stroke field from the same chamfer and stayed facetted on screen. The second commit adds FieldKind::StrokeOutsideExact, used only by the stroke. The spread of drop shadows and softer outer glows keeps the chamfer on purpose (fitted to Photoshop, #224); precise glows and chiselled bevels already used the exact transform.

Test: `a_raster_stroke_uses_the_exact_outer_field` (crates/gpu/src/fx.rs); `cargo test -p photocraft-compose --lib` (206 passed) and `cargo test -p photocraft-gpu --lib` (25 passed).

Closes #3646.

title: PSD: composite_rgba8 checks the output budget and converts planes fallibly (#3639)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3639

Root cause: `Layer::rgba8` rejects `n*4 > MAX_DECODED_BYTES` up front, but `PsdFile::composite_rgba8` did not: it decoded the merged image and converted every plane first. `plane_to_u8` and `unpack_bits` also allocated infallibly (abort, not Err) and multiplied `width*height` unchecked.

Fix: same output guard at the top of `composite_rgba8`; `plane_to_u8`/`unpack_bits` use checked arithmetic and `try_reserve_exact` and return `LimitExceeded`. `unpack_bits` now returns `Result` (only caller was `plane_to_u8`).

Scenario: a 60000x60000 1-bit PSB (RGBA 14.4 GB) is refused before decoding; absurd plane sizes give Err instead of a capacity panic.

Tests: `composite_rgba8_checks_the_output_budget_first` (fails without the guard: verified by removing it), `plane_conversion_reports_absurd_sizes` (panicked/aborted with the old infallible allocation).

Commands: `cargo test -p photocraft-psd`, `cargo xtask test-corpus -p photocraft-psd -p photocraft-io`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-psd --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p photocraft-psd -- --check`, `cargo xtask wasm`, `cargo xtask layers`.

title: PSD: don't preallocate knots from untrusted path length counts (#3635)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3635

Root cause: `PathData::subpaths()` did `Vec::with_capacity(remaining.min(4096))` per length record, with the count an untrusted u16 and PsdKnot 56 bytes (~229 KB each). `from_bytes` allows 4M records, so a ~2 MB vmsk/vsms block of consecutive length records (count 0xFFFF) reserves ~15 GB and `with_capacity` aborts the process.

Fix: no preallocation; knots grow as knot records are parsed.

Tests: `subpaths_does_not_preallocate_from_untrusted_counts` (100k length records, count 0xFFFF; asserts zero capacity). Fails with the old code, passes now.

title: fix(engine): Displace smart filter ignores its mapPath displacement map (#3670)
author: horknfbr
body:
Fixes #3670

## What's wrong
A Displace applied to a smart object is rendered through `apply_smart_filters` → `filters::apply_filter_to_surface`, which built `FilterParams` with `params_for` alone. Displace's map stayed `None`, so the smart filter was a silent no-op, on the first render and on every re-render. Only `run_filter` resolved `mapPath`, and that result was thrown away.

## Change
- `filters_ext::map_from_path`: the existing `mapPath` read and import, factored out of `resolve`.
- `filters_ext::resolve_map_path`: a new session-free path that uses the same function, called from `apply_filter_to_surface`. There is now one code path for reading the map, not two.
- A map that can no longer be read on re-render leaves the pixels alone, as for an unknown filter id. The command still returns `Err` for an unreadable map when the filter is added.
- `mapDocument` needs the session and is still unresolved on re-render; see the note in #3670.

## Tests
`smart_cmds::tests::displace_smart_filter_reads_its_map_path_on_re_render` runs at 8, 16 and 32 bit. It converts a layer to a smart object, applies Displace with a white map, asserts the pixels moved, then hides the filter (pixels unchanged) and shows it again (moved again). It fails on `main` at the first assertion.

## Checks run (macOS arm64)
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests`: all pass except `adjust_params::tests::destructive_levels_dont_clip_in_32_bit`, which also fails on `main`.
- `panic_hunt -- --ignored`: pass.
- `xtask layers`, `xtask wasm`, `fmt --check`: pass.
- clippy `-D warnings` on engine with stable (1.99): clean. With 1.95 it stops on existing lints in other crates.

title: PSD: smart object Trnf frames the custom warp's control points, not the source rect (#3671)
author: horknfbr
body:
Fixes #3671. Refs #579.

## What's wrong
For a `warpCustom` placement, Photoshop's `Trnf` is the image of the custom warp's **control-point bounding box**. PhotoCraft mapped the source rect onto it, so a mesh that spills past the source counted the overhang twice and the smart object re-rendered stretched. Export wrote `Trnf` from the source rect too, so saving such a file shifted its quad.

## Change
- `blocks::placed_frame`: the rule in one place. It returns the control-point box of a single-patch custom warp; anything else uses the source rect. A box with no area or non-finite values also falls back to the source rect.
- `blocks::parse_smart` (and therefore `smart_map::parse_sold`): maps that frame onto `Trnf`.
- `smart_map::quad_points`: export writes `Trnf` and `PlLd` from the same frame, so a spilled mesh round-trips and `quad_moved` keeps the imported quad.
- Distort and Perspective placements are unchanged.

## Measured
On a real shirt mockup, compared with Photoshop's render of the same Replace Contents:
- **`main`:** about a 1.6% vertical stretch.
- **This PR:** exact alignment, RMSE 0.49%.
- **Warp-outline box instead of control points:** 5.4% RMSE on another file.

## Tests
- `blocks::more_tests::smart_transform_maps_the_warp_control_box_onto_the_quad` (fails on `main`)
- `blocks::more_tests::smart_transform_with_a_degenerate_warp_box_uses_the_source_rect`
- `smart_map::tests::warp_control_box_quad_round_trips` (the export side fails on `main`)

## Checks run (macOS arm64)
- `cargo test -p photocraft-io --lib --tests`: pass.
- `--features corpus` on psd, codecs and io: 1391 passed, 0 failed.
- `xtask layers`, `xtask wasm`, `fmt --check`: pass.
- clippy `-D warnings` on io: clean with `--no-deps`. The full run stops on an existing `collapsible_match` in `affinity/src/preview.rs:98`.

title: fix(algo): mesh warps filter their source when shrinking, so thin lines don't alias (#3672)
author: horknfbr
body:
Fixes #3672

## What's wrong
`warp_triangles` took one Catmull-Rom sample per output pixel with no minification filter. Mesh warps that shrink their source alias thin lines. The affine path already pre-reduces below 50%; the mesh path had nothing equivalent.

## Change
- Each triangle now carries its inverse-map Jacobian, computed from its vertices.
- Where a triangle shrinks the source, each output pixel averages `nx × ny` bilinear subsamples over its source footprint: about one per source pixel per axis, anisotropic, capped at 8. Averaging is done on premultiplied values.
- Triangles that keep or enlarge the source still take the exact single sample, so identity and unscaled warps are bit-for-bit unchanged.
- The per-tile read region grows by the subsamples' actual spread.
- The filter is per pixel rather than one global pre-reduce, because a mesh warp's scale varies across the surface.

## Measured
- **Against Photoshop renders of real mockups,** with an earlier cut of this approach: RMSE 1.78% → 0.81% and 0.49% → 0.29%.
- **Performance:** 30 MP source, Arc 10, release build:

| Placed size | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 1/3 | 55 ms | 87 ms |
| 1/1 | 240 ms | 239 ms |

## Tests
`warp::tests::a_shrinking_mesh_warp_is_prefiltered` runs at 8, 16 and 32 bit. A 1 px grid every 4 px is placed at 1/5 size through an Arc warp.
- On `main` it is 0.5625 off the area average.
- With this PR it is 0.20 off, the limit for that footprint.

## Checks run (macOS arm64)
- `cargo test -p photocraft-algo --lib --tests`: pass.
- Engine lib tests: all pass except the levels test that also fails on `main`.
- `xtask layers`, `xtask wasm`: pass.
- clippy: `warp.rs` is clean. There is an existing `nonminimal_bool` at `algo/src/transform.rs:173`.

title: feat(io): import Photoshop Displace smart filters with their embedded map (#3673)
author: horknfbr
body:
Fixes #3673

## What's wrong
Displace smart filters (`Dspl`) imported as `psd.unsupportedFilter` and passed through on re-render, so mockups that bend a replaceable design over fabric rendered flat.

## Change
- New `io::displace_map`: parses the filter's settings and the embedded map in `DspD`. The map is a u32 LE height, u32 LE width and u16 LE mode 3, then horizontal and vertical 8-bit planes.

- **Storage:** following the Camera Raw pattern, the whole item, map included, is kept as hex in `__displacePsd`. So it re-renders, survives `.pcraft`, and is written back to PSD with only the editable settings and blending replaced. An unedited filter round-trips byte-identical.
- `engine::filters_ext::params_for` resolves the embedded map. Smart filters already pass the document rectangle as the bounds, so the map is stretched over the canvas, as Photoshop does.
- **Defensive parsing:** checked sizes, maps capped at 2^26 pixels. Another mode, a missing or truncated map, or unknown enum values keep the item opaque, as before.
- Independent of #3670's fix; that one only fills a map when none is set.

## Tests
- `displace_map` unit tests: layout, every truncation length, hostile and corrupted headers (512 corrupted blobs, no panics), round trip, edited settings, opaque fallbacks, bad exports.
- `smart_psd::displace_psd_filter_renders_with_its_embedded_map` at 8, 16 and 32 bit: renders displaced, and PSD export → import and `.pcraft` both keep it.

title: PSD: bound the zero padding of undersized pattern channels (#3652)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3652

Root cause: a pattern channel whose rectangle is smaller than the pattern rectangle is zero-padded to the full pattern plane, but the input-size check only compares the small channel size with the data. The only cap was `MAX_DECODED_BYTES` (8 GiB) summed over up to 66 channels.

Scenario: a few-hundred-byte pattern declaring 30000x30000 with 1x1 (or 5x3) channels allocated gigabytes of zeros.

Fix: new named budget `MAX_PADDED_PATTERN_BYTES` (512 MiB, same as `abr::MAX_TOTAL_BYTES`) summed over channels that need padding. Channels written at the pattern rectangle, which is what Photoshop writes, never count, so real files are unaffected (corpus run green). The 8 GiB check still runs first; the two existing huge-rect tests now accept either `LimitExceeded` since the smaller budget can trip first.

Tests: `tiny_channels_in_a_huge_pattern_rect_are_not_zero_padded_without_bound` (fails without the check: verified by disabling it).

Commands: `cargo test -p photocraft-psd`, `cargo xtask test-corpus -p photocraft-psd -p photocraft-io`, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt --check, `cargo xtask wasm`, `cargo xtask layers`.

title: fix(transform): keep nearest-neighbor previews on original texels
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Free Transform can display blurry previews when Nearest Neighbor interpolation is selected and the image is scaled down.

At small preview scales, the renderer chooses a downsampled mipmap even when Nearest Neighbor is active. This causes adjacent pixels to be averaged before the preview is drawn.

For pixel art and other images with sharp pixel boundaries, the preview can therefore look smoother than the selected interpolation mode should produce.

## Root Cause

`PreviewTextures::choose` selects a mip level based on the effective screen-space scale before checking whether Nearest Neighbor interpolation is enabled.

The mipmaps are generated through 2×2 box filtering. Once the source pixels have been averaged, selecting the nearest texel cannot recover their original values.

## Changes

- Keep Nearest Neighbor previews on the full-resolution texture (level 0).
- Apply nearest sampling directly to the original available texels.
- Preserve mipmap selection for other interpolation modes when minifying.
- Add regression assertions for 25% zoom and extreme downscaling.

## Validation

- Reviewed the updated sampling logic and regression assertions.
- Verified the pushed branch against the latest upstream main.
- Confirmed the branch contains only the intended `transform_tex.rs` changes.
- Added two regression assertions covering Nearest Neighbor sampling at reduced scales.
- Rust unit tests and formatting checks were not executed because the Rust toolchain was unavailable.
- CI validation remains pending.

## Compatibility

This change only affects texture-level selection for Nearest Neighbor transform previews. Other interpolation modes retain their existing mipmap behavior.

title: fix(ui): Free Transform frames a smart object by its placement (#3649)
author: dottedt
body:
Fixes #3649.

After confirming a rotation on a Smart Object, re-opening Free Transform drew an axis-aligned box around the rotated pixels instead of following the content (see the issue's two screenshots).

The transform session's reference frame was an axis-aligned `rect`, and `begin()` derived it from the rendered content bounds — which lose the placement's rotation. The session now carries an optional `from` quad; `begin()` seeds it from the smart object's placement applied to its recorded source size, and the commit maps frame → quad with the new `Homography::quad_to_quad`, so the delta is applied exactly once.

`SmartObject` gains `source_size`, recorded on File › Place and mapped through the `.pcraft` format; older files default to `None` and keep the previous bounds-based frame. Everything else (`from == rect` corners) is unchanged, so other transforms, selections, paths and warp behave as before.

Test: `smart_cmds::tests::frame_quad_follows_a_rotated_placement_and_from_quad_composes_the_delta`. Suites: algo 466, format (all targets), io roundtrip 36, engine 1288, ui-egui 2084; fmt and clippy clean.

title: Levels: Alt turns Cancel into Reset, Alt-drag clipping display (#3328)
author: funkvay-star
body:
Part of #3328. This is the Alt-drag clipping display. Alt+Cancel → Reset for Levels comes from #3871, so I took my Levels-specific Reset out of this PR. The eyedroppers landed in #3128.

## What changed

**Alt-dragging the black or white Input slider shows the clipping display.** This is Photoshop's threshold view.
- With the black slider the image turns white and every channel that gets clipped to black drops to 0. A pixel clipped in all three channels shows black, a pixel clipped only in red shows cyan.
- With the white slider the image turns black and clipped channels go to 255. Red alone shows red, all three show white.
- Grayscale documents only show black and white.

Let go of Alt or the mouse and the normal preview comes back. Nothing changes in the document until OK, and OK applies only the Levels values.

A channel counts as clipped when an Input slider flattens it, either in its own channel or in the composite. Gamma and Output Levels don’t affect the display, it follows the input sliders.

The display reads the target layer's own pixels inside the selection and is drawn as a texture over the visible part of the image at roughly screen resolution. If any pixel under a texel is clipped, the texel shows it, so a single clipped highlight doesn't disappear when you zoom out.

**For agents.** The control channel can't hold Alt during a drag, so `ui.dialog.set {"field": "__clipping", "value": "shadows" | "highlights"}` turns the display on. It's documented in docs/control-protocol.md, and the field never reaches OK.

**Choices I couldn't check against Photoshop**
- With a selection, only pixels that are at least half selected count.
- The display shows even with Preview off.
- It covers the whole image, including layers above the target.
- A per-channel gamma below 1 that rounds a level to black shows as clipped, even with the composite black point at 0.

title: PSD: cap descriptor list/object preallocation from untrusted counts (#3636)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3636

Root cause: `read_descriptor` and the `obj ` / `VlLs` readers did `Vec::with_capacity(n)` with n straight from the file. `check_count` only demands 10/8/4 bytes per item while parsed items are ~100/~80 bytes, so large tdta/lfx2/SoLd blocks reserved 10-20x their size up front, and `with_capacity` aborts rather than returning an error.

Failure scenario: a list declaring n = remaining/4 items reserves n * sizeof(Value) up front.

Fix: `vec_for_count` caps the preallocation at 4096 items; vectors still grow as items parse. UnFl (f64, exactly 8 bytes/item) is unchanged.

Tests: `declared_counts_do_not_drive_preallocation` (helper cap with n = u32::MAX, plus a 1M-item VlLs still parses). Without the cap the test process aborts with `memory allocation of 343597383600 bytes failed`.

title: Generative Fill: three variations to choose from, and fills that blend in (#41)
author: texjer
body:
TLDR:

**Depends on #2878 and #2879**: this branch is #2879 plus six commits (from "three variations to choose from" on); review only those until the two below it land, then I'll rebase.

Generative Fill now makes **three variations** to choose between, as the spec linked from #41 proposes, and the fill blends into the photo instead of leaving a seam or redrawing what was selected.

## Variations

- `edit.generativeFill` takes `variations` (1–4, default 3) and asks the provider once per variation, in parallel in one cancellable job (sequential on the web). Failed calls are dropped while any succeed.

- `layer.generative.selectVariation` shows one variation (one undo step); `layer.generative.more` resends the same request and adds the results. Automation may not run `more`, as with Generative Fill.
- Properties shows a generative layer's variations as thumbnails with **Generate More**. The settings text says each fill sends three billed requests.

## Fill quality

Tried against real photos with Gemini; each fix answers a failure seen there.

- **The selection is blurred out before sending** (push-pull fill of the colours around it), so the model can't copy what was there and an empty prompt removes the selected object. Flat grey was tried first and was drawn in as objects.

The area outside the selection should come back unchanged, so it measures the change: a tone curve on brightness (hue kept), fitted without the pixels whose detail the model changed, then the remaining edge difference carried inward by push-pull (`match_surroundings`).

title: Codecs: refuse implausible PNG/WebP headers before allocating (#3691)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3691

Root cause: PNG and WebP sized the output buffer from the header and allocated it (`vec![0u8; size]`) before any data was checked. A ~100 byte PNG declaring 32768x32768 RGBA16 equals the default `max_alloc` (8 GiB), passes the limits and asks for 8 GiB up front. On Windows, low-RAM machines and wasm32 a failed allocation aborts (not a panic), so the shell's catch_unwind cannot save the document. Only TIFF had a plausibility guard.

Fix:
- `Limits::check_plausible(declared_bytes, file_len, max_ratio)` (+1 MiB slack): PNG uses 1100:1 on the stored sample bytes (zlib tops out at 1032:1), WebP a generous 65536:1.
- `alloc_zeroed` (fallible `try_reserve_exact`) for the PNG and WebP output buffers.
- 32-bit/wasm32 default `max_alloc` lowered from 2 GiB to 1 GiB (4 GiB address space shared with document, history and decoder buffers).

title: PSD: avoid cloning layer data when padding and presize the output buffer (#3687)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3687

Root cause: `ImageSourceData::to_bytes` cloned the whole `LayerInfo` (every channel's pixel data) only to call `pad_to`, and `PsdFile::to_bytes` grew its output from an empty Vec.

Changes:
- `LayerInfo::pad_len` computes the padding from `unpadded_len` on `&self`; `write_unpadded` writes the body without padding; `write_body` is now `write_unpadded` plus its padding. `pad_to` uses `pad_len`. The TIFF writer writes the original and appends the zeros: one full pixel-data copy less per layered TIFF save.
- `PsdFile::to_bytes` and the TIFF layer block reserve the channel/image data size up front (`try_reserve`, saturating arithmetic, `LimitExceeded` on failure) instead of doubling reallocations.

Behaviour-preserving. No benchmarks (the machine is too loaded to measure); this is justified by reasoning: it removes a full copy and repeated regrow-and-copy cycles.

Tests: `unpadded_write_matches_pad_to_on_a_clone` compares the new path byte for byte with the old clone + `pad_to` + `write_body` route for PSD/PSB, 8/16/32-bit, Raw/RLE and alignments 1/2/4/8; the existing round-trip and TIFF tests and the corpus run still pass. Not a bug fix, so no fail-without proof.

title: Codecs: bound the TIFF IFD walk by a file-size entry budget (#3683)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3683

**Root cause:** the IFD walk's seen-set keys on the directory offset only. A ~800 KB file with 10,000 directories 4 bytes apart, each declaring 65,535 (overlapping) entries, parsed ~6.5e8 entries per walk, and the walk runs several times per decode.

**Fix:** `Walk` carries an entry budget of `file_len/12 + 64`; the declared count is peeked before a table is parsed, and the walk ends early (`complete == false`) when the budget is exhausted. Real tables are disjoint, so normal files are unaffected.

**Tests:** `tiff_ifd::tests::overlapping_directory_tables_exhaust_the_entry_budget` (synthetic file, asserts <200 directories parsed and incomplete; fails without the fix: 10000 parsed).

title: Select the Normal RGB blend kernel once per buffer
author: Streetblock
body:
CPU compositing checks the thread-local Lab context for every contributing Normal pixel. In the audited Windows GNU build this puts shared synchronization in the pixel loop and hurts parallel scaling.

Select the Normal RGB kernel once per buffer when gamma is 1 and Lab mixing is disabled. Share the existing straight-alpha formula without changing arithmetic order, alpha skips or opacity handling. Lab, other gamma values, Dissolve, other blend modes and special Fill keep their existing paths.

Three regressions cover an independent scalar oracle, buffer dispatch and fallbacks at U8/U16/F32, alpha edge cases and nested Lab/HDR scopes.

Measured complete `render_reduced` calls on a 6000×4000 document with four semitransparent patterned Normal layers (56×37 output):

| Depth | Workers | Upstream median | Fixed median | Paired repetitions |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| U8 | 1 | 12.257 s | 2.903 s | 5 |
| U8 | 4 | 18.501 s | 1.668 s | 5 |
| U16 | 4 | 18.035 s | 2.847 s | 3 |
| F32 | 4 | 21.845 s | 3.160 s | 3 |

All timings alternate AB/BA order. Every reduced output is bit-exact against the baseline, and twelve additional complete 64×48 RGB/Lab and depth/blend controls are bit-exact. This does not claim a bit comparison over every full-resolution 24 MP pixel. U8 scaling from one to four workers changes from 0.663× to 1.741× using these medians.

Separate U8 memory processes show practically unchanged peak process commit: 242.547 → 242.648 MiB (+0.04%, one process per variant, three timed calls each). This patch saves CPU time, not a demonstrated amount of memory.

Measurement scope: the tables above compare this optimization independently against `f8af27d2618c48575f80a71a79cd795931b5020f`. They were collected before the rebase and have not been remeasured on the current main base. title: Allow empty vector masks in downsampled preview proxies
author: Streetblock
body:
An enabled vector mask disables the downsampled preview proxy even when its path is empty. A large thumbnail then composites the entire source resolution. Empty paths have constant coverage and no bounds that can anchor fill layouts.

Allow truly empty vector-mask paths through the existing proxy guard. Preserve inversion, density, feathering and U16 mask quantization. Nonempty paths remain excluded even at density zero, because their geometry can affect gradient frames. Effects and size thresholds keep their guards.

Six regressions cover all three depths, empty subpaths, inversion/density/feathering, pixel-mask multiplication, gradient frames, effects/geometry guards and the large-thumbnail branch.

Measured complete `thumbnail_buffer` calls on a 6000×4000 U8 document with four uniform layers and an enabled empty, density-zero mask (four workers, three AB/BA pairs per size):

| Maximum side | Upstream median | Fixed median |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 56 | 19.104 s | 33.312 ms |
| 512 | 19.307 s | 861.563 ms |

The fixed masked output is bit-exact against the existing eligible no-mask proxy. Versus the old full-resolution reduction, RGBA8 pixels match in this uniform fixture, but float bits differ (maximum absolute differences 7.96e-5 and 1.07e-6). title: fix(text): scale faux bold dilation with glyph scaling (#3705)
author: nicolasfalesy
body:
Fixes #3705

### Root cause
In `crates/text/src/render.rs`, faux-bold glyph dilation was calculated as `Xform([1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, ox * r, oy * r]).mul(&glyph)`. Because `Xform::mul(&self, o)` performs `self ∘ o` (applying `o` first), the translation offset `(ox * r, oy * r)` was added after the glyph transform, applying the offset directly in text space rather than font-local coordinates.

When glyphs have horizontal or vertical scaling (`HorizontalScale` / `VerticalScale` in PSD `EngineData`, as reported in #3705 with 0.62 / 0.6 scaling), the dilation was not scaled down with the glyph, resulting in faux bold strokes appearing ~1.7× too heavy compared to Photoshop.

### Fix
Compose the glyph transform first: `glyph.mul(&Xform([1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, ox * r, oy * r]))`. This applies the dilation offset before glyph scaling, so dilation scales proportionally with `horizontal_scale` and `vertical_scale`.

### Tests
- Added regression test `faux_bold_scales_with_glyph_scaling` in `crates/text/src/tests.rs` verifying that horizontal and vertical dilation bounds scale proportionally with 2x horizontal and vertical font scaling.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-text --lib` (123 passed, 0 failed)
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-text --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean)
- `cargo fmt --check` (clean)
- `cargo xtask layers` (clean)

title: Codecs: decode only the requested EXR part (#3721)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3721

Root cause: `exr::read_layer` used `all_layers()` and then `nth(index)`, so every part of a multi-part file was decompressed and held to return one (the io layer calls it once per selected part/group, so a 40-AOV file was decoded 40 times). `exr_cryptomatte::decode` did the same and only checked each part against `Limits` separately, bypassing the cumulative `read_meta` cap. The `exr` crate's `rayon` feature was off, so block decompression was single-threaded natively.

Fix:
- `read_layer` uses `first_valid_layer` through a small `ReadChannels` wrapper that declines every header but the requested one; other parts' chunks are skipped unread and their planes never allocated.
- Cryptomatte decode goes through `read_meta` (cumulative cap) and the shared `read_layer`.
- `exr/rayon` enabled in the `cfg(not(wasm32))` dependency table only (`cargo tree --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` shows no exr rayon; Cargo.lock gains only the rayon-core edge).

Tests: `decoding_one_part_does_not_decode_the_others` (crates/codecs/tests/exr_multipart.rs) writes a 2-part ZIP1 file and overwrites part 0's chunks with garbage; part 1 must decode, part 0 must error. Fails without the fix (verified by stashing src).

title: Answer a repeat auth with "already authenticated" (#3668)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Sending `auth` a second time on a connection that had already authenticated went to the normal method dispatcher, which doesn't know `auth`. The headless `serve` TCP server answered ``unknown method `auth` (try `methods`)`` and the desktop control server answered ``unknown method `auth` `` (after a round trip through the UI thread). The `methods` hint made it worse, because on a fresh connection `methods` only gets `authentication required`.

Both TCP loops now call a new shared helper, `security::repeat_auth_reply`, before they dispatch. If the frame is an `auth` call it replies `{"id": <same id>, "ok": false, "error": "already authenticated"}` and the connection stays open. Any other frame is dispatched as before. I added one sentence about it to the auth section of docs/control-protocol.md. Stdio `serve` has no handshake, so I didn't change it.

Tests, each written first and seen failing:
- `security::tests::repeat_auth_on_an_authenticated_connection_says_so` (the helper)
- `rpc::tests::tcp_repeat_auth_reports_already_authenticated_and_keeps_serving` (headless TCP: auth twice, then `methods` still works)
- `control_server::tests::repeat_auth_reports_already_authenticated_without_dispatching` (desktop: the repeat auth never reaches the UI dispatcher, and the next request is still served)

Gate: I ran a scoped gate locally, not the full `cargo xtask ci`: fmt check, clippy -D warnings and tests for photocraft-automation and photocraft, plus `cargo xtask wasm` and `cargo xtask layers`. Everything passed except `bridge_reports_unreachable_app`. In my sandbox, connecting to 127.0.0.1:1 times out instead of being refused, and this change doesn't touch that code. The full workspace run is left to CI. I didn't try this by hand against a running desktop app.

Fixes #3668

title: Codecs: integer fast paths for Image::convert (#3717)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3717

## What / why
`Image::convert` went through `to_normalized` (f32 Vec, 4 B/sample), `convert_layout` (second f32 Vec) and `quantize` for every depth or layout change except one. `converted()` in every encoder and `to_rgba8()` use it, so a 16-bit RGB document exported to 8-bit JPEG/PNG/BMP peaked at source + 4N + 4N + dest bytes, uncharged to Limits.

New `Image::convert_int_direct` (called from `convert`, nothing else in existing code touched) handles U8/U16 sources and targets where the result is a pure channel copy: same colour model (alpha added opaque or dropped, alpha copied otherwise) and gray to RGB(A). Depth conversion is `v*257` (U8 to U16) and `(v+128)/257` (U16 to U8). It writes straight into the destination, so both f32 buffers disappear. Everything else (F16/F32, RGB to gray luma, CMYK model changes) stays on the generic path unchanged. Not benchmarked (loaded machine); the gain is the removed 8 B/sample of temporaries and the per-sample float math.

## Equivalence
Output is bit-identical to the old route; the old f32 route is kept in the tests as the reference:
- exhaustive: all 256 U8 and all 65536 U16 values through U8/U16 x U8/U16 into Gray and Rgb;
- every source layout x every target layout x every sample type, with edge values (0, 1, 1/255, 254/255) plus random ones, incl. alpha 0/255. Mutating the rounding (`+127`) makes the exhaustive test fail.

## Overlap
Open #3121, #3123, #3124 (TIFF extra samples) edit only the `Metadata` struct in image.rs; this PR adds a method and tests, so no textual conflict expected.

title: fix(ui): anchor zoom to viewport center when pointer is on pasteboard (#3720)
author: nicolasfalesy
body:
Fixes #3720

### Root cause
In `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, `zoom_about()` anchored all zoom operations to the cursor position `p`, converting it into document coordinates via `xf.to_doc(p)`. When the pointer is on the pasteboard (outside the document image bounds), `xf.to_doc(p)` produces coordinates outside `[0..w, 0..h]`. As the user zooms in or out, `view.center` shifts to keep that empty space pinned under the cursor, which rapidly pushes the document canvas out of the viewport.

### Fix
In `zoom_about()`, if the document has valid dimensions (`w > 0 && h > 0`) and the pointer lies outside `0.0 <= doc_x <= w && 0.0 <= doc_y <= h`, anchor the zoom to the viewport center (`xf.rect.center()`) instead of the pasteboard cursor position. This keeps the canvas centered in the viewport while zooming, matching Photoshop's behavior. When the cursor is on the image, it continues to zoom into the exact point under the pointer.

### Tests
- Added regression test `zoom_about_with_pointer_on_pasteboard_anchors_to_viewport_center` in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` verifying that pasteboard pointers preserve `view.center` while document pointers remain under the cursor.
- Verified all `zoom_about` tests pass.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean)
- `cargo fmt --check` (clean)
- `cargo xtask layers` (clean)

title: Canvas: wheel/pinch zoom over the pasteboard keeps the image in view (#3720)
author: FredApps
body:
Fixes #3720

## Root cause
Wheel zoom (plain wheel with *Zoom with Scroll Wheel*, Alt+wheel otherwise) and trackpad pinch all arrive as `Wheel::Zoom` in `canvas.rs` and call `zoom_about` with the raw pointer position. When the pointer is on the gray pasteboard, the document point kept fixed lies outside the image, so each zoom-in notch slides the image away from the pointer. After a few notches it leaves the window. Ctrl+wheel only pans sideways, so it is not affected.

## Fix
New `wheel_anchor`: over the image the anchor is still the pointer, so nothing changes there. Off the image, the pointer's document position is clamped to the image bounds and that point (the nearest edge or corner) becomes the anchor. Because the clamp happens in document space, rotated and flipped views work too. The same rule covers zooming out and pinch, so all wheel and pinch zoom paths behave the same. The Overscroll-off view clamp (`scrollbars::clamp_view`) is left as it is.

## Tests
- `input_tests::wheel_zoom_over_the_pasteboard_keeps_the_image_in_view`: 20 notches from the pasteboard corner, with *Zoom with Scroll Wheel* on (plain wheel) and off (Alt+wheel), then a ×4 pinch. The image stays in view and its nearest corner stays under the pointer. **This test fails on main.**
- `input_tests::wheel_zoom_over_the_image_still_anchors_on_the_pointer`: no change over the image.
- `canvas::tests::wheel_anchor_is_the_pointer_over_the_image_and_the_nearest_image_point_off_it`: covers rotated and flipped views and an empty document.

title: Shape Arabic in fonts without OpenType positional features
author: diax7
body:
## Problem

The font Muna (`alfont_com_Muna.ttf`) renders every Arabic letter isolated in PhotoCraft, while LibreOffice joins them. "هذا النص العربي بخط Muna" in Muna at 96 pt:

Before:

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/diax7/photocraft/pr-assets/pr-assets/muna-before.png)

After:

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/diax7/photocraft/pr-assets/pr-assets/muna-after.png)

## Cause

Muna's GSUB has the `arab` script but only the features `jp78`, `liga`, `rlig` and `smpl`: no `init`, `medi`, `fina` or `isol`. Its `cmap` does map 150 Arabic Presentation Forms (U+FB50..U+FDFF, U+FE70..U+FEFF), including the lam-alef ligatures. HarfBuzz's Arabic shaper falls back to synthesising the positional forms and lam-alef ligatures from those presentation forms (`hb-ot-shaper-arabic-fallback.hh`), which is why LibreOffice joins the font. parley shapes with harfrust 0.12, whose `arabic_fallback_shape` returns false, so nothing joins.

## Fix

New module `crates/text/src/layout/arabic_fallback.rs`, applied after shaping and only for a run whose face has no `init`/`medi`/`fina`/`isol` GSUB feature (fonts that have them take the normal path and are untouched):

- Each Arabic letter's joining form (isolated, final, initial, medial) is computed from the paragraph text. Combining marks are transparent, ZWJ joins, ZWNJ and any other character break the join.
- The letter's glyph is replaced by the `cmap` glyph of its presentation form, using a table derived from HarfBuzz's `hb-ot-shaper-arabic-table.hh`. A letter the table does not list, or a form the font does not map, keeps its shaped glyph.
- Lam followed by alef, alef-madda, alef-hamza-above or alef-hamza-below becomes the lam-alef ligature (U+FEF5..U+FEFC) when the font maps it. The ligature takes the lam's glyph; the alef becomes the font's space glyph with its advance taken back.
- Clusters holding more than one letter (the font already ligated them) are left alone.

It works on glyphs, not text, so byte offsets, cl…

title: Menus: keep clear of the taskbar when Wayland hides the window position (#3737)
author: FredApps
body:
## What and why

On Linux under Wayland, long menus (Layer, View and Window in the report, and Filter, Image and Edit too) were sized to the whole window and ran under a bottom panel or taskbar. Their last items were hidden and unreachable.

**Root cause.** The menu-scrolling work (#160, #272) bounds each menu level by `work_area::visible_rect`, and #315 cuts that rect at the taskbar using the monitor size plus the window's position on the desktop (`ViewportInfo::inner_rect`). On Wayland, winit's `inner_position()`/`outer_position()` always fail, so egui-winit leaves `inner_rect` and `outer_rect` as `None`. `visible_part` then fell back to the whole window. `fit_window`, which maximizes a window that's too big for its monitor, also bailed out without an `outer_rect`. As a result, a window taller than the monitor minus the panel was never maximized, and its menus filled the window right down under the panel.

## The fix

`crates/ui-egui/src/work_area.rs`:
- `visible_part`: when the monitor size is known but the window's position isn't, the window's content can be seen at most down to the monitor height minus `TASKBAR`, wherever the window is. The content rect is cut to that, with the same sanity guard as before (`MIN_VISIBLE`). Maximized and full-screen windows, and an unknown monitor, still use the whole window.
- `fit_window`: when there's no `outer_rect`, the content size is used as the window's (lower-bound) size. So an oversized window on Wayland is maximized at startup too, like on X11 and Windows.

All menu levels, top-level and submenus, and the other popups that use `visible_rect` (e.g. the combo-box popups in `widgets.rs`) pick this up through the existing `level_room_in`/scroll-arrow path. No menu code changed.

## Tests

- `menu_nav_tests::reported_menus_stay_above_the_panel_when_the_window_position_is_unknown` (replaces the earlier scaffold, which passed on main): opens Layer, View, Window, Filter, Image and Edit at 1× and 1.5× in a 1366×740 window on a …

title: PSD: write kept 8B64 blocks as 8BIM so Photoshop opens PSB-derived files
author: MrCloudy2
body:
A PSD re-saved from a PSB kept the source's global `FMsk` and `cinf` blocks with their `8B64` signature. Photoshop 27.11 refuses such a file: "not compatible with this version of Photoshop". `8B64` exists only in PSB, so a kept block is now written as `8BIM` when the output is a PSD. A PSB keeps `8B64`.

## Evidence (Photoshop 27.11, scripted)
- Of 427 corpus re-exports, Photoshop refused 3, all PSB-derived: `ag-psd/read-write/psb2/src`, `psb2/expected` and `psd-tools/broken-groups`.
- A bisection over 127 variants showed each file opens once its `8B64` global blocks are gone. Their bytes are otherwise the same as working files'.
- With this change, all 3 re-exports contain no `8B64` blocks.

## Tests
- New: `kept_psb_blocks_are_written_as_8bim_in_a_psd`, which checks a PSD gets `8BIM` and a PSB keeps `8B64`.
- `psd_raw_resources_and_global_blocks_preserved` used to expect `8B64` to survive a PSD round trip, which is the case Photoshop refuses. It now expects `8BIM`.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-io`, clippy (`--no-deps`), fmt, `cargo xtask wasm` and `cargo xtask layers` all pass locally.

title: Toolbar: the colour chips sit right under the tools again
author: Unemars
body:
**TL;DR:** the colour chips, Quick Mask and Screen Mode buttons sit right under the tools again, as in Photoshop, instead of at the bottom of a tall toolbar.

**Problem.** Since the shared docking migration (#3097) the toolbar's tool column is a scroll area with `auto_shrink([false, false])`. Photoshop keeps them right under the last tool and only lets a column that does not fit scroll.

title: Shortcuts: a command can answer a second key (F2/F3/F4, Shift+F7, Cmd++) (#3665)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #3665.

**Why**
Photoshop's default set gives some commands a second key besides the one the menu shows: F2/F3/F4 for Cut/Copy/Paste next to ⌘X/C/V, Shift+F7 for Inverse next to ⌘⇧I, ⌘+ next to ⌘= for Zoom In, and Shift+Backspace for Fill. In PhotoCraft a command could hold only one key, so these couldn't exist, and a `.kys` import kept only a row's first key: a set listing Copy as F3 and ⌘C could leave ⌘C unbound.

**Change**
- `prefs::ALTERNATE_SHORTCUTS` holds Photoshop's second keys. `Preferences.alternate_shortcuts` (`alternateShortcuts`) replaces a command's defaults per command; an empty list removes them. Older settings files load with the defaults.
- `edit.keyboardShortcuts` takes `alternates`. Reset, taking a key from another command (whether it was that command's main key or an alternate) and the conflict list count every key. A call's changes now apply atomically: a bad key leaves the set as it was.
- `.kys` import keeps a row's other keys as the command's alternates.
- Dispatch matches every key (a user's main key wins over a default alternate). The UI-only secondary table is folded in, so Fill's Shift+Backspace survives an override of its main key. Menus still show only the main key, as in Photoshop.
- The Keyboard Shortcuts dialog shows each command's alternates, removable one by one, with Add Shortcut to add one. Use Default / Reset All restore them.

**Tests**
- `engine`: prefs tests for defaults, overrides, removal, conflicts across main keys and alternates, atomic failure and bad params; `kys` tests for a row's further keys.
- `ui-egui`: `kys_import_tests`, `shortcut_dispatch` tests (F3 copies, a user's main key beats a default alternate, Shift+Backspace after Fill is rebound).

title: Type: editing text keeps its ligatures and OpenType alternates (#3617)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #3617.

**Why**
In Photoshop, clicking into a type layer with the Type tool keeps its glyphs: ligatures, stylistic sets and other OpenType alternates stay as they were. Photoshop stores Stylistic Sets, Contextual Alternates, Swash, Fractions, Ordinals, Titling Alternates, Stylistic Alternates and Ornaments only in the PSD's `Txt2` block, not in EngineData. PhotoCraft read only EngineData, so once our engine laid the text out for editing, those glyphs fell back to the defaults.

**Change**
- `apply_txt2` (already used for the auto-kerning modes) now also reads each `Txt2` style run's OpenType flags (`TXT2_FEATURES`: `/20` calt, `/23` frac, `/24` ordn, `/25` swsh, `/26` titl, `/28` salt, `/29` ornm) and the Stylistic Sets bit mask (`/85` → `ss01`..`ss20`) into the runs' font features.
- A feature EngineData already set keeps its value. Contextual Alternates off is written as `calt` 0, because shapers apply `calt` by default while Photoshop's default is off.
- Hostile input (wrong types, masks beyond 20 sets, negative masks, unknown keys) changes nothing.

**Tests**
- `txt2_carries_opentype_features`: per-run features from a synthetic `Txt2`, the glyph ids our layout draws match a layer with those features set (with Inter: `ss01`/`ss02` change the glyphs, `->` stays two glyphs without `calt`), plus the bad-input cases.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-text --lib --tests`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-text --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`: 124 passed, clippy and fmt clean.

**Not verified**
- Not checked against the reporter's own file (it isn't attached); the `Txt2` keys come from PSDs saved by Photoshop with each option turned on alone.

title: control: suggest near matches for unknown command ids and methods (#3674)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
`engine.execute {"command": "engine.commands"}` failed with a bare ``unknown command `engine.commands` ``, so an agent that guessed an id had to list the whole registry to correct itself. Unknown protocol methods had the same problem.

`EngineError::UnknownCommand` now appends up to three registered ids close to the bad one, so every path that reports it (headless serve, the desktop control server, MCP `command_run`, `Session::disabled_reason`) gets the hint:

```
unknown command `engine.commands`; did you mean `command.list`?
unknown command `document.undo`; did you mean `edit.undo`, `history.undo` or `edit.purge.undo`?
unknown command `filter.blur.gaussian`; did you mean `filter.blur.gaussianBlur`?
```

Matching is deterministic and only runs on the error path: case-insensitive edit distance (the spell checker's existing Damerau-Levenshtein, now exposed as `photocraft_text::spell::edit_distance`), then ids that start with the given name, the same last segment in another namespace, and the same namespace with a longer last segment. `engine.commands` -> `command.list` is a small explicit table since spelling can't find it. No aliases are added (#3675 is left alone).

Both protocol servers also cover the reverse case. A protocol method sent through `engine.execute` (`doc.inspect`, `ui.inspect`) says it is a protocol method. An engine command id sent as a method (`edit.undo`) points at `engine.execute`. Other unknown methods get near method names. The desktop server gains a `METHODS` list for this, and a test checks that every entry is served.

title: Brushes: Photoshop's texture Height/Subtract modes, Brightness and Contrast (#3340)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #3340.

**Why**
Many imported Photoshop brushes use a Texture in Height or Linear Height mode at a low depth with a darkened pattern. PhotoCraft modelled those modes backwards (paint only on the brightest texels, and more of it with more depth), so these brushes painted nothing. Measured against Photoshop with single dabs over a 0..255 ramp pattern, Brightness, Contrast and Subtract were off too.

**Change**
- New `texture_combine` for the Texture section (the Dual Brush keeps `mask_combine`):
  - Height: the paint reaches `12 × depth × coverage` into the pattern and fills what lies below it (dark valleys first). Linear Height grades the shallow end by the pattern.
  - Subtract takes `depth × pattern` away (white removes the most). Color Dodge/Burn move toward their neutral as depth falls.
- `Texture::level`, shared by the renderer and the Brush Settings swatch: Brightness shifts by `value/255`, not `value/150`. Positive Contrast steepens by `1/(1−c/100)` after the shift, negative flattens by `1+c/100` before it. Invert is last.
- ABR import: `textureContrast` mapped positive values with `/50`; Photoshop's 0..100 is now `/100`, matching the model and the Brush Settings field.
- Built-in Subtract presets get Invert, so they look as before.

**Tests**
- `paint`: `texture_brightness_and_contrast_match_photoshop` and `texture_modes_match_photoshop` (values read back from Photoshop, ±2–3 levels), `low_depth_height_texture_paints`, range/NaN checks for every mode.
- `io`: `texture_contrast_maps_both_halves`, `low_depth_height_texture_brush_paints` (an imported Height/Linear Height preset set up like the reported "Pen" brushes paints the whole stroke).
- - `cargo test -p photocraft-paint -p photocraft-io --lib --tests`: all pass (paint 93, io 133 + integration). `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests --no-fail-fast`: 2162 passed; the failures are unrelated and fail on main too (`i18n::bundled_catalogs_are_consistent` "cs: duplicate Tool", two type-panel test…

title: Windows/Linux: open files in the running PhotoCraft instead of a second instance (#3708)
author: bommerts
body:
Fixes #1540 and #3708.

## What changes
Opening a file from Explorer (or a Linux file manager) while PhotoCraft is running now opens it as a new tab in the running window and brings that window forward, like Photoshop. Previously every open started a separate process.

## How
- New `apps/photocraft/src/single_instance.rs`. The first launch takes an exclusive OS lock on `instance.lock` in the settings directory. It listens on a loopback port and writes the port plus a fresh 256-bit token to `instance.json` (written atomically).
- A later launch that finds the lock taken sends its file arguments, made absolute, to that port and exits. The running instance queues them as `OsEvent::Open`, the same path macOS Finder opens use, so they open as tabs and the window comes forward.
- Explorer starts one process per file when several are opened at once. The lock decides the race, so all of them land in one window.
- If anything fails (no settings directory, a hung primary, a stale `instance.json` after a crash), the launch starts normally, so a file is never lost. The OS releases the lock when the process exits, crash included.
- `--new-instance` keeps the old behaviour. `--control` launches always get their own process, so automation is unaffected. macOS is unchanged, since LaunchServices already does this.
- `drain_os_events` now restores a minimized window before focusing it.
- Documented in `docs/development.md` › One instance per user, including the `cargo run` + installed-app note.

## Testing
- 5 new unit tests:
  - a second launch hands off its paths
  - 6 simultaneous launches end up as 1 primary and 5 hand-offs

title: Pen tool: Shift constrains segments and handles to 45° (TOOL-214-10, #3751)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #3751 (scorecard TOOL-214-10, part of #214)

## What was missing
The Pen tool ignored Shift. `pen_down`/`pen_move` (crates/ui-egui/src/vector_ui.rs) placed anchors and pulled handles at the raw pointer; only the Alt/Ctrl/Backspace/close-drag parts of TOOL-214-10 were done (#790, #1466, #3306).

## Change
- Shift-click: the next anchor lands on the nearest 45° ray from the previous anchor, at the pointer's projection onto that ray. The first anchor, a click on the first anchor (close) and a click on the last anchor (break) are unaffected.
- Shift-drag: the direction handles snap to 45° steps around their anchor, read live on every move (press or release Shift mid-drag). After Alt breaks the pair, Shift constrains the outgoing handle alone.
- The rubber band to the pointer previews the constrained point.
- Reuses `stroke_constraint::snap45` (the Gradient tool's helper); degenerate or non-finite input returns the point unchanged.
- Scorecard TOOL-214-10 → done; docs/scorecard.md regenerated; docs/ui-parity.md row updated.

## Photoshop reference
Holding Shift while clicking with the Pen tool constrains the new segment to multiples of 45°; holding Shift while dragging out direction lines constrains them to multiples of 45° (https://photoshoptrainingchannel.com/tips/straight-lines-creating-paths/).

title: Camera raw colour fit: read a Sony Adobe RGB preview as Adobe RGB, not sRGB
author: Madcat71
body:
## What

The per-file camera colour fit (`photocraft_io::raw::fit_preview_look`) converted the embedded JPEG to sRGB only when the JPEG carried an ICC profile, and otherwise read it as sRGB. A Sony body set to **Adobe RGB** writes no profile into its previews. It states the colour space only in the raw's EXIF: ColorSpace = Uncalibrated (0xFFFF) with InteropIndex `R03`, the DCF option file for Adobe RGB. The fit therefore targeted a desaturated, hue-shifted reference, and the developed raw came out that way. Blue skies were the most visible case.

- `photocraft_raw::embedded_preview_color_space` (new, public) reads that EXIF and returns sRGB, Adobe RGB or unstated. It never applies to a DNG, whose previews are the converter's.
- `preview_profile` (in `crates/io/src/raw.rs`) uses it when the preview has no ICC profile of its own. A preview's own profile still wins.

LightCraft reads the same tags for the same reason (storytold/lightcraft#778). This change follows the project's rule to never assume sRGB.

## Evidence

Measured on 19 private Sony ILCE-1M2 ARWs, all shot in Adobe RGB, against the camera's own JPEG read as Adobe RGB (median CIE76 ΔE at 240 px):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| full-frame 400 mm shots against blue sky (7 files) | 5.6–7.0 | **1.5–2.4** |
| their mean a* offset | +4.3 … +4.9 | +0.7 … +1.1 |
| all 19 files, mean of the medians | 4.9 | **2.2** |

Every file improved. Before the fix, PhotoCraft matched the JPEG *read as sRGB* closely (median ΔE 1.4–2.3 on the same sky shots), which is what the misread reference predicts. The files are not included.

## Tests

- `preview::tests::exif_colour_space_of_the_previews`: sRGB and Adobe RGB are recognised. R98, a missing interop IFD, other values, a DNG and junk all return unstated.
- `raw::tests::a_preview_without_a_profile_takes_the_raws_exif_colour_space`: fails without the EXIF fallback, and checks that the preview's own ICC profile wins.
- `tests/hostile.rs` now also calls `embedded_preview_co…

title: Shadows/Highlights: Photoshop's, measured
author: Unemars
body:
**Problem.** Image › Adjustments › Shadows/Highlights was a heuristic and did not behave like Photoshop's:
- the neighbourhood was a Gaussian of luma, so dark areas next to bright ones got halos;
- the masks were smoothsteps and the lift a gamma curve;
- Color scaled saturation by a guess.

On 16 cases on three public-domain pictures it differed from Photoshop 25.4 by 3.6–14.5/255 on average, and by up to 58/255.

**How Photoshop does it.** Photoshop 25.4 was measured as a black box: synthetic 16-bit images went through the adjustment by script, and the results were read back exactly. No Photoshop code or assets were used.

| | Photoshop 25.4 |
|---|---|
| Structure | Each channel moves by mask(neighbourhood) × (curve(v) − v). Shadows lift, highlights darken, and the two add. Only the Rec. 601 luma of that is kept: the pixel's own colour differences are added back. In the (neighbourhood, value) tables the change splits into mask × curve to 0.2 %. |
| Curve (Amount) | The image screened with itself 0 to 3 times: 1 − (1 − v)^q blended between q = 1, 2, 4 and 8, exact to 0.05/255. The number of screens is s = u/0.3 below 1, and (1 + 20u)/7 above, with u = (Amount/100)^0.6216. So 15 % screens once, 50 % twice and 100 % three times. |
| Mask (Tone) | A fixed 8-bit table of the neighbourhood's brightness. It does not depend on the image, the radius or the pixel. Tone 95 and over give 1 − L. Below that it is the complement of a Beta distribution function, from about Beta(1.95, 23) at Tone 0. Highlights use the same table on 1 − L. |
| Neighbourhood (Radius) | It is computed from (brightest channel + luma)/2 and is edge-aware. At low contrast it behaves like a Gaussian with σ ≈ 1.1 × Radius. Across a strong edge the other side counts much less (0.3 of its weight at a 0.8 step), and a single odd pixel does not affect its own value. It is quantised to 8 bits. |
| Color | Colour differences are scaled by exp(h · \|ΔY\| / max(Y, Y′)) for positive Color, with h = 0.87 at the def…

title: G'MIC filters via a user-installed gmic (Filter › G'MIC) and About Plug-ins
author: thomasmeadows
body:
## Summary
Adds G'MIC (https://gmic.eu) filters by running the **user's own `gmic` command-line program**. Nothing of G'MIC is linked, bundled or vendored, so the project stays Rust-only, `unsafe`-free and MIT/Apache (G'MIC is CeCILL). Docs: `docs/gmic.md`.

- **`crates/gmic` (photocraft-gmic, L4):** reads and writes G'MIC's `.cimg` format at float32 precision; turns `gmic parse_gui json` into typed filter parameters, dialog specs and safely quoted command lines; and runs `gmic` in a temporary folder with no stdin, drained output pipes, a timeout, cancellation and kill-and-reap. `apply` blends the result through the selection and handles alpha at 8, 16 and 32 bits per channel. On wasm, every run returns `Unsupported`.
- **Engine `gmic.status` / `gmic.list` / `gmic.filter` / `gmic.run`** (`gmic_cmds.rs`): each run is one undo step, can run as a cancellable background job, and works on a layer or a targeted channel. The filter list loads in the background and is cached per G'MIC version. New preference: `plugIns.gmicPath`.
- **UI:** **Filter › G'MIC** (filters by category; appears once G'MIC is found) and **About Plug-ins…** (end of Filter › Plug-ins, and Help). About Plug-ins explains plug-ins and gives install steps for the user's OS (pacman/apt/dnf/zypper read from os-release, Homebrew, or the Windows zip), plus Download, Locate and Check Again. New strings are translated in all 16 catalogs.

## Safety
G'MIC script can run programs and write files, so a raw `gmic.run` pipeline is **never stored in a document**. Smart filters record only catalogue filter ids plus parameter values, and the command line is rebuilt and escaped on re-render. Filters with file or folder parameters are never re-run from documents.

## Testing
- `cargo test -p photocraft-gmic -p photocraft-engine -p photoh no G'MIC needed (stand-in `gmic` scripts on Unix).
- `clippy -D warnings`, `xtask layers`, `xtask wasm`, `panic_hunt`, `xtask scorecard` (never-crash lints on 29 of 29 crates; the new pr…

author: dottedt
body:
76bd0631 ("satisfy clippy's collapsible_match") collapsed

title: feat(ui): the brush cursor follows the tip's shape, roundness and angle
author: FinnNk
body:
Photoshop's brush cursor is the outline of the tip itself. PhotoCraft always drew a circle, so an elliptical (Roundness), rotated (Angle), flipped or sampled tip, or turning the tip with the arrow keys (#3725), showed nothing until you painted.

A tip that isn't a plain circle now shows its own outline:
- **Normal Brush Tip:** the tip's contour at half coverage, like the circle today. **Full Size Brush Tip:** its very edge.
- The outline is traced (marching squares) from the same coverage image that draws the Brush Settings thumbnails (`brush_preview::tip_alpha`), so it matches the tip, and cached per tip setting.
- The canvas maps it through the view every frame, so zoom, view rotation and view flips apply.
- It's an OS cursor bitmap where the platform takes one, like the circle (no pointer lag), drawn with the same light line between dark ones; on the web, or past the bitmap size limit, it is painted, with the small crosshair, as the circle is.
- A plain round tip keeps the exact circle; the Pencil keeps its pixel-grid cursor.

## Review map

- `tool_cursor/tip.rs` (new): `needs_outline`, the cached `unit_outline` and `contour` (marching squares).
- `tool_cursor.rs`: `outline`, a bitmap or painted cursor from screen-space segments; each segment only touches the pixels within its stroke, so the cost follows the outline's length.
- `canvas.rs`: picks the outline for non-circular tips and maps it through the view (`brush_outline_on_screen`).
- `docs/brush-parity.md`: the cursor row.

## Evidence

Checked in a clean checkout on Windows x86_64 (rustc 1.99.0), on `2bbe6c3f`: `cargo fmt --check`, workspace clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`, `cargo xtask scorecard --check` and `git diff --check` pass. title: paint.stroke: fill: true fills the enclosed region (#3659)
author: dottedt
body:
paint.stroke paints dabs along the path only, so a closed-outline gesture meant as an organic filled dab rendered as a ring: paint landed on the outline and the interior stayed untouched. There was no fill mode and no fill-oriented primitive.

paint.stroke now takes fill: true, which fills the polygon the points enclose with the brush colour and opacity, its edge anti-aliased and softened by the brush hardness, in one history step, honouring the selection and alpha locking. title: Black & White: tint like the Color blend mode, as in Photoshop
author: MrCloudy2
body:
Photoshop's Black & White **Tint** keeps the grey's luminosity and takes the tint's hue and saturation, exactly like the Color blend mode (SetLum + ClipColor, luma 0.30 / 0.59 / 0.11). PhotoCraft instead mixed half the grey with twice grey × tint, which was up to 141 levels off.

| corpus `photoshop/adjustments/rgb16/black-white-tint.psd` | 69, 77.1 % | 1, 0.0 % |

title: Hue/Saturation: Photoshop's saturation curve, lightness order and Colorize lightness
author: MrCloudy2
body:
Four Hue/Saturation behaviours, measured in Photoshop 27.11 on a grey ramp and three hue sweeps (18 cases):

1. **Raising Saturation divides by (1 − s).** +50 doubles HSL saturation: (204, 102, 102) becomes (254, 51, 51). Main multiplied by (1 + s), giving (229, 77, 77). Lowering is unchanged: × (1 + s) already matched.
2. **Master Lightness applies first.** Hue and saturation then work on the lightened or darkened colour. With Hue +40, Saturation +25 and Lightness −10, (240, 160, 30) becomes (173, 243, 0) in Photoshop. Main gave (168, 230, 14); this PR gives (174, 243, 0).
3. **Colorize uses the adjusted lightness.** It builds the colour at L + (1 − L)·l (or L·(1 + l) when l < 0), so black with Lightness +30 becomes (0, 152, 0) instead of grey (77, 77, 77).
4. **A colour range's positive Lightness lightens toward the pixel's brightest channel**, not toward white. Blues +50 turns (0, 29, 115) into (57, 71, 115). Negative range lightness is unchanged and not yet measured.

## Results
| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 18 probe cases, worst | 78 levels | 4 |
| `photoshop/adjustments/rgb8/hue-saturation.psd` | 17, 11.8 % px > 2 | 2, 0.0 % |
| `photoshop/adjustments/rgb16/hue-saturation.psd` | 17, 11.8 % | 1, 0.0 % |
| `photoshop/adjustments/rgb8/hue-saturation-colorize.psd` | 6, 15.8 % | 3, 0.4 % |

| `psd-tools/adjustments/huesaturation_colorize_rgb.psd` | 120, 49.0 % | 3, 0.6 % |

The psd-tools files with custom range bounds (`huesaturation_rgb`, `_lightness_rgb`, `_saturation_rgb`) improve only slightly (bad pixels 67 → 51 % and 70 → 46 %). They depend on how Photoshop fades custom range bounds, which is a separate follow-up.

- GPU `compose.wgsl` gets the same changes.

title: fix(ui): show a magnifier cursor for the Zoom tool on Windows (#3735)
author: bommerts
body:
Fixes #3735.

## Problem
With the Zoom tool selected, Windows showed the plain arrow. The canvas already asked for `CursorIcon::ZoomIn` / `ZoomOut`, but winit 0.30 has no Windows mapping for them and falls back to `IDC_ARROW` (`platform_impl/windows/util.rs`). macOS and the Linux cursor themes do draw magnifiers.

## Fix
This uses the same approach as the Hand tool fix (#2196): on Windows (root viewport) the Zoom tool's cursor is now an OS cursor bitmap.
- `tool_cursor/zoom.rs`: a magnifier as signed distance fields. The lens is centred on the hotspot and the handle points down-right. It shows a **+**, or a **−** while Alt zooms out (Photoshop's behaviour).
- `tool_cursor.rs`: new `Shape::Zoom { out }` and `zoom(ctx, out)`. The hand and the magnifier now share a `silhouette()` coverage helper.
- `canvas.rs` and `camera_raw_preview_ui.rs` (the Camera Raw preview's zoom tool) call `tool_cursor::zoom`. Off Windows they still return the stock `ZoomIn` / `ZoomOut`.

The cursor tracks the hardware pointer (it isn't painted per frame) and scales with DPI. It is cached like the other tool cursors.

## Tests
- `zoom_bitmaps_are_outlined_magnifiers_centred_on_the_lens_at_each_dpi`: checks the shape and hotspot at 1–3× scale, that the handle points down-right, and that the plus has a vertical arm and the minus doesn't.
- `hostile_scales_get_no_zoom_bitmap`
- `the_magnifier_is_a_bitmap_only_where_the_os_has_none`
- The canvas harness test now also selects the Zoom tool and toggles Alt. It checks for a bitmap on Windows and the stock icon elsewhere.
- `write_cursor_preview` includes the magnifiers for visual QA.

OK creates the spot channel from the selection, as before, and remembers the ink and solidity for next time. `channel.newSpot` with params still runs the engine directly. The engine's `next_alpha_name` is now `pub` so the prefilled name matches the engine's default.

title: fix(ui): drag a document tab off the strip to float it in its own window (#3733)
author: bommerts
body:
Fixes #3733.

## What
Dragging a document tab off the tab strip now detaches it into its own OS window, placed where the tab was dropped, so it can be moved anywhere, including other monitors (as in Photoshop). Previously dragging a tab only reordered it.

- **Gesture** (`canvas.rs`): both tab strips (Studio and Pro) share a new `tab_drag` helper. Sideways drags still reorder (#217). Past 24 pt above or below the strip, an outline of the new window follows the pointer, and releasing floats the document, which becomes active.
- **Command** (`view_cmds.rs`): the drag goes through `window.arrange.floatInWindow`, which now takes optional `document` (index) and `position` (`[x, y]` screen points). Bad values return `Err`, never panic.
- **State** (`state.rs`): `DocWindow` gains `position: Option<[f32; 2]>` (`#[serde(default)]`), used as the viewport's initial position.

## Tests
- `dragging_a_tab_off_the_strip_floats_it_in_a_window`: kittest drag in both strip styles, plus the tear-off threshold.
- `float_in_window_takes_a_document_and_position`: params and error cases.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask wasm`: all green.

## Not covered yet
- Not tried by hand in the running app; window placement on a second monitor needs a manual check.
- As with the existing Float in Window, the document's tab stays in the main window (Photoshop removes it).
- Dragging a floating window back onto the strip doesn't re-dock it; Consolidate All to Tabs still does.
