title: View: remember Extras, Show and Snap To across restarts (#3762)
author: bommerts
body:
Fixes #3762.

## What

View › Extras, the View › Show items (Pixel Grid, Grid, Guides, Layer Edges, …) and the View › Snap To targets reset to their defaults on every launch. They're now remembered across restarts, as Photoshop keeps them.

- New `Preferences::view_extras` (JSON key `viewExtras`, owned by the shell), next to `brush_picker` and `tool_options`.
- `view_cmds::persist` runs every frame once the pointer is up, so items toggled from the menu, a shortcut, the Show Extras Options dialog or the control channel are all saved. `view_cmds::restore` runs at launch from `prefs_ui::load`.
- Only items that differ from their defaults are stored (`{"show": {"pixelGrid": false}}`), so a default changed in a later release still reaches users who never touched it.
- A hand-edited file can't break anything: unknown keys and non-boolean values keep their defaults.

View › Snap (the master switch) and Lock Guides are left out on purpose. Several tools switch `extras.snap` off for the length of a drag, so saving it could store a temporary state. Rulers were already remembered.

## Tests

- New `prefs_ui::tests::view_show_items_survive_a_restart`: toggles Pixel Grid, Grid, Snap To › Layers and Extras through the menu commands, checks what's stored, restores in a fresh app, and checks that malformed files fall back to the defaults.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` all pass.
- ui-egui lib and tests: 2108 passed. One failure, `type_tool::canvas_tests::multi_layer_formatting::options_font_family_preserves_peer_faces_and_batches_layer_flags`, hit the harness's `max_steps` limit on a text-cursor repaint under parallel load. It passes when run alone (3 out of 3) and doesn't touch this code.
- engine lib: the only failure is `destructive_levels_dont_clip_in_32_bit`, which also fails on unmodified main. It's tracked in #3546.

title: Web: repair clipboard routing and recover editing sessions in Rust
author: mmmbeer
body:
Browser image clipboard services were missing, and menu paste could miss the active type-edit target. This repairs PNG/RGBA publication and asynchronous image/text reads, preserves focused text controls, and cancels paste when its destination changes.

Browser recovery preserves documents, ordered tabs, dirty state, undo/redo history and serializable workspace state. The former handwritten JavaScript coordinator, inline bridges, session stylesheet and npm/fake-DOM tests have been removed. Storage uses Rust web-sys IndexedDB transactions and Rust futures. Recovery controls use egui. Each load has an independent random writer id. Storage errors leave editing usable and expose retry.

Recovery is also exposed through the existing command registry as session.recovery.capture, session.recovery.inspect and session.recovery.restore. PhotoCraft's existing session.inspect endpoint is retained. JSON transport is bounded to 8 MiB; the browser binary adapter is bounded to 512 MiB without truncating history.

Related to #2976 (browser text-box paste), #217 (persistence) and #3163 (recovery foundation). These reports include broader platforms and are not automatically closed. Native clipboard reports, masks/channels and multi-layer semantics are not claimed fixed.

Validation:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check passed.
- Native Clippy for engine/UI/web with --all-targets and -D warnings passed. The workspace CI Clippy stage also passed.
- WebAssembly compilation and strict WebAssembly Clippy passed, including the optional Rust browser-storage probe.

No quality gate or lint was weakened. No fonts, external assets, launcher customizations or branding changes are included. Contributor credit remains @mmmbeer as requested. See docs/browser-session-recovery.md.

title: io: read version 3 Photo Filter colour as XYZ, not Lab (#3777)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #3777

Photoshop CS2 saves Photo Filter layers as `phfl` version 3, where the colour is "4 bytes each for XYZ color" (Adobe's PSD spec). We read those three values as Lab x100, following ag-psd, so a real block like (24191, 25002, 3827) became L = 241.91, failed the range check and the layer fell back to Unsupported.

The fix reads version 3 as D50 XYZ and converts it to sRGB with the existing `XYZ_D50_TO_SRGB` matrix. Values above 2.0 are rejected as garbage. Writing doesn't change: an untouched version 3 block is saved back byte for byte, and an edited filter is written as version 2 RGB as before.

About the scale: the spec doesn't give one, so 1.0 = 32768 is my inference, not documented. It is the ICC 16-bit PCSXYZ encoding, and the issue's sample comes out as a bright warm yellow with it (1.0 = 65536 gives a dull olive). I also rendered the attached 900px PSD with a few scales and compared each to Photoshop's export, scaled down to the same size. Mean absolute difference: 8.26 on main, 6.75 at 65536, 5.77 at 45000, 5.07 at 36000, 4.84 at both 32768 and 30000, 5.0 at 26000. So the fit is flat between 30000 and 32768, and I picked the value that matches a known encoding. The filter has Preserve Luminosity on, which hides some of the brightness error, so this one file can't pin the scale down exactly. There is still a red offset of about -7.6 against Photoshop that this change doesn't explain.

Tests:
- `adjust_map`: the D50 white point decodes to white, and the Warming Filter (85) colour #EC8A00 decodes back to itself from its D50 XYZ. That XYZ value is something I computed, not read from a Photoshop file. The test also parses the exact bytes from the issue, checks that the 19-byte form without padding reads the same, and checks that out-of-range values give Unsupported.
- `psd_export`: a version 3 layer is saved back byte for byte while unedited, and once edited it is written as version 2 with the same colour.

Gate: I ran fmt, clippy -D warnings on photocr…

title: View: Extras, Show and Snap To settings survive a restart (#3762)
author: brennanMKE
body:
Fixes #3762.

View › Extras, the View › Show items (Pixel Grid, Smart Guides, Grid, Guides, …), Snap and the View › Snap To targets went back to their defaults on every launch. Turning off Pixel Grid had to be redone each time. Photoshop keeps these settings between sessions.

## Cause

The flags live in `UiState` (`ViewOptions::extras`, `show` and `snap_to`; `Extras::grid`, `guides` and `snap`). That state is never written to the preferences, so each launch started from the defaults.

## Fix

The new `view_memory` module follows the pattern `tool_memory` uses for tool options (#2814):

- **What it saves:** the flags that differ from their defaults, in a new preference, `Preferences::view_extras`. Each flag is keyed by its menu id without `view.`, for example `{"extras": false, "show.pixelGrid": false, "snapTo.layers": false}`.
  - A default changed in a later release still reaches users who never touched that flag.
  - Back at the defaults, nothing is stored.
- **When:** `persist` runs each frame. It compares 22 bools and saves only when one changed, so a menu click, a shortcut (⌘H, ⌘', ⌘;) and the control channel are all covered.
- **Restore:** `restore` applies the saved flags at launch, after the other remembered settings.
- **Bad input:** an unknown key or a value that isn't a bool is skipped with a warning, and that flag keeps its default.

Rulers was already remembered (`unitsAndRulers.showRulers`) and is unchanged. Lock Guides is not included.

## Screenshots

Taken in a disposable [Tart](https://tart.run) VM (macOS 26.6.2) with `--in-window-menus`. [How we run UI tests in Tart VMs](https://gist.github.com/brennanMKE/cf0ea3ec5f1b8655b76ce54f485bb30d).

title: Image > Mode > 32 Bits/Channel: convert to linear light, as Photoshop does
author: MrCloudy2
body:
PhotoCraft already treats 32-bit documents as **linear light**: `Transfer::for_document` returns gamma 1.0 for F32, and Exposure, Photo Filter and Photoshop-authored 32-bit PSDs all assume it. But `Image > Mode > 32 Bits/Channel` only rescaled the samples. An 8-bit sRGB grey 128 stayed 0.502 after conversion, where Photoshop stores 0.2159, and every adjustment then worked on the wrong values.

## Change
- `convert_depth` now decodes the colour samples through the document's tone curve after widening to 32 bits. It encodes them before narrowing from 32 bits, so a linear value is never quantised to 8 or 16 bits first.
- Alpha, layer masks and alpha channels keep their values.
- It applies to RGB and Grayscale, the modes that support 32 bits.
- New `Surface::map_color` applies a function to colour samples only, including the default pixel. `Transfer::decode` and `Transfer::encode` are now public.

## Evidence (Photoshop 27.11, scripted)
An sRGB chart was opened, converted to 32 Bits/Channel, adjusted, and saved as 32-bit float TIFF. Photoshop's values are exactly sRGB→linear (32 → 0.0144, 64 → 0.0513, 128 → 0.2159, 192 → 0.5271). Results against Photoshop, worst error after sRGB encoding:

| case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| conversion only | 0.287 raw (≈ 71 levels) | 0 |
| Levels 15 / 1.3 / 230 → 10 / 245 | 79 | 0 |
| Black & White (default) | 72 | 0 |
| Brightness/Contrast 50 / 50 | 43 | 1.6 |
| Hue/Saturation Colorize | 73 | 0 |

The other 32-bit adjustments (legacy Brightness/Contrast, Channel Mixer, Color Balance, Hue/Saturation, Photo Filter, Selective Color, B&W tint) still differ because of their own 32-bit maths: Photoshop leaves them unclamped. That's a separate follow-up.

## Tests
- New: `thirty_two_bit_holds_linear_light`, covering 8 → 32 → 8 with alpha kept.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-raster -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-io`: all pass except `destructive_levels_dont_clip_in_32_bit`, which also fails on main (#3704 fixes i…

title: Selective Color (Absolute): scale by the room the ink has, as in Photoshop
author: MrCloudy2
body:
In **Absolute** mode, Photoshop scales each range's ink change by how much that ink can still move:
- adding ink is scaled by `min(1, 2 × (1 − ink))`;
- removing ink is scaled by `min(1, 2 × ink)`.

PhotoCraft added the full percentage and clipped it. For example, Neutrals Cyan +50 on grey 64 gives red 32 in Photoshop, but main gives 0. Relative mode is unchanged.

## Evidence (Photoshop 27.11, scripted)
Every range (Reds … Magentas, Whites, Neutrals, Blacks) × every ink (C, M, Y, K) × ±50 % was measured in Absolute mode: 72 cases on a grey ramp, three hue sweeps and two pastel sweeps.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| cases within 3 levels | 8 / 72 | 72 / 72 (all within 1) |
| worst case | 32 levels | 1 |

The 4 Relative-mode controls already matched. One, Magentas Black +50 relative, is 11 levels off on a few pixels; that's a separate follow-up.

## Changes
- `compose::adjust::selective_color`: the absolute branch now uses this scaling.
- GPU `compose.wgsl` `selective_row` gets the same change.
- New test `absolute_selective_color_matches_photoshop` uses the measured grey values.

`cargo test -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu`, clippy (`--no-deps`), fmt and `cargo xtask wasm` pass. Any red checks are main's own failures (the Levels test and the wasm size gate).

title: Release workflow: pass the Azure signing secrets
author: echelon
body:
Since this repo's `release.yml` moved to `storytold/craft-common-actions`, it has passed the Apple and `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE*` secrets to the shared workflow, but not the six `AZURE_*` secrets that Azure Trusted Signing uses.

The shared workflow's signing jobs run in this repo's `release` environment and read the values from there, but only for names the caller lists. So the next release would have built **unsigned** Windows MSIs and portable zips, with only a warning. craft-launcher 0.3.1 did exactly this, and storytold/craft-launcher#174 fixed it with this same change.

This adds the six names. All twelve secrets are already set in this repo's `release` environment. storytold/craft-common-actions#3 makes release builds fail outright if signing secrets are missing, and fixes the riscv64 `--formats` call. This PR should land first.

title: Layer styles: editing effects no longer re-enables a disabled effect list (#3648)
author: notdezzi
body:
Fixes #3648

## Root cause
#3648 reports a disabled stroke reappearing after toggling another effect's preview. The per-effect preview/enabled round-trip in the Layer Style dialog is already correct on main; the live defect is in the engine: `replace_effects` (the `layer.layerStyle.replace` command the dialog's OK runs) and every `set_effect` command forced `l.effects.enabled = true`. So an effect list the user switched off wholesale (the Layers panel "Effects" eye, `layer.setEffectsVisible`) silently came back after any layer-style edit.

## Fix
Both paths now preserve the layer's existing list-level `enabled` flag; a layer that never had effects keeps the `enabled: true` default from `Layer::new`, so a first effect still shows. Explicit re-enable intents (style presets, rasterize-style, Show All Effects, Clear Layer Style) are untouched.

## Tests
- `replacing_the_list_keeps_a_disabled_effect_list_disabled` — hide the list, run `layer.layerStyle.replace`: master switch stays off, per-effect state still updated, composite unchanged until re-shown.
- `set_effect_keeps_a_disabled_effect_list_disabled` — same via `layer.layerStyle.colorOverlay`.
- `a_first_effect_shows_on_a_layer_that_never_had_effects` — unchanged first-effect behaviour.

`cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib`: 1291 passed; the one failure (`adjust_params::tests::destructive_levels_dont_clip_in_32_bit`) is the known order-dependent #3546 and reproduces on clean main. `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

title: Shift Edge moves by a fraction of a pixel so the slider does not snap
author: Desayuno64
body:
## Summary

Select and Mask's Shift Edge slider was changing the mask in whole-pixel jumps. Dragging it produced long stretches where nothing happened, then the edge leapt by a full pixel.

Shift Edge is a percentage of `max(radius, 4)` pixels, clamped to ±64. That distance was rounded to an integer before the morphological grow or shrink. With Radius at 1 the whole −100…100 range is only 4 pixels, so each pixel is 25% of the slider:

- below 12.5% rounds to 0 px (the mask does not move)
- 12.5% to 37.5% rounds to exactly 1 px
- the next plateau is 2 px, and so on

That matches what showed up in the dialog. Radius 1, Feather 2, Contrast about 69: Shift Edge −6.8 stayed put, and −31.2 jumped by one pixel of shrink. Values between those two looked identical. Feather and Contrast run before the shift, and the morph itself is a hard min/max of an integer radius, so they do not fill the gap.

The scale is unchanged: 100% is still `max(radius, 4)` pixels. The distance is no longer rounded. A whole number of pixels still uses one morph, so the existing exact cases stay bit-identical (100% grows by 4 px, −50% shrinks by 2 px). Anything in between blends that result with the next pixel: 12.5% is half coverage on the new rim, 25% fills it, and the following pixel is left alone. Halo and spread use the farther of the two radii, so the partial pixel is inside the tile instead of being clipped. Preview and OK both go through `RefineParams`, so the dialog and the committed mask move the same way.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p photocraft-algo --lib feather_contrast_and_shift` (half-pixel grow and shrink, plus the existing 100% / −50% pixels)
- [ ] Select and Mask, Radius 1: drag Shift Edge from 0 toward 30. The edge should creep, not sit still and then jump once.
- [ ] Radius 0, Shift Edge 100 and −50: the mask still moves by exactly 4 px and 2 px.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

title: Blur Gallery: Field Blur pins on the image (#3373)
author: timothydaly1

Closes #3373. Filter › Blur Gallery › Field Blur opened a parameter dialog with a single centre, though `filter.blurGallery.fieldBlur` already blends any number of `pins`. It now works like Photoshop's Blur Gallery workspace.

title: Layer styles: Photoshop's measured contour presets; Satin's contour lookup
author: MrCloudy2
body:
The 11 built-in contour presets (Cone, Gaussian, Ring, Ring − Double, Cove, Half Round, Rolling Slope, Rounded Steps, Sawtooth) were hand-drawn guesses, and none matched Photoshop. This PR replaces them with **Photoshop 27.11's own curves, measured**.

## How the curves were measured
For each preset, Photoshop rendered a Satin with that contour, plus the same Satin with Linear. Pairing the two images pixel by pixel reads off the curve at 38 levels, which I thinned to within 1 % and joined with straight segments.

The same data shows how **Satin applies a contour: `|c(1 − v) − c(1)|`**, i.e. read from its far end:
- Cone and Cone − Inverted Satins are identical;
- a Gaussian Satin is 0.36 at 0.5, while the Gaussian on a glow is 0.64.

New `effects::satin_lut` implements this and is used on both the CPU and GPU satin paths. Glows and bevels use the curve directly, as before.

Some measured presets don't start at 0: Cove − Deep starts at 0.26 and Rounded Steps at 0.23.

## Results against Photoshop (max level error on a profile through the effect)
| case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Satin, each of the 11 presets | 19–128 | ≤ 3 (Cove − Shallow 9) |

title: Remove tool: Create a new layer, and Remove after each stroke off
author: diegochagas
body:
Closes #1750 (the two options its last comment lists; the Remove tool itself landed in #2193).

## What changed

Photoshop's Remove tool options bar has three switches; PhotoCraft's had one. This adds the other two.

- **Create a new layer** (`paint.remove` `"newLayer": true`): the fill lands on a new layer inserted directly above the target, named like any new layer, opaque only where the hole is and transparent elsewhere; the target keeps every pixel. With Sample All Layers the fill comes from the composite, so an empty layer above a photo works as it does in Photoshop. The new layer becomes active; one undo step removes it again. The result carries `"layer"`. On a mask or channel target the option is ignored, as a mask has no "above".
- **Remove after each stroke** off (`paint.remove` `"strokes": [[[x, y, pressure?], …], …]`): the engine takes several strokes in one call and fills them as **one job and one undo step**, so the completion sees every hole at once instead of sampling from the area the next stroke is about to remove. In the UI, with the option off, each released stroke joins the waiting set and stays tinted on the canvas (the Remove tool's own tint, `stroke_trail`); the status bar counts them; **↩** or the options bar's **✓** applies them together, **Esc** or **⊘** drops them. Waiting strokes are dropped when the tool or the document changes under them, so they can never land on the wrong picture.
- `ToolOptions` gains `remove_new_layer` (false) and `remove_after_each_stroke` (true), both serde-defaulted, so saved tool options load as before.
- Docs: the scorecard row for the Remove tool (TOOL-213-19) lists the options and drops "Remove after each stroke off" from its missing list; a dated note in `docs/target-app-parity.md`; the command's params doc. The three new labels are translated in all 16 catalogs (the `every_tl_literal_is_translated` test checks them).

title: Camera Raw on raw opens: Clarity, Texture and Dehaze in linear light, measured
author: Unemars
body:
**TL;DR:** when a raw opens, Clarity, Texture and Dehaze act inside the raw development, in linear light before the tone curve, as Photoshop's Camera Raw does. Their models were measured against Photoshop 25.4 on 29 Nikon D4 NEFs.

**Stacked on #2919.** This PR adds one commit to #2919's branch. Only that commit is new: [compare with #2919](https://github.com/Unemars/photocraft/compare/camera-raw-tone...camera-raw-clarity-texture-dehaze). It is the first of four separate Camera Raw PRs; maintainers can stop at any of them:
1. this one;
2. the dialog laid out as Camera Raw 16.1.1, plus a demosaic choice;
3. preview speed and fidelity;
4. colour noise reduction.

**Problem.** #2919 moved Shadows and Highlights of a raw open into the raw stage. Clarity, Texture and Dehaze still ran as the filter, on the developed pixels after the camera curve. The filter's own models are textbook versions (Clarity through a guided filter, Dehaze through He's dark channel on gamma-encoded pixels), so on a NEF their effect did not look like Photoshop's.

**How Photoshop does it.** Black box: NEFs opened through Camera Raw by script (descriptor keys `Cl12`, `CrTx`, `Dhze`). Each slider was set to ±100 and +50, plus +100 at exposure −1; 348 opens in all. No Adobe code or data was used, only rendered output.
- **All three act before the tone curve.** The change at exposure −1 equals the change at 0 (correlation 0.98–0.99).
- **Clarity** works on log₂ luminance, split into bands between guided-filter bases with radii 2, 8, 32 and 128 (on the 1232 px work copy). Each band is scaled by a gain that follows its base's tone, plus a tone term. +100 roughly doubles midtone detail and darkens dark areas. −100 flattens midtones and highlights and leaves the shadows alone.
- **Texture** uses Gaussian bands from σ 0.5 to 16 on a half-size copy. Each band goes through a measured, non-linear response: small detail is raised more than strong edges, and flat areas don't change.
- **Dehaze** is He, Sun and …

title: Camera Raw: fast while editing, and the open-time preview as Open develops it
author: Unemars
body:
**TL;DR:** editing in the Camera Raw dialog no longer slows down with every setting. On a 16 MP Nikon D4 NEF:
- colour edits take 250 → 30 ms;
- the sharp refinement takes 5–6 s → 0.002–0.5 s;
- dragging a raw-stage slider takes 230–370 → 60–70 ms;
- dragging the filter's Shadows takes 500 → 20 ms.

The open-time preview now also applies Exposure and white balance where Open does, so what you see before Open is what you get after it. Sliders take the arrow keys and the mouse wheel.

**Stacked on #2919, #3815 and #3816 (the Camera Raw 16.1.1 dialog).** The new commits are the five after #3816: [compare](https://github.com/Unemars/photocraft/compare/camera-raw-photoshop-dialog...camera-raw-preview-speed). This is the third of four separate Camera Raw PRs; #3818 (colour noise) builds on it. #3427, now in main, already sends the preview through the canvas's document → monitor conversion, and this PR keeps that conversion.

**Problem.** Every change re-ran the whole pipeline on the proxy and then on the full frame. title: Camera Raw open: colour noise reduction as Photoshop's (Color 25 by default), measured
author: Unemars
body:
**TL;DR:** raw development gets Camera Raw's colour noise reduction (Detail › Noise Reduction › Color, Detail and Smoothness), measured against Photoshop 25.4. A raw opens with Camera Raw's default Color 25, and the dialog previews it as Open develops it. On 14 held-out Nikon D4 frames (ISO 100–12800), the mean ΔE76 to Photoshop is 1.51, against 2.83 for PhotoCraft's previous chroma blur and 4.27 with no reduction. Luminance noise reduction is not touched.

**Stacked on #2919, #3815, #3816 and #3817 (preview speed and fidelity).** The new commits are the two after #3817: [compare](https://github.com/Unemars/photocraft/compare/camera-raw-preview-speed...camera-raw-color-noise). This is the last of four separate Camera Raw PRs. The noise reduction itself (`photocraft_raw::chroma`, the first commit) is a self-contained module; only its hook in `develop.rs` sits next to the raw stage of the earlier PRs.

**Problem.** Camera Raw opens raw files with Color noise reduction 25. PhotoCraft opened them with none, so high-ISO frames showed colour blotches that Photoshop removes. The filter's Color slider was a Gaussian chroma blur on developed pixels, which bleeds colour across edges.

title: PSD type: read styles from the run's sheets and place text at its Txt2 frame (#3795, #1317)
author: FredApps
body:
## What and why

Two PSD type-layer import bugs show up when you start an edit with the Type tool. Starting an edit redraws a PSD text layer with PhotoCraft's own layout instead of Photoshop's saved pixels (`type_tool::begin_edit`), so anything read wrongly from the file appears at that moment:

- **#3795**: centred text layers jump sideways (they come back read as Left).
- **#1317**: text disappears when clicked to edit, and point text jumps.

@phquiste attached a real Photoshop PSD on #1317 (recent Photoshop, Arial, two box and two point text layers). I verified this PR against it locally. **That file is not committed** (its licence is unclear); all tests use synthetic fixtures with the same structure.

## Root causes

### 1. Style sheets (#3795)

`photocraft_text::psd::apply_engine_data` filled a run's missing attributes only from the Normal sheets. A run's `ParagraphSheet.Properties` / `StyleSheet.StyleSheetData` hold only its overrides, so anything it inherits from a named sheet got Normal's value instead. That covers a paragraph style named by `Parent` index or `Name`, and the paragraph's `DefaultStyleSheet`. A centred paragraph style was read as Left. PhotoCraft's own save wrote such files too: with named styles, `write_style_sheets` writes `Parent` plus overrides only.

### 2. Txt2 frame position (#1317)

Recent Photoshop keeps part of a type layer's position in the document's `Txt2` block, in the text object's frame (`Txt2 /0 /8 /0[frame]`):
- a frame-to-text-space matrix `/2 /2`;
- for point text, the anchor `/0`.

Meanwhile EngineData's `PointBase` stays at `[0 0]`, and `BoxBounds` stays in the frame's space. In phquiste's file, the frame matrix is `translate(462.5, -1227)` for the boxes, and the point anchor is `(8386.7, 10078.3)` with `translate(-375.7, -2888.6)`. PhotoCraft ignored both:
- **Box text** was laid out at `BoxBounds` mapped by the TySh transform, about 445 px left and 1175 px below Photoshop's pixels on a 735×414 canvas. When the edit star…

title: Blur Gallery: Iris Blur's pins and handles on the image (#3373)
author: timothydaly1
body:
**Depends on #3801** (Field Blur pins). This branch is stacked on it, so the first commit here is #3801's. Once that merges, this PR's diff is only the Iris commit.

Iris Blur opened a parameter dialog with a single ellipse. It now uses the same Blur Gallery workspace as Field Blur, with Photoshop's Iris handles on the selected pin:

- **Four handles on the outline:** drag one to resize that axis and turn the shape. The handle follows the pointer: its distance from the centre is the radius, and its direction is the rotation.
- **The square at the corner:** drag it out along the diagonal to round the shape towards a rectangle, or in to bring it back to an ellipse.
- **The four dots inside:** drag them to set the sharp core, where the blur starts (`feather`).
- As with Field Blur, a click adds a pin (taking the selected pin's shape and blur), pins drag, the ring around the centre sets the blur, Delete removes a pin, and the live preview follows every change.

### How
`blur_pins.rs` now handles both filters. Iris pins keep the command's own keys (`radiusX`/`radiusY` as fractions of the bounds' shorter side, plus `angle`, `roundness` and `feather`). The handles use the engine's geometry: the superellipse exponent is 2 + roundness/100 × 6, and the corner handle sits at the shape's diagonal point (t, t) with t = 2^(−1/m). So the outline drawn is where the filter reaches full blur, and the dots are where it starts. Pin values from automation are cleaned (finite, clamped, angle wrapped) before anything uses them.

### Tests
- `iris_opens_with_its_shape_as_a_pin`: opening gives one pin with the command's default shape.
- `iris_handles_resize_turn_round_and_feather` uses real drags on each handle: an axis handle dragged a quarter turn gives the expected radius and 90°; the corner square dragged to 0.9 gives the expected roundness; a feather dot gives the expected core. It then checks that a new pin copies the shape and that OK runs `filter.blurGallery.irisBlur` with both pins…

author: timothydaly1
body:
**Depends on #3822**, which depends on #3801. This branch is stacked on both. Its own change is the last commit, and the diff shrinks to it as those two merge.

Tilt-Shift and Spin Blur opened parameter dialogs. They now use the same Blur Gallery workspace as Field and Iris Blur, with Photoshop's handles.

### Tilt-Shift
- **Solid lines:** bound the sharp band. Drag either one to widen or narrow it (`focus`).
- **Dashed lines:** mark where the blur becomes full. Drag either one to set the transition.
- **Dots on the solid lines:** drag to turn the band (kept in the command's −90…90° range). The dots sit just beside the pin's ring, so they stay grabbable however narrow the band.
- **Pin and ring:** the pin moves the band; its ring and the dialog set the blur.
- **One band only:** the engine takes a single band (no `pins` param), so a click adds none and Delete keeps it. The dialog keeps the command's own `centerX`, `centerY`, `angle`, `focus`, `transition` and `blur`. Supporting several bands, as Photoshop does, would need an engine change; I've left that out of this PR.

### Spin Blur
- Pins work like Iris Blur's: add, move and delete them, and drag the four outline handles to resize and turn the ellipse.
- The ring and the dialog's **Blur Angle** set the spin. One turn of the ring is 360°, and the arc shows the angle.
- Pins keep the command's keys (`radiusX`, `radiusY`, `angle`, `blurAngle`).

### Tests
- `tilt_shift_lines_and_dots_shape_the_band` uses real drags. The dashed line sets the transition and the solid line the focus, each checked to the pixel. title: Engine: Flatten All Layer Effects keeps layer and vector masks (#3804)
author: dottedt
body:
File ▸ Scripts ▸ Flatten All Layer Effects baked the whole layer (effects and masks) into the pixels and then unconditionally cleared `mask` and `vector_mask`, permanently destroying unrelated mask pixels and their enabled/disabled state after save.

Bake the effect visuals with the masks left out of the render (the clone used by `bake` drops them), and keep the original `LayerMask` and `VectorMask` objects and their state on the layer, so each mask still applies exactly once to the baked raster and the command stays a visual no-op. Flatten All Masks is unchanged; it is meant to consume masks.

Test: `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib file_cmds` (new `flatten_all_layer_effects_keeps_masks`: an enabled raster mask, a vector mask and a disabled raster mask survive, composite before == after, undo/redo, and a `.pcraft` round trip at 8/16/32-bit); `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored`.

Closes #3804.

title: Security: linked-source read bypass, symlinked bundle saves, FIFO/size-bounded reads, token-file checks, pinned build tools
author: horknfbr
body:
## What

Fixes six findings from a source security audit of `7c2e8c3d`, one commit per finding, each with a regression test.

| Finding | Commit | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **SEC-01** Linked Smart Object bypasses the automation read root | `fix(engine)` | A document is stamped `metadata.deny_ambient_linked_sources` when it enters a session that has an authorization gate (`Session::add_document`). `smart_cmds::read_file`, the only place linked files are opened, then treats the source as missing. Render jobs with no session in reach follow the same rule. Desktop sessions install the gate per control request only, so documents the user opened are untouched. Matches the policy the Smart Object contents commands already apply (any linked path is ambient, in-root or not). |
| **SEC-03** Directory `.pcraft` save follows symlinked members | `fix(format)` | `save_dir` refuses a symlinked `tiles/`, `blobs/`, `composite/`, manifest, preview or object before it writes or removes anything. `atomic_write` keeps writing through symlinks for a user's own file path. |
| **SEC-05** FIFO blocks before the regular-file check | `fix(automation)` | `AuthorizedWorkspace::read` and `DirHandle::get` open with `O_NONBLOCK`, reject non-regular files, then read. |
| **SEC-06** Whole-file reads have no ceiling | same commit | Reads stop at `budgets::MAX_OPEN_BYTES` (2 GiB), enforced on the read via `read_entry`, so a file growing while open is refused too. |
| **SEC-07** Existing token file accepted on text alone | `fix(automation)` | Opened with `O_NOFOLLOW`, must be a regular file, Unix mode must have no group/other bits; the error says to `chmod 600` it. |
| **SEC-04** Unverified downloaded build tools | `build` | `package.sh` pins appimagetool 1.9.1 and type2-runtime 20251108, checks their SHA-256 (from the release asset digests, cross-checked by download), caches per version and passes `--runtime-file`. `ci.yml` checks the Trunk archive against its published `.sha256`. `freebsd.yml` installs a…

title: Windows Ink pen reader: tilt, barrel rotation, eraser end and coalesced pressure (#2046, #2285)
author: Leon69924
body:
## Windows Ink pen reader: tilt, barrel rotation, eraser end and coalesced pressure

> **Stacked on #1911** (Wintab reader). GitHub can't base a PR on another fork's branch, so this PR also shows #1911's commits. **Only the last commit (`75f2bd91`) is new here.** Once #1911 merges, this diff shrinks to that commit.

Fixes #2046 ("jumpy" pen pressure on Windows), #2285 (eraser end of a flipped Wacom pen on Windows). This is the Windows Ink follow-up that #1911's description leaves open ("needs the `WM_POINTER` window subclass ... can follow separately").

### Problem

winit 0.30 turns a `WM_POINTER` pen frame into `WindowEvent::Touch` with a normalised force and drops the rest of `POINTER_PEN_INFO`. On Windows Ink, which is the default for every vendor's pen, PhotoCraft therefore got:
- one pressure value per message instead of every coalesced frame, so the pressure is jumpy (#2046)
- no tilt and no barrel rotation (Art Pen)
- no eraser end (#2285)

### Fix (`crates/tablet/src/ink.rs`)

- A window subclass reads each pen message's `GetPointerPenInfoHistory` (newest-first from the system, reported oldest first). It then passes **every message on to winit unchanged**: it synthesizes no input, so the mouse emulation and #2475's barrel-button work are untouched.
- Each frame becomes a `Sample` in the crate's existing conventions:
  - pressure / 1024
  - tilt X/Y and rotation as Windows Ink already reports them (W3C signs, degrees clockwise)
  - eraser = `PEN_FLAG_INVERTED | PEN_FLAG_ERASER`
- `penMask` is honoured: an axis the device doesn't report reads as neutral, and a pen without a pressure sensor paints at full pressure, never at zero.
- Hover reports pressure 0, a cancelled contact reads as a lift, and `WM_POINTERLEAVE` (or a frame out of range) hands input back to the mouse.
- History is capped (`HISTORY_CAP`), and the proc is panic-contained.
- `unsafe` lives only in the gated `win` module, with a `SAFETY:` comment on every block. It uses the same subclass lifeti…

title: feat(codecs): read JPEG XL files, read-only on native targets
author: chrstphrbrns
body:
Photoshop reads and writes JPEG XL; we could not open one at all. The decoder is jxl-oxide, already a dependency for the JPEG XL-compressed tiles of a DNG in photocraft-raw, so this costs no binary size on native targets. It is left out of the browser wasm, which has a hard per-file cap (packaging/web/package.sh), as photocraft-raw already does.

Both file shapes open: the bare codestream (signature FF 0A) and the ISOBMFF container, which is where the Exif and xml boxes live. Depth is kept (8-bit, 10/12/16-bit integer and float), as are grayscale, alpha and CMYK, with the embedded ICC. Every call into jxl-oxide runs under catch_unwind, as in photocraft-heif: it parses untrusted files and still panics on some of them.

Orientation lives in the JPEG XL image header, not in EXIF, and jxl-oxide applies it while writing the stream, so the EXIF and XMP Orientation tags are rewritten to 1 to keep a later export from turning the picture twice. A file whose colour space is an ICC profile that cannot be mapped onto a built-in encoding is rendered in its own space rather than converted, since no CMS is linked in.

Writing needs a full JPEG XL encoder, which the pure-Rust zune-jpegxl does not provide, so Format::Jxl joins HEIF in ASYMMETRIC_EXCEPTIONS. Fixtures come from zune-jpegxl plus containers the tests build around its codestream; what that cannot produce (header orientation end to end, animations, float and CMYK) stays untested until corpus/jxl is wired up from libjxl's testdata.

title: fuzz: raw has no .gitignore, so a fuzz run leaves its corpus untracked
author: Erica4fr
body:
`crates/raw/fuzz` has no `.gitignore` at all, and `crates/psd/fuzz` has one without `Cargo.lock`.
Running the fuzzers [the book invites you to run](book/src/development/fuzzing.md) then leaves
this behind:

```text
?? crates/raw/fuzz/Cargo.lock
?? crates/raw/fuzz/artifacts/
?? crates/raw/fuzz/corpus/
?? crates/psd/fuzz/Cargo.lock
```

AGENTS.md says **never to commit corpus files**, and `artifacts/` is where libFuzzer writes the
inputs that made a target fail, so `git add -A` after a run stages exactly what the rules say to
keep out. `codecs`, `format` and `affinity` already ignore all of it.

So `raw` gets the same list those three use, and `psd` gets the missing `Cargo.lock` line.
`target/` is already covered by the root `.gitignore`, so corpus, artifacts and the lock were the
only things exposed — I checked that rather than assume it.

**Checked** by creating the files a run produces in both crates and confirming `git status` is
clean afterwards, with and without the change. Found while fuzzing the parsers on this branch's
base (8 targets, ~91M executions, no crashes — nothing to report there, but the leftovers in
`git status` were hard to miss).

The branch is cut from this fork's `main` rather than today's upstream: syncing the fork pulls in
upstream workflow changes, which my token cannot push. The two files are identical in both, so it
applies cleanly.

title: fix(gpu): flush every 1000 passes so deep stacks don't pile into one command buffer
author: JameEnder
body:
The compositor only submits between 2048² page cells, so a deep stack puts everything for one cell into a single command buffer. 700 full-size layers on a small doc is 1403 render passes with zero flushes, and wgpu-core opens two hal command buffers per pass. Metal caps a queue at 4096, so that's the kind of thing that can take the device down there (P12 territory).

`run_cell` now counts copies + render passes and submits once it hits 1000, same wait-for-the-previous-batch as the page-cell flush. Chunk textures / uniforms / bind groups outlive the submit and the queue keeps order, so a chunk just continues in the next buffer. If the device is lost in one of those submits, the refresh stops with an error instead of recording more.

Speed-wise it's a no-op, perf_scenarios is within noise:

| row | main | this |
|---|---|---|
| set layer opacity + refresh | 2.75 ms | 2.71 ms |
| undo move + refresh | 6.06 ms | 6.32 ms |
| move styled layer 10 px + refresh | 12.42 ms | 12.32 ms |
| nudge 1 px in the many-layer document + refresh | 2.51 ms | 2.11 ms |
| new layer in the many-layer document + refresh | 0.65 ms | 0.64 ms |

New test `many_layers_submit_inside_one_chunk` (700 noise layers, 64×48) wants `flushes > 0` inside one chunk and CPU parity. Fails on main.

Couldn't actually reproduce the Metal limit, I'm on Linux, so it's verified by the pass/flush counts, not on a Mac. If someone with a Mac wants to poke at it, that'd be nice.

<sub>Benched on: Ryzen 9 9900X, 32 GB, RTX 3090 (driver 580.119), NixOS / Linux 6.12, Vulkan, release build, rustc 1.97.1. Medians, A/B runs interleaved.</sub>

title: perf: the Navigator redraws only the area an edit changed
author: JameEnder
body:
With the Navigator open, every edit re-renders the whole doc into a new thumbnail on the UI thread, a full-res CPU composite. On a 20 MP layered doc that's a noticeable hitch after every edit.

The cache now also remembers the revision it was made at. If the doc is exactly one edit ahead with a bounded `last_damage` (same preview key, same size), it only renders the damage, grown by the effect reach, and `set_partial`s it into the texture. Empty damage (rename, selection, new empty layer) costs nothing. Everything else falls back to the full thumbnail like before. Added `compose::thumbnail_size` so both paths agree on the size.

20 MP layered doc, UI-thread time for the navigator after an edit:

| after | main | this |
|---|---|---|
| opacity change | 303 ms | 36 ms |
| brush stroke | 486 ms | 171 ms |

New test `navigator_damage_updates_match_a_full_thumbnail` patches a thumbnail after translate / opacity / stroke / blend / new layer, on a doc with a drop shadow, and compares it to a full one. It catches it if the effect reach inflation goes away.

<sub>Benched on: Ryzen 9 9900X, 32 GB, RTX 3090 (driver 580.119), NixOS / Linux 6.12, Vulkan, release build, rustc 1.97.1. Medians, A/B runs interleaved.</sub>

title: perf: draw marching ants as one mesh instead of a line shape per dash
author: JameEnder
body:
Every ants segment was a white line + a black line per 4 px dash, all tessellated by egui each frame, ten frames a second while a selection's up. For normal selections it's fine, but a messy one (speckle, magic wand on noise) seen zoomed out gets expensive.

Horizontal/vertical segments now go into a single `egui::Mesh` of 1 px quads, with the same pixel-centre rounding, dash length and phase. The white base sticks out half a pixel on both ends so the corners join like the line caps did. Slanted segments (Content-Aware Move's transformed outline from #3095) stay as line shapes so egui keeps antialiasing them. I tried a repeating textured dash first, but egui-wgpu clamps UVs, so no.

Idle frame with a speckled selection:

| zoom | segments | main | this |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30% | 94,666 | 45.6 ms | 12.0 ms |
| 125% | ~22k | 6.6 ms | 4.5 ms |

Screenshots at 100% and 800% are pixel-identical to main.

title: perf: edits, undo and redo recomposite only where added or removed layers draw
author: JameEnder
body:
Follow-up to #2884 / #2917. Those made Duplicate and Paste report where the new layer draws, but `Session::edit` itself still only reported damage when no pixels changed. So Fill, Invert, filters, Delete Layer, and undo/redo of a duplicate, paste or delete still recomposite the whole document.

- `Session::edit` reports `step_damage(before, after)`, the same bound undo/redo already use.
- `step_damage` handles layers only one side has in both directions, so a deleted layer counts where it drew, same as an added one. That makes `bounded_additions` / `insert_damage` unnecessary, and `added_bounds` → `one_sided_bounds`. Clip bases, adjustments, video and excluded channels still recomposite everything (keeps #3090 happy).
- The subject-mask cache only gets dropped when pixels could have changed.

Layered 20 MP doc, edits on a 1 MP layer:

| row | main | this |
|---|---|---|
| delete 1 MP layer + refresh | 9.1 ms | 1.4 ms |
| undo duplicate 1 MP layer + refresh | 9.3 ms | 1.6 ms |
| fill 500 px square + refresh | 17.4 ms | 5.5 ms |
| invert 1 MP layer + refresh | 16.7 ms | 9.2 ms |
| duplicate / paste 1 MP layer (repeat) | 2.7 / 2.9 ms | 2.6 / 2.8 ms |

(Those rows aren't in perf_scenarios yet, can add if needed:) )

Tests: new `duplicate_paste_and_delete_report_where_the_layer_draws` checks each step + its undo/redo report the same bounded rect and that nothing outside it changes. Renamed `new_layers_that_change_pixels_still_recomposite_everything` → `..._change_clipping_...`, since a painted new layer is bounded now. A new clip base or an adjustment still isn't.

<sub>Benched on: Ryzen 9 9900X, 32 GB, RTX 3090 (driver 580.119), NixOS / Linux 6.12, Vulkan, release build, rustc 1.97.1. Medians, A/B runs interleaved.</sub>

title: perf(gpu): a duplicated layer's texture starts as a copy of its source
author: JameEnder
body:
A duplicate shares its source's tiles, but on the GPU side it got a brand new resident texture, so every tile was converted and uploaded again. Duplicating a 20 MP photo layer pushed 330 tiles.

Now, when a new resident shares tiles with an existing one (same role, region, kind, format, default pixel), its texture starts as a `copy_texture_to_texture` of that one and the normal per-tile pass fixes up whatever differs.

The copy is recorded in the frame encoder, but queued writes land *before* the encoder runs, so a write to either texture in the same refresh would get clobbered by the copy, or leak into it. Both get marked `ordered`, and from then on their writes go through the encoder. (#2902's `keep_overlap` uses its own submit instead, but that doesn't work here: the donor may still have copies pending in the frame encoder.)

| row | main | this |
|---|---|---|
| duplicate 20 MP photo layer + refresh | 25.1 ms | 6.3 ms |
| tiles uploaded | 330 | 0 |

Paste doesn't change, since the pasted layer has fresh tiles.

New parity test `duplicates_copy_their_source_texture`: plain duplicate (no uploads), duplicate and source each painted in the same refresh, and a duplicate missing a tile. Drop the `ordered` routing and the middle case is off by 167/255, so it's load-bearing.

<sub>Benched on: Ryzen 9 9900X, 32 GB, RTX 3090 (driver 580.119), NixOS / Linux 6.12, Vulkan, release build, rustc 1.97.1. Medians, A/B runs interleaved.</sub>

title: Brushes: drag a brush folder into another folder (#2014)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #2014.

**Why**
In Photoshop's Brushes panel you can drag a brush group (folder) onto another group to nest it inside, and drag it back out to the top level; a group can't be dropped into itself or into one of its own folders. PhotoCraft could only reorder a folder among its siblings.

**Change**
- `brush.presets.moveGroup` takes `into: {group?, folder?}`: moves a group or nested folder, with all its content in order, inside another folder or group (`folder: []` = directly in the group). `into: {}` moves it out to the top level as a group of its own. `before` places it before a sibling there.
- Errors, library unchanged: into itself or one of its own folders, a name clash at the destination, nesting deeper than `MAX_FOLDER_DEPTH`, the ungrouped presets, `index` together with `into`, malformed params.
- The preset store follows the move: a group moved into another loses its group file, a folder moved out gets one.
- Brushes panel: dropping a group or folder header on another header puts it inside; dropping on the header's upper third places it before that folder (sibling reorder, or out to the top level before a group). Each drop is one journaled `moveGroup` command, mapped by the pure `folder_drop`.

**Tests**
- Engine: `folders_move_into_folders_and_groups`, `bad_moves_into_folders_fail_without_changes` (cycle, depth limit, name clashes, bad params), `preset_store::folders_moved_into_other_folders_persist` (files rewritten, layout survives a reload).
- UI: `folder_drops_map_to_move_commands` (drop mapping incl. no-op cases), `dragging_a_folder_header_onto_another_moves_it_inside` (kittest drag and drop in the real panel).
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests brush` (89 passed), `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib brush` (53 passed), `--lib preset_store` (20 passed), `panic_hunt -- --ignored` (passed), `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`.

**Not verified**
- No visual check…

title: Save: an in-place OpenRaster save no longer drops layers or marks clean (#3806)
author: dottedt
body:
An `.ora` counts as a layered format, so File ▸ Save on an opened `.ora` wrote back in place, and Save As to a `.ora` adopted it, even when the document held features OpenRaster cannot represent. Adjustment layers were silently left out, and layer styles, group masks, clipping masks and vector masks were not saved; the document was still marked clean, so the loss was permanent and unannounced.

Add `photocraft_io::ora_would_lose_data` (surfaced as `file_cmds::ora_would_lose_data`), which reports the editable layer data OpenRaster drops: adjustment layers, layer styles, group masks, clipping masks and vector masks. The desktop save paths (`write_save`, so File ▸ Save and Save As), the `app.save` automation path and the headless `doc.save` now refuse such a save before writing, with an error naming the loss and a remedy (save as `.pcraft`/`.psd`/`.psb`, or flatten first). The original file, the source identity and the dirty state are left untouched. Lossless OpenRaster round trips (raster layers, groups, blend/opacity/visibility, and pixel masks, which ORA bakes) are unchanged, and Save a Copy / batch / Export As (explicit copies) still write and warn as before.

title: Keep CMYK ink values when flattening and merging (#3778)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Part of #3778

Flattening a CMYK document changed its ink values, even with only a Background layer. Two things were going on. The compositor works in display RGB, so every flatten read the CMYK pixels through the document's profile and separated the result back to CMYK. On top of that, the separation in `flatten_to_surface` and the engine's `composite_layers` ran outside the document's CMYK space, so it used the built-in coated profile instead of the embedded one (SWOP in the report). Merge Down also built its scratch document without the profile.

The fix:

- New `compose::native::flatten_cmyk`. When a CMYK document's visible layers are all plain raster layers (Normal, no enabled masks, effects, clipping, Blend If, excluded channels or advanced blending), it composites straight on the stored ink values. Normal is a linear mix, which is what Photoshop does in CMYK. Opaque pixels are copied as they are, so a lone Background comes out bit-identical and 16-bit stays 16-bit. Flattening onto paper treats white as zero ink.
- `flatten_to_surface` (now a wrapper around `composite_to_surface`) tries that path first. Flatten Image, Merge Visible and Merge Down all go through it.
- When the stack still needs the RGB compositor (adjustment layers, other blend modes and so on), the separation back to CMYK now runs inside the document's own CMYK space.
- `merge_down` takes the document, so its scratch document carries the ICC profile.

Tests are in `crates/engine/src/flatten_cmyk_tests.rs`. They use a 16x8, 16-bit CMYK document tagged with a synthetic profile: a lone Background flattens to identical values, a Normal layer with solid, half-transparent and empty areas flattens/merges (Flatten, Merge Visible, Merge Down) to the expected ink mix within one 16-bit code, and a stack with a Multiply layer, which still goes through RGB, round-trips light inks near their printed colour (mean error 0.013 vs 0.077 before). The first three failed on main with ink shifts up to 0.41.

Regression tests cover RGB/grayscale, U8/U16/F32, alpha/no-alpha, all three interpolation modes, and a fractional bilinear translation. Both new tests were observed failing before the fix.

title: Keep masks when flattening all layer effects (#3804)
author: vbasky
body:
Flatten All Layer Effects baked each layer with its masks applied, then cleared `mask` and `vector_mask`. Disabled masks never entered the pixels, so they were deleted outright.

This change bakes effects with masks stripped from the temporary layer, leaves the original raster and vector masks (and their enabled state) on the layer, and keeps the vector-mask PSD blocks that still belong there.

Fixes #3804

title: Do not overwrite OpenRaster files that would lose adjustment layers (#3806)
author: vbasky
body:
OpenRaster cannot store adjustment layers or live layer styles, but File → Save treated `.ora` as a lossless in-place format. Saving back to the original file omitted those layers and marked the document clean.

Pixel-only OpenRaster files still save in place. When the writer would drop editables, Save no longer overwrites the document's own `.ora`; a write to a different `.ora` path is a copy and leaves path and dirty state alone.

Fixes #3806

title: Control: control requests starve when the window gets no frame callbacks (#2493)
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
Fixes #2493. Also addresses the `health` liveness probe half of #3667.

## The bug

On Wayland the frame update (and with it the control drain) only runs on compositor frame callbacks. When the display is asleep or the window is fully occluded, `ctx.request_repaint()` from the transport thread no longer produces a `logic` pass, so every queued `ControlRequest` times out after 60 s while the app itself is healthy. `auth` is answered on the socket thread, which is why it keeps working — but it proves nothing about the frame loop (#3667).

## The design

- **`ControlWatch`** (`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs`): an `Arc`-shared liveness record the transport threads read off-thread. The frame loop notes each logic pass and each drawn frame; `drain_control` stores the last reply of the read-only getters agents probe with (`ui.inspect`, `document.inspect`, `session.inspect`, `engine.commands`, `jobs.list`), keyed per document index.
- **`health` method** (`apps/photocraft/src/control_server.rs`): answered entirely on the socket thread, no frame loop involved — the liveness probe #3667 asks for.
- **Stall fallback** (`wait_reply`): after `STALL_CHECK` (1 s) without a reply, a logic pass that advanced since the send means the loop is alive, so keep waiting to the 60 s deadline; a wedged getter with a stored snapshot gets it served with `frameStalled: true` and `snapshotAgeMs`; a wedged getter without a snapshot fails fast with a "not drawing frames" error naming `health` as the probe; mutating methods always keep waiting. The logic count is read before the send, so a later read can't attribute to a live loop the logic pass the request itself woke. A served snapshot drops the reply receiver first — the frame thread's later real reply only refreshes the stored snapshot.
- MCP: bridge-only `health` tool (`call_read`, read-only annotation), protocol docs updated (`health` entry, stall behaviour + stamp placement, bridge tool lists/tables).

title: Free Transform: solid pixel stretch (edge-repeat sampling, selected-pixel bounds) (#3773)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #3773

I couldn't find a 1000% cap anywhere. The W/H fields go up to 1000000% (#1267) and the engine takes any scale. What breaks the pixel stretch is that the stretched column fades out. Bicubic and bilinear sampling read transparent pixels past the source edge, so a 1 px column scaled up came out with alpha around 0.56 at its ends, blending into whatever was underneath. With a selection it was worse. The edge used was the whole layer's bounds, because lifted pixels kept their colour at zero alpha and so still counted as content.

The fix:

- `algo::transform::warp`: samples past the source rect now repeat the edge pixel, and the outline is antialiased by coverage. A stretched row or column stays solid, and an upscaled layer keeps a crisp 1 px antialiased edge instead of a ramp k pixels wide. Nearest neighbour is unchanged.
- `split_selected` clears unselected pixels in the lifted surface, so its bounds are the selection's, and the selected-pixels path warps from those bounds.

Large scales still build the whole stretched raster, which is slow and memory hungry at extreme sizes. As suggested in review, I'll send a bound for that separately, one that refuses with a clear error past a pixel budget instead of dropping pixels. This PR doesn't clip anything: pixels moved off the canvas are kept as before.

Tests:

- algo: a 1x4 column scaled 100x stays fully opaque, bicubic and bilinear.
- engine: a 1x8 column on a 256x256 canvas at 5000% gives exact bounds and is opaque throughout. A selected column of an image stretched 2400% stays solid over the image, with the image either side untouched.
- engine: an 8x8 layer on a 64x64 canvas moved 3 canvas widths right with `edit.transform` and back again keeps every pixel and its bounds.
- The algo and engine lib suites, clippy -D warnings on both, fmt and the layers check pass. I left the full `cargo xtask ci` run (workspace tests and the wasm build) to GitHub CI.

title: Use craft-print for system printing
author: skylartaylor
body:
PhotoCraft now submits its composed PDF bytes through immutable `craft-print` revision `d991bf6792f8ade99c51358bf3c1d902c8cd96b5` for CUPS and Windows. PhotoCraft retains layout, ICC conversion, print marks, mirroring, copies and explicit PDF export; the spooler receives Exact scaling.

Desktop printing takes an immutable document snapshot and runs on a worker, reports actual queue acceptance/refusal, applies completion hooks to the source document and waits before quitting. Headless execution stays synchronous. Printing is not cancellable through app jobs; the UI directs users to the system print queue. Recording keeps one replayable print command.

Only explicit `output` paths retain PDFs. Spool-only jobs and dry runs without output return `pdf: null`; dry runs report the backend command without submitting. `send: false` requires an output or `dryRun: true`. Remembered Print One Copy settings omit `output`, `dryRun` and `send`, so export-only requests cannot disable the next real print. CUPS streams bytes; `craft-print` owns and cleans Windows transport files, while explicit app exports remain caller-owned.

The final rollout integrates PhotoCraft 0.8.2's lossless UI-font compression, packed translation keys and WASM profile settings, retaining font and language coverage. It also repairs AppRun's ShellCheck condition and missing Hungarian/Turkish preference translations and Turkish depth labels. All six pixel-processing kernels stay at optimization level 3 and native optimization profiles are unchanged. The existing MCP resource comparison validates paired purge availability and normalizes only process-global cache state. Background-job tests now observe the required frames under a blocked fake worker with a bounded timeout, avoiding a minimum frame-rate assumption on software-rendered CI. The unchanged 24 MiB package gate passes: the locally built and browser-smoked artifact is 24,136,129 bytes; the separately hosted CI build is 24,136,972 bytes.

title: fix(layer-style): support Blend If Alt-split handle feathering and throttle live preview
author: Gotix-eg
body:
### Summary
1. Fixes Blend If slider handle interaction: Alt-dragging a black or white triangle now splits it into two half-handles (`[min, max]`) for smooth feathered luminance blending, matching Photoshop 1:1.
2. Resolves heavy CPU spikes and stuttering during slider drag by throttling live Layer Style document preview compositing to ~30 FPS on the UI thread.

### Details
- **Alt-Split Triangle Handles:** Refactored slider drag math in `blend_if_bar` (`layer_style.rs`). Alt-dragging the black triangle splits the right half (`[0, max]`); Alt-dragging the white triangle splits the left half (`[min, 255]`). Dragging halves back together seamlessly reunites them. Handle ordering `0 <= black_lo <= black_hi <= white_lo <= white_hi <= 255` is strictly maintained.
- **Live Preview CPU Throttling:** In `canvas.rs`, dragging sliders previously triggered full synchronous CPU composite passes on every pointer move event (up to 120+ times/sec), pegging CPU cores at 100%. Live Layer Style preview rendering is now throttled to ~30 FPS (>= 33ms) during rapid drag gestures, while guaranteeing the final state is always rendered immediately upon release or timer trigger.
- Adds `[people.Gotix-eg]` to `contributors/people.toml`.

### Testing
- Added unit test `blend_if_alt_split_and_drag_behavior` verifying Alt-split, dragging split halves, seamless reunion, drag without Alt, and boundary clamping.

title: macOS: ⌘H hides PhotoCraft, as in every other Mac app; View › Extras moves to ⌃⌘H
author: texjer
body:
TLDR:

On macOS, ⌘H now hides PhotoCraft like it does in every other Mac app, and View › Extras moves to ⌃⌘H. It's a preference (Interface › **⌘H Hides PhotoCraft**), on by default on macOS. Turning it off brings back Photoshop's layout. It isn't shown on other platforms.

Photoshop handles this clash by asking the first time you press ⌘H. PhotoCraft's Mac menu currently moves Hide to ⌃⌘H silently, so ⌘H does something different from every other app on the Mac. This flips that default and keeps the Photoshop layout one checkbox away. If you'd rather keep Photoshop's layout as the default, it's a one-line change (`cmd_h_hides_app: cfg!(target_os = "macos")` → `false`).

title: UI: Photoshop-style in-dialog preview for the generic filter dialogs (#3769)
author: dottedt
body:
Photoshop shows the filtered result in a preview window inside its filter dialogs. PhotoCraft's generic schema dialog only had the parameter widgets, with the live result on the canvas behind the dialog.

The generic dialogs now draw an in-dialog preview window built from the same downsampled proxy the canvas already computes (`filter_dialog::preview_document`), so there is no second preview pipeline: − / + zoom steps with a percentage readout, drag to pan, a click to centre the view on a document point, and press-and-hold to compare against the unfiltered image. Zoom is document-scale, so 100% is one document pixel per point (the k-reduced proxy is scaled up by k). The window sits under the parameters and reserves its own height so a small window still fits OK/Cancel; the Preview checkbox still toggles the on-canvas live result, unchanged. Colours come from `theme::Tokens`, the zoom buttons from `icons::button`, and the tooltips reuse the existing localized "Zoom in"/"Zoom out" entries.

Scope notes for review:
- The generic filter dialog is an `egui::Modal`, whose backdrop swallows canvas clicks, so "click to centre" is observed inside the preview window rather than on the canvas. It is not possible to observe canvas clicks while the modal is open without changing the dialog model.
- At 100% on a large document the proxy is upscaled by k, so the preview is softer than a full-resolution render would be. A sharper 100% would mean running the filter at full resolution for the preview.

Test: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib` (only the pre-existing Czech `cs.tsv` duplicate-key test fails); `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -A clippy::nonminimal_bool -A clippy::collapsible_match -D warnings`; `cargo xtask wasm`; a snapshot of the Emboss dialog shows the window and its zoom controls; new unit tests cover the document-scale zoom/pan/centre maths, clamping and corrupt-state recovery.

Closes #3769.

title: OpenRaster: never overwrite an .ora with less than the document has (#3806)
author: timothydaly1
body:
Closes #3806. File › Save wrote any document back to its `.ora`, though OpenRaster drops adjustment layers, layer styles, vector masks and clipping, applies masks and fill opacity to the pixels, and rasterises type and shape layers. The save then marked the document saved, so the editable content was lost without asking.

### The rule
An OpenRaster file counts as the document's own file only while it **holds everything in it**.

- **`photocraft_io::ora_losses(doc)`** lists what an OpenRaster save would leave out. The writer gained a dry-run mode, so this list and the export warnings come from the same checks; nothing is rendered or encoded. A test checks the two are equal for eight different lossy documents.
- **`file_cmds::holds(doc, ext)` / `holds_at` / `losses_at`**: PSD, PSB and .pcraft always hold the document; OpenRaster holds it when `ora_losses` is empty. The path-only `saves_in_place` and `layered_extension` stay for callers without a document.

### What changes when an `.ora` can't hold the document
| Route | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| File › Save | overwrote the `.ora`, marked saved | Save As opens on a **PSD** of the same name, with a notice listing what OpenRaster would drop; the `.ora` is untouched |
| Save As to an `.ora` | became the document's file, marked saved | writes a **copy**, as Photoshop does for formats that can't keep everything: the document keeps its file and stays unsaved |
| Automation `app.save` / headless `doc.save` without a path | overwrote | refused, with the reasons |
| Automation save to an `.ora` path | became the document's file | a copy |

A plain document (pixel layers and groups) still saves back to its `.ora` exactly as before; the existing round-trip test is unchanged.

One small behaviour change: an **sRGB** colour profile is no longer reported as lost, because OpenRaster readers assume sRGB. Any other profile still is.

### Tests
- **io** `ora::tests`: `losses_are_exactly_what_the_exporter_warns_about` covers adjust…

title: Merged and stamped layers keep their content bounds in CMYK and Lab
author: dgliwa
body:
## Problem

In CMYK and Lab documents, **Stamp Visible**, **Stamp Down** and **Copy Merged** produced a layer as large as the whole canvas, however small the content was. **Merge Layers**, **Merge Visible** and **Merge Down** did the same whenever an input could draw anywhere (for example a fill layer, even a masked one). Free Transform, the Move tool and alignment then acted on the full canvas. RGB and Grayscale were unaffected.

## Cause

Merging and stamping convert the straight-RGBA composite into the document's colour model. Fully transparent pixels are transparent black, and converting that leaves colour behind: K = 100% in CMYK, neutral a/b = 0.5 in Lab. Those pixels no longer equal the surface's default pixel, so `prune()` keeps them and the layer's content bounds span everything that was rendered.

## Fix

Fully transparent pixels are written as the surface's default pixel in both conversion paths (only when the format has alpha; over a Background everything stays opaque as before):

- `photocraft_compose::flatten_to_surface`: Stamp Visible, Stamp Down, Copy Merged.
- `photocraft_engine::pixels::composite_layers`: Merge Layers, Merge Visible, Merge Down.

## Tests

- New `engine/tests/merge_transparent_bounds.rs`: Merge Layers, Merge Visible (transparent document, with a masked fill layer, and onto a Background), Stamp Visible, Stamp Down and undo, in RGB/Grayscale at 8/16/32-bit and CMYK/Lab at 8/16-bit. On current `main` the stamp and masked-fill-layer merge tests fail (layer = full 300×400 canvas in CMYK); they pass with this change.
- New compose unit test `flatten_to_surface_leaves_transparent_pixels_empty_in_every_mode`.
- Passing locally on current `main` (c450e755): `cargo fmt`, clippy `-D warnings` on compose and engine, `cargo xtask layers`, compose and engine unit and integration tests, `panic_hunt -- --ignored`. `cargo xtask wasm` and `cargo xtask test-corpus` (2,769 passed, 0 failed) passed on the previous base (a0ff3a01); the latest rebase ont…

title: Layers: Merge Group for a selected group (#3832)
author: FredApps
body:
## What and why

#3832 asks for Photoshop's **Merge Group**. Before this PR, the Layers panel's right-click menu on a group offered only **Merge Down**. **Layer › Merge Layers (⌘E)** with a lone group selected also ran Merge Down, which merged the whole group *into the layer below it*: the group's contents and that unrelated layer became a single layer named after the lower one.

## Root cause

`layer.mergeLayers` passes a single selection to `layer.mergeDown`, and there was no group-specific path. The panel's context menu (`layer_menu_ui::entries`) always listed Merge Down for one selected layer.

## The fix

- **Engine:** new `layer.mergeGroup` command (`{"layer": id?}`, a group only, one undo step). It flattens the group's visible contents into one pixel layer in its place, under the group's name and id. As in Photoshop, the new layer keeps the group's opacity, blend mode (Pass Through becomes Normal), clipping and locks; the group's mask and style are baked into the pixels. Hidden children are dropped, and a hidden group refuses to merge.
- `layer.mergeLayers` (⌘E) with a lone group selected now runs Merge Group. With a single plain layer it still runs Merge Down, and with several layers selected it still runs Merge Layers.
- `layer.mergeDown` is unchanged, so scripts that call it on a group behave as before (`merging_a_group_down_preserves_the_composite` still passes).
- **UI:** a group's right-click menu shows **Merge Group** instead of Merge Down. The Layer menu's ⌘E item reads **Merge Group** while a lone group is selected.
- Added the "Merge Group" string, with Photoshop's terms, to the 16 bundled catalogs.

## Tests

- `engine::tests::merge_down_on_a_group_merges_the_group`: ⌘E on a group gives one layer named after the group, the layer below is untouched, the composite is unchanged, and undo brings the group back. It fails on main: the result is named "Below", because the group was merged into it.

title: Count video footage in history memory budgets
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Fixes #3882.

Deleting off-playhead video frames left their undo-retained pixels outside the history byte budget. Visit both edited frames and original footage in the shared tile visitor, so direct totals, incremental accounting and eviction see the same allocations. Existing pointer deduplication counts shared displayed/original frames only once; the newest-step retention policy stays intact.

Two regression tests fail before the fix and pass after it. They cover U8/U16/F32, original/altered/displayed aliases, rasterizing a video layer, undo/redo, and budget eviction. This complements the selection-only change in #3614 without incorporating it.

### Validation

- `cargo test -p photocraft-ops`: 13 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ops --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Scoped formatting and diff checks: passed.
- Full workspace wasm checks and dependency layering: passed.
- `cargo xtask perf --quick`: completed with exit 0. This uses smaller synthetic documents; it does not certify the full-size performance budgets. Some displayed latency targets remain exceeded.

### Bounded release measurement

Six independent 2048×2048 RGBA8 frames, frame 0 displayed, four off-playhead deletions, and a 48 MiB history budget, with trimming after each edit:

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Actual unique retained tile bytes | 96 MiB | 48 MiB |
| Reported current + history bytes | 16 MiB | 48 MiB |
| Reported history-only bytes | 0 MiB | 16 MiB |
| Undo states retained | 4 | 1 |

Actual retained bytes were counted independently from tile pointers; these are not process-RAM measurements. Four record/trim calls took 0.108 ms before and 11.233 ms after in single runs amid concurrent builds; the latter now performs eviction and deallocation. This is a correctness and memory-retention fix, not a runtime improvement claim.

title: Color: convert input-only embedded profiles to the working space on open (#3876)
author: HEOJUNFO
body:
Fixes #3876.

## What changed

Apple's Wide Color Sharing Profile, which iPhone photos embed, is an input-class (`scnr`) profile with only AToB tables. Under the default Preserve policy, open kept it as the document's profile. Reading from the document works through the AToB table, but nothing can be converted into it. So pasting, copying a layer from another document, or any other composite into the document failed with "RGB profile without matrix/TRC or BToA tags".

- `photocraft-cms`: new `Profile::can_be_destination()`, true when `pcs_to_device` succeeds for every intent.
- `ColorState::apply_open_policy`: when the embedded profile can't be a destination, Preserve now converts from it to the working space, as Convert does. Off still discards it, and the report adds `"inputOnly": true`. Profiles that can be a destination behave as before.

The pixels are converted from the embedded profile, not reinterpreted, so the photo looks the same after opening.

## Tests

- New test `color_cmds::settings_tests::input_only_profiles_are_converted_on_open`.
  - It builds Display P3 as an input-only profile (an `mAB` A2B0 table, no matrix/TRC, no BToA) and tags a document with it.
  - It checks that open converts the document to sRGB, and that `layer.copyToDocument` into it succeeds. It also checks that Off still discards the profile and that a Display P3 file is still kept.

author: Ni-zav

Addresses #3726.

When a key-release event is missed, subsequent key events may be treated as repeats, causing Undo or Redo to execute repeatedly.

This change:
- Ignores repeated key events for Undo and Redo.
- Preserves fresh key presses and other repeating shortcuts.
- Adds regression tests covering repeated Undo/Redo events, pointer movement, and fresh presses.

The regression tests are included but have not been executed. Physical XP-Pen/Xwayland validation is also pending.

title: fix(color): convert input-only ICC profiles when opening documents
author: Ni-zav
body:
Fixes #3876.

Some camera photos, including iPhone images using Apple's Wide Color Sharing Profile, contain input-only ICC profiles. These support converting image colors into a working space but cannot serve as destination profiles.

PhotoCraft previously preserved these profiles as document profiles, causing operations such as pasting layers and cross-document compositing to fail.

This change:
- Detects embedded profiles that support source conversion but cannot serve as destinations.
- Converts their pixels into the configured working color space when opening the document.
- Ensures the resulting document has a usable destination profile.
- Adds regression tests using a synthetic input-only ICC profile across color depths and profile policies.

The regression tests are included but have not been executed. Validation with an actual iPhone photo remains pending.

title: Engine: fix the stale 32-bit destructive Levels test
author: dottedt
body:
The engine test `adjust_params::tests::destructive_levels_dont_clip_in_32_bit` still expected the 32-bit Levels result to be clamped to 0..1 (black at 0, white at 255). Commit 53d09f58 ("Preserve HDR range in float adjustments and stack statistics", #2592) deliberately replaced the 0..1 LUT for 32-bit RGB Levels with direct `levels_float` evaluation so signed, unbounded HDR samples survive: black lands below the output black and white above the output white. That commit updated the compose test `levels_dont_clip_in_32_bit` but missed this engine test, so it asserts the stale clipped result and fails on `main` in both debug and release (`black @32: [-0.0796427, ...]`), reddening `cargo test` and `cargo xtask test-corpus` for every PR.

The compositor behaviour is the oracle-validated one (`compose::adjust::levels_float` matches the rgb32 and gray32 Photoshop oracles), so this fixes the stale test: integer depths still assert the clipped 10..245 output range, and the 32-bit case asserts the unclipped signed result.

Test: `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib` and `--release --lib` (1344 passed, 0 failed); `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.

Refs #2592.

title: Convert iPhone input ICC profiles into a working space on open (#3876)
author: vbasky
body:
iPhone JPEGs embed Apple's Wide Color Sharing profile: an input-class RGB ICC with AToB tables only. Opening worked because device→PCS uses AToB; compositing *into* that document failed (`RGB profile without matrix/TRC or BToA tags`).

On import, if the embedded profile cannot map PCS→device, convert the pixels into sRGB (or sGray), tag that working space, and warn. Pixel-only matrix/TRC and BToA profiles are unchanged.

Fixes #3876

title: Detect physical RAM on Windows for the GPU budget (#3814)
author: vbasky
body:
`detect_physical_memory` covered macOS, Linux, and FreeBSD. Windows used the catch-all that returns `None`, so the GPU compositor budget assumed 16 GB of RAM.

Query installed RAM through CIM (`Win32_ComputerSystem.TotalPhysicalMemory`), with WMIC as a fallback, matching the existing sysctl / `/proc/meminfo` approach. No `unsafe`.

Fixes #3814

title: Layer › Export As exports every selected layer or artboard (#3629)
author: fabianghe

I rendered the dialog with the `snapshot` example: two artboards (460×215 and 300×450) selected, then `ui.menu.invoke layer.exportAs`. The dialog reads "Export As: 2 layers" and previews the first board at 460 × 215 px.

## Tests

title: Reject oversized .pcraft pattern sizes on load (#3478)
author: vbasky
body:
A `.pcraft` pattern stores `width`/`height` in the manifest. A tiny hostile file can claim 65535×65535 with no tiles. Opening it and painting the pattern allocated `width × height × 16` bytes and aborted.

The loader now refuses a pattern that is empty or larger than the PSD reader's 30 000 px edge. Compose, GPU plan, and pattern commands skip tiles that cannot be painted, using overflow-free pixel counts.

Fixes #3478

title: Harden blob and ZIP reads against size overflow (#3486)
author: vbasky
body:
Two panic paths in `photocraft-format` bundle readers:

- `LoadFetch::blob` used `take(max_blob_bytes as u64 + 1)`, which overflows when the caller passes `usize::MAX` (unlimited). Debug panics; release wraps to `take(0)` so every blob fails its hash.
- `ZipReader::read` sliced compressed bytes without a bounds check. A cloned `Entry` from another archive panicked instead of returning `Err`.

Saturate the take limit, share the zstd decode helper, and return `Corrupt` for a foreign or out-of-range ZIP entry.

Fixes #3486

title: Open monochrome LinearRaw DNG files (#3497)
author: vbasky
body:
VueScan (and Leica M Monochrom) write greyscale DNG as LinearRaw with 1 sample per pixel. Decode required 3 samples for non-CFA data, so those files failed to open.

Allow 1-sample LinearRaw and replicate the grey plane into RGB during develop, which is valid DNG 1.7.

Fixes #3497

title: fix(automation): exit idle MCP stdio servers when clients go quiet
author: Ni-zav
body:
Fixes #3660.

MCP server processes can remain alive indefinitely when a client stops communicating without closing its connection.

This change:
- Adds a 30-minute inactivity timeout to the MCP stdio transport.
- Shuts down idle servers even when the client leaves stdin open.
- Resets the inactivity timer whenever a request arrives.
- Preserves normal shutdown when stdin reaches EOF.
- Adds regression tests for abandoned connections and active clients.
- Documents the new lifecycle behavior.

Tests are included but have not been executed.

title: fix(automation): release idle headless TCP server ports
author: Ni-zav
body:
Addresses #3682.

Headless TCP servers currently keep their listening ports indefinitely, even after all clients have disconnected.

This can leave stale daemon processes occupying ports needed by subsequent sessions.

This change:
- Adds a 30-minute inactivity timeout to the headless TCP server.
- Tracks active client connections.
- Prevents idle shutdown while clients remain connected.
- Releases the listening socket when the server becomes inactive.
- Preserves existing authentication and connection limits.
- Adds a regression test verifying that active connections remain usable and idle ports are released.
- Documents the new TCP server lifecycle.

Tests are included but have not been executed.
