title: PSD: read Gradient Map stops in Grayscale, HSB, CMYK and Lab
author: timothydaly1
body:
## What

The PSD reader assumed every Gradient Map stop was RGB. Photoshop records each stop's colour in the colour structure of the space it was picked in: 0 RGB, 1 HSB, 2 CMYK, 7 Lab, 8 Gray. Non-RGB stops therefore came out as the wrong colour. Grayscale documents were hit hardest: their maps rendered inverted, because a Gray stop stores ink, where 10000 means black.

`parse_gradient_map` now decodes stops with the shared `channel_map::decode_color`, the same decoder Solid Color and the other colour structures already use. Two changes support this:
- `decode_color` gains the HSB space.
- Stops in colour-book or other spaces still return `None`. The layer then keeps its raw block, as before.

## Measured (Photoshop-authored oracles, `crates/io/tests/corpus.rs`)

Comparison: the same corpus and the same build, with and without this change.

| Oracle | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| gradient map, gray 8-bit | DIFF | **PASS** (0.0039) |
| gradient map, gray 16-bit | DIFF | **PASS** (0.0020) |
| gradient map, CMYK / Lab | 0.98–1.0 error | 0.43–0.49 error |
| every other oracle | — | unchanged |

- The Photoshop-oracle floor goes from **133 to 139** of 258. `docs/gaps.md` (G1) and `docs/file-format-parity.md` are updated.
- The CMYK and Lab maps are now in the right colours. What still separates them from Photoshop is how they render, not how they are read.

## Tests

- New `adjust_map::tests::gradient_map_stops_in_every_colour_space` covers Gray (ink), HSB, Lab, CMYK, and an unsupported space, which stays raw.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-io` passes.
- The full release corpus run (`psd`, `codecs`, `io`, `engine` with `corpus`) passes everything except `adjust_params::tests::destructive_levels_dont_clip_in_32_bit`, which also fails on main.
- clippy (`-D warnings`), `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` are clean.
- `docs/scorecard.md` is regenerated.

title: fix(color): validate RGB working profiles atomically
author: zenjabba
body:

title: CMYK: Invert, Posterize and Threshold on the inks; 16-bit Lab Invert keeps greys neutral
author: timothydaly1
body:
## What

This builds on main's `adjust::apply_in` (#4038), which already evaluates Lab Invert, Posterize, Threshold, Brightness/Contrast and Gradient Map on L, a and b. It adds what main doesn't have yet:

- **CMYK Invert, Posterize and Threshold on the inks.**
  - Photoshop inverts and posterizes each ink, black included, so white paper inverts to 400% ink.
  - Its Threshold gives either paper or 100% black ink alone.
  - The cmyk8 and cmyk16 oracles follow these rules on every pixel of the files' own inks.
  - `apply_in`'s mode dispatch gains CMYK, and `cmyk_channel_adjustment` says which adjustments it covers.
- **16-bit Lab Invert keeps greys neutral.**
  - Photoshop mirrors a and b around neutral at 16 bits, while 8-bit bytes become `255 - v`, so a lands on −1 − a.
  - Main's `apply_lab` used `1 - v` at every depth.
  - `stored_channels` holds the rules for both depths, and `apply_lab` now calls it for Invert and Posterize.
- **Exact destructive path.** Image › Adjustments on a Lab or CMYK layer runs Invert, Posterize and Threshold on the layer's stored channels (`engine::pixels::adjusted_channels`), with no trip through RGB, and a selection mixes the stored values.
- **GPU:** `adjustment_on_gpu` sends CMYK Invert, Posterize and Threshold to the CPU, as it already does for the Lab rules.

## Measured (`oracle_diff` over `corpus/photoshop`, on main as of `0a32b359`)

| Oracle (8 and 16 bit) | Bad pixels on main | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| cmyk invert | 77% | 10% |
| cmyk posterize-4 | 71% | 9% |
| cmyk threshold-128 | 37% | 1.6% |
| lab16 invert | 52% | 1.2% |

- Nothing else in the table changes. The pass count stays at **145/258**, which main already reaches, so `pass_floor` goes **133 → 145**. That includes the gain from #4033's Gradient Map stops.
- The rest is the separation, not the rules. In CMYK, the inks come from the screen colour separated through the document's CMYK profile. Our synthetic coated profile puts much more black into neutrals than Ph…

A paired release smoke comparison also completed: 6000×4000 RGB8, 12 dense translucent raster layers, prefix cache disabled, GPU completion awaited, one cold/upload and one adapted warm-up excluded before three measured samples per run. title: fix(ui): allow selecting shapes and editing color with path selection (#3915)
author: seotarek
body:
### Summary
Resolves #3915: "can't change rectangle color after drawing it. No way to select a rectangle with rectangle tool, select with path or move tool, can't change color."

### Root Cause
1. `options_bar` in `crates/ui-egui/src/vector_ui.rs` previously returned early whenever `tool == Tool::PathSelection` or `tool == Tool::DirectSelection` by displaying static hint strings, hiding the shape options bar (Fill swatch/checkbox, Stroke swatch/width/style, and corner radius) even when a shape layer was active.
2. `path_selection_finish` in `crates/ui-egui/src/vector_ui.rs` returned early without doing anything when movement was `< 0.5` px, meaning clicking a shape with the Path Selection tool never selected the shape layer.
3. `candidates` in `crates/ui-egui/src/direct_select.rs` only queried the active shape layer or work path, ignoring other visible shape layers on the canvas.

title: Fix: Preview pixelation in Sharpen filters
author: AvrazAkraye
body:
## Summary

Fixes preview pixelation in **15 edge-detection, noise-reduction, blur, and morphological filters** by ensuring they preview at full resolution instead of using a downsampled proxy.

### All Filters Fixed (15 total)

**Sharpen Filters (5):**
- Sharpen
- Sharpen More
- Sharpen Edges
- Unsharp Mask
- Smart Sharpen

**Edge-Detection Filters (3):**
- High Pass - Extracts edge/detail information
- Find Edges - Performs pure edge detection
- Emboss - Creates 3D effect via edge detection

**Noise Reduction (2):**
- Median - Removes noise by replacing pixels with neighborhood median
- Despeckle - Removes one-pixel speckles/noise

**Morphological Operations (2):**
- Maximum (Dilate) - Expands features by one pixel
- Minimum (Erode) - Shrinks features by one pixel

**Blur Filters (3):**
- Motion Blur - Creates directional blur streaks with pixel-sized distance
- Box Blur - Creates rectangular blur artifacts with pixel-sized radius
- Surface Blur - Selective blur that preserves edges while smoothing

## Problem

When preview was enabled for these filters, the preview appeared **pixelated, blocky, or inaccurate**. This happened because:

- These filters work on **pixel-level details**: edges, noise specks, one-pixel boundaries, directional artifacts, rectangular patterns
- The preview was using a **downsampled proxy image** with fewer pixels
- On a proxy, pixel-sized features either **disappear or distort**
  - Edges average away → edge detection fails
  - Speckles are smoothed → despeckle finds nothing
  - One-pixel boundaries become fractions → morphological ops distort
  - Rectangular blur artifacts change shape → blockiness increases
  - Blur streaks change length → inaccurate motion preview
- The preview does **not match the final result**

## Root Cause Analysis

These 15 filters fall into 5 categories, each with specific pixel-level dependencies:

title: Security: pin and verify the Windows signing client (#2936)
author: Erica4fr
body:
## Summary

`packaging/windows/sign.ps1` downloaded `Microsoft.Trusted.Signing.Client` from the unversioned NuGet URL and loaded its dlib into `signtool`, next to the Azure signing secrets, with no version or integrity check (#2936, finding 1 of #1372). Once #3794 passes the Azure secrets to the release workflow, this branch is what PhotoCraft's own Windows releases will run.

The script now downloads a pinned version (1.0.95) and checks its SHA-256 before extracting it. On a mismatch it throws and never runs `signtool`. Upgrading the client is now a deliberate change to both values, and the comment above them says how to make it.

## No change to what gets signed today

- The unversioned URL resolves to 1.0.95 today (it redirects to `microsoft.trusted.signing.client.1.0.95.nupkg`). I downloaded it and the versioned URL, and the two files are byte-identical: SHA-256 `3bfcf1e0a3cb42af1692f0a8ed45c15de070c2de86f28a59b2795d904d8a920f`.
- NuGet's catalog entry for 1.0.95 lists the same SHA-512 and size (14,651,525 bytes).
- The package's `.signature.p7s` names Microsoft Corporation as the author signer, countersigned by the NuGet.org repository. I decoded it but did not validate the certificate chain.
- nuget.org keeps the existing signatures on published packages when it rotates its repository certificate ([NuGet blog, March 2024](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/nuget/the-nuget-org-repository-signing-certificate-will-be-updated-as-soon-as-april-8th-2024/)), so the pinned bytes shouldn't change underneath us.

## Testing

`sign.ps1` has no automated test and real signing needs the release secrets. I ran the Azure branch on Windows 11 under PowerShell 7.6 (the release workflow's `pwsh`) with dummy `AZURE_*` values and `SIGNTOOL` pointing at a stub. The stub logs its arguments and exits 1, the way signtool fails on dummy credentials.

- **Pinned version, expected hash:** the script downloads 1.0.95, the hash matches, and it passes `client\bin\x64\Azure.CodeSigning.Dlib.dll…

title: File Handling: wire Maximize PSD and PSB File Compatibility (#204)
author: Erica4fr
body:
## Summary

Preferences › File Handling › Maximize PSD and PSB File Compatibility was stored but read nowhere, so it was hidden from the dialog (`HIDDEN_UNTIL_IMPLEMENTED`). This PR wires it up and shows it.

- **Always** (the default) and **Ask When Saving** save as before: the real merged image, resource 1057 `has_real_merged_data = true`. Ask has no dialog yet, so it saves the merged image because Photoshop's checkbox starts on. Image Previews already handles Ask this way.
- **Never** writes Photoshop's placeholder instead of the merged image and sets 1057 `has_real_merged_data = false`. The composite isn't rendered at all, so saves are smaller and faster. Layers, alpha channels, spot channels and the Quick Mask are written as usual, and the file reopens the same.

The preference applies to every save that reads the File Handling preferences: Save, Save As, Save a Copy and automation saves in the app (`ExportSettings` / `save_settings`), the engine's save commands (`SaveOpts`), and the web build. The CLI's `--out` keeps its stateless default (Always).

## What the placeholder is

The placeholder is white, has no alpha channel and uses the document's colour channels. I checked this against Photoshop's own files: the PSD corpora have 36 Photoshop-saved files with `has_real_merged_data = 0` (psd-tools and ag-psd, one PSB among them). Every one stores a uniform `0xFF` merged image with 3 channels and no merged alpha, including `ag-psd/read/alpha-composite`, whose document has transparency. `photocraft-psd`'s `PsdBuilder` already writes the same placeholder when no composite is given.

The placeholder is encoded the same way as a real merged image (`placeholder_planes` beside `merged_planes`). So it comes out as exact white in every model: CMYK white is no ink, and Lab white is L 100 with neutral a*/b*, including the 16-bit Lab chroma scale.

title: feat(input): touchscreen two-finger pan and pinch-zoom
author: MXJinjing
body:
The issue you mentioned has been fixed.

When the left mouse button is held, wheel, trackpad, or Wacom touch-ring navigation no longer cancels an active mouse or pen stroke. The existing stroke remains active and is committed normally when the button is released.

The touch input handling has also been improved:

- A first finger can begin drawing immediately.
- The grace period remains open while the first finger stays near its initial position.
- If a second finger arrives before tool ownership is established, the input becomes navigation without leaving a partial stroke.
- If the first finger has already exceeded the grace period, its current stroke is committed before pinch/pan navigation takes over.
- Multi-touch navigation no longer causes a visible jump, and the cursor/tool indicator is hidden while navigating.

### Summary

- Preserve active mouse, pen, and touch-ring strokes during wheel or trackpad navigation.
- Add a touch grace state machine for reliable single-finger drawing and two-finger navigation.
- Commit an owned stroke before transitioning to pinch/pan navigation.
- Prevent compatibility pointer events from starting a new tool press during wheel navigation.
- Hide the cursor while multi-touch navigation is active.

### Test Plan

- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib input_tests::`
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib touch_nav::`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `git diff --check`
- Built the WASM release successfully.
- Tested the WASM build in a tablet browser with mouse, trackpad, wheel, and multi-touch interactions.

The core touch state machine is shared by WASM and native egui backends. Native Windows/Surface touch input still needs additional hardware validation because I do not currently have a compatible device available.

title: Selection: lasso polygons scan only the edges that cross each row
author: xsvm
body:
## Problem

`algo::selection::polygon` (`crates/algo/src/selection.rs`) builds the mask for the Lasso, Polygonal Lasso and Magnetic Lasso tools (`select.lasso` → `polygon_selection`). For every pixel row of the document, and for each of the 4 anti-aliasing sub-rows, it tested every edge of the polygon. That is O(document height × 4 × points) on one thread, and it scanned the full height even when the lasso covered only a few rows. A freehand lasso easily reaches thousands of points, so the selection appeared with a visible delay after release.

## Change

- The edges are sorted by their top y. Each band of 64 rows takes the edges that reach it and keeps an active edge list, so each sub-row tests only the edges that cross it. Horizontal and NaN edges are dropped up front, since they never crossed a sub-row before either.
- The bands are filled in parallel (rayon). On wasm they run serially, using the same `cfg` pattern as the rest of the file.
- The crossing formula, the `total_cmp` sort and the span accumulation order are unchanged, so the mask is bit-identical.

## Tests

`polygon_matches_the_every_edge_fill_bit_for_bit` keeps the previous fill in the test module as the oracle. It compares `to_bits()` of every mask value, with and without anti-aliasing.

Polygons:
- a self-intersecting star;
- horizontal edges, repeated points and collinear runs;
- vertices on sub-row centres and pixel edges;
- polygons entirely outside the area, and ones straddling every side;
- NaN, infinite and `-0.0` coordinates;
- random polygons and lasso-like random walks of 3–400 points.

Areas: one taller than a band, one with a negative offset, and one 1 pixel wide.

## Numbers

24 MP (6000×4000). Before is `main` at f14817a5, after is this branch. Both ran on the same CI runner type (AMD EPYC 7763, 4 cores), best of 3.

| Lasso | Points | `polygon` before → after | `select.lasso` before → after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| large (5400×3600) | 100 | 111 → 52 ms | 124 → 65 ms |
| large | 1,000…

title: Verify PngSuite archives and cached corpus files
author: zenjabba
body:
PngSuite downloads were extracted without a checksum, and restored caches were accepted based only on the number of `.png` filenames. Bound curl stdout to 1 MiB, verify the fixed archive before extraction and every cached file against a committed manifest, then install a verified staged replacement with rollback. Failed restoration retains and identifies the old cache backup.

The archive checksum is corroborated by pinned HTTPS repository records in [rivet-png](https://github.com/safewords/rivet-png/blob/134faad88038d1bab62d6dccb5b5ed955b2f79d5/tests/pngsuite/SHA256SUMS) and [opencodecs](https://github.com/kevinjohncutler/opencodecs/blob/6f070029cbca18ad9b9093944ef4d904d63c8b22/corpus/checksums.json), and the existing corpus bytes. A loopback-only curl 7.88.1 reproduction proved its size flag alone did not bound unknown-length responses; bounded copying now rejects excess bytes and kills/reaps that child before extraction. The legacy upstream URL remains; this establishes integrity pinning, not signed upstream authenticity. The existing CI cache key includes the archive pin and new manifest.

Fixes #3939.

Validation: unchanged-baseline fake-cache and unexpected-archive reproductions fail the expected rejection checks; all 60 xtask tests (including 11 new regressions and one subprocess fixture), strict all-target Clippy, formatting and layers pass. The retained real archive passes the production pin and exact 178-file manifest; the focused real PngSuite decoder oracle compares 162 PNGs successfully. Unit tests use owned fixtures and subprocesses; transport acceptance uses only loopback chunked responses. No external network or shared-cache mutation. title: Preserve grayscale appearance in profileless exports
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Fixes #3948.

Exporting linear-gray pixels to TGA previously wrote their linear values and dropped the ICC profile: an 8-bit sample decoded as 0.2509804 instead of the approximately 0.5380651 required by PhotoCraft's default sGray encoding. The result appeared too dark. The profileless export branch now reuses `convert_gray` to convert grayscale samples to sGray, alongside the existing RGB conversion.

The expected values follow PhotoCraft's sGray default (sRGB tone curve) and the [ICC-published sRGB transfer function](https://registry.color.org/rgb-registry/files/sRGB.pdf), with grayscale profiles interpreted through their tone reproduction curve ([ICC profile specification](https://www.color.org/icc32.pdf)). This is an encoding/appearance consistency fix; Photoshop acceptance was not tested.

Regression tests decode TGA/BMP/GIF/QOI output from 8-, 16-, and 32-bit sources and check the transfer function independently. Controls cover untagged/default sGray, grayscale alpha preservation, and PNG retaining its profile and samples. The linear-gray test failed before the fix while the default-gray control passed. Existing EXR/HDR handling remains covered by the flat-format tests. The shared profileless branch also applies to Netpbm; these tests do not establish an independent PFM convention.

title: Corpus: verify PngSuite downloads and cached files
author: arthurdeka
body:
Fixes #3939.

PngSuite is fetched over HTTP, and the existing cache check accepted any directory containing enough PNGs. Verify the fixed 2017-07-19 archive against a committed SHA-256 **before invoking tar**, then verify every extracted or cached file against `xtask/pngsuite.sha256`.

- Stage downloads and extraction separately; keep the existing corpus until verification succeeds.
- Refetch missing or modified files and reject unexpected files and symlinks. Bound checksum reads of a corrupt cache or download.
- Verify all 176 PNGs, the license and the README. The existing CI cache key hashes the pin file and `xtask/*.sha256`, so these pins invalidate the old cache without a workflow change.
- Preserve the previous corpus if installation fails and report its recovery path if restoration fails.

The PNGs and license were checked byte-for-byte against the pinned HTTPS copies in [Crunch](https://github.com/chrissimpkins/Crunch/tree/a343532e128bef8d49636b7044b012bf05824658/benchmarks/img) and [image-png](https://github.com/image-rs/image-png/tree/b2f10c6a7e3127d4aaf231f3eae731a33e6eb0bc/tests/pngsuite). The README is from the official archive. No corpus images or new dependencies are committed.

### Validation

Passed in [fork validation](https://github.com/arthurdeka/photocraft/actions/runs/38208100543):
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p xtask --locked` — 53 tests, including archive rejection before extraction, verified cache reuse, cache corruption/refetch, and extracted-file rejection.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`

title: Dismiss Home when closing a document tab (#3981)
author: vbasky
body:
## Summary
Closing a document tab no longer re-opens the Home overlay when the remaining document count matches the count stored when Home was last opened.

## Problem
`ChromeState.home` stored the document count at the moment Home opened so File › New / Open could leave the overlay. Closing a later tab restored that count, `shows_home` matched again, and Home covered the remaining document with its tabs hidden until the user created another document.

## Fix
Clear `home` as soon as the live document count differs from the stored value. Home then stays dismissed until the user opens it again. Empty workspace still auto-shows Home when Preferences › Auto show the Home Screen is on.

## Tests
- `home_screen_closes_when_a_document_opens` now asserts that returning to the stored count after a dismiss does not re-open Home.
- `closing_a_tab_does_not_return_to_home` creates two documents, opens Home, creates another, closes it, and checks Home stays off.

Closes #3981

title: Edit › Transform › Rotate and Skew no longer scale (#3941)
author: vbasky
body:
## Summary
Edit › Transform › Rotate turns the box from handle drags. Edit › Transform › Skew skews from corners as well as edges.

## Problem
Scale, Rotate, and Free Transform all used `TransformMode::Free`. Corner and edge drags always scaled. Skew only treated **edge** handles as ⌘-skew, so a corner still scaled.

## Fix
- `TransformMode::Rotate` from `edit.transform.rotate`. Handle drags rotate about the reference point (same as dragging outside in Free Transform).
- Skew remaps a corner to the adjacent edge so the parallelogram shears instead of resizing.
- The transform context menu can check Rotate as the live mode.

## Tests
- `rotate_mode_turns_the_box_from_a_corner_handle`
- `skew_mode_skews_from_a_corner_handle`

Closes #3941

title: fix(ui): show a paint-bucket cursor for the Paint Bucket tool (#3968)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3968.

The Paint Bucket is not `is_brushlike()`, so the canvas cursor match in `canvas.rs` fell through to the catch-all `CursorIcon::Crosshair`.

It now has its own arm, built the same way as the Eyedropper and Color Sampler arms just above it. `paint_bucket_cursor` draws the existing `paint-bucket` toolbar icon at the pointer with `icons::cursor`, the same helper `pipette_cursor` uses, and hides the OS pointer. The hotspot is the left end of the bucket's rim, where the paint pours out. Preferences › Cursors › Other Cursors = Precise still shows the crosshair, as it does for the pipette tools.

What does not change:
- ⌥ held over the Paint Bucket still shows the sampling pipette. That arm comes earlier in the match.
- The Gradient tool keeps its crosshair. The issue says the Gradient tool takes the same fallback, but Photoshop's Gradient cursor is also a crosshair.

Test: `paint_bucket_shows_a_bucket_cursor` (in `input_tests.rs`) hovers the canvas with the Paint Bucket selected and expects `CursorIcon::None`, which means the drawn bucket replaces the pointer. After setting `cursors.other` to `precise` it expects `CursorIcon::Crosshair`. Without the fix the first check gets `Crosshair` and fails.

title: Pencil: no 8-bit dither on aliased strokes, one flat colour at partial opacity
author: cloudalister
body:
## What

The 8-bit stroke dither (`dither8` in `crates/paint/src/render.rs`) ran on every stroke, including aliased ones. An aliased stroke paints each pixel by the same amount, so it has no gradient to band; the dither only scattered it over neighbouring levels.

Repro (8-bit RGB, white background, Pencil 1 px, foreground 219/41/61, opacity 30%): one straight line comes out as four colours — 244/191/197, 245/191/197, 244/190/196, … A foreground that falls between 8-bit levels does the same at 100% opacity. Photoshop's Pencil paints a single value.

This matters for pixel art: a tolerance-0 Magic Wand or Paint Bucket stops on the grain (a block painted with the Pencil at 30%, then a tolerance-0 Paint Bucket click in its middle, filled 2 pixels before this change and the whole block after), and Indexed Color picks up extra palette entries.

## Fix

`composite` skips the dither when the brush is aliased (Pencil, Eraser in Pencil and Block modes). Soft brushes keep it, so `an_8bit_soft_stroke_is_dithered_instead_of_banded` still holds.

## Tests

- New: `an_aliased_stroke_at_partial_opacity_is_one_flat_colour` — fails before the fix (pixel 5 differs), passes after.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-paint`: 96/96
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests`: 1529/1529
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib pencil`: 13/13
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-paint --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: clean
- Also checked in the running app over the control channel (`paint.pencil` at opacity 0.3, `document.sampleColor`, `paint.bucket` tolerance 0).

Windows 11, rustc 1.99.0.

title: Remote Canvas: draw in PhotoCraft from a tablet or phone
author: rippelz
body:
## What

**Window › Remote Canvas…** lets you draw in PhotoCraft from a tablet or phone over your local network, with a pen or a finger. PhotoCraft serves a page that mirrors its window. The page sends pen, finger and gesture input back. There's nothing to install on the device: scan the QR code and draw.

- **Devices:** iPad and iPhone (Safari), Android (Chrome, Samsung Internet, Firefox) and Windows tablets (Edge, Chrome). The desktop side is plain `std::net` plus `tungstenite`, so it runs on Windows, macOS and Linux.
- **Pen:**
  - Pressure and tilt.
  - Apple Pencil is read from `touchType == "stylus"` touches, which Safari reports at a higher rate than its pen pointer events.
  - The eraser end or eraser button erases.
  - Hovering shows the brush outline, including brush-tip outlines. The OS cursor bitmap never appears in the capture, so the page draws the outline itself.
- **Fingers (Procreate-style):**
  - One finger pans.
  - Two fingers pan, pinch-zoom and rotate (snapping to 90°).
  - Two-finger tap undoes; three-finger tap redoes.
  - Holding a finger still picks a colour, using the Eyedropper's Sample Size and Sample Layers settings.
  - Palm rejection while the pen is down.
- **Finger drawing toggle:** a toolbar toggle on the page makes one finger draw, for phones without a pen. A finger only starts drawing once it moves, so pinches and holds don't leave marks.
- **Toolbar:** undo, redo, fit on screen, and full window or canvas only.
- **Turning it on:** `--remote [port]` or `PHOTOCRAFT_REMOTE=<port>`; the default port is 9876. It stays on across restarts until turned off.

Docs: `docs/remote-canvas.md`.

## Layout

- `apps/photocraft-remote` is a new wasm app (Rust, `wasm-bindgen`) for the page. The input logic is platform-free and tested natively: `gesture.rs`, `finger.rs`, `smooth.rs`, `cursor.rs` and `frame.rs`. `web.rs` is the browser glue.

title: fix(#3470): Missing Adjustment Layer: Clarity/Dehaze
author: roaldosulejmani
body:
Closes #3470

## What changed

#### What changed

**Document model (`crates/doc`)**
- `Adjustment::ClarityDehaze { clarity, dehaze }` (both `-100..=100`, 0 = off), label "Clarity and Dehaze", `Adjustment::clarity_dehaze()` constructor, and `Adjustment::is_spatial()` which reports that the kind reads its neighbours (only this kind today). `crates/doc/src/adjust.rs`.

- New `crates/compose/src/clarity.rs`: `apply(buf, clarity, dehaze)` — Dehaze (dark-channel-prior transmission of He, Sun & Tang 2010, estimated on a ≤768 px proxy and guided-filtered) then Clarity (large-radius guided-filter local-contrast boost, strongest in the midtones). This is the same pair of stages the Camera Raw filter already runs (`crates/algo/src/camera_raw.rs`), reimplemented here because the compositor may not depend on `algo` (layering). - `crates/compose/src/adjust.rs`: `apply_depth` dispatches `ClarityDehaze` to `crate::clarity::apply`.
- `crates/compose/src/lib.rs`: because the effect is spatial, the compositor now evaluates it once over the whole canvas before tiling (`prepare_spatial_adjustments`), caches the full-canvas result (`spatial_maps` keyed by layer id + params) and crops it per tile/band (`adjusted_backdrop`). Documents above `MAX_SPATIAL_PIXELS` (64 MP) skip the pre-pass and evaluate per region (documented seam limitation). A new compose test renders a Clarity/Dehaze document in tiles, bands and a sub-rectangle and asserts bit-identical results.

title: Linux: StartupWMClass in the launcher matches the window class (X11 icon and grouping)
author: DomiLuebben
body:
## Problem
`packaging/linux/ai.storyteller.photocraft.desktop` says `StartupWMClass=photocraft`, but the window's class is the app id: the app sets it with `with_app_id(APP_ID)`, and on X11 that becomes `WM_CLASS`. Read back from a running build under XWayland:

```
$ xprop -id <window> WM_CLASS
WM_CLASS(STRING) = "", "ai.storyteller.photocraft"
```

Shells that pair a window with its launcher by `StartupWMClass` (GNOME on X11, many panels and docks) can't match the two, which shows as a generic icon and a second taskbar entry on X11 sessions. This may be part of #3157 and #1838 (icons missing on some installs); I only verified the mismatch itself, not those reports. Wayland sessions match by app id and are unaffected. FilmCraft's launcher already uses its full app id.

## Fix
`StartupWMClass=ai.storyteller.photocraft`, plus a test that keeps the launcher's value equal to `APP_ID` (and `Icon=` equal to it). The line came in with the first packaging commit (d98bee4c), before the app id was set.

## Tests
- `tests::the_launcher_names_the_window_class_the_app_uses` fails with the old value and passes now.
- `cargo test -p photocraft --bin photocraft` (104 tests), `desktop-file-validate` and `packaging/linux/apprun-test.sh` pass.
- Not tested: a GNOME-on-X11 session (I run KDE on Wayland, where the class mismatch is visible with `xprop` under XWayland but the shell pairs by app id).

title: Layers panel: show the Background layer and generated layer names in the UI language (display only)
author: DomiLuebben
body:
## Problem
The Layers panel shows the engine's English names in every UI language: the Background layer, and every generated name ("Layer 1", "Group 1", "Curves 2", "Gradient Fill 1", "Layer 1 copy").

## Why display only
The names are stored in the document, in PSD files and in recorded actions. Since #4036 the engine finds the Background structurally and no longer by name, but the stored name is still what File › New wrote, and generated names such as "Layer 1" are part of saved files and actions; creating layers with translated names would make recorded actions and exported PSDs depend on the UI language.

## Changes (`layer_row_ui::display_name`)
1. **Background**: a layer named "Background" that has the Background traits (`Layer::has_background_traits`, the same test #4036 builds on) shows `tr("Background")` ("Hintergrund"). A layer that merely carries the name, or a PSD's own name for it ("Hintergrund", "背景"), is shown as it is.

title: Clone Stamp and History Brush: releasing a stroke commits the live pixels
author: xsvm
body:
## Problem

Releasing a Clone Stamp or History Brush stroke ran `paint.cloneStamp` / `paint.historyBrush` from scratch: it rebuilt the coverage of the whole stroke, sampled the source and composited everything again. `LiveRetouch` had already drawn exactly those pixels while the stroke was being made. The Brush stopped rendering twice in #2131; the retouching tools still did.

## Change

The retouching tools reuse the Brush's mechanism; there is no second offer slot.

- `brush_cmds::LiveCommit` is shared. Its `seed` becomes `Option<u64>`: the Brush and Pencil have one, the retouching tools don't. The match rule is unchanged: same command, document revision, params and points.
- `Session::offer_live_retouch` turns a finished `LiveRetouch` into a `LiveCommit`. `paint.cloneStamp` and `paint.historyBrush` take it with the same one line `paint.stroke` uses, and report `"fromLive": true`. Anything that doesn't match renders as before.
- The offer is refused in two cases:
  - The Healing Brush: it shows only its texture while drawing and blends on release, so it has nothing to offer.
  - The brush, the target layer or the clone source changed during the stroke. The document revision doesn't cover those. The check runs once at offer time, which is right before the commit.
- `LiveRetouch::push` uses only the position and pressure of its points, which is all the retouching commands parse. Before, the live stroke got the pen's tilt and the times, but the commit didn't. Now the preview shows exactly what the commit paints, whoever feeds the points: the canvas, the control channel or tests.
- On the canvas, `finish_gesture` offers the live Clone Stamp or History Brush stroke before the commit, together with any drag points it hasn't rendered yet, and withdraws the offer afterwards.

## Tests

- `a_live_clone_or_history_stroke_commits_its_own_pixels`: at 8, 16 and 32 bits, with and without a feathered selection, the commit takes the live pixels. They equal a fresh run of the comm…

title: fix(ui): cancel unfinished Polygonal Lasso when switching tools
author: Ni-zav
body:
Fixes #4012.

Switching from Polygonal Lasso to another tool could leave an unfinished polygon outline visible on the canvas.

Clear the pending polygon vertices and selection mode when switching tools. This removes the stale outline without changing the existing selection or undo history.

Added a regression test covering the switch to Quick Selection and back to Polygonal Lasso, including selection and history preservation.

Validation: Regression test added; local Cargo checks were not executed.

title: i18n(es): add 548 missing rows, fix five filter and video terms
author: diegozpy
body:
Spanish catalog (`crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/es.tsv`): 548 rows added, 5 changed. Only that file changes.

**Missing rows (548)**
Strings the code shows but Spanish didn't have, so they appeared in English. Each one already exists in at least three other catalogs (pt-BR, nl, el, uk, ja, pl…) and its English text appears in the code. Rows that only stale catalogs still carry were left out. Most are not `tl!` literals, so the coverage gate doesn't see them:
- filter and effect names built from the parameter enums (Accented Edges, Glass, Sumi-e, Lens Flare lens types…);
- tool-group labels (Wand, Healing, Patch, Dodge/Burn…), panel and dialog labels, measurement columns (Area, Perimeter, Integrated Density…);
- Camera Raw labels (`cameraRaw` context), the `No Color` layer label and four `@id` command overrides.

They are appended as one section at the end and follow the catalog's existing vocabulary and formal register. Where a row already existed with "…" (`HDR Toning…`, `Shear…`, `Picture Frame…`), the new row matches it.

**Changed (5)**
These are terms that read like product branding or lose the meaning. They now match the new rows:
- *Smart Sharpen…*: «Enfoque suavizado» (smoothed: the opposite of sharpening) → «Enfoque inteligente», like *Smart Blur*.
- *Mezzotint…*: «Grabado» (any engraving) → «Grabado a media tinta».

title: fix(psd): Multichannel alpha channels stay alpha; a save keeps resources and global blocks
author: echelon

title: feat(save): File › Save keeps a JPEG's quality and a WebP's lossy/lossless encoding (#2399)
author: echelon
body:
## What

In Photoshop, File › Save writes a file back the way it came: a JPEG keeps the quality it was saved at, and a WebP stays lossy or lossless. Until now PhotoCraft saved every JPEG at the codec default (quality 90) and every WebP lossless, so a lossy WebP more or less doubled in size and a JPEG's quality changed for no reason.

- **JPEG:** on open, the quality is estimated from the file's quantisation tables (DQT): the ITU-T T.81 Annex K luminance and chrominance tables scaled by the IJG quality curve. The estimate is exact for tables made that way and the closest fit for others (`photocraft_codecs::jpeg_quality`).
- **WebP:** on open, `VP8L` means lossless and `VP8 ` means lossy. A lossy file's quality is read back from its key frame's base quantiser index (RFC 6386 §9.6), taking segment quantisers into account and looking inside animation frames (`photocraft_codecs::webp_encoding`). If the quality can't be read, a lossy file is saved at 75.
- The settings are stored on the document as `Document::file_encoding` and go into `.pcraft` saves (`#[serde(default)]`, so older files still load). A save that doesn't ask for a quality uses them: the engine's `encode` (Save a Copy, the headless server, automation) and the UI's `save_settings` (File › Save, Save As, Save a Copy, TIFF/Targa option flows).
- An explicit `quality` param still wins. New documents and files in other formats keep the codec defaults.
- Never crash: every DQT, RIFF and VP8 header read is bounds-checked. A hostile or truncated header gives no estimate, never a panic.

Refs #2399. That issue also covers the quality setting for Quick Export and batch, and the WebP DPI warning; those are still open. There is no JPEG Options dialog yet (FILE-215-19), so reusing a quality picked in Save As is left for when that dialog exists.

## Tests

- `crates/codecs/tests/source_settings.rs`:
  - JPEG at q ∈ {1, 5, 10, 25, 40, 50, 60, 70, 75, 80, 85, 90, 95, 98, 100}, RGB and Gray: the estimate is within ±2.
  - A…

title: feat(psd): Gradient Map stops in CMYK, Lab, Gray and HSB import and round-trip
author: echelon
body:
## What

A Gradient Map adjustment layer made in a CMYK, Lab or Grayscale document stores its colour stops in that document's colour space (Photoshop also writes HSB stops). PhotoCraft only read RGB stops, so these layers imported as `Unsupported` and had no effect on the composite.

- `grdm` colour stops now decode every plain PSD colour space: 0 RGB, 1 HSB (hue 0..65535 → 0..360°), 2 CMYK (stored inverted, 65535 = no ink), 7 Lab, 8 Grayscale. CMYK goes through the document's own embedded CMYK profile via `photocraft-cms` (the import now runs layer building inside the document's CMYK profile scope), Lab through the D50 Lab conversion. No sRGB/coated-CMYK assumption.
- Book colours and unknown space ids are not guessed: the block stays `Unsupported` and round-trips verbatim.
- Round trip: when the stops are unchanged, export keeps the file's own `grdm` block, so stops stay in their original colour space (plus smoothness/method). Toggling Reverse or Dither patches those two flag bytes in place. Edited stops are written as RGB, as before.
- `channel_map::decode_color` now shares the decoder (`decode_known_color`) and gains HSB.

## Tests

- `adjust_map` unit tests: CMYK K-only black, Lab neutral/chromatic, Grayscale, HSB blue; book/unknown ids stay unsupported; every truncation of the block never panics; Reverse/Dither retargeting keeps the stops bytes and refuses edited stops.
- `crates/io/tests/color.rs`: CMYK (with a synthetic non-default embedded profile, checked against a direct `photocraft-cms` transform and shown to differ from the built-in profile), Lab and Grayscale documents at 8/16/32-bit: the layer imports as a Gradient Map, changes the composite, re-saves its `grdm` byte for byte, and Reverse/Dither edits keep the stops' colour space and reopen identically.
- `channel_map` test: HSB decoding.

## Gate

Local (macOS): `cargo test -p photocraft-io --lib --tests`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `ca…

title: PSD: rasterized fill and smart layers stay rasterized after save and reopen
author: echelon
body:
Layer › Rasterize › Fill Content / Smart Object swapped a layer's content to pixels but kept the fill (`SoCo`/`GdFl`/`PtFl`) or placed-layer (`SoLd`/`PlLd`/`SoLE`) blocks read from the PSD. Saved and reopened (by PhotoCraft or Photoshop), the layer was a fill layer or smart object again and the rasterized pixels were gone. Photoshop writes none of these blocks for a pixel layer.

- Rasterize drops the fill / placed blocks from the layer (`crates/engine/src/extra_cmds.rs`).
- Backstop in the PSD exporter: a raster layer never writes fill, placed, type (`TySh`), shape-fill (`vscg`), adjustment or `CgEd` blocks, nor a shape stroke (`vstk`) beside a vector mask, whichever command made it a pixel layer. A `vstk` on a pixel layer without a vector mask stays (Photoshop writes it there: corpus `psd-tools/effects/stroke-without-vector-mask.psd`), and so does a vector mask (`vmsk`/`vsms`, `vogk`).

Tests (`crates/engine/tests/rasterize_psd_reopen.rs`), all failing before the fix:
- a solid fill layer and a smart object opened from a PSD, rasterized, saved and reopened: raster layers, no content blocks written;
- a raster layer carrying stale `SoCo`/`TySh`/`vscg`/`levl` blocks writes none of them;
- Photoshop-authored files (corpus `psd-tools/gradient-fill.psd`, `photoshop/smart-filters/sf-none-plain.psd`, feature `corpus`): rasterized layers reopen as pixels.

Local gate: `cargo test -p photocraft-io -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests` (103 test binaries green), the new test with `--features corpus`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`. The full corpus run and other-OS checks are left to PR CI (local machine overloaded).

Related: #3873 prunes the placed-layer blocks for smart objects in the rasterize command; this PR also covers fill layers and adds the exporter backstop.

title: fix(cmyk): Flatten Image and merges keep the inks of a tagged CMYK document (#3778)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #3778

## What was wrong

PhotoCraft composites in RGB. For a CMYK document, the layers are read through the document's embedded CMYK profile (for example U.S. Web Coated (SWOP) v2), but the composite was separated back to CMYK through the built-in coated profile. So the pixels were read with one profile and written with another. Every pixel of a tagged CMYK document moved on Layer › Flatten Image, even with only a Background layer. The same flatten path also serves Stamp Visible, Merge Visible, Merge Layers, Copy Merged, Background from Layer and Rasterize Layer Style. Merge Down also built its temporary document without the document's profile.

## What changed

- `compose::flatten_to_surface`, the engine's `composite_layers` and Rasterize Layer Style now separate the composite through the document's own CMYK profile. Merge Down's temporary document keeps the profile.
- When a CMYK document's composite is a single plain pixel layer (Normal, 100 % opacity and fill, no masks, effects, Blend If, channel exclusion or advanced blending, same depth), Flatten copies its inks exactly, as Photoshop does. Black isn't regenerated, and inks outside the display gamut aren't clipped. Partly transparent pixels that are flattened onto paper still go through the compositor.
- `photocraft_io::merged_composite`, the helper that turns a PSD's stored merged image into RGB for corpus comparisons, now reads CMYK through the file's embedded profile. Before, every comparison of a CMYK file tagged with a non-default profile was off.

## Tests

- `crates/engine/tests/cmyk_flatten_profile.rs`: a CMYK document at 8 and 16 bit, tagged and untagged, holding separations plus inks no separation produces (K only, rich black, solid cyan, paper). After Flatten Image, Stamp Visible and Background from Layer the inks are bit-identical. After Merge Down and Merge Visible (which go through RGB) they stay within the profile's own round trip. A transparent pixel still flattens to paper. Five of the s…

title: fix(layers): identify the Background by structure, never by its English name
author: echelon
body:
## What changed

In Photoshop, the Background is the bottom layer of a file that has no transparency: a pixel layer, transparency-protected and position-locked. Its name depends on the language of the Photoshop that saved the file ("Hintergrund", "背景", "Arrière-plan"). PhotoCraft found it by the English name "Background". In a localized PSD, a Deep knockout (or a top-level Shallow one) therefore revealed transparency instead of the Background. Engine and UI behaviour that depends on the Background broke in the same way.

- The doc model gets `Document::background()` / `background_mut()` / `is_background(id)` and `Layer::has_background_traits()`. The rule is structural: the bottom layer, a pixel layer, not clipped, with transparency and position locked. It replaces every name check:
  - compose: the knockout target (only the `is_background` line changes);
  - engine: Cut/Clear, Merge Visible, Copy, Free Transform and transform locks, Warp, Perspective Crop, Distort, the Magic and Background Erasers, layer styles, Add Mask, Image Size/Crop, Straighten, Lens Correction, style presets, smart-object unpack, Layer From Background, Background From Layer, Delete Hidden;
  - UI: the Properties document view, the italic Background name in the Layers panel, the tab title.
- One helper, `extra_cmds::background_to_layer`, now does the Background → "Layer 0" conversion that four copies used to do.
- PSD import: the bottom record is marked position-locked when it is transparency-protected and has no transparency channel (−1), whatever its name and whether or not the file has an `lspf` block. A bottom layer with Lock Transparent Pixels that keeps its transparency channel is not the Background.
- Affinity import and HDR Toning now lock the Background's position too, as File › New and every other place that creates a Background already did.

## Tests
- `compose`: a Deep knockout reveals a Background named "Hintergrund", "背景" or "Arrière-plan" (all depths). An unlocked bottom layer th…

title: fix(type): type with a missing font keeps its pixels through transforms
author: echelon
body:
## What changed

A type layer whose font is not installed (for example a PSD opened on a machine without the file's font) no longer re-renders in the fallback face when it is transformed or the canvas changes. Photoshop keeps such a layer as it was drawn, transforms its pixels as pixels, and only substitutes the font when you edit the text. PhotoCraft now does the same:

- **Free Transform** (`edit.transform`), **Image Size** and **canvas rotation** warp the layer's existing rendered pixels instead of laying the text out again. Moving the layer already kept the pixels (#3218).
- The PSD `TySh` block keeps the file's text data and EngineData byte for byte. Only its transform is updated (new `photocraft_text::psd::set_transform`), so the layer still saves as live type with the original font name.
- Editing the text lays it out again, in the substitute face, as Photoshop does after its missing-font warning.
- Missing-font detection (`type.resolveMissingFonts` / `missing_fonts`) now also accepts a stored PostScript name that names an installed face. Such a run is no longer reported missing and is not kept as pixels.

Type in an installed font still lays out again after a transform, as before.

Related: #3617, #3556. Both are about font substitution. This change does not fully fix either one.

## Tests

- `crates/engine/tests/type_missing_font.rs` (new, 7 tests): move, Free Transform, Image Size and arbitrary canvas rotation keep and transform the drawn pixels; the `TySh` transform follows while the rest of the block stays as it was; undo restores the layer; a text edit renders again; installed fonts still render again; a matching PostScript name is not missing.
- `crates/text`: `set_transform_patches_only_the_transform` (also covers truncated or empty blocks returning `None` without panicking).

## Local gate (macOS)

- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-text --lib --tests`: all green
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-text --all-targets -- -…

title: feat(compose): Lab documents evaluate Invert, Posterize, Threshold, Brightness/Contrast and Gradient Map on L, a, b
author: echelon
body:
## What

In Lab documents Photoshop evaluates several adjustments on the Lab channels rather than on the screen RGB colour. PhotoCraft applied them to the RGB working colour, so they were wrong on nearly every pixel of a Lab document. Now, with channels normalised as L/100, (a+128)/255, (b+128)/255:

- **Invert**: n → 1 − n on L, a and b alike (L → 100 − L, a and b mirrored about neutral on the 0..255 grid).
- **Posterize**: the same step function on L, a and b.
- **Brightness/Contrast** (modern and legacy): the tone curve on L only; a and b are unchanged (added as a difference of two round trips, like the existing Lab Levels/Curves path).
- **Threshold**: split on L alone; the result is neutral black or white.
- **Gradient Map**: driven by L (Reverse uses 1 − L); a grey and a saturated colour with equal L map to the same stop colour.

Levels and Curves keep their existing Lab records; Hue/Saturation, Photo Filter and the rest stay on the screen colour.

### How

- `photocraft_compose::adjust::apply_in(adj, buf, transfer, depth, mode)` dispatches the Lab rules (`lab_channel_adjustment`) in Lab documents and otherwise calls `apply_depth` unchanged.
- The CPU compositor (both adjustment-layer paths) and destructive Image › Adjustments (`engine::pixels`) use it; layer masks still adjust as Grayscale.
- The GPU plan defers these adjustments to the CPU in Lab documents (`adjustment_on_gpu` now takes the mode).

No change to CMYK compositing.

## Tests

- `compose::adjust` unit tests: Invert mirrors L/a/b (and differs from the RGB invert), Posterize steps all three, Threshold neutral output split on L, B/C moves L and keeps a/b within 0.5 (both kinds), Gradient Map follows L (forward and reverse), other modes and adjustments keep the old path exactly, NaN/inf/transparent pixels don't panic.
- `compose` document test at 8/16/32-bit: Lab document with Invert, Threshold and Gradient Map adjustment layers renders the Lab results through `flatten`.
- `engine::pixels` test at 8…

title: PSD: descriptor ids warp, list and time are written as strings, as Photoshop writes them
author: echelon
body:
A descriptor class or key id is a u32 length followed by bytes, where length 0 means a 4-byte code follows. Photoshop stores `warp`, `list` and `time` as **length-4 strings** (`00000004 'warp'`) and treats the code form (`00000000 'warp'`) as a different key. PhotoCraft made every four-character name a code, so freshly built data used the form Photoshop does not recognise: the warp of new smart objects (`SoLd`/`PlLd`), new or edited type warps (`TySh`) and regenerated layer comp lists (resource 1065).

Confirmed on the corpus (byte counts over every PSD/PSB/TIFF): `warp` 741 as a string, 0 as a code; `list` 5 / 0 (Photoshop layer-comp files); `time` 7 / 0. (`view` appears in both forms, so it is left alone.)

- `Id::new` makes `warp`, `list` and `time` string ids, both as keys and as class ids (`photocraft_psd::descriptor::STRING_IDS`).
- `Id::is` stays byte-based, so reading accepts both forms, and a code read from a file is written back unchanged.

Tests: exact bytes for each name as class and key, round trip, a file's code form kept and still found; a fresh placed-layer warp writes `warp` as a string in `SoLd` (key + class) and `PlLd` (class); the layer comp resource writes `list` as a string.

Local gate: `cargo test -p photocraft-psd -p photocraft-io --lib --tests`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers`. The corpus, wasm and other-OS checks are left to PR CI (local machine overloaded).

title: fix(compose): clipped layers take the base's shape, not its fill; clipped Dissolve dissolves (#3052)
author: echelon
body:
## What and why

**Clipping base fill opacity.** In Photoshop, a clipping base's Fill opacity fades only the base's own pixels. The clipped layers show at full strength inside the base's *shape* (its alpha × masks), and the whole group then blends onto the backdrop in the base's mode at the base's (layer) opacity. A common setup is a base at Fill 0 % (an invisible shape or text) with photos clipped to it. PhotoCraft composited the clipped layers into the base's content and faded the combined buffer by the base's fill, so they vanished at 0 % and were half-strength at 50 %.

- CPU compositor: plain, shape-layer and effects bases below 100 % fill (Blend Clipped Layers as Group on) build the group in the base's shape: base at fill, then each clipped layer composited as an ordinary layer and kept only inside the base's unfaded alpha. With effects, the base's alpha stays the effect shape and the group's own alpha becomes a per-pixel fill. At 100 % fill the existing atop path is kept (the two models agree).
- GPU compositor: the same model in the planner (a Lerp by the base's alpha, and a per-pixel fill in the effect init), so these documents stay on the GPU and match the CPU oracle.

**Clipped Dissolve (#3052).** A clipped Dissolve layer blended as Normal (uniform grey). It now draws each pixel fully or not at all with the same document-coordinate noise as an unclipped layer; clipping only limits where it can draw. Fixed on CPU and GPU.

## Tests

- `advanced_tests`: white backdrop, red base, blue Multiply clipped, at 8/16/32-bit: fill 0 % → blue, 100 % → black, 50 % → (0, 0, 0.5); base opacity 50 %; group off at fill 0 % / 50 %; base mask at 0 % fill; base with an outside stroke at 0 % / 50 % fill.
- Clipped Dissolve: only source or base pixels, never a mix; the #3052 case (black Solid Color fill, Dissolve 50 %, clipped to a white Background) renders the same pixels as unclipped.
- GPU parity (Metal): bases with Normal/Multiply/Screen, opacity, masks, fill 100/50/0 %, c…

title: PSD type layers: TySh bounds, AntiAlias numbers and version info written as Photoshop writes them
author: echelon
body:
Three byte-level differences in the type layers PhotoCraft writes, each confirmed against Photoshop 2026 files in `corpus/photoshop` before changing behaviour:

1. **`TySh` trailing bounds are four big-endian f32**, not i32 (the Adobe spec's wording on this tail is ambiguous). Photoshop writes zeros for unwarped type and the type's text-space bounds (the `bounds` descriptor's rectangle) for warped type: `text/warp-arc-50.psd` ends with 0.0, −34.316, 288.906, 15.059, which is nonsense read as integers. We read and wrote i32 filled from the rounded ink bounds. Now read/written as f32, zeros unwarped, text-space bounds warped; an unchanged layer keeps its file's bytes as before.
2. **EngineData `AntiAlias` numbering**, on write and on read: 0 None, 1 Crisp, 2 Strong, 3 Smooth, 4 Sharp (the `AntA` descriptor and the EngineData integer side by side in `text/antialias-*.psd`). We wrote Sharp 1, Crisp 2, Strong 3, Smooth 4, so the default Smooth said Sharp. Reading now falls back to the EngineData number when `AntA` is absent. The platform modes have no corpus file to confirm their numbers, so they write Smooth (3) and keep their exact mode in `AntA`, as before.
3. **Version info resource 1057**: writer "Adobe Photoshop", reader "Adobe Photoshop 2026", no NUL terminator: byte for byte what all 258 Photoshop 2026 oracles write (checked over the whole corpus). We wrote NUL-terminated "Adobe Photoshop" / "Adobe Photoshop CS6".

Tests:
- `crates/text/src/tests.rs`: trailing bounds are f32 (zeros unwarped, bounds warped, round trip); AntiAlias numbers per mode and read back from EngineData alone.
- `crates/psd/src/resources.rs`: exact 1057 bytes.
- `crates/io/tests/psd_type_photoshop_bytes.rs` (feature `corpus`): our regenerated TySh matches the Photoshop file's AntiAlias number for all five modes and its trailing bounds (warped and unwarped); our 1057 equals the file's.

Local gate: `cargo test -p photocraft-psd -p photocraft-text -p photocraft-io --lib --tests`, the corpus te…

title: feat(canvas): rotate view with Shift + middle-mouse drag
author: Ni-zav
body:
Addresses #3950.

Adds Shift + middle-mouse dragging to rotate the canvas while preserving ordinary middle-mouse panning.

The rotation keeps the document point beneath the cursor in place, including flipped views and non-square pixel aspect ratios.

Adds regression tests for pointer anchoring and invalid drag input.

title: fix(algo): reject oversized Magic Eraser masks without overflow
author: Ni-zav
body:
Magic Eraser validates a region's mask length by multiplying its bounding-box dimensions. Extreme coordinates can overflow that multiplication before the invalid mask is rejected.

Use checked multiplication and return an empty damaged rectangle when the dimensions cannot be represented.

Adds a regression test using extreme rectangle coordinates to verify rejection without modifying the target surface.

title: fix(ui): reject rotation angles outside f32 range
author: Ni-zav
body:
The Rotate View command accepts finite JSON numbers that can exceed the range of f32.

Converting those values to f32 produces infinity, which the angle-wrapping logic turns into zero. An invalid rotation request can therefore unexpectedly reset the canvas rotation.

Reject values outside the representable f32 range before conversion.

Adds regression cases for overflowing angle and delta parameters.

title: fix(selection): avoid panics when sampling incomplete region masks
author: Ni-zav
body:
Region::at directly indexes its coverage mask using the bounding-box coordinates.

If the mask is shorter than the declared region, sampling a point inside the bounds can panic. Extremely large coordinate differences can also overflow index calculations.

Use checked index arithmetic and bounds-checked reads, treating missing coverage as zero.

Adds regression tests for incomplete masks, negative coordinates, and extreme rectangle bounds.

title: fix(selection): validate Magic Wand pixel buffers before indexing
author: Ni-zav
body:
The Magic Wand selection routines assume their input pixel arrays cover the requested rectangle.

With incomplete pixel buffers, seed lookup and subsequent region traversal can index outside the available data. Extreme dimensions can also overflow the expected pixel count.

Validate the pixel count using checked multiplication before allocating masks or reading seed pixels.

Invalid inputs now return an empty selection result instead of panicking. Adds regression tests for truncated arrays, extreme dimensions, and valid inputs.

title: fix(liquify): pointer speed no longer changes the warp (continuous dab spacing)
author: echelon
body:
## What changed

Liquify placed dabs a fifth of the brush radius apart and restarted the spacing at every pointer event. The result therefore depended on how fast the mouse moved. A fast drag (few, far-apart events) and a slow drag (many close events) along the same path gave different warps, and a slow drag piled up one dab per event. Photoshop's Liquify gives the same warp for the same path at any speed.

Now:

- Dabs fall every **1/20 of the brush radius** of distance travelled, measured along the **whole stroke**. The spacing carries from one pointer segment to the next instead of restarting, so any sampling of a path gives the same displacement field.

title: feat(styles): import and export .asl layer style libraries (#1051)
author: echelon
body:
## What

Photoshop's Styles panel can **Import Styles…** and **Export Styles…** as `.asl` layer style libraries. PhotoCraft now reads and writes them.

- **`photocraft-psd::asl`** (new): a pure, panic-free reader and writer for the version-3 `8BSL` style library: header, a pattern section in the `Patt` record format, then per style an identity descriptor (`Nm  `, `Idnt`) and a `Styl` descriptor (`documentMode`, `Lefx`, optional `blendOptions`). It accepts record lengths with or without the 4-byte padding. A pattern section that doesn't decode is skipped with a note so the styles still load. Wrong signature or version, truncation, or a count that can't fit return `Err`.
- **`photocraft-io::asl_map`** (new): maps styles onto PhotoCraft effects through the same descriptor code as a layer's `lfx2` (`effects_from_descriptor` / `effects_descriptor` are factored out of `parse_lfx2` / `write_lfx2`, with no change in behaviour). `blendOptions` maps to blend mode, opacity and fill opacity, and embedded patterns become `Pattern`s. Empty names get "Style N" and repeated names get "Name 2". Anything PhotoCraft doesn't model (unknown effect keys, advanced blending keys, a non-100 % effects scale, missing patterns) is left out with a warning that names the style.

title: Affinity: rectangles keep per-corner radii and straight corners (#1606)
author: callmeBalloch
body:
## What

Affinity rectangles store a radius and a corner type for each corner (`ShCR`, `CTyp`: top left, top right, bottom right, bottom left) and a `Lock` flag. The reader always used the first radius for all four corners and drew every corner round, so a rectangle with unlocked corners imported as a uniform pill.

Now:
- unlocked corners (`Lock = false`) keep their own radius and type; locked ones (or no `Lock`) still follow the top-left corner, as before
- straight corners (type 1) are cut across instead of rounded; concave and other types still warn and import round
- two radii that don't fit along one side shrink in proportion

Uniform rectangles produce exactly the same outline as before. This is the same change as VectorCraft's copy of the reader, storytold/vectorcraft#1362.

## Evidence

`tiny-shapes.af` from [SethRobinson/Patchy](https://github.com/SethRobinson/Patchy/blob/de84eab550758b30fa062e479f5778cce7693b73/test-fixtures/af/tiny-shapes.af) (MIT, pinned in VectorCraft's corpus) has a rectangle with radii `[0.5, 0.1, 0.3, 0]` and types `[round, round, straight, 4]`. Against the thumbnail Affinity embedded in it, the PhotoCraft import's mean difference drops from 2.48 to 0.98 (export at the document's 120×80 size), and the corner-type warning goes away.

## Tests

- New unit test `shapes::unlocked_rectangle_corners_keep_their_own_radius_and_type` in `crates/affinity/src/tests.rs`: unlocked corners (round, round, straight, none), and the locked default
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-affinity --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`, `cargo fmt`
- `cargo test -p photocraft-affinity --all-features`; `photocraft-io` Affinity tests with `--features corpus` (render-reference ceilings unchanged); `photocraft-engine` Affinity tests

title: Affinity import: pie shapes with huge angles no longer hang the reader
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What's wrong

`ShPi` in `crates/affinity/src/shapes.rs` (`:117-125` on `main`) reads a pie's start and end angles (`AngS`, `AngE`) from the file and raises the end angle until it reaches the start:

```rust
while end < start {
    end += TAU;
}
```

The loop runs about `(AngS - AngE) / TAU` times, and it never ends once adding `TAU` no longer changes `end`. With `AngS` = 1e308 and `AngE` = -1e308, the read in the first test below had not returned after 20 seconds, and one core stayed busy. File › Open reads Affinity files through this reader (`crates/io/src/lib.rs:262-263`, `crates/io/src/affinity.rs:37`).

## What changed

The `ShPi` arm computes the angles in constant time with `rem_euclid`, which `segment` already uses for the angle of a circular segment:

- the start angle is `AngS` modulo `TAU`;
- the sweep is `AngE - AngS` capped at one turn, or its remainder modulo `TAU` when `AngE` is below `AngS`;
- when `AngE` is below `AngS` and `AngE - AngS` overflows to negative infinity, the sweep comes from the remainders of the two angles.

A pie with angles of ordinary size covers the same arc as before, up to rounding: the sweep is still `AngE - AngS`, raised by whole turns while it is negative and capped at one turn.

This is Riccardo Balloch's fix for the same loop in VectorCraft's copy of this reader, from https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/79c5d673ff5e4f2011da9c31d4c55aa4484e9f1a. The `ShPi` lines are the same as in that commit, and the commit here carries a `Co-authored-by` line for him. The change adds an implemented control: the reader no longer loops on hostile pie angles.

A second commit adds my own entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

## Tests

A new `mod shapes` in `crates/affinity/src/tests.rs` holds the two pie tests from `crates/affinity/tests/outline_limits.rs` in that commit. They build their documents with the existing `synth` builders. Their `read` helper reads each document on a thread of its own and fails the test when reading …

title: Quick Selection: cut window sizes in parallel, cancel the larger ones once one is kept (-37% on 24 MP strokes, identical masks)
author: syncroot
body:
## Why

On a 24 MP photo, releasing a Quick Selection stroke freezes the canvas for about 0.2 s on an Apple M5 Pro (0.5 s on a Linux x86 dev box). It's worse for longer strokes.

The time goes into the window-growing loop in `quick_select_using`. It cuts a window around the stroke, and if the selection touches a side of that window, it doubles the margin and **starts over**. On a real photo, every stroke I tried needed 2–4 window sizes. The smaller windows were thrown away, which was about 40% of the total time. What's left is the last cut, mostly `Graph::maxflow_with` (55% in `perf`).

## What

- **Parallel window sizes.** The window sizes don't depend on each other, so `quick_select_using` now cuts the next `SPECULATE = 4` window sizes at once (rayon) and keeps the **first one in growing order** that stays clear of its sides. That's the same result as trying them one after another.
- **Cancellation.** As soon as a window is kept, larger windows of the same batch stop cutting. They poll a cancel flag through `select_working_using` → `cut_levels` → `grid_cut_impl`, which already had a `cancel` hook that `maxflow_with` honours. A cut that isn't cancelled does exactly what it did before.
- **Extra cancel points.** `grid_cut_impl` also checks the flag before building the graph and before `maxflow_with`, and `cut_levels` checks it between the coarse and fine levels. Every other caller passes `&|| false`, so it's unchanged for them.
- **wasm32.** It keeps the one-after-another loop, since it has no threads.
- **Comment fix.** I removed the comment saying a selection clear of the window's sides "is the best over the whole canvas too". The measurements below show the result depends on the window sizes tried, so the comment was wrong. The code still tries the same sizes in the same order.

## Results

title: fix(move): no trail when dragging a shape past the canvas edge (#3946)
author: alonfaraj
body:
Fixes #3946

## Problem
If a shape layer sticks out past the canvas edge and you drag it with the Move tool, it leaves a trail along that edge. During a drag the canvas only redraws the area the moving layers cover. That area comes from the shape's pixels, which are cut off at the canvas edge. When the hidden part of the shape comes into view, the strip near the edge isn't redrawn.

## Fix
`move_ui::display_doc` now adds each moving shape's full outline to the redraw area (`CompiledShape::bounds`), plus room for its layer effects. It's worked out once per drag. Saving the move already redrew the right area, so only the live preview changes.

## Test
`move_ui::tests::dragging_a_shape_past_the_canvas_edge_leaves_no_trail` checks that every pixel that changes between two drag frames gets redrawn.

title: Stylus: a light Windows pen tap is pressure 0, not a full-pressure click
author: Furash
body:
## Problem
On Windows, a light pen tap left a mark as if it were a mouse click at 100% pressure.

## Cause
winit's Windows `WM_POINTER*` path maps pen pressure 0 to `force: None` (`normalize_pointer_pressure` only accepts 1..=1024). A tap lighter than the pen's first pressure level therefore reached egui as a force-less `Event::Touch`. `Stylus::update` ignored force-less touches, so `sample()` returned `None` and the tap painted at pressure 1, like a mouse.

## Fix (`crates/ui-egui/src/stylus.rs`)
- Track the touch contacts that are down.
- A touch move outside a contact (only a pen hovers) or any reported force marks a pen.
- A pen contact with no force yet is pressure 0, so a light tap gives a minimal dab and a light stroke start ramps up from 0 instead of starting with a full-pressure blob.
- A finger on a touchscreen without force sensing still paints at full pressure.
- A contact that starts in the same frame another lifts keeps its own force (it used to be cleared the next frame).

Known limit: winit doesn't expose the pointer type, so a light tap that comes before the pen has ever hovered or reported a force in the session still paints at 1.

Also adds my own `contributors/people.toml` entry (`sync_github_name = true`).

## Testing
- New tests: `a_light_windows_pen_tap_is_not_full_pressure`, `a_finger_without_force_still_paints_at_full_pressure`, `a_new_tap_in_the_frame_an_old_one_lifted_keeps_its_force`.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib` filtered to stylus, pressure, tap, stroke and pen tests: all pass. `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests -D warnings` is clean.
- Tested by hand with a Windows pen tablet in a release build: light taps no longer paint at full pressure.

body:

After making two of them and selecting both, the first Delete went through `delete_key_command`'s mask branch and only removed the active layer's mask (`layer.layerMask.delete`). author: marcoarnulfo
body:

title: perf: reuse sampled composite across channel visibility toggles
author: Ni-zav
body:
The Channels panel recomposites the document whenever a colour channel is hidden, even when only the channel visibility state changes. On large documents, repeatedly toggling RGB channels can therefore trigger expensive full-resolution compositing on the UI thread.

This change renders sampled composites in bands and caches the resulting pixels independently of the channel visibility state. Subsequent eye toggles reuse those pixels and only apply the requested channel masking.

The cache uses weak document identity to detect pixel changes without retaining old document snapshots. Its memory use is bounded to 128 MiB across open documents.

Regression tests cover downsampling across compositor band boundaries, reuse across successive channel toggles, and invalidation after pixel edits.

**Validation:** Source and branch diff reviewed. Tests added but not executed locally because the Rust toolchain was unavailable. Native testing and before/after measurements on large layered documents are still required.

The initial switch into a partial-colour view can still require compositing; this primarily optimizes subsequent visibility changes and reduces temporary rendering memory.

title: Object Selection: hover preview of the object it would select (Object Finder) (#4087)
author: FredApps
body:
Fixes #4087

Photoshop's Object Finder for the Object Selection tool: with the tool active, resting the pointer on the canvas highlights the object a click there would select; a click selects it. Selection *quality* is out of scope and tracked in #2788 (this reuses the classical heuristics).

## What changed
- **algo** `segment::grabcut::object_at`: object under a point. On a ~60k px working copy, a lightly smoothed CIELAB region is grown from the cursor (bounded by the distance to the running mean and the local edge step); a region covering most of the canvas counts as background (nothing found). GrabCut then refines it inside its padded box (cursor = definite FG, outside the box = BG), keeps the part connected to the cursor, and re-cuts the boundary at full resolution like the rectangle mode.
- **engine** `select.object` now also takes `"point": [x, y]` (modes replace/add/subtract/intersect). New `ObjectFinderCache` on the `Session` (keyed by document pixels like Select Subject's cache, document held weakly, dropped on pixel edits and close; any point inside a cached object hits it), plus `find_object` / `sampled_target` for the UI.
- **ui-egui** new `object_finder.rs`: after a 120 ms rest the lookup runs on a worker thread (inline on wasm) and the UI never waits for it. Results go into the session cache, which the click reuses. The overlay is a translucent theme-accent tint with a 1-texel outline, drawn as a textured quad through the view transform so rotated or flipped views work. It clears on pointer leave, tool switch, button down, option off, and revision, layer or Sample All Layers changes.
- A click without a drag commits the object (⇧ add, ⌥ subtract, ⇧⌥ intersect, otherwise new). A drag keeps the rectangle mode. With Object Finder off, a click keeps the old Quick Selection fallback.
- Options bar: **Object Finder** checkbox (default on, persisted in `ToolOptions`, reset by Reset Tool). Two new strings are translated in all 17 catalogs. `docs/ui-parity.md`…

title: Workspace: wire Auto-show hidden panels (#204)
author: reynold-hu

title: Integrations: wire Allow Agent Control and Control Port (#204)
author: Erica4fr
body:
`integrations.allowAgentControl` and `integrations.controlPort` were in Preferences ›
Integrations and in `prefs::HIDDEN_UNTIL_IMPLEMENTED`: nothing read them, so `--control` (or
`PHOTOCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT`) was the only way to open the control channel.

They now do what their own doc comments describe — *"Allow agents to drive the app over the
loopback control channel / MCP bridge"* and *"Default control port (0 = only when `--control` is
given)"*.

### Behaviour

| preferences | `--control` | listens on |
|---|---|---|
| none | — | nothing |
| `controlPort: 7878` | — | **7878** |
| `controlPort: 7878` | `9000` | 9000 — the flag wins |
| `allowAgentControl: false` | `9000` | nothing, **and says so** |
| `allowAgentControl: false`, `controlPort: 7878` | — | nothing |
| `controlPort: 70000` | — | nothing, and names the value |

The defaults are unchanged (allow on, port 0), so a launch that touches neither preference
behaves exactly as it does today.

Refusals are not silent. With Allow Agent Control off and `--control 9000`, the flag is dropped
*and* explained:

```text
photocraft: Preferences › Integrations › Allow Agent Control is off: not listening on port 9000
photocraft: Preferences › Integrations › Control Port 70000 is not a usable port: not listening
```

A `--control` that does nothing without a word is the shape #2449 was about, so it seemed wrong to
add another one. The out-of-range case only a hand-edited `preferences.json` can produce — the
dialog clamps to 0..65535 — but it is refused by name rather than silently truncated.

### How it reads the preferences

`integrations()` reads the saved file before the window opens, the same way `custom_titlebar()`
already does for System Title Bar, and falls back to the defaults when the file is missing or
unparseable. `control_port_for()` is the decision, kept pure so the table above is a test.

### Checked

Two tests: the decision table (every row above) and the file reading (absent, unparseable, valid).

title: Move: drag over locked background layer starts marquee selection (#4058)
author: safvanedge
body:

In Adobe Photoshop, with the Move tool and Auto-Select enabled, dragging starting from a locked background layer initiates a marquee selection box to select unlocked layers touching the box.

In PhotoCraft, starting a drag over a locked background layer hit-tested the locked layer and triggered the error modal:

Dragging was only permitted if initiated from outside the canvas where no pixels existed.

- Added contributor credit in \contributors/people.toml\.

title: Codecs: open and save DPX frames (#1049)
author: przemyslvw
body:
Closes #1049.

Adds DPX (SMPTE 268M) as a raster format: open and save Digital Picture Exchange frames, keeping 10- and 12-bit code values exact and the header fields a film or TV pipeline relies on.

## Reading

- Both byte orders: `SDPX` (big-endian) and `XPDS` (little-endian).
- The first image element, descriptor 6 (luma), 50 (RGB) or 51 (RGBA), unsigned, unencoded, at 8, 10, 12 or 16 bits.
  - 10-bit: packing 0 (packed), 1 (method A) and 2 (method B).
  - 12-bit: packing 0 and 1 (method A).
  - Lines start on a 32-bit word boundary. 8- and 16-bit files whose lines are not padded to a word also open.
- 8- and 16-bit code values become U8/U16 unchanged. 10- and 12-bit code values become U16 `round(c × 65535 / (2^b − 1))`.
- No colour transform. `DecodeWarning::DpxEncoding` reports the transfer characteristic and colorimetric specification in the import notes, e.g. "DPX transfer characteristic: logarithmic (3), colorimetric: printing density (1); the code values were imported as stored, without a colour transform".
- More than one element: `DecodeWarning::MoreElements` ("only the first of 2 image elements was imported").
- Orientation codes 1–7 are mapped to EXIF orientations and applied on import.
- Unsupported descriptors, signed or run-length-encoded data, other bit depths and unsupported packings return `CodecError::Unsupported` naming the field and value. Malformed headers, offsets past the end and truncated data return errors under the existing `Limits`.

## Writing

- Big-endian, one unencoded element, descriptor 6/50/51.
  - 8 and 16 bits: packing 0.
  - 10 and 12 bits: packing 1 (method A).
- The bit depth is `EncodeOptions::dpx_bits` (`DpxBits`, re-exported from `photocraft-io`). It is exposed as:
  - `dpxBits` on `file.saveACopy`, the batch and export-layers commands, MCP `doc_save`/`doc_export` (headless) and RPC `doc.save`;
  - `--dpx-bits <8|10|12|16>` on CLI `convert`, `run` and `batch`.
- Unset, the bit depth follows the document: 8 → 8, 16 → 16, 3…

title: Brush cursor: the tip's centre mark follows Show Crosshair in Brush Tip
author: Furash
body:
## Problem
A small cross was always drawn inside the brush tip when painting, and Preferences › Cursors › **Show Crosshair in Brush Tip** could not turn it off.

## Cause
`brush_tip_centre` in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` returned `show_crosshair || radius > 6.0 || …`, so any tip wider than 6 screen pixels drew the centre mark whatever the preference said. Photoshop shows it only when the preference is on.

## Fix
Drop the size rule: the centre mark follows the preference. Kept as before:
- the Background Eraser always shows its sampling hotspot (Photoshop);
- Clone Stamp / Healing Brush show it while Option/Alt is held;
- Quick Selection never shows it;
- the Pencil's tiny-tip hotspot (under 6 px) is unchanged.

## Testing
- Updated `clone_stamp_centre_appears_only_with_option`; new `brush_tip_centre_follows_the_crosshair_preference_at_any_size` (Brush, Eraser, Pattern Stamp, Dodge with the preference off and on).
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib` filtered to cursor, centre, crosshair, caps_lock and brush_tip tests: all pass; clippy `-D warnings` clean.
- Checked by hand on Windows: no cross with the preference off, back when it's on.
