title: Stylus: a pen held still is not a press-and-hold right click
author: Furash
body:
## Problem
On Windows, holding a pen still on the canvas (or a panel) for about a second registered as a right click: a context menu opened. Seen with a Huion GT-191.

## Cause
Not Windows' own press-and-hold gesture: egui's. winit delivers Windows pen input as `WindowEvent::Touch`, and egui treats any touch contact held still past `InputOptions::max_click_duration` (0.8 s) as a touch screen's press-and-hold (`InputState::is_long_touch`). The widget under it gets `secondary_clicked()` (so the canvas opened its context menu), and egui also drops the drag in progress.

## Fix (`crates/ui-egui/src/stylus.rs`, `lib.rs`)
- `PenContacts` follows the raw touch events in `raw_input_hook` and tells a pen contact from a finger: only a pen hovers (a touch move with no contact down), and a pen reports pressure.
- While a pen contact is down, and through the frame it lifts in, `max_click_duration` is infinite, so there is no long-touch secondary click and a long still press releases as the click a tap would be. Otherwise it is egui's default again.
- Fingers on a touch screen keep press-and-hold → context menu.

## Testing
- `a_held_pen_is_not_a_right_click_but_a_held_finger_still_is` drives an `egui::Context` through 1.3 s of a held contact. Without the fix, the hovered pen gets a secondary click (reproduced); with it, no pen case does, and a held finger still does.
- `pen_contacts_follow_hover_force_and_lift`.
- Stylus tests pass; `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests -D warnings` clean.
- Checked by hand on Windows with a Huion GT-191: holding the pen no longer opens a context menu.

Independent of #4072 (light pen tap pressure); both touch `stylus.rs` in separate places.

title: PSD: a zero-length annotation entry no longer hangs the import (#4149)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4149.

## Why
A malformed PSD `Anno` (annotations) block whose entry length is 0 hung the import, then aborted the process when memory ran out. The 16-byte block `00 02 00 01 FF FF FF FF 00 00 00 00 73 6E 64 41` is enough. After each entry the parser sets the cursor to `start + len`, so any length below 8 (the length field plus the 4-byte type) put it back on the same entry, and a count of 0xFFFFFFFF repeated that about 4.3e9 times. An out-of-memory abort is not a panic, so the import's panic guard couldn't keep the document.

## Change
- `parse_entries` (`crates/io/src/annotations_map.rs`) rejects an entry length below 8, so every entry moves the cursor forward at least 8 bytes.
- The block is then treated as unreadable and kept verbatim on save, like any other `Anno` block that doesn't parse (#944).

## Tests
- New unit test `short_entry_length_is_unreadable_not_a_loop`: lengths 0, 4 and 7 for `sndA` and `txtA` entries, plus the hostile block above. It fails without the fix.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-io --lib --tests`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

## Not included
- The corpus tests (`cargo xtask test-corpus`) were not run locally. Real files have entry lengths far above 8.

title: Swatches: reject colour values beyond f32 range so presets survive a restart (#4150)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4150.

## Why
`swatches.add` with an HSB hue beyond f32 range (such as `1e39`) returned Ok and stored a NaN hue: the value passed the f64 finite check, became inf as f32, and `rem_euclid(360)` turned that into NaN. The prefs file writes NaN as `null`. On the next launch the presets loader can't parse that one value and throws away the whole presets blob, so every user gradient, style, shape, tool preset, document preset and swatch silently goes back to the defaults, and the next save writes the defaults over them. Same class as #4044.

## Change
- `SwatchColor::from_param` rejects colour values whose magnitude exceeds `f32::MAX`, for every colour model, with a BadParams error instead of storing inf or NaN.

## Tests
- New `values_beyond_f32_range_are_rejected_so_presets_survive_a_restart`: out-of-range values in hsb, rgb, cmyk, lab and gray give BadParams and leave the library unchanged; a hue of exactly `f32::MAX` is still accepted; user swatches survive a `prefs_to_json` → `load_prefs_json` round trip. It fails on main.
- `colour_params` now also rejects hsb `1e39` and rgb `-1e39`.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `panic_hunt -- --ignored` pass.

## Not included
- Making the presets loader keep the valid preset sets when one entry is malformed, instead of discarding the whole blob. That's a more robust follow-up for a separate PR.

title: Compose: the effect cache follows Transparency Shapes Layer and Blend If (#4151)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4151.

## Why
The layer-effect map cache key (`layer_identity` in `crates/compose`) left out a layer's Advanced Blending and Blend If, although both change the shape effects are built from:
- With Transparency Shapes Layer off, the whole layer becomes the effect shape.
- A styled group's shape is its children's composite, and a child's Blend If or knockout changes it.

The cache region didn't change either, so the stale maps were reused. A Stroke kept rimming a transparent hole after Transparency Shapes Layer was turned off, and a group's Drop Shadow ignored a child's new Blend If, until Edit › Purge.

## Change
- `layer_identity` now also hashes `layer.advanced` and `layer.blend_if`. Group children are covered through the existing recursion.

## Tests
- `effect_cache_follows_transparency_shapes_layer` and `effect_cache_follows_a_group_childs_blend_if` render with the cache warm, make the edit, and compare the result with a cold render after `purge_effect_cache()`. Both failed on main and pass with the fix.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-compose`: 232 passed in the library tests.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-compose --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

## Not included
- The key is not narrowed to only the Advanced Blending fields that affect the maps. Toggling one of the others (Blend Interior, for example) now rebuilds the maps; that costs a rebuild but can't change the output.
- No GPU-path changes: the GPU already falls back to the CPU for Transparency Shapes Layer off and for Blend If.

title: Layer Style: OK keeps an Inner Glow's Center source (#4152)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4152.

## Why
Opening Layer Style on a layer with a Center-source Inner Glow (from `layer.layerStyle.innerGlow {"source":"center"}` or a PSD) showed Source: Edge and previewed Edge, and OK without any edit turned the glow into an Edge glow. The dialog starts each effect from its factory defaults and never loaded the Inner Glow's own source, and the engine applies the `source` it receives.

## Change

title: Auto-Select: honour layer mask density when picking layers (#4153)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4153.

## Why
`layer.pickAt` (Move tool Auto-Select, the canvas right-click layer list and the Move rollover highlight) read a layer mask's raw pixel. The compositor draws masks through `LayerMask::value`, which applies the mask's Density. So a layer whose hide-all mask is at density 0 is fully visible, yet clicking it selected the layer underneath and the right-click list left it out.

## Change
- `layers_hit` reads the mask through `LayerMask::value`, the same call the compositor uses (density applied, 1.0 when the mask is disabled).

## Tests
- New `pick_cmds::tests::mask_density_is_honoured_when_picking`: a red layer with a hide-all mask is clicked through at full density; at density 0, `pickAt` returns the red layer and the list form returns [red, Background]. It fails on main.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `panic_hunt -- --ignored` pass.

## Not included
- Feathered pixel masks and vector masks: the compositor blurs and combines these (`compose::masks::combined_mask`), while picking still samples the unblurred pixel mask and ignores vector masks, so picks near a feathered edge or under a vector mask can still differ slightly from what is drawn.

title: Liquify, Puppet Warp and Perspective Warp: refuse locked smart objects (#4155)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4155.

## Why
On a smart object with Lock All or Lock Pixels (on the layer or a parent group), Filter › Liquify, Puppet Warp and Perspective Warp still added a smart filter and recorded a history step. Regular filters refuse locked smart objects. `run_on_layer` in `distort_cmds.rs` recorded the smart filter and returned before it checked the locks.

## Change
- Check the pixel and full locks (the layer's own and its groups') before recording the smart filter, as filters do. The position lock still doesn't block, because the smart object itself doesn't move.
- The distort lock error now uses the filters' wording, "Could not complete your request because the layer \"X\" is locked", also on the raster path. No test or UI code depended on the old text.

## Tests
- `locked_smart_objects_refuse_distortions`: Lock All and Lock Pixels, on the layer or its group; each of the three commands returns Err, adds no smart filter, leaves the pixels unchanged and adds no history step. It fails on main.
- `unlocked_or_position_locked_smart_objects_take_distortions`: unlocked, position-locked and transparency-locked smart objects still get one smart filter and one history step.
- Engine lib and integration tests, `panic_hunt -- --ignored`, clippy `-D warnings` and fmt pass.

title: Count tool: Marker Size and Label Size fields take effect (#4156)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4156.

## Why
On the Count tool's options bar, changing Marker Size or Label Size did nothing. The UI sent the values as JSON floats (`8.0`) and `count.setGroup` read them with `as_u64`, which is None for floats, so the command returned Ok without changing anything. Agents and recorded actions that send floats hit the same silent no-op.

## Change
- `count.setGroup` accepts whole numbers sent as floats (`8.0`) for `markerSize` and `labelSize`.
- Fractions, negatives, non-finite values and non-numbers now return BadParams instead of being silently ignored.
- Clamping to 1..=10 and 8..=72 happens in u64/f64, so huge values no longer wrap through `as u32` (2^32+1 used to become 1).
- The options bar sends integers through a small `count_size_params` helper.

## Tests
- Engine: `count_set_group_takes_sizes_sent_as_whole_floats` and `count_set_group_rejects_sizes_that_are_not_whole_numbers` (BadParams, no change, no history step). Both fail on main.
- UI: `count_size_fields_send_whole_numbers_the_engine_applies` checks the JSON the options bar sends and that the engine applies it.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests`, `panic_hunt -- --ignored`, clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` for both crates pass.

## Not included
- Other commands weren't audited for the same float/`as_u64` pattern.
- No visual check in the running app.

title: View: Esc leaves full screen modes (part of #4116)
author: FredApps
body:
Part of #4116 (the Esc part only; the Windows taskbar part is tracked there).

Esc now returns to Standard Screen Mode from **both** full screen modes (Full Screen Mode With Menu Bar and Full Screen Mode), as in Photoshop.

- Before: only Full Screen Mode handled Esc, in `lib.rs`'s UI pass, consuming it before dialogs, popups and later-frame handlers could see it.
- Now: handled in `shortcuts::handle`, just before Esc-deselect, so it only fires when nothing else owns Esc (dialogs, menus, text fields, inline type, transform, pen, lasso, crop, marquee drag, popups, palette, brush picker, Rotate View, …; the same `esc_taken` guard as deselect). It goes through `view.screenMode.standard`, so the window leaves fullscreen and the menu check updates. When a selection exists, the first Esc leaves full screen and the next deselects.

title: Automation: reject an invalid document index instead of using the active document (#4160)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4160.

## Why
The JSON-lines automation server (`photocraft-cli serve`, `crates/automation/src/rpc.rs`) read the optional `index` param with `as_u64`. Any value that isn't a non-negative integer (`"0"`, `-1`, `0.5`, `true`) was treated as "not given" and fell back to the active document, so `doc.close {"index":"0"}` closed the active (possibly unsaved) document instead of failing. The MCP server types `index` as `Option<usize>` and already rejects these, so the two interfaces disagreed.

## Change
- `index_of` returns `Result<Option<usize>, AutomationError>`: missing or `null` still means the active document, a non-negative integer is used, anything else is a bad request ("`index` must be a non-negative integer").
- Every `doc.*` method that takes `index` passes the error on: place, save, exportLayers, exportDataSets, importDataSets, inspect, render, select, close.

## Tests
- New `rpc::tests::invalid_document_index_is_rejected_not_the_active_document`: with two documents open, `doc.close`, `doc.inspect` and `doc.select` with `"0"`, `-1`, `0.5` or `true` return `ok:false` and both documents stay open; `index: null` still means the active document; `index: 0` still closes that document. It fails on main.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-automation --lib --tests`, clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

## Not included
- No change to the MCP server, which already rejects these values.
- Other loosely typed params in `rpc.rs` (e.g. `quality`) are unchanged.
- #4104 also edits `rpc.rs` (DPX); the hunks don't overlap.

title: Image Size and Canvas Size: no silent resize of large documents in physical units (#4162)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4162.

## Why
With Rulers set to a physical unit, Image Size and Canvas Size silently resized large documents. A 40000×4 px document at 72 ppi is 40000 pt wide, but the Width field capped non-pixel units at 30000. egui's DragValue clamps the shown value to its range when it's drawn, and our `number_edit` reports that clamp as an edit, so the dialog opened at 30000 pt (height 3 with Constrain on) and OK without touching anything resized the image (Image Size) or cropped it (Canvas Size).

## Change
- `dim_field` in `crates/ui-egui/src/sizing.rs` bounds non-pixel units by the engine's 300000 px limit converted into the current unit and resolution, never below the old 30000. Pixel fields keep their 300000 limit.

## Tests
- New `sizing::tests::large_documents_in_physical_units_open_unchanged`: for `image.imageSize` and `image.canvasSize`, a 40000×4 document at 72 ppi shown in points keeps 40000/4 in the fields after a few frames, and OK leaves it at 40000×4. Fails on main for both dialogs.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib sizing`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`. The remaining local failures of the full suite also fail on unchanged main (checked in a separate worktree).

## Not included
- Other value fields whose range is narrower than their valid values (same egui clamp mechanism) aren't audited here.
- No change to egui's clamp behaviour or to `number_edit`'s change detection.

title: Exposure: the slider keeps fractional stops (#4164)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4164.

## Why
Exposure (Image › Adjustments › Exposure and the adjustment layer's Properties) snapped to whole stops: typing 0.5 stored 1, and 0.4 stored 0. The shared slider rows rounded any range wider than 10 to whole numbers, and Exposure's range is ±20. In Photoshop, Exposure has 2 decimals, Offset 4 and Gamma Correction 2. The engine already accepts fractional values.

## Change
- Each slider row of the adjustment editors can carry its own decimal places: Exposure 2, Offset 4, and their fields show that many places (`widgets::slider_row_prec`).
- Rows without their own decimals keep the old rule (2 decimals up to a range of 10, else whole numbers), so Gamma, Posterize, Threshold, Brightness/Contrast, Vibrance, the Hue/Saturation range sliders and Photo Filter Density behave exactly as before.
- The rounding is a small function, `row_value`.

## Tests
- `exposure_keeps_fractional_stops_and_offset_four_decimals` (kittest): types 0.5 and -1.37 into Exposure, 0.0123 into Offset and 1.234 into Gamma, and checks the stored values and the field text. Fails on main.
- `integer_adjustment_rows_stay_whole_numbers` (kittest): Posterize, Threshold, Brightness and Vibrance still store whole numbers.
- `row_values_round_to_their_own_decimals`: rounding unit test, including NaN and a huge decimals count.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib` (3 local failures that also fail on main: Windows path separators, font metrics), clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`.

title: Paint Bucket and Gradient: validate opacity like the Magic Eraser (#4167)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4167.

## Why
`paint.bucket` and `paint.gradient` read `opacity` with no range check, although their params doc says `1..100`. A value above 100 became a coverage above 1 and overshot the blend: on a white document `paint.bucket {"color":"#808080","opacity":200}` painted near-black instead of #808080, and a 32-bit document could store alpha above 1. A non-numeric opacity was silently treated as 100.

## Change
- Both commands read opacity with the same helper as `paint.magicEraser`: clamped to 1..100, missing or null means 100, anything that isn't a finite number returns BadParams before any edit or history step.
- The helper (`eraser_cmds::number`) is now `pub(crate)` so the two files share it. The UI already sends 1..100, so it behaves as before.

## Tests
- `bucket_and_gradient_clamp_opacity_like_the_magic_eraser`: at 8, 16 and 32 bit, for both commands, opacity 200 or 1e9 gives the same pixels as 100, and -50 the same as 1.
- `bucket_and_gradient_reject_non_numeric_opacity_without_editing`: string, bool, array and object opacity return BadParams with pixels and history unchanged; null still means 100%.
- Both fail on main. `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests`, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt and `panic_hunt -- --ignored` pass.

## Not included
- No range check for `tolerance` or other params of these commands; they don't overshoot the blend.

title: Video layers: edits keep the timeline work area (#4170)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4170.

## Why
Every video-layer edit (Show Altered Video, Restore Frame, Interpret Footage, inserting, duplicating or deleting frames) reset the timeline's work-area end to the full duration, so a work area narrowed to frames 2–10 was lost on the next edit.

## Change
- A small `grow_duration` helper in `crates/engine/src/video_cmds.rs` grows the timeline to fit a video layer's frames (never shrinks it). The work-area end follows the new duration only if it reached the old end; a narrowed work area stays where the user put it. `Timeline::clamp()` still keeps it valid.
- All video edits and New Video Layer from File use it, so longer footage still extends a work area that covers the whole timeline.

## Tests
- `video_edits_keep_a_narrowed_work_area`: a 30-frame timeline with the work area at 2–10 keeps it after showAlteredVideo, restoreFrame and interpretFootage. Fails on main.
- `a_full_work_area_grows_with_the_duration`: insertBlankFrame grows a full work area (30 → 31) and leaves a narrowed one alone.
- `longer_footage_grows_only_a_full_work_area`: New Video Layer from File with 5 frames on a 3-frame timeline grows a full work area to 5 and keeps a narrowed one at 1–2.
- `grow_duration_never_shrinks_and_keeps_the_work_area_valid`.

title: Warp: move only the selected part of a linked mask (#4175)
author: davidmann4
body:

title: Contours (.shc): keep long names valid and readable (#4177)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4177.

## Why
Contour preset (.shc) files lost data around very long names:
- Saving a name that hits the 1024-unit cap in the middle of an emoji or another non-BMP character left a lone surrogate, which reloads as U+FFFD.
- Loading a file in which a contour with a 1024+ unit name has no points misread the following bytes, so the whole file failed to load ("unknown contour version").

## Change
- Writer: the name is capped with `io::utf16_units`, the helper `.aco` and `.ase` already use, so the cap never splits a surrogate pair.
- Reader: the check for a name count that leaves out the null now looks at the last unit actually read, not the last one kept under the cap. A counted null past the cap no longer makes the reader swallow the next `00 00` (such as an empty contour's point count). The old comment "a point count is never 0" was wrong, since our writer allows 0 points.

## Tests
- `shc_name_cap_never_splits_a_surrogate_pair`: 1023×"a" + 😀 round-trips to exactly 1023×"a".
- `shc_names_at_and_over_the_cap_keep_the_stream_in_sync`: names of 1024, 1025 and 3072 characters on contours with 0 and 3 points, followed by another contour; everything parses and the following contour is intact.
- `shc_name_count_without_null_at_the_cap_still_reads`: guards the existing leniency for a count without the null.
- The first two fail on main. `cargo test -p photocraft-psd`, clippy `-D warnings` and fmt are clean.

## Not included
- No change to the 1024-unit name cap or to other preset formats.
- Not checked against Photoshop-authored .shc files with very long names.

title: Global Light: reject angles beyond f32 range instead of storing NaN (#4181)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4181.

## Why
`layer.layerStyle.globalLight` cast its numeric params straight to f32. An angle such as `1e39` overflowed to inf, and `rem_euclid` turned that into NaN. The command succeeded, recorded a history step, stored NaN and replied `{"angle":null}`, so every Drop Shadow, Inner Shadow or Bevel using Global Light got a NaN light direction. Same class as #4044.

## Change
- Angle and altitude are read as f64; a value that isn't finite or is beyond f32 range is rejected with BadParams before the edit, so the document and history stay unchanged.
- In-range wrapping into -180..180 and the 0..90 altitude clamp are unchanged. The shared `num` helper other commands use is untouched.

## Tests
- New `global_light_rejects_numbers_beyond_f32`: an angle or altitude of ±1e39 returns Err, leaves `global_light` unchanged and adds no history step; 450 wraps to 90 and an altitude of 120 clamps to 90. It fails on main.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib layer_menu_cmds`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `panic_hunt -- --ignored` pass.

## Not included
- Other commands that cast numbers with `as f32` through `num`; they're separate fixes.
- 540 still wraps to -180 (the same direction as +180), as before.

title: Save for Web and Export As remember their settings across restarts (FILE-215-18)
author: reynold-hu
body:
Remembers the two export dialogs' settings across restarts, closing FILE-215-18 (#215):

- **Save for Web (Legacy)** already reopened with the settings used last within a session (`file_menu.last_web`), but that state is not saved, so a restart started from the defaults. A complete export now also writes the settings into the preferences' remembered dialog settings (`prefs.dialogs`, the store Fill, Liquify and the filter dialogs already use), and `open_web` seeds from the session's last export first, else from the preferences. The destination is never remembered, and neither is a one-off trusted-markup decision.
- **Export As** opened with fixed defaults every time. It now remembers the settings it was used with last — format, quality, lossless, transparency, scale, metadata and TGA bits — and reopens with them, so the scaling used last is offered again. Each remembered value is validated against its control, so a hand-edited preferences file falls back to the default.

Tests:
- `web_cmds::tests::a_complete_export_remembers_its_settings_in_the_preferences` — the settings are remembered, the destination is not, and preview estimates change nothing (they already must not replace `file_menu`).

title: Color Table: keep the transparent index inside the palette (#4186)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4186.

## Why
Image › Mode › Color Table could leave the document's transparent index pointing past the end of the palette. Replacing the colours with a shorter list (for example 4 entries with transparent = 3, then 2 colours) kept the old index, and Indexed PNG export then failed with "palette must ... cover every index". An invalid explicit `transparent` (out of range, negative, non-integer, wrong type) was silently ignored: the old value was kept and the command reported success.

## Change
- An explicit `transparent` must be an integer index inside the new table, or `null`; anything else is BadParams before any edit, so the document and history stay unchanged.
- When `transparent` isn't passed and the new colours shrink the table below the current transparent index, the index is dropped. The pixels end up exactly as with an explicit `"transparent": null`.
- Checked the other paths that set a colour table (Indexed Color, PSD import, presets, the commands that drop the table): none can produce an index past the end.

## Tests
- `shrinking_the_color_table_drops_a_transparent_index_past_its_end`: RGB with transparency → Indexed Color (4 colours, transparent = 2) → 2-colour Color Table; the index is dropped, pixels match the explicit-`null` result, palette PNG export through `photocraft_io::export` succeeds, and undo restores the index.
- `color_table_rejects_an_invalid_transparent_index_without_editing`: `999`, `3`, `-1`, `1.5`, `"0"` and `true`, alone and with new colours, are rejected with table and history unchanged; a valid index still applies.
- Both fail on main. `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests`, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt and `panic_hunt -- --ignored` pass.

## Not included
- No load-time check for `.pcraft` files that already carry an out-of-range index.
- What Photoshop does with formerly transparent pixels when the transparent entry goes away wasn't checked; this keeps the existing `null` behaviour.

title: Color Sampler: keep the CMYK readout in range on 32-bit documents (#4191)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4191.

## Why
On 32-bit documents, samples can lie outside 0..1. The Color Sampler and Info panel RGB readout clamps them, but the CMYK readout didn't: a pixel at 1.5 read K: -50% (2.0 read K: -100%), and negative values gave C/M/Y above 100%.

## Change
- `sampler_cmds::device_cmyk` clamps each channel to 0..1 before the naive device CMYK conversion, and a NaN channel reads as 0. The Color Sampler (`view.colorSamplers.*`) and the Info panel's pointer readout both use this function. Readouts within 0..1 are unchanged.

## Tests
- `device_cmyk_clamps_out_of_range_and_nan_samples`: values above 1, negative, NaN and ±inf stay within 0..=100 per channel; (1.5,1.5,1.5) gives `[0,0,0,0]`.
- `hdr_pixel_on_a_32_bit_document_reads_in_range`: a 32-bit document with a pixel at 2.0 reports rgb `[255,255,255]` and cmyk `[0,0,0,0]`.
- Both fail on main. Engine lib and integration tests, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt and `panic_hunt -- --ignored` pass.

## Not included
- ICC-managed CMYK readouts with the document's or working CMYK profile; every readout is still the naive device conversion, as before.

title: Layer Comps: the warning icon clears only its own comp (#4197)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4197.

## Why
Clicking the warning triangle on one layer comp in the Layer Comps panel removed the stale (deleted-layer) states from every comp, although the icon's tooltip says it acts on that comp. In Photoshop, the icon offers Clear Layer Comp Warning for that comp only; Clear All Layer Comp Warnings is a separate command.

## Change
- `layerComp.updateWarnings` takes an optional `"comp"` (id or name) that limits both the warnings report and the `"clear": true` clean-up to that comp. An unknown comp is a BadParams error and changes nothing. Without `"comp"` the command acts on every comp, as before.
- The history step is named "Clear Layer Comp Warning" for one comp and "Clear All Layer Comp Warnings" for all.
- The warning icon on each comp row sends its own comp id. The params doc is updated.

## Tests
- Engine: two comps record a layer that is then deleted; clearing comp 1 leaves comp 2's warning; the report can be limited to one comp; clearing without a comp still clears all.
- Engine: an unknown id or name, or a wrong-type `"comp"`, returns an error with the comps unchanged.
- UI: the icon's action carries its comp id, and running it clears only that comp.
- All three fail on main. `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests comps`, `panic_hunt -- --ignored`, clippy `-D warnings` and fmt pass for both crates.

## Not included
- No panel-menu entry for Clear All Layer Comp Warnings (the call without `"comp"` already does it).
- No check in the running app.

title: Composited CMYK documents now export as CMYK TIFF and JPEG with their profile (#2220)
author: KnottyDyes
body:
A CMYK document with more than one layer, a mask, an effect or layer opacity is flattened through the RGB compositor, and its TIFF and JPEG exports came out as sRGB RGB ("Cmyk composite written as sRGB RGB"). The document's mode and ICC profile were lost.

- For TIFF and JPEG, the composite is converted back through the document's CMYK profile (relative colorimetric with black point compensation, the existing policy) and written as four ink channels plus straight alpha at the document's depth. The conversion runs inside each parallel worker with the document's CMYK space installed.
- The file embeds the document's profile, or the built-in coated CMYK profile when the document is untagged.
- An invalid, non-CMYK or unusable profile is rejected for these CMYK exports rather than writing CMYK pixels with a mismatched tag. RGB-only formats (PNG and others) keep the existing sRGB composite and behave exactly as before, including with a damaged profile.
- A single plain raster layer still exports its native samples, and PSD and layered TIFF are unchanged.
- `book/src/formats/raster-formats.md` documents the behaviour and its limit: this fixes the output mode and tagging, but the RGB roundtrip doesn't preserve the original ink separations, black generation or CMYK-native blending.

Validation: 6 of the 10 new tests in `crates/io/tests/cmyk_composite_export.rs` fail before the change (the other 4 pin behaviour that must not change). `cargo test --workspace` (6,507 passed), `cargo xtask test-corpus` (2,768 passed), clippy, fmt, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` pass. After rebasing onto today's `main`, `cargo test -p photocraft-io` (493 passed), clippy, fmt and `cargo xtask layers` pass again.

Fixes #2220.

title: fix(type): key font menu caches on the shared engine's fonts (flaky font menu tests)
author: bommerts
body:
## What was flaky

`type_tool::canvas_tests::multi_layer_formatting::options_font_family_preserves_peer_faces_and_batches_layer_flags` failed in roughly 1 of 3 full `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib` runs on Windows, and always passed alone. The failure:

```
panicked at crates\ui-egui\src\type_tool_tests.rs:1365:11:
Harness::run exceeded max_steps (4). ...
Repaint causes: [ ..., crates\ui-egui\src\font_preview.rs:149 ]
```

It passes with `--test-threads=1`, so the cause is concurrency, not test order. The sibling font-picker tests (`font_cycle_in_options_bar_edits_the_layer_and_can_be_undone`, `options_bar_hover_previews_on_canvas_without_committing`, `localized_font_names_label_the_menu_but_pick_the_family`) fail the same way under load.

## Root cause

The font menu's preview cache (`font_preview::key`) was keyed on two process-wide counters:

- `photocraft_text::fonts::generation()`, which goes up when *any* `FontDb` registers fonts. Every `TextEngine::new()` in another test moves it, not just changes to the shared engine the menu reads from.
- `photocraft_text::served::generation()`, the served catalog. Other tests add families to it (`the_font_menu_lists_served_families`, the served-fonts tests).

When either one moved while a font menu was open, every visible sample missed the cache and was re-rendered. Families that cover Arabic call `request_repaint()` on a fresh render, so `Harness::run` never settled. #3021 didn't introduce this, but it does make the shared engine scan system fonts in ui-egui tests, which gives the menu many real (Arabic-covering) families.

The same churn affects the app: every unrelated engine re-rendered all visible samples and rebuilt the family and localized-name lists.

## Fix

- `photocraft-text`: a new `fonts::shared_generation()` that only the shared engine's `FontDb` moves (`FontDb::mark_shared`, called from `new_shared`). `fonts::generation()` is unchanged.
- `ui-egui`: `families()`, `localized_families()` and the previe…

title: Vector masks: validate feather like pixel masks (#4201)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4201.

## Why
`layer.vectorMask.edit` stored the feather as `f.max(0.0) as f32`. A huge value such as `1e39` overflowed to inf, so the mask rendered hard-edged, `info` reported `null`, and the document could no longer be saved as .pcraft (`format/src/finite.rs` refuses non-finite values). Any feather above the pixel-mask limit was accepted too, and a non-numeric feather was silently ignored but still recorded an edit. The sibling `layer.layerMask.edit` already validates a finite 0..1000 px.

## Change
- `layer.vectorMask.edit` validates `feather` exactly like `layer.layerMask.edit`: finite, within 0..=1000 px, otherwise BadParams, checked before the edit so a bad value leaves the mask and history untouched.
- The params doc says `"feather":0..1000? (pixels)`.

## Tests
- New `vector_mask_edit_rejects_out_of_range_feather`: `1e39`, `-1`, `1001`, `"x"` and `null` are rejected with the feather and history unchanged; `12.5` and `1000` are stored. Fails on main.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `panic_hunt -- --ignored` pass.

## Not included
- The shape-fill gradient angle/scale casts in the same file: open PR #3446 rewrites that code, so they're left for after it.
- Vector mask density is already clamped to 0..1 and can't become non-finite.

title: Shapes: a rectangle with a negative size extends from its origin like the other shapes (#4203)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4203.

## Why
A rectangle created with a negative width or height (`shape.create {"kind":"rect","rect":[50,10,-20,30]}`) was drawn on the wrong side of its origin: it covered x 50..70, while an ellipse or polygon with the same `rect` covers x 30..50. `rounded_rect` took the absolute size but didn't move the origin.

## Change
- `photocraft_vector::shapes::rounded_rect` normalises `(x, w)` and `(y, h)` when a size is negative, so rectangles and rounded rectangles extend from their origin like `ellipse` and `polygon`. Positive sizes give exactly the same path as before.
- The stored live-shape `rect` is unchanged. The Shape tool drag already normalises its rect, so drawing in the app is unaffected; the shape hit-test already treated a negative rect as `min..max`.

## Tests
- `vector`: `negative_size_rect_extends_from_its_origin_like_the_ellipse`: `rounded_rect(50,10,-20,30)` with radii 0 and 5 has the ellipse's bounds (x 30..50), also with both sizes negative.
- `engine`: `shape_create_negative_size_rect_covers_the_ellipse_box`: at 8, 16 and 32 bit, rect, roundedRect and a rect with both sizes negative report the ellipse's bounds and fill the same pixels.
- Both fail on main. `cargo test -p photocraft-vector`, `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests`, clippy `-D warnings` and fmt pass.

## Not included

title: Shape tools: the click-to-open-dialog tolerance is the same on HiDPI displays (#4205)

title: Cryptomatte: decode the .blue/.alpha rank of every channel set (#4208)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4208.

## Why
Cryptomatte stores two (ID, coverage) ranks in every RGBA channel set: `.red/.green` (rank 2n) and `.blue/.alpha` (rank 2n+1). PhotoCraft only read red/green, so every second rank was lost and mattes got holes at object edges and overlaps. Suffixes were also matched case-sensitively, so files with `.R/.G/.B/.A` (Blender) showed no Cryptomatte layer at all.

## Change
- Each stream channel has a rank within its set: 0 for red/green, 1 for blue/alpha. Suffixes (`red/r`, `green/g`, `blue/b`, `alpha/a`) match in any case.
- `decode` keeps two (ID, coverage) pairs per set and stores each channel at `slot*2+rank` through a bounds-checked index. Pixels are still sorted by descending coverage.
- The allocation pre-check counts four f32 channels per set. Layer listing is unchanged: each set is listed once.

## Tests
- `blue_alpha_rank_of_a_set_decodes_too`: a synthetic `crypto00.{red,green,blue,alpha}` file with a second ID at coverage 0.4 in blue/alpha; both pairs decode and the set is listed once.
- `uppercase_channel_suffixes_decode_both_ranks`: the same with `.R/.G/.B/.A`, `.Red/…` and `.r/.g/.b/.a`.
- Both fail on main. `cargo test -p photocraft-codecs --lib --tests`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo xtask wasm` pass.

## Not included
- #3722 (decode only the requested EXR part) edits neighbouring lines in `decode()`; whichever lands second needs a small rebase, the logic is independent.
- `select.cryptomatte` (#2811) benefits without changes.
- Not checked against the Psyop sample file itself.

title: Color Table: drop a transparent index past a shrunk palette (#4186)
author: mroxso
body:
## Why
`image.mode.colorTable` shrank the palette but kept the old `transparent` index when it fell past the new table's end, and the reply reported that dangling index. Saving as PNG then failed in `codecs::png::encode_indexed` ("palette must have 1..=256 entries covering every index"). An invalid explicit `{"transparent": …}` was also silently ignored and the old index kept.

## What
In `color_table` (`crates/engine/src/mode_cmds.rs`):
- an explicit `transparent` that is not a non-negative integer, or is past the table, now returns a BadParams error instead of falling back to the old index;
- after the palette changes, a transparent index past the new table's end is dropped (`None`), so the document stays exportable.

Fixes #4186.

## Tests
`color_table_shrink_drops_transparent_index_past_the_end` reproduces the issue (exact palette with a transparent entry, shrink past it), checks the reply and document state, the new error cases, and that the Indexed PNG export that used to fail now succeeds. It fails on `main` and passes with the fix.

`cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib mode_cmds`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `panic_hunt` are green.

title: Bitmap mode: validate the halftone screen angle (#4214)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4214.

## Why
Image › Mode › Bitmap with the Halftone Screen method passed its `angle` param through unchecked. A huge value such as `1e39` became inf as f32, the screen rotation turned it into NaN, and an almost white bitmap was flattened and recorded in history. title: Free Transform: apply a large layer's warp in the background, with progress and Esc to cancel (#1015)
author: ianswope
body:
Part of #1015 (the transform-commit stall reported there).

### Problem

Committing Free Transform runs `edit.transform` synchronously on the UI thread. On the 300–550 MP layers in #1015 that means several seconds of a frozen window with no feedback, every commit. Measured here on a 20000 × 16000 layer with a perspective quad (Intel ARL, Vulkan), the step took about 7.8 s. About 6.6 s of that was the engine command, the bicubic warp in `warp_surface`, and about 1.2 s was the GPU refresh afterwards.

### Change

- **algo:** `warp_surface_with` takes an `Interrupt`. It reports progress per destination tile, and once cancelled it skips the remaining tiles and returns `Ok(None)`. `warp_surface` and `warp_surface_clipped` pass `Interrupt::NONE` and behave as before.
- **engine:** `edit.transform` is an `edit_job`, like the filters. The edit body moved into `transform_doc`, and a layer's pixel warp goes through `transform_layer_with`, which uses the interruptible warp. `transform_layer` keeps its signature for its other callers. With `Session::execute` (tests, CLI, scripts, nested calls such as Straighten) it runs inline exactly as before.

title: SVG import: set text in an installed font when the named ones are missing
author: przemyslvw
body:
## Problem

On a Linux system without Windows fonts, text in an imported SVG is dropped. For example, Fedora 44 has neither Arial nor DejaVu Sans. The import then only warns "SVG: nothing to draw (an empty drawing)", although hundreds of fonts are installed. Because of this, `crates/io/tests/svg.rs` `text_becomes_outline_shapes_or_warns_without_a_font` fails on Fedora 44 on `main`.

## Cause

The SVG importer shapes text with its own `usvg::fontdb` database (`svg.rs` `fonts()`), not with the Fontconfig path of `photocraft-text` (#2961). fontdb does not know Fontconfig's aliases, and it maps the generic families to Windows fonts: `sans-serif` to Arial, `serif` to Times New Roman, `monospace` to Courier New.

So on such a system every family of a usual `font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif"` misses, including the generic one, and so does the `serif` default that usvg appends. usvg then drops the text chunk while parsing.

The warning from #3168 only fires when the font database is empty, so here the user just gets "nothing to draw".

```
$ fc-match 'DejaVu Sans'; fc-match Arial; fc-match sans-serif
NotoSans-Regular.ttf: "Noto Sans" "Regular"
LiberationSans-Regular.ttf: "Liberation Sans" "Regular"
NotoSans-Regular.ttf: "Noto Sans" "Regular"
```

Official builds are affected too: the bundled craft fonts are in the database, but no generic family points at them.

## Fix

`resolve_generic_families` points each generic family at a font the database holds, the way a browser falls back. In order of preference:

1. the system's choice, when the database has it (`fc-match <generic>` on Linux native; nothing elsewhere);
2. the first installed stand-in:
   - Liberation and Croscore, which are metric-compatible;
   - DejaVu and Noto;
   - the bundled Inter or JetBrains Mono;
3. the sans-serif choice;
4. any installed font.

A generic whose font is already installed is left alone, so systems with Arial and friends behave as before. `fc-match` runs at most once per process, wh…

author: DeWarePeb
body:
Fixes #4178.

## Symptom

Switching from Pro (Dark) or Pro (Medium Gray) to any other theme removed tool options from the options bar. With the Crop tool, Adwaita showed only the sentence "Drag a crop box · drag inside to move · …" where the Pro themes show the ratio preset dropdown, the W/H fields with the swap button, Clear, Straighten, the overlay and shield menus, Delete Cropped Pixels, and the commit/cancel buttons.

title: Find Edges and Solarize: treat CMYK values as ink (#4222)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4222.

## Why
CMYK samples are ink (1 = full ink), but Find Edges and Solarize assumed light values (1 = white):
- Find Edges turned flat areas of a CMYK document into 100% ink (solid black); Photoshop leaves them at 0/0/0/0 (white).
- Solarize inverted the high-ink channels, so CMYK 10/20/80/90% became 10/20/20/10; Photoshop gives about 90/80/80/90, because it inverts the channels below 50% ink.

## Change
- `stylize::find_edges` checks `fxutil::subtractive(ctx)`, as Trace Contour already does: in CMYK it writes the edge strength itself as ink; other modes still get `1 - edge`.
- New `stylize::solarize`: in CMYK it inverts the channels below 50% ink; other modes still invert the channels above 50%.
- Alpha is untouched. RGB, Grayscale, Lab and the other modes are unchanged.

## Tests
- `find_edges_and_solarize_treat_cmyk_as_ink` (CMYKA at 8, 16 and 32 bit): a flat CMYK surface through Find Edges gives ink 0 with alpha kept; Solarize on [0.1, 0.2, 0.8, 0.9] gives about [0.9, 0.8, 0.8, 0.9]; RGB keeps its results for both. Fails on main.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-algo`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo xtask wasm` pass.

## Not included
- Lab and other non-CMYK modes keep their behaviour; other Stylize filters are unchanged.

title: Rotate View: the image follows the pointer in a flipped view (#4226)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4226.

## Why
With View › Flip Horizontal on, the Rotate View tool spun the image against the pointer (dragging clockwise turned it counter-clockwise), and the trackpad rotate gesture was mirrored the same way. `ViewXform::to_screen` mirrors x after rotating, so in a flipped view a larger angle turns the image the other way on screen. The compass overlay already accounted for this; the drag and the trackpad didn't.

## Change
- New `rotate_view::screen_delta(delta, flip)` turns an on-screen angle change into a change of the view rotation: negated in a flipped view, wrapped, and a non-finite value becomes 0.
- The Rotate View drag and the trackpad rotate in `canvas.rs` both use it. Shift still snaps the final angle to 15°.

## Tests
- `drag_follows_the_pointer_in_a_flipped_view`: a harness drag of +30° about the pivot leaves the document point that was under the press at +30° on screen, flip off and on. With flip on it fails on main (−30°).
- `screen_delta_mirrors_only_in_a_flipped_view`: sign, the ±180 edge, non-finite input, and Shift snapping in a flipped view.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib rotate` (30 passed), clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`. The full ui-egui run only shows failures that also happen on main locally.

## Not included
- The Shift+middle-drag rotate proposed in #4042 has the same direction issue in a flipped view (`rotation + delta_x * 0.35`); it could reuse `screen_delta`. No conflict with #4042 or #4044.
- No check with a real mouse or trackpad in the running app.

title: Brush resize HUD: horizontal is size and vertical is hardness in a rotated view (#4228)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4228.

## Why
The on-canvas brush resize HUD (Control+Alt drag, or Alt+right-drag) worked in document axes and only corrected for View › Flip Horizontal. In a rotated view the axes swapped: at 90° a horizontal drag changed the hardness, and at 180° dragging right shrank the brush. Photoshop's HUD works in screen terms: horizontal is the size and vertical the hardness, however the view is rotated.

## Change
- `brush_resize::update` maps the drag anchor and pointer to screen with the active `ViewXform` and divides the screen delta by the view zoom. Without rotation the numbers are identical to before, flipped or not (`xf.zoom` equals `point_zoom()`).
- The manual flip handling is gone because the transform covers it. With no view, the old document-axis code still runs.

## Tests
- New `a_rotated_view_keeps_horizontal_for_size_and_vertical_for_hardness`: rotation 0 with and without flip (unchanged); 90° (a horizontal screen drag changes the size, a vertical one the hardness); 180° (right still grows, down still hardens); 90° with flip. Fails on main.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib brush_resize`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`. The full ui-egui run only shows failures that also happen on main locally.

## Not included
- No change to how the HUD is drawn (#2058 covers that).
- No test for pixel-aspect correction; there horizontal size follows the stretched screen distance, matching how the HUD circle is drawn.
- No check in the running app.

title: fix(compose): paint interior effects over the layer's blend mode (#3996)
author: alonfaraj
body:
Fixes #3996

A layer with a non-Normal blend mode plus a Color Overlay (or any interior effect) ignored the overlay. E.g. a black layer in Color mode with a red Overlay color overlay over grey: should tint red, stayed grey.

We were painting the overlay onto the layer's own pixels and then blending the result in the layer's mode. Photoshop does that only when "Blend Interior Effects as Group" is on. By default it blends the layer first, then paints the overlay on top. Now we do the same, on both CPU and GPU.

Normal-mode layers and layers with Blend Interior on render exactly as before.

**Repro:** grey Layer 1 → black Layer 2 above it, set to Color → Layer Style › Color Overlay on Layer 2, red, blend Overlay. Before: grey. After: red tint.

**Tests:** new CPU test for the issue's setup (fails before), plus a Color-mode case in the GPU vs CPU parity test. Compose/gpu tests, clippy and test-corpus pass.

title: feat(ui): spring-loaded tool letters (#2672)
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #2672.

In Photoshop, holding a tool's letter gives a temporary ("spring-loaded") tool: releasing the key returns to the tool you had. #2672 asks for this for Z. This does it for every tool letter, Z included. #2977 implements the Z case on its own (and says other letters are out of its scope); I posted a heads-up there, and whichever lands second will reconcile.

## Behaviour

A tool letter still switches tools when pressed. If the key then stays down for 300 ms or more, or the canvas is used while it's down, the switch was temporary: the release gives the previous tool back, with its options. A quick tap stays a permanent switch.

- ⇧+letter (cycling the group) and ⌥+letter never spring; nor do letters while typing in a field, editing type or under a dialog.
- The current group's own letter keeps or cycles the group as before, following Preferences › Tools › Use Shift Key for Tool Switch (on by default since #3528).
- A drag in progress when the key comes up finishes with the temporary tool; the previous tool returns once the button is up.
- The newest held letter wins; the original tool returns when every letter is up.
- A tool picked another way while a letter is down (the toolbar, a menu, automation) stands.
- Key repeats of tool letters are dropped instead of cycling the group.
- Z: hold Z to zoom, add ⌥ to zoom out.

## Review map

- `ui-egui/src/spring_tools.rs` (new): the state machine (`pressed`, `note_canvas_press`, `tick`) and its docs.
- `shortcuts.rs`: the tool-letter loop reports presses and drops key repeats; `canvas.rs` reports canvas presses.
- `state.rs`: `UiState::spring`, readable over the control channel and never restored from settings.

title: feat(ui): Photoshop's type formatting keys while editing text
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #4237.

Photoshop's character and paragraph formatting keys while editing type. Ctrl means Cmd and Alt means Option, as usual.

| Key, while editing type | Effect |
|---|---|
| ⇧⌘K / ⇧⌘U / ⇧⌘B / ⇧⌘I / ⇧⌘/ | All Caps / Underline / Faux Bold / Faux Italic / Strikethrough on the selection: off when every selected character has it, else on |
| ⌥↑ / ⌥↓ | leading −/+ 2 pt (⌘ for 10) |
| ⇧⌥↑ / ⇧⌥↓ | baseline shift ±2 pt (⌘ for 10) |
| ⌥← / ⌥→ over a selection | tracking −/+ 20 (⌘ for 100); a collapsed caret still kerns |
| ⌘⌥⇧H | Hyphenate for the paragraphs touched |

Each press is one `type.setStyle` history step. While typing, the keys no longer reach Color Settings, Desaturate, Auto Color or Inverse; outside an edit those shortcuts work as before.

A collapsed caret in non-empty text changes nothing. Photoshop styles the next characters typed, which the document model can't hold apart from the text. In empty text the style becomes the typing style.

## Review map

1. **Engine** (`type_cmds.rs`): `type.setStyle` gains relative steps, `leadingBy`, `baselineShiftBy` and `trackingBy`.
   - Each character moves from its own value, so mixed values keep their differences.
   - Auto leading starts from the laid-out value (the paragraph's auto-leading percentage of the size).
   - Results clamp to Photoshop's ranges, and non-finite or oversized steps are bad params.
   - `leadingBy` follows `metricsAsShown` like `leading`.
2. **UI** (`type_tool.rs`): `toggle_char_style`, `step_char_metric` and `toggle_hyphenate`, called from the key handling while an edit is active.

title: Camera Raw: faster Detail, Shadows/Highlights and Apply, bit for bit the same
author: Unemars
body:
**TL;DR:** Camera Raw's filter stages run 1.4–3.9× faster on a 16 MP frame, with the pixels bit for bit the same. Applying the filter to a layer (OK, Smart Filters) loses most of its I/O time.
- Shadows 1477 → 401 ms, Highlights 1470 → 422 ms, both 1966 → 521 ms.
- Luminance noise reduction 831 → 314 ms, colour noise reduction 708 → 419 ms.
- Sharpening 385 → 254 ms, Clarity 280 → 176 ms, Texture 359 → 261 ms, Dehaze 130 → 86 ms, Defringe 151 → 97 ms.
- Filter on the D4 NEF at OK: 1568 → 925 ms.

**Stacked on #4241 (the 1:1 refinement)**, and through it #4240 and #3818. The new commits are the two after it: [compare](https://github.com/Unemars/photocraft/compare/camera-raw-visible-region...camera-raw-fast-filters).

**Problem.**
- The Shadows / Highlights local Laplacian filter upsampled every reference's whole coarse level, although each coefficient takes only the two references within a step of it.
- Its pyramid blur computed a modulo for every tap, and its log luminance was built on one thread over the whole frame.
- Detail built its Y and chroma planes, blended the noise reduction and recombined on one thread.
- The guided filter guided by itself computed two box means that equal others.
- `box_mean` copied its column bands back on one thread; Dehaze's proxy sums, Defringe's luminance and `guided_fast`'s reduction ran on one thread.
- Applying the filter read the area, read it again only for its alpha, converted it and wrote it back, all on one thread: about 0.6 s around a 1 s develop on a 16 MP 16-bit layer.

**Change.**
- **Shadows / Highlights** (`local_tone`):
  - each reference's Laplacian is computed only where its weight is non-zero, the coarse level brought up pixel by pixel (`up_at`, the same taps over the same zero-filled samples in the same order as `up`);
  - the references run in parallel, and their shares are added in reference order;
  - `mirror` skips the modulo inside the plane;
  - the log luminance and the full-size change are built in paralle…

title: Replace Color: a canvas eyedropper picks the From colour (#4143)
author: mroxso
body:
## What

Fixes #4143.

The Replace Color dialog had no way to choose the colour to replace: the engine command defaulted `color` to the foreground colour, and the spec declared it as `json`, so the dialog rendered no colour control at all.

## How

- **Engine** (`adjust_cmds.rs`): the `color` param is now declared `color` instead of `json`, so the generic filter-dialog machinery renders a swatch row. The command still accepts `"#rrggbb"` or `[r,g,b,a]` and still defaults to the foreground when the param is absent, so automation is unchanged.
- **Dialog** (`filter_dialog.rs`): Replace Color seeds the field from the foreground colour (Photoshop's behaviour) and shows a pipette button next to the swatch. Clicking the swatch opens the regular Color Picker (as everywhere else, #2144).
- **Canvas** (`canvas.rs`): while the eyedropper is armed, the image becomes the picker — the next primary click samples the merged composite (the same `composite_color` sampler the Curves picker and the Color Picker use, never the reduced preview) into the dialog's `color` field. Off-image or transparent clicks are consumed and leave the picker armed; the button toggles it off.

## Verified

- New tests: `replace_color_eyedropper_samples_the_image` (seeding, sampling, invalid-sample behaviour, disarm) and `replace_color_dialog_arms_the_eyedropper_button` (kittest click on the pipette).
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib` (2299 passed), `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib` (1430 passed), `panic_hunt` ignored test green, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo xtask layers` OK.

title: Compare the Export As sibling path as a path, not as a string
author: persi-man
body:
`export_as_with_several_artboards_selected_writes_one_file_each` fails on Windows on current `main`.

`batch_paths` returns the chosen path verbatim for the first file and builds the siblings with `Path::join`, so the two carry different separators there:

```
["/out/boards.jpg", "/out\boards-2-Capsule.jpg"]
```

The test asserted on the literal prefix `"/out/boards-2-"`, which can never match, so it fails:

```
thread 'file_dialog::tests::export_as_with_several_artboards_selected_writes_one_file_each'
panicked at crates\ui-egui\src\file_dialog\tests.rs:722:5:
["/out/boards.jpg", "/out\boards-2-Capsule.jpg"]
```

This is an assertion problem, not a behaviour one: the Win32 API accepts mixed separators, so the file is still written where it should be. The fix compares the parent, the file name and the extension through `Path`, which checks the same intent on every platform. Nothing outside the test changes.

Introduced by #3909. The Windows job on `main` has not reported it yet; the recent CI runs were cancelled by the pushes that followed.

### Checks

- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib file_dialog::tests::export_as` passes on Windows (rustc 1.96.1), and the rest of `cargo test --workspace` was already green apart from this one test
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored` passes, untouched by this change

title: Tests: GPU startup marker tests wait while another test's child process holds the lock
author: dotCooCoo
body:
**Root cause.** `gpu_startup::tests::returned_non_graphics_errors_do_not_trigger_backend_recovery` fails at random in a full `cargo test`:

```text
panicked at apps/photocraft/src/gpu_startup.rs:742:13:
assertion `left == right` failed: gpu-error: Err(Wgpu(CustomNativeAdapterSelectionError("no adapter")))
  left: false
 right: true
```

For its `gpu-error` case, the test drops the sentinel, which leaves `gpu-starting.json` in place, and then calls `Sentinel::begin` for the same directory (`:741` on `main`). The `monitor_profile` tests spawn processes in the same test binary: `a_hung_helper_is_stopped_and_big_replies_dont_block` runs `sleep` and `/bin/sh`, and on macOS `detected_displays_parse` runs `osascript`. A child process started while the marker is open gets a copy of its file descriptor, and the marker stays locked through that copy until the child's exec closes it. If `begin` runs in that window, it returns `Previous::Busy`, `previous.crashed()` is `None`, and the assertion fails with that message.

3b7870be (the squash merge of #289) describes the same race: "between fork and exec the child holds a copy of the marker file descriptor, so flock reports WouldBlock and begin() returns Busy". That commit made `sentinel_detects_a_crash_and_clears_on_success` retry `begin` (`:702-711` on `main`). #1228 added the failing test two days later, without the retry.

**What changed** (test only). The retry loop moves, unchanged, into a helper in the tests module, `begin_when_unlocked`. title: Canvas: a tool drag past the edge auto-scrolls the view (#4183)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Fixes #4183.

**What:** a tool drag held past the edge of the canvas (marquee, lasso, brush stroke, crop…) now scrolls the view toward the pointer, as in Photoshop, so a selection can be larger than what is on screen. Speed grows with distance past the edge (capped, and bounded per frame). The view stops at the scroll limits, an axis where the image already fits does not scroll, and a view the user overscrolled is never pulled back.

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`: clean. `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests`: all pass except `arbitrary_rotation_preview::size_changing_rotation_preview…` and `full_res_preview::filter_dialog_previews…`, which fail identically on unmodified `main` in the same lavapipe environment.

title: feat(codecs): open DDS textures, uncompressed and BC1-BC3 (#1327)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Closes #1497. Part of #1327 (opening DDS files; saving and exporting as DDS is left for a follow-up).

Adds a read-only DDS (DirectDraw Surface) codec, so game and 3D textures open like any other flat image. It follows the PCX codec from #3701: a built-in decoder in `crates/codecs/src/codecs/dds.rs`, registered in `Format`, `caps`, `detect` (the `DDS ` signature) and the decode/encode dispatch. It is listed in `ASYMMETRIC_EXCEPTIONS` and added to the desktop app's Open extensions.

What opens:

- uncompressed pixels described by channel masks: 8, 16, 24 or 32 bits per pixel, RGB or luminance, with alpha when `DDPF_ALPHAPIXELS` is set. This covers RGBA8/BGRA8, X8R8G8B8, R8G8B8, R5G6B5, A1R5G5B5, A4R4G4B4, L8 and A8L8.
- BC1, BC2 and BC3 (DXT1, DXT3, DXT5), including BC1's one-bit-alpha mode (`c0 <= c1`). BC2/BC3 colour blocks always use four colours, as the format requires.
- the DX10 header for the same formats: R8G8B8A8, B8G8R8A8, B8G8R8X8 and BC1–BC3, UNORM, sRGB or typeless.

Everything decodes to 8-bit Gray, GrayA, RGB or RGBA. Only the top mip level is read. Cubemaps, texture arrays, volume textures, premultiplied DXT2/DXT4 and any other format (BC4–BC7, float, other FourCCs) are refused with `CodecError::Unsupported`, and the error names what was found. A cubemap isn't silently opened as its first face.

All header fields are treated as untrusted: reads go through `get()`, and the level size uses checked arithmetic. `Limits` are checked before the output buffer is allocated, and a file shorter than its top level is an error, not a partial image. Writing isn't provided. #1327 asks for Save As as well, and a useful DDS writer means choosing a block compression and generating mip levels, so that is left for a follow-up.

Docs: a row in the codecs README capability matrix with a note under its limitations, and a row in `docs/file-format-parity.md` under formats Photoshop doesn't have (it needs a plug-in for DDS), with the revision history.

title: Control: a transport that gives up knows whether the command was dispatched (#3662)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #3662.

Both timeout sites replied with the same text, "timeout: no reply in 60s — the command may still be running…", so a client couldn't tell a request that never ran (safe to re-send) from one that was dispatched and may still apply (re-sending could apply it twice, as with `paint.stroke` in the issue).

Two texts, both still starting with `timeout` so existing prefix matches keep working:

- `timeout: not run — the request was still queued when its 60s deadline passed, so it was dropped before dispatch and is safe to re-send; …`
- `timeout: no reply in 60s — the command may still be running and may still apply, or …`

Splitting the text alone wasn't enough. The control server's transport thread and the UI thread share the same deadline, and the transport's `recv_timeout` gives up at that instant, so the UI thread's "not run" reply almost always arrives after the transport has already answered with its own text. That is the `layer.new.layer` case in the issue: the request was still queued, but the client got the transport's message. So `ControlRequest` now carries a small `Dispatch` flag shared by both threads and settled once with a compare-exchange. The UI thread claims it before running a request, and the transport abandons it when it stops waiting. If the transport wins, the request is guaranteed not to run and the reply says `not run`. If the UI thread won, the command was dispatched and the reply says it may still apply. A request the transport gave up on is never run later, even if the UI drains it before its own deadline check would reject it.

Scope: this settles the "never ran" case for certain. A dispatched command that doesn't reply in time is still a genuine unknown. Idempotency keys or a status lookup, as suggested in the issue, would be a separate change. `docs/control-protocol.md` describes both replies. The MCP bridge (`crates/automation/src/bridge.rs`) still gives up at 55 s with its own message, so agents driving the app over MCP don't g…

title: feat(codecs): support full X11 rgb.txt color names in XPM
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Extend XPM image decoding with support for the complete X11 rgb.txt
color-name database.

This follows up on #3702, where the review identified that XPM files
containing colors such as LightGray and DarkBlue could not be opened.

The original implementation supported a limited set of common names.
However, many legacy X11 applications and icon themes use names from
the full X11 color database.

## Changes

- Add 657 normalized color entries derived from X.Org's rgb.txt.
- Support case-insensitive and multiword color names.
- Support numbered X11 color variants.
- Use the original X11 RGB values rather than CSS equivalents.
- Implement efficient lookup using a sorted static table.
- Preserve existing supported aliases.
- Add regression tests for X11 color decoding.
- Include source attribution.

## Testing

Added regression coverage for:
- X11 color names outside the original supported list.
- Multiword color names.
- Numbered X11 color variants.
- Colors whose X11 values differ from CSS.

Cargo tests have not yet been executed locally.
CI validation is pending.

## Related

- #3702 — Original XPM3 image import implementation.
- #3692 — Image format support tracking issue.

This directly addresses the X11 color compatibility issue raised
during the review of #3702.

## Scope

This PR only extends XPM named-color decoding. It does not change
image export functionality or introduce additional image formats.

Depends on #3702.

title: feat(codecs): add XPM2 plain-text image import support
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Add support for importing XPM2 plain-text images alongside the
existing XPM3 C-string representation.

This follows up on #3702, where XPM2 support was identified as
a missing capability during review.

XPM3 stores image definitions inside C-style string arrays, while
XPM2 uses a simpler plain-text representation beginning with
the "! XPM2" signature.

Both representations describe indexed-color images, so they can
share the existing decoding and validation logic.

## Changes

- Detect XPM2 files using their "! XPM2" signature.
- Support LF and CRLF line endings.
- Parse plain-text image headers, palettes, and pixel rows.
- Preserve whitespace and special characters in palette keys.
- Support multicharacter palette keys.
- Support transparent pixels.
- Reuse the existing XPM color decoder.
- Reuse dimension, palette, and allocation limits.
- Reject malformed and truncated XPM2 input.

## Implementation

The existing XPM3 decoder is extended with a separate parser
for XPM2's plain-text representation.

Both parsers feed into the same image-decoding implementation.

This avoids duplicating palette handling, pixel decoding,
and input validation.

## Testing

Added regression coverage for:
- XPM2 format detection.
- LF and CRLF files.
- Transparent pixels.
- Multicharacter palette keys.
- Whitespace-sensitive palette keys.
- Malformed headers and pixel rows.
- Unknown palette entries.
- Invalid hexadecimal colors.
- Oversized image dimensions.

Cargo tests have not yet been executed locally.
CI validation is pending.

## Related

- #3702 — Original XPM3 image import implementation.
- #3692 — Image format support tracking issue.

This addresses the XPM2 compatibility gap mentioned during
the review of #3702.

## Scope

This PR adds read-only support for XPM2.

XPM1 and XPM export remain outside the scope.

The implementation shares existing decoding infrastructure rather
than introducing a separate image codec.

Depends on #3702.

title: fix(io): read CS2 placed layers that carry only a PlLd block (#2465)
author: Kartik8Dwivedi
body:
## Summary
Photoshop CS2 smart objects now open as live smart objects whose contents can be edited. Before this change, Edit Contents on one said "the smart object's contents are unavailable". Edited CS2 smart objects also save their new placement.

## Root cause
CS2 predates the `SoLd` block, so its placed layers carry only a `PlLd` (`plcL`) record, and the embedded file sits in a global `lnkD` block. Import chose `PlLd` as the smart-object key, but `blocks::parse_smart` only decoded `SoLd`/`SoLE`. The layer got an empty source id, so `linked::find_linked_file` found nothing and Edit Contents failed. The placement also came back as identity.

## What changed
- **Reading `PlLd`:** `blocks::parse_plld` reads the unique id and the 8 corner doubles of a `plcL` record, following the public Adobe PSD spec ("Placed Layer") and our own `plld_bytes` writer. Every read is bounds-checked; truncated, mis-tagged or non-finite data gives `None`, and an unreadable `PlLd` produces an import warning.
- **Source size:** `PlLd` stores no source size, so import takes it from the embedded file's header (`linked::source_size_probe`: PSD, TIFF, PNG and JPEG headers; any other image is decoded flat by `photocraft-codecs`), cached per source id. It never imports the embedded file as a document, because a layered TIFF can carry PSD layer data whose `lnkD` holds another file, which would nest without bound. Without the file, 100 % scale is assumed.
- **Placement, consistent with #3677:** the `PlLd` corners are the same placed quad as `SoLd`'s `Trnf`, so they frame the same source-space box (`blocks::placed_frame`): the bounding box of a single-patch custom warp's control points, else the source rect. `corners_affine` maps that frame onto the corners, is shared by `parse_smart` and the new `plld_transform`, and is the inverse of `smart_map::quad_points`. Non-parallelogram corners give the projective placement, as for `SoLd`.
- **Warps:** CS2 can warp a smart object, and `PlLd` keeps that warp…

title: Camera Raw Filter: save and load settings as .xmp
author: FredApps
body:
Fixes #4274

Adds **Save Settings…** and **Load Settings…** to the Camera Raw Filter. They read and write Adobe Camera Raw `.xmp` presets (the `crs:` namespace, in both attribute and element form), so settings can move between Photoshop and PhotoCraft.

### What's supported

- **HSL:** all 24 hue, saturation and luminance adjustments

- **Detail:** sharpening, and luminance and colour noise reduction
- **Effects:** grain and post-crop vignette (Style 1, 2 and 3)

- Loading only changes the settings the file contains and keeps the rest, the way Photoshop does. Values are clamped to the slider ranges.
- Fields we have no control for are ignored. The status bar counts the ones set to something other than neutral, for example "(2 not supported)".
- A malformed file shows an error and changes nothing. Tested with empty, non-UTF-8, unclosed XML, DOCTYPE/entity, NaN and broken-curve input.
- Saving writes every supported control in Photoshop's own layout.
- The control channel also accepts `{"ui":{"saveSettings":true}}` and `{"ui":{"loadSettings":true}}`.

Three tests on `main` fail after #3630 and #3877. Each fix is its own commit.

## 1. CLI prints the same missing-font warning more than once (#3630)

`missing_typeface_is_reported_by_run_info_and_convert` failed: `left: 2, right: 1`.

#3630 made `Headless::open` and `Headless::save` return missing-font warnings, but the CLI (#1299) already reported them itself:

- `run --new … --out` printed the warning twice (once after the command, once from `save`).
- `run <file> --out` printed it three times.

title: Gradients: Photoshop's interpolation method for Gradient Overlay, gradient Stroke and the Gradient tool
author: MrCloudy2
body:
`layer.layerStyle.gradientOverlay`, `layer.layerStyle.stroke` (gradient fill) and `paint.gradient` take a new **`method`** param (`classic`, `perceptual`, `linear` or `smooth`) and a **`smoothness`** param (0–100, default 100 as in Photoshop).

The two stops are baked into dense stops with the same model PSD import already uses (`io::gradient_bake`). The compositors' linear interpolation then reproduces Photoshop's curve. Without `method`, the stops stay exactly as before.

`gradient_bake::bake` and `Method` are now public, as `photocraft_io::{bake_gradient, GradientMethod}`. `Method::from_name` parses the param.

## Evidence (Photoshop 27.11, scripted, whole images compared)
| case | main (max levels) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Gradient Overlay Classic, Linear/Reflected style, any angle/scale/reverse | 12 | 0–1 |
| Gradient Overlay Classic, Radial / Diamond | 16 | 4–5 |
| gradient Stroke, linear / radial | 12 / 8 | 2 / 4 |
| Gradient tool, black → white Classic (5 styles, dither on/off, diagonal) | 13–14 (Angle 32) | 2–3 |
| Gradient tool red → blue: Classic / Perceptual / Linear / Smooth | 12 / 83 / 64 / 83 | 1 / 2 / 4 / 3 |

The Angle style keeps one 36–40-level line along its seam, covering 0.3–0.4 % of pixels. A 3-stop Classic gradient improves only from 14 to 10: the multi-stop smoothness spline in `gradient_bake` is a separate follow-up.

Photoshop's *default* method for a newly created overlay isn't measured yet, so the default behaviour is unchanged.

## Tests
- New: `gradient_overlay_method_matches_photoshop` (Classic black → white is 0.037 at t = 1/16, against 0.0625 for straight stops).
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-io` passes.
- `panic_hunt` (`--ignored`), fmt and `cargo xtask wasm` pass.
- clippy (`--no-deps`) is clean in the touched files. My local clippy 1.95 flags `psd_export.rs`, which this PR doesn't touch.

title: Free Transform: refuse outputs over a pixel budget instead of building them
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
This is the follow-up echelon asked for in #3867: a separate memory bound for huge Free Transform scales that refuses the transform rather than clipping content. It doesn't depend on #3867 and is based on main.

What was wrong: a big scale, like 200x on a thin column, made the warp fill every tile of a result that can reach 2^21 px on a side. Memory ran out before anything could fail cleanly.

The fix: before building anything, Free Transform works out how big each warp's result will be (new `warp_output_bounds` in `algo::transform`, the same rectangle `warp` fills). If a result would go over `MAX_TRANSFORM_PIXELS`, the transform is refused with an error in the style of the `allocation` errors: "not enough memory for transforming pixels (the transformed layer "Layer 1" would be W x H px, more than the N px limit); the document was not changed". The limit is 2^30 px, the same as Puppet Warp's `MAX_WARP_PIXELS`. Only the size of the result counts, not where it lands, so moving a small layer far off the canvas still works. Nothing gets clipped.

The check covers the layer pixels, a smart object's cache and filter mask, linked masks, a lone mask/alpha channel/Quick Mask target, and the selection outline. It runs over the whole layer tree before any layer changes, so a group where only some layers fit is never half-transformed. `select.transformSelection` gets the same check. Image Rotate and smart-object unpack also call `transform_layer`, so they get the check too.

In the UI, a refused commit used to close the transform box and only put the error in the status bar. Now the box stays open as the user left it, with the error in the status bar, so they can shrink it or press Esc. If the user switches tools or layers, the refused transform is cancelled, so it can't keep retrying every frame.

Tests: engine tests run with a 2^20 px budget (cfg(test)), so a refusal never gets close to allocating the real limit, and every raster in them is a few pixels.

title: Propose plug-in ABI v2: panel plug-ins with loopback-only network
author: MehranMarxian
body:
Hi! I maintain [OpenLayer] (https://github.com/MehranMarxian/OpenLayer), an MIT-licensed ComfyUI plugin for Photoshop (14 generation tools, all running on the artist's own GPU). I'd like it to work in PhotoCraft too. This PR is a design proposal only, with no code: a concrete design for the ABI v2 line in #219 that would make that possible without bending any of PhotoCraft's rules.

What's in this PR
docs/plugins-v2.md: the proposal (status: proposal, not implemented).
docs/plugins.md: a two-line pointer to it under "Not in v1".
The proposal in short
A panel kind with a host-drawn, declarative UI (egui + theme::Tokens, so plug-ins can't go off-theme), as #219 already plans.
Still no imports. The plug-in exports one new function, pc_event(json) -> [operations]. The host carries the operations out asynchronously and returns the results as later events. v1's "a module that imports anything is rejected" stays exactly as it is, and the same model works on the web build, where fetch is async.
Blobs: image bytes stay host-side, so the interpreter never encodes a PNG.
Document access: doc.capture (composite, layer or selection, converted to sRGB through photocraft-cms) and doc.commit (new layers with optional masks, converted back into the document's mode and depth, as one undo step through Session::edit).
Network: loopback only (127.0.0.0/8, ::1, localhost), declared in the manifest and approved by the user in the app. Automation can't grant it, because prefs.set already refuses plugIns. No TLS and no async runtime are needed. The first PR proposes a stub HostNet for the web build, so the wasm gate stays green.
Agent-drivable: panel state in ui.inspect, and every click and edit goes through plugin.panel.event.

On #41: this doesn't pick a generative backend, and PhotoCraft still ships no model and no AI code. It only lets a user's own local tool add layers through a sandbox. A later provider kind could make a local ComfyUI one of the backends behind #41's planned provider …

title: Filter > Other > Frequency Separation (#1714)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Closes #1714.

**Filter › Other › Frequency Separation…** sets up frequency separation in one step, instead of the duplicate / Gaussian Blur / Apply Image / blend mode routine.

From the active pixel layer it adds a **Frequency Separation** group right above it, holding:

- **Low Frequency** (Normal): the layer through Gaussian Blur at the chosen radius. These are the same pixels Filter › Blur › Gaussian Blur produces.
- **High Frequency** (Linear Light): `High = (Source − Low) / 2 + ½` in each colour channel, keeping the source's transparency.

This is Photoshop's recipe: Apply Image › Subtract, Scale 2, Offset 128 in 8-bit, and Add + Invert, Scale 2, Offset 0 in 16-bit, which give the same values. Linear Light computes `Low + 2·High − 1`, so the result is the source again. In 32-bit our Linear Light uses the same formula, so the recipe is unchanged there. The source layer itself is not modified, it is one history step, and the High layer ends up targeted, ready for healing.

The command is `layer.frequencySeparation` with `{"radius": 0.1..1000 = 4}`. From the menu it opens the existing schema dialog, which has a single Radius field. Photoshop has no menu item for this (people record it as an action), so the id is our own. The menu entry goes after Color to Alpha (`PLACE_AFTER`). I kept it out of `filter.*` because it adds layers rather than filtering the target, so mask/channel routing, Fade and Last Filter would all be wrong for it. The menu label is in all 17 catalogs, which the coverage test requires.

**Limits**

- Only RGB and Grayscale. In CMYK and Lab the compositor does not blend on the stored values (in a test the rebuild was off by 0.7 and 0.14), so the command is refused there rather than giving a wrong split.
- Linear Light clips to 0..1, so 32-bit values above 1 come back as 1.
- 8-bit stores High to the nearest level, so the rebuild is within ±1 level, the same as Photoshop's recipe.
- The new layers carry only the source's pixels (no mask, style, op…
