title: Layers: Fill and the Paint Bucket edit an adjustment layer's mask when its icon is targeted (#4298)
author: dhiorns15
body:
## Problem

An adjustment layer has no pixels of its own, so in Photoshop painting or filling it always edits its mask. In PhotoCraft, Edit > Fill on an adjustment mask was fixed in #2471, but only while the Layers panel targets the mask. Clicking the adjustment layer's icon thumbnail (the usual way to open its settings) untargets the mask, and so does reaching the layer with Alt+[ / Alt+]. After that:

- Edit > Fill (Shift+F5) and the fill keys are greyed out ("active layer is an Adjustment layer, not a pixel layer").
- The Paint Bucket and the brushes do nothing and show "not a pixel layer" in the status bar.

## Fix

The two functions that decide where pixel edits go now send them to the mask whenever the active layer is an adjustment layer: `PhotocraftApp::layer_mask_targeted` (used by Fill, the fill keys, filters and adjustments such as Invert) and `canvas::paint_target` (used by the Paint Bucket and the brushes). The Layers panel's own target is unchanged: the brackets, the footer trash and Delete behave as before. Fill layers keep their Rasterize prompt.

- New: `canvas::tests::fills_on_an_adjustment_layer_edit_its_mask_when_the_icon_is_targeted`. With the icon targeted, Fill and the fill keys are enabled, the Paint Bucket fills the mask black, Edit > Fill fills it white, and a pixel layer with an untargeted mask still paints its pixels. The same steps failed on `main` before this change.
- Updated: `command_i_inverts_the_targeted_mask` asserted that Invert was disabled on an adjustment layer with the icon targeted. It is now enabled and inverts the mask, as in Photoshop.

title: Codecs: open DPX (SMPTE 268M) digital-intermediate frames (#1049)
author: vbasky
body:
## What
Adds a pure-Rust, read-only **DPX** (SMPTE 268M) decoder to `photocraft-codecs`, implementing the frame format written by film scanners and grading systems. `Format::Dpx` is registered (detect on `SDPX`/`XPDS`, extension `.dpx`, caps, an `ASYMMETRIC_EXCEPTIONS` entry since there is no writer), routed in `decode`/`encode` and given the frame orientation, and `.dpx` is added to the desktop and web open filters.

Supported: one image element with descriptor 50 (RGB), 51 (RGBA), 52 (ABGR), 1 (single channel) or 6 (luminance); 8/10/12/16-bit integer samples; packing 0 (packed MSB-first bit fields) and 1 (filled to 16-bit); both byte orders; the per-element reference low/high levels; and the DPX orientation code. Bounds are checked before allocating (limits are validated against the declared size, rows and slices are `get()`-checked), and any other descriptor, bit depth, packing, multiple elements or RLE returns a clear `Unsupported`/`Malformed` error — never wrong pixels or a panic.

## Why
#1049. Photoshop reads DPX (via Camera Raw) and the file-format parity table listed it as unsupported; DPX is common in film/DI pipelines and was the only flat-intra format among the missing ones that has a fully public spec (SMPTE 268M), so it can be implemented clean-room.

## Verification
- Unit tests in `crates/codecs/src/codecs/dpx.rs`: 10-bit filled RGB decodes to exact levels, 8-bit to U8, truncation at many offsets errors, an unknown descriptor is `Unsupported`.
- `crates/codecs/tests/detect_caps.rs`: magic/extension/caps for DPX (and a PCX detection case).
- Full `photocraft-codecs` suite green (668 passed, 3 ignored); `cargo xtask layers` OK; fmt + clippy `-D warnings` clean.
- Not run: `cargo xtask wasm` — the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target is not installed in this environment. The decoder is pure Rust (`Vec`/slices only) and wasm-safe by inspection.

## Docs
`crates/codecs/README.md` capability matrix + asymmetry notes, `docs/file-format-parity.md` DPX/PCX rows.

title: Layers panel: Clip Thumbnails to Layer Bounds (#4281)
author: badaaif
body:
Closes #4281

## What

Adds Photoshop's **Clip Thumbnails to Layer Bounds** option for the Layers panel. When on, a pixel layer's thumbnail frames the layer's own pixels instead of the whole canvas, so small objects in a large document are visible in the panel.

- New preference `interface.clipThumbnailsToLayerBounds` (default **off**, so existing behaviour is unchanged). It's drivable by agents via `prefs.set`.
- Toggled from the Layers panel menu (☰), or Preferences > Interface.
- The frame is the layer's content bounds cut to the canvas. Empty layers, or layers with no pixels on the canvas, keep the canvas frame.
- The thumbnail cell is fitted to the frame's aspect ratio, so there are no empty bars.

## How

- `layer_thumb` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`) returns the thumbnail and the document area it frames. `thumb_image` now samples a `Rect` rather than the whole document.
- The frame uses `photocraft_compose::bounds::content_bounds`, which is tile-cached. It is computed only when the thumbnail is rebuilt, never per frame. The preference is part of the thumbnail cache key, so toggling it rebuilds.
- Translations for both labels in all 19 catalogs. `docs/ui-parity.md` updated and `docs/scorecard.md` regenerated (preference count 156 → 157, unread unchanged at 27).

## Tests

- New `crates/ui-egui/src/layer_thumb_bounds_tests.rs`:
  - default frames the canvas
  - toggling on frames the filled rect and rebuilds the texture, and toggling off restores it
  - empty and off-canvas layers
- Passing: `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`, `cargo test -p photocraft-engine`.
- Checked visually with the `snapshot` example: a 60×40 px object in a 3000×2000 document is invisible in its thumbnail by default and fills it with the option on.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui`: everything passes except four tests that fail identically on current `main`, so they're unrelated to this change…

title: Simplify the raster stale-block filter for clippy's nonminimal_bool
author: persi-man
body:
Clippy 1.96 flags the `retain` predicate in `crates/io/src/psd_export.rs` that strips stale content blocks from pixel layers on export, so `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` fails on current stable:

```
error: this boolean expression can be simplified
   --> crates\io\src\psd_export.rs:605:37
    = note: `-D clippy::nonminimal-bool` implied by `-D warnings`
```

This rewrites it as a single negated disjunction, which is clippy's own suggestion. The four terms, their order and the short-circuiting are unchanged, so exactly the same blocks are kept and dropped. I checked the two forms agree on all 32 combinations of the five booleans involved.

### Checks (Windows, rustc 1.96.1)

- `cargo xtask test-corpus`: 143 test binaries, 3155 passed, 0 failed, including `photoshop_oracle_corpus`, `psd_tools_mutations_never_panic` and `global_layer_block_roundtrips_with_opaque_neighbors`
- `cargo test -p photocraft-io` on the rebased branch: 490 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

The repository has no `rust-toolchain.toml`, so each contributor runs the lints of whatever stable they have. Pinning one would keep local clippy in line with CI; left out of this PR since it is a project-wide choice.

title: Codecs: open uncompressed DICOM single-frame images (#1048)
author: vbasky
body:
## What
Adds a pure-Rust, read-only **DICOM** decoder to `photocraft-codecs`. `Format::Dicom` is registered (detect on the `DICM` magic, extensions `.dcm/.dicom/.dc3`, caps, an `ASYMMETRIC_EXCEPTIONS` entry as there is no writer), routed in `decode`/`encode`, and the extensions join the desktop/web open filters.

Supported: the file meta group's transfer syntax — implicit VR little-endian, explicit VR little-endian and explicit VR big-endian — with MONOCHROME1/2 (gray, honouring the 1 = white inversion) and RGB/YBR_FULL (8-bit), 8- and 16-bit allocated samples, interleaved or planar layouts, samples scaled from `BitsStored`/`HighBit` and mapped up when `PixelRepresentation` is signed. Compressed transfer syntaxes, undefined-length (sequence) elements, multi-frame pixel data and other photometric interpretations return a clear `Unsupported`/`Malformed` error. Bounds are `get()`-checked, dimensions are validated against `Limits` before allocating, and no input panics.

## Why
#1048. DICOM is the one remaining common *medical* raster format Photoshop reads; it has a fully public spec (PS3.5) so it is clean-room implementable.

## Verification
- Unit tests in `crates/codecs/src/codecs/dicom.rs`: 8-bit MONOCHROME2, 16-bit with level scaling, MONOCHROME1 inversion, truncation at many offsets errors, and a compressed transfer syntax is `Unsupported`.
- `crates/codecs/tests/detect_caps.rs`: magic/extension/caps for DICOM.
- Full `photocraft-codecs` suite green (670 passed, 3 ignored); `cargo xtask layers` OK; `cargo check -p photocraft` clean; fmt + clippy `-D warnings` clean.
- Not run: `cargo xtask wasm` (`wasm32-unknown-unknown` target not installed here); the decoder is pure Rust and wasm-safe by inspection.

Also fixes a small miss: `.pcx` was absent from the **web** open filter.

## Docs

title: fix(engine): step small brush and pencil sizes down to 1 px with [ (#4067)
author: Korg1ch
body:
Fixes #4067

### Problem
Pressing [ (	ools.decreaseBrushSize) with a brush or pencil tool stops decreasing the size at 2 px instead of reaching 1 px, because (2.0 / 1.25).round() evaluates to 1.6_f32.round() == 2.0. While the upward step (]) guaranteed at least a 1 px increase via .max(size + 1.0), the downward step ([) lacked the symmetric .min(size - 1.0) bound.

### Solution
- Apply .min(size - 1.0) before .clamp(1.0, MAX_SIZE) in  rush_key_cmds::size_step when stepping down so small sizes (3 -> 2 -> 1 px) always step down by at least 1 px until reaching 1 px.
- Add unit tests in  rush_key_cmds::tests verifying size_step(2.0, false) == 1.0 and repeated 	ools.decreaseBrushSize calls reaching 1.0.

title: Wayland: show a proper X on the Close button (#4260)
author: PrimusCicada
body:
Fixes #4260 (replaces #4285, closed when its fork was deleted)

On Wayland compositors that leave window decorations to the app (GNOME, Hyprland), the Camera Raw window's Close button was a filled square instead of an X.

**Cause:** winit was built without `wayland-csd-adwaita`, so it fell back to SCTK's basic frame, which draws Close as a solid rectangle.

**Fix:** enable `wayland-csd-adwaita` on the `winit` dependency in `apps/photocraft/Cargo.toml`. winit then draws an Adwaita title bar with proper minimize/maximize/close icons. This also fixes extra document windows and the main window when System Title Bar is on.

- Linux only; new deps: `sctk-adwaita` (MIT), `ab_glyph`, `ab_glyph_rasterizer`, `owned_ttf_parser` (Apache-2.0)
- `cargo test -p photocraft` passes

title: Free Transform: unlinking W and H frees the handles too (#4174)
author: dhiorns15
body:
## Problem

#4174 reports that in Free Transform, unlinking W and H doesn't let you resize the two sides independently.

The options bar's **Maintain aspect ratio** link only affected values typed into W and H. Dragging a corner or edge handle always scaled proportionally, whatever the link said, so turning the link off seemed to do nothing on the canvas.

In Photoshop CC 2019 and later, the same link also sets what a handle drag does by default:
- linked: drags keep the proportions, and Shift frees them;
- unlinked: drags stretch freely, and Shift keeps the proportions.

## Fix

- New `unlinked_mods` swaps Shift for corner and edge drags while the link is off, next to the existing `legacy_mods`. Linked (the default) behaves as before, and so does the **Use Legacy Free Transform** preference, which is already free by default. ⌘ gestures (skew, distort) are left alone.
- The link state moves from egui temp data into `UiState::transform_unlinked`, so the options bar and the drag code read the same value.

This covers only the Transform part of #4174. The PDF import and Arabic file name parts are separate, so this PR doesn't close the issue.

## Tests

- New: `transform_tool::tests::the_aspect_link_decides_whether_handle_drags_keep_proportions` runs a corner drag and an edge drag for each case: linked, unlinked, unlinked with Shift, and unlinked with the legacy preference. With the swap disabled, the unlinked corner drag gave 32 × 32 instead of 32 × 16.
- Ran: `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib` and its integration tests, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm`.
- `prefs_ui::tests::preference_labels_are_translated` (hu) and `new_doc_ui::tests::new_document_depth_labels_and_tooltips_are_translated` (tr) also fail on `main` without this change. #4304 fixes them.

No screenshots: nothing looks different, only how a drag behaves.

Refs #4174

title: Save As JPEG: JPEG Options dialog (quality 0–12, Baseline / Optimized / Progressive) (FILE-215-19)
author: SckraT
body:
Save As and Save a Copy to a JPEG now ask for JPEG Options before writing, as Photoshop does.

## What the dialog does

- **Quality:** Photoshop's 0–12 scale, with Low/Medium/High/Maximum presets. It defaults to the Export preference's JPEG quality.
- **Format Options:** Baseline ("Standard"), Baseline Optimized or Progressive.
- **How it works:** it is built like Targa Options. The save waits behind a modal, Cancel drops it, and the answer is recorded in the `file.saveAs` step, so actions replay it without asking.

- **codecs:** `JpegFormat` on `EncodeOptions`. Progressive writes SOF2. Optimized Huffman tables are used only at 4:4:4 or for progressive: jpeg-encoder 0.6 writes corrupt 4:2:0 baseline scans with them.

title: fix(type): the Type tool's canvas pick skips text in hidden groups (#4320)
author: FredApps
body:
Fixes #4320

### Root cause
Clicking type on the canvas, with the Type tool or with a Move-tool double-click (`edit_at`), picks a layer through `hit_layer` in `crates/ui-egui/src/type_tool.rs`. Its filter (line 64 on main) checked only the layer's **own** `visible` flag, not the groups around it. So text inside a hidden group was still picked. A PSD that keeps text variants in hidden groups above the shown one gets the hidden variant on click. The engine's `type.hitTest` (`topmost` in `crates/engine/src/type_caret_cmds.rs`) already checked ancestors since #3173, but the UI pick was separate code and never got that check.

### Fix
- New `Document::shown_at(path)` in `crates/doc`: the layer and every enclosing group are visible.

title: Filters on a type layer: ask to rasterize or convert to a Smart Object instead of greying out
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #4303.

The filters are greyed out on a type layer because the engine only filters pixel layers (and, for most filters, Smart Objects). The engine stays as it is: the UI now keeps a filter live when the only thing missing is a rasterized layer, and choosing it opens the "Rasterize?" prompt that painting on a type layer already uses (same message, already translated everywhere), with Photoshop's Convert to Smart Object / Rasterize / Cancel. Cancel changes nothing. Filters the engine only runs on pixels (Vanishing Point, Average, Clouds, Difference Clouds) offer Rasterize only. Last Filter asks only when there is a filter to repeat. Locked type layers, other layer kinds and filters greyed for some other reason (a job running) stay greyed out.

One walks every Filter menu item that is live on a pixel layer and checks it asks on a type layer and then runs; kittest clicks Rasterize and Convert to Smart Object in the rendered dialog and checks Vanishing Point has no Convert button

title: Add a Nix flake (NixOS, GNOME and Hyprland)
author: untypequicode
body:
## What

Adds `flake.nix` and `nix/package.nix` so that `nix build`, `nix run` and an overlay give a source-built photocraft and photocraft-cli on NixOS, modelled on the existing LightCraft flake.

- `Cargo.lock` drives the dependencies (git sources through `cargoLock.allowBuiltinFetchGit`), so there is no `vendorHash` to maintain. The version comes from `[workspace.package]`.
- Installs the desktop file, hicolor icons, MIME types and AppStream metadata from `packaging/linux/`, validated at build time (`desktop-file-validate`, `appstreamcli`).
- Wayland and X11: the binaries are wrapped so the libraries winit/wgpu/rfd `dlopen` are found on NixOS — `libwayland-client`, `libxkbcommon` (incl. x11), the X11 libs, the Vulkan loader, `libEGL` and `libdbus` (xdg-desktop-portal file chooser). It runs natively on Wayland under GNOME and Hyprland, with X11/XWayland as fallback. Hyprland needs a portal backend for the file dialogs (`xdg.portal.extraPortals = [ pkgs.xdg-desktop-portal-gtk ]`); this is noted in `nix/package.nix`.
- The fonts from `storytold/craft-fonts`, where the app embeds them, are a pinned non-flake input at the revision the release workflow uses.
- Also: `overlays.default`, `apps.default`, a dev shell, `nix fmt` and a formatting check.
- `doCheck` is off: the suite needs corpora and a GPU the sandbox cannot provide (`cargo xtask ci` stays the gate); it can be turned on with `overrideAttrs`.

No Rust, packaging or CI file is touched.

## Testing

`nix build .#photocraft` builds both binaries and passes the desktop-file and AppStream validation, on NixOS. The GUI starts under Hyprland.

title: Color Picker: CMYK foreground fills a CMYK document with the picked inks (#4196)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #4196

## Root cause
The foreground/background colours are stored as sRGB. A colour picked as CMYK (100/0/0/0) was converted to sRGB (clamped, since pure cyan is outside sRGB) and then back through the profile when a CMYK document was filled, giving 100/28/0/17.

## Fix
- `tools.setColors` accepts `foregroundCmyk` / `backgroundCmyk` (inks 0..1; malformed values are an error). `ToolState` remembers the last 8 CMYK picks keyed by their sRGB stand-in, so swap/reset/mask pairs need no bookkeeping.
- Edit > Fill and the fill keys (foreground/background/explicit colour) write the remembered inks as they are into a CMYK target (`Source::Cmyk`); other modes and blend modes keep using the sRGB stand-in.
- The Color Picker sends the entered CMYK on OK and shows the remembered inks when reopened.
- Fill now enters the document's own CMYK profile while it converts colours (as the brush and compositor already do).

Not covered: brush strokes still paint the sRGB colour, so a CMYK pick painted with a brush still goes through sRGB.

## Tests
- `fill_key_cmds::cmyk_pick_fills_a_cmyk_document_with_the_picked_inks` (fails without the fix: 73/15/0/0), `malformed_cmyk_pick_is_an_error_not_a_panic`
- `color_picker_ui::cmyk_values_survive_ok_and_a_reopen`

title: Smart Objects Warp: mesh knots span the contents on a skewed placement (#4113)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #4113

## Root cause
`layer.smartObjects.warp` stores the warp in source space with bounds = bounding box of the warp `rect` mapped back through the placement. On a skewed/perspective placement that box (B) is larger than the contents, and the mesh `us`/`vs` knots were measured in B, so a mesh equal to the placement shrank the contents into the middle of B.

## Fix
When a `mesh` param is given (not the full `warp` object the Free Transform UI sends, which keeps its box-relative knots), the knots now span the smart object's source contents, as in a PSD's custom-warp mesh. They are re-expressed over hull(contents, B) and degenerate patches pad the sides where B extends past the contents, so the stored warp, `smart_warp_doc_space` and the editing handles are unchanged. Points stay in document px. Param docs updated. If the source cannot be read, the old behaviour is kept.

## Tests
- `smart_cmds::tests::identity_mesh_on_a_skewed_smart_object_changes_nothing` (mean diff 0.107 without the fix, under 0.01 with it).

## Commands run
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib -- warp smart_cmds` (56 passed)
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p photocraft-engine -- --check`

title: Brush: CMYK foreground paints the picked inks into a CMYK document (#4344)
author: vangel76

Fixes #4344

**Stacked on #4339 and must merge after it** (this branch contains its commit; once #4339 lands, only the second commit remains in the diff).

title: Type: faux bold keeps antialiased edges at small sizes (#4130)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #4130

Root cause: faux bold draws every glyph at 8 small offsets into a single signed-area coverage accumulator. The antialiased edge coverage of the copies summed and was clamped to 1, so edge pixels saturated: stems looked hard and pixelated at 72 dpi and the ink grew far more than the dilation (about 2.2x for 12 px "Ill").

Fix: rasterize plain glyphs/decorations once, draw each bold offset into its own coverage buffer and merge with max (union). Bounds and outline paths are unchanged.

Weight tuning: a plain union with the old tiny ring (0.018 em) made stems visibly lighter than before (12 px "Ill" ink 28.3 plain, 62.3 old, 40.5 union). `FAUX_BOLD_RADIUS` is now 0.036 em, which brings total ink for "Bold Test" to 0.87 (12 px), 1.00 (16 px) and 1.07 (24 px) of the old summed result (244.7/282.7, 448.5/446.8, 1017.0/947.2); "Ill" is 0.84, 1.11, 1.12.

Tests: `faux_bold_keeps_antialiased_edges_at_small_sizes` now also asserts total ink for "Bold Test" at 12 px is within 0.85..1.15 of the old summed result (282.7, hard-coded), besides partial-coverage pixels staying at plain level.

Commands: `cargo test -p photocraft-text --lib` (141 passed), `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib -- type text`, `cargo test -p photocraft-io --lib -- text`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-text --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p photocraft-text -- --check`, `cargo xtask layers`.

title: Engine: reject unknown params for layer.hideLayers/showLayers, opt-in registry check (#4336)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #4336

## Root cause
Commands read the keys they know from the params object and ignore the rest, so `layer.hideLayers {"ids":[4]}` fell back to the active layer and reported success.

## Change
- New `crates/engine/src/param_check.rs`, called once in `Session::dispatch` (so CLI, MCP, control channel, UI and actions all get it). For commands listed in `STRICT` it rejects any key their `params` doc does not name, with `unknown parameter \`ids\` (expected: layer)`. `coalesce` and `target` are always accepted. title: Type: type on a path, glyphs follow the curve (#4365)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #4365 (first slice of TYPE-218-1, part of #218).

## What
- `TextShape::Path { path, start, flip }` in `photocraft-doc` (path in the layer's text space; `TextShape` is no longer `Copy`).
- Text engine: the text is laid out as one point-text line, then each glyph is placed rigidly on the flattened path by arc length and turned to the tangent at its centre (like Photoshop; not bent point by point). title: Preserve HDR and signed colors in 32-bit text rasterization
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
32-bit float text clips authored color values while removing glyph coverage: `[2.5, -0.25, 0.5]` becomes `[1, 0, 0.5]`. Preserve finite float components during unpremultiplication. Integer output and non-finite intermediates retain their existing behavior.

Fixes #4326.

The regression fails on main `184c226` and passes at `93a349e`, covering opaque/translucent text and bounded 8/16-bit output. A fresh release CLI preserves HDR red at 2.5. With text gamma disabled, it preserves all three authored components. Default text gamma still clips negative components in the compositor; this change fixes the straight text surface.

- Text crate: 136 passed, 4 ignored. All-target Clippy with warnings denied, formatting, layering and complete WebAssembly checks passed.
- Full corpus command: 3,159 passed, 0 failed, 25 ignored across 143 test groups; pinned manifests verified.
- Fresh release CLI pixel assertions passed for both gamma settings on an RGB32 document.
- Quick type benchmark completed: 20 layers, 2000x1500, 15 edits; total latency p50 8.88 ms / p95 9.64 ms. The saved baseline is from a different machine class, so regression comparison was skipped. No speedup claim.

title: Menus keep clear of a panel that covers a maximized window (X11) (#3737)
author: FredApps
body:
Fixes #3737. Follow-up to #3739.

## Problem
#3739 kept menus clear of the taskbar on Wayland, where the window position is unknown. The reporter is on Linux Mint (X11, 1920×1080) and still sees long menus (Layer, View, Window) run under the bottom panel, with no way to scroll to the hidden rows.

On X11 a window manager that doesn't reserve a panel's space maximizes the window to the whole monitor, and the panel covers its bottom. `work_area::visible_part` (#315) treated every maximized window as already inside the work area and skipped the taskbar check, so menus used the full window height and their ▼ arrow ended up under the panel.

## Fix
- `visible_part` now takes a `WindowState` (`Normal` / `Maximized` / `FullScreen`) instead of a single `fills_screen` flag.
- A maximized window whose position is known is checked like any other window. A window manager that does keep it above the panel still gets the whole window, because the window already ends above the panel.
- Full screen still uses the whole window, since it covers the panel on purpose.
- A maximized window with no known position (Wayland) is still treated as fitting, as before.

## Tests
- `work_area::a_maximized_window_under_a_panel_is_still_cut_at_the_taskbar`: a 1920×1080 monitor at 1× and 1.5×, maximized under a panel, maximized above a panel, and full screen.
- `menu_nav::menus_of_a_maximized_window_stay_above_a_panel_it_runs_under`: Filter, Layer, Image, Edit, View and Window at 1× and 1.5×. Every popup stays above the panel, the ▼ arrow is visible, and resting on it scrolls to the last row.
- Both tests fail without the fix.

Implements issue #3470, the missing **Clarity and Dehaze** adjustment layer (Photoshop 2026's

title: Raw: treat DNG samples piled up below the stated white level as clipped
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #4348.

Same cause as storytold/lightcraft#548, ported from the fix there (storytold/lightcraft#586). The iPhone 15 Pro Max Bayer DNG states WhiteLevel 4095 but its sensor stops at 3567 (about 85% of the range) in all three colours. `develop_sensor` clips each channel at 1 after white balance, so with the camera's multipliers (red x2.46, blue x1.59) red and blue reach 1 while green stays at 0.85: blown areas come out magenta. On DNG decode, `photocraft-raw` now looks for a per-colour pile-up of samples on one value clearly below the stated white level (upper half of the range, at least 0.01% of the colour's samples and 100, 16x the values just below it, almost nothing above it) and raises those samples to the white level, so the channels clip together. Unclipped samples keep their values; files whose data reaches the white level, has no pile-up, or uses a LinearizationTable are untouched. One addition over the LightCraft detector: a colour with nothing darker than the plateau (a uniform flat field) is left alone, since the existing `forward_matrix_path_maps_neutral_to_white` test frame would otherwise be lifted. Happy to drop that if you'd rather match LightCraft exactly.

Validation:
- `highlights_that_clip_below_the_stated_white_level_stay_neutral` (crates/raw/tests/dng.rs): fails on main (wall renders `[63736, 60683, 64898]`, magenta), passes here
- `saturation::tests` (8 unit tests: plateau lifted and idempotent, data reaching white, no plateau, popular value with data above, few stuck samples, flat field, linearized data, hostile levels)
- `cargo test -p photocraft-raw --test dng --test hostile`
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-raw --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check -p photocraft-raw --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`

I did not have the reporter's file to check the render end to end; the numbers above are the ones measured on it in lightcraft#548.

title: Content-Aware Move: live preview of the result (#4385)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #4385

Umbrella #213, scorecard row TOOL-213-4.

**What.** With the Content-Aware Move tool the canvas now shows the move/extend result: during the drag once the pointer rests, and in the Transform On Drop box once the box rests (scale/rotate/move). Any change cancels the running job and restarts the wait; a stale result is never shown for a different offset. The document and History are untouched until release/Enter, which runs the exact `paint.contentAwareMove`.

**How.** `retouch_cmds::content_aware_move_preview` (engine) builds a `Send` job from the session and runs the same `run_move` as the command on a copy of the document, with a smaller sampling margin (48 px instead of 512) and only for selections up to 256x256 px; it observes a `JobCtx` for cancellation. `cam_preview.rs` (UI) debounces (150 ms), runs it on a worker thread, polls without blocking, and feeds the result through the canvas preview-document hook. Not available on wasm (no threads). No timing claims are made.

**Tests.** Engine: preview shows the move, leaves the session and revision alone, honours cancel, rejects bad params and oversize selections. UI: drag waits out the debounce then shows the result, drops it on further movement and at release; Transform On Drop box preview and its cancel; oversize selection is not retried.

**Commands run.** `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib -- content_aware_move`, `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- cam_preview content_aware_move`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`, `cargo xtask scorecard`. No snapshot render (a pointer drag cannot be scripted through the snapshot example).

**Left.** A progressive/coarse-to-fine preview for selections over 256x256 px; the preview recomposites the whole canvas (no damage-rect refresh).

title: Windows: keep full screen and maximized apart; never restore full screen
author: aweussom
body:
Fixes #4116. Probably same cause as #3550, #4018 and #4230 (taskbar black or gone after maximize), but I have not reproduced those setups.

Cause is in winit, rust-windowing/winit#4756: on Windows, a window that goes full screen from maximized keeps `WS_MAXIMIZE`. The shell draws the taskbar black instead of hiding it, and on the way out the window stays maximized at full monitor size, on top of the taskbar. #3308 does not cover this path; I reproduced it on `main` after that merge.

Two changes:

1. `view_cmds::screen_mode_commands` (Windows only): un-maximize before entering full screen, maximize again after leaving it. Full screen and maximized never overlap. This is the workaround from the winit issue. It can go once winit has a fix and PhotoCraft picks it up.
2. `restored_window` in `apps/photocraft/src/main.rs`: eframe restores full screen from `ui.ron`, as full screen and maximized at once. The hook now drops the full-screen flag, so PhotoCraft starts in Standard Screen Mode, which is what its own state says anyway. Size, position and maximized are kept.

Windows 11. The bug shows on both my machines, 1920x1200 at 125 % and 3840x2160 at 150 %: starting maximized, full screen gave a black taskbar, and back in Standard the window covered the taskbar. With the fix, tested on the 1920x1200 one only: clean full screen, normal maximize afterwards, by `F` and by the menu, and a restart after closing in full screen opens in Standard.

I confirmed the winit side with a minimal eframe app that logs window style and rect at each step: https://gist.github.com/aweussom/3f80ffb82df7f0102341858afbbffd9b (numbers in my comment on the winit issue).

Ran: `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- view_cmds`, `cargo test -p photocraft --bins`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui -p photocraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`. `panic_hunt` not run: no engine command added or changed.

title: Hard brushes: a 2 px anti-aliased edge, so curves and diagonals aren't stair-stepped (#4088)
author: tanish2k09
body:
Fixes #4088. A 100 % hard brush looked pixelated next to Photoshop.

## Cause
A computed tip's anti-aliasing was a 1 px linear ramp at its radius. On curves and diagonals, overlapping dabs leave each edge pixel decided by whichever dab comes nearest, so the edge stair-steps. In the report's screenshots, Photoshop's hard-round fringe is about **1.6×** ours (4.0 vs 2.5 screen px per edge, at matching stroke widths of ~100 px).

## Change
- The ramp is now **2 px** (`EDGE_HALF = 1.0`), defined once in `edge_ramp` and used by `dab_coverage`, the vectorised `rasterize_round`, and the reference renderer. Dab rects grow with it (`rect_around`).
- A dab is still exactly 50 % covered at its radius, so brush size and the cursor's rings don't move.
- Soft brushes barely change, the Pencil and Block eraser stay aliased, and tips under 3 px radius keep their own 4×4 sub-pixel coverage.

Measured on a hard 30 px stroke with a 0.17 slope:

| Edge half-width | Partly painted px/column | Edge wobble (sd) | Edge bias |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5 (before) | 0.87 | 0.074 px | +0.10 px |
| **1.0 (this PR)** | 1.56 | **0.032 px** | +0.34 px |

The width was chosen by the owner from side-by-side renders (0.5 / 0.75 / 1.0).

## Tests
- New `a_hard_strokes_edge_is_smooth_not_stair_stepped` checks slopes 0.17, 0.4 and 1.0. New `a_hard_dab_keeps_its_size_and_a_two_pixel_edge` checks that the dab is half covered at the radius and that the rect holds the ramp at sub-pixel offsets. Both fail on main.
- Three bound tests updated for the extra half pixel:
  - The scatter rect test allows ≤ 25 px, and its damage expectation is `[16,13,25,25]`.
  - The Spot Healing footprint stays within `radius + EDGE_HALF`, under the ring's 3 px line.
  - The live Color Replacement test still allows at most 2 levels, plus f32 slack. It hit exactly 2/255 + 1e-8.
- Local results:
  - `photocraft-paint`: 101 tests pass.
  - `photocraft-engine`: all tests pass.
  - `photocraft-ui-egui` lib: all pass except two translatio…

title: macOS: big brushes keep a native outline too, and big cursor bitmaps rasterise 7x faster (#1343)
author: tanish2k09
body:
Follow-up to #3243 for #1343, from @syncroot's macOS measurements.

## What
- **macOS takes cursor bitmaps up to 2048 points**, the same cap as Windows; it was 255. Past the old cap, the outline fell back to the app-drawn one, which trails the pointer by 26 ms on a 120 Hz Mac (1000 px brush at fit, 300 px at 200 %, per syncroot's table). Apple's docs set no size limit on `NSCursor` images since 10.3. Linux keeps 255, because X servers and hardware cursor planes cap there.
- **Big cursor bitmaps rasterise ~7× faster on every platform.** A circle bitmap used to evaluate every pixel of its square, though only a thin ring is painted. Now it starts transparent and evaluates only the ring's two arcs in each row, plus the centre mark. Shaped-tip outlines likewise only write the pixels their segments reach.

| Brush radius (1×) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 120 px | 0.67 ms | 0.21 ms |
| 500 px | 10.6 ms | 1.7 ms |
| 1000 px | 41.6 ms | 6.2 ms |

Bitmaps are cached per size and scale, so this cost lands on each zoom step or `[` / `]` resize. On Windows, which already allowed 2048, a 1000 px outline hitched about 40 ms there.

## Tests
- New `circle_bitmaps_evaluate_only_the_ring_and_match_every_pixel` checks that the fast path equals evaluating every pixel, for radii 0.4 to 90, scales 1 to 2×, with and without the centre mark.
- `cursor_bitmaps_stay_within_the_platform_limit` now covers macOS and a 2000 px brush.
- Local results: the tool_cursor and input tests pass, and clippy `-D warnings` and fmt are clean.

## Not merging until tested on a Mac
@syncroot, could you re-run your rig on this branch (`fix/macos-large-brush-cursor`)? The rows to check are 1000 px @ fit, 2000 px @ fit, 1000 px @ 100 % and 300 px @ 200 %. I'd like to know whether the outline is now an OS cursor with ~10.5 ms lag, and whether macOS draws a cursor that size correctly (no clipping, no flicker, right position). If AppKit does have a practical limit, I'll set the cap just under it.

title: Stroke latency trace: PHOTOCRAFT_STROKE_TRACE times each frame of a brush stroke (#1343)
author: tanish2k09
body:
For #1343. Testers report about 50 ms from input to pixel while painting on Linux (X11/NVIDIA, Wayland, Intel) and macOS. @VoronBrothers-VoronBrothers asked for a per-stage breakdown. This adds one that anyone can switch on without rebuilding.

## Use
```sh
PHOTOCRAFT_STROKE_TRACE=1 photocraft            # a summary per stroke on stderr
PHOTOCRAFT_STROKE_TRACE=strokes.csv photocraft  # also every frame, appended to that CSV
```
```text
stroke trace: 62 frames on vulkan NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (p50/p95 ms): interval 8.33/8.53 moves/frame 0.00/0.00 stroke 0.80/1.53 canvas 0.40/0.75 ui 0.91/1.41 cpu 2.20/2.84 wait 6.04/6.64
```

For each frame of a stroke, it records:
- `interval`: the time between frame starts;
- `moves/frame`: pointer moves the OS delivered;
- `stroke`: rendering the live stroke's new points, or the commit on release;
- `canvas`: the canvas refresh, composite plus upload;
- `ui`: the UI build;
- `cpu`: eframe's CPU time per frame, i.e. UI, tessellation and GPU submission (`Frame::info().cpu_usage`);
- `wait`: `interval − cpu`, the vsync or swap-chain wait.

The first line names the GPU backend. That matters because the GL backend ignores the surface's frame-latency setting, so GL may queue more frames. The last summary is also in the control channel's `perf.strokeTrace`. All of this is documented in `docs/development.md` › Stroke latency trace.

What the app can't time is the rest of input-to-photon: the OS input queue before a frame starts, frames queued for the display, and the compositor. The summary shows how much of each frame is the app's own work, and how many refresh periods remain for the queue and display.

## First numbers
RTX 5090, Vulkan, 120 Hz, a 60 px brush on a 3000×2000 canvas: the frame is 8.33 ms, of which the app's CPU is 2.2 ms (UI 0.9, stroke 0.8, canvas 0.4); the other ~6 ms is vsync wait. The app keeps up within one refresh here. Together with the 25 ms input-to-photon I measured with PresentMon on this machine, about two ref…

title: Send a document to Telegram from the File menu
author: benjarogit
body:
File › Send to Telegram… sends the open document through a Telegram bot. The item sits in the File menu after Save a Copy.

![File menu with Send to Telegram and Submit to DeviantArt](https://github.com/benjarogit/photocraft/raw/93bf5262/file-menu.png)

The dialog chooses the saved file, a PSD, or a PNG. A PSD can also send a PNG preview. The two files go out as one album of documents, because Telegram will not mix a document with a photo. A single image (PNG, JPEG, GIF, or WebP) is sent as a photo. A PSD without a preview stays a document. Several chat ids are allowed. Pinning is off unless the checkbox is on. If the bot is not an admin, the file is still sent and the status says the pin failed. Optional auto-send follows Save, Save As, Save a Copy, and Export, and waits until that file is on disk.

When the send finishes, a dialog names the file and gives the message link. A public chat uses https://t.me. A private chat has no web page, so the link opens the message in the Telegram app. Get files lists files sent from PhotoCraft and the ten newest files and photos sent to the bot. One click downloads a file of at most 20 MB and opens it. Nothing is fetched in the background.

![Send to Telegram dialog](https://github.com/benjarogit/photocraft/raw/93bf5262/telegram-dialog.png)

The bot token is stored in the OS keychain: macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux Secret Service, and the same interface on FreeBSD and OpenBSD. If the keychain cannot store it, PhotoCraft reports the error and does not write the token into `telegram.json`. Chat ids, the switches, and the file ids of documents sent from PhotoCraft stay in that file, mode 0600 on Unix. The caption is Telegram Markdown: file name, format, size, time, and path. Dialog labels are translated. Status and errors stay English. The web build does not send. The form scrolls, so the title and OK stay on screen in a short window.

title: Save As: on Windows, picking another file type changes the extension (#4394)
author: dhiorns15
body:
## Problem

In **File › Save As** on Windows, picking **PhotoCraft** in "Save as type" after the dialog opened with `image.psd` still saved `image.psd` (#4394). This happens when Explorer shows file name extensions: the Windows save dialog leaves an extension it can see in the name box alone when the type changes. With extensions hidden it already switched to `image.pcraft`.

rfd sets the dialog's default extension from the first type, and Windows updates that default whenever the user picks another type. It only applies it to a name without an extension, though.

## Fix (Windows)

`apps/photocraft/src/services.rs`:

- On Windows the save dialog now starts with the bare name (`image`). The suggested type still leads the type list, so leaving it alone gives `image.psd`, and picking PhotoCraft gives `image.pcraft`.
- `save_filters` also puts the suggested extension first within its type, so `.psb`, `.fit` and `.jpeg` stay what they were instead of becoming the type's first extension.
- Kept as the whole name: a stem that still has a dot (`scan.jpg.psd`), an upper-case extension (the user's spelling), and names without an extension.

Checked by hand on Windows 11 with rfd 0.17.2 (the version in `Cargo.lock`), picking PhotoCraft in the real dialog:

| Explorer extensions | Name given to the dialog | Saved as |
|---|---|---|
| shown | `image.psd` (before) | `image.psd` ✗ |
| shown | `image` (this PR) | `image.pcraft` ✓ |
| hidden | `image.psd` (before) | `image.pcraft` ✓ |
| hidden | `image` (this PR) | `image.pcraft` ✓ |

Leaving the type alone with the bare name still gives `image.psd`.

## Other platforms

- **macOS:** unchanged. rfd's save panel has no type list (all extensions are allowed together), so the format follows the extension the user types.

title: Swatches: an RGB group with the exact primaries and secondaries (#4302)
author: FredApps
body:
Fixes #4302.

## Problem
The reporter's text turned dull green when they picked **Swatches › Pure › Green**, while Photoshop gave a vivid `#00FF00`. Rendering and colour management are fine:
- In their own video, the text run that is `#00FF00` in their PSD (RGB/16, sRGB profile) measures about `0,253,8` on PhotoCraft's canvas.
- Our built-in **Pure** group is a vivid palette, not the pure channel values. Its green is `#28C850` (40, 200, 80), its red `#E62828`, and so on.
- Photoshop users reach for its **RGB** group, which holds the exact values.

## Fix
- Add an **RGB** swatch group with Photoshop's exact six colours, in its order: `#FF0000`, `#FFFF00`, `#00FF00`, `#00FFFF`, `#0000FF`, `#FF00FF`. They're named "RGB Red" … "RGB Magenta" so swatch names stay unique.
- It sits right after **Grays**, near the top of the panel. Grays stays first because new swatches are added to the first group.
- **Pure** is left unchanged, so documents, actions and saved libraries that use those colours keep them.
- Users with a saved swatch library keep it as is and get the new group from **Reset Swatches**. This is the same behaviour as any other change to the default swatches.
- Group names aren't translated, so no catalogs change.

## Tests
- New: `presets::swatches::the_rgb_group_holds_exact_primaries_and_secondaries`.
- `swatches.list` now checks that RGB Green is `#00ff00`.
- Counts and indices in the swatch command tests are updated for 46 default swatches.
- `photocraft-engine`: all tests pass (1436 in the library).
- `cargo +1.99.0 fmt --check` is clean. Clippy 1.95 shows no new warnings.
- `photocraft-ui-egui`: the 4 failures are also on current main (#4359 and the known `multi_layer_formatting` test).

title: perf(raster): moved fills keep sharing one copy-on-write tile
author: SckraT
body:
## What

- `Surface::translated` gives a target tile **one shared tile** when the window it reads lies entirely on existing source tiles that all hold one single pixel value, instead of building a fresh copy.
- A per-call memo (`UniformTiles`) scans each source tile once (keyed by its `Arc` address) and keeps one canonical tile per value. Targets reading the same value from different source tiles therefore share one tile. This includes uniform tiles that an earlier nudge copied.
- Targets that are fully covered but not uniform skip the default-pixel pre-fill, because the copy overwrites every pixel.
- The shortcut requires the source window to be the exact preimage of the target (`sr.translate(dx, dy) == dr`). An offset of `i32::MIN` saturates its negation and takes the old path.

Only `crates/raster/src/lib.rs` changes.

## Why

`fill_rect` already shares one `Arc<Tile>` across a solid fill. But any move that isn't a whole number of tiles rebuilt every target tile. After its first nudge, a fill became one unique tile per coordinate. From then on, each move (with its refresh) rescanned and re-uploaded all of them, because the bounds cache and the GPU page sync key on tile identity. Undoing a move re-uploaded them all again, and history kept all of them.

Callers:
- the Move tool drag preview and `layer.translate` (`layer_multi_cmds::shift_surface`)
- committed moves of layers and masks (`commands::translate_layer`)
- `algo::resample::translate_surface` (floating selections, smart objects, canvas operations)

Related to the move rows of #209 (P1, P6, P12, P14, P17; P12 can't be measured yet). This PR does not claim to meet those budgets.

## Measurements

The surface is moved ±(10, 7) twenty times and `translated` is timed. Each cell is the mean of two runs' p50 (release build, 4-core cloud container, `MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_` fixed so glibc's dynamic threshold doesn't swing the numbers).

title: perf(compose): stop sweeping the bounds cache on every call once it i…
author: SckraT
body:
## What

- `compose::bounds` drops entries of dead tiles past a **high-water mark**: when the cache holds more than twice the entries that survived the last sweep, and at least 65,536. Before, once more than 65,536 tiles were alive, *every* call walked and kept the whole map.
- The per-tile scan moves to raster as `Tile::content_bounds(dp)`. `Surface::content_bounds` and the cache now share it, instead of keeping two copies of the same loop.
- `Tile::content_bounds` returns no content for an empty pixel instead of panicking in `chunks_exact(0)`. It is public now, so it shouldn't rely on its callers.

## Why

`compose::bounds::content_bounds` is called per render tile for styled layers (CPU compositor), per frame by the GPU planner, and for fill frames and mask bounds. The sweep condition was `len > 65_536` with no memory of the last sweep. Once more than 65,536 queried tiles were alive, every call paid an O(cache) `retain` under the global lock.

That case is rare: history trimming caps each document's tiles plus its history at Memory Usage (8192 MB by default, about 32,768 RGBA8 tiles). Reaching it takes several large documents open at once, 8-bit grayscale, or a raised Memory Usage. For scale, a 15000×10000 layer is 2,360 tiles.

## Measurements

None. Reproducing it needs more than 65,536 live tiles, about 4 GB even as 8-bit gray. The change removes an O(n) pass per call past that size. The scan itself is unchanged code.

## Behaviour

title: perf(engine): move layers without a second document clone
author: SckraT
body:
## What

`move_layers` takes `before: &Document`, the document as it was before any of the moves. It no longer clones the document itself. Its three callers pass in the starting state they hold as an `Arc`:
- `layer.translate` already held it, for `note_damage`.
- Align and Distribute now take it with `s.active().ok_or(EngineError::NoDocument)?.doc.clone()` just before `Session::edit`. That clone only bumps a refcount.

Only `crates/engine/src/layer_multi_cmds.rs` changes (+10/−8).

## Why

`move_layers` cloned the `Document` on every call. The only reason was that `translate_layer` and `translate_vectors` read the pre-move state while type and shape layers re-render. `Session::edit` already clones the document for the edit, so each nudge, Align and Distribute cloned it twice.

The clone copies the layer tree, strings and paths, plus every surface's tile map (one refcount bump per tile). The pixels themselves are shared. Its cost therefore grows with the number of layers and tiles (one map entry per 256×256 tile in use), not with the pixel data those tiles hold.

## Measurements

A 4000×3000 document with 150 layers holding 1024² fills, plus a small layer. `layer.translate` nudges the small layer ±1 px: 70 timed calls per run after 10 warm-up calls, 5 runs. Release build, 4-core container, glibc's `MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_` pinned. The "after" build also carried the selection-coverage PR of this set, which doesn't touch this path.
- Median per run: 0.78–0.84 ms before, 0.66–0.87 ms after.
- Median of the 5 runs: **0.80 → 0.71 ms**.

## Behaviour

Unchanged.
- `Session::edit` hands the closure a copy of the Document inside the same `Arc` the callers take (`(*before).clone()`), and changes nothing in it first.
- In all three callers the closure only reads `doc` before `move_layers`, so `before` equals the old in-function snapshot:
  - translate: the mask-target partition and `move_targets`
  - Align: `bounded_selection`, `doc.bounds()`/`doc.selection`, `with_links`, `de…

title: perf(compose): read PHOTOCRAFT_FX_NOCACHE once
author: SckraT
body:
## What

`effect_maps` reads `PHOTOCRAFT_FX_NOCACHE` once, through a `OnceLock`, the same way the GPU compositor reads `PHOTOCRAFT_FX_TRACE`. Before, it called `std::env::var_os` on every effect-map lookup.

Only `crates/compose/src/lib.rs` changes (+2/−1).

## Why

The CPU compositor calls `effect_maps` for each styled layer in each render tile its effects reach, plus once per layer before the tiles start. `std::env::var_os` takes the process environment's read lock and scans the environment. That costs **≈140–180 ns per lookup here (157 variables), against ≈0.5 ns from the `OnceLock`** (1M lookups per variant, release build, 3 single-threaded runs).

For scale: a 7360×4912 canvas is at most 580 render tiles (29 × 20 at 256²). With 9 styled layers whose effects cover the whole canvas, that's about 5,200 lookups. That works out to roughly 0.8 ms of CPU time per full CPU render, spread across the render threads; layers covering less cost proportionally less. It's small, but it's paid on every render, every tile thread takes the shared environment read lock for it, and the fix is free.

## Behaviour

The variable is a debugging switch documented in `docs/development.md`, set before launch. It is now read once, on the first effect-map lookup. Nothing sets it at runtime, and no test toggles it. The only difference is that flipping it mid-process no longer takes effect.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-compose --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p photocraft-compose --lib --tests`: 240 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p photocraft-compose`. On wasm, `var_os` returns `None` as before.
- **All five PRs of this set merged together** (on `67e4b8a`): clippy `-D warnings` on raster, compose, gpu, engine and ui-egui; `cargo test --lib --tests` on those crates: 4334 passed, 2 failed. The two failures are ui-egui GPU-harness tests (`size_changing_rotation_preview_…`, `filter_dialog_previews_at_full_resol…

title: perf(engine): read selection coverage per row when mixing edits back
author: SckraT
body:
## What

- Destructive adjustments (`pixels::adjusted`, under `adjust_surface`) and the RGBA filter helper (`adjust_cmds::process_surface`) each had the same loop. It mixed the edited pixels back over the original by selection coverage. They now share `pixels::mix_through_selection`.
- The shared helper reads the selection's coverage **one row at a time** with `Surface::sample_row_strided`: one tile lookup per tile per row, into a buffer the width of one row. Before, every pixel called `sample_channel`, which costs a `BTreeMap` lookup per pixel.

Files: `crates/engine/src/pixels.rs`, `adjust_cmds.rs`, `pixels_tests.rs`.

## Why

Most destructive adjustments through a selection take this path: Image › Adjustments on a layer, layer mask or channel (Desaturate and Auto Tone/Contrast/Color included), plus Shadows/Highlights, Replace Color and Match Color. Equalize is the exception: it has its own loop in `extra_cmds::map_pixels`, which this PR leaves alone. The mix runs once per pixel of the layer's content bounds, whether or not the pixel is selected.

## Measurements

`image.adjustments.invert` on a 4000×3000 RGBA8 layer through a selection covering 3600×2600 px at 50%: 7 timed calls per run after 2 warm-up calls, 5 runs. Release build, 4-core container, glibc's `MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_` pinned. The "after" build also carried the move-layers PR of this set, which doesn't touch this path.
- Median per run: 258–310 ms before, 230–263 ms after.
- Median of the 5 runs: **286 → 248 ms**.

Values are unchanged. `sample_row_strided` reads the same samples as `sample_channel`, including the default pixel for untouched tiles.

title: SVG: a group clipped by one path opens as editable shapes with a vector mask (#4266)
author: itsF4LCON
body:
Fixes #4266.

TLDR:

Opening PhotoCraft's own icon (`assets/app-icon/photocraft.svg`) warned "SVG: a group with a clip-path was rasterised, so it is not editable as shapes": the whole drawing sits in a group clipped to a rounded square, and any clipped group became one pixel layer.

Now, when the clip-path is a single visible path with no clip of its own (the common case: a rectangle, rounded or not, a circle, one outline), the group stays a group of editable shapes and the clip becomes its **vector mask**, which is how Photoshop clips layers with a path. The mask is placed as resvg draws the clip: the group's transform, then the clip-path's, with the clip rule as its fill rule. A lone child takes the mask itself, unless it already has one. Clips of several shapes, nested clip-paths, masks and filters are still rasterised with the warning, as before.

Changes:

- `io/src/svg.rs`: `clip_mask` turns a one-path clip-path into a `VectorMask`; groups with one are kept (never flattened into their parent) and carry it.

Tests:

- `svg::tests::a_single_path_clip_becomes_the_groups_vector_mask`:
  - a translated group clipped by a rounded rect opens as a group of two shape layers with the clip as its vector mask, in the group's space, and the composite matches resvg's render of the SVG except for edge anti-aliasing
  - PhotoCraft's icon opens without the clip-path warning, with a vector mask
  - a clip of two shapes is still rasterised, with the warning
- `tests/svg.rs` `clip_paths_masks_filters_patterns_and_images_are_rasterised` now clips with two shapes, so it still covers a rasterised clip.

title: Compose: key the vector-mask cache by content, not a temporary's address (#4426)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #4426

## Root cause
`RenderVectorMasks::values` cached compiled vector masks keyed by `ptr::from_ref(mask) as usize`. `hiding_mask` and `effects_source` (advanced.rs) feed it temporary clones; the clone is dropped, the next clone reuses the address, and the map never evicts. A later, different mask therefore got an earlier layer's compiled mask (and entries accumulated).

## Fix
The cache is now keyed by mask content (`VectorMask: PartialEq`): a small `Vec<(VectorMask, slot)>` searched linearly. Distinct masks never collide, identical masks still share one compiled instance across tiles, and the `OnceLock` slot semantics (compile outside Rayon) are unchanged.

## Repro
12x8 RGB doc, white Background, layers A (blue) and B (green) full canvas, each with an Inside stroke and `vector_mask_hides_effects = true`; A's vector mask covers x<6, B's x>=6. Before: x=2 green, x=9 white (render and render_tiled). After: x=2 blue, x=9 green.

## Tests
`advanced_tests::vector_mask_cache_does_not_mix_up_layers` (U8/U16/F32, checks both `render` and `render_tiled(..,3)`). Verified it fails without the fix (x=2 got green) and passes with it.

## Commands
- `cargo test -j 8 -p photocraft-compose --lib` (238 passed)
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-compose --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt -p photocraft-compose -- --check`

title: Compose: no overflow or unbounded allocation on hostile coordinates (#4427)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #4427

## Root cause and fix
- `masks.rs` build_mask: `floor() as i32 - 2` / `ceil() as i32 + 2` overflowed once path points saturate the cast; now `saturating_sub/add`.
- `effects.rs` Map::shifted: the layer-style distance was never clamped, so `x - fx as i64` overflowed; the shift is now clamped to +-1e9 (non-finite reads as 0).
- `pattern.rs` Tile::sample: `x0 + dx` at i64::MAX; now `saturating_add`.
- `proxy.rs` downsample: `x * k` products now saturate, and the row copy uses `get` so saturated edges cannot index out of range.
- `lib.rs` render_tiled_with: width compared as `i64` (a u32 width >= 2^31 wrapped negative as i32 and took the single-tile path), and rects over the new documented cap `MAX_RENDER_PIXELS` (2^30 px, a 16 GiB buffer) return an empty buffer instead of allocating. The cap is in the render entry only; signatures are unchanged.
- `adjust.rs` lut3d_sample (pub): returns the colour unchanged for n < 2 or a table shorter than n^3*3 (it also panicked on short tables).

## Tests
One regression test per group (masks, effects, pattern, lut3d, render cap). The first four were run with the fix reverted and panic with "attempt to subtract/add with overflow". The render-cap test was not run unfixed (it would try a ~64 GB allocation).

title: Text: binary-search the run lookup and probe smcp once per layout (#4430)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #4430

## Root cause
In `crates/text/src/layout.rs`:
- `style_at` was a linear `rposition` over the run start offsets and is called per character, so layout was O(chars x runs).
- `small_caps` was rebuilt for every paragraph and called `selected_face_has_feature` (family lookup, font load, GSUB parse) for every style, even styles whose `caps` is not `SmallCaps`: O(paragraphs x runs) font probes.

## What changed
- `run_index_at`: `partition_point` on the (non-decreasing) run starts. Same result as the old `rposition` for every input, including empty runs, equal starts and offsets past the end. Per lookup this is O(log runs) instead of O(runs).
- `small_caps` is computed once per layout, and only styles with `Caps::SmallCaps` probe the font; the others are `SmallCapsMode::None`, which is what `small_caps_mode` returned for them anyway. Font probes drop from paragraphs x runs to at most one per small-caps run.

Not touched (follow-ups): `psd.rs` `para_of`, `psd_styles.rs` `run_at`, the per-tab tail rescan, `fonts.rs`.

## Tests
- `run_lookup_matches_the_linear_reference`: compares the new lookup with the old linear implementation over many pseudo-random run layouts (empty runs, equal adjacent starts, offsets past the end, empty list).
- `small_caps_probe_runs_once_per_small_caps_style`: counts smcp probes (test-only counter, no timing). A layer with 300 paragraphs and 600 one-byte runs does 0 probes with no small-caps style and exactly one per small-caps style otherwise. Checked that it fails with the gate removed (600 probes instead of 0). The lookup equivalence test cannot fail against the old code by construction (same results); it guards the new implementation.

- `cargo test -j 8 -p photocraft-io --lib -- text`

title: Text: non-finite numbers and negative indices from PSD files are sanitized (#4429)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #4429

None of these panic, but corrupt or hostile PSD data silently corrupted text.

## Root causes and fixes (crates/text)
- **Non-finite numbers (B3).** EngineData parsed `inf`, `nan` and `1e999` as reals, and `char_style`/`para_style`, the FillColor reader and the warp reader passed them into size, leading, tracking, scales, indents, spacing, colour and warp, so text vanished. `Value::as_f64` and `dnum` now reject non-finite values, and a new `numk` helper also drops values that overflow f32 after scaling. A dropped field takes its default. A FillColor with any non-finite entry becomes black. Chosen range: finite only, no clamps, since I have no documented Photoshop limit to cite. Finite in-range values behave as before.
- **dpi (B8).** `dpi > 0.0` let `inf` through, so `size_pt / k` was inf and `format_real` saved `0.0`. All five sites (layout, lib, psd x2, psd_styles) now require `dpi.is_finite()`.
- **Negative indices (B7).** `psd_styles.rs` used `as usize` on `Parent`, `TheNormal*Sheet` and `DefaultStyleSheet`, so a negative index became huge and suppressed the `Name` fallback. They now use `usize::try_from`, like psd.rs.
- **sri (B9).** `u8::from_str_radix` accepts a leading `+`, so `sri` now requires 64 ASCII hex digits.
- **raster (B10).** `Coverage::line` now re-checks finiteness after the f64 to f32 cast. No test, because it is unreachable today (defensive).

## Tests
`psd::nonfinite_tests` (2), `psd_styles::index_tests` (1), `served::tests::sri_rejects_non_hex_digits`. The dpi, negative Parent and sri tests were verified to fail with the fix reverted. The non-finite style test is covered by the `numk` filter and the FillColor check, so it also passes with only the `as_f64` change reverted.

title: Compose: build effect-map layer identity once per render, not per tile (#4437)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #4437

## What work is no longer done

`effect_maps` (`crates/compose/src/lib.rs`) rebuilt a layer's cache-key identity (`layer_identity`: `format!("{:?}")` of the effects block and vector mask, a walk over every tile of the layer's pixels and mask, and the same for every child of a group) on every call. That is once per render tile per effect layer, plus once in `prepare_effects`. The identity depends only on the layer, so it is now computed once per layer per render and memoised in the render's `Ctx` (`LayerKeys`).

Why this is safe (output unchanged): the memo applies only to layers whose address is in the document tree being rendered. `Ctx` borrows the document for the render, so no other object can live at such an address; this is the aliasing problem #4426 hit with temporary clones. Temporaries (`advanced::effects_source` copies for "mask hides effects") are never in the tree and keep computing the identity per call. The identity function itself is unchanged; only the cache key's hash input is now "hash of the identity" instead of the identity fed directly, which is an internal value and does not affect any pixel.

## Skipped, and why

- O2 `masks.rs` `combined_mask` key and O3 `shape_split.rs` `split` key: #2028 (both files), #3446 and #3409 (`shape_split.rs`, which rewrites the key) change these functions.
- O7 outside-stroke `base.clone()` / `ones` / `share` in `effects.rs`: #3650 rewrites the stroke loop; #4231, #4040, #3193 touch the same function.
- `apply_blend_if` / `composite_clipped_individually` repeating `render_content`: would need a signature change threaded through code #4040 and #3193 edit, and the inputs are only the same by construction, not provably in every path.

author: sssehnsuchttt
body: On Linux the title bar drew one fixed set of minimize / maximize / close buttons, so PhotoCraft looked out of place next to native windows: wrong side, buttons the user had turned off, and glyphs that ignored the icon theme. The layout now comes from the desktop: GNOME `button-layout` through the settings portal (live), KDE `kdeglobals` `ButtonsOnLeft`/`ButtonsOnRight`, otherwise `gtk-3.0/settings.ini`. Buttons the layout omits are hidden, and a left-side layout puts them before the brand mark. The style family (GNOME round, Breeze chevrons, Windows-like) follows the desktop, then the GTK theme. Glyphs are the icon theme's `window-*-symbolic.svg`, the ones GTK apps use, found by the freedesktop lookup (`Inherits`, then `hicolor`, best size first). Directories a theme forgets to list in `index.theme` (custom themes often add `symbolic/ui` this way) are still searched, lazily, before the parent theme. title: Frame tool: take type, shape and smart object layers into the frame (#4435)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #4435.

Drawing a frame with the Frame tool (K) over a selected type layer created an empty frame group, and the type layer stayed outside it. Pixel layers worked.

**Cause:** two checks accepted only pixel layers:
- `content_layer()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/frame_tool.rs`, which picks the selected layer under the drawn frame, returned `None` for anything that was not `LayerContent::Raster`, so the tool sent `layer.new.frame` with no layer.
- `new_frame` in `crates/engine/src/frame_cmds.rs` refused any non-raster `layer` with "only a pixel layer (not the Background) can go in a frame".

**Fix:** both checks now also accept type, shape and smart object layers. These are the layer kinds that `Layer::surface()` already renders (from their cache), so the overlap test in the tool works for them too. The engine path is the same as before: insert the group, move the layer into it, add the clip mask, all in one undo step. The Background, groups, adjustment and fill layers are still refused, and the engine error text and the `layer.new.frame` help text name the accepted kinds.

**Test:** `new_frame_takes_a_type_layer` makes a type layer, frames it with `layer.new.frame`, checks that the frame group holds it, and checks that one undo gives the layer back. Without the fix the command returns the "only a pixel layer" error and the test fails.

title: Paths: curves stay smooth when zoomed in (#4084)
author: dhiorns15
body:
## Problem

Zoomed in, a Pen path's curve is drawn as a chain of straight lines with visible corners (#4084). The path overlays sampled every Bézier segment at a fixed 16 points (24 for the Curvature Pen's preview), however large the curve is on screen.

## Fix

`crates/ui-egui/src/vector_ui.rs`: a new `curve_points` maps a segment's four points to the screen (the view transform is affine, so the curve maps exactly), then picks the number of chords from how much the curve bends *on screen*. The chord error stays within 0.3 px, using the same bound as `photocraft-vector`'s flattening (`max|B''| / 8n²`), capped at 1024 chords per segment. A straight segment, with its handles retracted or along the line, is a single chord, so typical paths draw fewer points than before.

Used everywhere the overlays drew curves:
- `path_lines`: work path, shape and vector-mask outlines, Direct Selection, the shape-drawing preview, Paths panel thumbnails
- the Pen's path in progress
- the Curvature Pen's next-segment preview

Before / after at 1200%, one curved segment drawn with the Pen:

## Tests

title: Select Subject: keep subject parts coloured like the backdrop, leave enclosed gaps open
author: diegochagas
body:
## What changed

Select Subject on a person against a plain wall dropped clothes that are close in colour to the wall, and bridged the gap between an arm and the torso (the reports from @HassanJb961, @LimitlessRam and @switch87 on #2788). Both come from the same place in `crates/algo/src/segment/subject.rs`: the saliency pass labels low-contrast parts of the subject as background, the background colour model then learns them and explains them away, and the final blind hole fill closes every enclosed gap up to 5 % of the mask.

- **A second GrabCut pass whose background model only knows the backdrop.** A colour model is fitted to the image frame (minus a margin around the salient blob, in case the subject runs out of the picture). Every pixel that model explains becomes probable background; the blob and whatever the backdrop cannot account for (a cream shirt on a near-white wall) start as probable foreground, so the cut keeps them. Only components touching the first pass's result survive, so the pass cannot pull in unrelated objects.
- **Hole filling that consults the colour models** (`segment::fill_holes_by_model`). Specks up to 0.2 % of the mask always fill; larger holes up to 5 % fill only when their pixels fit the foreground model better than the background's, so a patch of wall enclosed by the subject stays open.
- Module docs updated with the two new steps.

No UI, command or i18n changes; the engine's cached repeat path (P29) is untouched.

title: Linux window: low-latency presentation and no launch busy cursor
author: astigmata
body:
## Summary

Two Linux desktop fixes, one commit each.

**Low-latency window presentation** (b290483)
- Menus lagged the pointer: egui's default surface config queues two frames under FIFO vsync, and a compositing WM adds another.
- The window now queues one frame and uses mailbox where the surface supports it, else vsync. Mailbox frames are capped at 240 fps so continuous repaints don't spin.
- `PHOTOCRAFT_PRESENT_MODE` / `PHOTOCRAFT_FRAME_LATENCY` override it. Help › System Info shows the presentation mode.

**Launch busy cursor** (46d2f02)
- Launched from the GNOME/X11 menu, the "starting" cursor kept spinning ~15 s after the window was up. eframe never hands winit the `DESKTOP_STARTUP_ID`, so nobody sent the startup-notification `remove` message.

title: Select › Color Range: Skin Tones
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #4455.

## What

`select.colorRange` gets the **Skin Tones** preset from Photoshop's Select menu: `{"select": "skinTones"}`. The Color Range dialog lists it between Shadows and Out Of Gamut, with Fuzziness enabled and no eyedroppers or clusters, as in Photoshop.

The use case is recolouring a garment on a model photo: select the garment, subtract Skin Tones, add a fill layer. Here, a rectangle over the tank top minus `reds` (left, the only option until now) and minus `skinTones` (right), then a navy fill layer:

![Subtract Reds vs. subtract Skin Tones](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/switch87/photocraft/issue-assets/issue-assets/4455-subtract-skin-tones.png)

`reds` is weighted by chroma, so the arms stay mostly selected. Skin Tones takes the arms, the neck and the shadows along the armholes out, and the cream shirt stays selected.

## How

- **`photocraft_algo::selection::skin_tones(px, fuzziness)`**: a soft skin model in the YCbCr chroma plane (Rec. 601). It is based on the skin region of Chai & Ngan (1999, Cb ≈ 77..127, Cr ≈ 133..173). The ellipse lies along the run from pale skin (higher Cb, lower Cr) to saturated skin (lower Cb, higher Cr). Inside the ellipse coverage is 1. Outside, it falls off linearly over Fuzziness (100 = one ellipse radius). A luminance gate fades out near-black and near-white pixels, whose chroma is noise. Pale neutrals such as cream and beige sit just off the pale end, so they stay out.
- **Engine:** the `skinTones` arm in `select.colorRange`, through the same `sample_pixels`, Invert, mode and scoping as the hue families. The spec and the "unknown select" message list it.
- **Detect Faces:** PhotoCraft has no face detector yet (that would come with the local models of #2788 / #4098). So `detectFaces: true` is refused with a message that says so, instead of being silently ignored. A follow-up can add it on top.
- **Dialog:** the Skin Tones entry. The comment that said it was left out "because the engine has no skin-tone model" is …

title: Replace Color: Localized Color Clusters (points, localized, range)
author: switch87
body:
Refs #4457 (engine part; the dialog part follows once #4247 is in).

## What

`image.adjustments.replaceColor` gets Photoshop's **Localized Color Clusters**, with the same parameters as `select.colorRange`:

- `points`: `[[x, y], …]`, where the colour was picked (document pixels)
- `localized`: `bool = false`
- `range`: `0..100 = 100`, as a % of the canvas's longer side

With clusters on, the colour only matches near the points. The same colour elsewhere in the photo is left alone, typically a near-white background next to a cream garment. Without `localized` nothing changes, so automation that sends only `color` behaves as before.

Here, the same Replace Color (`#E7E1CA`, Fuzziness 150, Hue +180, Saturation +80) on a product photo. On the left is the current behaviour: the background and the skin shift too. On the right, it is localized on three points on the shirt with Range 40:

![Replace Color without and with Localized Color Clusters](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/switch87/photocraft/issue-assets/issue-assets/4457-replace-color-localized.png)

Measured on the same image, the number of changed pixels:

| | background strip (150×600 px) | shirt patch (200×300 px) |
|---|---|---|
| plain | 1,636 | 9,260 |
| localized | **0** | 7,004 |

As in Color Range, a sample's match fades linearly with distance and reaches 0 at Range. So parts of the garment far from every point change less, and more points or a larger Range cover them.

## How

- `tone::replace_color_masked`: the hue, saturation and lightness shift split out of `replace_color`, applied through any coverage mask. `replace_color` is unchanged and calls it.
- Engine: with `localized`, the mask comes from `selection::color_range_samples` (the Color Range clusters code). The points are moved into the coordinates of the processed area, so an active selection that doesn't start at the origin keeps the samples where they were picked. `localized` without `points`, and malformed points, are refused with a message.…

title: Puppet Warp: ⌘Z / ⌘⇧Z undo and redo pin edits (#4440)
author: itsF4LCON
body:
Fixes #4440.

TLDR:

While Puppet Warp was open, Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z did nothing: the warp mode takes the keyboard (↩ commits, Esc cancels) and swallowed the rest, and pin edits weren't recorded anywhere. Now the session keeps its own undo stack, as Liquify's does and as in Photoshop:

- placing a pin, removing one (⌥-click), dragging one, and the options bar's pin edits (depth, rotation, Remove All Pins) are a step each; a click that moves nothing isn't
- ⌘Z undoes the last one, ⌘⇧Z redoes it; a new edit after an undo drops what was undone
- the document's History is untouched until Commit, which is still one step
- the control channel gets the same: `edit.puppetWarp {"ui": {"undo": true}}` / `{"redo": true}`

Changes:

- `ui-egui/src/puppet_ui.rs`: `PuppetSession` keeps the pins before each edit (`undo`, `redo`), recorded on pointer edits and in the options bar; `undo()` / `redo()` and the control params.
- `ui-egui/src/distort_ui.rs`: `keys` sends ⌘Z / ⌘⇧Z to the open Puppet Warp, next to ↩ and Esc.

Tests:

- `puppet_ui::tests::pin_edits_undo_and_redo_inside_the_session`: adds, drags, a no-op click and a removal, then ⌘Z twice through the keyboard handling (the removal, then the drag, not the click), ⌘⇧Z, undo/redo through the control channel, a new edit clearing redo, and undo stopping at no pins with the document's History unchanged.
- The existing Puppet Warp and distort tests pass.

## Checks

- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib puppet_ui`, `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib distort`
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`

title: Fix Intel Mac crash: probe Metal shader language version support
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes crashes on Intel Macs where all ArtCraft apps fail to launch with `Metal: error: invalid value 'metal3.2' in '-std=metal3.2'`.

The wgpu Metal backend was choosing MSL version purely from OS version, but legacy Intel GPUs have older Metal compilers that reject newer MSL versions.

## Solution

Vendors wgpu-hal 30.0.1 with the patch from gfx-rs/wgpu#10592:
- Probes the Metal compiler at adapter creation by compiling a test kernel
- Steps down from OS-selected version until compiler accepts it
- Modern Macs: tries Metal 3.2 → succeeds immediately
- Legacy Intel Macs: tries 3.2 → 3.1 → ... → 2.4/2.3 until one works

## Issues Fixed

Fixes storytold/photocraft#1859
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2126  
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2190

## Testing

- ✅ Compiles on macOS
- ✅ Passes clippy
- ⚠️ Untested on real Intel Mac hardware (awaiting community testing)

## Notes

The vendored wgpu-hal will be removed once upstream releases the fix and ArtCraft can bump to that version.

---

title: TIFF: save uncompressed by default, like Photoshop
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #4484.

Every TIFF PhotoCraft saved used Adobe Deflate (Compression 8) with the horizontal predictor, because that was the `EncodeOptions` default and nothing in the app overrides it. Neither is baseline TIFF 6.0, so tools with a minimal reader (embroidery software like Melco Design Shop, plotters, older Windows apps) refuse the file, while a re-save from PSP, which writes it uncompressed and much larger, opens fine. This makes no compression the default, the same as Photoshop's TIFF Options. LZW, Deflate and PackBits are still available through `tiff_compression`. Uncompressed files are bigger. If you'd rather default to LZW (smaller, and still read almost everywhere), I'm happy to switch.

Validation:
- `default_tiff_is_baseline` in `crates/codecs/tests/tiff_regressions.rs` checks that a default RGB/RGBA 8-bit save has Compression 1, no predictor, strips, chunky planar config and ExtraSamples=2 for alpha, and that it reads back identically. It fails on main (`Compression: left Some(8), right Some(1)`) and passes here.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-codecs --test tiff_regressions --test tiff_photoshop`, `cargo test -p photocraft-io --test tiff_layers`
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-codecs --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(compose): redraw shapes crossing canvas bounds and include vector bounds in damage (#3946)
author: seotarek
body:
Fixes #3946.

### Problem
When dragging or translating a shape layer across canvas boundaries or within the canvas:
1. `crates/compose/src/lib.rs` lacked `shape_bounds` calculation in `layer_bounds` for `LayerContent::Shape`, causing `MovePreview` damage calculation to underestimate vector bounds when transformed or stroked.
2. `crates/engine/src/layer_multi_cmds.rs` in `shift_shown` fast-translated cached shape surfaces even when crossing boundaries or with stroke padding, leaving visual trails/artifacts on canvas edges.

### Solution
1. In `crates/compose/src/lib.rs`: Added unclipped `shape_bounds` using vector path bounds and stroke width, feeding accurate damage rectangles to `MovePreview`.
2. In `crates/engine/src/layer_multi_cmds.rs`: Enhanced `shift_shown` to ensure shapes only use fast cached translation when strictly `was_inside && stays_inside` within canvas bounds (including `f64` stroke padding), falling back to full redraw when crossing edges.
