title: fix(#4484): Unable to use .tiff files produced by photocraft.
author: roaldosulejmani
body:
Closes #4484

## What changed

#### What changed

Issue #4484: `.tif` files written by PhotoCraft were refused by Melco Design Shop. The only workaround the reporter had was to re-save through Photoshop, which produced a much larger (uncompressed) file that Melco accepted. Inspecting our encoded output with `tiffdump`/`tiffinfo` showed two directory fields that a limited reader can choke on. Both are fixed in the TIFF writer, which is the only place the file format is produced.

- **`crates/codecs/src/options.rs`** — the default TIFF compression is now **LZW** instead of **Deflate**. ZIP/Deflate is TIFF compression tag 8, an Adobe extension, not part of TIFF 6.0; LZW (tag 5) is a scheme of the format proper, so any reader that accepts a TIFF at all accepts it. `None`, `Deflate` and `PackBits` remain available programmatically. The variant doc records why.
- **`crates/codecs/src/codecs/tiff.rs`** — new `rows_per_strip(img, compression)` helper, threaded through `write_one`, `write_image` and `encode`. The `tiff` crate sizes a strip for ~1 MB of samples but never clamps the row count to the image, so a 37×23 image was written with `RowsPerStrip` 9010 while `ImageLength` was 23. A reader that trusts `RowsPerStrip` over `StripByteCounts` then reads past the strip. We now write `min(rows, height)` (PackBits stays one row per strip, since it must not compress across a row boundary). Both the classic and BigTIFF paths use it.
- **`crates/codecs/tests/tiff_interop.rs`** (new) — regression tests for both fixes, plus a `tiff_tag_u64` tag reader added to `crates/codecs/tests/common/mod.rs`.
- **`docs/file-format-parity.md`** — the TIFF row now notes the baseline-LZW default and the clamped `RowsPerStrip`.

Not done deliberately: no `Orientation` or `PlanarConfiguration` tag was added (both are optional and default to 1, the value we already imply), and the stray `Predictor` tag libtiff warns about under `None`/`PackBits` was left alone. Neither is believed to be the failure an…

title: Symmetry: Transform Symmetry gets commit/cancel buttons and its own cursors (#4495)
author: dhiorns15
body:
## Problem

After Brush/Pencil options bar › Symmetry › **Transform Symmetry** (#4495):
- The transform could only be applied with Enter or dropped with Esc. Nothing on screen said so, and a tablet or touch user may have no keyboard at hand.
- The canvas kept the round brush cursor, although a press there moves or rotates the symmetry and never paints.

## Fix

title: Speed up Blur/Sharpen convolution while preserving exact output
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Large, soft Blur-tool strokes repeatedly clamp, copy and premultiply the same source pixels for every horizontal Gaussian tap. Prepare one padded, premultiplied row instead, then accumulate horizontal and vertical weights over contiguous samples. Each output sample retains the original arithmetic order and low-alpha hidden-color fallback. Brush spacing, hardness, strength and the blur approximation are unchanged.

Related to #3952. This improves the shared Blur/Sharpen kernel; the timings below measure Blur paint commands, not canvas repaint or UI frame rate. The issue remains open for interactive follow-up.

Added `cargo run --release -p photocraft-engine --example bench_blur_tool`: a 6,000 × 4,000 striped RGB document, 1,000-pixel horizontal stroke, hardness 20%, strength 50%, spacing 25%. title: Face detection: libfacedetection's CNN in pure Rust, and image.detectFaces
author: switch87
body:
Step 1 of 3 for #3603 (Face-Aware Liquify), and the base for Detect Faces in Select › Color Range › Skin Tones (#4455 / #4473). This PR is complete on its own.

## What

- **`photocraft_algo::faces::detect(px, w, h, min_score)`**: the faces in an RGBA image, each with a score, a box and five landmarks (eyes, nose tip, mouth corners).
- **`image.detectFaces {minScore = 0.5, sampleAllLayers = true}`**: the same for the document (composite or active layer), in document pixels, as `{"faces": [{"score", "rect": [x, y, w, h], "landmarks": {"rightEye", "leftEye", "nose", "mouthRight", "mouthLeft"}}]}`. It is read-only (`journal: false`, no history step) and has no menu entry.

Four public-domain NASA portraits (Wikimedia Commons) plus the fourth rotated 20°, as one image through `photocraft-cli run … --cmd image.detectFaces`. The boxes, scores and landmarks are drawn from the command's output:

![Detected faces and landmarks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/switch87/photocraft/issue-assets/issue-assets/3603-face-detection.png)

## How

`faces.rs` is a port of **[libfacedetection](https://github.com/ShiqiYu/libfacedetection)** (Shiqi Yu, **BSD-3-Clause**), the YuNet design:
- the input is 3×3 stride-2 patches (so the first convolution is pointwise), then a backbone of 1×1 pointwise and 3×3 depthwise convolutions with 2×2 max pooling;
- a feature pyramid at strides 8, 16 and 32 (nearest ×2 upsampling plus add);
- per-cell heads for the class, objectness, box and landmarks, decoded against the cell grid;
- score √(cls · obj), then non-maximum suppression (IoU 0.45), as in the library.

There is **no runtime dependency**. It is plain Rust using `par::chunks_mut` (rayon natively, sequential on wasm), so it also works offline and in the web build. The weights are the library's, converted from `facedetectcnn-data.cpp` to half precision: **107 KB** in `crates/algo/data/libfacedetection.bin`, with a small header per layer and parsed defensively (damaged data gives `None`, never a…

title: Record actions in a document-independent form (#219) [depends on #4496]
author: FabioLissi
body:
**Depends on #4496** (stacked; rebased onto `main` after #4434, #4456, #4465, #4470 and #4698 merged). A fork can't base a PR on another fork branch, so this targets `main` and shows #4496's commit too until it merges; please review that first, then only the last commit here ([compare](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/compare/74ad8ee5..a8c8036f)). I'll rebase once it is in.

Closes the first item of G11 / AUTO-219-1 in #219: a recorded action now means the same thing on another document.

## Problem

Journal entries are what Actions record, and the UI names the layer it clicked by id (`"layer": 7`). Ids are per document, so a step recorded that way replays only on the document the recording came from, and typing records one `type.edit` per keystroke with character offsets into the old text.

## What

New `crates/engine/src/actions_record.rs`, applied by the dispatcher before an entry is journaled (inline commands and background jobs alike):

- A `layer` id that was the active (and only selected) layer is dropped: the step acts on the active layer when played, as Photoshop's "current layer" does. With several layers selected it stays explicit, because without it a layer command acts on the whole selection.
- Any other id becomes the layer's name when the name is unique in the document; `layer.select` always records the name (Photoshop's "Select layer 'Name'"). An ambiguous name keeps the id, which still replays on the recording document.
- Type tool keystrokes (`type.edit` with `replace` and the editing session's `coalesce` key) fold into the entry before them: the `type.create` that made the layer gets the final text, and keystrokes in an existing layer become one `type.edit` with the whole text, as Photoshop records "Make text layer" / "Set current text layer". The session remembers which text layer the last entry typed into, because the Type tool selects a clicked layer without a command, so keystrokes into another layer start their own step.

title: macOS: open SVG files dropped on the Dock icon or opened from Finder
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #4504: this covers dragging an .svg onto the Dock icon (and Finder's Open With). Pasting vectors from the clipboard isn't in here.

PhotoCraft already handles Finder/Dock opens through the `kAEOpenDocuments` path in `apple_events.rs`, and SVG already opens through that same `open_paths` route, but macOS never offered SVG files to the app because the bundle didn't list `public.svg-image` in `CFBundleDocumentTypes`. This adds it to the existing "Image" group with `Alternate` rank, the same as PNG/JPEG, so PhotoCraft shows up for SVGs without trying to become their default handler. `.svgz` has no system UTI, so it isn't covered here; happy to add an imported type for it if you want.

For the paste half, the clipboard service today only reads images (`clipboard_get_image`), so pasting vectors needs a text/SVG flavor read from the clipboard plus a decision on what a paste becomes (smart object like File › Place, or shape layers/paths). I'd rather leave that for a follow-up once that choice is made.

title: Document tabs: keep whole names, hide what doesn't fit, list every document in the » menu
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #4487.

Both document tab strips (Pro and Studio) passed a fixed 72 pt minimum to `tab_strip::fit`, so with many documents open every tab was squeezed and elided down to `ch1-p…` before any of them moved into the » menu. title: Pen: Ctrl/Cmd edits the path being drawn in place (#4022)
author: bazmarth
body:
Part of #4022 (the "Ctrl point selection doesn't work consistently" part) and #214.

## What
As in Photoshop, while a Pen or Curvature Pen path is being drawn:
- **Ctrl/Cmd-drag** an anchor, a shown handle or a segment of that path edits it in place (Ctrl-click an anchor selects it and shows its handles; smooth handles stay collinear, Alt breaks them, as with Direct Selection).
- Release Ctrl/Cmd and the next click carries on from the path's last anchor.
- **Ctrl/Cmd-press anywhere else** still ends the path (unchanged).

Before, any Ctrl/Cmd-press committed the path first, so you could not fix a point without ending the path.

## How
- `direct_select::PathRef::Pen`: the path in progress (`ui.pen`, via `vector_ui::pen_path`) is the first Direct Selection candidate while the Pen isn't mid-drag.
- `direct_select::pointer` only commits the Pen path when the press misses it (`hits_pen`); `release` applies a Pen-target edit with the same `photocraft_vector::edit` functions as the preview, then `vector_ui::pen_replace` writes it back (the Curvature Pen recomputes its handles).
- No command and no history step: the path isn't in the document until it's finished, exactly as before. The finished path is still one History step.
- `pen_commit` / `pen_undo_last_point` drop or trim a Direct Selection on the Pen path; the anchor tools edit a `PathRef::Pen` hit in memory instead of sending a command.
- The Pen overlay steps aside while Ctrl-dragging, so Direct Selection's preview is the only path drawn.

## Tests (`direct_select_tests.rs`)
- `pen_with_command_ends_the_path_being_drawn_when_pressed_off_it` (replaces the old test, whose Ctrl-drag on the path being drawn now edits it)
- `pen_with_command_edits_the_path_being_drawn_in_place`
- `pen_with_command_turns_a_handle_of_the_path_being_drawn`
- `curvature_pen_with_command_moves_an_anchor_of_the_path_being_drawn`

title: Pen: Auto Add/Delete anchors on the active path (#4144)
author: bazmarth
body:
Closes #4144. Part of #214.

## What
Photoshop's Pen **Auto Add/Delete** option (options bar, on by default):
- Pen click on a **segment** of the active path → adds an anchor there (`path.addAnchor`).
- Pen click on an **anchor** of the active path → deletes it (`path.deleteAnchor`).
- One History step each, and no new Pen path is started.
- Falls through to the plain Pen when: the option is off, **Shift** is held (temporarily disables it, as in Photoshop), Alt (Convert Point) or Cmd/Ctrl (Direct Selection) is held, a path is being drawn, or the anchor is an **end point of an open subpath** (left to the Pen for continuing paths later).
- Feedback: hovering highlights the segment (with the anchor-to-be) or the anchor, and the cursor shows the + / − badge, exactly like the Add/Delete Anchor Point tools.

The "active path" is what the Pen shows: the targeted vector mask or the active shape layer's path, then the work path (`direct_select::active_paths`, split out of `candidates`).

## How
- `ToolOptions::pen_auto_add_delete` (`#[serde(default = "yes")]`), reset with the Pen (`tool_reset.rs`), checkbox in the Pen options bar; "Auto Add/Delete" added to all 19 catalogs with Photoshop's localized terms.
- `anchor_tools::pen_auto` decides; `anchor_tools::pointer` applies it on a Pen press through the same `apply` the anchor tools use; `draw_pen_hover` and `tool_feedback::badge` show it.

## Tests (`anchor_tools_tests.rs`)

title: feat(gpu): composite Blend If on the GPU (#4395)
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #4395.

A layer with Blending Options › Blend If made the GPU planner refuse the whole document, so every refresh of it ran the CPU compositor, for every edit to any layer. This composites Blend If on the GPU instead.

## Measured

Release build, `perf_scenarios --group layered --reps 10` on an RTX 4090 laptop (Windows, Vulkan). The Blend If rows use the #209 layered document with one lower panel given an Underlying Gray range (a local, uncommitted switch in the example, applied identically to both builds).

| Edit | `main` with Blend If | This PR with Blend If | This PR without Blend If |
|---|---|---|---|
| Change layer opacity | 140 ms | 6.2 ms | 3.8 ms |
| Toggle visibility | 106 ms | 5.6 ms | 3.8 ms |
| Move styled layer 10 px | 331 ms | 24.5 ms | 17.4 ms |
| Move tool drag frame, full-canvas layer | 762 ms | 131 ms | 130 ms |
| Same, with a drop shadow | 1,484 ms | 196 ms | 182 ms |
| Paste a 12 MP layer (repeat) | 819 ms | 66 ms | 55 ms |

## How

`compose::apply_blend_if` mixes the composite (backdrop with the layer drawn) back towards the backdrop by a per-pixel weight. The weight comes from the layer's own content with its masks ("This Layer", or the result for an adjustment layer) and the backdrop ("Underlying Layer"), through the Gray and R/G/B ranges. That is the existing `Lerp` mix with a computed weight:

- **Planner** (`plan.rs`): `restricted` keeps the backdrop, composites the layer as before, applies channel restrictions, then `blend_if` renders the layer's own content (`content`, masks included) and emits one `Lerp` pass with the new `F_BLEND_IF` flag. Base layers and clipped layers both go through it, as `composite_layer` and `composite_atop` do on the CPU. The ranges are packed exactly into the pass parameters (`blend_if_params`: two bytes per float).
- **Shader** (`compose.wgsl`): `blend_if_weight` mirrors `BlendRange::weight` and `compose::blend_if_weight`, and the mix is `apply_blend_if`'s premultiplied formula.
- Blend If only reads th…

title: Background Eraser: one pass clears the whole stroke
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Each dab of a Background Eraser stroke read its hotspot colour and its match colours from the working copy that earlier dabs had already erased, and a fully erased pixel also has its colour zeroed. With 25% spacing the next hotspot almost always lands on a pixel the previous dab cleared, so:

- Continuous sampling found a transparent hotspot and skipped the dab. Only dabs roughly a radius apart did anything, which leaves scalloped, unerased patches along the stroke edges.
- With Contiguous limits (the default) the fill started from that erased hotspot, saw no match and erased nothing, with Once sampling too.

The fix takes a copy of the pixels at the first dab and samples and matches against that pre-stroke copy. Erasing still writes to the working copy as before, and the contiguous fill now goes through pixels the stroke has already cleared.

Tested with a new unit test in `crates/paint/src/bg_erase.rs`: a hard 20 px brush across a single-colour 60x30 surface, Continuous and Once with Contiguous limits, and every pixel within radius - 1 of the line has to end up transparent. Before the fix it failed for both modes at (14, 6). The existing bg_erase tests and the engine eraser command tests still pass. Locally `cargo xtask ci` passed fmt, clippy, layers and wasm, and the workspace tests passed except `photocraft-automation --test mcp` `bridge_reports_unreachable_app`, which times out connecting to 127.0.0.1:1 in my WSL sandbox and doesn't touch this code. I have not tried it by hand in the app.

Fixes #1280

title: Codecs: PCX runs may cross plane boundaries within a scanline
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
PCX RLE runs may cross plane boundaries within a scanline. The ZSoft spec says there is a decoding break at the end of each scanline but not at the end of each plane, and its sample encoder compresses the whole scanline at once. The reader decoded each plane separately and rejected such runs with "RLE packet crosses a scanline or has zero length", so a valid 24-bit file like `C4 FF C2 00` (a 2x1 image) failed to open, and 16-colour four-plane files hit the same check.

`decode` now reads the whole scanline in one call. Runs that would cross the end of the scanline are still rejected.

Tested:

- New `decodes_rgb_runs_across_planes` (with a PNG round trip) and `decodes_four_plane_runs_across_planes` fail on main (`cd36d1ea`) and pass with the fix. The overshoot case in `rejects_truncated_and_overshooting_rle_without_panicking` now uses a seven-byte run against the six-byte scanline.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-codecs --test pcx`: 8 passed. `cargo xtask test-corpus` passes.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt and clippy pass. In the test step, `a_move_tool_click_selects_without_moving` and `auto_select_moves_the_layer_under_the_pointer` in `photocraft-ui-egui/tests/layout_perf.rs` fail on my machine, and fail the same way on unchanged main.

The first commit adds my contributor display name.

title: Filter › Liquify: Face-Aware Liquify (engine: faces and their sliders)
author: switch87
body:
Step 2 of 3 for #3603. **Stacked on #4513** (face detection): its commit `ce8d7547` is the first one here. Please review that PR first; this one's own change is the second commit. The dialog (step 3) follows.

## What

`filter.liquify` takes a new param `faces`. Each face is
`{"face": n?, "landmarks": [[x,y]×5]?, …sliders}`.
- `face` is the index of a face that `photocraft_algo::faces` detects on the target layer. It defaults to the face's place in the list.
- `landmarks` gives the geometry instead of detecting it: eyes, nose tip and mouth corners, image-left first, as `image.detectFaces` reports them.

The sliders are Photoshop's Face-Aware Liquify ones, each −100..100 with 0 as unchanged:

| group | sliders |
|---|---|
| Eyes | `eyeSize`, `eyeHeight`, `eyeWidth`, `eyeTilt` (a number for both eyes, or `[left, right]`), `eyeDistance` |
| Nose | `noseHeight`, `noseWidth` |
| Mouth | `smile`, `upperLip`, `lowerLip`, `mouthWidth`, `mouthHeight` |
| Face shape | `forehead`, `chinHeight`, `jawline`, `faceWidth` |

The faces are applied before the strokes, in the same single history step. Selections, smart objects (smart filter) and the freeze mask work as for strokes. The result has `faces`: the landmarks used, so the dialog or a script can record them. Unknown sliders, out-of-range values, bad landmarks and a face index that isn't there (`no face 0 (found 0)`) are refused.

Each slider at ±100 on a public-domain NASA portrait. The face is detected automatically: `--params '{"faces":[{"smile":100}]}'`.

![Face-Aware Liquify sliders](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/switch87/photocraft/issue-assets/issue-assets/3603-face-aware-liquify.png)

## How

- **`LiquifyField::apply_warp(&LocalWarp)`** (`liquify.rs`): a smooth local affine move about a centre, weighted by `falloff` (Density 50 %) down to zero at its radius, and held back by the freeze mask. It is composed with the field exactly as the brush tools are (`d'(p) = q + d(q) − p`, `q` the first-order inverse), so face w…

title: Interface: Animation Effects follows the system setting, or is on or off
author: JeremyYao
body:
## What

Preferences › Interface › **Animation effects** replaces the Enable animations checkbox (#3276) with three choices:

- **Use system setting** (the default): follow the operating system's own animation setting
- **On**
- **Off**

The preference is `interface.animationEffects` (`system`, `on`, `off`). A saved `enableAnimations: false` loads as `off`. `prefs.set interface.enableAnimations` is now an unknown preference.

## Why

With animations turned off in Windows, PhotoCraft still faded menus and dialogs in and glided when scrolling. Two causes:

1. PhotoCraft never read the system setting. Animations were on unless the user found the checkbox.
2. The checkbox only covered fades and `scroll_to`. egui spreads each mouse wheel notch over about 0.2 s (`egui/src/input_state/wheel_state.rs`, hard-coded), so scrolling kept gliding with the checkbox off.

## How

**System setting.** A new `Services::system_animations` returns `Some(false)` when the system has animations off and `None` when it cannot tell (animations then stay on). The desktop readers are in `apps/photocraft/src/animations.rs`, all through safe bindings:

| Platform | Source |
|---|---|
| Windows | `UISettings.AnimationsEnabled` (Settings › Accessibility › Visual effects › Animation effects) |
| macOS | `NSWorkspace.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion` |
| Linux | Settings portal: `reduced-motion`, then GNOME `enable-animations`, then KDE `AnimationDurationFactor`; followed live through `SettingChanged` |
| Linux without the portal, FreeBSD, other BSDs | KDE `kdeglobals`, `gsettings` `enable-animations` (GNOME, MATE), GTK `settings.ini`; read on a worker thread at start-up and when the window regains focus |
| Web | `prefers-reduced-motion` |

**Wheel glide.** `wheel_nav::unsmooth`, called from `PhotocraftApp::logic` while animations are off, replaces the frame's `smooth_scroll_delta` with what the frame's wheel events add up to, so a notch scrolls its whole distance on the frame it arrives. Trac…

title: Save for Web: no matte by default, as Photoshop's scripted export (#4115)
author: itsF4LCON
body:
Fixes #4115.

TLDR:

`file.export.saveForWebLegacy` defaulted to a white matte. title: Batch: subfolders, open documents, file naming, stop on error, error log, progress and cancel (#219)
author: FabioLissi
body:
Closes the last item of G11 in #219 besides scripting: AUTO-219-5, "Batch: subfolders, open documents, naming template, progress/cancel, error log, stop". Independent of the `.atn` stack (#4470, #4496, #4514); it only touches the same lines of `docs/gaps.md`, which I'll resolve on whichever lands second.

## What

`file.automate.batch` now covers Photoshop's Batch dialog:

- **Source**: a folder with Include All Subfolders (`includeSubfolders`; the output mirrors the folder tree, so same-named files in different subfolders don't collide), or the open documents (`"source": "open"`: the steps run on every open document as history steps; with an `output` folder a copy of each is saved there, else they just stay changed, Photoshop's Destination: None).

The default `{name}.{ext}` is the old naming. Path separators and `..` are refused.
- **Errors**: `stopOnError` stops at the first failing file and the result lists `stopped` and `skipped`; `errorLog` writes the failures to a text file (Log Errors To File).
- **Progress and cancel**: the command runs through `jobs::run`, so the UI's status bar shows "n of total: file" and Cancel stops after the current file (the files written so far stay, the log is still written).

The options live in a new engine module `batch` and are shared by Image Processor, the Lens Correction batch and the CLI (`batch --recursive --naming <template> --start-serial <n> --stop-on-error --error-log <file>`). The Batch dialog gained the fields, grouped as Photoshop's (Play, Source, Destination, Errors) through a small `__order` hint the generic form dialog now takes.

title: Free Transform: the live preview feathers a linked layer mask
author: marcoarnulfo
body:

On main a linked layer mask already moves with the pixels in the Free Transform preview (#242), so the plain case from the video works. title: Open Canon CR3 as labelled camera JPEG previews
author: optimalbytee
body:
Canon CR3 files were recognised but could not open their camera JPEG fallback reliably. Read bounded ISO BMFF JPEG sample tables or PRVW containers, validate references against media ranges, and use CMT1 orientation when the JPEG carries no orientation itself. Imports explicitly report an 8-bit camera preview rather than sensor RAW.

Split from #3238 and based directly on current main `992d945d`. This contains only the CR3 reader, preview/orientation wiring and generated regressions. It does not include or depend on #2371's RAF decoder. Native CRX decoding and burst frame selection remain unsupported.

Synthetic tests cover JPEG tracks/PRVW, orientation, box counts/depth, extended and zero-length boxes, truncated/invalid sample tables, out-of-media references and overflowing offsets. The I/O regression verifies rotated document dimensions, U8 depth and the explicit preview warning. The implementation follows public ISO BMFF and Laurent Clévy's format description, with no third-party decoder source copied.

Fresh validation: seven CR3 container regressions and the focused CR3 document-import test passed. Strict RAW/I/O all-target Clippy, changed-source formatting, whitespace and layering checks passed. Used 12 Cargo workers and the default existing target/cache. No application build, unrelated runtime suites or private images.

title: Check peak RAW development memory and bound AHD scratch
author: optimalbytee
body:
Default development rejected 100 MP images because it summed allocations from disjoint processing phases and reserved AHD scratch for every worker even when fewer bands could fit. Check peak live working buffers, free the padded plane before the encoding phase, and limit simultaneous AHD scratch bands only when required. Keep the existing 2 GiB development limit and normal load balancing when it fits.

Split from #3238 and based directly on current main `992d945d`. Includes overflow-safe public Sensor/CFA validation and regression tests for allocation boundaries, extreme origins, invalid sample layouts and identical AHD pixels across concurrency limits. It does not include or require #2371's RAF decoder; compressed-RAF decode remains that PR's responsibility. The source audit's compressed Fuji imports used that decoder in its separate validation stack.

The limit describes development working allocations, not total process memory or caller-owned sensor/document storage. Original source-machine 24 MP before/after release timings remained similar (one before run, median of three after runs): AHD DNG 214→216 ms, tiled lossless-JPEG DNG 220→211 ms, CR2 222→219 ms. These exclude file reads, fitting and document construction; no universal speedup is claimed. New local performance benchmarks were not run for this split.

title: Align tighter camera JPEGs for RAW colour fitting
author: optimalbytee
body:
A camera JPEG framed slightly tighter than the RAW could fail the existing lightness-correlation gate, leaving the neutral colour fallback. Align the reference proxy with a centred 90–100% framing search using training cells only. Require correlation at least 0.9 and an improvement of at least 0.05, then retain the existing held-out colour, matrix and picture-validation gates.

Split from #3238 and based directly on current main `992d945d`. Only the fitting proxy changes: the developed crop, output resolution and measured camera calibration remain unchanged. This does not include or depend on the unmerged RAF decoder #2371.

The generated tighter-framing regression verifies that a valid reference becomes usable. Existing unrelated/monochrome/wrong-shaped reference rejection tests remain in place. The original source audit's eight Z7 samples passed fitting after this alignment, with proxy-grid errors improving from 18.82–19.02 to 7.11–7.38. Those measurements estimate appearance against each camera's JPEG, not independent full-frame calibration accuracy; private samples and derived images are excluded.

Fresh validation on this standalone branch: all seven colour-fitting tests passed, including tighter framing, unchanged RAW crop, known matrix/curve recovery, orientation and unusable-reference rejection. Strict RAW all-target Clippy, formatting and whitespace passed; the unchanged dependency graph passes layering. Used 12 Cargo workers and the existing default target/cache.

title: Fill keys: Alt/Cmd+Backspace recolour the text of a type layer
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #4580.

The shape-layer half landed with #3925: the four colour fill keys now recolour a shape's fill. On a type layer they still fell through to `edit.fill` and were disabled ("active layer is a Type layer, not a pixel layer"). In Photoshop, Alt/Cmd+Backspace on a type layer changes the text colour and keeps it live type, so the fill keys now do the same through `type.setStyle` on the whole text: one undo step, every run takes the colour, no rasterizing. A layer with locked pixels is refused like the pixel fill. The Shift (Preserve Transparency) variants recolour the text too, as they already do for shapes. Fill from History stays disabled on type layers, since it can only fail there.

title: Color: Dot Gain 20%-compatible default working gray, as in Photoshop
author: MrCloudy2
body:
Photoshop's default working gray is **Dot Gain 20%**. PhotoCraft defaulted to sGray, so **Image › Mode › Grayscale** kept the sRGB value and came out up to 24 levels lighter than Photoshop.

## Evidence (Photoshop 27.11, default Color Settings, scripted)
RGB → Grayscale fits exactly as D50 luminance encoded with gamma 1.732, PhotoCraft's existing fitted curve for gray documents (`Transfer::for_document`):

| sRGB input | Photoshop | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| grey 64 | 46 | 64 | 46 |
| grey 128 | 105 | 128 | 105 |
| grey 192 | 177 | 192 | 177 |
| pure red | 107 | 130 | 107 |

## Change
- **New built-in profile** "Dot Gain 20%-compatible (gamma 1.732, Photocraft)", id `dot-gain-20-compat` (aliases `dotgain20`, `dotgain`). It is our own fitted curve, not Adobe's profile.
- **It's the default working gray** (`edit.colorSettings`) and the fallback for untagged gray documents (`cms::default_for(Gray)`). sGray and Gray Gamma 2.2 stay selectable.

**⚠ This changes a default.** Untagged gray documents now convert and display as Photoshop shows them, so midtones look lighter than under sGray. Documents with an embedded profile are unchanged, and file decoders keep their own handling. Re-rendering the gray corpus oracles (photoshop gray8/16, psd-tools grayscale) gives identical results on main and on this branch, since stored gray values don't depend on the working profile.

## Tests
- New: `grayscale_conversion_matches_photoshop`, using the measured values above.
- Four tests that assumed sGray now state their profile:

  - the identity fast-path and EXR round-trip tests tag their document sGray;

title: Gradient options bar: the swatch covers its checkerboard at half-pixel offsets
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #4577.

The line is the transparency checkerboard showing through, one pixel row at the bottom of the swatch. `paint_ramp` paints the checker with `rect_filled` and the gradient as a mesh on top. egui's tessellator snaps rects to whole pixels but leaves meshes where they were laid out. So when the options bar puts the swatch at a half-pixel offset, the checker grows to the next pixel row and the gradient stops half a pixel short of it. The fix snaps the swatch rect to pixels once, before painting both. That way they share the same edges. The Gradient Editor's ramp goes through the same function, so it gets the same fix.

title: Brushes: Photoshop's measured round tip (hardness falloff and reach)
author: MrCloudy2
body:
PhotoCraft's round brush tip falls off as `(1 − t²)⁴` from the hard core to **exactly 0 at the radius**. Photoshop's soft tips are much wider: a hardness-0 dab is a Gaussian (σ ≈ 0.47 R) that still paints 8 % at 1.05 R and holds more than twice the coverage. This PR replaces the tip with **Photoshop 27.11's measured shape**.

## Model (measured on single dabs: hardness 0–100 in steps of 10 at 40 px, checked at 100, 9, 7, 5, 3, 2, 1 px)
- A solid core of radius `r0·R`, then a Gaussian shoulder `exp(−((d − r0)/s)²)` of width `s·R`. Both come from an 11-entry table by hardness (`TIP_SHAPE` in `paint/src/lib.rs`).
- The edge stays at least ~1 px wide (0.3 R on small tips, never under ¼ px), as Photoshop's hard tips have a ~1 px soft edge.
- `exp` is computed as `(1 − u/64)⁶⁴` by squaring, so it's exact and the same on every platform, like the old curve.
- New `tip_reach()` sizes dab rectangles, reach checks, the small-tip path, the retouch footprint and the reference renderer. `half_coverage_radius()` (the Normal Brush Tip cursor ring) follows the new curve.

## Results against Photoshop (max levels / mean, whole images)
| case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| single 40 px dabs, hardness 0–70 | 70–156 / 12–15 | 2–6.5 / < 0.7 |
| single 100 px dabs, hardness 0–100 | 70–177 | 2–27 (hardness 100: 48 at the edge, mean 0.1) |
| strokes, soft and medium, 20–60 px | 133–178 / up to 17 | 4–26 / ≤ 0.5 |
| spacing sweeps (1–150 %) | 134–221 | 7–9 |
| soft Flow 50 % build-up | 85 / 7.5 | 5 / 0.16 |
| small tips 1–7 px (total error) | – | lower in 21 of 30 cases |

Follow-ups:
- Medium hardness at 2–5 px is a little worse than before.
- One end-dab case (a path exactly 10 spacings long at 1000 % spacing) still differs. Photoshop paints the end dab in every other exact-multiple case we measured.

title: perf(engine): Edit › Copy shares whole tiles instead of rebuilding them (#4516)
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #4516.

Edit › Copy, and Layer via Copy / Cut with a selection, built the clip by reading the whole copied area into one `f32` buffer (16 bytes per RGBA pixel, about 366 MiB at 24 MP). It multiplied in the selection and wrote everything back into new tiles, so the clip shared nothing with the layer.

`lift` now works tile by tile:
- **Shared:** a source tile the copy takes whole is shared copy-on-write. That means it's inside the canvas, there's no selection or the selection tile is fully selected, and it's already in the clip's format.
- **Read per tile:** every other tile goes through the old per-pixel code (`lift_region`), one tile at a time instead of the whole area at once.

## Measured

`edit.copy` through `Session::execute` on a 6000×4000 RGBA8 full layer: release build, 7 reps, two runs per build, on this PR's base and on this PR (Windows, Ryzen/RTX 4090 laptop).

| Copy | Before (p50) | After (p50) |
|---|---|---|
| No selection | 273 / 279 ms | 18 / 17 ms |
| Select All | 341 / 356 ms | 44 / 39 ms |
| Paste, for comparison (unchanged) | 0.08 ms | 0.08 ms |

The transient whole-area buffer is gone too: about 366 MiB plus the mask at 24 MP. That figure is estimated from the buffer sizes.

## Same result

The clip is bit-identical. The old whole-area `lift` is kept in the tests as the oracle (`lift_reference`), and `tiled_lift_matches_the_whole_area_lift` compares every pixel and the bounds:
- at 8, 16 and 32 bits;
- with and without alpha;
- with no selection, Select All, a partial feathered selection and a noisy selection off the tile grid;
- with content reaching past the canvas.

`copy_shares_whole_tiles_with_the_layer` checks that the tiles really are shared. The existing injected-allocation-failure test still passes: a no-alpha Background takes the per-tile path.

## Evidence

`564ea6d5` was checked in a clean checkout on Windows x86_64 (rustc 1.99.0), on `13f5c104`:
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`, workspace clippy…

title: Codecs: FITS keeps long CONTINUE strings intact on open and save
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
Opening a FITS file whose header uses long strings (FITS 4.0, section 4.2.1.2) kept each `CONTINUE` record as a separate metadata entry and left the `&` on the first part of the value. Saving wrote that entry back as `CONTINUE= ...`, which is not a valid record, and any string value longer than 68 characters was cut off.

- Reading joins a string that ends in `&` with the quoted strings of the `CONTINUE` records that follow it, ignoring any comment after them. An orphaned `CONTINUE` stays a card of its own (commentary text, as the standard says), and a trailing `&` with no continuation stays part of the value.
- Writing splits a string too long for one card into `CONTINUE` cards, every piece but the last ending in `&`, never splitting a doubled quote. A 68-character string still takes one card. A `CONTINUE` metadata entry is not written as a keyword. No `LONGSTRN` keyword is written; FITS 4.0 no longer requires or recommends it.

Tests: `continue_strings_decode` (joining, a comment after the string, empty continuations, a literal trailing `&`, an orphaned `CONTINUE`) and `continue_strings_round_trip` (100 characters, a quote at a card boundary, 100 quotes, the 68-character boundary). Both fail on main and pass with the fix. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm` and `cargo xtask test-corpus` pass. `cargo test --workspace` passes apart from two `layout_perf` tests (`a_move_tool_click_selects_without_moving`, `auto_select_moves_the_layer_under_the_pointer`) that fail the same way on main in my environment.

Reference: https://fits.gsfc.nasa.gov/standard40/fits_standard40aa-le.pdf, section 4.2.1.2.

title: Free Transform / Warp: Photoshop's Bicubic (Keys −0.75) and a reduction prefilter
author: MrCloudy2
body:
Free Transform and Warp sampled Bicubic with **Catmull-Rom** (Keys a = −0.5). Photoshop's Bicubic is the **Keys cubic at a = −0.75**, the kernel PhotoCraft's Image Size already uses. When a transform *reduces*, Photoshop widens that kernel by 1/scale; PhotoCraft only pre-reduced below 50 % and by powers of two, so 50–99 % reductions aliased.

## Change (`algo/src/transform.rs`, `warp.rs`)
- The 4×4 sampler uses Keys a = −0.75 (`transform::bicubic`, shared by Warp).
- A Bicubic transform that reduces resizes the source first by the whole local scale, using Image Size's widened Bicubic (`resize_surface`). The warp then samples it at about 1:1.
- Bilinear still samples the source directly; it already matched Photoshop exactly at 50 %.

## Evidence (Photoshop 27.11 Free Transform, scripted, whole images)
| case | main (max / mean) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Bicubic 200 % (step edge) | 10 / 0.36 | 1 / 0.01 |
| Bicubic 50 % (impulse image) | 48 / 0.97 | 6 / 0.05 |
| Bicubic 50 % (filter chart) | 59 / 1.18 | 8 / 0.02 |
| Bicubic 150 % | 19 / 0.59 | 21 / 0.17 |
| Bilinear 50 % | 1 / 0.02 | 1 / 0.02 |

Follow-ups:
- Photoshop's Bicubic Smoother, Sharper and Automatic (Free Transform's default) aren't offered by `edit.transform` yet.
- Rotated edges still differ by up to ~90 levels on a thin band.

## Tests
- New: `bicubic_upscale_matches_photoshop`, using the measured 200 % row.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-algo -p photocraft-engine`, clippy (`--no-deps`), fmt and `cargo xtask wasm` pass.

title: Screen color picker: Esc, right-click and any click always end it (#4291)
author: dhiorns15
body:
## Problem

The screen colour picker covers every screen and stays on top. A user [reported on #4291](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/4291) that their picker opened and then ignored Esc, right-click and left-click. The computer was unusable until they remote-desktopped in from a phone. Whatever the trigger, there should be no input that leaves someone stuck in it.

In `screen_picker.rs`, three things could leave the picker running:
- **Esc** was only read once Windows gave the picker window keyboard focus. The window starts hidden and is shown after its first paint, and nothing asked for focus. Windows doesn't always hand focus to a window shown that way.
- **Right-click** wasn't handled at all.
- **Left-click:**
  - The frame returned early, ignoring the click, whenever no snapshot pixel mapped to the pointer.
  - A press that moved even slightly before release didn't count as a click (`Sense::click`), so a slightly shaky click did nothing.

## Fix

The picker window's per-frame code moved into `screen_picker::frame`, so it can be tested, with these changes:
- **Esc**, closing the window, or a **right-click** cancels.
- **Any left release** over the picker ends it, whether a click or a press that moved. It picks the pixel under the pointer, or cancels when there's no pixel to sample. It is never ignored.
- The picker sends `ViewportCommand::Focus` on its first shown frame, so Esc reaches it.

Picking, the loupe, wheel zoom and the main window's own Esc cancel are unchanged.

I couldn't reproduce the stuck picker here: running it on this machine would have covered the screens of the person I'm working for. So this makes every input end the picker rather than fixing one confirmed cause. The original crash in #4291 is a separate failure that's still being narrowed down, hence "Refs", not "Fixes".

**Update:** the reporter has since added that, on 0.8.2 at 150% scaling, Esc *does* reach the picker. The screen flashes black for a frame and the picker stay…

title: Select › Sky: a white or grey backdrop that reaches the bottom is not sky
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #4634.

## Cause

`segment::sky::colour_prior` counts bright, nearly neutral colour as overcast sky (its `white` term). A seamless studio or product backdrop starts at the top edge, seeds the region growing, and floods the whole background. The repro from the issue, a dark disc on `#F2F2F0`, gave `coverage: 0.79`.

## Fix

A sky doesn't reach the bottom of a photo, but a backdrop does. After the mask is cleaned up, `is_backdrop` checks two things: whether the region covers **at least 60 % of the bottom rows** (the same band height as the seed rows at the top), and whether it is **nearly neutral** (mean saturation < 0.1). If both hold, it is taken for a backdrop and `select_sky` returns `None` ("No sky was detected"), as Photoshop leaves such a photo unselected. A blue sky that reaches the bottom, as in a photo taken upward, is not neutral and is still selected. The overcast-sky case (a grey sky over ground) doesn't reach the bottom and is unchanged.

This is deliberately narrow. It does not make the heuristic tell a **blue-grey** studio backdrop from sky: one of my test portraits, with such a background, still gets 22 %. That needs more than a colour prior (#2788's model route).

## Tests

`segment::sky::tests::a_white_backdrop_is_not_sky_but_a_blue_sky_down_to_the_bottom_is`: a dark disc on near-white selects nothing, and the same disc on blue sky selects the sky down to the bottom row. The first half fails without the rule. The existing sky tests (landscape, ground only, overcast, colour prior) and the engine's `select.sky` tests pass. With `photocraft-cli` built from this branch, the issue's image gives `"No sky was detected"`.

`cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p photocraft-algo --all-targets -D warnings` pass.

title: Hue/Saturation: colour ranges apply in full to dull colours
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #4089.

Hue/Saturation faded every colour-range edit by the pixel's chroma (`(max - min) * 4`), so anything with less than about 64/255 of spread between its channels got only part of the edit. Photoshop doesn't do that: in the psd-tools merged images a dull magenta like (126, 97, 120) gets the full range Lightness, same as a vivid one. This drops the fade on the CPU path and in `compose.wgsl`. Greys are still untouched, since a grey has no hue to shift, no saturation to scale, and range Lightness pulls towards a channel they all share.

Against the merged images of the files in the issue (mean / max abs difference, 0-255):

| file | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| huesaturation_lightness_rgb | 1.11 / 13 | 0.34 / 7 (0.3 % px > 2) |
| huesaturation_rgb | 3.73 / 124 | 3.19 / 124 |
| huesaturation_saturation_rgb | 8.83 / 111 | 7.88 / 111 |
| huesaturation_colorize_rgb | 0.47 / 3 | 0.47 / 3 |

What's left of #4089:
- Hue and saturation edits on ranges with very wide or overlapping custom bounds (in `_rgb` and `_saturation_rgb`) still differ. Summing the overlapping ranges is right for lightness, but for saturation it isn't. I tried first/last/max-weight/max-abs and none of them fit, so I'd rather not guess without measuring in Photoshop.
- Re-saving still writes our render as the merged image. Keeping Photoshop's merged image for an unmodified document, or warning on save, is a product call, so I left it out.

Validation:
- `adjust::tone_tests::hue_ranges_apply_in_full_to_dull_colours`: fails on main ((126, 97, 120) gives green 134.6 instead of 148), passes here
- `cargo test -p photocraft-compose --lib hue`, `cargo test -p photocraft-gpu --test parity` (46 passed)
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Fix isolated channel transforms and preserve channel visibility
author: hidoba
body:
Ctrl/Cmd+T on an individual colour channel currently transforms the full layer. This change makes Free Transform, rotate/flip presets and Warp edit only the targeted native component, including a selected or feathered portion. Untargeted colour samples and transparency remain bit-exact.

Fixes https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/4615

- Share target resolution between geometric commands. Add `target: {"color": index}` while preserving the existing pixel, mask, saved-channel and Quick Mask forms. Explicit targets win; an explicit layer without a target retains whole-layer behaviour.
- Capture the interactive target, source and background without changing channel eyes. Refuse a hidden target at start, lock targeting and document edits until commit/cancel, and keep all eyes usable. Hiding/revealing the target preserves geometry; visibility remains view state through commit, cancel and undo.
- Support native 8/16/32-bit RGB, CMYK and Lab components, alpha/spot channels, Quick Mask and linked/unlinked raster masks. Preserve signed/HDR float samples, Background identity and other layer properties. Explicit masks transform alone; whole-layer transforms retain linked-mask behaviour.
- Cache native RGB samples on a supported GPU for one visible raster layer; affine dragging changes uniforms and Warp changes bounded geometry. Curved maps share the CPU sampling grid and sparse components share its lifted source bounds. The shader matches upstream's Keys Bicubic weights and affine/projective edge-repeat sampling with per-tile outline coverage; affine Bicubic reductions needing its widened prefilter, unsupported stacks/profiles/modes, coverage and footprint filtering retain the CPU oracle. Full-resolution commit is unchanged.
- Enable Warp for scalar targets, including grid/split edits, and make selected mask coverage and Warp source frames agree. Cache reduced previews and commit at full resolution as one undo step. Native Free Transform retains upstream's background…

title: Cursors: the pen tools show their icon, and Caps Lock swaps it for the crosshair (#4639)
author: dhiorns15
body:
## Problem

With the Pen tool, the canvas cursor was always a crosshair, and Caps Lock did nothing (#4639). The pen tools fell through to the canvas's default `Crosshair` arm, so they ignored Preferences › Cursors › Other Cursors entirely.

In Photoshop, Other Cursors *Standard* shows the tool's own icon and *Precise* shows a crosshair. Caps Lock swaps between the two.

## Fix

In `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`:
- **Pen tools:** Pen, Freeform Pen, Curvature Pen, Add Anchor Point, Delete Anchor Point and Convert Point now draw their toolbar icon as the cursor (`pen_cursor`). The point sits on the pen's nib: the full-size pen's at (2.3, 2.3) of its 24-unit icon, and the smaller pen in the Freeform and Curvature icons. For Convert Point, the point is its apex anchor. The OS pointer is hidden, as for the pipette and paint bucket cursors.
- **Precise or standard:** `precise_other_cursor` decides: the Other Cursors preference, flipped while Caps Lock is on.
- **Caps Lock for other tools:** the Eyedropper, Color Sampler and Paint Bucket already followed the preference, and now swap with Caps Lock too.
  - The Eyedropper's comparison ring while sampling is unchanged.
  - Move and the Type tools keep their current cursors.
  - Painting tools keep their existing Caps Lock crosshair (#1758).

## Tests

New `caps_lock_swaps_the_other_cursors_between_their_icon_and_the_crosshair` in `caps_lock_tests.rs`. It drives the canvas for each of the nine tools and checks:
- the Standard cursor is the drawn icon
- the Precise cursor differs from it
- Caps Lock turns Precise back into the icon, and Standard into the crosshair
- releasing Caps Lock restores the icon

Without the change it fails: the Pen tool's Standard cursor is the crosshair. The existing Caps Lock tests for painting tools, and the one checking that Move, the marquees, Crop, Zoom and Hand are left alone, still pass.

title: Filters: Photoshop's Blur More kernel, Find Edges strength and Polar Coordinates direction
author: MrCloudy2
body:
Three filters measured against Photoshop 27.11 (scripted probe on a 256×256 test chart, whole-image comparison, 8-bit RGB):

| Filter | Before (mean diff / pixels off by >2 levels) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Blur ▸ Blur More | kernel too weak: 55 levels max | mean 0.00, max 1, 0 % |
| Stylize ▸ Find Edges | 191 levels max (edges ¼ as strong) | mean 0.11, max 1, 0 % |
| Distort ▸ Polar Coordinates, Rectangular → Polar | mean 173.5 | mean 0.04, max 2, 0 % |
| Distort ▸ Polar Coordinates, Polar → Rectangular | mean 153.6 | mean 0.04, max 2, 0 % |

- **Blur More** uses Photoshop's 3×3 kernel `[1 2 1; 2 2 2; 1 2 1] / 14`.
- **Find Edges** is the full Sobel gradient magnitude (it was divided by 4).
- **Polar Coordinates** turns counter-clockwise from 12 o'clock, repeats edge pixels past the source (the corners are filled, not transparent), and uses Photoshop's sampling grid: the map is evaluated at pixel corners, Polar → Rectangular's angle runs one column ahead of its radius row, and the 12 o'clock seam reads the source's right edge (360°, not 0°). These were fitted to the probe output.

Test: `polar_coordinates_turn_counter_clockwise`.

Checks: `cargo test -p photocraft-algo -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask wasm`.

title: Filter dialogs: the preview keeps square pixels
author: marcoarnulfo

The preview in the filter dialogs clamped the texture UV to the image, but still painted that clamped crop over the whole preview region. title: PSD save: keep the Lr16/Lr32 padding outside the block length
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #4654: the Lr16/Lr32 length. The second issue in the report, the duplicated "Transparency" channel when re-saving a Photoshop 16-bit PSB, is separate and not touched here.

The exporter padded the layer info to 4 bytes inside its own body (`pad_to(4)`, from #200). That's right for the classic Layer Info section, but in 16/32-bit files the layers go in a global `Lr16`/`Lr32` block, so the padding ended up inside the block length. Photoshop writes that length unpadded and pads after the block, and readers that check it exactly (Unity's PSD Importer: "Incorrect length for InfoLayers") reject the file. Now a global-block layer info is written unpadded, and `PsdFile::to_bytes` already pads the block to 4 after its length, so readers that step in 4-byte units (the #200 case) still land on the next block. 8-bit saves are unchanged. The shared `strict_block_errors` test helper now counts that outer padding when it checks the layer info alignment.

Validation:

title: perf(engine): Fill, Stroke and Clear keep tiles the selection doesn't reach (#4517)
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #4517.

`blend_into` serves Edit › Fill, Edit › Stroke, Clear on a channel and its other callers. It took every tile in the selection's bounds and blended each one into a fresh copy. History holds the previous document, so `Arc::try_unwrap` always failed and every tile was deep-copied, including ones with nothing selected. Each history step therefore stored duplicates of tiles it never changed.

`blend_tile` skips every pixel whose weight (selection × opacity) is zero, so such a tile comes out byte-identical. Now `blend_into` keeps the original tile instead (`Mask::empty`, next to `Mask::full`).

## Measured

A probe through `Session::execute` on a 20 MP layer, release build, two runs on this PR's base and two on this PR (Windows). The memory figure is the history's `pixel_bytes` before and after the step.

| Step | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Edit › Stroke 4 px on Select All, full layer | +82.5 MB | +17.5 MB |
| Edit › Fill, 4000×3000 ellipse | +26.0 MB | +14.2 MB |

Time is unchanged within noise: Stroke took 445–477 ms before and 522–822 ms after, with a verification build running alongside. The saving is memory, not speed.

## Tests

`unselected_tiles_stay_shared` puts two small selections in opposite corners, so the selection's bounds span every tile while only the two corner tiles have anything selected. It then runs Fill, Stroke and Clear. For each, the 14 tiles in between must stay the same `Arc`, and the corners must change. The test fails on the old code: "edit.fill: unselected tile … was copied".

## Evidence

`0a9b65cc` was checked in a clean checkout on Windows x86_64 (rustc 1.99.0), on `ae72084a`:
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`, workspace clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo xtask scorecard --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Workspace tests: 7,554 passed and 3 failed.

title: perf(ui): Channels thumbnails skip selection-only steps and reuse their textures (#4518)
author: FinnNk
body:
Part of #4518 (the Channels half; the Navigator follows separately).

`channel_thumbs` was keyed by the document snapshot. So every step rebuilt the thumbnails, including steps that only change the selection, such as a marquee or Deselect. A rebuild recomposites the whole document (`compose::thumbnail(&doc, 56)`), and it also allocated new textures with `load_texture` each time.

- **Selection-only steps:** a new snapshot that differs from the previous one only in its selection now keeps the thumbnails. `same_but_selection` gives the old document the new selection and compares it with the new one. Tiles compare by pointer first, so this is cheap, and any other difference still rebuilds.
- **Real rebuilds:** these update the existing textures with `TextureHandle::set` instead of loading new ones.

## Cost avoided

On the #209 layered document (5472×3648, styled layers), one rebuild's `compose::thumbnail(&doc, 56)` measured 659 ms p50: release build, probe on `main` at `d43db3e1`, Windows. With the Channels panel open, every marquee and Deselect paid that on the UI thread. Now they pay nothing.

## Tests

`channel_thumbs_skip_selection_steps_and_reuse_textures` counts egui texture uploads per pass:
- a marquee and Deselect upload nothing and return the same texture ids;
- a fill rebuilds into the same textures.

On the old code it fails at the marquee ("a marquee changes no pixels").

title: perf(text): applying preferences no longer waits for the system font scan (#4519)
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #4519.

`Session::apply_prefs` set the shared text engine's missing-glyph protection through `photocraft_text::shared()`. That call blocks until the system font scan finishes, the scan launch starts in the background with `warm_fonts`. `apply_prefs` runs on the UI thread at launch, whenever a preferences file exists, and on every preferences change. So the first frame waited for the rest of the scan.

`photocraft_text::set_shared_missing_glyph_protection` records the setting and:
- applies it at once when the engine is already built (`try_shared`);
- otherwise has one helper thread wait for the scan and apply it.

Both read the newest setting while holding the engine's lock, so a later change is never overwritten by an earlier one. If no thread can be started, it applies the setting in place, as before. On the web, and without system fonts, the engine is always ready, so no thread is used.

## Measured

A probe replaying the launch order: `warm_shared()`, `Session::new()`, then `apply_prefs()` on the calling thread. Release build, three runs each, on this PR's base and on this PR (Windows; about 250 ms of font scan on this machine).

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `apply_prefs` on the UI thread | 254 / 248 / 257 ms | 0.1 / 0.1 / 0.1 ms |
| Scan still running afterwards (in the background) | 0 ms (it had waited) | 257 / 236 / 250 ms |

Machines with more fonts, or slower disks, wait correspondingly longer before this change.

## Tests

`shared_missing_glyph_protection_follows_the_setting` (text crate): the shared engine follows the setting, and the newest of several settings wins.

## Evidence

`36244547` was checked in a clean checkout on Windows x86_64 (rustc 1.99.0), on `46740ad4`:
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`, workspace clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo xtask scorecard --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Workspace tests: 7,630 passed and 3 failed.

title: PSD: 16- and 32-bit saves write the Lr16/Lr32 length without its padding (#4654)
author: dhiorns15
body:
## Problem

A 16- or 32-bit PSD or PSB save puts its layers in a global `Lr16`/`Lr32` tagged block. The export padded that block's layer info to 4 bytes *inside* the block's length (#4654). Photoshop writes the exact length and adds the padding to a multiple of 4 *after* the block.

Readers that check the length exactly reject PhotoCraft's files. Unity's 2D PSD Importer, which bundles the Paint.NET PSD reader, fails with "Incorrect length for InfoLayers" and loses every layer. 8-bit saves weren't affected: their layers go in the layer and mask section's layer info, where Photoshop does pad inside the length.

The test corpus has a Photoshop-authored file showing the convention: `gray32/baseline-layer-copy.psd` has an `Lr32` length of 22,722 bytes, not a multiple of 4, with no padding inside.

## Fix

`crates/io/src/psd_export.rs`:
- **Layers in an `Lr16`/`Lr32` block:** the layer info now carries no padding of its own (`padding: Some(vec![])`). `PsdFile::to_bytes` already pads after a global block to 4 bytes.
- **Layers in the section (8-bit):** they keep `pad_to(4)`, as before (#200).

The tests' strict block checker (`crates/io/tests/common/mod.rs`, `strict_block_errors`) now holds each placement to Photoshop's rule:
- In the section, the layer info is padded to 4 inside its length.
- In `Lr16`/`Lr32`, there is no padding inside the length, and padding to 4 after the block.

The second part of #4654 isn't addressed here: re-saving a Photoshop 16-bit PSB adds a second "Transparency" channel.

## Tests

- **New `lr16_and_lr32_lengths_exclude_their_padding`:**
  - It saves a pixel layer and a group, at 16 and 32 bit, as PSD and PSB, in four sizes, and reads the block straight from the bytes.
  - It checks the bytes after the declared length are only zero padding up to a multiple of 4, followed by the next block or the image data.
  - It checks the reader finds no padding inside the length and all three layer records come back.
  - It also checks that some case has a …

title: Codecs: open Cineon (.cin) film frames read-only
author: vbasky
body:
## What
Adds a read-only **Kodak Cineon** (`.cin`) decoder to `photocraft-codecs`. Cineon is the 10-bit logarithmic film-scan format DPX grew from, so it is read from the same Kodak header family and shares the DPX unpacking in `crates/codecs/src/codecs/dpx.rs`:

- The generic 1024-byte header, big-endian (`802A5FD7`), orientation at 192, channel count at 193, and the channel-1 bits-per-pixel / pixels-per-line / lines-per-image fields.
- One (Gray) or three (RGB) channels, three 10-bit samples packed into each 32-bit word, lines on a word boundary (the same layout as DPX 10-bit packing method A).
- 10-bit code values open as U16 `round(c × 65535 / 1023)`; the file's log black/white reference points are a display choice and are not applied (as the DPX reader does not transform).
- A depth other than 10 bits or a channel count other than 1/3 returns `CodecError::Unsupported`; truncation errors rather than panicking.

`Format::Cineon` is registered (detect on the magic, extension `.cin`, caps, an `ASYMMETRIC_EXCEPTIONS` entry since there is no writer), routed in `decode`/`encode`, and given the frame orientation; `.cin` joins the desktop and web open filters.

## Why
#1049 (Cineon/DPX) closed with DPX only; `docs/file-format-parity.md` and G10 both list "Cineon: no / still missing". This lands Cineon read to close most of that gap.

## Verification
- Unit tests in `dpx.rs`: 10-bit RGB decodes to exact levels, 10-bit Gray decodes, an 8-bit header is `Unsupported`, and truncation at several offsets errors (never panics).
- `crates/codecs/tests/detect_caps.rs`: magic/extension/caps for Cineon.
- Full `photocraft-codecs` suite green (722 passed, 3 ignored); `cargo xtask layers` OK; `cargo check -p photocraft` clean; fmt + clippy `-D warnings` clean. (`cargo xtask wasm` not run: the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target is not installed here; the decoder is pure Rust.)

title: Play real Photoshop action sets: TrueGrit .atn mappings and fixes (#4356, #219)
author: VegaEX
body:
Follows up #4356 ("Please photoshop Action import") and the `.atn` load/save that landed in 3204231 (#4434, part of #219).

That work made `.atn` files load. This PR makes real third-party action sets **play**. I tested it against four commercial TrueGrit Texture Supply sets that a working illustrator relies on:

| Set | Unmapped steps before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Debaser Comic Coloring Actions (38 actions, 351 steps) | 149 | 0 |
| Distress Press (8 actions, 97 steps) | 50 | 1 (a no-op, imported switched off) |
| Halftone Zine Machine Helper Actions (10 actions, 80 steps) | 22 | 2 |
| True Grit Transparency Action (1 action, 5 steps) | 2 | 0 |

That's **223 → 3** of 533 steps. All four sets play end to end in the desktop app. The `.atn` files are commercial, so they are **not** in the repo. The tests rebuild the same step shapes from synthetic descriptors instead.

## How this was approached

1. **Measured first.** I wrote a throwaway `.atn` dumper and ran each set through PhotoCraft's own `actions.load` to get the exact list of unsupported steps, grouped by event and descriptor shape. The importer's mapping depends on what a step does, not just its event name: `select`, `set`, `make` and `move` map only for some targets.

title: Free Transform: H and V skew fields in the options bar

body:
## Problem

Photoshop's Free Transform options bar has **H** and **V** skew fields after the angle. Ours stopped at the angle: `docs/ui-parity.md` lists "Options bar H/V skew fields" as missing, and so does gap G5.

There was also a readout bug. A box sheared by dragging (⌘-edge) showed a taller **H** (100 / cos *h* %) instead of a skew.

title: Embed craft-fonts by default via .cargo/config.toml [env]
author: sblount2025-design
body:
A plain `cargo build --release` from a clean clone silently produces a CJK-blind binary. build.rs warns and carries on:

```
warning: no craft-fonts embedded: Chinese and Japanese text will render as empty
boxes. Clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts next to this repo and
rebuild with CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=../craft-fonts
```

With craft-fonts already cloned beside the repo exactly as the warning asks, the build *still* needs `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` passed by hand on every invocation. A build-time requirement that lives only in a warning is one that gets forgotten, and then comes back as a bug report about missing glyphs.

This adds it to `.cargo/config.toml`:

```toml
[env]
CRAFT_FONTS_DIR = { value = "../craft-fonts", relative = true }
```

**This is not a new convention — it mirrors `deckcraft/.cargo/config.toml`, which already ships this exact block.** The other craft apps that read `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` don't, which is the inconsistency this closes.

Properties:

- `relative = true` resolves against the repo root, so no absolute path is committed.
- No `force`, so a `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` already in the environment still wins for a one-off build against a different font set.
- If craft-fonts is **not** cloned beside the repo, behaviour is unchanged — build.rs warns exactly as it does today.
- The existing `[alias]` entry is untouched.

## Verification

Built with the variable explicitly removed from the environment, so only the config could supply it:

```
env -u CRAFT_FONTS_DIR cargo build --release
```

The crate recompiled and the "no craft-fonts embedded" warning did not appear. Tested on macOS (Apple silicon), Rust 1.99.0, against craft-fonts at its current main.

title: perf(ui): the Navigator draws the GPU canvas's texture instead of a CPU thumbnail (#4518)
author: FinnNk
body:
Part of #4518 (the Navigator half; the Channels half is #4678).

With the GPU canvas, the Navigator still composited the document on the CPU, on the UI thread, after every edit:
- `render_reduced_damage` over the full-resolution damage;
- or a full `thumbnail_buffer` composite whenever the document has effects or vector masks.

On the #209 layered 20 MP document, measured on `main` at `d43db3e1`, that was:

| Edit | Navigator update |
|---|---|
| Opacity change on one styled panel | 126–137 ms |
| Opacity change on a full-canvas layer | about 700 ms |
| The canvas itself, same edit | 3.4 ms |

## Change

While the main canvas shows the plain document on the GPU canvas, the Navigator paints that same texture through the canvas's own shader (`GpuCanvas::paint`) at the Navigator's size:
- no composite and no readback;
- the display transform the canvas uses;
- the display tiles' mip chain for the reduction.

`canvas::ensure_gpu` records whether the texture holds the plain document, and the main canvas's GPU branch remembers its view parameters per document (`navigator_gpu`). Everywhere else, the Navigator keeps its CPU thumbnail as before:
- a CPU canvas;
- a flipped or aspect-corrected view;
- an adjustment proxy or a live preview, which may be composited only where the view is.

When a document opens, the Navigator can draw before the canvas has drawn it. It then waits up to three frames, showing the checkerboard, rather than build a CPU thumbnail it would use only once. After that it falls back, so it can never stay empty.

## How it looks

Navigator preview of a 2000×1300 test image (thin 3 px stripes, shapes), enlarged 3×. Left: this PR (GPU canvas texture). Right: the current CPU thumbnail.

![Navigator preview: GPU canvas texture (left), CPU thumbnail (right)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FinnNk/photocraft/pr-assets/navigator-gpu/compare-gpu-left-cpu-right.png)

- **Thin lines:** the CPU thumbnail's sampling aliases them into alternating dark and faint line…

title: Screen color picker: no DX12 crash, and the overlay can be left on Windows (#4443)
author: zuujiscom
body:
Fixes #4443.

## What was wrong

"Pick screen color" opens a borderless, monitor-sized window showing a snapshot of the desktop. On Windows that window had two problems, found on Windows 11 with an Intel UHD 630 (release 0.8.2 and current `main`):

1. **Crash on DX12 (the default for Intel on Windows).** The window was created with `WindowLevel::AlwaysOnTop`. DXGI refuses to create the flip-model swapchain for it (`0x887A0001`, `DXGI_ERROR_INVALID_CALL`), the GPU health handler falls back to the CPU renderer, and wgpu then panics in `Surface::get_current_texture_view` ("Surface is not configured for presentation"). I bisected the window attributes with an environment-switchable build: half size alone still crashed, position and monitor binding were fine, and removing only the always-on-top level fixed it.
2. **Overlay could not be left (seen on the OpenGL backend).** The picker was a deferred viewport. Once it was up, the main window stopped being redrawn, so `tick()` never ran. A click and Esc reached the picker window (they set `answer`), but nothing took that answer, so the overlay stayed. Scroll-zoom kept working because the picker paints itself.

## Change

`crates/ui-egui/src/screen_picker.rs`:

- Do not create the window always-on-top. Raise it with `ViewportCommand::WindowLevel(AlwaysOnTop)` once, after its first frame is painted (same place that already sends `Visible(true)`).
- Show it with `show_viewport_immediate` instead of `show_viewport_deferred`, so it is painted inside the main window's frame.
- New test `screen_picker_viewport_is_not_created_always_on_top`.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib screen_picker`: 7 passed (macOS).
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Manually, Windows 11, Intel UHD 630, driver 30.0.101.1273:
  - DX12 (default): opens, a click picks and closes, Esc cancels, no errors in the log. Before: crash.

title: Content-Aware Fill: no tinted blotch in a smooth gradient
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #4706.

## Cause

`inpaint::fit` adapts a copied patch per channel as `gain · source + bias`. The gain is the ratio of the two patches' standard deviations, clamped to the Color Adaptation level's range, and the bias is computed after it and clamped to `±bias`. On a **nearly flat** patch, such as a clear sky where each row is one colour, that ratio is noise, so the gain often sits at its limit. Because the gain scales about **zero**, a gain of 1.1 moves a mean of ≈ 0.7 by ≈ 0.07, which Default's ±0.04 bias can't bring back. Every channel is left off by a different amount, and the result is a purple and green blotch.

## Fix

For **nearly flat** patches (both deviations under `FLAT` = 0.02, about 5 levels) whose means are **already within the bias** of each other, `fit` narrows the gain range to where the bias can still match the means, then clamps the deviation ratio into it as before. The mean is matched exactly, and the gain stays as close to the ratio as that allows. Everything else is fitted exactly as before:
- textured patches, where the ratio means something;
- flat patches of clearly different colours. This is what Content-Aware Move's **Color** slider does on purpose, and its Photoshop-measured test (`content_aware_move_structure_and_color_shape_the_result`) still passes. A first, broader version of this change broke that test, which is how I narrowed it.

The issue's sky gradient: original, `main` (Default), this branch (Default), magnified 2×:

![Content-Aware Fill in a sky gradient](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/switch87/photocraft/issue-assets/issue-assets/caf-gradient-tint.png)

| Color Adaptation | `main` (worst error /255) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| None | 0 | 0 |
| Default | 14 | 1 |
| High | 27 | 1 |
| Very High | 1 | 1 |

title: Codecs: open Amiga IFF/ILBM bitmaps read-only
author: vbasky
body:
## What
Adds a read-only **Amiga IFF/ILBM** decoder to `photocraft-codecs`, written from the published IFF/ILBM layout (EA IFF 85 + ILBM). It parses the `FORM` container's `BMHD`, `CMAP` and `BODY` chunks, in both the interleaved `ILBM` and planar `PBM ` variants:

title: Modern Brightness/Contrast: Photoshop's brightness curve (six oracles pass)
author: timothydaly1
body:
## What

Modern (non-legacy) Brightness/Contrast's **brightness** curve now follows Photoshop's. The contrast curve was already exact. Before, brightness was a line rolled off to white by a `v^P` term:
- up to 4 levels below Photoshop in the highlights;
- up to 2.3 levels off when lowered.

The fit uses every piece of Photoshop ground truth we have:
- the ±50 samples captured in 4759d12b (`modern_brightness_matches_photoshop`);
- the photoshop corpus's `brightness-contrast.psd` (brightness +25, contrast +30) in rgb and gray at 8, 16 and 32 bit. Inverting them through the exact contrast curve gives Photoshop's whole brightness table at +25.

## The curve

*Updated:* psd-tools' `brightnesscontrast_rgb.psd` masks four layers to their own columns, which gives Photoshop's brightness at −95, −31, +23 and +150. The first fit extrapolated badly past ±50: 22 levels off at −95 and 25 at +150. The curve below is refit to all of it.

- **Raised (b > 0):** the line `s·x` with `s = 1.375^(b/50)`, as before, up to a knee at **output** 126/255, then a cubic Hermite to (1, 1) whose end slope is `1/(1 + 0.084 b)`. Every measured setting puts the knee at about the same output level.
- **Past about +110:** no such cubic stays below white, so the roll-off is `1 − (1 − y0)(1 − u)^α`, with the slope continuous at the knee.
- **Lowered (b < 0):** the exact inverse of the curve raised by as much. The −50 samples match the inverse of the +50 fit within 0.81 levels, which is rounding.
- **Range:** the curve stays monotone and inside 0..1 across the slider's −150..150. A test checks every 5 steps, plus the inverse property.

title: perf(raster): mode and depth conversion keep shared tiles shared (#4531)
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #4531.

Image › Mode and bit-depth conversion converted tile by coordinate:
- `Surface::convert`, `try_convert` and `map_color`, which linearises when a document becomes 32-bit;
- the ICC path, `color_cmds::convert_surface`, which also staged every coordinate's tile.

A tile shared across the grid therefore came out as one fresh tile per coordinate. A filled background is the usual case: `fill_rect` shares one `Arc<Tile>` for all of it.

| White background | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 2048×1024 | 1 tile allocation → 32 | stays 1 |
| 24 MP | 1 tile allocation → 384 (96 / 192 / 384 MiB at 8 / 16 / 32 bits) | stays 1 |

Each distinct tile is now converted once, and every coordinate that shared the original shares the result.
- **`convert` / `try_convert`:** a map from source tile to converted tile.
- **`map_color`:** works in place. The keys are the original tiles, which are all alive until their coordinates are reached, so a freed address can't be mistaken for another original.
- **ICC path:** converts each distinct tile once, in the existing single parallel pass, then `put_tiles` shares it.

Pixels are unchanged.

## Tests

- `raster` `conversion_keeps_shared_tiles_shared`:
  - for `convert` and `try_convert` to 16 and 32 bits, the distinct-tile count is unchanged and every pixel equals `convert_pixel` of the source pixel;
  - `map_color` keeps the sharing and leaves the source untouched.
- `color_cmds` `mode_conversion_keeps_shared_tiles_shared`: Image › Mode › CMYK on a white 2048×1024 document keeps one tile for the whole grid, with the same converted colour everywhere.

## Evidence

`982b27b1` was checked in a clean checkout on Windows x86_64 (rustc 1.99.0), on its base:

title: Pen: a new path joins the selected path instead of replacing the Work Path (#4721)
author: itsF4LCON
body:
Fixes #4721.

TLDR:

Drawing a second path with the Pen made the first one disappear: every finished path was written as the whole Work Path, replacing what was there. In Photoshop a finished path joins the path selected in the Paths panel as a new subpath. That's the Work Path right after drawing one, so path after path builds up. Only with no path selected does a new Work Path replace the old one.

Now PhotoCraft does the same, using the existing `path.set` append (`op: "combine"`, Photoshop's default path operation):

- With the Work Path selected (as it is after each Pen path), the new path is added to it.
- With a saved path selected in the Paths panel, the new path is added to that saved path, and the Work Path is left alone.
- With no path selected, the new path replaces the Work Path, as before.

Each path is still one History step. The Freeform Pen and the Curvature Pen finish paths through the same code, so they behave the same way. Shape mode and a targeted vector mask are unchanged.

Changes:

- `ui-egui/src/vector_ui.rs`: `commit_path` appends to the selected path when it exists in the document (`path_exists`), and writes a new Work Path otherwise.

Tests:

- `vector_ui::tests::a_new_pen_path_joins_the_selected_path`: a second closed path joins the Work Path as its second subpath, and undo takes back only that one. With a saved path selected, it joins the saved path and leaves the Work Path alone. With nothing selected, it replaces the Work Path.
- `pen_draw_tests::dragging_on_the_first_anchor_closes_with_its_handles_in_one_step` draws two paths in a row, so it now reads the second one as the Work Path's last subpath and checks the first is still there.

## Checks

- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib vector_ui pen_ path_selection curvature freeform work_path input_tests path anchor`
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`

title: Control: scoped place, replace contents and layer export; document user data and persistent layer ids
author: krishnaavril
body:
## Why

A tool that drives the running app from outside (an asset pipeline's workfile, load and publish steps, for example an AYON host integration) can open and save through the automation roots, but it cannot:

- load a file into the document that is already open,
- switch a loaded file to another version,
- write one layer or group out as an image,

because `file.placeEmbedded`, `layer.smartObjects.replaceContents` and `layer.exportAs` take ambient paths and the control channel refuses them. It also has nowhere to keep its own records in the file, and no way to name a layer across a save and reopen: the `id` in `document.inspect` is a session id, and a PSD's layers get new ones every time the file opens.

## What changed

**Scoped file methods**

- Control channel: `app.place`, `app.replaceContents` and `app.exportLayer`. The file goes through the read or write root the app was launched with, and the command's own body does the rest, as `doc.place` already does on the headless server. The path-taking commands stay refused.
- Headless server: `doc.replaceContents` and `doc.exportLayer`, to match.
- `layer.exportAs` takes `trim: false`, which keeps the document's canvas instead of cropping to the layer's pixels, so exported layers line up with the document and with each other.
- MCP bridge: `doc_place` now forwards `app.place`. It forwarded `file.placeEmbedded`, which the app refuses over control, so the tool could not work against the running app.
- Place refuses a placed size above 300,000 px a side or 2³⁰ pixels, and a `center` beyond the largest canvas, before the resized pixels are allocated. A `scale` of `1e9` used to reach the allocation.

**Records in the file**

- `document.userData` keeps JSON under caller-chosen keys in the document's XMP packet (`photocraft:UserData`), so it is saved with PSD, PSB, TIFF and `.pcraft` files. Both XMP serializations of the property (element and attribute) are read.
- `layer.persistentId` returns the layer's PSD layer id (…
