title: perf(ui): Duotone and live-adjust display documents are built once per snapshot (#4527)
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #4527.

`canvas::display_doc` runs 3–4 times a frame: for the canvas, the Navigator, the area beyond the canvas, and the texture paths. In two cases it built a new document on every call:
- **Duotone documents:** a whole-document clone to add the ink display layer (`mode_cmds::display_document`). This happened before any cache check, every frame, for as long as a Duotone document is open.
- **Live adjustment previews:** a whole-document clone on every call while an adjustment's slider is dragged, to swap in the previewed settings.

`memo_display` now keeps the built document per document id, keyed by the snapshot (a `Weak`) and the preview key. Each is built once per edit or setting and shared after that. Entries of closed documents go when another is stored.

Two panels also cloned a layer every frame just to read a few fields:
- The Channels panel cloned the masked active layer; for a masked group, that's the whole subtree. It now borrows it.
- The adjustment Properties cloned the whole layer to read `visible` and `clipped`. It now copies just those two.

**Cost avoided (not timed separately):** a document clone rebuilds every layer's tile map (an atomic increment per tile, no pixel copy) and deep-clones groups' children and owned blobs such as XMP. The saving per frame is small on most documents and grows with layer count, tile count and nesting. It recurs every frame of a Duotone document and of every adjustment drag.

## Tests

`canvas_display_memo_tests` checks:
- **Duotone:** a second call returns the same `Arc` as the first (with the ink layer), and an edit builds it again.
- **Live adjust:** a repeated setting shares the document; a new setting rebuilds; no preview returns the document itself.

Both fail on the old code, which built a fresh document per call.

`cc6a8813` was checked in a clean checkout on Windows x86_64 (rustc 1.99.0), with the touched-crate set:

title: Handle signed coordinate limits in the Offset filter
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Offset accepts signed 32-bit distances, but subtracting `i32::MIN` from a pixel coordinate overflowed before sampling. The engine caught the panic and returned an internal error instead of applying the filter. Both an algorithm regression and a command regression reproduced this on base `70e182b`.

Apply the selected edge policy using 64-bit coordinates before narrowing. This preserves the actual wrapped position; saturating the subtraction first would choose the wrong pixel. The change stays within Offset.

Regressions cover both signed limits, Wrap/Repeat/Transparent, shifted origins, bounds near the signed limits, and signed/HDR samples. The engine test compares exact output at 8/16/32-bit depth with an equivalent small offset and verifies undo/redo.

Validation: algorithm suite 515 passed (18 ignored); engine suite 1,515 unit and 162 integration tests passed (19 ignored); explicit adversarial-command test passed. Strict all-target Clippy, layering, formatting and WASM checks passed. Native tests ran on `4568b1b`; rebasing onto the next upstream commit (merged #4694, eight lines in UI tile-overlay code) left the algorithm/engine source and Cargo files identical. WASM passed on rebased `6e97d57`.

`cargo xtask perf --quick --bench perf_scenarios` completed successfully on `6e97d57` (LTO disabled, 16 codegen units); its regression comparison was skipped because the stored baseline uses different hardware. A separate local release-kernel comparison against the pre-fix loop produced identical pixels in 18 ordinary-offset cases (Gray/RGBA, all edge policies, zero/small/large offsets), with no measured slowdown in that run. This is not an application frame-rate measurement or a general speedup claim.

title: fix(macos): bundle photocraft-cli and resolve it from droplet scripts

Addresses #4714.

The macOS package builds photocraft-cli but only includes it in the separate CLI download. Generated droplet scripts therefore fail when PhotoCraft is installed without that download.

This change bundles and signs photocraft-cli inside PhotoCraft.app. Generated droplet scripts now check PHOTOCRAFT_CLI first, then common application installation paths, and finally PATH.

title: fix(ui): disable toolbar and tool options on the home screen
author: Ni-zav

The toolbar and tool-specific options remain interactive when no document is open, even though their operations require a document.

Disable those controls in the empty-document state while keeping the Home button available. Controls become interactive again after opening or creating a document.

title: feat(export): offer ICO in Export As with dimension validation
author: Ni-zav
body:
Addresses #4609.

PhotoCraft already supports ICO through its codec and Save As workflow, but ICO is missing from the Export As format selector.

Add ICO to the available export formats, show guidance when the output exceeds the format's 256 × 256 pixel limit, and reject oversized exports with an actionable error.

title: fix(type): preserve keyboard focus when searching for fonts
author: Ni-zav
body:
Addresses #4732.

While inline text editing is active, the Type tool's keyboard handler can consume text intended for a focused font-search field. Typing a font name then changes the canvas text instead.

Let focused UI text inputs handle their own keyboard events before the inline Type editor processes them.

Add a regression test that enters a font-search query and checks that the edited layer's text remains unchanged. Tests have not been run locally.

title: fix(macos): default generated droplets to a user directory
author: Ni-zav
body:
Addresses another part of #4714.

For unsaved documents, Create Droplet defaults to the process working directory. This is unreliable for a macOS application launched outside a terminal and may point somewhere unsuitable for writing files.

Keep using the saved document's directory when available. Otherwise, on macOS, prefer ~/Documents and fall back to the user's home directory.

Add a regression test covering saved-document paths and the platform-specific fallback. macOS behavior has not been tested locally.

title: fix(batch): skip recorded Quick Export steps when writing batch output
author: Ni-zav
body:
Batch already skips recorded Save and Save As commands because each processed file must be written to the batch destination. It does not skip Quick Export.

A recorded Quick Export step can consequently fail on a temporary document without a saved path or attempt an export outside the intended destination.

Skip recorded Quick Export during Batch processing and retain the batch's own output handling.

Add a regression test with multiple input files and a recorded Quick Export step. Tests have not been run locally.

title: fix(clipboard): paste JPEG, BMP and other non-PNG images on Wayland (#2546)
author: nicolasfalesy
body:
Fixes #2546

### Root cause
As @tydude001 found in the issue, arboard 3.6.1's `get_image` requests only `image/png`. A screenshot tool or clipboard manager that offers just `image/jpeg`, `image/bmp`, `image/webp` (or any other non-PNG `image/*` type) gets "Nothing to paste: the clipboard holds no image".

### Fix
In `apps/photocraft/src/services.rs`, when arboard finds no file list and no PNG, `clipboard_get_image` now falls back (Linux only) to `wayland_clipboard_image`:
- It lists the offered types with `wl-clipboard-rs` (the same data-control protocol arboard already uses; the crate is already in `Cargo.lock` through arboard's `wayland-data-control` feature, now a direct dependency pinned `=0.9.4`).
- It fetches `image/*` offers in the source's order and decodes the first one `photocraft-codecs` can read. Text offers are never transferred.
- It caps a read at 1 GiB (a 16K × 16K RGBA BMP), so a broken source can't make us allocate without end.
- Like `image_from_files`, it trusts TGA (which has no magic number) only when the type names it.

Off Wayland (X11, or under XWayland) the connection fails and it returns `None` as before. X11 still reads PNG only. That would need a hand-written selection reader over `x11rb` (INCR transfers included), so I left it for a follow-up.

### Tests
- New unit tests in `services.rs`: `non_png_clipboard_images_paste` (BMP pixels exact, JPEG size; text offers not fetched), `undecodable_clipboard_offers_fall_through_to_the_next`, and `clipboard_tga_is_trusted_only_by_its_type`.
- End to end on Hyprland 0.56 (nested session): `wl-copy -t image/jpeg < test.jpg` (`wl-paste --list-types` shows only `image/jpeg`), then `file.newFromClipboard` over the control channel.
  - Before (current main): `{"pasted": false}`.
  - After: a new 64×48 document holding the gradient.
- `cargo test -p photocraft` (131 passed), `cargo clippy -p photocraft --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean), `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (clean).

title: perf(ui): the Info panel composites its Color Sampler readouts once per revision (#4528)
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #4528.

While the Info tab was visible, every frame ran `view.colorSamplers.list` through the command dispatcher. title: perf(algo): filters read the selection once per tile when mixing it back (#4533)
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #4533.

When a filter runs through a selection, `mix_selection` mixes each tile's result back towards the original pixels by the selection's coverage. It looked the selection up one pixel at a time (`sel.pixel(x, y)`), and each lookup allocates a `Vec` and walks the tile map. That's about 24 million allocations and map lookups at 24 MP, for every tiled filter and for Motion Blur.

It now reads the selection over the tile once (`read_region`) and indexes it.

## Same result

Bit-identical. `mix_selection_reads_the_selection_once_per_tile` keeps the old per-pixel version as the oracle and compares every value:
- a soft selection with fully selected, unselected and partial pixels;
- with and without alpha;
- on a tile that crosses the selection's tiles.

## Measured

`filter.blur.gaussianBlur` radius 2 on a 24 MP layer through `Session::execute`, release build, p50 of 5, two runs each on this PR's base and on this PR. Verification builds were running at the same time, so allow ±20–30 %.

| Selection | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Select All | 602 / 707 ms | 486 / 580 ms |
| Feathered 5000×3000 rectangle | 493 / 705 ms | 376 / 528 ms |
| None (path unchanged) | 503 / 647 ms | 540 / 598 ms |

So about 100–120 ms, or 20–25 %, comes off a filter applied through a selection at this size.

## Evidence

`e280e5bd` was checked in a clean checkout on Windows x86_64 (rustc 1.99.0), with the touched-crate set:
- `cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo xtask layers` pass.
- Tests: 4,242 passed, 0 failed. The `crop_default_mode` and `marquee_autoscroll` wgpu binaries crash under parallel load on my machine and pass on their own.
- `cargo xtask wasm` fails on `main`'s `crates/ui-egui/src/tile_overlay.rs` (#4217, `rayon`), not on this change.

title: perf(camera-raw): convert both previews in parallel bands (#4682)
author: nicolasfalesy
body:
Refs #4682

### What was slow
#3427 colour-managed the refined (zoomed-in) Camera Raw preview. `crop_image` in `crates/ui-egui/src/camera_raw_detail_ui.rs` now calls `CanvasDisplay::to_rgba8` once per row. A row is below `photocraft-cms`'s parallel threshold (`PAR_MIN_PIXELS`, 16K pixels), so on every edit the whole display transform ran on one core of the UI thread, with two allocations per row on top.

The transform runs whenever the document profile isn't the monitor's. On Wayland the monitor is always sRGB, so that means any Adobe RGB or ProPhoto document, which is common for raw opens.

### Fix
A new `display_image` helper reads and converts 64K-pixel bands, in parallel through rayon off wasm, the same pattern as `channel_view.rs`. Each band still goes through the same `to_rgba8`, so the output is identical. Both previews use it:
- the refined preview's `crop_image`, which was converting per row, and
- the main preview's `CameraRawDialog::image`, which copied the whole proxy and converted it on one thread on every edit.

### Numbers
2560×1600 visible crop, median of 15 runs, 22-thread laptop, dev profile (optimized):

| Document | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| sRGB (no transform) | 31.5 ms | 3.9 ms |
| Adobe RGB → sRGB monitor | 125.0 ms | 12.5 ms |
| ProPhoto → sRGB monitor | 117.5 ms | 12.7 ms |

Main preview (`CameraRawDialog::image`), median of 21 runs:

| Proxy | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 858×572 sRGB | 4.72 ms | 1.00 ms |
| 858×572 Adobe RGB | 7.39 ms | 2.06 ms |
| 1716×1144 sRGB | 18.58 ms | 2.48 ms |
| 1716×1144 Adobe RGB | 28.78 ms | 6.88 ms |

I can't confirm this is all of #4682. The reporter didn't say which document profile they used. It is a UI-thread cost that 0.8 added on every edit while the refined preview shows, though, so I've marked this as "Refs", not "Fixes".

title: feat(ui): step numeric fields by the caret's decimal place on mouse wheel
author: Ni-zav
body:
Closes #4614.

Numeric fields currently lack precision-aware mouse-wheel adjustments.

This change makes wheel adjustments follow the decimal place under the text insertion caret.

Changes:
- Determine the step from the caret's position.
- Support integer, decimal and negative values.
- Respect the field's minimum and maximum.
- Avoid changing unfocused fields when scrolling.
- Preserve normal scrolling in surrounding panels.
- Reject malformed numeric text when determining the step.

Add unit tests for decimal-place calculations and an egui interaction test for focused and unfocused fields.

title: fix(screen-picker): allow cancelling pending captures and prevent stale answers
author: Ni-zav
body:
Partially addresses #4737.

The screen color picker can leave the application waiting while an asynchronous screen capture is being prepared. During this phase, the application disables its regular controls without displaying the picker's cancellation action.

Changes:
- Display a cancellation dialog throughout the pending-capture phase.

Add a regression test for cancelling a queued capture and starting another request.

This addresses the pending-capture cancellation path; platform-specific picker behavior still requires verification.

title: refactor(liquify): reuse native brush resizing and anchored HUD feedback
author: Ni-zav
body:
Addresses #4739.

Liquify implements its own brush-resize calculations instead of reusing the established canvas brush-resize behavior.

This creates inconsistent diameter adjustments and visual feedback between Liquify and regular painting tools.

Changes:
- Reuse the existing native brush-resize gesture detection.
- Reuse the shared diameter and vertical-adjustment calculations.
- Account for the Liquify preview's zoom factor.
- Map Liquify density to the shared normalized adjustment model.
- Keep the brush outline anchored at the drag starting position.
- Reuse the brush HUD preview rendering.
- Display diameter and density feedback while resizing.
- Keep resizing separate from painting operations.

Update regression tests for the shared gesture calculations, including zoom and adjustment boundaries.

title: Smart Filters: Delete removes the selected filter, not its smart object
author: marcoarnulfo
body:

Since #4371 a click selects a Smart Filter row and dragging it onto Delete removes it, but clicking the Delete button still went to the layer (the "Delete layer?" prompt), so a selected filter couldn't be removed with the trash icon. title: fix(matting): defringe feathered edges without fully transparent pixels
author: Ni-zav
body:
Addresses a reproducible Defringe no-op case related to #4644.

The existing Defringe implementation requires at least one nearly transparent pixel in the processed region.

A feathered or antialiased cutout can contain partially transparent edge pixels without any fully transparent pixels inside its cropped content bounds. In that case, Defringe returns without modifying the contaminated edge colors.

Changes:
- Detect partially transparent boundaries when no fully transparent boundary exists.
- Propagate clean interior colors toward the contaminated fringe.
- Preserve the original alpha values.
- Preserve existing behavior for cutouts containing fully transparent pixels.
- Keep fully opaque images unchanged when no fringe exists.
- Validate dimensions before processing the pixel buffer.

Add regression tests for feathered boundaries, alpha preservation, opaque-image behavior and invalid dimensions.

title: perf: encode and quantize canvas pixels in parallel (display_color, Buffer::to_rgba8)
author: nicolasfalesy
body:
### What was slow
Four conversions ran one pixel at a time on one thread:
- `CanvasDisplay::texture_buffer`, which runs `linear_to_srgb` (a `powf` per channel) on every CPU-path canvas upload of a linear document. That's every 32-bit document since #3792: `canvas.rs` full uploads, and `gpu_canvas.rs` damage-rect and band uploads.
- The sRGB encode inside `CanvasDisplay::to_rgba8` (`encode_rgba8`), which the Camera Raw and Color Range previews use.
- `Buffer::to_rgba8` in `photocraft-compose`, the plain 8-bit quantize behind the CPU canvas (`canvas.rs` `display_image`), filter previews, the navigator, thumbnails and 8-bit exports. This covers most documents.
- `canvas.rs` `display_image` then ran egui's `ColorImage::from_rgba_unmultiplied` over every pixel, which is also single-threaded.

### Fix
In `display_color.rs`, a small `par_pixels` helper splits the pixels into 16K-pixel pieces across rayon off wasm, with a plain call on wasm (the same gating as `analysis_cmds.rs`). The per-pixel maths is unchanged. `texture_buffer` also writes into a fresh buffer instead of cloning and then overwriting. `Buffer::to_rgba8` gets the same split inline. In `canvas.rs`, the identity path quantizes straight to `Color32` in one parallel pass, and the colour-managed path converts in parallel (`color_image`).

### Numbers
24 MP (6000×4000) linear document, median of 5, 22-thread laptop, dev profile (optimized):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `texture_buffer` | 348.5 ms | 29.6 ms |
| `CanvasDisplay::to_rgba8` (sRGB encode) | 107.8 ms | 10.6 ms |
| `Buffer::to_rgba8` | 122.3 ms | 11.9 ms |
| `canvas::display_image` (identity, whole path) | 50.9 ms* | 12.7 ms |

\* Already with the parallel `Buffer::to_rgba8`; on main the whole path is about 122 + 37 ms.

### Tests
- New `parallel_linear_encodes_match_the_scalar_curve`: three pieces plus a ragged one, with HDR, negative and NaN values. It checks both functions bit for bit against the scalar curve and code table. `parallel_plain_q…

title: Layered TIFF: read Photoshop's mixed-order TySh, and keep unreadable type as pixels
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #4758.

Photoshop on Windows writes a layered TIFF's `TySh` with the version and the six transform doubles little-endian, and everything after them big-endian (text version `00 32`, descriptors, warp, bounds), exactly as measured in the issue. The transcoder read the whole block in the container's order, failed in the descriptor and kept the block as foreign-order `MIB8` bytes, which the importer then decoded as a big-endian `TySh`: correct styles, garbage matrix. The `TySh` arm now recognises the mixed layout (a little-endian text version 50 would read `32 00`, so `00 32` is unambiguous) and converts only the leading fields; the tail is already in the model's order and is copied as is, so a save back to a little-endian TIFF writes it the way Photoshop did. Plain big-endian and fully little-endian blocks take the same path as before.

On the import side, a `TySh` that is still foreign-order, or whose transform is not finite, no longer becomes an editable type layer: the layer keeps Photoshop's pixels, with a warning, and a foreign-order `TySh` is not carried into the layer's PSD blocks (its bytes can't be written as a big-endian block). That covers "respect unresolved foreign-order markers" and stops NaN geometry before it reaches the renderer or the UI rects. Happy to switch to a different fallback if you'd rather keep these as type layers with an empty model.

Not in this PR: the selection/panel path mutating type data, and hardening UI rect construction against finite-but-absurd values (1e62, 1e307), which still import as type layers as they do today. With the TIFF fix those values no longer come out of the issue's file, but I didn't want to guess at a threshold.

@TheSeanLavery, if you get a chance, could you try this branch on the original file? The synthetic fixture reproduces the byte layout you measured, but your file is the real oracle.

- `photocraft-psd` `tiff::tests::mixed_order_type_block_from_photoshop_on_windows`: fails on main (`T…

title: Fix mixed-order layered TIFF type geometry and unsafe text fallback
author: TheSeanLavery
body:
Photoshop-written Intel-order layered TIFFs can store `TySh` as a little-endian version/matrix, a big-endian text version/descriptor, then little-endian warp data and bounds. The current transcoder retains that block as foreign-order; the editable type reader then interprets its affine matrix as big-endian. A scale of 1.8054 can become 1.3158e62, and other terms become NaN. Saved layer pixels hide the problem until text is selected or edited.

Normalize each type descriptor using its own byte order, while preserving the matrix and bounds in container order. Reject nonfinite or unrepresentable affine terms, and keep unresolved/unsafe type as saved pixels with its original type data and an import warning.

Fixes #4758.

Validation:
- Synthetic mixed-order TIFF import checks editable text, affine matrix, point size, saved pixels, and rendered bounds; byte-order round trips and malformed geometry/fallback tests cover the format boundary.
- Native validation on the original private TIFF: all six type layers retain their measured transforms, select and enter editing without invalid geometry or a crash, and restore saved pixels after undo. The original file is unchanged and is not included in this PR.
- Missing fonts still use available substitutes; this change does not install fonts. An unrelated `FEid` smart-filter-mask warning remains.

Local checks passed on the final branch through upstream `becc27ac`:
- 1,085 tests across the touched crates (`--lib --tests`).
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, strict Clippy for psd/text/io, `cargo xtask layers`, and `cargo xtask wasm`.
- `cargo xtask test-corpus -p photocraft-psd -p photocraft-io`, with optimized release builds using `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=false` and `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS=16`. All pinned corpora verified; the earlier LTO builds were cancelled to avoid excessive test-link time.

The diff contains only this fix on current upstream `main`.

title: perf(gpu): closing a document frees what the compositor holds for it (#4529)
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #4529.

`GpuCanvas::retain` freed a closed document's compositor memory (`forget_doc`) only for documents still in its texture map. Three paths drop a document's entry while keeping the compositor and what it already uploaded:
- `DocTextures::new` failed;
- a fresh render failed with a non-fault error after uploading pages;
- the document no longer fits the canvas budget, for example after Canvas Size grows it.

Close such a document and its resident pages, effect maps and lower-stack composite stayed in VRAM. They went only when another document pushed the budgets over; with no other GPU document in use, they stayed indefinitely.

`Compositor::retain_docs(keep)` now forgets every document the caller doesn't list as open, whatever the texture map says, and `retain` calls it each time. The live list already holds each open document's id, its two preview ids and the adjustment proxies, so nothing in use is dropped. `Compositor::held_docs` reports what the compositor holds.

## Tests

`parity.rs` `retain_docs_frees_closed_documents` (GPU):
- after rendering two documents, it holds both;
- `retain_docs` keeping one leaves only that one;
- keeping none leaves nothing, and the lower-stack cache is empty;
- a forgotten document renders correctly again.

## Evidence

`7049fbe4` was checked in a clean checkout on Windows x86_64 (rustc 1.99.0), with the touched-crate set:
- `cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo xtask layers` pass.
- Tests: 4,269 passed, 0 failed.
- The `crop_default_mode` and `marquee_autoscroll` wgpu binaries crash under parallel load on my machine and pass on their own.
- `cargo xtask wasm` fails on `main`'s `crates/ui-egui/src/tile_overlay.rs` (#4217, `rayon`), not on this change.

Rebased onto `cda46050` without conflicts as `79d79fa2`; the new test and gpu clippy pass, and ui-egui builds.

title: perf(engine): lasso and polygon selections rasterise only the rows they span (#4532)
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #4532.

`polygon_selection` rasterised every lasso and polygon over the whole canvas (a `w×h` `f32` mask) and combined it over the whole canvas, whatever the polygon's size.

Without feather, it now:
- rasterises only the full-width band of rows the polygon spans;
- combines over that band. Outside it, Add and Subtract keep the old selection, and Replace and Intersect leave it empty, exactly as the whole-canvas combine does.

**Why full-width rows:** they keep `polygon`'s coverage bit-identical. Its x arithmetic is relative to the area's left edge, so a narrower window could round differently. Its y samples are whole rows plus the same fractions.

**Feather:** a feathered lasso keeps the whole-canvas path, since its blur reaches past the polygon.

## Same result

`lasso_over_its_rows_matches_the_whole_canvas` compares 24 random polygons with the old whole-canvas path:
- partly off the canvas;
- in every mode, over an existing selection;
- with and without anti-aliasing.

## Measured

A 2000-point lasso of a 400 px circle on a 5472×3648 document, release build, p50 of 9, two runs each on this PR's base and on this PR:

| Mode | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Replace | 15.3 / 16.5 ms | 5.5 / 5.1 ms |
| Add to a selection | 29.9 / 30.2 ms | 29.8 / 29.8 ms (its time is in the old selection, not the polygon) |

title: perf(compose): the shape stroke split cache keeps to a byte budget and empties on Purge (#4530)
author: FinnNk
body:
Part of #4530 (the shape stroke cache; the effect cache's pinned layers and History snapshot accounting follow separately).

`compose::shape_split` caches a stroked shape's fill and stroke, each rendered over the whole canvas, for shapes with clipped layers. It had a 32-entry cap but no byte cap: two canvas-sized surfaces per entry, so several GB at 24 MP. Nothing in Edit › Purge › All cleared it.

It now:
- evicts least-recently-used entries until a new one fits both the 32-entry cap and a 256 MiB pixel budget;
- uses an entry larger than the whole budget without keeping it;
- is cleared by Purge › All as "shape stroke cache", with its bytes reported like the other caches.

## Tests

`split_cache_keeps_to_its_budget_and_purges` runs under a test-sized 8 MiB budget, so a few 1024×512 shapes exercise eviction. The cache never exceeds the budget, and a purge frees bytes. The engine's purge test still passes.

title: Fix/4758 type extreme finite geometry 20261013s1215
author: Ni-zav
body:
Follow-up to #4769. Addresses the remaining text-geometry safety case in #4758.

The existing TySh parser can accept extremely large but finite transform coefficients. These may produce unusable coordinates when imported text is selected, edited, or rendered.

Changes:
- Reject nonfinite and excessively large TySh transform coefficients.
- Share the validation between the main text parser and the fallback parser.
- Prevent fallback decoding from reintroducing an invalid transform.

title: perf(paint): sampled tips share their samples, so cloning brush settings is cheap (#4534)
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #4534.

A stroke clones its brush settings on every pointer event: `StrokeRenderer::tail_preview` clones the dab generator and the brush context, each holding a `BrushSettings`. A sampled tip's `GrayTile` held its samples in a `Vec<u16>`, so with a large sampled tip, common in imported ABR brushes, every pointer event copied the whole tip, at a pen's 120+ events a second.

`GrayTile::data` is now an `Arc<[u16]>`, so a clone copies a pointer.
- Nothing mutates a tile's samples after building it, so only construction changes (`.into()`, in three files).
- Equality, serde and every read are unchanged.
- Textures and patterns stored as `GrayTile` share their samples the same way.

## Measured

A paint-crate probe with a radial sampled tip of each size (`size` 300, `spacing` 0.25): one `BrushSettings` clone, and `tail_preview` per pointer event along a stroke (p50 of 40). Release build, on this PR's base and on this PR.

| Tip | Clone, before | Tail preview per event, before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| 500² | 0.01 ms | 0.19 ms | 0.00 ms |
| 1500² | 1.17 ms | 1.14 ms | 0.00 ms |
| 2500² | 3.44 ms | 3.80 ms | 0.00 ms (max 0.01) |

## Tests

`tile::tests::clones_share_their_samples`: a cloned tile, and the tip inside cloned brush settings, share the original's samples, and the clones still compare equal.

## Evidence

`370f5a24` was checked in a clean checkout on Windows x86_64 (rustc 1.99.0), with the full set:
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` pass.
- Workspace tests: 7,951 passed, 3 failed: `complete_languages_translate_every_menu_string`, `preference_labels_are_translated` and `source_key_set_is_covered_by_complete_catalogs`. All three come from `main` at that base: the new Serbian catalogue lacked the "Soft Dark/Light Theme" strings. This change adds no strings.

- `shortcut_asks_first_and_alt_shortcut_makes_a_layer_at_once`: ⇧⌘N opens the dialog without a layer; ⌥⇧⌘N makes one layer per press, no dialog.
- `alt_shortcut_follows_a_custom_new_layer_shortcut_and_yields_to_a_bound_command`: with New Layer on F2, Alt+F2 makes the layer; with Layer via Copy bound to ⌥⇧⌘N, the key runs Layer via Copy.

title: Crop: content-aware fill for canvas extensions + content-edge snapping
author: Gotya-OFFCIAL
body:
Two crop workflow upgrades sharing one goal: the crop frame should follow the image, not the other way round.

**1. Content-aware fill for extensions (Layer › crop options › Content-Aware)**
When the crop frame extends past the old canvas, the extension is filled with the same content-aware pipeline Edit › Fill uses (Wexler patched-image sampling via the PatchMatch search engine with image melding), including the group recursion, hidden/empty layer rules and the #963 memory budget guard. A crop commit stays a single undo step. Rotated crops keep today's behavior (fill applies to the unrotated case only).

`image.crop` gains a `contentAware` param; the crop options bar grows a Content-Aware checkbox; the canvas shows live extension preview while dragging.

**2. Content-edge snapping (View › Snap To › Content)**
The crop frame's dragged edges now also snap to the image's own edges — Sobel gradient ridges with non-maximum suppression, reused from the magnetic lasso tracer (block-cached field, no new dependencies). Geometry keeps priority: content edges only fill axes where guides/grid/canvas/layer targets did not hit, matching the existing snapping hierarchy. New snap-line kind renders content alignments distinctly.

Tests: engine fill tests, algo edge tests, and an end-to-end UI test (crop frame drawn 4 px past a content edge snaps onto it; toggling Content off restores the pointer). The 1787 existing UI tests pass unchanged; one pre-existing machine-dependent pixelate NaN assertion also fails at the 0.7.0 baseline.

title: Matting: RMBG-2.0 neural background removal on DirectML
author: Gotya-OFFCIAL
body:
Adds Layer › Matting › **Remove Background (AI)…** — BiRefNet-based RMBG-2.0 segmentation running fully in-process on ONNX Runtime.

**Why native and not a plugin:** the plugin ABI (docs/plugins.md) forbids all imports — no file access to read weights, no device model to reach a GPU, and the instruction budget cannot carry a 200 M-parameter network. So this ships the way every other capability does: a native crate (`photocraft-matting`) plus an engine command (`layer.removeBackgroundAI`). The wasm build keeps compiling; the crate answers `UnsupportedOnWasm` there.

**GPU selection:** on native Windows the session is created with the DirectML execution provider — one API over NVIDIA/AMD/Intel. The adapter list is enumerated first (wgpu/DXGI order, discrete first, D3D12-reachable adapters ranked ahead) and the winner's index becomes the DirectML device id. A CPU fallback exists but is never silent: the command result always reports the provider, the adapter and the timing. ONNX Runtime is loaded dynamically at runtime (`load-dynamic`), nothing links at build time, so CI and the wasm build are unaffected.

**Weights are not distributed:** RMBG-2.0 is BRIA's CC-BY-NC-4.0 research export — `bat/deploy_matting.bat` installs the runtime DLLs next to the executables and documents where to fetch the model; the loader searches the executable directory, `models/`, then the user data dir. Missing model/runtime produce actionable errors, never a hang.

**Behavior:** the matte multiplies into the active layer's alpha in one undoable step (lossless; never deletes pixels). Params: `variant` (rmbg2 @1024 / rmbg2Sharp @2048), `device` (auto/cpu). Menu label translated into all shipped locales.

Verified end-to-end on Intel Arc A770: `{"provider":"DirectML","gpu":"Intel(R) Arc(TM) A770 Graphics (intel, DiscreteGpu, Dx12, device 0)","ms":…}` with a correct matte (subject opaque, background fully transparent). Crate unit tests cover the preprocessing contract (ImageNet normalization + g…

title: PSD: save Indexed Color, Bitmap and Duotone documents in their own mode
author: switch87
body:

title: Palette PNGs open in Indexed Color mode with their colour table
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #4804.

The PNG decoder expands palette images to RGB(A), and `import_flat` only kept the colour table for BMPs (#3802), so a PNG-8 like the one in the issue opened in RGB Color. This adds `png_palette` to `photocraft-codecs`, which reads `PLTE` and `tRNS` from the headers without decoding pixels, and `import_flat` uses it on the same path as BMP: the document opens in Indexed Color with the whole table and the `tRNS` entry as its transparent index. A palette whose `tRNS` has partial alpha or more than one transparent entry still opens in RGB, because an Indexed Color document only holds one transparent entry. Happy to switch if you'd rather flatten those to the nearest fit.

Not in this PR: the second point of the issue. Image › Mode › Color Table… is the generic schema dialog, so it shows only the Table dropdown and has no swatch grid to edit entries. That needs its own UI. GIF and palette TIFF also still open in RGB.

Validation:

title: Canvas: the CPU canvas shows crisp pixels when zoomed in
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Should fix #4810, if PhotoCraft is drawing with the CPU canvas on your Mac (see the end).

The GPU canvas shader already draws pixels with its sharp nearest filter at 200% and up, but the CPU canvas (what draws the document when the GPU canvas is off or fell back: Performance > Use Graphics Processor unchecked, a failed GPU init, a lost device, a flipped view) uploads the document texture in `ensure_texture` with `TextureOptions::LINEAR`, so every pixel gets blended with its neighbours when zoomed in. Free Transform's preview uses `NEAREST`, which is why it looked right there. The canvas texture now magnifies with `Nearest` and keeps `Linear` minification, so zoomed out is unchanged. A document over `MAX_TEXTURE` keeps a reduced texture whose texels average several pixels, so it stays bilinear: squares of those would be blocks the image doesn't have.

On the CPU path this is nearest at every zoom above 100%, as Photoshop does, while the GPU path keeps bilinear between 100% and 200% at non-integer scales; happy to match the GPU thresholds instead if you prefer.

Validation:
- `canvas::tests::cpu_canvas_shows_crisp_pixels_when_zoomed_in`: fails on main (the canvas texture is uploaded with `magnification: Linear`), passes here; it checks both the first upload and a damage-rect update
- `canvas::tests::cpu_canvas_of_a_reduced_document_stays_bilinear`: pins the reduced-texture case
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib cpu_canvas_`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

@Adro7687, could you check whether Preferences › Performance › Use Graphics Processor is on, and what zoom level the screenshots were at? On the GPU canvas pixels are already crisp from 200%; if that is where you see the blur, this PR is not the fix and I will look at that path instead.

title: fix: validate invert plugin buffer dimensions and channel layout
author: s1ddiq
body:
## Summary

Improves input validation in the example Invert WebAssembly filter to prevent malformed pixel buffers from being processed incorrectly.

## Changes

- Validate channel counts and alpha channel layouts.
- Verify buffer length against the expected image dimensions.
- Use checked arithmetic to prevent integer overflow.
- Handle empty image buffers safely.
- Preserve the existing optimized RGBA processing path.

## Motivation

Previously, the filter used `chunks_exact_mut()`, which silently ignores incomplete trailing pixels. This could result in partially processed images when the provided buffer length did not match the expected dimensions.

The updated implementation rejects invalid buffer layouts before modifying pixel data.

## Testing

Tests have not yet been added or run.

## Additional Notes

- No additional dependencies.
- Maintains `no_std` compatibility.
- Preserves existing behavior for valid pixel buffers.

title: UI fonts: draw a variable CJK fallback at Regular, not Thin (#4820)
author: dhiorns15
body:
## Problem

On a system with only Noto Sans CJK's **variable** collection installed (Fedora's `google-noto-sans-cjk-vf-fonts`, `NotoSansCJK-VF.ttc`), CJK text in the UI (panel labels, layer names) is drawn at Thin weight (#4820). The UI font fallback (`cjk_fonts.rs`) registers the face with egui at its default instance, and that collection's `wght` axis defaults to 100 (Thin); its Regular is 400.

## Fix

`cjk_fonts::add_to_all_families` reads the fallback face's `fvar` table. If the face has a `wght` axis whose default isn't Regular, it registers the face with `wght` = 400 (clamped into the axis range) through egui's `FontTweak::coords`, which epaint 0.36 applies when it draws glyphs.

- Static fonts, faces without a weight axis, and variable faces that already default to Regular are untouched (no variation coordinates).
- Works for collections: the axis is read from the registered face's own directory.
- The table walk is shared with `vertical_metrics` (bounds-checked: truncated or garbage bytes give `None`).

## Tests

- `cjk_fonts::tests::variable_fallbacks_are_drawn_at_regular_weight`: synthetic fonts with only an `fvar` table (no font files committed): a Thin-default weight axis in face 1 of a collection → 400; a weight axis after a width axis → 400; a 500–900 range → 500; a Regular default → none; no weight axis → none; static Inter → none; truncated and garbage bytes → none. A static face registered as a fallback keeps default coordinates.
- Checked by hand (not committed): Windows' variable Bahnschrift drawn through egui with `wght` 300 / default (400) / 700 inks 1.07M / 1.35M / 1.67M atlas alpha, so epaint does apply the coordinate. Its `fvar` is found and, defaulting to Regular, it gets no override.

Not reproduced on a real Fedora VF-only install (this machine is Windows); the reporter's axis values (min 100, default 100, max 900) are what the synthetic test uses.

title: Layer Style applies an open Free Transform first, so its preview shows
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #4821.

While the Free Transform box is open, the canvas draws the box's own preview document (`display_doc` returns it before it gets to the Layer Style preview), so whatever the dialog previews stays hidden until Enter. The styled box from #3696 doesn't help here either: it is set up only when the layer already has a style when the box opens, and it reads the committed layer, not the dialog's unsaved fields. `layer_style::open` now applies the pending box first, as the issue describes for Photoshop and Photopea, so the dialog previews on the transformed layer. Every way into the dialog goes through it (Layer menu, the fx button and effect rows in the Layers panel, the control channel). An untouched box (a file just dropped on the canvas) simply closes and the place stays, as Enter does. If the commit is refused (over the pixel budget), the box stays open with the reason in the status bar and the dialog doesn't open. I went with commit rather than making the box preview the dialog's live fields because it is much smaller and matches the reported behaviour; happy to switch if you'd rather keep the box open.

title: perf(raster): moving a layer no longer stores tiles of only the default pixel
author: deadmeu
body: Moving a layer by an amount that isn't a multiple of the 256 px tile size stored fully transparent tiles it didn't need. The image was correct, but each empty tile used a full tile of memory (256 KB at 8-bit RGBA). Snapshots, undo history, saves and the canvas also processed them, and nudging a layer back and forth kept adding more. ### Cause `Surface::translated` (`crates/raster/src/lib.rs`), which every layer move and the Move drag preview use, allocated every target tile that a moved source tile reached. The transparent margins of a layer's edge tiles landed on target tiles of their own, and those tiles were stored even though they held only the default pixel. #4414's shared uniform tiles were stored too when their value was the default pixel. `Surface::prune` drops such tiles, but nothing called it after a move. ### Change A target tile that ends up holding only the default pixel is no longer stored: - **Copied tiles** are compared after the copy, one row at a time, with a row of the default pixel. That's one `memcmp` per row, and a tile with content stops at its first row. (Tracking a flag inside the copy loop instead made full layers about 25% slower, so the check runs after the copy.) - **Shared uniform tiles** (#4414) whose value is the default pixel are skipped. Moves by whole tiles still re-share the existing tiles unchanged. ### Before / after Seen with the developer tile grid overlay (`ui.set {"tileGrid": true}`). Blue cells are stored tiles with unique pixels. Pink cells are stored tiles with identical pixels, here all fully transparent. Two blocks on one layer, moved by (100, 56) and then back by (−100, −56): Without the fix, the move leaves 5 empty tiles stored next to the red block. Moving back makes it clearest: the image is the same as at the start, but 10 empty tiles are now stored, up from none.

title: fix(segment): stop push/relabel looping forever on unreachable nodes
author: LloydNicholson
body:
## Problem

On some photos, Remove Background stays on "Finding subject" (10%) indefinitely, with one CPU core pinned. Cancel doesn't stop it either.

A `sample` of the stuck app showed every rayon worker idle except one. That worker was inside `refine_band` → `grid_cut` → `Graph::maxflow_with`, in the push/relabel discharge loop, with periodic `global_relabel` calls. A refinement tile (≤216×216 px) normally solves in milliseconds; this one ran for more than 10 minutes.

## Cause

The push/relabel admissibility test was

```rust
self.dist[i] == self.dist[j].saturating_add(1)
```

`global_relabel` gives nodes reachable from neither terminal the height `u32::MAX`. Because `u32::MAX.saturating_add(1) == u32::MAX`, two neighbouring unreachable nodes counted as admissible for each other. When f32 rounding strands excess on such nodes, they push it back and forth forever. The rounding happens with source capacities near 3e8, where one f32 ulp is 32, next to links of a few units. An instrumented run counted ~205M pushes from `dist == u32::MAX` nodes against ~8K ordinary pushes.

## Fix

Use `self.dist[j].checked_add(1) == Some(self.dist[i])`. An unreachable node is then never a push target. Its stranded excess stays where it is, the node relabels to `MAX` (no-op) and drops out, and the loop terminates.

title: Distort: a quad dragged past the horizon draws only its front side, in the preview and the result (#4863)
author: itsF4LCON
body:
Fixes #4863.

TLDR:

In Free Transform › Distort, pulling the bottom corners in and then dragging one far out brings part of the image past the perspective's horizon. A projective map sends that part to the far side of the horizon, wrapped round infinity. PhotoCraft drew it there anyway, as a mirrored, stretched copy: corrupted output in both the preview and the applied result. Photoshop shows only the sensible part.

Now both draw only the front side:
- the side of the horizon that most of the image's corners land on (the centre's on a tie)
- the corner dragged past the horizon, and the cells beyond it, are left out instead of wrapped round

A quad wholly in front of the horizon, which is every ordinary Free Transform, Perspective or Distort, renders exactly as before.

Changes:

- `algo/src/transform.rs`:
  - `Homography::w` (the homogeneous w of a point) and `Homography::front_side` (the side most corners map to)
  - the warp already clipped tiles against the horizon when the whole source was on one side (#2271); when the source straddles it, each output pixel is now kept only if the inverse w there has the front side's sign (the sign of the forward w at the source point it samples)
- `ui-egui/src/transform_tool.rs`: the 24×24 preview mesh leaves out cells with a corner past the horizon (`front_vertices`), so no triangle stretches across the canvas.

Tests:

- `transform::tests::a_distort_past_the_horizon_draws_only_its_front_side`:

title: TIFF: write and read EXIF as the file's own Exif and GPS directories
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #4875.

TIFF is EXIF's own container. IFD0 points to the Exif directory (34665) and the GPS directory (34853), and holds the descriptive tags itself. The TIFF codec now writes and reads EXIF that way.

## Changes

- **`codecs/tiff_exif.rs` (new):**
  - Reads the EXIF parts of any classic TIFF stream: a TIFF file, or an EXIF block, which is itself a TIFF stream. That is IFD0's descriptive tags (ImageDescription, Make, Model, Software, DateTime, Artist, Copyright) plus the Exif and GPS directories, as raw fields.
  - `block` builds an EXIF block from those parts. `write_directory` / `write_fields` put them into a file through `tiff`'s `extra_directory` / `write_entry_bytes`.
  - Values are copied as bytes and reordered per element when the byte orders differ, so tags PhotoCraft doesn't know survive.
  - The Interoperability pointer isn't carried: it would point nowhere.
- **Export (`tiff.rs`):**
  - The Exif and GPS directories are written before the image, outside the page chain, and IFD0 points to them. This works for classic TIFF and BigTIFF.
  - IFD0 gets the block's descriptive tags, except those the text metadata already wrote.
  - Structure, resolution and orientation stay the image's own.
- **Import:** IFD0 of a classic TIFF with an Exif or GPS directory gives `meta.exif`. A TIFF with only descriptive tags still reads them as text metadata, as before, and gets no EXIF block made up for it.
- **`FormatCaps` for TIFF:** `exif: true`, so the export no longer warns "EXIF not supported".
- **Layered TIFFs:** they keep EXIF in resource 1058 (#1545), which is read back unchanged. A block rebuilt from the Exif directory would lose the thumbnail and IFD0's orientation. The layered importer already prefers the TIFF's own EXIF when there is one, so a Photoshop-made layered TIFF now gets its EXIF too. Only the comments there changed.

## Checked

- `tests/tiff_exif.rs`:
  - A camera-style block (Make, Model, Artist, Orientation; ExposureTime, ISO, DateTimeOriginal, …

title: fix(segment): let Remove Background's cancel stop Select Subject's min cuts
author: LloydNicholson
body:
## Problem

When Remove Background is on "Finding subject", Cancel/Esc does nothing until the whole step finishes. The job checks `ctx.cancelled()` only before and after `subject::select_subject`. Inside it, every graph cut runs through the non-cancellable `grid_cut`, so `Graph::maxflow_with` gets the `never` callback. That covers the GrabCut iterations and the full-resolution band re-cut in `refine_band` (`finish_region`, tiles on rayon). A slow tile, or the push/relabel loop fixed in #4869, therefore couldn't be cancelled. This is the follow-up #4869 left out ("Not in this PR").

## Fix

- `segment::finish_region_with`, `grabcut::grabcut_with` and `subject::select_subject_with` take an `Interrupt` and return `Result<Option<_>, Cancelled>`.
- `refine_band` checks `ctl` before it reads each tile and runs that tile's cut with `grid_cut_cancellable` (same weight as `grid_cut`). Tiles already in flight stop at the max-flow's next poll (every 1024 steps), and the rayon `collect::<Result<_, _>>` short-circuits. GrabCut checks once per iteration and inside its cut. Select Subject also checks after the saliency stage.
- Remove Background runs the step under `ctx.stage(0.1, 0.6, "Finding subject", …)`, the same pattern Content-Aware Fill uses.
- `select_subject`, `grabcut` and `finish_region` keep their signatures and results by passing `Interrupt::NONE`. `select.subject`, Object Selection, the layer menu and `bench_smartselect` are unchanged.

## Tests

- `finish_region_cancel_stops_inside_the_band_cut`: a single band tile, where nothing polls after the re-cut. Uncancelled, it gives the same region as `finish_region` (IoU > 0.95) and the cut itself polls. Cancelled at the cut's first poll (the second poll overall), it returns `Err(Cancelled)` after exactly 2 polls, so the cut stopped partway through.
- `select_subject_cancelled_in_the_band_recut_reads_no_more_tiles`: a 3000×2000 scene. Uncancelled, it matches `select_subject`, and the band cuts poll more often than once pe…

author: Ni-zav

When a selection is active, the status bar displays its actual pixel bounds as X, Y, width and height. Otherwise, it shows the active layer's effective bounds, including groups and fill layers.

title: fix(ui): avoid overflow when allocating layer style instance IDs
author: Ni-zav
body:
Prevent an integer overflow when adding a layer-style effect after an existing instance uses the maximum u64 ID.

Previously, next_id incremented the highest fxN identifier without checking for overflow. An imported or automation-provided fx18446744073709551615 could therefore panic in debug builds or generate an invalid identifier in release builds.

Use checked addition and, when the numeric range is exhausted, select an unused positive identifier instead. Existing effect ordering and selection behavior are preserved.

Added a regression test with fx1 and fx18446744073709551615, verifying that the next instance receives fx2.

Validation: Regression test added but not executed locally; CI pending.

title: fix(psd): reserve imported layer IDs when allocating section dividers
author: Ni-zav
body:
Fix PSD export when imported layers contain IDs near or at u32::MAX.

The exporter previously generated section-divider IDs by incrementing the highest imported layer ID without checking for overflow.

Track reserved layer IDs and allocate generated IDs using wrapping arithmetic, skipping identifiers already in use.

This preserves imported layer identities while preventing generated group-divider IDs from colliding with them.

Added a regression test using a group with an imported u32::MAX ID. The test checks ID uniqueness, preservation of the original ID, and serialization/reimport consistency.

Validation: Regression test added but not executed locally; CI pending.

title: fix(ui): Match Color's preview reads the Source document (#4851)
author: kavishkashehan726-sudo
body:
The filter preview runs the command in a fresh session holding only a proxy of the edited document, so a document param such as Match Color's Source (or Displace's map) pointed at nothing there: with another document as the Source the preview failed and the canvas kept showing the unchanged image, and with the first open document it matched the image to itself. OK then applied a different result from what the dialog showed.

The preview now adds each referenced open document (as a proxy at the same factor) to its session and points the param at it, so it shows what OK applies.

title: fix(ui): make the Histogram panel follow the selection
author: JohnXu28
body:
## Problem

Selecting an area never updated the Histogram panel — nor the Levels/Curves/Threshold
histograms. A selection change moves no pixels, so the view-only fast path from #125 promoted
the cached whole-image histogram across the revision, and `compute_histograms` never looked at
`doc.selection` at all. Photoshop shows only the selected pixels (statistics and the Pixels
count too).

## Solution

- `compute_histograms` masks each 384-px proxy sample by the selection (coverage >= 1/2).
- Both histogram caches now key on a selection fingerprint (the mask's tile `Arc` pointers, so
  clones keep the key and any rewritten mask changes it): a selection change invalidates the
  cache while genuine view-only revisions still hit it (`layout_perf`'s no-recompute-on-
  layer-select stays green).
- The panel's Pixels statistic reports the selection's exact pixel count, scanned at full
  resolution (GRAY8 tile fast path) on the histogram worker.
- `contributors/people.toml`: my own entry (`@JohnXu28`, display name "JohnXu"), added in my
  own PR as `contributors.md` asks.

## Tests

5 new (selection-restricted histogram + exact pixel counts, feathered mask, fingerprint
identity, tone-cache invalidation, panel end-to-end follows the selection), 2 updated for the
pixels payload. `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib` (2216 ok), `--test layout_perf`,
clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm` all green.

title: feat(cli): run authenticated JSONL command files
author: haranishi
body:
Fixes #3669

`photocraft-cli run --control PORT --control-token-file FILE script.jsonl` runs a command file against an existing control server. `--token-file` is an alias. Each line dispatches `{ "command": ..., "params": ... }` in order, using the existing authenticated, loopback-only `BridgeClient`.

An optional `saveAs` captures a command result. String parameters such as `$ink/layer` select a captured value with a JSON pointer and preserve its JSON type; `$$ink` produces a literal `$ink`. Scripts are checked for syntax, shape, references and capture order before connecting. Input, nesting and capture budgets prevent unbounded allocation. A failed command or connection stops execution; dispatched edits are never retried. Earlier edits remain applied.

The existing local `run --new/--cmd` behavior is preserved. Server authentication, filesystem capabilities and command policy are unchanged. Usage and examples are in `docs/cli-command-files.md`.

title: Brush import: Dual Brush spacing comes from its tip (#4809)
author: dhiorns15
body:
## Problem

Importing a Photoshop `.abr` brush with Dual Brush enabled set the dual tip's spacing to 100% whatever the preset said (#4809, part 1). The reporter's test file has presets named "SPACING 10%", "SPACING 18%" and "SPACING 24%"; all three came in at 100%.

## Cause

Photoshop CC stores the spacing that its Dual Brush panel shows in the dual tip itself, `dualBrush › Brsh › Spcn` (10, 18 and 24% in the reporter's file). It also writes a `Spcn` of 100% on the `dualBrush` object beside it, in every preset of the file. `abr_map.rs` read the tip's value first and then let the outer one overwrite it.

## Fix

The tip's spacing wins. The `dualBrush`-level `Spcn` is only used when the tip has none, which keeps the existing synthetic test (spacing only on the outer object) as it was.

## Tests

- `abr_map::tests::dual_brush_spacing_comes_from_its_tip`: tip 10% with an outer 100% → 10%; no tip spacing → the outer value. Fails on main (100%).
- Checked by hand with the reporter's `Test.ABR` (not committed): the three dual brushes now import at 0.10, 0.18 and 0.24, matching their names.

Gates: `cargo test -p photocraft-io`, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo check -p photocraft-io --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo xtask test-corpus`.

## Not in this PR

- **Part 2 of #4809** (the dual tip not following the main brush size): PhotoCraft keeps the dual tip's size in pixels, so following the main size means storing it as a ratio or rescaling it everywhere the size changes. That's a design choice, left for the maintainers.
- The file's fourth preset ("UNREADABLE TIP") uses one of Photoshop's **erodible tips** (`dTips` class), which PhotoCraft doesn't support yet; it still imports with a round tip and a warning.

title: fix(gpu): contain errors in unwatched compositor work
author: haranishi
body:
Refs #1154; related historical device-loss report #243.

Native `Compositor` callers without `DeviceHealth` can still panic in wgpu's default error handler when GPU work fails, even with the uniform-buffer preflight already merged in #3931. A small destroyed-device fixture reproduces the invalid-buffer panic without a large document.

An error also discards resident uploads, effect maps, prefix results and temporary texture caches. Their metadata advances while recording an encoder; reusing it after failed work can otherwise produce missing effects on a later successful render. Regression tests invalidate an encoder, then compare the recovery render with a fresh compositor.

author: ahmedhosnypro

## Summary

PhotoCraft's automation surfaces — MCP, the TCP control channel, `photocraft-cli serve`,

contracts that existed in code but nowhere on paper. This branch fixes **33 such issues**,

Every fix follows one of five styles, chosen to be the smallest change that makes the

title: Smart Filters: drag a filter up or down its stack to reorder it
author: abc2cb
body:
TLDR:

In Photoshop the order of smart filters matters, and you change it by dragging a filter row up or down its stack. The bottom filter is applied first: Unsharp Mask over a Gaussian Blur sharpens the blurred image, while under it the sharpening gets blurred. The engine already had `layer.smartFilter.move` and re-renders in the new order (`smart_cmds::tests::filter_stack_order_blend_disable_and_clear`), but the Layers panel had no way to reach it. Since #4371 a filter row can be dragged onto another smart object or onto Delete, but a drop inside the filter's own stack did nothing.

Now:

- **Drag** a filter row over another row of the same smart object's stack. A line shows where it will land: above that row on the row's upper half, below it on the lower half. Dropping on the Smart Filters row puts the filter on top of the stack.
- **Release** runs `layer.smartFilter.move {layer, index, to}`, which is one undo step. The moved filter ends up selected and its smart object becomes active, the same as after a click.
- A drop next to the filter's current place, or on the filter itself, does nothing. Drops onto other smart objects and onto Delete work as before.

Related: #3967 (by another author) adds Move Up / Move Down / Delete to a filter row's menu. That PR has no drag. The two don't overlap in code, and Photoshop offers both ways.

Changes:

- `ui-egui/src/smart_ui.rs`:
  - `reorder_target` maps "dropped above/below row `i`" to the `to` index of `layer.smartFilter.move`. `move` removes the filter first, which shifts the rows above it.
  - `reorder_drop` draws the insertion line and emits the command on release.
  - `filter_rows` calls `reorder_drop` and selects the moved filter.
- `docs/ui-parity.md`: a row for the new behaviour and a 2026-10-13 history entry.

No new commands and no new `tl!` strings.

Tests:

- `smart_ui::tests::a_filter_dropped_above_or_below_a_row_lands_next_to_it`: the index math. It covers above and below rows on both sides of the filter, t…

title: Layer locks: locking the pixels clears the transparency lock, as in Photoshop (#4892)
author: itsF4LCON
body:
Fixes #4892.

TLDR:

Lock Transparent Pixels and Lock Image Pixels could both be on at once, although Lock Image Pixels already covers transparency, so the pair made no sense. In Photoshop, locking the image pixels turns the transparency lock off, and it stays unavailable until the pixels are unlocked. PhotoCraft now does the same, everywhere a lock is set.

- Turning Lock Image Pixels on clears Lock Transparent Pixels.
- While the pixels are locked, Lock Transparent Pixels stays off. Its Layers panel button is greyed, and a command asking for it leaves it off.
- Unlocking the pixels makes it available again. The other locks are unchanged.

Changes:

- `doc/src/lib.rs`: `Locks::set(key, on)` sets a lock by its command name and applies the rule.
- `engine/src/commands.rs` (`layer.setProps`) and `engine/src/layer_multi_cmds.rs` (`layer.lockLayers`): both set locks through `Locks::set`, so the panel, scripts and actions all agree.
- `ui-egui/src/panels.rs`: the Layers panel's transparency lock button is disabled while the pixels are locked.

Tests:

- `layer_multi_cmds::tests::locking_pixels_clears_and_holds_off_the_transparency_lock`:
  - locking the pixels clears an existing transparency lock
  - asking for the transparency lock while the pixels are locked leaves it off, and both at once leaves only the pixel lock
  - after unlocking the pixels it can be set again
  - `lockLayers` does the same, and an unknown lock name is still an error

## Checks

- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib lock`, `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib lock`, `cargo test -p photocraft-doc --lib`
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-doc -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`

author: Zenodeon
body:
Shared-library prerequisite: [storytold/craft-libs#110](https://github.com/storytold/craft-libs/pull/110). Merge that PR first, then pin this integration to an immutable storytold/craft-libs revision.

Panels and document views can detach into movable, resizable windows inside PhotoCraft. Panels dock on all four workspace sides or around the main/floating document area, with independent floating-size memory and persisted workspace arrangements.

Dragging uses one validated candidate for measured feedback and atomic release. Actual panel content follows the pointer; affected groups animate over 150 ms with warning-colored outlines, while receiving tab strips stay fixed and reachable. Hovering a panel tab strip fades the moving UI to 40% opacity. Shared-divider drops insert between neighboring groups and shrink both neighbors. Bounded accent insertion markers stay above preview overlays, and resize focus clears on release.

Extends craft-ui through additive shared APIs, pinned to immutable revision 975bce73e09602b5dc51e2485ad122dcbb120d7a in Zenodeon/craft-libs. Includes control/docking documentation and a Windows source launcher. Separate desktop-window tear-off by dragging remains unfinished.

### Interaction fixes

Returning a tab to its source group highlights the content area in blue while leaving the tab strip clear and its insertion marker fully opaque. title: Deep EXR: open cropped renders on their full display-window stage
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## Summary

Our render passes write deep EXRs whose `data_window` is the crop of the frame (e.g. MY27 renders: data 1782×1267 at (1109, 1100) inside a 4000×3000 stage). PhotoCraft opened them cropped to the data window, so a pass that composited to the full frame came in as a small tile.

`decode_deep` now reads the `display_window`, validates it against the limits (sane size, data region fully inside it) and reports it as `stage` + `origin` on `DeepImage`. `flatten` pads the composed region to the stage at its offset — transparent elsewhere — and tags the image with a new `DisplayWindowStage` warning, so the UI shows what happened. Files without a usable display window open exactly as before.

Opening `beauty.0001.exr` (the MY27 sample this was built against) now yields a 4000×3000 document with the composited pass at its crop offset instead of a 1782×1267 crop.

## Evidence

- new test `cropped_deep_data_opens_on_the_display_stage` (a 24×16 data region at (8, 6) on a 48×32 stage): opens at stage size, data at the offset, rest transparent; full `photocraft-codecs` suite 63+7+13+14+15+29 passed.
- verified against the real sample: `photocraft-cli info` reports 4000×3000 and the stage warning.
- `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p photocraft-codecs` clean; clippy and fmt clean on both touched crates.

## Follow-ups

- The deep-layer import path (Deep layers PR, still in review) consumes these fields next so stacked deep layers land at their crop offset on the stage rather than being cropped.
- Flat (non-deep) EXRs with a display window different from their data window still open data-window-sized; the same stage mechanism can extend there if wanted.

title: ACEScg: File Handling option opens colour-less EXR renders in the ACES working space
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## Summary

Our CG render pipelines write EXRs in ACEScg (AP1 primaries, ACES white ~D60, linear) and — like most renderers — state no colour space in the header. PhotoCraft tagged such EXRs with its linear-sRGB default, which misrepresents AP1 colours (saturated hues shift noticeably; try a pure AP1 red next to a Rec.709 red).

- **cms**: `AcesCg` joins the built-in profiles, generated from the published AP1 primaries and the ACES white point with a linear TRC (id `aces-cg`, alias `acescg`), same CC0 public-domain generation as the other built-ins.
- **engine**: Preferences ▸ File Handling gets **"Open color-less EXR as ACEScg"** (off by default). When on, an EXR that io tagged with the linear-sRGB default opens as ACEScg instead; a file that states its own profile (embedded ICC or a declared default) is untouched.

This is the document-source half of an ACES pipeline: renders open, convert and save through the existing CMS correctly. OCIO-config-based view transforms for display are future work; this PR deliberately does not attempt them.

## Evidence

- new engine test `exr_aces_cg_preference_retags_the_opened_document`: same EXR bytes open as linear sRGB with the preference off and as ACEScg with it on.
- `photocraft-cms` builtins test covers the new profile's encode/reparse roundtrip (26 tests green; AcesCg converts to Lab and back through the CMS).
- all four touched crates green (4903 tests), `cargo xtask wasm` clean, clippy and fmt clean; the new preference label is translated in every catalog (18/18 translation tests).

## Follow-ups

- OCIO config support (reading an `Aces_1.0.3` config's colour spaces and applying LUT-based transforms) is a separate, larger piece.
- An ACES view transform for display (the ODT half of the pipeline) would let 32-bit documents preview like the DCC's ACES viewer; tracked as future work.

title: Channels: keep the cached composite across view-only changes

body:

title: Panels: Customizable dock panels
author: D-monized
body:
Panels can be opened floating, docked anywhere, moved to their own OS windows (including another monitor) and docked to the icon bar beside the dock — and undocked again from each of those. Relates to #1828, #1379 and #4641, and the scorecard row UI-217-5 ("panel groups can float (menu + drag out of the dock)").

## What changes

**Window menu opens panels floating.** Window › <panel> for a dock panel that isn't showing opens it as a floating window (cascading, so several don't stack exactly). A panel closed while floating reopens where it was. A panel already showing keeps the usual toggle. New setting **Window › Workspace › Open Panels Floating** (on by default; off docks as before, as Photoshop does). A locked workspace never floats.

**Dock columns that make room.** Dropping a panel on the left/right edge of a docked group adds a column; the dock now **grows by a column** instead of halving its groups, and shrinks back when a column leaves (by drag, menu or command). The dock's width range scales with the column count.

**Separate OS windows.** A group's ⋯ menu has **Move to Separate Window**: the group becomes a real window (egui immediate viewport, like the screen colour picker — deferred viewports stopped the main window redrawing on Windows) that can leave the app window, e.g. for a second monitor (#4641). title: Web: show the brush preset storage banner only while a change is unsaved
author: kuvshin888
body:
## Problem

#2054 opens a usable, session-only session when the browser denies IndexedDB, and #3805 limited the top panel to storage errors so routine saves no longer move the canvas. One error case is left where the panel stays for the whole session with nothing at risk: storage denied from the start. From the first frame, before any preset has been touched, the app shows

> Brush preset changes are not saved: SecurityError: Failed to execute 'open' on 'IDBFactory': access to the Indexed Database API is denied in this context.
> Browser storage is unavailable; brushes are session-only. Keep this tab open to retain them.

Nothing has changed yet, so the first line doesn't apply. The panel can't be dismissed, and with no database there is no Retry button either. It stays above the canvas for the session, the same layout cost #3805 removed for routine saves. By comparison, preferences that can't be saved get the dismissible "Preferences can't be saved" notice.

We hit this embedding the web build in an `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts allow-downloads">` (no `allow-same-origin`). The document gets an opaque origin, and Chrome throws `SecurityError` from `indexedDB.open` (and from `localStorage`).

Cause: `Bridge::unavailable` sets the error at startup, and `WebShell::ui` shows the panel whenever `presets.error()` is set, unsaved changes or not.

## Change

- The panel shows only while there is an error **and** a preset change is unsaved (`presets.unsaved()`). A failed write requeues its records and a rejected record stays pending, so both keep the panel exactly as now. The only case that changes is "storage denied or timed out at startup, nothing changed yet", where nothing can be lost. title: Control: list and answer the unsaved-changes prompt (#4920)
author: dhiorns15
body:
## Problem

When a dirty document is closed, reverted, or the app is asked to quit, the Save / Don't Save / Cancel prompt appears in the window, but `ui.inspect` reported `dialogs: []` and nothing in the control protocol could answer it (#4920). A control client was stuck until someone clicked; only `app.quit` got out, discarding silently.

## Fix

- `discard_ui::inspect`: `ui.inspect` lists the prompt among its `dialogs` with the id `"discard"` (like the shell dialogs' `"shell"`). Its `fields` give the waiting `command` (`file.close`, `file.revert`, `file.exit`…), the `document` it asks about, how many are `remaining`, the `choices` and the `default`.
- `ui.dialog.confirm {"dialog": "discard", "choice": "save" | "dontSave" | "cancel"}` (default `save`) answers it through the same code as the window's buttons: quitting asks about each dirty document in turn, then lets the window close. Revert takes `dontSave` or `cancel`. Save of an untitled document opens the save dialog first; the reply's `fileDialog` says so and the prompt stays until that's answered. `ui.dialog.cancel {"dialog": "discard"}` cancels it.
- Before a `save` / `dontSave` answer runs the parked command, the automation policy (`Services::automation_command`) sees that command and its params, as it does for other dialog confirms.
- `ui.dialog.set` / `ui.dialog.apply` on it say to use `ui.dialog.confirm` with a `choice`.
- `docs/control-protocol.md` documents it next to the shell dialogs.

The window's own prompt is unchanged: `show` now calls the same `apply` the control path uses.

## Tests

`control::tests::the_unsaved_changes_prompt_is_listed_and_answered_through_ui_dialog`: not listed with no prompt; closing a dirty document lists it with its command and choices; a bad choice and `ui.dialog.set` are refused; cancel keeps the document; `dontSave` closes it; quitting with two dirty documents lists `remaining: 2`, then 1, and after the second answer the app may close with no documents left.

title: Layers: Ctrl+Alt+G releases the clipping mask when pressed again, as in Photoshop
author: OctaNebula
body:
## Problem

Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+G creates a clipping mask, but pressing it again on the clipped layer does nothing. In Photoshop the same key releases it: Layer › Create Clipping Mask is one menu item that reads **Release Clipping Mask** (still ⌥⌘G / Alt+Ctrl+G) while the selected layer is clipped. Here the key was bound only to `layer.createClippingMask`, which sets `clipped = true` again, and the Layer menu had a separate "Release Clipping Mask" item, with no shortcut, at the bottom of the menu.

## Fix

- **Shortcut** (`shortcut_dispatch.rs`): Create Clipping Mask's key runs `layer.releaseClippingMask` when there is nothing left to clip. That means every layer Create would clip is already clipped: the selected layer, or with several selected, every one above the lowest. This sits next to the existing Delete-key redirect (`delete_key_command`), and it follows whatever key the user assigns to Create Clipping Mask in Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts. The engine commands are unchanged, so agents, actions and the control channel still get exactly the command they call.
- **Layer menu** (`menus.rs`): the Create Clipping Mask slot reads **Release Clipping Mask** with the same shortcut, and runs it, while the key would release. The engine's separate Release item is no longer listed at the bottom of the Layer menu, so there is one slot, as in Photoshop. The right-click menu and the Alt-click on the line between layers are unchanged.

| Clipped layer selected | Not clipped |
|---|---|
| Layer › **Release Clipping Mask** Ctrl+Alt+G | Layer › **Create Clipping Mask** Ctrl+Alt+G |

title: CMYK: Brightness/Contrast curves each ink, as Photoshop does
author: timothydaly1
body:
**Stacked on #4722** (modern Brightness/Contrast's brightness curve). Until that lands, review only the last two commits.

## What

In a CMYK document, Photoshop applies Brightness/Contrast to each ink's stored value, `1 - ink`, black included, with both the modern and the legacy curve. Raising brightness therefore takes ink away, and paper and solid ink stay put. We applied it to the screen colour.

The photoshop corpus's `cmyk8/brightness-contrast.psd` and `brightness-contrast-legacy.psd` follow the rule on the files' own inks:
- modern: every pixel within 0.85 of a level;
- legacy: within 1.14 (half-level rounding).

The same probe confirms main's Lab rule (L only, a and b kept) on every pixel.

**CMYK Threshold's luma.** Photoshop's CMYK Threshold splits on the Rec. 601 luma of the inks' plain complement, `(1 - c)(1 - k)` and so on, whatever the document's profile. On the files' own inks this puts every pixel of cmyk8 and cmyk16 `threshold-128.psd` on the right side of level 128; the profile's RGB luma, which #3930 used, missed 100. `stored_channels` now works that luma out from the inks itself (`ink_luma`) instead of taking one. The engine's stored-channel path no longer converts pixels to RGB at all.

## How

- `adjust::cmyk_channel_adjustment` gains Brightness/Contrast. `apply_in`'s CMYK dispatch builds the channel curve once (`brightness_contrast_lut`: the modern table from #4722, or the legacy line) and runs each separated ink through it (`ink_through`).
- Destructive Image › Adjustments › Brightness/Contrast on a CMYK layer curves the stored inks directly, so it is exact, and a selection mixes the stored values.
  - `engine::pixels::adjusted_channels` now takes the per-pixel operation.
  - It works out a pixel's luma (a CMYK → RGB conversion) only for CMYK Threshold, which compares it.
- The GPU leaves CMYK Brightness/Contrast to the CPU, like the other ink rules.

## Measured (`oracle_diff` over `corpus/photoshop`)
