title: PSD Duotone: read and write the ink block (names, colours, curves)
author: switch87
body:
Follow-up to #4814, **on top of #4816**: until that PR is merged, this PR's diff includes its commits. The new work is the last commit.

PhotoCraft can now read and write the Duotone ink block (the PSD's Color Mode Data in Duotone mode).
- Opened duotones show their inks, not just the grey plate.
- Duotones made in PhotoCraft are saved as Duotone too. Before, they were saved as Grayscale with a warning.

## The block

The PSD specification leaves it undocumented. Photoshop 2025 writes 524 bytes; I made monotone, duotone, tritone and quadtone files with known inks in Photoshop and read the layout from them:

| offset | size | content |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 2 | version, 1 |
| 2 | 2 | ink count, 1–4 |
| 4 | 4 × 10 | ink colours, as in swatch files (`AcoColor`); space 0xFFFF = no ink |
| 44 | 4 × 64 | ink names, Pascal strings |
| 300 | 4 × 28 | curves: 13 × i16 then an i16 0, the PSD's transfer-function layout |
| 412 | 2 | dot gain, 20 |
| 414 | 11 × 10 | overprint colours, 0xFFFF = computed |

A curve's 13 values are the ink density in tenths of a percent at gray densities of 0, 5, 10, 20, …, 90, 95 and 100 %, and −1 leaves a point out. I checked the positions in Photoshop. PhotoCraft wrote a black monotone whose curve is 0 up to 60 % density and 100 % at 100 %, and Photoshop, after converting it to RGB, keeps it white exactly up to 60.4 % density.

## Changes

- **`duotone_map.rs` (new):**
  - `parse` reads the inks: RGB, CMYK, Lab and gray colours shown in sRGB, plus names and curves.
  - `write` makes the block from `Duotone::inks`. It writes RGB colours. A curve whose points lie on the 13-point grid keeps exactly those points; any other curve is sampled at all 13. It also writes the default dot gain and computed overprints.
- **Import:** interprets the inks. A colour-book ink can't be shown here, so it shows as black with a warning. The block is still kept raw (`psd_raw`) and written back unchanged while the inks are unedited, as before.
- **Export:** a Duotone wi…

title: Toolbar: clicking a tool's button again closes its open flyout (#4932)
author: dhiorns15
body:
## Problem

Right-clicking a toolbar button opens the flyout of the tools grouped with it. Clicking the same button again, with either mouse button, didn't close it (#4932). Any press outside the flyout closes it (#4460), but that check leaves out the tool button itself, and nothing else handled a click there.

## Fix

`panels.rs` toolbar: a click on the button of its own open flyout closes it, as in Photoshop.

- A right-click just closes it (right-click toggles the flyout).
- A left click closes it and picks the tool, as any click on the button does.
- The release that ends the long press that opened the flyout still keeps it open (held-button state, #4453).

## Tests

`panels::type_flyout_tests::a_drag_outside_closes_the_tool_flyout` gets the #4932 cases:
- a second right-click on the button closes the flyout;
- a left click on the button closes it and selects the tool;
- a long press opens it, and the release keeps it open.

Its `open` helper now right-clicks only when the flyout is closed, since a right-click on an open one closes it.

Fixes #4932

title: Layer Style: one dialog size on every page, and it fits short screens
author: OctaNebula
body:
## Problem

The Layer Style dialog's height jumps with each page: it is sized by its content, so Drop Shadow, Blending Options and Bevel & Emboss each make it a different height (Photoshop's keeps one size). Bevel & Emboss makes it about 732 pt tall, and nothing scrolls, so on a window shorter than that (a 768 pt laptop screen once the taskbar and title bar are taken) OK and Cancel are pushed off the bottom.

## Fix

- **One size** (`dialogs.rs`): Layer Style is drawn in a fixed-size `egui::Resize` area, the same path the web-page dialog already uses (now a small `Sizing` per dialog: size, minimum, resizable or not, outline). It is 600 × 760, the room the tallest page needs on a 900 pt screen, and no larger than the window less a margin. It is **not** resizable, as in Photoshop; the web-page dialog keeps its resize grip.
- **Fits and scrolls** (`layer_style.rs`): the effects list and the settings page each sit in a vertical scroll area as tall as the dialog leaves them, so a short window scrolls the page and OK / Cancel stay visible. The separator follows that height (it was a fixed 330 pt), and the settings column takes the dialog's width. The Styles gallery lost its own fixed 340 pt scroll area: the page scrolls now. The Blend If bars were capped at 320 pt; they span the column, so they stay under their 0 / 255 labels.

This already broke that strip on the web-page dialog on `main`. title: CMYK: adjustment layers composite on the document's own inks (14 oracles pass)
author: timothydaly1
body:
**Stacked on #4930 → #4722.** Until those land, review only the last two commits (`CMYK: adjustment layers composite on the document's own inks`, `CMYK ink compositing inlines open groups`).

## What

The compositor works in display RGB. In a CMYK document, an adjustment layer that Photoshop evaluates on the inks could only act on our separation of the RGB composite, and that separation's black differs from the file's. Even exact ink rules (#3930, #4930) missed: CMYK Invert by 10% of pixels, Levels and Curves by 50–65%.

The ink-native compositor `compose::native` already flattened plain raster stacks on their stored inks (#3855). It now takes adjustment layers too:

- **Adjustments:**
  - Invert, Posterize and Threshold use `adjust::stored_channels`.
  - Brightness/Contrast (modern and legacy) uses `adjust::ink_brightness_contrast_lut` through `ink_through`.
  - Levels and Curves on CMYK channels use `adjust::tone_luts_depth`, a table per ink on the stored value.

  Each is prepared once per composite (`InkStack`, `InkOp`) and applied to the straight inks.
- **Opacity and masks:** opacity and an unfeathered layer mask mix the inks linearly, as Photoshop does. A raster layer's mask now scales its coverage the same way, where such layers used to fall back to the RGB compositor.
- **Display:** `render_tiled_with` renders a CMYK stack of plain raster layers plus such adjustments on the inks and converts to display RGB once (`native::render_cmyk`, rows of tiles in parallel). That covers the canvas's CPU path, export and reduced views (`render_bands`, `render_reduced*`).
- **Flatten and merge:** they keep the adjusted inks exactly.
- **Groups:** a group at full opacity without a mask is inlined. Pass-through groups composite their children straight onto the backdrop, and isolated groups of raster layers alone composite as their children would. An isolated group with an adjustment, which only sees the group, keeps the RGB compositor.
- **Out of scope:** stacks of raster l…

title: io: a tagged CMYK file's merged image reads through its own profile
author: timothydaly1
body:
## What

`io::merged_composite`, the reference every oracle test compares our composite against, showed a CMYK file's merged image through the built-in coated CMYK profile. The compositor reads the same file's layers through its embedded profile (`compose::cmyk_space`). For any tagged CMYK file the comparison therefore measured two different profiles, not our rendering. The photoshop corpus is untagged and unaffected, but psd-tools' CMYK files were 88–100% off even with nothing to adjust: `colormodes/4x4_8bit_cmyk.psd`, a plain image, was 100% off.

`merged_composite` now converts inside the document's CMYK space, the same scope the compositor uses. Its only callers are tests and `oracle_diff`.

## Measured (`oracle_diff` over `corpus/psd-tools`)

| File | Bad pixels before | After |
|---|---|---|
| adjustments/invert_cmyk | 98.5% | 14.9% |
| adjustments/levels_cmyk | 95.1% | 13.9% |
| adjustments/curves_cmyk | 98.4% | 37.5% |
| adjustments/threshold_cmyk | 64.6% | 7.2% |
| adjustments/posterize_16bits_cmyk | 88.4% | 13.4% |
| adjustments/posterize_cmyk | 94.8% | 22.6% |
| adjustments/brightnesscontrast_legacy_cmyk | 99.3% | 49.2% |
| colormodes/4x4_8bit_cmyk | 100% | 6.3% |

- **Counts:** the pass count is unchanged (213/309). The io (127/170) and photoshop (145/258) corpora don't change at all.
- **With #4945:** combined with #4945's ink compositing, `invert_cmyk` and `brightnesscontrast_legacy_cmyk` pass (215/309).

title: fix(psd): prioritize 16-bit and 32-bit global layer blocks over compatibility section (#4928)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
Fixes #4928

### Root cause

When opening a 16-bit PSD file saved by Photoshop with multiple layers, PhotoCraft showed no visible layers (or only a synthesized background from the merged image). Resaving the file as 8-bit in Photoshop made all layers visible in PhotoCraft.

In 16-bit and 32-bit PSD documents, Photoshop stores the actual layer records and channel data in the global `Lr16` (or `Lr32`) tagged block. The standard Layer Info section (`li_len`) is either empty (layer count 0) or contains 8-bit compatibility layers for legacy readers.

In `crates/psd/src/file.rs`, `PsdFile::from_bytes` initialized `candidate_seen` to `layer_info.is_some()`. When `li_len > 0`, `candidate_seen` was set to `true` before reading global blocks. When `read_blocks_with` subsequently encountered `Lr16`, it skipped it as a duplicate candidate. PhotoCraft then retained either 0 layers or 8-bit compatibility records whose channels failed to decode at depth 16, resulting in empty layer surfaces (invisible layers).

### Fix

In `PsdFile::from_bytes`:
- For documents with depth > 8, prioritize the depth-specific tagged block (`Lr16` for 16-bit, `Lr32` for 32-bit) over any section layer info.
- `candidate_seen` is not set to `true` before reading global blocks when depth > 8, allowing `Lr16`/`Lr32` to replace any compatibility section records.
- For 8-bit documents, existing behavior is preserved (`Layr` in global blocks is only read if section layer info is empty).

### Tests

- `crates/psd/src/file.rs` (`write_tests::global_layers_prioritized_over_compatibility_section`): validates across PSD and PSB at 16-bit and 32-bit that when a file has compatibility section records alongside a global `Lr16`/`Lr32` block, `PsdFile::from_bytes` prioritizes the `Lr16`/`Lr32` block and decodes the actual layers.

title: Submit the open document to DeviantArt Sta.sh
author: benjarogit
body:
File › Submit to DeviantArt… uploads the open document to Sta.sh, DeviantArt's private drafts. The item sits in the File menu after Save a Copy. It is not a public gallery post. Publishing stays a separate step under More options, and it never runs on auto-save.

![File menu with Send to Telegram and Submit to DeviantArt](https://github.com/benjarogit/photocraft/raw/93bf5262/file-menu.png)

The dialog asks for a public app id, with no client secret in the binary. The redirect address is copied from the dialog. After login the button reads Connected, and Disconnect clears the login. OK uploads a PNG by default. A PSD is stored only as a file. When the upload finishes, a dialog says it stays private until published and links to the Sta.sh page.

![Submit to DeviantArt dialog](https://github.com/benjarogit/photocraft/raw/93bf5262/deviantart-dialog.png)

Get files lists Sta.sh drafts uploaded from PhotoCraft. A click opens that page. DeviantArt no longer offers an API to list or download Sta.sh files, so drafts cannot be opened back into PhotoCraft. Published works from the gallery can. One click downloads one and opens it. The refresh token stays in the OS keychain. Saving the dialog does not write an older token over the one DeviantArt just issued. The web build does not submit. The form scrolls, so the title and OK stay on screen in a short window.

## Testing

`cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib every_tl_literal_is_translated` and `complete_languages_translate_every_menu_string` passed. `cargo test -p photocraft --bin photocraft deviantart_api::` passed (5 tests). In the running app, a PNG upload opened the completion dialog with the Sta.sh link, and Get files listed that draft.

title: PSD: a version 3 Photo Filter colour is XYZ relative to the D50 white (#4940)
author: mroxso
body:
## What

A version 3 `phfl` block stores the filter colour as XYZ **relative to the D50 white** (X / 0.9642, Y, Z / 0.8249), so white is stored as (32768, 32768, 32768). We read those values as absolute D50 XYZ (#3790), which gives every Photoshop CS2 Photo Filter a slightly wrong colour.

This multiplies by the white point before converting to sRGB.

## Evidence (from #4940, verified against the reporter's attached CS2 files)

| file | stored (v3) | before | after | Photoshop preset |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo-filter-yellow.psd` | (24191, 25002, 3827) | #FFE03A | **#F9E31C** | Yellow |
| Warming Filter (85) | (15548, 12029, 0) | #F18600 | **#EC8A00** | Warming (85) |

Decoded relative to the white point, every version 3 colour in the attached files is exactly a Photoshop preset.

I also rendered the attached `blinds02-small.psd` (Cooling Filter 82) against Photoshop's own export with this build: mean abs error 4.03/255 (was 4.01) — unchanged, as the issue itself reports ("4.0 of 255 off now"). Cooling (82) is outside sRGB, so its remaining error comes from clamping the colour into gamut, which the issue lists as a separate possible follow-up (keeping the colour unclamped until `photo_filter_matrix`); that would change the semantics of `Adjustment::PhotoFilter::color` across doc/compose/gpu/UI and is out of scope here.

## Tests

- `photo_filter_golden_blocks`: the v3 white case now stores (32768, 32768, 32768); the Warming (85) case uses the real CS2 bytes; the #3777 block is asserted to decode to #F9E31C; a new Cooling (82) case pins the parse and the in-gamut clamp.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-io` green; `cargo clippy -p photocraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

Fixes #4940

title: Puppet Warp: a linked layer mask moves with the pixels (#4910)
author: DeWarePeb
body:
Fixes #4910.

Edit › Puppet Warp warped only the layer's pixels and left a linked layer mask behind, so mask and content no longer lined up. Free Transform, Warp and Perspective Warp (#3083) already move a linked mask.

**Change**
- `photocraft_algo::puppet::puppet_warp_with_mask` solves the mesh once and moves the mask on the same mesh: the mask under the mesh is lifted, deformed like the pixels and laid over the rest; the vacated area takes the mask's default, and the mask away from the mesh keeps its values.
- `edit.puppetWarp` passes the linked mask through; with a selection only the lifted part moves. Unlinked masks stay put.

**Tests**
- Engine: moved stripe at 8/16/32-bit plus undo, unlinked mask, selection (the first and last fail on main).
- Algo: hide-all mask, default left behind, mask outside the mesh untouched.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-algo -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers` green. `cargo xtask wasm` not run locally (no wasm target available); no new platform code.

**Not in this PR:** the live preview while dragging pins still shows the mask unwarped (it applies on commit). Content-Aware Scale also ignores a linked mask; I wasn't sure of Photoshop's exact behaviour there, so I left it for a follow-up.

Made with Claude Code.

title: Fix Color Balance Preserve Luminosity with multiple midtone sliders
author: Ni-zav
body:
Fixes #4941.

Preserve Luminosity previously compounded gamma adjustments independently for each midtone slider. Moving multiple sliders could therefore produce unintended brightness changes.

Calculate the midtone correction from the channel's position between the minimum and maximum slider offsets instead. This preserves existing single-slider behavior and leaves the non-preserving path unchanged.

The shared Color Balance lookup-table implementation also carries the correction into GPU rendering.

Added regression tests for multiple slider combinations, individual sliders, and Preserve Luminosity disabled.

Tests added but not executed locally.

title: Deselect layers when clicking the pasteboard with Move Auto-Select
author: Ni-zav
body:
Addresses #4923.

A click on the pasteboard previously left the existing layer selection unchanged, even when Move Auto-Select found no layer under the pointer.

Update the Move tool's empty-area marquee handling so an ordinary click outside the document deselects all layers.

Preserve the existing interactions:
- Clicking transparent pixels inside the document does not deselect layers.
- Shift-clicking the pasteboard preserves the current selection.
- Dragging from the pasteboard still creates a layer-selection marquee.

Added a focused regression test covering these interactions.

Tests added but not executed locally.

title: Preserve Dissolve coverage when compositing clipped layers
author: Ni-zav
body:
Fixes #4921.

Clipped layers using Dissolve were composited through the ordinary blend path, producing fractional transparency instead of Dissolve's binary pixel coverage.

Apply the deterministic Dissolve coverage decision before compositing clipped layers in both the CPU renderer and GPU shader.

The correction:
- Uses the source alpha, layer opacity and fill opacity.
- Produces the expected stochastic source-or-backdrop pixels.
- Preserves the clipping base's alpha.
- Uses document-coordinate noise to keep the pattern stable across rendering regions.

Added a CPU regression test for binary coverage, opacity/fill interaction and clipping boundaries, plus GPU parity cases at different opacity and fill settings.

Tests added but not executed locally.

title: Prevent control-channel engine commands from editing behind modal dialogs
author: Ni-zav
body:
Fixes #4919.

The control channel applied the existing modal-dialog guard to `ui.menu.invoke` but bypassed it for `engine.execute`. Consequently, automation could change a document while an adjustment dialog still displayed its original state.

Apply the same modal-availability policy to both command entry points.

Keep the existing Camera Raw continuation exception, which operates on its active dialog rather than issuing an unrelated document command.

Added a regression test that:
- Opens a Hue/Saturation dialog.
- Rejects Invert through both command entry points.
- Confirms the document revision and dialog fields remain unchanged.
- Verifies the command succeeds after the dialog is cancelled.

Tests added but not executed locally.

title: Validate merged PSD channel indices before decoding
author: Ni-zav
body:
Fixes #4981.

`ImageData::decode_channel` previously decoded the merged image before checking whether the requested channel index existed.

Its subsequent range calculation also used unchecked multiplication and addition, allowing sufficiently large invalid indices to overflow.

Reject indices outside the header's channel count before decoding, then calculate the channel's byte range with checked arithmetic.

Valid channel decoding is unchanged, while invalid requests return a PSD error rather than potentially panicking.

Added regression coverage for valid channels, the first out-of-range index, `usize::MAX`, and invalid-index handling with corrupt merged data.

Tests added but not executed locally.

title: CMYK: Hue/Saturation and Color Balance keep the black ink
author: timothydaly1
body:
**Stacked on #4945 → #4930 → #4722.** Until those land, review only the last commit.

## What

In a CMYK document, Photoshop applies Hue/Saturation (not Colorize) and Color Balance to C, M and Y as the complement of an RGB colour, and leaves the black ink alone. I measured this on the photoshop corpus's own inks:
- `cmyk16/hue-saturation.psd`: every pixel within half a level (cmyk8 within two, 8-bit rounding);
- `color-balance.psd`: within our RGB Color Balance's own error, which still misses the RGB oracles by up to 4 levels.

We applied both to the separated screen colour, which also rewrote K.

Colorize separates its colour again, black included (its K changes from 0 to 73 on the oracle), so it keeps the screen-colour path.

## How

- `adjust::cmy_adjustment` says which adjustments use the rule. `adjust::apply_cmy` runs the existing RGB adjustment once per band on `(1 - c, 1 - m, 1 - y)` and puts the result back with K kept.
- Callers:
  - the ink compositor from #4945 (`InkOp::Cmy`);
  - the RGB compositor's CMYK branch (`apply_in`), for stacks the ink compositor can't take;
  - destructive Image › Adjustments on a CMYK layer (`engine::pixels::adjusted_cmy`), on the stored inks with selection mixing.
- `cmyk_channel_adjustment` includes the two, so the GPU leaves them to the CPU in CMYK documents, like the other ink rules.

## Measured (`oracle_diff` over `corpus/photoshop`)

| Oracle | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| cmyk8 / cmyk16 hue-saturation | 100% bad | 0.7% / 0.4% bad |
| cmyk8 / cmyk16 color-balance | 74% bad | 26% / 25% bad |

- **Not passing yet:** at saturated cyan, half a level of C becomes about 3 levels of red through the profile, and our RGB Hue/Saturation and Color Balance models leave about that much (they pass, or nearly pass, the RGB oracles).
- **Counts:** the pass count stays at 165, and psd-tools and io don't change.

title: Large document: full CPU canvas redraws run in the background, visible part first (#4024)
author: ianswope
body:
Fixes #4024 (part 1 of the plan in https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/4024#issuecomment-6126744426).

### Problem

When the wgpu compositor can't draw a refresh (the layers exceed its memory budget, or the document uses something it doesn't cover, such as Advanced Blending), `GpuCanvas::refresh` falls back to `upload_composite`, which composites the whole document on the CPU inside the draw call. Nothing can cancel it and the window stops answering until it finishes: about 3.5 minutes on the 2.6 GB PSB in the report. Measured here with `huge_doc_bench` (20000 × 20000, 12 layers, Memory Usage 2 GB, so the 512 MB budget floor): 17–26 s per full redraw.

The same happens for an edit whose damage covers most of a large document (filling part of a layer with Blend If, which can change the composite anywhere, for example): the damage path composites it synchronously too.

### Change

- **`background_redraw` (new):** with background jobs (the desktop app), a CPU refresh of 4 MP or more goes to a worker instead of the draw call.
  - The worker composites the region in 1024 px blocks: whole render tiles, and a power of two so each block's mips are self-contained. It renders four blocks at a time in parallel, the visible ones first, nearest the view's centre first. At most four finished blocks wait for the UI thread, so a redraw holds little memory.
  - Each frame, `ensure_gpu` uploads the finished blocks (`upload_rect`). Until a block lands, the canvas keeps what the texture showed before.
  - **An edit while it runs:** a small one is drawn at once as before, then the worker restarts on the edited document with the blocks it still had to draw, so older blocks can't overwrite the edit. A large one adds its blocks to the running redraw. A full change (a new display transform, a resized canvas) starts over.
  - The status bar shows "Redrawing N%" for the active document (strings added to every catalog, including the new `sr`, `hu` and `tr`).
  - When it finishes, it…

title: PSD: a smart object's filter mask shows when the file opens
author: timothydaly1
body:
## What

A PSD whose smart object has a **filter mask** opened with the filter applied everywhere. The mask only took effect once something re-rendered the smart object, such as a transform or a filter edit. The photoshop corpus's `sf-filter-mask-hard.psd`, `sf-filter-mask-gradient.psd` and `sf-stack-blend-and-mask.psd` are the only failing smart-filter oracles, up to 0.91 off on 38–79% of pixels.

The cause: Photoshop stores a smart object's layer pixels with its filters applied but **not** its filter mask. When it composites, it mixes the unfiltered pixels back in through the mask; those pixels are cached in the global `FEid` block. We showed the stored pixels as they were. Our engine's re-render already mixes the mask in (`smart_cmds::render`), so import disagreed with it.

## How

- **`compose::filter_mask`:**
  - `mix` is the engine's former private `mask_mix`, now shared.
  - `unmix` is its inverse: the filtered pixels that mix with the unfiltered ones through the mask to a given result. Where the mask hides the filter entirely it gives the unfiltered pixels, and transparent pixels stay empty.
- **Import:**
  - `smart_map::unfiltered_from_item` decodes `FEid`'s unfiltered planes, the inverse of `feid_item`, CMYK and 16-bit Lab included.
  - A smart object whose mask shows is imported with the mixed pixels, as the engine renders them.
- **Export:** writes the layer record the way Photoshop does, unmixed against the unfiltered pixels it puts in `FEid`. Those are either the kept item (unchanged smart object) or the freshly placed source. Photoshop then mixes back to what the document showed, and re-opening the file shows the same.

## Measured

| Oracle | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| sf-filter-mask-hard | 0.66 max, 49% bad | **PASS** (0.0019) |
| sf-filter-mask-gradient | 0.63 max, 79% bad | **PASS** (0.0057) |
| sf-stack-blend-and-mask | 0.91 max, 38% bad | **PASS** (0.0020) |

- **Counts:** photoshop oracles 145 → **148 of 258**, so the floor goes 145 → 148…

title: Crop: a turned crop rotates only what the frame keeps (#5006)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5006

## What

A turned crop (`image.crop` with an `angle`) rotated the whole canvas and then cropped to the frame. With **Delete Cropped Pixels** on, `rotated_crop` now first trims every layer, layer mask and channel to the frame's source area, grown by 4 px so the bicubic kernel still reads every sample it needs. The rotation then costs about the frame's size. With Delete Cropped Pixels off, nothing changes: every pixel is kept, so everything still turns.

Rotate Canvas (`image.rotation.arbitrary`) also fills the Background with `fill_rect` (shared tiles, the same encoded pixel) instead of building a canvas-sized `f32` buffer.

The trim runs inside the crop's existing `compound` step, so it is still one undo step.

## Numbers

`cargo run --release -p photocraft-engine --example bench_crop -- <image>` (new example), on the Great Wave scan (3859×2594) + a duplicated layer:

| Crop | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Upright 512×442 | 11 ms | 11 ms |
| Turned 3°, 512×442 | 541 ms | **42 ms** |
| Turned 3°, 3000×2000 | 621 ms | 409 ms |

A large turned frame is now limited by the bicubic warp of the pixels it keeps.

## Tests

- New `turned_crop_deleting_pixels_matches_turning_the_whole_canvas`: inside the new canvas, a turned crop that deletes pixels gives exactly the same bytes as one that keeps them, for every layer, the layer mask and an alpha channel. It runs at 8, 16 and 32 bits, at 3°, −7.5°, 33° and 181°, with a 700×500 document so the frame spans several tiles.
- `crop_at_90_degrees_is_rotate_then_crop_in_one_step` now compares a pixel's colour only where its alpha is above 1e-3. The warp spreads colour into fully transparent pixels from nearby content, and the turned crop no longer turns content the crop deletes, so the invisible colour of alpha-0 pixels can differ. Alpha and every visible pixel still match exactly.

author: timothydaly1
body:
## What

In 32-bit documents Photoshop keeps these adjustments' results outside 0..1: above 1 for highlights pushed past white, and below 0. We clipped all four. Measured on the photoshop corpus's `rgb32` and `gray32` files, against the adjustment's input from our composite without the layer:

| Adjustment | Photoshop at 32 bit | Fit |
|---|---|---|
| Brightness/Contrast (legacy) | contrast pivots at **127/255** (128 in 8/16 bit), unclipped | exact on every pixel; with pivot 128 it's 0.43 of a level off |
| Channel Mixer | each source percentage **cut to 1/1024** toward zero (0.8 → 819/1024, −0.1 → −102/1024), the constant counts **255/512** of its value (5% → 25.5/1024), unclipped | exact on pure red, green, blue, black and white |
| Photo Filter | works on the linear samples, unclipped (yellow → 1.07, 0.98, −0.035) | ours is now within 0.035; the remaining difference is the filter colour, which #3790 addresses |
| Black & White tint | the Color blend mode without its clip at 1, like the blend mode in 32-bit documents (white → 1.05, 1.00, 0.87) | within 0.0002 |

## How

- **`compose::adjust`:** each of the four takes a 32-bit branch (`depth == Some(F32)`). 8/16-bit documents are unchanged, and a test checks they still clip.
- **GPU:**
  - The adjustment kernels skip their clamps under `F_HDR` (already set for 32-bit documents).
  - The planner passes the 32-bit legacy pivot and the mixer's 1/1024 steps and halved constant.
  - Photo Filter uses the matrix directly on the linear samples, and the tint uses `set_lum` without the clip.
  - `hdr_adjustments_preserve_range_and_cpu_parity` now covers all four (GPU = CPU, values above 1 kept).
- **Destructive edits:** Image › Adjustments on a 32-bit layer goes through the same code, so it behaves the same.

| Oracle | Before | After |

title: Gradient Map is driven by the W3C luminosity, as in Photoshop
author: timothydaly1
body:
## What

Photoshop's Gradient Map picks each pixel's place on the gradient by its **W3C luminosity**, `0.3 R + 0.59 G + 0.11 B`, the same weights its blend modes use. We used the Rec. 601 grey, `0.299 R + 0.587 G + 0.114 B`. The difference is a few thousandths, but on the steep stretches of a gradient it moves a pixel two levels.

On the photoshop corpus, `rgb8/gradient-map.psd` and `rgb16/gradient-map.psd` failed by just over the tolerance: 2 levels off on 0.8% and 1.65% of pixels. With the luminosity weights they pass within a level:

| Oracle | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| rgb8 gradient-map | 0.0078 max, 0.82% bad | **PASS** (0.0039) |
| rgb16 gradient-map | 0.0082 max, 1.65% bad | **PASS** (0.0021) |

Other ideas I tried did no better: sampling the gradient through a 256-, 1024- or 4096-entry table, rounding the output, and Rec. 709 weights (far worse).

## How

- **`compose::adjust`:** Gradient Map uses `photocraft_color::blend::lum`.
- **GPU:** the shader's Gradient Map kernel uses its `lum` too, so the GPU still matches the CPU.
- **Unchanged:** Lab documents keep their Gradient Map driven by L (#4038), grey pixels map as before, and Threshold and the other adjustments keep the grey they were measured with.

## Measured

- **Photoshop oracles:** 145 → **147 of 258**, so the floor goes 145 → 147. The cmyk8/cmyk16 gradient-map files, which Photoshop re-separates, move by under 0.004.
- **Other corpora:** psd-tools (213) and io (127) don't change on any file.

## Tests

- **compose:** new `gradient_map_follows_the_w3c_luminosity` maps pure red, green, blue and a mixed colour through a black-to-white map.
- **Full runs:**
  - `cargo test -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests` passes, including GPU parity for Gradient Map.
  - The photoshop corpus test passes at 147.
  - clippy (`-D warnings`) and `cargo +1.99.0 fmt --all -- --check` pass. The wasm check passes for compose and gpu.

title: fix(doc): variable definitions follow layer id remapping on copy and load
author: mroxso
body:
Closes #4969.

`VariableDef.layer` was cloned unchanged when a document was copied or reloaded with remapped ids, so datasets silently drove no layer (or a colliding one after remap).

- `reidentify_copied_layers` (engine) now remaps variable targets with the same map as layer comps, so `image.duplicate` and `history.newDocument` keep variables bound to the copied layers.
- The `photocraft-format` loader remaps variable targets through `id_map` when ids were remapped (`preserve_ids: false` or the defensive flip); preserved loads keep defs byte-identical. A dangling target gets the same non-colliding placeholder layer comps use.
- A merged-only `image.duplicate` drops the whole variable binding set (defs, data sets, active index), matching how it drops comps for the discarded template layers.

Tests:
- `crates/engine/tests/duplicate_variables.rs`: visibility/text/pixel variables remap on both copy commands and datasets drive the copy; a dangling target stays dangling; merged-only clears.
- `variables_follow_layer_id_remapping` in `crates/format/tests/roundtrip.rs`: preserved round-trip equality, remapped targets follow their layers, dangling stays non-colliding.
- All four tests fail without the fix (verified by stashing), pass with it.

title: Angle Gradient: anti-alias the wrap seam (#4933)
author: notdezzi
body:
Fixes #4933.

**Root cause.** An Angle gradient's ramp position is `(gradient_angle − atan2(−dy, dx)) / 2π mod 1`. At the 2π wrap the position jumps from the ramp's last stop back to its first stop with no interpolation, so the seam renders as a hard, aliased 360° step.

**Fix.** Only the seam is anti-aliased. A pixel whose centre lies within half a pixel's arc of the wrap (`0.5 / (2π·r)` in ramp units, `r` = distance from the gradient centre, capped at half the ramp near the centre) covers both sides of the seam, so it mixes `ramp(t)` with `ramp(t±1)` (which clamps to the first/last stop) proportionally to the fraction of the pixel beyond the seam — an exactly one-pixel-wide transition. Behaviour everywhere else, and for the other four gradient styles, is unchanged.

Mirrored in all three copies of the gradient geometry:
- `crates/compose/src/effects.rs` + `crates/compose/src/gradient_fill.rs` (CPU compositor: overlay effects and gradient fills)
- `crates/gpu/src/compose.wgsl` (GPU compositor; `gradient_seam` returns `(t, wrapped_t, weight)`, both LUT sample sites mix by the weight)
- `crates/vector/src/lib.rs` (shape fills, which carry a compose-parity-kept copy)

**Tests.** New seam tests in compose and vector: pixels straddling the wrap get intermediate values instead of a hard step; non-seam pixels are unchanged. `cargo test -p photocraft-compose` 256 passed / 0 failed, `cargo test -p photocraft-gpu` 83 passed / 0 failed (the parity suite ran on a real adapter, so the WGSL was compiled and matched the CPU oracle within 2/255 including Angle fills), `cargo test -p photocraft-vector` 58 passed / 0 failed, clippy `-D warnings` clean on all three, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` green.

**Follow-up (out of scope).** The Gradient tool's destructive drag path (`photocraft_algo::paint::tool_gradient_t`) has its own copy of the geometry and still renders an un-anti-aliased seam; it can be mirrored the same way later.

title: UI: dialogs, menus and popups fade out when they close
author: OctaNebula
body:
## Problem

Dialogs, menus, dropdowns and popups fade in when they open (egui fades every area in over the style's animation time, 0.2 s), but vanish in a single frame when they close. egui has no fade-out for `Modal`, `Popup` or plain `Area`s (only for a `Window` that is kept drawn while closing), and PhotoCraft stops drawing a closed dialog or menu at once. Photoshop's dialogs and menus fade out with the system's window animations on Windows.

## Fix

A new `fade_out` module, run once per frame after every window is drawn (`PhotocraftApp::ui`, after `native_menu::sync`):

- It remembers each foreground window drawn this frame (dialogs, menus, dropdowns, popups: egui areas of `Order::Foreground`) with its shapes.
- When one is no longer drawn, its last frame is painted on a layer of its own for one animation time, fading linearly from where it was last drawn. That layer is not an area, so it takes no input: a click where the window was goes to what is under it. Reopening the window ends the fade.
- **Interface › Enable Animations** off (animation time 0) turns it off with the fades in; it will follow #4573's system setting the same way.
- No fade when another foreground window appears in the same frame (moving between menus or submenus, a dialog that opens another), for a window drawn for one frame only, and for full-window workspaces (90% of the window or more: Camera Raw, Liquify, Adaptive Wide Angle, a modal's backdrop).
- It repaints the window's shapes, not the window's code, so a closed dialog's logic (Layer Style's preview, a filter preview) never runs again. GPU paint callbacks and images whose texture was freed with the window are left out of the fade.

Cost: about 4 µs a frame (25 µs at most) with Layer Style open on Bevel & Emboss, measured in a dev build; nothing without a foreground window. `ui.screenshot` already waits twice the animation time plus 60 ms, so captures never include a fading window.

- `a_closed_window_fa…

title: perf(paint): parallelize brush composite and rasterization for large dabs
author: lsysyem
body:
## Summary

The live brush preview runs fully sequential on the UI thread and its cost scales with the brush diameter squared, which made 8K canvases unusable with large brushes (a 1000 px soft brush cost 17.9 ms p50 / 44.2 ms p95 per input batch on an RTX 4060 Laptop — about 3 dropped frames per pen movement). Measured with a new `live_stroke_bench` example that times `LiveStroke::push` exactly as the canvas feeds it (600 points in chunks of 2).

What changed (all in `crates/paint/src/render.rs`):

- **composite**: a straight-Normal fast path runs one rayon job per raster (surface) tile — take the tile out, blend every dirty coverage tile inside it, quantize in place, put it back. Anything with stroke-level features (selection, dual brush, texture, wet edges, per-dab colour, non-Normal modes) keeps the sequential generic loop.
- **CoverageMap::accumulate**: per-tile jobs over disjoint tiles on the rayon pool; small dabs stay inline.
- **rasterize_round**: hoist `tip_shape` out of the pixel loop (it was recomputed per pixel), skip rows and spans the reach ellipse misses (same per-pixel test decides), rows parallel for dabs of 64K pixels and up.
- **small-stroke bypasses** (composite ≤ 24 dirty coverage tiles, accumulate ≤ 4) so small brushes don't pay the rayon dispatch.

The fast path is bit-identical to the sequential path (`sa >= 1` / `sa <= 0` are exact shortcuts of the over operator; the quantize step replicates `Surface::write_region`'s row conversion). One subtlety worth flagging for review: `quantize_region_into` offsets by **per-sample** bytes (`fmt.sample.bytes()`), matching `write_region` — using per-pixel bytes silently breaks 8-bit targets.

## Results (8K = 7680×4320, RTX 4060 Laptop, per push = one frame's preview cost)

| brush | before p50/p95 | after p50/p95 |
|---|---|---|
| 1000 px soft | 17.9 / 44.2 ms | **2.5 / 4.6 ms** |
| 500 px soft | 8.5 / 13.1 ms | 1.9 / 2.9 ms |
| 200 px soft | 2.4 / 3.5 ms | 1.7 / 2.8 ms |
| 120 px hard | 0.7 / 1.3 ms | …

title: Fix Free Transform Alt-scaling around moved reference points (#5019)
author: firaslamouchi21
body:
Fixes #5019

## Root cause

In `apply_drag`, Alt-scaling mirrored the dragged side around the reference point, while proportional corner and edge scaling centred the bounding box on that point. This only worked correctly when the reference point was centred. Moving it caused the bounding box to jump as soon as a drag started.

## Fix

- Calculate scale factors around an explicit anchor for each axis.
- Preserve existing normal-drag behaviour by anchoring to the opposite side.
- Use the reference point as the anchor when Alt is held.
- Preserve proportional corner scaling using the larger scale factor.
- Make the other axis follow during proportional edge scaling.
- Preserve unconstrained Shift+Alt corner scaling and single-axis Shift+Alt edge scaling.
- Handle reference points on dragged edges without infinite or NaN scale factors.
- Align drag scaling with the options bar's existing `scale_about_pivot` implementation.
- Fix shared interactions used by Content-Aware Move's Transform On Drop and the Type tool's Ctrl/Cmd-drag transform.

## Regression tests

Added `alt_scales_about_a_moved_reference_point_without_jumping`, covering stationary handle presses, moved reference points, proportional and unconstrained scaling, crossing the reference point, edge cases, and the reported pointer-interaction sequence.

The regression test fails on `main` because the bounding box moves on the initial press and passes with this fix.

## Validation

- [x] `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests` — passed.
- [x] `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed.
- [x] `cargo fmt -p photocraft-ui-egui -- --check` — passed.
- [x] `cargo xtask layers` — passed.
- [x] `cargo xtask wasm` — passed.
- [x] Manual verification in the running desktop application.

## Contributor credit

Added `firaslamouchi21` to `contributors/people.toml`.

title: Refuse rasterizing unavailable uncached Smart Objects
author: zenjabba

author: LorenzoFasolino
body:
The Italian catalog named the `Screen` blend mode **`Schermo`** — the display, which is what that
word means and how all the display strings use it (`Modalità schermo`, `Risoluzione schermo`) —
instead of **`Scherma`**, the word Adobe uses.

title: docs(perf): how to measure one scenario and read its numbers
author: LorenzoFasolino
body:
The performance section explained how to run the whole benchmark, how to add a scenario and what CI
does — but not how to measure **one** scenario, nor the traps in reading the numbers. This adds both
to `docs/development.md` §"Scorecard and performance budgets":

- `xtask perf`'s exact flags, and the fact that it has **no `--only`**: to time one row you run the
  bench binary itself (`--only` matches row names with `contains`, plus `--group` and `--reps`),
  which writes its own report and does **not** evaluate budgets.
- `--reps` defaults to 7 in `--quick` and 15 otherwise, is per bench, and some rows cap it
  themselves (the `#211` algorithm rows use `b.reps.min(5)`). Percentiles are nearest-rank, so
  **at n ≤ 5 the "p95" is simply the maximum**.
- A budgeted scenario the baseline has no row for **fails** the run (`missing` is in
  `Status::fails()`), so the `[[scenario]]` and its baseline row belong together.
- A red `cargo xtask perf` is not necessarily your budget: the committed baseline carries
  `failed.P12` (a wgpu panic writing `pc_compose_uniforms`).
- The committed baseline was written on 2026-10-05 at a load average near 225 on a 14-core M4 Pro,
  which is why P26/P27 read as over budget there while `perf/budgets.toml` records 20–45 ms p95 for
  P26 on a clean 16-core machine.
- What flipping `enforce` commits you to, and why the flip and the baseline refresh belong in one
  change on the nightly's own machine class.

Docs only: no code. `cargo xtask scorecard --check` is unaffected — `xtask/src/scorecard.rs` reads
`scorecard/*.toml`, `perf/budgets.toml`, `perf/baseline.json`, `crates/io/tests/corpus.rs`,
`crates/engine/src/prefs` and `docs/parity-checklist.md`, not `docs/development.md`.

title: Free Transform: resize cursors turn with the box and the view
author: deadmeu
body:
After rotating something with Free Transform, the resize cursor on each handle pointed the way that handle pointed before the rotation. At 90°, every corner showed the opposite diagonal and every edge the other axis (↕ on a handle that resizes left–right).

### Cause

`transform_tool::cursor` chose the arrow from the handle's index alone: corners 0 and 2 ↖↘, 1 and 3 ↗↙, edges 0 and 2 ↕, 1 and 3 ↔. That ignored the box's rotation and skew, and the view's rotation and flip.

Checked against each handle's on-screen direction, before this change (8 handles per case):

| Box turned | Normal view | View › Flip Horizontal |
|---|---|---|
| 0° | 0 wrong | 4 wrong |
| 45° | 8 wrong | 8 wrong |
| 90° | 8 wrong | 4 wrong |
| 135° | 8 wrong | 8 wrong |

So a flipped view gave wrong corner arrows even on a box that wasn't rotated.

### Change

- A handle resizes the box away from the opposite handle: corner `i` from corner `i + 2`, an edge from the opposite edge. The arrow now follows that direction as the view shows it (`ViewXform::map_vec`: view rotation, flip and pixel aspect). Because it uses the box's actual corners, it stays right after the box has been skewed, distorted or given perspective.
- The rounding to the nearest of egui's four resize arrows reuses `type_transform::resize_cursor`, which the type transform and Content-Aware Move's Transform On Drop box already use with the same opposite-handle direction. The direction passed in is already as the view shows it, so its `flip` argument is `false`.

### Testing

`resize_cursors_turn_with_the_box_and_the_view` checks all 8 handles for the box at 0°, 45° and 90°, with View › Flip Horizontal on, and with the view rotated 90°. The expected arrows are written out by hand rather than computed with the same formula. It fails on the old code (first at "box 90°, view 0°, flip false").

Checked by hand in the app: a 600 × 400 box rotated 90° with Free Transform shows ↔ on its left and right edges, ↕ on the top and bottom, and th…

title: fix(photocraft): use the wgpu low-latency surface so the cursor tracks the pointer (#1343)
author: rollroyces
body:
Closes #1343.

**Cause.** `eframe::NativeOptions`' default `WgpuConfiguration` uses `SurfaceConfig::HIGH_THROUGHPUT` (`desired_maximum_frame_latency: Some(2)`), so the presentation engine queues two frames in advance. On X11 with a discrete NVIDIA/AMD GPU that's an extra ~16 ms of cursor lag on top of vsync, and on a 60 Hz display input-to-cursor-display reaches 3-4 frames. The crosshair trails the physical mouse and brush strokes are hard to aim — particularly noticeable for an image editor where cursor precision is the whole point.

**Fix.** `SurfaceConfig::LOW_LATENCY` keeps `AutoVsync` (smoothness) but caps the queue at one frame. The change is one field in `native_options()`:

```rust
wgpu_options: eframe::egui_wgpu::WgpuConfiguration {
    surface: eframe::egui_wgpu::SurfaceConfig::LOW_LATENCY,
    ..Default::default()
},
```

`gpu_startup::configure` later mutates `wgpu_options.wgpu_setup` (backends, adapter selection, marker); the `surface` field is what we set here, and `configure` doesn't touch it.

**Test.** `native_options_uses_low_latency_wgpu_surface` asserts `desired_maximum_frame_latency` is `Some(1)` and the surface equals `SurfaceConfig::LOW_LATENCY`. `cargo test -p photocraft --bin photocraft tests::` → **94 passed, 0 failed**.

title: fix(raw): reject truncated or oversized Deflate tiles in DNG import (#4977)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #4977.

The DNG Deflate path (compression 8) in `crates/raw/src/sensor.rs` called `Decompress::decompress` with `FlushDecompress::Finish` and only handled the `Err` case. The returned `Status` was dropped, so:

- a **truncated** stream was accepted whenever the bytes it produced were enough for `unpack`;
- a stream that decodes to **more** bytes than the tile holds was silently cut at the tile size.

The inflate now lives in a small helper, `inflate_tile`, and it returns `RawError::malformed` unless the status is `StreamEnd`. This matches how the PSD importer already handles zlib (`crates/psd/src/compression.rs` rejects an "incomplete zlib stream").

Policy, as the issue asks for one:
- A complete stream that decodes to fewer bytes than the tile is still accepted, as before. `unpack` then checks whether the bytes cover the samples.
- Bytes after the end of the zlib stream are ignored, as before. Only the stream itself must be complete.

The size checks before the allocation have not changed.

## Tests

`inflate_tile_requires_stream_end` covers the cases the issue suggests:
- a valid complete stream decodes to the original bytes;
- a complete stream shorter than the tile is still accepted;
- a truncated stream is rejected;
- a stream with more output than the tile is rejected.

Before this fix, the last two were accepted.

title: Rasterize: undo the layers already converted when a later step fails (#4974)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #4974.

Layer › Rasterize (one layer or every selected layer), Rasterize › All Layers and Rasterize › Layer Style run several history steps that coalesce into one. If a later step failed (the vector-mask step after the content, or a later layer of the selection), the command returned an error but left the earlier layers rasterized and committed.

A new helper, `all_or_nothing` in `crates/engine/src/extra_cmds.rs`, now wraps the loops in `rasterize`, `rasterize_all` and `rasterize_layer_style`. If the work fails, it:

- truncates the journal back to where it was, so nothing half-done gets recorded,
- undoes until the active document is the same `Arc` it was before. The limit is the number of new history states, and at least one. A full history (50 states by default) drops its oldest state for each new one, so the number of past states does not always go up,
- clears the redo stack, and only if it undid something.

This is the same rollback that `edit.transformAgainCopy` (`edit_cmds.rs`) and `layer.frameFromLayers` (`frame_cmds.rs`) already use. On success nothing changes: the command is still one history step.

Tests (`extra_cmds.rs`):
- `failed_compound_rasterize_leaves_nothing_committed`: one layer is rasterized, then the next step fails. The fill layer is back, the history length and the journal are as before, and there is nothing to redo.
- `failed_compound_rasterize_rolls_back_with_a_full_history`: the same failure with `max_states` equal to the current history length, so the history length stays the same. Counting history states alone would miss this case.

title: Linked smart objects: don't refresh a document while a background job runs on it (#4973)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #4973.

The desktop app's linked-file watcher (`poll_link_scan` → `apply_link_stamps`, every two seconds and on window focus) doesn't go through the command conflict check. When a linked file changed while a background job ran on the same document, it applied Update Modified Content through `Session::edit`, which replaced the document snapshot, and the job's result was then thrown away as stale.

`apply_link_stamps` now returns `{updated: []}` without touching the stored stamps while `active_job()` reports a job on the document (the same check `job_conflict` uses for commands). Because the stamps aren't consumed, the first look after the job ends sees the change and applies it once. Jobs on other documents don't hold up the refresh; the watcher only ever refreshes the active document anyway.

The module docs in `link_watch.rs` describe the new wait.

Tests (`crates/engine/src/link_watch.rs`):
- `a_refresh_waits_for_a_running_job_on_the_document`: a gated job locks the document and the linked file changes. The watcher's path updates nothing and the job's snapshot stays the same `Arc`. The job then finishes, the next look applies the change exactly once, and a further look finds nothing to do. Without the fix the first look returns the layer as updated and the test fails.
- `a_job_on_another_document_does_not_hold_up_a_refresh`: a job on a second document doesn't block the refresh of the active one (a control case that passes with or without the fix).

title: fix(history): count fill caches and smart filter masks in undo memory (#4972)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #4972.

History pixel accounting (`tiles::surfaces`, used by `History::pixel_bytes`, `unique_bytes`, `trim` and the incremental tile counter) visited layer surfaces, layer masks, video frames, channels and the selection, but skipped two kinds of stored pixels:

- `Layer::fill_cache` (Photoshop-rendered pixels of fill layers)
- `SmartObject::filter_mask` (the smart filter mask)

`Layer::surface()` does not reach either, so undo states holding their tiles were left out of the history budget.

## Change

`tiles::surfaces` now also visits the fill cache surface and, for smart object layers, the smart filter mask surface. Everything goes through the same walker, so byte counting, the alias-aware deduplication (a tile shared by several states counts once) and the incremental counter used by `trim` pick it up together. Effect-cache pins, shape split caches and named snapshots (#4530) are left out of this PR.

## Test

`fill_caches_and_smart_filter_masks_count_toward_history_bytes` builds a document with a one-tile fill cache and a one-tile smart filter mask, then checks:

- both tiles are counted (fails on main, where the count is 0)
- a pixel-free edit shares the tiles, so they are counted once
- after a fill cache edit (copy-on-write), the old tile is counted as history-only
- the incremental counter matches the full recount
- with a two-tile budget, `trim` drops the oldest state and keeps the most recent one

title: fix(format): keep and list committed autosave bundles whose sidecar was never written (#4967)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #4967.

The autosave worker commits `<key>.pcraft` (manifest written last) and only then writes `<key>.json`. If the process stopped between the two on a document's first autosave, `list_recovery` never offered the document, and `sweep_orphans` deleted the valid bundle 24 hours later.

What changed (`crates/format/src/autosave.rs` only):

- `list_recovery` also lists a `<key>.pcraft` bundle that has no sidecar but has a manifest that reads. The new `sidecarless_entry` rebuilds `RecoveryInfo` from it: key from the folder name (same `sanitize` check as sidecars), document name from the manifest, `saved_at` from the manifest's modification time, no original path, revision 0. The manifest is read by the same `store::read_manifest` a load uses (migration, size and depth limits), so a document with deeply nested groups is not missed.
- `sweep_orphans` keeps exactly the bundles `list_recovery` lists. Bundles with no manifest, or a manifest that does not read, are still swept after the age threshold, as before. Fresh bundles (another instance's in-progress first autosave) are still protected by the age check.
- Bundles with anything at the sidecar path, symlinks, and bad key names are handled as before.

Test: `a_committed_bundle_without_a_sidecar_is_listed_and_survives_the_sweep` autosaves a document, deletes the sidecar (the crash after commit), and checks that the document is listed, recovers identically, and survives an aged sweep. A bundle with no manifest and one with an unreadable manifest are neither listed nor kept. The existing `sweep_removes_orphaned_bundles_and_foreign_temp_files_only` still covers fresh (active-writer) data not being swept. Without the fix, the new test fails at the first `list_recovery` assertion (0 entries).

title: fix(format): keep a replaced file's permissions from the first byte and fail the save if they cannot be kept (#4963)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #4963.

Both write paths named in the issue could leave a replaced file's bytes in a temporary file with the process default mode (e.g. 0644 under umask 022) even when the original was restricted (e.g. 0600):

- `crates/format/src/atomic.rs`: the temporary file was written first, and the target's mode copied onto it only afterwards. The result of that copy was ignored (`let _ = fs.copy_permissions(...)`), so if the copy failed the new file was still renamed into place with the looser mode.
- `crates/automation/src/workspace.rs`: the cap-std write never copied permissions at all, so a 0600 file replaced through automation became 0644.

Changes:

- `AtomicFs::write_new_like` (new trait method with a default that keeps the old behaviour for other implementors): `RealFs` creates the temporary file, sets the target's permissions on the open handle, and only then writes bytes. The temporary file never holds content with a more open mode than the target.
- `atomic_write_with_progress`: a failed `copy_permissions` now fails the save, removes the temporary file and leaves the original untouched, with the same "the original file was not changed" error style as the other failures. The `copy_permissions` doc no longer says "best effort".
- `AuthorizedWorkspace::write`: when the target exists, its permissions are set on the temporary file handle before any byte is written. A new file keeps the process default, as before. A metadata error other than `NotFound` fails the write and removes the temporary file.

On Windows `Permissions` only carries the read-only flag, so the behaviour there is unchanged apart from the flag being set before the write instead of after.

Tests:

- `a_failed_permission_copy_fails_the_save` (format, all platforms): injects a `copy_permissions` failure. The save returns `PermissionDenied`, the original bytes stay, and no temporary file is left.
- `the_temporary_file_has_the_original_mode_while_it_is_written` (format, Unix): checks the temporary file…

title: fix(engine): apply document-wide image and colour conversions to stored video frames (#4956)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #4956.

A video layer's displayed content is only a copy of the frame at the playhead. The document-wide pixel traversals skipped `VideoData::frames` and `original_frames`, so after a crop, canvas size, image size, bit depth change or profile/mode conversion, every other frame (and the original footage) kept its old geometry, depth and colour, and came back stale when scrubbing or toggling original/altered.

- `image_cmds::for_each_surface` now also visits every stored frame and every original frame. This covers the commands that already go through it: Crop, Canvas Size and artboard moves (`translate_doc`), Image Size, Bit Depth (including the tone-curve step across 32 bits), Convert to Profile / mode changes (`color_cmds::convert_document`, Duotone inking) and depth/profile matching of layers copied between documents.
- `canvas_geom::remap_pixels` (Image Rotation 90° / 180° / flips) has its own traversal with the same gap; it now remaps the stored frames too.

Both frame sets get the same transform as the displayed content, so the frame at the playhead and its copy stay in step and nothing is transformed twice.

Tests:
- `image_cmds::tests::crop_moves_stored_video_frames`: a crop that shifts the canvas moves both stored frames and both original frames.
- `canvas_geom::tests::turns_move_stored_video_frames`: a horizontal canvas flip mirrors both stored frames and both original frames.

Both fail on `main` (the frames keep the old pixel positions).

title: Close All, Close Others and Quit ask again about documents dirtied during the prompt (#4954)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #4954.

The unsaved-changes prompt for Close All, Close Others and Quit takes its list of dirty documents once, when it opens. Once every listed document had been answered, `advance()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/discard_ui.rs` ran the parked command (or let the app quit) without looking again. A document that a save or close hook dirtied while the prompt was up, or a new dirty document a hook opened, was then discarded without being asked about.

Now, before the final close, `advance()` checks the open documents again. If any are dirty, the prompt goes on with those (and shows the first one's tab) instead of closing. Close Others still leaves out the document it keeps, so a dirty target is not asked about, as before.

The other points in the issue:
- Later revisions of answered documents: with Close All, Close Others and Quit, each document closes as soon as it is answered (#2547), so an answered document cannot change afterwards. Every document still open at the end is checked again.
- Close (single document) and Revert are not changed: they only cover one document, which is asked about right before it is closed.

Tests: `a_document_dirtied_during_the_prompt_is_asked_about_before_the_final_close` covers Close All, Quit and Close Others (where the kept target also becomes dirty and is not asked about). Without the fix it fails, because the final close runs straight away.

title: Fix: native gesture fallback dedupe
author: Ni-zav
body:
Summary

Follow-up to #4786, related to #4566.

- Prevent double zoom when native "egui::Event::Zoom" and legacy Ctrl+wheel events arrive together.
- Clear legacy pinch continuation state when native zoom takes over.
- Add regression tests for overlapping gesture streams and subsequent mouse-wheel input.
- Verify native rotation event handling and preference gating.

Scope

This is a correctness improvement, not a complete resolution of #4566.

PhotoCraft currently uses "eframe" 0.36 and "winit" 0.30.13, which do not expose native Wayland pinch and rotation events. Full support requires a compatible windowing backend and hardware validation on Fedora/Hyprland.

Validation

- Branch based on upstream "main".
- Two focused input files modified.
- Synthetic regression tests added.
- CI and real-device testing remain pending.

Related: #4566, #4786.

Does not close #4566.

title: fix(ui): keep the close prompt up when a Save Document script edits the document after saving (#4953)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #4953.

When you answer Save in the close (or quit) prompt and the save runs synchronously, `discard_ui::save` released the prompt as soon as `file.save` returned `Ok` and no dialog, save options or background job was pending. But `saved_inner` runs the "Save Document" script events after it records the written revision, so a binding that edits the document (for example adds a layer) leaves it dirty again. The prompt then moved on and closed the document, and the script's edits were never written.

The synchronous `Ok` branch now checks the same thing as the deferred path (`saved_document`, used after the save dialog, TIFF Options and background saves): the original `DocId` must still be open and clean. If a hook has made it dirty, the prompt stays up and asks again, so the user can save again or discard.

## Tests

- `a_save_document_script_that_edits_the_document_keeps_the_prompt_up`: a `saveDocument` binding adds a layer. Saving from the prompt now returns false and the document stays dirty. The same save with script events off still releases the prompt (no-hook control). Without the fix the first assertion fails.
- The background-save path already had this check and is covered by `saving_from_the_prompt_waits_for_a_background_save_then_closes`.

title: fix(mixer-brush): Alt-click samples the foreground colour like the Brush (#4873)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #4873.

Holding Alt with the Mixer Brush did nothing: `alt_samples` in `canvas.rs`, which decides which painting tools turn into the Eyedropper while Alt is held, listed the Brush, Pencil, Gradient and Paint Bucket but not the Mixer Brush. This adds `Tool::MixerBrush` to that list, so Alt-click (and held or latched Alt, which go through the same check) samples the foreground colour and shows the Eyedropper cursor, as with the Brush. Control+Alt stays the brush-resize drag.

Tests:
- `alt_click_with_the_mixer_brush_samples_the_foreground` (alt_click_tests.rs): Alt-click on a red pixel with the Mixer Brush sets the foreground to red and paints nothing.
- An extra assertion in the `alt_samples` unit test.

title: Large document: large damage over the GPU budget redraws in the background; open warms layer bounds (#4024)
author: syncroot
body:
Follow-up to #5001 (merged) for #4024, as agreed in https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/4024#issuecomment-6146509922.

### Problem

Two UI-thread stalls remain with #5001 on a 16000×10000, 30-layer PSB whose layers exceed the GPU memory budget:

- **Hiding or showing a large layer freezes for 0.27–0.35 s.** `GpuCanvas::composite` checks `fits_budget` only when `region == doc.bounds()`. The damage from a layer covering most of the canvas isn't the whole canvas, so it takes the synchronous GPU path and pages every layer in on the UI thread.
- **The first draw after opening freezes for 1.6 s.** GPU planning (`Compositor::supports` → `Planner::layer_plain`) scans every layer's content bounds cold on the UI thread.

### Change

- **`gpu_canvas`:** damage of `DEFER_PX` (4 MP) or more gets the same budget check as a full refresh. Over budget, it goes to #5001's background redraw. Small edits keep the GPU path and skip the check.
- **`engine::jobs`:** the open job warms the shared tile bounds cache (`warm_layer_bounds`, cancellable between layers) before handing the document over.

### Measured

M5 Pro, macOS 26.7.1, Metal, same PSB. Each number is the longest wait for an input reply, over 2 runs. The file was opened from the command line, so it goes through the background open job.

| Step | `main` | #5001 | #5001 + this |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Open + first draw | 3.2 s | 1.6 s | 30 ms |
| Hide / show one large layer | 0.35 / 0.27 s | 0.35 / 0.27 s | 10 / 8 ms |
| Restore all | 1.6 s | 6 ms | 12 ms |

- **No hidden stalls:** status queries sent between the inputs caught no longer stall. Those queries take about 0.3 s each on every build.
- **Time to the full picture:** hide/show now finishes in 1.0–1.6 s, against 0.8 s inline.
- **Pixels:** the final canvas is byte-identical to a `PHOTOCRAFT_INLINE_JOBS=1` (synchronous CPU) run in all five steps. `main`'s GPU path differs from that reference by one 8-bit level in 3 pixels (hide) and 1 pixel (show).
- **Not cove…

title: Keep applied guide layouts visible after preview closes
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Related to #5026.

With Extras or either guide visibility flag disabled, New Guide Layout shows its preview, but applying it makes the guides disappear when the dialog closes. Reveal guides after a successful Apply; cancellation and rejected layouts preserve visibility. Turning Extras back on also reveals any other individually enabled extras.

The regression fails on upstream 6f850542 after confirming the guides were created, then passes with this fix. It covers all three visibility gates and cancel/invalid/empty-layout guards. This reproduces one cause of the reported symptom; the issue does not specify the reporter's settings.

Validation on 6fcc97f:
- 14 focused guide-layout tests passed. Full UI library/integration/doc tests: 2,700 passed, 1 failed, 12 ignored; examples passed.
- The failure is `adjustment_layer_drag_previews_at_full_resolution_when_low_res_is_off` at `full_res_preview.rs:93:52` (`render`), independently reproduced on the exact upstream base; that test is unchanged. The full suite is not green.
- Strict all-target UI Clippy, dependency layers, full WASM checks and affected-crate formatting passed.
- Fresh native DX12 snapshot captures inspected: preview visible with Extras disabled; confirming closes the dialog and leaves the guides visible. Control logs contain no command errors.

AI assistance: Codex implemented and verified this patch for jonathnwxh.

title: Swatches: importing an .ase file numbers repeated group names in linear time
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## Why
`swatches.import` named each imported group with `unique_group` (`crates/engine/src/presets/gradients.rs:652-655` on `main`), which compares a candidate name with the library's groups one by one and tries "Name", "Name 1", "Name 2" and so on until one is free. Groups without a name all take the import's group name (`crates/engine/src/swatch_cmds.rs:507`), so an `.ase` file with n unnamed groups costs about n³/6 string comparisons. On `main`, importing the new test's file of 9,994 unnamed groups took about 4.5 minutes of one core in a `cargo test` build. `swatches.import` does not run as a background job, so Import Swatches… in the Swatches panel and File › Open run it on the UI thread.

## Change
- `import` builds the set of the library's group names once and keeps the next number to try for each repeated name, as the swatch loop in the same function already does for swatch names. Group numbers still start at 1, and each group gets the same name as before. `unique_group` and its other callers are unchanged.
- `UniqueNames` in https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/pull/644 also resumes the numbering of each repeated name where it stopped. Its numbers start at 2.
- The change adds an implemented control: the work of naming imported groups grows linearly with the number of groups.

## Tests
- New `unnamed_groups_are_numbered_in_linear_time` imports a file of 9,994 unnamed groups into a library that has a group named "Ink 2", on a thread of its own, and fails when the import takes more than 20 seconds. It checks that the names run "Ink", "Ink 1", "Ink 3", "Ink 4" up to "Ink 9994" and that they are unique. Without the change it fails at the 20-second limit; with it, the test finishes in 0.01 s.
- New `repeated_group_names_take_the_first_free_number` checks the names when a group in the file has a name that the import already gave to an earlier group. It passes with and without the change.

title: feat(input): Ctrl scroll acts as pinch preference for touchpads that send whole-notch pinches (#2463)
author: josephebarrera
body:
Addresses #2463.

## Problem
Some touchpad drivers (older ELAN and Synaptics) send a pinch as Ctrl + a **whole** wheel notch. That is byte for byte what a mouse wheel with Ctrl held sends, so since #635 those pinches scroll the canvas sideways instead of zooming, and PhotoCraft cannot tell the two apart. This is the option suggested in the #2463 thread.

## Change
New preference **Enhanced Controls › Ctrl scroll acts as pinch** (`enhancedControls.ctrlScrollActsAsPinch`).

- **Off by default**, so mouse users keep Photoshop's Ctrl + wheel = sideways scroll. Nothing changes for anyone who doesn't turn it on.
- **On**: every Ctrl + wheel event becomes a pinch step at egui's Ctrl-scroll zoom speed, whole notches included.
- Only Ctrl + wheel is touched; plain, Shift and Alt wheel keep their meaning. It still honours *Zoom with Trackpad Pinch*.
- `wheel_nav::legacy_pinch_to_zoom` keeps its exact behaviour and delegates to a new `ctrl_wheel_to_zoom(.., always)`.

## Testing
- **Real hardware:** verified on a Windows 11 laptop touchpad whose pinch previously scrolled sideways. With the preference on it zooms; off, it scrolls sideways as before.
- New unit tests: whole notches zoom with the preference and scroll without it, other modifiers are untouched, and an end-to-end test through egui.
- `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, and the `wheel`, `prefs`, `i18n` and `input_tests` UI tests pass.
- `prefs_ui::shortcut_capture_tests::ctrl_k_is_recorded_as_ctrl_k_not_the_control_key` crashes with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` on my Windows machine. It crashes identically on unmodified `main`, so it is unrelated to this change.

title: Actions: add editable PhotoCraft Essentials starter presets

body:

It detects the subject on the active pixel layer, excludes subject coverage from Gaussian color sampling, and blends the result inside the current selection. It preserves transparency, selection, masks, other layers and off-canvas pixels, with one Undo. No detected subject or cancellation commits no edit. This avoids a recorded Subject → Inverse → Blur sequence accidentally using an old selection after detection fails.

title: Menu bar from the keyboard: Alt / F10 focus, Alt+letter, underlined mnemonics (#4988)
author: FabioLissi
body:
Fixes #4988. The in-window menu bar (Windows and Linux; macOS keeps the native bar) now works from the keyboard the way Photoshop's does on Windows.

## What

- **Alt or F10 put the keyboard on the bar**: File is lit, ← and → move along the bar (wrapping), ↓, Enter and Space open the lit menu with its first row lit, Esc or any click leave. A second Alt tap leaves too, and an Alt tap closes an open menu.
- **Alt+letter opens that menu**, whether another one is open or not (Alt+F → File, Alt+E → Edit …).
- **In an open menu, a letter runs the row with that mnemonic** or opens its submenu (with its first row lit).
- **Mnemonics are underlined** while Alt is held, the bar is focused or the menu was opened from the keyboard; a menu opened with the mouse shows none until Alt is pressed, as Windows does. Disabled rows stay dim (the underline uses the placeholder colour), and without underlines the text path is byte-for-byte what it was.
- **Assignment** is per menu level from the labels as shown (so it follows the UI language), unique within the level: Photoshop's F E I L Y S T V W H for the top menus where the label has the letter, else the first unused letter, trying word starts first. Only ASCII letters and digits, since those are the keys the keyboard reports as keys; a Japanese or Chinese label without one has no mnemonic rather than a wrong one.
- The shortcut dispatcher defers to the focused bar as it already does to an open menu, so E opens Edit instead of picking the Eraser and the arrows don't nudge the layer.

New module `crates/ui-egui/src/menu_keys.rs`; `menu_nav::Row` carries its mnemonic; `menus.rs` draws the focused title and the underlines; one line in `shortcuts.rs`. Agents can drive it: `ui.key {"key": "AltLeft"}` is the tap, `{"key": "F", "alt": true}` the shortcut (noted in `docs/control-protocol.md`).

After an Alt tap and →, then Alt+F:

title: Canvas: themes without a dot pattern draw no dots texture (#4542)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #4542.

Switching the dark theme to Pro filled the empty workspace with red and black blocks.

### What the screenshot shows

The blocks in the issue's screenshot repeat exactly every 22 px in both directions, and only two colours occur: `(255, 40, 40)` and Pro's canvas colour `(40, 40, 40)`. 22 px is the tile of the canvas-surround dots texture (`dots()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, a 22×22 repeating texture), and nothing else in the empty workspace is tiled. So the pattern is that texture, drawn with contents it was never given: the image built on the CPU is transparent apart from four grey texels.

### The change

Pro has no dot pattern: its `canvas_dot` token equals its `canvas` token, which is how eleven of the fourteen themes say "no dots". They still uploaded a texture for it and tiled it over the whole pasteboard, relying on it being invisible.

`dots()` now returns `None` when `canvas_dot == canvas`, as it already did for the bevel (Classic) theme, so those themes upload and draw nothing there. Studio, Studio Light and Solarized Dark, whose dots differ from the canvas, are unchanged.

Two small side effects of no longer drawing an "invisible" texture:

- In the Pro themes the dots were not quite invisible: premultiplied rounding left a grid of `(39, 39, 39)` pixels on the `(40, 40, 40)` canvas. Those are gone.
- In Full Screen Mode the backdrop is black rather than the canvas colour, so themes without a pattern showed their canvas-coloured dots on it. They now show plain black.

### What this does not establish

I could not reproduce the red blocks. On Windows 11 with DX12 (release build, `--control`, isolated `PHOTOCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR`), switching `interface.darkTheme` between `proMedium`, `pro` and `studio` rendered correctly every time. Nothing in PhotoCraft or in egui-wgpu's upload path writes such data, so why that texture came up wrong on the reporter's machine (a GPU or driver problem with the upload is my guess, not a finding) is still open…

title: Count document patterns in history budgets
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Related to #4972; complements #5075.

A pattern fill or layer style copies its pattern into the document (`pattern_cmds::ensure_in_doc`), and PSD import keeps a file's patterns there too. The tile visitor behind History's byte budget (`crates/ops/src/tiles.rs`) skipped `Document::patterns`, so their pixels were left out of the budget, trimming and the bytes Edit › Purge › Histories reports. That includes a pattern only the redo states hold after an undo.

Visit `Document::patterns` in the shared visitor. Direct totals, the incremental counter and trimming all go through it, and a pattern shared by several states still counts once. #5075 adds fill caches and smart filter masks to the same visitor for #4972; with both, every `Surface` field in the document model is visited. The two change different lines and merge in either order, and with both applied `cargo test -p photocraft-ops` passes 17 tests.

Like layer tiles shared between documents, a pattern that the pattern library also holds counts in each document that uses it. The canvas's GPU budget (Memory Usage minus the document's pixels and History) subtracts these bytes too.

The regression test fails on `main` (`pixel_bytes` is 0 with a pattern in the document) and passes here at 8, 16 and 32 bits. It adds the pattern in a Pattern Fill step, then checks sharing across states, undo leaving the pattern to the redo states, redo, and the incremental counter against a direct count after each step.

### Validation

Windows x86_64, Rust 1.99.0, base `6f850542`, tested commit `afafc5fb`:

title: Performance: brush dab on a CMYK document within budget (#5108)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5108 (scorecard P33, part of #5106 and #211)

## Root cause
Measured first, with the app's own `GpuCanvas` on A4 2480×3508 CMYK, 40 px dabs, 60 reps in release:
- `paint.stroke`: 0.39 ms p50
- `GpuCanvas::refresh`: 4.79 ms p50, 9.22 ms p95, always on the GPU path (`gpu-rect`, no fallback)
- `device.poll`: 0.09 ms
- The same probe on RGB 8-bit: 0.38 ms p50 for the refresh

The cost scales with the tiles uploaded: about 5 ms per 256×256 tile. `convert_tiles` → `convert_tile` (`crates/gpu/src/lib.rs`) sends each of a tile's 65,536 pixels through the CMYK → sRGB transform (`photocraft_raster::to_rgba`, about 75 ns per pixel) on one thread per tile. A dab that crosses tile corners uploads 2–4 tiles; that is the p95 tail.

## Change
- CMYK and Lab tiles that become 8-bit or half-float texels are converted in 16-row bands as flat parallel jobs, with no nested rayon. Even the single tile a dab touches now uses every core. Other formats keep the existing one-job-per-tile path.
- A run of bitwise-identical pixels, such as the transparent area around a dab, is converted once. The same input bits give the same output, so the result doesn't change.
- **Colour fix found along the way:** each band now enters the CMYK profile scope of the calling thread (`active_cmyk_space` / `with_cmyk_space`). On main, the rayon workers in `convert_tiles` never entered it. So the GPU tiles of a CMYK document tagged with its own profile were converted through the built-in coated CMYK instead of the document's profile. Untagged documents, including P33's, were unaffected.
- `photocraft-cms` becomes a dev-dependency of `photocraft-gpu`, for the synthetic profile in the test.

## Numbers
P33 (`brush dab on A4 300 ppi CMYK + refresh`), release, Windows 11, 32 threads, RTX 5070 Ti. The machine was under background load (about 31 % CPU from parallel builds), so before and after were run interleaved:

| Row | Before (main) | After |
