title: Large documents: a gigapixel New Document draws without freezing (#4017)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4017 (part of #5106)

## Root cause
`file.new` isn't the slow part: it's already lazy and takes 70–165 ms even at 157,480 × 78,740 px (20 × 10 m at 200 ppi). The freeze comes from the first canvas refresh after it. Measured in the real app over `--control` (release, Windows, 32 threads, RTX 5070 Ti, 128 GB RAM, throwaway config dir), plus headless timings:

1. **CPU canvas.** When the canvas is over the GPU texture budget (RAM/4: 12 GB on a 48 GB Mac, less than the ~16.5 GB a 3.1 GP canvas needs), the reduced CPU canvas (`compose::render_reduced`) composited every document pixel at full resolution before averaging down about 20×. For a plain white 10 × 5 m document that is 3.1 billion composited pixels, 23–25 s with every core busy. That matches the report: the 20 × 10 m document froze, and at 10 × 5 m the system lagged so much the mouse wouldn't move.
2. **GPU canvas.** Where the budget allowed the GPU path, the ~16 GB of canvas textures failed with an uncaught `Out of Memory`. Device health then disabled the GPU for the whole session, and the CPU canvas froze the UI for 25.2 s.

## Change
- **`compose/src/uniform.rs` (new) and `render_reduced`.** This path applies only when every layer's composite at a pixel depends only on its own surfaces at that pixel: raster layers, groups, per-pixel adjustments and unfeathered masks.
  - Documents with effects, Dissolve, feathered masks, dithered adjustments, fill/shape/text/smart layers, artboards or Multichannel mode take the existing path unchanged.
  - On the document's tile grid, a tile where every surface holds one value is composited once per combination of values, then summed per run of output columns.

  - Damage renders give exactly the same pixels as the whole reduction.

title: DNG: decode lossy (JPEG-compressed) DNG tiles (FILE-215-11)
author: FabioLissi
body:
Lossy DNG (DNG 1.4 compression 34892: baseline-DCT JPEG tiles or strips of 8-bit samples, gray for CFA, YCbCr for three-sample LinearRaw) now decodes the way the spec describes it. The arm from #2021 widened every decoded sample by 257, so the values no longer matched the file's own levels: an 8-bit WhiteLevel (or its default, 255) clipped everything to white and a 256-entry LinearizationTable was indexed past its end. It also required the JPEG frame to match the clipped row count, which rejected the padded edge tiles real tiled files carry. This closes the "lossy DNG" part of FILE-215-11; the scorecard row itself is left for the coordinating branch.

## What

- `crates/raw/src/sensor.rs`: the 34892 arm is now `lossy_jpeg()`. Decoded 8-bit values are the stored samples; BlackLevel, WhiteLevel (default 255 for 8-bit data) and the LinearizationTable apply to them exactly as for every other compression.
- Tiles may be coded at the full tile size (edge tiles padded, as DNG 1.4 says) or at the image's row count; strips at their row count; the width must be the segment's.
- BitsPerSample must be 8 and the JPEG's component count must equal SamplesPerPixel (1 or 3); anything else is `Unsupported` / `Malformed`, never a silent conversion.
- The frame header is checked before any pixel is decoded, and zune-jpeg's own size cap is the segment the IFD declares (already charged against `Limits`), so a hostile SOF cannot size a buffer past the tile.
- `testgen`: `LossyJpegTiles` writes true 8-bit fixtures, new `LossyJpegStrips`, `lossy_segments` (pre-encoded segments for hostile tests), `baseline_jpeg()` public, `white = 0` leaves WhiteLevel out.
- Docs: `docs/file-format-parity.md` DNG row and revision history, `crates/raw/README.md`, the lib.rs summary.

## Verification

- `crates/raw/tests/dng.rs` (37 green): `lossy_jpeg_cfa_tiles_and_strips_decode_stored_values`, `lossy_jpeg_linearraw_rgb_tiles_and_strips_decode_stored_values` (37x23: partial edge tiles and a short last strip)…

title: fix(puppet-warp): drop open Puppet Warp and other distort sessions when the active document changes (#5092)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #5092.

**Cause.** The Puppet Warp session (like Liquify, Perspective Warp, Vanishing Point and the Filter Gallery) lives in app-wide `app.distort`, not on the document. `distort_ui::display_doc` shows the session's `preview_doc` for whatever document is active, so after closing the file, creating a new one or opening a saved one, the canvas kept showing the old document's Puppet Warp preview instead of the new document's layers, until the app was restarted.

**Fix.** `Distort` now notes the document its open sessions belong to (`owner`, a `DocId`). The new `distort_ui::drop_foreign` runs at the start of `canvas::document_area` and `distort_ui::show`. When the active document is no longer that one (closed, a new one created, another one opened or switched to), it drops the open sessions, just as Esc cancels them. Nothing is applied to the old document. Doc ids are never reused, so a new document can't be mistaken for the closed one.

This covers every way of reaching the bug in the report: close (with or without saving), File > New and opening a saved file. All of them change the active document.

**Test.** `puppet_ui::tests::session_is_dropped_when_another_document_becomes_active` starts Puppet Warp, creates a new document and checks that the old preview was shown there (the bug) and is gone after the fix. It then starts Puppet Warp again on the first document, closes that document and checks that the session is dropped.

title: fix(layers): merging layers keeps pixels that lie outside the canvas (#5067)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #5067.

**Cause.** Merge Layers built the merged layer with `pixels::composite_layers`, which intersects the area it renders with the canvas. Any pixels of the selected layers that lay outside the canvas were lost, so the merged layer was cropped to the visible area. Merge Down (`pixels::merge_down`) and Merge Group (`commands::merge_group`) used the same function and cropped in the same way.

**Fix.** The new `pixels::composite_layers_uncropped` renders the union of the layers' composite bounds without cropping it to the canvas. Each layer's bounds, grown by the reach of its layer effects, are added to the area first, so `composite_bounds` does not cut a layer or its drop shadow at the canvas edge. Merge Layers, Merge Group and Merge Down now use it. Merge Down into the Background still crops, because the Background stays canvas-sized. Merge Visible, Flatten Image and the stamps are not changed.

**Test.** `layer_multi_cmds::tests::merge_keeps_pixels_outside_the_canvas` merges two layers that extend past the top-left and bottom-right corners of the 100x80 canvas. It checks that the merged layer spans both of them and that pixels outside the canvas are still opaque. Without the fix the merged layer is cropped to 0,0-100,80. `merge_down_and_merge_group_keep_pixels_outside_the_canvas` checks the same thing for Merge Down and Merge Group.

title: Camera Raw: Calibration panel, Auto, raw sidecars and live Camera Raw Defaults (FILE-215-11)
author: FabioLissi
body:
Three quick items of G14 (Camera Raw depth), moving FILE-215-11 from missing to partial. Independent of the other open PRs; it only shares the scorecard and gaps docs with #5112 (lossy DNG, whose evidence this PR's scorecard note already cites).

## What

- **Calibration panel**: Shadows › Tint and Red / Green / Blue Primary › Hue and Saturation, as a develop stage in linear light. A pixel's hue turns by the weighted Hue of the primaries it is made of (triangular weights at 0°, 120° and 240°; ±100 is ±30° towards the next primary) and its saturation scales by their weighted Saturation; luminance is kept, so neutrals are untouched. The shadow tint is magenta or green weighted by darkness, luminance kept, white untouched. The seven `crs:` keys (ShadowTint, RedHue … BlueSaturation) load and save with the settings file, and `filter.cameraRaw` takes `shadowTint`, `calibrationHue`, `calibrationSat`.
- **Auto**: the Light panel's button (and `"auto": true` on the control channel) sets Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites and Blacks from the image's luminance histogram, and the sliders show what it chose. The *Apply auto tone* preference opens a raw with it.
- **Raw sidecars**: a raw opened from a path reads `IMG_0001.xmp` beside it into the open-time dialog (the status bar names what the loader skipped, e.g. the absolute kelvin white balance, which has no counterpart), and Open writes the sidecar back when the settings aren't the defaults or one exists; never beside a DNG, off with the new *Write xmp sidecars* preference. With *Open in Camera Raw* off the sidecar still develops the file.
- **Camera Raw Defaults are live**: the six preferences the dialog hid as dead (#204) now act when a raw opens, with or without the dialog: colour space (a conversion from the develop's ProPhoto; Adobe RGB by default, as Photoshop's workflow options), bit depth, resolution (300 ppi), Sharpen For (folded into the Camera Raw step as 25/1.0, 35/1.2 or 40/1.0), Open as Smart Object,…

title: Legacy Brightness/Contrast: Photoshop's 8-bit table around level 127 (six legacy oracles exact)
author: timothydaly1
body:
## What

Legacy Brightness/Contrast ("Use Legacy") now matches Photoshop exactly. Photoshop builds it as a table of the 256 levels that scales contrast around **level 127**, not 128:

| Contrast | Level `i` maps to |
|---|---|
| raised (≥ 0) | `127 + round((i + brightness − 127) · 255 / (255 − L))` |
| lowered (< 0) | `127 + round((i − 127) · (255 − L) / 255) + brightness` |

- `L` is |contrast| % of 255. At 8 bits it is truncated to whole levels: 30 % gives 76, not 76.5.
- Halves round away from the pivot. psd-tools +20/+57 has two ties, 96 → 101 and 118 → 153.
- **16-bit** keeps the fraction of `L`, but Photoshop's result still lands exactly on 8-bit levels (every value in rgb16 and gray16).
- **Lab16's L** and **32-bit** follow the line itself.

The old `1 / (1 − c)` slope around 128 came out up to 2 levels dark.

## Evidence

The rule was fitted on every level of the corpus's Photoshop-authored legacy oracles.

| Oracle | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| photoshop `rgb8/brightness-contrast-legacy.psd` (+25/+30) | 0.0039 | **0.0000** |
| photoshop `gray8/…` | 0.0039 | **0.0000** |
| photoshop `rgb16/…` | 0.0034 | **0.0000** |
| photoshop `gray16/…` | 0.0034 | **0.0000** |
| psd-tools `brightnesscontrast_legacy_rgb.psd` (+20/+57) | 0.0078, 2.38 % bad, **DIFF** | **0.0000, PASS** |
| psd-tools `brightnesscontrast_legacy_grayscale.psd` (−23/−26) | 0.0039 | **0.0000** |

- psd-tools corpus: 237 → 238 pass, so I raised the floor from 236 to 238.
- Photoshop oracles: 145, unchanged. io corpus: 148, unchanged.
- **Lab** files stay DIFF, as on main. On the *stored* Lab, the new rule is exact: every L byte of lab8 matches, every L of lab16 matches, and 0.00 % of pixels are bad, checked with a throwaway probe on the raw channels. What remains is our display-RGB round trip, which clips out-of-gamut colours (the worst pixels have a channel pinned at 0 or 255). That round trip also moves their bad % a little: lab8 goes from 5.12 % to 5.70 % (max unchanged at 0.0371), and lab1…

title: fix(engine): list the document's layers when a layer id or name is unknown
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #5058

## What
- A command that fails because a layer id isn't in the document now says which layers there are, top-down, as id and name (at most 20, then a pointer to `document.inspect`):
  `no such layer 1; the document's layers are 2 "Background" (a `layer` param takes an id or a name)`
- An unknown layer *name* gets the same listing.
- A layer name that matches no layer exactly now matches regardless of case, so `"layer":"background"` finds the Background. An exact match still wins.
- Ids are not renumbered.

## Why
Layer ids are not positions: a freshly opened PNG's Background is layer 2, so `layer.setProps {"layer":1}` failed with `no such layer LayerId(1)`, and the only way to find the real ids was `document.inspect`. An agent can now recover from the error message alone.

## How
`Session::dispatch` turns an `EngineError::NoLayer(id)` for an id the active document doesn't have into the new `EngineError::UnknownLayer { id, known }`. Its message keeps the `no such layer` prefix that existing checks look for. The one test that matched `NoLayer(_)` for a missing id now matches `UnknownLayer`.

## Tests
- New `crates/engine/tests/missing_layer_error.rs`: an unknown id lists the ids and names, an unknown name lists them too, case-insensitive name fallback, an exact name wins over a case-insensitive one.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests`: all green.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo fmt` clean; `cargo check` of automation, CLI, ui-egui and the app is fine.

title: Levels: whole levels at every step and Photoshop's shadow toe (levels_rgb + stack oracle pass)
author: timothydaly1
body:
## What

Levels now matches Photoshop level for level in 8-bit documents. Two changes:

1. **Every step rounds to a whole level.** In 8 bits Photoshop rounds each of the three Levels steps to a whole level, half up:
   1. the input-range stretch (we already did this);
   2. the midtone gamma;
   3. the output range.

   A narrow output range therefore merges neighbouring gamma levels. psd-tools `levels_rgb.psd` maps R 43..48 to **58**: a 0.47 channel gamma, then the master's 48..255 output. The unrounded curve gave 56..59, and blue was 3 levels off.
2. **Photoshop's shadow toe.** Above gamma 1, the power curve `u^(1/g)` is infinitely steep at black. Photoshop starts instead along a toe `a·u − b·u^q` of slope **a = 2^gamma**, which joins the power curve with the same value and slope (`q = 2.2`, fitted; see below). It replaces the soft-min (p-norm) toe.

   Gamma below 1 stays the plain power curve: every level is exact at gamma 0.67 and 0.7.

## Evidence

I read the gamma step off every Levels oracle whose other steps are known. These are single-stage or channel-then-master regions of:
- psd-tools `levels_rgb` and `levels_grayscale`;
- the photoshop corpus's `rgb8` and `gray8` `levels.psd`;
- the measured 0..255 ramp at gamma 2.0 in `levels_matches_photoshop`.

| Model (with the rounding) | Levels wrong of 1118 (gamma 1.16, 1.22, 1.3, 1.78, 2.0) |
|---|---|
| pure power | 21 |
| soft-min toe (main) | 52 |
| **toe of slope 2^g, q = 2.2** | **2** (each 1 level: gamma 1.78 at 52, and the gamma 2.0 ramp at 16) |

`q` between about 2.15 and 2.25 gives the same result; 2.2 is the middle.

| Oracle | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| psd-tools `levels_rgb.psd` | 0.0118, 0.16 % bad, **DIFF** | 0.0039, **PASS** |
| photoshop `rgb8/stack-levels-curves-hue-posterize.psd` | 0.2000, **DIFF** | **0.0000, PASS** |
| photoshop `rgb8/levels.psd`, `gray8/levels.psd` | 0.0039 | **0.0000** |
| photoshop `rgb16/levels.psd`, `gray16/levels.psd` | 0.0039 / 0.0041 | 0.0020 |

title: Add ML Select Subject (local model) and Generative Fill (user-chosen provider)
author: sdobke
body:
Closes part of G15 in `docs/gaps.md` (ML Select Subject, Generative Fill). I know owner decision #41 (model licences, local vs remote) is still open, so I kept both choices swappable and nothing is bundled in the repo. Happy to adapt this to whatever you decide.

## What it does

**ML Select Subject / Remove Background**
- Local IS-Net general-use ONNX model (Apache-2.0; ONNX export by rembg, MIT), run on the CPU by the pure-Rust `tract` runtime.
- The model is **not** in the repo: it is downloaded once into the user's cache folder, with a pinned SHA-256 (`PHOTOCRAFT_MODEL_DIR` overrides the folder for offline installs).
- Falls back to the existing classical algorithm when the model is missing or fails. New `engine` param (`auto|classic|model`); `PHOTOCRAFT_ML=off` disables it. Runs as a background job. Tests, CLI and scripts stay offline by default; only the desktop app enables auto-download.
- On photos the selection follows edges and fur much more closely than the heuristic.

**Generative Fill** (Edit menu + button next to Select Subject)
- Sends a crop around the selection plus a prompt to a provider the user picks: Cloudflare Workers AI (free tier), a local AUTOMATIC1111/Forge server, Gemini, OpenAI/compatible, or Stability. Nothing is sent until Generate.
- The result goes on a new pixel layer masked by the selection (one undo step). Empty prompt removes the selection's content.
- Credentials are **not** preferences: API keys and account ids live in a separate `ai-credentials.json` in the user config folder (owner-only on unix; in memory only until an app enables the file, so tests/CLI/scripts never write it) or come from `PHOTOCRAFT_<PROVIDER>_API_KEY`. The file is the single source of truth, saves merge under a lock, and no command returns a key.

title: feat(engine): layer.list, a read-only listing of the layer tree
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #5059

## What
A new read-only command, `layer.list` (new module `crates/engine/src/layer_list_cmds.rs`):

```
photocraft-cli run some.png --cmd layer.list
{"activeLayer":2,"layers":[{"active":true,"bounds":[0,0,8,6],"id":2,"kind":"Pixel","name":"Background","selected":true,"visible":true}]}
```

- Layers top-down (Layers panel order): `id`, `name`, `kind`, `visible`, `bounds` (`[x,y,w,h]`, a group's is the union of its children, null for fill/adjustment layers), `selected`, `active`.
- Groups list their `children`. With `"flat": true`, every layer is one row with its `depth` and `parent` group id.
- Takes the same optional `"document"` index as `document.inspect`. It is not journaled and doesn't change the document. Nesting is depth-bounded.
- Documented in `docs/control-protocol.md` next to `document.inspect`.

## Why
The layer list was only in `document.inspect`, together with history, channels and much more, so agents went looking for a `layer.*` command that didn't exist.

## Tests
- `layer_list_cmds::tests`: ids/names/kinds/visibility/bounds/active and group nesting, the flat form with depth and parent, that it's a query (revision and journal unchanged), bad params (`flat` not a bool, bad or missing `document` index, no document) are errors.

title: Free Transform: Alt moves the pivot, it snaps to the box, Alt-scale keeps it
author: Furash
body:
## Snapping with an active selection
- Each layer's snap edges come from its full bounds, not the part inside the selection. Before, every layer (the Background too) offered edges along the selection, so a Free Transform box on a selection stuck to its own outline: the pivot and the box wouldn't move, and snap lines were drawn on the box border.
- What a move drags is still the selected part.
- A box dragged from inside no longer snaps back to the selection it started from.

## Moving the pivot
- The pivot is grabbed only with Alt held:
  - Alt-press on the pivot drags it, even when it sits on a corner or edge handle.
  - Alt-press anywhere else in the box puts the pivot there.
  - A plain press on the pivot moves the box like any other press inside it; a plain press on a handle always takes the handle.
- The cursor shows a crosshair only when Alt is held over the box.
- Dragging the pivot snaps the pivot itself, not the box's bounds (before, a pivot drag snapped as if the whole box were moving, so the pivot stuck).
- The pivot snaps to the box's nine points: four corners, four edge midpoints and the centre, measured on the box as drawn, so it works on a rotated box. Snapping to other layers' edges and guides still applies. Holding Ctrl during the drag, or turning snapping off, disables it.
- While Alt is held or the pivot is dragged, a dot marks the box's centre.

## Alt-scaling around the pivot
- Alt-dragging a handle scales around the pivot: the dragged side sets the factor and the opposite side moves by the same factor, so the pivot keeps its position in the box. Before, the dragged side was mirrored around the pivot, which recentred the box on it.
- Works for edges and corners, proportional and with Shift. If the pivot lies on the dragged edge's line, that direction can't scale and stays put.

## Snap lines
- Snap lines are drawn after the transform preview and the other overlays, so the moving pixels no longer cover them (a draw-order change only, no extra wor…

title: Control: event log, `events.poll` long polls and pushed subscriptions (#4939)
author: FabioLissi
body:
Closes #4939.

Tools driving PhotoCraft had to re-inspect the whole document after every command to learn what changed. This adds an event log to the engine and exposes it on every transport: polling everywhere, long polls and pushed subscriptions on the TCP control server.

## Engine

- `photocraft_engine::events`: `Event {seq, event, document, source, time, data}` in a bounded ring (4096) with a `gap` flag for readers that fall behind. Kinds: `document.opened` / `closed` / `activated` / `saved` / `changed`, `selection.changed`, `layers.selected`, `history.changed`, `tool.changed`.
- `dispatch` takes a `Snapshot` of the active document before a command (a background job carries its own) and `after_command` diffs revision, damage rect, layer ids added/removed, selection bounds, active/selected layers, history length (step / undo / redo / clear / trim) and saved revision.
- `Session::add_document`, `close`, `set_active` log opened / closed / activated. `Session::document_saved(index, path, revision)` is the one place saves are recorded (the UI's background save and headless `doc.save` use it), since `file.saveAs` is not an engine command.
- Only committed changes are logged, never previews.

## Control channel (`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs`, `apps/photocraft/src/control_server.rs`)

- `events.poll {since?, limit?, events?, documents?, waitMs?}` → `{events, next, gap}`. `waitMs` (≤ 25 s) long-polls on the desktop server: the server re-asks the app every 50 ms until something arrives.
- `events.subscribe {events?, documents?, since?}` → `{subscribed, next, events, subscribers}`: matching events are pushed on the same connection as JSON lines without an `id`, between replies, once a frame. A subscribed connection is no longer closed for being idle. A reader that stops reading loses events, not frames: the per-connection queue holds 1024 and a `{"event":"gap","dropped":n}` line reports the loss once there is room. `events.unsubscribe` or closing the connection ends it.…

title: fix(psd): preserve editable text round trips with Photoshop
author: David2766
body:
## Problem

Editing and saving PSD text can produce files Photoshop cannot open correctly, or lose editable type information on a later round trip.

The exporter can replace a complete document-wide text object (`Txt2`) with a text/kerning stub. EngineData serialization can turn opaque binary strings into Unicode, and import does not fully recover styles stored only in the global model. Exhausting the available `TextIndex` slots can also assign an index the writer silently skips.

## Fix

- Write current global character/paragraph models and valid views from the emitted local type data (`TySh`). Preserve recognized complete unchanged native objects, stable indices, frames and unaffected siblings.
- Preserve opaque EngineData byte strings, including malformed UTF-16 payloads. Actual Unicode text retains its UTF-16 encoding.
- Recover a matching global-only model at document DPI when local EngineData is missing or malformed. Keep valid local styles authoritative, resolve inherited kerning/OpenType flags, and reject invalid recovery atomically.
- Validate paragraph ancestry and run references iteratively. Fresh Normal paragraph styles have no parent. Narrowly repair the known factory self-loop introduced during development of this writer; reject other cycles.
- Reject exhausted text-object capacity and invalid supplied indices before producing an incomplete global model. Preserve the highest valid index and untouched native objects, including unreferenced occupied slots.
- Propagate errors through fallible PSD/layered-TIFF conversion and nested conversion. Preserve the outer Smart Object path's existing warning-and-pixel fallback contract.
- Make minimal existing upstream lint cleanups, preserving behavior and adding focused regression tests.

Complete valid output replaces #3529's fresh-Metrics omission workaround and extends #2427/#3747. Based on main at `6f850542`, retaining its newer font, text-path, style-validation and PSD-padding changes. #4771 touches adjacent …

title: fix(geom): clamp huge sizes in Rect::from_xywh instead of wrapping, and saturate TileCoord::rect
author: saadkhantareen
body:
## What was wrong

In `crates/geom` (L0 geometry):

- `Rect::from_xywh` cast the `u32` width straight to `i32`. Widths above `i32::MAX` wrapped negative and produced an empty, inverted rect instead of clamping the far edge to `i32::MAX`. For example `from_xywh(0, 0, u32::MAX, 10)` produced `x1 = -1`.
- `TileCoord::rect()` multiplied deserialized coordinates by `TILE_SIZE` in `i32`, which panics on overflow in debug builds for extreme (hostile/corrupt) input.

## What changed

- `from_xywh`: widen to `i64` and clamp the far edge to `i32::MAX`.
- `TileCoord::rect()`: use `saturating_mul`.
- Two regression tests: `from_xywh_clamps_huge_sizes_instead_of_wrapping` and `tile_rect_saturates_on_extreme_coords`.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p photocraft-geom` — 23 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo fmt --check` clean, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-geom --all-targets` clean.
- Regression check: with the fix temporarily reverted, both new tests fail (wrong rect `x1: -1`; multiply-overflow panic). With the fix restored the suite is green again.

Only the affected leaf crate was built/tested.

title: Masks: feathers blur with exactly the feather's variance (mask-parameters-no-real-channel passes)
author: timothydaly1
body:
## What

Feathered masks now render as Photoshop draws them.

We render a mask feather as a Gaussian with sigma = feather, approximated by three box blurs per axis. The boxes had whole-pixel radii, which rounded the variance:

| Feather | Old blur equivalent |
|---|---|
| 6 px | 6.48 px |
| 3 px | 3.46 px |

As a result, feathered edges were too soft, by up to 4 levels against Photoshop.

Each pass is now an **extended box** (Gwosdek et al., *Theoretical foundations of Gaussian convolution by extended box filtering*, 2011). It gives weight 1 to the whole radius and a fractional weight to the one sample beyond it on each side, so three passes have variance σ² exactly. The GPU compositor uses the same mask (`masks::combined_mask`), so both stay in step.

## Evidence

On psd-tools `mask-parameters-no-real-channel.psd` (a 6 px vector feather and a 3 px pixel feather), I recovered Photoshop's mask from its merged image and compared candidate blurs against it in 2-D:

| Blur | Max error | Pixels > 2/255 |
|---|---|---|
| whole-pixel boxes (main) | 4.3 | 4.0 % |
| exact Gaussian, σ = feather | 1.95 | 0 % |
| **extended boxes, σ = feather** | **1.5** | **0 %** |
| Gaussian, σ = 0.83 × feather | 9.3 | 12.7 % |

| Oracle | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| psd-tools `mask-parameters-no-real-channel.psd` | 0.0168, 4.31 %, DIFF | **0.0060, PASS** |
| psd-tools `layer_mask_data.psd` | 0.0743, 26.94 % | 0.0368, 3.89 % |
| psd-tools `layer_mask_data.psb` | 0.0547, 25.88 % | 0.0263, 1.78 % |

Nothing else changes in any corpus.
- psd-tools corpus test: 239 → 240 pass; floor 236 → 240.
- The photoshop and io corpora are unchanged.
- What remains wrong in `layer_mask_data` is on its shapes' antialiased edges.

## Performance

The pass is still O(n). The low-end weight reuses the sample leaving the window, so each sample still costs two clamped reads. Measured with `benchmark_50mp_mask_blur` (50 MP at a 1000 px feather):

| Blur | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| parallel | 172 ms | 18…

title: Lab: adjustment layers composite on the stored L, a and b (seven Lab oracles pass)
author: timothydaly1
body:
## What

Some adjustments in Lab documents now match Photoshop even on saturated colours. Photoshop applies Invert, Posterize, Threshold, Brightness/Contrast, and Levels or Curves with Lab records to the document's own L, a and b.

Before, the compositor read a Lab document's layers through display RGB (`lab_to_srgb`). That clips every colour outside the sRGB gamut, so those adjustments only saw the clipped colours. The existing `apply_lab` round trip then added their change in RGB. The photoshop corpus's Lab oracles were up to 11 levels off on saturated colours.

The new `compose::native_lab` works such a stack out on the **stored values**, the same way #4945 does for CMYK inks:

- **Layers:** Normal mixes L, a and b linearly, as Photoshop does in Lab. An opaque layer keeps its values exactly, and an unfeathered layer mask scales the mix.
- **Adjustment layers:** each pixel goes through the new `adjust::lab_stored_op`, which reuses the existing Lab rules (`stored_channels`, the L tone curves, the Lab tables of Levels and Curves) at the layer's opacity and mask.
- **Groups:** a pass-through or Normal group at full opacity without a mask is inlined. An isolated group holding an adjustment is not.
- **Display:** stacks with such adjustment layers render this way (`render_lab`). The GPU already sends these adjustments to the CPU in Lab documents (`adjustment_on_gpu`), so app display follows too.
- **Flattening:** `flatten_lab` keeps the stored values of any plain Lab stack, so exports no longer clip out-of-gamut colours.
- **Everything else keeps the RGB compositor:** other blend modes, effects, vector or feathered masks, clipping, and other adjustments such as Hue/Saturation or Photo Filter.

## Evidence

All corpora were measured with `oracle_diff` against current `main`.

| photoshop oracle | main | this PR |

| `lab16/invert.psd` | 0.0314, DIFF | **0.0003, PASS** |
| `lab16/posterize-4.psd` | 0.7292, DIFF | **0.0059, PASS** |

title: Linux: Arch Linux package (.pkg.tar.zst)
author: willheisenberg
body:
## What

Adds an Arch Linux package to the Linux release formats. `packaging/linux/package.sh` gains the format `arch`, on by default, which builds `photocraft-<version>-linux-<arch>.pkg.tar.zst` with nfpm's `archlinux` packager from the same staged tree as the `.deb` and `.rpm`.

Install and remove:

```sh
sudo pacman -U photocraft-<version>-linux-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst
sudo pacman -R photocraft
```

## Why

There was no native option for Arch and its derivatives (Manjaro, EndeavourOS, CachyOS): the choices were the AppImage, the Flatpak bundle or unpacking the tarball by hand, none of which pacman tracks.

## How it reaches a release

The shared release workflow runs `packaging/linux/package.sh` without a format list and uploads everything in `dist/release`, and it already installs nfpm 2.47.0, so the package joins the x86_64 and aarch64 assets with no workflow change. The riscv64 job passes `--formats "deb rpm tar"` and is unaffected.

## Details

- **Dependencies** use Arch package names. pacman has no alternative dependencies, so both `vulkan-icd-loader` and `libglvnd` are required where the `.deb` asks for one of them.
- **No install script.** pacman hooks refresh the desktop, MIME and icon caches. The cache script moved from the top level of `nfpm.yaml` under the `deb` and `rpm` overrides, so those two packages keep it.
- **Licences** are also installed to `/usr/share/licenses/photocraft`, as Arch expects.
- **File list instead of `type: tree`.** nfpm 2.47 gives the directories of a tree a mode with Go's directory bit (`20000000755` in `.MTREE`), and pacman then warns "directory permissions differ" for every directory on install. `package.sh` writes one entry per staged file for the Arch package, so nfpm creates the directories itself as 0755.
- **Whole-second mtimes.** nfpm rounds mtimes in the archive but truncates them in `.MTREE`, which made `pacman -Qkk` report most files as changed.
- **Pre-releases:** `0.2.0-rc.1` becomes `0.2.0rc.1`, which pacman sorts be…

title: PSD: Mt16/Mt32 blocks mark the merged image's transparency (no spurious Transparency channel)
author: timothydaly1
body:
## What

PhotoCraft now recognises the merged-transparency marker Photoshop uses for 32-bit PSDs. Opening such a file no longer adds a spurious "Transparency" alpha channel, and the corpus oracle no longer treats its transparent areas as opaque white.

A PSD's merged image carries its transparency in its first extra channel in either of two cases:
- the layer count is stored negative, or
- a "Saving Merged Transparency" global block (`Mtrn`, `Mt16`, `Mt32`, Adobe's file-format spec) is present.

Photoshop saves 32-bit documents the second way: a positive layer count, `Mt32`, and a fourth channel named "Transparency" (psd-tools `transparentbg.psd` and `.psb`).

`PsdFile::merged_has_alpha` only checked the layer count, which had two effects:
- **Opening such a file** turned that channel into a user alpha channel named "Transparency" in the Channels panel.
- **The corpus oracle** (`merged_composite`) treated the merged image as opaque, comparing white against our transparent pixels.

It now also checks for the global blocks.

## Evidence

| psd-tools | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `transparentbg.psd` | 1.0000, 83.67 % | 0.2161, 0.91 % |
| `transparentbg.psb` | 1.0000, 83.67 % | 0.0812, 0.47 % |

What remains is on the shape's top and bottom edges, where our coverage is slightly fuller. That's a separate geometry question. No other file in the three corpora changes, so the pass counts and floors stay where they are. Round trips are unchanged.

## Tests

`mt32_marks_the_merged_transparency` builds a 32-bit file the way Photoshop saves it: positive layer count, `Mt32`, and a fourth channel named "Transparency". It checks three things:
- `merged_has_alpha` is false without the block and true with it;
- the merged composite's alpha comes from that channel;
- opening the file adds no alpha channel.

It fails on main.

Checks run:
- `cargo test -p photocraft-psd -p photocraft-io`
- the corpus test
- `cargo clippy -D warnings`
- `cargo xtask wasm`
- the touched files are r…

title: Smart Sharpen: remove Lens Blur and Motion Blur by deconvolution (#4866)
author: zuujiscom
body:
## What

Smart Sharpen was a Gaussian unsharp mask. This gives it Photoshop's **Remove** menu, so it can undo lens and motion blur by deconvolution (#4866):

- **Gaussian** is unchanged. Saved filters and smart filters without the new fields keep decoding as Gaussian.
- **Lens Blur** runs Richardson–Lucy deconvolution with a disc point-spread function, for an out-of-focus lens.
- **Motion Blur** runs the same with a line at an angle; **Angle** is its direction.
- **More Accurate** runs three times the iterations (24 instead of 8).

New command parameters on `filter.sharpen.smartSharpen`: `remove` (`gaussian|lens|motion`), `angle` (-360..360), `moreAccurate` (bool).

## How

- The blur and correlation steps of each iteration run by FFT, so the cost does not depend on the radius and Photoshop's whole 0.1–64 px range works. The pixels are real, so rows are transformed at half length and only half the spectrum is kept (half the work and memory). Native builds use `rustfft` (already a dependency). The browser build uses a small in-place mixed-radix FFT (`sharpen/smallfft.rs`: radix-4, 2, 3 and 5 passes, the same 2-3-5-smooth sizes), because `rustfft`'s planner pulled the web wasm over the 24 MiB gate: with `rustfft` it was 25,194,635 bytes (limit 25,165,824; `main` is 25,014,166); with the small transform it is 25,033,527, +19,361 over `main`. The small transform is tested against `rustfft` across 31 lengths and through the whole deconvolution, and both engines give the same picture.
- Browser speed, measured as wasm in Node (RGBA, Lens Blur, 8 iterations): 1024×768 at radius 3 takes 0.80 s, 2048×1536 takes 3.18 s; a complex `rustfft` in wasm took 1.88 s and 5.87 s on the same images.
- The layer is processed in blocks of at most 3072 px (2304 px in the browser) with an apron of up to 768 px, so memory stays bounded on large layers. Within the apron a tile agrees with a whole-layer run.
- Colour is deconvolved premultiplied, one channel at a time; alpha is untouched. Neg…

title: Curvature Pen: edit finished paths (drag, add, smooth/corner) with an adaptive cursor
author: bazmarth
body:
## Summary
In Photoshop, the Curvature Pen edits a finished path directly, with no modifier. PhotoCraft only allowed edits while the path was still being drawn; once it was closed or finished, a press started a new path and the anchors weren't shown.

Now, with no path being drawn, the Curvature Pen works on the **active path** (work path, active shape layer or targeted vector mask):
- **shows its anchors**;
- **drag an anchor**: it moves and the curve reflows. Every smooth knot of that subpath gets its handles recomputed with the Curvature Pen's own `curvature_knots`, so neighbouring segments move too; corners keep their handles, so a Pen-drawn polygon keeps straight sides;
- **click a segment**: adds an anchor there (`path.addAnchor`), and a drag pulls it straight away; adding and dragging are **one history step**;
- **double-click an anchor**: toggles smooth ↔ corner and reflows, so a Pen corner rounds off and the segments around it curve through it; a second double-click makes it a corner again;
- **adaptive cursor**: a **+** badge over a segment (a click adds an anchor), **four arrows** over an anchor (a press drags it), also on the anchors of the path being drawn; nothing over empty canvas (a click starts a new path).

Every drag previews live and commits exactly the preview. Editing the path being drawn is unchanged, and Ctrl/Cmd is still Direct Selection.

title: Vector: bound flattening memory, keep over-budget dashes, cheaper edge build (#5195)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #5195
Fixes #5211

## Root cause
- **Flattening memory (B1).** `flatten::pieces` allows up to 65536 pieces per cubic and nothing capped a whole path. Paths that never pass `validate_shape` (PSD `vmsk` vector masks, compose vector masks, SVG import, effect outlines) could ask for about 1e9 points and abort on allocation.
- **Vanishing dashed strokes (B2).** When `dash_polyline` exceeded its 100000-step guard (or stalled below coordinate precision), it returned an empty list, so the whole stroke disappeared.
- **NaN edges (B4).** In `Rasterizer::add_component`, coordinates around ±1e308 overflowed the edge slope to infinity. `x_at` then returned NaN at the edge's top, which dropped that boundary and filled the row.
- **Unbounded stroke outline (#5211).** Stroke expansion after flattening had no budget. A round cap is a full circle of up to ~629 points (the `arc_step` floor of 0.01 rad, reached on wide strokes), every dash gets two, and the 100000-step dash guard applied per polyline. A wide round-capped dashed stroke from an SVG `stroke-dasharray` or a PSD `vstk` could therefore reach ~1e8 outline points, and many subpaths multiplied that further.

## Changes
- `flatten`: there is now one point budget per path (`1 << 20`). Past it, each curve keeps a proportional share of its pieces, at least one. This works like a larger tolerance and does not depend on the small-curve tolerance clamp in `pieces`. `flatten_path` and `fill_rasterizer` use one budget for the whole path, and `flatten_subpath` bounds itself. Paths under the budget flatten exactly as before.
- `stroke::dash_polyline`: past the step budget it keeps the dashes made so far and draws the rest of the polyline solid. On closed outlines the solid tail still joins the first dash at the seam. Open polylines are now borrowed instead of copied (`Cow`).
- `raster`: polygon coordinates are clamped to ±1e15, far outside any `i32` pixel rectangle. An edge whose slope is still non-finite is vanishingly short, and l…

title: PSD import: flat fallback respects the decode budget; checked sizes (#5200, #5202)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #5200
Fixes #5202

## Root cause

**#5200.** In `psd_to_document_with`, the non-layered branch (Bitmap, Indexed, Duotone, 1-bit files) called `file.composite_rgba8().or_else(..)`. The fallback, written for Multichannel, ran for *every* error. That included `PsdError::LimitExceeded`, which `composite_rgba8` returns when `width * height * 4` is over `MAX_DECODED_BYTES`. The fallback then ran `vec![255u8; n * 4]`, the same allocation that had just been refused. A large 1-bit Bitmap PSB, a tiny file whose merged plane decodes fine (e.g. 50000x50000, all white RLE), aborted the app with an OOM. The same block also:
- cloned the whole merged image (`merged.clone()`);
- sliced planes without `get`;
- collected a full-size `Vec<f32>` (`n * channels * 4` bytes) where it could convert a band at a time;
- dropped a failed composite silently, so the document opened empty with no warning.

**#5202.** Several file-derived sizes were multiplied unchecked. They overflow a 32-bit `usize` (wasm32):
- `unicode_names`: `n * 2`;
- `psd_to_document_with`: `w * hh` and `row_bytes() * hh`. A 1-bit plane can decode within the budget while `w * hh` does not fit in 32 bits;
- `adjust_map::parse_gradient_map`: `be32 as usize * 2`.

## Fix

- New `flat_composite(file, merged, cap)`:
  - `LimitExceeded` propagates. Only other errors (Multichannel) reach the fallback.
  - The fallback checks `w * h * 4` against `cap` and reserves fallibly.
  - It borrows the merged image and reads planes through a checked `merged_plane` helper.
- `write_rgba8` converts into the surface in `TILE_SIZE` row bands.
- `flat_background` now checks opacity a band at a time (it read the whole surface into floats) and stops at the first transparent pixel.
- The RGBA8 buffer is dropped before that check.
- A composite that can't be read now gives a warning. A merged-image decode failure is already reported, so it isn't reported twice.
- Sizes use `checked_mul`/`checked_add` in `unicode_names`, the merged plane offset…

title: PSD: cap pattern memory across a parse, reject mixed-depth pattern channels (#5198)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #5198

Follow-up to #3652 / #3686, from a read-only audit of `crates/psd`.

## Root causes and fixes

**Pattern memory budget was per pattern only** (`patterns.rs` `read_pattern`). The decoded-bytes cap (`MAX_DECODED_BYTES`) and the zero-padding cap (512 MiB) were counted per pattern. Nothing totalled them across a `Patt`/`Pat2`/`Pat3` block, a `.pat` file (up to 100000 patterns), repeated pattern blocks in one PSD, or the `patt` sections of an `.abr`. A 1x1 raw channel in a 23170x23170 gray pattern is about 100 input bytes and commits 512 MiB of zeros, so N copies get the process OOM-killed.
- New public `patterns::PatternBudget` and `patterns::parse_pattern_block_with(data, &mut budget)`. `parse_pattern_block` and `parse_pat_file` keep their signatures. Each one now uses one budget for the whole parse. The budget is charged before any plane is decoded, and only for blocks that parse successfully.
- `io::pattern_map::from_global_blocks` now shares one budget across all pattern global blocks of a document.
- `.abr`: `patt` sections are now charged to the same 512 MiB budget as the samples. **Behaviour change:** before, `.abr` patterns had their own allowance (8 GiB decoded, 512 MiB padded). A brush file whose samples and patterns together exceed 512 MiB now drops its patterns with a warning instead of loading them. That matches what happens to samples.

**Mixed-depth pattern channels were accepted.** `PsdPattern.depth` was taken from the last channel, while earlier planes kept the size of their own depth. The parsed pattern then could not be written back: `write_pattern_block` followed by a re-parse fails, which is the `expect` in `fuzz/fuzz_targets/patterns.rs`. A channel whose depth differs from the first one is now rejected. I scanned every PSD/PSB in the pinned corpus (680 pattern blocks, 24 patterns) and none fails.

**Slice descriptor numbers wrapped** (`slices.rs`). `LargeInteger` and `Double` values were cast with `as i32` / `as u32`, so a sliceID of 2…

title: PSD import: ResolutionInfo is pixels per inch whatever the display unit (#5201)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #5201

## Root cause

`psd_to_document_with` multiplied the ResolutionInfo (resource 1005) `hRes`/`vRes` by 2.54 when `hResUnit`/`vResUnit` was 2 (cm). The Adobe Photoshop File Formats Specification defines `hRes` as Fixed 16.16 **pixels per inch**. The unit that follows is only the unit Photoshop *displays* the resolution in. `photocraft_codecs::resolution::photoshop_resolution` already reads it that way ("Fixed 16.16 hRes / vRes are pixels per inch whatever display unit follows them"). The `psd::ResolutionInfo` field doc said "pixels per inch/cm", which is probably where the conversion came from.

Evidence from Photoshop-authored files in the pinned psd-tools corpus. Each stores a round ppi value together with unit 2:

| File | hRes | hResUnit |
|---|---|---|
| `artboard.psd` | 300.0 | 2 |
| `empty-layer.psd` / `empty-layer.psb` | 72.0 | 2 |
| `empty-group.psd` | 72.0 | 2 |

If the value were pixels per cm, these would read 118.11 and 28.35. Before this PR, PhotoCraft opened `artboard.psd` at 762 ppi and the others at 182.88 ppi.

## Change

- `psd_import.rs`: use `ri.h_res()` / `ri.v_res()` directly.
- `psd/src/resources.rs`: the `ResolutionInfo` doc comments now say the value is ppi and the unit is for display.

## Tests changed (this reverses an assertion from #1445)

Two existing tests asserted the old conversion: 100 "px/cm" with unit 2 opened as 254 ppi. Both now assert that 300.0 with unit 2 opens at 300 ppi:
- `crates/io/tests/resolution_axes.rs`, `psd_with_equal_axes_opens_silently`. This part came with the merged #1445.
- `crates/io/tests/psd_structure.rs`: `resolution_in_cm_converted` is renamed to `resolution_with_cm_display_unit_stays_ppi`.

With the old code restored, the updated `psd_structure` test fails with `762` (verified).

## Commands

```
cargo test -p photocraft-io --test resolution_axes --test psd_structure
cargo test -p photocraft-io --features corpus --test text_corpus --test corpus
cargo clippy -p photocraft-io -p photocraft-psd --…

title: fix(ui): guides draw over the Free Transform preview, under its box (#5086)
author: sabbirshawon
body:
Fixes #5086

## What was wrong

The lines covered in the report are **guides** (the ruler strips themselves were never covered). `canvas_view` drew the grid and guides, then `transform_tool::draw_overlay`, which painted the moving pixels of the Free Transform preview over them. In Photoshop guides sit above the image, including a layer being transformed, and the transform box and handles sit above the guides.

## Fix

- `transform_tool::draw_overlay` is split in two:
  - `draw_content` draws image content only: the preview mesh (plain, styled or warped), the Content-Aware Scale result, and the layers above the moving one.
  - `draw_overlay` keeps the box, handles, reference point, path outline, warp grid, control points and split guides.
- `canvas_view` calls `draw_content` right after `paint_canvas`, before the grid and guides; `draw_overlay` stays where it was, after them. The hand-pan drag path does the same.
- No behaviour change other than draw order: `pv.committing` still hides the box only.

## Test

`canvas::tests::guides_draw_over_the_transform_preview_and_under_its_box` opens Free Transform on a 100×60 layer with a vertical guide through it and checks the painted shape order: preview mesh < guide line < box outline. Before the fix it fails (`the guide (5) draws over the transform preview (6)`); after it passes.

Checked locally: the new test (fails before the fix, passes after), `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`. The full `photocraft-ui-egui` suite passed on the pre-rebase base except one existing test that looked for the preview mesh in `draw_overlay`; it now calls `draw_content`. On this commit the `photocraft-ui-egui` lib suite passes (2683 tests); the integration tests are left to CI.

## Not in this PR

`cam_transform`, `distort_ui` (Puppet Warp, Perspective Warp) and `perspective_crop_ui` draw their previews after the guides too; the same split would fix them.

title: IO: smart-object source sizes from WebP/GIF/BMP/EXR headers, not a full decode
author: vangel76
body:
From the crates/io audit (finding O3). No user-visible bug, so no issue.

## What changed
`linked::source_size_probe` (the source size a `PlLd` record leaves out) already read PSD/TIFF/PNG/JPEG sizes from their headers, but decoded every other embedded file in full just to learn its width and height.

New `photocraft_codecs::probe_size(bytes)` returns the upright size `decode` would return, from headers only:
- WebP: the container chunks (`image_webp::WebPDecoder::new`), same `limits.check` and `check_plausible` as decode (shared `open` helper)
- GIF/BMP/TGA/ICO/QOI/HDR: the `image` crate decoder's header (shared `open` helper with decode, same limits and `check_bytes`)
- flat OpenEXR: the part decode picks (`pick_part`), refused when that part has no colour/Y channels (decode refuses it too)
- EXIF orientation 5-8 swaps the size, as `finish_decode` does

Deep EXR, AVIF (its decoder decodes on open) and other formats return `Unsupported`; `source_size_probe` then falls back to the full decode as before.

## Behaviour
The probe runs only checks that decode also runs, so wherever the old decode succeeded the size is identical. One difference: a file with a valid header but a corrupt or truncated body used to give no size and now gives its header size, as the existing PNG/JPEG/TIFF/PSD branches already did.

`source_geometry` is unchanged on purpose: it also needs the resolution, which comes from the import path (pHYs, EXIF/XMP, TIFF tags, layered TIFF, .pcraft), and a header probe would have to replicate those rules.

## Tests
- `codecs/tests/orientation.rs` `probe_size_matches_decode`: for every read/write format, `probe_size` equals `decode`'s size where it answers, every probed format answers, and a file cut inside its header is refused
- `webp_opens_upright`: probe returns the upright size for orientations 3/6/8
- `io` `linked::tests::source_size_probe_reads_headers`: now also WebP, GIF, EXR, TGA, plus truncated headers give `None`
```

title: IO: ABR fit and gradient bake check their own bounds (io audit S1)
author: vangel76
body:
From the crates/io audit (finding S1, the indexing sweep). No reachable crash, so no issue.

## What changed
- `abr_map::fit` (box downsampling of brush tips and pattern tiles) computed `(y + 1) * h / nh` in u32. For a plane taller than 2^32 / `max` rows that overflows: a panic in debug builds, wrong rows in release. The ABR (8192) and pattern (30000) parsers' edge caps keep real input below that, but the guard lived in another crate. The spans are now computed in u64, with the same formula.
- `gradient_bake::eval` indexed `stops[0]`, `stops[n - 1]` and `stops[i + 1]`, relying on `bake`'s check that there are at least two stops. It now handles an empty list or a single stop itself, including one at a NaN position that neither end test catches.

Results are the same for every input that worked before.

## Sweep scope
I checked every `indexing_slicing` site in crates/io/src outside files that open PRs touch (psd_import, psd_export, pixels (#2580), exr_parts, adjust_map, blocks, effects_map, smart_map, multichannel_map, comps_map, lib, flat, tiff_layers, pattern_map, linked (#5216)). The sites left in annotations_map, vector_map, channel_map, affinity and the rest of abr_map are guarded right where they occur (`take(n)` readers, `chunks_exact`, `position`, length-filtered planes), so they are unchanged.

## Tests
- `abr_map::fit_tests::fit_tall_planes_without_overflow`: a 1 x 5,000,000 plane fits to 1 x 1024 with every row averaged. It panicked with "attempt to multiply with overflow" before the change.
- `gradient_bake::tests::eval_with_fewer_than_two_stops_does_not_index_out_of_range`

title: panic_hunt: count panics that Session::execute contains (#4982)

body:

## Problem

`Session::execute` catches a command's panic and returns an ordinary `Err` (the last-resort guard in `crates/engine/src/jobs.rs`).
So the unwind never reached `panic_hunt`'s own `catch_unwind`, and a command that panicked counted as a pass.
The never-panic gate (Rule 9) could not see the panics it exists to find.

## Solution

- `panic_hunt` installs a panic hook once that counts every panic in the process, on any thread (rayon workers included), then calls the default hook.
- A run fails if the count moved while it ran, whether the panic unwound to the harness or was contained.
  Graceful `Err`s still pass.
- Runs are serialised by a mutex, so a panic is charged to the run that caused it.
- Test-only: no production code changes, and no matching on error-message text.

## How checked

- New fast test `contained_panics_count_and_graceful_errors_do_not`: a panic caught inside the run fails it, and `layer.delete` on a missing layer (a graceful `Err`) passes.
  The first assertion fails with the old classification (checked by reverting it).
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored`: the full registry fuzz stays green (18.9 s), so no command panics on these params today.
- `cargo fmt -p photocraft-engine -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --tests -- -D warnings`.

## Not in this PR

Third-party decoder panics that `photocraft-heif` and `photocraft-raw` contain on purpose would also count if a fuzzed command reached them.
None do with the current params.

- **O1, `ImageSourceData::to_bytes`** (tiff.rs): the global layer mask and every global block were cloned, data included, only to set padding to 4. title: Type: hovering a font previews it with the Character section shown too (#5152)
author: prekabreki
body:
Fixes #5152

## Problem

Hovering a font in the Type tool's options-bar font menu didn't preview it on the canvas.
The options bar and the Properties panel's Character section both draw the same `"type-font"` family picker, and the Character one is drawn later in the frame.
With its menu closed, it removed the shared `type-font-hover` key every frame, wiping the hover the options bar had just written.

In a full-app test harness at 1600×1000 this fails under Studio as well as Pro and Pro Medium, whenever the Character section is on screen.
The existing test (`options_bar_hover_previews_on_canvas_without_committing`) draws only the options bar, so it didn't catch this.

## Solution

One condition in `family_picker_in` (`crates/ui-egui/src/type_tool.rs`): a picker clears the hover key only while its own menu is open.
A closed picker leaves the key alone, and `type_font_preview::follow_hover` already drops the key each frame once nothing writes it, so leaving the row or closing the menu still restores the canvas.

## How checked

- New test `options_bar_hover_previews_with_the_character_picker_also_shown` runs the whole app (Pro theme, both pickers on screen).
  It hovers a font in the options bar, checks the canvas shows it, then checks that leaving the row restores the committed font.
  It fails without the fix (`left: "Inter"`, `right: "JetBrains Mono"`).
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests`: 2683 pass.
  One fails, `font_preview::tests::a_system_arabic_face_renders_both_samples`, and it fails the same way on clean `main` on this machine (it depends on installed system fonts), so it's unrelated.
- `cargo fmt -p photocraft-ui-egui -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask wasm`.

title: fix(ui): centre number-field digits level with their unit (#5150)
author: nathanZW
body:
Fixes #5150 (the first screenshot: digits not centred in the box and not level with the `%`). The second screenshot, the focus outline not matching the box, is what #3933 fixes.

## Why

Measured on `main` by rendering a value field with wgpu, the digits' ink sat **1.5 pt above** the box's centre at 100 % display scale (6 px above it, 9 px below). Their bottom sat **2 px above** the `%`'s bottom. At 150 % and 200 % it was still 0.5–0.7 px off. That was the same in every theme, with or without the Layers panel's ▾.

Two causes:
- The 1 pt upward nudge from #1322 now overshoots. With the current slot and font, a centred row already puts the digits' ink within half a point of centre, so the extra point lifts them too far.

- **The unit sits on the digits' baseline.** It is now drawn as a galley at that baseline, so `%`, `px` and `°` line up with the number.
- No panic paths: the helper returns `Option` and falls back to the row centre.

title: Dependencies: require ruzstd 0.9.1 for RUSTSEC-2026-0344 (#4952)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #4952.

`Cargo.lock` resolved `ruzstd 0.9.0`, which is affected by [RUSTSEC-2026-0344](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0344.html): a crafted zstd input under 128 KB can make the decoder allocate several gigabytes at once. PhotoCraft decodes zstd when it opens `.pcraft` files (`crates/format/src/store.rs`) and Affinity files (`crates/affinity/src/container.rs`), so such a file could end the process with an out-of-memory abort. The advisory is a denial of service only (no memory corruption).

### The change

- `crates/format/Cargo.toml` and `crates/affinity/Cargo.toml`: `ruzstd = "0.9"` becomes `"0.9.1"`, so the affected version can no longer be resolved.
- `Cargo.lock`: `ruzstd` 0.9.0 → 0.9.1 (`cargo update -p ruzstd`; no other package changed).

0.9.1 is a patch release that enforces the per-block output bound; there is no API change for the two call sites.

### Not done here

- No new regression test: the issue does not attach a sample (per `SECURITY.md`), and I did not build a decompression bomb. The existing `.pcraft` and Affinity round-trip tests cover the decoder paths.
- Nothing was built or tested locally before opening this; relying on CI.

title: ICC parser: checked arithmetic on offsets and counts from the file (#4976)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #4976.

Offsets and counts stored in an ICC profile reach `u32::MAX`, which is `usize::MAX` on 32-bit targets such as wasm32 (the web build). `crates/cms/src/profile.rs` added to or multiplied several of them before any bounds check. A malformed profile could then panic where overflow checks are on, or read from a wrapped offset where they are off.

### The change

| Where | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `curv` | `12 + n * 2` computed before the "curve too long" check | the count is rejected first |
| `mAB `/`mBA ` matrix | `off + k * 4`, `off + 36…44` on a stored offset | one bounds-checked 48-byte slice at the offset |
| `mAB `/`mBA ` CLUT | `off + k`, `off + 16`, `off + 20` on a stored offset | a bounds-checked 20-byte header slice, then a checked sample offset |
| `mluc` | `16 + k * size`, `o + 4`, `o + 8` with a stored record size | checked offset, one 12-byte record slice |
| `Reader::xyz` | `off + 4`, `off + 8` | one 12-byte slice |

The matrix and CLUT closures became the free functions `lut_ab_matrix` and `lut_ab_clut` so they can be tested with offsets a 64-bit test run can't get from a `u32` field. A new `extent(base, n, size)` helper does the checked `base + n * size`.

Valid profiles parse exactly as before: every changed read needs the same bytes to be present as it did.

### Tests added (`profile::tests`)

- `offsets_at_the_top_of_the_address_space_are_truncated_not_overflowed`: `xyz`, the matrix and the CLUT at offsets near `usize::MAX` return `Truncated`. Before the change these additions overflowed.
- `a_curve_count_is_checked_before_its_length_is_computed`: a `curv` count of `u32::MAX` is "curve too long"; identity and table curves keep their lengths.
- `lut_ab_elements_at_hostile_offsets_are_rejected`: a 3→3 `mAB ` parses, and fails cleanly with its B-curve, matrix or CLUT offset at `u32::MAX - 8`.
- `multilingual_records_with_a_huge_record_size_give_the_first_record`: `mluc` still prefers English, and a record size of `u32::MAX` falls bac…

title: Control channel: connections must authenticate within 10 s, however active (#4965)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #4965.

The only limit on an unauthenticated control connection was the 30 s idle timeout (`IO_TIMEOUT`), and that starts again with every read. A local client that kept sending bytes or blank lines without ever completing `auth` kept its connection, and one of the 16 connection permits (`MAX_CONNECTIONS`), for as long as it liked. Sixteen such connections lock every other client out with "connection limit reached".

### The change

- `photocraft_automation::security::AuthDeadlineStream` wraps the read half of a connection. Until `authenticated()` is called, a read fails with `TimedOut` once the deadline has passed, and a blocking read waits no longer than the time that is left. So both an active and a silent client are dropped at the deadline, and dropping the connection releases its permit.
- `AUTH_DEADLINE` is 10 s from the moment the connection is accepted.
- Both transports use it: the desktop app's control server (`apps/photocraft/src/control_server.rs`) and the headless `photocraft-cli serve` (`crates/automation/src/rpc.rs`).
- Once `auth` succeeds the read timeout goes back to `IO_TIMEOUT` and nothing else changes for authenticated clients.

A client that connects and waits more than 10 s before sending `auth` is now disconnected. The bundled clients (the MCP bridge, the CLI) authenticate immediately after connecting.

Not changed: the pre-authentication frame size is still bounded by `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` (1 MiB) as before; the deadline bounds how long that can take.

### Tests added

- `security::tests::an_active_connection_is_dropped_at_the_authentication_deadline`: a byte every 20 ms and no newline; the read fails at the 300 ms test deadline, not later.
- `security::tests::a_silent_connection_is_dropped_at_the_authentication_deadline`.
- `security::tests::an_authenticated_connection_outlives_the_authentication_deadline`: a frame sent after the deadline is still read once `authenticated()` was called.

title: GPU compositor: pattern textures are freed on close, when idle and over a budget (#4971)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #4971.

The GPU compositor kept every pattern texture it ever uploaded until the device was lost. `forget_doc` and `retain_docs` freed a closed document's layer pages, effect maps and lower-stack composite but skipped `patterns`, and neither the resident budget nor the effect budget covered them. Pattern textures are RGBA32F (16 bytes per pixel), so a 2048 × 2048 pattern holds 64 MiB. A long session that opened and closed documents with pattern fills or pattern effects only ever grew.

### The change (`crates/gpu/src/lib.rs`)

Each cached pattern now records the document that last painted with it, the frame it last painted in, and its size.

- **Close:** `forget_doc` drops the patterns of that document, and `retain_docs` / `held_docs` count pattern owners like the other caches.
- **Idle:** a pattern no frame has painted with for `PATTERN_IDLE_FRAMES` (240, the same age the effect temporaries use) is dropped at the end of a refresh.
- **Budget:** over `PATTERN_BUDGET` (256 MiB, `set_pattern_budget`) the least recently painted go first. A pattern the current frame paints with is never dropped, since it would only be uploaded again on the next frame.

A dropped pattern is uploaded again the next time something paints with it, so this changes memory use, not output. New public API: `Compositor::pattern_cache_bytes`, `Compositor::set_pattern_budget`, `PATTERN_BUDGET`, `PATTERN_IDLE_FRAMES`.

If two open documents paint with the same pattern, the cache entry belongs to whichever painted last; closing that one costs the other a single re-upload.

### Not done here

- The pattern budget is separate from `set_memory_budget`; it is not carved out of the Preferences › Performance memory figure, and `gpu_canvas::compositor_bytes` does not report it yet.
- `Stats::evicted` still counts layer pages and effect maps only.

### Tests added (`crates/gpu/tests/parity.rs`)

- `closed_documents_release_their_pattern_textures`: two documents each paint a 4 × 4 pattern; `forget_doc`…

title: perf(gpu): cap the GPU memory budgets by a discrete GPU's own memory
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #4536.

The GPU canvas sized both of its GPU memory budgets from system RAM only:
- the compositor's (layer pages, effect maps): what Memory Usage leaves, at most RAM / 4;
- the canvas's (one document's display textures): RAM / 4.

Nothing looked at the card. On a discrete GPU with less memory than that, the compositor planned for more than the card holds, and the driver paged instead of the compositor evicting.

## Change

`gpu_canvas::video_memory` reads a discrete adapter's own memory, found by the vendor and device ids wgpu reports:
- **Windows:** DXGI's `DedicatedVideoMemory`, through `winsafe` (its `dxgi` feature; the crate is already a dependency for RAM), so no `unsafe`.
- **Linux:** amdgpu's `mem_info_vram_total` in sysfs.
- **Elsewhere, and for integrated or software adapters:** `None`. Their textures live in system memory, which the RAM-based budgets already cover.

Each budget is now also capped at three eighths of that memory (`vram_share`), so together they leave a quarter of the card for the swapchain, egui and other applications. Where nothing is reported, both budgets keep their RAM-based values, and the 512 MB floor is unchanged. `PHOTOCRAFT_VRAM_MB` simulates a smaller card, like `PHOTOCRAFT_RAM_MB`. The `perf` control-channel output reports the detected size as `gpuInfo.videoMemoryMb`; no UI text changes.

A 16-bit document under `F16_BUDGET_PX` used to get an `Rgba16Float` canvas whatever the budget. On a card of about 2.8 GB or less, three eighths can't hold a 100 MP float canvas (1.07 GB). It would then fall back to the CPU canvas, although its `Rgba8Unorm` set (half the size) fits. `format_for` now chooses the float canvas only when it fits the canvas budget, and otherwise uses 8-bit textures on the GPU. To make that check possible, the budget is shared with the paint callback's resources as an `AtomicU64`, because `format_for` runs while the renderer is locked.

title: perf(algo): Content-Aware Scale 2x faster, within its P28 budget (#211)
author: SckraT
body:
Perf scenario P28 (#211): Content-Aware Scale of a 24 MP photo to 90 % width, budget 3 s. Before this PR the row measured 3.3 s; after, 1.6 s. Output is unchanged.

## What changed (`crates/algo/src/seam.rs`)

**Seam search kept across seams.**
- After a seam is removed, `Dp::update` recomputes only the pixels near the seam and those whose parents' costs actually changed.
- The map stays bit-identical to a full pass.
- The direction buffer is gone: the seam is traced back from the costs.

**The carver moves no pixels.**
- It keeps a `u32` source-column index and reads pixels through it.
- Each removal shifts the shorter side of each row, in three 4-byte buffers.
- The image is no longer copied.

**Parallel full-resolution stages.**
- The tall-image proxy build and its rebuild run in parallel over rows.
- The transposes are blocked and run in parallel; so does the plain resample.

**Robustness.**
- Degenerate inputs no longer panic: zero channels, an empty width combined with a height change, and short protection maps or images.
- NaN no longer steers seams by payload: an energy that isn't a number counts as the highest energy.
- Infinite protection now also protects in the height pass.

## Exactness

**Inputs whose energy stays a number** (finite images without overflow) give output bit-identical to the previous code. The guards:
- `output_bits_are_pinned`, plus the new `tall_proxy_output_bits_are_pinned`, pinned from the old code before any change.
- `carver_matches_reference`.
- The new `incremental_dp_matches_full_dp`, which checks after every removal.
- A 37 000-case differential review of the old and new code.

**NaN and infinities are now deterministic everywhere.** This is pinned by `nan_payloads_do_not_steer_seams` and `infinite_samples_carve_deterministically`.

## Measurements

4-vCPU VM, CPU only; before and after builds run interleaved:

| | Before | After |

title: Render Mixer Brush live and remove extra brush frame delay
author: bommerts
body:

title: Layer masks: Reveal Selection drops the selection, as Photoshop does
author: abc2cb
body:
TLDR:

In Photoshop, a mask made from the selection uses up the selection: after Layer › Layer Mask › Reveal Selection (the Layers panel's Add Mask button while something is selected) the marching ants are gone. PhotoCraft kept the selection. So the usual next step, Invert (Ctrl/Cmd+I) on the new mask, inverted only the part inside the old selection, and the mask ended up all black instead of flipped. Hide Selection (Alt-click on the button) already dropped the selection, so the two variants also behaved differently.

Now:

- **Reveal Selection** (`layer.layerMask.revealSelection`) makes the mask and drops the selection in the same history step, as Hide Selection does.
- **One undo** removes the mask and brings the selection back.
- Invert right after Reveal Selection flips the whole mask, as in Photoshop.

I checked the Photoshop behaviour by hand, and tested the fix by hand in a Windows build.

Related: #1123 (Layer Masks: incomplete aspects) does not list this case. No other issue or PR covers it.

- `engine/src/commands.rs`: Reveal Selection goes through a new `set_mask_and_deselect`. `set_mask` and it share `set_mask_with(..., deselect)`, which clears `doc.selection` inside the same `s.edit`.
- Tests that called `select.deselect` right after Reveal Selection no longer do: Deselect is disabled without a selection and would now return an error. That is one line each in `file_cmds`, `filters`, `mask_view_cmds`, `rasterize_style_cmds`, `selection_cmds`, `smartselect_cmds`, `vector_cmds` and `ui-egui/src/mask_thumbs_ui` tests.

title: fix(ui): swatches touch with no padding, as in Photoshop (#5103)
author: sabbirshawon
body:
Fixes #5103

## What was wrong

The Swatches panel used the shared preset browser grid, which puts a 4 px gap between cells and gives each cell a rounded, bordered card look. Photoshop's Swatches panel has no gaps: the colours are flat squares that touch, so the panel shows as many as possible.

## Fix

- `Place` (the shared preset browser's layout options) gets a `flush` flag.
- With `flush`, the grid has no gap between cells, the columns are computed without it, and a cell draws no border of its own. Only the selected (accent) and the hovered cell are outlined, over their neighbours. Corners are square.
- The Swatches panel sets `flush: true` and paints its colour squares without a border or rounding.
- Gradients, Patterns, Styles and Shapes keep the 4 px gap and card borders (`flush: false`); the gap and the 8 px inset are now named constants instead of repeated literals.

At the default 22 px size in the default dock width, the ten Grays now fit on one row instead of wrapping the white onto a second row.

## Test

`swatches_ui::tests::swatches_touch_without_a_gap` clicks 1 px past the first swatch's right edge and expects the second swatch to be selected. With the 4 px gap that point was empty. The other six Swatches panel tests pass unchanged.

Checked locally: `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib swatches_ui`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt`. Before and after captured with the offscreen `snapshot` example.

title: Threshold: split on Photoshop's luminosity of whole samples (threshold_rgb, threshold_16bits_rgb pass)
author: timothydaly1
body:
## What

Threshold now splits pixels exactly where Photoshop does, in 8- and 16-bit documents.

Photoshop splits on the luminosity **0.30 R + 0.59 G + 0.11 B**, not the Rec. 601 grey we used. It's the blend modes' `lum`, which Gradient Map also uses (#5018). The luminosity is taken over the document's whole sample values, and the comparison depends on bit depth:

| Depth | White when |
|---|---|
| 8 bits | `30 R + 59 G + 11 B > 100 · level − 50`: the luminosity rounded to a level, halves down, reaches the level |
| 16 bits | `30 R + 59 G + 11 B ≥ 100 · round(level · 32768 / 255)`: the level in 16 bits, so mid grey 16448 is level 128 |
| 32 bits | the luminosity reaches the level |

The sums over whole samples are exact in f32 (at most 3 276 800), on the CPU (`adjust::threshold_white`) and in the GPU kernel. Greys sitting exactly on the level therefore split the same way on both. The planner passes the depth's rule and the 16-bit level.

## Evidence

The rules were fitted pixel by pixel. They are exact on every pixel of:

| Oracle | Pixels | Rec. 601 (main) got wrong |
|---|---|---|
| psd-tools `threshold_rgb.psd` (levels 60, 115, 172, 232) | 36 432 | 28 |
| psd-tools `threshold_16bits_rgb.psd` | 36 432 | 100 |
| psd-tools `threshold_16bits_grayscale.psd` | 36 432 | 0 (still exact) |
| photoshop `rgb16/threshold-128.psd` | 9 216 | 0 (still exact) |

The two other candidate 16-bit rules each broke one of these:
- Comparing against the level in continuous units broke `rgb16/threshold-128`, whose grey 16448 is 0.25 below 128 · 32768/255.
- Rounding the luminosity to 8-bit levels broke `threshold_16bits_rgb`.

`threshold_rgb` contains one exact tie (131, 109, 99 → 114.5 at level 115), and Photoshop rounds it down.

| psd-tools | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `threshold_rgb.psd` | 1.0000, 0.07 %, DIFF | **0.0000, PASS** |
| `threshold_16bits_rgb.psd` | 1.0000, 0.27 %, DIFF | **0.0011, PASS** |

title: affinity: decoded layers are admitted against an aggregate pixel budget (#4960)
author: lu123bing
body:
Addresses the admission gap in #4960 (audit finding 9/32).

**What was missing**

`Limits` bounded what one import *extracts* (256 MiB an entry, 1 GiB in total), and `decode` skips a single pixel layer past 64 megapixels — but nothing bounded what the materialized layers cost. Each bitmap's declared `BmpW`/`BmpH` sizes its RGBA output and the planes it decodes through, whether or not the archive holds any tile data, so a document of a few hundred bytes can declare layer after layer of pixels and every one of them is allocated as it is read.

**What changes**

- `Limits` gains `max_pixel_bytes`, 1 GiB by default — the budget the other importers allow decoded pixels (`photocraft-io`'s `MAX_PIXEL_BYTES`) — so callers can inject their own.
- `Reader` admits a layer in `decode` before it allocates: the layer's RGBA joins the layers already materialized, and its working planes count with them, since every earlier layer is still live while this one decodes. The sizes go through checked arithmetic, as the report asks.
- Past the budget the import fails with `Error::Limit`. `photocraft-io` already reports that reason and falls back from it to the file's embedded preview, so an oversized file opens as a preview instead of driving an allocation the process may not survive.
- The crate README's safety-limits paragraph documents the new budget; the fuzz targets get a 64 MiB pixel budget so mutations reach the rejection path.

**Tests** (`crates/affinity/src/tests.rs`, synthetic `synth` containers)

- one 64×64 layer inside a 40 KiB budget imports;
- a two-layer document (a few hundred bytes) is rejected on its second layer before allocation, and imports once the budget covers both;
- a declared 2048×2048 layer is rejected under a 1 MiB budget — the header costs the memory, not the tiles.

All three fail on `main`: the second and third import and materialize the pixels.

title: Posterize: 16-bit documents bin the 16-bit sample, as Photoshop does (two oracles pass)
author: timothydaly1
body:
## What

16-bit Posterize now matches Photoshop exactly.

At 16 bits, Photoshop doesn't round to 8-bit levels before binning. It bins the **16-bit sample** and lands on 8-bit levels through a 16-bit step:

- bin `b = ⌊v16 · n / 32768⌋` (at most n − 1)
- step `o = ⌊b · 32768 / (n − 1)⌋`
- level `⌊(o · 255 + 16384) / 32768⌋`

So the middle of 3 levels comes out as **128** where 8 bits give 127, while 42.5 and 25.5 stay at 42 and 25. 8-bit Posterize is unchanged.

`adjust::posterize_in(v, levels, depth)` implements this. It runs in RGB and Grayscale documents and on the channel path for CMYK and Lab (`stored_channels`).

The GPU kernel runs the same rule. Its arithmetic is all whole numbers below 2²⁴, so exact in f32, but 16-bit layers reach the GPU as half floats (`Rgba16Float`). A sample within half-float precision of a bin edge can therefore land in the neighbouring bin on screen. The CPU, which exports and flattens, is exact. That's why I didn't add a 16-bit GPU parity case for Posterize: it fails at such edges whichever rule the kernel uses.

## Evidence

Fitted sample by sample. Both files are exact on every sample:

| psd-tools | levels | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `posterize_16bits_rgb.psd` | 3, 7, 13, 21 | 0.5020, 4.93 %, DIFF | **0.0038, PASS** |
| `posterize_16bits_grayscale.psd` | 2, 6, 9, 11 | 0.2000, 0.97 %, DIFF | **0.0018, PASS** |

CMYK at 16 bits follows the same rule. On the stored inks (with #4945's native CMYK path), `posterize_16bits_cmyk.psd` goes from 4.26 % to 0.01 % of pixels off. Through main's RGB path, CMYK and Lab are dominated by their other errors and barely move: photoshop `cmyk16/posterize-4` goes from 9.34 % to 9.45 %, and `lab16/posterize-4` from 0.10 % to 0.07 %.

- **Corpus test:** psd-tools 239 → **241**; floor 236 → 241.
- **Unchanged:** the photoshop corpus (145; every rgb, gray and posterize oracle that passed still passes) and the io corpus.

title: Layer Style: Gradient Overlay takes any number of colour stops (#5177)
author: FabioLissi
body:
Closes #5177.

The Gradient Overlay page modelled its gradient as a From and To colour, so a rainbow gradient on text, as in Photoshop, was impossible. Richer gradients (from PSDs or styles) only survived the dialog through its snapshot.

## Engine

Location and Delete act on the selected stop, and a dropdown offers the Gradients panel's presets to start from.

## What

A pass-through group composites its children straight into the backdrop, so an adjustment layer inside it also adjusts the layers beneath the group. That's right, except for one case. When the group is the **base of a clipping group** and holds an **adjustment layer**, Photoshop renders it isolated. The adjustment then no longer reaches the layers beneath.

In psd-tools `passthrough_clipping_mask_adjustment.psd`, an Exposure inside such a group leaves the backdrop alone in Photoshop. We darkened it: half the image was 170 levels off.

The rule turns on the adjustment, not on the clipping alone. I first tried isolating every pass-through clipping base. That broke `clipping-mask4` and `passthrough_clipping_mask_blendmode`, so the condition is narrowed to groups holding an adjustment layer.
