title: Low-Latency Drawing (vsync off) by default, plus present-mode overrides for testers (#1343)
author: tanish2k09
body:
Fixes the drawing lag in #1343: the stroke trailing the pen by about 50 ms.

## Evidence (testers, via the stroke trace from #4403)
- **@VoronBrothers-VoronBrothers, RTX 5060 Ti, X11, Vulkan, 60 Hz.**
  - The app's frame is about 9 ms of CPU, and then it waits **7–9 ms every frame on the swap chain**. Default mode lags about 50 ms.
  - With **vsync off** the lag is gone.
  - Frame latency 1 does not help: the wait stays about 7 ms.
- **@zevnda, Windows/NVIDIA:** forcing vsync off in the driver removes the lag too.
- **@Photon89, Iris Xe:** a different bottleneck. Frames take about 90–116 ms, with eframe's CPU at about 39 ms against our UI's 5 ms, and no present mode changes that. To be investigated separately.

## Change
- **Preferences › Performance › Low-Latency Drawing** (`performance.lowLatencyDrawing`), **on by default** (owner's decision).
  - The surface presents with `AutoNoVsync`: wgpu picks Immediate, else Mailbox, else Fifo by what the driver offers.
  - Off brings vsync back. It applies at the next launch, as the other graphics settings do (eframe's painter owns the live surface config).
- **Tester overrides:** `PHOTOCRAFT_PRESENT_MODE` (`fifo`, `autovsync`, `novsync`) and `PHOTOCRAFT_FRAME_LATENCY` (1–3).
  - They are applied over the preference and shown in every stroke-trace line.
  - **Never a crash:** `immediate` / `mailbox` map to `AutoNoVsync`. wgpu panics on an explicit mode the driver lacks, and `mailbox` crashed X11/NVIDIA in the first version of this PR.

## Trade-offs
- Where the driver offers only Immediate (no Mailbox), the canvas may **tear** while it changes. Turning the preference off avoids it.
- Without vsync, frames render as fast as input arrives **during a stroke** (about 430 fps on an RTX 5090) and stop when idle, so a stroke costs more GPU and battery.
- #3487 (Windows `AutoNoVsync`) overlaps. This preference covers it on every platform, with an opt-out.

title: Flatpak on Wayland: say why a paste finds nothing, and how to paste anyway (#5031)
author: nicolasfalesy
body:
Refs #5031.

## Root cause

In the Flatpak on Wayland, `arboard::Clipboard::new()` fails outright. The sandbox hides the data-control protocol (`ext-data-control` / `wlr-data-control`), and `--socket=fallback-x11` gives no X server while a compositor runs, so arboard has nothing to fall back to. The #4752 `image/*` fallback uses data-control too. Paste then said "Nothing to paste: the clipboard holds no image", even when the clipboard held a valid `image/png`.

A real image read in the sandbox would need the app's own `wl_data_device` connection. The only crate here that offers that is `smithay-clipboard`, which reads text only and takes the display through an `unsafe fn`. So this PR doesn't try a read. It makes the failure honest and shows the existing workaround.

## Fix

- `Services::clipboard_unreadable`: the native clipboard service records whether the last read could open any clipboard at all.
- When a paste finds nothing and that flag is set, a notice explains the sandbox and gives `xwayland_command` for this install (`flatpak run --nosocket=wayland --socket=x11 ai.storyteller.photocraft`), the same command the file-drop notice uses. The status bar says the clipboard can't be read, not that it holds no image. A second paste doesn't stack a second notice.
- An ordinary clipboard without an image keeps the old quiet message.
- The 4 new strings are translated in all 20 catalogs.
- Also adds my own `contributors/people.toml` entry.

title: PSD import: ResolutionInfo is pixels per inch whatever the display unit
author: Zer0C00L01
body:
Fixes #5201

A ResolutionInfo block stores hRes and vRes as 16.16 fixed-point pixels per inch. The following shorts are display units only (1 = show as px/in, 2 = show as px/cm). Import multiplied those values by 2.54 when the unit was centimetres, so a 300 ppi file opened at 762 ppi.

Import now reads hRes and vRes as pixels per inch and ignores the display unit for scaling. Export already writes the document resolution through ResolutionInfo::from_dpi and does not divide by 2.54; a round trip of a synthetic 300 ppi file with unit cm stays 300 ppi.

title: PSD save: choose PSB by the encoded size, not the raw estimate (#5285)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5285 (part of #5106)

## What gets better
**Before:** a document that compresses to 34 MB was saved as **PSB** when you chose `.psd`, because its *uncompressed* pixels add up to more than 2 GB. Many PSD readers can't open PSB.
**After:** it's saved as **PSD**. Only files whose real size is over 2 GB (Photoshop's PSD limit) become PSB.

Save time and memory are unchanged (numbers below).

## Root cause
The auto-PSB switch (#212) chose the version before encoding, using `estimate_psd_size`. That estimate added up the uncompressed size of every layer, mask and merged plane, plus fixed overheads. The channels are RLE-compressed afterwards, so the real file is usually far smaller. On main, a 12000² document with three compressible layers (2.16 GB raw) was written as a 35 MB PSB. The Multichannel writer used the same estimate.

## Change
- The document is encoded as PSD (as PSB only when forced or past 30000 px). The version is then chosen from the exact length of the file that will be written: `PsdFile::encoded_len`, computed without serializing the channel data.
- **Converting an over-limit file to PSB copies no data.** `PsdFile::promote_to_psb` checks every RLE row-count table and then only marks the model `write_as_psb`. The model in memory stays a valid PSD, so everything that decodes it reads it as before.
- **Widening happens on write.** `to_bytes` writes version 2 and the PSB length fields, and widens each 2-byte row count to 4 bytes while copying the stream out. The packed rows are the same in both versions.
- **The result is byte-identical** to a PSB written directly from the same pixels.
- **A damaged table** fails the promotion and leaves the model unmarked; the write never panics.
- The layer info is re-padded for PSB, and kept `8B64` global-block signatures are resolved from the version that is actually written.
- 1 MB of headroom covers the image-preview resource the save adds afterwards.
- The raw-size estimate is removed.

title: Performance: the lower-stack cache follows an edit up the stack (P9 / P11, #5286)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5286 (scorecard P9 / P11, part of #5106)

## Root cause
Repeating Duplicate Layer or Paste of a 12 MP layer cost as much as the first time: P9 / P11 at 24 ms, budget 20 ms.

The command itself is not the cost. It takes 0.2–0.5 ms, and its tiles are already shared on the GPU (204 tiles copied, 0 uploaded). History, copy-on-write and thumbnails are not involved either.

The time goes to the GPU refresh of the damage rect (about 4300×2900):
- per refresh: about 10 ms of CPU pass recording plus about 10 ms of GPU time;
- 110–132 passes run, and only 23 per chunk are skipped.

The compositor's lower-stack cache (`Prefix`) kept the checkpoint of the first edit after it was filled. Later edits higher up only checked that the layers below that checkpoint were unchanged, so the cache never moved up. Every refresh therefore re-ran everything above it, including about ten full 12 MP layers.

## Change
- Each cached chunk remembers the checkpoint it holds.
- `prepare` compares the root layers with the previous render's. It drops only the chunks whose checkpoint lies above the first changed layer, and captures at the highest checkpoint below that change.
- `run_cell` resumes each chunk from its own checkpoint. It also captures when it resumed from a lower one, so the cache follows the edit up within the same render. The repeat, undo or redo then resumes just below it.
- When a chunk moves up, its texture is overwritten in place. That write is ordered after the restore copy in the same encoder, so no extra memory is used.
- Validity is unchanged: a chunk survives only while the layers below its checkpoint are untouched.

Trade-off: a chunk moved by a partial capture holds only that rectangle afterwards, so the rest of it misses once, like a fresh entry. Moving a chunk only when the capture covers all of it kept the hits but lost nearly all the gain (P9 stayed at about 20 ms), because the edge chunks of a damage rect are partial.

title: Fibers: fill an empty layer, as Photoshop does (#5241)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #5241

Filter › Render › Fibers on an empty layer did nothing, and a following `edit.transform` then reported "nothing to transform". Photoshop fills the layer, because Fibers is drawn from the foreground and background colours and never reads the layer's pixels.

**Cause:** `algo::output_area` gives a filter with halo `Radius(0)` the layer's content box. That box is empty on an empty layer, and on a partly filled layer it covers only the painted part.

**Fix:** `FilterParams::renders_from_nothing()` (true for Fibers). `output_area` then returns the reference bounds: the selection's bounds, or the canvas when there is no selection. The halo stays `Radius(0)`, so the tiler still doesn't read the whole layer the way `Halo::Bounds` filters do. The fix sits in `output_area`, so smart filters and the Filter Gallery preview pick it up too. Lens Flare isn't changed: it screens over existing pixels.

**Tests**
- `algo::tests::halos_and_output_area`: Fibers with empty content returns the bounds, clipped to the selection.
- `filters_ext::tests::fibers_fill_an_empty_layer`: an empty layer comes out fully opaque and `edit.transform.flipHorizontal` works after it; with a selection, only the selection is filled.

title: Content-Aware Fill: no ghost edges or object colour around thin removed objects
author: switch87
body:
Refs #1366: the thin-object case (strings, wires, small knobs) only. The workspace UI is #2376 and is not touched here.

**Problem.** Removing long, thin objects, such as coiled guitar strings over a blurred background, left their outline visible as darker and lighter blotches. Pieces of other strings were copied into the fill, and the small tuning knobs selected along with the strings came back as discs of the wrong colour.

![Before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/switch87/photocraft/issue-assets/issue-assets/caf-thin-objects-5290.png)

1. **The pyramid was sized by the hole's bounds.** The completion shrinks the image until the hole is about four patches across. For a string across the image, its bounding box decides that, so at the coarsest level the hole has swallowed its surroundings. The matches found there copy whatever looks like the blur, such as a dark patch or a piece of another string. The finer levels keep them, and above 192 px they only refine.

title: layer.setProps: refuse opacity and fill outside 0..1 (#5242)

title: macOS DMG: hdiutil create -srcfolder, so the installed app passes codesign --strict
author: Deeev201
body:
## What

The macOS DMG is built with `hdiutil create -srcfolder` instead of `hdiutil makehybrid -hfs` + `convert`, the way VectorCraft (storytold/vectorcraft#1085) and PdfCraft (storytold/pdfcraft#823) already do, with the same five-try `hdiutil_retry` for CI's "Resource busy". After signing, the image is mounted and the app inside is checked with `codesign --verify --strict --deep`, so this can't regress silently.

## Why

`makehybrid -hfs` stamps a `com.apple.FinderInfo` extended attribute on every file in the image. Gatekeeper still accepts the app (`spctl` says "Notarized Developer ID"), but `codesign --verify --strict --deep` on the app in the mounted DMG, or on a copy installed from it with Finder or `ditto`, fails:

```
PhotoCraft.app: resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed
```

This shows up in the current releases of PhotoCraft, FilmCraft, EffectCraft and DesignCraft (VectorCraft, LightCraft and PdfCraft, which already switched, pass).

## Checked

- `bash -n packaging/macos/package.sh`
- A small signed test bundle packed both ways: `makehybrid -hfs` left FinderInfo on all 7 files and `--strict` failed; `create -srcfolder -fs HFS+` left none and `--strict` passed.
- I couldn't run the full signed/notarized packaging locally (no Developer ID), so CI's packaging job is the real test.

title: Color Range presets: weigh dark colours like Photoshop (#5243)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #5243

I checked this against Photoshop 2025 (26.5) on the same pixels. Its **Blues** gives the muted navy `#3d3f54` a 14 % selection (35/255), and PhotoCraft gave 8 % (21/255). Both are well below 50 %, so in Photoshop this colour isn't really "a blue" either: Sampled Colors is the right tool for it. Comparing more colours did show that our preset weighting is wrong for darker colours, and this PR fixes that.

**Measurement:** in Photoshop I made 8-bit sRGB documents with 126 swatches per preset: hue at centre ±5/20/40°, saturation 5–100 %, brightness 33/60/100 %. I ran Color Range (Reds, Yellows, Blues) via `executeAction('ClrR')`, stored the selection, and read the level of every swatch.
- Bright colours (brightness 100 %) already matched exactly. That is hue weight × chroma, which is what `sel::hue_range` computes.
- Darker colours are selected more strongly in Photoshop, by a factor of `2 − max(R, G, B)`. With that factor, all 378 measured swatches match Photoshop within 1 level, for all three presets. Without it they were off by up to 61 levels.

**Change:** `sel::hue_range` multiplies by `2 − max`. The new test `hue_families_weigh_dark_colours_like_photoshop` pins three of the Photoshop values: the navy at 35, `(0,0,84)` at 140 and `(61,61,153)` at 129.

title: Linux: a virtual keyboard claiming BTN_TOOL_PEN no longer sends the window through Xwayland (#5284)
author: dutraroberto
body:
Fixes #5284: the blurred UI of #1072 ("[UI] Fractional scaling") persisted after #1237 on machines with a virtual keyboard that claims `BTN_TOOL_PEN`.

## Environment

Zorin OS, GNOME Shell 46.0, Wayland session, LG 4K (3840×2160) at a 125% fractional scale (`scale-monitor-framebuffer` on). RustDesk installed, no pen tablet attached.

## What happened

#1237 made UI Scale "Auto" follow the system's fractional scale, and that part works: on native Wayland, winit 0.30 binds `wp_fractional_scale_manager_v1` and `wp_viewporter`, gets `preferred_scale(150)` (150/120 = 1.25), sets the viewport destination to the logical 3072×1696 and renders the swapchain at the physical 3840×2120, with `pixels_per_point = 1.25`. The UI is sharp.

But the window never opened on native Wayland. Since #639 the app opens through Xwayland when a pen is attached, and `has_pen` took any `/proc/bus/input/devices` entry whose `B: KEY=` bitmap has `BTN_TOOL_PEN` for a pen. RustDesk's uinput keyboard (`N: Name="RustDesk UInput Keyboard"`, `B: EV=20013`, no `B: ABS=` line) claims every key code, that one included, so the app printed `photocraft: pen found; opening the window through Xwayland` and opened an X11 window (listed by `xwininfo -root -tree`; `xlsclients` doesn't show it because winit sets no `WM_COMMAND`, which is why the window looked like a native one). On this desktop the Xwayland screen is the logical 3072×1728 with `Xft.dpi: 120`, so the app rendered at 1.25× into a 3072 px wide framebuffer that the compositor then upscaled by 1.25 to 3840 px: everything was blurred/pixelated. `PHOTOCRAFT_NATIVE_WAYLAND=1` confirmed it: with it the UI is sharp.

Other tools that create a uinput keyboard advertising every key would likely trigger the same path. I only tested RustDesk.

## The fix

A pen now also needs `ABS_X` and `ABS_Y` in its `B: ABS=` bitmap, which is what libinput requires of a tablet tool; a keyboard has no absolute axes. `has_pen` reads each device block on its own, so a keyboard…

title: Color Range: sample colours outside the active selection (#5244)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #5244

With an active selection, Color Range refused eyedropper samples outside it. The command's `points`/`subtractPoints` returned an error, and clicks on the canvas while the dialog was open were ignored. Photoshop lets you sample anywhere and only limits the *result* to the selection, for example to pick a colour from a reference area and select it only inside the selection. title: Object Selection: say so when the sampled layer is empty (#5246)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #5246

`select.object` samples only the active layer by default (`sampleAllLayers: false`). When that layer was empty, which happens easily when a script adds a new layer above the photo, it found nothing and returned `changed: false` with no error. The problem only showed up at the next `select.saveSelection`.

**Change:** before running, `select.object` (both the rectangle and the point form) checks the layer it would sample. If that layer has no pixels in the rectangle or at the point, the command fails with a message that names the cause and the fix:
- `the active layer is empty; set "sampleAllLayers": true or select a layer with pixels`
- `the active layer has no pixels in that area; …`

With `sampleAllLayers: true`, or on a layer with pixels, nothing changes. The check uses the surface's exact content bounds.

**Test:** `smartselect_cmds::tests::object_selection_on_an_empty_active_layer_says_so` covers the rectangle and point forms on an empty layer, `sampleAllLayers: true` still finding the disc below, and a layer whose pixels are outside the rectangle.

title: --version: name the commit of a dev build from git (#5247)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #5247

A plain `cargo build` from `main` reported `photocraft --version` as `0.8.2 (dev build)`, which doesn't say which commit a bug report is about. It now reports `0.8.2 (dev build, 6f8505421)`.

**How:**
- `apps/photocraft/git_checkout.rs` is a build-script helper shared by the desktop and CLI `build.rs`. It runs `git rev-parse HEAD` and emits `PHOTOCRAFT_CHECKOUT_SHA`, and it asks for a rerun when `HEAD` or the current branch's ref changes (so on a commit or checkout). This works in worktrees as well.
- At startup the binaries pass that value to the new `build_info::set_checkout`. `long_version()` uses it only when `PHOTOCRAFT_BUILD_SHA` is unset.
- The engine still doesn't shell out to git (the existing design note in `build_info.rs`). The value lives in the two app crates, so a new commit rebuilds only those and not the engine and everything above it. I checked: after an empty commit, only `photocraft-cli` recompiled (17 s), and `--version` showed the new hash.

**Release logic unchanged:** when `PHOTOCRAFT_BUILD_SHA` is set (CI, `packaging/`, Docker), the build script does nothing and the output stays `0.8.2 (<sha>, <date>)`.

**Fallbacks:** with no git, no checkout, or a workspace that isn't the root of the repository it sits in (for example a source tarball unpacked inside another repo), nothing is set and the output stays `(dev build)`.

`docs/releasing.md` now mentions the dev-build format. Unit tests are in `build_info::tests::long_version_formats`.

title: Drop shadow: knocked out beneath the whole shape when the layer's mode blends with it
author: Deeev201
body:
## What

Layer Knocks Out Drop Shadow now knocks the shadow out from under the layer's whole shape when the layer's blend mode blends with what's beneath it (anything but Normal, Dissolve and Pass Through), in both the CPU compositor (`effects::composite_with_effects_prepared`) and the GPU plan (`plan.rs`), through one helper, `effects::shadow_see_through`.

## Why

The knockout only applied through see-through fill: at 100 % fill the layer was assumed to cover its own shadow. That holds in Normal mode, but a layer in Exclusion, Difference, Multiply, Screen etc. blends with the shadow beneath it.

Real case (a client logo, so not attached): a black rectangle shape layer, **Exclusion**, with a **Drop Shadow** and an **Invert** adjustment clipped to it, over black type. Photoshop's merged image shows white type on a black bar. PhotoCraft 0.8.2 drew a blank white bar: the bar inverted its own shadow, so the type vanished. With the bar's drop shadow hidden, PhotoCraft matched Photoshop, which pinned it down. With this change the whole document's render matches Photoshop's merged image (mean absolute difference 5.67 → 0.05 per channel, 0–255).

## Tests

- New `tests::shadow_knockout_beneath_a_layer_in_a_blending_mode` (Exclusion and Multiply, at 8, 16 and 32-bit): fails before the change, passes after; it also checks that with knockout unticked the shadow still shows through, as in Photoshop.
- The existing shadow tests (`shadow_knockout_needs_see_through_fill`, `drop_shadow_uses_global_light_and_knockout`, …) pass unchanged: Normal-mode behaviour (no double attenuation of anti-aliased edges at 100 % fill) is untouched.
- `cargo test --release -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu -p photocraft-io`: 691 passed, 0 failed (2 ignored, as on main).
- `cargo xtask test-corpus -p photocraft-io` (the Photoshop oracles and the psd-tools / ag-psd corpora): 214 passed, 0 failed.

title: Web: ship the wasm as compressed parts behind a boot module (#5302)
author: zuujiscom
body:
## What

The release site no longer holds the app's wasm as one file. `packaging/web/package.sh` gzips it and cuts it into parts of at most 20 MiB, and a small new module, `apps/photocraft-web-boot`, starts the app from them. No file in the site is near Cloudflare's 25 MiB cap however large the app grows, so the size gate stops failing feature PRs (#5302; before it #2213, #3904, #3907).

This is one of two alternative PRs for #5302. They are the same except for one commit: **this one relies on the browser to inflate the parts** (`DecompressionStream`: Safari 16.4, Firefox 113, Chrome 80). #5308 adds an inflater of its own for older browsers, at the cost of a larger boot module. Please merge whichever fits and close the other.

## How

- **`apps/photocraft-web-boot`** (Rust, `wasm-bindgen` + `web-sys`; no hand-written JS). It reads `app/parts.txt`, fetches the parts in order into one stream, has the browser inflate it, wraps the result in a `Response` typed `application/wasm` and passes it to the app's own generated `init`, imported with `#[wasm_bindgen(raw_module = "./app/photocraft-web.js")]`. The browser still compiles while it downloads. Built: 39,099 bytes of wasm and 21,105 of generated glue.
- **Failures.** A failed download is tried again after 1 s and 3 s, the later tries past the browser's cache. After the third the page says "PhotoCraft couldn't be downloaded. Check your connection, then try again: Reload". `parts.txt` starts with a marker line and a `text/html` answer is refused, because Cloudflare Pages answers a missing file with the home page and HTTP 200. A browser without `DecompressionStream` is told it needs a newer browser.
- **`packaging/web/package.sh`** builds both with Trunk, then assembles the site: the boot module's page and files, `app/photocraft-web.js` (the app's glue under a fixed name, since `raw_module` is a compile-time path), the parts (named with the app's content hash and an extension no server knows, so nothing decodes or relabels…

title: fix(windows): prefer WARP over GL to avoid black window (#5191)
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
Fixes #5191

## Problem
PhotoCraft launches to a black window on some Windows systems (reported in #5191, #1952, #1788, #1647). System Info from #1788 shows VMware VMs with GL on SVGA3D virtual GPU render black, but switching to WARP (Windows software renderer) displays correctly.

## Solution
On Windows with automatic backend selection, GL adapters now rank below all other adapters including WARP. GL is still used if it's the only adapter available.

## Changes
- `apps/photocraft/src/gpu_startup.rs`: Modified adapter ranking on Windows
- Added regression test `windows_auto_prefers_warp_over_gl`

## Testing
- All 23 tests in `gpu_startup` pass including new regression test
- `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy -p photocraft --all-targets -D warnings` pass

## Trade-offs
On real machines with old GPUs that only have GL drivers (no DX12/Vulkan), PhotoCraft will now use WARP which may be slower (~10fps reported in #1647). Users can still select GL manually in Preferences › Performance › GPU Backend.

title: Display profile notice: one card for all displays without a usable profile
author: nicolasfalesy
body:
## Root cause

`monitor_status::apply` posted one \"Display profile not used\" notice per display. On a desk with two monitors that have no ICC profile (common on Linux, here two VG248s on DP-4 and DP-5), every launch opened with two cards that say the same thing.

## Fix

A reading now posts one notice. It has one reason line per display (\"DP-4 has no ICC profile\", \"DP-5 has no ICC profile\"), then the existing advice line with the names joined (\"The canvas on DP-4, DP-5 is shown as sRGB. …\"). The template strings are unchanged, so no catalog needs updating. Per-display dedup (`reported`) is kept: a reading with nothing new stays quiet, and a display added later gets a card of its own.

title: fix(engine): reject layer.setProps opacity outside 0..1 instead of clamping it (#5242)
author: saadkhantareen
body:
Fixes #5242

## Summary

`layer.setProps` documents opacity as 0..1, but an out-of-range value was clamped silently: `{"opacity": 55}` — the 0..100 scale used by the `layerStyle.*` commands — was accepted and set the layer to 100 %. The result looks plausible (an opaque layer) instead of failing, so the scripting mistake stays hidden.

The handler now validates opacity before applying anything and rejects values outside 0..1 with an error that names the range, e.g. `opacity must be 0..1, got 55`. A rejected call leaves the layer unchanged.

## Changes

- `crates/engine/src/commands.rs` — in the `layer.setProps` handler, reject an `opacity` param outside `0.0..=1.0` (NaN included) with a bad-params error before the document is edited; the in-range assignment is unchanged.
- `crates/engine/tests/layer_set_props_opacity.rs` — new regression tests: `opacity: 55` and `opacity: -0.5` are rejected with the range named in the error and the layer's opacity untouched; 0.0, 0.25 and 1.0 still apply.

Scope note: `fill` has the same documented 0..1 range and is still clamped; this PR covers the opacity case the issue reports.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test layer_set_props_opacity` — 2 passed, 0 failed.
- Existing suites that drive `layer.setProps`: `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test background_layer_consistency --test duplicate_layer_comps` — 5 + 5 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo fmt -p photocraft-engine -- --check` — clean.

title: io: report CMYK and spot colour warnings on PDF import
author: ModularKarma1
body:
### Summary

When rasterizing PDF pages to 8-bit sRGB in photocraft-io, CMYK artwork and spot inks (such as Pantone) are flattened and converted through their alternate color spaces without retaining separations. 

This PR adds preflight scanning for CMYK and spot colour spaces and content streams, reporting explicit import warnings to the user so that color changes and plate separation loss are never silent.

### Changes

- **Preflight ink detection (crates/io/src/pdf_guard.rs):**
  - Identifies DeviceCMYK, CalCMYK, and 4-channel ICCBased color spaces.
  - Detects /Separation and /DeviceN colorants, extracting up to 16 spot color names in alphabetical order (BTreeSet) while ignoring process inks (Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, Black, All, None).
  - Limits spot names to 64 chars and caps nested dictionary walk depth to 32 to guarantee bounded execution.
  - Scans content streams for CMYK operators (k / K) outside comments, literals, and dictionary tokens.
- **Import warnings (crates/io/src/pdf.rs):**
  - Emits clear warnings in ImportResult.warnings informing the user that spot inks and CMYK values were converted to 8-bit sRGB and cannot be output as separation plates.
- **Documentation (docs/pdf-support.md):**
  - Updated to note the spot and CMYK rasterization conversion warnings.
- **Contributor credit (contributors/people.toml):**
  - Added entry for @modularkarma112.

### Validations

- cargo fmt --all -- --check: passed
- cargo clippy --locked -p photocraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings: passed (0 warnings)
- cargo test --locked -p photocraft-io --test pdf: 11 passed, 0 failed

title: fix(transform): keep masked objects visible during transform (#5239)
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
Fixes #5239

## Problem
Objects with masks applied disappeared during Ctrl+T transform, leaving only the transform bounding box visible. The object reappeared when pressing Enter or Esc.

Specifically: smart objects, type layers, shape layers, and groups that were clipped to the layer below them rendered as completely transparent in the transform preview.

## Solution
When building the transform preview for non-raster layers,  creates a solo render with all other layers hidden. This was also hiding the clipping base, causing clipped layers to render as nothing.

**Fix:** Clear the  flag when hiding other layers in the solo document, so the transformed layer previews unclipped (matching the existing behavior for clipped raster layers).

## Changes
- `crates/ui-egui/src/transform_tool.rs`: Clear `clipped` flag in solo preview document
- New test: `preview_of_a_clipped_smart_object_is_not_empty` (fails without fix, passes with it)

## Testing
- ✅ `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- ✅ `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui`: all 2681 tests passed, 0 failed
- Test proves the fix: smart object clipped to base layer now has visible preview pixels

## Known limitations
- When transforming the clipping **base** itself, layers clipped to it still disappear (different scenario, larger change needed)
- The preview shows the clipped layer unclipped rather than maintaining the clip (matches raster behavior)

body:
Fixes #5324. Part of #2966.

In Photoshop, clicking a snapshot in the History panel selects it, and the trash button then deletes that snapshot instead of a history state. Dragging a snapshot or a state onto the trash deletes it too. In PhotoCraft the trash always ran `history.deleteState`, so a snapshot could only be deleted through right-click › Delete.

## Change
- **Selected snapshot:** clicking a snapshot row (which returns the document to it, as before) also selects it. The row is highlighted in place of the current state. It stays selected only while the history is still at the state that click made; an edit, Undo, a click on a state row or a deleted snapshot deselects it.
- **Trash:** with a snapshot selected, the footer's trash runs `history.deleteSnapshot {snapshot}`; otherwise `history.deleteState` as before.
- **Drag onto the trash:** snapshot rows and past state rows can be dragged onto the trash, with the same name ghost and button highlight as the Layers panel. A snapshot runs `history.deleteSnapshot`; a state runs `history.deleteState {state}`, which drops it and the states after it. The oldest state and redo states can't be dragged.
- No new commands: everything goes through the existing engine commands, so agents and MCP keep using `history.deleteSnapshot` / `history.deleteState` directly.
- `docs/ui-parity.md`: History snapshots row, status line and revision history.

## Tests
- New in `panels.rs` › `snapshot_row_tests`:
  - `the_trash_deletes_the_selected_snapshot`: the click selects the snapshot, the trash deletes it and leaves the states alone; after an edit the snapshot is deselected and the trash deletes the current state again.

title: Add guarded scratch storage and owned memory supervision
author: vistaero
body:
Large documents need cold live tiles and undo snapshots to leave RAM without losing their original pixels. This adds compressed, integrity-checked scratch extents and guards that keep tile bytes resident while a consumer uses them.

- Fresh preferences default to **70% of physical RAM** (configurable 1–95%); legacy preferences without a percentage retain their MiB allowance, with migration/default regression coverage.
- Windows scratch handles use delete-on-close. Unix files use mode `0600` and conservative startup sweeping that preserves live-process files, symlinks and other users' files.
- A shared, stoppable supervisor is owned by engine sessions and joined when its last owner drops; L0 exposes synchronous measurement/eviction, without immortal monitor threads. Native `sysinfo` uses only its `system` feature and disables defaults.
- Failed scratch reads block edit/save publication and cache admission; display placeholders cannot silently become source pixels. Full or unavailable scratch storage retains resident data and reports an error.

Includes guarded raster/COW consumer adaptations and synthetic spill, integrity, memory-policy and lifetime regressions. The storage work builds on [robertocantore126's implementation](https://github.com/robertocantore126/photocraft/commit/8c0d36bc1b6bfe79437202c36018885f21aa691e). Unix runtime behavior has not been exercised on this Windows host.

title: Stream native PSD/PSB and EXR imports through bounded bands
author: vistaero
body:
Large PSD/PSB files should not require whole-channel buffers or successful decoding of the merged preview, and the 65,536 × 32,768 scanline EXR should retain its dimensions and HDR values. Native path imports now index seekable sources and decode bounded bands directly into guarded tiles.

- Preserve PSD layers, masks, groups, metadata, depth and color mapping through the existing document mapper; defer channel pixels and validate source bounds.
- Stream supported single-part flat scanline EXR blocks, retaining HDR samples and linear color profiles. HALF samples become F32 with a warning, without changing dimensions.
- Preserve source read-only/template flags, SVG group-depth options and normal color-profile questions. Authorized control imports reopen channels only under held read-directory capabilities.
- Check cancellation between bands and reject truncated/changed sources without publishing a partial document. Add seekable PSD/PSB output primitives for the later save-service integration.

Tiled/deep/multipart EXR and unsupported layouts retain the guarded legacy decoder when its limits permit. Non-streaming formats still need admitted working memory. Regression coverage includes EXR depth/compression/color fidelity, real PSD parity, capability boundaries and cancellation.

title: Integrate streamed PSB saves with the shared save service
author: vistaero
body:
Large PSB saves should use bounded original-depth channel bands while keeping the background-save design already merged in #2072. This connects the native encoder to the landed `Services::save_file`/`SaveCtl` path rather than introducing a second save job model.

- Keep upstream's Arc snapshot, document lock, saved revision, same-destination exclusion and close/quit waiting behavior. Scratch-backed documents do not require editing during a save; the upstream lock remains.
- The encoder owns its temporary output, reports band progress, flushes it and calls `SaveCtl.commit()` immediately before atomic replacement. Precommit failure/cancellation preserves the destination; late cancellation cannot report a published save as failed.
- Automation uses the upstream save service where available and a synchronous fallback otherwise; held write-directory capabilities cover temporary output and rename. It does not require an independent background-save design.
- Share encoding preferences across native and byte routes, preserving PSD/PSB Maximize Compatibility, previews and other format depth settings. PSD output exceeding the size limit is promoted through the streamed PSB writer.

Streamed PSB uses raw channels and can be larger than the compressed source. Regressions cover commit rejection, temporary cleanup, late cancellation, tab changes/saved identity, authorized paths and encoding preferences.

title: fix(io): keep transforms on imported SVG text
author: ahmed0magdy
body:
Refs #4806. This complements #4219.

## The bug

When an SVG's text is positioned by a `transform`, whether on the `<text>` itself or on an enclosing `<g>`, the importer drops that transform and draws the glyph outlines in the wrong place, often off the canvas.

- `<text transform="translate(10 40)" font-size="24">IHI</text>` imports as an empty canvas. With the transform lost, the text sits at y = 0 and grows upward from its baseline, above the canvas.
- `transform="translate(10 0)" x="20"` draws at x = 20 instead of 30.
- `transform="scale(2)"` draws at half size.

Adobe Illustrator exports every text element as `transform="matrix(1 0 0 1 x y)"`, so this affects text from Illustrator SVGs.

**Relation to #4806:** the sample `Test.svg` has two kinds of text.

- The large "TEST" uses plain `x`/`y`. Its problem is missing fonts, which #4219 addresses.
- The colour-bar labels (`green100`, `txgrey89`, …) sit inside `<g transform="translate(2 220)">` and similar groups. That is the case this PR fixes.

So the two PRs together cover #4806. They touch different code in `crates/io/src/svg.rs`: font fallback there, transform placement here.

## Cause

Inside `usvg::Text::flattened()`, every `abs_transform()` is the identity, because the glyph outlines are in the text element's own space (usvg's source has a TODO about this). The importer read `abs_transform()` on every path, so glyphs lost all their ancestor transforms.

## Fix

All changes are in `crates/io/src/svg.rs` (`impl Conv`). The converter already walks the tree top-down with the parent's absolute transform, so it now builds absolute transforms from that instead of trusting `abs_transform()`:

- **Groups:** the absolute transform is `parent.pre_concat(g.transform())`. This is the same operation usvg itself uses, so the numbers are bit-identical outside text. It is passed down to children and to `clip_mask`.
- **Text:** glyph outlines get `t.abs_transform()`, which is correct on the text node, combined with `flatten…

title: perf: keep effect-cache pins and History snapshots inside the memory budgets
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #4530 (with #4774, which capped the shape stroke cache).

The two remaining parts of #4530: pixels that outlived every memory budget.

## 1. Effect caches pinned whole layers

The effect-map cache key identifies a layer's pixels by their copy-on-write tile addresses. So that no new tile could reuse a cached tile's address and match a stale key, each entry kept a clone of the layer: a deep clone of the subtree for a styled group. That clone kept the layer's pixels alive, uncounted, after an edit replaced them or the layer was deleted, until the entry was evicted. The entry counted only its maps. At 24 MP, 8-bit, that is 96 MB of tiles per cached state of a styled layer, beside a 768 MB budget that saw none of it. The GPU compositor did the same for styled groups, and kept strong references to each styled layer's last shape-source tiles for damage tracking.

Now:
- **Both caches:** each entry keeps a `Weak` to every tile its key hashes. A `Weak` keeps the `Arc`'s allocation, so no other tile can take that address, but not the tile's pixel buffer (`Tile` holds a `Box<[u8]>`). The `Weak`s are collected by the same walk that hashes the key (`layer_identity` / `group_key` take a `pin` callback), so they cover exactly the tiles the key depends on.
- **CPU cache size:** an entry's `bytes` now also counts the 32 bytes per tile those `Weak`s keep allocated.
- **GPU damage tracking:** the shape-source snapshots (`fx::Tiles`) hold `Weak`s too. Damage still compares addresses, which the `Weak` keeps unique.

## 2. History panel snapshots were outside every budget

A snapshot's tiles were in no budget: not the history budget, not the document bytes the GPU budget subtracts, and not Purge. A Merged Layers snapshot is a full flattened copy (96 MB at 24 MP, 8-bit), and nothing limits the number of snapshots.

Now:
- **History budget:** trim counts the tiles only snapshots hold as fixed cost (`History::trim_with`, through `DocState::trim_history` at the three trim sites). A lar…

title: Free Transform: the box is the selection, and the marching ants follow it (#5297)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #5297. Part of #3402.

With a selection, ⌘T and the Move tool's Show Transform Controls framed the layer's content clipped to the selection, so the box was smaller than the marching ants wherever the layer did not fill the selection (Figure 1 of the issue). While the box was open the ants stayed where the selection started and only jumped to the box when the transform was applied (Figure 2).

### The change

- **The box is the selection.** New `transform_frame` and `target_frame` in `crates/engine/src/transform_cmds.rs` return the selection's own bounds when a selection limits the transform. `begin`, `begin_lone` and the Move tool's `transform_controls_rect` use them. Type, shapes, smart objects and groups still move whole, and a selection that holds none of the layer still leaves nothing to transform.
- **The ants follow the box.** `transform_tool::draw_selection` draws the selection outline through the open box: the box's projective map for move, scale, rotate, skew, distort and perspective, and the warp in Warp mode (straight runs are drawn in short pieces so they bend). This is the same map `edit.transform` and `edit.transform.warp` apply to the selection, so the ants are where applying the transform leaves them.
- **The whole outline is traced while such a box is open.** The canvas normally outlines only the part of the selection in view; a box can carry a part that started out of view into view.
- **`marching_ants_lines`** (`canvas.rs`): the ants renderer now takes screen-space lines. Lines with non-finite ends are skipped and lines longer than 8192 points are clipped to the view, so an outline near a Distort's horizon cannot stall the frame. `marching_ants_mapped` (Content-Aware Move) goes through it unchanged.

`transform_bounds` itself is unchanged, so snapping and the command defaults behave as before.

title: Color Balance: fold the tones into one Levels per channel (#3423)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #3423.

## Why
Photoshop doesn't apply the Color Balance shadows, midtones and highlights curves one after another. For each channel it builds a single Levels: a black point from shadows, a white point from highlights and one midtone gamma. A gamma above 1 starts with a finite slope at black. main applied the curves in sequence, so a lowered shadows slider and a raised highlights slider compounded instead of cancelling (up to 85/255 off on mixed settings). Its pure power curve brightened the shadows of the issue's red +100 / magenta −100 repro by up to 16.5/255. A black point at or past the white point was also wrong (up to 252/255).

## Change
- `compose::adjust::color_balance_channel` folds the three tones into one Levels per channel:
  - Black point: the lowered shadows slider in levels (Preserve Luminosity on: max − own).
  - White point: 255 − the raised highlights slider (Preserve Luminosity on: own − min).
  - Gamma: 2^(m/100), with m = midtones + (shadows + highlights)/2. With Preserve Luminosity on, m = own − (max + min)/2, unchanged from #4990.
- A gamma above 1 starts at slope 2^gamma and joins the power curve with a cubic Hermite (`balance_gamma`).
- A black point at or past the white point makes a hard step at the white point, as Photoshop does.
- The GPU builds its LUT from the same function (`gpu/src/plan.rs`), so no shader change is needed.

## Measured against Photoshop
All inputs were generated for this, on 16-bit gray ramps, a 16³ RGB cube and pure R/G/B/Y/C/M ramps. Max error in 1/255:

| case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Issue repro (midtones red +100, magenta −100) | 16.46 | 0.02 |
| Issue's sequoia14 settings, PL off / on | 0.72 / 1.06 | 0.72 / 0.60 |
| Shadows only (13, 30, 24), PL off / on | 0.55 / 0.10 | 0.55 / 0.03 |
| Single sliders at ±100, PL off (shadows / midtones / highlights) | 3.24 / 16.48 / 3.17 | 0.42 / 0.02 / 0.39 |
| 2–3 tones or two sliders at once, PL off / on | 23.88 / 27.75 | 0.72 / 0.61 |

title: Gradient Overlay: repaint the whole layer when a stroke moves its frame (#4053)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #4053.

## Why
In Photoshop a Gradient Overlay (Align with Layer on) spans one gradient across the layer's current content bounds. It is drawn again after every stroke, so the layer always shows one continuous gradient. In PhotoCraft the compositors already lay the gradient out over the grown layer (a cold render is right). But a stroke's damage covered only the stroke, and the canvas kept the pixels it had already drawn. So every stroke that grew the layer left the old gradient around the earlier strokes: one gradient per stroke.

## Change
- `photocraft_compose::relayout_damage(before, after)`: when a visible layer's frame moved, the whole composite area of that layer, before and after. It applies to layers whose effects are laid out over that frame (`effects::spans_frame`): Gradient Overlay, gradient stroke, and layer-linked patterns and bevel textures with no effects reference point. `effects_frame` replaces three inline copies of the `paint_bounds`-or-`layer_bounds` expression.
- Engine (`jobs.rs`): after a command succeeds, `dispatch` adds that area to the damage it reported.
- Canvas (`canvas.rs`): a committed live stroke stores the same area (`CommittedStroke.relayout`), and `damage_since` repaints it.
- Strokes inside the layer's current bounds, and effects that don't depend on the bounds (e.g. Color Overlay), keep their tight stroke damage, so ordinary painting doesn't redraw more.

## Tests
All new tests fail without the fix.
- `crates/engine/tests/gradient_overlay_strokes.rs`:
  - A canvas that redraws only the reported damage matches a cold render, within 1e-6, after strokes that grow, extend and erase-shrink the layer.
  - A stroke inside the bounds keeps exactly its own damage.
  - A Color Overlay keeps the stroke's damage.
- `compose` unit test `relayout_damage_covers_a_layer_whose_gradient_frame_moved`.
- `ui-egui` harness test `a_committed_stroke_repaints_a_gradient_overlay_over_the_whole_layer`: two real mouse strokes.

title: .kys import: tool keys and sets saved on Windows (K3)
author: tanish2k09
body:
**Stacked on #5283** (shortcut sets), which is itself on #3746. The base is `feat/shortcut-sets`, so the diff shows only this change. Part of the shortcut work, phase K3 (import fidelity), the part that doesn't need real Photoshop files.

## What
- **Tool keys import (#5036).**
  - Each `<tool name="Pencil Tool">N</tool>` row matches our tool by name (our tool names are Photoshop's), or by `pc-id` in sets PhotoCraft exported (#5283).

  - A key that isn't one letter is skipped. Unknown tools are reported (`unknownTools`) and counted in the import message.
- **Sets saved on Windows.**
  - Photoshop on Windows writes **Ctrl** for the primary modifier, where a Mac set writes Cmd and keeps Control for the Control key.
  - So a set with no Cmd or Opt anywhere but some Ctrl is read as a Windows set (`KysSet::windows`), and its Ctrl is read as our Cmd (`kys::to_ours`).
  - `Ctrl+L` is then the `Cmd+L` default. Before, it became a literal Control-key override: on a Mac that would mean Control+L, and every row would show as changed.
  - The import reports `windows`.
- The engine command's `importKys` reports `windows` too. Tools stay a dialog-side import, because the engine doesn't know the tools.

## Not covered yet
Matching by Photoshop's numeric command ids (`id="1801"`), and verifying the Windows spelling against real files, need real `.kys` files. I've asked for them on #2281.

title: Keyboard Shortcuts: Accept and Go to Conflict / Undo Changes, and reserved keys (K4a)
author: tanish2k09
body:
**Stacked on #5345 (K3), which is on #5283 (K2) and #3746 (K1).** The base is `feat/kys-import-fidelity`, so the diff shows only this change. This is part of the shortcut work, phase K4 (dialog parity), split into smaller PRs; this is the first.

## What
- **Conflicts, as in Photoshop.** When a key you assign is already held by another command, the warning now offers:
  - **Accept and Go to Conflict:** takes the key from the other command now, whether it was its main key or an alternate, and selects that command so you can give it a new key.
  - **Undo Changes:** restores the edited command's main and further keys as they were.
  - Clicking OK without choosing still accepts, as Photoshop does.
- **Reserved keys.** Keys the system takes before the app sees them are refused with a message:
  - Off the Mac: Alt+Tab, Alt+Shift+Tab, Alt+F4, Ctrl+Alt+Delete, Ctrl+Esc, Ctrl+Shift+Esc.
  - On the Mac: ⌘Tab, ⌘⇧Tab, ⌘`, ⌘⌥Esc.

## Next K4 PRs
- **Shortcuts For: Panel Menus.** Panel flyout items have no ids today: about 15 items across 4 panels, each running inline code. That needs a small `panel_menu_items` table plus a dispatch branch first.
- **The tree layout.** Collapsible menu sections, as in Photoshop's dialog.

## Tests

title: perf(gpu): keep the DX12 mip scratch textures for Intel adapters only
author: FinnNk
body:
Part of #4515.

On DX12, the default backend on Windows, every GPU canvas refresh rebuilt the display mips through separate scratch textures: one created per tile and per level, then copied back. That path is a workaround for reduced-preview corruption on Intel DX12 drivers (#892, verified on Intel UHD 620 with driver 31.0.101.2130). But it was gated on the backend alone, so every DX12 adapter took it. Every other backend renders straight into the level.

## What it cost

I split a brush-dab refresh into phases with a local probe (not part of this PR): the composite's encode and submit, the mips' encode and submit, and each GPU wait. Measured on an RTX 4090 Laptop GPU on DX12, with release `perf_scenarios` and the `bit depths` brush-dab rows, as time per dab. The GPU waits were 0.1–0.4 ms throughout, so the work is CPU-side:

| Mips encode and submit | 16-bit 15000×10000 | 32-bit, 20 layers |
|---|---|---|
| Vulkan | 0.52 ms | 0.32 ms |
| DX12, scratch textures | 1.86 ms | 1.74 ms |
| DX12, straight into the level | 1.05 ms | 0.72 ms |

My earlier attempt (described on #4515) sized each scratch texture to the damage. It still created a texture per level on every refresh, which is the expensive part on DX12, so it saved nothing.

## Change

`separate_mip_targets(backend, vendor, setting)` keeps the scratch path for Intel adapters (vendor `0x8086`) under DX12 only. Every other adapter renders straight into the level, like Vulkan, Metal and GL already do. `PHOTOCRAFT_SEPARATE_MIPS=1` or `=0` forces it either way, in case another driver shows the same fault.

## Measured

Release `perf_scenarios`, `--group "bit depths" --only "brush dab" --reps 40`, on the same machine, quiet. Three alternating runs each of `main` and this branch on DX12, and two each on Vulkan for reference. Each value is a run's p50 per dab.

| Row | DX12 `main` | DX12, this PR | Vulkan (either build) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Brush dab, 16-bit 15000×10000 | 2.64 / 2.44 / 2.57 ms | 1.59 / 2.32 / 1.49 ms |…

title: fix(gpu): catch validation errors in watched compositor work
author: geduful
body:
The scoped_work function skipped error scopes when watched is true (always the case in the app because the canvas sets up health monitoring). But error scopes are needed on native platforms to catch synchronous validation errors (e.g. invalid buffer in queue.write_buffer). The health callbacks only handle device loss and async errors.

This fixes P12 (arrow-key nudge in a 150-layer document) which crashed with: wgpu error: Validation Error / Caused by: / In Queue::write_buffer / Buffer with pc_compose_uniforms label is invalid

Now scoped_work always uses error scopes on native (non-WASM) to catch validation/internal/OOM errors, while WebGPU relies on health callbacks for async errors.

title: Layers panel and title: Arabic and Hebrew names read right to left (#5159)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #5159.

### What was wrong

An Arabic layer name such as "لاشي مكتوب هنا" showed in the Layers panel and in the app-drawn title bar with every word spelled correctly but the word order reversed ("هنا مكتوب لاشي"). The canvas was fine because it uses PhotoCraft's own type engine.

The cause is how egui (0.36) lays out text. `epaint` splits a string into runs by font face (`segment_into_runs` in `epaint/src/text/text_layout.rs`), shapes each run with harfrust and places the runs left to right. An Arabic word resolves to the Arabic fallback font and is one run, which harfrust shapes right to left, so the word itself is correct. The spaces between words resolve to the Latin font, so each word is a separate run, and the runs end up in logical order from left to right. egui has no bidirectional reordering (its own source notes "TODO: heed bidi characters").

### The change

- New `crates/ui-egui/src/bidi_text.rs` with `visual(text) -> Cow<str>`. It runs the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (`unicode-bidi` 0.3, already in `Cargo.lock` through usvg) and emits the visual runs in order. Inside a right-to-left run, right-to-left words (letters, combining marks, joiners and Arabic-block punctuation) stay in logical order, because the shaper reverses them itself; spaces and other neutral characters are reversed around them, and brackets are mirrored. Text with no right-to-left characters is returned borrowed, without allocating, so Latin names cost one character scan.
- Applied where the report shows the bug:
  - Layers panel names: `layer_row_ui::truncated`, which lays out every layer row's name.
  - The app-drawn title bar (`panels.rs`).
- The OS window title (`ViewportCommand::Title`) is unchanged: the OS lays it out itself, so it gets the logical text.
- `crates/ui-egui/Cargo.toml` adds `unicode-bidi = "0.3"`; `Cargo.lock` only gains the dependency edge (same 0.3.18 already in the tree).

The function is for display only. Stored names, rename fields and anything sent to…

title: fix(ui): Color Picker hex field takes every pasted colour, not just the first
author: Pharbi
body:
Follow-up to #3375 / #3408.

## Problem

Pasting a colour into the Color Picker's hex field only works once. #3408 selects the hex code when the picker opens, so the first paste replaces it. After that the selection is gone and the field is full, and the field's 6-character `char_limit` makes egui drop every later paste. A paste with a leading `#` (`#00ff00`, 7 characters) is cut to `#00ff0`, which isn't a valid colour.

Reproduced in the test harness before the fix:

```
paste "ff8800"  -> field "ff8800" color #ff8800   ✓
paste "#00ff00" -> field "ff8800" color #ff8800   ✗ ignored
paste "1234ab"  -> field "ff8800" color #ff8800   ✗ ignored
```

## Fix

While the hex field has focus, `take_hex_paste` removes any `Event::Paste` that parses as a hex colour (with or without `#`, surrounding whitespace allowed) before the text edit sees it. The pasted colour then replaces the whole code and is applied. A paste that isn't a colour still goes to the field as before, and the 6-character limit for typing is unchanged.

## Tests

- New `hex_field_takes_every_paste_with_or_without_hash`: three pastes in a row (plain, `#`-prefixed, padded with whitespace). It also checks that a paste that isn't a colour still reaches the field.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib color_picker` passes, as do `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- Not yet checked in the running app, and there are no before/after screenshots yet. That's why this is a draft.

title: Reduce avoidable work in PSD parsing, loading and display
author: TheSeanLavery
body:
Large PSD imports copy encoded payloads, build full-image packing buffers, repeat mask/merged conversion work and render unnecessary intermediate surfaces. This PR removes that work while preserving owned PSD parsing/roundtrips, imported pixel data and full-resolution composition.

Implemented:
- Borrowed encoded-channel parsing with shared validation, bounded channel/RLE workers and deterministic warnings.
- Direct plane-to-tile assembly for RGB, Gray, CMYK and Lab at U8/U16/F32; malformed layouts retain the existing fallback.
- Native RGBA8/GRAY8 GPU uploads borrow existing tile bytes; flattened merged planes and retained mask buffers are reused.
- Discarded synthetic masks receive complete validation without pixel/tile materialization.
- Dense raster content/blend fusion for full-float accumulation, with original half-float rounding/fallback retained.
- One-shot first-open cache population deferral; subsequent edits populate the unchanged cache budgets normally.

title: perf(testkit): RSS sampler reads /proc/self/statm, not smaps, on Linux
author: xsvm
body:
The benches' `RssSampler` polls `memory_stats::memory_stats()` every 2 ms. On Linux that crate reads `/proc/self/smaps` by default. Each read makes the kernel format one block per mapping and walk its page tables while holding the mmap lock. For a large document that is far more than "one syscall per sample".

This enables memory-stats' `always_use_statm` feature. It reads `/proc/self/statm` instead: the kernel's RSS counters, the same figure `VmRSS` reports. The measured code is unchanged; only the harness overhead goes. The feature only changes the crate's Linux path, so macOS and Windows are unaffected. `memory-stats` is used only by `photocraft-testkit`, which is a dev-dependency of `ui-egui`, so the app binary doesn't change. Cargo.lock doesn't change either.

author: safvanedge

Resolves #5410

### Summary
In Photoshop, when opening the New Document dialog (`File > New` / `Cmd+N`) without specifying a custom name, the suggested document name increments based on open untitled documents:
- If `Untitled-1` and `Untitled-2` are open and `2` is closed, the next suggested document is `Untitled-2`.

title: fix(format): report a failed directory flush after a save instead of ignoring it
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #4968.

`atomic_write` and the directory-bundle writer renamed the new file into place, then discarded the result of flushing the directory (`let _ = fs.sync_dir(&dir)`). Until that flush succeeds, the rename may not survive a power loss or crash. Yet the save reported complete success. Callers act on that success, so the risk was real:
- the document is marked saved;
- its crash-recovery entry is discarded;
- a bundle save goes on to remove the objects only the old manifest referenced.

The directory flush is real on Unix only (it's a no-op on Windows), so this affects Linux and macOS.

## Change

- **Flush failures are reported.** When the flush fails, `atomic_write` now returns an error. It keeps the error's kind and says the file was written but the save may not survive a power loss or crash. The caller then treats it as a failed save: the document stays unsaved, its recovery data stays, and the user can save again or elsewhere.
- **Bundle saves stop early.** The bundle writer (`write_bundle_file`) does the same. A failed flush after writing the manifest now stops the save before it removes unreferenced objects.
- **Unsupported flushes still count as saved.** A file system that can't flush directories at all still saves normally (`dir_synced`). That means EINVAL (some Linux file systems), ENOTSUP or EOPNOTSUPP, ENOTTY on Apple platforms, or `ErrorKind::Unsupported`. Retrying won't change those, and failing every save there would make saving impossible.

A folder that can't be opened for the flush at all, because it has write and search permission but no read permission, also counts as saved (`open_dir_for_sync`). No flush can be attempted there, and the existing permission tests save into such folders.

The errno values are spelled out per OS, as the existing Apple full-flush fallback already does, so no Unix-only API is needed.

## Tests

- `a_failed_directory_flush_is_reported_not_swallowed` injects a failing `sync_dir` through `AtomicFs`. The save retur…

title: fix(format): serialise directory bundle saves with a bundle-wide lock
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #4957.

A directory-bundle save:
1. lists the objects already in the bundle;
2. writes the objects its document needs that are missing or damaged;
3. publishes its manifest;
4. removes the listed objects its manifest doesn't reference.

Nothing coordinated two writers. Two `PcraftWriter`s, or two processes, saving into one bundle could interleave. One writer could then remove an object that the other writer reused, and whose manifest wins. Both saves report success, and the final bundle references a missing object.

## Change

`save_dir` now holds an exclusive lock on `save.lock` in the bundle root for the whole save, from listing objects through cleanup. The lock is the OS advisory file lock: std `File::try_lock`, `LockFileEx` on Windows and `flock` on Unix.
- **Crash-safe:** the lock is released when the save ends or the process dies, so a crash leaves no stale lock.
- **Waiting:** a save that finds the lock held retries for up to 10 s (`PcraftWriter::set_lock_wait`). It then fails with "another save of … is in progress; nothing was written", before writing anything.
- **No file locks:** a file system without file locks (some network shares) saves unlocked, as before.
- **Safe to open:** `save.lock` is validated like the bundle's other entries (it must be a plain file below the root, not a symlink) before it's opened. It's empty, and loaders ignore it.

The crate docs, the format chapter of the book and `docs/development.md` list the new entry.

This covers concurrent writers. Readers that load while a save removes objects aren't covered, as before; the issue mentions them, but they're a separate change.

## Tests

`directory_save_waits_for_the_bundle_lock`: the test holds the bundle's lock itself.
- A save with a 100 ms wait fails with the "in progress" error, and no manifest or object is written.
- Once the lock is released, the same writer saves and the bundle loads as the document.

On `main` the save ignores the lock and writes. I also tried a randomize…

title: GPU composite: lower-stack cache chunks have no texture view
author: mcsantiago
body:
## What

The lower-stack (prefix) cache in `crates/gpu/src/prefix.rs` stores composited chunks in textures that are only copied to and from (`COPY_SRC | COPY_DST`). They were created through `Tex::new`, which always creates a default view. Vulkan rejects a view on an image with no sampled, storage or attachment usage:

```
VALIDATION [VUID-VkImageViewCreateInfo-image-04441]
vkCreateImageView(): pCreateInfo->image (VkImage …[pc_compose_prefix]) was created with
VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_SRC_BIT|VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT but requires …
```

wgpu doesn't validate this, so it only shows up in debug builds on Linux with the Vulkan validation layers installed, once for each new chunk while painting. The view was never used.

## Fix

`Chunk` now holds a bare `wgpu::Texture` created directly, with no view. No change to rendering or to the cache's behaviour.

## Testing

- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test -p photocraft-gpu --lib --tests`: all pass
- Debug build on Linux (Vulkan, validation layers on): the validation error appeared while painting before this change and is gone after it. The existing tests don't hit this path with validation enabled, so there's no automated regression test.

## Related

#5288 also edits `prefix.rs` (the lower-stack cache follows an edit up the stack) but keeps the `Tex::new(... COPY_SRC | COPY_DST)` call, so it doesn't fix this. The two will probably conflict. Whichever merges second should keep the view-less chunk texture.

File › Scripts › Browse listed Photoshop `.js`/`.jsx` files, then failed with a JSON parse error. PhotoCraft scripts are JSON or one-command-per-line lists, not ExtendScript.

- `file.scripts.browse` rejects `.js`/`.jsx`/`.jsxbin`/`.psjs`/`.ccjs` (path or `name`) with an error that PhotoCraft scripts are JSON/command lists, not Photoshop ExtendScript.
- The picker keeps listing Photoshop's script types (as #2452 asked, matching Photoshop's filter) plus `.json`, `.txt` and `.pcdroplet`, so someone looking for their Photoshop scripts gets told why they won't run instead of not finding them. The UI passes the picked file's name to the engine so the rejection fires for picker picks, not just CLI/MCP paths.

Fixes #5406

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib automate_cmds::tests`
- [x] `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib file_dialog`
- [ ] File › Scripts › Browse… picker shows json/txt/pcdroplet plus jsx/js, and picking a `.jsx` shows the ExtendScript error

title: IO: open .psd through the PSD reader, not codecs (#5258)
author: vbasky
body:
## Summary
Opening a `.psd` (and `.psb` / `.psdt`) went through `photocraft-codecs` whenever the import path did not see an `8BPS` prefix first. Codecs do not handle Photoshop documents (`from_extension("psd")` is `None`), so File › Open failed with `codec: unrecognized image format`.

PSD/PSB/PSDT now follow the same rule as `.pcraft` / `.ora` / `.pdn`: a declared Photoshop extension always reaches the PSD loader (magic still wins for a renamed file). The open dialog also lists a Photoshop filter.

Fixes #5258.

## Test plan
- `cargo test -p photocraft-io --lib photoshop_extension_reaches_the_psd_loader`
- Open a `.psd`, `.PSD`, `.psb`, and `.psdt` with File › Open; they should load as documents, not `codec: unrecognized image format`.
- A non-Photoshop file named `.psd` should report a PSD parse error, not a codec miss.

title: TIFF: keep ExtraSamples unassociated alpha as a channel (#5301)
author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #5301.

TIFF ExtraSamples unassociated alpha (`2`) is now a document alpha channel (opaque Background + Alpha 1), as in Photoshop, instead of layer transparency that hid the colour samples. Saving a document with an alpha channel writes ExtraSamples again. Associated extra samples (`1`) stay layer transparency.

Tests cover 8/16/32-bit RGB, gray, and CMYK.

title: Color Picker: Only Web Colors snaps every edit (#4995)
author: vbasky

- Remember the checkbox on the Color panel so foreground, field, command, type-style and layer-style pickers all open with the same setting.
- Keep the hex field in sync when another path changes the colour (it used to keep the unsnapped digits while focused).

Fixes #4995.

title: Restore Ctrl/Cmd + mouse-wheel zoom (#5363)
author: vbasky
body:

Ctrl + scrollwheel zoomed in 0.5.0 and panned sideways in 0.8.2 because egui treated COMMAND as a horizontal-scroll modifier. Ctrl/Cmd + a notched wheel zooms ×1.1 around the pointer again. Shift still pans sideways. Fractional Ctrl+wheel from a precision touchpad remains a pinch.

title: Trackpad pinch: two-axis scroll zooms the canvas (#5122)
author: vbasky
body:

A pinch on some Linux/Wayland pads arrived as a two-axis mouse-wheel scroll and panned. Those gestures become pinch zoom. A one-axis two-finger scroll still pans.

title: Isolate live distortion tools per document (#5115)
author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #5115.

Modal distort tools (Puppet Warp, Liquify, Free Transform distortions) kept UI state across documents, which broke undo, leaked layers into other tabs, and could block delete. The live tool is cancelled when its document is left or closed.

title: Curves: apply to masks, alpha, and Quick Mask (#5335)
author: vbasky
body:
Fixes #5335.

Curves only ran on colour components. When a layer mask, saved selection, or Quick Mask is targeted, Curves applies to that channel. The channel popup shows its Channels-panel name and a neutral curve; colour components keep their tints.

title: Fix integer overflow in clipped warp bounds
author: Skyfuller1303
body:
`warp` converted the inverse-mapped tile footprint to `i32` and then added or subtracted 3. For strongly skewed finite affines the cast saturates, so that arithmetic overflowed (panic in debug builds, wrap-around in release). The footprint now uses `saturating_sub`/`saturating_add`, and the source-centre fallback sums in `f64`, so rects with large coordinates cannot overflow either.

Adds `crates/algo/tests/warp_clipped.rs` with four tests. `inverse_footprint_handles_extreme_finite_affines` panicked with "attempt to subtract with overflow" before this change. `source_center_does_not_add_extreme_coordinates_in_i32` already passes without the fix (the invertible clip path is taken), so it only loosely guards the `f64` change.

This fix was found while working on #3446 and is split out from it.

## Checks
- Windows: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test -p photocraft-algo --locked`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-algo --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`
- Ubuntu (local WSL, clean cache): workspace tests and clippy (`-D warnings`)

Refs #3446

author: Skyfuller1303
body:
Preparation for splitting #3446 into reviewable parts. These are moves and signature changes only, with no behaviour change, so the later feature PRs show only the new code:

- The Shape tools' options bar body moves from `vector_ui.rs` into a new `shape_options.rs`, and the fill/stroke swatch with its colour helpers moves into a new `shape_paint_ui.rs`. The code is unchanged; `vector_ui` keeps the mode dropdown and calls `shape_options::options_bar`.
- The gradient stop strip no longer reaches into the app: it returns a `StopAction` (preview, commit, edit colour) and the gradient panel / preset editor run the same commands as before.
- The pattern library grid is pulled out of `pattern_picker` as `pattern_grid`, so another popup can show it inline.
- `move_ui::shown_offset` is renamed to `shown_layer_offset`.

Existing tests pass unchanged (two test imports follow the moved helpers). No UI change, so no screenshots.

title: Shapes: independent fill and stroke paints (solid, gradient, pattern), part 1
author: Skyfuller1303
body:
Pattern fills on shape layers rendered as transparent, and the shape commands only kept part of a paint. Gradient opacity stops, midpoints, offset, dither and align, solid alpha or non-RGB colours, and pattern angle, phase and link were dropped or reset on the way through `shape.create`, `shape.edit` and `shape.info`.

This is the first part of splitting #3446. It changes only the rendering and engine side, with no UI changes:

- Pattern tiles and placement move from `photocraft-compose` into `photocraft-vector` (`photocraft_vector::pattern`, re-exported by compose). Sampling now handles non-finite and huge coordinates. A tile over 64 MiB samples its copy-on-write surface instead of allocating a second full buffer.
- The vector renderer resolves pattern paints from the document's pattern table and samples them in the document's colour mode, for the fill and the stroke independently (`Paint::Pattern`, `CompiledShape::with_patterns`, `render_shape_with_patterns`). The CPU and GPU fill/stroke split for clipped layers and interior effects uses the same patterns.
- `shape.create` and `shape.edit` accept and report the complete paint model. Malformed values return errors before the document changes. A pattern paint resolves a document or library pattern and embeds its tile in the same undo step.
- Copy/Paste Fill and Copy/Paste Stroke keep a snapshot of the referenced pattern. Pasting still works after the source document is closed, and pasting refuses to overwrite a different pattern that has the same id.

## Checks
- Windows: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked --features heif`, tests and clippy (`-D warnings`) for vector, compose, engine and gpu (the GPU parity suite ran on a real adapter, including the new `patterned_shape_fill_and_stroke_clip_and_effects_match_cpu`), `cargo xtask layers`, the `panic_hunt` fuzz test (`--ignored`) and `cargo xtask wasm`

title: Make interactive printing use native system dialogs
author: ZyntaaX
body:
Interactive Print previously either submitted directly or fell back to PDF-oriented behavior, and some settings such as grayscale could leave the preview out of sync with the generated job. This change makes File > Print prepare the page in PhotoCraft and then always ask for confirmation in the platform print UI.

## What changed

- keep orientation, auto-rotation, paper, scaling, position, resolution, grayscale, duplex, copies, collate, and driver choices consistent between the preview and generated output
- open the native confirmation path for every interactive Print action: Preview's standard print sheet on macOS, the XDG Print portal on Linux, and the Windows Print dialog
- treat cancellation as a no-op: no job is submitted, no settings are remembered, and no print event is emitted
- retain direct submission for Print One Copy, matching its repeat-last-job behavior
- add focused macOS/Linux/Windows CI and document the adapters and remaining print-parity limits

On macOS, PhotoCraft first opens its uniquely named temporary PDF through Launch Services so sandboxed Preview receives permission to read it, then asks Preview to show the standard print sheet. The temporary document is closed after confirmation, cancellation, or error.

## Validation

- `PHOTOCRAFT_NO_PRINT=1 cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests`

title: i18n(rtl): Arabic and RTL chrome strings read in visual word order (#5159)
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
Fixes #5159.

## Root cause

Canvas text was always correct — the text engine lays it out with parley, which does UAX #9 bidi. The UI chrome was not: egui/epaint 0.36 has **no bidi reordering at all** — it segments text only by font face and lays those runs out left-to-right in stream order. Arabic words are each shaped correctly by HarfRust, but spaces resolve to the default Latin font, so `لا شيء مكتوب هنا` becomes font runs `[لا][sp][شيء][sp]…` placed in logical order — **word order reads reversed** in the Layers panel row, the in-app window title, tabs and other chrome labels.

## Fix

`photocraft_ui_egui::bidi::visual(&str) -> Cow<str>` (`unicode-bidi`, already in the lock graph through usvg):
- LTR-only input returns the borrowed input (zero cost for the common case).
- RTL runs emit their whitespace-separated units in reverse order; characters inside a unit keep logical order (HarfRust already produces within-word visual order — reversing characters would double-reverse).
- The paragraph level is forced LTR, so a filename's extension and any trailing markers (zoom, depth, the dirty `*`) stay to the right of the Arabic name, as Photoshop lays them out. (First-strong put `.jpg` at the far left of a tab title; caught by a visual audit of an offscreen snapshot and fixed before this PR.)

~50 display call sites go through it: layer rows (`truncated`), Layer Properties, layer picker, drag ghost, in-app title bar, tab strips (`elided`), canvas tab meta, status bar, in-app menu labels (Open Recent, Window), command palette, dialogs, notices, dropdown widgets, brush/preset/artboard/comp/channel names, camera-raw/liquify/wide-angle/gallery dialog titles, stack dialog, jobs cards, prefs.

Kept logical **on purpose**: `ViewportCommand::Title` and native macOS menus (the OS does its own bidi), `TextEdit` content (egui's caret indexing is off in RTL text, emilk/egui#8576, #8577), accessibility labels (screen readers do their own bidi).

## Tests

- 10 unit tests in `bidi.r…

title: fix(automation): refuse a group/world-readable control-token file (#4966)
author: wwewtech
body:
﻿Fixes #4966. An operator-supplied --control-token-file was read and syntax-validated without checking the file itself, so a group- or world-readable token file would be trusted as the control credential. Newly created files are already 0600 (create_token_file); this closes the gap for existing files.

read_token_file now opens the handle and validates what was actually opened: it must be a regular file, and on Unix its mode must not be group/other-accessible (mode & 0o077 == 0), otherwise it is refused with an actionable message. The token is then read from the same handle and validated as before. A missing file still maps to an Io error so server_token auto-creates it unchanged.

Adds a Unix regression test (0644 refused, 0600 read). The two existing token tests are unaffected: control_exit_code.rs passes both a token and a file (rejected before any read), and the round-trip test creates its file at 0600.

Note: I verified by source review and rustfmt --check; the workspace test suite was not run locally (cold build of the engine dependency is too heavy for this environment), so CI is the gate.

title: fix(pen): keep unfinished paths in their original document

title: Canvas: paint after the frame's input, so releases don't blink
author: deadmeu
body:
Several tools blink for one frame when you let go of the mouse. A Rectangle shape vanishes and reappears; a marquee loses its marching ants, or flashes the previous selection's; a guide dragged with the Move tool jumps back to where it was, then to where it was dropped. They share one cause: the canvas paints the image before it handles the frame's mouse input.

### What was wrong

Each frame, `canvas::canvas_view` copied the document, painted the image (the document, the selection's ants, artboards, pixel grid), then handled the pointer (tools run their commands here), then drew the overlays (guides, drag previews, path outlines, transform boxes). The image showed the document before the frame's input; the overlays mostly showed tool state after it.

On the frame that handles a release, the release clears the tool's preview and commits its result, but the image was already painted without the result:

| Case | What showed for one frame |
|---|---|
| Rectangle shape tool (and the other shape tools) | Nothing: the preview was gone, the new layer not yet painted |
| Rectangular Marquee, first selection | No ants |
| Rectangular Marquee, replacing a selection | The previous selection's ants |
| Guide dragged with the Move tool | The guide back at its old position (guides were drawn from the copy taken before the input) |

The same order also made everything the pointer does show a frame late: a Move drag drew the layer where the previous frame left it (`move_outline_tests` documented this).

It had been patched case by case: Crop's default mode paints after the input since #3206 ("other tools keep their existing paint order"), and Layer Edges reserves its drawing slot and fills it after the input (#2413).

### Change

- `canvas_view` paints after the input for every tool, as Crop's default mode already did, from the document as the input left it. The image, the selection outline, guides, path outlines and the tools' previews then all show the same moment. The paint clo…

title: feat(android): add tablet and S Pen shell
author: wroomhers
body:
Adds PhotoCraft's first Android tablet shell, so the editor can be used directly on tablets and with an S Pen.

- Enlarges the automatic interface scale for touch-first devices while retaining explicit user scale choices.
