title: fix(engine): reserve the define-brush tip buffer fallibly (#212)
author: wwewtech
body:
﻿Part of the #212 fallible-allocation effort. brush.defineFromSelection built the sampled brush tip as one raw vec![0.0f32; w*h] over the whole selection, so a large selection could abort the process on allocation instead of failing gracefully. Route it through the engine fallible allocator (crate::allocation::filled), matching read_rgba/blend_into in the same crate, so an allocation failure is a normal Err and the document and brush are left untouched. Same size expression, only fallible.

Adds a regression test using the existing failpoint (fail_next_for_test) that mirrors fade_allocation_failure_keeps_document_and_history.

Note: verified by source review and rustfmt --check; the engine test suite was not run locally (cold build of the engine and its dependencies is too heavy for this environment), so CI is the gate.

title: fix(tiff): keep a TIFF's alpha channel, and add a tiffCompression save option
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #5301.

Photoshop writes a document's alpha channel into a TIFF as an *unspecified* extra sample (`ExtraSamples = 0`), as opposed to transparency (`2`, unassociated, or `1`, associated). PhotoCraft's TIFF decoder kept only samples marked as transparency and dropped the rest without a word. So:
- the reporter's `decal_common.tif` (RGB plus one unspecified extra sample, layered) opened without its "Alpha 1" channel;
- a document's alpha channel was never written to a TIFF.

## Change

**Decode** (`photocraft-codecs`):
- With no extra sample marked as transparency, the first unspecified one is decoded as the alpha, flagged by the new `Metadata::alpha_is_channel`. Like an alpha that isn't the first extra sample (#1349), it's read through the decoder's every-sample path.
- Extra samples beyond the colour and the alpha are still not imported, but now say so: `DecodeWarning::ExtraSamplesSkipped`.

**Open** (`photocraft-io`):
- A flat TIFF with such an alpha opens as an opaque Background plus that alpha channel. It's named from the TIFF's Photoshop resources (1045 Unicode names, else 1006 Pascal names), else "Alpha 1". It reuses the Targa helper (`alpha_to_channel`).
- A layered TIFF already turns the merged image's extra channels into named alpha channels through the PSD path. It now receives the channel instead of a three-channel image.

**Save:**
- With no transparency, a flat or layered TIFF writes the document's first alpha channel (spot channels don't count) as an unspecified extra sample, with its name in the Photoshop resources.
- The encoder writes `ExtraSamples = 0` for a flagged alpha and `2` for transparency.
- With transparency, the one extra sample stays the transparency, as before.
- Alpha channels left out are named in a warning.

**Compression**, the comment on the issue: the TIFF encoder already supports LZW and ZIP, but nothing exposed them, so every TIFF was saved uncompressed.
- Save, batch and export commands now take `"tiffCompression": "none" |…

title: test(type): PostScript names guessed apart from their installed family resolve exactly
author: FinnNk
body:
Closes #5044 (already fixed on `main`; this adds its cases as a regression test).

#5044 reported, on 0.8.2, two PSD fonts reported missing although installed:
- `BMDoHyeon`: the family is "BM DoHyeon", but the name was guessed as "BM Do Hyeon".
- `Daum_SemiBold`: the name was guessed as "Daum_Semi Bold".

On current `main` both resolve to their installed faces, and neither is reported missing:
- `FontDb::resolve_postscript` finds the exact face by PostScript name (#1844).
- Since #608, missing-font detection and Replace Missing Fonts follow that same resolution instead of the stored family label.

## Test

`camel_case_and_underscore_postscript_names_resolve_to_their_installed_faces` registers the bundled Inter face renamed in memory (the existing `renamed_face` helper, so no font file is added) as each of the reporter's fonts. For each one, it checks three things:
- the family guessed from the PostScript name isn't installed;
- `resolve_postscript` returns the installed family with `exact: true`;
- a run stored with the guessed family isn't reported missing.

## Evidence

`9131eaa3` was checked in a clean checkout on Windows x86_64 (rustc 1.99.0), touched-crate set:
- `cargo fmt --check`, the engine tests (4,568 passed, 0 failed) and engine clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` pass.

title: perf: chisel bevel size changes, CPU passes on threads and GPU fields share their sharp edges (results unchanged)
author: xsvm
body:
A chisel bevel size change rebuilds the bevel's maps over the whole layer region. That is what dragging the Size slider does (P52–P59 in `perf/budgets.toml`). #2119 / #2162 put the distance fields on threads. This PR takes the next two steps, one for each compositor. Every result is bit for bit what it was.

### 1. CPU compositor: the passes after the fields go on threads

Inside `bevel_height` / `bevel_maps`, these passes still ran on one thread over every pixel:

- the chisel height from the two distances
- the texture term
- the highlight/shadow shading (`shade_into`), which runs twice for emboss styles
- the emboss inside/outside `mix`

Each pixel of these passes reads only its own inputs. They now go row by row through the existing `par_units` / `par_fill`, the scoped OS threads the fields use (not rayon, see #276). The per-pixel arithmetic and its order are unchanged. Maps under 65536 pixels, and wasm, stay on the calling thread.

### 2. GPU canvas: a bevel's two fields find their sharp edges once

On the GPU canvas a size change recomputes `BevelInside` and `BevelOutside` on the CPU. Each was its own `distance_field` call, so `sharp_edges` (edge pixels plus refined normals) ran twice on the same window. That was about 17% of the CPU time of these size changes in a profile. The CPU compositor already shared that work.

- The bevel program now asks for both fields in one call (`B::bevel_fields`), so the two always share one reach.
- `sync_fx` recomputes them together through `fx::bevel_fields` → `compose::effects::bevel_distance_fields`.
- If the two are not due over the same rectangle at the same reach, that is an invariant broken. `sync_fx` now returns `Result` and reports it as `Unsupported` rather than falling back to computing them one at a time.
- `field` and `bevel_fields` share one windowing function, `fields_in_windows`: one window natively, bands on wasm.
- In compose, `bevel_height` and `bevel_distance_fields` share `bevel_dists`.
- Cost: while a pai…

title: Blend mode keys: Shift+Alt+letter picks a mode, as in Photoshop
author: paulou-jpg
body:
## What

Photoshop's blend mode letter keys: **Shift+Alt+letter** (Shift+Option on a Mac) picks a blend mode, with Photoshop's letters (N Normal, I Dissolve, R Clear, P Pass Through, K Darken, M Multiply, B Color Burn, A Linear Burn, G Lighten, S Screen, D Color Dodge, W Linear Dodge, O Overlay, F Soft Light, H Hard Light, V Vivid Light, J Linear Light, Z Pin Light, L Hard Mix, E Difference, X Exclusion, U Hue, T Saturation, C Color, Y Luminosity). Darker Color, Lighter Color, Subtract and Divide have no letter, as in Photoshop.

Where the key goes follows Photoshop and the existing Shift+Plus/Minus stepping (#3102):

| Active tool | Effect |
|---|---|
| Brush, Pencil | That tool's mode only, never the layer's. R = Clear |
| Gradient | The gradient's mode |

- Behind (Shift+Alt+Q is consumed and does nothing; there is no Behind mode yet).

title: Design/home screen dashboard
author: ALI88708
body:
## What this changes

The Home screen is what PhotoCraft shows when no document is open. It was a
460-wide card with New, Open, up to six recent files, a Discord button and a row
of community links. Around it the rest of the shell kept drawing: the tool strip,
the tool options bar and the panels dock.

**None of that can act.** With no document open no tool has anything to act on,
and every panel reads "No document". A first-time user lands on a screen framed by
a column of controls that do nothing.

This change makes the Home screen a landing screen.

### The editing chrome hides while Home is up

The tool strip, the tool options bar and the panels dock are hidden while the Home
screen is shown, and come back the moment a document is open. The menu bar and the
status bar stay — they still open files and report zoom and window state. Photoshop
hides the same three on its Home screen.

### TemplatesThe Home screen now shows the New Document dialog's presets as cards, seven
categories, click to open a new document at that size. The cards are drawn by the
dialog's own card drawing and labelled by its own `title`/`size_line`, so a print
preset reads `8.5 x 11 in @ 300 ppi` on both screens rather than drifting into raw
pixels on one of them.

The panel opens on **Photo**, not Recent: Recent lists documents this machine
created, so on a fresh install it is two default sizes and the Home screen reads as
empty.

**Search** matches preset names across every category at once. The tabs are seven
pages to flip through; a name is one.

### A settings column

The Discord button and the link row are off the screen you land on — they live in
the app's own menus. In their place the right column offers the settings a person
wants *before* they start rather than after:

- the current theme, one click to the next (all fourteen; the title bar's theme
  button already cycles them the same way)
- Preferences
- Keyboard Shortcuts

The card below the routing width offers the same things, so…

title: fix(ui): a held arrow key keeps stepping the focused value field (#5474)
author: JuanAntonioRC
body:
Fixes #5474

**Problem.** Holding Up/Down in a value field (e.g. Character panel tracking or font size) stepped it a couple of times, then focus jumped to the field above.

**Cause.**
- After each arrow step, `value_field_box` called `request_focus` on the field, even though the field already had focus.
- egui's `request_focus` replaces the focus state and resets the field's event filter. The `TextEdit` only re-applies `vertical_arrows: true` while it is drawn on the next frame.
- egui reads the next frame's arrow keys in `Focus::begin_pass`, before that happens. So a key repeat landing on the frame right after a step is taken as "move focus up".
- Single presses almost never land on that frame. Held keys repeat every frame, so they always do.

**Fix.** Only request focus when the field no longer has it. That only happens after a typed sum such as `5+5` gives focus up so it can be worked out, which is the case the call was there for.

**Tests.**
- New `held_arrow_keeps_stepping_the_focused_value_field` feeds key-down repeats on consecutive frames, with another field above the focused one.
  - Before the fix: `(14.0, 61.0)`. Focus moved after two steps and the remaining repeats stepped the field above.
  - After the fix: `(10.0, 65.0)`.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib`: 2685 passed. `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings` and rustfmt are clean.

title: perf(retouch): row-parallel Blur/Sharpen dabs, 2.6-3.3x faster strokes (#5426)
author: JuanAntonioRC
body:
Refs #5426. This makes the Blur tool much faster with large brushes. I could not reproduce the crash in the report, so the issue stays open.

**Cause.** The Blur and Sharpen tools ran each dab on a single thread: both passes of `local_blur`'s separable Gaussian, plus the mix back onto the working copy. A 2500 px dab is about 10⁹ multiply-adds.

**Change.**
- Both passes of `algo::retouch::local_blur` now process rows in parallel with rayon, as `blur.rs` already does. So does the per-dab mix in `DabTool::Focus`.
- Each row does exactly the same arithmetic in the same order, so the **output is bit-identical**. After the benchmark strokes, the layer pixels hash the same on main and on this branch, and so do `local_blur`/`local_sharpen` outputs on a random 777×513 RGBA image with alpha.

**Numbers.** `paint.blur`, 200-point stroke on a 6000×4000 noise layer, release build, 10-core Apple silicon:

| brush | commit, main → this | live stroke (`LiveDab`), main → this |
|---|---|---|
| 300 px | 323 ms → 124 ms | 497 ms → 314 ms |
| 1000 px | 1.11 s → 312 ms | 1.70 s → 996 ms |
| 2500 px | 2.77 s → 843 ms | 4.26 s → 2.44 s |

**Still open.** The live stroke gains less because of its serial region copies and `mix_back` on each push. That is left for a follow-up. I did not run `cargo xtask perf`.

**Tests.** `cargo test -p photocraft-algo -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests`: 2342 passed, 0 failed. clippy (`-D warnings`) and rustfmt are clean.

author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5495.

**Why.** Dropdown lists were stuck at about 400 pt. egui's `ComboBox` caps its list at the size its popup has on the frame it opens (`default_area_size`), not only at `.height(420)`. So the Layers panel's 27 blend modes opened with a scrollbar even in tall windows. Next to wheel stepping (#1747) that scrollbar made the list look broken. Photoshop opens the Blend Mode menu at full height, with no scrollbar, whenever it fits on screen.

author: paulou-jpg
body:
> **Stacked on #5478:** this branch includes #5478's commit. Review the second commit only; I'll rebase once #5478 merges.

## What

Photoshop gives these painting tools a **Mode** in the options bar. In PhotoCraft they always painted in Normal.

| Tool | Modes | Where the mode lives |
|---|---|---|
| Clone Stamp, Pattern Stamp, History Brush | the layer modes | the tool's own brush (like its size) |
| Healing Brush | Normal, Multiply, Screen, Darken, Lighten, Color, Luminosity | the tool's own brush |
| Paint Bucket | the layer modes, plus **Clear** after Dissolve | `tool_options.bucket_blend_mode` / `bucket_clear` |

- **Engine:** `paint.bucket` takes `"mode"` (any blend mode, or `"clear"` to erase the filled area). Pass Through, unknown names and non-strings are errors. `algo::paint` gains `FillMode`, threaded through `bucket_fill_inks`, `bucket_fill_region_inks` and `composite_area`. The stamps, History Brush and Healing commands already took `"mode"`; the UI now sends it for both the live stroke and the commit.
- **First brush starts in Normal:** the first time you pick a tool, it used to inherit the previous tool's whole brush, mode included. That was harmless while these tools ignored the mode. It isn't now: a Multiply Brush made the first Clone Stamp stroke multiply. Each tool now starts in Normal, as in Photoshop.
- **Blend mode keys (#5478):** Shift+Alt+letter and Shift+Plus/Minus now reach these tools, staying within each tool's menu (for example, Overlay does nothing on the Healing Brush). `blend_keys::tool_modes` drives both the menus and the keys. Tools with no blend mode of their own (the Erasers, Mixer Brush, Dodge, Burn, Sponge) now pass the keys to the selected layers. This follows the rule for the keys in Photoshop: a tool with a mode takes them, and any other tool passes them to the layers.

## Not in this PR

- Healing's **Replace** mode, which needs engine work.
- A Mode for Spot Healing, Color Replacement, Blur, Sharpen and Smudge. Until then …

title: fix(ui): ⇧ marquee square keeps equal sides on the pixel grid (#5472)
author: sabbirshawon
body:
Fixes #5472

## What was wrong

Holding ⇧ with the Rectangular (or Elliptical) Marquee builds the square in continuous document coordinates (`chrome_ui::marquee_end`). `marquee_px` then snapped each axis to the pixel grid on its own: floor the near edge, ceil the far one. A press between pixels (any zoom other than 100 %, where pointer points land on whole pixels), e.g. (50.3, 50.7) dragged 100.5 px, snapped x to 101 and y to 102. The W/H readout showed uneven values and the committed selection was off by one on one axis.

## Fix

`canvas::marquee_preview_px` now runs `square_px` when the drag is square-constrained (`marquee_is_square`: ⇧ pressed during the drag with the Normal style, or Fixed Ratio with w == h). The shorter side grows to the longer one, away from the press point, so the square still covers every pixel the drag touched. Ants, readout and the release commit share this path, so all three agree.

A non-square Fixed Ratio (e.g. 2:1) still snaps each axis separately; Photoshop's exact rounding there is unverified, so it is left out of this change.

## Tests

- `canvas::tests::square_px_equalises_the_sides_away_from_the_press_point`: documents the uneven snap (`[50, 50, 151, 152]`) and checks both drag directions and the already-square no-op.
- `marquee_tests::shift_square_pressed_between_pixels_has_equal_sides`: Rect and Ellipse marquee through the real canvas: readout 102 × 102, selection 50..152 on both axes. Failed before the fix (readout 101 × 102).

Gate: `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib` (marquee/canvas/chrome_ui modules, 107 pass), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

title: fix(ui): reset caret blink phase on navigation and typing (#5511)
author: safvanedge
body:
### Summary

1. **Photoshop Parity**: In Photoshop and standard OS text controls, pressing an arrow key, typing, or clicking immediately resets the caret blink phase so the caret stays solid and visible while navigating or typing.
2. In `UiState`, added a transient `caret_blink_time: f64` timestamp (`#[serde(skip)]`).
3. In `type_tool::handle_keys`, reset `app.ui.caret_blink_time` whenever any keyboard event (arrow navigation, text insertion, deletion, paste) is handled.
4. In `type_tool::draw_overlay`, compute blink phase relative to elapsed time since `app.ui.caret_blink_time`, keeping the caret solid for 530ms upon each interaction before resuming blinking.
5. In `type_tool::handle_keys`, schedule precise repaint requests at the next phase toggle boundary.
6. Added a regression test `arrow_keys_reset_caret_blink_phase` in `type_tool.rs`.

Closes #5511

title: Layered TIFF: Photoshop opened only the composite of a many-layer file (PSB-style layer data)
author: llduyll10
body:
## Problem

A layered TIFF saved by PhotoCraft from a document with many canvas-sized layers opens in Photoshop with an error and only one locked Background layer (the composite); the layers are gone. PhotoCraft itself reopens the file with all its layers, so the problem is invisible from our side.

Seen on a 3000×3441 RGB/8 mockup with 180 layers (6 smart objects): the export warns `estimated encoded size exceeds 2 GB; written as PSB`, and tag 37724 starts with `Adobe Photoshop Document Data V0002` (8-byte lengths). Every layered TIFF that Photoshop itself writes, including large ones, uses `Adobe Photoshop Document Data Block` (4-byte lengths). A reader that parses the block with PSD-style lengths, as Photoshop does, finds 0 layers in our file.

## Cause

`export_layered` (`crates/io/src/tiff_layers.rs`) builds the layer data through the PSD exporter, which switches to PSB when `estimate_psd_size` passes 2 GB (`document_to_psd_nested`). The estimate counts every layer plane uncompressed: 180 layers, 49 of them canvas-sized, plus a 6388×9069 smart object, come to ~2.57 GB, while the real layer data is ~111 MB. So the layered TIFF got PSB-style data it never needed.

## Fix

- `PsdExportOptions` gains `size_limit_psb` (default `true`): whether the exporter may switch to PSB on the size estimate. `.psd` saves are unchanged.
- The layered TIFF turns it off and writes PSD-style data, as Photoshop does. It writes PSB-style data only past 30000 px, when PSB is forced, or when encoding really overflows a 32-bit length (`PsdError::LimitExceeded`). In that last case it rebuilds the model as PSB and warns.

## Tests

- New `tiff_layers::tests::layered_tiff_ignores_the_uncompressed_size_estimate`: 140 hidden solid fills on a 2048² canvas pass the 2 GB estimate (each counts as a canvas-sized plane) while their real pixels are empty. The layered TIFF carries `SIGNATURE` (PSD-style), with no PSB warning, and reopens with every layer. A `.psd` save of the same document is still w…

Adds an **opt-in, off-by-default** `self-hosted-update` feature to `apps/photocraft-web`, for one case only: people who **host PhotoCraft's web build on their own server**. title: i18n: add the Bulgarian (bg) catalog
author: cecobald
body:
## What and why

title: Value fields: the mouse wheel steps them, as in Photoshop (#5473)
author: wanikhawar
body:
Closes #5473. Also covers the number-field part of #4061. Its dropdowns are a separate change.

## What changes

The mouse wheel now changes the value of PhotoCraft's number fields (`widgets::value_field` and everything built on it: options bar, Layers panel Opacity/Fill, dialogs).

- **Clicked into a field (Photoshop's behaviour):** the wheel changes it wherever the pointer is, even over the canvas. `field_wheel::begin_frame` runs at the top of `App::ui` and takes plain and Shift wheel events out of the frame's input. The canvas and panels therefore don't scroll or pan. Alt and Ctrl/Cmd + wheel still go to the view (zoom).
- **Hovering without clicking (Photopea's behaviour):** the wheel changes the field too, but only for a scroll that *starts* over it. Events less than 0.3 s apart count as one scroll. A panel being scrolled keeps scrolling when a field passes under the pointer, so values don't change by accident. Hovering never puts the cursor in the field.
- **Step size** is the same as the Up/Down keys: 1 per notch (0.01 for small-range fields such as gamma), ×10 with Shift. A typed sum such as `5+5` is calculated before the step. A step that would give a non-finite value is dropped.
- `widgets::count_notches` is now shared by the slider wheel and the fields.

## Photoshop behaviour

I didn't have Photoshop to test with. Photoshop shortcut guides and user reports agree that a field takes the wheel once it has been clicked into, and that Shift gives bigger steps. They also say hovering alone does nothing in Photoshop. Photopea does change the value on hover, and we chose to keep that. Nothing I found says whether Photoshop needs the pointer to stay over the field after the click. For that reason the `docs/ui-parity.md` row is marked **partial**.

title: Type: keep text selection highlight visible while Command/Ctrl is held
author: safvanedge
body:
Fixes #5541.

### Description
1. In `crates/ui-egui/src/type_tool.rs:draw_overlay`, when `mods.command` is active (holding `Ctrl`/`Cmd`, such as during `Ctrl + A` or text editing shortcuts), `type_transform::draw` draws the temporary transform handles and returns `true`, which previously caused `draw_overlay` to `return;` early. This suppressed the drawing of active text selection highlights, carets, and preedit underlines until `Ctrl` was released.
2. - Match Photoshop's Type transform visual styling: crisp 1px dark border, white square handles with dark stroke, no 3px shadow, and no center pivot crosshair.

title: fix(zoom): Restore smooth wheel zoom and animate committed zoom field inputs
author: sn-o-w
body:
This also closes https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/5102

### Description
1. **Snapping wheel zoom:** In 0.5.0, canvas wheel zooming was driven by `egui`'s `smooth_scroll_delta`, which smoothly interpolated each mouse wheel notch across frames. When `wheel_nav` was introduced in 0.6.0, continuous wheel zooming (`⌥/Alt + wheel` and `Zoom with Scroll Wheel`) switched to reading the unsmoothed `i.raw` delta and dropped the smoothed tail, causing notched mouse wheels to snap instantaneously on the first frame.
2. **Abrupt per-keystroke zoom field jumps:** Typing a new percentage into the status bar or Navigator zoom fields updated the canvas on every keystroke and jumped instantaneously without animation.

### Solution

#### 1. Smooth wheel zoom (`wheel_nav`)
Update `wheel_nav::classify` to feed `i.scroll` (`smooth_scroll_delta`) into `step(...)` instead of `i.raw`:
- **Restores smooth 0.5.0 wheel zoom:** Notched wheel zoom once again animates smoothly across frames using `egui`'s built-in scroll smoothing, matching wheel panning behaviour.
- **Preserves exact `×1.1` per-notch scaling:** Because `step(dy)` is exponential (`NOTCH.powf(dy / notch)`) and `egui`'s smoothed per-frame deltas sum to the full notch distance ($\sum \Delta y_k = \text{notch}$), multiplying the per-frame zoom factors across the smoothed tail converges to the exact `×1.1` step per notch:
  $$\prod 1.1^{\Delta y_k / \text{notch}} = 1.1^{(\sum \Delta y_k) / \text{notch}} = 1.1$$
- **Keeps `⇧/Shift` snap-zoom instant:** Ladder snap zooming (`Wheel::SnapZoom`) continues to read `i.raw` so discrete rung steps remain immediate without tail overshoot.
- **Safe `Alt` release during the tail:** `wheel_nav::read` latches the `Alt` modifier state from the latest `Event::MouseWheel` into temporary context storage (`alt_id`), so releasing `Alt` mid-tail finishes the zoom cleanly rather than turning into a pan.

title: Fix filter preview live during drag
author: agent-346022
body:
## Summary

Dragging a filter slider repainted nothing: the canvas changed only after the pointer came to rest, in one jump.

`ensure_filter_preview` had two gates for what may be shown, and they disagreed. The **publish gate** took a finished worker result only on exact equality with the current request, parameters included — so while the slider keeps moving, every completion landed after the value had moved on, none ever matched, and nothing was stored. The **display gate**, further down the same function, compared document, revision, dialog, layer, channel target, command and proxy factor but deliberately omitted `params`, so a slightly old frame stays up mid-drag. Its comment says so:

> Keep the last preview during a drag, but never one from another source or dialog.

It was written to keep exactly the frame the publish gate refused to store.

- `filter_dialog.rs` — add `FilterPreviewKey::same_target`: those seven fields, deliberately not the parameters. That is what a drag produces.
- `canvas.rs` — publish on `same_target` instead of full equality and let the display gate decide. Both now share one predicate, so they cannot drift apart again.

Three guards on a stale frame, each with a test:

| Guard | Without it |
|---|---|
| must have a frame to show | an empty result replaces a good frame and the gate paints "nothing" — the canvas blinks back to unfiltered |
| must not displace an exact frame | drag away and back, and the frame for the value on the way out overwrites the correct one |
| errors stay on the exact request | a value the pointer has passed raises a notice the user cannot act on |

`fresh` stays an exact match: relaxed, the canvas would believe it had the current request after the first frame and never compute again.

title: fix(heif): a grid's ICC profile is inherited from its tiles
author: sidney
body:
Fixes the profile half of #5539. The range half is upstream and is explained below.

### What was wrong

`colr` is optional on a `grid` derivation, and phone cameras write it on the coded tiles rather than
on the grid item. A OnePlus 11 photograph carries one `prof` (Display P3) on each of its 48 `hvc1`
tiles and nothing on the grid, so `metadata()` — which asked `ctx.props(ctx.meta.primary)` and
stopped there — came back with no profile, and the photo was taken for sRGB. Exporting such a
document to PNG wrote no colour information at all (IHDR, pHYs, eXIf, IDAT, IEND), while a
JPEG-sourced document kept its profile.

### The change

`icc_for_item` returns the item's own profile when it has one and otherwise the first tile that
does, reached through `heic_rs::Context::grid`. Six lines in `crates/heif`; no new dependency, so
the crate stays standalone.

A coded picture is unaffected — `grid` returns `Ok(None)`, so there is nothing to inherit from — and
a grid that labels itself still wins over its tiles.

### Why the range is not fixed here

The same root cause has a second half: the samples are decoded as limited range and clipped. That
one cannot be fixed in this repo.

`crates/heif` pins `heic-rs = "=0.1.4"`, whose `decode.rs:57` resolves colour as
`p.nclx.unwrap_or_default()` on the primary item, with `Nclx::default()` being BT.709 *limited*. For
a file whose only range signal is the HEVC SPS VUI — heic-rs documents its VUI parser as "traversed
but not used" — that default is wrong, and 7% of the photograph's pixels come back with a channel
pinned to 0. `DecodeOptions` offers no range override, the grid colour path
(`convert_source`/`Source::Mosaic`) is `pub(crate)`, and the clipping happens inside heic-rs before
PhotoCraft sees the buffer, so there is nothing to override or undo at this layer.

Both halves are already open upstream: tbraun96/heic-rs#11 (inheritance, for their issue 6) and
tbraun96/heic-rs#7 (the VUI range fallback). Neither is merged, and that r…

title: Linux: build an Arch package (.pkg.tar.zst)
author: ujo4eva
body:
Adds an Arch Linux package to the Linux release, next to the `.deb` and `.rpm`. Arch users (Manjaro, EndeavourOS, Omarchy, ...) can then `sudo pacman -U` it, and ArtCraft Launcher can install and update it through pacman (storytold/craft-launcher#389).

## What changes

- `packaging/linux/package.sh`:
  - adds an `arch` format, on by default;
  - builds `photocraft-<ver>-linux-<arch>.pkg.tar.zst` with nfpm's `archlinux` packager from the same `nfpm.yaml`.

  nfpm can't rename a package per format and doesn't env-expand `archlinux.packager`, so the script writes a copy of the config with both set.
- `packaging/linux/nfpm.yaml`:
  - an `overrides.archlinux` block with Arch dependencies: `glibc gcc-libs hicolor-icon-theme libxkbcommon libxkbcommon-x11 wayland libx11 libxcb libxcursor libxi vulkan-icd-loader`;
  - `provides: photocraft`;
  - `conflicts: photocraft, photocraft-bin, photocraft-git`.
- **Named `ai.storyteller.photocraft`, not `photocraft`.** The AUR already has `photocraft`, `photocraft-bin` and `photocraft-git`. An AUR helper treats an installed package with an AUR name as its own and would rebuild it on the next update. The bundle id is also how the launcher tells this package (which it updates) from an AUR build (which it leaves to the AUR helper).
- The README's Linux download table gains an Arch row.

**No workflow change is needed.** `craft-common-actions` uploads and checksums everything `package.sh` writes to `dist/release`, and the riscv64 job passes `--formats "deb rpm tar"`.

## Notes

- nfpm has no `optdepends` for Arch, so the Debian `recommends` have no Arch equivalent.
- Pre-releases sort correctly: `0.7.0-rc.1` becomes pkgver `0.7.0rc.1`, which pacman places before `0.7.0`. Arm64 maps to `aarch64`.

## Testing

- I ran `package.sh --skip-build --formats arch` with the binaries from the published v0.8.2 x86_64 tarball, checked against `SHA256SUMS.txt`. It produced `photocraft-0.8.2-linux-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst`.

title: Autosave test: wait for the sidecar before checking the retried revision (fixes Windows CI on main)
author: Higgs32584
body:
`main` has failed `test (windows-latest)` since ed7df56a ("recover autosaves with missing sidecars", #4967), and every PR that merges `main` inherits it ([main's run](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/actions/runs/38532362162)):

```
services::tests::failed_background_autosave_is_reported_and_retried_without_another_edit ... FAILED
panicked at apps\photocraft\src\services.rs:941:9
  left: 0
 right: 2
```

### Cause

ed7df56a made `list_recovery` also list a committed `.pcraft` bundle that has no `.json` sidecar yet, rebuilding its info from the manifest with `revision: 0`. An autosave publishes the bundle first and the sidecar after it.

The retry half of this test polled `list_recovery` until the list was non-empty while the background autosave was running. So it could catch the bundle between those two steps, stop polling, and read revision 0. On Linux that window is too short to hit; on the Windows runner it is hit every time.

### The change

The poll now waits until an entry carries the expected revision (the sidecar has been written) instead of stopping at the first entry. The assertions after it are unchanged. Test-only.

This leaves ed7df56a's behaviour alone: listing a sidecar-less bundle is what #4967 asked for, and in the app `list_recovery` runs at start-up, not while the same session is autosaving.

`rustfmt --check` on the changed file. Not built or run locally; the Windows CI job on this PR is the check. #5337 is one of the PRs that went red on Windows only because it merged `main` after ed7df56a.

title: Large document: a zoomed-out background redraw shows a reduced picture first (part of #5106)
author: ianswope
body:
Part of #5106 ("Gigapixel documents with dense content still cost a full-resolution composite per full refresh", the zoomed-out case), as claimed in https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/5106#issuecomment-6167574522. Part 2 of the plan in #4024.

### Problem

Since #5001, a full CPU redraw of a large document runs in the background, visible blocks first. At fit-to-screen every block is visible, though, so the picture appears block by block over the whole redraw: about 7 s on a 16000 × 10000 document here before the canvas is complete.

### Change

- **`background_redraw`:** when a redraw starts with the view at 50% or less and covering what the view shows, the worker first composites a reduced picture, then the blocks as before.
  - The scale matches the mip level the canvas shader samples, `⌊−log2(scale)⌋`, from 1/2 to 1/16 (`preview_level`).
  - It covers only the blocks still to draw that the view shows (`preview_area`). At 40% on a huge document, the off-screen part isn't composited twice.
  - It's drawn from `preview_document`: `proxy::proxy_document` with layer effects (`scale_effects`), mask and vector-mask feathers and vector-mask paths scaled by 1/k. So documents with styles or vector masks get a believable picture too. `proxy_faithful` would otherwise rule them out.
  - The UI thread uploads it only where blocks are still pending (one upload for a fresh redraw).
  - An edit before it lands restarts it on the edited document, like the blocks. A stale picture can't land over the edit: the old worker's channel is dropped.
- **`gpu_canvas`:** `upload_level` writes a rect of one mip level and rebuilds the levels below it (`write_level`, `regenerate_mips_from`; `write` and `regenerate_mips` are now the level-0 cases). Each full-resolution block still rebuilds every level from level 0 as it lands. That replaces the reduced picture there, so **the finished texture is the same as before**.
- **`canvas`:** `ensure_gpu` passes the view's scale (`zoom × pixel…

title: Fix flaky autosave retry test: wait for the sidecar, not the first listed entry
author: Skyfuller1303
body:
`services::tests::failed_background_autosave_is_reported_and_retried_without_another_edit` fails intermittently (seen on Windows CI: `left: 0, right: 2` at `assert_eq!(recovered[0].info.revision, revision)`).

Since ed7df56a2 (#4967), `list_recovery` also reports a committed `.pcraft` bundle whose JSON sidecar has not been written yet, with metadata rebuilt from the manifest and `revision: 0`. The autosave worker writes the bundle first and the sidecar right after it, so for a moment the retried autosave is listed with revision 0. The test polled every 10 ms and stopped at the first entry, so when it looked inside that window it read revision 0 instead of the retried revision.

The test now waits until the listed entry carries the expected revision (the sidecar is published). The assertions after the loop are unchanged, so a wrong revision still fails after the 30 s deadline. No production code changes; recovery listing only runs at launch, not while a write is in flight.

## Checks
- Reproduced deterministically by temporarily adding a 300 ms sleep between the bundle write and the sidecar write in `crates/format/src/autosave.rs` (local only, not part of this PR): without this change the test failed 5 of 5 runs with the CI error (`left: 0, right: 2` at `services.rs:941`); with it, 0 of 5. Without the sleep the window is too short to hit locally (0 of 40 failures on Windows).
- Windows: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --locked -p photocraft --bins` (111 passed), `cargo clippy --locked -p photocraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- Ubuntu (local WSL): `cargo test --locked -p photocraft --bins` (127 passed, 1 ignored), the test repeated 20 times (0 failures), `cargo clippy --locked -p photocraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

Refs #4967

title: Make the Pencil cursor outline the pixels its dab fills
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Fixes #5262.

From 4 px up, the Pencil cursor (and the Eraser's in Pencil mode) was a smooth circle inside the dab's whole-pixel square. An aliased dab paints a stair-stepped disc of whole pixels: 4 px fills 12 pixels, 5 px fills 21, 9 px fills 69. The circle cut through the edge pixels, so it didn't show which ones a click would change. It also ignored roundness and angle: a 9 px tip at 50 % roundness showed the circle over a 37-pixel ellipse, and a 2.6 px tip showed a 3×3 square over a 5-pixel plus. In a rotated view, the 1–3 px square and the Block-mode Eraser's square were drawn as an upright box between two of their turned corners.

Trace the dab with the renderer's own rasterizer (`outline::aliased_outline`, next to `tip_outline`) and draw the boundary of the pixels it fills, with the dark-outside, light-inside one-pixel lines the square used. The outline is traced once per brush change and cached like `brush_cursor`'s tip outline, then moved by whole pixels to the pointer's grid cell and mapped through the view, so it turns, flips and follows Pixel Aspect Ratio Correction. The Block-mode Eraser's square takes the same path, at every zoom.

When a document pixel is smaller than a physical one (below 100 % on a 1× display), or for a tip too big to trace (round over 508 px, sampled over about 359 px), the Pencil falls back to the tip's smooth outline from `brush_cursor`, centred on the pointer. Under 6 points across it still adds the hotspot crosshair, as the old cursor did. The size cap keeps a trace to a few milliseconds; past it the smooth outline is within a pixel of the stair-steps.

Also:
- The line colours come from `Tokens::cursor_outline`, like the other brush cursors, so the light line's alpha is 235 instead of 230.
- Both outline caches, `pencil_cursor`'s and `brush_cursor`'s, now trace a stored tip again once the preset store loads its full bitmap. Stored tips compare equal whether loaded or not, so a cursor first drawn during loading kept the previe…

author: PierrunoYT
body:
Closes #5563.

## What

Saving to a JPEG (File › Save As, File › Save a Copy, and a Save that goes through Save As) now opens **JPEG Options**, as Photoshop does, instead of writing silently at a fixed quality:

- **Quality 0–12** on Photoshop's scale, with its **Low / Medium / High / Maximum** presets (3 / 5 / 8 / 10; the preset follows the slider).

- Cancel writes nothing ("Save cancelled"). A close or quit prompt waits behind it, as it does for TIFF and Targa Options.

## Scripts and actions

- `file.save` / `file.saveAs` take `"quality": 0..12` and skip the prompt. It's the same param name and the same 0–12 → 1–100 mapping (`round(q / 12 × 99 + 1)`) the engine already uses for `file.saveACopy`, batch and Layers to Files. A bad value is an error, and nothing is written.
- A recorded action keeps the answer (`{"path": …, "quality": n}`) and replays it without asking.
- Automation saves (`app.save`, MCP) never prompted and still don't.

## Implementation

- New `crates/ui-egui/src/jpeg_options_ui.rs`, built like `targa_options_ui.rs`: the save is parked in a `Prompt` while the modal is up.
- The save paths' Targa-only `tga_bits: Option<TgaBits>` argument becomes `SaveAnswers { tga_bits, jpeg_quality }` (`from_params`, `apply`, `record`), so both answers go through the menus, Save a Copy and action replay the same way. The repeated "Answer TIFF or Targa Options…" error string becomes one `SAVE_OPTIONS_OPEN` constant.
- The 4 new strings are translated in all 20 catalogs. `book/src/formats/raster-formats.md` documents the dialog.

title: Warp: apply a large layer's warp in the background, with progress and Esc to cancel (#1015)
author: ianswope
body:
Part of #1015, as proposed in https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/1015#issuecomment-6170728316. It's the Warp counterpart of #4218.

### Problem

Committing Edit › Transform › Warp ran on the UI thread, with no progress and no cancel. On an 8000 × 6000 layer the window froze for 6.9 s (Arc) and 9.3 s (Flag).

Timing the steps of a Flag warp showed where that time goes. The mesh warp itself (`warp_triangles`) took 1.3 s. Writing its tiles took 0.5 s. Then two serial whole-layer passes in `warp_layer` took most of the rest:

- `surf.convert(…)` re-encoded every tile into the format the layer already had: **2.0 s**.
- `composite_over` blended the warp over the cleared layer in float buffers: **2.3 s**. When the warp box holds the whole layer, there is nothing under it to blend.

My claim comment said the mesh warp was 7–9× slower per pixel than Free Transform's. That was wrong for Flag: most of that time was these two steps.

### Change

- **`warp_cmds`:** `edit.transform.warp` (and `layer.smartObjects.warp`, which shares `apply`) runs its edit through `edit_job`, as Free Transform does since #4218. In the desktop app, a commit is a background job with progress, and Esc cancels it without touching the layer. Scripts, tests and the web build run inline as before.
  - `warp_layer` takes the job's `Interrupt`. It checks it between the steps that don't check it themselves.
  - A layer that already has alpha is cloned (its tiles are shared) instead of converted.
  - When clearing the warp box leaves the layer empty, the warp is the result, without `composite_over`. A test checks this gives the old path's pixels: exactly at 8 and 16 bits, and within one float ulp at 32 bits, where the old blend's `t·a / a` rounded a few values.
- **`algo::warp`:** `warp_mesh_surface_with` reports progress per destination tile and skips the remaining tiles once cancelled, like `warp_surface_with` (#4218). `warp_mesh_surface` and `warp_triangles` keep their signatures.

author: nrq6993-a11y
body:
Fixes part of #5599 (finding 2: PSB long-key length bug in the TIFF writer).

title: Security: don't open network paths stored in documents; ruzstd 0.9.1
author: panteliskts
body:
## Summary

Two hardening fixes for files from other people, mainly affecting the Windows build:

1. **Don't open network paths stored in documents.** A linked smart object's path and a Displace smart filter's `mapPath` come from the document. On Windows, even looking at a UNC path (`\\server\share\...`) connects to that server and signs in with the user's Windows credentials, and the link watcher looks at every linked path of the active document every two seconds.
2. **ruzstd 0.9.1** for [RUSTSEC-2026-0344](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0344.html). 0.9.0 doesn't bound a compressed block's decoded size, so a small frame in a `.pcraft` or Affinity file can make the decoder allocate gigabytes before our own output limit applies.

## Changes

- `photocraft_io::linked::is_network_path` classifies UNC (`\\server\share`, `//server/share`), device (`\\.\...`), verbatim UNC (`\\?\UNC\...`) and NT object (`\??\...`) paths by text, on every platform. A verbatim path to a drive letter (`\\?\C:\...`, what `canonicalize` returns) stays local.
- The paths that come from a document are checked before they reach the file system:

| Where | Network path now |
|---|---|
| `engine::link_watch` (background stamps) | not looked at |
| `engine::smart_cmds` source reads (re-render) | source unavailable, cached pixels kept |
| `io::psd_export` (embedding a linked file) | layer written as pixels with a warning, as for an unreadable link |
| `file.package` | reported in `missing` |
| `layer.smartObjects.revealInFinder` | refused |
| Displace `mapPath` (also re-read by smart filters) | refused |

- `ruzstd = "0.9.1"` in `crates/format` and `crates/affinity`, so the lockfile can't resolve back to 0.9.0.
- My own entry in `contributors/people.toml`.

**Behaviour change:** a linked file or Displace map on a UNC share no longer loads. Shares mapped to a drive letter (`Z:\...`) keep working. Happy to narrow this (for example, allow paths the user picked in this session) if you'd pref…

Horizontal scale was applied after line breaking, so lines were measured at 100% width: paragraph text below 100% wrapped early and text above 100% overflowed its box. Box text now breaks at the box width divided by the horizontal scale, and the first-line indent and centre/right alignment offsets are scaled back to fit the box. A line's right edge no longer counts the scaled trailing space.

- Adds a regression test in `crates/text/src/tests.rs` covering 60% and 150% scale with left, centre and right alignment; it fails without the fix.
- `cargo test` (all 155 tests) and `cargo clippy` pass for `photocraft-text`.

Known limitation: when one paragraph mixes several horizontal scales, lines are broken using the largest one. Those lines never overflow the box but can wrap slightly early.

title: Engine: enforce frame and canvas limits in Render Video (#5599)
author: krinry
body:
Fixes finding 1 in #5599.

### Problem

1. **Unbounded timeline duration:** A document loaded from a file carries whatever timeline duration its manifest held without validation against `timeline.create`'s duration cap (`MAX_DURATION = 1_000_000`). Calling `file.export.renderVideo` sizes a frame buffer vector and attempts to write files up to that duration, causing `capacity overflow` panics, OOM aborts, or runaway disk filling.
2. **Dense GIF canvas allocation:** In `render_video_with`, animated GIF export allocates dense RGBA `f32` buffers (`vec![[0.0f32; 4]; w * h]`). On extreme canvas dimensions (up to 300,000 per side allowed by PhotoCraft), this infallible allocation immediately causes process termination / OOM aborts.

### Fix

- Expose `timeline_cmds::MAX_DURATION` as `pub(crate)` and reject timelines with duration exceeding `MAX_DURATION` in `render_video_with`.
- Cap GIF frame canvas dimensions to `MAX_GIF_FRAME_PIXELS` (64 MP) before staging dense frame buffers.
- Add regression tests verifying that oversized timelines and canvas dimensions are gracefully rejected with an error.

### Validation

- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine`: 1,620 passed
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: 0 warnings
- `cargo xtask layers`: 29 crates ok, no layering violations
- `cargo xtask wasm`: all 24 crates ok
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored`: ok (adversarial params fuzzing passed)

title: Smart Filters: deleting the last filter removes its filter mask (#5619)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5619.

When the last smart filter was deleted, its filter mask stayed. `add_smart_filter` only builds a mask from the selection when there is none, so the next smart filter reused the old one. Select the left half, blur, delete the filter, select the right half and blur again: the blur landed on the left half. In Photoshop, removing the last smart filter removes the Smart Filters entry, mask included. `clearSmartFilters` and moving all filters already cleared it.

## Change
- `engine/smart_cmds.rs`: in `delete_filter`, and when a single filter moves to another smart object in `transfer_filters`, the filter mask is cleared once no filters remain.

## Tests
- New `smart_cmds::tests::removing_the_last_filter_removes_its_filter_mask`:
  - delete, then filter a new selection: only the new area changes;
  - move the only filter to another smart object: the source has no mask left.
  - Both halves fail on main on their own.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests smart`: all pass (lib 88).
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

title: FITS: clamp 32-bit saves to 0..1 and warn, so they reopen as saved (#5627)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5627.

A 32-bit document saved as FITS reopened almost black as soon as any sample was above 2.0. The writer stored float samples unclamped, although the module documents `BITPIX = -32` as 0..1. The reader (ours, and the usual astronomy convention) picks the white point from the data range, so it took the file as ADU data and divided everything by 65535.

## Change
- `codecs/fits.rs`: 32-bit samples are clamped to 0..1 on save, and NaN is written as 0, as documented.
- `codecs/fidelity.rs`: a float image with out-of-range values saved as FITS now reports `RangeClipped`, so the save dialog warns. Before, that warning came only for float → integer saves.

## Tests
- `fits::tests::hdr_float_saves_clamped_and_reopens_as_saved`: [0.5, 3.0] round-trips as [0.5, 1.0]. On main it reopened as `[7.6e-6, 4.6e-5]`.
- `tests/fidelity.rs::hdr_float_to_fits_clips`: HDR to FITS warns `RangeClipped`; an in-range float image doesn't. Fails on main.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-codecs --lib --tests`: all pass (lib 66, fidelity 28, roundtrip 348, metadata 27).
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-codecs --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- `cargo check -p photocraft-codecs --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`: OK.

## Not included or not verified

- Not checked in the running app: whether the warning shows in the save dialog. It is only covered at the codec level.

title: Check deep EXR tile count tables against max_alloc
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Addresses #4958 (audit finding 7/32). The finding's exact trigger isn't public, so this closes the gap its recommended direction describes: allocation admission for the intermediate buffers of deep tiled EXR import, including the fallback path and the scratch copy. The auditor may want to confirm it covers their case.

A deep tile's sample-count table may be stored at the full tile size, so `decode_deep` first decompresses it at `tile_w × tile_h × 4` bytes, then falls back to the clipped size. That size comes from the header's tile size alone, which nothing ties to the data window, and nothing checked it against `Limits::max_alloc`. A small RLE or ZIPS table could inflate to the full tile size, and `interleave_byte_blocks` then allocated a second buffer of the same size. The default budget (8 GiB, 1 GiB on wasm32) didn't bound this either, because the table grows with the tile. The decompression buffers also reserved past their expected size (`read_to_end` and `Vec` doubling), so a table and its copy could take three times the table size, and the scratch copy and RLE growth allocated infallibly.

Try the full tile size only when `max_alloc` has room for the table and its scratch copy; otherwise read only the clipped size, and return `LimitExceeded` if the table doesn't decode at that size. RLE and ZIPS buffers now grow by doubling, capped at their expected size, and that growth and the scratch copy allocate fallibly. The tile size uses checked arithmetic.

For real files nothing changes: the full size is still tried whenever a tile's table and copy fit `max_alloc`, which at the default 8 GiB means tiles up to 2^30 pixels (2^27 on wasm32). Scan lines and interior tiles, whose full and clipped sizes are equal, now decode once instead of repeating the same call after an error.

Tests (the files are generated in `crates/codecs/tests/deep_exr.rs`):
- `deep_tile_count_table_is_admitted_against_max_alloc`: one 1024×1024 tile over a 4×4 image with its table stored at full s…

title: Animated WebP: every frame loads into video layers (#1198)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #1198.

## What changed

An animated WebP used to bring only its first frame into a video layer. Now **New Video Layer from File**, **Replace Footage**, **Reload Frame** and **Import › Video Frames to Layers** take every frame, the same way they handle an animated GIF since #2999 (#572).

- **`photocraft-codecs`**: new `decode_webp_frames` returns each frame composited onto the canvas by `image-webp`, so frame offsets, alpha blending and disposal are applied. Each frame comes with its duration in milliseconds and the file's ICC profile.
  - A still WebP, or a one-frame animation, gives one frame, decoded the way `decode` reads it.
  - If a later frame is damaged, the frames before it are kept and the first one is marked `Truncated`.
  - The frame count (`MAX_GIF_FRAMES`) and the total decoded bytes are checked against `Limits`.
  - `webp_is_animated` tells an animated file from a still one.
  - New `decode_webp` fuzz target.
- **`photocraft-io`**: new `import_webp_frames`, which shares its loop with `import_gif_frames`.
- **`photocraft-engine`**: `load_frames` takes every frame of an animated WebP. The timeline rate comes from the most common duration (`fps_from_delays`, as for GIF). A still WebP keeps its existing path and the 30 fps default.
- **Docs**: the WebP row and the revision history in `docs/file-format-parity.md`, plus `crates/codecs/README.md`.

File › Open is unchanged: it still opens the first frame and shows the existing "only the first frame" warning, as it does for GIF.

- `cargo xtask ci` on macOS passes all 5 steps (fmt, clippy, test, layers, wasm).

  - frames come back in order with their millisecond durations

title: Fix brush cursor alignment on scaled Hyprland displays
author: alex190291
body:
On native Wayland under Hyprland 0.56.2 with a 160% display scale, brush paint appeared in the upper-left portion of the cursor circle rather than around its center crosshair. winit 0.30.13 scales the cursor hotspot and sets a viewport destination, while Hyprland renders this cursor surface using its buffer scale. The resulting bitmap is enlarged and offset from the actual paint position. See [Hyprland cursor surface sizing](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/v0.56.2/src/pointer/PointerManager.cpp#L156-L196) and [winit custom cursor handling](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/blob/v0.30.13/src/platform_impl/linux/wayland/window/state.rs#L778-L810).

Detect native Hyprland in the desktop platform services and use the canvas painter for tool cursors whenever the native display scale differs from 100%. Use native cursor bitmaps on 100% displays and other compositors. The choice follows monitor changes and treats interface zoom separately from display scaling.

Added regression coverage for 160%/200%/100% monitor transitions with 125% UI zoom, and an offscreen test that drives actual screen-space mouse input at 160%. The latter verifies that a 64-pixel hard brush at 200% canvas zoom produces a 128-physical-pixel dab centered inside the cursor. Updated the brush parity and gap documentation.

Canvas-drawn outlines follow the application's frame rate and can trail fast pointer motion on slow frames; the remaining brush-latency gap stays open.

title: Add native Riot TEX import and export
author: DeliriumOverdose
body:
## What changes

PhotoCraft currently cannot open or save Riot `.tex` textures. This adds native import and export through its existing Rust codec pipeline, without loading a Photoshop plugin.

- Read and write BC1, BC3, BC5, BC7 and BGRA8, including complete smallest-first mip chains.
- Add TEX to desktop/web file handling, Save As and Save a Copy, with compression and mipmap choices. Remember source settings across saves and `.pcraft` projects.
- Preserve RGB underneath zero alpha by importing texture alpha as a separate channel. Reject ambiguous multiple alpha channels and BC1 exports that would lose alpha.
- Expose the same choices in CLI conversion and engine save parameters; record and replay the selected options.
- Validate headers, payload sizes and allocation limits, with synthetic round-trip, malformed-input and randomized compressed-block tests.

The implementation follows the [public RitoTex format description](https://github.com/RitoShark/RitoTex-Photoshop/tree/de4e252a36561ffd77a58f9cd1b66ab9f558423e), using the MIT-licensed `block_compression` Rust CPU encoder/decoder. References and license texts are included in `ATTRIBUTION.md` and `licenses/`.

## Behavior and limits

New textures default to BGRA8 with mipmaps. Saving regenerates the mip chain from the edited full-resolution image; existing custom mip levels are not preserved. BC formats require dimensions divisible by four. BC5 stores red/green only; BC1 export requires opaque alpha. Cube maps, layer-authored mipmaps and normal-map editing tools are outside this change. See `docs/ritotex.md` for details and automation examples.

## Validation

- Desktop and CLI compilation checks passed. A current-branch CLI conversion to BC7 with mipmaps also passed, with the output header verified.
- `cargo test --locked -j4 -p photocraft-codecs -p photocraft-io -p photocraft-doc -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-cli --lib --tests --features heif`: **3,223 passed, 0 failed, 27 ignored**. This includes the TEX c…

title: Layer Mask Display Options: set the layer mask rubylith's colour and opacity
author: Trade-Mottoes
body:
The layer mask rubylith (`\`, or ⇧⌥-click on a mask thumbnail) was always red at 50 %. This adds Photoshop's **Layer Mask Display Options** so you can set its colour and opacity.

## Behaviour (checked against Photoshop 2026)
- One setting for every layer mask, kept across saves and restarts.
- Changing it isn't an undo step.
- The dialog has Color and Opacity (%), red at 50 by default.
- The rubylith is drawn as before: over the picture as it looks, mask applied. Opacity sets how much of what lies beneath shows through the colour.

## Where to set it
As in Photoshop:
- double-click the layer mask's row in the Channels panel, or right-click it › **Layer Mask Display Options…**;
- **Mask Options…** in the Layers panel mask-thumbnail menu (this fills the gap noted in `layer_menu_ui::show_mask`);
- Channel Options… while the mask is targeted, including by `\`.

All of these open the existing Channel Options dialog with just Color and Opacity.

## Engine
- A new preference, `layerMaskOverlay` (`{"color":"#rrggbb","opacity":0..100}`, `prefs::LayerMaskOverlay`). It's top-level, so Edit › Preferences doesn't show it, and `prefs.set` validates it like other colours and ranges.
- `channel.options {"channel":"mask","color"?,"opacity"?}` sets it, and returns it as `layerMaskOverlay`. With no fields it just reads it back. `name`, `indicates` and `solidity` are refused for a layer mask.
- This follows Quick Mask Options, which also go through `channel.options`. Unlike them it's a preference rather than session state, because Photoshop keeps it across restarts.

## Rendering
`channel_view::render` takes a small `Look` (Show Channels in Color plus the rubylith's colour and opacity) in place of `in_color: bool`. The canvas texture key includes the options, so changing them redraws the view. The rendering path and its cost are unchanged.

title: Guides: ⌥ turns a dragged guide; dropping one on either ruler deletes it (#5034)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #5034.

## What changed

Two Photoshop guide behaviours:

- **⌥ (Alt) turns a guide while it's dragged.** This works whether the guide comes out of a ruler or an existing guide is dragged with the Move tool (or with ⌘ and another tool).
  - The guide turns between horizontal and vertical about the pointer, so out of the left ruler it comes out horizontal.
  - Letting go of ⌥ before the release turns it back.
  - An ⌥-click on a guide turns it in place.
- **Dropping a guide on either ruler deletes it, whichever way it runs.** Before, a horizontal guide dropped on the left ruler was still level with the image, so it only moved.

### Implementation

- **engine:** `view.moveGuide` takes an optional `toOrientation`. A turned guide is one undo step and keeps its colour, and a `%` position is of the new axis. A bad value, or `toOrientation` on another guide command, is refused without touching the guides.
- **ui (`rulers.rs`):**
  - `GuideDrag` keeps the guide's own orientation (so `index` still points into the right list), plus two new fields: `flipped` (⌥ held) and `over_ruler`.
  - `GuideDrag::track` follows the pointer for both drag paths, and `shows_vertical` is what's drawn and committed.
  - The rulers set `over_ruler` from the pointer each frame.
  - `finish_drag` creates, moves or turns the guide, or deletes it when it's dropped outside the canvas or on a ruler.
- **canvas.rs:** the Move-tool and ⌘ guide drags use `track` with ⌥.
- **docs/ui-parity.md:** new row and revision entry.

## How it was checked

- `cargo xtask ci` on macOS passes all 5 steps (fmt, clippy, test, layers, wasm).
- New tests:
  - `edit_cmds::tests::move_guide_turns_a_guide`: turn with `%` of the new axis, colour carried, one undo step each, bad params refused.
  - `rulers::tests::alt_turns_a_guide_dragged_out_of_a_ruler`: a real egui drag out of the left ruler with ⌥ held gives a horizontal guide at the pointer's y.
  - `rulers::tests::alt_turns_a_guide_moved_with_the_move_tool`: ⌥-dra…

title: feat(perspective): globally rectify photos from independent quadrilateral guides
author: Darmonia
body:
## Why

Using several independent door/window rectangles as local Perspective Warp planes caused artificial folds, sheared walls and unwanted distortions between planes. The requested workflow is different: **local geometry guides → one global rectification** across the active photo layer, without touching, overlapping, or linking those guides.

## Main contribution

- Adds **Edit → Global Perspective Warp**, separate from the legacy multi-plane tool.
- Adds independent quadrilateral guides for door and window edges, robustly estimating one homography from mutually compatible orientations.
- Applies that map across the entire raster layer via safe inverse sampling, with projective-domain, output-budget and positive-Jacobian guards.
- Reports incompatible guides rather than attempting dangerous folds. Uses a consistent matrix for preview, engine execution and final commit, preserving atomic validation and Undo/Redo.
- Exposes `edit.perspectiveWarpGlobal` to the structured control API, including guide inspection and diagnostics, with documentation, translations and regression tests.

## Precision-editing follow-up (V3.1)

- **Ctrl + drag a corner:** constrain translation horizontally or vertically, choosing the first dominant mouse axis; release Ctrl to return to free movement.
- **Drag an edge:** hovering changes the cursor; dragging translates both adjacent vertices together, preserving the other two corners. Ctrl can also constrain this translation.
- **Drag beyond the image:** guide corners and edges may extend into the surrounding pasteboard when architecture lies outside the photograph; the guide must remain convex, finite and non-degenerate, and the resulting map must remain safe over the *entire image domain*. Corners win hit-testing near vertices.

The new handles are for **guide editing** only. They do not introduce independently warped photo patches.

title: Count tool: deleting an earlier count group keeps the active group (#5653)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5653.

`count.deleteGroup` only clamped the active count group to the new length. Deleting a group *before* the active one left the index pointing at the next group, so the active group silently changed and the next `count.add` went into the wrong group (API/CLI/MCP/actions; the Count panel deletes the active group). Deleting another count group shouldn't change which one is selected.

## Change
- `crates/engine/src/analysis_cmds.rs` (`count_delete_group`): shift the active index down by one when the removed group comes before it, then clamp as before.

## Tests
- New `deleting_an_earlier_count_group_keeps_the_active_group` (4 groups, group 2 active: delete 0 → active 1 = "Count Group 3"; delete a later group → unchanged; delete the active last group → new last group). Failed on main (`left: 2, right: 1`), passes now.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib count`: 8 passed; `--lib analysis_cmds`: 18 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean; `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

## Not included
- `count.add` with an out-of-range `"group"` still clamps silently while the other count commands error; left for a separate change.

title: Image > Adjustments: locked smart objects refuse new smart filters (#5655)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5655.

Every `image.adjustments.*` command (and Shadows/Highlights) on a smart object goes through `adjust_as_smart_filter`, which added the smart filter without a lock check. The generic `filter.*` path refuses a smart object with a pixel or full lock, and a locked raster layer refuses the adjustment too, so adjustments were the one route that still edited a locked smart object.

## Change
- `crates/engine/src/adjust_cmds.rs` (`adjust_as_smart_filter`): call `check_pixels_unlocked` before building the smart filter, the same rule as `filter.*` (pixel or full lock, including locks inherited from a group).
- Open PRs #4759 and #3615 route Desaturate/Equalize/Replace Color through `adjust_as_smart_filter` and get the check for free; no overlapping lines.

## Tests
- New `locked_smart_objects_refuse_adjustment_smart_filters`: Invert and Shadows/Highlights on a smart object locked with `{"all":true}` and `{"pixels":true}` → Err, no smart filter, no history step, pixels unchanged. Failed on main (`Ok(Null)`), passes now.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib adjust`: 56 passed; `--lib smart`: 88 passed; `--test filter_locked --test smart_psd --test smart_duplicates --test pixel_lock_edits`: green.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean; `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored`: 1 passed.

title: Video: Interpret Footage and New Video Layer from File reject an invalid frame rate (#5657)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5657.

Interpret Footage and New Video Layer from File stored the `fps` param as `f as f32` with no check: 0 or a negative rate was kept, and a finite JSON value like `1e39` became an infinite rate that the next `.pcraft` save refuses. The timeline frame-rate commands already validate with `fps_param` (finite, > 0, ≤ `MAX_FPS`, #1009).

## Change
- `crates/engine/src/timeline_cmds.rs`: `fps_param` is `pub(crate)`.
- `crates/engine/src/video_cmds.rs`: `interpret_footage` and `new_from_file` read `fps` through `fps_param`. A missing/null `fps` keeps the old fallback (footage rate, then 30).
- Behaviour change: a wrong-type `fps` (e.g. `"x"`) is now an error in both commands, as in the timeline commands. Before, Interpret Footage ignored it and New Video Layer from File used the footage rate.

## Tests
- New `an_invalid_frame_rate_is_an_error_and_changes_nothing`: fps 0, -1, 1e39, "x" → Err and the layer stays at 30 fps (Interpret Footage) / no layer added (New Video Layer from File, GIF fixture); fps 24 is stored. Failed on main ("fps 0"), passes now.

title: Type: Paste Lorem Ipsum inserts into the type layer named by "layer" (#5659)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5659.

`type.pasteLoremIpsum` decided "insert into existing text or make a new type layer" from the *active* layer, while the insert itself targets `p["layer"]`. With a pixel layer active, `{"layer": <type layer>, "at": 0}` created a new paragraph type layer and left the named layer unchanged.

Without `"layer"` nothing changes (active type layer → insert, otherwise a new paragraph layer); `"new": true` still forces a new layer. Lock All is still checked by `with_text`.

title: Properties / New Document: tiny sizes in physical units no longer resize the document (#5661)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5661.

The Document Width/Height fields in Properties and the New Document dialog only accepted 0.01–300000 in the ruler unit. egui clamps the *existing* value to the range and the field reports a change, so a 1 x 1 px document at 300 ppi (0.0033 in) shown with the rulers in inches was clamped to 0.01 in: Properties ran `image.canvasSize` and the document became 3 x 3 px with two history steps and no user edit (up to 23 px at 2400 ppi). New Document turned 1 px into 3 px the same way. Showing a value must never edit the document.

## Change
- `crates/ui-egui/src/doc_props_ui.rs`, `crates/ui-egui/src/new_doc_ui.rs`: the lower bound of those fields is 0. The pixel result is already clamped to 1–300000 px afterwards (and non-finite → 1), so 0 still gives 1 px, never 0 px or a division by zero.

## Tests
- New kittest `tiny_document_in_inches_is_not_resized_by_showing_it` (1x1 px, 300 ppi, rulers Inches, render Properties 3 frames → still 1x1, no history step) and `tiny_size_in_inches_is_not_changed_by_showing_it` (New Document 1x1 px, 300 ppi, unit in → params stay 1x1). Both failed on main (`(3, 3)`), pass now.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- doc_props new_doc properties widgets`: 122 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean; `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

## Not included / not verified

- Open PR #2683 rewrites the two New Document lines; the conflict is the same one-token change.

title: fix: limit Render Video timeline and GIF staging allocations
author: Ni-zav
body:
Addresses #5599.

Render Video now rejects timelines exceeding the existing maximum duration, including timelines loaded from files that bypass command-level validation.

Animated GIF export also checks the canvas against a 64-million-pixel staging budget before allocating its dense RGBA frame buffer.

Added regression tests for oversized timelines and GIF canvases. The tests are committed but have not been executed locally.

title: fix(svg): budget rasterised fallback layers across imports
author: Ni-zav
body:
Addresses the SVG import finding in #5599.

SVG import previously limited individual rasterised elements without limiting their combined memory usage. Drawings containing many masked groups could therefore exhaust available memory.

Added a 1 GiB aggregate decoded-pixel budget. Rasterised elements are charged against this budget before allocation, and elements exceeding the remaining allowance are skipped with a warning.

Added a regression test using multiple masked groups and a deliberately small memory budget. The test is committed but has not been executed locally.

title: fix(ui): keep the Color panel in sync with selected shape fills
author: Ni-zav
body:
Addresses #5568.

The Color panel previously displayed and edited the toolbox foreground color even when a solid-filled shape was selected. Changes made through Shape Properties were therefore not reflected in the Color panel, and Color panel edits did not recolor the selected shape.

The Color panel now reads the selected shape's solid fill. Editing the foreground color also updates that shape through `shape.edit`, preserving its existing alpha and respecting layer locks.

Repeated edits use the existing gesture-based history coalescing mechanism.

Added a regression test covering shape fill synchronization, Color panel edits, and undo. The test is committed but has not been executed locally.

title: fix(psd): write the layer block after a kept merged-transparency marker
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #5068.

A 16- or 32-bit document keeps its layers in a global `Lr16`/`Lr32` block when saved as PSD. The writer always put that block **first** among the global blocks. When the document was opened from a file with merged transparency, the file's `Mtrn`/`Mt16`/`Mt32` marker is kept verbatim and so ended up **after** the layer block. Photoshop refuses a file in that order ("Could not complete your request because of a program error"; Photopea reports "Wrong Signature"). Photoshop writes the marker first.

## How it was found

The Testy PSD compatibility run linked from #5220 flagged dozens of PSDs that PhotoCraft 0.7.0 re-saved as corrupt. I re-saved those corpus files with v0.8.2 and with `main`, and they were opened in Photoshop 2026. On `main` all of them open except psd-tools' `transparentbg.psd`: 32-bit, merged transparency marked by `Mt32`, `Lr32` written before it. Three byte-patched copies of that file were then opened in Photoshop:

| Change to `main`'s file | Opens in Photoshop |
|---|---|
| Layer count inside `Lr32` made positive | no |
| `Mt32` moved before `Lr32` | yes |
| Both | yes |

So the order is what matters. With this change, `transparentbg.psd` and `transparentbg.psb`, re-saved as `.psd`, both open in Photoshop. The 32-bit file shows Photoshop's usual HDR notice.

## Change

`document_to_psd_with` places the layer block right after the last kept `Mtrn`/`Mt16`/`Mt32` block. Without one, it still goes first, as before.

## Tests

`layer_block_follows_a_kept_merged_transparency_marker`: for a 32-bit document with a kept `Mt32` (behind another kept block), a 16-bit one with `Mt16`, and a 32-bit one with `Mtrn`, the saved file's marker comes before its layer block. Without a marker the layer block stays first. The test fails on `main`.

## Evidence

`c26124b9` was checked in a clean checkout on Windows x86_64 (rustc 1.99.0), touched-crate set:
- `cargo fmt --check`, the io (and dependents') tests (4,616 passed, 0 failed) and their clippy `-D wa…

title: Layer masks: From Transparency and Mask All Objects convert the Background and match the document depth (#5679)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5679.

Two gaps in Layer › Layer Mask › From Transparency and Mask All Objects:
1. They assigned `layer.mask` without `background_to_layer_for_mask`, which every other add-mask path calls. On a Background-only document the Background stayed a Background and carried a mask. In Photoshop adding a mask turns the Background into "Layer 0" first.
2. They (and Hide Selection) started from `LayerMask::hide_all()` / `reveal_all()`, which are 8-bit; #3359 routed the other mask paths through `mask_at_depth` and missed these. In a 16/32-bit document From Transparency cut the layer's alpha to 256 levels and then made the pixels opaque, so the full-precision alpha was lost.

## Change
- `crates/engine/src/commands.rs`: `mask_at_depth` is `pub(crate)`.
- `crates/engine/src/layer_menu_cmds.rs`: From Transparency, Hide Selection and Mask All Objects build their mask at the document depth; From Transparency and Mask All Objects convert the Background first, as Hide Selection already does. 8-bit documents are bit-identical to before.

## Tests
- New `from_transparency_and_mask_all_objects_turn_the_background_into_a_layer` (fromTransparency, maskAllObjects and hideSelection as reference → "Layer 0" with a mask) and `layer_masks_are_built_at_the_document_depth` (8/16/32-bit: mask sample type U8/U16/F32, alpha 0.5003 kept within 1/255, 1/65535, 1e-6; outside stays hidden). Both failed on main ("the Background became a layer", "left U8, right U16"), pass now.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests`: all green (lib 1654 passed, 13 ignored).
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean; `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored`: passed.

## Not included
- Mask All Objects' segmentation itself is 8-bit; its mask is now stored at document depth but still has 256 levels.

title: Preset Manager: renaming or deleting a brush keeps the current preset and names consistent (#5681)

title: Security: enforce the automation read boundary on stored smart-filter params
author: skylartaylor
body:
# Security: enforce the automation read boundary on stored smart-filter params

Credit: this fix was independently reported twice. @coygeek reported the ambient-authority read of document-stored Smart Object sources (#2927), establishing the trust model — document-stored paths are data, not authority. A private security report (2026-10-14) then identified the `layer.smartFilter.setParams` ambient-path escape with a working PoC, together with the recommendations this change implements: authorizing stored smart-filter params at the merge point, render-side defense in depth covering filters arriving from `.pcraft` files, layer transfer and `actions.play`, and inverted-PoC regression tests. Both findings describe one boundary violation: a document or stored params must never grant filesystem authority the session does not have.

## Summary

- Smart filters store a command id and params inside the document. A crafted `.pcraft` could resolve stored ambient paths (`filter.distort.displace` `mapPath`, color-lookup LUT `file`) at render time without the automation authorize gate: synchronous smart-object rendering has no `Session` argument, spawned job threads drop the requesting session's authority, and a trusted UI render could warm the process-wide stack cache with a stage the gate never sees.
- Thread the requesting session's gate through a thread-local `RENDER_AUTHORIZATION` in `jobs.rs`: entered around command execution, reinstalled on spawned workers and on job apply, restored on drop so restriction never leaks into later trusted work on the same thread.
- Re-check every stored smart-filter command in `render_in` before source resolution and before any cache lookup, and in `apply_filter_to_surface`, so replayed filter paths, adjustment LUTs, and plug-in inputs obey the requesting session's authority before any resolver reads them.
- Re-authorize `layer.smartFilter.setParams` with the complete merged params after the edit merges stored document params, including when t…

title: packaging: RPM declares the glibc 2.35 floor, so RHEL 9 refuses it
author: tydude001
body:
## What and why

PhotoCraft's RPM declares no glibc floor, though the deb has `libc6 (>= 2.35)`. On Rocky Linux 9 (glibc 2.34)
the RPM installs, and then `photocraft-cli` fails with ``/lib64/libm.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.35' not found``.

This adds `libm.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)(64bit)`. The binaries' only GLIBC_2.35 symbols are `hypot` and `hypotf`
from libm. It names libm rather than libc because RHEL 9's current glibc (`2.34-283.el9_8`) provides
`libc.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)` through backports but not libm's, so a libc floor would still let it install.

## How it was tested

PhotoCraft 0.8.2's released x86_64 binaries, repackaged with nfpm 2.47.0 and this branch's `nfpm.yaml`, then
installed with the distro's own package manager in a fresh x86_64 container and run with `photocraft-cli --version`.

| | released 0.8.2 RPM | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Fedora 44 | installs, runs | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Tumbleweed | installs, runs | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Leap 15.6 | installs, runs | installs, runs |
| Rocky Linux 9 (glibc 2.34) | installs; `photocraft-cli` can't start | refused: `nothing provides libm.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)(64bit)` |

The aarch64 RPMs get the same requires. I checked that side on FilmCraft only: its 0.7.2 arm64 binaries need
GLIBC_2.35 for the same two libm symbols, and its branch RPM installs and runs on arm64 Fedora 44,
Tumbleweed and Leap 15.6 (qemu-user).

`cargo xtask ci` on this branch: fmt, clippy, layers and wasm pass. `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` fails
one test, a failure of `main` (`c699e3cd`) itself, since this branch changes no code:
`text_becomes_outline_shapes_or_warns_without_a_font` (`crates/io/tests/svg.rs`), which needs Arial or DejaVu Sans,
and Fedora 44 has neither (#4219 fixes it). Every other test passes. (Run with debug info set to `line-tables-only`
and 8 jobs, to fit the disk.) Installation and CLI only, not the GUI. Results for every Crafting App:
https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/issues/341#issuecomment-61715700…
