title: perf(ui): bound transform outlines and stabilize perspective clipping
author: LabDennis
body:
Free Transform traces the entire carried selection, including pixels that started offscreen. At 100% zoom, a 6000×6000 selection currently creates a 36-million-cell outline grid. Bound this preview trace to 1,048,576 cells, including alignment and padding, and use f64 intermediates when clipping perspective lines whose endpoints are far outside the viewport.

This is the small follow-up requested in https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/5353#issuecomment-6175094756. The frame/preview behavior has already landed through #5337 (`3ee78a368b10`); it is retained. Related: #5297 and #3402, without claiming those broader issues are completely resolved.

- Increase the sampling step only for whole-selection transform previews; ordinary viewport traces retain their existing cache behavior.
- Sample overlapping boundary cells so a thin selection does not vanish merely because a coarse sample falls just outside its bounds.
- Preserve the full-resolution mask and commit behavior. The displayed contour remains an approximation at coarse sampling levels.
- Keep near-horizon line clipping accurate at viewport scale. The new regression fails with the original upstream clipping function and passes with the change.

Validation on Windows:

- 6 outline tests pass; 165 transform-filtered tests pass, with 3 existing ignored tests. These sets overlap. Repeated on the final source.
- Changed-crate rustfmt and dependency layering pass.

title: GPU: a group's effect cache follows its vector mask and children's Blend If (#5706)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5706.

A styled group's Stroke / Drop Shadow is built from the group's composite, which depends on the group's own vector mask and on each child's Blend If and Advanced Blending. The GPU effect cache key (`group_key`) hashed none of these, and group tiles carry no damage sources, so after such an edit the GPU kept drawing the effect around the old outline. The CPU compositor's `layer_identity` already hashes them; Photoshop redraws the effect.

## Change
- `crates/gpu/src/fx.rs` `group_key`: the group arm hashes the group's `vector_mask`; `walk` hashes each child's `blend_if` and `advanced`.

## Tests
- New `fx::tests::group_key_follows_vector_mask_blend_if_and_advanced` (no GPU device): the key changes when the group gets a vector mask, when the mask moves, when a child's Blend If changes and when a child's knockout changes. Failed on main ("adding the group's vector mask"; with only the mask fix it failed at "a child's Blend If").
- `cargo test -p photocraft-gpu --lib`: 30 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean; `cargo fmt -p photocraft-gpu -- --check`: clean.

## Not verified
- No GPU-vs-CPU render comparison of a styled group; the test checks the cache key.
- #5336 changes `group_key`'s signature (adds `pin`); whichever lands second needs a small textual merge.

title: Posterize and Threshold commands use the 16-bit rules on 16-bit layers (fixes main)
author: echelon
body:
Main is red since #5267 / #5263: `photocraft-ui-egui`'s `adjust_preview::tests::preview_composite_matches_the_destructive_command` fails for 16-bit Posterize and Threshold (preview vs command up to 92/255).

title: Type: a scaled type layer keeps its size when the Character fields show it (#5717)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5717.

## Why
Selecting a type layer scaled so that its shown size or leading lies outside the Character fields' range (e.g. 200 pt Free Transformed ×10, shown as 2000 pt) silently shrank the text and added a history step without any edit. egui's `DragValue` clamps the value it merely displays (`clamp_existing_to_range` defaults to true), the shared value field reported that as a change, and the type panel turned it into `type.setStyle`. The low end did the same (a value shown below the 0.1 pt minimum). Showing a value must never change the document.

## Change
- `widgets::number_edit` (behind `value_field` and the type tool's fields) builds its `DragValue` with `clamp_existing_to_range(false)` and clamps only real edits itself (typing, dragging, arrow keys, scrubbing, AccessKit), guarded against a reversed/NaN range.
- This protects every value field in the app from changing a value just by drawing it; the call lines in `type_tool.rs` (also touched by #3551/#3558) are unchanged.

## Tests
- `type_tool::canvas_tests::multi_layer_formatting::showing_a_scaled_layer_past_the_size_range_does_not_change_it`: type layers scaled ×200 and ×0.005, shown in the Properties panel and the options bar, keep their style and history length. Failed on main (12 pt → 6.48 pt), passes now.
- `widgets::tests::value_field_keeps_a_shown_value_past_its_range_and_clamps_edits`: 2400 in a 0.1–1296 field shows unchanged with no change reported; typing 5000 still clamps to 1296.

title: Scripts: Flatten All Layer Effects bakes with the document's Global Light and patterns (#5719)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5719.

## Why
Scripts › Flatten All Layer Effects and Flatten All Masks baked each layer through `photocraft_compose::render_layer`, which renders without the document's context. Effects that use Global Light baked at the default angle (the shadow jumps), a Pattern Overlay vanished and a Pattern Fill with effects baked transparent (no patterns were passed), and fill layers were laid out on the padded render area instead of the canvas. Flattening effects should leave the composite unchanged.

## Change
- `photocraft_compose::render_layer_in(doc, layer, rect)`: renders one layer alone with the document's patterns, Global Light, tone transfer, colour mode, depth and canvas, inside the same CMYK-profile and Lab/32-bit blend wrappers `render` uses (`doc: None` in the context, so a deep knockout still reveals transparency, not the Background). `render_layer` is unchanged.
- `bake` in `crates/engine/src/file_cmds.rs` takes the document and renders through it.

Both failed on main (shadow moved / overlay gone) and pass now.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-compose --lib --tests`: all pass. `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests file_cmds`: 50 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask wasm`: clean.

- Other `render_layer` callers (`adjust_cmds.rs`, `extra_cmds.rs`, `smart_cmds.rs`, `filters_ext.rs`, `io/src/ora.rs`) still render without document context; left for follow-ups.

title: Brush smoothing: the lagging brush keeps the pressure of where it is (#5713)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #5713.

### What was wrong

#5713 was flagged as a possible duplicate of #316, but it's a different bug. #316 was about fast strokes turning into polylines. In the #5713 screenshot the curves are smooth, but where a fast pressure stroke ends the width steps down from thick to a straight hairline (the red circles).

The cause is in `Smoother::push` (`crates/paint/src/dynamics.rs`). With smoothing on, the brush moves only part of the way toward the pointer, but every smoothed point took the pointer's **newest** pose (`..p`): pressure, tilt, rotation and wheel. On a fast stroke the brush trails far behind the pointer. When the pen lifts, its last samples have near-zero pressure. The trailing brush then painted with that pressure while it was still well short of the end. Catch-Up On Stroke End then drew a straight segment at that pressure from the brush to the pointer: the hairline.

### The change

- New `pull(brush, p, f)` in `dynamics.rs`: moves the brush `f` of the way to the pointer, and moves pressure, tilt, wheel and rotation by the same fraction. Rotation goes the short way round, and the time is the pointer's.
- Used by both the exponential smoother and the pulled string.
- The end catch-up segment now runs from the brush's own pressure to the pen's last sample, so the path walker's interpolation draws a taper instead of a step.

With smoothing off, nothing changes: the smoother passes points through untouched.

### Tests (`crates/paint/src/brush_tests.rs`)

- `a_smoothed_brush_keeps_the_pressure_of_where_it_is_when_the_pen_lifts`: a fast full-pressure stroke lifted at the last sample. The stroke still ends at the pen's last sample, the brush still trails, and no trailing point drops to the lift's pressure. This failed before the fix, when the point at the lift had pressure 0.05.
- `a_pulled_string_brush_takes_the_pose_along_the_string`: the string brush's pressure, tilt and rotation are the blend at its position along the string, with rotation 350° → 10°…

title: Move tool: ΔX/ΔY readout beside the pointer while dragging (#5727)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #5727.

### What was wrong

The report says the Move tool used to show the same "how far I've moved it" tooltip as Ctrl+T, and doesn't in 0.9.0. In the code, no release (0.6.0 through 0.9.0, and `main`) ever drew a readout for a plain Move-tool drag. The only ΔX/ΔY readout is Free Transform's (`transform_tool::live_readout`, `Hit::Inside`). The Move tool reaches it only when a drag starts on one of its transform-control handles or the rotation band, which opens a Free Transform session. A drag *inside* the box, or with Show Transform Controls off, is an ordinary Move drag and showed nothing. So the reporter most likely saw it through Free Transform. Either way, Photoshop shows ΔX/ΔY for an ordinary Move drag, and PhotoCraft didn't.

### The change

- `move_ui::offset_readout`: the ΔX/ΔY strings for the Move drag in progress. It uses the same whole-pixel offset (`drag_offset`) that the live preview shows and the release commits through `layer.translate`. It returns `None` until the pointer has moved, so a click shows nothing.
- `canvas::draw_drag_preview` draws it at the pointer (`"move-readout"`), before the early return for selected-pixel drags, so it shows both when dragging a layer and when dragging selected pixels.
- It goes through `draw_value_readout`, so **Preferences › Tools › Show Transformation Values** hides it, like the marquee, crop and Free Transform readouts. Same `ΔX:`/`ΔY:` labels and `N px` format as Free Transform's offset readout.

### Test

`move_ui::tests::a_move_drag_reads_out_the_offset_it_will_commit`: no readout before the drag or right after the press; a drag to (+10.4, −3.2) reads `10 px` / `-3 px`, the offset the release commits; and nothing after the release.

### Not verified

Nothing was built or run locally (only `rustfmt --check`), and I took no screenshot. CI is the first compile and test run.

title: Pen and Path Selection: Delete deletes the finished work path (#5702)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #5702.

### What was wrong

The reporter finishes a path with the Pen and can't get rid of it. It disappears when they switch tools, comes back when they press P, and is still there after closing and reopening the document.

Two of those are expected and match Photoshop:
- The work path is drawn whenever a vector tool is active (`vector_ui::draw_overlay`), which is why it hides under other tools.
- A Work Path is part of the document and is saved with it (`.pcraft` and PSD), which is why it survives reopening.

The bug is deleting it. While a path is being drawn, ⌫/Delete removes its last anchor (#1466). Once the path is finished, the key fell through to **Edit › Clear**, which acts on the pixels under the path and leaves the path where it was. The only ways to delete it were right-click › Delete Path and the Paths panel's trash button, which this report shows aren't easy to find. In Photoshop, Delete with the Pen or Path Selection tool deletes the path.

### The change

- `vector_ui::delete_key_deletes_work_path`: true when **all** of these hold:
  - the tool is the Pen, the Freeform Pen or Path Selection;
  - no path is being drawn and no Free Transform is open;
  - View › Show › Target Path is on;
  - the work path is the path these tools edit (`target_path` is `Work`: no active shape layer or targeted vector mask in front of it).
- `shortcuts::handle`: in that state, an unmodified ⌫/Delete runs `path.delete {"name": "work"}`, one undoable **Delete Path** History step, before Edit › Clear's shortcut can see the key. It sits after the path-in-progress handling, so ⌫ while drawing still removes the last anchor. Focused text fields and the Curves graph (a widget that uses ⌫ itself) keep the key.

title: Affinity import: budget decoded pixels across the document
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Opening a crafted Affinity document (`.af`/`.afphoto`) with many embedded images could exhaust memory and kill the process: each image decodes into a surface of up to 256 MB and resamples into another of the same order, and nothing tracked the cumulative total — a few-megabyte file could allocate until the process died, which `catch_unwind` cannot stop. The existing caps were all per call (a 64 Mpx per-image pixel cap and container byte limits on the compressed data that a handful of solid-colour PNGs never approach). This change gives the import a 1 GiB decoded-pixel budget: an embedded image is charged its decoded `w × h × 4` bytes, resampling is charged its staging buffer, and an image the remaining budget cannot cover is left out with a warning — the same shape as the existing "left out" paths and the budgets ORA and KRA already use.

Regression tests exercise both charge sites with tiny in-memory fixtures (an embedded PNG decode and an RGBA resample) plus the accounting primitive; with the charges removed the two call-site tests fail, and with the fix `cargo test -p photocraft-io --lib affinity` passes 3/3 (crate lib suite: 207 passed).

Partially addresses #5599 (finding 4, Affinity decode budget). Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: Fill layers: reject non-finite gradient angles and pattern angle/phase (#5752)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5752.

## Why
`layer.newFillLayer.gradient` and `gradient.presets.apply` cast `angle` to f32 unchecked: `{"angle": 1e39}` stored an infinite angle, so the render went NaN and .pcraft save/autosave refused the document (`format/src/finite.rs`). `{"angle": 450}` was stored as 450. Pattern placement (Pattern Fill layer, Edit > Fill with a pattern, Paint Bucket in pattern mode) had the same problem for `angle` and `phase`. The sibling `gradient.fill.set` already rejected non-finite angles and normalised to (-180, 180], like Photoshop's angle fields.

## Change
- The `gradient.fill.set` angle parsing is now a shared `angle_param`: a non-finite or non-number angle is BadParams, and the angle is normalised to (-180, 180]. Both gradient fill-layer commands use it (default 90).
- `pattern_cmds::placement` returns `Result`: the angle goes through `angle_param` (default 0), and phase coordinates must be finite and within ±1e7, the same rule as `pattern.fill.set`. Its callers in `edit.fill` and `paint.bucket` propagate the error.
- The now unused `f32_or` helper is removed.

Behaviour notes: a non-number `angle` (e.g. `"90"`) used to fall back silently to the default; these commands now refuse it, as `gradient.fill.set` does. Pattern angles are normalised (270 is stored as -90, which draws the same).

## Tests
- `gradient_fill_layer_angles_are_finite_and_normalised` (both gradient commands: 1e39, -1e300, `"90"` → Err with no layer added; 450 → 90, -180 → 180, default 90).
- `pattern_placement_rejects_non_finite_angle_and_phase` (pattern fill layer, `edit.fill`, `paint.bucket`: bad angle or phase → Err, no layer added; 270 / [3,-4] stored as -90 / (3,-4)).
- Both failed on main. `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored` are green.

title: Place Scale Marker: lay out the label in points, not pixels (#5754)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5754.

## Why
Image > Analysis > Place Scale Marker passes `fontSize` to `type.create` in points, and the type layer renders at resolution/72 px per point (as in Photoshop, where the marker's font size is in points). The bar height, label height and baseline were computed as if `fontSize` were pixels, so at 300 ppi a 12 pt label (50 px) overlapped the bar. At 72 ppi the units are equal, which is why nobody saw it.

## Change
- `place_scale_marker` lays out the bar and label with `font_px = fontSize * resolution / 72` (1 px per point if the resolution is invalid). The type layer still gets the size in points.
- Nothing changes at 72 ppi.

## Tests
- New `place_scale_marker_lays_out_its_label_in_points_at_high_resolution` (72 and 300 ppi): the label's top is at or below the bar's bottom, the label stays on the canvas, the type layer is still 12 pt. On main it failed at 300 ppi ("label top 821.5625 overlaps the bar ending at 858").
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests scale_marker`: 3 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored`: passed.

## Not verified
The label is measured from the layout's line bounds, not rendered pixels (tests run without system fonts); not checked visually in the app. The text-on-top position uses the same change but has no dedicated 300 ppi test.

title: PSD: layer_tree_max_depth hoists layers under unclosed dividers past the cap (#5758)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5758.

## Why
`PsdFile::layer_tree` hoists the layers under a group divider that no folder record ever closes to the enclosing level. `layer_tree_max_depth` lost them instead once the unclosed dividers sat at or past `max_depth`: frames past the cap collect nothing, so nothing was left to hoist at the end. `[a, </Layer group>, b, c]` gave `a, b, c` from `layer_tree()` but only `a` from `layer_tree_max_depth(0)`. PSD import calls it with `MAX_GROUP_DEPTH`, so malformed files with many unclosed dividers lost layers.

## Change
- A first pass matches section dividers to folder records (the same stack pairing as before). Only dividers that a folder closes open a frame; the layers under an unclosed divider go straight to the enclosing level, in the same order the old end-of-loop hoist gave.
- Frame depth now equals final depth, so the capped tree is `layer_tree()` cut at `max_depth`: a group at the cap keeps its node and loses its children. Still iterative, at most `max_depth + 1` levels deep, O(n) extra memory, no new panic paths.
- `layer_tree()` (no cap) gives the same result as before.

## Tests
New in `crates/psd/tests/tree.rs` (all three failed on main):
- `layer_tree_max_depth_hoists_unclosed_divider_children`: `[a, divider, b, c]` gives `a,b,c` at caps 0 and 1.
- `layer_tree_max_depth_keeps_closed_group_inside_unclosed_dividers`: a closed `g0[g1[x]]` inside two unclosed dividers gives `g0[g1[]]` at cap 1 and `g0[]` at cap 0.
- `layer_tree_max_depth_bounds_deep_unclosed_chain`: 16000 unclosed dividers each followed by a layer keep all 16001 roots and stay depth-bounded.

`cargo test -p photocraft-psd` (205 lib, tree 18/18), `cargo test -p photocraft-io --lib --tests`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-psd --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green.

## Not verified

title: GPU canvas: 2048 px texture tiles by default, so a large canvas's first uploads don't stall (part of #5106)
author: ianswope
body:
Part of #5106, as proposed in https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/5106#issuecomment-6176700507.

### Problem

When the background redraw of a large document (#5001) uploads its first blocks, some frames stall for 425–476 ms. The upload itself is small: writing a 1024 px block takes 2–5 ms. But the first write into each fresh canvas texture tile makes wgpu zero-fill the rest of that tile's mip levels. With the 8192 px default, that's 256 MB at level 0 per tile, and here (Intel ARL, Vulkan) it took 95–310 ms per tile.

Clearing the textures up front doesn't help: an explicit clear of a 16000 × 10000 canvas's texture set took 451 ms, all in one frame. The cost looks like the system backing the memory on first touch, so it can only be spread out, not avoided.

### Change

- **Preferences › Performance › cache tile size** defaults to **2048** instead of 8192 (`prefs::CACHE_TILE_SIZE`). `gpu_canvas::DEFAULT_TILE` now follows it instead of repeating the number. Each first touch then clears 16 MB, and the cost spreads over many short frames.
- **Saved preferences:** version 1 files store every value, so every one holds the old 8192. `load_prefs_json` moves a stored 8192 to the new default once, in files below version 2, and files are now saved as version 2. A size set after that is kept.
  - Trade-off: someone who deliberately chose 8192 under version 1 gets moved once and can set it back. A missing key can't serve as the signal (as it does for the appearance-mode migration), because version 1 wrote this key every time.

Documents up to 2048 px still use one texture. Larger ones use more, smaller ones; the per-tile paths (paint, mips, readback, budget pricing) already handle any number of them. `PHOTOCRAFT_GPU_TILE` still overrides the preference.

### Measured

Same build, tile size set with `PHOTOCRAFT_GPU_TILE`, three runs each. Intel Core Ultra 7 255H, Intel ARL graphics, Vulkan.

title: PSD smart objects: keep Photoshop's Cylinder warp when re-rendered (#4112)
author: alvarohn
body:
Fixes #4112.

A placed layer warped with Transform Warp's **Cylinder** (`warpStyle = warpCylinder`, seven `warpValues`) was read as having no warp. On open it looked right, because Photoshop's cached pixels are shown. Replace Contents, Relink and Edit Contents then drew the contents flat, and a regenerated `SoLd` wrote `warpNone`, which dropped the warp from the file.

## Changes
- **geom:** `WarpStyle::Cylinder` and `Warp::cylinder`.
  - The cylinder becomes a 4 × 1 patch Bezier mesh (back, front left, front right, back) in the warp's value space, like a custom mesh, so `map`, `to_mesh` and `is_identity` treat it as one.
  - It uses the model and shape table the reporter measured against Photoshop 2026's renders. Nothing is taken from Adobe's code.
  - `Warp` keeps the values (serde omits them when empty, so older `.pcraft` files load).
  - Cylinder is not one of the fifteen bend presets and isn't listed in the Warp menus yet: there is no editor for it.
- **io:**
  - Import reads the seven `warpValues` of a horizontal cylinder without perspective, as a list of doubles or as unit floats.
  - Like a custom warp (#3677), its control-point box is what the placement quad frames. That holds for affine corners and, for this style, also for projective ones (`nonAffineTransform`): `perspective_frame`, `corners_perspective_in`. Custom warps keep the source rect for projective placements, since there is still no reference for that combination.
  - Export writes `warpCylinder` and its values back, framing the same box. An unchanged layer is still written verbatim.
  - Vertical cylinders and ones with perspective were never measured, so they stay unread as before.
- **engine:** `edit.transform.warp` and `layer.smartObjects.warp` take `style: "cylinder"` with `values`, or a full `warp` object whose mesh is rebuilt from its values.
  - Anything else is refused rather than silently ignored. On type it is refused like a custom mesh.

title: Lab: adjustment results are whole samples, as Photoshop stores them (lab8 curves passes)
author: timothydaly1
body:
## What

On screen, Lab documents with adjustment layers now show the values Photoshop stores, rounded to whole samples.

The native Lab path (`compose::native_lab`, #5171) worked a stack out on the stored L, a and b but kept each adjustment layer's result unrounded. Photoshop stores every result at the document's depth, so the screen showed values between two samples where Photoshop has whole bytes (or 1/32768 steps at 16 bits). On saturated colours, half a byte of L is a couple of RGB levels.

Each adjustment layer's result is now rounded to the depth's samples (`adjustment_quantum`: 8 and 16 bits; 32-bit stays unrounded). The RGB compositor already does this for adjustment layers. Flattening went through the document's own surface and was rounded anyway; now the screen matches it.

## Evidence

| photoshop oracle | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `lab8/curves.psd` | 0.0084, 0.01 %, DIFF | **0.0000, PASS** |
| `lab8/brightness-contrast.psd` (modern) | 0.0081, 0.02 %, DIFF | 0.0099, 1.05 %, DIFF |
| `lab16/*` | PASS | PASS (unchanged) |

- **Corpus test against current main:** Photoshop oracles 185 → **186**; floor 185 → 186. psd-tools and io are unchanged.
- **Modern Brightness/Contrast on L:** I compared our modern curve with Photoshop's byte by byte. It is within half a byte of Photoshop's, but not exact (49 of 205 L bytes round the other way), so whole samples now show those misses. Fixing that means refining the brightness curve, which is separate work.
- **Legacy Brightness/Contrast in Lab8:** #5132's table already lands on whole bytes, so it stays exact with this change.

## Tests

`lab_adjustment_results_are_whole_samples`: a Lab Curves that maps L 100 to 120.4 shows a whole sample on the native path, at 8 and 16 bits. It fails on main, landing 0.4 and 0.2 of a step off.

title: CI: add Renovate dependency-update automation
author: Emin-ACIKGOZ
body:
Adds Renovate configuration so Cargo crates and GitHub Actions are kept up to date. This is configuration only. The Mend-hosted app still has to be installed for the repository. Refs #5760.

### What changed

- **`.github/renovate.json5`** — extends `config:recommended` + `:dependencyDashboard` + `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests`:
  - weekly batch, Monday before 06:00 UTC;
  - `minimumReleaseAge: 7 days` so a fresh release is not adopted immediately;
  - Cargo non-major updates group into one PR, GitHub Actions into another; majors stay separate;
  - patch and digest updates auto-merge once CI is green; majors need Dependency Dashboard approval;
  - OSV and GitHub advisories raise a PR immediately, bypassing the schedule and cooldown.
- **`book/src/development/dependencies.md`** — documents the policy.
- **`contributors/people.toml`** — adds the author's credit entry.

### Testing

- `npx --package renovate renovate-config-validator .github/renovate.json5` → "Config validated successfully".
- No runtime behaviour changes; no source or test files touched.

### Notes for reviewers (maintainer steps after merge)

- Install the Mend Renovate App for `storytold/photocraft`.
- Enable the repository's "Allow auto-merge" setting (needed by `platformAutomerge`).
- Branch protection (#5118) so auto-merge waits on the CI checks.
- Renovate creates the `dependencies` / `security` labels on first run (or create them first).
- The first run opens one large Actions digests-pinning PR (expected from `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests`).

### Related

- Refs #5760 — configuration lands here; installing the app remains.
- Depends on #5118 for safe auto-merge.
- Complements #2939 (pinning Actions).

title: Home screen: fit the card and stack the buttons in a narrow window
author: TaylorBurke
body:
## Problem

The Home screen's card is a fixed 460 points wide, centred on the canvas, with the **New document** and **Open** buttons (190 points each) side by side. When the canvas is narrower than the card, the buttons are clipped at the window edges.

A tiling window manager hits this easily. On Omarchy (Arch, Hyprland, Wayland, native Wayland client), a tiled PhotoCraft window was **728 points wide**, below the 760-point minimum the app asks for (Hyprland tiling does not enforce it), and the buttons were cut off on both sides.

## Change

- The card is as wide as the canvas when the canvas is narrower than 460 points.
- The button width comes from the labels (`widgets::button_width`), so longer translations are accounted for.

title: Adjustment layers: a live preview is never coarser than the screen (#5764)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #5764.

### What was wrong

The issue gives no steps or screenshot, so I matched it to the one path that goes blocky only while a curve point moves and turns sharp again on release: editing an adjustment layer (Curves, Levels and the rest) in the Properties panel on a large document with the GPU canvas.

While a Properties control moves, `adjust_editors::layer_editor` sets `app.live_adjust`. The GPU canvas then draws through `canvas::ensure_proxy_preview` (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, around line 1887). That function took its downscale factor from the document size alone: `proxy::preview_factor` gives k = ceil(sqrt(px / 2.5 MP)) for anything over 5 MP. It ignored the view's zoom. A 12 MP photo was previewed from a 3x-reduced copy, and a 36 MP one from a 4x-reduced copy, at every zoom, including 100 %. So the canvas showed 3-4 px blocks for as long as the point was dragged. On release `live_adjust` clears and the full-size composite comes back.

The Image > Adjustments > Curves dialog does not have this problem. Its GPU proxy (`adjust_preview::gpu_proxy`) already picks the factor from the zoom with `adjust_preview::proxy_factor`, which keeps the proxy at least at screen resolution and uses none at 50 % and closer.

### The change

- `crates/ui-egui/src/proxy.rs`: new `view_factor(k, zoom)`. It caps a live preview's factor with the same `proxy_factor(zoom)` rule the dialogs use.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`: `ensure_proxy_preview` now takes the view's zoom and applies that cap, but only when the wgpu compositor supports the document (`GpuCanvas::supports`, the same test as `adjust_preview::cheap`). In that case a closer view gets the full-size `display_doc` composite on the GPU, where only the adjustment's uniforms or LUT change. Zoomed out, a proxy is still used, but never coarser than the screen.
- Documents the GPU compositor can't draw keep the old proxy. For them the full size would mean a CPU composite on every change, so the old trade-off still app…

title: Smart Objects: Curves preview no longer zooms in on a reduced proxy (#5766)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #5766.

### What was wrong

Image › Adjustments › Curves (and any adjustment or filter) on a smart object records a smart filter (`adjust_as_smart_filter` in `crates/engine/src/adjust_cmds.rs` → `add_smart_filter` in `crates/engine/src/smart_cmds.rs`), which re-renders the smart object from its source through its placement (`render_in` → `place(.., sm)` using `sm.transform` / `sm.perspective`).

The dialog's live preview on a smart object takes the CPU proxy path (`adjust_preview::unsupported` rejects non-pixel layers), which runs the command on `proxy_document(doc, k)` (`crates/ui-egui/src/filter_dialog.rs`, `preview_document_for_target`). On documents above ~5 MP, k ≥ 2. `proxy_document` (`crates/compose/src/proxy.rs`, `shrink_layer`) downsampled the smart object's `cache` but left its `transform`, `perspective` and `filter_mask` in full-size document coordinates. So the re-render came out k times too large on the 1/k proxy canvas, and the canvas drew it scaled up by k: the image "zoomed in" while the dialog was open and snapped back after OK, when the real command ran at full size. The view zoom never changed. The reporter's screenshot matches this: a smart object layer in a large photo, shown magnified behind the open Curves dialog.

### The change

`shrink_layer` now calls `shrink_smart`, which scales the smart object along with the proxy: its cache (as before), its filter mask (downsampled like any other mask), its affine `transform` (pre-multiplied by `scale(1/k)`), and its `perspective` (the first two rows scaled by 1/k). The warp grid stays as it is because it is in source coordinates. Other `proxy_document` users (the adjustment proxy, thumbnails, Color Range) only composite the cache, so they don't change.

### Test

- `compose::proxy::tests::proxy_scales_smart_object_placement`: the proxy's smart object has its transform, perspective, cache and filter mask scaled by 1/k, and the source document is left alone.
- `ui-egui filter_dialog::tests::smart_…

title: 32-bit Hue/Saturation as Photoshop does it: unclipped saturation and Colorize (two rgb32 oracles pass)
author: timothydaly1
body:
## What

32-bit Hue/Saturation now matches Photoshop exactly on both of the photoshop corpus's 32-bit oracles. Photoshop's 32-bit Hue/Saturation differs from the 8/16-bit one in two ways; 8 and 16 bits are unchanged.

**1. The raised saturation isn't clipped, and its slider is on whole 8-bit levels.**
- Saturation is raised by `1 / (1 − s)` as at 8/16 bits, but not clipped at 1, so saturated colours leave 0..1. In `rgb32/hue-saturation.psd` (Hue +40, Saturation +25, Lightness −10), red becomes (1.0477, 0.649, −0.1477), where 8 bits clip it to (0.9, 0.6, 0).
- The slider is cut to whole 8-bit levels: 25 % raises by 1 / (1 − 63/255) = **1.328**, not 1/0.75 = 1.333. In-gamut colours show the same factor.
- Implemented in `adjust::hue_saturation_in(…, depth)`. The GPU kernel does the same when `F_HDR` is set.

**2. Colorize scales its saturation by `1 − |Lightness|`.**
- In `rgb32/hue-saturation-colorize.psd` (hue −160, saturation 40, lightness +5), every output has our hue and HSL lightness but exactly **0.95 of the chroma**, at every input lightness.
- Implemented in `adjust::colorize_saturation`, shared by the CPU and the GPU planner.
- Only a raised Lightness is measured; a lowered one is taken to scale the same way. Likewise, lowered saturation at 32 bits uses the same whole-level cut, which is unmeasured.

Neither change applies at 8 or 16 bits, whose oracles are exact without them. Applying the Colorize scale there breaks rgb16 hue-saturation-colorize.

## Evidence

| photoshop oracle | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `rgb32/hue-saturation.psd` | 0.1477, 58.46 %, DIFF | **0.0002, PASS** |
| `rgb32/hue-saturation-colorize.psd` | 0.0100, 52.94 %, DIFF | **0.0000, PASS** |
| `rgb8`/`rgb16` hue-saturation(-colorize), psd-tools huesaturation_* | unchanged | unchanged |

- **Corpus test against current main:** Photoshop oracles 185 → **187**; floor 185 → 187. psd-tools and io are unchanged.

## Tests

- `thirty_two_bit_hue_saturation_is_unclipped`: three oracle pixels…

title: Paint: Lock Transparency blends source-atop on semi-transparent pixels (#5783)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5783.

## Why
With Lock Transparent Pixels, or Fill's Preserve Transparency, PhotoCraft composited source-over and then restored the old alpha. Semi-transparent pixels therefore took the new colour by αs/αo instead of αs. Example: on a transparent layer, fill white at 50%, then black at 50% with Preserve Transparency. Photoshop gives (127,127,127,128); PhotoCraft gave (85,85,85,128). Opaque and empty pixels were already right, which is why the existing tests passed.

## Change
When alpha is kept, painting blends source-atop: `Co = (1-αs)·Cb + αs·B(Cb,Cs)`, alpha unchanged.
- New helper `blend::composite_atop` in photocraft-color.
- Used by Fill (`blend_tile`), Gradient and Paint Bucket (`composite_area`), and the brush and `apply_coverage` non-Normal paths.
- `over_native`'s lock branch (brush and mixer, Normal mode) lerps by the source alpha, like `mix_back`.

## Tests
New regression tests for Fill, Gradient, a brush stroke and `apply_coverage`, each at 8, 16 and 32-bit in Normal and Multiply, plus a unit test for `composite_atop`. The site tests all failed on main (0.333 instead of 0.5) and pass now.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-color -p photocraft-paint -p photocraft-algo -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests`: all pass.
- `cargo clippy` on the same crates with `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `panic_hunt -- --ignored`: green.

## Not included / not verified
- Non-Normal modes on semi-transparent pixels follow the formula above; only Normal was compared with Photoshop.
- `mix_back` (Blur/Sharpen strokes) already lerped under the lock and is unchanged.
- #5504 edits the signature of `composite_area` in the same file; this PR only touches the inner composite line.

title: Lens Flare: don't darken 32-bit pixels above 1.0 (#5785)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5785.

## Why
Lens Flare blends its light with screen written as `1 - (1 - c)(1 - a)`. In a 32-bit document a pixel above 1.0 makes `(1 - c)` negative, so the filter that adds light pulls HDR highlights down towards white: 2.0 with a = 0.5 became 1.5, and the flare core turned 2.0 into 1.0. A filter that adds light should never darken a pixel.

## Change
- `crates/algo/src/render.rs`: `c += min(a, 1) · max(1 - c, 0)`. For c ≤ 1 this is the same screen blend, so 8- and 16-bit results don't change; values already above 1.0 are kept as they are.

## Tests
- `lens_flare_never_darkens_32_bit_values_above_one`: 32-bit image filled with 2.0, every output channel ≥ 2.0 (failed on main: 1.9888…).
- `lens_flare_8_bit_result_is_the_screen_blend`: 8-bit output equals the old screen formula, rounded to 8 bits, for every pixel.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-algo` (552 passed), `cargo clippy -p photocraft-algo --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`: green.

## Not included
- Making the flare add light above 1.0 in 32-bit: Photoshop's exact 32-bit Lens Flare result isn't confirmed, so values above 1.0 are only kept, not raised.

CMYK pixels are stored as ink (1 = full ink), but the Channels panel and Photoshop show a CMYK channel as its tone: white where there is no ink. The engine copied raw ink, so on a white CMYK document Duplicate Channel of Cyan made an all-black alpha channel (Photoshop: white), Load Selection from Cyan selected nothing (Photoshop: everything), Split Channels made black grayscale documents, Merge Channels of white grayscale documents made a black CMYK image, and copy/paste with a CMYK channel targeted was inverted.

title: PSD Multichannel: alpha channels are stored as-is, not as ink (#5790)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5790.

## Why
A Multichannel PSD stores its ink planes as tone (0 = solid ink), but the planes DisplayInfo (1077) marks as alpha-type (kind 0 = selected areas, 1 = masked areas) are stored as-is, like alpha channels in every other mode. PhotoCraft inverted every plane on import and on export, so a white (selected) alpha channel opened as black (Load Selection selected nothing), and RGB → Multichannel → save wrote alpha channels black.

Measured with a file Photoshop saved itself: a new 8x4 8-bit white RGB document with a "selected areas" alpha channel (white left half, black right half), converted to Multichannel and saved as PSD. Merged planes: Cyan, Magenta, Yellow = 255 everywhere (no ink on white paper); alpha = `255 255 255 255 0 0 0 0` on every row (255 = selected). DisplayInfo kinds: 2, 2, 2, 0.

## Change
- `io` (`multichannel_map.rs`): after DisplayInfo is applied, alpha-type channels are flipped back to the stored values; export inverts only spot channels.
- `compose` (`multichannel.rs`): an alpha-type channel still prints as a transparent black ink, now of `1 − value`, so a Multichannel file's composite is unchanged (an all-black alpha prints solid black, as before).

## Tests
- New (8 and 16 bit), both failing on main: a kind-0 alpha plane stored max/0 imports as 1.0/0.0 while the spot plane is still read as ink, the composite is unchanged, and the round trip is byte-for-byte; a full alpha exports as a max plane next to a solid ink stored as 0.
- Adapted from #4031: the "alpha composite equals a black ink" check now compares against a black ink of the inverted alpha (within f32 rounding); the compose unit test writes its alpha in as-is polarity and also checks that unselected areas print black. Round-trip and corpus assertions are unchanged.

author: optimalbytee
body:

title: fix(ui): brush outline matches the stroke on Wayland at fractional scales
author: wanikhawar
body:
## Problem

On Wayland at a fractional scale (reported on Hyprland 0.56.2 at 1.25), every brush's outline was 1.25× too large and sat right of and below where the brush actually painted. The offset grew with the brush size, so strokes looked off-centre toward the top left.

## Cause

The engine is exact: a single dab's centroid lands within 0.005 px of the requested point. The OS cursor bitmap was wrong. winit 0.30 sizes custom cursor bitmaps on Wayland with a `wp_viewport` destination whenever the scale isn't 1. Hyprland, like Mutter before GNOME 48, ignores viewports on cursor surfaces. It shows the bitmap at one pixel per logical pixel, with the hotspot that winit divided by the scale.

## Fix

A client can't tell which compositors honour the viewport, so on Wayland at any scale other than 1, `tool_cursor::native` now refuses OS bitmaps. The brush outline and crosshairs are painted in-app, as the web build already does. Windows, macOS, X11 and Wayland at scale 1 keep the low-latency bitmap. `Services::is_wayland` reaches the cursor code via `tool_cursor::set_wayland` on every pass.

Trade-off: in this configuration the painted outline can trail a fast pointer by a frame or two (#1343).

## Measured

Hyprland 0.56.2 at 1.25, 100 % zoom, 100 px hard brush. The real pointer was moved with `hyprctl` and screenshots were taken with `grim -c`.

| | centre (px) | diameter (px) |
|---|---|---|
| painted dab | (288.5, 560.5) | 97 |
| outline before | (303, 574.5) | ~130 |
| outline after | (288.5, 562) | 107 (incl. border) |

## Tests

- New: `tool_cursor::tests::scaled_wayland_paints_the_brush_outline_instead_of_an_os_bitmap`. Before the fix it fails because an OS bitmap is used.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib tool_cursor`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` all pass.

title: Options bar: Show Transform Controls in every theme (#5740)
author: vangel76
body:

The Move tool's options bar has two branches. The Pro themes get Auto-Select, the target dropdown, **Show Transform Controls** and the align buttons. Every other theme (Studio, Adwaita, Breeze, …) got only Auto-Select (#1275) and the hint "Drag to move the active layer", which is what the reporter's screenshot shows. `move_show_transform` defaults to off, so in those themes there was no way to turn the box on: a click on a shape with the Move tool only showed the rollover outline, while ⌘T showed the handles. Once it's on, the live-rectangle corner-radius widgets show with the Move tool there too, as they do in the Pro themes (`corner_radius::shows`).

Related: #4546 (open) turns Show Transform Controls on by default; this PR is independent of it and makes the toggle reachable in every theme either way. #5669 edits the adjacent Auto-Select line in the same branch, so whichever lands second gets a trivial conflict.

title: fix(paint): clip Blur/Sharpen/Smudge and toning dab buffers to the canvas (#5633)
author: aryamanchhikara
body:
Fixes the large-brush part of #5633. Blur, Sharpen, Smudge, Dodge, Burn and Sponge sized their working buffers from the brush instead of the canvas, so a 5000 px soft brush allocated several GB per dab and froze the app (and should abort it on lower-memory machines). Buffers are now clipped to the canvas plus the effect's halo, and oversized strokes are refused with an error instead of aborting. Live preview of one 5000 px soft Blur stroke: **6.3 GB / 31 s → 194 MB / 0.55 s**.

Part of #5633 (the crash). The slowness and the purple bug in the same issue are separate and not touched here.

## What happened

With a soft 5000 px Blur brush, PhotoCraft peaked at 4.8 GB (Activity Monitor) and froze for about 14 s on an M1 Pro / 16 GB (one 7.8 s frame for the live stroke, then 6.5 s on release). It didn't crash on my machine, but on machines with less free memory these allocations should fail, and Rust aborts the process on a failed allocation, so the shell's panic guard can't catch it. That is most likely the crash in the report.

## Root cause

The sequential-dab tools (Blur, Sharpen, Smudge, Dodge, Burn, Sponge) sized every buffer from the dab and stroke rectangles, which were never clipped to the canvas:

- [`LiveDab::push`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/32fdc4e40211e66f92d1a1df468afae15471538b/crates/engine/src/retouch_cmds.rs#L1130) copied each dab's whole rectangle, and [`apply_dab_stroke`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/32fdc4e40211e66f92d1a1df468afae15471538b/crates/paint/src/retouch.rs#L238-L242) copied the whole stroke's bounding box twice, plus a third time when mixing back, with an unclipped footprint per dab ([`BrushContext::footprint`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/32fdc4e40211e66f92d1a1df468afae15471538b/crates/paint/src/render.rs#L382)).
- [`Surface::read_region`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/32fdc4e40211e66f92d1a1df468afae15471538b/crates/raster/src/lib.rs#L553) allocates the full requested rect…

title: Type: keep superscript and subscript when a text layer is re-rendered (#5645)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #5645

## Root cause
`CharStyle` had no superscript/subscript attribute, so PSD import ignored the EngineData `FontBaseline` key (0 normal, 1 superscript, 2 subscript). An imported layer first shows Photoshop's pixel cache; entering text editing re-renders it with PhotoCraft's engine, which drew C₂ as C2. Saving the PSD dropped the attribute too.

## Fix
- `photocraft-doc`: new `FontBaseline` enum and `CharStyle::baseline` (default `Normal`; `#[serde(default)]` keeps older `.pcraft` files loading).
- `photocraft-text`: read and write `FontBaseline` in the character style data; layout draws a superscript/subscript run at 58.3% of its size with its baseline moved up/down by 33.3% of its size (Photoshop's default Superscript/Subscript Size and Position). Applied to the run's drawn style, so glyphs, underline and ink bounds all follow; the stored `size_pt` and `baseline_shift_pt` are untouched.
- `photocraft-engine`: character params accept `"baseline": "normal|superscript|subscript"` (documented in the params string).

Not in this PR: Superscript/Subscript toggle buttons in the Character panel (Photoshop has 8 toggles, PhotoCraft 6); the attribute is settable through `type.setCharacter`-style params.

## Tests

title: Type: Swap and Default Colors recolour the selected text (#5690)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5690.

## What changes

While you edit type with characters highlighted, the toolbar's **Switch Colors** (X) and **Default Colors** (D) buttons now recolour the highlighted characters with the new foreground colour, as in Photoshop. Picking a colour in the Color picker or Swatches already did this. Before this change, the chips only changed the tool colours and the selected text kept its colour. With no characters highlighted, nothing changes: the buttons only swap or reset the foreground and background.

The fix covers both buttons, Switch Colors and Default Colors.

## How it works

`color_chips` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs` now runs both buttons through a small `chip_command` helper. The helper dispatches the existing engine command (`tools.swapColors` / `tools.defaultColors`). If that succeeds, it calls `type_tool::foreground_changed`, the same hook the Color and Swatches panels use. That hook applies the new foreground to the highlighted range through the `type.setStyle` engine command, coalesced into the current type-editing session. No new commands and no new UI state.

## Tests

- New `panels::color_tests::swap_and_default_colors_recolour_selected_type` clicks both chips in an egui_kittest harness, once with characters highlighted in a type layer being edited and once without. It checks the tool colours, that the highlighted characters take the new foreground, and that the other characters keep theirs. It fails without the fix.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests`: everything passes except 6 tests (`profile_open_tests` ×3, `jobs_ui` ×2, `filter_dialog::…smart_object_curves_preview…`). The same 6 also fail locally on plain main, so they come from this machine, not this change.

title: Menus: one checkmark column keeps every label aligned (#5705)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #5705.

### Why
Menu rows put their label behind a text prefix: "✔ " when checked, three spaces when unchecked, and nothing for plain rows and submenu headers. Those widths differ, so unchecked toggles (Lock Guides, Lock Slices) started at a different x than plain items like Clear Guides; with Chinese labels the gap is easy to see. Photoshop's menus on Windows, like standard Windows menus, reserve one checkmark column on every row so all labels line up.

### Change
- `menu_keys::menu_row_text` lays out a row behind a fixed-width checkmark column (`check_gutter`: the width of "✔ " in the button font). Checked rows draw ✔ in the column; all other rows leave it empty through the layout job's leading space. Alignment therefore no longer depends on padding characters or on the label's script. Mnemonic underlines are kept.
- Leaf rows and submenu headers in the main menu bar menus use it. Menus without checkable items now also reserve the column, as Windows menus do.

### Tests
- New `menu_keys::harness_tests::every_menu_row_starts_its_label_after_one_checkmark_column`: checked, unchecked and underlined rows (Latin and Chinese labels) start the label at the same x, at the gutter width.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib menu`: 218 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Offscreen snapshot of the zh-Hans View menu: every label is aligned, including submenu headers and checked rows.

### Not included / not verified
- The new test covers the new helper, so there is no before/after run against the old prefix code.
- Not checked in the live Windows app, only in the offscreen snapshot. The macOS native menu uses the OS menu and is unaffected.
- The Channels and Rulers context menus still use their own "✓ " prefix on checked rows only; left as they are.

title: Warp: a thin layer stretched and bent keeps its curve on commit (#5793)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #5793

## Root cause
`warp_mesh_surface` (crates/algo/src/warp.rs) approximates the warp with a triangle grid whose cell count came from the source rectangle only (one cell per 4 source px). In the report, the layer is a 3 px wide column: Free Transform stretches it into a wide band, Warp bends it, and the preview shows the curve. On commit the grid had a single cell across the 3 source pixels, so the band was mapped affinely and came out straight.

## Fix
The grid now also follows the destination: the forward map is probed on a 17x17 grid, and the longest mapped row and column set the cell count when they are longer than the source (still capped at `MAX_CELLS`). Layers that are not stretched get the same grid as before. Masks and selections (`warp_mesh_gray`) and smart-object placement (`place_source`) use the same function, so they get the fix too.

## Tests
- `algo` `warp::tests::a_thin_layer_stretched_into_a_curve_keeps_the_curve`: a 3x40 px column mapped through a 100x stretch plus an arch must follow the arch.
- `ui-egui` `transform_tool::tests::a_thin_layer_scaled_then_warped_commits_the_curve`: the report's steps (3 px column, scale 30x, Warp, pull the middle down, commit).

Both fail without the fix (the middle stays straight) and pass with it.

## Commands
- `cargo test -p photocraft-algo --lib`, `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib`, `cargo test -p photocraft-io --lib`
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- transform`, `-- warp`, `-- smart`
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-algo -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt -p photocraft-algo -p photocraft-ui-egui -- --check`
- `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo check -p photocraft-algo --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`

Note: #5590 moves the body of `warp_mesh_surface` into a new `mesh()` function, so whichever lands second has a small textual conflict on the grid-size lines.

title: Swatches: the .ase reader refuses files with more than 10,000 groups
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## Problem
`photocraft_psd::ase::parse` counted colors toward `MAX_SWATCHES` but not group starts (`crates/psd/src/ase.rs:200-205` on `main`), so the number of groups it read grew with the file's size. An empty group start is six bytes, and `parse` held about 64 bytes for each: in a test build, parsing a 60 MB file of 10,000,000 empty group starts raised the process's peak memory from 63 MB to 705 MB. `swatches.import` reads files of up to 512 MiB, and `read_file` built a group for each group start (`crates/engine/src/swatch_cmds.rs:505-508`) before the import refused more than 10,000 groups (`:594-595`).

## Fix
- `parse` counts group starts and returns `LimitExceeded("too many groups in an .ase file")` past the new `ase::MAX_GROUPS`, 10,000, the most groups the Swatches panel holds (`swatch_cmds::MAX_GROUPS`). Files with at most 10,000 groups parse as before, so every file `swatches.import` accepted still loads. Files with more were refused before as well; now `parse` refuses them before it holds more than 10,000 groups.
- `write` also refuses more than `MAX_GROUPS` groups, as it refuses more than `MAX_SWATCHES` colors.
- vectorcraft's `.ase` reader also counts group starts toward a limit (https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/pull/644).
- The change adds an implemented control: the `.ase` reader limits the number of groups it reads, and `ase_group_cap_is_enforced_on_hostile_input` is its regression test.

## Tests
- New `ase_group_cap_is_enforced_on_hostile_input` in `crates/psd/tests/swatch_malformed.rs` parses 10,001 empty group starts and expects `LimitExceeded`, then parses the same file with one block fewer and expects all 10,000 groups. Without the check in `parse`, it fails at its first assertion.
- New `too_many_groups` in `ase.rs` checks that `write` refuses 10,001 groups and that 10,000 groups are written and read back. Without the check in `write`, it fails.
- With the change, the 60 MB file above is refused in 0.3 ms, and the process's peak memory …

title: fix(ui): smart filter adjustments open their own editor on double-click
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
An Image › Adjustments applied to a smart object is recorded as an `image.adjustments.<kind>` smart filter. Double-clicking its row in the Layers panel called `smart_ui::open_editor`, which only handled `filter.*` commands and returned silently for adjustments, so the Brightness/Contrast (and Levels, Curves, …) settings could never be reopened. The editor now routes adjustment commands to `adjust_dialog`, seeds the dialog with the recorded parameters, and OK updates the existing filter through `layer.smartFilter.setParams` instead of stacking a second one. The regression test builds a smart object with a Brightness/Contrast filter, opens its editor, and checks the recorded settings survive a confirm. Test: `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib an_adjustment_smart_filter_opens_its_editor_and_updates_it`.

Fixes #5689

title: fix(ui): the Switch Colors arrow recolours selected type
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The Switch Colors arrow changed the foreground/background pair but never notified the text editor, so characters selected in a type layer kept their colour while the Color, Swatches and Color Picker paths recoloured them. The button now calls `type_tool::foreground_changed` after the swap, so a selection takes the swapped-in foreground in the editing session's history step; a caret still leaves the type alone. The regression test clicks the arrow with a caret and with a selection and checks the run colours. Test: `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib swap_colors_recolours_selected_type_only`.

Fixes #5690

title: fix(ui): the Move tool keeps Photoshop's arrow pointer
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The canvas cursor table mapped the Move tool to `CursorIcon::Move`, the 4-way move cursor; Photoshop shows its standard arrow pointer and marks the movable layer under the pointer with the hover outline. The Move tool now uses `CursorIcon::Default` (Preferences › Cursors › Precise still overrides it with the crosshair, and hovering a guide keeps the guide cursor). The regression test hovers the canvas with the Move tool and asserts the arrow pointer. Test: `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib the_move_tool_keeps_the_arrow_pointer`.

title: perf(doc): share the XMP packet, Duotone PSD data and unsupported adjustment bytes between snapshots
author: FinnNk
body:
Fixes #4535.

Every edit clones the document (`Session::edit`), and history keeps one document per state. Three fields held their payloads as owned buffers, so every clone duplicated them, and nothing counted the copies:
- `Metadata.xmp: Option<String>`: hundreds of KB to MBs in files with long `DocumentAncestors` lists.
- `Duotone.psd_raw: Option<Vec<u8>>`: also cloned per frame by the Duotone preview.
- `Adjustment::Unsupported.raw: Vec<u8>`.

Their siblings (`exif`, `psd_resources`, `psd_global_blocks`, a layer's `psd_raw`) were already `Arc`.

## Change

- **The three fields** are now `Option<Arc<str>>`, `Option<Arc<[u8]>>` and `Arc<[u8]>`. Behaviour is unchanged.
  - **Reads compile as they were,** because `Arc<str>` derefs to `str` (`metadata.xmp.as_deref()` and so on).
  - **The edits are at the boundaries** to the codecs, the `.pcraft` manifest and the PSD model, which keep their own `String`/`Vec`. Those boundaries convert once per open or save, which is negligible next to the file I/O. The codecs crate stays standalone and owns its decoded data, as before.
  - **In all:** 18 files, +26/−26. 12 sites are in production code and 11 in test fixtures.
- **`docs/architecture.md`, principle 5** ("immutable snapshots, copy-on-write tiles") now says that every large payload in `photocraft-doc` is `Arc`-shared, and that new fields follow the rule. That way the next one doesn't regress silently.
- **Docs:** the three fields say they're shared, and `xmp` says why it stays text (properties PhotoCraft doesn't model must survive).

I also tried a copy-on-write wrapper (`Shared<T>` with `DerefMut` through `Arc::make_mut`). It needed a similar number of edits, plus a new type. It also hid copies behind ordinary field writes, and shared at the level of the whole `Metadata` rather than per payload. Explicit `Arc` fields match the existing convention and say plainly that these payloads are only ever replaced, never edited in place.

title: Auto-Blend Layers: blend a layer the canvas crops to all-overlap (#5745)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #5745.

### What was wrong
With two photos, the bottom (often the Background) covers the whole canvas. Auto-Align moves the second photo partly off the canvas, and Auto-Blend cropped its work area to the canvas. That left the second layer entirely overlap, and `seam_labels` (`crates/algo/src/panorama.rs`) skipped any image whose coverage was all overlap. The top layer got an all-black mask and the picture didn't change: "it just creates 2 layer masks".

### Changes
- `seam_labels`: an image lying wholly inside the composite takes the side of the seam it lies towards from the composite's centre. An image centred on the composite (or covering the same cells) still has no side, and the earlier images keep it.
- `edit.autoBlendLayers`: masks and blends the whole layers, off the canvas too, as Photoshop does, so Reveal All shows the whole panorama. This only applies when their union isn't mostly empty.
- Seamless Tones and Colors now also turns on gain compensation over the overlaps.
- The Background is turned into a normal layer before it gets a mask.

### Tests
- `panorama::tests::an_image_wholly_inside_the_composite_still_gets_its_side`
- `align_cmds::tests::auto_blend_panorama_of_a_layer_hanging_off_the_canvas` (8/16/32-bit)

I didn't run the tests locally; CI runs them.

title: Web: Place Embedded and canvas drops place images (#5749)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #5749.

### What was wrong

Files to place arrive through a new `Services::place_inbox` and go through the existing one-at-a-time Free Transform queue (`DropPlace::Bytes`).

title: Fill layers: reject non-finite angle/phase, normalise degrees (#5752)
author: NibrasAz7
body:
Fixes storytold/photocraft#5752.

`layer.newFillLayer.gradient`, `gradient.presets.apply` and the pattern placement shared by `layer.newFillLayer.pattern`, `edit.fill` and `paint.bucket` stored `as f32` unchecked: JSON `1e39` saturated to `inf`, rendering hit `cos(inf) = NaN`, and `format/src/finite.rs` then refused `.pcraft` saves.

- new `angle_deg` param helper: finite check + normalise to (-180, 180], matching `gradient.fill.set`
- `pattern_cmds::placement()` returns `Result` with the same checks for `scale`/`phase`
- regression test: the reported inputs are bad-params errors and add no layer; `450` stores as `90`, `270` as `-90`

author: nrq6993-a11y

Creating a new group with several layers selected left an empty group and the selected layers outside it. With a single selected layer it still creates an empty group above the active layer, and Shift-click on the folder button still groups the selection.

title: IO: name the missing 8BPS signature for unopenable .psd/.psb files (#5258)
author: secureusnetworks
body:
Closes #5258.

A `.psd`/`.psb`-named file that lacks the `8BPS` signature and is not a recognised image format previously failed deep in the codec layer with the unhelpful:

> codec: unrecognized image format

The open path now names the missing signature instead, returning a `PsdError::InvalidSignature { expected: "8BPS", found }` so the user can act on it - a corrupt, truncated, or mislabeled file.

A real known raster that is merely mislabeled `.psd` still opens: its magic is detected earlier and wins over the suffix.

## Changes
- `crates/io/src/lib.rs`: in the PSD/PSB open path, when the suffix is `.psd`/`.psb` but `photocraft_codecs::detect` finds no known magic, return an actionable signature error instead of delegating to the codec layer. The first 4 bytes actually found are included in the error.
- `crates/io/tests/flat.rs`: regression test `psd_named_unknown_magic_reports_missing_signature`.

## Verification

title: Shapes: rounded corners on live triangles, polygons and stars (TOOL-214-12)
author: bazmarth
body:
## Summary
Photoshop rounds the corners of live triangles and polygons, like a rectangle's. PhotoCraft's live polygons (the Triangle tool draws a 3-sided one; stars too) had no corner radius, so only rectangles could be rounded. This adds it, with the same on-canvas widgets as rectangles (#5276).

Dragging any widget gives **every selected shape the same radius** (each within its own size), with the corner radius cursor and the `R:` readout, as **one history step**. Alt still changes a single corner of a rectangle; a triangle or polygon has one radius for all its corners.
- **Fix**: the widgets now take the **unsnapped** press, like Free Transform's handles. Snapping used to pull a shape tool's press off a widget onto a nearby vertex or guide, so the Triangle tool drew a new triangle instead of rounding the selected one.

title: Free Transform: shapes and paths stay on whole pixels (#5751)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #5751.

### What was wrong
*Preferences › Tools › Snap Vector Tools and Transforms to Pixel Grid* (on by default) only rounded the **pointer**, and only while a shape or pen tool was active (`snap_ui::pixel_round`). Free Transform of a shape layer under the Move tool (the usual ⌘T) left the box's edges between pixels. So did a handle grabbed a little off its edge, or a proportional corner drag. A test reproducing the report left the edges at 20.6 and 1040.4; committed, the shape kept those coordinates and rasterized with a soft column. So a rectangle couldn't be dragged to exactly 540 px. (The Move tool itself already moves by whole pixels.)

### Change
`transform_tool::round_to_pixel_grid`, called after every Free Transform drag step: with the preference on, an **upright** box (moved or scaled; rotated, skewed and distorted boxes are left alone) on a **shape layer or a path** has its corners rounded to whole pixels, whatever the tool. Selection transforms, warps, Content-Aware Scale and mask/channel targets are untouched, and a box is never collapsed below 1 px.

### Test
`snap_ui::tests::free_transform_of_a_shape_keeps_whole_pixels`: a rectangle on a 1080 px canvas at 60% zoom is resized under the Move tool, first by an edge handle grabbed 1.3 px off its edge, then by a proportional corner drag. With the preference on, every corner is a whole pixel, before and after commit. With it off, the box follows the pointer. I ran this test locally and it passes (`cargo check -p photocraft-ui-egui --tests` is clean); I didn't run the full suite.

title: Color: a picked colour recolours the selected type and shapes
author: bazmarth
body:
## Summary
Picking a colour in the Color panel, the Swatches panel or the Color Picker only changed the foreground; it recoloured nothing selected, except characters selected while editing type (#364). Now the three colour sources go through one place (`apply_color.rs`) that also recolours the selection, following the tool in hand:

| Tool | A new foreground colour… |
|---|---|
| Editing type, characters selected | recolours those characters (unchanged) |
| Type / Vertical Type, not editing | recolours **every selected type layer** (`type.setStyle`) |
| Shape tools, Pens, anchor tools, Path / Direct Selection | sets **every selected shape layer's fill** (`shape.edit`) |
| **Move** (layers picked by a click, Shift-click or its marquee) | **both**: every selected type layer and every selected shape |
| Any other tool (brushes, pixel selections, Eyedropper, Type Mask…) | changes only the foreground |

The Type, shape and path tools behave as Photoshop does. The Move tool goes further: layers picked with it take the colour as well, so a set of shapes box-selected with the Move tool can be recoloured from the Swatches panel directly.

One pick is **one history step** for all the layers it recolours, and a drag in the Color panel's field or sliders is one step too (`coalesce`), so it doesn't record a step per frame.

title: Actions: Photoshop Shadows/Highlights steps play (#5830)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Refs #5830 (fixes the Shadows/Highlights part).

### What was wrong
Importing a Photoshop action that uses **Image › Adjustments › Shadows/Highlights** stopped at that step: *Photoshop step "Sombra/Realce" (adaptCorrect) has no PhotoCraft equivalent yet*. PhotoCraft has the command (`image.adjustments.shadowsHighlights`), but the `.atn` event table (`crates/engine/src/atn_cmds.rs`, `EVENTS`) had no entry for `adaptCorrect`.

### Change
A new `adaptCorrect` event (string ID only; it has no char ID), mapped both ways:

| Photoshop descriptor | PhotoCraft param |
|---|---|
| `shadowMode` › `amount` / `width` / `radius` | `shadowAmount` / `shadowTone` / `shadowRadius` |
| `highlightMode` › `amount` / `width` / `radius` | `highlightAmount` / `highlightTone` / `highlightRadius` |
| `blackClip`, `whiteClip` | `blackClip`, `whiteClip` |
| `center` | `midtone` |
| `colorCorrection` | `color` |

The descriptor shape comes from a public ScriptListener recording of Shadows/Highlights (Adobe community forum). Each key is also accepted as its char ID (`sdwM`, `hglM`, `Amnt`, `Wdth`, `Rds `, `BlcC`, `WhtC`, `Cntr`, `ClrC`), and absent keys keep the command's defaults. Recording a Shadows/Highlights step and saving the set as `.atn` now writes the same shape.

### Not in this PR (the rest of #5830)
- **Lens Blur** (`Bokh`): I couldn't confirm its descriptor keys from a public source, so I didn't map them by guesswork. Mapping it needs a recorded `.atn` (or a ScriptListener log) with non-default settings, ideally as a photocraft-corpus oracle.

title: Displace: OK asks for the displacement map, as in Photoshop (#5806)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #5806.

### What was wrong
In Photoshop, **Filter › Distort › Displace** asks for the displacement map file (a PSD) after you click OK. PhotoCraft's dialog is generated from the command spec. It offered the map only as *Map Document* (a dropdown of open documents) or *Map Path* (a plain text field to type a path into). title: Layers panel: blend mode, Opacity, Fill and locks change every selected layer; Photoshop's History names
author: tanish2k09
body:
From the first-party layers audit (phase L2, silently wrong results).

## Problem
With several layers selected, the Layers panel's **blend mode, Opacity, Fill and lock buttons changed only the active layer**. Every call passed `"layer": active`, and nothing told the user the other layers were left alone. Photoshop changes all the selected layers.

## Change

title: Batch: Format "Same" saves camera raws as PSD instead of failing (#5799)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Refs #5799.

### What was wrong
The reporter's screenshot shows **File › Automate › Batch** run over a folder of Sony **ARW** files with **Format: Same**. `process_tree` (`crates/engine/src/file_cmds.rs`) gave every output its input's extension, so each result was saved as `.arw`. `file_cmds::tests::batch_same_format_saves_camera_raws_as_psd`: a folder with a synthetic DNG and a PNG, batched with Format "Same", writes `IMG_0001.psd` and `b.png` with no errors. Not built or run locally; CI runs it.

### Possibly still open in #5799
If the recorded action itself contains a step tied to the open document (selecting a document by name, or a Save to a fixed path), Batch would still only touch that one file. I'd need the reporter's action to confirm that, so this is `Refs`, not `Fixes`.

title: Title bar: dialogs no longer stop the window dragging on macOS (#5826)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #5826.

### What was wrong
With a dialog open (for example the *Embedded Profile Mismatch* prompt when opening a screenshot), the main window couldn't be dragged by its title bar on macOS.

The app's title strip starts window drags itself (`panels::title_bar`, `ViewportCommand::StartDrag`). A dialog's modal layer blocks that strip, so #4913 added `titlebar::modal_drag_overlay`, which keeps the strip's free gap draggable above the modal. But `lib.rs` only ran it when `self.custom_titlebar` was set. On macOS `CUSTOM_TITLEBAR` is false (`apps/photocraft/src/main.rs`): the window keeps the OS traffic lights over the app's own strip (`with_fullsize_content_view`, `with_titlebar_shown(false)`). So the overlay never ran there, and any dialog froze the window in place. The same applies on Windows and Linux with *Preferences › Interface › system title bar* turned on.

### Change
The condition moves into `PhotocraftApp::titlebar_modal_drag(chrome)`: the overlay runs whenever the title strip is drawn (`chrome && menu_bar`) and a dialog is open, whatever the title bar style. The overlay is unchanged: it still covers only the free gap, and only when no popup is open and no dialog has been moved over that gap.

### Test
`titlebar::tests::a_dialog_keeps_the_title_strip_draggable_with_either_title_bar`: with and without the custom title bar, an open dialog turns the overlay on. It stays off with no dialog, with chrome hidden, or with no menu bar. Not built or run locally; CI runs it.

In the Brushes panel (and the Brush Preset picker), dragging a row picks up the preset, group or folder to move it, as in Photoshop. But the list didn't scroll while dragging. title: Save: a flat file that keeps the document is saved in place (#5733)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #5733.

### What was wrong
"When you open a file, change it and save it (via Save), it opens a Save As dialog instead." File › Save on a document opened from a flat file (PNG, JPEG, TIFF…) always went through Save As (`menus.rs`, `file.save`: `_ => app.save_dialog_flow(..)`), even when the file still held everything. Photoshop's Save writes such a file back in place, and only asks once the document has something the format can't keep (layers, transparency in a JPEG, 16-bit in a JPEG…).

### Change
`saves_flat_in_place(doc, path)` (`lib.rs`): Save writes the document's own flat file back when that file keeps the whole document:
- one plain raster layer (`plain_raster`: visible, 100% opacity, Normal, no masks, effects or blending restrictions);
- no extra channels, RGB or Grayscale;
- a format that writes the document's bit depth (`FormatCaps::depths`);
- transparency only where the format has alpha, or the layer is the Background.

Anything else keeps today's behaviour (Save As, so the original is never overwritten with less, #3806). The replay rule for recorded Saves (#3531) is unchanged.

### Test
`file_open::tests::a_flat_file_that_keeps_the_document_saves_in_place`: a PNG with one plain layer saves in place. Add a second layer and Save asks. A JPEG whose one layer isn't the Background (JPEG has no alpha) asks too. The existing `pcraft_documents_save_in_place_but_flat_files_ask` still holds: its PNG has no plain layer. Not built or run locally; CI runs it.

title: Twirl, Pinch and Spherize fill the inscribed ellipse (#5643)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Refs #5643.

### What was wrong
**Filter › Distort › Twirl / Pinch / Spherize** acted inside a circle of radius `min(w, h) / 2` (`distort::centre`), so on any non-square image or selection only a central disc changed and the rest stayed untouched: "only apply to a sharp circle in the centre". Photoshop's versions act inside the ellipse inscribed in the selection or layer bounds, which reaches all four edges.

### Change
`crates/algo/src/distort.rs`: Twirl, Pinch and Spherize (Normal mode) map each point to unit-circle coordinates of the bounds' inscribed ellipse, apply the same radial or rotational profile as before, and map back. For square bounds the ellipse is the old circle, so square results are unchanged. Spherize's Horizontal/Vertical-only modes already used the full half-width/height. ZigZag keeps its inscribed circle.

### Test
`tests::round_distortions_fill_the_inscribed_ellipse`: on an 80×40 image, points 30 px left and right of centre on the middle row (outside the old 20 px circle) now change for all three filters, and the four corners stay as they were. The existing square-image tests (`twirl_keeps_centre_and_outside`, the identity-at-zero checks) still hold. Not built or run locally; CI runs it.

### Not changed
The issue also asks for a softer edge and an adjustable radius. The radius isn't a Photoshop option (the selection sets the area). How soft Photoshop's boundary is would need a side-by-side oracle before changing the falloff, so that's left for a follow-up.

title: fix(codecs): preserve unrelated XMP when normalizing orientation
author: 0x6Ason
body:
String-based XMP orientation rewriting can modify unrelated properties, descriptions, comments, or literal text that happen to contain tiff:Orientation.

- Resolve TIFF Orientation properties by XML namespace and edit only numeric attribute/simple-element values, preserving unrelated source bytes.
- Support namespace aliases, whitespace, numeric CDATA and character references.
- Bound XML structure and cumulative text work; preserve malformed, DTD-containing, over-budget or ambiguous packets unchanged.
- Add the existing roxmltree version to the codecs dependencies and update fixtures to well-formed namespace-qualified XML.

Regression coverage: Regression tests cover unrelated metadata and literals, namespace scope, quoting/whitespace, malformed packets, non-scalar elements, XML work limits, and JPEG/PNG/WebP/TIFF export round trips.

Scope: XMP orientation normalization only. Conservatively rejected packets remain unchanged, including any orientation they contain.

title: Preferences: old settings files take Shift-to-switch-tools on (#5647)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #5647.

### What was wrong
Pressing a tool's letter again cycled through its group (V: Move → Artboard, B: Brush → Pencil → …). In Photoshop the plain letter keeps the tool, and **Shift+letter** cycles ("Use Shift Key for Tool Switch", on by default).

PhotoCraft already behaves that way when the preference is on (`shortcuts.rs`), and #3528 (2026-10-12, first released in 0.8.2) made it on by default. But the preferences file stores **every** key, chosen or not. Every install that ran an earlier build has `"useShiftKeyForToolSwitch": false` saved, the old default, so the new default never reached existing users. The existing test only covers a file *without* the key.

### Change
`Session::load_prefs_json`: a settings file older than version 2 that stores `useShiftKeyForToolSwitch: false` drops that key, so it takes the new default (on). `prefs_value` now writes `"version": 2` (`PREFS_VERSION`), so a user who turns the preference off from now on keeps it off. This follows the existing appearance-mode migration in the same function.

One trade-off: someone who deliberately turned the preference off on 0.8.2–0.9.0 (when the file still said version 1) gets it back on once, and can turn it off again.

### Test
`prefs::tests::old_settings_files_take_the_shift_key_tool_switch_default`: files without a version and with version 1 storing `false` load with the switch on, and other Tools settings are kept. A preference turned off and saved now writes version 2 and stays off when reloaded. Not built or run locally; CI runs it.

title: macOS: a bundled app keeps its own Dock icon (#5849)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #5849.

### What was wrong
`native_options` (`apps/photocraft/src/main.rs`) always called `.with_icon(app_icon::window_icon())`. On macOS, a runtime window icon replaces the application icon in the Dock. So even in the packaged `PhotoCraft.app`, whose `Info.plist` points `CFBundleIconFile` at `PhotoCraft.icns`, the Dock showed the flat 1024 px PNG. It never got the system's rendering of the bundle icon (Liquid Glass, tinted and dark appearances).

### Change
- `app_icon::sets_runtime_icon(exe)`: false only on macOS when the running executable sits in an app bundle (`…/Name.app/Contents/MacOS/binary`); true everywhere else.
- `native_options` adds `with_icon` only then.

Unbundled runs on macOS (`cargo run`, where there is no `.icns` to fall back on) and the Windows and Linux builds (title bar, taskbar, `_NET_WM_ICON`) behave as before.

### Test
`app_icon::tests::only_a_macos_app_bundle_skips_the_runtime_icon`: bundle paths are recognised, case-insensitively (`.APP`). A plain binary, a `Contents/MacOS` folder outside any `.app`, and a bare `.app` aren't. The runtime icon is skipped only for a bundle and only on macOS. Not built or run locally; CI runs it.
