title: refactor(engine): drop the second damage pass after single-edit duplicates and pastes
author: FinnNk
body:
Addresses #5695.

#5695 points at `note_insert` in Duplicate Layer, Duplicate Layers and Paste: each keeps the document from before the edit and works out the damage again with `step_damage` afterwards. Since #3847, `Session::edit` reports exactly that damage itself, so for these single-edit commands the second pass gives the same answer as the first. This change removes it.

## Change

- **Duplicate Layer (`layer.duplicate`), Duplicate Layers (`duplicate_selected`) and Paste (`edit.paste`):** the `before` clone and the `note_insert` call are removed. `Session::edit` already set `last_damage` to the new layer's bounds.
- **Paste Into keeps `note_insert`:** it makes three edits (paste, reveal-all mask, set mask), so `edit` only sees the last one.
- **`note_insert`'s doc** now says it is for commands made of more than one edit, and not to call it after a single `edit`.

## Measurements (why this is a clean-up, not a speed-up)

I timed both `step_damage` calls inside `perf_scenarios`' P8–P11 rows (12 MP layer, 20 MP layered document) with a temporary instrumented release build on Windows x86_64. Each call takes **0.012–0.043 ms**. P8–P11 take 12–30 ms per row here, so removing the second call makes no measurable difference, and the P8–P11 increases reported in #5695 don't come from these calls. `step_damage` compares tiles by pointer, and the "full `Document` clone" is an `Arc` clone, so neither copies pixel data.

So this is a simplification: three fewer document clones held across the edit, one fewer tree walk, and the code says what each damage path is for.

## Tests

- `duplicate_paste_and_delete_report_where_the_layer_draws` now also duplicates **two selected layers** (`duplicate_selected`, which had no damage test). It checks the damage is the union of both copies (`Rect::new(10, 10, 40, 40)`), that nothing outside it changes, and that undo and redo report the same damage.
- The existing tests for a single duplicate, a duplicate that becomes a clipping base (unbo…

title: Paste Layer Style carries Blend If and channels; align to an active selection with several layers
author: tanish2k09
body:
From the first-party layers audit (phase L2, silently wrong results).

- **Paste Layer Style** dropped Blend If and the channel restrictions (Advanced Blending › Channels). It copied only the effects, blend mode, Fill and advanced blending. Photoshop's layer style carries all its Blending Options. Pasting into a document in another colour mode keeps only Blend If's Gray range and resets the channels, since RGB channel ranges don't map onto CMYK. The copied style is now a named `CopiedStyle` struct instead of a 4-tuple.
- **Align with an active selection:** the `auto` target aligned two or more layers to their own combined bounds. Photoshop aligns them to the selection (Layer › Align Layers to Selection), as the code already did for a single layer.

## Tests
- New `tests/style_and_align.rs`, with two tests. **Both fail on `main` and pass here.**
  - Blend If (Gray plus a channel range) and an unchecked channel carry over in RGB; into CMYK only the Gray range carries over and the channels reset.
  - Two layers align their left edges to the selection's left edge.
- The engine suite and `panic_hunt -- --ignored` pass. Clippy `-D warnings` is clean, and the changed files are fmt-clean.

author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #5863.

### What was wrong
The keyboard menu bar (#4988) assigns each row a mnemonic from its label **as shown**. Only ASCII letters and digits can be typed as access keys, so in Chinese, Japanese or Korean no menu had one: Alt+F didn't open 文件, and letters didn't pick rows. title: Canvas: no scroll glide with Enable Animations off (#5721)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #5721.

### What was wrong
The request is an option to turn off smooth scrolling on the canvas. **Preferences › Interface › Enable Animations** already exists for this. Off, it stops egui's fades and makes scroll areas jump straight to their target (#3273, `prefs_ui::sync_animations`). But the canvas ignored it: `wheel_nav::read` always panned from egui's `smooth_scroll_delta`, so each wheel notch kept gliding for several frames whatever the preference said.

### Change
- `wheel_nav::read_with(…, smooth)`: with `smooth` off, a **plain** wheel scroll pans by this frame's own wheel events (already collected and converted to points for snap zoom), so the canvas moves the whole notch in the frame it arrives, with no tail. Alt/Shift gestures, pinch and zoom-with-wheel are unchanged. `read` keeps the old behaviour for its other callers (Camera Raw preview, Navigator).
- `canvas.rs` passes `interface.enableAnimations`.

Photoshop has no smooth-scroll setting of its own; its wheel moves the view directly, which is what animations-off now gives. The default (animations on) is unchanged.

### Test
`wheel_nav::tests::unsmoothed_wheel_pans_at_once_without_a_glide`: with smoothing off, one notch pans exactly `line_scroll_speed` points in its frame and nothing afterwards. Smoothed, the first frame moves only part of it and later frames follow. Not built or run locally; CI runs it.

title: Layer Style: drag on the image to move a drop or inner shadow (#5701)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #5701.

### What was wrong
In Photoshop, while the Layer Style dialog shows a **Drop Shadow** (or Inner Shadow) page, you can drag on the image to move the shadow, which is much quicker than the Angle dial and Distance slider. In PhotoCraft the image under the dialog only panned (Space, middle button, Hand tool) or sampled for colour pickers.

### Change
- `layer_style::drags_shadow(fields)`: the selected page is a Drop Shadow or Inner Shadow instance.
- `layer_style::drag_shadow(fields, start, total)`: on the press it records the instance's angle and distance. The shadow's offset is then the recorded one plus the pointer's movement since the press (document px), stored back as a whole-degree **angle** and whole-pixel **distance**, using the compositor's convention (`offset = (−cos a, sin a) · d`, `compose/src/effects.rs`). Working from the press (not frame by frame) keeps slow drags from losing sub-pixel steps to rounding. Edits go through `set_param`, so an effect using **Global Light** moves the shared angle and every instance tied to it, as in Photoshop. Dragging back onto the layer gives distance 0 and keeps the angle.
- `canvas.rs`: under a Layer Style dialog on a shadow page, a primary drag that starts on the free canvas moves the shadow (Move cursor). Space and middle-button panning still win, the Hand tool doesn't pan there, and an armed colour picker still samples. The live preview follows, since it's keyed on the dialog's params.

### Test
`layer_style::tests::dragging_on_the_image_moves_the_selected_shadow`: the press keeps the shadow in place. Dragging it to straight right of the layer gives 180° and 15 px, moving a Global Light sibling's angle but not an instance with its own. Dragging back gives 0 px with the starting angle. On the Blending Options page nothing moves. Not built or run locally; CI runs it.

title: Windows pen strokes no longer end in a thin tail (Windows Ink)
author: VegaEX
body:
## Problem

With Windows Ink on, every pen stroke ends in a thin, faint "fish tail": the stretch drawn while the pen lifts comes out at near-zero pressure. Textured brushes with a minimum size show it most. Found on a Wacom Cintiq Pro 24.

A pen-event log showed the cause. winit 0.30.13 walks the coalesced entries of each `WM_POINTER*` message (`GetPointerFrameInfoHistory`) but reads each pen entry's pressure with `GetPointerPenInfo(pointerId)`, which returns the **latest** reading. Every sample of a message gets the newest pressure, so a pen lifting while it moves fast draws its whole last batch (~100 px) at the lift's near-zero force. Logged example, one frame before a lift: four moves, all `force=0.035`, while the previous frame was at 0.47.

## Changes

- **`vendor/winit`** (via `[patch.crates-io]`, excluded from the workspace): winit 0.30.13 with one change in `platform_impl/windows`. It loads `GetPointerPenInfoHistory` and gives each coalesced pen entry its own pressure (matched by pointer id and frame id), falling back to `GetPointerPenInfo` when there is no match. The note in `Cargo.toml` says to drop the patch once winit ships the fix.
- **`stylus.rs`**: repeated touch forces within a frame count as one sample, so `select`'s per-move interpolation ramps from the previous frame instead of stepping. This is a fallback for when the pen history is unavailable.
- **`canvas.rs`**: a stroke ends where the button was released (`release_pos`), not at the pointer's latest position. Both the Up position and the "no raw move this frame" fallback used `interact_pointer_pos()`, which a move after the release in the same frame had already carried elsewhere, adding a final point with the pen's last pressure.

## Tests

- `paint_mouse::a_move_after_the_release_draws_no_tail`: a release and a later move in one frame. Without the fix the stroke's last point jumps to the later move.
- `stylus::repeated_touch_forces_ramp_across_the_frame`: the logged lift frame. Without the fix…

title: Window › Timelapse: record a painting session as a video, with reference layers left out (#5004)
author: VegaEX
body:
Closes #5004.

## Why

I come from an art background and I'm trying to make PhotoCraft my daily driver for painting. One thing kept pulling me back to other apps: **timelapses**. Procreate and Clip Studio Paint record your process as you paint, and artists post those videos everywhere (portfolio pieces, social posts, teaching, proof the work is hand-made). #5004 asks for the same thing.

I'd previously started a Photoshop UXP plug-in for this (frames into a folder next to the file, a reference-layer prefix that's left out, ffmpeg for the video). PhotoCraft's plug-in system is sandboxed WebAssembly filters only, with no file system, clock or document events, and panel plug-ins are listed as later work in `docs/architecture.md`. So this is a **built-in, self-contained module** that keeps the plug-in's design and on-disk layout.

## What it does

**Window › Timelapse** opens a small panel:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Start / Stop Recording** | Records the active document. The first frame is taken right away so every (re)start is visible in the video. |
| **Capture Frame Now** | Forces a frame, even if nothing changed. |
| **Min seconds between frames** | Default 20 s. Saved per session. |
| **Reference layer prefix (not recorded)** | Default `REF_`. Any layer **or group** whose name starts with it (case-insensitive, at any depth) is hidden in every frame. |
| **Export Video (MP4 + 30 s)** | Runs ffmpeg in the background and writes `full_timelapse.mp4` (every frame at 24 fps) and `sped_up_30s.mp4` (the whole session squeezed into 30 seconds). Progress and errors show in the panel. |
| **Open Frames Folder** | Opens the session folder in the file manager. |
| Status rows + log | Document, frame count with disk use (e.g. `312 · 148 MB`), state, and a short log. |

title: fix(gpu): start on Macs whose Metal compiler is older than the OS
author: alecanales
body:
## Problem
On a GeForce GT 755M running macOS 15.7 (patched OS), PhotoCraft panicked on every start:

```
Shader translation error for stage VERTEX: Metal: error: invalid value 'metal3.2' in '-std=metal3.2'
In Device::create_render_pipeline, label = 'egui_pipeline'
wgpu: Handling wgpu errors as fatal by default
```

wgpu-hal picks the Metal shading language version from the OS version alone (macOS >= 15 gives MSL 3.2), but this machine's shader compiler only accepts up to `metal3.1`. egui's pipeline then failed while eframe built its renderer, before our `DeviceHealth` handler existed, so wgpu's fatal default handler panicked.

## Changes
- `vendor/wgpu-hal` (wgpu-hal 30.0.1, `[patch.crates-io]`): one change in `src/metal/adapter.rs`, `supported_msl_version`. It compiles a tiny kernel per candidate version and uses the newest the compiler accepts. `WGPU_METAL_MAX_MSL=3.1` overrides. Row added to `ATTRIBUTION.md`.
- `apps/photocraft/src/gpu_startup.rs`, `main.rs` (macOS): `precreate_device` creates the wgpu device before eframe with an uncaptured-error sink. Errors raised while the renderer is built stop startup with a readable message instead of a panic.

## Testing
- New unit test for the startup failure message; `cargo test -p photocraft --bin photocraft gpu_startup` passes (23).
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo xtask layers` pass.
- Launched the debug build on the affected machine: log shows `using MSL 3.1`, no panic, ran normally.

## Not done / for review
- `cargo xtask wasm`, `panic_hunt`, `test-corpus`, `perf` not run. The change is macOS-only and native-only.
- GPU canvas not exercised on this adapter.
- Vendoring is a stopgap; happy to move the patch to craft-libs or send it upstream to wgpu if you prefer.

title: Move: a click on an empty spot or a locked layer deselects every layer
author: bazmarth
body:
## Summary
With the Move tool, a click where no layer can be picked left the selection as it was, and a click on a locked layer (the Background) selected that locked layer. Either way the previously selected layers stayed selected, so there was no quick way to drop the selection from the canvas.

Now, with Auto-Select on (or Cmd/Ctrl-click with it off), a **click** on:
- an empty or transparent spot, or the pasteboard, or
- a **locked layer** such as the Background

**deselects every layer** (`select.deselectLayers`, one undoable step), so nothing is left to move and the transform controls and corner widgets go away.

- **Shift-click** keeps the selection (Shift adds).
- A click with nothing selected records nothing.
- A **drag** there still draws the layer marquee (#2844, #4058) and selects what it touches.
- A press no longer picks a locked layer.
- A release within **3 screen points** of the press counts as a click, so a slightly jittery mouse click works. A flat marquee (a purely horizontal or vertical drag) still selects nothing and changes nothing.

### Screenshots (offscreen `snapshot` example)

title: Add Craft AI: the family's built-in local assistant (Gemma 4 catalogue, loopback runtimes, shared models folder)
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
## What this is

**Craft AI** — one assistant across the ArtCraft family, as a floating window in PhotoCraft. It talks to a local model runtime on this machine and never to a cloud service:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Local and private** | Every request is `http://127.0.0.1` — Ollama (11434), LM Studio (1234) or llama.cpp's server (8080), whichever answers. No account, no key, no telemetry, and no address a cloud service could be reached at exists in the code. |
| **Light by design** | No inference engine, no weights, no GPU code enters the app. The runtime the user already has (or installs) does the running — Craft AI is a loopback conversation. |
| **Optional** | Without a runtime or a model the window says so and touches nothing beyond loopback. Downloading is a button, never a default. |
| **Specialised** | The system prompt tells the model it is inside PhotoCraft and names this app's world — layers, masks and selections, retouching and healing, adjustments and curves, camera raw, smart objects, export — so answers are about this app, not generic advice. The ready-made tasks (retouch plan, layers and masks strategy, menu path finder, export recipe, alt text for the image) are framed for it, with the honesty clause: never invent menu or tool names. |
| **One download serves every app** | The model file lands in a shared folder the whole family reads — `<data_home>/ArtCraft/Craft AI/models` — so a model downloaded here is already there in every other ArtCraft app, no second download. Ollama's own store works the same way machine-wide. |

## The three tabs

- **Assistant** — runtime and model pickers, the task, the question, the answer; the conversation is kept, copyable, and Arabic answers are drawn through the same visual-order pass as the rest of the Arabic interface. Worker thread, so the UI never blocks; a busy timer ticks while the model thinks.
- **Models** — the Gemma 4 catalogue, every figure from the model's own card: **E2B** (3.1 GB, 4 GB RAM) for the lightest …

title: Fix HEVC 4:2:2 decoding with the upstream chroma mode correction
author: optimalbytee
body:
HEVC 4:2:2 pictures can fail with “slice runs past the end of the picture” or decode incorrectly because heic-rs 0.1.4 has an incorrect Table 8-3 chroma mode map. Pin the existing optional decoder to immutable revision `e3d0a074978323ccf49089703233d4831076ccb0`, the 0.1.4-based correction proposed in [upstream PR #10](https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs/pull/10).

This is the standalone dependency correction invited in [#5795](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/5795#issuecomment-6180178871). It contains no Canon CRX sensor decoder, calibration profiles or CR3 import changes. The existing std/parallel feature choices are preserved.

A synthetic 128×128 10-bit 4:2:2 regression checks every Y/Cb/Cr sample against the upstream fixture author's independent FFmpeg hash. The small fixture, source information and MIT/Apache licences are included; it is not a camera photograph.

Validation with the normal project cache and 12 Cargo workers:

- Regression fails on released 0.1.4 with the slice error; passes with the pinned correction.
- Eight HEIF wrapper tests and the new regression pass.
- All 11 existing HEIF corpus tests pass, including independent Apple references, ten-bit alpha, orientation/metadata, limits and exhaustive truncation checks.
- Strict all-target HEIF Clippy, formatting and whitespace checks pass.

`cargo-fuzz` is unavailable here; no fresh fuzzing run is claimed. The optional feature's distribution/patent policy is unchanged. The correction is still awaiting upstream merge and release; the immutable fork revision is explicit rather than a moving branch.

title: Preserve CR3 JPEG preview metadata and colour declarations
author: optimalbytee
body:
CR3 JPEG-preview import currently retains little of the independent container metadata. Preserve CMT1–4 EXIF/GPS/maker blocks, bounded per-frame CTMD metadata and XMP while keeping the existing 8-bit camera-preview import path.

Independent TIFF values and IFD pointers are relocated when rebuilding EXIF. An embedded JPEG ICC profile wins; otherwise sRGB/Adobe RGB tagging follows explicit camera declarations, and an uncalibrated EXIF value alone is not assumed to mean Adobe RGB. JPEG orientation takes precedence over container orientation, is applied once and is normalized for subsequent saves. Malformed metadata produces a warning when a valid preview can still open.

This is a container/preview-only subset of closed #5795. It contains no CRX entropy/wavelet decoding, sensor reconstruction, DNGLab-derived calibration data or external RAW decoder. A regression asserts CR3 sensor decoding remains unsupported. Existing RAW formats, development/tone controls and ICC display code are unchanged. It is independent of #5921 and does not change HEIF dependencies.

Validation using the normal cache and 12 Cargo workers:

- 90 RAW library tests, seven existing CR3 preview tests and two new metadata integration tests passed.
- Three new I/O preview tests and all 12 existing RAW import tests passed, including .pcraft metadata/profile persistence and graceful handling of corrupt metadata.
- Strict all-target RAW/I/O Clippy, formatting, whitespace and 29-crate layering passed.

All new fixtures are generated in memory. No photographs, native sensor oracles, calibration profiles, binaries, or additional mandatory corpus downloads are introduced. Format references and limitations are documented in `docs/cr3-previews.md`; this does not claim native CR3 development or patent clearance for a sensor decoder.

title: Open CR3 HEVC camera previews through the optional HEIF decoder
author: optimalbytee
body:
Open supported camera-rendered HEVC previews inside CR3 files through PhotoCraft's existing optional HEIF decoder. This recovers preview opening, not native CRX RAW/C-RAW development.

**Prerequisites: #5921 (HEIF 4:2:2 correction) and #5922 (CR3 JPEG/container metadata).** This branch includes both prerequisite changes while they await merge. Please merge those first, then rebase this PR. The HEVC-specific seven-file change is [commit c435ccf9](https://github.com/optimalbytee/photocraft/commit/c435ccf93feedb8d8b4e468f6996e3ec25193a3f).

The adapter reads bounded HEVC preview properties/sample tables or PRVW boxes and wraps the existing coded cells into standard HEIF items/grids. It preserves crop geometry, metadata and declared colour encoding. Ten-bit previews remain in 16-bit documents with matching Rec.2020/ST 2084 PQ ICC tagging; supported sRGB declarations are also retained. Unknown transfer declarations produce errors rather than assumed sRGB.

When both previews exist, prefer the larger supported one. Keep a valid JPEG usable when HEIF is not compiled in or the HEVC preview cannot decode, reporting a downgrade when appropriate. HEVC-only files give a clear missing-feature error without HEIF. Import warnings always identify the camera-rendered preview and its original precision.

This is the preview-only recovery of part of closed #5795. It contains no Canon CRX entropy decoder, wavelet reconstruction, native-sensor fixtures/oracles, DNGLab-derived calibration profiles or external RAW decoder. Sensor decoding remains explicitly unsupported in regression tests. It uses the project's existing optional codec policy; it does not claim HEVC is patent-free or introduce a new sensor-decoding exception.

Validation with the normal cache and 12 Cargo workers:

- Four HEVC tests pass with HEIF: cropped multi-cell grids, comparison of all stored pixels against the existing decoder, ten-bit precision, PQ profile serialization, orientation, metadata persistence, unsupport…

title: BMP export: Indexed Color documents save as palette BMPs
author: Sir-Starch
body:
Follow-up to #3869, which made palette BMPs open in Indexed Color mode. The other direction was still missing: saving an Indexed Color document as BMP went through the ordinary RGB path and wrote a 24-bit file, so the colour table was gone on reopen. The PNG exporter already had a palette branch for this.

- `export_mode_specific` now sends Indexed Color to BMP as well as PNG, through a new `encode_bmp_indexed` that writes an 8-bit palette BMP with the document's colour table. BMP has no transparency, so a transparent index is written as its palette colour and the export warns about it. A document without a usable table (none, or more than 256 colours) keeps the old RGB path.
- `bmp_palette` returned the decoder's 256-entry padding, so a 3-colour BMP reopened with 253 extra black entries. It now trims the table to the colours the header declares. (The test added in #3869 only checks the first two entries, so it still passes.)

Checked on `upstream/main` at `cb319fd7`:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -j 12 -p photocraft-codecs -p photocraft-io --lib --tests -- --test-threads=8`
- `cargo clippy -j 12 -p photocraft-codecs -p photocraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo xtask layers`

New tests cover the codec round trip (table and pixels, row padding, bad input, header parsing) and the export/import round trip through `photocraft_io`. I did not run `cargo xtask wasm` or the corpus; the change is pure Rust on the existing `image` encoder, and CI runs both.

title: fix(ui): ensure turning View -> Snap off disables all snapping (#5782)
author: seotarek
body:
Fixes #5782

### Summary of Changes
- Guarded smart guide target generation in `crates/ui-egui/src/snap_ui.rs` behind `snap_on(app)` in `begin()`.
- Added an early return check in `apply()` (`if !snap_on(app) || snap.disabled { return ...; }`) ensuring smart guides and bounds snapping are completely bypassed when View -> Snap is toggled off.
- Preserved user snap preference across view commands in `crates/ui-egui/src/view_cmds.rs`.

title: fix(compose): prevent outside stroke from bleeding into opaque character interior (#5861)
author: seotarek
body:
Fixes #5861

### Summary of Changes
- In `crates/compose/src/effects.rs`, corrected the discontinuity in `outline_share(cov, l)` by immediately returning `0.0` when `outside <= 1e-6`, preventing opaque pixel interiors (`cov=1.0, l=1.0`) from evaluating `rest <= 1e-6` and receiving 100% outside stroke share.
- In `composite_with_effects_prepared`, unified the outside stroke share calculation using `band * outline_share(...)` across raster and vector layers, eliminating the smudge artifact.
- Added regression test `outside_stroke_on_raster_layer_does_not_paint_inside_opaque_pixels` in `crates/compose/src/stroke_tests.rs`.

title: fix(ui): allow clipboard operations in modal dialogs and color picker (#5904)
author: seotarek
body:
Fixes #5904

### Summary of Changes
- Permitted clipboard actions (`"edit.copy" | "edit.cut" | "edit.paste" | "select.all"`) in `modal_allows()` within `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs`, preventing macOS AppKit from disabling Edit menu commands and swallowing `Cmd+C` / `Cmd+V` keystrokes when modal dialogs are active.
- Elevated `TextFieldMenu` rendering order to `Order::Tooltip` so right-click context menus are never obscured by modal dialog layers.
- In `crates/ui-egui/src/text_field_menu.rs`, enabled right-click Copy without prior text selection to automatically select and copy the entire field content.
- In `crates/ui-egui/src/color_picker_ui.rs`, allowed leading `#` to be pasted or typed and automatically stripped while preserving case and input responsiveness.

title: fix(paint): scale blur sigma with brush size and eliminate false selection trail (#5892)
author: seotarek
body:
Fixes #5892

### Summary of Changes
- In `crates/engine/src/retouch_cmds.rs`, decoupled the blur tool sigma calculation from sharpen: blur sigma now scales with brush size `(stroke.brush.size * 0.15).clamp(1.0, 64.0)` instead of `(stroke.brush.size * 0.03).clamp(1.0, 4.0)`, ensuring visible, perceptually expected blur changes at standard 8-bit quantization.
- In `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, excluded retouch tools (`Tool::Blur | Tool::Sharpen | Tool::Dodge | Tool::Burn | Tool::Sponge | Tool::Smudge`) from drawing the fallback white polyline trail (`Color32::from_white_alpha(60)`), which previously created a false selection appearance.

#1729 deliberately kept the chips at one size, centred across both columns of a double toolbar. This PR keeps that centring and changes only the size.

### Solution
- `chip_metrics(pro, double)`: in two columns the chips grow by about a third. Pro goes from 18 to 24 pt (offset 10 → 13) and Classic from 21 to 28 pt (12 → 16). The group still fits both columns (37 of 62 pt in Pro, 44 of 74 pt in Classic) and stays centred.
- `chips_height(pro, studio, double)` now takes the column count for square chips too, and the toolbar's footer reserve uses it. On a short window the tools scroll and the bigger chips stay fully visible.
- The round Studio-style chips are unchanged.
- `docs/ui-design.md`: one sentence on the new size.

I haven't measured Photoshop's exact sizes. "About a third" is my reading of "a little bit bigger", and it's easy to tune in `chip_metrics`.

### Tests
- New `square_color_chips_grow_in_two_tool_columns` in `panels.rs`, run for Pro and Classic. It checks that the sizes fit and that the reserved height grows. It then clicks near the bigger chip's bottom-left corner, beyond egui's interact radius from where the old chip sat, and checks that the foreground Color Picker opens. The test fails if the chips are drawn at the old size.
- Checked visually in offscreen `snapshot` renders: Pro and Classic in one and two columns, and a 1100×480 window in two columns.

  - `filter_dialog::tests::…

title: Canvas textures fit the device's texture limit; GPU tests use the app's device and the GPU lock
author: tanish2k09
body:
Fixes the intermittent `background_redraw` failures reported on main (egui `context.rs:2399` texture assertion, then "GPU device lost").

**App fix (real bug).** `ensure_texture` and `draw_beyond_canvas` reduced the CPU canvas texture to fit `MAX_TEXTURE` (4096) whatever the device allows. On a device with a smaller `max_texture_side` (2048 on some older GPUs and WebGL contexts) a 2600×1700 document was uploaded at full size: egui debug-asserts (`Texture "canvas-…" has size 2600x1700, but the maximum texture side is 2048`) and the backend can't create the texture. Both now fit `min(MAX_TEXTURE, max_texture_side)` (`canvas.rs` `texture_side`). New test `cpu_canvas_texture_fits_the_device_limit` (2600×1700 and 5000×2000 on a 2048 device, 5000×2000 on 8192); `live_stroke_uses_pen_tilt_…` now states its 8192 device, since egui's default context reports 2048.

**Test fixes.**
- `background_redraw` and `navigator_gpu_tests` built their harness with `.wgpu()`, egui's default device limits, not the app's `gpu_canvas::wgpu_setup()` (adapter limits). On that device the GPU canvas lost the device in `hiding_a_large_layer_over_the_gpu_budget_…` on every run here (wgpu `DeviceLostReason::Unknown`, RTX 5090). They now use `.wgpu_setup(wgpu_setup())`, the device the app actually runs on.
- Eleven tests built a wgpu device without `photocraft_testkit::gpu_lock()`, which `testkit/src/gpu.rs` requires so devices aren't created concurrently. They now hold it.

**Verified (Windows, RTX 5090):** `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib` twice: every GPU test passes; the only failures are the four that #5950 fixes (profile label, proxy edge coverage). `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` on 1.99.0 clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean.

**Follow-up (not in this PR):** the GPU canvas lost the device on egui's default limits instead of falling back; on a low-limit device it should degrade to the CPU path without a device loss.

title: Add Color Wheel display mode to the Color panel

body:
## Summary - Adds a Hue Cube / Color Wheel selector to the Color panel group menu. - The Color Wheel shows a hue ring and a saturation/brightness triangle. - H, S and B sliders with editable values stay synchronized with the wheel. - The last selected hue is remembered when saturation or brightness is zero.

title: fix(ui): preview Layer Style blend modes on hover (#5945)
author: agustinpabon
body:
## Problem

In the Layers panel, hovering a mode in the open Blend Mode list previews it live on the canvas (#970). The Layer Style dialog's Blend Mode lists didn't: the canvas only changed once a mode was clicked, on every effect page and on Blending Options.

## Root cause

The dialog drew its Blend Mode lists with `widgets::dropdown`, which drops the hovered option that `dropdown_hovered` reports. The canvas's Layer Style preview (`canvas::display_doc` → `layer_style::preview_hash` / `preview_document`) only renders the dialog's pending fields, so nothing hovered could reach it.

## Solution

- `layer_style/blend_hover.rs` (new, ~70 lines). The dialog body records the mode under the pointer in `PhotocraftApp::style_blend_hover`, keyed by **dialog id + page** (the effect *instance* id, or `blendingOptions`), the parameter it edits, and the frame the list was drawn in.
- `canvas::display_doc` lays it over a *copy* of the fields after the Color Picker's live colour (`color_picker::preview_fields`), following the same pattern. Because the copy changes `preview_hash`, the existing `style_preview` cache renders each hovered mode once and is reused while the pointer rests. Going back to the pending mode gives back the pending key, so the cache never shows stale pixels. There is no second render path, no engine command and no new dialog field.
- The overlay applies only when:
  - the hover belongs to the Layer Style dialog being previewed;
  - the list was drawn this frame or the last one (the canvas is drawn before the dialogs);
  - its page is the one selected;
  - the effect is switched on;
  - the mode differs from the page's pending one.
  
  A change of hover requests a repaint, so the canvas catches up even when the pointer stops.
- `layer_style::body` now takes the dialog id; `blending_page` returns its hovered mode. A dialog disabled under its Color Picker records no hover.
